title: (A cap C) cup (B cap Complement C) = Empty iff B subset C subset Complement A

title: *-Algebra Homomorphism between C*-Algebras is Norm-Decreasing
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ and $\struct {B, \dagger, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be $	ext C^\ast$-algebras. Let $\phi : A 	o B$ be a $\ast$-algebra homomorphism. Then: $
orm {\map \phi x}_B \le 
orm x_A$ for each $x \in A$.

title: *-Algebra Homomorphism preserves Canonical Preordering of C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ and $\struct {B, \square, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be $\text C^\ast$-algebras. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be a $\ast$-algebra homomorphism. Let $\le_A$ and $\le_B$ be the canonical preorderings on $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $x, y, z \in A$ be such that: $x \le_A y \le_A z$ Then we have: $\map \phi x \le_B \map \phi y \le_B \map \phi z$

title: *-Algebra obtains Banach *-Algebra Structure through *-Algebra Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $\struct {B, \square, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be a Banach $\ast$-algebra. Let $\phi : A 	o B$ be a $\ast$-algebra isomorphism. Define $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A : A 	o \R$ by: $
orm a_A = 
orm {\map \phi a}_B$ Then $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ is a Banach $\ast$-algebra. Further if $\struct {B, \square, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ is a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra, then so is $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$.

title: -1^n by -n choose k-1 equals -1^k by -k choose n-1

title: 0 in B-Algebra is Left Cancellable Element
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-Algebra. Then: $\forall x, y \in X: 0 \circ x = 0 \circ y \implies x = y$

Define $0$ as the unique element in the set $P \setminus \map s P$, where: $P$ is the Peano Structure $\map s P$ is the image of the mapping $s$ defined in Peano structure $\setminus$ denotes the set difference. Then: $1 + 1 = 2$ where: $1 := \map s 0$ $2 := \map s 1 = \map s {\map s 0}$ $+$ denotes addition $=$ denotes equality $\map s n$ denotes the successor mapping.

title: 1-Seminorm on Continuous on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions is Norm
snippet: Let $C \closedint a b$ be the space of real-valued functions continuous on $\closedint a b$. Let $x \in C \closedint a b$ be a continuous real valued function. Let $\ds \norm x_1 := \int_a^b \size {\map x t} \rd t$ be the 1-seminorm. Then $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_1$ is a norm on $C \closedint a b$.

title: 1-Sequence Space Continuously Surjects into Separable Banach Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_1} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_1}$ be the $1$-sequence space. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space over $\GF$. Then there exists a bounded linear surjection $Q : \map {\ell_1} \GF \to X$.

title: 1-Sequence Space is Proper Subset of 2-Sequence Space

snippet: $\ell^1$ space is a separable space.

title: 100 in Golden Mean Number System is Equivalent to 011
snippet: Consider the golden mean number system. Let $p$ and $q$ be arbitrary strings in $\set {0, 1}$. Let $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ have a representation which includes the string $100$, say: $x = p100q$ Then $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ also has the representation: $x = p011q$ Similarly, let $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ have a representation which includes the string $011$, say: $x = p011q$ Then $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ also has the representation: $x = p100q$ That is, any instance of $100$ appearing in a representation of a non-negative real number $x$ is equivalent to $011$, and vice versa.

title: 123456789 x 8 + 9 = 987654321
snippet: The above pattern is an instance of the identity: $\ds \paren {b - 2} \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n j b^{n - j} + n = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \paren {b - j} b^{n - j}$ where $b = 10$ and $n$ goes from $1$ to $9$.

title: 123456789 x 9 + 10 = 1111111111

snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Suppose that $f = g$ almost everywhere. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \int g \rd \mu$

title: AM-HM Inequality
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{> 0}$ be strictly positive real numbers. Let $A_n $ be the arithmetic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Let $H_n$ be the harmonic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then $A_n \ge H_n$.

title: ARIMA Model subsumes ARMA Model
snippet: Let $S$ be a stochastic process based on an equispaced time series. Let $M$ be an ARMA model for $S$. Then $M$ is also an implementation of an ARIMA model.

title: ARIMA Model subsumes Autoregressive Model
snippet: Let $S$ be a stochastic process based on an equispaced time series. Let $M$ be an autoregressive model for $S$. Then $M$ is also an implementation of an ARIMA model.

title: ARIMA Model subsumes Moving Average Model
snippet: Let $S$ be a stochastic process based on an equispaced time series. Let $M$ be a moving average model for $S$. Then $M$ is also an implementation of an ARIMA model.

title: Abel's Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\sequence a$ and $\sequence b$ be sequences in an arbitrary ring $R$.

title: Abel's Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k$ be a convergent series in $\R$. Then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-} \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k} = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k$ where $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-}$ denotes the limit from the left.

title: Abel's Summation Formula
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \in \N_{>0} }$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $f : \R_{\ge 1} \to \R$ be a continuously differentiable function. Let $A : \R_{\ge 1} \to \R$ be defined as: $\ds \map A x := \sum_{1 \mathop \le n \mathop \le x} a_n$ Then for all $x \in \R_{\ge 1}$: $\ds \sum_{1 \mathop \le n \mathop \le x} a_n \map f n = \map A x \map f x - \int _1 ^x \map A u \map {f'} u \rd u$

title: Abel's Test
snippet: Let $\ds \sum b_n$ be a convergent real series. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a decreasing sequence of positive real numbers. Then the series $\ds \sum a_n b_n$ is also convergent.

title: Abel's Test for Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ and $\sequence {\map {b_n} z}$ be sequences of complex functions on a compact set $K$. Let $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ be such that: $\sequence {\map {a_n} z}$ is bounded in $K$ $\ds \sum \size {\map {a_n} z - \map {a_{n + 1} } z}$ is convergent with a sum which is bounded in $K$ $\ds \sum \map {b_n} z$ is uniformly convergent in $K$. Then $\ds \sum \map {a_n} z \map {b_n} z$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

title: Abel-Plana Formula
snippet: Let $\map f z$ be analytic for real part of $\map \Re z \ge 0$. Suppose that either $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \map f n$ converges or $\ds \int_0^\infty \map f x \rd x$ converges. Assume further that: $\ds \lim_{y \mathop \to \infty} \size {\map f {x \pm i y} } e^{-2 \pi y} = 0$ uniformly in $x$ on every finite subdivision $\ds \int_0^{\infty} \size {\map f {x \pm i y} } e^{-2 \pi y} \rd y$ exists for every $x \ge 0$ and tends to $0$ as $x \to \infty$.

title: Abel-Ruffini Theorem
snippet: There is no general algebraic solution for determining all the roots of a polynomial of degree $5$ or higher.

title: Abelian Group Factored by Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Let $p$ be a prime. Factor the order of $G$ as: $\order G = m p^n$ such that $p$ does not divide $m$. Then: $G = H \times K$ where: $H = \set {x \in G : x^{p^n} = e}$ and: $K = \set {x \in G : x^m = e}$ Furthermore: $\order H = p^n$

title: Abelian Group Induces Commutative B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let $*$ be the product inverse operation on $G$: $\forall a, b \in G: a * b = a \circ b^{-1}$ where $b^{-1}$ is the inverse element of $b$ under the operation $\circ$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {G, *}$ is a commutative $B$-algebra. That is: $\forall a, b \in G: a * \paren {0 * b} = b * \paren {0 * a}$

title: Abelian Group Induces Entropic Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group. Let the operation $*$ be defined on $G$ such that: $\forall x, y \in G: x * y = x \circ y^{-1}$ Then $\struct {G, *}$ is an entropic structure.

title: Abelian Group is Simple iff Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-trivial abelian group. Then $G$ is simple $G$ is a prime group.

title: Abelian Group of Order Twice Odd has Exactly One Order 2 Element
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let the order of $G$ be $2 n$ such that $n$ is odd. Then there exists exactly one $g \in G$ with $g \ne e$ such that $g = g^{-1}$.

title: Abelian Group of Prime-power Order is Product of Cyclic Groups
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group of prime-power order. Let $a$ be an element of maximal order in $G$. Then $G$ can be written in the form $\gen a \times K$ for some $K \le G$.

title: Abelian Group of Semiprime Order is Cyclic
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct prime numbers. Let $G$ be an abelian group such that: $\order G = p q$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$. Then $G$ is cyclic.

title: Abelianization of Free Group is Free Abelian Group
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {F_X, \iota}$ be a free group on $X$. Let $F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }$ be its abelianization. Let $\pi : F_X \to F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }$ be the quotient group epimorphism. Then $\struct {F_X^{\mathrm {ab} }, \pi \circ \iota}$ is a free abelian group on $X$.

title: Abelianization of Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $G^{\mathrm {ab} }$ denote the abelianization of $G$. Then $G^{\mathrm {ab} }$ is an abelian group.

title: Abi-Khuzam Inequality
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Then: $\sin A \cdot \sin B \cdot \sin C \le k A \cdot B \cdot C$ where: $A, B, C$ are measured in radians $k = \paren {\dfrac {3 \sqrt 3} {2 \pi} }^3 \approx 0 \cdotp 56559 \, 56245 \ldots$

title: Abnormal Subgroup is Self-Normalizing Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be an abnormal subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is a self-normalizing subgroup of $G$.

title: Absolute Continuity of Measures is Transitive Relation
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$, $
u$ and $\lambda$ be measures on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ such that: $\mu$ is absolutely continuous $

title: Absolute Cumulative Frequency/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Absolute Cumulative Frequency ==

title: Absolute Difference Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The absolute difference function $\operatorname {adf}: \N^2 \to \N$, defined as: $\map {\operatorname {adf} } {n, m} = \size {n - m}$ where $\size a$ is defined as the absolute value of $a$, is primitive recursive‎.

title: Absolute Error of Sum is not Greater than Sum of Absolute Errors
snippet: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be approximations to a collection of (true) values $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ respectively. Let $\Delta X_i$ be the absolute error of $X_i$ in $x_i$ for $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Then: $\ds \map \Delta {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i} \le \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \Delta X_i$ That is, the absolute error of a sum of approximations is not greater than the sum of the absolute errors of those approximations.

title: Absolute Net Convergence Equivalent to Absolute Convergence
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\sequence {v_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of elements in $V$. Let $r \in \R_{\mathop \ge 0}$ Then the following two statements are equivalent: $(1): \quad$ the generalized sum $\ds \sum \set {v_n: n \in \N}$ is absolutely net convergent to $r$ $(2): \quad$ the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty v_n$ is absolutely convergent to $r$

title: Absolute Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Absolute Numbers == Examples of absolute numbers include: $2$, $\sqrt 5$, $1.976$, $\dfrac 2 3$, $\pi$ (pi), $e$ (Euler's number)

title: Absolute Polar Reverses Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq B \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $A^\circ$ and $B^\circ$ denote the absolute polars of $A$ and $B$ in $\innerprod E F$. Then $B^\circ \subseteq A^\circ$.

title: Absolute Polar is Absolute Prepolar in Transpose
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$ be the transpose dual system. Let $A \subseteq E$ be a non-empty set. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$ taken in $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$. Let $A_{\circ^T}$ be the absolute prepolar of $A$ taken in $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$. Then we have: $A^\circ = A_{\circ^T}$

title: Absolute Polar is Balanced
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$. Then $A^\circ$ is balanced.

title: Absolute Polar is Closed in Weak-* Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\map \sigma {F, E}$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$. Then $A^\circ$ is $\map \sigma {F, E}$-closed.

title: Absolute Polar is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$. Then $A^\circ$ is convex.

title: Absolute Polar is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$. Then $A^\circ \ne \O$.

title: Absolute Polar of Absorbing Set is von Neumann-Bounded in Weak-* Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\map \sigma {F, E}$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be an absorbing set. Let $A^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$. Then $A^\circ$ is $\map \sigma {F, E}$-von Neumann bounded.

title: Absolute Polar of Closed Unit Ball in Normed Vector Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast,

orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $B_{X^\ast}^-$ be the closed unit ball of $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$. Let $\paren {B_X^-}^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $B_X^-$ taken in the dual system $\innerprod X {X^\ast}$. Then: $\paren {B_X^-}^\circ = B_{X^\ast}^-$

title: Absolute Polar of Dilation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $\lambda > 0$. Let $A^\circ$ and $\paren {\lambda A}^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $A$ and $\lambda A$ respectively. Then: $\paren {\lambda A}^\circ = \dfrac 1 \lambda A^\circ$

title: Absolute Prepolar is Absolute Polar in Transpose
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$ be the transpose dual system. Let $B \subseteq F$ be a non-empty set. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$ taken in $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$. Let $B^{\circ^T}$ be the absolute polar of $B$ taken in $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$. Then we have: $B_\circ = B^{\circ^T}$

title: Absolute Prepolar is Balanced
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq F$ be non-empty. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$. Then $B_\circ$ is balanced.

title: Absolute Prepolar is Closed in Weak Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\map \sigma {E, F}$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Let $B \subseteq E$ be non-empty. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$. Then $B_\circ$ is $\map \sigma {E, F}$-closed.

title: Absolute Prepolar is Convex Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq F$ be non-empty. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$. Then $B_\circ$ is convex.

title: Absolute Prepolar is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq F$ be non-empty. Let $B_\circ$ be the absolute prepolar of $B$. Then $B_\circ \ne \O$.

title: Absolute Prepolar of Closed Unit Ball in Normed Dual Space

title: Absolute Value/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Absolute Values ==

title: Absolute Value Function is Completely Multiplicative
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Then: $\size {x y} = \size x \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Thus the absolute value function is completely multiplicative.

title: Absolute Value Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \size x$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $f$ is a continuous real function.

title: Absolute Value Function is Convex
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the absolute value function on the real numbers. Then $f$ is convex.

title: Absolute Value Function is Even Function
snippet: Let $\size {\, \cdot \,} : \R \to \R$ denote the absolute value function on $\R$: Then $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ is an even function.

title: Absolute Value Function on Integers induces Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Absolute Value induces Equivalence Compatible with Integer Multiplication
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \struct {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is a congruence relation for integer multiplication.

title: Absolute Value induces Equivalence not Compatible with Integer Addition
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \size x = \size y$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$. Then $\RR$ is not a congruence relation for integer addition.

title: Absolute Value is Bounded Below by Zero
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then the absolute value $\size x$ of $x$ is bounded below by $0$.

title: Absolute Value is Many-to-One
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the absolute value function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$ Then $f$ is a many-to-one relation.

title: Absolute Value is Norm
snippet: The absolute value is a norm on the set of real numbers $\R$.

title: Absolute Value of Absolutely Continuous Function is Absolutely Continuous
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f : I \to \R$ be an absolutely continuous function. Then $\size f$ is absolutely continuous.

title: Absolute Value of Absolutely Convergent Product is Absolutely Convergent
snippet:
Let $\struct {\mathbb K, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converge absolutely to $a \in \mathbb K$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 
orm {a_n}$ converges absolutely to $
orm a$.

title: Absolute Value of Complex Cross Product is Commutative
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Let $z_1 \times z_2$ denote the (complex) cross product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then: $\size {z_1 \times z_2} = \size {z_2 \times z_1}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the absolute value function.

title: Absolute Value of Complex Dot Product is Commutative
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Let $z_1 \circ z_2$ denote the (complex) dot product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then: $\size {z_1 \circ z_2} = \size {z_2 \circ z_1}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the absolute value function.

title: Absolute Value of Components of Complex Number no greater than Root 2 of Modulus
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\size x + \size y \le \sqrt 2 \cmod z$ where: $\size x$ and $\size y$ denote the absolute value of $x$ and $y$ $\cmod z$ denotes the complex modulus of $z$.

title: Absolute Value of Continuous Real Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be continuous at a point $a \in \R$. Then: $\size f$ is continuous at $a$ where: $\map {\size f} x$ is defined as $\size {\map f x}$.

title: Absolute Value of Convergent Infinite Product
snippet:
Let $\struct {\mathbb K, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converge to $a \in \mathbb K$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 
orm {a_n}$ converges to $
orm{a}$.

title: Absolute Value of Cut is Greater Than or Equal To Zero Cut
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $\size \alpha$ denote the absolute value of $\alpha$. Then: $\size \alpha \ge 0^*$ where: $0^*$ denotes the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$ $\ge$ denotes the ordering on cuts.

title: Absolute Value of Cut is Zero iff Cut is Zero
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $\size \alpha$ denote the absolute value of $\alpha$. Then: $\size \alpha = 0^*$ $\alpha = 0^*$ where $0^*$ denotes the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$.

title: Absolute Value of Divergent Infinite Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ diverges to $0$ $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \norm {a_n}$ diverges to $0$.

title: Absolute Value of Even Power
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\size {x^{2 n} } = x^{2 n}$

title: Absolute Value of Function is Composite with Absolute Value Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $f: S \to \R$ be real-valued function. Let $\size f$ denote the absolute value of $f$, that is, $\size f$ is the mapping defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\size f} s = \size{\map f s}$ Then: $\size f = \size{\,\cdot\,} \circ f$ where: $\size{\,\cdot\,} : \R \to \R$ denotes the absoute value function $\size{\,\cdot\,} \circ f$ denotes the composite mapping of $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ and $f$

title: Absolute Value of Infinite Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence{a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$.

title: Absolute Value of Integer is Primitive Recursive
snippet: For every $n \in \N$, let $n$ code the integer $k_n$. Let $a : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\map a n = \size {k_n}$ Then, $a$ is primitive recursive.

title: Absolute Value of Integer is not less than Divisors
snippet: A (non-zero) integer is greater than or equal to its divisors in magnitude: $\forall c \in \Z_{\ne 0}: a \divides c \implies a \le \size a \le \size c$

title: Absolute Value of Martingale is Submartingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a continuous-time filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a $\sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}$-martingale. Then $\sequence {\size {X_t} }_{t \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}$-submartingale.

title: Absolute Value of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then: $\size f$ is a $\Sigma$-measurable function.

title: Absolute Value of Negative
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\size x = \size {-x}$ where $\size x$ denotes the absolute value of $x$.

title: Absolute Value of Pearson Correlation Coefficient is Less Than or Equal to 1
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the variances of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then: $\size {\map \rho {X, Y} } \le 1$ where $\map \rho {X, Y}$ denotes the Pearson correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y$.

title: Absolute Value of Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$ be real numbers. Let $x^y$, $x$ to the power of $y$, be real. Then: $\size {x^y} = \size x^y$

title: Absolute Value of Real-Valued Random Variable is Real-Valued Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable. Then $\size X$ is a real-valued random variable.

title: Absolute Value of Signed Measure Bounded Above by Variation
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\size \mu$ be the variation of $\mu$. Then: $\size {\map \mu A} \le \map {\size \mu} A$ for each $A \in \Sigma$.

title: Absolute Value of Simple Function is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f: X \to \R$ be a simple function. Then $\size f: X \to \R$, the absolute value of $f$, is also a simple function.

title: Absolute Value of Trigonometric Function
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle embedded in a Cartesian plane. Let $\theta$ be such that the vertex of $\theta$ is located at the origin while one arm is coincident with the $x$-axis. Let $\phi$ be the acute angle made by the other arm with the $x$-axis. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a trigonometric function. Then $\size {\map f \theta}$ is equal to $\map f \phi$. That is, a trigonometric function of an angle can be calculated by working out its quadrant to determine its sign, then using the equivalent value of what it is between $0$ and $90 \degrees$ to get its value.

title: Absolute Value of Uniformly Convergent Product
snippet:
Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X 	o \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly to $f$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 
orm {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $
orm f$.

title: Absolute Value on Ordered Integral Domain is Strictly Positive except when Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain. For all $a \in D$, let $\size a$ denote the absolute value of $a$. Then $\size a$ is (strictly) positive except when $a = 0$.

title: Absolutely Continuous Random Variable is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then $X$ is a continuous random variable.

title: Absolutely Continuous Real Function has Derivative Almost Everywhere

title: Acceleration Due to Gravity
snippet: == Physical Law == A body $B$ in a uniform gravitational field experiences a force which gives rise to a constant acceleration independent of the mass of the body. If the force due to the gravitational field is the only force on $B$, it is said to be in free fall.

title: Acceleration Vector in Polar Coordinates
snippet: Consider a particle $p$ moving in the plane. Let the position of $p$ at time $t$ be given in polar coordinates as $\polar {r, \theta}$. Then the acceleration $\mathbf a$ of $p$ can be expressed as: $\mathbf a = \paren {r \dfrac {\d^2 \theta} {\d t^2} + 2 \dfrac {\d r} {\d t} \dfrac {\d \theta} {\d t} } \mathbf u_\theta + \paren {\dfrac {\d^2 r} {\d t^2} - r \paren {\dfrac {\d \theta} {\d t} }^2} \mathbf u_r$ where: $\mathbf u_r$ is the unit vector in the direction of the radial coordinate of $p$ $\mathbf u_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of the angular coordinate of $p$

title: Acceleration is Second Derivative of Displacement with respect to Time
snippet: The acceleration $\mathbf a$ of a body $M$ is the second derivative of the displacement $\mathbf s$ of $M$ from a given point of reference time $t$: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d^2 \mathbf s} {\d t^2}$

title: Acceleration of Particle moving in Circle at Constant Speed
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle moving in a circular path $C$ at a constant speed. Then the acceleration of $P$, denoted by $\mathbf a \in \R$, is given as: $\mathbf a = -\dfrac {\size {\mathbf v}^2 \mathbf r} {\size {\mathbf r}^2}$ where: $\mathbf v$ is the instantaneous velocity of $P$ $\mathbf r$ is the vector whose magnitude equals the length of the radius of $C$ and whose direction is from the center of $C$ to $P$ $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the magnitude of a vector.

title: Acceleration of Point in Plane in Intrinsic Coordinates
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be the acceleration of a particle $P$ in space. Let $P$ be moving in a plane $\PP$. Then the motion of $P$ can be expressed in intrinsic coordinates as: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d \map v t} {\d t} \mathbf s + \dfrac {\paren {\map v t}^2} \rho \bspsi$ where: $\mathbf s$ denotes the unit vector along the tangential direction of $P$ $\bspsi$ denotes the unit vector toward the center of curvature of the motion of $P$ $\map v t$ is the speed of $P$ at the time $t$ $\rho$ is the radius of curvature of the motion of $P$ at time $t$.

title: Acceleration of Point in Straight Line
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be the acceleration of a particle $P$ in space. Let $P$ be moving along a straight line $\LL$ whose positive direction has been established. Then the motion of $P$ can be defined by: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d^2 s} {\d t^2} \mathbf i$ where $\mathbf i$ denotes the unit vector in the positive direction of $\LL$.

title: Acceleration of Rocket in Outer Space
snippet: Let $B$ be a rocket travelling in outer space. Let the velocity of $B$ at time $t$ be $\mathbf v$. Let the mass of $B$ at time $t$ be $m$. Let the exhaust velocity of $B$ be constant at $\mathbf b$. Then the acceleration of $B$ at time $t$ is given by: $\mathbf a = \dfrac 1 m \paren {-\mathbf b \dfrac {\d m} {\d t} }$

title: Acceleration with respect to Relative Acceleration
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be bodies in space. Let $\mathbf a_A$ and $\mathbf a_B$ denote the accelerations of $A$ and $B$. Let $\mathbf a_{AB}$ denote the acceleration of $A$ relative to $B$. Then: $\mathbf a_A = \mathbf a_{AB} + \mathbf a_B$

title: Accumulation Point of Infinite Sequence in First-Countable Space is Subsequential Limit

title: Accumulation Point of Sequence iff Cluster Point of Net

title: Accumulation Point of Sequence is not necessarily Limit Point

title: Accumulation Point of Sequence of Distinct Terms is Omega-Accumulation Point of Range
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence of distinct terms of $S$. Let $\alpha$ be an accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $\alpha$ is also an $\omega$-accumulation point of $\set {x_n: n \in \N}$.

title: Accumulation Point of Sequence of Reciprocals and Reciprocals + 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ denote the sequence in $\struct {\R, \tau}$ defined as: {{eqn | l = a_n | r = \begin {cases} \dfrac 2 {n + 1} & : \text {$n$ odd} \\ 1 + \dfrac 2 n & : \text {$n$ even} \end {cases} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sequence {\dfrac 1 1, 1 + \dfrac 1 1, \dfrac 1 2, 1 + \dfrac 1 2, \dfrac 1 3, 1 + \dfrac 1 3, \dotsb} | c = }} Then $0$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_n}$.

title: Accumulation Points for Sequence in Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be an infinite sequence in $T$. Let $\beta$ be an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_i}$. Then $\beta$ is such that an infinite number of terms of $\sequence {a_i}$ are equal either to $\beta$ or to $p$.

title: Accumulation Points of Sequence of Distinct Terms in Infinite Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Let $U \in \tau_p$ be a countably infinite open set of $T$. Let the elements of $U$ be arranged into a sequence $\sequence {a_i}$ of distinct terms in $T$. Then while every element $x$ of $U$ such that $x \ne p$ is a limit point of $U$, there exists no $x \in U$ such that $x$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {a_i}$.

title: Accuracy of Convergents of Continued Fraction
Accuracy of Convergents of Continued Fraction Expansion of Irrational Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number. Let $(a_0, a_1, \ldots)$ be its continued fraction expansion. Let $\left \langle {C_n}\right \rangle_{n \geq 0}$ be its sequence of convergents. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Then: $\forall k \ge 1: \left\vert{x - \dfrac {p_{k + 1} } {q_{k + 1} } }\right\vert < \dfrac 1 {q_{k + 1} q_{k + 2} } \le \dfrac 1 {2 q_k q_{k + 1} } < \left\vert{x - \dfrac {p_k} {q_k} }\right\vert$ Thus: The of the inequality gives an indication of how close each convergent gets to its true value.

title: Accuracy of Convergents of Convergent Simple Infinite Continued Fraction
snippet: Let $C = \tuple {a_0, a_1, \ldots}$ be an simple infinite continued fraction in $\R$. Let $C$ converge to $x \in \R$. For $n \ge 0$, let $C_n = \dfrac {p_n} {q_n}$ be the $n$th convergent of $C$, where $p_n$ and $q_n$ are the $n$th numerator and denominator. Then for all $n \ge 0$: $\size {x - \dfrac {p_n} {q_n} } < \dfrac 1 {q_n q_{n + 1} }$

title: Achilles Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == and a are to have a . Achilles (not surprisingly) is expected to run considerably faster than the tortoise. So, to make it marginally more fair, he gives the tortoise a head start. But it is apparent that Achilles cannot actually catch up with the tortoise. Suppose he gives the tortoise a headstart of $x_0$. By the time he has got to $x_0$, the tortoise has moved on, to $x_1$, say. title: Addition Law of Probability
snippet: Let $\Pr$ be a probability measure on an event space $\Sigma$. Let $A, B \in \Sigma$. The probability of the occurrence of the union of $A$ and $B$ can be evaluated as: $\map \Pr {A \cup B} = \map \Pr A + \map \Pr B - \map \Pr {A \cap B}$ That is, the probability of either event occurring equals the sum of their individual probabilities less the probability of them both occurring. This is known as the addition law of probability.

title: Addition in Minimally Inductive Set is Unique
snippet: Let $\omega$ be the minimally inductive set. Let $A: \omega \times \omega \to \omega$ be the mapping defined as the addition operation: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in \omega \times \omega: \map A {x, y} = \begin {cases} x & : y = 0 \\ \paren {\map A {x, r} }^+ & : y = r^+ \end {cases}$ where $r^+$ is the successor set of $r$. Then $A$ exists and is unique.

title: Addition is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^2 \to \N$ be defined as: $\map f {x, y} = x + y$ Then there exists a WFF $\map \phi {z, x, y}$ of $3$ free variables and containing no quantifiers such that: $z = \map f {x, y} \iff \N \models \map \phi {\sqbrk z, \sqbrk x, \sqbrk y}$ where $\sqbrk a$ is the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Addition of 1 in Golden Mean Number System
snippet: == Algorithm == Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The following algorithm performs the operation of addition of $1$ to $x$ in the golden mean number system. Let $S$ be the representation of $x$ in the golden mean number system in its simplest form. Step $1$: Is the digit immediately to the left of the radix point a zero? If Yes, replace that $0$ with $1$. Go to Step $4$. If No, set $m = 2$ and go to Step $2$. Step $2$: Does the $m$th place after the radix point contain $0$? If Yes, expand the $100$ in the $3$ places ending in the $m$th place with $011$. Subtract $2$ from $m$. Go to Step $3$.

title: Addition of Coordinates on Cartesian Plane under Chebyshev Distance is Continuous Function

title: Addition of Cross-Relation Equivalence Classes on Natural Numbers is Cancellable

Let $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$ be the (external) direct product of $\struct {\N, +}$ with itself, where $\oplus$ is the operation on $\N \times \N$ induced by $+$ on $\N$. Let $\boxtimes$ be the cross-relation defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ Let $\eqclass {x, y} {}$ denote the equivalence class of $\tuple {x, y}$ under $\boxtimes$.

title: Addition of Cuts is Associative
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let the operation of $\alpha + \beta$ be the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\paren {\alpha + \beta} + \gamma = \alpha + \paren {\beta + \gamma}$

title: Addition of Cuts is Commutative
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Let the operation of $\alpha + \beta$ be the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\alpha + \beta = \beta + \alpha$

title: Addition of Division Products
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {U_R, \circ}$ be the group of units of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $a, c \in R, b, d \in U_R$. Then: $\dfrac a b + \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a \circ d + b \circ c} {b \circ d}$ where $\dfrac x z$ is defined as $x \circ \paren {z^{-1} }$, that is, $x$ divided by $z$.

title: Addition of Division Products in Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$ and whose unity is $1$. Let $a, b, c, d \in F$ such that $b \ne 0$ and $d \ne 0$. Then: $\dfrac a b + \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a d + b c} {b d}$ where $\dfrac x z$ is defined as $x \paren {z^{-1} }$.

title: Addition of Fractions
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ such that $b d \ne 0$. Then: $\dfrac a b + \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a D + B c} {\lcm \set {b, d} }$ where: $B = \dfrac b {\gcd \set {b, d} }$ $D = \dfrac d {\gcd \set {b, d} }$ $\lcm$ denotes lowest common multiple $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor.

title: Addition of Integers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $a : \N^2 \to \N$ be defined as: $\map a {m, n} = p$ where: $m$ codes an integer $k$ $n$ codes an integer $\ell$ $p$ codes the integer $k + \ell$ Then $a$ is a primitive recursive function.

title: Addition of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ and $\struct {H, +_H}$ be abelian groups. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}$ be $R$-modules. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\oplus_H$ be defined as pointwise addition on $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$: $\forall \phi, \psi \in \map {\LL_R} {G, H}: \forall x \in G: \map {\paren {\phi \oplus_H \psi} } x := \map \phi x +_H \map \psi x$ Then $\phi \oplus_H \psi: G \to H$ is a linear transformation.

title: Addition of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$ be natural numbers. Then there exists formal proof of: $\sqbrk x + \sqbrk y = \sqbrk {x + y}$ in minimal arithmetic, where $\sqbrk a$ is the unary representation of $a$.

title: Addition of Numbers is not Distributive over Multiplication
snippet: Addition of numbers is not distributive over multiplication. That is, for numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ it is not necessarily the case that $a + \paren {b \times c} = \paren {a + b} \times \paren {a + c}$.

title: Addition of Order Types/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Addition of Order Types ==

title: Addition of Real and Imaginary Parts
snippet: Let $z_0, z_1 \in \C$ be two complex numbers. Then: $\map \Re {z_0 + z_1} = \map \Re {z_0} + \map \Re {z_1}$ and: $\map \Im {z_0 + z_1} = \map \Im {z_0} + \map \Im {z_1}$ Here, $\map \Re {z_0}$ denotes the real part of $z_0$, and $\map \Im {z_0}$ denotes the imaginary part of $z_0$.

title: Addition on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $+$ be addition on $\N_{>0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a + c = b + c \implies a = b$ $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a + b = a + c \implies b = c$ That is, $+$ is cancellable on $\N_{>0}$.

title: Addition on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Cancellable for Ordering
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $0}$. Let $+$ be addition on $\N_{>0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a + c 0}: a + b 0}$ for $<$.

title: Addition on Numbers has no Zero Element
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ there exists no zero element for addition.

title: Additive Function (Algebra)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Additive Functions == In the field of abstract algebra, this operation can be seen to be a endomorphism on $\struct {S, +}$. In the field of linear algebra, it can be seen that a linear transformation is additive. When the domain is the set of real numbers, this is the Cauchy Functional Equation.

title: Additive Function is Linear for Rational Factors
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an additive function. Then: $\forall r \in \Q, x \in \R: \map f {x r} = r \map f x$

title: Additive Function is Odd Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an additive function. Then $f$ is an odd function.

title: Additive Function is Strongly Additive
snippet: Let $\SS$ be an algebra of sets. Let $f: \SS \to \overline \R$ be an additive function on $\SS$. Then $f$ is also strongly additive. That is: $\forall A, B \in \SS: \map f {A \cup B} + \map f {A \cap B} = \map f A + \map f B$

title: Additive Function of Zero is Zero
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an additive function. Then: $\map f 0 = 0$

title: Additive Function on Empty Set is Zero
snippet: Let $\AA$ be an algebra of sets. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be an additive function on $\AA$. Then $\map f \O = 0$.

title: Additive Group and Multiplicative Group of Field are not Isomorphic
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $\struct {F, +}$ denote the additive group of $F$. Let $\struct {F_{\ne 0_F}, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of $F$. Then $\struct {F, +}$ and $\struct {F_{\ne 0_F}, \times}$ are not isomorphic to each other.

title: Additive Group of Complex Numbers is Direct Product of Reals with Reals
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then the direct product $\struct {\R, +} \times \struct {\R, +}$ is isomorphic with $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Integers Modulo m/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Additive Groups of Integers Modulo $m$ == Category:Examples of Additive Groups of Integers Modulo m

title: Additive Group of Integers is Countably Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms a countably infinite abelian group.

title: Additive Group of Integers is Normal Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Integers is Normal Subgroup of Rationals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\Q, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Integers is Normal Subgroup of Reals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\R, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Integers is Subgroup of Rationals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\Q, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Integers is Subgroup of Reals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\Z, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\R, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Rational Numbers is not Finitely Generated
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, +}$ is not finitely generated.

title: Additive Group of Rational Numbers is not Isomorphic to Multiplicative Group of Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\Q_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Q_{\ne 0}, \times}$ is not isomorphic to $\struct {\Q, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Rationals is Normal Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Rationals is Normal Subgroup of Reals
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, +}$ be the additive group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\R, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Real Numbers is Not Isomorphic to Multiplicative Group of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ denote the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\R_{\ne 0}, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\R, +}$ is not isomorphic to $\struct {\R_{\ne 0}, \times}$.

title: Additive Group of Reals is Normal Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\R, +}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Additive Group of Reals is Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\R, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Additive Groups of Integers and Integer Multiples are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\struct {n \Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integer multiples. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Then $\struct {n \Z, +}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {\Z, +}$.

title: Additive Inverse in Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $f \in \map {C^*} {S, \R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{-f}} s = - \map f s$

title: Additive Inverse in Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with zero $0_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Let $f \in \map C {S, R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{-f}} s = - \map f s$

title: Additive Inverse in Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $f \in \map C {S, \R}$. Then: the additive inverse of $f$ is the pointwise negation $-f$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {-f} s = - \map f s$

title: Additive Inverse in Vector Space is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_F$ be a vector space over a field $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then for every $\mathbf v \in \mathbf V$, the additive inverse of $\mathbf v$ is unique: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: \exists! \paren {-\mathbf v} \in \mathbf V: \mathbf v + \paren {-\mathbf v} = \mathbf 0$

title: Additive Nowhere Negative Function is Subadditive
snippet: Let $\AA$ be an algebra of sets. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be an additive function such that: $\forall A \in \AA: \map f A \ge 0$ Then $f$ is subadditive.

title: Additive Regular Representations of Topological Ring are Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {R, + , \circ, \tau}$ be a topological ring. Let $x \in R$. Let $\lambda_x$ and $\rho_x$ be the left and right regular representations of $\struct {R, +}$ with respect to $x$. Then $\lambda_x, \,\rho_x: \struct {R, \tau} \to \struct {R, \tau}$ are homeomorphisms with inverses $\lambda_{-x}, \,\rho_{-x}: \struct {R, \tau} \to \struct {R, \tau}$ respectively.

title: Additive and Countably Subadditive Function is Countably Additive
snippet: Let $\Sigma$ be a $\sigma$-algebra over a set $X$. Let $f: \Sigma \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be an additive and countably subadditive function, where $\overline \R_{\ge 0}$ denotes the set of positive extended real numbers. Then $f$ is countably additive.

title: Additivity of Riemannian Length of Admissible Curve
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : \closedint a b \to M$ with $t \stackrel \gamma \mapsto \map \gamma t$ be an admissible curve. Let $c \in \R$ be a real number such that $a < c < b$. Let $\map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a b} }$ be the Riemannian length of $\gamma$ from $t = a$ to $t = b$. Then: $\map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a b} } = \map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint a c} } + \map {L_g} {\valueat \gamma {\closedint c b} }$

title: Adherent Point of Filter iff Superfilter Converges
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a filter on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is a adherent point of $\FF$ there exists a superfilter $\FF'$ of $\FF$ on $S$ which converges to $x$.

title: Adjacency Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Adjacency Matrices ==

title: Adjacency Matrix for Undirected Graph is Symmetric
snippet: Let $G$ be an undirected graph. The adjacency matrix for $G$ is a symmetric matrix.

title: Adjoined Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Adjoined Numbers ==

title: Adjoining Commutes with Inverting
snippet: Let $\HH$ and $\KK$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $\map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be the set of bounded linear transformations from $\HH$ to $\KK$. Let $A \in \map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded linear transformation on $\HH$. Let $A^{-1} \in \map \BB {\KK, \HH}$ be an inverse for $A$. Let $A^*$ denote the adjoint of $A$. Then $A^*$, is invertible, and: $\paren {A^*}^{-1} = \paren {A^{-1} }^*$

title: Adjoint is Conjugate Linear
snippet: Let $\HH$ and $\KK$ be Hilbert spaces over $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be the set of bounded linear transformations from $\HH$ to $\KK$. Let $A, B \in \map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be bounded linear transformations. Let $\lambda \in \mathbb F$ be a scalar. Then: $\paren {A + \lambda B}^* = A^* + \bar \lambda B^*$ where $A^*$ is the adjoint of $A$ $\bar \lambda$ is the complex conjugate of $\lambda$ That is, the adjoint is conjugate linear.

title: Adjoint is Involutive
snippet: Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A : \HH \to \KK$ be a bounded linear transformation. Define: $A^{**} = \paren {A^*}^*$ where $A^*$ denotes the adjoint of $A$. Then $*$ is an involutive operation in the sense that: $A^{**} = A$

title: Adjoint of Closure of Closable Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a closable densely-defined linear operator with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$. Let $\tuple {\map D {\overline T}, \overline T}$ be the closure of $T$ with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {\paren {\overline T}^\ast}, \paren {\overline T}^\ast}$. Then: $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast} = \tuple {\map D {\paren {\overline T}^\ast}, \paren {\overline T}^\ast}$

title: Adjoint of Composition of Linear Transformations is Composition of Adjoints
snippet: Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\HH$, $\KK$ and $\LL$ be a Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A : \KK \to \LL$ and $B : \HH \to \KK$ be bounded linear transformations. Then: $\paren {A B}^* = B^* A^*$ where $^*$ denotes adjoining.

title: Adjoint of Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator. Let $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ be the adjoint of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$. Then $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ is closed.

title: Adjoint of Densely-Defined Linear Operator reverses Extension of Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ and $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ be densely-defined linear operators such that: $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ extends $\tuple {\map D T, T}$. Let $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ and $\tuple {\map D {S^\ast}, S^\ast}$ be the adjoints of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ and $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ respectively. Then $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ extends $\tuple {\map D {S^\ast}, S^\ast}$.

title: Adjoint of Direct Sum of Bounded Linear Operators on Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\sequence {\family {\HH_i, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a $I$-indexed family of Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. For each $i \in I$, let $T_i : \HH_i \to \HH_i$ be a bounded linear operator. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{i \mathop \in I} \norm {T_i}_{\map B {\HH_i} } < \infty$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {\HH_i} }$ is the norm of a bounded linear operator on $\HH_i$.

title: Adjoint of Direct Sum of Densely-Defined Linear Operators on Hilbert Spaces
snippet: Let $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH_n} } }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of Hilbert spaces over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$. For each $n \in \N$, let $\tuple {\map D {T_n}, T_n}$ be a densely-defined linear operator with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T_n^\ast}, T_n^\ast}$. Let $\ds \tuple {\map D T,T}$ be the direct sum of $\sequence {\tuple {\map D {T_n}, T_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ with adjoint $\tuple {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$.

title: Adjoint of Finite Rank Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. Let $T \in \map {B_{00} } {\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded finite rank operator. Then: $T^* \in \map {B_{00} } {\KK, \HH}$ that is, the adjoint of $T$ is also a bounded finite rank operator.

title: Adjoint of Identity Transformation
snippet: Let $\tuple {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I_\HH$ be the identity transformation on $\HH$. Then: ${I_\HH}^* = I_\HH$ where ${I_\HH}^*$ denotes the adjoint of $I_\HH$.

title: Adjoint of Normal Operator has Same Eigenvectors and Complex Conjugated Eigenvalues
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\mathbf T: \HH \to \HH$ be a normal operator. Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $\mathbf T$. Let $\mathbf v$ be a eigenvector of $\mathbf T$ associated with $\lambda$. Then, $\mathbf v$ is also an eigenvector of the adjoint $\mathbf T^*$ with an associated eigenvalue $\overline \lambda$, where $\bar \lambda$ is the complex conjugate of $\lambda$. That is: $\mathbf T^* \mathbf v = \bar \lambda \mathbf v$

title: Adjoint of Symmetric Densely-Defined Linear Operator Extends Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a symmetric densely-defined linear operator. Let $\struct {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ be the adjoint of $T$. Then $\map D T \subseteq \map D {T^\ast}$ and: $T x = T^\ast x$ for each $x \in \map D T$.

title: Adjugate Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Adjugate Matrices ==

title: Adjunction Induces Counit of Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Let $\beta$ be the inverse of the natural isomorphism $\alpha$. Then: there exists a counit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ That is, there exists a natural transformation $\xi: FG \to \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf C}$ where: for each $C$ of $\mathbf C: \xi_{_C} = \map {\beta_{\tuple{GC, C}}} {\operatorname {id}_{GC}}$ $\operatorname {id}_{\mathbf C}$ is the identity functor on $\mathbf C$ $FG$ is the composite functor of $F$ with $G$

title: Adjunction Induces Unit of Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Then: there exists a unit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ That is, there exists a natural transformation $\eta: \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D} \to GF$ where: for each object $D \in \mathbf D: \eta_{_D} = \map {\alpha_{_\tuple{D, FD}}} {\operatorname {id}_{FD}}$ $\operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D}$ is the identity functor on $\mathbf D$ $GF$ is the composite functor of $G$ with $F$

title: Admissible Curve in Riemannian Manifold has Unique Forward Reparametrization by Arc Length
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be an admissible Curve. Then $\gamma$ has a unique forward reparametrization by arc length.

title: Admissible Family of Curves Symmetry Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ is a closed real interval. Let $J$ is an open real interval. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be an admissible family of curves. Let $\tuple {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{n - 1}, a_n}$ be a finite subdivision of $I$. Then: $\forall i \in \N_{> 0} : i \le n : \forall s \in J : \forall t \in \closedint {a_{i - 1} }{a_i} : D_s \partial_t \Gamma = D_t \partial_s \Gamma$ where $D_t$ denotes the covariant derivative along the main curve, and $D_s$ denotes the covariant derivative along the transverse curve.

title: Affine Coordinates are Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an affine space with difference space $V$ over a field $k$. Let $\RR = \left({p_0, e_1, \ldots, e_n}\right)$ be an affine frame in $\EE$. Define a mapping $\Theta_\RR : k^n \to \EE$ by: $\ds \map {\Theta_\RR} {\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n} = p_0 + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i e_i$ Then $\Theta_\RR$ is a bijection.

title: Affine Functional is Convex and Concave
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be an affine functional on $X$. Then $f$ is convex and concave.

title: Affine Group of One Dimension as Semidirect Product
snippet: Let $\map {\operatorname{Af}_1} \R$ be the $1$-dimensional affine group on $\R$. Let $\R^+$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\R^\times$ be the multiplicative group of real numbers. Let $\phi: \R^\times \to \Aut {\R^+}$ be defined as: $\forall b \in \R^\times: \map \phi b = \paren {a \mapsto a b}$ Let $\R^+ \rtimes_\phi \R^\times$ be the corresponding semidirect product. Then: $\map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R \cong \R^+ \rtimes_\phi \R^\times$ where $\cong$ denotes (group) isomorphism.

title: Affine Group of One Dimension is Group
snippet: Let $\map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R$ be the $1$-dimensional affine group on $\R$. Then $\map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R$ is a group.

title: Affine Subspace of 3 Dimensional Euclidean Space
snippet: Let $\R^3$ denote the (real) Euclidean $3$-space. Let $\SS$ be an affine subspace of $\R^3$. Then $\SS$ is one of the following: a point a straight line a plane the whole space $\R^3$.

title: Affirming the Consequent
snippet: == Fallacy == Let $p \implies q$ be a conditional statement. Let its consequent $q$ be true. Then it is a fallacy to assert that the antecedent $p$ is also necessarily true. That is: This fallacy is called affirming the consequent.

snippet: == Examples of Aggregate Statistics ==

snippet: == Examples of Air Resistance ==

title: Al-Khwarizmi/The Algebra/Inheritance Problem
snippet: == Problem == A woman dies, leaving her husband, a son and three daughters. She also leaves $\frac 1 8 + \frac 1 7$ of her estate to a stranger. According to law: the husband receives one quarter of the estate the son receives double the share of a daughter but this division is made only after the legacy to the stranger has been paid. How should the inheritance be divided?

title: Alaoglu-Bourbaki Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\map \sigma {E, F}$ be the weak topology on $E$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Let $V \subseteq E$ be a neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\map \sigma {E, F}$. Let $V^\circ$ be the absolute polar of $V$. Let $\map \sigma {F, E}$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F$. Then $V^\circ$ is $\map \sigma {F, E}$-compact.

title: Aleph-Null
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the minimally inductive set. $\omega = \aleph_0$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

title: Aleph-Null is Smallest Infinite Cardinal Number
snippet: Aleph-null, that is $\aleph_0$, is the smallest infinite cardinal.

title: Aleph Product is Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $\left|{\aleph_x \times \aleph_x}\right| = \aleph_x$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

title: Aleph Zero equals Cardinality of Naturals
snippet: $\aleph_0 = \card \N$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping, $\card \N$ denotes the cardinality of $\N$.

title: Aleph Zero is less than Cardinality of Continuum
snippet: $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak c$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping, $\mathfrak c$ denotes the cardinality of the continuum.

title: Aleph is Infinite
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. $\aleph_x \ge \omega$ where: $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping $\omega$ denotes the minimally inductive set.

title: Aleph is Infinite Cardinal
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then $\aleph_x$ is an infinite cardinal where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

title: Alexander Polynomial is a Knot Invariant
snippet: The Alexander polynomial of an elementary knot $K$ is invariant under Reidemeister moves.

title: Alexandroff Extension is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $T^*$ is a compact topological space.

title: Alexandroff Extension is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $\tau^*$ is a topology on $S^*$.

title: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Biconnected
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a biconnected space.

title: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a connected space.

title: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a sequentially compact space.

title: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is T1
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is not T2
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ is not a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Alexandroff Extension which is T2 is also T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Let $T^*$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $T^*$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism is Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring. Let $f : R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let the image of $f$ be a subset of the center of $S$. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is an algebra over $R$.

title: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism is Associative
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring with unity. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let the image of $f$ be a subset of the center of $S$. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is an associative algebra.

title: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism on Commutative Ring is Commutative
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a commutative ring. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is a commutative algebra.

title: Algebra Defined by Ring Homomorphism on Ring with Unity is Unitary
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {S, +, *}$ be a ring with unity. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\struct {S_R, *}$ be the algebra defined by the ring homomorphism $f$. Then $\struct {S_R, *}$ is a unitary algebra.

title: Algebra Loop/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebra Loops ==

title: Algebra from Cayley-Dickson Construction is not Real Star-Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a $*$-algebra. Let $A'$ be constructed from $A$ using the Cayley-Dickson construction. Then $A'$ is not a real $*$-algebra.

title: Algebra obtains Norm Structure through Algebra Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $A$ and $B$ be algebras over $\GF$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B$ be an algebra norm on $B$. Let $\phi : A 	o B$ be an algebra isomorphism. Define $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A : A 	o \R$ by: $
orm a_A = 
orm {\map \phi a}_B$ Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A$ is an algebra norm on $A$.

title: Algebra of Propositions is Boolean Algebra
snippet: The algebra of propositions is a Boolean algebra.

title: Algebra of Sets contains Empty Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\O \in \RR$ where $\O$ denotes the empty set.

title: Algebra of Sets contains Underlying Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $S \in \RR$

title: Algebra of Sets is Boolean Algebra
snippet: An algebra of sets is a Boolean algebra.

title: Algebra of Sets is Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\forall A, B \in S: A \cap B \in \RR$

title: Algebra of Sets is Closed under Set Difference
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an algebra of sets on $S$. Then: $\forall A, B \in S: A \setminus B \in \RR$

title: Algebra of all Mappings is Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {A, +_A, \circ_A, \ast_A}$ be an $R$-algebra. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {A^S, +, \circ, \ast}$ the $R$-algebra of all mappings from $S$ to $A$. Then $\struct {A^S, +, \circ, \ast}$ is an $R$-algebra.

title: Algebra over Field/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebras over Fields ==

title: Algebra over Field Embeds into Unitization as Ideal
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Let: $A_0 = \set {\tuple {x, 0_K} : x \in A} \subseteq A_+$. Then $A_0$ is an ideal in $A_+$.

title: Algebra over Field Embeds into Unitization as Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$ that is not unital. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Let: $A_0 = \set {\tuple {x, 0_K} : x \in A} \subseteq A_+$. Then $A_0$ is a vector subspace of $A_+$.

title: Algebraic Closure of Field is Unique
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Let $K$ and $L$ be algebraic closures of $F$. Then $K$ and $L$ are $F$-isomorphic.

title: Algebraic Closure of Rational Number Field is Algebraic Number Field
snippet: Let $\Q$ denote the field of rational numbers. Let $\Bbb A$ denote the field of algebraic numbers. The algebraic closure of $\Q$ is $\Bbb A$.

title: Algebraic Closure of Real Number Field is Complex Number Field
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the field of real numbers. Let $\C$ denote the field of complex numbers. The algebraic closure of $\R$ is $\C$.

title: Algebraic Curve/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Curves ==

title: Algebraic Dual Separates Points of Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $E$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $E^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $E$. Then $E^\#$ separates points.

title: Algebraic Element of Degree 3 is not Element of Field Extension of Degree Power of 2
snippet: Let $K / F$ be a finite field extension of degree $2^m$. Let $\alpha \in K$ be algebraic over $F$ with degree $3$. Then $\alpha \notin K$.

snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Elements of Ring Extensions ==

snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Expansions ==

snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Functions ==

title: Algebraic Integers form Subring of Complex Numbers
snippet: The set of algebraic integers, under the operations of complex addition and complex multiplication, forms a subring of the set of complex numbers $\C$.

title: Algebraic Invariants for Group of Permutations of Variables
snippet: Let $S = \set {x_1, x_2, \ldots,x_n}$ be a set of algebraic variables. The algebraic invariants for the group of permutations of $S$ are those generated by the elementary symmetric polynomials: {{eqn | l = p_2 | r = x_1 x_2 + x_1 x_3 + \cdots + x_{n - 1} x_n }}

title: Algebraic Irrational Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Irrational Numbers ==

title: Algebraic Multiplicity is not Less than Geometric Multiplicity
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $R$ of order $n > 0$. Let $\map {p_{\mathbf A} } x$ be the characteristic polynomial of $\mathbf A$: $\map {p_{\mathbf A} } x = \map \det {\mathbf I_n x - \mathbf A}$ where $R \sqbrk x$ denotes the polynomial ring in one variable over $R$. Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $\mathbf A$. Let $\map a \lambda$ denote the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda$. Let $\map g \lambda$ denote the geometric multiplicity of $\lambda$. Then: $\map a \lambda \ge \map g \lambda$

title: Algebraic Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Numbers == The algebraic numbers include the following:

title: Algebraic Numbers are Countable
snippet: The set $\Bbb A$ of algebraic numbers is countable.

title: Algebraic Numbers form Countable Subfield of Complex Numbers
snippet: The set $\Bbb A$ of algebraic numbers forms a countable subfield of the field of complex numbers.

title: Algebraic Numbers form Field
snippet: Let $\Bbb A$ denote the set of algebraic numbers in $\C$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\Bbb A, +, \times}$ is a field. In the above, $+$ and $\times$ denote complex addition and complex multiplication respectively.

title: Algebraic Structures formed by Left and Right Operations are not Isomorphic for Cardinality Greater than 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\gets$ and $\to$ denote the left operation and right operation respectively. Let $\card S > 1$. The algebraic structures $\struct {S, \gets}$ and $\struct {S, \to}$ are not isomorphic.

title: Algebraic Variety/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Algebraic Varieties ==

title: Algebraic iff Continuous and For Every Way Below Exists Compact Between
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Then $L$ is algebraic : $L$ is continuous and: $\forall x, y \in S: x \ll y \implies \exists k \in \map K L: x \preceq k \preceq y$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$.

title: Algebraically Closed Field is Infinite
snippet: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field. Then $F$ is infinite.

title: Algebraically Closed Field is Perfect
snippet: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field. Then $F$ is perfect.

title: Algorithm to determine whether Polynomial Diophantine Equation has Integer Solution
snippet: There is no algorithm to determine whether a given polynomial Diophantine equation with integer coefficients has an integer solution.

title: Algorithmic Complexity/Examples

title: Algorithmic Complexity of Euclidean Algorithm
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let the Euclidean Algorithm be employed to find the GCD of $a$ and $b$. Let $\CC$ be the algorithmic complexity of this operation. Then: $\CC = \map \OO {\map \ln {\max \set {a, b} } }$ where $\OO$ denotes big-$\OO$ notation.

snippet: == Examples of Aliasing ==
