title: Associatehood is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$ and whose unity is $1_D$. Let $\sim$ be the relation defined on $D$ as: $\forall x, y \in D: x \sim y$ $x$ is an associate of $y$ Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Associates in Ring of Polynomial Forms over Field
snippet: Let $F \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms over the field $F$. Let $\map d X$ and $\map {d'} X$ be polynomial forms in $F \sqbrk X$. Then $\map d X$ is an associate of $\map {d'} X$ $\map d X = c \cdot \map {d'} X$ for some $c \in F, c \ne 0_F$. Hence any two polynomials in $F \sqbrk X$ have a unique monic GCD.

title: Associative Algebra has Multiplicative Inverses iff Unitary Division Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ be an associative algebra over the ring $A_R$. Then: $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ has a unique multiplicative inverse for every non-zero $a \in A_R$ $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ is a unitary division algebra.

title: Associative Commutative Idempotent Operation is Self-Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, such that: Then $\circ$ is self-distributive. That is: $\forall a, b, c \in S: \paren {a \circ b} \circ \paren {a \circ c} = a \circ b \circ c = \paren {a \circ c} \circ \paren {b \circ c}$

title: Associative Idempotent Anticommutative
snippet: Let $\circ$ be a binary operation on a non-empty set $S$. Let $\circ$ be associative. Then $\circ$ is anticommutative : $(1): \quad \circ$ is idempotent and: $(2): \quad \forall a, b \in S: a \circ b \circ a = a$

title: Associative Law of Addition
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\N, \Z, \Q, \R$ and $\C$. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in \mathbb F: x + \paren {y + z} = \paren {x + y} + z$ That is, the operation of addition on the standard number sets is associative.

title: Associative Law of Multiplication
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\N, \Z, \Q, \R$ and $\C$. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in \mathbb F: x \times \paren {y \times z} = \paren {x \times y} \times z$ That is, the operation of multiplication on the standard number sets is associative.

title: Associative Operation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Associative Operations ==

title: Associative and Anticommutative
snippet: Let $\circ$ be a binary operation on a set $S$. Let $\circ$ be both associative and anticommutative. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in S: x \circ y \circ z = x \circ z$

title: Associativity of Group Direct Product
snippet: The group direct product $G \times \paren {H \times K}$ is (group) isomorphic to $\paren {G \times H} \times K$.

title: Associativity of Hadamard Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \cdot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $S$. For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_S} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A \circ \mathbf B$ be defined as the Hadamard product of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$. The operation $\circ$ is associative on $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ $\cdot$ is associative on $\struct {S, \cdot}$.

title: Associativity of Operation in Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of the two groups $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$. Then the operation $\circ$ in $\struct {G \times T, \circ}$ is associative.

title: Associativity on Four Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $a, b, c, d \in S$. Then: $a \circ b \circ c \circ d$ gives a unique answer no matter how the elements are associated.

title: Associativity on Indexing Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $\family {x_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of terms of $S$ indexed by a finite non-empty set $A$. Let $\family {B_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be a family of distinct subsets of $A$ forming a partition of $A$. Then: $\ds \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {\prod_{a \mathop \in B_k} x_\alpha} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in A} x_\alpha$

title: Associator of Associative Algebra is Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ be an associative algebra. Let $\sqbrk {a, b, c}$ denote the associator of $a, b, c \in A_R$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in A_R: \sqbrk {a, b, c} = \mathbf 0_R$

title: Astroid is Envelope of Line Segment whose End Points lie on Coordinate Axes
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a line segment of length $a$. Let the endpoints of $\LL$ be constrained to lie on the coordinate axes of a Cartesian plane: one on the $x$-axis and one on the $y$-axis The envelope of $\LL$ forms an astroid whose cusps lie on the points at which the coordinate axes intersect a circle of radius $a$ whose center is at the origin.

snippet: Let $S$ be a strophoid embedded in a Cartesian plane with the equation $y^2 = x^2 \dfrac {x + a} {a - x}$. Then the straight line $x = a$ is an asymptote to $S$.

title: Autocorrelation Matrix is Positive Definite
snippet: Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence of $n$ successive values of $T$: $\sequence {s_n} = \tuple {z_1, z_2, \dotsb, z_n}$ Let $\mathbf P_n$ denote the autocorrelation matrix associated with $S$ for $\sequence {s_n}$. Then $\mathbf P_n$ is a positive definite matrix.

title: Autocorrelation at Zero Lag for Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process is 1
snippet: == Example of Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process == Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Then the autocorrelation at zero lag is given by: $\rho_0 = 1$

title: Autocorrelation of Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process
snippet: == Example of Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process == Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. It is necessary that: The autocorrelation between every two observations $z_t, z_{t + k}$ separated by a given lag $k$ is the same as: the autocorrelation between every other two observations $z_{t + m}, z_{t + m + k}$ separated by a given lag $k$ For such a strictly stationary stochastic process: $\rho_k = \dfrac {\gamma_k} {\gamma_0}$ where $\gamma_k$ denotes the autocovariance of $S$.

title: Autocovariance Matrix for Stationary Process is Variance by Autocorrelation Matrix
snippet: Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence of $n$ successive values of $T$: $\sequence {s_n} = \tuple {z_1, z_2, \dotsb, z_n}$ Let $\boldsymbol \Gamma_n$ denote the autocovariance matrix associated with $S$ for $\sequence {s_n}$. Let $\mathbf P_n$ denote the autocorrelation matrix associated with $S$ for $\sequence {s_n}$. Then: $\boldsymbol \Gamma_n = \sigma_z^2 \mathbf P_n$ where $\sigma_z^2$ denotes the variance of $S$.

title: Autocovariance Matrix is Positive Definite
snippet: Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence of $n$ successive values of $T$: $\sequence {s_n} = \tuple {z_1, z_2, \dotsb, z_n}$ Let $\boldsymbol \Gamma_n$ denote the autocovariance matrix associated with $S$ for $\sequence {s_n}$. Then $\boldsymbol \Gamma_n$ is a positive definite matrix.

title: Autocovariance at Zero Lag for Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process is Variance
snippet: == Example of Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process == Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Then the autocovariance at zero lag is given by: $\gamma_0 = \sigma_z^2$ where $\sigma_z^2$ is the variance of $S$.

title: Autocovariance is Autocorrelation by Variance
snippet: Let $\map S z$ be a stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $S$ be weakly stationary of order $2$ or greater. Let $\gamma_k$ denote the autocovariance coefficient of $S$ at lag $k$. Let $\rho_k$ denote the autocorrelation coefficient of $S$ at lag $k$. Then: $\gamma_k = \rho_k \sigma_z^2$ where $\sigma_z^2$ denotes the variance of $S$.

title: Automorphic Numbers in Base 10
snippet: If leading zeroes are allowed, there are exactly $4$ $n$-digit automorphic numbers in base $10$: $00 \dots 00$ $00 \dots 01$ $5^{2^{n - 1} } \pmod {10^n}$ $6^{5^{n - 1} } \pmod {10^n}$

title: Automorphism Group/Examples

title: Automorphism Group Acts Faithfully on Generating Set
snippet: Let $E/F$ be a field extension. Let $\operatorname{Aut}(E/F)$ be its automorphism group. Let $S\subset E$ be a generating set of the extension. Let $S$ be stable under the group action of $\operatorname{Aut}(E/F)$. Then the induced group action on $S$ is faithful.

title: Automorphism Group is Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\Aut S$ be the automorphism group of $\struct {S, *}$. Then $\Aut S$ is a subgroup of the symmetric group $\struct {\Gamma \paren S, \circ}$ on $S$.

title: Automorphism Group of Complex Numbers over Real Numbers
snippet: The field extension $\C / \R$ of complex numbers $\C$ over real numbers $\R$ has automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}$: $\operatorname{Aut} \paren {\C / \R} = \set {\operatorname{id}, \sigma}$ where: $\operatorname{id}$ denotes the identity mapping $\sigma$ denotes complex conjugation

title: Automorphism Group of Cyclic Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Let $\Aut G$ denote the automorphism group of $G$. Then $\Aut G$ is abelian.

title: Automorphism Maps Generator to Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Let $g$ be a generator of $G$. Let $\phi$ be an automorphism on $G$. Then $\map \phi g$ is also a generator of $G$.

title: Auxiliary Approximating Relation has Interpolation Property
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, z \in S$ such that: $x \ll z \land x \ne z$ Let $\RR$ be an auxiliary approximating relation on $S$. Then $\exists y \in S: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \land \tuple {y, z} \in \RR \land x \ne y$

title: Auxiliary Approximating Relation has Quasi Interpolation Property
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, z \in S$. Let $\RR$ be an auxiliary approximating relation on $S$ such that $\tuple {x, z} \in \RR \land x \ne z$ Then: $\exists y \in S: x \preceq y \land \tuple {y, z} \in \RR \land x \ne y$

title: Auxiliary Relation Image of Element is Upper Section
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $R$ be an auxiliary relation on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $\map R x$ is an upper section where $\map R x$ denotes the image of $x$ under $R$.

title: Auxiliary Relation is Congruent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\RR$ be relation on $S$ satisfying conditions $(2)$ and $(3)$ of auxiliary relation. Then: $\forall x, y, z, u \in S: \tuple {x, z} \in \RR \land \tuple {y, u} \in \RR \implies \tuple {x \vee y, z \vee u} \in \RR$

title: Auxiliary Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\RR$ be relation on $S$ satisfying conditions $(1)$ and $(2)$ of auxiliary relation. Then $\RR$ is a transitive relation.

title: Ax-Grothendieck Theorem
snippet: Let $f: \C^n \to \C^n$ be a polynomial map. Let $f$ be injective. Then $f$ is surjective.

title: Axes of Symmetry for Ellipse
snippet: Let $K$ be an ellipse. Then $K$ has exactly $2$ axis of bilateral symmetry: the major axis of $K$ the minor axis of $K$.

title: Axes of Symmetry for Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. Then $\EE$ has exactly $3$ axes of symmetry: the major axis of $\EE$ the mean axis of $\EE$ the minor axis of $\EE$.

title: Axes of Symmetry of Hyperbola
snippet: The hyperbola has $2$ axis of bilateral symmetry: the transverse axis the conjugate axis. When expressed in reduced form in a cartesian plane, these correspond respectively with the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis.

snippet: Let $\KK$ be a kappa curve expressed in Cartesian coordinates as: $x^4 + x^2 y^2 = a^2 y^2$ $\KK$ has two axes of bilateral symmetry: the $x$-axis the $y$-axis. 520px

snippet: The aleph hypothesis is the proposition: $\aleph_{\alpha} = \beth_{\alpha}$ for all ordinals $\alpha$ where $\aleph_\alpha$ is the Aleph ($\aleph$) mapping and $\beth_\alpha$ is the Beth ($\beth$) mapping.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Abstraction
snippet: The states: Given any property $P$, there exists a unique set which consists of all and only those objects which have property $P$: $\set {x: \map P x}$ From the definition of a set: A set is any aggregation of objects, called elements, which can be precisely defined in some way or other.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Approximation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. The axiom of approximation says $\forall x \in S: x = \map \sup {x^\ll}$ where $x^\ll$ denotes the way below closure of $x$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Formulation 1
snippet: For every set of non-empty sets, it is possible to provide a mechanism for choosing one element of each element of the set. $\ds \forall s: \paren {\O \notin s \implies \exists \paren {f: s \to \bigcup s}: \forall t \in s: \map f t \in t}$ That is, one can always create a choice function for selecting one element from each element of the set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Formulation 2
snippet: Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of sets all of which are non-empty, indexed by $I$ which is also non-empty. Then there exists an indexed family $\family {x_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ such that: $\forall i \in I: x_i \in X_i$ That is, the Cartesian product of a non-empty family of sets which are non-empty is itself non-empty.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Formulation 3
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a set of non-empty pairwise disjoint sets. Then there exists a set $C$ such that for all $S \in \SS$, $C \cap S$ has exactly one element. Symbolically: $\forall s: \paren {\paren {\O \notin s \land \forall t, u \in s: t = u \lor t \cap u = \O} \implies \exists c: \forall t \in s: \exists x: t \cap c = \set x}$ That is, there exists a choice set $C$ for $\SS$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Formulation 3/Also known as
snippet: == Axiom of Choice: Also known as == This form of the is sometimes called the .

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Formulation 4
snippet: Let $A$ be a non-empty set. Then there exists a mapping $f: \powerset A \to A$ such that: for every non-empty proper subset $x$ of $A$: $\map f x \in x$ where $\powerset A$ denotes the power set of $A$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on == exposited the in order to prove what is now known as Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem. He himself did not invent the idea of the choice function; he explains that he is merely formalizing a concept ubiquitous in mathematics. Formulation 1 and formulation 2 are written in a letter from to , postmarked $24$ September $1904$: Der vorliegende Beweis beruht auf der Voraussetzung [...] daß es auch für eine unendliche Gesamtheit von Mengen immer Zuordnungen gibt, bei denen jeder Menge eines ihrer Elemente entspricht, oder formal ausgedrückt, daß das Produkt einer unendlichen…

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice for Finite Sets
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a non-empty set of finite, non-empty sets. Then there exists a choice function for $\SS$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice for Finite Sets/Proof from Hall's Marriage Theorem
snippet: Suppose that Hall's Marriage Theorem holds for all sets of finite sets. Let $\SS$ be a non-empty set of finite, non-empty sets. Then there exists a choice function for $\SS$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Choice for Finite Sets/Proof from Ordering Principle
snippet: Suppose that the Ordering Principle holds. Let $\SS$ be a non-empty set of finite non-empty sets. Then there exists a choice function for $\SS$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Countable Choice/Form 1
snippet: Let $\sequence {S_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of non-empty sets. The axiom of countable choice states that there exists a sequence: $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ such that $x_n \in S_n$ for all $n \in \N$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Countable Choice/Form 2
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set of non-empty sets. Then $S$ has a choice function.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Countable Choice for Finite Sets
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set of non-empty finite sets. Then $S$ has a choice function.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Dependent Choice/Left-Total
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a binary relation on a non-empty set $S$. Suppose that: $\forall a \in S: \exists b \in S: a \mathrel \RR b$ that is, that $\RR$ is a left-total relation (specifically a serial relation). The axiom of dependent choice states that there exists a sequence $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $S$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: x_n \mathrel \RR x_{n + 1}$ Dependent Choice

title: Axiom:Axiom of Dependent Choice/Right-Total
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a binary relation on a non-empty set $S$. Suppose that: $\forall a \in S: \exists b \in S: b \mathrel \RR a$ that is, that $\RR$ is a right-total relation. The axiom of dependent choice states that there exists a sequence $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $S$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: x_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR x_n$ Dependent Choice

title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension
snippet: The is the fundamental definition of the nature of a collection: it is completely determined by its elements.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension/Class Theory
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Then: $\forall x: \paren {x \in A \iff x \in B} \iff A = B$ Hence the order in which the elements are listed in the classes is immaterial.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on == The nature of the , or as it is frequently called, suggests that the ought in fact to be the preferred name, as it gives a precise definition of the extent of a collection. However, the word extensionality is a term in logic which determines equality of objects by its external features, as opposed to intensionality, which is more concerned with internal structure. title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension/Set Theory
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. The states that: $A$ and $B$ are equal they contain the same elements. That is, : every element of $A$ is also an element of $B$ and: every element of $B$ is also an element of $A$. This can be formulated as follows:

title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension/Set Theory/Formulation 1
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. The axiom of extension can be formulated as: $\forall x: \paren {x \in A \iff x \in B} \iff A = B$

title: Axiom:Axiom of Extension/Set Theory/Formulation 2
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. The can be formulated as: $\forall x: \paren {\paren {A = B \land A \in x} \implies B \in x}$ This formulation is used in set theories that define $=$ instead of admitting it as a primitive.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Foundation
snippet: For all non-empty sets, there is an element of the set that shares no element with the set. That is: $\forall S: \paren {\paren {\exists x: x \in S} \implies \exists y \in S: \forall z \in S: \neg \paren {z \in y} }$ The antecedent states that $S$ is not empty.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Foundation (Classes)
snippet: For any non-empty class, there is an element of the class that shares no element with the class. $\forall X: X \ne \O \implies \exists y: y \in X \land y \cap X = \O$

title: Axiom:Axiom of Global Choice
snippet: In the context of class theory, the axiom of global choice is as follows: There exists a mapping $f : V \setminus \set \O \to V$, where $V$ is the universal class, such that: $\forall x \in V: \map f x \in x$ Symbolically: $\exists A: \map {\text{Fnc}} A \land \forall x: x \ne \O \implies \exists y: y \in x \land \tuple {x, y} \in A$

snippet: Let $\omega$ be the class of natural numbers as constructed by the Von Neumann construction: Then $\omega$ is a set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Infinity/Class Theory/Formulation 2
snippet: There exists an inductive set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Infinity/Class Theory/Formulation 3
snippet: Not every set is a natural number.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Infinity/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on == Mathematicians had unsuccessfully attempted to prove the existence of an infinite set using existing axioms. determined in $1908$ that it was necessary to assume the existence of such a set by creating an axiom specifically for that task. Hence his introduction of the .

title: Axiom:Axiom of Infinity/Set Theory
snippet: There exists a set containing: $(1): \quad$ a set with no elements $(2): \quad$ the successor of each of its elements. That is: $\exists x: \paren {\paren {\exists y: y \in x \land \forall z: \neg \paren {z \in y} } \land \forall u: u \in x \implies u^+ \in x}$ In this context, the successor of the set $u$, written $u^+$, is defined as $u^+ := u \cup \set u$. The symbol $\cup$ represents set union and $\set u$ represents the singleton containing $u$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of K-Approximation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. The axiom of $K$-approximation says $\forall x \in S: x = \map \sup {x^{\mathrm{compact} } }$ where $x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Limitation of Size
snippet: For any class $\CC$, a set $x$ such that $x = \CC$ exists there is no bijection between $\CC$ and the universal class. Limitation of Size

title: Axiom:Axiom of Pairing/Class Theory
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Then the class $\set {a, b}$ is likewise a set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Pairing/Set Theory/Strong Form
snippet: For any two sets, there exists a set to which only those two sets are elements: $\forall a: \forall b: \exists c: \forall z: \paren {z = a \lor z = b \iff z \in c}$ That is, let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Then there exists a set $c$ such that $c = \set {a, b}$. Thus it is possible to create a set whose elements are two sets that have already been created.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Pairing/Set Theory/Weak Form
snippet: For any two sets, there exists a set to which those two sets are elements: $\forall a: \forall b: \exists c: \forall z: \paren {z = a \lor z = b \implies z \in c}$ That is, let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Then there exists a set $c$ such that $a \in c$ and $b \in c$. Thus it is possible to create a set that contains as elements two sets that have already been created.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Powers/Class Theory

title: Axiom:Axiom of Powers/Set Theory
snippet: For every set, there exists a set of sets whose elements are all the subsets of the given set. $\forall x: \exists y: \paren {\forall z: \paren {z \in y \iff \forall w: \paren {w \in z \implies w \in x} } }$

title: Axiom:Axiom of Replacement/Class Theory/Formulation 1
snippet: For every mapping $f$ and set $x$ in the domain of $f$, the image $f \sqbrk x$ is a set. Symbolically: $\forall Y: \map {\text{Fnc}} Y \implies \forall x: \exists y: \forall u: u \in y \iff \exists v: \tuple {v, u} \in Y \land v \in x$ where: $\map {\text{Fnc}} X := \forall x, y, z: \tuple {x, y} \in X \land \tuple {x, z} \in X \implies y = z$ and the notation $\tuple {\cdot, \cdot}$ is understood to represent Kuratowski's formalization of ordered pairs.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Replacement/Class Theory/Formulation 2
snippet: For every mapping $f$ and set $x$, the restriction $f \restriction x$ is a set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Replacement/Class Theory/Formulation 3
snippet: Every mapping whose domain is a set is also a set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Replacement/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Axiom of Replacement == The axiom of replacement was added to the axioms of Zermelo set theory by , and also independently by . The resulting system of axiomatic set theory is now referred to as Zermelo-Fraenkel Set Theory.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Replacement/Set Theory
snippet: For every mapping $f$ and subset $S$ of the domain of $f$, there exists a set containing the image $f \sqbrk S$. More formally, let us express this as follows: Let $\map P {x, z}$ be a propositional function, which determines a mapping. That is, we have: $\forall x: \exists ! y : \map P {x, y}$. Then we state as an axiom: $\forall A: \exists B: \forall y: \paren {y \in B \iff \exists x \in A : \map P {x, y} }$

title: Axiom:Axiom of Segment Construction
snippet: Let $\equiv$ be the relation of equidistance. Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. The axiom of segment construction is given by the following statement: $\forall a, b, c, q: \exists x: \mathsf{B} qax \land ax \equiv bc$ where $a, b, c, q, x$ are points.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification
snippet: For every set and every condition, there corresponds a set whose elements are exactly the same as those elements of the original set for which the condition is true. Because we cannot quantify over functions, we need an axiom for every condition we can express. Therefore, this axiom is sometimes called an axiom schema, as we introduce a lot of similar axioms. This axiom schema can be formally stated as follows:

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification/Also known as
snippet: The is also known as: The Axiom of Subsets (although this unnecessarily reduces the scope of this axiom to pure set theory) The Axiom of Comprehension The Axiom of Selection (this axiom allows one to select the elements of a subset) The Axiom of Separation or Separation Principle (although this can be confused with the Tychonoff separation axioms, which arise in topology, so this name is deprecated on ) The Axiom of Segregation, under its German name Aussonderungsaxiom The limited abstraction principle, in apposition to the unlimited abstraction principle, also known as the axiom of…

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification/Class Theory
snippet: The is an axiom schema which can be formally stated as follows: Let $\map \phi {A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n, x}$ be a propositional function such that: $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ are a finite number of free variables whose domain ranges over all classes $x$ is a free variable whose domain ranges over all sets Then the gives that: $\forall A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n: \exists B: \forall x: \paren {x \in B \iff \map \phi {A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n, x} }$ where each of $B$ ranges over arbitrary classes.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on == The was created by as a replacement for the of Frege set theory. The latter had been demonstrated, via Russell's Paradox, to lead to the conclusion that Frege Set Theory is Logically Inconsistent. Thus, rather than allowing a set to be constructed of any elements at all which satisfy a given property $P$, the elements in question are restricted to being elements of some pre-existing set. This in turn leads to the further question of how to create such a pre-existing set in the first place.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification/Set Theory
snippet: The axiom of specification is an axiom schema which can be formally stated as follows: For any well-formed formula $\map P y$, we introduce the axiom: $\forall z: \exists x: \forall y: \paren {y \in x \iff \paren {y \in z \land \map P y} }$ where each of $x$, $y$ and $z$ range over arbitrary sets. This means that if you have a set, you can create a set that contains some of the elements of that set, where those elements are specified by stipulating that they satisfy some (arbitrary) condition.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Specification/Set Theory/Also presented as
snippet: == : Also presented as == The can also be specified as follows: If $\phi$ is a property (with parameter $p$), then for any $X$ and $p$ there exists a set: $Y = \paren {u \in X: \map \phi {u, p} }$ that contains all those $u \in X$ that have the property $\phi$. $\forall X: \forall p: \exists Y: \forall u: \paren {u \in Y \iff \paren {u \in X \land \map \phi {u, p} } }$

title: Axiom:Axiom of Swelledness
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. $V$ is a swelled class. That is, every subclass of a set which is an element of $V$ is a set in $V$. Briefly: Every subclass of a set is a set.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Transitivity
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. $V$ is a transitive class. That is, every set $S$ which is an element of $V$ is a subclass of $V$. Briefly: Every set is a class.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Triangle Existence
snippet: Let $\equiv$ be the relation of equidistance. Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. Then the following axiom holds: $\forall a,a',b,b',c',p: ab \equiv a'b' \implies$ $\exists c,x: \left({ac \equiv a'c' \land bc \equiv b'c' \land \mathsf{B}cxp}\right) \land \left({\mathsf{B}abx \lor \mathsf{B}bxa \lor \mathsf{B}xab}\right)$ where $a, b, c, a', b', c', x, p$ are points.

title: Axiom:Axiom of Union
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Then their union $x \cup y$ is a set.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty
snippet: == Axiom Schema == Let $Z$ be a random variable. Let $Z$ take the values $a_i$ with probability $p_i$, where $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Let $H_n: Z^n \to \R$ be a mapping which is to be defined as the uncertainty of $Z$. Then $H_n$ fulfils the following conditions, which are to be known as the axioms of uncertainty:

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 1
snippet: $H_n$ fulfils the following axiom: $\map {H_n} {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n}$ is a maximum when $p_1 = p_2 = \dotsb = p_n = \dfrac 1 n$

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 2
snippet: $H_n$ fulfils the following axiom: For any permutation $\pi$ of $\tuple {1, 2, \dotsc, n}$: $\map {H_n} {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n} = \map {H_n} {p_{\map \pi 1}, p_{\map \pi 2}, \ldots, p_{\map \pi n} }$ That is, $H_n$ is a symmetric function of the arguments $p_1, p_2, \dotsc, p_n$.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 3
snippet: $H$ fulfils the following axiom: $\map {H_n} {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n} \ge 0$ and: $\map {H_n} {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n} = 0$ $\exists i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: p_i = 1$ That is, uncertainty is always a positive quantity, and only reaches zero when one of the arguments is $1$.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 4
snippet: ${H_n}$ fulfils the following axiom: $\map {H_{n + 1} } {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n, 0} = \map {H_n} {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n}$ For example: a $7$-sided die which has no chance of showing a $7$, but is otherwise fair, has the same uncertainty as a fair $6$-sided die.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 5
snippet: ${H_n}$ fulfils the following axiom: $\map {H_n} {\dfrac 1 n, \dfrac 1 n, \dotsc, \dfrac 1 n} \le \map {H_{n + 1} } {\dfrac 1 {n + 1}, \dfrac 1 {n + 1}, \dotsc, \dfrac 1 {n + 1} }$ Thus, for example, a $2$-horse race is less uncertain than a $3$-horse race.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 6
snippet: ${H_n}$ fulfils the following axiom: $H_n$ is a continuous function of its arguments.

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 7
snippet: ${H_n}$ fulfils the following axiom: $\map {H_{m n} } {\dfrac 1 {m n}, \dfrac 1 {m n}, \dotsc, \dfrac 1 {m n} } = \map {H_m} {\dfrac 1 m, \dfrac 1 m, \dotsc, \dfrac 1 m} + \map {H_n} {\dfrac 1 n, \dfrac 1 n, \dotsc, \dfrac 1 n}$

title: Axiom:Axioms of Uncertainty/Axiom 8
snippet: ${H_n}$ fulfils the following axiom: Let: $p = p_1 + p_2 + \dotsb + p_m$ $q = q_1 + q_2 + \dotsb + q_n$ such that: each of $p_i$ and $q_j$ are non-negative $p + q = 1$ Then: $\map {H_{m + n} } {p_1, p_2, \dotsc, p_m, q_1, q_2, \dotsc q_n} = \map {H_2} {p, q} + p \map {H_m} {\dfrac {p_1} p, \dfrac {p_2} p, \dotsc, \dfrac {p_m} p} + q \map {H_n} {\dfrac {q_1} q, \dfrac {q_2} q, \dotsc, \dfrac {q_n} q}$

title: Axiom:Euclid's Fifth Postulate/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Euclid's Fifth Postulate == During the course of the history of mathematics, many mathematicians have attempted to prove Euclid's fifth postulate from the remaining four, as it seems less intuitive than the rest of Euclid's Postulates. himself avoided using the fifth postulate until the $29$th proposition (part $1$): Parallelism implies Equal Alternate Angles in his . Eventually, in $1823$ and, independently in $1832$, , realized that self-consistent, non-euclidean geometries could be developed by not accepting this postulate.

title: Axiom:Five-Segment Axiom
snippet: Let $\equiv$ be the relation of equidistance. Let $\mathsf B$ be the relation of betweenness. Let $=$ be the relation of equality. This axiom asserts that: $\forall a, b, c, d, a', b', c', d':$ $\paren {\neg \paren {a = b} \land \paren {\mathsf B a b c \land \mathsf B a' b' c'} \land \paren {a b \equiv a' b' \land b c \equiv b' c' \land a d \equiv a' d' \land b d \equiv b' d'} }$ $\implies c d \equiv c' d'$ where $a, b, c, d, a', b', c', d'$ are points.

Category:Axioms/Abstract Algebra

title: Axiom:Group Axioms/Also known as

title: Axiom:Hilbert's Axioms
snippet: Hilbert's Axioms are a series of axioms whose purpose is to provide a rigorous basis for the definition of Euclidean geometry. In the following the primitive objects are: points (denoted by $A, B, C \ldots$) lines (denoted by $a, b, c \ldots$) planes (denoted by $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \ldots$) the composite objects are segment ray angle the primitive relations are: distinct (binary)(defined for all objects) betweenness (ternary)(point between two other points) lies on (binary)(point lies on line, point lies on ray, segment lies on line) congruence (binary)(defined for segments and angles).

title: Axiom:Identity of Betweenness
snippet: Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. Let $=$ be the relation of equality. Then the following axiom holds: $\forall a,b: \mathsf{B}aba \implies a = b$ where $a$ and $b$ are points.

snippet: Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. $\struct {L, \preceq}$ is a frame $\struct {L, \preceq}$ satisfies the axiom: {{axiom | q = \forall a \in L, S \subseteq L | m = a \wedge \bigvee S = \bigvee \set {a \wedge s : S \in S} }} where $\bigvee S$ denotes the supremum $\sup S$. title: Axiom:Inner Connectivity of Betweenness

title: Axiom:Inner Transitivity of Betweenness

title: Axiom:Leibniz's Law
snippet: Let $=$ represent the relation of equality and let $P$ be an arbitrary property. Then: $x = y \dashv \vdash \map P x \iff \map P y$ for all $P$ in the universe of discourse. That is, two objects $x$ and $y$ are equal $x$ has every property $y$ has, and $y$ has every property $x$ has.

title: Axiom:Leibniz's Law/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Leibniz's Law == used this law as the definition of equality. However, notes: To regard Leibniz's law here as a definition would make sense only if the meaning of the symbol "$=$" seemed to us less evident than that of expressions [such as 'every property $x$ has, $y$ has']. Hence it can be argued that Leibniz's law should either be adopted as an axiom, or not adopted at all. Category:Historical Notes

snippet: Let $\equiv$ be the relation of equidistance. Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. This axiom asserts: $\forall x,y,z,x',y',z' : \left({\mathsf{B}xyz \land \mathsf{B}x'y'z' \land xy \equiv x'y' \land yz \equiv y'z'}\right) \implies xz \equiv x'z'$ where $x, y, z, x', y', z'$ are points.

title: Axiom:Outer Connectivity of Betweenness
snippet: Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. Let $=$ be the relation of equality. This axiom asserts that: $\forall a, b, c, d: \left({\mathsf{B}abc \land \mathsf{B}abd \land \neg \left({a = b}\right) }\right) \implies \left({\mathsf{B}acd \lor \mathsf{B}adc}\right)$ where $a, b, c, d$ are points.

title: Axiom:Outer Transitivity of Betweenness
snippet: Let $\mathsf{B}$ be the relation of betweenness. Let $=$ be the relation of equality. This axiom asserts that: $\forall a, b, c, d: \mathsf{B}abc \land \mathsf{B}bcd \land \neg \paren {b = c} \implies \mathsf{B}abd$ where $a, b, c, d$ are points.

title: Axiom:Parallel Postulate
snippet: If two straight lines are drawn which intersect a third in such a way that the sum of the measures of the two interior angles on one side is less than the sum of the measures of two right angles, then the two lines must intersect each other on that side if extended far enough.

title: Axiom:Pasch's Axiom (Euclidean Geometry)
snippet: Let a triangle and a straight line lie in the same plane such that the line does not go through any of the vertices of the triangle. Then if the line intersects one side of the triangle, it intersects another. 600px That is, such a straight line intersects two of the triangle's sides or none.

The treatments are similar, but the $1$-based system results in an algebraic structure which has no identity element for addition, and so no zero for multiplication.

title: Axiom:Playfair's Axiom
snippet: Exactly one straight line can be drawn through an arbitrary point not on a given line parallel to the given straight line in a plane. Or: Given any straight line and a point not on it, there exists one and only one line which passes through this point and does not intersect the first line no matter how far they are extended. This unique line is defined as being parallel to the original line in question. Or: Two straight lines which intersect one another cannot both be parallel to one and the same straight line.

title: Axiom:Playfair's Axiom/Also known as

title: Axiom:Playfair's Axiom/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Playfair's Axiom == Playfair's axiom was not actually originated by . He merely published it. However, when he did so, he credited others, specifically , for having used it earlier. It is a frequently seen alternative presentation of Euclid's Fifth Postulate. It can easily seen to be equivalent to that given by , and it can be argued that it is easier to understand. Texts on analytic geometry often gloss over its intrinsic significance, merely deducing it from the general equation of a straight line and the point of intersection of two such.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence
snippet: == Axioms == The propositions of incidence are basic properties of projective geometry which are accepted as true. It is possible to derive these propositions from the basics of linear algebra.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Line
snippet: A (straight) line contains an infinite number of is points, and is completely determined by any two distinct points of that line. Thus, if a line determined by points $A$ and $B$ also contains the points $X$ and $Y$, then the line determined by points $X$ and $Y$ is the same line, and also contains the points $A$ and $B$.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Line in Plane
snippet: A line defined by any two distinct points in a plane lies entirely within that plane.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Plane
snippet: A plane consists of an infinite number of points, and is completely determined by any three distinct points of that plane which are not collinear.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Plane and Line
snippet: A plane and a (straight) line which does not lie in that plane have exactly one point in common. That is, a point is completely determined by any two of the infinite number of distinct (straight) lines which intersect at that point.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Point
snippet: Any two distinct (straight) lines lying in a plane have exactly one point in common. That is, a point is completely determined by any two of the infinite number of distinct (straight) lines which intersect at that point.

title: Axiom:Propositions of Incidence/Space
snippet: A (three-dimensional) space is completely determined by any four distinct points of that space which are not coplanar.

title: Axiom:Ring of Sets Axioms

title: Axiom:Ring of Sets Axioms/Axioms 1
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a system of sets. $\RR$ is a ring of sets $\RR$ satisfies the following axioms: {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 1_1 | lc= Non-Empty: | m = \RR \ne \O }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 2_1 | lc= Closure under Intersection: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \cap B \in \RR }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 3_1 | lc= Closure under Symmetric Difference: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \symdif B \in \RR }} These criteria are called the ring of sets axioms.

title: Axiom:Ring of Sets Axioms/Axioms 2
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a system of sets. $\RR$ is a ring of sets $\RR$ satisfies the following axioms: {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 1_2 | lc= Empty Set: | m = \O \in \RR }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 2_2 | lc= Closure under Set Difference: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \setminus B \in \RR }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 3_2 | lc= Closure under Union: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \cup B \in \RR }} These criteria are called the ring of sets axioms.

title: Axiom:Ring of Sets Axioms/Axioms 3
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a system of sets. $\RR$ is a ring of sets $\RR$ satisfies the following axioms: {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 1_3 | lc= Empty Set: | m = \O \in \RR }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 2_3 | lc= Closure under Set Difference: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \setminus B \in \RR }} {{axiom | n = \text {RS} 3_3 | lc= Closure under Disjoint Union: | q = \forall A, B \in \RR | m = A \cap B = \O \implies A \cup B \in \RR }} These criteria are called the ring of sets axioms.

title: Axiom:Semiring of Sets Axioms/Axioms 1
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a system of sets. $\SS$ is a semiring of sets $\SS$ satisfies the following axioms: {{axiom | n = 3 | q = \forall A, A_1 \in \SS : A_1 \subseteq A | tr = $\exists n \in \N$ and pairwise disjoint sets $A_2, A_3, \ldots, A_n \in \SS : \ds A = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^n A_k$ }} These criteria are called the semiring of sets axioms.

title: Axiom:Semiring of Sets Axioms/Axioms 2
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a system of sets. $\SS$ is a semiring of sets $\SS$ satisfies the following axioms: {{axiom | n = 3' | q = \forall A, B \in \SS | tr = $\exists n \in \N$ and pairwise disjoint sets $A_1, A_2, A_3, \ldots, A_n \in \SS : \ds A \setminus B = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^n A_k$ }} These criteria are called the semiring of sets axioms.

title: Axiom:Sigma-Algebra Axioms
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\Sigma$ be a system of subsets over $X$.

title: Axiom:Sigma-Algebra Axioms/Formulation 1
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\Sigma$ be a system of subsets over $X$. $\Sigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra over $X$ the following axioms are satisfied: {{axiom | n = \text {SA 1} | lc= Unit: | m = X \in \Sigma }} {{axiom | n = \text {SA 2} | lc= Closure under Complement: | q = \forall A \in \Sigma | m = \relcomp X A \in \Sigma }} {{axiom | n = \text {SA 3} | lc= Closure under Countable Unions: | q = \forall A_n \in \Sigma: n = 1, 2, \ldots | m = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n \in \Sigma }} These criteria are called the $\sigma$-algebra axioms.

title: Axiom:Sigma-Algebra Axioms/Formulation 2
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\Sigma$ be a system of subsets over $X$. $\Sigma$ is a $\sigma$-algebra over $X$ the following axioms are satisfied: {{axiom | n = \text {SA 1}' | lc= Unit: | m = X \in \Sigma }} {{axiom | n = \text {SA 2}' | lc= Closure under Set Difference: | q = \forall A, B \in \Sigma | m = A \setminus B \in \Sigma }} {{axiom | n = \text {SA 3}' | lc= Closure under Countable Disjoint Unions: | q = \forall A_n \in \Sigma: n = 1, 2, \ldots | m = \bigsqcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n \in \Sigma }} These criteria are called the $\sigma$-algebra axioms.

title: Axiom:Sigma-Ring Axioms/Formulation 2

title: Axiom:Strict Ordering Axioms

title: Axiom:Strict Ordering Axioms/Formulation 1
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. $\RR$ is a strict ordering on $S$ $\RR$ satisfies the axioms: {{axiom | n = 1 | lc= Asymmetry | q = \forall a, b \in S | ml= a \mathrel \RR b | mo= \implies | mr= \neg \paren {b \mathrel \RR a} }} {{axiom | n = 2 | lc= Transitivity | q = \forall a, b, c \in S | ml= \paren {a \mathrel \RR b} \land \paren {b \mathrel \RR c} | mo= \implies | mr= a \mathrel \RR c }} These criteria are called the strict ordering axioms.

title: Axiom:Strict Ordering Axioms/Formulation 2

title: Axiom:Sure-Thing Axiom
snippet: The sure-thing axiom states that: If a rational decision-maker $P$ would prefer: option $1$ over option $2$ when event $A$ occurs and: option $1$ over option $2$ when event $A$ does not occur then $P$ would prefer option $1$ over option $2$ in absence of any information about the occurrence or not of event $A$.

title: Axiom:Von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel Axioms
snippet: == Axioms == The Von Neumann-Bernays-Gödel axioms are a basis for axiomatic set theory. By convention, a variable denoting a class is written as an uppercase letter, and a variable denoting a set is written as a lowercase letter. However, since sets are defined according to the class-theoretical definition, that means that any quantifier over a set variable is an abbreviation: $\paren {\forall x: \phi} \iff \paren {\forall x: (\exists Y: x \in Y) \implies \phi}$ $\paren {\exists x: \phi} \iff \paren {\exists x: (\exists Y: x \in Y) \land \phi}$ With these definitions in effect, the axioms are…

title: Axiom:Zermelo-Fraenkel Axioms
snippet: == Axioms == The Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms are the most well-known basis for axiomatic set theory. There is no standard numbering for them, and their exact formulation varies. Certain of these axioms can in fact be derived from other axioms, so their status as "axioms" can be questioned. The axioms are as follows:

title: Axiom of Abstraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of ==

title: Axiom of Approximation in Up-Complete Semilattice
snippet: Let $\mathscr S = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be an up-complete meet semilattice. Let: $\forall x \in S: x^\ll$ is directed Then: $\mathscr S$ satisfies the axiom of approximation $\forall x, y \in S: x \npreceq y \implies \exists u \in S: u \ll x \land u \npreceq y$

title: Axiom of Archimedes
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then there exists a natural number greater than $x$. $\forall x \in \R: \exists n \in \N: n > x$ That is, the set of natural numbers is unbounded above.

title: Axiom of Choice/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Axiom of Choice ==

title: Axiom of Choice Implies Axiom of Dependent Choice
snippet: The axiom of choice implies the axiom of dependent choice.

title: Axiom of Choice implies Hausdorff's Maximal Principle
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then Hausdorff's Maximal Principle holds.

title: Axiom of Choice implies Kuratowski's Lemma
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then Kuratowski's Lemma holds.

title: Axiom of Choice implies Maximal Principles
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then the Maximal Principles hold.

title: Axiom of Choice implies Tukey's Lemma
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then Tukey's Lemma holds.

title: Axiom of Choice implies Zorn's Lemma
snippet: Let the be accepted. Then Zorn's Lemma holds.

title: Axiom of Choice is Independent of ZF
snippet: The Axiom of Choice can be neither proved nor disproved from the axioms of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory.

title: Axiom of Dependent Choice Implies Axiom of Countable Choice
snippet: The axiom of dependent choice implies the axiom of countable choice.

title: Axiom of Foundation (Strong Form)
snippet: Let $B$ be a class. Suppose $B$ is non-empty. Then $B$ has a strictly minimal element under $\in$.

title: Axiom of Pairing from Axiom of Specification
snippet: Let it be supposed that there exists a set which contains at least two elements. Then the Axiom of Pairing is a consequence of the Axiom of Specification.

title: Axiom of Pairing from Infinity and Replacement
snippet: The Axiom of Pairing is a consequence of: the Axiom of Infinity and the Axiom of Replacement.

snippet: Let the Axiom of Replacement (in the context of class theory) be accepted. Let $A$ be a class which can be put into one-to-one correspondence with a set. Then $A$ is a set.

title: Axiom of Subsets Equivalents
snippet: The Axiom of Specification states that: $\forall z: \forall \map P y: \exists x: \forall y: \paren {y \in x \iff \paren {y \in z \land \map P y} }$ We will prove that this statement is equivalent to the following statements: $\forall z: \forall A: \paren {\paren {z \cap A} \in U}$ $\forall z: \forall A: \paren {A \subseteq z \implies A \in U}$ In the above statements, the universe is $U$.

title: Axiom of Swelledness is implied by Axiom of Replacement
snippet: Let the (in the context of class theory) be accepted. Then the holds.

title: Axiomatize all of Physics
snippet: == Hilbert $23$: Problem $6$ == Mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics: $(1): \quad$ An axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems for foundation of statistical physics $(2): \quad$ The rigorous theory of limiting processes "which lead from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua".

title: Axioms of Hilbert Proof System Instance 1 for Predicate Logic are Tautologies
snippet: Let $\mathscr H$ be Instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system for predicate logic. Then the axioms of $\mathscr H$ are tautologies.

title: B-Algebra/Examples
snippet: == Examples of $B$-Algebras==

title: B-Algebra Identity:0(0x)=x
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x \in X: 0 \circ \paren {0 \circ x} = x$

title: B-Algebra Identity:x (y z) = (x (0 z)) y
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in X: x \circ \paren {y \circ z} = \paren {x \circ \paren {0 \circ z} } \circ y$

title: B-Algebra Identity:xy=x(0(0y))
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x, y \in X: x \circ y = x \circ \paren {0 \circ \paren {0 \circ y} }$

title: B-Algebra Identity:xy = 0 iff x = y
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x, y \in X: x \circ y = 0 \iff x = y$

title: B-Algebra Induced by Group Induced by B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be a $B$-algebra. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be the group described on $B$-Algebra Induces Group. Let $\struct {S, *'}$ be the $B$-algebra described on Group Induces $B$-Algebra. Then $\struct {S, *'} = \struct {S, *}$.

title: B-Algebra Induces Group
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Let $*$ be the binary operation on $X$ defined as: $\forall a, b \in X: a * b := a \circ \paren {0 \circ b}$ Then the algebraic structure $\struct {X, *}$ is a group such that: $\forall x \in X: 0 \circ x$ is the inverse element of $x$ under $*$. That is: $\forall a, b \in X: a * b^{-1} := a \circ b$

title: B-Algebra Power Law
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Let $n, m \in \N$ such that $n \ge m$. Then: $\forall x \in X: x^n \circ x^m = x^{n - m}$ where $x^k$ for $k \in \N$ denotes the $k$th power of the element $x$.

title: B-Algebra Power Law with Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Let $n, m \in \N_{>0}$ such that $n > m$. Then: $\forall x \in X: n, m \in \N_{>0} \implies x^m \circ x^n = 0 \circ x^{n - m}$ where $x^k$ for $k \in \N_{>0}$ denotes the $k$th power of the element $x$.

title: B-Algebra is Commutative iff x(xy)=y
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then $\struct {X, \circ}$ is commutative : $\forall x, y \in X: x \circ \paren {x \circ y} = y$

title: B-Algebra is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then $\circ$ is a left cancellable operation.

title: B-Algebra is Quasigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then $\struct {X, \circ}$ is a quasigroup.

title: B-Algebra is Right Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then $\circ$ is right-cancellable for $X$. That is: $\forall x, y, z \in X: x \circ z = y \circ z \implies x = y$

title: Babbage's Congruence
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\dbinom {a p} {b p} \equiv \dbinom a b \pmod {p^2}$ where $\dbinom a b$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Babczyński Theorem
snippet: Let $n$ be a $6$-digit integer of the form $\sqbrk {xyxyxy}$ for digits $x$ and $y$. Then $n$ is divisible by $3$, $7$, $13$ and $37$.

title: Backward Path of Well-Ordering is Finite
snippet: Let $A$ be a class under a well-ordering $\preccurlyeq$. Let $S$ be a backward path of $\preccurlyeq$ in $A$. Then $S$ is finite.

title: Baer's Criterion
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be a left $R$-module. Then $M$ is injective the following condition holds: For all left ideals $I$ of $R$ with inclusion map $\iota : I \to R$, and for all $R$-module homomorphisms $f : I \to M$, there exists an $R$-module homomorphism $\tilde f : R \to M$ such that: $\tilde f \circ \iota = f$

title: Baire-Osgood Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a Baire space. Let $Y$ be a metrizable topological space Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping which is the pointwise limit of a sequence $\sequence {f_n}$ in $\map C {X, Y}$. {{explain|$\map C {X, Y}$}} Let $\map D f$ be the set of points where $f$ is discontinuous. Then $\map D f$ is a meager subset of $X$.

title: Baire Category Theorem
snippet: The Baire Category Theorem consists of two statements, each of which is independent of the other:

title: Baire Characterisation Theorem
snippet: A real-valued function $f$ defined on a Banach space $X$ is a Baire-$1$ function : for every non-empty closed subset $K$ of $X$, the restriction of $f$ to $K$ has a point of continuity relative to the topology of $K$.

title: Baire Function may not be Continuous
snippet: Let $X \subseteq \R$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a Baire function. Then $f$ is not necessarily continuous.

title: Baire Space iff Open Sets are Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a Baire space every non-empty open set of $T$ is non-meager in $T$.

title: Baire Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Baire space (in the context of topology). Then $T$ is non-meager in $T$.

title: Balance a Stick on its End on a Finger
snippet: == Problem == How can a stick be made to balance securely on the tip of a finger?

title: Balanced Hull is Intersection of Balanced Sets containing Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $\map {\operatorname {bal} } A$ be the balanced hull of $A$. Then: $\ds \map {\operatorname {bal} } A = \bigcap \set {B \supseteq A: B \text { is balanced} }$

title: Balanced Set/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Balanced Sets ==

title: Balanced Set in Topological Vector Space is Connected
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq X$ be a balanced set. Then $B$ is connected.

title: Balanced Set in Vector Space is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a balanced set. Then $C$ is symmetric.

title: Balanced Subset of Complex Plane is Bounded or Entire Space
snippet: Consider $\C$ as a vector space over $\C$. Let $E$ be a balanced subset of $\C$. Then $E$ is bounded, or $E = \C$.

title: Balanced Subset of Real Numbers is Bounded or Entire Space
snippet: Consider $\R$ as a vector space over $\R$. Let $E$ be a balanced subset of $\R$. Then $E$ is bounded, or $E = \R$.

title: Banach-Alaoglu Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a separable normed vector space. Then the closed unit ball in its normed dual $X^*$ is sequentially compact with respect to the weak-$\ast$ topology.

title: Banach-Dieudonné Theorem
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $B_{X^\ast}^-$ be the closed unit ball in $X^\ast$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology in $X^\ast$. Let $A$ be a convex set in $X^\ast$ such that: $A \cap n B_{X^\ast}^-$ is $w^\ast$-closed for each $n \in \N$. Then $A$ is $w^\ast$-closed.

title: Banach-Schauder Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be Banach spaces. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a surjective bounded linear transformation. Then $T$ is an open mapping.

title: Banach-Tarski Paradox
snippet: Let $\mathbb D^3 \subset \R^3$ be a unit ball in real Euclidean space of $3$ dimensions. Then $\mathbb D^3$ is equidecomposable to the union of two such unit balls.

title: Banach Algebra of Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space is Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map \CC X = \map \CC {X, \C}$ be the vector space of continuous functions on $X$. Let $\ast$ be pointwise multiplication on $\C^X$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\map \CC X$. Then $\struct {\map \CC X, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a Banach algebra.

title: Banach Algebra with Unity is Unital Banach Algebra
snippet:
Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot}$ be a non-trivial Banach algebra over $\mathbb F$. Suppose that $X$ has an identity element $\mathbf 1_X$. Then there exists a norm $
orm \cdot '$ on $X$ equivalent to $
orm \cdot$ such that $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot '}$ is a unital Banach algebra. That is: $(1): \quad
orm \cdot$ and $
orm \cdot '$ are equivalent $(2): \quad\struct {X, 
orm \cdot '}$ is a Banach algebra $(3): \quad
orm {\mathbf 1_X}' = 1$

title: Banach Fixed-Point Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $f: M \to M$ be a contraction. That is, there exists $q \in \hointr 0 1$ such that for all $x, y \in M$: $\map d {\map f x, \map f y} \le q \, \map d {x, y}$ Then there exists a unique fixed point of $f$.

title: Banach Isomorphism Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be Banach spaces. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bijective bounded linear transformation. Then the inverse of $T$ is a bounded linear transformation. That is, $T$ is a normed vector space isomorphism.

title: Banach Space-Valued Function Constant on each Set in Countable Partition of Domain is Bochner Measurable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\sequence {\Omega_n'}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of Lebesgue measurable subsets of $I$ such that: $\ds \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} \Omega_n' = I$ Let $f : I \to X$ be a function that is constant on each $\Omega_n'$. Then $f$ is Bochner measurable.

title: Banach Space-Valued Simple Function has Standard Representation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then $f$ is a simple function there exists: disjoint Lebesgue measurable sets $\Omega_1, \ldots, \Omega_n \subseteq I$ of finite Lebesgue measure $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in X$ such that: $\ds \map f t = \sum_{r \mathop = 1}^n x_r \map {\chi_{\Omega_r} } t$ for each $t \in I$.

title: Banach Space-Valued Simple Function is Bochner Measurable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then $f$ is Bochner measurable.

title: Banach Space-Valued Simple Function takes Finitely Many Values
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then $\Img f$ is a finite set.

title: Banach Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Banach Spaces ==

title: Banach Space Valued Function is Analytic iff Weakly Analytic
snippet: Let $U$ be an open set of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $f : U \to X$ be a function. Then $f$ is analytic it is weakly analytic.

title: Banach Space is F-Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. From Normed Vector Space is Hausdorff Topological Vector Space, we may consider $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ as a topological vector space. With this identification, $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ is an $F$-Space.

title: Banach Space is Reflexive iff Normed Dual is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Then: $X$ is reflexive $X^\ast$ is reflexive.

title: Banach Space with Schur Property is Weakly Sequentially Complete
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space with the Schur property. Then $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ is weakly sequentially complete.

title: Banach Space with Weak Topology has Countable Tightness
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Then $\struct {X, w}$ has countable tightness.

title: Barber Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == There exists a community, one of whose members is a . This barber operated under an unusual rule: his task was to shave every man in the community who did not shave himself, and only those men. Who shaves the barber? If he does not shave himself, then he must shave himself. But if he shaves himself, he must not shave himself.

title: Barbier's Theorem
snippet: Let $K$ be a closed curve of constant diameter. Let the circumference of $K$ be $c$. Let the diameter of $K$ be $d$. Then: $\dfrac c d = \pi$

title: Barlow's Prediction
snippet: == Prediction == ascertained that $2^{31} - 1 = 2147483647$ is a prime number; and this is the greatest at present known to be such, and, consequently, the last of the above perfect numbers [that is, $2^{30}\left({2^{31} - 1}\right)$], which depends upon this, is the greatest perfect number known at present, and probably the greatest that ever will be discovered; for, as they are merely curious without being useful, it is not likely that any person will attempt to find one beyond it. This statement was made by , in his $1811$ work .

title: Barycenter Exists and is Well Defined
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an affine space over a field $k$. Let $p_1, \ldots, p_n \in \EE$ be points. Let $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n \in k$ such that $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i = 1$. Then the barycentre of $p_1, \ldots, p_n$ with weights $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n$ exists and is unique.

title: Barycentric Coordinates are Unique iff Vertices are Affinely Independent
snippet: Let $V = \tuple {v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_k}$ be a set of $k + 1$ vertices in $\mathbb R^k$. Let $x$ be any point in $\mathbb R^k$. Let $\tuple {\lambda_0, \lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_k}$ be the barycentric coordinates of $x$ the vertices. Then the barycentric coordinates are unique $V$ is affinely independent.

title: Barycentric Coordinates of Centroid of Triangle
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be the position vectors of the $3$ vertices of a triangle $T$ in the plane. Let $p$ be the centroid of $T$. Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be the barycentric coordinates of $p$ $T$ Then: $\alpha = \beta = \gamma = \dfrac 1 3$

title: Barycentric Coordinates of Point inside Triangle
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be the position vectors of the $3$ vertices of a triangle $T$ in the plane. Let $p$ be an arbitrary point inside $T$. Then the barycentric coordinates of $p$ $T$ are all positive.

title: Basel Problem
snippet: $\ds \map \zeta 2 = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty {\frac 1 {n^2} } = \frac {\pi^2} 6$ where $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function.

title: Basel Problem as Infinite Product
snippet: $\ds \dfrac {\pi^2} 6 = \prod_{p \mathop \in \mathbb P} \dfrac {p^2} {p^2 - 1}$

title: Bases of Finitely Generated Free Module have Equal Cardinality
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module. Let $M$ be finitely generated. Let $B$ and $C$ be bases of $M$. Then $B$ and $C$ are finite and have the same cardinality.

title: Bases of Finitely Generated Vector Space have Equal Cardinality
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $G$ be a finitely generated $K$-vector space. Then any two bases of $G$ are finite and equivalent.

title: Bases of Free Module have Equal Cardinality
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module. Let $B$ and $C$ be bases of $M$. Then $B$ and $C$ are equivalent. That is, they have the same cardinality.

title: Bases of Vector Space have Equal Cardinality
snippet: Let $R$ be a division ring. Let $V$ be a vector space over $R$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be bases of $V$. Then $X$ and $Y$ are equivalent. That is, $X$ and $Y$ have the same cardinality.

title: Basic Inequality/One-Sided Shift Space of Finite Type
snippet: Let $\struct {X_\mathbf A ^+, \sigma}$ be a one-sided shift of finite type. Let $F_\theta ^+$ be the space of Lipschitz functions on $X_\mathbf A ^+$. Let $\size \cdot_\theta$ be the Lipschitz seminorm on $F_\theta ^+$. Let $\norm \cdot_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $F_\theta ^+$. Let $f \in F_\theta ^+$. Let $u := \map \Re f$ be the real part of $f$. Let $\LL_f$ and $\LL_u$ denote the transfer operators. If $\LL_u$ is normalized, then there is a $C > 0$ such that: $\size {\LL_f ^n w}_\theta \le C \norm w_\infty + \theta ^n \size w_\theta$ for all $w \in F_\theta ^+$ and $n \in \N$.

title: Basic Primitive Recursive Functions are Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^k \to \N$ be a basic primitive recursive function. Then there is a WFF $\map \phi {y, x_1, \dotsc, x_k}$ of $k + 1$ free variables and no quantifiers such that: $y = \map f {x_1, \dotsc, x_k}$ $\N \models \map \phi {y \gets \sqbrk y, x_1 \gets \sqbrk {x_1}, \dotsc, x_k \gets \sqbrk {x_k} }$ where $\sqbrk a$ denotes the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Basic Separating Hyperplane Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $A, B \subseteq X$ be disjoint convex sets such that $A$ has an internal point. Let $X^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $X$. Then there exists a linear functional $\hat f \in X^\#$ such that the affine hyperplane $\sqbrk {\hat f = \alpha}$ properly separates $A$ and $B$.

title: Basic Sequence Congruent to Complemented Basic Sequence is Complemented
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a complemented basic sequence. Let $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $Y$ that is congruent to $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is complemented in $Y$.
