Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$. Let $\sqbrk {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sqbrk {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the closed linear spans of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ respectively.

title: Basic Universe has Infinite Number of Elements
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Then $V$ has an infinite number of elements.

title: Basic Universe is Inductive
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Then $V$ is an inductive class.

title: Basic Universe is Supercomplete
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Then $V$ is supercomplete.

title: Basic Universe is not Empty
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe Then $V$ is not the empty class.

title: Basic Universe is not Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Then $V$ is not a set.

title: Basis (Hilbert Space)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Basis (Hilbert Space) ==

title: Basis Condition for Coarser Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\BB_1$ and $\BB_2$ be two bases on $S$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be the topologies generated by $\BB_1$ and $\BB_2$ respectively. If $\BB_1$ and $\BB_2$ satisfy: $\forall U \in \BB_1 : \exists \AA \subseteq \BB_2: U = \bigcup \AA$ then $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$.

title: Basis Constant is Greater Than or Equal to One
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach space over $\GF$ with $X \ne \set { {\mathbf 0}_X}$. Let $E = \sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Schauder basis for $X$. Let $K_b$ be the basis constant for $E$. Then $K_b \ge 1$.

title: Basis Element of Furstenberg Topology is Clopen
snippet: Let $\tau$ be the Furstenberg topology on the set of integers $\Z$. Let $a, b \in \Z$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then $a \Z + b$ is clopen in $\struct {\Z, \tau}$.

title: Basis Expansion/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Basis Expansions ==

title: Basis Expansion of Irrational Number
snippet: A basis expansion of an irrational number never terminates and does not recur.

title: Basis Expansion of Rational Number
snippet: Let $b$ be a number base. Let $x$ be a real number. Then $x$ is a rational number the basis expansion of $x$ in base $b$ terminates or recurs.

title: Basis Representation Theorem
snippet: Let $b \in \Z: b > 1$. For every $n \in \Z_{> 0}$, there exists one and only one sequence $\sequence {r_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le t}$ such that: $(1): \quad \ds n = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^t r_k b^k$ $(2): \quad \ds \forall k \in \closedint 0 t: r_k \in \N_b$ $(3): \quad r_t \ne 0$ This unique sequence is called the representation of $n$ to the base $b$, or, informally, we can say $n$ is (written) in base $b$.

title: Basis Representation Theorem for Ordinals
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x > 1$ and $y > 0$. Then there exist unique finite sequences of ordinals: $\sequence {a_i}, \sequence {b_i}$ both of unique length $n$ such that: $(1): \quad \sequence {a_i}$ is a strictly decreasing sequence for $1 \le i \le n$ $(2): \quad 0 < b_i < x$ for all $1 \le i \le n$ $(3): \quad \ds y = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} b_i$

title: Basis Representation is No Longer than Number
snippet: Let $b > 1$ and $n > 0$ be natural numbers. Let the base-$b$ representation of $n$ be: $\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \dotsm r_1 r_0}_b$ Then: $n > m$

title: Basis Representation is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $\operatorname{basis} : \N^3 \to \N$ be defined as follows: $\map {\operatorname{basis} } {b, n, i} = \begin{cases} 1 & : b = 1 \land i 1 \land i \le m \\ 0 & : \text {otherwise} \end{cases}$ where $\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \dots r_1 r_0}_b$ is the base-$b$ representation of $n$.

title: Basis Test for Adherent Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis of $T$. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $x \in S$ is an adherent point of $H$ : $\forall U \in \BB : x \in U$ satisfies $H \cap U \ne \O$

title: Basis Test for Isolated Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis of $T$. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $x \in H$ is an isolated point of $H$ : $\exists U \in \BB : U \cap H = \set x$

title: Basis Test for Limit Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis of $T$. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $x \in S$ is a limit point of $H$ : $\forall U \in \BB : x \in U$ satisfies $H \cap U \setminus \set x \ne \O$

title: Basis Theorem
snippet: Let $E$ be a vector space of $n$ dimensions. Let $H$ be a linearly independent subset of $E$. $H$ is a basis for $E$ it contains exactly $n$ elements.

title: Basis for Box Topology
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {S_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological spaces. Let $S$ be the cartesian product of $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. That is: $\ds S := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ Define: $\ds \BB := \set {\prod_{i \mathop \in I} U_i: \forall i \in I: U_i \in \tau_i}$ Then $\BB$ is a synthetic basis on $S$.

title: Basis for Discrete Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau$ be the discrete topology on $S$. Let $\BB$ be the set of all singleton subsets of $S$: $\BB := \set {\set x: x \in S}$. Then $\BB$ is a basis for $T$.

title: Basis for Either-Or Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the either-or space. Let $\BB$ be the set: $\BB := \set {\set x: x \in S, x \ne 0} \cup \set {\openint {-1} 1}$ that is, the set of all singleton subsets of $S$ less $\set 0$ and including the open real interval $\openint {-1} 1$. Then $\BB$ is a basis for $T$.

title: Basis for Element of Real Number Line
snippet: Let $M = \struct {\R, d}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $M$. Then the set of all open intervals containing $a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

title: Basis for Euclidean Topology on Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\BB$ be the set of subsets of $\R$ defined as: $\BB = \set {\openint a b: a, b \in \R}$ That is, $\BB$ is the set of all open real intervals of $\R$: $\openint a b := \set {x \in \R: a < x < b}$ Then $\BB$ forms a basis for the Euclidean topology on $\R$.

title: Basis for Excluded Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be an excluded point space. Consider the set $\BB$ defined as: $\BB = \set {\set x: x \in S \setminus \set p} \cup \set S$ Then $B$ is a basis for $S$.

title: Basis for Finite Submodule of Function Space
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $A$ be a set. For each $a \in A$, let $f_a: A \to R$ be defined as: $\forall x \in A: \map {f_a} x = \begin{cases} 1 & : x = a \\ 0 & : x \ne a \end{cases}$ Then $B = \set {f_a: a \in A}$ is a basis of the Finite Submodule of Function Space $R^{\paren A}$.

title: Basis for Open Ordinal Topology
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Consider the set $\BB$ of subsets of $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ of the form: $\openint \alpha {\beta + 1} = \hointl \alpha \beta = \set {x \in \hointr 0 \Gamma: \alpha < x < \beta + 1}$ for $\alpha, \beta \in \hointr 0 \Gamma$. Then $\BB$ forms a basis for $\hointr 0 \Gamma$.

title: Basis for Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Consider the set $\BB$ defined as: $\BB = \set {\set {x, p}: x \in S} \cup \set p$ Then $B$ is a basis for $S$.

title: Basis for Partition Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\PP$ be a partition of $S$. Let $\tau$ be the partition topology on $S$ defined as: $a \in \tau \iff a$ is the union of sets of $\PP$ Then $\PP$ forms a basis of $\tau$.

title: Basis for Product of Metric Spaces under Chebyshev Distance
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}, \ldots, M_n = \struct {A_n, d_n}$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i$ be the cartesian product of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$. Let $d_\infty: \AA \times \AA \to \R$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_\infty} {x, y} = \max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {\map {d_i} {x_i, y_i} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. For $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$, let $U_i$ be open in $M_i$.

title: Basis for R-Module R
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}_R$ denote the $R$-module $R$. Then $\set {1_R}$ is a basis for $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}_R$.

title: Basis for Set of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module such that $\map \dim G = n$. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module such that $\map \dim H = m$. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be an ordered basis for $G$. Let $\sequence {b_m}$ be an ordered basis for $H$.

title: Basis for Topological Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct {A, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\O \subseteq H \subseteq A$ and so let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ be a subspace of $T$. Let $\BB$ be a (synthetic) basis for $T$. Let $\BB_H$ be defined as: $\BB_H = \set {U \cap H: U \in \BB}$ Then $\BB_H$ is a (synthetic) basis for $H$.

title: Basis for Topology on Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{A_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct{A_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $A_1 \times A_2$ be the Cartesian product of $A_1$ and $A_2$. Let $\PP = \set {U_1 \times U_2 : U_1 \in \tau_1, U_2 \in \tau_2}$ Then $\PP$ is a synthetic basis on $A_1 \times A_2$.

title: Basis for Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals considered as a topological space: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Let $\BB_1$ and $\BB_2$ be the set of subsets of $\R$ defined as: {{eqn | l = \BB_1 | r = \set {\openint x y: x, y \in \R \cap \openint a b, x < y} | c = }} {{eqn | l = \BB_2 | r = \set {\openint x y: x, y \in \R \cap \openint b c, x < y} | c = }} Let $\BB = \BB_1 \cup \BB_2$. Then $\BB$ is a basis for $T$.

title: Basis has Subset Basis of Cardinality equal to Weight of Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\BB$ be a basis of $T$. Then there exists a basis $\BB_0$ of $T$ such that $\BB_0 \subseteq \BB$ and $\card {\BB_0} = \map w T$ where: $\card {\BB_0}$ denotes the cardinality of $\BB_0$ $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$.

title: Basis induces Local Basis
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\BB$ be an analytic basis for $\tau$. Let $x \in S$, and denote with $\BB_x$ the set $\set {B \in \BB: x \in B}$. Then $\BB_x$ is a local basis at $x$.

title: Basis of Free Module is No Greater than Generator
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module with basis $B$. Let $S$ be a generating set for $M$. Then: $\size B \le \size S$. That is, there exists an injection from $B$ to $S$.

title: Basis of Point Lattice is not Necessarily Unique
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a point lattice of dimension $n$. Let $\BB = \set {\mathbf v_1, \mathbf v_2, \ldots, \mathbf v_n}$ be a basis of $\LL$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\BB$ is the only basis of $\LL$.

title: Basis of Vector Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bases of Vector Spaces ==

title: Basis of Vector Space Injects into Generator
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $B$ be a basis of $V$. Let $G$ be a generator of $V$. Then there exists an injection from $B$ to $G$.

title: Basis of Vector Space of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $B$ be the set of all the identity functions $I^n$ on $\R^n$ where $n \in \N^*$. Then $B$ is a basis of the $\R$-vector space $\map P \R$ of all polynomial functions on $\R$.

title: Bayes' Theorem
snippet: Let $\Pr$ be a probability measure on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\condprob A B$ denote the conditional probability of $A$ given $B$. Let $\map \Pr A > 0$ and $\map \Pr B > 0$. Then: $\condprob B A = \dfrac {\condprob A B \, \map \Pr B} {\map \Pr A}$

title: Bearing/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bearing ==

title: Beatty's Theorem
snippet: Let $r, s \in \R \setminus \Q$ be an irrational number such that $r > 1$ and $s > 1$. Let $\BB_r$ and $\BB_s$ be the Beatty sequences on $r$ and $s$ respectively. Then $\BB_r$ and $\BB_s$ are complementary Beatty sequences : $\dfrac 1 r + \dfrac 1 s = 1$

title: Beer-Lambert-Bouguer Law
snippet: == Physical Law == The fraction of incident light absorbed by a thin layer of translucent material is proportional to the thickness of the layer.

title: Begging the Question
snippet: == Fallacy == Let $p$ be a proposition whose truth value is to be proved (either true or false). Suppose a logical argument is created which uses $p$ as a premise. That is, that the proposition to be derived is used to derive itself. Then the fallacy of begging the question has been perpetrated.

title: Behaviour of Function Near Limit
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $f \left({x}\right) \to l$ as $x \to \xi$. Then: If $l > 0$, then $\exists h > 0: \forall x: \xi - h 0$ If $l 0: \forall x: \xi - h < x < \xi + h, x \ne \xi: \map f x < 0$

title: Behaviour of Parametric Equations for Folium of Descartes according to Parameter
snippet: Consider the folium of Descartes $F$, given in parametric form as: $\begin {cases} x = \dfrac {3 a t} {1 + t^3} \\ y = \dfrac {3 a t^2} {1 + t^3} \end {cases}$ Then: $F$ has a discontinuity at $t = -1$. For $t < -1$, the section in the $4$th quadrant is generated For $-1 < t \le 0$, the section in the $2$nd quadrant is generated For $0 \le t$, the section in the $1$st quadrant is generated.

title: Bell Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bell Numbers ==

title: Bell Number as Summation over Lower Index of Stirling Numbers of the Second Kind
snippet: Let $B_n$ be the Bell number for $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $B_n = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n {n \brace k}$ where $\ds {n \brace k}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Bellman's Principle of Optimality
snippet: Let $P$ be an optimal path in an exercise in dynamic programming. Then any part of $P$ is also an optimal path.

title: Belphegor's Prime
snippet: == Interesting Number == Belphegor's prime is the palindromic prime: $1000000000000066600000000000001$ It has: $666$: the Number of the Beast in its center Unlucky number $13$ zeroes either side of the $666$ $31$ digits, which is not only itself prime, but backwards is $13$ which is also prime.

title: Bendixson-Dulac Theorem
snippet: Suppose there exists a continuously differentiable function $\map \alpha {x, y}$ on a simply connected domain. Suppose that: $\nabla \cdot \paren {\alpha F}$ is either always positive or always negative. Then the two-dimensional autonomous system: $\tuple {x, y}' = \map F {x, y}$ does not have a periodic solution.

title: Benford's Law
snippet: Benford's law is an empirical observation concerning the leading digits in a given number base (usually $10$). In a data set containing data spanning several orders of magnitude, the leading digits are more likely to be small.

title: Beppo Levi's Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+$ be an increasing sequence of positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Let $\ds \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be the pointwise supremum of $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, where $\overline \R$ denotes the extended real numbers. Then: $\ds \int \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n \rd \mu = \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the supremum on the is in the ordering on $\overline \R$.

title: Berlin Papyrus 6619/Examples
snippet: == Examples from ==

title: Bernoulli's Equation/2 x y dx + (x^2 + 2 y) dy = 0
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad 2 x y \rd x + \paren {x^2 + 2 y} \rd y = 0$ has the solution: $y \paren {x^2 + y} = C$

title: Bernoulli's Equation/x^2 dy = (2 x y + y^2) dx
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 \rd y = \paren {2 x y + y^2} \rd x$ has the general solution: $y = -\dfrac {x^2} {x + C}$

title: Bernoulli's Equation/x y' + y = x^4 y^3
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad x y' + y = x^4 y^3$ has the general solution: $\dfrac 1 {y^2} = - x^4 + C x^2$

title: Bernoulli's Equation/x y^2 y' + y^3 = x cosine x
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad x y^2 y' + y^3 = x \cos x$ has the general solution: $y^3 = 3 \sin x + \dfrac {9 \cos x} x - \dfrac {18 \sin x} {x^2} - \dfrac {18 \cos x} {x^3} + \dfrac C {x^3}$

title: Bernoulli's Equation/y' - (1 over x + 2 x^4) y = x^3 y^2
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' - \paren {\dfrac 1 x + 2 x^4} y = x^3 y^2$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {2 x} {C \map \exp {-\dfrac {2 x^5} 5} - 1}$

title: Bernoulli's Equation/y^2 dx = (x^3 - x y) dy
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y^2 \rd x = \paren {x^3 - x y} \rd y$ has the general solution: $3 y = 2 x^2 + C x^2 y^2$

title: Bernoulli's Hanging Chain Problem
snippet: Consider a uniform chain $C$ whose physical properties are as follows: $C$ is of length $L$ The mass per unit length of $C$ is $\lambda$ $C$ is of zero stiffness. Let $C$ be suspended in a vertical line from a fixed point and otherwise free to move. Let $C$ be slightly disturbed in a vertical plane from its position of stable equilibrium. Let $\map y t$ be the horizontal displacement at time $t$ from its position of stable equilibrium of a particle of $C$ which is a vertical distance $x$ from its point of attachment.

title: Bernoulli's Inequality
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > -1$. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\paren {1 + x}^n \ge 1 + n x$

title: Bernoulli's Theorem
snippet: Let the probability of the occurrence of an event be $p$. Let $n$ independent trials be made, with $k$ successes. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \frac k n = p$

title: Bernoulli Number in terms of Euler Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: {{eqn | l = B_{2 n} | r = \frac {2 n} {2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} } \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \dbinom {2 n - 2} {2 k} E_{2 k} E_{2 n - 2 k - 2} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac {2 n} {2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} } \paren {\binom {2 n - 2} 0 E_0 E_{2 n - 2} + \binom {2 n - 2} 2 E_2 E_{2 n - 4} + \binom {2 n - 2} 4 E_4 E_{2 n - 6} + \cdots + \binom {2 n - 2} {2 n - 2} E_{2 n - 2} E_0} | c = }} where: $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number.

title: Bernoulli Numbers are Rational
snippet: The Bernoulli numbers are rational.

title: Bernoulli Process as Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $\sequence {X_i}$ be a binomial experiment with parameter $p$. Let $\EE$ be the experiment which consists of performing the Bernoulli trial $X_i$ until a failure occurs, and then stop. Let $k$ be the number of successes before a failure is encountered. Then $k$ is modelled by a geometric distribution with parameter $p$.

title: Bernstein's Theorem
snippet: Bernstein's Theorem (Approximation Theory) Bernstein's Theorem (Monotone Functions) Bernstein's Theorem on Unique Global Solution to y=F(x,y,y') Bernstein's Lethargy Theorem

title: Bernstein's Theorem on Unique Global Solution to y''=F(x,y,y')
snippet: Let $F$ and its partial derivatives $F_y, F_{y'}$ be real functions, defined on the closed interval $I = \closedint a b$. Let $F, F_y, F_{y'} $ be continuous at every point $\tuple {x, y}$ for all finite $y'$. Suppose there exists a constant $k > 0$ such that: $\map {F_y} {x, y, y'} > k$ Suppose there exist real functions $\alpha = \map \alpha {x, y} \ge 0$, $\beta = \map \beta {x, y}\ge 0$ bounded in every bounded region of the plane such that: $\size {\map F {x, y, y'} } \le \alpha y'^2 + \beta$ Then one and only one integral curve of the equation $y' ' = \map F {x, y, y'}$ passes through…

title: Berry Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Every number can be defined by a sentence in natural language. For the purpose of this argument, let that natural language be . It is assumed without proof that has a finite number of words. Let $n$ be an integer such that $n \ge 15$. Then the cardinality of the set of integers that can be defined in no more than $n$ words is finite. Consider the integer that is defined as: the smallest integer which cannot be defined by a sentence of at most fifteen words. Let this number be $N$. That is $N$ cannot be defined by a sentence of at most fifteen words.

title: Bertrand's Ballot Theorem
snippet: Consider an election involving two candidates $A$ and $B$, which $A$ has won. Let $p$ be the number of votes that $A$ received, and $q < p$ be the number of votes that $B$ received. We assume that $A$ did not win by default, and that at least one vote was cast. We put all $p + q$ votes in a ballot box and draw them at uniform random. As we do this, we keep a tally $T_A$ of the votes cast for candidate $A$ and a tally $T_B$ of the votes cast for candidate $B$.

title: Bertrand's Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Let $C$ be a circle. The expectation of the length of a chord of $C$ chosen at random is not well-defined. That is, there are several ways of randomly selecting a chord of $C$, and each way leads to a different expectation of its length. For example: Select a random point $P$ in $C$ and select the chord perpendicular to the diameter which $P$ lies on For a given point $P$ on the circumference of $C$, pick another point $Q$, also on the circumference of $C$, and let $PQ$ be the random chord and so on.

title: Bertrand's Theorem
snippet: Let $U: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be analytic for $r > 0$. Let $M > 0$ be a nonvanishing angular momentum such that a stable circular orbit exists. Suppose that every orbit sufficiently close to the circular orbit is closed. Then $U$ is either $k r^2$ or $-\dfrac k r$ (for $k > 0$) up to an additive constant.

title: Bertrand-Chebyshev Theorem
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{>0}$, there exists a prime number $p$ with $n < p \le 2 n$.

title: Bessaga-Pełczyński Selection Principle
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Schauder basis for $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ with basis constant $K_b$. Let $\sequence {e_n^\ast}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the coordinate functionals associated with $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ such that: $\ds \inf_n 
orm {x_n} > 0$ and: $\map {e_k^\ast} {x_n} 	o 0$ as $n 	o \infty$ for each $k \in \N$.

title: Bessel's Correction
snippet: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ form a random sample from a population with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$. Let: $\ds \bar X = \frac 1 n \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i$ Then: $\ds \hat {\sigma^2} = \frac 1 {n - 1} \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {X_i - \bar X}^2$ is an unbiased estimator of $\sigma^2$.

title: Bessel's Equation/x^2 y'' + x y' + (x^2 - (1 over 4)) y = 0

title: Beta Function is Defined for Positive Reals
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\map \Beta {x, y}$ be the Beta function: $\ds \map \Beta {x, y} := \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} t^{x - 1} \paren {1 - t}^{y - 1} \rd t$ Then $\map \Beta {x, y}$ exists provided that $x, y > 0$.

title: Beta Function of Real Number with 1

snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $\expect X = \mu$ for some $\mu \in \R$. Let $\var X = \sigma^2$ for some $\sigma^2 \in \R_{> 0}$. Then, for all $k > 0$: $\map \Pr {\size {X - \mu} \ge k \sigma} \le \dfrac 1 {k^2}$

title: Biholomorphic Function from Open Unit Disk to Right Half-Plane
snippet: Let $\mathbb D = \set {z : \cmod z 0}$ be the right half-plane. Define $f : \mathbb D \to \C$ by: $\ds \map f z = \frac {1 - z} {1 + z}$ for each $z \in \mathbb D$. Then $f$ is a biholomorphic function $\mathbb D \to \mathbb H_r$.

title: Bijection Iff Isomorphism in Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{Set}$, i.e. a mapping. Then: $f$ is a bijection it is an isomorphism in $\mathbf{Set}$.

title: Bijection Preserves Set Partition
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a partitioning of $S$ indexed by $I$. Hence, let $\set {S_i: i \in I}$ be the resulting partition of $S$. Then the image of $f$ is a partition of $T$ indexed by $I$ such that: $T = \set {f \sqbrk {S_i}: i \in I}$

title: Bijection between Integers and Even Integers
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of integers. Let $2 \Z$ be the set of even integers. Then there exists a bijection $f: \Z \to 2 \Z$ between the two.

title: Bijection between Power Set of Disjoint Union and Cartesian Product of Power Sets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be disjoint sets. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Then there exists a bijection between $\powerset {S \cup T}$ and $\paren {\powerset S} \times \paren {\powerset T}$. Hence: $\powerset {S \cup T} \sim \paren {\powerset S} \times \paren {\powerset T}$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence.

title: Bijection between Power Set of nth Initial Section and Initial Section of nth Power of 2
snippet: Let $\N_n$ be used to denote the first $n$ non-zero natural numbers: $\N_n = \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ Then there exists a bijection between the power set of $\N_n$ and $\N_{2^n}$.

title: Bijection between Prüfer Sequences and Labeled Trees
snippet: There is a one-to-one correspondence between Prüfer sequences and labeled trees. That is, every labeled tree has a unique Prüfer sequence that defines it, and every Prüfer sequence defines just one labeled tree.

title: Bijection between R x (S x T) and (R x S) x T
snippet: Let $R$, $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $S \times T$ be the Cartesian product of $S$ and $T$. Then there exists a bijection from $R \times \paren {S \times T}$ to $\paren {R \times S} \times T$. Hence: $\card {R \times \paren {S \times T} } = \card {\paren {R \times S} \times T}$

title: Bijection between S x T and T x S
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $S \times T$ be the Cartesian product of $S$ and $T$. Then there exists a bijection from $S \times T$ to $T \times S$.

title: Bijection between Specific Elements
snippet: == Lemma == Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $f: A \leftrightarrow B$ be a bijection. Then given $a \in A$ and $b \in B$, there exists another bijection $g: A \leftrightarrow B$ such that $\map g a = b$.

title: Bijection from Cartesian Product of Initial Segments to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\N_k$ be used to denote the set of the first $k$ non-zero natural numbers: $\N_k := \set {1, 2, \ldots, k}$ Then a bijection can be established between $\N_k \times \N_l$ and $\N_{k l}$, where $\N_k \times \N_l$ denotes the Cartesian product of $\N_k$ and $\N_l$.

title: Bijection from Divisors to Subgroups of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group of order $n$ generated by $a$. Let $S = \set {m \in \Z_{>0}: m \divides n}$ be the set of all divisors of $n$. Let $T$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$ Let $\phi: S \to T$ be the mapping defined as: $\phi: m \to \gen {a^{n / m} }$ where $\gen {a^{n / m} }$ is the subgroup generated by $a^{n / m}$. Then $\phi$ is a bijection.

title: Bijection has Left and Right Inverse
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Let: $I_S$ be the identity mapping on $S$ $I_T$ be the identity mapping on $T$. Let $f^{-1}$ be the inverse of $f$. Then: $f^{-1} \circ f = I_S$ and: $f \circ f^{-1} = I_T$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Bijection iff Left and Right Cancellable
snippet: Let $f$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a bijection $f$ is both left cancellable and right cancellable.

title: Bijection iff Left and Right Inverse
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. $f$ is a bijection : where: $g_1$ and $g_2$ are mappings $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. It also follows that it is necessarily the case that $g_1 = g_2$ for such to be possible.

title: Bijection iff exists Mapping which is Left and Right Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a bijection : there exists a mapping $g: T \to S$ such that: $g \circ f = I_S$ $f \circ g = I_T$ where $I_S$ and $I_T$ are the identity mappings on $S$ and $T$ respectively.

title: Bijection in Yoneda Lemma for Contravariant Functors
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ be a contravariant functor. Let $A \in \mathbf C$ be an object. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ be its identity morphism. Let $h_A = \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-,A}$ be its contravariant hom-functor.

snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ be a covariant functor. Let $A \in \mathbf C$ be an object. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ be its identity morphism. Let $h^A = \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {A, -}$ be its covariant hom-functor.

title: Bijection is Open iff Closed
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a bijection. Then $f$ is open $f$ is closed.

title: Bijection is Open iff Inverse is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a bijection. Then $f$ is open $f^{-1}$ is continuous.

title: Bijection on Total Ordering is Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection to an arbitrary set $T$. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $T$ defined such that: $\RR: = \set {\tuple {\map f x, \map f y}: x \preccurlyeq y}$ Then $f$ is an order isomorphism between $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ and $\struct {T, \RR}$.

title: Bijection on Total Ordering reflects Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping to an arbitrary set $T$. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $T$ defined such that: $\RR: = \set {\tuple {\map f x, \map f y}: x \preccurlyeq y}$ That is, $a$ is related to $b$ in $T$ they have preimages $x$ and $y$ under $f$ such that $x$ precedes $y$. Then: $f$ is a bijection $\RR$ is a total ordering.

title: Bijective Continuous Linear Operator is not necessarily Invertible
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the normed vector space. Let $\map {CL} X := \map {CL} {X, X}$ be a continuous linear transformation space. Let $I \in \map {CL} X$ be the identity element. Suppose $A \in \map {CL} X$ is bijective. Then $A$ is not necessarily invertible.

title: Bijective Identification Mapping is Homeomorphism from Original Topology to Identification Topology

title: Bijective Relation has Left and Right Inverse

Binet-Cauchy Identity
snippet: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n a_i c_i} \paren {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n b_j d_j} = \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n a_i d_i} \paren {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n b_j c_j} + \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {a_i b_j - a_j b_i} \paren {c_i d_j - c_j d_i}$ where all of the $a, b, c, d$ are elements of a commutative ring. title: Binomial Coefficient 2 n Choose n is Divisible by All Primes between n and 2 n
snippet: Let $\dbinom {2 n} n$ denote a binomial coefficient. Then for all prime numbers $p$ such that $n < p < 2 n$: $p \divides \dbinom {2 n} n$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

title: Binomial Coefficient as Infinite Product
snippet: {{eqn | l = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {n + b} } n \frac {\paren {n + a - b} } {\paren {n + a} } | r = \frac {\paren {1 + b} } 1 \frac {\paren {1 + a - b} } {\paren {1 + a} } \times \frac {\paren {2 + b} } 2 \frac {\paren {2 + a - b} } {\paren {2 + a} } \times \cdots | c = }}

title: Binomial Coefficient expressed using Beta Function
snippet: Let $\dbinom r k$ denote a binomial coefficient. Then: $\dbinom r k = \dfrac 1 {\paren {r + 1} \map B {k + 1, r - k + 1} }$

title: Binomial Coefficient involving Power of Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $k \in \Z$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Then: $\dbinom {p^n k} {p^n} \equiv k \pmod p$ where $\dbinom {p^n k} {p^n}$ is a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient involving Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\dbinom n p$ be a binomial coefficient. Then: $\dbinom n p \equiv \floor {\dfrac n p} \pmod p$ where: $\floor {\dfrac n p}$ denotes the floor function.

title: Binomial Coefficient is Integer
snippet: Let $\dbinom n k$ be a binomial coefficient. Then $\dbinom n k$ is an integer.

title: Binomial Coefficient is instance of Gaussian Binomial Coefficient
snippet: Let $\dbinom r m_q$ denote the Gaussian binomial coefficient: Then: $\ds \lim_{q \mathop \to 1^-} \dbinom r m_q = \dbinom r m$ where $\dbinom r m$ denotes the conventional binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient n Choose j in terms of n-2 Choose r
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n \ge 4$. Let $\dbinom n k$ denote a binomial coefficient for $k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k = \dbinom {n - 2} {k - 2} + 2 \dbinom {n - 2} {k - 1} + \dbinom {n - 2} k$ for $2 \le k \le n - 2$.

title: Binomial Coefficient n Choose k by n Plus 1 Minus n Choose k + 1
snippet: Let $\sequence {A_{n k} }$ be a sequence defined on $n, k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ as: $A_{n k} = \begin{cases} 1 & : k = 0 \\ 0 & : k \ne 0, n = 0 \\ A_{\paren {n - 1} k} + A_{\paren {n - 1} \paren {k - 1} } + \dbinom n k & : \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ Then the closed form for $A_{n k}$ is given as: $A_{n k} = \paren {n + 1} \dbinom n k - \dbinom n {k + 1}$

title: Binomial Coefficient of Half
snippet: Let $k \in \Z$. $\dbinom {\frac 1 2} k = \dfrac {\left({-1}\right)^{k - 1} } {4^k \left({2 k - 1}\right)} \dbinom {2 k} k$ where $\dbinom {\frac 1 2} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient of Minus Half
snippet: Let $k \in \Z$. $\dbinom {-\frac 1 2} k = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^k} {4^k} \dbinom {2 k} k$ where $\dbinom {-\frac 1 2} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient of Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then: $\forall k \in \Z: 0 < k < p: \dbinom p k \equiv 0 \pmod p$ where $\dbinom p k$ is defined as a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient of Prime Minus One Modulo Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then: $0 \le k \le p - 1 \implies \dbinom {p - 1} k \equiv \left({-1}\right)^k \pmod p$ where $\dbinom {p - 1} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient of Prime Plus One Modulo Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then: $2 \le k \le p - 1 \implies \dbinom {p + 1} k \equiv 0 \pmod p$ where $\dbinom {p + 1} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient of Real Number with Half
snippet: $\dbinom r {1 / 2} = \dfrac {2^{2 r + 1} } {\dbinom {2 r} r \pi}$ where $\dbinom r {1 / 2}$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Binomial Coefficient over Power Not Greater than Reciprocal of Factorial
snippet: Let $r > 0$. Let $k \in \N$ such that $k \le 2r + 1$. Then: $\dfrac {\dbinom r k} {r^k} \le \dfrac 1 {k!}$

title: Binomial Coefficient with One
snippet: $\forall r \in \R: \dbinom r 1 = r$ where $\dbinom r 1$ denotes a binomial coefficient. The usual presentation of this result is: $\forall n \in \N: \dbinom n 1 = n$

title: Binomial Coefficient with Self
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z: \dbinom n n = \sqbrk {n \ge 0}$ where $\sqbrk {n \ge 0}$ denotes Iverson's convention. That is: $\forall n \in \Z_{\ge 0}: \dbinom n n = 1$ $\forall n \in \Z_{< 0}: \dbinom n n = 0$

title: Binomial Coefficient with Self minus One
snippet: $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: \dbinom n {n - 1} = n$

title: Binomial Coefficient with Two
snippet: $\forall r \in \R: \dbinom r 2 = \dfrac {r \paren {r - 1} } 2$

title: Binomial Coefficient with Zero
snippet: $\forall r \in \R: \dbinom r 0 = 1$ The usual presentation of this result is: $\forall n \in \N: \dbinom n 0 = 1$

title: Binomial Distribution/Example/Arbitrary Example 1
snippet: == Example of Binomial Distribution == Let a die be cast $4$ times. Let a score of $6$ be denoted as a success. Then the experiment can be modelled by a binomial distribution $\Binomial n p$ such that $n = 4$ and $p = \dfrac 1 6$. Thus the probability of $2$ successes is $\dfrac {25} {216}$.

title: Binomial Distribution Approximated by Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable which has the binomial distribution $\Binomial n p$. Then for large $n$ and such that both $n p$ and $n q$ are approximately $5$ or more: $\Binomial n p \approx \Gaussian {n p} {n p q}$ where $\Gaussian {n p} {n p q}$ denotes the normal distribution.

title: Binomial Distribution Approximated by Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable which has the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Then for $\lambda = n p$, $X$ can be approximated by a Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \binom n k p^k \paren {1 - p}^{n - k} = \frac {\lambda^k} {k!} e^{-\lambda}$

title: Binomial Experiment has Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $\sequence {X_i}$ be a finite binomial experiment of length $n$ such that each of the $X_i$ in the sequence is a Bernoulli trial with parameter $p$. Then the number of successes in $\sequence {X_i}$ is modelled by a binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Hence it can be seen that: $X \sim \Binomial 1 p$ is the same thing as $X \sim \Bernoulli p$

title: Binomial Form of Relation between Riemann Zeta Function and Dirichlet Eta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\map \Re s > 1$. Then: $\ds \map \zeta s = \frac 1 {1 - 2^{1 - s} } \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {\frac 1 {2^{n + 1} } \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^k \binom n k \paren {k + 1}^{-s} }$

title: Biot-Savart Law
snippet: Let $s$ be a wire carrying a steady current $I$. Let $\map {\mathbf B} {\mathbf r}$ be the total magnetic field due to $I$ flowing through $s$ at a point $P$ whose position vector is $\mathbf r$. Then: $\ds \map {\mathbf B} {\mathbf r} = \dfrac {\mu_0 I} {4 \pi} \oint_s \dfrac {\d \mathbf l \times \paren {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'} } {\size {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'}^3}$ where: $\d \mathbf l$ is an infinitesimal vector associated with $s$ $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of $P$ $\mathbf r'$ is the position vector of $\d \mathbf l$ $\mu_0$ denotes the vacuum permeability.

title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == When the solution to a Diophantine equation in polynomials are the points of an Abelian variety, the order of the group of rational points is related to the behavior of an associated $\zeta$ (zeta) function $\map \zeta s$ near $s = 1$. In particular: if $\map \zeta 1 = 0$ then there is an infinite set of rational points if $\map \zeta 1 \ne 0$ then there is a finite set of rational points.

title: Birkhoff's Ergodic Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \BB, \mu, T}$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then a $\mu$-integrable function $\tilde f$ exists such that: $\forall x \in X : \map {\tilde f} {T x} = \map {\tilde f} x$ and: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac 1 n \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} f \circ T^n = \tilde f$ converges $\mu$-almost everywhere and in $L^1$-norm.

title: Boadicea/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on == Yes, I know this is not about mathematics. It's far more important than that. The name Boadicea is also presented as Boudicca or Boudica. Other spellings abound. Its pronunciation is correctly Bo-dee-ca. The name derives from the old English word for victory. Hence the modern form of Boadicea or Boudicca can be argued as being Victoria. Beware that in general usage there exists the incorrect pronunciation: Bow-er-di-see-a. The explanation is that Boadicea is the Roman form, and Boudicca the English form.

title: Bochner Integral is Additive
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f, g : I \to X$ be Bochner integrable functions. Then $f + g$ is Bochner integrable and: $\ds \int \paren {f + g} \rd \lambda = \int f \rd \lambda + \int g \rd \lambda$

title: Bochner Integral is Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a Bochner integrable function. Let $\alpha \in \GF$. Then $\alpha f$ is Bochner integrable and: $\ds \int_I \paren {\alpha f} \rd \lambda = \alpha \int_I f \rd \lambda$

title: Bochner Integral is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a Bochner integrable function. Then the Bochner integral of $f$ is well-defined.

title: Bochner Integral of Scalar Multiple of Simple Function
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $\alpha \in \GF$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then: $\ds \int \paren {\alpha f} \rd \lambda = \alpha \int f \rd \lambda$ where $\int$ denotes the Bochner integral.

title: Bochner Integral of Simple Function is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then the Bochner integral of $f$ is well-defined.

title: Bochner Integral of Sum of Simple Functions
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f, g : I \to X$ be simple functions. Then: $\ds \int \paren {f + g} \rd \lambda = \int f \rd \lambda + \int g \rd \lambda$ where $\int$ denotes the Bochner integral.

title: Bootstrapping/Example/Arbitrary Example 1
snippet: == Example of Bootstrapping == Let $B$ bootstrap samples be taken of a population. Let $m$ be the median of the population as a whole. Let ${m_b}^*$ be the median of the $b$th bootstrap sample, where $b = 1, 2, \ldots, B$. Then the bootstrap estimated standard error of $m$ is given by: $\map {\operatorname {se} } m = \sqrt {\dfrac 1 {B - 1} \ds \sum_b \paren { {m_b}^* - {\overline m}^*}^2}$ where ${\overline m}^*$ is the mean of the ${m_b}^*$.

title: Borel-Cantelli Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable sets. Let: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map \mu {E_n} < \infty$ Then: $\ds \map \mu {\limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} E_n} = 0$ where $\limsup$ denotes limit superior of sets.

title: Borel-Cantelli Lemma 10 to Kochen-Stone Theorem
snippet: Let $A_n$ be a sequence of events with $\ds \sum \map \Pr {A_n} = \infty$ and: $\ds \liminf_{k \mathop \to \infty} \frac {\ds \sum_{1 \mathop \le m, n \mathop \le k} \map \Pr {A_n \cap A_m} } {\ds \paren {\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^k \map \Pr {A_n} }^2} < \infty$ Then there is a positive probability that $A_n$ occur infinitely often.

title: Borel-Cantelli Lemma in Probability
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}$ be an arbitrary countable sequence of events. Let the sum of the probabilities of $\sequence {E_n}$ be finite. Then the probability that infinitely many of the events occur is zero.

title: Borel-Cantelli Lemmata to Kochen-Stone Theorem
snippet: == Lemmata to Kochen-Stone Theorem ==

title: Borel-Carathéodory Lemma
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open set with $0 \in D$. Let $R > 0$ be such that the open disk $\map B {0, R} \subset D$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be analytic with $\map f 0 = 0$. Let $\map \Re {\map f z} \le M$ for $\cmod z \le R$. Let $0 < r < R$. Then for $\cmod z \le r$: {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \cmod {\map f z} | o = \le | r = \frac {2 M r} {R - r} }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall k \ge 1 | l = \cmod {\map {f^{\paren k} } z} | o = \le | r = \frac {2 M R k!} {\paren {R - r}^{k + 1} } }}

title: Borel Sigma-Algebra Generated by Closed Sets
snippet: Let $\map \BB {S, \tau}$ be a Borel $\sigma$-algebra generated by the set of open sets in $S$. Then $\map \BB {S, \tau}$ is equivalently generated by the set of closed sets in $S$.

title: Borel Sigma-Algebra of Subset is Trace Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space, and let $A \subseteq X$ be a subset of $X$. Let $\tau_A$ be the subspace topology on $A$. Then the following equality of $\sigma$-algebras on $A$ holds: $\map \BB {A, \tau_A} = \map \BB {X, \tau}_A$ where $\BB$ signifies Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and $\map \BB {X, \tau}_A$ signifies trace $\sigma$-algebra.

title: Borel Sigma-Algebra on Euclidean Space by Monotone Class
snippet: Let $\sqbrk {\R^n, \tau}$ be the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. Then: $\map \BB {\R^n, \tau} = \map {\mathfrak m} \tau$ where $\BB$ denotes Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and $\mathfrak m$ denotes generated monotone class.

title: Borell-TIS Inequality
Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $f: \mathbb S^n \to \R^n$ be a continuous mapping from an $n$-sphere to $\R^n$. Then there exists $x \in \mathbb S^n$ such that $\map f x = \map f {-x}$.

title: Borsuk Null-Homotopy Lemma
snippet: Let $\Bbb S^2$ denote the unit sphere in $\R^3$. Let $a,b \in \Bbb S^2$. Let $\struct {A, \tau_A}$ be a compact topological space. Let $f : A \to \Bbb S^2 \setminus \set {a,b}$ be a continuous injective mapping. Let $f$ be null-homotopic. Then $a$ and $b$ lie in the same component of $\Bbb S^2 \setminus \Img f$. Here, $\Img f$ denotes the image of $f$.

title: Bott-Milnor-Kervaire 1,2,4,8 Theorem
snippet: Let $A$ be a division algebra with real scalars. Then the dimension of $A$ is either: $1$: the real numbers $\R$ $2$: the complex numbers $\C$ $4$: the quaternions $\Bbb H$ or: $8$: the octonions $\Bbb O$.

title: Bottom-Up Form of Top-Down Grammar defines same Formal Language
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a formal language. Let $\TT$ be a top-down grammar for $\LL$. Let $\BB$ be the bottom-up form of $\TT$. Then $\BB$ is also a formal grammar for $\LL$.

title: Bottom-Up Specification of Propositional Logic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bottom-Up Specification of Propositional Logic ==

title: Bottom Relation is Auxiliary Relation
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $B = \left\{ {\left({\bot, x}\right): x \in S}\right\}$ where $\bot$ denotes the smallest element in $L$. Then $B$ is auxiliary relation.

title: Bottom Relation is Bottom in Ordered Set of Auxiliary Relations
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map {\it Aux} L$ be the set of all auxiliary relations on $S$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\it Aux} L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where: $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq \restriction_{ \map {\it Aux} L \times \map {\it Aux} L}$ Let $B = \set {\struct {\bot_L, x}: x \in S}$ where $\bot_L$ denotes smallest element in $L$. Then $B \mathop = \bot_P$

title: Bottom in Compact Closure
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded below ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then: $\bot \in x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ where: $\bot$ denotes the smallest element in $L$ $ x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$.

title: Bottom in Compact Subset
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Then $\bot \in K\left({L}\right)$ where $\bot$ denotes the smallest element of $L$, $K\left({L}\right)$ denotes the compact subset of $L$.

title: Bottom in Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded below ordered set. Let $I$ be a ideal in $S$. Then $\bot \in I$ where $\bot$ denotes the smallest element of $S$.

title: Bottom in Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $P = \struct {\tau, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion ordered set of $\tau$. Then $P$ is bounded below and $\bot_P = \O$

title: Bottom is Compact
snippet: Let $L$ be a bounded below ordered set. Then $\bot$ is a compact element where $\bot$ is the smallest element in $L$.

title: Bottom is Way Below Any Element
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $\bot \ll x$ where $\bot$ denotes the smallest element in $S$.

title: Bottom not in Proper Filter
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded below preordered set. Let $F$ be a filter on $L$. Then $F$ is proper filter $\bot \notin F$ where $\bot$ denotes the smallest element of $S$.

title: Bottom of Lattice is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Then $S$ has at most one bottom.

title: Boubaker's Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$ whose zero is $0_D$ and whose unity is $1_D$. Let $X \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in $X$ over $D$. Finally, consider the following properties: {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^N \map {p_n} 0 | r = -2N }} {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^N \map {p_n} {\alpha_k} | r = 0 }} {{eqn | n = 3 | l = \valueat {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^N \frac {\d \map {p_x} x} {\d x} } {x \mathop = 0} | r = 0 }} {{eqn | n = 4 | l = \valueat…

title: Bound Variable/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bound Variables ==

title: Bound for Analytic Function and Derivatives
snippet: Let $f$ be a complex function. Let $z_0$ be a point in $\C$. Let $r$ be a real number in $\R_{>0}$. Let $\Gamma$ be a circle in $\C$ with center at $z_0$ and radius $r$. Let $f$ be analytic on $\Gamma$ and its interior. Let $t \in \C$ be such that $\cmod {t - z_0} < r$. Then a real number $M$ exists such that, for every $n \in \N$: $\cmod {\map {f^{\paren n} } t} \le \dfrac {M r \, n!} {\paren {r - \cmod {t - z_0} }^{n + 1} }$

title: Bound for Cardinality of Matroid Circuit
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $C \subseteq S$ be a circuit of $M$. Let $\rho: \powerset S \to \Z$ denote the rank function of $M$. Then: $\card C \le \map \rho S + 1$

title: Bound for Difference of Irrational Number with Convergent
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number. Let $\sequence {C_n}$ be the sequence of convergents of the continued fraction expansion of $x$. Then $\forall n \ge 1$: $C_n < x < C_{n + 1}$ or $C_{n + 1} < x < C_n$ $\size {x - C_n} < \dfrac 1 {q_n q_{n + 1} }$

title: Bound for Negative Part of Pointwise Sum of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be extended real-valued function. Suppose that the pointwise sum $f + g$ is well-defined, that is: there exists no $x \in X$ such that $\set {\map f x, \map g x} = \set {\infty, -\infty}$. Then: $\paren {f + g}^- \le f^- + g^-$ where $\paren {f + g}^-$, $f^-$ and $g^-$ denote the negative parts of $f + g$, $f$ and $g$ respectively.

title: Bound for Norm of Difference of Element with Non-Negative Multiple of Element in Unital C*-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering of $A$. Let $a, b \in A$ be such that: ${\mathbf 0}_A \le_A a \le_A b \le_A {\mathbf 1}_A$ Then we have: $
orm {x - b x}^2 \le 
orm {x^\ast \paren { {\mathbf 1}_A - a} x}$ and: $
orm {x - x b}^2 \le 
orm {x \paren { {\mathbf 1}_A - a} x^\ast}$ for each $x \in A$.

title: Bound for Positive Part of Pointwise Sum of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be extended real-valued function. Suppose that the pointwise sum $f + g$ is well-defined, that is: there exists no $x \in X$ such that $\set {\map f x, \map g x} = \set {\infty, -\infty}$. Then: $\paren {f + g}^+ \le f^+ + g^+$ where $\paren {f + g}^+$, $f^+$ and $g^+$ denote the positive parts of $f + g$, $f$ and $g$ respectively.

title: Bound for Variation of Complex Measure in terms of Jordan Decomposition
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\cmod \mu$ be the variation of $\mu$. Let $\tuple {\mu_1, \mu_2, \mu_3, \mu_4}$ be the Jordan decomposition of $\mu$. Then: $\map {\cmod \mu} A \le \map {\mu_1} A + \map {\mu_2} A + \map {\mu_3} A + \map {\mu_4} A$ for all $A \in \Sigma$.

title: Bound on C0 Semigroup
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a $C_0$ semigroup. Let $\struct {\map B X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations equipped with the canonical norm. Then there exists $M \ge 1$ and $\omega \ge 0$ such that: $\norm {\map T t}_{\map B X} \le M e^{\omega t}$ for each $t \in \hointr 0 \infty$.

title: Bound on Complex Values of Gamma Function
snippet: Let $\map \Gamma z$ denote the Gamma function. Then for any complex number $z = s + i t$, we have for $\size b \le \size t$: $\size {\map \Gamma {s + i t} } \le \dfrac {\size {s + i b} } {\size {s + i t} } \size {\map \Gamma {s + i b} }$

title: Bound on Difference of Values of Convex Real Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set. Let $f : C \to \R$ be a convex function. Let $x \in C$. Let $z \in C$ be such that: $x + z \in C$ and $x - z \in C$. Let $\delta \in \closedint 0 1$. Then $x + \delta z \in C$, $x - \delta z \in C$, and further: $\cmod {\map f {x + \delta z} - \map f x} \le \delta \max \set {\map f {x + z} - \map f x, \map f {x - z} - \map f x}$

title: Bound on Inner Product of Differences with Metric Projection
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\R$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_\HH$ be the inner product norm. Let $C \subseteq \HH$ be a non-empty closed convex set. Let $\pi_C : \HH \to C$ be the metric projection of $\HH$ onto $C$. Let $x \in \HH$ and $y \in C$. Then we have: $\innerprod {x - \map {\pi_C} x} {y - \map {\pi_C} x} \le 0$

title: Bound on Inverse in Canonical Preordering of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering on $A$. Let $a \in A$ and $\alpha, \beta > 0$ be such that: $\alpha {\mathbf 1}_A \le_A a \le_A \beta {\mathbf 1}_A$ Then: $\beta^{-1} {\mathbf 1}_A \le_A a^{-1} \le_A \alpha^{-1} {\mathbf 1}_A$

title: Bound on Norm of Power of Element in Normed Algebra
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\GF$. Let $x \in A$ and $n \in \N$. Then: $
orm {x^n} \le 
orm x^n$

title: Bound on Norm of Real and Imaginary Parts of Element of Banach *-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach $\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map \Re x$ and $\map \Im x$ be the real and imaginary parts of $x$ respectively. Then: $
orm {\map \Re x} \le 
orm x$ and: $
orm {\map \Im x} \le 
orm x$ for each $x \in A$.

title: Bound on Riemannian Distance Inside Coordinate Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $d_g$ be the Riemannian distance. Suppose $U \subseteq M$ is an open subset. Let $p \in M$ be a point. Then $p$ has a coordinate neighborhood $V \subseteq U$ such that: $\forall q \in V : \exists C \in \R_{> 0} : \map {d_g} {p, q} \le C \map {d_{\bar g} } {p, q}$ where $\bar g$ is the Euclidean metric in the given coordinates on $V$.

title: Bound on Riemannian Distance Outside Coordinate Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $d_g$ be the Riemannian distance. Suppose $U \subseteq M$ is an open subset. Let $p \in M$ be a point. Then $p$ has a coordinate neighborhood $V \subseteq U$ such that: $\forall q \in M \setminus V : \exists D \in \R_{> 0} : \map {d_g} {p, q} \ge D$ where $\setminus$ denotes the set difference.

title: Bound on Survival Function of Pointwise Product
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Let $F_{f g}$ be the survival function of the pointwise product $f g$. Let $F_f$ and $F_g$ be the survival functions of $f$ and $g$ respectively. Then: $\ds \map {F_{f g} } {\alpha \beta} \le \map {F_f} \alpha + \map {F_g} \beta$ for all $\alpha, \beta \in \hointr 0 \infty$.

title: Bound on Survival Function of Pointwise Sum
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions such that the pointwise sum $f + g$ is well-defined. Let $F_{f + g}$ be the survival function of the pointwise scalar multiple $f + g$. Let $F_f$ and $F_g$ be the survival functions of $f$ and $g$ respectively. Then: $\ds \map {F_{f + g} } {\alpha + \beta} \le \map {F_f} \alpha + \map {F_g} \beta$ for all $\alpha, \beta \in \hointr 0 \infty$.

title: Bound on Total Variation of Scalar-Valued Measure associated with Resolution of the Identity
snippet:
Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\map B {\HH}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations on $\HH$. Let $\EE : \map \BB X 	o \map B {\HH}$ be a resolution of the identity. For each $x, y \in \HH$, define $\EE_{x, y} : \map \BB X 	o \C$ by: $\map {\EE_{x, y} } A = \innerprod {\map \EE A x} y$ for each $A \in \map \BB X$. Let $
orm {\EE_{x, y} }$ denote the total variation of $\EE_{x, y}$. Then: $
orm {\EE_{x, y} } \le 
orm x 
orm y$

title: Boundary (Topology)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Boundaries in the context of Topology ==

title: Boundary Condition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Boundary Conditions ==

title: Boundary Line in Nested Rectangle Space is Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the nested rectangle space in the Euclidean plane. Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ denote the boundary lines of $T$. Then $L_1$ and $L_2$ are each components of $T$.

title: Boundary is Intersection of Closure with Closure of Complement
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X \subseteq S$. Let $\partial X$ denote the boundary of $X$ in $T$, defined as: $\partial X = X^- \setminus X^\circ$ Let $\overline X = S \setminus X$ denote the complement of $X$ in $S$. Let $X^-$ denote the closure of $X$ in $T$. Then: $\partial X = X^- \cap \paren {\overline X}^-$

title: Boundary of Boundary is Contained in Boundary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then: $\map \partial {\partial H} \subseteq \partial H$ where $\partial H$ is the boundary of $H$ in $T$. That is, the boundary of the boundary of $H$ is contained in the boundary of $H$.

title: Boundary of Boundary is not necessarily Equal to Boundary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $\partial H$ denote the boundary of $H$. While it is true that: $\map \partial {\partial H} \subseteq \partial H$ it is not necessarily the case that: $\map \partial {\partial H} = \partial H$

title: Boundary of Boundary of Subset of Indiscrete Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then: $\map \partial {\partial H} = \O$ where $\partial H$ denotes the boundary of $H$.

title: Boundary of Cartesian Product of Subsets
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $H \subseteq T_1$ and $K \subseteq T_2$. Then: $\map \partial {H \times K} = \paren {\map \partial H \times \map \cl K} \cup \paren {\map \cl H \times \map \partial K}$ where: $\map \cl H$, for example, denotes the closure of $H$. $\map \partial H$, for example, denotes the boundary of $H$.

title: Boundary of Compact Closed Set is Compact
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $K\subset X$ be a compact subspace of $X$. Let $K$ be closed in $X$. Then its boundary $\partial K$ is compact.

title: Boundary of Compact Convex Set with Nonempty Interior is Homeomorphic to Sphere
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$. Let $C \subseteq \R^n$ be a compact convex subset of real Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose that the interior $C^\circ$ is non-empty. Then, the boundary $\partial C$ is homeomorphic to $\Bbb S^{n - 1}$, the unit $n - 1$-sphere.

title: Boundary of Compact Set in Hausdorff Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff topological space. Let $K \subset S$ be a compact subspace of $T$. Then its boundary $\partial K$ is compact.

title: Boundary of Empty Set is Empty
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Then: $\partial_T \O = \O$ where $\partial_T \O$ denotes the boundary in topology $T$ of $\O$.

title: Boundary of Intersection is Subset of Union of Boundaries
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\map \partial {A \cap B} \subseteq \partial A \cup \partial B$ where $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

title: Boundary of Mandelbrot Set is Fractal
snippet: Let $M$ be the Mandelbrot set. Then the boundary of $M$ in the complex plane $\C$ is fractal.

title: Boundary of Mandelbrot Set is Self-Similar
snippet: Let $M$ be the Mandelbrot set. Then the boundary of $M$ in the complex plane $\C$ is self-similar.

title: Boundary of Polygon as Contour
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in the complex plane $\C$. Denote the boundary of $P$ as $\partial P$. Then there exists a simple closed contour $C$ such that: $\Img C = \partial P$ where $\Img C$ denotes the image of $C$.

title: Boundary of Polygon is Jordan Curve
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in $\R^2$. Then there exists a Jordan curve $\gamma: \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ such that the image of $\gamma$ is equal to the boundary $\partial P$ of $P$.

title: Boundary of Polygon is Topological Boundary
snippet: Let $P$ be a polygon embedded in $\R^2$. Denote the boundary of $P$ as $\partial P$. Let $\Int P$ and $\Ext P$ denote the interior and exterior of $\partial P$, where $\partial P$ is considered as a Jordan curve. Then the topological boundary of $\Int P$ is equal to $\partial P$, and the topological boundary of $\Ext P$ is equal to $\partial P$.

title: Boundary of Set is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $\partial H$ denote the boundary of $H$ in $T$. Then $\partial H$ is closed in $T$.

title: Boundary of Spectrum of Element in Subalgebra of Unital Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_B} x$ be the spectra of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then: $\partial \map {\sigma_B} x \subseteq \partial \map {\sigma_A} x$ where $\partial$ denotes topological boundary.

title: Boundary of Subset of Discrete Space is Empty Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $\partial A = \O$ where: $\partial A$ is the boundary of $A$ in $T$.

title: Boundary of Subset of Indiscrete Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $\O \subsetneq H \subsetneq S$ (that is, let $H$ be a non-empty proper subset of $T$). Then: $\partial H = S$ where $\partial H$ denotes the boundary of $H$. If $H = \O$ or $H = S$ then $\partial H = \O$.

title: Boundary of Union is Subset of Union of Boundaries
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\map \partial {A \cup B} \subseteq \partial A \cup \partial B$ where $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

title: Boundary of Union of Separated Sets equals Union of Boundaries
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $T$. Let $A$ and $B$ are separated. Then: $\map \partial {A \cup B} = \partial A \cup \partial B$ where: $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$ $A \cup B$ denotes the union of $A$ and $B$.
