title: Bounded Below Weakly Null Sequence in Infinite-Dimensional Banach Space contains Basic Subsequence with Basis Constant Arbitrarily Close to 1
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence converging to $x$ in $\struct {X, w}$ such that: $\ds \inf_{n \mathop \in \N} 
orm {x_n}_X > 0$ Let $\epsilon > 0$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ has a basic subsequence $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ with basis constant at most $1 + \epsilon$.

title: Bounded Class is Set
snippet: Let $B$ be a class. Let it be assumed that $B$ is a subclass of a basic universe $V$. Let $B$ be bounded by a set $x$. Then $B$ is itself a set.

title: Bounded Complex-Valued Continuous Functions on Topological Space form Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\map {\CC_b} {X; \C} := \map {\CC_b} X$ be the space of bounded continuous functions on $X$ valued in $\C$. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\map {\CC_b} X$. For each $f \in \map {\CC_b} X$, define $\overline f : X \to \C$ by: $\map {\overline f} x = \overline {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Equip $\map {\CC_b} X$ with pointwise multiplication. Then $\struct {\map {\CC_b} X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty}$ is a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

title: Bounded Continuous Functions on Topological Space form Banach Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\map {\CC_b} {X; Y}$ be the space of bounded continuous functions on $X$ valued in $Y$. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\CC$. Then $\struct {\map {\CC_b} {X; Y}, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty}$ is a Banach space over $\GF$.

title: Bounded Function Continuous on Open Interval is Darboux Integrable
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $\closedint a b$ such that $a < b$. Let $f$ be continuous on $\openint a b$. Let $f$ be bounded on $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable on $\closedint a b$.

title: Bounded Function is of Exponential Order Zero
snippet: Let $f: \hointr 0 \to \to \mathbb F$ be a function, where $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $f$ be continuous everywhere on its domain, except possibly for some finite number of discontinuities of the first kind in every finite subinterval of $\hointr 0 \to$. Let $f$ be bounded. Then $f$ is of exponential order $0$.

title: Bounded Generalized Sum is Absolutely Convergent
snippet: Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\family {v_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of elements of $V$. Let $\FF$ denote the set of finite subsets of $I$. Then: the generalized sum $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} v_i$ is absolutely net convergent there exists $M \in \R_{\mathop \ge 0}$ such that for all $F \in \FF$: the summation $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in F} \norm{v_i} \le M$

title: Bounded Lattice has Both Greatest Element and Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded lattice. Then: $(1): \quad \struct {S, \preceq}$ has a smallest element, namely: $\bot := \sup \O$ $(2): \quad \struct {S, \preceq}$ has a greatest element, namely: $\top := \inf \O$

title: Bounded Linear Operator on Hilbert Space Direct Sum
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\sequence {\family {\HH_i, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a $I$-indexed family of Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. For each $i \in I$, let $T_i : \HH_i \to \HH_i$ be a bounded linear operator. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{i \mathop \in I} \norm {T_i}_{\map B {\HH_i} } < \infty$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {\HH_i} }$ is the norm of a bounded linear operator on $\HH_i$.

title: Bounded Linear Operator on Space of Bounded Sequences Vanishing on Zero-Limit Sequences also Vanishes on Bounded Sequences with certain Support
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of bounded sequences. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} {\N, \GF}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Let $T : \map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF} \to \map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF}$ be a bounded linear transformation with: $T \xi = {\mathbf 0}_{\ell_\infty}$ for each $\xi \in \map {c_0} {\N, \GF}$ Then there exists a countably infinite set $A \subseteq \N$ such that: $T \xi = {\mathbf 0}_{\ell_\infty}$ for each $\xi \in \map {\ell_\infty} {A, \GF}$, where $\map…

title: Bounded Linear Transformation Induces Bounded Sesquilinear Form
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_V}$ and $\struct {U, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_U}$ be inner product spaces over $\Bbb F$. Let $A : V \to U$ and $B : U \to V$ be bounded linear transformations. Let $u, v: V \times U \to \C$ be defined by: $\map u {h, k} := \innerprod {Ah} k_U$ $\map v {h, k} := \innerprod h {Bk}_V$ Then $u$ and $v$ are bounded sesquilinear forms.

title: Bounded Linear Transformation is Into Linear Isomorphism iff Dual Operator is Surjective
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ and $Y^\ast$ be the normed duals of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $T^\ast : Y^\ast \to X^\ast$ be the dual operator of $T$. Then $T$ is an into linear isomorphism $T^\ast$ is surjective.

title: Bounded Linear Transformation is Isometry iff Adjoint is Left-Inverse
snippet: Let $\HH, \KK$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $A \in \map B{\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded linear transformation. Then $A$ is an isometry : $A^*A = I_\HH$ where $A^*$ denotes the adjoint of $A$, and $I_\HH$ the identity operator on $\HH$.

title: Bounded Linear Transformation preserves Cauchy Sequences
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {T x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $Y$.

title: Bounded Linear Transformation to Banach Space has Unique Extension to Closure of Domain
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\map D {T_0}$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Let $\map D T = \paren {\map D T}^-$. Let $\map \BB {\map D {T_0}, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations on $X$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {\map D {T_0}, Y} }$ be the norm on $X$. Let $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$ be a Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\map \BB {\map D T, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $\map D T 	o Y$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {\map D T, Y} }$ be the norm on $X 	o Y$.

title: Bounded Measurable Function is Uniform Limit of Simple Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then there exists a sequence $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \map \EE \Sigma$ of simple functions, such that: $\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists n \in \N: \forall x \in X: \size {\map f x - \map {f_n} x} < \epsilon$ That is, such that $\ds f = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n$ uniformly. The sequence $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ may furthermore be taken to satisfy: $\forall n \in \N: \size {f_n} \le \size f$ where $\size f$ denotes the absolute value of $f$.

title: Bounded Metric Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bounded Metric Spaces == Category:Examples of Bounded Metric Spaces

title: Bounded Metric Space is not necessarily Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a bounded metric space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M$ is totally bounded.

title: Bounded Piecewise Continuous Function has Improper Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on a closed interval $\closedint a b$, $a < b$. Let $f$ be piecewise continuous and bounded on $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is a piecewise continuous function with improper integrals.

title: Bounded Piecewise Continuous Function is Darboux Integrable
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $f$ be piecewise continuous and bounded on $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable on $\closedint a b$.

title: Bounded Piecewise Continuous Function may not have One-Sided Limits
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on a closed interval $\closedint a b$, $a < b$. Let $f$ be a bounded piecewise continuous function. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f$ is a piecewise continuous function with one-sided limits:

title: Bounded Product is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let the function $f: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be primitive recursive. Then so is the function $g: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ defined as: $\map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, z} = \begin{cases} 1 & : z = 0 \\ \ds \prod_{y \mathop = 1}^z \map f {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y} & : z > 0 \end{cases}$

title: Bounded Rank implies Small Class
snippet: Let $S$ be a class. Suppose the rank, denoted $\map {\operatorname{rank} } x$, of each $x \in S$ is bounded above by some ordinal $y$. Then $S$ is a small class.

title: Bounded Real-Valued Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bounded Above Real-Valued Functions ==

title: Bounded Real-Valued Linear Functional is Real Part of Unique Bounded Complex-Valued Linear Functional
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\C$. Let $\struct {X_\R, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\R}$ be the realification of $X$ equipped with the restricted norm. Let $f : X_\R \to \R$ be a bounded linear functional. Then there exists a unique bounded linear functional $g : X \to \C$ such that: $\map f x = \map \Re {\map g x}$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Bounded Real Function may not be of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a bounded function. Then $f$ is not necessarily of bounded variation.

title: Bounded Real Sequence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bounded Real Sequences ==

title: Bounded Right-Continuous Increasing Function Vanishing at Infimum is Distribution Function of Finite Borel Measure
snippet: Let $K$ be a closed interval. Let $F : K \to \R$ be a bounded right-continuous increasing function such that: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to \inf K} \map F x = 0$ and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to \sup K} \map F x = M \in \hointr 0 \infty$ Then there exists a finite Borel measure $\mu$ on $K$ such that the distribution function $F_\mu$ of $\mu$ is equal to $F$. Further, $\map \mu K = M$.

title: Bounded Sequence in Euclidean Space has Convergent Subsequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_i}_{i \mathop \in \N}$ be a bounded sequence in the Euclidean space $\R^n$. Then some subsequence of $\sequence {x_i}_{i \mathop \in \N}$ converges to a limit.

title: Bounded Subset of Banach Space is Relatively Weakly Compact iff Weak-* Closure in Second Normed Dual is Contained in Embedding of Original Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $S \subseteq X$ be bounded. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the second normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$. Let $\cl_w$ be closure taken in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $\cl_{w^\ast}$ be closure taken in $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, w^\ast}$. Let $\iota : X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation.

title: Bounded Subset of Minimally Closed Class under Progressing Mapping has Greatest Element
snippet: Every bounded subset of $N$ has a greatest element.

title: Bounded Subset of Normed Dual Space is Relatively Weak-* Compact
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Let $\cl_{w^\ast}$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$. Let $S \subseteq X^\ast$ be bounded. Then $S$ is relatively compact in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$. That is, $\struct {\map {\cl_{w^\ast} } S, w^\ast}$ is compact.

title: Bounded Subset of Real Numbers/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bounded Subsets of Real Numbers ==

title: Bounded Subspace of Euclidean Space is Totally Bounded
snippet:
Let $\struct {\R^n, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Euclidean space, where $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the usual metric. Let $M$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {\R^n, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $M$ be bounded. Then $M$ is totally bounded.

title: Bounded Summation is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let the function $f: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be primitive recursive. Then so is the function $g: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ defined as: $\ds \map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, z} = \begin{cases} 0 & : z = 0 \\ \ds \sum_{y \mathop = 1}^z \map f {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y} & : z > 0 \end{cases}$

title: Bounded Summation of Integers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let the function $f : \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be primitive recursive. Let the function $g : \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be defined as: $\ds \map g {n_1, \dotsc, n_k, z} = \paren {\sum_{y = 0}^{z - 1} \ell_y}_\Z$ where $\map f {n_1, \dotsc, n_k, y}$ codes the integer $\ell_y$. Then, $g$ is primitive recursive.

title: Bounded Universal Quantification of Provable Arithmetic Formula is Provable
snippet: Let $\map \phi x$ be a WFF in the language of arithmetic with $1$ free variable. Let $\tau$ be a term in the language of arithmetic with no variables. Let $\sqbrk a$ denote the unary representation of $a$. Suppose that, for every $n \in \N$ such that $\N \models \map \phi {x \gets \sqbrk n}$: $\map \phi {x \gets \sqbrk n}$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic. Suppose also that: $\N \models \forall x < \tau: \map \phi x$ Then: $\forall x < \tau: \map \phi x$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

title: Bounded Variation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Bounded Variation ==

title: Boundedness is not Topological Property
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be homeomorphic. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $M_1$ is bounded $M_2$ is bounded. That is, boundedness is not a topological property.

title: Boundedness of Real Sine and Cosine
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then:

title: Boundedness of Sine X over X
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\size {\dfrac {\sin x} x} \le 1$

title: Bounds for Complex Exponential
snippet: Let $\exp$ denote the complex exponential. Let $z \in \C$ with $\cmod z \le \dfrac 1 2$. Then $\dfrac 1 2 \cmod z \le \cmod {\exp z - 1} \le \dfrac 3 2 \cmod z$

title: Bounds for Complex Logarithm
snippet: Let $\ln$ denote the complex logarithm. Let $z \in \C$ with $\cmod z \le \dfrac 1 2$. Then: $\dfrac 1 2 \cmod z \le \cmod {\map \ln {1 + z} } \le \dfrac 3 2 \cmod z$

title: Bounds for Cumulative Distribution Function
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function. Then: $0 \le \map {F_X} x \le 1$ for each $x \in \R$

title: Bounds for Finite Product of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ be positive real numbers. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k \le \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {1 + a_k} \le \map \exp {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k}$

title: Bounds for Integer Expressed in Base k
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $k \in \Z$ such that $k \ge 2$. Let $n$ be expressed in base $k$ notation: $n = \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^s a_j k^j$ where each of the $a_j$ are such that $a_j \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, k - 1}$. Then: $0 \le n < k^{s + 1}$

title: Bounds for Modulus of e^z on Circle x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 2y - 2 = 0
snippet: Consider the circle $C$ embedded in the complex plane defined by the equation: $x^2 + y^2 - 2 x - 2 y - 2 = 0$ Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a point lying on $C$. Then: $e^{-1} \le \cmod {e^z} \le e^3$

title: Bounds for Prime-Counting Function in terms of Second Chebyshev Function
snippet: There exists a real function $R : \hointr 2 \infty \to \R$ such that: $\ds \frac {\map \psi x} {\ln x} + \map R x \le \map \pi x \le \frac {2 \map \psi x} {\ln x} + \sqrt x$ for all real numbers $x \ge 2$, where: $\pi$ is the prime counting function $\psi$ is the second Chebyshev function $R = \map \OO {\sqrt x \ln x}$ where $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Bounds for Rank of Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\rho: \powerset S \to \Z$ be the rank function of $M$. Let $A \subseteq S$ be subset of $S$. Then: $0 \le \map \rho A \le \size A$

title: Bounds for Weierstrass Elementary Factors
snippet: Let $E_p: \C \to \C$ denote the $p$th Weierstrass elementary factor: $\quad\map {E_p} z = \begin {cases} 1 - z & : p = 0 \\ \paren {1 - z} \map \exp {z + \dfrac {z^2} 2 + \cdots + \dfrac {z^p} p} & : \text {otherwise} \end {cases}$ Let $z \in \C$.

title: Bounds of GCD for Sum and Difference Congruent Squares
snippet: Let $x, y, n$ be integers. Let: $x \not \equiv \pm y \pmod n$ and: $x^2 \equiv y^2 \pmod n$ where $a \equiv b \pmod n$ denotes that $a$ is congruent to $b$ modulo $n$. Then: $1 < \gcd \set {x - y, n} < n$ and: $1 < \gcd \set {x + y, n} < n$ where $\gcd \set {a, b}$ is the GCD of $a$ and $b$.

title: Bounds of Natural Logarithm
snippet: right Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$ where $x \in \R_{>0}$. Then $\ln$ satisfies the compound inequality: $1 - \dfrac 1 x \le \ln x \le x - 1$

title: Bounds of Riemannian Metric by Euclidean Metric on Euclidean Space
snippet: Let $W \subseteq \R^n$ be a subset of an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $g$ be a Riemannian metric on $W$. Let $\tilde g$ be a Euclidean metric on $W$. Let $K \subseteq W$ be a compact subset. Let $c, C \in \R_{\mathop > 0}$ be positive constants. Let $T_x \R^n$ be the tangent space of $\R^n$ at $x \in \R^n$. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}_g$ be the Riemannian inner product norm. Then: $\forall K \subseteq W : \exists c, C \in \R_{\mathop > 0} : \forall x \in K : \forall v \in T_x \R^n : c \size v_{\tilde g} \le \size v_g \le C \size v_{\tilde g}$

snippet:

orm a {\mathbf 1}_A$

title: Bounds on Number of Odd Terms in Pascal's Triangle
snippet: Let $P_n$ be the number of odd elements in the first $n$ rows of Pascal's triangle. Then: $0 \cdotp 812 \ldots < \dfrac {P_n} {n^{\lg 3} } < 1$ where $\lg 3$ denotes logarithm base $2$ of $3$. The lower bound $0 \cdotp 812 \ldots$ is known as the Stolarsky-Harborth constant.

title: Bounds on Projection in Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering of $A$. Let $p$ be a projection on $A$. Then we have: ${\mathbf 0}_A \le_A p \le_A {\mathbf 1}_A$

title: Bourbaki-Witt Fixed Point Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \le}$ be a non-empty chain complete ordered set (that is, an ordered set in which every chain has a supremum). Let $f: X \to X$ be an inflationary mapping, that is, so that $\map f x \ge x$. Then for every $x \in X$ there exists $y \in X$ where $y \ge x$ such that $\map f y = y$.

title: Box-and-Whisker Diagram/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Box-and-Whisker Diagrams ==

title: Box Topology contains Product Topology
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $X$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$: $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ Let $\tau$ be the product topology on $X$. Let $\tau'$ be the box topology on $X$. Then: $\tau \subseteq \tau'$

title: Box Topology may not be Coarsest Topology such that Projections are Continuous
snippet: Let $\family {\struct{X_i, \tau_i}}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological spaces. Let $X$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$, that is: $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ Let $\tau$ be the box topology on $X$. For each $i \in I$, let $\pr_i: X \to X_i$ denote the $i$th projection on $X$: $\forall \family {x_j}_{j \mathop \in I} \in X: \map {\pr_i} {\family {x_j}_{j \mathop \in I} } = x_i$ Then $\tau$ may not be the coarsest topology on $X$ for which the projections $\family{\pr_i} _{i \mathop \in I}$ are continuous.

title: Box Topology may not form Categorical Product in the Category of Topological Spaces
snippet: Let $\family {\struct{X_i, \tau_i}}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological spaces. Let $X$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$, that is: $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ Let $\tau$ be the box topology on $X$. Then $\struct{X, \tau}$ may not be the categorical product in the category of topological spaces.

title: Box Topology on Finite Product Space is Product Topology
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. For all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$, let $T_k = \struct {X_k, \tau_k}$ be topological spaces. Let $\ds X = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n X_k$ be the cartesian product of $X_1, \ldots, X_n$. Then the box topology and the product topology on $X$ are identical.

title: Brachistochrone Problem
snippet: == Problem == Let a point $A$ be joined by a wire to a lower point $B$. Let the wire be allowed to be bent into whatever shape is required. Let a bead be released at $A$ to slide down without friction to $B$. What is the shape of the wire so that the bead takes least time to descend from $A$ to $B$?

title: Brachistochrone is Cycloid
snippet: The shape of the brachistochrone is a cycloid.

title: Brahmagupta's Formula
snippet: The area of a cyclic quadrilateral with sides of lengths $a, b, c, d$ is: $\sqrt {\paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} \paren {s - c} \paren {s - d} }$ where $s$ is the semiperimeter: $s = \dfrac {a + b + c + d} 2$

title: Brahmagupta-Fibonacci Identity
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d$ be numbers. Then: $\paren {a^2 + b^2} \paren {c^2 + d^2} = \paren {a c + b d}^2 + \paren {a d - b c}^2$

title: Brahmagupta Theorem
snippet: If a cyclic quadrilateral has diagonals which are perpendicular, then the perpendicular to a side from the point of intersection of the diagonals always bisects the opposite side. Specifically: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral whose diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ are perpendicular, crossing at $M$. Let $EF$ be a line passing through $M$ and crossing opposite sides $BC$ and $AD$ of $ABCD$. Then $EF$ is perpendicular to $BC$ $F$ is the midpoint of $AD$.

snippet: == Examples of Branch Points of Complex Multifunctions ==

title: Branch and Bound Method/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Branch and Bound Method ==

title: Branch of Finite Propositional Tableau is Finite
snippet: Let $T$ be a finite propositional tableau. Let $\Gamma$ be a branch of $T$. Then $\Gamma$ is a finite branch.

title: Branch of Finite Tree is Finite
snippet: Let $T$ be a finite rooted tree with root node $r_T$. Let $\Gamma$ be a branch of $T$. Then $\Gamma$ is a finite branch.

title: Branches of Conchoid of Nicomedes are Asymptotic to Directrix
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a conchoid of Nicomedes. Let $\CC$ be the directrix of $\KK$. Then $\CC$ is an asymptote to both branches of $\KK$ in both directions.

title: Bretschneider's Formula
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a general quadrilateral. Then the area $\AA$ of $ABCD$ is given by: $\AA = \sqrt {\paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} \paren {s - c} \paren {s - d} - a b c d \map {\cos^2} {\dfrac {\alpha + \gamma} 2} }$ where: $a, b, c, d$ are the lengths of the sides of the quadrilateral $s = \dfrac {a + b + c + d} 2$ is the semiperimeter $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ are opposite angles.

title: Brianchon's Theorem
snippet: Let tangents to $6$ points on a conic section $K$ form a hexagon $H$ to circumscribe the $K$. Then the main diagonals of $H$ meet at a single point. 400px

title: Brianchon's Theorem is Projective Dual to Pascal's Theorem
snippet: Brianchon's Theorem is the projective dual of Pascal's Theorem.

title: Bridge divides Graph into Two Components
snippet: Let $G$ be a connected graph. Let $e$ be a bridge of $G$. Then the edge deletion $G - e$ contains exactly $2$ components.

title: Bridges of Königsberg
snippet: == Problem == Through the city of flowed the . In this river were two large islands, which were part of the city. Joining the mainland either side of the river and those two islands there stood seven bridges. File:Konigsberg_bridges.png It was a popular exercise among the citizens to take a pleasure stroll across the bridges. The question naturally arose: was it possible to cross each bridge once and once only during the course of a single walk? More to the point: could this be done such that the walkers end up back at their starting point?

snippet: The first and second Brocard Points are Isogonal Conjugates.

title: Broken Chord Theorem
snippet: 300px Let $A$ and $C$ be arbitrary points on a circle in the plane. Let $M$ be a point on the circle with arc $AM = $ arc $MC$. Let $B$ lie on the minor arc of $AM$. Draw chords $AB$ and $BC$. Find $D$ such that $MD \perp BC$. Then: $AB + BD = DC$

title: Brouwerian Lattice iff Meet-Continuous and Distributive
snippet: Let $\mathscr S = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Then $\mathscr S$ is a Brouwerian lattice $\mathscr S$ is meet-continuous and distributive.

title: Brouwerian Lattice iff Shift Mapping is Lower Adjoint
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is a Brouwerian lattice : $\forall x \in S, f: S \to S: \paren {\forall s \in S: \map f s = x \wedge s} \implies f$ is a lower adjoint

title: Brouwerian Lattice is Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a Brouwerian lattice. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is a distributive lattice

title: Brouwerian Lattice is Upper Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a Brouwerian lattice. Then $S$ is upper bounded.

title: Brun's Theorem
snippet: The sum of the reciprocals of all the twin primes converges.

title: Buffon's Needle
snippet: Let a horizontal plane be divided into strips by a series of parallel lines a fixed distance apart, like floorboards. Let a needle whose length equals the distance between the parallel lines be dropped onto the plane randomly from a random height. Then the probability that the needle falls across one of the parallel lines is $\dfrac 2 \pi$.

title: Buffon-Laplace Problem
snippet: Let a horizontal plane be divided into rectangles by a rectangular grid of straight lines of distances $a$ and $b$ apart. Let a needle whose length equals $l$ be dropped onto the plane randomly from a random height. Then the probability that the needle falls across one or more lines is $\dfrac {2 l \paren {a + b} - l^2} {\pi a b}$.

title: Bullseye Illusion
snippet: == Classic Problem == 400px The circle of radius $3 a$ at the center has the same area as the outer annulus whose width is $1$. However, it appears to be larger.

title: Bung that fits Triangular, Square and Circular Holes
snippet: == Problem == What shape of bung can be used to plug three different holes: one square one triangular one circular?

title: Bunyakovsky Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Let $P$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree two or higher whose coefficients are all integers. Then, for arguments which are all natural numbers, $P$ generates either: $(1):\quad$ an infinite set of numbers with greatest common divisor exceeding $1$ or: $(2):\quad$ infinitely many prime numbers.

title: Burali-Forti Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == The ordinal of the set of all ordinals must be larger than any of the ordinals in that set. Hence this would be an ordinal which is not contained in that set. That is, it is an ordinal which is not contained in the set of all ordinals. Hence the set of all ordinals is not an allowable set.

title: Buridan's Ass
snippet: == Paradox == Choice cannot be determined by reasoned preference alone.

title: Burnout Height of Upward Rocket under Constant Gravity
snippet: Let $R$ be a rocket whose structural mass is $m_1$. Let $R$ contain fuel of initial mass $m_2$. Let $R$ be fired straight up from the surface of a planet whose gravitational field exerts an Acceleration Due to Gravity of $g$, assumed constant. Let $R$ burn fuel at a constant rate $a$, with a constant exhaust velocity $b$ relative to $R$. Let all forces on $R$ except that due to the gravitational field be neglected. Then the burnout height of $R$ is given by: $h_b = -\dfrac {g m_2^2} {2 a^2} + \dfrac {b m_2} a + \dfrac {b m_1} a \ln \dfrac {m_1} {m_1 + m_2}$

title: Burnout Velocity of Upward Rocket under Constant Gravity
snippet: Let $R$ be a rocket whose structural mass is $m_1$. Let $R$ contain fuel of initial mass $m_2$. Let $R$ be fired straight up from the surface of a planet whose gravitational field exerts an Acceleration Due to Gravity of $g$, assumed constant. Let $R$ burn fuel at a constant rate $a$, producing a constant exhaust velocity $b$ relative to $R$. Let all forces on $R$ except that due to the gravitational field be neglected. Then the burnout velocity of $R$ is given by: $v_b = b \ln \left({1 + \dfrac {m_1} {m_2} }\right) - \dfrac {g m_2} a$

title: Burnside's Lemma
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group acting on a set $X$. Let $X / G$ be the set of orbits under this action. For $x \in X$, let $\Stab x$ be the stabilizer of $x$ by $G$. For $g \in G$, let $X^g$ denotes the set of all elements of $X$ which are fixed by $g$: $X^g := \set {x \in X: g x = x}$ Then: $\size {X / G} = \dfrac 1 {\order G} \ds \sum_{g \mathop \in G} \size {X^g}$ In words, the number of orbits equals the average number of fixed elements.

title: Burnside's Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let the order of $G$ be $p^m q^n$ where: $p, q$ are prime $m, n \in \N$ Then $G$ is solvable.

title: Bézout's Identity
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ such that $a$ and $b$ are not both zero. Let $\gcd \set {a, b}$ be the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$. Then: $\exists x, y \in \Z: a x + b y = \gcd \set {a, b}$ That is, $\gcd \set {a, b}$ is an integer combination (or linear combination) of $a$ and $b$. Furthermore, $\gcd \set {a, b}$ is the smallest positive integer combination of $a$ and $b$.

title: Bézout's Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be two plane projective curves defined over a field $F$ that do not have a common component. Then the total number of intersection points of $X$ and $Y$ with coordinates in an algebraically closed field $E$ which contains $F$, counted with their multiplicities, is equal to the product of the degrees of $X$ and $Y$.

title: C*-Algebra Generated by Commutative Self-Adjoint Set is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a self-adjoint set such that: $x y = y x$ for each $x, y \in S$. Let $\map {\text C^\ast} S$ be the $\text C^\ast$-algebra generated by $S$. Then $\map {\text C^\ast} S$ is commutative.

title: C*-Algebra embeds into Multiplier Algebra as C*-Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\struct {\map M A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map M A} }$ be the multiplier algebra of $A$. Define $\phi : A \to \map M A$ by: $\map \phi a = \tuple {L_a, R_a}$ for each $a \in A$, where $\tuple {L_a, R_a}$ is the double centralizer generated by $a$. Then $\phi \sqbrk A$ is a $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $\map M A$.

title: C6 is not Isomorphic to S3
snippet: Let $C_6$ denote the cyclic group of order $6$. Let $S_3$ denote the symmetric group on $3$ letters. Then $C_6$ and $S_3$ are not isomorphic.

title: CNF Satisfiability Problem is NP-Complete
snippet: The conjunctive normal form boolean satisfiability problem (CNF SAT) is NP-complete.

title: C^k Function Space is Banach Space
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\struct {\map {C^k} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the vector space of real-valued functions, k-times differentiable on $I$. Let $x \in \map {C^k} I$ be a real-valued function of differentiability class $k$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map {C^k} I}$ be the $C^k$ norm on $I$. Then $\struct {\map {C^k} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ equipped with $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map {C^k} I}$ is a Banach space.

title: C^k Norm is Norm
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\struct {\map {C^k} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the vector space of real-valued functions, k-times differentiable on $I$. Let $x \in \map {C^k} I$ be a real-valued function of differentiability class $k$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map {C^k} I}$ be the $C^k$ norm on $I$. Then $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map {C^k} I}$ is a norm on $\struct {\map {C^k} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$.

snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a finite algebraic structure. Let $\TT$ be the Cayley table for $\left({S, \circ}\right)$. Let $a \in S$ be an element of $S$. Then $a$ is cancellable for $\circ$ : $(1): \quad$ no element of $S$ is repeated in $\TT$ in the row headed by $a$ and: $(2): \quad$ no element of $S$ is repeated in $\TT$ in the column headed by $a$.

title: Cancellability of Congruences
snippet: Let $a, b, c, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $c a \equiv c b \pmod n \iff a \equiv b \pmod {n / d}$ where $d = \gcd \set {c, n}$.

title: Cancellable Element is Cancellable in Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$. Let $x \in T$ be cancellable in $S$. Then $x$ is also cancellable in $T$.

title: Cancellable Elements of Monoid form Submonoid
snippet: The cancellable elements of a monoid $\struct {S, \circ}$ form a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Cancellable Elements of Semigroup form Subsemigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $C$ be the set of cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\struct {C, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Cancellable Finite Semigroup is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a non-empty finite semigroup in which all elements are cancellable. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

title: Cancellable Infinite Semigroup is not necessarily Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup whose underlying set is infinite. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be such that all elements of $S$ are cancellable. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

title: Cancellable Semiring with Unity is Additive Semiring
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *, \circ}$ be a cancellable semiring with unity $1_S$. Then the distributand $*$ is commutative. That is to say, $\struct {S, *, \circ}$ is also an additive semiring.

title: Cancellable iff Regular Representations Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then $a \in S$ is cancellable : the left regular representation $\map {\lambda_a} x$ is injective and: the right regular representation $\map {\rho_a} x$ is injective.

title: Cancellation Law for Field Product
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $a, b, c \in F$. Then: $a \times b = a \times c \implies a = 0_F \text { or } b = c$

title: Cancellation Law for Ring Product of Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Let $D^*$ denote $D \setminus \set {0_D}$, that is, $D$ without its zero. Let $a \in D^*$. Then: $\forall x, y \in D: a \circ x = a \circ y \implies x = y$ That is, all elements of $D^*$ are cancellable for the ring product.

title: Cancellation Laws

title: Cancellation Property of Product Inverse Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\oplus: G \times G \to G$ be the product inverse of $\circ$ on $G$. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in G: \paren {x \oplus z} \oplus \paren {y \oplus z} = x \oplus y$

title: Canonical Form of Rational Number is Unique
snippet: The canonical form of a rational number is unique.

title: Canonical Form of Underdamped Oscillatory System
snippet: Consider a physical system $S$ whose behaviour can be described with the second order ODE in the form: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d t^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d x} {\d t} + a^2 x = 0$ for $a, b \in \R_{>0}$. Let $b < a$, so as to make $S$ underdamped. Then the value of $x$ can be expressed in the form: $x = \dfrac {x_0 a} \alpha e^{-b t} \map \cos {\alpha t - \theta}$ where: $\alpha = \sqrt {a^2 - b^2}$ $\theta = \map \arctan {\dfrac b \alpha}$ This can be referred to as the canonical form of the solution of $(1)$.

title: Canonical Homomorphism to Polynomial Ring is Ring Monomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {R \sqbrk X, \iota, X}$ be a polynomial ring over $R$ in one indeterminate $X$. Then the canonical homomorphism $\iota : R \to R \sqbrk X$ is a ring monomorphism.

title: Canonical Injection from Ideal of External Direct Sum of Rings
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \dotsc, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be rings. Let $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ be their external direct product. For each $k \in \closedint 1 n$, let: $R'_k = \set {\tuple {x_1, \dotsc, x_n} \in R: \forall j \ne k: x_j = 0}$ Let $\inj_k: R_k \to R$ be the canonical injection on the $k$th coordinate from $R_k$ into $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $\pr_k: R \to R'_k$ be the projection on the $k$th coordinate of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ onto $R'_k$.

title: Canonical Injection into Cartesian Product of Modules
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be the cartesian product of a sequence $\sequence {\struct {G_n, +_n, \circ_n}_R}$ of $R$-modules. Then for each $j \in \closedint 1 n$, the canonical injection $\inj_j$ from $\struct {G_j, +_j, \circ_j}_R$ into $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ is a monomorphism.

title: Canonical Injection is Injection
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures with identities $e_1, e_2$ respectively. The canonical injections: $\inj_1: \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {S_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in S_1: \map {\inj_1} x = \tuple {x, e_2}$ $\inj_2: \struct {S_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {S_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in S_2: \map {\inj_2} x = \tuple {e_1, x}$ are injections.

title: Canonical Injection is Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures with identities $e_1, e_2$ respectively. The canonical injections: $\inj_1: \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {S_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in S_1: \map {\inj_1} x = \tuple {x, e_2}$ $\inj_2: \struct {S_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {S_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {S_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in S_2: \map {\inj_2} x = \tuple {e_1, x}$ are monomorphisms.

title: Canonical Injection is Right Inverse of Projection
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be groups with identity elements $e_1$ and $e_2$ respectively. Let $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ Let: $\pr_1: \struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ} \to \struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ be the first projection from $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ to $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ $\pr_2: \struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be the second projection from $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ to $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$.

title: Canonical Injection of Real Number Line into Complex Plane
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $f: \R \to \C$ be the mapping from the real numbers to the complex numbers defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f z = x + 0 y$ Then $f: \struct {\R, +} \to \struct {\C, +}$ is a monomorphism.

title: Canonical Injection on Group Direct Product is Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be groups with identities $e_1, e_2$ respectively. Let $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ Then the canonical injections: $\inj_1: \struct {G_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {G_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {G_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in G_1: \map {\inj_1} x = \tuple {x, e_2}$ $\inj_2: \struct {G_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {G_1, \circ_1} \times \struct {G_2, \circ_2}: \forall x \in G_2: \map {\inj_2} x = \tuple {e_1, x}$ are group monomorphisms.

title: Canonical Mapping of Locale to Powerset of Points is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\map {\operatorname{pt}} L$ denote the points of $L$ as completely prime filters. For each $a \in L$, let: $\Sigma_a = \set{p \in \map {\operatorname{pt}} L : a \in p}$ Let $\Sigma : L \to \powerset {\map {\operatorname{pt}} L}$ be the mapping defined by: $\forall a \in L : \map \Sigma a = \Sigma_a$ where $\powerset {\map {\operatorname{pt}} L}$ denotes the powerset of $\map {\operatorname{pt}} L$. Then: $\Sigma: \struct{L, \preceq} \to \struct{\powerset {\map {\operatorname{pt}} L}, \subseteq}$ is a frame homomorphism.

title: Canonical Order Well-Orders Ordered Pairs of Ordinals
snippet: The canonical order, $R_0$ strictly well-orders the ordered pairs of ordinal numbers.

title: Canonical P-adic Expansion of Rational is Eventually Periodic
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p$. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then: $x$ is a rational number the canonical expansion of $x$ is eventually periodic.

title: Canonical Preordering of C*-Algebra is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering of $A$. Let $a, b \in A$ such that: $a \le_A b$ and: $b \le_A a$ Then $a = b$. That is, $\le_A$ is antisymmetric and hence $\le_A$ is a partial ordering.

title: Canonical Preordering of C*-Algebra of Continuous Functions Vanishing at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $A = \map {\CC_0} X$ be the set of continuous complex-valued functions vanishing at infinity. Consider $A$ as a $\text C^\ast$-algebra with pointwise addition, pointwise scalar multiplication, pointwise multiplication and pointwise complex conjugation. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering of $A$. Let $f, g \in \map {\CC_0} X$. We have $f \le_A g$ $\map g x - \map f x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Cantor's Diagonal Argument
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $\card S > 1$, that is, such that $S$ is not a singleton. Let $\mathbb F$ be the set of all mappings from the natural numbers $\N$ to $S$: $\mathbb F = \set {f: \N \to S}$ Then $\mathbb F$ is uncountably infinite.

title: Cantor's Intersection Theorem
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\sequence {S_n}$ be a nested sequence of closed balls in $M$ defined by: $S_n = \map {B^-_{\rho_n} } {x_n}$ where $\rho_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ and: $S_1 \supseteq S_2 \supseteq \cdots \supseteq S_n \supseteq \cdots$ Then there exists a unique $x \in A$ such that: $\ds \bigcap_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty S_n = \set x$

title: Cantor's Leaky Tent is Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be Cantor's leaky tent. Then $T$ is connected.

title: Cantor's Leaky Tent is Punctiform
snippet: Let $T$ be Cantor's leaky tent. Then $T$ is a punctiform space.

title: Cantor's Leaky Tent is Totally Pathwise Disconnected
snippet: Let $T$ be Cantor's leaky tent. Then $T$ is totally pathwise disconnected.

title: Cantor's Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Let $\CC$ be the set of all sets. Let $\powerset \CC$ denote the power set of $C$. Is the cardinality of $\CC$ greater than or equal to the cardinality of $\powerset \CC$? The sets of $\powerset \CC$ must be elements of $\CC$. Hence: $\powerset \CC \subseteq \CC$ Hence: $\card {\powerset \CC} \le \card \CC$ But by Cantor's Theorem: $\card {\powerset \CC} > \card \CC$

title: Cantor's Theorem
snippet: There is no surjection from a set $S$ to its power set for any set $S$. That is, $S$ is strictly smaller than its power set.

title: Cantor's Theorem (Strong Version)
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map {\PP^n} S$ be defined recursively by: $\map {\PP^n} S = \begin{cases} S & : n = 0 \\ \powerset {\map {\PP^{n - 1} } S} & : n > 0 \end{cases}$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then $S$ is not equivalent to $\map {\PP^n} S$ for any $n > 0$.

title: Cantor-Bernstein-Schröder Theorem
snippet: If a subset of one set is equivalent to the other, and a subset of the other is equivalent to the first, then the two sets are themselves equivalent: $\forall S, T: T \sim S_1 \subseteq S \land S \sim T_1 \subseteq T \implies S \sim T$ Alternatively, from Equivalence of Definitions of Dominate (Set Theory), this can be expressed as: $\forall S, T: T \preccurlyeq S \land S \preccurlyeq T \implies S \sim T$ where $T \preccurlyeq S$ denotes the fact that $S$ dominates $T$.

title: Cantor-Dedekind Hypothesis
snippet: The points on an infinite straight line are in one-to-one correspondence with the set $\R$ of real numbers. Hence the set of all points on an infinite straight line and $\R$ are equinumerous.

title: Cantor Distribution has Continuous CDF but no PDF
snippet: The Cantor distribution is an example of a probability distribution with a continuous cumulative distribution function, but has no probability density function.

snippet: == Examples of Cantor Function ==

title: Cantor Function is Differentiable Almost Everywhere
snippet: The Cantor function $C$ is differentiable almost everywhere on its domain $\closedint 0 1$. The derivative of $C$, where it exists, is $0$. $C$ is not differentiable only on the Cantor set.

title: Cantor Function is Everywhere Continuous
snippet: The Cantor function is continuous on its entire domain $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Cantor Function is Uniformly Continuous
snippet: The Cantor function is uniformly continuous on its entire domain $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Cantor Function is not Absolutely Continuous
snippet: The Cantor function is not absolutely continuous on its domain $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Cantor Pairing Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The Cantor pairing function is primitive recursive.

title: Cantor Pairing Function is Well-Defined
snippet: The Cantor pairing function is well-defined.

title: Cantor Set has Zero Lebesgue Measure
snippet: Let $\CC$ be the Cantor set. Let $\lambda$ denote the Lebesgue measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\map \BB \R$ on $\R$. Then $\CC$ is $\map \BB \R$-measurable, and $\map \lambda \CC = 0$. That is, $\CC$ is a $\lambda$-null set.

title: Cantor Set is Closed in Real Number Space
snippet: Let $\CC$ be the Cantor set. Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number space $\R$ under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\CC$ is a closed subset of $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$.

title: Cantor Set is Uncountable
snippet: The Cantor set $\CC$ is uncountable.

title: Cantor Space as Countably Infinite Product
snippet: Let $A_n = \struct {\set {0, 2}, \tau_n}$ be the discrete space of the two points $0$ and $2$. Let $\ds A = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n$. Let $\struct {A, \tau}$ be the product space where $\tau$ is the product topology on $A$. Then $A$ is homeomorphic to the Cantor space.

title: Cantor Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\CC$ be the Cantor set. Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number space $\R$ under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\CC$ is a compact subset of $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$.

title: Cantor Space is Complete Metric Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is a complete metric space.

title: Cantor Space is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is dense-in-itself.

title: Cantor Space is Meager in Closed Unit Interval
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is meager in $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Cantor Space is Non-Meager in Itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is non-meager in itself.

title: Cantor Space is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is nowhere dense in $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Cantor Space is Perfect
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $\CC$ is a perfect set of the real number space $\R$ under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$.

title: Cantor Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

title: Cantor Space is Totally Separated
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is totally separated.

title: Cantor Space is not Extremally Disconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is not extremally disconnected.

title: Cantor Space is not Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is not locally connected.

title: Cantor Space is not Scattered
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ is not scattered.

title: Cantor Space satisfies all Separation Axioms
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\CC, \tau_d}$ be the Cantor space. Then $T$ satisfies all the separation axioms.

title: Capelli's Sum
snippet: $\ds \paren {x + y}^{\overline n} = \sum_k \binom n k x^{\overline k} y^{\overline {n - k} }$ where: $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient $x^{\overline k}$ denotes $x$ to the $k$ rising.

snippet: == Examples of Capture-Recapture Sampling ==

title: Carathéodory's Theorem
snippet: Carathéodory's Theorem (Analysis) Carathéodory's Theorem (Convex Analysis) Carathéodory's Theorem (Measure Theory)

title: Carathéodory's Theorem (Analysis)
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$. Let $c \in I$ be an interior point of $I$. Let $f : I \to \R$ be a real function. Then $f$ is differentiable at $c$ : There exists a real function $\varphi : I \to \R$ that is continuous at $c$ and satisfies: $(1): \quad \forall x \in I: \map f x - \map f c = \map \varphi x \paren {x - c}$ $(2): \quad \map \varphi c = \map {f'} c$

title: Carathéodory's Theorem (Convex Analysis)
snippet: Let $E \subset \R^l$. Let $\mathbb x \in \map {\operatorname {conv} } E$, where $\map {\operatorname {conv} } E$ denotes the convex hull of $E$. Then $\mathbf x$ is a convex combination of affinely independent points of $E$. In particular, $\mathbf x$ is a convex combination of at most $l + 1$ points of $E$.

title: Carathéodory's Theorem (Measure Theory)
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\SS \subseteq \powerset X$ be a semi-ring of subsets of $X$. Let $\mu: \SS \to \overline \R$ be a pre-measure on $\SS$. Let $\map \sigma \SS$ be the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\SS$. Then $\mu$ extends to a measure $\mu^*$ on $\map \sigma \SS$.

title: Card Game with Bluffing is Completely Mixed Game
snippet: The game of cards with bluffing is a completely mixed game.

snippet: Let $P$ be the cubic equation: $a x^3 + b x^2 + c x + d = 0$ with $a \ne 0$ Then $P$ has solutions: {{eqn | l = x_1 | r = S + T - \dfrac b {3 a} }} {{eqn | l = x_2 | r = -\dfrac {S + T} 2 - \dfrac b {3 a} + \dfrac {i \sqrt 3} 2 \paren {S - T} }} {{eqn | l = x_3 | r = -\dfrac {S + T} 2 - \dfrac b {3 a} - \dfrac {i \sqrt 3} 2 \paren {S - T} }} where: {{eqn | l = S | r = \sqrt [3] {R + \sqrt {Q^3 + R^2} } }} {{eqn | l = T | r = \sqrt [3] {R - \sqrt {Q^3 + R^2} } }} where: {{eqn | l = Q | r = \dfrac {3 a c - b^2} {9 a^2} }} {{eqn | l = R | r = \dfrac {9 a b c - 27 a^2 d - 2 b^3} {54 a^3} }} The…

title: Cardinal Equal to Collection of All Dominated Ordinals
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\preccurlyeq$ denote the dominance relation. Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $x = \set {y \in \On: y \preccurlyeq S}$ Then:

title: Cardinal Inequality implies Ordinal Inequality
snippet: Let $T$ be a set. Let $\card T$ denote the cardinal number of $T$. Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $x < \card T \iff \card x < \card T$

title: Cardinal Number Equivalence or Equal to Universe
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Let $\mathbb U$ denote the universal class. Then: $S \sim \card S \lor \card S = \mathbb U$

title: Cardinal Number Less than Ordinal
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Let $x$ be an ordinal such that $S \sim x$. Then: $\card S \le x$

title: Cardinal Number Plus One Less than Cardinal Product
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal such that $x > 1$. Then: $\card {x + 1} \le \card {x \times x}$ Where $\times$ denotes the Cartesian product.

title: Cardinal Number is Ordinal
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $S \sim x$ for some ordinal $x$. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinality of $S$. Then: $\card S \in \On$ where $\On$ denotes the class of all ordinals.

title: Cardinal One is Cancellable for Cardinal Sum
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a + \mathbf 1 = \mathbf b + \mathbf 1 \implies \mathbf a = \mathbf b$ where $\mathbf 1$ is (cardinal) one.

title: Cardinal Product Distributes over Cardinal Sum
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \paren {\mathbf b + \mathbf c} = \mathbf a \mathbf b + \mathbf a \mathbf c$ where: $\mathbf a + \mathbf b$ denotes the sum of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$. $\mathbf a \mathbf b$ denotes the product of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$.

title: Cardinal Product Equal to Maximum
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets that are equinumerous to their cardinal number. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Suppose $S$ is infinite. Suppose $T > 0$. Then: $\card {S \times T} = \map \max {\card S, \card T}$

title: Cardinal Product Equinumerous to Ordinal Product
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets that are equivalent to their cardinal numbers. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Let $\cdot$ denote ordinal multiplication and let $\times$ denote the Cartesian product. Then: $S \times T \sim \card S \cdot \card T$

title: Cardinal Zero is Less than Cardinal One
snippet: The zero cardinal $0$ is less than one: $0 < 1$

title: Cardinal of Cardinal Equal to Cardinal
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $S$ is equivalent to its cardinal. If the axiom of choice holds, then this condition holds for any set. Then: $\card {\paren {\card S} } = \card S$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinal number of $S$.

title: Cardinal of Finite Ordinal
snippet: Let $n$ be a finite ordinal. Let $\card n$ denote the cardinal number of $n$. Then: $\card n = n$

title: Cardinal of Union Equal to Maximum
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets that are equinumerous to their cardinal number. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Suppose $S$ is infinite. Then: $\card {S \cup T} = \map \max {\card S, \card T}$

title: Cardinal of Union Less than Cardinal of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets that are equivalent to their cardinal numbers. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Let $\card S > 1$ and $\card T > 1$. Then: $\card {S \cup T} \le \card {S \times T}$

title: Cardinalities form Inequality implies Difference is Nonempty
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $\card X < \card Y$ where $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$. Then: $Y \setminus X \ne \O$

title: Cardinality/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cardinality ==

title: Cardinality Less One
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let: $\card S = n + 1$ where $\card S$ is the cardinality of $S$. Let $a \in S$. Then: $\card {S \setminus \set a} = n$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Cardinality is Additive Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. The function $C: \powerset S \to \R$, where $C$ is defined as the cardinality of a set, is an additive function.

title: Cardinality of Basis of Sorgenfrey Line not greater than Continuum
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the Sorgenfrey line. Let $\BB = \set {\hointr x y: x, y \in \R \land x < y}$ be the basis of $T$. Then $\card \BB \le \mathfrak c$ where $\card \BB$ denotes the cardinality of $\BB$ $\mathfrak c = \card \R$ denotes the continuum.

title: Cardinality of Cartesian Product of Finite Sets
snippet: Let $S \times T$ be the cartesian product of two finite sets $S$ and $T$. Then: $\card {S \times T} = \card S \times \card T$ where $\card S$ denotes cardinality. This is convenient, given the symbology.

title: Cardinality of Codomain of Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let: $\card S = n$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$. Let $f: S \to T$ be a surjection. Then $\card T \le n$. The equality: $\card T = n$ occurs $f$ is a bijection.

title: Cardinality of Complement
snippet: Let $T \subseteq S$ such that $\card S = n, \card T = m$. Then: $\card {\relcomp S T} = \card {S \setminus T} = n - m$ where: $\relcomp S T$ denotes the complement of $T$ relative to $S$ $S \setminus T$ denotes the difference between $S$ and $T$.

title: Cardinality of Conjugacy Class is Divisor of Order of Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. For $x \in G$, let $\conjclass x$ denote the conjugacy class of $x$. Then the cardinality of $\conjclass x$ is a divisor of the order of $G$.

title: Cardinality of Empty Set
snippet: $\card S = 0 \iff S = \O$ That is, the empty set is finite, and has a cardinality of zero.

title: Cardinality of Even and Odd Permutations on Finite Set
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$ be a natural number greater than $0$. Let $S$ be a set of cardinality $n$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $S$ of order $n$. Let $R_e$ and $R_o$ denote the subsets of $S_n$ consisting of even permutations and odd permutations respectively. Then the cardinality of both $R_e$ and $R_o$ is $\dfrac {n!} 2$.

title: Cardinality of Extensions of Function on Subset of Finite Set
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $S$ be a set with $m$ elements. Let $T$ be a set with $n$ elements. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$ with $r$ elements where $0 \le r < m$. Let $f: A \to T$ be a mapping. Then there are $n^{m - r}$ distinct extensions of $f$ to $S$.

title: Cardinality of Finite Set is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Then there is a unique natural number $n$ such that $S \sim \N_n$, where: $\sim$ represents set equivalence and: $\N_n = \set {0, 1, \dotsc, n - 1}$ is the initial segment of $\N$ determined by $n$.

title: Cardinality of Finite Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a Galois field. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space. Let the dimension of $V$ be finite. Then: $\size V = \size K^{\map \dim V}$

title: Cardinality of Generator of Vector Space is not Less than Dimension
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$. Let $\BB$ be a generator for $V$ containing $m$ elements. Then: $\map {\dim_F} V \le m$ where $\map {\dim_F} V$ is the dimension of $V$.

title: Cardinality of Image of Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \rightarrowtail T$ be an injection. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a finite subset of $S$. Then: $\card {f \paren A} = \card A$ where $\card A$ denotes the cardinality of $A$.

title: Cardinality of Image of Mapping not greater than Cardinality of Domain
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Then: $\card {\Img f} \le \card S$

title: Cardinality of Image of Mapping of Intersections is not greater than Weight of Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f: X \to \tau$ be a mapping such that: $\forall x \in X: \paren {x \in \map f x \land \forall U \in \tau: x \in U \implies \map f x \subseteq U}$ Then the cardinality of the image of $f$ is no greater than the weight of $T$: $\card {\Img f} \le \map w T$

title: Cardinality of Image of Set not greater than Cardinality of Set
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $A$ be a subset of $X$. Then: $\card {\map {f^\to} A} \le \card A$ where $\card A$ denotes the cardinality of $A$.

title: Cardinality of Infinite Sigma-Algebra is at Least Cardinality of Continuum
snippet: Let $\MM$ be an infinite $\sigma$-algebra on a set $X$. Then $\MM$ is has cardinality at least that of the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$: $\map \Card \MM \ge \mathfrak c$

title: Cardinality of Infinite Union of Infinite Sets
snippet: Let $\kappa$ be an infinite cardinal. Let $X_i$ be sets of cardinality at most $\kappa$ indexed by a set $I$ of cardinality at most $\kappa$. Then their union $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ has cardinality at most $\kappa$. Furthermore, if at least one of the $X_i$ is size $\kappa$, then the union has cardinality $\kappa$.

title: Cardinality of Integer Interval
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right]$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Then $\left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right]$ is finite and its cardinality equals: $\begin{cases} b - a + 1 & : b \ge a - 1 \\ 0 & : b \le a - 1 \end{cases}$

title: Cardinality of Linearly Independent Set is No Greater than Dimension
snippet: Let $E$ be a vector space of $n$ dimensions. Let $H$ be a linearly independent subset of $E$. Then: $H$ has at most $n$ elements.

title: Cardinality of Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set whose cardinality is $n$: $\card S = n$ Let $T$ be a non-empty set Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\card f = n$

title: Cardinality of Master Code
snippet: Let $\map V {n, p}$ be a master code of length $n$ modulo $p$. Then there are $p^n$ elements of $\map V {n, p}$.

title: Cardinality of Maximal Independent Subset Equals Rank of Set
snippet: Let $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $X$ be a maximal independent subset of $A$. Then: $\card X = \map \rho A$ where $\rho$ is the rank function on $M$.

title: Cardinality of Power Set is Invariant
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $\card X = \card Y$ where $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$. Then: $\card {\powerset X} = \card {\powerset Y}$ where $\powerset X$ denotes the power set of $X$.

title: Cardinality of Power Set of Finite Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that: $\card S = n$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$, Then: $\card {\powerset S} = 2^n$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Thus it can be seen that the power set's alternative notation $2^S$ is indeed appropriate. However, because of possible confusion over the conventional meaning of $2^n$, its use is deprecated.

title: Cardinality of Power Set of Natural Numbers Equals Cardinality of Real Numbers
snippet: The cardinality of the power set of the natural numbers is equal to the cardinality of the real numbers. $\card {2^\N} = \card \R$

title: Cardinality of Proper Subset of Finite Set
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets such that $A \subsetneqq B$. Let $\card B = n$, where $\card {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality. Then $\card A < n$.

title: Cardinality of Reduced Residue System
snippet: Let $n \ge 2$. Let $\Z'_n$ be the reduced residue system modulo $n$. Then: $\card {\Z'_n} = \map \phi n$ where $\map \phi n$ is the Euler phi function.

title: Cardinality of Set Difference
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $T$ is finite. Then: $\card {S \setminus T} = \card S - \card {S \cap T}$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Cardinality of Set Difference with Subset
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $T$ is finite. Let $T \subseteq S$. Then: $\card {S \setminus T} = \card S - \card T$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Cardinality of Set is Finite iff Set is Finite
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. $\card A$ is finite $A$ is finite where $\card A$ denotes the cardinality of $A$.

title: Cardinality of Set is Topological Property
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. The cardinality of $S$ is a topological property of $T$.

title: Cardinality of Set less than Cardinality of Power Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Then: $\card X < \card {\powerset X}$ where $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$, $\powerset X$ denotes the power set of $X$.

title: Cardinality of Set of All Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. The cardinality of the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$ (that is, the total number of mappings from $S$ to $T$) is: $\card {T^S} = \card T^{\card S}$

title: Cardinality of Set of All Mappings from Empty Set
snippet: Let $T$ be a set. Let $T^\O$ denote the set of all mappings from $\O$ to $S$. Then: $\card {T^\O} = 1$ where $\card {T^\O}$ denotes the cardinality of $\O^S$.

title: Cardinality of Set of All Mappings to Empty Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\O^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $\O$. Then: $\card {\O^S} = \begin{cases} 1 & : S = \O \\ 0 & : S \ne \O \end{cases}$ where $\card {\O^S}$ denotes the cardinality of $\O^S$.

title: Cardinality of Set of Bijections
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets with the same cardinality: $\size S = \size T = n$ Then there are $n!$ bijections from $S$ to $T$.

title: Cardinality of Set of Characteristic Functions on Finite Set
snippet: Let $I$ be a finite set. The number of characteristic functions on $I$ is: $2^{\card I}$ where $\card I$ denotes the cardinality of $I$.

title: Cardinality of Set of Combinations with Repetition
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set with $n$ elements The number of $k$-combinations of $S$ with repetition is given by: $N = \dbinom {n + k - 1} k$

title: Cardinality of Set of Endorelations
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\card S = n$, where $\card {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality (that is, the number of elements). Let $\RR$ denote the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the cardinality of $\RR$ is given by: $\card \RR = 2^{\paren {n^2} }$

title: Cardinality of Set of Induced Equivalence Classes of Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S \times S$ be the relation induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $f$ be an injection. Then there are $\card S$ different $\RR_f$-classes.

title: Cardinality of Set of Induced Equivalence Classes of Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S \times S$ be the relation induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $f$ be a surjection. Then there are $\card T$ different $\RR_f$-classes.

title: Cardinality of Set of Injections
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. The number of injections from $S$ to $T$, where $\card S = m, \card T = n$ is often denoted ${}^m P_n$, and is: ${}^m P_n = \begin {cases} \dfrac {n!} {\paren {n - m}!} & : m \le n \\ 0 & : m > n \end {cases}$

title: Cardinality of Set of Relations
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $\card S = n$ and $\card T = m$, where $\card {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality (that is, the number of elements). Let $\RR$ denote the set of all relations from $S$ to $T$. Then the cardinality of $\RR$ is given by: $\card \RR = 2^{n m}$

title: Cardinality of Set of Residue Classes
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of residue classes modulo $m$. Then: $\card {Z_m} = m$ where $\card {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality.

title: Cardinality of Set of Restrictions of Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the cardinality of $S$ be $n$. Let $F$ be the set of restrictions of $f$ to a subset of $S$. Then there are $2^n$ elements of $F$.

title: Cardinality of Set of Self-Mappings on Finite Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let the cardinality of $S$ be $n$. The cardinality of the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself (that is, the total number of self-maps on $S$) is: $\card {S^S} = n^n$

title: Cardinality of Set of Singletons
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T = \set {\set x: x \in S}$ be the set of all singletons of elements of $S$. Then: $\card T = \card S$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Cardinality of Set of Strictly Increasing Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ be tosets. Let the cardinality of $S$ and $T$ be: $\card S = m, \card T = n$ Then the number of strictly increasing mappings from $S$ to $T$ is: $\dbinom n m = \dfrac {n!} {m! \ \paren {n - m}!}$. where $\dbinom n m$ is a binomial coefficient.

title: Cardinality of Set of Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $\card S = n$. Let $m \le n$. Then the number of subsets $T$ of $S$ such that $\card T = m$ is: $\dbinom n m = \dfrac {n!} {m! \paren {n - m}!}$

title: Cardinality of Set of Surjections
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $\card S = m, \card T = n$. Let $C$ be the number of surjections from $S$ to $T$. Then: $C = n! \ds {m \brace n}$ where $\ds {m \brace n}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Cardinality of Singleton
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Then $\card A = 1$ $\exists a: A = \set a$ where $\card A$ denotes the cardinality of $A$.

title: Cardinality of Subset Relation on Power Set of Finite Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that: $\card S = n$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$. From Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering we have that $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set. The cardinality of $\subseteq$ as a relation is $3^n$.

title: Cardinality of Subset of Finite Set
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be finite sets such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $\card B = n$ where $\card {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes cardinality. Then $\card A \le n$.

title: Cardinality of Union not greater than Product
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a set of sets. Let: $\size \FF \le \mathbf m$ where $\size \FF$ denotes the cardinality of $\FF$ $\mathbf m$ is cardinal number (possibly infinite). Let: $\forall A \in \FF: \size A \le \mathbf n$ where $\mathbf n$ is cardinal number (possibly infinite). Then: $\ds \size {\bigcup \FF} \le \size {\mathbf m \times \mathbf n} = \mathbf m \mathbf n$

title: Cardinals are Totally Ordered
snippet: == Corollary to Zermelo's Theorem == Every set of cardinals is totally ordered under $\le$.

title: Cardinals form Equivalence Classes
snippet: Let $\map \Card S$ denote the cardinal of the set $S$. Then $\map \Card S$ induces an equivalence class which contains all sets which have the same cardinality as $S$.

title: Cardioid is Special Case of Pascal's Snail
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle of diameter $a$ with a distinguished point $O$ on the circumference. Let $OQ$ be a chord of $C$. Let $\LL$ be a limaçon of Pascal defined as the locus of points $P$ in the plane such that: $PQ = b$ where: $OPQ$ is a straight line $b$ is a real constant. Let $a = b$. Then $\LL$ is a cardioid

title: Carmichael's Theorem
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n > 12$. Then the $n$th Fibonacci number $F_n$ has at least one prime factor which does not divide any smaller Fibonacci number. The exceptions for $n \le 12$ are: $F_1 = 1, F_2 = 1$: neither have any prime factors $F_6 = 8$ whose only prime factor is $2$ which is $F_3$ $F_{12} = 144$ whose only prime factors are $2$ (which is $F_3$) and $3$ (which is $F_4$).

title: Carmichael Number/Examples

title: Carmichael Number/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of Carmichael numbers begins: $561, 1105, 1729, 2465, 2821, 6601, 8911, 10585, 15841, \ldots$

title: Carmichael Number has 3 Odd Prime Factors
snippet: Let $n$ be a Carmichael number. Then $n$ has at least $3$ distinct odd prime factors.

title: Carmichael Number with 4 Prime Factors
snippet: $41 \, 041$ is the smallest Carmichael number with $4$ prime factors: $41 \, 041 = 7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 41$

title: Carnot's Theorem
snippet: All reversible heat engines operating between the same temperatures are equally efficient.

title: Cartan-Hadamard Theorem
snippet: Let $M$ be a complete connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Suppose all sectional curvatures of $M$ are less than or equal to zero. Then the universal covering space of $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\R^n$.

title: Cartan Subalgebra as Maximal Abelian Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional, semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field. Let $\mathfrak h \subset \mathfrak g$ be a Lie subalgebra. $\mathfrak h$ is a Cartan subalgebra of $\mathfrak{g}$ : {{axiom | n = 2 | t = $\forall H \in \mathfrak h$, the adjoint representation $\operatorname {ad}_H: \mathfrak g \to \mathfrak g$ is diagonalizable}}

title: Cartesian Equation of Conchoid of Nicomedes
snippet: Let $a \in \R$, $b \in \R_{>0}$ be real constants. Let the focus point of a conchoid of Nicomedes $\KK$ be located at the origin of a Cartesian plane. Let the directrix of $\KK$ be the straight line $x = a$. Then $\KK$ can be expressed in Cartesian coordinates as: $\paren {x - a}^2 \paren {x^2 + y^2} = b^2 x^2$

snippet: The cartesian equation of the Witch of Agnesi can also be seen presented as: $x^2 y = 4 a^2 \paren {2 a - y}$ Some sources present the curve with the $y$-axis as the asymptote: $x y^2 = 4 a^2 \paren {2 a - x}$

title: Cartesian Form of Discrete Moment of Inertia
snippet: Let $B$ be a rigid body which is rotating in space about some axis $\LL$. Let $B$ be embedded in Cartesian $3$-space whose origin lies on $\LL$. Let $I_{xx}$, $I_{yy}$, and $I_{zz}$ be the moments of inertia of $B$ about the coordinate axes $\mathbf O x$, $\mathbf O y$ and $\mathbf O z$ respectively. Let $B$ be composed of a countable number of particles $P_1, P_2, \ldots$ such that: each $P_i$ has mass $m_i$ each $P_i$ has perpendicular distance $r_i$ from $\LL$. each $P_i$ has coordinates $\tuple {x_i, y_i, z_i}$.

snippet: Let $B$ be a rigid body which is rotating in space about some axis $\LL$. Let $B$ be embedded in Cartesian $3$-space whose origin lies on $\LL$. Let $I_{xx}$, $I_{yy}$, and $I_{zz}$ be the moments of inertia of $B$ about the coordinate axes $\mathbf O x$, $\mathbf O y$ and $\mathbf O z$ respectively. title: Cartesian Metric is Rotation Invariant
snippet: The cartesian metric does not change under rotation.

Let $\CC'$ denote the Cartesian plane in its new position. Let $\mathbf r$ be kept fixed during this rotation. Let $\tuple {x, y}$ denote the components of $\mathbf r$ $\CC$.
