title: Cartesian Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cartesian Products ==

title: Cartesian Product Distributes over Set Difference
snippet: Cartesian product is distributive over set difference: $(1): \quad S \times \paren {T_1 \setminus T_2} = \paren {S \times T_1} \setminus \paren {S \times T_2}$ $(2): \quad \paren {T_1 \setminus T_2} \times S = \paren {T_1 \times S} \setminus \paren {T_2 \times S}$

title: Cartesian Product Distributes over Union
snippet: Cartesian product is distributive over union: $A \times \paren {B \cup C} = \paren {A \times B} \cup \paren {A \times C}$ $\paren {B \cup C} \times A = \paren {B \times A} \cup \paren {C \times A}$

title: Cartesian Product Exists and is Unique
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $A \times B$ be the cartesian product of $A$ and $B$. Then $A \times B$ exists and is unique.

title: Cartesian Product Preserves Cardinality
snippet: Let $R$, $S$, and $T$ be sets. Suppose that $S$ is equivalent to $T$. Then: $R \times S \sim R \times T$ $S \times R \sim T \times R$

title: Cartesian Product is Anticommutative
snippet: Let $S, T \ne \O$. Then: $S \times T = T \times S \iff S = T$

title: Cartesian Product is Empty iff Factor is Empty
snippet: $S \times T = \O \iff S = \O \lor T = \O$ Thus: $S \times \O = \O = \O \times T$

title: Cartesian Product is Set Product
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $S \times T$ be the Cartesian product of $S$ and $T$. Let $\pr_1: S \times T \to S$ and $\pr_2: S \times T \to T$ be the first and second projections respectively on $S \times T$. Then $\struct {S \times T, \pr_1, \pr_2}$ is a set product.

title: Cartesian Product is Small
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be small classes. Then their Cartesian product $a \times b$ is small: $\map {\MM} {a \times b}$

title: Cartesian Product is Small iff Inverse is Small
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Then the Cartesian product $A \times B$ is a small class $B \times A$ is small.

title: Cartesian Product is Unique
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. If there exists a cartesian product of $A$ and $B$, then it is unique.

title: Cartesian Product is not Associative
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Then: $A \times \paren {B \times C} \ne \paren {A \times B} \times C$ where $A \times B$ is the cartesian product of $A$ and $B$.

title: Cartesian Product of Bijections is Bijection
snippet: Let $S_1 \times S_2$ be the Cartesian product of two sets $S_1$ and $S_2$. Let $T_1 \times T_2$ be the Cartesian product of two sets $T_1$ and $T_2$. Let $f_1: S_1 \to T_1$ and $f_2: S_2 \to T_2$ be bijections. Let $f_1 \times f_2: S_1 \times S_2 \to T_1 \times T_2$ be the Cartesian product of $f_1$ and $f_2$ defined as: $\forall \left({s_1, s_2}\right) \in S_1 \times S_2: f_1 \times f_2 \left({s_1, s_2}\right) := \left({f_1 \left({s_1}\right), f_2 \left({s_2}\right)}\right)$ Then $f_1 \times f_2$ is a bijection.

title: Cartesian Product of Convex Sets is Convex in Direct Product
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\family {X_\alpha}_{\alpha \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of vector spaces over $\GF$. Let: $\ds X = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} X_\alpha$ be the direct product of $\family {X_\alpha}_{\alpha \in I}$. For each $\alpha \in I$, let $C_\alpha \subseteq X_\alpha$ be a non-empty convex set. Let: $\ds C = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} C_\alpha$ Then: $C$ is a convex set.

title: Cartesian Product of Countable Sets is Countable
snippet: The cartesian product of two countable sets is countable.

title: Cartesian Product of Equivalence Relations
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be equivalence relations on $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $\TT$ be the relation on $A \times B$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {u, v}, \tuple {x, y} \in A \times B: \tuple {u, v} \mathrel \TT \tuple {x, y} \iff u \mathrel \RR x \land v \mathrel \SS y$ Then $\TT$ is an equivalence relation on $A \times B$. The equivalence class $\eqclass {\tuple {a, b} } \TT$ of an element $\tuple {a, b}$ of $\TT$ is: $\eqclass {\tuple {a, b} } \TT = \set {\tuple {x, y}: x \in \eqclass a \RR, y \in \eqclass b \SS}$

title: Cartesian Product of Family/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cartesian Products of Families ==

title: Cartesian Product of Group Actions
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $*_S: G \times S \to S$ and $*_T: G \times T \to T$ be group actions. Then the operation $*: G \times \paren {S \times T} \to S \times T$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {g, \tuple {s, t} } \in G \times \paren {S \times T}: g * \tuple {s, t} = \tuple {g *_S s, g *_T t}$ is a group action.

title: Cartesian Product of Homeomorphisms is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $f_1: S_1 \to T_1$ and $f_2: S_2 \to T_2$ be mappings. Let: $f_1 \times f_2: S_1 \times S_2 \to T_1 \times T_2$ be defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in S_1 \times S_2: \map {\paren {f_1 \times f_2} } {x, y} = \tuple {\map {f_1} x, \map {f_2} y}$ where $S_1 \times S_2$ denotes the product space of $S_1$ and $S_2$, and similarly for $T_1 \times T_2$. Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be homeomorphisms. Then $f_1 \times f_2$ is also a homeomorphism.

title: Cartesian Product of Infinite Set Equivalent to Itself implies Axiom of Choice
snippet: Suppose that, for every Dedekind-infinite set $A$, it holds that: $A \sim A \times A$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence, and $\times$ denotes the cartesian product. Then, the holds.

title: Cartesian Product of Intersections
snippet: $\paren {S_1 \cap S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cap T_2} = \paren {S_1 \times T_1} \cap \paren {S_2 \times T_2}$ where $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ are sets.

title: Cartesian Product of Intervals is Convex Set
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. For all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$, let $\Bbb I_k$ be a real interval of any of the real interval types. Then the cartesian product $\Bbb I_1 \times \ldots \times \Bbb I_n$ is a convex set.

title: Cartesian Product of Intervals is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. For all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$, let $\Bbb I_k$ be a real interval of any of the real interval types. Let $\tau_0$ denote the subspace topology on the cartesian product $\Bbb I_1 \times \ldots \times \Bbb I_n$, induced by the Euclidean topology on $\R^n$. Then $\struct {\Bbb I_1 \times \ldots \times \Bbb I_n, \tau_0}$ is simply connected.

title: Cartesian Product of Mappings is Continuous iff Factor Mappings are Continuous
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $f_1: S_1 \to T_1$ and $f_2: S_2 \to T_2$ be mappings. Let: $f_1 \times f_2: S_1 \times S_2 \to T_1 \times T_2$ be defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in S_1 \times S_2: \map {\paren {f_1 \times f_2} } {x, y} = \tuple {\map {f_1} x, \map {f_2} y}$ where $S_1 \times S_2$ denotes the product space of $S_1$ and $S_2$, and similarly for $T_1 \times T_2$. Then: $f_1 \times f_2$ is continuous both $f_1$ and $f_2$ are continuous.

title: Cartesian Product of Natural Numbers with Itself is Countable
snippet: The Cartesian product $\N \times \N$ of the set of natural numbers $\N$ with itself is countable.

title: Cartesian Product of Open Ordinal Space with Uncountable Cartesian Product of Closed Unit Interval is Countably Compact Space
snippet: Let $T = \Bbb I^\Bbb I$ be the cartesian product of the open ordinal space with the uncountable cartesian product of the closed unit interval. Then $T$ is a countably compact space.

title: Cartesian Product of Open Ordinal Space with Uncountable Cartesian Product of Closed Unit Interval is not Compact Space
snippet: Let $T = \Bbb I^\Bbb I$ be the cartesian product of the open ordinal space with the uncountable cartesian product of the closed unit interval. Then $T$ is not a compact space.

title: Cartesian Product of Open Ordinal Space with Uncountable Cartesian Product of Closed Unit Interval is not Sequentially Compact Space
snippet: Let $T = \Bbb I^\Bbb I$ be the cartesian product of the open ordinal space with the uncountable cartesian product of the closed unit interval. Then $T$ is not a sequentially compact space.

title: Cartesian Product of Preimage with Image of Relation is Correspondence
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then the restriction of $\RR$ to $\Preimg \RR \times \Img \RR$ is a correspondence.

title: Cartesian Product of Projections is Projection on Cartesian Product of Mappings
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {S_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ and $\family {T_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be families of sets both indexed by $I$. For each $\alpha \in I$, let $f_\alpha: S_\alpha \to T_\alpha$ be a mapping. There exists a unique mapping: $\ds f: \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha \to \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} T_\alpha$ such that: $\forall \alpha \in I: \pr_\alpha \circ f = f_\alpha \circ \pr_\alpha$ where: $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings $\pr_\alpha$ denotes the $\alpha$th projection on either $\ds \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha$ or $\ds…

title: Cartesian Product of Semirings of Sets
snippet: Let $\SS$ and $\TT$ be semirings of sets. Then $\SS \times \TT$ is also a semiring of sets. Here, $\times$ denotes Cartesian product.

title: Cartesian Product of Sets is Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $A$ and $B$ be sets in $V$. Then their cartesian product $A \times B$ is also a set.

title: Cartesian Product of Subsets
snippet: Let $A, B, S, T$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B$ and $S \subseteq T$. Then: $A \times S \subseteq B \times T$ In addition, if $A, S \ne \O$, then: $A \times S \subseteq B \times T \iff A \subseteq B \land S \subseteq T$

title: Cartesian Product of Unions
snippet: $\paren {A \cup B} \times \paren {C \cup D} = \paren {A \times C} \cup \paren {B \times D} \cup \paren {A \times D} \cup \paren {B \times C}$

title: Cartesian Product under Chebyshev Distance of Continuous Mappings between Metric Spaces is Continuous
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}, \ldots, M_n = \struct {A_n, d_n}$ be metric spaces. Let $N_1 = \struct {B_1, d'_1}, N_2 = \struct {B_2, d'_2}, \ldots, N_n = \struct {B_n, d'_n}$ be metric spaces. Let $f_i: M_i \to N_i$ be continuous mappings for all $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Let $\ds \MM = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n M_i$ be the cartesian product of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$. Let $\ds \NN = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n N_i$ be the cartesian product of $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_n$.

title: Cartesian Product with Complement
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$ and $B \subseteq T$ be subsets of $S$ and $T$, respectively. Let $\relcomp S A$ denote the relative complement of $A$ in $S$. Then: {{eqn | l = \relcomp S A \times T | r = \relcomp {S \times T} {A \times T} }} {{eqn | l = S \times \relcomp T B | r = \relcomp {S \times T} {S \times B} }}

title: Cartesian Product with Proper Class is Proper Class
snippet: Let $A$ be a proper class. Let $B$ be a class which is not empty. Then the Cartesian product $\paren {A \times B}$ is a proper class.

title: Cartesian Space of Topological Field is Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $K^n$ be the cartesian $n$-th power of $K$, defining scalar multiplication and vector addition component-wise. Equip $K^n$ with the product topology given by $K$. Then $K^n$ is a topological vector space. Further, if $K$ is a Hausdorff topological field, then $K^n$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space.

title: Cassini's Identity
snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: $F_{n + 1} F_{n - 1} - F_n^2 = \paren {-1}^n$

title: Casting Out Nines
snippet: == Proof Technique == Casting out nines is a technique for checking that the result of an addition sum is correct. Let $a$ and $b$ be two integers for which their sum: $c = a + b$ is to be calculated. For each of $a$ and $b$, expressed in conventional decimal notation, the digital root is extracted. These are added together, and the digital root of the result is extracted. During this process, any occurrences of the digit $9$ can be cast out, as they have no effect on the digital root.

title: Catalan's Conjecture
snippet: The only solution to the Diophantine equation: $x^a - y^b = 1$ for $a, b > 1$ and $x, y > 0$, is: $x = 3, a = 2, y = 2, b = 3$

title: Catalan's Identity
snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: ${F_n}^2 - F_{n - r} F_{n + r} = \left({-1}\right)^{n - r} {F_r}^2$

title: Catalan-Dickson Conjecture
snippet: == Unproven Conjecture == It has been conjectured that all aliquot sequences are bounded. That is, all aliquot sequences end in one of the following ways: $(1): \quad$ It reaches $1$, the previous term being a prime number $(2): \quad$ It reaches a perfect number $(3): \quad$ It reaches a sociable chain, which may or may not be an amicable pair. However, this is not known for certain.

title: Catalan Number/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence of Catalan Numbers == The sequence of Catalan numbers begins: $(1,) \, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, 429, 1430, 4862, \ldots$ where the inclusion or not of the initial $1$ depends on whether $n$ starts from $0$ or $1$.

title: Categories of Elements of Ring
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a ring. The elements of $R$ are partitioned into three classes: $(1): \quad$ the zero $(2): \quad$ the units $(3): \quad$ the proper elements.

title: Categories of Elements under Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be a well-ordering on $A$. Let $x \in A$ be an element of $A$. Then $x$ falls into one of the following $3$ categories: $(1): \quad x$ is the smallest element of $A$ $\preccurlyeq$ $(2): \quad x$ is the immediate successor of another element $y \in A$ $\preccurlyeq$ $(3): \quad x$ is a limit element of $A$ under $\preccurlyeq$.

snippet: Let $\mathbf{OrdSet}$ be the category of ordered sets. Then $\mathbf{OrdSet}$ is Cartesian closed.

title: Category of Ordered Sets is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{OrdSet}$ be the category of ordered sets. Then $\mathbf{OrdSet}$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Pointed Sets as Coslice Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}_*$ be the category of pointed sets. Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $1 := \left\{{*}\right\}$ be any singleton. Then: $\mathbf{Set}_* \cong 1 \mathbin / \mathbf{Set}$ where $1 \mathbin / \mathbf{Set}$ denotes the coslice of $\mathbf{Set}$ under $1$ and $\cong$ signifies isomorphic categories.

title: Category of Pointed Sets is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}_*$ be the category of pointed sets. Then $\mathbf{Set}_*$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Relations is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Rel}$ be the category of relations. Then $\mathbf{Rel}$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Semilattices is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{SLat}$ denote the category of semilattices. Then: $\mathbf{SLat}$ is a metacategory

title: Category of Sets is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Then $\mathbf{Set}$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Subobject Classes is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf C} } C$ be the category of subobject classes of $C$. $g \circ f : X \to Z$ called the composition of $f$ and $g$. Then $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf C} } C$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Subobject Classes is Order Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\overline{\mathbf{Sub}}_{\mathbf C} \left({C}\right)$ be the category of subobject classes of $C$. Then $\overline{\mathbf{Sub}}_{\mathbf C} \left({C}\right)$ is an order category.

title: Category of Subobjects is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\map {\mathbf{Sub}_{\mathbf C}} C$ be the category of subobjects of $C$. Then $\map {\mathbf{Sub}_{\mathbf C}} C$ is a metacategory.

title: Category of Subobjects is Preorder Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\map {\mathbf{Sub}_{\mathbf C} } C$ be the category of subobjects of $C$. Then $\map {\mathbf{Sub}_{\mathbf C} } C$ is a preorder category.

title: Category of Vector Spaces is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Vect}$ be the category of vector spaces. Then $\mathbf{Vect}$ is a metacategory.

title: Catenary is Symmetric about Y-Axis
snippet: Consider a catenary $\CC$. Let a cartesian plane be arranged so that the $y$-axis passes through the lowest point of the catenary. $\CC$ exhibits reflectional symmetry in that $y$-axis.

title: Catenoid is Only Minimal Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a surface of revolution. Let $\SS$ be a minimal surface. Then $\SS$ is a catenoid. That is, the only minimal surface of revolution is the catenoid.

title: Catesian Product of Open Real Intervals is Open in Real Number Plane
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d}$ denote the real number plane with the Euclidean metric. Let $\openint a b$ and $\openint c d$ be open real intervals. Then their Cartesian product: $S = \openint a b \times \openint c d$ is an open set of $\struct {\R^2, d}$.

title: Cauchy's Convergence Criterion for Series
snippet: A series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^\infty a_i$ is convergent for every $\epsilon > 0$ there is a number $N \in \N$ such that: $\size {a_{n + 1} + a_{n + 2} + \cdots + a_m} n$. {{explain|What domain is $\sequence {a_n}$ in?}}

title: Cauchy's Group Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group whose identity is $e$. Let $p$ be a prime number which divides the order of $G$. Then $G$ has a subgroup of order $p$.

title: Cauchy's Inequality
snippet: $\ds \sum {r_i}^2 \sum {s_i}^2 \ge \paren {\sum {r_i s_i} }^2$ where all of $r_i, s_i \in \R$.

title: Cauchy's Integral Formula
snippet: Let $D = \set {z \in \C: \cmod z \le r}$ be the closed disk of radius $r$ in $\C$. Let $f: U \to \C$ be holomorphic on some open set containing $D$. Then for each $a$ in the interior of $D$: $\ds \map f a = \frac 1 {2 \pi i} \oint_{\partial D} \frac {\map f z} {z - a} \rd z$ where $\partial D$ is the boundary of $D$, and is traversed anticlockwise.

title: Cauchy's Lemma
snippet: Cauchy's Lemma (Group Theory) Cauchy's Lemma (Number Theory) Category:Named Theorems/Cauchy

title: Cauchy's Lemma (Group Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group of finite order whose identity is $e$. Let $p$ be a prime number which divides the order of $G$. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ has an element of order $p$.

title: Cauchy's Lemma (Number Theory)
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be odd positive integers. Suppose $a$ and $b$ satisfy: Then there exist non-negative integers $s, t, u, v$ such that:

title: Cauchy's Mean Theorem
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R$ be real numbers which are all positive. Let $A_n$ be the arithmetic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Let $G_n$ be the geometric mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $A_n \ge G_n$ with equality holding : $\forall i, j \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: x_i = x_j$ That is, all terms are equal.

title: Cauchy's Residue Theorem
snippet: Let $U$ be a simply connected open subset of the complex plane $\C$. Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be finitely many points of $U$. Let $f: U \to \C$ be analytic in $U \setminus \set {a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n}$. Let $L$ be a contour in $\C$ oriented anticlockwise. Let $\partial U_k$ denote the closed contour bounding $U_k$. Then: $\ds \oint_L \map f z \rd z = 2 \pi i \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \Res f {a_k}$ where $\Res f {a_k}$ denotes the residue at $a_k$ of $f$.

title: Cauchy's Theorem
snippet: Cauchy's Lemma (Group Theory), also known as Cauchy's Group Theorem, concerning elements of prime order in a finite group Cauchy's Lemma (Number Theory) (on representation of integers as sums of $4$ integers or squares) Cauchy's (Group) Theorem or Cauchy's Theorem for Groups, concerning existence of a subgroup of prime order in a finite group Cauchy's Theorem (Geometry): concerning congruent polytopes Cauchy Mean Value Theorem: extension to the Mean Value Theorem Cauchy-Goursat Theorem: value of integrals in complex analysis Cauchy-Hadamard Theorem: radius of convergence of a power series…

title: Cauchy-Binet Formula
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix. Let $\mathbf B$ be an $n \times m$ matrix. Let $1 \le j_1, j_2, \ldots, j_m \le n$. Let $\mathbf A_{j_1 j_2 \ldots j_m}$ denote the $m \times m$ matrix consisting of columns $j_1, j_2, \ldots, j_m$ of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf B_{j_1 j_2 \ldots j_m}$ denote the $m \times m$ matrix consisting of rows $j_1, j_2, \ldots, j_m$ of $\mathbf B$.

title: Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality for Definite Integrals/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality for Definite Integrals == The Cauchy-Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Inequality for Definite Integrals was first stated in this form by in $1859$, and later rediscovered by in $1888$. Category:Historical Notes

title: Cauchy-Goursat Theorem
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a holomorphic function, where $D \subseteq \C$ is a simply connected domain. Let $C$ be a closed contour in $D$. Then: $\ds \oint_C \map f z \rd z = 0$

title: Cauchy-Kovalevsky Theorem
snippet: Let $\KK$ denote the field of either the real or complex numbers. Let $V = \KK^m$. Let $W = \KK^n$. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_{n − 1}$ be analytic functions defined on some neighborhood of $\tuple {0, 0}$ in $W \times V$, taking values in the $m \times m$ matrices. Let $b$ be an analytic function with values in $V$ defined on the same neighborhood.

title: Cauchy-Riemann Equations
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be an open subset of the set of complex numbers $\C$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex function on $D$. Let $u, v: \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: x + i y = z \in D} \to \R$ be the two real-valued functions defined as: {{eqn | l = \map u {x, y} | r = \map \Re {\map f z} }} {{eqn | l = \map v {x, y} | r = \map \Im {\map f z} }} where: $\map \Re {\map f z}$ denotes the real part of $\map f z$ $\map \Im {\map f z}$ denotes the imaginary part of $\map f z$.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality/Complex Numbers
snippet: $\ds \paren {\sum \cmod {w_i}^2} \paren {\sum \cmod {z_i}^2} \ge \cmod {\sum w_i z_i}^2$ where all of $w_i, z_i \in \C$.

title: Cauchy Condensation Test
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}: n \mapsto \map a n$ be a decreasing sequence of strictly positive terms in $\R$ which converges with a limit of zero. That is, for every $n$ in the domain of $\sequence {a_n}$: $a_n > 0$, $a_n \ge a_{n + 1}$, and $a_n \to 0$ as $n \to +\infty$. Then the series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converges the condensed series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty 2^n \map a {2^n}$ converges.

title: Cauchy Distribution has no Finite Moments
snippet: The Cauchy distribution has no finite moments. That is, for example, it has no defined: expectation variance moment generating function and so on.

title: Cauchy Distribution is Symmetric about Median
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with a Cauchy distribution: $\map {f_X} x = \dfrac 1 {\pi \lambda \paren {1 + \paren {\frac {x - \gamma} \lambda }^2} }$ for: $\lambda \in \R_{>0}$ $\gamma \in \R$ $X$ is (reflectionally) symmetric about the vertical line through the median $\gamma$.

title: Cauchy Integral Test
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous, positive and decreasing on the interval $\hointr 1 {+\infty}$. Let the sequence $\sequence {\Delta_n}$ be defined as: $\ds \Delta_n = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \map f k - \int_1^n \map f x \rd x$ Then $\sequence {\Delta_n} $ is decreasing and bounded below by zero. Hence it converges.

title: Cauchy Mean Value Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Suppose: $\forall x \in \openint a b: \map {g'} x \ne 0$ Then: $\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \dfrac {\map {f'} \xi} {\map {g'} \xi} = \dfrac {\map f b - \map f a} {\map g b - \map g a}$

title: Cauchy Product of Absolutely Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty b_n$ be two real series that are absolutely convergent. Then the Cauchy product of $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty b_n$ is absolutely convergent.

title: Cauchy Sequence Converges Iff Equivalent to Constant Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$ Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences. Let $\\CC \,\big / \NN$ be the quotient ring of Cauchy sequences of $\CC$ by the maximal ideal $\NN$. Let $\sequence {x_n} \in \CC$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges in $\struct {R, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ : $\exists a \in R: \sequence {x_n} \in \sequence {a, a, a, \dotsc} + \NN$ where $\sequence {a, a, a, \dotsc} + \NN$ is the left coset in $\CC \, \big / \NN$ that contains the constant sequence $\sequence {a, a, a, \dotsc}$.

title: Cauchy Sequence Is Eventually Bounded Away From Non-Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $R$. Suppose $\sequence {x_n}$ does not converge to $l \in R$. Then: $\exists K \in \N$ and $C \in \R_{>0}: \forall n > K: C < \norm {x_n - l}$

title: Cauchy Sequence in Metric Space is not necessarily Convergent
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $M$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M$ is a convergent sequence in $M$.

title: Cauchy Sequence in Positive Integers under Scaled Euclidean Metric
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $\delta: \Z_{>0} \times \Z_{>0} \to \R$ be the scaled Euclidean metric on $\Z_{>0}$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z_{>0}: \map \delta {x, y} = \dfrac {\size {x - y} } {x y}$ The sequence $\sequence {x_n}$ in $\Z_{>0}$ defined as: $\forall n \in \N: x_n = n$ is a Cauchy sequence in $\struct {\Z_{>0}, \delta}$.

title: Cauchy Sequence in Positive Integers under Usual Metric is eventually Constant
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $d: \Z_{>0} \times \Z_{>0} \to \R$ be the usual (Euclidean) metric on $\Z_{>0}$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $\struct {\Z_{>0}, d}$. Then: $\exists m, n \in \Z_{>0}: \forall r > n: x_r = m$ That is, $\sequence {x_n}$ is eventually constant.

title: Cauchy Sequence of Subring iff Cauchy Sequence of Normed Division Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\struct {S, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_S }$ be a normed division subring of $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\sequence{x_n}$ be a sequence in $S$. Then: $\sequence{x_n}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $\struct {S, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_S }$ $\sequence{x_n}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$

title: Cauchy Sequence with Finite Elements Prepended is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $R$. Let $N \in \N$ Let $\sequence {y_n}$ be the sequence defined by: $\forall n, y_n = x_{N + n}$ Let $\sequence {y_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $R$. Then: $\sequence {x_n}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $R$.

title: Cauchy Sequences form Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +, \circ}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$ with unity $\tuple {1, 1, 1, \dotsc}$. Let $\CC \subset R^\N$ be the set of Cauchy sequences on $R$. Then: $\struct {\CC, +, \circ}$ is a subring of $R^\N$ with unity $\tuple {1, 1, 1, \dotsc}$.

title: Cauchy Sequences in Vector Spaces with Equivalent Norms Coincide
snippet:
Let $M_a = \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a}$ and $M_b = \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $M_a$. Suppose, $
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a$ and $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b$ are equivalent norms, that is: $
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a \sim 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b$ Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is also a Cauchy sequence in $M_b$.

title: Caustic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Caustics ==

title: Cavalieri's Principle
snippet: Let two solid figures $S_1$ and $S_2$ have equal height. Let sections made by planes parallel to their bases and at equal distances from the bases always have equal area. Then the volumes of $S_1$ and $S_2$ are equal.

title: Cayley's Formula
snippet: The number of distinct labeled trees with $n$ nodes is $n^{n - 2}$.

title: Cayley's Representation Theorem
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Every finite group is isomorphic to a subgroup of $S_n$ for some $n \in \Z$.

title: Cayley's Theorem
snippet: {{item|*| Cayley's Theorem (Graph Theory), also known as Cayley's Formula: The number of distinct labeled trees with $n$ nodes is $n^{n - 2}$.}} Category:Cayley's Theorems

title: Cayley's Theorem (Category Theory)
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a small category. Denote with $\mathbf{Set}$ the category of sets. Then there exists a category $\mathbf D$, subject to: $(1): \quad $ The objects of $\mathbf D$ are sets. $(2): \quad $ The morphisms of $\mathbf D$ are mappings. $(3): \quad \mathbf C \cong \mathbf D$, i.e. $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ are isomorphic. That is, $\mathbf C$ is isomorphic to a subcategory of $\mathbf{Set}$.

title: Cayley-Dickson Construction forms Star-Algebra
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a $*$-algebra. Let $A' = \struct {A'_F, \oplus'} = \struct {A, \oplus}^2$ be the algebra formed from $A$ by the Cayley-Dickson construction. Then $A'$ is also a $*$-algebra.

title: Cayley-Dickson Construction from Commutative Associative Algebra is Associative
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a $*$-algebra. Let $A' = \struct {A_F, \oplus'}$ be constructed from $A$ using the Cayley-Dickson construction. Then: $A'$ is an associative algebra $A$ is both a commutative algebra and an associative algebra.

title: Cayley-Dickson Construction from Nicely Normed Algebra is Nicely Normed
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a $*$-algebra. Let $A' = \struct {A_F, \oplus'}$ be constructed from $A$ using the Cayley-Dickson construction. Then $A'$ is a nicely normed algebra $A$ is also a nicely normed algebra.

title: Cayley-Dickson Construction from Real Star-Algebra is Commutative
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a $*$-algebra. Let $A' = \struct {A_F, \oplus'}$ be constructed from $A$ using the Cayley-Dickson construction. Then $A$ is a real star-algebra $A'$ is a commutative algebra.

title: Cayley Table/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cayley Tables ==

title: Cayley Table for Commutative Operation is Symmetrical about Main Diagonal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then: the Cayley table for $\struct {S, \circ}$ is symmetrical about the main diagonal $\circ$ is a commutative operation.

title: Ceiling Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Ceiling Function == === Ceiling of $\sqrt 2$ ===

title: Ceiling Function is Idempotent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ceiling x$ denote the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\ceiling {\ceiling x} = \ceiling x$ That is, the ceiling function is idempotent.

title: Ceiling Function is Integer
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then the ceiling function of $x$ is an integer: $\ceiling x \in \Z$

title: Ceiling defines Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be the relation defined on $\R$ such that: $\forall x, y, \in \R: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \ceiling x = \ceiling y$ where $\ceiling x$ is the ceiling of $x$. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence, and $\forall n \in \Z$, the $\RR$-class of $n$ is the half-open interval $\hointl {n - 1} n$.

title: Ceiling is between Number and One More
snippet: $x \le \ceiling x < x + 1$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Ceiling minus Real Number
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: \ceiling x - x \in \hointr 0 1$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Ceiling of Floor is Floor
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ denote the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\ceiling {\floor x} = \floor x$ That is, the ceiling of the floor is the floor.

title: Ceiling of Half of n+m plus Ceiling of Half of n-m+1
snippet: Let $n, m \in \Z$ be integers. $\ceiling {\dfrac {n + m} 2} + \ceiling {\dfrac {n - m + 1} 2} = n + 1$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Ceiling of Negative equals Negative of Floor
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\ceiling {-x} = -\floor x$

title: Ceiling of Non-Integer
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $x \notin \Z$. Then: $\ceiling x > x$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Ceiling of Number plus Integer
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z: \ceiling x + n = \ceiling {x + n}$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Ceiling of Root of Ceiling equals Ceiling of Root
snippet: Let $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive real number. Let $\ceiling x$ denote the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\ds \ceiling {\sqrt {\ceiling x} } = \ceiling {\sqrt x}$

title: Ceiling of x+m over n
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$. Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\ceiling {\dfrac {x + m} n} = \ceiling {\dfrac {\ceiling x + m} n}$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Celestial Body moves along Parallel of Declination
snippet: Consider the celestial sphere $C$ whose observer is $O$. Let $B$ be a celestial body on $C$. Let $\delta$ be the declination of $B$. Let $P_\delta$ be the parallel of declination whose declination is $\delta$. Then $B$ appears to move along the path of $P_\delta$, in the direction from the north to east to south to west. It takes $1$ sidereal day for $B$ to travel around $P_\delta$.

title: Celestial Equator is Parallel to Geographical Equator
snippet: Consider the celestial sphere with observer $O$. The plane of the celestial equator is parallel to the plane of the geographical equator.

title: Center is Characteristic Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Then its center $\map Z G$ is characteristic in $G$.

title: Center is Element of Closed Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a positive real number. Let $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} a$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Then: $a \in \map {{B_\epsilon}^-} a$

title: Center is Element of Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a positive real number. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Then: $a \in \map {B_\epsilon} a$

title: Center is Intersection of Centralizers
snippet: The center of a group is the intersection of all the centralizers of the elements of that group: $\ds \map Z G = \bigcap_{g \mathop \in G} \map {C_G} g$

title: Center of Conic is Center of Symmetry
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a central conic. Let $C$ be the center of $\KK$. Then $C$ is a center of symmetry for $\KK$.

title: Center of Conway Circle is Incenter
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $\KK$ be the Conway circle of $ABC$. Then the center of $\KK$ coincides with the incenter of $\triangle ABC$.

title: Center of Dihedral Group
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number such that $n \ge 3$. Let $D_n$ be the dihedral group of order $2 n$, given by: $D_n = \gen {\alpha, \beta: \alpha^n = \beta^2 = e, \beta \alpha \beta = \alpha^{−1} }$ Let $\map Z {D_n}$ denote the center of $D_n$. Then: $\map Z {D_n} = \begin{cases} e & : n \text { odd} \\ \set {e, \alpha^{n / 2} } & : n \text { even} \end{cases}$

title: Center of Division Ring is Subfield
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be an division ring. Let $\map Z K$ be the center of $K$. Then $\map Z K$ is a subfield of $K$.

title: Center of Ellipsoid is Center of Symmetry
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. The center of $\EE$ is a center of symmetry for $\EE$.

title: Center of Gravity equals Center of Mass if it exists
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in a gravitational field $\mathbf G$. Let $B$ have a center of gravity $P$. Then the center of mass of $B$ is also $P$.

title: Center of Gravity in Non-Uniform Gravitational Field
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in a gravitational field $\mathbf G$ which is non-uniform. The forces on $B$ are reducible to: $(1): \quad$ a single force $\mathbf F$ $(2): \quad$ a couple $C$ whose plane is perpendicular to the line of action of $\mathbf F$. The line of action of $\mathbf F$ does not pass through some fixed point as $B$ rotates in $\mathbf G$ unless $C$ is zero.

title: Center of Gravity in Uniform Gravitational Field is Center of Mass
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in a uniform gravitational field. The center of gravity of $B$ is the same point as the center of mass of $B$.

title: Center of Gravity of Barycentric Body is Center of Mass
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in a gravitational field $\mathbf G$ which is non-uniform. Let $B$ be barycentric. Then the couple on $B$ induced by $\mathbf G$ is reduced to zero As a consequence, the center of gravity of $B$ is coincident with the center of mass of $B$.

snippet: == Historical Note on Center of Gravity of Solid Hemisphere == The Center of Gravity of Solid Hemisphere was found by . He demonstrates how it was found in Proposition $6$ in his .

title: Center of Group is Abelian Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\map Z G$ be the center of $G$. Then $\map Z G$ is an abelian subgroup of $G$.

title: Center of Group is Kernel of Conjugacy Action
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $Z$ be the kernel of the conjugacy action. Then $Z$ is the center of $G$.

title: Center of Group is Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group The center $\map Z G$ of $G$ is a normal subgroup of $G$.

title: Center of Group is Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. The center $\map Z G$ of $G$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Center of Group of Order Prime Cubed
snippet: Let $G$ be a group of order $p^3$, where $p$ is a prime. Let $\map Z G$ be the center of $G$. Then $\order {\map Z G} \ne p^2$.

title: Center of Group of Prime Power Order is Non-Trivial
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose order is the power of a prime. Then the center of $G$ is non-trivial: $\forall G: \order G = p^r: p \in \mathbb P, r \in \N_{>0}: \map Z G \ne \set e$

title: Center of Mass/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Centers of Mass ==

title: Center of Mass Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ denote the set of massy particles in ordinary space. Let $\circ$ denote the binary operation defined as: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ y =$ the center of mass of $x$ and $y$ Then $\circ$ is an associative operation.

title: Center of Mass in Barycentric Coordinates
snippet: Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, p_3$ be fixed non-coplanar points, such that $p_i = \tuple {x_i, y_1, z_i}$. Let $p$ be a point in ordinary space expressed in barycentric coordinates $\set {p_0, p_1, p_2, p_3}$: $p = \lambda_0 p_0 + \lambda_1 p_1 + \lambda_2 p_2 + \lambda_3 p_3$ such that: $\lambda_0 + \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 1$ Let point masses of mass $\lambda_0, \lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3$ be placed at $p_0, p_1, p_2, p_3$ respectively. Then $p$ is the center of mass of $\set {p_0, p_1, p_2, p_3}$.

title: Center of Mass of System of Particles in Cartesian Plane
snippet: Let $B$ be a system of $n$ discrete particles embedded in a cartesian plane, each with: mass $m_i$ position $\tuple {x_i, y_i}$ where $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Then the coordinates $\tuple {\bar x, \bar y}$ of the center of mass of $B$ are given by: {{eqn | l = M \bar x | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n m_i x_i }} {{eqn | l = M \bar y | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n m_i y_i }} where: $\ds M = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n m_i$

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Circular Arc
snippet: Let $\WW$ be a wire of uniform density. Let $\WW$ be bent into the shape of the arc of a circle $\CC$ of radius $r$ subtending an angle of $2 \alpha$ from the center of $\CC$. Then the center of mass of $\WW$ is the point $\dfrac {r \sin \alpha} \alpha$ from the center of $\CC$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Circular Sector
snippet: Let $\WW$ be a uniform lamina in the shape of the sector of a circle $\CC$ of radius $r$ of an angle of $2 \alpha$. Then the center of mass of $\PP$ is the point $\dfrac {2 r \sin \alpha} {3 \alpha}$ from the center of $\CC$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Conical Shell
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a uniform lamina in the shape of a (right circular) cone of height $h$. Then the center of mass of $\CC$ is the point $\dfrac {2 h} 3$ from the vertex of $\CC$ along the axis of $\CC$ to the base of $\CC$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Density Body is Centroid
snippet: Let $B$ be a body of uniform density. Then the center of mass of $B$ coincides with the centroid of $B$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Hemispherical Shell
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a uniform lamina in the shape of a hemisphere of radius $r$. Then the center of mass of $\HH$ is the point $\dfrac r 2$ from the center of $\HH$ along the radius of $\HH$ perpendicular to the base of $\HH$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Solid Cone
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a solid cone of uniform density. Then the center of mass of $\CC$ is the point $\dfrac 3 4$ of the distance from the vertex of $\CC$ to the center of mass of the base of $\CC$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Solid Hemisphere
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a solid hemisphere of radius $r$ of uniform density. Then the center of mass of $\BB$ is the point $\dfrac {3 r} 8$ from the center of $\BB$ along the radius of $\BB$ perpendicular to the base of $\BB$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Solid Pyramid
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a solid pyramid of uniform density. Then the center of mass of $\PP$ is the point $\dfrac 3 4$ of the distance from the vertex of $\PP$ to the center of mass of the base of $\PP$.

title: Center of Mass of Uniform Triangular Lamina
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina in the shape of a triangle. Then the center of mass of $\LL$ is at the centroid of $\LL$. That is, it lies $\dfrac 2 3$ of the way along an arbitrary median of $\LL$ from its vertex.

title: Center of Non-Abelian Group of Order pq is Trivial
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct prime numbers. Let $G$ be a non-abelian group of order $p q$ whose identity is $e$. Then the center of $G$ is trivial: $\map Z G = \set e$

title: Center of Opposite Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be the opposite group to $G$. Let $\map Z {G, \circ}$ and $\map Z {G, *}$ be the centers of $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {G, *}$, respectively. Then: $\map Z {G, \circ} = \map Z {G, *}$

title: Center of Quaternion Group
snippet: Let $Q = \Dic 2 = \gen {a, b: a^4 = e, b^2 = a^2, a b a = b}$ be the quaternion group. Let $\map Z {\Dic 2}$ denote the center of $\Dic 2$. Then: $\map Z {\Dic 2} = \set {e, a^2}$

title: Center of Ring is Commutative Subring
snippet: The center $\map Z R$ of a ring $R$ is a commutative subring of $R$.

title: Center of Square is Axis of Rotational Symmetry of Order 4
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a square. Let $\AA$ be a straight line passing through the center of $\SS$. Then $\AA$ is an axis of rotational symmetry of $\SS$ of order $4$.

title: Center of Symmetric Group is Trivial
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group of order $n$. Let $n \ge 3$. Then the center $\map Z {S_n}$ of $S_n$ is trivial.

title: Centered Hexagonal Number as Sum of Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the $n$th centered hexagonal number. Then: $C_n = 6 T_{n - 1} + 1$ where $T_{n - 1}$ denotes the $n - 1$th triangular number.

title: Central Binomial Coefficient/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of central binomial coefficients begins: $2, 6, 20, 70, 252, 924, 3432, 12 \, 870, 48 \, 620, 184 \, 756, \ldots$ Category:Central Binomial Coefficients

title: Central Dilatation Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Central Dilatation Mappings ==

title: Central Dilatation Mapping in Euclidean Space is Conformal
snippet: Let $f$ be a central dilatation mapping in Euclidean space. Then $f$ is a conformal transformation.

title: Central Field is Field of Functional
snippet: Let $\mathbf y$ be an $N$-dimensional vector. Let $J$ be a functional, such that: $\ds J \sqbrk {\mathbf y} = \int_a^b \map F {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf y'} \rd x$ Let the following be a central field: $\map {\mathbf y'} x = \map {\boldsymbol \psi} {x, \mathbf y}$ Then this central field is a field of functional $J$.

title: Central Force/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Central Forces ==

title: Central Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed real-valued random variables with: expectation $\expect {X_i} = \mu \in \R$ variance $\var {X_i} = \sigma^2 > 0$ Let: $\ds S_n = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i$ Then: $\dfrac {S_n - n \mu} {\sqrt {n \sigma^2} } \xrightarrow D \Gaussian 0 1$ as $n \to \infty$ that is, converges in distribution to a standard normal distribution.

title: Central Moment of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable of the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$ for some $\beta \in \R_{> 0}$ Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Then the $n$th central moment $\mu_n$ of $X$ is given by: $\ds \mu_n = n! \beta^n \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {k!}$

title: Central Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Central Products ==

title: Central Subgroup is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a central subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is a normal subgroup of $G$.

title: Centralizer in Subgroup is Intersection
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\forall x \in G: \map {C_H} x = \map {C_G} x \cap H$ That is, the centralizer of an element in a subgroup is the intersection of that subgroup with the centralizer of the element in the group.

title: Centralizer is Normal Subgroup of Normalizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $\map {C_G} H$ be the centralizer of $H$ in $G$. Let $\map {N_G} H$ be the normalizer of $H$ in $G$. Let $\Aut H$ be the automorphism group of $H$. Then: $(1): \quad \map {C_G} H \lhd \map {N_G} H$ $(2): \quad \map {N_G} H / \map {C_G} H \cong K$ where: $\map {N_G} H / \map {C_G} H$ is the quotient group of $\map {N_G} H$ by $\map {C_G} H$ $K$ is a subgroup of $\Aut H$.

title: Centralizer of Group Element is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group and let $a \in G$. Then $\map {C_G} a$, the centralizer of $a$ in $G$, is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Centralizer of Ring Subset is Subring
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ Then $\map {C_R} S$, the centralizer of $S$ in $R$, is a subring of $R$.

title: Centralizer of Self-Inverse Element of Non-Abelian Finite Simple Group is not That Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite simple group. Let $t \in G$ be a self-inverse element of $G$. Then: $\map {C_G} t \ne G$ where $\map {C_G} t$ denotes the centralizer of $t$ in $G$.

title: Centralizer of Subset is Intersection of Centralizers of Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S \subseteq G$. Let $\map {C_G} S$ be the centralizer of $S$ in $G$. Then: $\ds \map {C_G} S = \bigcap_{x \mathop \in S} \map {C_G} x$ where $\map {C_G} z$ is the centralizer of $x$ in $G$.

title: Centrifugal Force on Particle
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle which is stationary in a rotating frame of reference which itself is rotating with constant angular velocity $\omega$. Let the mass of $P$ be $m$. Let $P$ be a distance $r$ from the axis of rotation of the frame of reference. Then $P$ can be treated as a particle in an inertial frame of reference experiencing a radial centrifugal force of magnitude $m r \omega^2$.

title: Centripetal Force on Body in Circular Path
snippet: Let $B$ be a body of mass $m$ constrained to move at constant speed $v$ in a circular path $C$ or radius $r$. Let $\mathbf F$ denote the centripetal force on $B$. Then: $(1): \quad$ The direction of $\mathbf F$ is towards the center of $C$ $(2): \quad$ The magnitude of $\mathbf F$ is given by: $\size {\mathbf F} = \dfrac {m v^2} r$ or: $\size {\mathbf F} = m r \omega^2$ where $\omega$ denotes the angular speed of $B$.

title: Centroid of Combined Systems of Weighted Points
snippet: Let $O'$ be a point whose position vector from $O$ is $\mathbf l$. Let $S = \set {A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n}$ be a set of $n$ points in Euclidean space. Let $W_S: S \to \R$ be a weight function on $S$. Let $T = \set {B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_m}$ be a set of $m$ points in Euclidean space. Let $W_T: T \to \R$ be a weight function on $T$. Let $H$ be the centroid of $S$ with weight function $W_S$. Let $H'$ be the centroid of $T$ with weight function $W_T$.

title: Centroid of Triangle is Centroid of Medial
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $\triangle DEF$ be the medial triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Let $G$ be the centroid of $\triangle ABC$. Then $G$ is also the centroid of $\triangle DEF$.

title: Centroid of Weighted Pair of Points
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be two points in Euclidean space. Let $A$ and $B$ have weights $p$ and $q$ respectively. Let $G$ be the centroid of $A$ and $B$. Then $G$ divides the line $AB$ in the ratio $q : p$. That is: $AG = \dfrac q {p + q} AB$ $BG = \dfrac p {p + q} AB$

title: Centroid of Weighted Set of Points is Independent of Origin
snippet: Let $O'$ be a point whose position vector from $O$ is $\mathbf l$. Let $S = \set {A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n}$ be a set of $n$ points in Euclidean space whose position vectors are given by $\mathbf a_1, \mathbf a_2, \dotsc, \mathbf a_n$ repectively. Let $W: S \to \R$ be a weight function on $S$. Let $G$ be the centroid of $S$ with weight function $W$: $\vec {OG} = \dfrac {w_1 \mathbf a_1 + w_2 \mathbf a_2 + \dotsb + w_n \mathbf a_n} {w_1 + w_2 + \dotsb + w_n}$ where $w_i = \map W {A_i}$ for each $i$. Let $\vec {OG'}$ be the centroid of $S$ with weight function $W$ with respect to $O'$.

title: Cesàro Mean
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence of complex numbers. Suppose that $\sequence {a_n}$ converges to $\ell$ in $\C$: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} a_n = \ell$ Then also: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \frac {a_1 + \dotsb + a_n} n = \ell$

title: Cesàro Summation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cesàro Summation ==

title: Cesàro Summation Operator is Continuous Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\ell^\infty$ be the space of bounded sequences. Let $A : \ell^\infty \to \ell^\infty$ be the Cesàro summation operator. Then $A$ is a continuous linear transformation.

title: Ceva's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $L$, $M$ and $N$ be points on the sides $BC$, $AC$ and $AB$ respectively. Then the lines $AL$, $BM$ and $CN$ are concurrent : $\dfrac {BL} {LC} \times \dfrac {CM} {MA} \times \dfrac {AN} {NB} = 1$

title: Chain Rule for Partial Derivatives
snippet: Let $F: \R^2 \to \R$ be a real-valued function of $2$ variables. Let $X: \R^2 \to \R$ and $Y: \R^2 \to \R$ also be real-valued functions of $2$ variables. Let $F = \map f {x, y}$ be such that: {{eqn | l = x | r = \map X {u, v} }} {{eqn | l = y | r = \map Y {u, v} }} Then: $F = \map F {u, v}$ and: {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial u} | r = \dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x} \dfrac {\partial X} {\partial u} + \dfrac {\partial f} {\partial y} \dfrac {\partial Y} {\partial u} | c = }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial v} | r = \dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x} \dfrac {\partial X}…

title: Chain Rule for Probability
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A, B \in \Sigma$ be events of $\EE$ such that $\map \Pr B > 0$. The conditional probability of $A$ given $B$ is: $\condprob A B = \dfrac {\map \Pr {A \cap B} } {\map \Pr B}$

title: Chain Rule for Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $f: \R^n \to \R, \mathbf x \mapsto z$ be a differentiable real-valued function. Let $\mathbf x = \begin {bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end {bmatrix} \in \R^n$. Further, let every element $x_i: 1 \le i \le n$ represent an implicitly defined differentiable real function of $t$. Then $z$ is itself differentiable $t$ and: {{eqn | l = \frac {\d z} {\d t} | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \frac {\partial z} {\partial x_i} \frac {\d x_i} {\d t} }} where $\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x_i}$ is the partial derivative of $z$ $x_i$.

title: Chain is Directed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $C$ be a non-empty chain of $S$. Then $C$ is directed.

title: Chain of Sets/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Chains of Sets ==

title: Champernowne Constant is Normal
snippet: The Champernowne constant: $0 \cdotp 12345 \, 67891 \, 01112 \, 13141 \, 51617 \, 18192 \, 02122 \ldots$ is normal base $10$.

title: Champernowne Constant is Transcendental
snippet: The Champernowne constant: $0 \cdotp 12345 \, 67891 \, 01112 \, 13141 \, 51617 \, 18192 \, 02122 \ldots$ is transcendental.

title: Change of Base of Logarithm
snippet: Let $\log_a x$ be the logarithm to base $a$ of $x$. Then: $\log_b x = \dfrac {\log_a x} {\log_a b}$ Thus a convenient formula for calculating the logarithm of a number to a different base.

title: Change of Basis Matrix from Basis to Itself is Identity
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite dimension $n > 0$. Let $\BB$ be an ordered basis of $M$. Then the change of basis matrix from $\BB$ to $\BB$ is the $n\times n$ identity matrix: $\mathbf M_{\BB, \BB} = \mathbf I$

title: Change of Basis Matrix is Nonsingular
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite dimension $n > 0$. Let $\AA$ and $\BB$ be ordered bases of $M$. Let $\mathbf P$ be the change of basis matrix from $\AA$ to $\BB$. Then $\mathbf P$ is nonsingular, and its inverse $\mathbf P^{-1}$ is the change of basis matrix from $\BB$ to $\AA$.

title: Change of Basis Matrix under Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ and $H$ be free unitary $R$-modules of finite dimensions $n, m > 0$ respectively. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ and $\sequence { {a_n}'}$ be ordered bases of $G$. Let $\sequence {b_m}$ and $\sequence { {b_m}'}$ be ordered bases of $H$. Let $u: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Let $\sqbrk {u; \sequence {b_m}, \sequence {a_n} }$ denote the matrix of $u$ relative to $\sequence {a_n}$ and $\sequence {b_m}$.

title: Change of Coordinate Vector Under Change of Basis
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module of finite dimension $n > 0$. Let $\BB$ and $\CC$ be bases of $M$. Let $\mathbf M_{\BB, \CC}$ be the change of basis matrix from $\BB$ to $\CC$. Let $m \in M$. Let $\sqbrk m_\BB$ and $\sqbrk m_\CC$ be its coordinate vectors relative to $\BB$ and $\CC$ respectively. Then $\sqbrk m_\BB = \mathbf M_{\BB, \CC} \cdot \sqbrk m_\CC$.

title: Change of Coordinate Vectors Under Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M, N$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $m, n > 0$ respectively. Let $\AA, \BB$ be ordered bases of $M$ and $N$ respectively. Let $f: M \to N$ be a linear transformation. Let $\mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$ be its matrix relative to $\AA$ and $\BB$. Then for all $m \in M$: $\sqbrk {\map f m}_\BB = \mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA} \cdot \sqbrk m_\AA$ where $\sqbrk {\, \cdot \,}_-$ denotes the coordinate vector with respect to a basis.

title: Change of Index Variable of Product
snippet: $\ds \prod_{\map R i} a_i = \prod_{\map R j} a_j$ where $\ds \prod_{\map R i} a_i$ denotes the product over $a_i$ for all $i$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R i$.

title: Change of Index Variable of Summation
snippet: $\ds \sum_{\map R i} a_i = \sum_{\map R j} a_j$ where $\ds \sum_{\map R i} a_i$ denotes the summation over $a_i$ for all $i$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R i$.

title: Change of Index Variable of Supremum
snippet: Let $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of the non-negative real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$ indexed by $I$. Let $\map R i$ be a propositional functions of $i \in I$. Let $\ds \sup_{\map R i} a_i$ be the indexed supremum on $\family {a_i}$. Then: $\ds \sup_{\map R i} a_i = \sup_{\map R j} a_j$

title: Change of Lead in Prime Number Race 4n+1 vs. 4n-1
snippet: Consider the prime number race between $4 n + 1$ and $4 n - 1$. While the prime numbers of the form $4 n - 1$ appear usually to be in the majority, the lead changes from one to the other an infinite number of times.

title: Change of Measures Formula for Integrals
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be $\sigma$-finite measures on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ such that: $
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$. Let $g$ be a Radon-Nikodym derivative of $
u$ with respect to $\mu$. Let $f : X 	o \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then: $\ds \int f d 
u = \int \paren {f \cdot g} d \mu$ where: $f \cdot g$ is the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$ $\ds \int \cdot d 
u$ denotes the integral of a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function with respect to $
u$.

title: Change of Variables Theorem (Multivariable Calculus)
snippet: Let $\mathbf F: U \to V$ be a diffeomorphism between open subsets of $\R^2$. Let $D^* \subset U$ and $D = \map {\mathbf F} {D^*} \subset V$ be bounded subsets. Let $f: D \to \R$ be a bounded function. Then $\ds \iint_D \map f {x, y} \rd x \rd y = \iint_{D^*} \map f {\map {\mathbf F} {u, v} } \size {\map {\det D \mathbf F} {u, v} } \rd u \rd v$ where $\map {\det D \mathbf F} {u, v}$ is the Jacobian. The equality means that the left-hand integral exists if and only if the right-hand integral does and that, if so, the two integrals are equal.

title: Change of Variables in Indexed Summation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b, c, d$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $g: \closedint c d \to \closedint a b$ be a bijection. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i = \sum_{i \mathop = c}^d \map f {\map g i}$

title: Change of Variables in Summation over Finite Set
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $f: S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $g: T \to S$ be a bijection. Then we have an equality of summations over finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s = \sum_{t \mathop \in T} \map f {\map g t}$
