Classification of Open Neighborhoods in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $U \subseteq X$. Let $x \in X$. Then $U$ is an open neighborhood of $x$ $U - x$ is an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Equivalently, the open neighborhoods of $x$ are precisely the sets of the form $V + x$ where $V$ is an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$.

title: Clavius's Law
snippet: If, from the negation of a proposition $p$ we can derive $p$, we may conclude $p$:

title: Clavius's Law implies Law of Excluded Middle
snippet: From Clavius's Law: $\neg p \implies p \vdash p$ follows the Law of Excluded Middle: $\vdash p \lor \neg p$

title: Clear Registers Program
snippet: == URM Program == Let $a, b \in \N$ be natural numbers such that $0 b$ then $\map Z {a, b}$ is the null URM program. The length of $\map Z {a, b}$ is: $\map \lambda {\map Z {a, b} } = \begin {cases} 0 & : a > b \\ b - a + 1 & : a \le b \end {cases}$

title: Clopen Points in Arens-Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Arens-Fort space. Let $q \in S: q \ne \tuple {0, 0}$. Then $\set q$ is both open and closed in $T$. $\set {\tuple {0, 0} }$ itself is closed, but not open.

title: Clopen Points in Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on an infinite set $S$. Let $q \in S: q \ne p$. Then $\set q$ is both open and closed in $T$. $\set p$ itself, on the other hand, is closed but not open.

title: Clopen Points in Modified Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Then all points in $S \setminus \set {a, b}$ are clopen in $T$. $a$ and $b$ themselves are not open in $T$, but they are closed in $T$.

title: Clopen Set and Complement form Separation
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a clopen set of $T$. Let $\relcomp S H$ be the complement of $H$ relative to $S$. Then $H$ and $\relcomp S H$ form a separation of $T$.

title: Clopen Set contains Components of All its Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be both closed and open in $T$. Then $H$ contains the components of all of its points.

title: Clopen Sets in Finite Complement Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then the only clopen sets of $T$ are $S$ and $\O$.

title: Clopen Sets in Indiscrete Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. The only subsets of $S$ which are both closed and open in $T$ are $S$ and $\O$.

title: Clopen Sets in Modified Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be clopen in $T$. If $a \in H$, then $b \in H$ as well. That is, any clopen set of $T$ must contain both or neither of $a$ and $b$.

title: Closable Densely-Defined Linear Operator has Smallest Closed Extension
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a closable densely-defined linear operator. Then there exists a closed densely-defined linear extension $\struct {\map D S, S}$ of $T$ such that: the graph $\map \GG S$ is $\subseteq$-minimal among the graphs of closed densely-defined linear extensions of $T$. Further: $\map \GG S = \map \cl {\map \GG T}$

title: Closable Densely-Defined Operator is Closed iff Equal to Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a closable densely-defined linear operator. Let $\tuple {\map D {\overline T}, \overline T}$ be the closure of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$. Then $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ is closed $T = \overline T$.

title: Closed *-Subalgebra of C*-Algebra is C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a closed $\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Then $\struct {B, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

title: Closed Algebraic Structure/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Algebraic Structures ==

title: Closed Ball contains Smaller Closed Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon, \delta \in \R_{> 0}$ such that $\epsilon \le \delta$. Let $\map {B^-_\epsilon} a$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball on $a$. Let $\map {B^-_\delta} a$ be the closed $\delta$-ball on $a$. Then: $\map {B^-_\epsilon} a \subseteq \map {B^-_\delta} a$

title: Closed Ball contains Smaller Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon, \delta \in \R_{> 0}$ such that $\epsilon \le \delta$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball on $a$. Let $\map {B^-_\delta} a$ be the closed $\delta$-ball on $a$. Then: $\map {B_\epsilon} a \subseteq \map {B^-_\delta} a$

title: Closed Ball in Euclidean Space is Compact
snippet: Let $x \in \R_n$ be a point in the Euclidean space $\R^n$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then the closed $\epsilon$-ball $\map {B_\epsilon^-} x$ is compact.

title: Closed Ball in Metric Space is Closed Neighborhood
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x \in A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon^-} x$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $x$ in $M$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon^-} x$ is a closed neighborhood of $x$ in $M$.

title: Closed Ball in Normed Division Ring is Closed Ball in Induced Metric
Closed Ball in Normed Dual Space of Separable Normed Vector Space is Weak-* Metrizable
snippet: Let $X$ be a separable normed vector space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a countable everywhere dense subset of $X$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $\lambda > 0$. Let $B^-_{X^\ast}$ be the closed unit ball of $X^\ast$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology. Define $d : X^\ast \times X^\ast \to \R$ by: $\ds \map d {f, g} = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {2^n} \min \set {\norm {\map f {x_n} - \map g {x_n} }_X, 1}$ for each $f, g \in X^\ast$. Then $\struct {\lambda B^-_{X^\ast}, w^\ast}$ is metrized by the restriction $d'$ of $d$ to $\lambda B^-_{X^\ast}$.

title: Closed Ball is Connected
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. A closed ball in the metric induced by $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ is connected.

title: Closed Ball is Convex Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\map { {B_r}^-} x$ be a closed ball in $X$ with radius $r \in \R_{>0}$ and center $x \in X$. Then $\map { {B_r}^-} x$ is convex.

title: Closed Ball is Disjoint Union of Open Balls in P-adic Numbers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$: let $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} a$ denote the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ and: let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$. Then: $(1): \quad \forall n \in Z : \map {B^-_{p^{-n} } } a = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 0}^{p - 1} \map {B_{p^{-n} } } {a + i p^n}$ $(2): \quad \forall n \in Z : \set {\map {B_{p^{-n} } } {a + i p^n} : i = 0, \dotsc, p - 1}$ is a set of pairwise disjoint open balls.

title: Closed Ball is Disjoint Union of Smaller Closed Balls in P-adic Numbers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$, let $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} a$ denote the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$. Let $n, m \in Z$, such that $n < m$. Then: $(1) \quad \map {B^-_{p^{-n} } } a = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 0}^{p^{\paren {m - n} } - 1} \map {B^-_{p^{-m} } } {a + i p^n}$ $(2) \quad \set {\map {B^-_{p^{-m} } } {a + i p^n} : i = 0, \dots, p^{\paren {m - n} } - 1}$ is a set of pairwise disjoint closed balls

title: Closed Ball is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. A closed ball in the metric induced by $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ is path-connected.

title: Closed Ball is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $d: V \times V \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the metric induced by the norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ on $V$. Let $\tau$ be the the topology on $V$ induced by the metric $d$. Let $v \in V$ and $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon^-} v$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $v$. Let $\tau_B$ be the subspace topology on $\map {B_\epsilon} v$ induced by $\tau$. Then $\struct{ \map {B_\epsilon^-} v, \tau_B }$ is simply connected.

title: Closed Ball of P-adic Number
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ denote the $p$-adic integers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$, let $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} a$ denote the closed ball of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. Then: $\forall n \in Z : \map {B^-_{p^{-n} } } a = a + p^n \Z_p$ where $a + p^n \Z_p$ denotes the left coset of the principal ideal $p^n \Z_p$ containing $a$ in the subring $\Z_p$. That is, the closed ball $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} a$ is the set: $a + p^n \Z_p = \set{a + p^n z : z \in \Z_p}$

title: Closed Balls Centered on P-adic Number is Countable
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Then the set of all closed balls centered on $a$ is the countable set: $\BB^- = \set {\map {B^-_{p^{-n} } } a: n \in \Z}$

title: Closed Bounded Subset of Real Numbers is Compact
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a closed and bounded subspace of $\R$. Then $S$ is compact in $\R$.

title: Closed Class under Progressing Mapping Lemma
snippet: Let $N$ be a class which is closed under a progressing mapping $g$. Let $g$ be such that: $\forall x, y \in N: \map g x \subseteq y \lor y \subseteq x$ if $\map g x = x$, then $x$ is the greatest element of $N$. Let the following hold: $A \subseteq N$ is a subclass of $N$ $x \in N$ is an element of $N$ Let $x$ be: a proper subset of all elements of $A$ and: the greatest element of $A$ with that property. Then $\map g x \in A$ and is the smallest element of $A$.

title: Closed Continuous Injection is Embedding
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a closed and continuous injection. Then $f$ is an embedding of $T_1$ into $T_2$.

title: Closed Convex Hull in Normed Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\R$. Let $U \subseteq X$. Let $C$ be the closed convex hull of $U$. Then: $C$ is convex.

title: Closed Convex Hull in Topological Vector Space is Closed and Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $\cl$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\operatorname {conv}$ denote convex hull. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty. Then $\map \cl {\map {\operatorname {conv} } A}$ is closed and convex.

title: Closed Convex Set in terms of Bounded Linear Functionals
snippet: Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\R$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual of $X$. Let $C$ be a closed convex subset of $X$. Then: $\ds C = \bigcap_{f \in X^\ast} \set {x \in X : \map f x \le \sup_{c \in C} \map f c}$

title: Closed Curve has no Boundary
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a closed curve embedded in a plane $\PP$. Then $\CC$ has no boundary in $\PP$.

title: Closed Element of Composite Closure Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be closure operators. Let $h = f \circ g$, where $\circ$ represents composition. Suppose that $h$ is also a closure operator. Then an element $x \in S$ is closed $h$ it is closed $f$ and $g$.

title: Closed Elements Uniquely Determine Closure Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be closure operators on $S$. Suppose that $f$ and $g$ have the same closed elements. Then $f = g$.

title: Closed Euclidean Ball/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Euclidean Balls ==

title: Closed Extension Space is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_p$ is irreducible.

title: Closed Extension Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau^*_p$ be the closed extension topology of $\tau$. Then $\tau^*_p$ is a topology on $S^*_p = S \cup \set p$.

title: Closed Extension Topology is not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_p$ is not a $T_1$ space.

title: Closed Extension Topology is not T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_p$ is not a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Closed Extension Topology is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_p$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Closed Form for Centered Hexagonal Numbers
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the $n$th centered hexagonal number. Then: $C_n = 3 n \paren {n - 1} + 1$

title: Closed Form for Heptagonal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th heptagonal number is: $H_n = \dfrac {n \paren {5 n - 3} } 2$

title: Closed Form for Heptagonal Pyramidal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th heptagonal pyramidal number is: $Q_n = \dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {5 n - 2} } 6$

title: Closed Form for Hermite Polynomials
snippet: Let $\map {H_n} x$ denote the Hermite polynomial of order $n$. Then: {{eqn | l = \map {H_n} x | r = \paren {2 x}^n - \dfrac {n \paren {n - 1} } {1!} \paren {2 x}^{n - 2} + \dfrac {n \paren {n - 1} \paren {n - 2} \paren {n - 3} } {2!} \paren {2 x}^{n - 4} \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{\floor {n / 2} } \paren {-1}^k \dfrac {n^\underline {2 k} } {k!} \paren {2 x}^{n - 2 k} | c = where $n^\underline {2 k}$ denotes the falling factorial operator }}

title: Closed Form for Hexagonal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th hexagonal number is: $H_n = n \paren {2 n - 1}$

title: Closed Form for Hexagonal Pyramidal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th hexagonal pyramidal number is: $S_n = \dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {4 n - 1} } 6$

title: Closed Form for Lucas Numbers
snippet: The Lucas numbers have a closed-form solution: $L_n = \phi^n + \paren {1 - \phi}^n = \paren {\dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2}^n + \paren {\dfrac {1 - \sqrt 5} 2}^n$ where $\phi$ is the golden mean. Putting $\hat \phi = 1 - \phi = -\dfrac 1 \phi$ this can be written: $L_n = \phi^n + \hat \phi^n$

title: Closed Form for Millin Series
snippet: The Millin series has the closed form expression: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac 1 {F_{2^n} } = \frac {7 - \sqrt 5} 2$ where $F_k$ is the $k$th Fibonacci number.

title: Closed Form for Number of Derangements on Finite Set
snippet: The number of derangements $D_n$ on a finite set $S$ of cardinality $n$ is: {{eqn | l = D_n | r = n! \paren {1 - \dfrac 1 {1!} + \dfrac 1 {2!} - \dfrac 1 {3!} + \cdots + \dfrac {\paren {-1}^n} {n!} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = n! \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \dfrac {\paren {-1}^k} {k!} | c = }}

title: Closed Form for Octagonal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th octagonal number is: $O_n = n \paren {3 n - 2}$

title: Closed Form for Pentagonal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th pentagonal number is: $P_n = \dfrac {n \paren {3 n - 1} } 2$

title: Closed Form for Pentagonal Pyramidal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th pentagonal pyramidal number is: $Q_n = \dfrac {n^2 \paren {n + 1} } 2$

title: Closed Form for Pentatope Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th pentatope number is: $P_n = \dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {n + 2} \paren {n + 3} } {24}$

title: Closed Form for Polygonal Numbers
snippet: Let $\map P {k, n}$ be the $n$th $k$-gonal number. The closed-form expression for $\map P {k, n}$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map P {k, n} | r = \frac n 2 \paren {\paren {k - 2} n - k + 4} }} {{eqn | r = \frac {k - 2} 2 \paren {n^2 - n} + n }} {{eqn | r = 2 n + \dfrac 1 2 n k \paren {n - 1} - n^2 }}

title: Closed Form for Sequence 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, ...
snippet: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be the integer sequence: $\sequence {a_n} = 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, \ldots$ Then: $a_n = \ceiling {\dfrac {\sqrt {1 + 8 n} - 1} 2}$

title: Closed Form for Square Pyramidal Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th square pyramidal number is: $S_n = \dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {2 n + 1} } 6$

title: Closed Form for Tetrahedral Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th tetrahedral number is: $H_n = \dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {n + 2} } 6$

title: Closed Form for Triangular Numbers
snippet: The closed-form expression for the $n$th triangular number is: $\ds T_n = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i = \frac {n \paren {n + 1} } 2$ Plainly stated: the sum of the first $n$ natural numbers is equal to $\dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} } 2$. This formula pops up frequently in fields as differing as calculus and computer science, and it is elegant in its simplicity.

title: Closed Form of One Minus Golden Mean
snippet: $\hat \phi = \dfrac {1 - \sqrt 5} 2$ where: $\hat \phi$ denotes one minus the golden mean: $\hat \phi = 1 - \phi$.

title: Closed Graph Theorem
snippet: Closed graph theorems give conditions under which the closedness of the graph of a function between topological spaces is equivalent to continuity.

title: Closed Ideal of C*-Algebra is Self-Adjoint
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $I$ be a closed ideal of $A$. Then for each $x \in I$, we have $x^\ast \in I$. That is, $I$ is self-adjoint.

title: Closed Image of Closure of Set under Continuous Mapping equals Closure of Image
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $H \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a continuous mapping. Let $f \sqbrk {\map \cl H}$ be closed in $T_2$. Then: $f \sqbrk {\map \cl H} = \map \cl {f \sqbrk H}$

title: Closed Interval Defined by Absolute Value
snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then: $\set {x \in \R: \size {\xi - x} \le \delta} = \closedint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ where $\closedint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ is the closed real interval between $\xi - \delta$ and $\xi + \delta$.

title: Closed Interval in Complete Lattice is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $a, b \in L$ with $a \preceq b$. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be the closed interval between $a$ and $b$. Then $\struct {I, \preceq}$ is also a complete lattice.

title: Closed Interval in Reals is Uncountable
snippet: Let $a, b$ be extended real numbers such that $a < b$. Then the closed interval $\set {x \in \R : a \le x \le b} \subseteq \R$ is uncountable.

title: Closed Interval of Naturally Ordered Semigroup with Successor equals Union with Successor
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then: $\forall m, n \in \struct {S, \circ, \preceq}: m \preceq n \implies \closedint m {n \circ 1} = \closedint m n \cup \set {n \circ 1}$ where $\closedint m n$ is the closed interval between $m$ and $n$.

title: Closed Intervals form Neighborhood Basis in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $\BB_a$ be defined as: $\BB_a := \set {\closedint {a - \epsilon} {a + \epsilon}: \epsilon \in \R_{>0} }$ that is, the set of all closed intervals of $\R$ with $a$ as a midpoint. Then $\BB_a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

title: Closed Linear Span is Closed Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Let $\map \span S$ be the linear span of $S$. Let $\cl$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\map \cl {\map \span S}$ be the closed linear span of $S$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $\map \cl {\map \span S}$ is a closed vector subspace in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Closed Linear Span of Normalized Block Basic Sequence of Schauder Basis in P-Sequence Space is Range of Contractive Projection
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \hointr 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the Schauder basis given by P-Sequence Space admits Schauder Basis. Let $\sequence {y_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ be a block basic sequence of $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ with: $\norm {y_k}_p = 1$ for each $k \in \N$. Let $\sqbrk {y_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ be the closed linear span of $\sequence {y_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$.

title: Closed Linear Subspaces Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $V$ be a topological vector space. Let $\family {M_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of closed linear subspaces of $V$. Then $M := \ds \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} M_i$ is also a closed linear subspace of $V$.

title: Closed Linear Subspaces Closed under Setwise Addition
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $M, N$ be closed linear subspaces of $H$. Then $M + N$ is also a closed linear subspace of $H$, where $+$ denotes setwise addition.

title: Closed Ordinal Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ is a compact space.

title: Closed Ordinal Space is Complete Order Space
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ is a complete order space.

title: Closed Real Interval/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Real Intervals ==

title: Closed Real Interval is Closed Set
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $\closedint a b \subset \R$ be a closed interval of $\R$. Then $\closedint a b$ is a closed set of $\R$.

title: Closed Real Interval is Closed in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval of $\R$. Then $\closedint a b$ is closed (in the topological sense) in $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$.

title: Closed Real Interval is Compact Space
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Then $I$ is compact.

title: Closed Real Interval is Neighborhood Except at Endpoints
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $\closedint a b \subset \R$ be a closed interval of $\R$. Then $\closedint a b$ is a neighborhood of all of its points except $a$ and $b$.

title: Closed Real Interval is Regular Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval of $\R$. Then $\closedint a b$ is a regular closed set in $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$.

title: Closed Real Interval is not Open Set
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as a Euclidean space. Let $\closedint a b \subset \R$ be a closed interval of $\R$. Then $\closedint a b$ is not an open set of $\R$.

title: Closed Region/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Regions ==

title: Closed Set/Complex Analysis/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Sets in the context of Complex Analysis ==

title: Closed Set Measurable in Borel Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\map \BB \tau$ be the associated Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $C$ be a closed set in $\struct {S, \tau}$. Then $C$ is $\map \BB \tau$-measurable.

title: Closed Set iff Lower and Closed under Directed Suprema in Scott Topological Ordered Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with Scott topology where $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is an up-complete ordered set. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then $A$ is closed $A$ is lower and closed under directed suprema.

title: Closed Set in Coarser Topology is Closed in Finer Topology
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on $X$ such that $\tau_1 \subseteq \tau_2$. That is, $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$. Let $C$ be a closed set in $\struct {X, \tau_1}$. Then $C$ is closed in $\struct {X, \tau_2}$.

title: Closed Set in Linearly Ordered Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $C$ be a subset of $X$. Then $C$ is closed in $X$ for all non-empty subsets $S$ of $C$: If $s \in X$ is a supremum or infimum of $S$ in $X$, then $s \in C$.

title: Closed Set in Metric Space is G-Delta
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $F \subset A$ be a closed set of $M$. Then $F$ is a $G_\delta$ set of $A$.

title: Closed Set in Particular Point Space has no Limit Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $H \subsetneq S$ be closed in $T$. Then $H$ has no limit points.

title: Closed Set in Topological Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T' = \struct{H, \tau_H}$ be a subspace of $T$ where $H \subseteq S$. Then $V \subseteq T'$ is closed in $T'$ $V = T' \cap W$ for some $W$ closed in $T$.

title: Closed Set is F-Sigma Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $V$ be a closed set of $T$. Then $V$ is an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

title: Closed Set of Countable Fort Space is G-Delta
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Let $H \subseteq S$ be closed in $T$. Then $H$ is a $G_\delta$ set.

title: Closed Set of Ultraconnected Space is Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an ultraconnected topological space. Let $F \subset S$ be a closed set in $T$. Then $F$ is ultraconnected.

title: Closed Set of Uncountable Finite Complement Topology is not G-Delta
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Let $V \in \tau$ be a closed set of $T$. Then $V$ is not a $G_\delta$ set.

title: Closed Set under Chain Unions with Choice Function is of Type M
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which is closed under chain unions. Let there exist a choice function for $S$. Then $S$ is of type $M$, that is: every element of $S$ is a subset of a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

title: Closed Sets in Indiscrete Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. $H$ is a closed set of $T$ either $H = S$ or $H = \O$.

title: Closed Sets in Noetherian Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a Noetherian topological space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a non-empty closed set of $T$. Then there exist closed irreducible subsets $Y_1, \ldots, Y_r$ such that: $Y = Y_1 \cup \cdots \cup Y_r$ Furthermore, if we require: $\forall i, j : i \ne j \implies Y_i \not \subseteq Y_j$ then $Y_1, \ldots, Y_r$ are uniquely determined.

title: Closed Sets of Closed Extension Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then the closed sets of $T^*_p$ (apart from $S^*_p$) are the closed sets of $T$. This explains why $\tau^*_p$ is called the closed extension topology of $\tau$.

title: Closed Sets of Either-Or Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the either-or space. Then the closed sets of $T$ are: $\O$ $S$ $\set {-1}$ $\set 1$ $\set {-1, 1}$ Every subset $H$ of $\closedint {-1} 1$ such that $\set 0 \subseteq H$.

title: Closed Sets of Fortissimo Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fortissimo space. Then $H \subseteq S$ is closed in $T$ : $p \in H$ or $H$ is countable or both.

title: Closed Sets of Right Order Space on Real Numbers
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the right order space on $\R$. Then $H \subseteq S$ is closed in $T$ : $H = \O$ or $\R$ or $H = \hointl {-\infty} a$ for some $a \in \R$.

title: Closed Statement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Statements ==

title: Closed Subgroups of P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers for some prime $p$. Then the closed subgroups of $\Z_p$ are the principal ideals: $\text a) \quad \set 0$ $\text b) \quad \forall k \in \N : p^k \Z_p$

title: Closed Subset is Upper Section in Lower Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a transitive relational structure with lower topology. Let $A \subseteq S$ such that $A$ is closed. Then $A$ is an upper section of $S$.

title: Closed Subset of Irreducible Space with Same Krull Dimension is Itself
snippet: Let $X$ be an irreducible topological space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a closed subset. Suppose: $\map \dim Y = \map \dim X < + \infty$ where $\dim$ denotes the Krull dimension. Then: $Y = X$

title: Closed Subset of Real Number Line is G-Delta
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $H \subseteq \R$ be a closed subset of $\R$. Then $H$ is a $G_\delta$ set.

title: Closed Subset of Real Numbers with Lower Bound contains Infimum
snippet: Consider the real number line as a metric space under the usual metric. Let $A \subseteq \R$ such that $A$ is closed in $\R$ and $A \ne \O$. Let $A$ be bounded below. Then $A$ contains its infimum.

title: Closed Subsets of Symmetry Group of Square
snippet: Recall the symmetry group of the square:

title: Closed Subspace of Banach Space forms Banach Space
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a Banach space. Let $Y$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $
orm \cdot_Y$ be the restriction of $
orm \cdot_X$ to $Y$. Then $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$ is a Banach space.

title: Closed Subspace of Banach Space is Topologically Complemented iff has Topological Complement
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $Y$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$. Then $Y$ is topologically complemented in $X$ $Y$ has a topological complement.

title: Closed Subspace of Compact Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact topological space. Let $C = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ be a subspace of $T$. Let $C$ be closed in $T$. Then $\struct {H, \tau}$ is compact. That is, the property of being compact is weakly hereditary.

title: Closed Subspace of Lindelöf Space is Lindelöf Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Lindelöf space. Let $C = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ be a subspace of $T$. Let $C$ be closed in $T$. Then $\struct {H, \tau}$ is Lindelöf space. That is, the property of being Lindelöf is weakly hereditary.

title: Closed Subspace of Separable Banach Space Linearly Isomorphic to Space of Zero-Limit Sequences is Topologically Complemented
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Let $E$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$ that is linearly isomorphic to $\map {C_0} \GF$. Then $E$ is topologically complemented in $X$.

title: Closed Surface/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Surfaces ==

title: Closed Surface has no Boundary
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a closed surface in real Euclidean space of $3$ dimensions $\EE$. Then $\SS$ has no boundary in $\EE$.

title: Closed Topologist's Sine Curve is Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the closed topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is connected.

title: Closed Topologist's Sine Curve is not Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the closed topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is not locally connected.

title: Closed Topologist's Sine Curve is not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the closed topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is not path-connected.

title: Closed Unit Ball in Normed Dual Space is Weak-* Closed
snippet: Let $X$ be a normed vector space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $B^-_{X^\ast}$ be the closed unit ball in $X^\ast$. Then we have that $B^-_{X^\ast}$ is weak-$\ast$ closed.

title: Closed Unit Ball in Normed Dual Space of Separable Normed Vector Space is Weak-* Separable
snippet: Let $X$ be a separable normed vector space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $B^-_{X^\ast}$ be the closed unit ball of $X^\ast$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $B^-_{X^\ast}$. Then $\struct {B^-_{X^\ast}, w^\ast}$ is separable.

title: Closed Unit Ball in Normed Dual Space of Separable Normed Vector Space is Weak-* Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $X$ be a separable normed vector space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $B^-_{X^\ast}$ be the closed unit ball of $X^\ast$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $B^-_{X^\ast}$. Then $\struct {B^-_{X^\ast}, w^\ast}$ is sequentially compact.

title: Closed Unit Ball in Normed Vector Space is Balanced
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball of $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Then $B_X^-$ is balanced.

title: Closed Unit Ball in Normed Vector Space is Weakly Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $B^-$ be the closed unit ball in $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then $B^-$ is weakly closed.

title: Closed Unit Ball is Convex Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\map {B_1^-} 0$ be the closed unit ball in $X$. Then $\map {B_1^-} 0$ is convex.

title: Closed Unit Ball of Infinite-Dimensional Normed Vector Space has Empty Weak Interior
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$ that is infinite-dimensional. Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\operatorname {Int}_w$ be the interior taken in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $\map {\operatorname {Int}_w} {B_X^-} = \O$.

title: Closed Unit Ball of Space of Zero-Limit Sequences has no Extreme Points
snippet: Let $\struct {c_0, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the Banach space of zero-limit sequences. Let $B_{c_0}^-$ be the closed unit ball of $\struct {c_0, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$. Then $B_{c_0}^-$ has no extreme points.

title: Closed Unit Interval is Homeomorphic to Letter L
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line under the Euclidean metric. Let $\Bbb I := \closedint 0 1$ be the closed unit interval. Let $\mathsf L \subseteq \R^2$ denote the letter $L$: $\mathsf L := \closedint 0 1 \times \set 0 \cup \set 0 \times \closedint 0 1$ Then $\Bbb I$ and $\mathsf L$ are homeomorphic.

title: Closed Unit Interval is not Countably Infinite Union of Disjoint Closed Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbb I = \closedint 0 1$ be the closed unit interval. Then $\mathbb I$ cannot be expressed as the union of a countably infinite set of pairwise disjoint closed sets.

title: Closed Vector Subspace in Normed Vector Space is Weakly Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $Y$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$. Then $Y$ is weakly closed.

title: Closed Vector Subspace of Reflexive Banach Space is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a reflexive Banach space over $\GF$. Let $Y$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$. Then $Y$ is reflexive.

title: Closed Walk/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closed Walks ==

title: Closed and Bounded Subset of Normed Vector Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $K \subset X$ be a closed and bounded subset. Then $K$ is not necessarily compact.

title: Closed and Bounded Subspace is not necessarily Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Let $M_H = \struct {H, d_H}$ be the subspace of $M$ induced by $d$. Let $H$ be closed and bounded. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M_H$ is compact.

title: Closure (Metric Space)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closure in the context of a Metric Space ==

title: Closure (Topology)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Closure in the context of Topology ==

title: Closure Condition for Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff space : For all $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ne y$, there exists an open set $U$ such that $x \in U$ and $y \notin U^-$, where $U^-$ is the closure of $U$.

title: Closure Equals Union with Derivative
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $A^- = A \cup A'$ where $A'$ denotes the derivative of $A$ $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$.

title: Closure Operator Preserves Directed Suprema iff Image of Closure Operator Inherits Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $h: S \to S$ be a closure operator on $L$. Then $h$ preserves directed suprema $\struct {h \sqbrk S, \precsim}$ inherits directed suprema. where $h \sqbrk S$ denotes the image of $h$, $\mathord\precsim = \mathord\preceq \cap \paren {h \sqbrk S \times h \sqbrk S}$

title: Closure Operator does not Change Infimum of Subset of Image
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $c: S \to S$ be a closure operator on $L$. Let $X$ be a subset of $c\left[{S}\right]$ such that $X$ admits an infimum, where $c\left[{S}\right]$ denotes the image of $c$. Then $\inf X = c\left({\inf X}\right)$

title: Closure Operator from Closed Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $C \subseteq S$. Suppose that $C$ is a subset of $S$ with the property that every element of $S$ has a smallest successor in $C$. Let $\cl: S \to S$ be defined as follows: For $x \in S$: $\map \cl x = \map \min {C \cap x^\succeq}$ where $x^\succeq$ is the upper closure of $x$. That is, let $\map \cl x$ be the smallest successor of $x$ in $C$. Then: $\cl$ is a closure operator on $S$ The closed elements of $\cl$ are precisely the elements of $C$.

title: Closure Operator from Closed Sets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\CC$ be closed under arbitrary intersections: $\forall \KK \in \powerset \CC: \bigcap \KK \in \CC$ where $\bigcap \O$ is taken to be $S$. Define $\cl: \powerset S \to \CC$ by letting: $\map \cl T = \bigcap \set {C \in \CC: T \subseteq C}$ Then $\cl$ is a closure operator whose closed sets are the elements of $\CC$.

title: Closure and Complement Operations generate Monoid
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\AA$ be the set of subspaces of $T$. Let $\Phi: \AA \to \AA$ be the set of sequences of compositions of mappings consisting of: complementation relative to $S$ topological closure the identity mapping. Let $\otimes: \Phi \times \Phi \to \Phi$ denote the binary operation on $\Phi$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {\phi, \phi} \in \Phi \times \Phi: \phi \otimes \phi := \phi \circ \phi$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Closure for Finite Collection of Relations and Operations
snippet: Let $\RR_1, \RR_2, \ldots \RR_n$ be relations. Let $\SS_1, \SS_2, \ldots \SS_m$ be operations. Let $T$ be a small class. Let the image of $\RR_i$ over any small class $x$ be small classes for $1 \le i \le n$. Let the image of $\SS_i$ over any Cartesian product $x \times x$ be small classes for $1 \le i \le m$. Then there exists a small class $X$ such that: $(1): \quad$ $T \subseteq X$ $(2): \quad$ Each $\RR_i$ is closed $X$. Each $\SS_i$ is closed $X \times X$. $(3): \quad$ $X$ is the smallest small class satisfying conditions $(1)$ and $(2)$ above.

title: Closure in Infinite Particular Point Space is not Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Let $A \in \tau_p$ be open in $T$. Let $A^-$ be the closure of $A$. Then $A^-$ is not compact.

title: Closure in Weak-* Topology in terms of Annihilators
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Let $N$ be a linear subspace of $X^\ast$. Then: $\map {\cl_{w^\ast} } N = \paren { {}^\bot N}^\bot$ where: $\cl_{w^\ast}$ denotes closure in the weak-$\ast$ topology ${}^\bot N$ denotes the annihilator of $N \subseteq X^\ast$ $\paren { {}^\bot N}^\bot$ denotes the annihilator of ${}^\bot N \subseteq X$.

title: Closure is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\cl: S \to S$ be a closure operator. Let $x \in S$. Then $\map \cl x$ is a closed element of $S$ with respect to $\cl$.

title: Closure is Smallest Closed Successor
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f: S \to S$ be a closure operator on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $\map f x$ is the smallest closed element that succeeds $x$.

title: Closure of Absorbing Set is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be an absorbing set. Then $A^-$ is absorbing.

title: Closure of Balanced Set in Topological Vector Space is Balanced
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $B \subseteq X$ be a balanced set. Then the closure $B^-$ of $B$ is balanced.

title: Closure of Cartesian Product is Product of Closures
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $H \subseteq T_1$ and $K \subseteq T_2$. Then: $\map \cl {H \times K} = \map \cl H \times \map \cl K$ where $\map \cl H$, for example, denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Closure of Complement of Closure is Regular Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$. Let $A^-$ denote the closure of $A$ in $T$. Let $A'$ denote the complement of $A$ in $S$: $A' = S \setminus A$. Then $A^{-'-}$ is regular closed.

title: Closure of Connected Set is Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H$ be a connected set of $T$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$ in $T$. Then $H^-$ is connected in $T$.

title: Closure of Convex Balanced Hull as Intersection of Closed Convex Balanced Sets containing Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $\cl$ denote closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\operatorname {convbal}$ denote convex balanced hull. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty. Then: $\ds \map \cl {\map {\operatorname {convbal} } A} = \bigcap \set {C \supseteq A : C \text { is convex, balanced and closed} }$

title: Closure of Convex Hull is Smallest Closed Convex Set containing Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $\cl$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\operatorname {conv}$ denote convex hull. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty. Then $\map \cl {\map {\operatorname {conv} } A}$ is $\subseteq$-smallest closed convex set containing $A$.

title: Closure of Convex Set in Topological Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be convex. Then the closure $C^-$ of $C$ is convex.

title: Closure of Convex Set in Topological Vector Space with Non-Empty Interior coincides with Closure of Interior
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set with non-empty interior $\Int C$. Let $\cl$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then: $\map \cl C = \map \cl {\Int C}$

title: Closure of Convex Subset in Normed Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex subset of $X$. Let $C^-$ be the closure of $C$. Then $C^- \subseteq X$ is also a convex subset of $X$.

title: Closure of Dense-in-itself is Dense-in-itself in T1 Space
snippet: Let $T$ be a $T_1$ topological space. Let $A \subseteq T$. Let $A$ be dense-in-itself. Then the closure $A^-$ of $A$ is also dense-in-itself.

title: Closure of Densely-Defined Bounded Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator that is bounded. Let $\widetilde T : \HH \to \HH$ be the bounded linear operator extending $T$, given by Bounded Linear Transformation to Banach Space has Unique Extension to Closure of Domain. Then $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ is closable with closure $\tuple {\HH, \widetilde T}$.

title: Closure of Derivative is Derivative in T1 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_1$ topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then $A'^- = A'$ where $A'$ denotes the derivative of $A$ $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$.

title: Closure of Empty Set is Empty Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the closure of the empty set $\O$ in $T$ is $\O$.

title: Closure of Finite Union equals Union of Closures
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Let: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: H_i \subseteq T$ Then: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map \cl {H_i} = \map \cl {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}$ where $\map \cl {H_i}$ denotes the closure of $H_i$.

title: Closure of Hadamard Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \cdot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $S$. For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_S} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A \circ \mathbf B$ be defined as the Hadamard product of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$. The operation $\circ$ is closed on $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ $\cdot$ is closed on $\struct {S, \cdot}$.

title: Closure of Half-Open Real Interval is Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $H_1 = \hointl a b$ and $H_2 = \hointr a b$ be half-open intervals of $\R$. Then the closure of both $H_1$ and $H_2$ in $\R$ are the closed interval $\closedint a b$.

title: Closure of Image under Continuous Mapping is not necessarily Image of Closure
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $H \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a continuous mapping. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $f \sqbrk {\map \cl H} = \map \cl {f \sqbrk H}$

title: Closure of Infinite Subset of Finite Complement Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be an infinite subset of $S$. Then $H^- = S$ where $H^-$ is the closure of $S$.

title: Closure of Infinite Union may not equal Union of Closures
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be an infinite indexing set. Let $\family {H_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of a set $S$. Let $\ds H = \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} H_i$ be the union of $\family {H_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then it is not always the case that: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} \map \cl {H_i} = \map \cl {\bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} H_i}$ where $\map \cl {H_i}$ denotes the closure of $H_i$.

title: Closure of Integer Reciprocal Space
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $A^- = A \cup \set 0$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $\R$.

title: Closure of Interior of Closure of Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in R$ where $a < b < c$. Let $A$ be the union of the adjacent open intervals: $A := \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Then: $A^{- \circ -} = A^{\circ -} = A^- = \closedint a c$ where: $A^\circ$ is the interior of $A$ $A^-$ is the closure of $A$.

title: Closure of Intersection and Symmetric Difference imply Closure of Set Difference
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a system of sets such that for all $A, B \in \RR$: $(1): \quad A \cap B \in \RR$ $(2): \quad A \symdif B \in \RR$ where $\cap$ denotes set intersection and $\symdif$ denotes set symmetric difference. Then: $\forall A, B \in \RR: A \setminus B \in \RR$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Closure of Intersection and Symmetric Difference imply Closure of Union
snippet: Let $\R R$ be a system of sets such that for all $A, B \in \RR$: $(1): \quad A \cap B \in \RR$ $(2): \quad A \symdif B \in \RR$ where $\cap$ denotes set intersection and $\symdif$ denotes set symmetric difference. Then: $\forall A, B \in \RR: A \cup B \in \RR$ where $\cup$ denotes set union.

title: Closure of Intersection is Subset of Intersection of Closures
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\forall i \in I: H_i \subseteq T$. Then: $\ds \map \cl {\bigcap_I H_i} \subseteq \bigcap_I \map \cl {H_i}$ where $\map \cl {H_i}$ denotes the closure of $H_i$.

title: Closure of Intersection may not equal Intersection of Closures
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subsets of $S$. Let ${H_1}^-$ and ${H_2}^-$ denote the closures of $H_1$ and $H_2$ respectively. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\paren {H_1 \cap H_2}^- = {H_1}^- \cap {H_2}^-$

title: Closure of Intersection of Rationals and Irrationals is Empty Set
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\Q$ be the set of rational numbers. Then: $\paren {\Q \cap \paren {\R \setminus \Q} }^- = \O$ where: $\R \setminus \Q$ denotes the set of irrational numbers $\paren {\Q \cap \paren {\R \setminus \Q} }^-$ denotes the closure of $\Q \cap \paren {\R \setminus \Q}$.

title: Closure of Irrational Interval is Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real numbers under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\struct{\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the same topology. Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. Let $\Bbb I \subseteq \R$ be an interval of $\R$ Then the closure of the set: $\Bbb I \cap \paren {\R \setminus \Q}$ is the closed real interval $\closedint a b$.

title: Closure of Irrational Numbers is Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the same topology. Then: $\paren {\R \setminus \Q}^- = \R$ where $\paren {\R \setminus \Q}^-$ denotes the closure of $\R \setminus \Q$.

title: Closure of Irreducible Subspace is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $Y \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ which is irreducible in $T$. Then its closure $Y^-$ in $T$ is also irreducible in $T$.

title: Closure of Linear Subspace of Topological Vector Space is Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $Y$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Then the closure $Y^-$ of $Y$ is a linear subspace of $X$.

title: Closure of Non-Empty Bounded Subset of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $S \subseteq A$ be bounded in $M$. Then: $\map \cl S$ is also bounded in $M$. where $\map \cl S$ denotes the closure of $S$ in $M$.

title: Closure of Open 1-Ball in Standard Discrete Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be the standard discrete metric space on a set $A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {B_1} x$ be the open $1$-ball of $x$ in $M$. Then: $\map \cl {\map {B_1} x} = \set x$ while: $\set {y \in A: \map d {x, y} \le 1} = A$

title: Closure of Open Ball in Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be an open $\epsilon$-ball in $M$. Let $y \in \map \cl {\map {B_\epsilon} x}$, where $\cl$ denotes the closure of $\map {B_\epsilon} x$. Then $\map d {x, y} \le \epsilon$.

title: Closure of Open Ball may not equal Closed Ball of Same Radius
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball of $x$ of radius $\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Let $\map { {B_\epsilon}^-} x$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $x$ of radius $\epsilon$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\map \cl {\map {B_\epsilon} x} = \map { {B_\epsilon}^-} x$ where $\cl$ denotes closure.

title: Closure of Open Real Interval is Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\openint a b$ be an open interval of $\R$. Then the closure of $\openint a b$ is the closed interval $\closedint a b$.

title: Closure of Open Set of Closed Extension Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then: $U^- = S^*_p$ where $U^-$ denotes the closure of $U$ in $T^*_p$.

title: Closure of Open Set of Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $U \in \tau_p$ be open in $T$ such that $U \ne \O$. Then: $U^- = S$ where $U^-$ denotes the closure of $U$.

title: Closure of Pointwise Operation on Algebraic Structure
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $S \ne \O$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Let $f, g \in T^S$, that is, let $f: S \to T$ and $g: S \to T$ be mappings. Let $\oplus: T^S \to T^S$ be the pointwise operation on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\oplus$ is closed on $T^S$ $\struct {T, \circ}$ is closed.

title: Closure of Preimage under Continuous Mapping is not necessarily Preimage of Closure
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $H \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a continuous mapping. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $f^{-1} \sqbrk {\map \cl H} = \map \cl {f^{-1} \sqbrk H}$

title: Closure of Proper Ideal in Unital Banach Algebra is Proper Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $I$ be a proper ideal of $A$. Then $I^-$ is a proper ideal of $A$.

title: Closure of Range of Compact Linear Transformation is Separable
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $T \in \map {B_0} {H, K}$ be a compact linear transformation. Then $\map \cl {\Rng T}$ is separable.

title: Closure of Rational Interval is Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real numbers under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the same topology. Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. Let $\Bbb I \subseteq \R$ be an interval of $\R$ Then the closure of the set : $\Bbb I \cap \Q$ is the closed real interval $\closedint a b$.

title: Closure of Rational Numbers is Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the same topology. Then: $\Q^- = \R$ where $\Q^-$ denotes the closure of $\Q$.

title: Closure of Real Interval is Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $I$ be a non-empty real interval such that one of these holds: $I = \openint a b$ $I = \hointr a b$ $I = \hointl a b$ $I = \closedint a b$ Let $I^-$ denote the closure of $I$. Then $I^-$ is the closed real interval $\closedint a b$.

title: Closure of Self-Adjoint Subset of Banach *-Algebra is Self-Adjoint
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be self-adjoint. Then the closure $S^-$ of $S$ is self-adjoint.

title: Closure of Set of Condensation Points equals Itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $\paren {A^0}^- = A^0$ where $A^0$ denotes the set of condensation points of $A$ $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$

title: Closure of Set with Compact Closed Convex Hull in Hausdorff Locally Convex Space contains Extreme Points of Convex Hull
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a Hausdorff locally convex space over $\GF$ with its standard topology. Let $S \subseteq X$ be such that: $K = \map \cl {\map {\operatorname {conv} } S}$ is compact where $\operatorname {conv}$ denotes convex hull. Let $\map E K$ be the set of extreme points of $K$. Then $\map E K \subseteq \map \cl S$.

title: Closure of Singleton is Lower Closure of Element in Scott Topological Lattice
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a up-complete topological lattice with the Scott topology. Let $x \in S$. Then: $\set x^- = x^\preceq$ where $\set x^-$ denotes the topological closure of $\set x$ $x^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $x$.

title: Closure of Subalgebra in Normed Algebra is Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\GF$. Let $B$ be a subalgebra of $A$. Then $B^-$ is a subalgebra of $A$.

title: Closure of Subgroup is Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $H\leq G$ be a subgroup. Let $\overline H$ denote its closure. Then $\overline H$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Closure of Subset Contains Parallel Elements
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\sigma: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ denote the closure operator of $M$. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $x, y \in S$. If $x \in \map \sigma A$ and $y$ is parallel to $x$ then: $y \in \map \sigma A$

title: Closure of Subset contains Loop
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $x$ be a loop of $M$. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $x \in \map \sigma A$ where $\map \sigma A$ denotes the closure of $A$.

title: Closure of Subset in Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be an arbitrary subset of $S$. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ be the topological subspace on $H$. Let $A \subseteq H$ be an arbitrary subset of $H$. Then: $\map {\cl_H} A = H \cap \map \cl A$ where: $\map {\cl_H} A$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $T_H$ $\map \cl A$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $T$.

title: Closure of Subset of Closed Set of Metric Space is Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $F$ be a closed set of $M$. Let $H \subseteq F$ be a subset of $F$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$. Then $H^- \subseteq F$.

title: Closure of Subset of Closed Set of Topological Space is Subset
snippet: Let $T$ = $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F$ be a closed set of $T$. Let $H \subseteq F$ be a subset of $F$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$. Then $H^- \subseteq F$.

title: Closure of Subset of Double Pointed Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_S}$ be a topological space. Let $D$ be a doubleton endowed with the indiscrete topology. Let $\struct {S \times D, \tau}$ be the double pointed topology on $S$. Let $X \subseteq S \times D$ be a subset of $S \times D$. Then the closure of $X$ in $\tau$ is: $\map \cl X = \map \cl {\map {\pr_1} X} \times D$ where $\pr_1$ denotes the first projection on $S \times D$.

title: Closure of Subset of Indiscrete Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $\O \subsetneq H \subseteq S$ (that is, let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $T$). Then: $H^- = H^{- \circ} = H^{- \circ -} = S$ where: $H^\circ$ denotes the interior of $H$ $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Closure of Subset of Metric Space by Convergent Sequence
snippet: == Lemma == Let $M$ be a metric space. Let $C \subseteq M$. Let $x \in M$. Let $\map \cl C$ denote the closure of $C$ in $T$. Then $x \in \map \cl C$ there exists a sequence $\sequence {x_n}$ in $C$ which converges to $x$.

title: Closure of Subset of Metric Space is Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$. Then $H^-$ is a closed set of $M$.

title: Closure of Subset of Metric Space is Intersection of Closed Supersets
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$. Then $H^-$ is the intersection of all closed sets of $M$ of which $H$ is a subset.

title: Closure of Subspace of Normed Vector Space is Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a subspace of $X$. Let $Y^-$ be the closure of $Y$. Then $Y^- \subseteq X$ is also a subspace of $X$.

title: Closure of Symmetric Subset of Normed Vector Space is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $A \subseteq X$ be symmetric. Then the topological closure of $A$ is symmetric.

title: Closure of Topological Closure equals Closure
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then: $\map \cl {\map \cl H} = \map \cl H$ where $\cl$ denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Closure of Totally Bounded Subspace is Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space. Let $A \subseteq M$ be totally bounded. Let $\cl$ be the topological closure. Then $\map \cl A$ is totally bounded.

title: Closure of Union and Complement imply Closure of Set Difference
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a system of sets on a universe $\mathbb U$ such that for all $A, B \in \RR$: $(1): \quad A \cup B \in \RR$ $(2): \quad \map \complement A \in \RR$ where $\cup$ denotes set union and $\complement$ denotes complement (relative to $\mathbb U$). Then: $\forall A, B \in \RR: A \setminus B \in \RR$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Closure of Union contains Union of Closures
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\mathbb H$ be a set of subsets of $S$. That is, let $\mathbb H \subseteq \powerset S$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then the union of the closures of the elements of $\mathbb H$ is a subset of the closure of the union of $\mathbb H$: $\ds \bigcup_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} \map \cl H \subseteq \map \cl {\bigcup_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} H}$

title: Closure of Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in R$ where $a < b < c$. Let $A$ be the union of the two adjacent open intervals: $A := \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Then: $A^- = \closedint a c$ where: $A^-$ is the closure of $A$.

title: Closure of Union of Singleton Rationals is Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Let $B_\alpha$ be the singleton containing the rational number $\alpha$. Then the closure in the set of real numbers $\R$ of the union of all $B_\alpha$ is $\R$ itself: $\ds \map \cl {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in \Q} B_\alpha} = \R$

title: Closure of product equals product of closures
snippet: Let $\set {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an arbitrary family of topological spaces. Let: $A_i \subset X_i$ for each $i \in I$. Let $X = \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ have the product topology. Then: $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \overline{A_i} = \overline {\prod_{i \mathop \in I} A_i}$

title: Closure of von Neumann-Bounded Subset of Topological Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $E$ be a von Neumann-bounded subset of $X$. Then the closure $E^-$ of $E$ is von Neumann-bounded.

title: Closure under Chain Unions with Choice Function implies Elements with no Immediate Extension
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets which: is closed under chain unions has a choice function $C$ for its union $\bigcup S$. Let $b \in S$. Then $b$ is the subset of an element of $S$ which has no immediate extension in $S$.

title: Closures of Elements of Locally Finite Set is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\AA$ be a locally finite set of subsets of $T$. Then: $\set{A^- : A \in \AA}$ is locally finite in $T$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $T$.

title: Cluster Analysis/Examples
snippet: == Examples from Cluster Analysis ==

title: Cluster Point of Convergent Net in Hausdorff Space is Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $x \in X$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a convergent net with limit $x$. Let $y$ be a cluster point of $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Then $x = y$.

title: Cluster Point of Ultrafilter is Unique
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\FF$ be an ultrafilter on $S$. Let $x \in S$ be a cluster point of $\FF$. Then there is no point $y \in S: y \ne x$ such that $y$ is also a cluster point of $\FF$.

title: Cluster Sample/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cluster Samples ==

title: Co-Countable Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $X$ be an uncountable set. Let $\Sigma$ be the $\sigma$-algebra of countable sets on $X$. Then the co-countable measure $\mu$ on $X$ is a measure.

title: Co-Countable Measure is Probability Measure
snippet: Let $X$ be an uncountable set. Let $\AA$ be the $\sigma$-algebra of countable sets on $X$. Then the co-countable measure $\mu$ on $X$ is a probability measure.

title: Coarseness Relation on Topologies is Partial Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\mathbb T$ be the set of all topologies on $S$. Let $\le$ be the relation on $\mathbb T$ defined as: $\forall \tau_1, \tau_2 \in \mathbb T: \tau_1 \le \tau_2$ $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$. Then $\le$ is a partial ordering on $\mathbb T$.

title: Coarser Between Generator Set and Filter is Generator Set of Filter
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $F$ be a filter on $L$. Let $G$ be a generator set of $F$. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$ such that $G$ is coarser than $A$ and $A$ is coarser than $F$. Then $A$ is generator set of $F$.

title: Coarser Topology than Compact Space is Compact
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on $S$ such that $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$: $\tau_1 \subseteq \tau_2$ Let $\struct {S, \tau_2}$ be a compact space. Then $\struct {S, \tau_1}$ is also compact.

title: Code/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Codes ==

title: Code Number for Non-Negative Integer is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $c : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\map c n = m$ where $m$ is the code number for the integer $n : \Z$. Then $c$ is a primitive recursive function.

title: Code Number for Non-Positive Integer is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $c : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\map c n = m$ where $m$ is the code number for the integer $-n : \Z$. Then $c$ is a primitive recursive function.

title: Coded Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Coded Data ==

title: Codimension of Intersection of Finitely Many Vector Subspaces is Bounded Above by Sum of Codimensions
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n$ be vector subspaces of $X$. Let: $\ds U = \bigcap_{j \mathop = 1}^n U_j$ Then: $\ds \map {\operatorname {codim} } U \le \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \map {\operatorname {codim} } {U_j}$ where $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n$ denotes the cardinal sum.

title: Codomain of Bijection is Domain of Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Let $f^{-1}: T \to S$ be the inverse of $f$. Then the domain of $f^{-1}$ equals the codomain of $f$.

title: Codomain of Composite Relation
snippet: Let $\RR_2 \circ \RR_1$ be a composite relation. Then the codomain of $\RR_2 \circ \RR_1$ is the codomain of $\RR_2$: $\Cdm {\RR_2 \circ \RR_1} = \Cdm {\RR_2}$

title: Codomain of Internal Direct Isomorphism is Subset Product of Factors
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure with $1$ operation. Let $\struct {A, \circ {\restriction_A} }$ and $\struct {B, \circ {\restriction_B} }$ be closed algebraic substructures of $\struct {S, \circ}$, where $\circ {\restriction_A}$ and $\circ {\restriction_B}$ are the operations induced by the restrictions of $\circ$ to $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be the internal direct product of $A$ and $B$. Then $S$ is the subset product of $A$ and $B$: $S = A \circ B$

title: Coefficient of Kinetic Friction is usually Less than Coefficient of Static Friction
snippet: == Physical Law == Let $B$ be a body resting on a rough surface $S$. Let $\mu_k$ and $\mu_s$ denote the coefficient of kinetic fiction and coefficient of static fiction between $B$ and $S$ respectively. Then it is typically the case that $\mu_k < \mu_s$.

title: Coefficient of Restitution for Elastic Collision is 1
snippet: Let two solid bodies $B_1$ and $B_2$ be in an elastic collision. Let $e$ be the coefficient of restitution of that elastic collision. Then: $e = 1$

title: Coefficient of Restitution is between 0 and 1
snippet: Let two solid bodies $B_1$ and $B_2$ be in collision. Let $e$ be the coefficient of restitution of that collision. Then: $0 \le e \le 1$

title: Coefficients in Linear Combination forming GCD are Coprime
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Let there exist integers $x$ and $y$ such that: $a x + b y = \gcd \set {a, b}$ where $\gcd \set {a, b}$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$. Then: $x \perp y$ where $\perp$ denotes coprimality.

title: Coefficients of Coordinates in General Equation of Plane Form Vector Perpendicular to Plane
snippet: Let $P$ be a plane that is described by the general equation: $\alpha_1 x + \alpha_2 y + \alpha_3 z = \gamma$ Let $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf k$ denote the unit vectors in the positive directions of the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis, respectively. Then the vector: $\bsalpha = \alpha_1 \mathbf i + \alpha_2 \mathbf j + \alpha_3 \mathbf k$ is perpendicular to $P$.

title: Coefficients of Cosine Terms in Convergent Trigonometric Series
snippet: Let $\map S x$ be a trigonometric series which converges to $\map f x$ on the interval $\openint \alpha {\alpha + 2 \pi}$: $\map f x = \dfrac {a_0} 2 + \ds \sum_{m \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {a_m \cos m x + b_m \sin m x}$ Then: $\forall n \in \Z_{\ge 0}: a_n = \dfrac 1 \pi \ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \map f x \cos n x \rd x$

title: Coefficients of Polynomial Product
snippet: Let $J$ be a set. Let $p_1, \ldots p_n$ be polynomial forms in the indeterminates $\set {X_j : j \in J}$ over a commutative ring $R$. Suppose that for each $i$ with $1 \le i \le n$, we have, for appropriate $a_{i, k} \in R$: $p_i = \ds \sum_{k \mathop \in Z} a_{i, k} X^k$ where $Z$ comprises the multiindices of natural numbers over $J$. Then: $\ds \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n p_i = \sum_{k \mathop \in Z} b_k X^k$ where: $\ds b_k := \sum_{k_1 + \cdots + k_n \mathop = k} \paren {\prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n a_{i, k_i} }$

title: Coefficients of Polynomial add to 0 iff 1 is a Root
snippet: Let $\map E x$ be the equation in $x$ represented as: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n a_j x^j = 0$ where the $a_j$s are constants. Then $1$ is a root of $\map E x$ : $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n a_j = 0$ That is, $1$ is a root of $\map E x$ all the coefficients of the polynomial in $x$ sum to zero.

title: Coefficients of Product of Two Polynomials
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $f, g \in R \sqbrk x$ be polynomials over $R$. For a natural number $n \ge 0$, let: $a_n$ be the coefficient of the monomial $x^n$ in $f$. $b_n$ be the coefficient of the monomial $x^n$ in $g$.

title: Coefficients of Sine Terms in Convergent Trigonometric Series
snippet: Let $\map S x$ be a trigonometric series which converges to $\map f x$ on the interval $\openint \alpha {\alpha + 2 \pi}$: $\map f x = \dfrac {a_0} 2 + \ds \sum_{m \mathop = 1}^\infty \left({a_m \cos m x + b_m \sin m x}\right)$ Then: $\forall n \in \Z_{\ge 0}: b_n = \dfrac 1 \pi \ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \map f x \sin n x \rd x$

title: Coequalizer is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $q: D \to Q$ be the coequalizer of two morphisms $f, g: C \to D$. Then $q$ is an epimorphism.

title: Cofactor Sum Identity
snippet: Let $J_n$ be the $n \times n$ matrix of all ones. Let $A$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $A_{ij}$ denote the cofactor of element $\tuple {i, j}$ in $\map \det A$, $1 \le i, j \le n$. Then: $\ds \map \det {A - J_n} = \map \det A - \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_{i j} $

snippet: A and a are homeomorphic.

title: Coffee Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == The task of making coffee is too complex to accomplish unless one has first drunk a cup of coffee.

title: Cofinal Limit Ordinals
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $\mathrm {cof}$ denote the cofinal relation. Let $K_{II}$ denote the class of all limit ordinals. Then: $\map {\mathrm {cof} } {x, y} \implies \paren {x \in K_{II} \iff y \in K_{II} }$

title: Cofinal Ordinal Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then $x$ is cofinal to itself. That is: $\operatorname{cof} \left({x, x}\right)$

title: Cofinal Ordinal Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Let $\operatorname {cof}$ denote the cofinal relation. Then: $\map {\operatorname {cof} } {x, y} \land \map {\operatorname {cof} } {y, z} \implies \map {\operatorname {cof} } {x, z}$

title: Cofinal to Zero iff Ordinal is Zero
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $\operatorname{cof}$ denote the cofinal relation. Let $0$ denote the zero ordinal. {{item|(1):|$\map {\operatorname{cof} } {x, 0}$}} {{item|(2):|$\map {\operatorname{cof} } {0, x}$}}

title: Cofunction of Cofunction
snippet: Let $g$ be a cofunction of $f$. Then $f$ is a cofunction of $g$. That is, cofunctions exist in pairs.

title: Coherent Sequence Converges to P-adic Integer
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ be a coherent sequence. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then the sequence $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ converges to some $x \in \Z_p$. That is, there exists $x \in \Z_p$ such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \alpha_n = x$

title: Coherent Sequence is Partial Sum of P-adic Expansion
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ be a coherent sequence. Then there exists a unique $p$-adic expansion of the form: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty d_n p^n$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: \alpha_n = \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n d_i p^i$

title: Collection of All Ordered Sets is not Set
snippet: Let $\mathrm {OS}$ denote the collection of all ordered sets. Then $\mathrm {OS}$ is not a set.

title: Collection of Sets Equivalent to Set Containing Empty Set is Proper Class
snippet: Let $S = \set \O$ be the singleton whose element is the empty set. Let $C$ be the collection of all sets which are equivalent to $S$. $C$ is a proper class.

title: Column Equivalence is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Column equivalence is an equivalence relation.

title: Column Operation has Inverse
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a column operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists another column operation $\Gamma'$ which transforms $\mathbf B$ back to $\mathbf A$.

title: Column Operation is Equivalent to Post-Multiplication by Product of Elementary Matrices
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a column operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists a unique nonsingular square matrix $\mathbf K$ of order $n$ such that: $\mathbf A \mathbf K = \mathbf B$ where $\mathbf K$ is the product of a finite sequence of elementary column matrices.

title: Column Rank of Matrix equals Rank of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix. The column rank of $\mathbf A$ is equal to the rank of $\mathbf A$.

title: Column Rank of Matrix equals Row Rank
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix. The column rank of $\mathbf A$ is equal to the row rank of $\mathbf A$.

title: Columns of Pascal's Triangle contain Simplicial Polytopic Numbers
snippet: The columns of Pascal's triangle contain the simplicial polytopic numbers: Column $0$: repeated instances of number $1$ Column $1$: the (strictly) positive integers Column $2$: the triangular numbers Column $3$: the tetrahedral numbers Column $4$: the pentatope numbers and so on.

title: Comma Category is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ and $G : \mathbf E \to \mathbf C$ be covariant functors. Let $\paren{G \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $F$. Then: $\paren{G \downarrow F}$ is a metacategory.

title: Common Divisor Divides Difference
snippet: Let $c$ be a common divisor of two integers $a$ and $b$. That is: $a, b, c \in \Z: c \divides a \land c \divides b$ Then: $c \divides \paren {a - b}$

title: Common Divisor Divides GCD
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ such that not both of $a$ and $b$ are zero. Let $c$ be any common divisor of $a$ and $b$. That is, let $c \in \Z: c \divides a, c \divides b$. Then: $c \divides \gcd \set {a, b}$ where $\gcd \set {a, b}$ is the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$.

title: Common Divisor Divides Integer Combination
snippet: == Corollary to Common Divisor in Integral Domain Divides Linear Combination == Let $c$ be a common divisor of two integers $a$ and $b$. That is: $a, b, c \in \Z: c \divides a \land c \divides b$ Then $c$ divides any integer combination of $a$ and $b$: $\forall p, q \in \Z: c \divides \paren {p a + q b}$

title: Common Divisor in Integral Domain Divides Linear Combination
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Let $c$ be a common divisor of two elements $a$ and $b$ of $D$. That is: $a, b, c \in D: c \divides a \land c \divides b$ Then: $\forall p, q \in D: c \divides \paren {p \times a + q \times b}$

title: Common Factor Cancelling in Congruence
snippet: Let $a, b, x, y, m \in \Z$. Let: $a x \equiv b y \pmod m$ and $a \equiv b \pmod m$ where $a \equiv b \pmod m$ denotes that $a$ is congruent modulo $m$ to $b$. Then: $x \equiv y \pmod {m / d}$ where $d = \gcd \set {a, m}$.

title: Common Logarithm of Number in Scientific Notation
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive real number which is presented (possibly approximated) in scientific notation as: $n = a \times 10^d$ where: $1 \le a < 10$ $d \in \Z$ is an integer. Then: $\log_{10} n = \log_{10} a + d$ where: $0 \le \log_{10} a < 1$

title: Common Ratio in Integer Geometric Sequence is Rational

title: Common Ratio in Rational Geometric Sequence is Rational
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be a geometric sequence whose terms are rational. Then the common ratio of $\sequence {a_k}$ is rational.
