title: Commutation Property in Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then $x$ and $y$ commute $x \circ y \circ x^{-1} = y$.

title: Commutation of Inverses in Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x$ and $y$ are both invertible. Then $x$ commutes with $y$ $x^{-1}$ commutes with $y^{-1}$.

title: Commutation with Group Elements implies Commuation with Product with Inverse
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a, b, c \in G$ such that $a$ commutes with both $b$ and $c$. Then $a$ commutes with $b c^{-1}$.

title: Commutation with Inverse in Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $y$ is invertible. Then $x$ commutes with $y$ $x$ commutes with $y^{-1}$.

title: Commutative B-Algebra Implies (zy)(zx)=xy
snippet: Let $\struct {B, \circ}$ be a commutative $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in X: \paren {z \circ y} \circ \paren {z \circ x} = x \circ y$

title: Commutative B-Algebra Induces Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\left({X, \circ }\right)$ be a commutative $B$-algebra. Let $*$ be the binary operation on $X$ defined as: $\forall a, b \in X: a * b := a \circ \left({0 \circ b}\right)$ Then the algebraic structure $\left({X, *}\right)$ is an abelian group such that: $\forall x \in X: 0 \circ x$ is the inverse element of $x$ under $*$. That is: $\forall a, b \in X: a * b^{-1} := a \circ b$

title: Commutative B-Algebra is Entropic Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {G, *}$ be a commutative $B$-algebra. Then $\struct {G, *}$ is an entropic structure.

title: Commutative Diagram/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Commutative Diagrams ==

title: Commutative Law of Addition
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\N, \Z, \Q, \R$ and $\C$. Then: $\forall x, y \in \mathbb F: x + y = y + x$ That is, the operation of addition on the standard number sets is commutative.

title: Commutative Law of Multiplication
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\N, \Z, \Q, \R$ and $\C$. Then: $\forall x, y \in \mathbb F: x + y = y + x$ That is, the operation of multiplication on the standard number sets is commutative.

title: Commutative Linear Transformation is G-Module Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\rho: G \to \GL V$ be a representation. Let $f: V \to V$ be a linear transformation. Let: $\forall g \in G: \map \rho g \circ f = f \circ \map \rho g$ Then $f: V \to V$ is a $G$-module homomorphism.

title: Commutative Semigroup is Entropic Structure
snippet: A commutative semigroup is an entropic structure.

title: Commutative and Associative Product on Space of Distributions does not Exist
snippet: Let $\map {\DD'} \R$ be the distribution space. Let $\alpha \in \map {C^\infty} \R$ be a smooth function. Let $\circ$ be a product operation on $\map {\DD'} \R$. Suppose: $\forall T \in \map {\DD'} \R : \forall \alpha \in \map {C^\infty} \R : \alpha \circ T := \alpha \cdot T$ where $\cdot$ stands for multiplication of Schwartz distribution by a smooth function. Suppose $\circ$ is commutative and associative. Then $\circ$ does not exist.

title: Commutative and Unitary Ring with 2 Ideals is Field
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be such that the only ideals of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are: $\set {0_R}$ and: $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ itself. That is, such that $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ has no non-null proper ideals. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ is a field.

title: Commutativity of Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ_g}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_h}$ be groups. Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G, \circ_g}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_h}$, where the operation $\circ$ is defined as: $\tuple {g_1, h_1} \circ \tuple {g_2, h_2} = \tuple {g_1 \circ_g g_2, h_1 \circ_h h_2}$ Let $\struct {H \times G, \star}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {H, \circ_h}$ and $\struct {G, \circ_g}$, where the operation $\star$ is defined as: $\tuple {h_1, g_1} \star \tuple {h_2, g_2} = \tuple {h_1 \circ_h h_2, g_1 \circ_g g_2}$ The group direct product $\struct {G…

title: Commutativity of Hadamard Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \cdot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $S$. For $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in \map {\MM_S} {m, n}$, let $\mathbf A \circ \mathbf B$ be defined as the Hadamard product of $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$. The operation $\circ$ is commutative on $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ $\cdot$ is commutative on $\struct {S, \cdot}$.

title: Commutativity of Incidence Matrix with its Transpose for Symmetric Design
snippet: Let $A$ be the incidence matrix of a symmetric design. Then: $A A^\intercal = A^\intercal A$ where $A^\intercal$ is the transpose of $A$.

title: Commutativity of Parameters of Beta Function
snippet: Let $\map \Beta {x, y}$ be the Beta function. Then: $\map \Beta {x, y} = \map \Beta {y, x}$

title: Commutativity of Powers in Group
snippet: Let $\left ({G, \circ}\right)$ be a group. Let $a, b \in G$ such that $a$ and $b$ commute. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z: a^m \circ b^n = b^n \circ a^m$ This can be expressed in additive notation in the group $\left ({G, +}\right)$ as: $\forall m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = n b + m a$

title: Commutativity of Powers in Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $a, b \in S$ be invertible elements for $\circ$ that also commute. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z: a^m \circ b^n = b^n \circ a^m$

title: Commutativity of Powers in Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $a, b \in S$ both be cancellable elements of $S$. Then: $\forall m, n \in \N_{>0}: a \circ b = b \circ a \implies a^m \circ b^n = b^n \circ a^m$ but it is not necessarily the case that: $\forall m, n \in \N_{>0}: a^m \circ b^n = b^n \circ a^m \implies a \circ b = b \circ a$

title: Commutativity of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a commutative topological ring. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is a commutative ring

title: Commutativity of Spectrum in Algebra over Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ be an algebra over $\C$. Let $x, y \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} {x y}$ and $\map {\sigma_A} {y x}$ be the spectrum of $x y$ and $y x$ respectively in $A$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} {x y} \cup \set 0 = \map {\sigma_A} {y x} \cup \set 0$

title: Commutator is Identity iff Elements Commute
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $\sqbrk {x, y}$ denote the commutator of $x$ and $y$. Then $\sqbrk {x, y} = e$ $x$ and $y$ commute.

title: Commutator of Group Element with Identity is Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\sqbrk {g, h}$ denote the commutator of $g$ and $h$. Then: $\sqbrk {g, e} = e = \sqbrk {e, g}$

title: Commutator of Quotient Group Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $\sqbrk {x, y}$ denote the commutator of $x, y \in G$: $\sqbrk {x, y} = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ Then: $\forall x, y \in G: \sqbrk {x N, y N} = \sqbrk {x, y} N$ where $x N$ and $y N$ are left cosets of $N$, and so elements of the quotient group $G / N$ of $G$ by $N$.

title: Commutator of x and Distributional Derivative acting on Distribution
snippet: Let $T \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be a Schwartz distribution. Let: $\sqbrk {x, \dfrac \d {\d x} } T := x \dfrac {\d T} {\d x} - \dfrac {\d \paren {x T} } {\d x}$ where derivatives are to be understood in the distributional sense. Then: $\sqbrk {x, \dfrac \d {\d x} } T = - T$

title: Commutator on Algebra is Alternating Bilinear Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ be an algebra over a ring. Then the commutator on $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ is an alternating bilinear mapping: $\forall a, b \in A_R: \sqbrk {a, b} = -\sqbrk {b, a}$

title: Commutators are Identity iff Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. For $g, h \in G$, let $\sqbrk {g, h}$ denote the commutator of $g$ and $h$. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is abelian : $\forall g, h \in G: \sqbrk {g, h} = e$

title: Compact Closure is Directed
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ is directed where $x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$.

title: Compact Closure is Increasing
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \preceq y$ Then $x^{\mathrm{compact} } \subseteq y^{\mathrm{compact} }$ where $x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$.

title: Compact Closure is Intersection of Lower Closure and Compact Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^{\mathrm {compact} } = x^\preceq \cap \map K L$ where $x^{\mathrm {compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$, $x^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $x$, $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$.

title: Compact Closure is Set of Finite Subsets in Lattice of Power Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \preceq}$ be the lattice of power set of $X$ where $\mathord\preceq = \mathord\subseteq \cap \powerset X \times \powerset X$ Let $x \in \powerset X$. Then $x^{\mathrm{compact} } = \map {\operatorname{Fin} } x$ where $\map {\operatorname{Fin} } x$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $x$.

title: Compact Closure is Subset of Way Below Closure
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^{\mathrm {compact} } \subseteq x^\ll$ where $x^{\mathrm {compact} }$ denotes the compact closure of $x$, $x^\ll$ denotes the way below closure of $x$.

title: Compact Closure of Element is Principal Ideal on Compact Subset iff Element is Compact
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below algebraic join semilattice. Let $P = \struct {\map K L, \precsim}$ be an ordered subset of $L$ where $\map K L$ denotes the compact subset of $L$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^{\mathrm{compact} }$ is principal ideal in $P$ $x$ is a compact element.

title: Compact Complement Space is T0

snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact complement space. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement space on $\R$. Then $T$ is not a normal space.

title: Compact Complement Space is not Regular
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is not a regular space.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $\tau$ is coarser than the usual (Euclidean) topology in $\R$.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a compact space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology. Then $T$ is a connected space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a first-countable space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement space on $\R$. Then $T$ is an irreducible space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a locally connected space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a separable space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is a sequentially compact space.

title: Compact Complement Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement space. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $T$.

title: Compact Complement Topology is not Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Then $T$ is not an ultraconnected space.

title: Compact Convergence Implies Local Uniform Convergence if Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly locally compact topological space. Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n: X \to M$. Let $f_n$ converge compactly to $f: X \to M$. Then $f_n$ converges locally uniformly to $f$.

title: Compact Convex Set with Nonempty Interior is Homeomorphic to Cone on Boundary
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$. Let $T \subseteq \R^n$ be a compact convex subset of real Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose the interior of $T$ is non-empty. Then, $T$ is homeomorphic to the cone on its boundary.

title: Compact Convex Sets with Nonempty Interior are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$. Let $T, T' \subseteq \R^n$ be compact convex subsets of real Euclidean $n$-space. Then, $T$ is homeomorphic to $T'$.

title: Compact Element iff Existence of Finite Subset that Element equals Intersection and Includes Subset
snippet: Let $X, E$ be sets. Let $P = \struct {\powerset X, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set where $\powerset X$ denotes the power set of $X$ $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\powerset X \times \powerset X}$ Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a continuous lattice subframe of $P$. Then $E$ is compact element in $L$ : $\exists F \in \map {\mathit {Fin} } X: E = \bigcap \set {I \in S: F \subseteq I} \land F \subseteq E$ where $\map {\mathit {Fin} } X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

title: Compact Element iff Principal Ideal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $P = \struct {\map {\operatorname {Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set where $\map {\operatorname {Ids} } L$ denotes the set of all ideals in $L$, $\mathord\precsim = \mathord\subseteq \cap \paren {\map {\operatorname {Ids} } L \times \map {\operatorname {Ids} } L}$ Let $x \in \map {\operatorname {Ids} } L$ Then $x$ is compact element $x$ is principal ideal in $L$.

title: Compact First-Countable Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact first-countable topological space. Then every infinite sequence in $S$ has a convergent subsequence; that is, $T$ is sequentially compact.

title: Compact Hausdorff Space is Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space which is compact. Then $T$ is locally compact.

title: Compact Hausdorff Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Compact Hausdorff Space is not necessarily T5
snippet: A compact $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space is not necessarily a $T_5$ space.

title: Compact Hausdorff Space with no Isolated Points is Uncountable/Lemma
Compact Hausdorff Topology is Maximally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space which is compact. Then $\tau$ is maximally compact.

title: Compact Hausdorff Topology is Minimal Hausdorff
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space which is compact. Then $\tau$ is the minimal subset of the power set $\powerset S$ such that $T$ is a Hausdorff space.

title: Compact Hermitian Operator has Countable Point Spectrum
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $T \in \map {B_0} \HH$ be a compact Hermitian operator. {{explain|What is $\map {B_0} \HH$?}} Then its point spectrum $\map {\sigma_p} T$ is countable.

title: Compact Idempotent is of Finite Rank
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $T \in \map {B_0} H$ be a compact linear operator. Let $T$ be idempotent. Then: $T \in \map {B_{00} } H$ that is, $T$ is a bounded finite rank operator.

title: Compact Linear Transformation is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $\map {B_0} {\HH, \KK}$ be the space of compact linear transformations $\HH \to \KK$. Let $\map B {\HH, \KK}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $\HH \to \KK$. Let $T \in \map {B_0} {\HH, \KK}$. Then $T \in \map B {\HH, \KK}$. That is: $\map {B_0} {\HH, \KK} \subseteq \map B {\HH, \KK}$

title: Compact Linear Transformation is Weakly Compact
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be compact linear transformation. Then $T$ is weakly compact.

title: Compact Linear Transformations Composed with Bounded Linear Operator
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $T \in \map {B_0} {H, K}$ be a compact linear transformation. Let $A \in \map B H, B \in \map B K$ be bounded linear operators. Then the compositions $T A$ and $B T$ are also compact linear transformations.

title: Compact Metric Space is Complete
snippet: A compact metric space is complete.

title: Compact Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a compact metric space. Then $\struct {X, d}$ is separable.

title: Compact Metric Space is Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space which is compact. Then $M$ is totally bounded.

title: Compact Operator on Hilbert Space Direct Sum
snippet: Let $\sequence {\HH_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of Hilbert spaces. Denote by $\HH = \bigoplus_{n \mathop \in \N} \HH_n$ their Hilbert space direct sum. For each $n \in \N$, let $T_n \in \map B {\HH_n}$ be a bounded linear operator. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} \norm {T_n} < \infty$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \, }$ signifies the norm on bounded linear operators.

title: Compact Set of Irrational Numbers is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $S \subseteq \R \setminus \Q$ be a compact set of $\R \setminus \Q$. Then $S$ is nowhere dense in $\R \setminus \Q$.

title: Compact Set of Rational Numbers is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $S \subseteq \Q$ be a compact set of $\Q$. Then $S$ is nowhere dense in $\Q$.

title: Compact Sets in Countable Complement Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then the compact sets of $T$ are exactly the finite subsets of $S$.

title: Compact Sets in Fortissimo Space
snippet: A subset of a Fortissimo space is compact it is finite.

title: Compact Sets of Double Pointed Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_S}$ be a topological space. Let $D$ be a doubleton endowed with the indiscrete topology. Let $\struct {S \times D, \tau}$ be the double pointed topology on $S$. Then $X \subseteq S \times D$ is compact in $\tau$ for some compact set $C$ of $\tau_S$: $\map {\pr_1} X = C$ where $\pr_1$ denotes the first projection on $S \times D$.

title: Compact Space in Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Then $\set p$ is compact in $T$.

title: Compact Space is Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact space. Then $T$ is a countably compact space.

title: Compact Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Every compact space is also a Lindelöf space.

title: Compact Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact space. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Compact Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \tau}$ be a compact space. Then $\struct {K, \tau}$ is a pseudocompact space

title: Compact Space is Sigma-Compact
snippet: Every compact space is also a $\sigma$-compact space.

title: Compact Space is Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact space. Then $T$ is a strongly locally compact space.

title: Compact Space is Strongly Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact topological space. Then $T$ is strongly paracompact.

title: Compact Space is Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact topological space. Then $T$ is a weakly locally compact.

title: Compact Space is Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact space. Then $T$ is a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact space.

title: Compact Space is not necessarily Sequentially Compact
snippet: There exists at least one example of a compact topological space which is not also a sequentially compact space.

title: Compact Space satisfies Finite Intersection Axiom
Compact Subset is Bounded Below Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $P = \left({K\left({L}\right), \precsim}\right)$ be an ordered subset of $L$, where $K\left({L}\right)$ denotes the compact subset of $L$. Then $P$ is a bounded below join semilattice.

title: Compact Subset is Join Subsemilattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map K L$ be a compact subset of $L$. Then $\map K L$ is join subsemilattice: $\forall x, y \in \map K L: x \vee y \in \map K L$

title: Compact Subset of Compact Space is not necessarily Closed
snippet: A compact subset of a compact space is not necessarily closed.

title: Compact Subset of Hilbert Sequence Space is Closed
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Let $H$ be a compact subset of $\ell^2$. Then $H$ is closed in $\ell^2$.

title: Compact Subset of Hilbert Sequence Space is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Let $H$ be a compact subset of $\ell^2$. Then $H$ is nowhere dense in $\ell^2$.

title: Compact Subset of Normed Vector Space is Closed and Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}}$ be a normed vector space. Let $K \subset X$ be a compact subset. Then $K$ is closed and bounded.

title: Compact Subsets of T3 Spaces
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be compact in $T$. Then for each $U \in \tau$ such that $A \subseteq U$: $\exists V \in \tau: A \subseteq V \subseteq V^- \subseteq U$ where $V^-$ denotes the closure of $V$.

title: Compact Subspace of Hausdorff Space is Closed
snippet: Let $H = \struct {A, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $C$ be a compact subspace of $H$. Then $C$ is closed in $H$.

title: Compact Subspace of Linearly Ordered Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a non-empty subset of $X$. Then $Y$ is a compact subspace of $\struct {X, \tau}$ both of the following hold: $(1): \quad$ For every non-empty $S \subseteq Y$, $S$ has a supremum and an infimum in $X$. $(2): \quad$ For every non-empty $S \subseteq Y$: $\sup S, \inf S \in Y$.

title: Compact Subspace of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $C$ be a subspace of $M$. If $C$ is compact, then it is bounded.

title: Compact Subspace of Metric Space is Sequentially Compact in Itself
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $C \subseteq M$ be a subspace of $M$ such that $C$ is compact. Then $C$ is sequentially compact in itself.

title: Compact Subspace of Real Numbers is Closed and Bounded
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as a Euclidean space. Let $S \subseteq \R$ be compact subspace of $\R$. Then $S$ is closed and bounded in $\R$.

title: Compact Subspace of Topological Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $K$ be a compact subspace (where subspace is meant in the topological sense) of $X$. Then $K$ is von Neumann-bounded.

title: Compact in Subspace is Compact in Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $K \subseteq S$ be a subset. Let $\tau_K$ be the subspace topology on $K$. Let $T' = \struct {K, \tau_K}$ be the topological subspace of $T$ determined by $K$. Let $H \subseteq K$ be compact in $T'$. Then $H$ is compact in $T$.

If $T_A$ has one of the following properties, then $T_B$ has the same property: Compact Space $\sigma$-Compact Space Countable Compact Space Sequential Compact Space Lindelöf Space

snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. title: Compactness Theorem
snippet: Let $\LL$ be the language of predicate logic. Let $T$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. Then $T$ is satisfiable $T$ is finitely satisfiable.

title: Compactness Theorem for Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Let $\mathbf H$ be a countable set of WFFs of propositional logic. Suppose $\mathbf H$ is finitely satisfiable for boolean interpretations. That is, suppose that every finite subset $\mathbf H' \subseteq \mathbf H$ is satisfiable for boolean interpretations. Then $\mathbf H$ has a model.

title: Compactness and Sequential Compactness are Equivalent in Metric Spaces
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Then $\struct {X, d}$ is compact it is sequentially compact.

title: Compactness is Preserved under Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous surjection. If $T_A$ is compact, then $T_B$ is also compact.

title: Comparison Principle for Extremal Length
snippet: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface. Let $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ be families of rectifiable curves (or, more generally, families of unions of rectifiable curves) on $X$. Let every element of $\Gamma_1$ contain some element of $\Gamma_2$. Then the extremal lengths of $\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$ are related by: $\lambda \left({\Gamma_1}\right) \ge \lambda \left({\Gamma_2}\right)$ More precisely, for every conformal metric $\rho$ as in the definition of extremal length, we have: $L \left({\Gamma_1, \rho}\right) \ge L \left({\Gamma_2, \rho}\right)$

title: Comparison Test
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ be a convergent series of positive real numbers. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence $\R$ or sequence in $\C$. Let $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: \cmod {a_n} \le b_n$. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converges absolutely.

title: Comparison Test for Convergence of Power Series
snippet: Let $A = \ds \sum_{n \mathop \ge 0} a_n z^n$ and $B = \ds \sum_{n \mathop \ge 0} b_n z^n$ be power series in $\C$. Let $R_A$ and $R_B$ be the radii of convergence of $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $\cmod {b_n} \le \cmod {a_n}$ for all $n \in \N$. Then $R_A \le R_B$.

title: Comparison Test for Divergence
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ be a divergent series of positive real numbers. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let: $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: b_n \le a_n$ Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ diverges.

title: Comparison Test for Improper Integral
snippet: Let $I = \openint a b$ be an open real interval. Let $\phi$ be a real function which is continuous on $I$ and also non-negative on $I$. Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on $I$. Let $f$ satisfy: $\forall x \in I: \size {\map f x} \le \map \phi x$ If the improper integral of $\phi$ over $I$ exists, then so does that of $f$.

Compass and Straightedge Construction for Regular Heptagon does not exist
snippet: There exists no compass and straightedge construction for the regular heptagon.

title: Compatibility of Atlases is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological space. Let $d$ and $k$ be natural numbers. Let $\AA$ denote the set of all $d$-dimensional atlases of class $\CC^k$ on $M$. Define a relation $\sim$ on $\AA$ by putting, for any two $\CC^k$-atlases $\FF$ and $\GG$: $\FF \sim \GG$ $\FF$ and $\GG$ are $C^k$-compatible. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation on $\AA$.

title: Complement Operation between Union and Intersection Power Structures is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be its power set. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \cap, \subseteq}$ be the ordered semigroup formed from the set intersection operation and subset relation. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \cap, \supseteq}$ be the ordered semigroup formed from the set intersection operation and superset relation. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \cup, \subseteq}$ be the ordered semigroup formed from the set union operation and subset relation. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \cup, \supseteq}$ be the ordered semigroup formed from the set union operation and superset relation.

title: Complement Relative to Subset is Subset of Complement Relative to Superset
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B \subseteq C$. Then: $\relcomp B A \subseteq \relcomp C A$

title: Complement Union with Superset is Universe
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff \map \complement S \cup T = \mathbb U$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$ $\complement$ denotes set complement $\mathbb U$ denotes the universal set.

title: Complement in Boolean Algebra is Unique
snippet: Let $\left({S, \vee, \wedge}\right)$ be a Boolean algebra. Then for all $a \in S$, there is a unique $b \in S$ such that: $a \wedge b = \bot, a \vee b = \top$ i.e., a valid choice for $\neg a$ as in axiom $(BA \ 4)$ for Boolean algebras.

title: Complement in Distributive Lattice is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded distributive lattice. Then every $a \in S$ admits at most one complement.

title: Complement of Bounded Set has Exactly One Unbounded Component
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 1}$ Let $A \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subspace of real Euclidean $n$-space. Then, $\R^n \setminus A$ has exactly one unbounded component.

title: Complement of Bounded Set in Complex Plane has at most One Unbounded Component
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \C$ be bounded. Then $\C \setminus S$ has at most one unbounded component.

title: Complement of Clopen Set is Clopen
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a clopen set of $T$. Let $\relcomp S H$ denote the complement of $H$ relative to $S$. Then $\relcomp S H$ is also a clopen set of $T$.

title: Complement of Closed Disk in Complex Plane is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $R > 0$. Let: $S_R = \set {z \in \C : \cmod z > R}$ Then $S_R$ is path-connected.

title: Complement of Closed Interval Defined by Absolute Value
snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then: $\set {x \in \R: \size {\xi - x} > \delta} = \R \setminus \closedint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ where: $\closedint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ is the closed real interval between $\xi - \delta$ and $\xi + \delta$ $\setminus$ denotes the set difference operator.

title: Complement of Closed Set in Complex Plane is Open
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \C$ be a closed subset of the complex plane $\C$. Then the complement of $S$ in $\C$ is open.

title: Complement of Closed Set is Open Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F \subseteq S$ be a closed set in $T$. Then: $S \setminus F \in \tau$

title: Complement of Closed under Directed Suprema Subset is Inaccessible by Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $X$ be a closed under directed suprema subset of $S$. Then $\relcomp S X$ is inaccessible by directed suprema.

title: Complement of Complement
snippet: The complement of the complement of a set is the set itself: $\map \complement {\map \complement S} = S$

title: Complement of Complete Bipartite Graph
snippet: Let $K_{p, q}$ be a complete bipartite graph. The complement of $K_{p, q}$ consists of a disconnected graph with two components: The complete graph $K_p$ The complete graph $K_q$.

title: Complement of Complete Graph is Edgeless Graph
snippet: Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph of order $n$. Then the complement of $K_n$ is the $n$-edgeless graph $N_n$.

title: Complement of Countable Set in Topological Space where Open Neighborhood is Uncountable is Everywhere Dense
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space such that: every open set $U \in \tau$ is uncountable. Let $A \subseteq X$ be countable. Then $X \setminus A$ is everywhere dense in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Complement of Direct Image Mapping of Injection equals Direct Image of Complement
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping of $f$. Then: $\forall A \in \powerset S: \map {\paren {\complement_{\Img f} \circ f^\to} } A = \map {\paren {f^\to \circ \complement_S} } A$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Complement of Element is Irreducible implies Element is Meet Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $P = \struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an ordered set where $\mathord \preceq = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\tau \times \tau}$ Let $A \in \tau$. Then $\relcomp S A$ is irreducible implies $A$ is meet irreducible in $P$ where $\relcomp S A$ denotes the relative complement of $A$ relative to $S$.

title: Complement of Empty Set is Universal Set
snippet: The complement of the empty set is the universal set: $\map \complement \O = \mathbb U$

title: Complement of F-Sigma Set is G-Delta Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X$ be an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$. Then its complement $S \setminus X$ is a $G_\delta$ set of $S$.

title: Complement of G-Delta Set is F-Sigma Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X$ be an $G_\delta$ set of $T$. Then its complement $S \setminus X$ is an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

title: Complement of Horizontal Section of Set is Horizontal Section of Complement
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}^y = X \setminus E^y$ where: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of the set difference $\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E$ $E^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E$.

title: Complement of Inaccessible by Directed Suprema Subset is Closed under Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $X$ be an inaccessible by directed suprema subset of $S$. Then $\relcomp S X$ is closed under directed suprema.

title: Complement of Interior equals Closure of Complement
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$ and $H^\circ$ denote the interior of $H$. Let $\map \complement H$ be the complement of $H$ in $T$: $\map \complement H = T \setminus H$ Then: $\map \complement {H^\circ} = \paren {\map \complement H}^-$ This can alternatively be written: $T \setminus H^\circ = \paren {T \setminus H}^-$ which, it can be argued, is easier to follow.
