snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then:

title: Complement of Irreducible Topological Subset is Prime Element
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X$ be an irreducible subset of $S$ such that: $\relcomp S X \in \tau$ Let $L = \struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an inclusion ordered set of topology $\tau$. Then $\relcomp S X$ is prime element in $L$.

title: Complement of Limit Inferior is Limit Superior of Complements
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: $\ds \map \complement {\liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ E_n} = \limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ \map \complement {E_n}$ where $\liminf$ and $\limsup$ denote the limit inferior and limit superior, respectively.

title: Complement of Limit Superior is Limit Inferior of Complements
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: $\ds \map \complement {\limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ E_n} = \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \ \map \complement {E_n}$ where $\limsup$ and $\liminf$ denote the limit superior and limit inferior, respectively.

title: Complement of Lower Closure is Prime Element in Inclusion Ordered Set of Scott Sigma
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete Scott topological lattice. Let $D = \struct {\map \sigma L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set of the Scott sigma of $L$. Let $x \in S$. Then: $\relcomp S {x^\preceq}$ is a prime element in $D$ and: $\relcomp S {x^\preceq} \ne S$

title: Complement of Lower Closure of Element is Open in Scott Topological Ordered Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with Scott topology where $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is an up-complete ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $\relcomp S {x^\preceq}$ is topologically open, where $x^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $x$, $\relcomp S {x^\preceq}$ denotes the relative complement of $x^\preceq$.

title: Complement of Lower Section is Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $L$ be a lower section. Then $S \setminus L$ is an upper section.

title: Complement of Normal Subgroup is Isomorphic to Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group with identity $e$. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a complement of $N$. Then the quotient group $G / N$ is isomorphic to $K$.

title: Complement of Open Interval Defined by Absolute Value
snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then: $\set {x \in \R: \size {\xi - x} \ge \delta} = \R \setminus \openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ where: $\openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ is the open real interval between $\xi - \delta$ and $\xi + \delta$ $\setminus$ denotes the set difference operator.

title: Complement of Open Set in Complex Plane is Closed
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \C$ be an open subset of the complex plane $\C$. Then the complement of $S$ in $\C$ is closed.

title: Complement of Preimage equals Preimage of Complement
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $T_1$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $\relcomp S {f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1} } = f^{-1} \sqbrk {\relcomp T {T_1} }$ where: $\complement_S$ (in this context) denotes relative complement $f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1}$ denotes preimage. That is: $S \setminus f^{-1} \sqbrk {T_1} = f^{-1} \sqbrk {T \setminus T_1}$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of inverse image mappings as: $\forall T_1 \in \powerset T: \relcomp S {\map {f^\gets} {T_1} } = \map {f^\gets} {\relcomp T {T_1} }$

title: Complement of Prime Filter is Prime Ideal
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $F \subseteq S$. Then: $F$ is a prime filter of $P$ $S \setminus F$ is a prime ideal of $P$.

title: Complement of Prime Ideal is Prime Filter
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $I \subseteq S$. Then: $I$ is a prime ideal of $P$ $S \setminus I$ is a prime filter of $P$.

title: Complement of Prime Ideal of Ring is Multiplicatively Closed
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $P \subset R$ be a prime ideal of $R$. Then its complement $R \setminus P$ is multiplicatively closed.

title: Complement of Primitive Recursive Set
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be primitive recursive. Then its relative complement $\N \setminus S$ of $S$ in $\N$ is primitive recursive.

title: Complement of Reflexive Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation. Then $\RR$ is reflexive its complement $\relcomp {S \times S} \RR \subseteq S \times S$ is antireflexive. Likewise, $\RR$ is antireflexive its complement $\relcomp {S \times S} \RR \subseteq S \times S$ is reflexive.

title: Complement of Relation Compatible with Group is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $G$. Let $\RR$ be compatible with $\circ$. Let $\QQ = \complement_{G \times G} \RR$, so that: $\forall a, b \in G: a \mathrel \QQ b \iff \neg \paren {a \mathrel \RR b}$ Then $\QQ$ is a relation compatible with $\circ$.

title: Complement of Relative Complement is Union with Complement
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B \subseteq C$. Then: $\relcomp C {\relcomp B A} = A \cup \relcomp C B$

title: Complement of Set of Rational Pairs in Real Euclidean Plane is Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $S \subseteq \R^2$ be the subset of $\R^2$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \R^2: \tuple {x, y} \in S \iff x, y \in \Q$ Hence let $A := \R^2 \setminus S$: $\tuple {x, y} \in A$ either $x$ or $y$ or both is irrational. Then $A$ is injectively path-connected.

title: Complement of Singleton Closure is Meet-Irreducible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then: $S \setminus \set x^-$ is a meet-irreducible open set where $\set x^-$ denotes the closure of $\set x$

title: Complement of Strict Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a relational structure such that $\prec$ is a strict total ordering. Then the complement of $\prec$ is a weak total ordering.

title: Complement of Subgroup does not necessarily Exist
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroups of $G$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $H$ has a complement in $G$.

title: Complement of Subgroup is not necessarily Unique
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a complement of $H$ in $G$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $K$ is the only complement of $H$ in $G$.

title: Complement of Subset with Property (S) is Closed under Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$ with property (S). Then $\relcomp S X$ is closed under directed suprema.

title: Complement of Symmetric Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation. Then $\RR$ is symmetric its complement $\relcomp {S \times S} \RR \subseteq S \times S$ is also symmetric.

title: Complement of Universal Set is Empty Set
snippet: The complement of the universal set is the empty set: $\map \complement {\mathbb U} = \O$

title: Complement of Upper Closure of Element is Open in Lower Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with lower topology. Let $x \in S$. Then $\relcomp S {x^\succeq}$ is open and $x^\succeq$ is closed.

title: Complement of Upper Section is Lower Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $L$ be an upper section. Then $S \setminus L$ is a lower section.

title: Complement of Vertical Section of Set is Vertical Section of Complement
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}_x = Y \setminus E_x$ where: $\paren {\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of the set difference $\paren {X \times Y} \setminus E$ $E_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E$.

title: Complementary Error Function of Zero
snippet: $\map \erfc 0 = 1$ where $\erfc$ denotes the complementary error function.

title: Complementary Idempotent is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be an idempotent operator. Then the complementary idempotent $I - A$ is also idempotent.

title: Complementary Idempotent of Complementary Idempotent is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be an idempotent operator. Let $B$ be the complementary idempotent of A. Then the complementary idempotent of $B$ is $A$.

title: Complementary Projection is Complementary Idempotent
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A$ be a projection. Let $B$ be the complementary projection of A. Then $B$ is the complementary idempotent of $A$.

title: Complementary Projection is Projection
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A$ be a projection. Then the complementary projection $I - A$ is also a projection.

title: Complementary Projection of Complementary Projection is Projection
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $I$ be an identity operator on $\HH$. Let $A$ be a projection. Let $B$ be the complementary projection of A. Then the complementary projection of $B$ is $A$.

title: Complements of Components of Two-Component Partition form Partition
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with at least two elements. Let $A, B \subseteq S$. Let $\complement_S$ denote the complement relative to $S$. $A \mid B$ is a partition of $S$ $\relcomp S A \mid \relcomp S B$ is a partition of $S$.

title: Complete Archimedean Valued Field is Real or Complex Numbers
snippet:
Let $\struct{k, 
orm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a complete valued field with Archimedean norm $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$. Then either: $k$ is isomorphic to the real numbers $\R$ and $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$ is equivalent to the absolute value $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ on $\R$ or $k$ is isomorphic to the complex numbers $\C$ and $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$ is equivalent to the complex modulus $\size{\,\cdot\,}$ on $\C$

title: Complete Bipartite Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complete Bipartite Graphs == The following are examples of complete bipartite graphs: 720px

title: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Complete Graphs
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. $K_{0, 0}$ is the complete graph $K_0$ $K_{0, 1}$ and $K_{1, 0}$ are the complete graph $K_1$ $K_{1, 1}$ is the complete graph $K_2$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are complete.

title: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Cycle Graphs
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. $K_{2, 2}$ is the cycle graph $C_4$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are cycle graphs.

title: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Path Graphs
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. $K_{0, 0}$ is the path graph $P_0$ $K_{0, 1}$ and $K_{1, 0}$ are the path graph $P_1$ $K_{1, 1}$ is the path graph $P_2$ $K_{1, 2}$ and $K_{2, 1}$ are the path graphs $P_3$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are path graphs.

title: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Regular
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E} =: K_{m, n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $m$ vertices in $A$ and $n$ vertices in $B$. Then: $K_{n, n}$ is $n$-regular for all $n$ $K_{n, 0}$ and $K_{0, n}$ are $0$-regular for all $n$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are regular.

title: Complete Bipartite Graphs which are Trees
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E} =: K_{m, n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $m$ vertices in $A$ and $n$ vertices in $B$. Then: $K_{0, 0}$ is a tree $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{n, 1}$ is a tree for all $n$ and no other complete bipartite graphs are trees.

title: Complete Boolean Lattice is a Frame
snippet: Let $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \neg, \preceq}$ be a complete Boolean lattice. Then: $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a frame.

title: Complete Boolean Lattice is a Locale
snippet: Let $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \neg, \preceq}$ be a complete Boolean lattice. Then: $\struct{B, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a locale.

title: Complete Countable Metric Space has Isolated Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a countable complete metric space. Then $X$ has an isolated point.

title: Complete Derivation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complete Derivations ==

title: Complete Elliptic Integral of the First Kind as Power Series
snippet: The complete elliptic integral of the first kind: $\ds \map K k = \int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac {\rd \phi} {\sqrt {1 - k^2 \sin^2 \phi} } = \int_0^1 \frac {\rd v} {\sqrt {\paren {1 - v^2} \paren {1 - k^2 v^2} } }$ can be expressed as the power series: {{eqn | l = \map K k | r = \frac \pi 2 \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} \paren {\prod_{j \mathop = 1}^i \frac {2 j - 1} {2 j} }^2 k^{2 i} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac \pi 2 \paren {1 + \paren {\frac 1 2}^2 k^2 + \paren {\frac {1 \cdot 3} {2 \cdot 4} }^2 k^4 + \paren {\frac {1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5} {2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6} }^2 k^6 + \cdots} | c = }}

title: Complete Elliptic Integral of the Second Kind as Power Series
snippet: The complete elliptic integral of the second kind: $\ds \map E k = \int_0^{\pi / 2} \sqrt {1 - k^2 \sin^2 \phi} \, \rd \phi = \int_0^1 \dfrac {\sqrt {1 - k^2 v^2} } {\sqrt {1 - v^2}} \, \rd v$ can be expressed as the power series: {{eqn | l = \map E k | r = \frac \pi 2 \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} \paren {\prod_{j \mathop = 1}^i \frac {2 j - 1} { 2 j} }^2 \frac {k^{2 i} } {1 - 2 i} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac \pi 2 \paren {1 - \paren {\frac 1 2}^2 k^2 - \paren {\frac {1 \cdot 3} {2 \cdot 4} }^2 \frac {k^4} 3 - \paren {\frac {1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5} {2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6} }^2 \frac {k^6} 5 - \cdots} | c = }}

title: Complete Factorizations of Proper Element in Principal Ideal Domain are Equivalent
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be a principal ideal domain. Let $x \in D$ be a proper element of $D$. Let there be two complete factorizations of $x$: $x = u_y \circ y_1 \circ y_2 \circ \cdots \circ y_m = F_1$ $x = u_z \circ z_1 \circ z_2 \circ \cdots \circ z_n = F_2$ Then $F_1$ and $F_2$ are equivalent.

title: Complete Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complete Graphs == The first five complete graphs are shown below: 820px

title: Complete Graph K5 is not Planar
snippet: The complete graph $K_5$ is not planar.

title: Complete Graph is Hamiltonian for Order Greater than 2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 2$. Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph of order $n$. Then $K_n$ is Hamiltonian.

title: Complete Graph is Regular
snippet: Let $K_p$ be the complete graph of order $p$. Then $K_p$ is $p-1$-regular.

title: Complete Graph of Order 1 is Edgeless
snippet: The complete graph $K_1$ of order $1$ is the edgeless graph $N_1$.

title: Complete Hamiltonian Bipartite Graph
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. Then: $K_{m, n}$ is Hamiltonian $m = n > 1$.

title: Complete Join Semilattice is Dual to Complete Meet Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. The following are dual statements: $\struct{S, \preceq}$ is a complete join semilattice $\struct{S, \preceq}$ is a complete meet semilattice

title: Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice homomorphsim between $L_1$ and $L_2$. Then: $\phi$ is a frame homomorphism

title: Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice homomorphism. Then: $\phi : \struct {S_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ is a lattice homomorphism where: $\wedge_1, \vee_1$ denote the meet and join on $L_1$ $\wedge_2, \vee_2$ denote the meet and join on $L_2$

title: Complete Lattice Isomorphism is Isomorphism in Category CLat
snippet: Let $\mathbf{CLat}$ denote the category of complete lattices. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a morphism of $\mathbf{CLat}$. Then: $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbf{CLat}$ $\phi$ is a complete lattice isomorphsm

title: Complete Lattice has Both Greatest Element and Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct{S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then: $(\text{1}) \quad \struct{S, \preceq}$ has a smallest element, namely: $\quad \bot := \sup \O$ $(\text{2}) \quad \struct{S, \preceq}$ has a greatest element, namely: $\quad \top := \inf \O$

title: Complete Lattice is Bounded
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then $L$ is bounded.

title: Complete Lattice is Lattice
snippet: Let $L= \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then: $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a lattice where $\vee$ and $\wedge$ denote the join and meet operations on $S$, respectively.

title: Complete Linearly Ordered Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $\struct {X, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Then $\struct {X, \tau}$ is compact.

title: Complete List of Special Highly Composite Numbers
snippet: There are exactly $6$ special highly composite numbers: $1, 2, 6, 12, 60, 2520$

title: Complete Metric Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a complete metric space. Then $M$ is non-meager.

title: Complete Metric Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a complete metric space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M$ is also compact.

title: Complete Metrizability is Topological Property
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces which are homeomorphic. Let $T_1$ be completely metrizable. Then $T_2$ is also completely metrizable.

title: Complete Metrizability is Weakly Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is completely metrizable. Let $V \subseteq S$ be a closed subspace of $T$. Then $V$ is also completely metrizable. That is, complete metrizability is a weakly hereditary property.

title: Complete Metrizability is not Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is completely metrizable. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ be the topological subspace of $T$ induced by $H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ is also completely metrizable. That is, complete metrizability is not a hereditary property.

title: Complete Norms on Vector Space Equivalent iff Identity Mapping Bounded
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_1$ and $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_2$ be norms on $X$ such that: $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_i}$ is a Banach space for $i \in \set {1, 2}$. Let $I : \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_1} 	o \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the identity mapping. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_1$ and $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_2$ are equivalent $I$ is bounded.

title: Complete Residue System/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complete Residue Systems ==

title: Complete Residue System Modulo m has m Elements
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ne 0}$ be a non-zero integer. Let $S := \set {r_1, r_2, \dotsb, r_s}$ be a complete residue system modulo $m$. Then $s = m$.

title: Complete and Totally Bounded Metric Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be complete and totally bounded. Then $M$ is sequentially compact.

title: Completed Riemann Zeta Function has Order One
snippet: The completed Riemann zeta function $\xi$ has order at most $1$.

title: Completely Additive Function is Additive
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \C$ be a completely additive function. Then $f$ is also additive.

title: Completely Irreducible Element equals Infimum of Subset implies Element Belongs to Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X \subseteq S$, $p \in S$ such that $p$ is completely irreducible and $p = \inf X$ Then $p \in X$

title: Completely Irreducible Element iff Exists Element that Strictly Succeeds First Element
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $p \in S$. Then $p$ is completely irreducible $\exists q \in S: p \prec q \land \paren {\forall s \in S: p \prec s \implies q \preceq s} \land p^\succeq = \set p \cup q^\succeq$ where $p^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $p$.

title: Completely Irreducible and Subset Admits Infimum Equals Element implies Element Belongs to Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$ such that $x$ is completely irreducible. Let $X \subseteq S$ such that $X$ admits an infimum and $x = \inf X$ Then $x \in X$

title: Completely Irreducible implies Infimum differs from Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $p \in S$ such that $p$ is completely irreducible. Then $\map \inf {p^\succeq \setminus \set p} \ne p$ where $p^\succeq$ donotes the upper closure of $p$.

title: Completely Irreducible implies Meet Irreducible
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet semilattice. Let $p \in S$. Then if $p$ is completely irreducible, then $p$ is meet irreducible.

title: Completely Metrizable Space is Metrizable Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely metrizable topological space. Then, $\struct {S, \tau}$ is a metrizable space.

title: Completely Metrizable Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely metrizable topological space. Then $T$ is non-meager.

title: Completely Multiplicative Function is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $f: \Z \to \Z$ be a function on the integers $\Z$. Let $f$ be completely multiplicative. Then $f$ is multiplicative.

title: Completely Multiplicative Function of Quotient
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a completely multiplicative function. Then: $\forall x, y \in \R, y \ne 0: \map f {\dfrac x y} = \dfrac {\map f x} {\map f y}$ whenever $\map f y \ne 0$.

title: Completely Normal Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a completely normal space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a completely normal space. That is: The property of being a completely normal space is hereditary.

title: Completely Normal Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a completely normal space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: Completely Normal Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a completely normal space, then so is $T_B$.

title: Completely Normal Space is Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely normal space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a normal space.

title: Completely Normal Space is not necessarily Perfectly Normal
snippet: A completely normal topological space is not necessarily perfectly normal.

title: Completely Normal iff Every Subspace is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a completely normal space every subspace of $T$ is normal.

title: Completely Prime Filter Induced by Frame Homomorphism Induced by Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\struct{\mathbf 2, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ denote the (Boolean Lattice) $\mathbf 2$. For every completely prime filter $p$ of $L$, let: $\phi_p : L \to \mathbf 2$ be the frame homomorphism defined by: $\forall a \in L : \map {\phi_p} a = \begin{cases} \top & : a \in p\\ \bot & : a \notin p \end{cases}$ For every frame homomorphism $\phi : L \to \mathbf 2$, let: $p_\phi = \map {\phi^{-1}} \top$ where $\map {\phi^{-1}} \top$ denotes the preimage of $\top \in \mathbf 2$ under the mapping $\phi$ which is the completely prime filter of $L$…

title: Completely Prime Filter Induced by Frame Homomorphism Onto Two
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\struct{\mathbf 2, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ denote the (Boolean Lattice) $\mathbf 2$. Let $\phi : L \to \mathbf 2$ be a frame homomorphism. Then: $\map {\phi^{-1}} \top$ is a completely prime filter where $\map {\phi^{-1}} \top$ denotes the preimage of $\top \in \mathbf 2$ under the mapping $\phi$

title: Completely Prime Filter Induced by Meet Irreducible Element
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $b$ be a meet-irreducible element of $L$. Let: $p = \set{a \in L : a \npreceq b}$ Then: $p$ is a completely prime filter of $L$.

title: Completely Prime Filter Induced by Meet Irreducible Induced by Completely Prime Filter
snippet:
Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $	op$ denote the greatest element of $L$. For every completely prime filter $p$ of $L$, let: $b_p =  igvee \set{a \in L : a 
otin p}$ where: $ igvee \set{a \in L : a 
otin p}$ denotes the supremum of the set $\set{a \in L : a 
otin p}$ which is a meet irreducible element not equal to $	op$ For every meet-irreducible element $b$ of $L$ not equal to $	op$, let: $p_b = \set{a \in L : a 
preceq b}$ where $p_b$ is a completely prime filter of $L$. Let $p$ be a completely prime filter $p$ of $L$. Then: $p_{b_p} = p$

title: Completely Prime Filter Induces Meet-Irreducible Open Set
snippet: Let $\struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a completely prime filter in the complete lattice $\struct{\tau, \subseteq}$. Let $W = \bigcup \set{U \in \tau : U \notin \FF}$. Then: $W$ is a meet-irreducible open set

title: Completely Prime Ideal is Dual of Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $K \subseteq L$. The following are dual statements: $K$ is a completely prime filter of $\struct {L, \preceq}$ $K$ is a completely prime ideal of $\struct {L, \preceq}$

title: Completely Regular Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a completely regular space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a completely regular space. That is: The property of being a completely regular space is hereditary.

title: Completely Regular Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a completely regular space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: Completely Regular Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a completely regular space, then so is $T_B$.

title: Completely Regular Space is Regular
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a regular space.

title: Completely Regular Space is T1
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_1$ space.

title: Completely Regular Space is T2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Completely Regular Space is Urysohn
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a completely regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also an Urysohn space.

title: Completely Regular Space is not necessarily Normal
snippet: A topological space which is a completely regular space is not necessarily also a normal space.

title: Completeness Criterion (Metric Spaces)
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, d}$ be a metric space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a dense subset. Suppose that every Cauchy sequence in $A$ converges in $M$. Then $M$ is complete.

title: Completeness Theorem for Hilbert Proof System Instance 2 and Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Instance 2 of the Hilbert proof systems is a complete proof system for boolean interpretations. That is, for every WFF $\mathbf A$: $\models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf A$ implies $\vdash_{\mathscr H_2} \mathbf A$

title: Completeness Theorem for Propositional Tableaux and Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Tableau proofs (in terms of propositional tableaux) are a complete proof system for boolean interpretations. That is, for every WFF $\mathbf A$: $\models_{\mathrm{BI} } \mathbf A$ implies $\vdash_{\mathrm{PT} } \mathbf A$

title: Completeness Theorem for Semantic Tableaux
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of propositional logic. Let $\mathbf A$ be unsatisfiable for boolean interpretations. Then every completed tableau for $\mathbf A$ is closed.

title: Completing the Square
snippet: Let $a, b, c, x$ be real numbers with $a \ne 0$. Then: $a x^2 + b x + c = \dfrac {\paren {2 a x + b}^2 + 4 a c - b^2} {4 a}$ This process is known as completing the square.

title: Completion Theorem (Inner Product Space)
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_V}$ be an inner product space over a subfield $\GF$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_V$ be the inner product norm induced by $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_V$. Let $\struct {H, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_H}$ be a completion of $V$ with respect to $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ given by Completion Theorem (Normed Vector Space). Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_V$ can be extended to an inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_H$ on $H$. By definition, $H$ will be a Hilbert space.

title: Completion Theorem (Measure Space)
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Then there exists a completion $\struct {X, \Sigma^*, \bar \mu}$ of $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$.

title: Completion Theorem (Metric Space)
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Then there exists a completion $\tilde M = \struct {\tilde A, \tilde d}$ of $\struct {A, d}$. Moreover, this completion is unique up to isometry. That is, if $\struct {\hat A, \hat d}$ is another completion of $\struct {A, d}$, then there is a bijection $\tau: \tilde A \leftrightarrow \hat A$ such that: {{item|(2):|$\tau$ preserves metrics: $\forall x_1, x_2 \in A : \map {\hat d} {\map \tau {x_1}, \map \tau {x_2} } \map {\tilde d} {x_1, x_2}$}}

title: Completion Theorem (Normed Algebra)
Completion Theorem (Normed Vector Space)
Completion of Metric Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Completions of Metric Spaces ==

title: Completion of Nondegenerate Bases
snippet: Let $\struct {V, q}$ be an $n$-dimensional scalar product space. Let $\tuple {v_1, \ldots, v_k}$ be a nondegenerate $k$-tuple in $V$ with $0 \le k < n$. Then there exist vectors $v_{k+1}, \ldots, v_n \in V$ such that $\tuple {v_1, \ldots, v_n}$ is a nondegenerate basis for $V$.

title: Completion of Normed Division Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_R }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\CC$ be the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$. Let $\NN$ be the set of null sequences. Let $Q = \CC / \NN$ where $\CC / \NN$ denotes a quotient ring. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Q: Q 	o \R_{\ge 0}$ be the norm on the quotient ring $Q$ defined by: $\ds  orall \sequence {x_n} + \NN: 
orm {\sequence {x_n} + \NN }_Q = \lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} 
orm{x_n}_R$ Then: $\struct {Q, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Q}$ is a normed division ring completion of $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_R }$

title: Completion of Valued Field
snippet:
Let $\struct {k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Then there exists a completion $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$ of $\struct {k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ such that $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$ is a valued field. Furthermore, every completion of $\struct{k, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ is isometrically isomorphic to $\struct {k', 
orm {\,\cdot\,}'}$.

title: Complex-Differentiable Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex function, where $D \subseteq \C$ is an open set. Let $f$ be complex-differentiable at $a \in D$. Then $f$ is continuous at $a$.

title: Complex-Valued Function Dominated by Function Vanishing at Infinity also Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $g : X \to \C$ be a complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Let $f : X \to \C$ be such that $\cmod f \le \cmod g$. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

title: Complex-Valued Function Vanishing in Neighborhood of Infinity Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function vanishing in a neighborhood of infinity. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

title: Complex-Valued Function is Continuous iff Real Part and Imaginary Part are Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Then $f$ is continuous both the real part $\map \Re f$ and the imaginary part $\map \Im f$ are continuous.

title: Complex-Valued Function is Measurable iff Real and Imaginary Part Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\struct {\C, \map \BB \C}$ be the complex numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$ be the real numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Let $\map \Re f : X \to \R$ and $\map \Im f : X \to \R$ be the pointwise real part and imaginary part of $f$ respectively. Then $f$ is $\Sigma/\map \BB \C$-measurable $\map \Re f$ and $\map \Im f$ are $\Sigma/\map \BB \R$-measurable.

title: Complex-Valued Function on Compact Hausdorff Space Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

title: Complex Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Addition ==

title: Complex Addition Identity is Zero
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The identity element of $\struct {\C, +}$ is the complex number $0 + 0 i$.

title: Complex Addition is Associative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is associative: $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C: z_1 + \paren {z_2 + z_3} = \paren {z_1 + z_2} + z_3$

title: Complex Addition is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is closed under addition: $\forall z, w \in \C: z + w \in \C$

title: Complex Addition is Commutative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of complex numbers is commutative: $\forall z, w \in \C: z + w = w + z$

title: Complex Algebra/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Algebra ==

title: Complex Algebraic Curve is Riemann Surface
snippet: Let $\CC$ be an algebraic curve over the field of complex numbers. Then $\CC$ is a Riemann surface.

title: Complex Arithmetic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Arithmetic ==

title: Complex Conjugate/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Conjugates ==

title: Complex Conjugate Coordinates/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Conjugate Coordinates ==

title: Complex Conjugate of Complex-Valued Function Vanishing at Infinity Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Define $\overline f : X \to \C$ by: $\forall x \in \C: \map {\overline f} x = \overline {\map f x}$ where $\overline {\map f x}$ denotes the conjugate of $\overline {\map f x}$. Then $\overline f$ is a complex-valued function vanishing at infinity.

title: Complex Conjugate of Gamma Function
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote the gamma function. Then: $\forall z \in \C \setminus \set {0, -1, -2, \ldots}: \map \Gamma {\overline z} = \overline {\map \Gamma z}$

title: Complex Conjugation is Field Automorphism of Complex Numbers
snippet: Consider the field of complex numbers $\C$. The operation of complex conjugation: $\forall z \in \C: z \mapsto \overline z$ is a field automorphism of $\C$.

title: Complex Conjugation is Involution
snippet: Let $z = x + i y$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Then the operation of complex conjugation is an involution: $\overline {\paren {\overline z} } = z$

title: Complex Conjugation is Real Vector Space Automorphism
snippet: The operation of complex conjugation: $\forall z \in \C: z \mapsto \overline z$ is a vector space automorphism over the real vector space $\R^n$.

title: Complex Conjugation is not Complex Vector Space Automorphism
snippet: The operation of complex conjugation: $\forall z \in \C: z \mapsto \overline z$ is not a vector space automorphism over the complex vector space $\C^n$.

title: Complex Conjugation is not Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $\overline \cdot: \C \to \C: z \mapsto \overline z$ be the complex conjugation over the field of complex numbers. Then complex conjugation is not a linear mapping.

title: Complex Contour Integral as Contour Integrals
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex-differentiable function, where $D \subseteq \C$ is a connected domain. Let $u, v: \R^2 \to \R$ be defined by: $\map f {x + i y} = \map u {x, y} + i \map v {x, y}$ Let $C$ be a contour in $D$. Let $\phi: \R^2 \to \C$ be defined by: $\map \phi {x, y} = x + i y$ Then there exists a piecewise continuously differentiable function $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \R^2$ such that: $\ds \int_C \map f z \rd z = \ds \int_\gamma \tuple {u, -v} \cdot \rd \mathbf l + i \int_\gamma \tuple {v, u} \cdot \rd \mathbf l$ where the integral on the is a complex contour integral, and the…

title: Complex Cosine Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Cosine Function ==

title: Complex Cosine Function is Entire
snippet: Let $\cos: \C \to \C$ be the complex cosine function. Then $\cos$ is entire.

title: Complex Cosine Function is Unbounded
snippet: The complex cosine function is unbounded.

title: Complex Cross Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Cross Product ==

title: Complex Cross Product Distributes over Addition
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Then: $z_1 \times \paren {z_2 + z_3} = z_1 \times z_2 + z_1 \times z_3$ where $\times$ denotes cross product.

title: Complex Cross Product in Exponential Form
snippet: Let $z_1 := r_1 e^{i \theta_1}, z_2 := r_2 e^{i \theta_2} \in \C$ be complex numbers expressed in exponential form. Then: $z_1 \times z_2 = r_1 r_2 \map \sin {\theta_2 - \theta_1}$ where $z_1 \times z_2$ denotes the dot product of $z_1$ and $z_2$.

title: Complex Cross Product is Anticommutative/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Complex Cross Product is Anticommutative ==

title: Complex Division/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Division ==

title: Complex Division as Product with Conjugate over Square of Modulus
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Then the operation of division can be expressed as: $\dfrac {z_1} {z_2} = \dfrac {z_1 \overline {z_2} } {\cmod {z_2}^2}$ where: $\overline {z_2}$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z_2$ $\cmod {z_2}$ denotes the complex modulus of $z_2$.

title: Complex Dot Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Dot Product ==

title: Complex Dot Product in Exponential Form
snippet: Let $z_1 := r_1 e^{i \theta_1}, z_2 := r_2 e^{i \theta_2} \in \C$ be complex numbers expressed in exponential form. Then: $z_1 \circ z_2 = r_1 r_2 \, \map \cos {\theta_2 - \theta_1}$ where $z_1 \circ z_2$ denotes the dot product of $z_1$ and $z_2$.

title: Complex Eigenvalues of Real Matrix occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: The complex eigenvalues of a real matrix occur in conjugate pairs. That is, if $\lambda$ is a complex eigenvalues of a real matrix, then so is the complex conjugate $\overline \lambda$.

title: Complex Exponential Function is Entire
snippet: Let $\exp: \C \to \C$ be the complex exponential function. Then $\exp$ is entire.

title: Complex Exponential Tends to Zero
snippet: Let $\exp z$ be the complex exponential function. Then: $\ds \lim_{\map \Re z \mathop \to +\infty} e^{-z} = 0$ where $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$.

title: Complex Exponential is Uniformly Continuous on Half-Planes
snippet: Let $a \in \R$. Then $\exp$ is uniformly continuous on the half-plane $\set {z \in \C : \map \Re z \le a}$.

title: Complex Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Functions ==

title: Complex Function is Entire iff it has Everywhere Convergent Power Series
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a complex function. Then $f$ is an entire function $f$ can be given by an everywhere convergent power series: $\ds \map f z = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n z^n; \quad \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \sqrt [n] {\size {a_n} } = 0$

title: Complex General Harmonic Numbers extend Integer version
Complex Hyperbolic Functions are Entire
snippet: Let $F$ be a hyperbolic function over the complex numbers. Then $F$ is an entire function.

title: Complex Integration by Substitution
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\phi: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a real function which has a derivative on $\closedint a b$. Let $f: A \to \C$ be a continuous complex function, where $A$ is a subset of the image of $\phi$. If $\map \phi a \le \map \phi b$, then: $\ds \int_{\map \phi a}^{\map \phi b} \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f {\map \phi u} \map {\phi'} u \rd u$ If $\map \phi a > \map \phi b$, then: $\ds \int_{\map \phi b}^{\map \phi a} \map f t \rd t = -\int_a^b \map f {\map \phi u} \map {\phi'} u \rd u$

title: Complex Inverse Sine/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Inverse Sine Function ==

title: Complex Logarithm Function is Transcendental
snippet: Let $a \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number such that $a \ne 1$. Let $\log_a: \C \to \C$ denote the complex general logarithm base $a$. $\log_a$ is a transcendental function.

title: Complex Logarithm of 1
snippet: $\ln 1 = \set {2 k \pi i: k \in \Z}$ where $\ln 1$ denotes the complex natural logarithm of $1$.

title: Complex Modulus/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Modulus ==

title: Complex Modulus Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $z_0 \in \C$ be a complex number. Then the complex modulus function is continuous at $z_0$.

title: Complex Modulus equals Complex Modulus of Conjugate
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z = \cmod {\overline z}$

title: Complex Modulus equals Zero iff Zero
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z = 0 \iff z = 0$

title: Complex Modulus is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $z = a + i b \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod z \ge 0$

title: Complex Modulus is Norm
snippet: The complex modulus is a norm on the set of complex numbers $\C$.

title: Complex Modulus of Additive Inverse
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $-z$ be the negative of $z$: $z + \paren {-z} = 0$ Then: $\cmod z = \cmod {\paren {-z} }$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the modulus of $z$.

title: Complex Modulus of Difference of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be arguments of $z_1$ and $z_2$, respectively. Then: $\cmod {z_1 - z_2}^2 = \cmod {z_1}^2 + \cmod {z_2}^2 - 2 \cmod {z_1} \cmod {z_2} \map \cos {\theta_1 - \theta_2}$

title: Complex Modulus of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\struct {\C, \map \BB \C}$ be the complex numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a $\Sigma/\map \BB \C$-measurable mapping. Let $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$ be the real numbers made into a measurable space with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Then $\cmod f : X \to \R$ is $\Sigma/\map \BB \R$-measurable.

title: Complex Modulus of Product of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z_1 z_2} = \cmod {z_1} \cdot \cmod {z_2}$

title: Complex Modulus of Quotient of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers such that $z_2 \ne 0$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {\dfrac {z_1} {z_2} } = \dfrac {\cmod {z_1} } {\cmod {z_2} }$

title: Complex Modulus of Real Number equals Absolute Value
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then the complex modulus of $x$ equals the absolute value of $x$.

title: Complex Modulus of Reciprocal of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z \ne 0$. Let $\cmod z$ denote the complex modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {\dfrac 1 z} = \dfrac 1 {\cmod z}$

title: Complex Modulus of Sum of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be arguments of $z_1$ and $z_2$, respectively. Then: $\cmod {z_1 + z_2}^2 = \cmod {z_1}^2 + \cmod {z_2}^2 + 2 \cmod {z_1} \cmod {z_2} \, \map \cos {\theta_1 - \theta_2}$

title: Complex Multiplication/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Multiplication ==

title: Complex Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is distributive over the operation of addition. $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C:$ $z_1 \paren {z_2 + z_3} = z_1 z_2 + z_1 z_3$ $\paren {z_2 + z_3} z_1 = z_2 z_1 + z_3 z_1$

title: Complex Multiplication Identity is One
snippet: Let $\C_{\ne 0}$ be the set of complex numbers without zero. The identity element of $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ is the complex number $1 + 0 i$.

title: Complex Multiplication as Geometrical Transformation
snippet: Let $z_1 = \left\langle{r_1, \theta_1}\right\rangle$ and $z_2 = \left\langle{r_2, \theta_2}\right\rangle$ be complex numbers expressed in polar form. Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be represented on the complex plane $\C$ in vector form. Let $z = z_1 z_2$ be the product of $z_1$ and $z_2$. Then $z$ can be interpreted as the result of: rotating $z_1$ about the origin of $\C$ by $\theta_2$ in the positive direction multiplying the modulus of $z_1$ by $r_2$.

title: Complex Multiplication is Associative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is associative: $\forall z_1, z_2, z_3 \in \C: z_1 \paren {z_2 z_3} = \paren {z_1 z_2} z_3$

title: Complex Multiplication is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is closed under multiplication: $\forall z, w \in \C: z \times w \in \C$

title: Complex Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of complex numbers $\C$ is commutative: $\forall z_1, z_2 \in \C: z_1 z_2 = z_2 z_1$

title: Complex Natural Logarithm/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Natural Logarithm ==

title: Complex Natural Logarithm Function is not Entire
snippet: The complex natural logarithm function is not an entire function.

title: Complex Number equals Conjugate iff Wholly Real
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Then $z = \overline z$ $z$ is wholly real.

title: Complex Number equals Negative of Conjugate iff Wholly Imaginary
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Then $\overline z = -z$ $z$ is wholly imaginary.

title: Complex Number is Algebraic over Real Numbers
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then $z$ is algebraic over $\R$.

title: Complex Numbers are Parallel iff Cross Product is Zero
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers in vector form such that $z_1 \ne 0$ and $z_2 \ne 0$. Then $z_1$ and $z_2$ are parallel : $z_1 \times z_2 = 0$ where $z_1 \times z_2$ denotes the complex cross product of $z_1$ with $z_2$.

title: Complex Numbers are Perpendicular iff Dot Product is Zero
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers in vector form such that $z_1 \ne 0$ and $z_2 \ne 0$. Then $z_1$ and $z_2$ are perpendicular : $z_1 \circ z_2 = 0$ where $z_1 \circ z_2$ denotes the complex dot product of $z_1$ with $z_2$.

title: Complex Numbers are Uncountable
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ is uncountably infinite.

title: Complex Numbers as External Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the group of non-zero complex numbers under multiplication. Let $\struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the group of positive real numbers under multiplication. Let $\struct {K, \times}$ be the circle group. Then: $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times} \cong \struct {\R_{> 0}, \times} \times \struct {K, \times}$

title: Complex Numbers as Quotient Ring of Real Polynomial
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Let $P \sqbrk x$ be the set of polynomials over real numbers, where the coefficients of the polynomials are real. Let $\ideal {x^2 + 1} = \set {\map Q x \paren {x^2 + 1}: \map Q x \in P \sqbrk x}$ be the ideal generated by $x^2 + 1$ in $P \sqbrk x$. Let $D = P \sqbrk x / \ideal {x^2 + 1}$ be the quotient of $P \sqbrk x$ modulo $\ideal {x^2 + 1}$. Then: $\struct {\C, +, \times} \cong \struct {D, +, \times}$

title: Complex Numbers cannot be Extended to Algebra in Three Dimensions with Real Scalars
snippet: It is not possible to extend the complex numbers to an algebra of $3$ dimensions with real scalars.

title: Complex Numbers cannot be Ordered Compatibly with Ring Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ be the field of complex numbers. There exists no total ordering on $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ which is compatible with the structure of $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

title: Complex Numbers form Algebra
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms an algebra over the field of real numbers. This algebra is: $(1): \quad$ An associative algebra. $(2): \quad$ A commutative algebra. $(3): \quad$ A normed division algebra. $(4): \quad$ A nicely normed $*$-algebra. However, $\C$ is not a real $*$-algebra.

title: Complex Numbers form Field
snippet: Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\C, +, \times}$, where: $\C$ is the set of all complex numbers $+$ is the operation of complex addition $\times$ is the operation of complex multiplication Then $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ forms a field.

title: Complex Numbers form Integral Domain
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms an integral domain under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

title: Complex Numbers form Preordered Vector Space
snippet: Consider the complex numbers $\C$ as a vector space over itself. Define the relation $\ge^\C$ by: $z \ge^\C w$ $z - w \in \hointr 0 \infty$ for each $z, w \in \C$. Then $\struct {\C, \ge^\C}$ is a preordered vector space.

title: Complex Numbers form Ring
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$ forms a ring under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

title: Complex Numbers form Subfield of Quaternions
snippet: The field of complex numbers $\struct {\C, +, \times}$ is isomorphic to the subfields of the quaternions $\struct {\mathbb H, +, \times}$ whose underlying subsets are: $(1): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf i = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: c = d = 0}$ $(2): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf j = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: b = d = 0}$ $(3): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf k = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k \in \mathbb H: b = c = 0}$ That is: $(1): \quad \mathbb H_\mathbf i = \set {a \mathbf 1 + b…

title: Complex Numbers form Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\C$ be the complex numbers realised as a normed algebra (this is possible from Complex Numbers form Algebra). Let $\overline {\, \cdot \,}$ be complex conjugation. Then $\tuple {\C, \overline {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

title: Complex Numbers form Vector Space over Reals
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Then the $\R$-module $\C$ is a vector space.

title: Complex Numbers form Vector Space over Themselves
snippet: The set of complex numbers $\C$, with the operations of addition and multiplication, forms a vector space.

title: Complex Numbers of Type Rational a plus b root 2 form Field
snippet: Let $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set: $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {x \in \C: x = a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Q}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers, is a number field.

title: Complex Numbers under Addition form Group
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The structure $\struct {\C, +}$ is a group.

title: Complex Numbers under Addition form Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. The structure $\struct {\C, +}$ is an infinite abelian group.

title: Complex Numbers under Addition form Monoid
snippet: The set of complex numbers under addition $\left({\C, +}\right)$ forms a monoid.

title: Complex Numbers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\C, \times}$ consisting of the set of complex numbers $\C$ under multiplication $\times$ is not a group.

title: Complex Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of complex numbers under multiplication $\struct {\C, \times}$ forms a monoid.

title: Complex Numbers with Complex Modulus form Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of complex numbers. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ be the complex modulus. Then $\struct {\C, \size {\, \cdot \,}}$ is a normed vector space.

title: Complex Plane is Banach Space
snippet: The complex plane, along with the complex modulus, forms a Banach space over $\C$.

title: Complex Plane is Complete Metric Space
snippet: The complex plane, along with the metric induced by the norm given by the complex modulus, forms a complete metric space.

title: Complex Plane is Homeomorphic to Real Plane
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the complex plane. Let $\R^2$ denote the Euclidean plane. Then the function $\phi : \R^2 \to \C$ defined by: $\map \phi {x, y} = x + i y$ is a homeomorphism between $\R^2$ and $\C$.

title: Complex Plane is Metric Space
snippet: Let $\C$ be the set of all complex numbers. Let $d: \C \times \C \to \R$ be the function defined as: $\map d {z_1, z_2} = \size {z_1 - z_2}$ where $\size z$ is the modulus of $z$. Then $d$ is a metric on $\C$ and so $\struct {\C, d}$ is a metric space.

title: Complex Plane is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, \tau_d}$ be the complex number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\struct {\C, \tau_d}$ is separable.

title: Complex Power/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Powers ==

title: Complex Power Series/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Power Series ==

title: Complex Power by Complex Exponential is Analytic
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\psi, \eta \in \C$ be constant. Let $\map f z = z^\psi \, \map \exp {-\eta z}$, where: $z^\psi$ denotes $z$ to the power of $\psi$, defined on its principal branch $\map \exp {-\eta z}$ denotes the complex exponential function. Then $f$ is analytic on any simply connected domain that does not contain the origin nor any points on the negative real axis.

title: Complex Power is of Exponential Order Epsilon
snippet: Let: $f: \hointr 0 \to \to \C: t \mapsto t^\phi$ be $t$ to the power of $\phi$, for $\phi \in \C$, defined on its principal branch. Let $\map \Re \phi > -1$. Then $f$ is of exponential order $\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small in magnitude.

title: Complex Reciprocal Function is not Entire
snippet: Let $f: \C_{\ne 0} \to \C$ be the complex function defined as: $\forall z \in \C_{\ne 0}: \map f z = \dfrac 1 z$ Then $f$ is not an entire function.

title: Complex Riemann Integral is Contour Integral
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \C$ be a complex Riemann integrable function over some closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t = \int_\CC \map f t \rd t$ where: the integral on the is a complex Riemann integral the integral on the is a contour integral $\CC$ is a straight line segment along the real axis, connecting $a$ to $b$.

title: Complex Roots of Polynomial with Real Coefficients occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: Let $\map f z = a_n z^n + a_{n - 1} z^{n - 1} + \cdots + a_1 z + a_0$ be a polynomial over complex numbers where $a_0, \ldots, a_n$ are real numbers. Let $\alpha \in \C$ be a root of $f$. Then $\overline \alpha$ is also a root of $f$, where $\overline \alpha$ denotes the complex conjugate of $\alpha$. That is, all complex roots of $f$ appear as conjugate pairs.

title: Complex Roots of Unity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Roots of Unity==

title: Complex Roots of Unity are Vertices of Regular Polygon Inscribed in Circle
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ge 3$. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z^n = 1$. Let $U_n = \set {e^{2 i k \pi / n}: k \in \N_n}$ be the set of $n$th roots of unity. Let $U_n$ be plotted on the complex plane. Then the elements of $U_n$ are located at the vertices of a regular $n$-sided polygon $P$, such that: $(1):\quad$ $P$ is circumscribed by a unit circle whose center is at $\tuple {0, 0}$ $(2):\quad$ one of those vertices is at $\tuple {1, 0}$.

title: Complex Roots of Unity in Exponential Form
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 0$. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number such that $z^n = 1$. Then: $U_n = \set {e^{2 i k \pi / n}: k \in \N_n}$ where $U_n$ is the set of $n$th roots of unity. That is: $z \in \set {1, e^{2 i \pi / n}, e^{4 i \pi / n}, \ldots, e^{2 \paren {n - 1} i \pi / n} }$ Thus for every integer $n$, the number of $n$th roots of unity is $n$. Setting $\omega := e^{2 i \pi / n}$, $U_n$ can then be written as: $U_n = \set {1, \omega, \omega^2, \ldots, \omega^{n - 1} }$

title: Complex Roots of Unity include 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $U_n = \set {z \in \C: z^n = 1}$ be the set of complex $n$th roots of unity. Then $1 \in U_n$. That is, $1$ is always one of the complex $n$th roots of unity of any $n$.

title: Complex Roots of Unity occur in Conjugate Pairs
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $U_n$ denote the complex $n$th roots of unity: $U_n = \set {z \in \C: z^n = 1}$ Let $\alpha \in U_n$ be the first complex $n$th root of unity. Then: $\forall k \in \Z_{>0}, k < \dfrac n 2: \overline {\alpha^k} = \alpha^{n - k}$ That is, each of the complex $n$th roots of unity occur in conjugate pairs: $\tuple {\alpha, \alpha^{n - 1} }; \tuple {\alpha^2, \alpha^{n - 2} }; \ldots; \tuple {\alpha^s, \alpha^{n - s} }$ where: $s = \dfrac {n - 1} 2$ for odd $n$ $s = \dfrac {n - 2} 2$ for even $n$.

title: Complex Sequence is Null iff Modulus of Sequence is Null
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a complex sequence. Then: $z_n \to 0$ $\cmod {z_n} \to 0$ That is: $\sequence {z_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a null sequence $\sequence {\cmod {z_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a null sequence.

title: Complex Sequence is Null iff Positive Integer Powers of Sequence are Null
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a complex sequence. Let $k \in \N$. Then: $z_n \to 0$ ${z_n}^k \to 0$

title: Complex Sine Function is Entire
snippet: Let $\sin: \C \to \C$ be the complex sine function. Then $\sin$ is entire.

title: Complex Sine Function is Unbounded
snippet: Let $\sin: \C \to \C$ be the complex sine function. Then $\sin$ is unbounded.

title: Complex Singular Point/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Singular Points ==

title: Complex Subtraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Subtraction ==

title: Complex Subtraction is Closed
snippet: The set of complex numbers is closed under subtraction: $\forall a, b \in \C: a - b \in \C$

title: Complex System/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Complex Systems ==

title: Complex Trigonometric Functions are Entire
snippet: Let $F$ be a trigonometric function over the complex numbers. Then $F$ is an entire function.

title: Complex Vector Inner Product is Complex Inner Product
snippet: The complex vector inner product is an example of a complex inner product.

title: Complex Vector Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\C$ denote the set of complex numbers. Then the complex vector space $\C^n$ is a vector space.

title: Complex Vector Space with Dot Product is Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\C^d$ be a complex vector space with $d$ dimensions. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ be the dot product on $\C^d$. Then $\C^d$ endowed with $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a Hilbert space.

title: Component Mappings of Set Coproduct are Injective
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Let $\struct {C, i_1, i_2}$ be a coproduct of $S_1$ and $S_2$. Then $i_1$ and $i_2$ are injections.

title: Component is not necessarily Path Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $C$ be a component of $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $C$ is also an path component of $T$.

title: Component of Complement of Jordan Curve has Curve as Boundary
snippet: Let $\phi : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve. Let $J = \phi \closedint 0 1$ be the image of $\phi$. Suppose that $\R^2 \setminus J$ has at least two distinct components. Then, for any component $U$ of $\R^2 \setminus J$: $\partial U = J$ where $\partial U$ denotes the boundary of $U$.

title: Component of Finite Union in Ultrafilter
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\UU$ be a ultrafilter on $S$. Let $\set {Y_1, \dots, Y_n}$ be a pairwise disjoint set of subsets of $S$ such that $S = Y_1 \cup \cdots \cup Y_n$. Then there is a unique $k \in \set {1, \dots, n}$ such that $Y_k \in \UU$.

title: Component of Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Components of Graphs ==

title: Component of Locally Connected Space is Open
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a locally connected topological space. Let $G$ be a component of $T$. Then $G$ is open.

title: Component of Point is not always Intersection of its Clopen Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map {\operatorname {Comp}_x} T$ denote the component of $x$ in $T$. Let $K_x = \ds \bigcap_{x \mathop \in K} K$ clopen in $T$. Then it is not always the case that $\map {\operatorname {Comp}_x} T = K_x$

title: Component of Resolvent Set of Element in Unital Banach Algebra is Disjoint from or Component of Resolvent Set in Closed Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $U$ be a component of $\map {\rho_A} x$. Then either: $U$ is a component of $\map {\rho_B} x$ or: $U \cap \map {\rho_B} x = \O$

title: Component of Vector/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Components of Vectors ==

title: Component of Vector in Plane/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Component of Vector in Plane ==

title: Component of Vector is Scalar Projection on Standard Ordered Basis Element
snippet: Let $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \mathbf e_3}$ be the standard ordered basis of Cartesian $3$-space $S$. Let $\mathbf a = a_1 \mathbf e_1 + a_2 \mathbf e_2 + a_3 \mathbf e_3$ be a vector quantity in $S$. Then: $\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf e_i = a_i$

title: Components and Quasicomponents of Arens-Fort Space are Equal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Arens-Fort space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $A$ is a component of $T$ $A$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

title: Components are Open iff Union of Open Connected Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad$ The components of $T$ are open. $(2): \quad S$ is a union of open connected sets of $T$.

title: Components of Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero are Single Points
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then the components of $A$ are singletons.

title: Components of Metric at Origin of Normal Neighborhood of Pseudo-Riemannian Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Let $\struct {U_p, \tuple {x^i}}$ be a normal coordinate chart. Suppose $g_{ij}$ are the components of metric $g$ in coordinates $\tuple {x^i}$ at $p \in M$. Then: $g_{ij} = \pm_{ij} \delta_{ij}$ where $\delta_{ij}$ denotes the Kronecker delta, and $\pm_{ij}$ is a sign that depends on $i$ and $j$.

title: Components of Metric at Origin of Normal Neighborhood of Riemannian Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Let $\struct {U_p, \tuple {x^i}}$ be a normal coordinate chart. Suppose $g_{ij}$ are the components of metric $g$ in coordinates $\tuple {x^i}$ at $p \in M$. Then: $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$ where $\delta_{ij}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Components of Separation are Clopen
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \mid B$ be a separation of $T$. Then both $A$ and $B$ are clopen in $T$.

title: Components of Separation are Separated Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \mid B$ be a separation of $T$. Then $A$ and $B$ are separated sets of $T$.

title: Components of Vector between two Points
snippet: Let $A, B$ be points in the Euclidean space $\R^n$. Let their Cartesian coordinates be given by: {{eqn | l = A | r = \tuple {a_1 , a_2, \ldots, a_n } }} {{eqn | l = B | r = \tuple {b_1 , b_2, \ldots, b_n } }} Let $\vec {AB}$ be the vector quantity that represents the directed line segment with startpoint $A$ and endpoint $B$. Then the vector components of $\vec {AB}$ are: $\vec {AB} = \tuple {b_1 - a_1, b_2 - a_2, \ldots, b_n - a_n}$

Let $\mathbf a$ be expressed in component form: $\mathbf a = x \mathbf i + y \mathbf j + z \mathbf k$ Then:

snippet: Let $\mathbf r$ be a vector quantity embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf k$ be the unit vectors in the positive directions of the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Let $\cos \alpha$, $\cos \beta$ and $\cos \gamma$ be the direction cosines of $\mathbf r$ with respect to the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be the components of $\mathbf r$ in the $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf k$ directions respectively. Let $r$ denote the magnitude of $\mathbf r$, that is: $r := \size {\mathbf r}$ Then:

title: Components of Zero Vector Quantity are Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf r$ be a vector quantity embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $\mathbf r$ be expressed in terms of its components: $\mathbf r = x \mathbf i + y \mathbf j + z \mathbf k$ Let $\mathbf r$ be the zero vector. Then: $x = y = z = 0$

snippet: == Examples of Componentwise ==

title: Composite Complete Lattice Homomorphisms is Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{A_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct{A_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{A_3, \preceq_3}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi_1: L_1 \to L_2$ and $\phi_2: L_2 \to L_3$ be complete lattice homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : A_1 \to A_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a complete lattice homomorphism of $L_1$ to $L_3$

title: Composite Fibonacci Numbers with Prime Index
snippet: The sequence of composite Fibonacci numbers with a prime index begins: $4181, 1 \, 346 \, 269, 24 \, 157 \, 817, 165 \, 580 \, 141, \ldots$ The corresponding sequence of prime indices begins: $19, 31, 37, 41, 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, \ldots$

title: Composite Frame Homomorphism is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ be frames. Let $\phi_1: L_1 \to L_2$ and $\phi_2: L_2 \to L_3$ be frame homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : S_1 \to S_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a frame homomorphism of $L_1$ to $L_3$

title: Composite Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C, \mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ and $G: \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be covariant functors. Let $GF: \mathbf C \to \mathbf E$ be the composition of $G$ with $F$. Then $G F$ is also a covariant functor.
