snippet: == Examples of Composite Gaussian Integers == The following are examples of composite Gaussian integers: {{eqn | l = 2 | r = \paren {1 + i} \paren {1 - i} }} {{eqn | l = 46 + 9 i | r = \paren {5 + 12 i} \paren {2 - 3 i} }} {{eqn | l = 5 + 12 i | r = \paren {3 + 2 i}^2 }}

title: Composite Hypothesis Test/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composite Hypothesis Tests ==

title: Composite Lattice Homomorphisms is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{A_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct{A_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{A_3, \vee_3, \wedge_3, \preceq_3}$ be lattices. Let $\phi_1: L_1 \to L_2$ and $\phi_2: L_2 \to L_3$ be lattice homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : A_1 \to A_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a lattice homomorphism of $L_1$ to $L_3$

title: Composite Localic Mapping is Localic Mapping
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}, L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ be locales. Let $f_1 : L_1 \to L_2$ and $f_2 : L_2 \to L_3$ be localic mappings. Then: the composite $f_2 \circ f_1 : L_1 \to L_3$ is a localic mapping.

title: Composite Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, S_3$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ and $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings. Then the composite mapping $g \circ f$ is also a mapping.

title: Composite Mersenne Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composite Mersenne Numbers ==

title: Composite Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composite Numbers ==

title: Composite Number has Prime Factor
snippet: Let $a$ be a composite number. Then there exists a prime number $p$ such that: $p \divides a$ where $\divides$ means is a divisor of.

title: Composite Number has Prime Factor not Greater Than its Square Root
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ and $n = p_1 \times p_2 \times \cdots \times p_j$, $j \ge 2$, where $p_1, \ldots, p_j \in \Bbb P$ are prime factors of $n$. Then $\exists p_i \in \Bbb P$ such that $p_i \le \sqrt n$. That is, if $n \in \N$ is composite, then $n$ has a prime factor $p \le \sqrt n$.

title: Composite Number has Two Divisors Less Than It
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 1}$ such that $n \notin \mathbb P$. Then: $\exists a, b \in \Z: 1 < a < n, 1 < b < n: n = a b$ That is, a non-prime number greater than $1$ can be expressed as the product of two positive integers strictly greater than $1$ and less than $n$. Note that these two numbers are not necessarily distinct.

title: Composite Semilattice Homomorphisms is Semilattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $S_1 = \struct{A_1, \circ_1}$, $S_2 = \struct{A_2, \circ_2}$ and $S_3 = \struct{A_3, \circ_3}$ be semilattices. Let $\phi_1: S_1 \to S_2$ and $\phi_2: S_2 \to S_3$ be semilattice homomorphisms. Let $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1 : A_1 \to A_3$ be the composite mapping of $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ Then: $\phi_2 \circ \phi_1$ is a semilattice homomorphism of $S_1$ to $S_3$

title: Composite of Antisymmetric Relations is not necessarily Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be antisymmetric relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also antisymmetric.

title: Composite of Automorphisms is Automorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $\phi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be automorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an automorphism.

title: Composite of Bijection with Inverse is Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Then: {{eqn | l = f^{-1} \circ f | r = I_S }} {{eqn | l = f \circ f^{-1} | r = I_T }} where $I_S$ and $I_T$ are the identity mappings on $S$ and $T$ respectively.

title: Composite of Bijections is Bijection
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be mappings such that $\Dom f = \Cdm g$. Then: If $f$ and $g$ are both bijections, then so is $f \circ g$ where $f \circ g$ is the composite mapping of $f$ with $g$.

title: Composite of Connected Relation is not necessarily Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be connected relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also connected.

title: Composite of Continuous Mappings at Point between Metric Spaces is Continuous at Point
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {X_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {X_2, d_2}, M_3 = \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be continuous at $a \in X_1$. Let $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be continuous at $\map f a \in X_2$. Then their composite $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is continuous at $a \in X_1$.

title: Composite of Continuous Mappings between Metric Spaces is Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {X_1, d_1}$, $M_2 = \struct {X_2, d_2}$ and $M_3 = \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ and $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be continuous mappings. Then their composite $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is continuous.

title: Composite of Continuous Mappings between Normed Vector Spaces is Continuous
snippet: Let $X, Y, Z$ be normed vector spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be continuous mappings on $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $g \circ f : X \to Z$ be a composite mapping where: $\forall x \in X : \map {\paren {g \circ f} } x := \map g {\map f x}$ Then $g \circ f$ is continuous on $X$.

title: Composite of Continuous Mappings is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2, T_3$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ and $g: T_2 \to T_3$ be continuous mappings. Then the composite mapping $g \circ f: T_1 \to T_3$ is continuous.

title: Composite of Continuous Real Functions at Point is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real numbers. Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions. Let $g$ be continuous at a point $a \in \R$. Let $f$ be continuous at the point $\map g a \in \R$. Then their composite $f \circ g$ is continuous at $a$.

title: Composite of Continuous Real Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real numbers. Let $g: S \to T$ be a real function which is continuous on a real interval $S \subseteq \R$. Let $f: T \to \R$ be a real function which is continuous on a real interval $T \subseteq \R$. Then their composite $f \circ g: I \to \R$ is continuous on $I$.

title: Composite of Endomorphisms is Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $\phi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n} \to \struct {S, \odot_1, \odot_2, \ldots, \odot_n}$ be endomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an endomorphism.

title: Composite of Epimorphisms is Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ $\struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n} \to \struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an epimorphism.

title: Composite of Evaluation Mapping and Projection
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for some indexing set $I$. Let $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of continuous mappings. Let $\ds Y = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} Y_i$ be the product space of $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be the evaluation mapping induced by $\family{f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let: $pr_i : Y \to Y_i$ denote the $i$th projection on $Y$ Then: $\forall i \in I: pr_i \circ f = f_i$

title: Composite of Group Epimorphisms is Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \odot}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \odot} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be (group) epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (group) epimorphism.

title: Composite of Group Homomorphisms is Homomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \circ}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be homomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a homomorphism.

title: Composite of Group Isomorphisms is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ}$, $\struct {G_2, *}$ and $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ and $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be group isomorphisms. Then the composite of $\psi$ with $\phi$ is also a group isomorphism.

title: Composite of Group Monomorphisms is Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {G_1, \circ}$ $\struct {G_2, *}$ $\struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be groups. Let: $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ $\psi: \struct {G_2, *} \to \struct {G_3, \oplus}$ be monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a monomorphism.

title: Composite of Homeomorphisms between Metric Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M_1, M_2, M_3$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ and $g: M_2 \to M_3$ be homeomorphisms. Then $g \circ f: M_1 \to M_3$ is also a homeomorphism.

title: Composite of Homeomorphisms is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2, T_3$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ and $g: T_2 \to T_3$ be homeomorphisms. Then $g \circ f: T_1 \to T_3$ is also a homeomorphism.

title: Composite of Increasing Mappings is Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $\struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be ordered sets. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and: $\psi: \struct {S_2, \preceq_2} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be increasing mappings. Then $\psi \circ \phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ is also an increasing mapping.

title: Composite of Injection on Surjection is not necessarily Either
snippet: Let $f$ be an injection. Let $g$ be a surjection. Let $f \circ g$ denote the composition of $f$ with $g$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f \circ g$ is either a surjection or an injection.

title: Composite of Injections is Injection
snippet: A composite of injections is an injection. That is: If $f$ and $g$ are injections, then so is $f \circ g$.

title: Composite of Inverse of Mapping with Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $f \circ f^{-1} = I_{\Img f}$ where: $f \circ f^{-1}$ is the composite of $f$ and $f^{-1}$ $f^{-1}$ is the inverse of $f$ $I_{\Img f}$ is the identity mapping on the image set of $f$.

title: Composite of Isomorphisms of Categories is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C, \mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ and $G: \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be isomorphisms of categories. Let $GF: \mathbf C \to \mathbf E$ be the composition of $G$ with $F$. Let $F^{-1}: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ and $G^{-1}: \mathbf E \to \mathbf D$ be the inverse isomorphisms of $F$ and $G$ respectively. Then: $G F$ is also an isomorphism of categories. with inverse: $\paren{GF}^{-1} = F^{-1} G^{-1}$ where $F^{-1}: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ and $G^{-1}: \mathbf E \to \mathbf D$ denote the inverse isomorphisms of $F$ and $G$ respectively.

title: Composite of Mapping with Inverse
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\forall x \in S: \map {f^{-1} \circ f} x = \eqclass x {\RR_f}$ where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by $f$ $\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the $\RR_f$-equivalence class of $x$.

title: Composite of Mapping with Inverse of Another is Identity implies Mappings are Equal
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $f$ and $g$ be mappings on $A \times B$. Let $f$ and $g$ be such that: $f \circ g^{-1} = I_B$ where: $g^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $g$ $I_B$ denotes the identity mapping on $B$ $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. Then: $f = g$

title: Composite of Monomorphisms is Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ $\struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ $\psi: \struct {S_2, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n} \to \struct {S_3, \oplus_1, \oplus_2, \ldots, \oplus_n}$ be monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a monomorphism.

title: Composite of Order Isomorphisms is Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $\struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be ordered sets. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and: $\psi: \struct {S_2, \preceq_2} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be order isomorphisms. Then $\psi \circ \phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ is also an order isomorphism.

title: Composite of Ordered Ring Isomorphisms is Ordered Ring Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, +_1, \circ_1, \preccurlyeq_1}, \struct {S_2, +_2, \circ_2, \preccurlyeq_2}, \struct {S_3, +_3, \circ_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$ be ordered rings. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ and $\psi: S_2 \to S_3$ be ordered ring isomorphisms. Then the composite mapping $\psi \circ \phi: S_1 \to S_3$ is also an ordered ring isomorphism.

title: Composite of Ordered Ring Monomorphisms is Ordered Ring Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, +_1, \circ_1, \preccurlyeq_1}, \struct {S_2, +_2, \circ_2, \preccurlyeq_2}, \struct {S_3, +_3, \circ_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$ be ordered rings. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ and $\psi: S_2 \to S_3$ be ordered ring monomorphisms. Then the composite mapping $\psi \circ \phi: S_1 \to S_3$ is also an ordered ring monomorphism.

title: Composite of Ordered Semigroup Isomorphisms is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \circ_1, \preccurlyeq_1}, \struct {S_2, \circ_2, \preccurlyeq_2}, \struct {S_3, \circ_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$ be ordered semigroups. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ and $\psi: S_2 \to S_3$ be ordered semigroup isomorphisms. Then the composite mapping $\psi \circ \phi: S_1 \to S_3$ is also an ordered semigroup isomorphism.

title: Composite of Orderings is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also an ordering on $A$.

title: Composite of Permutations is Permutation
snippet: Let $f, g$ are permutations of a set $S$. Then their composite $g \circ f$ is also a permutation of $S$.

title: Composite of Quotient Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR_1$ be an equivalence on $S$, and $\RR_2$ be an equivalence on the quotient set $S / \RR_1$. We can find an equivalence $\RR_3$ on $S$ such that $\paren {S / \RR_1} / \RR_2$ is in one-to-one correspondence with $S / \RR_3$ under the mapping: $\phi: \paren {S / \RR_1} / \RR_2 \to S / \RR_3: \eqclass {\eqclass x {\RR_1} } {\RR_2} \mapsto \eqclass x {\RR_3}$.

title: Composite of Quotient Mappings in Topology is Quotient Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$, $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ and $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be quotient mappings. Then $g \circ f : S_1 \to S_3$ is a quotient mapping.

title: Composite of Reflexive Relations is Reflexive
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be reflexive relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is also reflexive.

title: Composite of Relation Isomorphisms is Relation Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \RR_1}$, $\struct {S_2, \RR_2}$ and $\struct {S_3, \RR_3}$ be relational structures. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \RR_1} \to \struct {S_2, \RR_2}$ and: $\psi: \struct {S_2, \RR_2} \to \struct {S_3, \RR_3}$ be relation isomorphisms. Then $\psi \circ \phi: \struct {S_1, \RR_1} \to \struct {S_3, \RR_3}$ is also a relation isomorphism.

title: Composite of Strictly Increasing Mappings is Strictly Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $\struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be ordered sets. Let: $\phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and: $\psi: \struct {S_2, \preceq_2} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be strictly increasing mappings. Then $\psi \circ \phi: \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ is also a strictly increasing mapping.

title: Composite of Surjection on Injection is not necessarily Either
snippet: Let $f$ be an injection. Let $g$ be a surjection. Let $g \circ f$ denote the composition of $g$ with $f$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $g \circ f$ is either a surjection or an injection.

title: Composite of Surjections is Surjection
snippet: A composite of surjections is a surjection. That is: If $g$ and $f$ are surjections, then so is $g \circ f$.

title: Composite of Symmetric Relations is not necessarily Symmetric
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be symmetric relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily symmetric.

title: Composite of Three Mappings in Cycle forming Injections and Surjection
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$, $g: B \to C$ and $h: C \to A$ be mappings. Let the following hold: $h \circ g \circ f$ is an injection $f \circ h \circ g$ is an injection $g \circ f \circ h$ is a surjection. where: $g \circ f$ (and so on) denote composition of mappings. Then each of $f$, $g$ and $h$ are bijections.

title: Composite of Total Relations is Total
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be total relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is also total.

title: Composite of Transitive Relations is not necessarily Transitive
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be transitive relations on $A$. Then their composite $\RR \circ \SS$ is not necessarily also transitive.

title: Composite with Constant Mapping is Constant Mapping
snippet: Let $f_c: S \to T$ be the constant mapping defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {f_c} x = c$ where $c \in T$. Then for all mappings $g: \Dom g \to S$: $f_c \circ g$ is a constant mapping and for all mappings $h: T \to \Cdm h$: $h \circ f_c$ is a constant mapping where: $\Dom g$ denotes the domain of $g$ $\Cdm h$ denotes the codomain of $h$ $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Composition Mapping of Restriction Mappings
snippet: Let $S$, $T$, and $U$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ and $g: T \to U$ be mappings. Let $A \subseteq S$, $B \subseteq T$ and $C \subseteq U$. Let $f \sqbrk S \subseteq B$ and $g \sqbrk T \subseteq C$. Then: {{eqn| l = \paren{g \circ f} \restriction_{A \times C} | r = \paren{g \restriction_{B \times C} } \circ \paren{f \restriction_{A \times B} } }} where: $\paren{g \circ f} \restriction_{A \times C}$ is the restriction of $g \circ f$ to $A \times C$ $f \restriction_{A \times B}$ is the restriction of $f$ to $A \times B$ $g \restriction_{B \times C}$ is the restriction of $g$ to $B \times C$

title: Composition Series/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Composition Series ==

title: Composition Series of Group of Prime Power Order
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$, and whose order is a prime power: $\order G = p^n, p \in \mathbb P, n \ge 1$ Then $G$ has a composition series: $\set e = G_0 \subset G_1 \subset \ldots \subset G_n = G$ such that: $\order {G_k} = p^k$ where: $G_k \lhd G_{k + 1}$ $G_{k + 1} / G_k$ is cyclic and of order $p$.

title: Composition of 3 Mappings where Pairs of Mappings are Bijections
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be sets. Let: $f: A \to B$ $g: B \to C$ $h: C \to D$ be mappings. Let $g \circ f$ and $h \circ g$ be bijections. Then $f$, $g$ and $h$ are all bijections.

title: Composition of Addition Mappings on Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $\alpha_a: \N \to \N$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \N: \map {\alpha_a} x = x + a$ Then: $\alpha_{a + b} = \alpha_b \circ \alpha_a$

title: Composition of Affine Transformations is Affine Transformation
snippet: Let $\EE$, $\FF$ and $\GG$ be affine spaces with difference spaces $E$, $F$ and $G$ respectively. Let $\LL: \EE \to \FF$ and $\MM: \FF \to \GG$ be affine transformations. Let $L$ and $M$ be the tangent maps of $\LL$ and $\MM$ respectively. Then the composition $\MM \circ \LL: \EE \to \FF$ is an affine transformation with tangent map $M \circ L$.

title: Composition of Cartesian Products of Mappings
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {S_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$, $\family {T_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ and $\family {U_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be families of sets all indexed by $I$. For each $\alpha \in I$, let: $f_\alpha: S_\alpha \to T_\alpha$ be a mapping $g_\alpha: T_\alpha \to U_\alpha$ be a mapping.

title: Composition of Commuting Idempotent Mappings is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be idempotent mappings from $S$ to $S$. Let: $f \circ g = g \circ f$ where $\circ$ denotes composition. Then $f \circ g$ is idempotent.

title: Composition of Compatible Closure Operators
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ be closure operators on $S$. Let $\CC_f$ and $\CC_g$ be the sets of closed sets of $S$ with respect to $f$ and $g$ respectively. For each subset $T$ of $S$, let the following hold: $(1): \quad$ If $T$ is closed with respect to $g$, then $\map f T$ is closed with respect to $g$. That is, if $T \in \CC_g$ then $\map f T \in \CC_g$. $(2): \quad$ If $T$ is closed with respect to $f$, then $\map g T$ is closed with respect to $f$. That is, if $T \in \CC_f$ then $\map g T \in \CC_f$. Let $\CC_h = \CC_f \cap \CC_g$.

title: Composition of Computable Real-Valued Functions is Computable
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be computable. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be computable. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is computable.

title: Composition of Computable Real Functions is Computable
snippet: Let $f,g : \R \to \R$ be computable real functions. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be defined as: $\map h x = \map f {\map g x}$ Then $h$ is computable.

title: Composition of Computably Uniformly Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Computably Uniformly Continuous
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be computably uniformly continuous. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be computably uniformly continuous. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is computably uniformly continuous.

title: Composition of Computably Uniformly Continuous Real Functions is Computably Uniformly Continuous
snippet: Let $f,g : \R \to \R$ be computably uniformly continuous real functions. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be defined as: $\map h x = \map f {\map g x}$ Then $h$ is computably uniformly continuous.

title: Composition of Continuous Linear Transformations is Continuous Linear Transformation
snippet:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$, $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$, $\struct{Z, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Z}$ be normed vector spaces over $K$. $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. Let $S \circ T : X 	o Z$ be the composition of mappings such that: $ orall T \in \map {CL} {X, Y} :  orall S \in \map {CL} {Y, Z} :  orall x \in X : \map {S \circ T} x := \map S {\map T x}$ Then $S \circ T \in \map {CL} {X, Z}$.

title: Composition of Continuous Mapping on Compact Space Preserves Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $\struct{ X, d_X }$ be a compact metric space. Let $\struct{ Y, d_Y }, \struct{ Z, d_Z }$ be metric spaces. Let $\phi : Y \to Z$ be a continuous mapping. For all $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to Y$ be a continuous mapping. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping such that $\sequence {f_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges to $f$ uniformly on $X$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\phi \circ f_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges to $\phi \circ f$ uniformly on $X$.

title: Composition of Dirac Delta Distribution with Function with Simple Zero
snippet: Let $\delta \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a delta sequence. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a real function with a simple zero at $x_0$. Let $f$ be strictly monotone. Let $\phi \in \map \DD \R$ be a test function. Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\map \delta {\map f x} = \dfrac {\map \delta {x - x_0} } {\size {\map {f'} {x_0} } }$ which can be interpreted as: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map \delta {\map f x} \map \phi x \rd x = \dfrac {\map \phi {x_0} } {\size {\map {f'} {x_0} } }$ which more strictly…

title: Composition of Direct Image Mappings of Mappings
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let: $f^\to: \powerset A \to \powerset B$ and $g^\to: \powerset B \to \powerset C$ be the direct image mappings of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f}^\to = g^\to \circ f^\to$

title: Composition of Direct Image Mappings of Relations
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq A \times B, \RR_2 \subseteq B \times C$ be relations. Let: ${\RR_1}^\to: \powerset A \to \powerset B$ and ${\RR_2}^\to: \powerset B \to \powerset C$ be the direct image mappings of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$. Then: $\paren {\RR_2 \circ \RR_1}^\to = {\RR_2}^\to \circ {\RR_1}^\to$

title: Composition of Direct Sums of Bounded Linear Operators on Hilbert Space
Composition of Distance-Preserving Mappings is Distance-Preserving
snippet: Let: $\struct {X_1, d_1}$ $\struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let: $\phi: \struct {X_1, d_1} \to \struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\psi: \struct {X_2, d_2} \to \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be distance-preserving mappings. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a distance-preserving mapping.

title: Composition of Elliptic Integral
snippet: An elliptic integral in $x$ can be reduced to the sum of: an elementary function and constant multiples of integrals in three standard forms involving $x$ and: the (elliptic) modulus $k$ the parameter $n$. Those three standard forms are known as Legendre's standard elliptic integrals.

title: Composition of Functors is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$, $\mathbf B$, $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf A \to \mathbf B$, $G: \mathbf B \to \mathbf C$ and $H: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be functors. Then composition of functors is associative: $H \paren {G F} = \paren {H G} F$

title: Composition of Galois Connections is Galois Connection
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ and $L_3 = \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be ordered sets. Let: $g_1: S_1 \to S_2, g_2: S_2 \to S_3, d_1: S_2 \to S_1, d_2: S_3 \to S_2$ be mappings such that: $\tuple {g_1, d_1}$ and $\tuple {g_2, d_2}$ are Galois connections. Then $\tuple {g_2 \circ g_1, d_1 \circ d_2}$ is also a Galois connection.

title: Composition of Idempotent Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be idempotent mappings. Suppose that $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ have the same images. That is, suppose that $f \sqbrk {g \sqbrk S} = g \sqbrk {f \sqbrk S}$. Then $f \circ g$ and $g \circ f$ are idempotent.

title: Composition of Identification Mappings is Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ and $S_3$ be sets. Let $f_1: S_1 \to S_2$ and $f_2: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f_1$ and $\tau_1$. Let $\tau_3$ be the identification topology on $S_3$ with respect to $f_2$ and $\tau_2$. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_3$ be the composition of $f_2$ with $f_1$: $\phi = f_2 \circ f_1$ Then $\phi$ is itself an identification mapping.

title: Composition of Inflationary Mappings is Inflationary
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be inflationary mappings. Then $f \circ g$, the composition of $f$ and $g$, is also inflationary.

title: Composition of Inflationary and Idempotent Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f$ and $g$ be inflationary and idempotent mappings on $S$. {{item|(3):|$\Img {f \circ g} \Img {g \circ f}$}} where: $\circ$ represents composition $\Img f$ represents the image of a mapping $f$.

title: Composition of Integer/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Compositions of Integers ==

title: Composition of Inverse Image Mappings of Mappings
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B, g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let: $f^\gets: \powerset B \to \powerset A$ and $g^\gets: \powerset C \to \powerset B$ be the inverse image mappings of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f}^\gets = f^\gets \circ g^\gets$

title: Composition of Isometries is Isometry
snippet: Let: $\struct {X_1, d_1}$ $\struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\struct {X_3, d_3}$ be metric spaces. Let: $\phi: \struct {X_1, d_1} \to \struct {X_2, d_2}$ $\psi: \struct {X_2, d_2} \to \struct {X_3, d_3}$ be isometries. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also an isometry.

title: Composition of Isomorphisms is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: B \to C$ be isomorphisms with inverses $f^{-1}: B \to A$ and $g^{-1}: C \to B$ respectively. Then: the composition $g \circ f: A \to C$ is an isomorphism with inverse $f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}: C \to A$.

title: Composition of Left Regular Representation with Right
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be a semigroup. Let $\lambda_x, \rho_y$ be the left and right regular representations of $\struct {S, *}$ with respect to $x$ and $y$ respectively. Let $\lambda_x \circ \rho_y$, $\rho_y \circ \lambda_x$, and so on, be defined as the composition of the mappings $\lambda_x$ and $\rho_y$. Then $\forall x, y \in S$: $\lambda_x \circ \rho_y = \rho_y \circ \lambda_x$

title: Composition of Left Regular Representations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be a semigroup. Let $\lambda_x$ be the left regular representation of $\struct {S, *}$ with respect to $x$. Let $\lambda_x \circ \lambda_y$ be defined as the composition of the mappings $\lambda_x$ and $\lambda_y$. Then $\forall x, y \in S$: $\lambda_x \circ \lambda_y = \lambda_{x * y}$

title: Composition of Linear Isometries is Linear Isometry
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$, $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, 
orm \cdot_Z}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X 	o Y$ and $S : Y 	o Z$ be linear isometries. Then $S T$ is a linear isometry.

title: Composition of Linear Isomorphisms is Linear Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$, $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Z}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X 	o Y$ and $S : Y 	o Z$ be linear isomorphisms. Then $S T : X 	o Z$ is a linear isomorphism.

title: Composition of Linear Real Functions
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\theta_{a, b}: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map {\theta_{a, b} } x = a x + b$ Let $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b}$ denote the composition of $\theta_{c, d}$ with $\theta_{a, b}$. Then: $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b} = \theta_{a c, b c + d}$

title: Composition of Linear Transformations is Isomorphic to Matrix Product
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $F$, $G$ and $H$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $p, n, m > 0$ respectively. Let $\sequence {a_p}$, $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$ be ordered bases Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ denote the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be the $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$. Let $\sqbrk {u; \sequence {c_m}, \sequence {b_n} }$ be the matrix of $u$ relative to $\sequence {b_n}$ and $\sequence {c_m}$.

title: Composition of Linear Transformations is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X, Y, Z$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T_1 : X \to Y$ and $T_2 : Y \to Z$ be linear transformations. Then the composition $T_2 \circ T_1 : X \to Z$ is a linear transformation.

title: Composition of Mapping and Inclusion is Restriction of Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then $f \circ i_A = f \restriction A$ where $i_A$ denotes the inclusion mapping of $A$, $f \restriction A$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to $A$.

title: Composition of Mapping with Inclusion is Restriction
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of the domain of $S$. Let $i_A: A \to S$ be the inclusion mapping from $A$ to $S$. Then: $f \circ i_A = f \restriction_A$ where $f \restriction_A$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to $A$.

title: Composition of Mapping with Mapping Restricted to Image
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Let $f : A \to B, g: B \to C$ be mappings. Let $g \circ f : A \to C$ denote the composite mapping of $f$ with $g$. Let $f \sqbrk A$ denote the image of $A$ under $f$. Let $f \restriction_{A \times f \sqbrk A} : A \to f \sqbrk A$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $A \times f \sqbrk A$. Let $g \restriction_{f \sqbrk A} : f \sqbrk A \to C$ denote the restriction of $g$ to $f \sqbrk A$.

title: Composition of Mappings/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Compositions of Mappings ==

title: Composition of Mappings is Associative
snippet: The composition of mappings is an associative binary operation: $\paren {f_3 \circ f_2} \circ f_1 = f_3 \circ \paren {f_2 \circ f_1}$ where $f_1, f_2, f_3$ are arbitrary mappings which fulfil the conditions for the relevant compositions to be defined.

title: Composition of Mappings is Composition of Relations
snippet: Let $f_1: S_1 \to S_2$ and $f_2: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings such that the domain of $f_2$ is the same as the codomain of $f_1$. Let $f_2 \circ f_1$ be the composite of $f_1$ and $f_2$. Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be considered as relations on $S_1 \times S_2$ and $S_2 \times S_3$ respectively. Then $f_2 \circ f_1$ defined as the composition of relations coincides with the definition of $f_2 \circ f_1$ as the composition of mappings.

title: Composition of Mappings is Left Distributive over Homomorphism of Pointwise Operation
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ and $\struct {T, \otimes}$ be algebraic structures. Let: $S^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $S$. Let $f$ be a homomorphism from $S$ to $T$. Let $g, h \in S^A$ be mappings from $A$ to $S$. Then: $f \circ \paren {g \odot h} = \paren {f \circ g} \otimes \paren {f \circ h}$ where: $g \odot h$ denotes the pointwise operation on $S^A$ induced by $\odot$ $f \circ h$ denotes the composition of $f$ with $h$.

title: Composition of Mappings is Right Distributive over Pointwise Operation
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let: $B^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $B$ $S^B$ denote the set of mappings from $B$ to $S$. Let $f, g \in S^B$ be mappings from $B$ to $S$. Let $h \in B^A$ be a mapping from $A$ to $B$. Then: $\paren {f \odot g} \circ h = \paren {f \circ h} \odot \paren {g \circ h}$ where: $f \odot g$ denotes the pointwise operation on $S^B$ induced by $\odot$ $g \circ h$ denotes the composition of $g$ with $h$.

title: Composition of Mappings is not Commutative
snippet: The composition of mappings is not in general a commutative binary operation: $f_2 \circ f_1 \ne f_1 \circ f_2$

title: Composition of Measurable Mappings is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X_1, \Sigma_1}$, $\struct {X_2, \Sigma_2}$ and $\struct {X_3, \Sigma_3}$ be measurable spaces. Let $f: X_1 \to X_2$ be a $\Sigma_1 \, / \, \Sigma_2$-measurable mapping. Let $g: X_2 \to X_3$ be a $\Sigma_2 \, / \, \Sigma_3$-measurable mapping. Then their composition $g \circ f: X_1 \to X_3$ is $\Sigma_1 \, / \, \Sigma_3$-measurable.

title: Composition of One-Variable URM Computable Functions
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \N$ and $g: \N \to \N$ be URM computable functions of one variable. Let $f \circ g$ be the composition of $f$ and $g$. Then $f \circ g: \N \to \N$ is a URM computable function.

title: Composition of Open Mappings is Open Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$, $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, \tau_Z}$ be topological spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be open mappings. Then $g \circ f : X \to Z$ is an open mapping.

title: Composition of Permutations is not Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma S$ denote the set of permutations on $S$. Let $\pi, \rho$ be elements of $\map \Gamma S$ Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\pi \circ \rho = \rho \circ \pi$ where $\circ$ denotes composition.

title: Composition of Product Mappings on Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $\mu_a: \N \to \N$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \N: \map {\mu_a} x = x a$ Then: $\mu_{a b} = \mu_b \circ \mu_a$

title: Composition of Regular Representations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be a semigroup. Let $\lambda_x, \rho_x$ be the left and right regular representations of $\struct {S, *}$ $x$. Let $\lambda_x \circ \lambda_y$, $\rho_x \circ \rho_y$ etc. be defined as the composition of the mappings $\lambda_x$ and $\lambda_y$ etc. Then $\forall x, y \in S$, the following results hold:

title: Composition of Relation with Inverse is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then the composition of $\RR$ with its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is symmetric: $(1): \quad \RR^{-1} \circ \RR$ is a symmetric relation on $S$ $(2): \quad \RR \circ \RR^{-1}$ is a symmetric relation on $T$.

title: Composition of Relations Preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $A, B, S, T$ be relations as subsets of Cartesian products. Let $A \subseteq B$ and $S \subset T$. Then: $A \circ S \subseteq B \circ T$

title: Composition of Relations is Associative
snippet: The composition of relations is an associative binary operation: $\paren {\RR_3 \circ \RR_2} \circ \RR_1 = \RR_3 \circ \paren {\RR_2 \circ \RR_1}$

title: Composition of Relations is not Commutative
snippet: Composition of relations is, in general, not commutative. That is, it is usually the case that: $\RR_1 \circ \RR_2 \ne \RR_2 \circ \RR_1$ for relations $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$.

title: Composition of Repeated Compositions of Injections
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Let the sequence of mappings: $f^0, f^1, f^2, \ldots, f^n, \ldots$ be defined as: $\forall n \in \N: f^n \left({x}\right) = \begin{cases} x & : n = 0 \\ f \left({x}\right) & : n = 1 \\ f \left({f^{n-1} \left({x}\right)}\right) & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}: f^n \circ f^m = f^{m + n}$ where $f^n \circ f^m$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Composition of Right Inverse with Mapping is Idempotent
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $g: T \to S$ be a right inverse mapping of $f$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f} \circ \paren {g \circ f} = g \circ f$

title: Composition of Right Regular Representations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *}$ be a semigroup. Let $\rho_x$ be the right regular representation of $\struct {S, *}$ with respect to $x$. Let $\rho_x \circ \rho_y$ be defined as the composition of the mappings $\rho_x$ and $\rho_y$. Then $\forall x, y \in S$: $\rho_x \circ \rho_y = \rho_{y * x}$

title: Composition of Ring Automorphisms is Ring Automorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a set. Let: $\struct {R, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be ring automorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) automorphism.

title: Composition of Ring Endomorphisms is Ring Endomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a set. Let: $\struct {R, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) endomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) endomorphism.

title: Composition of Ring Epimorphisms is Ring Epimorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) epimorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) epimorphism.

title: Composition of Ring Homomorphisms is Ring Homomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \odot_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \odot_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \odot_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \odot_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \odot_3}$ be homomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a homomorphism.

title: Composition of Ring Isomorphisms is Ring Isomorphism
snippet: Let: $\left({R_1, +_1, \circ_1}\right)$ $\left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right)$ $\left({R_3, +_3, \circ_3}\right)$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \left({R_1, +_1, \circ_1}\right) \to \left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right)$ $\psi: \left({R_2, +_2, \circ_2}\right) \to \left({R_3, +_3, \circ_3}\right)$ be (ring) isomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) isomorphism.

title: Composition of Ring Monomorphisms is Ring Monomorphism
snippet: Let: $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be rings. Let: $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ $\psi: \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2} \to \struct {R_3, +_3, \circ_3}$ be (ring) monomorphisms. Then the composite of $\phi$ and $\psi$ is also a (ring) monomorphism.

title: Composition of Sequence with Mapping
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_j}_{j \mathop \in B}$ be a sequence. Let $\sigma: A \to B$ be a mapping, where $A \subseteq \N$. Then $\sequence {a_j} \circ \sigma$ is a sequence whose value at each $k \in A$ is $a_{\map \sigma k}$. Thus $\sequence {a_j} \circ \sigma$ is denoted $\sequence {a_{\map \sigma k} }_{k \mathop \in A}$.

title: Composition of Sequentially Computable Real-Valued Functions is Sequentially Computable
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^n$ and $E \subseteq \R^m$ be subsets of real cartesian space. Let $f : D \to \R$ be sequentially computable. Let $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_n : E \to \R$ be sequentially computable. Suppose that, for every $\bsx \in E$: $\tuple {\map {g_1} \bsx, \map {g_2} \bsx, \dotsc, \map {g_n} \bsx} \in D$ Then $h : E \to \R$ defined as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}, \dotsc, \map {g_n} {x_1, \dotsc, x_m}}$ is sequentially computable.

title: Composition of Sequentially Computable Real Functions is Sequentially Computable
snippet: Let $f,g : \R \to \R$ be sequentially computable real functions. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be defined as: $\map h x = \map f {\map g x}$ Then $h$ is sequentially computable.

title: Composition of Symmetric Relation with Itself is Union of Products of Images
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a symmetric relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR \circ \RR = \ds \map {\bigcup_{s \mathop \in S} } {\map \RR s \times \map \RR s}$ where $\RR \circ \RR$ is the composition of $\RR$ with itself $\map \RR s$ is the image of $s$ under $\RR$ $\map \RR s \times \map \RR s$ is the Cartesian product of $\map \RR s$ with itself

title: Composition of Symmetries is Associative
snippet: Let $P$ be a geometric figure. Let $S_P$ be the set of all symmetries of $P$. Let $\circ$ denote composition of mappings. Let $\phi, \psi, \chi$ be symmetries of $P$. Then: $\paren {\phi \circ \psi} \circ \chi = \phi \circ \paren {\psi \circ \chi}$ That is, composition of symmetries is associative.

title: Composition of Symmetries is Symmetry
snippet: Let $P$ be a geometric figure. Let $S_P$ be the set of all symmetries of $P$. Let $\circ$ denote composition of mappings. Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be symmetries of $P$. Then $\phi \circ \psi$ is also a symmetry of $P$.

title: Composition of Three Mappings which form Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be non-empty sets. Let $f: A \to B$, $g: B \to C$ and $h: C \to A$ be mappings. Let the following hold: where: $g \circ f$ (and so on) denote composition of mappings $I_A$ (and so on) denote the identity mappings. Then each of $f$, $g$ and $h$ are bijections, and: {{eqn | l = f^{-1} | r = h \circ g }} {{eqn | l = g^{-1} | r = f \circ h }} {{eqn | l = h^{-1} | r = g \circ f }} where $f^{-1}$ (and so on) denote the inverse mappings.

title: Composition of Weakly Compact Linear Transformation and Bounded Linear Transformation is Weakly Compact
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$, $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ and $\struct {Z, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Z}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X 	o Y$ be a weakly compact linear transformation. Let $A : Y 	o Z$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $B : Z 	o X$ be a bounded linear transformation. Then: $(1): \quad$ $T B : Z 	o Y$ is weakly compact $(2): \quad$ $A T : X 	o Z$ is weakly compact.

title: Composition with Zero Morphism is Zero Morphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $0$ be a zero object in $\mathbf C$. Let $A, B, C, D$ be objects in $\mathbf C$. Let $f : A \to B$, $g : B \to C$ and $h : C \to D$ be morphisms in $\mathbf C$. Let $g$ be a zero morphism. Then $g \circ f$ and $h \circ g$ are zero morphisms.

title: Compositions of Closure Operators are both Closure Operators iff Operators Commute
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f$ and $g$ be closure operators on $S$. {{item|(3):|$\Img {f \circ g} \Img {g \circ f}$}} where $\Img \cdot$ denotes the image of a mapping.

title: Compound Distribution of Poisson Distributed Bernoulli Trials has Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $N$ be a discrete random variable with a Poisson distribution with expectation $\lambda$. Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_N$ be pairwise independent discrete random variables each with a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $P$. Let $S_N : X_1 + X_2 + \cdots + X_N$ be the resulting compound distribution. Then $S_N$ has a Poisson distribution with expectation $\lambda p$.

title: Computable Rational Sequence is Computable Real Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a computable rational sequence. Then, $\sequence {x_n}$ is a computable real sequence.

title: Computable Real Sequence iff Limits of Computable Rational Sequences
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_m}$ be a sequence of real numbers. Then, $\sequence {x_m}$ is computable there exist: A computable rational sequence $\sequence {a_k}$ Total recursive functions $\phi, \psi : \N^2 \to \N$ such that: $\forall m, p \in \N: \forall n \ge \map \psi {m, p}: \size {a_{\map \phi {m, n}} - x_m} < \dfrac 1 {p + 1}$

title: Computable Subsequence of Computable Rational Sequence is Computable
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a computable rational sequence. Let $\phi : \N \to \N$ be a total recursive function. Then: $\sequence {x_{\map \phi n}}_{n \in \N}$ is a computable rational sequence.

title: Concatenation of Contours is Contour
snippet: Let $C$ and $D$ be contours in the complex plane. That is, $C$ is a finite sequence of directed smooth curves $C_1, \ldots, C_n$. Let $C_k$ be parameterized by the smooth path $\gamma_k: \closedint {a_k} {b_k} \to \C$ for all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$. Similarly, $D$ is a finite sequence of directed smooth curves $D_1, \ldots, D_m$. Let $D_j$ be parameterized by the smooth path $\sigma_j: \closedint {c_j} {d_j} \to \C$ for all $j \in \set {1, \ldots, m}$. Suppose $\map {\gamma_n} {b_n} = \map {\sigma_1} {c_1}$. Then the finite sequence: $C_1, \ldots, C_n, D_1, \ldots, D_m$ defines a contour.

title: Concatenation of URM Programs is Associative
snippet: Let $P, Q, R$ be one-variable URM programs. Then the concatenated URM programs $P * \paren {Q * R}$ and $\paren {P * Q} * R$ are the same.

title: Concave Envelope is Concave Majorant of Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\R$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a non-empty closed convex set. Let $f : C \to \R$ be a function. Let $\hat f : C \to \overline \R$ be the concave envelope of $f$. Then $\hat f$ is concave and $f \le \hat f$.

title: Concave Real Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is concave on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then $f$ is continuous on $\openint a b$.

title: Concave Real Function is Left-Hand and Right-Hand Differentiable
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is concave on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then the left-hand derivative $\map {f'_-} x$ and right-hand derivative $\map {f'_+} x$ both exist for all $x \in \openint a b$.

title: Concentration of Lipschitz Functionals of Normal Vector
snippet: Let $X_1, \dots, X_n$ be continuous random variables with a standard normal distribution $\Gaussian 0 1$. Let $F: \R^n \to \R$ be L-Lipschitz. Then: $\map \Pr {\size {\map F X - \expect {\map F X} } > L u} \le \map \exp {-\dfrac {u^2} {2 C} }$ where: $\Pr$ denotes the probability function $\expect {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes expectation.

title: Concentric Circles do not Intersect
snippet: If two circles are concentric, they share no points on their circumferences. Alternatively, this can be worded: If two concentric circles share one point on their circumferences, then they share them all (that is, they are the same circle).

title: Condition for 3 Points in Plane to be Collinear
snippet: Let $A = \tuple {x_1, y_1}, B = \tuple {x_2, y_2}, C = \tuple {x_3, y_3}$ be points in the Cartesian plane. Then: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear the determinant: $\begin {vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \\ \end {vmatrix}$ equals zero.

title: Condition for 3 over n producing 3 Egyptian Fractions using Greedy Algorithm when 2 Sufficient
snippet: Consider proper fractions of the form $\dfrac 3 n$ expressed in canonical form. Let Fibonacci's Greedy Algorithm be used to generate a sequence $S$ of Egyptian fractions for $\dfrac 3 n$. Then $S$ consists of $3$ terms, where $2$ would be sufficient the following conditions hold: $n \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ $\exists d: d \divides n$ and $d \equiv 2 \pmod 3$

title: Condition for 4 Points to be Coplanar
snippet: Let: {{eqn | l = p_1 | r = \tuple {x_1, y_1, z_1} }} {{eqn | l = p_2 | r = \tuple {x_2, y_2, z_2} }} {{eqn | l = p_3 | r = \tuple {x_3, y_3, z_3} }} {{eqn | l = p_4 | r = \tuple {x_4, y_4, z_4} }} be distinct points in Cartesian $3$-space. Then $p_1$, $p_2$, $p_3$ and $p_4$ are coplanar : $\begin {vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & z_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & z_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & z_3 & 1 \\ x_4 & y_4 & z_4 & 1 \end {vmatrix} = 0$ where the construct is evaluated as a determinant.

title: Condition for Agreement of Family of Mappings
snippet: Let $\family {A_i}_{i \mathop \in I}, \family {B_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be families of non empty sets. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings such that: $\forall i \in I: f_i \in \map \FF {A_i, B_i}$ {{explain|Clarify: what is $\map \FF {A_i, B_i}$? From the context it can be understood as being the set of all mappings $f_i: A_i \to B_i$ but this is just a guess.

title: Condition for Alexandroff Extension to be T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $T^*$ is a $T_1$ space $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Condition for Alexandroff Extension to be T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $p$ be a new element not in $S$. Let $S^* := S \cup \set p$. Let $T^* =\struct {S^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $S$. Then $T^*$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space $T$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space.

title: Condition for Algebra Loop to be Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebra loop. Let $\struct {S \times S, \otimes}$ denote the external direct product of $\struct {S, \odot}$ with itself: $\forall \tuple {x_1, y_1}, \tuple {x_2, y_2} \in S \times S: \tuple {x_1, y_1} \otimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} = \tuple {x_1 \odot x_2, y_1 \odot y_2}$ Let $f$ and $g$ be mappings from $\struct {S \times S, \otimes}$ to $\struct {S, \odot}$. Let $f \odot g$ denote the pointwise operation on $S^{S \times S}$ induced by $\odot$.

title: Condition for Algebraic Structure to be Self-Distributive Quasigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure. Then: $\struct {S, \odot}$ is a self-distributive quasigroup for every $a \in S$, the left and right regular representations $\lambda_a$ and $\rho_a$ on $S$ are automorphisms of $\struct {S, \odot}$.

title: Condition for Bipartite Graph to be Hamiltonian
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E}$ be a bipartite graph. Let $G$ be Hamiltonian. Then $\card A = \card B$. That is, there is the same number of vertices in $A$ as there are in $B$.

title: Condition for Cartesian Product Equivalent to Associated Cardinal Number
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be nonempty sets. Let $\card S$ denote the cardinal number of $S$. Then: $S \times T \sim \card {S \times T} \iff S \sim \card S \land T \sim \card T$ where $S \times T$ denotes the cartesian product of $S$ and $T$.

title: Condition for Circles to be Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ be circles embedded in a Cartesian plane. Let $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ be described by Equation of Circle in Cartesian Plane as: Then $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ are orthogonal : $2 \alpha_1 \alpha_2 + 2 \beta_1 \beta_2 = c_1 + c_2$

title: Condition for Closed Extension Space to be T0 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_p$ is a $T_0$ space $T$ is.

title: Condition for Closed Extension Space to be T4 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then: $T^*_p$ is a $T_4$ space $T$ is a $T_4$ space vacuously and $T^*_p$ in this case is also a $T_4$ space vacuously.

title: Condition for Closed Extension Space to be T5 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_p = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_p}$ be the closed extension space of $T$. Then: $T^*_p$ is a $T_5$ space $T$ is a $T_5$ space vacuously and $T^*_p$ in this case is also a $T_5$ space vacuously.

title: Condition for Closure of Open Ball to be Closed Ball of Same Radius
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space. $(1) \quad$ for all $x \in X$ and $r > 0$ we have $\map \cl {\map {B_r} x} = \map { {B_r}^-} x$, where $\cl$ denotes closure $(2) \quad$ for each $\epsilon > 0$ and $x, y \in X$ with $x \ne y$, there exists $z \in X$ with $\map d {z, y} < \epsilon$ and $\map d {x, z} < \map d {x, y}$.

title: Condition for Codeword to be in Code
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear code over a Galois field $\GF$. Let $\mathbf H$ be a parity check matrix for $C$. A vector $\mathbf x$ is a codeword of $C$ : $\mathbf H \mathbf x^\intercal = \mathbf 0$ where: ${}^\intercal$ denotes the transpose of a matrix $\mathbf 0$ denotes the zero vector.

title: Condition for Cofinal Nonlimit Ordinals
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be nonlimit ordinals. Let $\operatorname{cof}$ denote the cofinal relation. Let $\le$ denote the subset relation. Furthermore, let $x$ and $y$ satisfy the condition: $0 < x \le y$ Then: $\map {\operatorname{cof}} { y,x }$

title: Condition for Collinearity of Points in Complex Plane
Condition for Commensurability of Roots of Quadratic Equation
snippet: Consider the quadratic equation: $(1): \quad a x - x^2 = \dfrac {b^2} 4$ Then $x$ and $a - x$ are commensurable $\sqrt{a^2 - b^2}$ and $a$ are commensurable.

title: Condition for Complete Bipartite Graph to be Edgeless
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E} =: K_{m, n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $m$ vertices in $A$ and $n$ vertices in $B$. Then: $K_{m, n}$ is edgeless either $m = 0$ or $n = 0$.

title: Condition for Complete Bipartite Graph to be Semi-Hamiltonian
snippet: Let $K_{m, n}$ be a complete bipartite graph. $K_{m, n}$ is semi-Hamiltonian either: $m = n = 1$ or: $m = n + 1$ (or $n = m + 1$).

title: Condition for Complex Number to be in Right Half Plane
snippet: Let $\C$ be the complex plane. Let $P$ be the half-plane of $\C$ to the right of the infinite straight line $x = \lambda$. The points in $P$ can be defined by: $\map \Re z > \lambda$ where $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$.

title: Condition for Complex Root of Unity to be Primitive
snippet: Let $n, k \in \N$. Then $\alpha_k = \map \exp {\dfrac {2 \pi i k} n}$ is a primitive $n$th root of unity $\gcd \set {n, k} = 1$.

title: Condition for Complex Sequence to Converge to Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence z_n$ be a complex sequence in the extended complex plane $\C_\infty$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} z_n = \infty$ if: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \cmod {z_n} = \infty$ in the extended real numbers $\overline \R$.

title: Condition for Composite Mapping on Left
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Suppose that $C$ is non-empty. Let $f: A \to B$ and $g: A \to C$ be mappings. Let $\RR: B \to C$ be a relation such that $g = \RR \circ f$ is the composite of $f$ and $\RR$. Then $\RR$ may be a mapping : $\forall x, y \in A: \map f x = \map f y \implies \map g x = \map g y$ That is: $\forall x, y \in A: \map f x = \map f y \implies \map g x = \map g y$ $\exists h: B \to C$ such that $h$ is a mapping and $h \circ f = g$

title: Condition for Composite Mapping on Right
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Let $f: B \to A$ and $g: C \to A$ be mappings. Let $\RR: C \to B$ be a relation such that $g = f \circ \RR$ is the composite of $\RR$ and $f$. Then $\RR$ may be a mapping : $\Img g \subseteq \Img f$ That is: $\Img g \subseteq \Img f$ $\exists h: C \to B$ such that $h$ is a mapping and $f \circ h = g$

title: Condition for Composite Mapping to be Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ and $g: T \to S$ be mappings such that: $g \circ f = I_S$ where $I_S$ is the identity mapping on $S$. Then $f$ is an injection and $g$ is a surjection.

title: Condition for Composite Relation with Inverse to be Identity
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR \circ \RR^{-1}$ be the composite of $\RR$ with its inverse. Let $I_T$ be the identity mapping on $T$. Then: $\RR \circ \RR^{-1} = I_T$ $\RR$ is many-to-one and: $\RR$ is right-total.

title: Condition for Composition Series
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Then: a normal series $\HH$ for $G$ is a composition series for $G$ every factor group of $\HH$ is a simple group.

title: Condition for Composition of Linear Real Functions to be Commutative
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\theta_{a, b}: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map {\theta_{a, b} } x = a x + b$ Let $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b}$ denote the composition of $\theta_{c, d}$ with $\theta_{a, b}$. Then: $\theta_{c, d} \circ \theta_{a, b} = \theta_{a, b} \circ \theta_{c, d}$ $b c + d = a d + b$

title: Condition for Conchoid of Nicomedes to have Cusp
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a conchoid of Nicomedes such that: the perpendicular distance from the directrix $\CC$ of $\KK$ to the focus point $P$ of $\KK$ is $a$ the constant length of the line segment between $\KK$ and $\CC$ passing through $P$ is $b$. Then: $\KK$ has a cusp at $P$ $a = b$

title: Condition for Conchoid of Nicomedes to have Loop
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a conchoid of Nicomedes such that: the perpendicular distance from the directrix $\CC$ of $\KK$ to the focus point $P$ of $\KK$ is $a$ the constant length of the line segment between $\KK$ and $\CC$ through $P$ is $b$. Then: $\KK$ has a loop $a < b$

title: Condition for Concurrency of Three Straight Lines
snippet: Let $3$ straight lines $\LL_1$, $\LL_2$ and $\LL_3$ be embedded in a cartesian plane $\CC$, expressed using the general equations: Then $\LL_1$, $\LL_2$ and $\LL_3$ are concurrent : $\begin {vmatrix} l_1 & m_1 & n_1 \\ l_2 & m_2 & n_2 \\ l_3 & m_3 & n_3 \end {vmatrix} = 0$ where $\begin {vmatrix} \cdot \end {vmatrix}$ denotes a determinant.

title: Condition for Conditional Expectation to be Almost Surely Non-Negative
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an integrable random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Then we have: $\expect {X \mid \GG} \ge 0$ almost everywhere $\expect {X \cdot \chi_A} \ge 0$ for each $A \in \GG$ where $\chi_A$ is the characteristic function of $A$.

title: Condition for Conic to be Central
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a conic section whose equation is given by: $a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2 + 2 g x + 2 f y + c = 0$ Then $\CC$ is a central conic $a b \ne h^2$.

title: Condition for Constant Operation to be Distributive over Another Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\sqbrk c$ denote the constant operation for some $c \in S$. Then: $\sqbrk c$ is distributive over $\circ$ $c \circ c = c$

title: Condition for Continuity on Interval
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $\mathbb I$. Then $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb I$ : $\forall x \in \mathbb I: \forall \epsilon > 0: \exists \delta > 0: y \in \mathbb I \land \size {x - y} < \delta \implies \size {\map f x - \map f y} < \epsilon$

title: Condition for Coordinate Axes to have Same Orientation
snippet: Let $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ be Cartesian coordinate systems of the same dimension. Let $\EE_1$ and $\EE_2$ denote an ordered basis of $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ respectively. Then: $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ have the same orientation the matrix representing $\EE_1$ in terms of $\EE_2$ (and $\EE_2$ in terms of $\EE_1$) has a (strictly) positive determinant .

title: Condition for Cosets of Subgroup of Monoid to be Partition
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e$. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let the identity element of $\struct {H, \circ}$ be $e$. Then: the set of left cosets of $\struct {H, \circ}$ in $\struct {S, \circ}$ form a partition of $S$ and: the set of right cosets of $\struct {H, \circ}$ in $\struct {S, \circ}$ form a partition of $S$.

title: Condition for Cross-Ratio to be Harmonic
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be points on a straight line. Let their cross-ratio $\set {A, B; C, D}$ be a harmonic ratio. Then: $\set {A, B; C, D} = \set {B, A; C, D}$

title: Condition for Curve to be Elliptic
snippet: Let $C$ be an elliptic curve embedded in the Cartesian plane expressed in standard form: $y^2 = x^3 + a x + b$ Then: $4 a^3 + 27 b^2 \ne 0$

title: Condition for Darboux Integrability
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f$ be a bounded real function defined on $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable : for every $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$, there exists a finite subdivision $S$ of $\closedint a b$ such that $\map U S - \map L S < \epsilon$ where $\map U S$ is the upper Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ $S$ $\map L S$ is the lower Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ $S$

title: Condition for Denesting of Square Root
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Q_{\ge 0}$. Suppose $\sqrt b \notin \Q$. Then: $\exists p, q \in \Q: \sqrt {a + \sqrt b} = \sqrt p + \sqrt q$ $\exists n \in \Q: a^2 - b = n^2$.

title: Condition for Difference of Field Elements to be Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $a, b \in F$ Then: $a - b = 0_F$ $a = b$ where $a - b$ denotes subtraction.

title: Condition for Differentiable Functional to have Extremum
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of mappings. Let $y, h \in S: \R \to \R$ be real functions. Let $J \sqbrk y: S \to \R$ be a differentiable functional. Then a necessary condition for the differentiable functional $J \sqbrk {y; h}$ to have an extremum for $y = \hat y$ is: $\bigvalueat {\delta J \sqbrk {y; h} } {y \mathop = \hat y} = 0$

title: Condition for Differential to be Exact
snippet: The expression: $\ds \sum_i P_i \rd x_i$ where $\set {P_i}$ are real-valued functions over $\set {x_1, x_2, \ldots}$ is an exact differential : $\forall i, j : \dfrac {\partial P_i} {\partial x_j} = \dfrac {\partial P_j} {\partial x_i}$

title: Condition for Divisibility of Powers of Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime. Let $k, l \in \Z_{>0}$. Then: $p^k \divides p^l \iff k \le l$

title: Condition for Division by Field Elements to be Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $a, b \in F$. Then: $\dfrac a b = 1_F$ $a = b$ where $\dfrac a b$ denotes division.

title: Condition for Double Root of Equation
snippet: Let $\map f x = 0$ have a double root $x = \alpha$. Then $x = \alpha$ is also a root of $\map {f'} x$, where $f'$ is the derivative of $f$ $x$.

title: Condition for Edge to be Bridge
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a connected graph. Let $e \in E$ be an edge of $G$. Then $e$ is a bridge $e$ does not lie on any circuit of $G$.

title: Condition for Element of Quotient Group of Additive Group of Reals by Integers to be of Finite Order
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\R / \Z$ denote the quotient group of $\struct {\R, +}$ by $\struct {\Z, +}$. Let $x + \Z$ denote the coset of $\Z$ by $x \in \R$. Then $x + \Z$ is of finite order $x$ is rational.

title: Condition for Elements of Group to be in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$ be such that $2$ elements of $\set {x, y, x y}$ are elements of $h$. Then all the elements of $\set {x, y, x y}$ are in $H$.

title: Condition for Equal Angles contained by Elevated Straight Lines from Plane Angles
Condition for Equality of Adjacent Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\dbinom n k$ denote a binomial coefficient for $k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k = \dbinom n {k + 1}$ $n$ is an odd integer $k = \dfrac {n - 1} 2$

title: Condition for Equilibrium using Force Polygon
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a system of forces $\SS$ act at a point. Let $\SS$ give rise to a force polygon $A_0 A_1 \ldots A_n A_0$. Then $\SS$ is in equilibrium $A_n$ and $A_0$ coincide.

title: Condition for Equivalence Relation for Max Operation on Natural Numbers to be Congruence
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on the set of natural numbers $\N$. Let $\vee$ denote the max operation on $\N$: $\forall a, b \in \N: a \vee b := \max \set {a, b}$ Then: $\RR$ is a congruence relation for $\vee$ on $\N$ every equivalence class under $\RR$ is an order-convex subset of $\N$.

title: Condition for Equivalence of Norms that induce Banach Spaces
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $
orm \cdot_1$ and $
orm \cdot_2$ be norms on $X$ such that $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_1}$ and $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_2}$ are Banach spaces. Suppose that, for some real number $C > 0$: $
orm x_2 \le C 
orm x_1$ for all $x \in X$. Then $
orm \cdot_1$ and $
orm \cdot_2$ are equivalent.

title: Condition for Existence of Cardinal Sum
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \le \mathbf b \iff \exists \mathbf c: \mathbf a + \mathbf c = \mathbf b$ where $\mathbf c$ is also a cardinal.

title: Condition for Existence of Epimorphism from Quotient Structure to Epimorphic Image
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \odot}$ and $\struct {B, \otimes}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on $\struct {A, \odot}$. Let $f: \struct {A, \odot} \to \struct {B, \otimes}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\struct {A / \RR, \odot_\RR}$ denote the quotient structure defined by $\RR$. Let $q_\RR: A \to A / \RR$ denote the quotient mapping induced by $\RR$: $\forall x \in A: \map {q_\RR} x = \eqclass x \RR$ where $\eqclass x \RR$ denotes the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR$.

title: Condition for Existence of Expectation of Real-Valued Measurable Function composed with Absolutely Continuous Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\R$. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be a $\map \BB \R$-measurable function. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Then $\map h X$ is integrable $h$ is $\lambda$-integrable function. In this case: $\ds \expect {\map h X} = \int_\R \map h x \rd \map {P_X} x$ where $\expect {\map h X}$ denotes the expectation of $\map h X$.

Condition for Existence of Hamilton Cycles
snippet: == Open Question == Does there exist a simple necessary and sufficient condition for a graph to have a Hamilton cycle? There is no known criterion for testing whether or not a graph is Hamiltonian. However, see Ore's Theorem and its corollary Dirac's Theorem for a sufficient conditon (albeit weak).
