title: Correspondence Theorem
snippet: Correspondence Theorem (Set Theory) Correspondence Theorem (Group Theory) Correspondence Theorem for Quotient Rings Correspondence Theorem for Ring Epimorphisms Correspondence Theorem for Localizations of Rings

title: Correspondence Theorem (Group Theory)
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N \lhd G$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then every subgroup of the quotient group $G / N$ is of the form $H / N = \set {h N: h \in H}$, where $N \le H \le G$. Conversely, if $N \le H \le G$ then $H / N \le G / N$. The correspondence between subgroups of $G / N$ and subgroups of $G$ containing $N$ is a bijection. This bijection maps normal subgroups of $G / N$ onto normal subgroups of $G$ which contain $N$.

title: Correspondence Theorem (Set Theory)
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $\mathscr A$ be the set of partitions of $S$ associated with equivalence relations $\RR'$ on $S$ such that: $\tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \tuple {x, y} \in \RR'$ Then there exists a bijection $\phi$ from $\mathscr A$ onto the set of partitions of the quotient set $S / \RR$.

title: Correspondence Theorem for Localizations of Rings
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. Let $A \overset \iota \to A_S$ be the localization at $S$. Let $I$ be the set of saturated ideals of $A$ by $S$. Let $J$ be the set of ideals of $A_S$.

title: Correspondence Theorem for Quotient Rings
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq A$ be an ideal. Let $A / \mathfrak a$ be the quotient ring and $\pi : A \to A / \mathfrak a$ the quotient ring epimorphism.

title: Correspondence Theorem for Ring Epimorphisms
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $\pi : A \to B$ be a ring epimorphism. Let $I$ be the set of ideals of $A$ containing the kernel $\ker \pi$. Let $J$ be the set of ideals of $B$.

title: Correspondence between Abelian Groups and Z-Modules
Correspondence between Irrational Numbers and Simple Infinite Continued Fractions
snippet: Let $\R \setminus \Q$ be the set of irrational numbers. Let $S$ be the set of all simple infinite continued fractions in $\R$. The mappings: $\R \setminus \Q \to S$ that sends an irrational number to its continued fraction expansion $S \to \R \setminus \Q$ that sends a simple infinite continued fractions to its value are inverses of each other.

title: Correspondence between Linear Group Actions and Linear Representations
snippet: Let $\struct {k, +, \cdot}$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $k$ of finite dimension. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be a finite group. There is a one-to-one correspondence between linear group actions of $G$ on $V$ and linear representations of $G$ in $V$, as follows: Let $\phi: G \times V \to V$ be a group action. Let $\rho: G \to \map {\operatorname {Sym} } V$ be a permutation representation of $G$ on $V$. Suppose this is the case.

title: Correspondence between Neighborhood Space and Topological Space
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {S, \NN}$ be the neighborhood space induced by $\tau$ on $S$. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \tau} \to \struct {S, \NN}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map \phi x = x$ $\forall U \in \tau: \phi \sqbrk U = U \in \NN$ Let $\struct {T, \NN'}$ be a neighborhood space. Let $\struct {T, \tau'}$ be the topological space induced by $\NN$ on $S$.

title: Correspondence between Rational Numbers and Simple Finite Continued Fractions
snippet: Let $\Q$ be the set of rational numbers. Let $S$ be the set of all simple finite continued fractions in $\Q$, whose last partial denominators is not $1$. The mappings: $\Q \to S$ that sends an rational number to its continued fraction expansion $S \to \Q$ that sends a simple finite continued fractions to its value are inverses of each other.

title: Correspondence between Set and Ordinate of Cartesian Product is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $T \ne \O$. Let $S \times T$ denote their cartesian product. Let $t \in T$ be given. Let $j_t \subseteq S \times \paren {S \times T}$ be the relation on $S \times {S \times T}$ defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {j_t} s = \tuple {s, t}$ Then $j_t$ is a mapping.

title: Cosecant Function in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $\csc x = \dfrac 1 x \map F {\dfrac 1 2, \dfrac 1 2; \dfrac 3 2; \sin^2 x}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \ne \paren {k \pi}$ with $k \in \Z$ $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

title: Cosecant Function is Odd
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\csc x$ be the cosecant of $x$. Then, whenever $\csc x$ is defined: $\map \csc {-x} = -\csc x$ That is, the cosecant function is odd.

title: Cosecant Minus Sine
snippet: $\csc x - \sin x = \cos x \ \cot x$

title: Cosecant in terms of Hyperbolic Cosecant
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \csc = -\csch \paren {i z}$ where: $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function $\csch$ denotes the hyperbolic cosecant $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Cosecant is Reciprocal of Sine
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\sin \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\csc \theta = \dfrac 1 {\sin \theta}$ where $\csc$ and $\sin$ mean cosecant and sine respectively.

snippet: Let $P = \tuple {x, y}$ be a point in the cartesian plane whose origin is at $O$. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the $x$-axis and the line $OP$. Let $r$ be the length of $OP$. Then: $\csc \theta = \dfrac r x$ where $\csc$ denotes the secant of $\theta$.

snippet: $\csc \left({x + 2 \pi}\right) = \csc x$

title: Cosecant of Complement equals Secant
snippet: $\map \csc {\dfrac \pi 2 - \theta} = \sec \theta$ for $\theta \ne \paren {2 n + 1} \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\csc$ and $\sec$ are cosecant and secant respectively. That is, the secant of an angle is the cosecant of its complement. This relation is defined wherever $\cos \theta \ne 0$.

title: Cosecant of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\csc \paren {a + b i} = \dfrac {\sin a \cosh b - i \cos a \sinh b} {\sin^2 a \cosh^2 b + \cos^2 a \sinh^2 b}$ where: $\csc$ denotes the complex cosecant function. $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

title: Cosecant of Conjugate Angle
snippet: $\map \csc {2 \pi - \theta} = -\csc \theta$ where $\csc$ denotes cosecant. That is, the cosecant of an angle is the negative of its conjugate.

title: Cosecant of Supplementary Angle

title: Coset Equals Subgroup iff Element in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x \in G$. Let: $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$ $H x$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $x$.

title: Coset Product is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $a, b \in G$. Then the coset product: $\paren {a \circ N} \circ \paren {b \circ N} = \paren {a \circ b} \circ N$ is well-defined.

title: Coset Product of Normal Subgroup is Consistent with Subset Product Definition
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $a, b \in G$. Let $a \circ N$ and $b \circ N$ be the left cosets of $a$ and $b$ by $N$. Then the coset product: $\paren {a \circ N} \circ \paren {b \circ N} = \paren {a \circ b} \circ N$ is consistent with the definition of the coset product as the subset product of $a \circ N$ and $b \circ N$: $\paren {a \circ N} \paren {b \circ N} = \set {x \circ y: x \in a \circ N, y \in b \circ N}$

title: Coset Product on Non-Normal Subgroup is not Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ which is not normal. Let $a, b \in G$. Then it is not necessarily the case that the coset product: $\paren {a \circ H} \circ \paren {b \circ H} = \paren {a \circ b} \circ H$ is well-defined.

title: Coset Space forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$.

title: Coset Space wrt Subring forms Ring iff Subring is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a subring of $R$. For $a \in R$, let $\paren {a + S}$ denote the coset of $S$ by $a$. Then: The coset space of $R$ $S$ forms a ring $S$ is an ideal of $R$.

title: Coset by Identity
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$.

title: Coset of Subgroup of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H, K \le G$ be subgroups of $G$. Let $K \subseteq H$. Let $x \in G$. Then either: $x K \subseteq H$ or: $x K \cap H = \O$ where $x K$ denotes the left coset of $K$ by $x$.

title: Coset of Trivial Subgroup is Singleton
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $E := \struct {\set e, \circ}$ denote the trivial subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Let $g \in G$. Then the left coset and right coset of $E$ by $g$ is $\set g$.

title: Cosets are Equal iff Element in Other Coset
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$.

title: Cosets are Equal iff Product with Inverse in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$.

title: Cosets are Equivalent
snippet: All left cosets of a group $G$ with respect to a subgroup $H$ are equivalent. That is, any two left cosets are in one-to-one correspondence. The same applies to right cosets. As a special case of this: $\forall x \in G: \order {x H} = \order H = \order {H x}$ where $H$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Cosets in Abelian Group
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group. Then every right coset modulo $H$ is a left coset modulo $H$. That is: $\forall x \in G: x H = H x$ In an abelian group, therefore, we can talk about congruence modulo $H$ and not worry about whether it is left or right.

title: Cosets of Positive Reals in Multiplicative Group of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be the positive real axis of the complex plane: $S = \set {z \in \C: z = x + 0 i, x \in \R_{>0} }$ Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {S, \times}$ as a subgroup of the multiplicative group of complex numbers $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$. The cosets of $\struct {S, \times}$ are the sets of the form: $\set {z \in \C: \exists r \in \R_{>0}: z = r e^{i \theta}}$ for some $\theta \in \hointr 0 {2 \pi}$ That is, the sets of all complex numbers with a constant argument.

title: Cosine Function in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\map \cos x = \map F {\dfrac 1 2, -\dfrac 1 2; \dfrac 1 2; \sin^2 x}$ where $x$ is a real number such that $\size x < 1$.

title: Cosine Function in terms of Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $\cos x = \map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {\dfrac 1 2; \dfrac {-x^2} 4}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \in \R$ $\cos$ denotes the cosine function $\map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {a; x}$ is the generalized hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac 1 { a^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

title: Cosine Function is Absolutely Convergent
snippet: Let $\cos$ be the cosine function. Then: $\cos x$ is absolutely convergent for all $x \in \R$.

title: Cosine Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\cos x$ be the cosine of $x$. Then: $\cos x$ is continuous on $\R$.

title: Cosine Function is Even
snippet: For all $z \in \C$: $\map \cos {-z} = \cos z$ That is, the cosine function is even.

title: Cosine Inequality
snippet: $1 - \dfrac {x^2} 2 \le \cos x$ for all $x \in \R$.

title: Cosine in Terms of Haversine
snippet: $\cos \theta = 1 - 2 \hav \theta$ where $\cos$ denotes cosine and $\hav$ denotes haversine.

title: Cosine in terms of Cotangent
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number such that $\cos x \ne 0$. Then: {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = +\frac {\cot x} {\sqrt {1 + \cot^2 x} } | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $2 n \pi < x < \paren {2 n + 1} \pi$ }} {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = -\frac {\cot x} {\sqrt {1 + \cot^2 x} } | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n - 1} \pi < x < 2 n \pi$ }} where $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function and $\cot$ denotes the real cotangent function.

title: Cosine in terms of Hyperbolic Cosine
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\cos z = \map \cosh {i z}$ where: $\cos$ denotes the complex cosine $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Cosine in terms of Sine
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then: {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = +\sqrt {1 - \sin^2 x} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n - \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi$ }} {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = -\sqrt {1 - \sin^2 x} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 3 2} \pi$ }} where $\sin$ denotes the real sine function and $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function.

title: Cosine in terms of Tangent
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number such that $\cos x \ne 0$. Then: {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = +\frac 1 {\sqrt {1 + \tan^2 x} } | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n - \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi$ }} {{eqn | l = \cos x | r = -\frac 1 {\sqrt {1 + \tan^2 x} } | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 3 2} \pi$ }} where $\sin$ denotes the real sine function and $\tan$ denotes the real tangent function.

title: Cosine is Reciprocal of Secant
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\cos \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\cos \theta = \dfrac 1 {\sec \theta}$ where $\cos$ denotes the cosine function and $\sec$ denotes the secant function.

title: Cosine is of Exponential Order Zero
snippet: Let $\cos t$ be the cosine of $t$, where $t \in \R$. Then $\cos t$ is of exponential order $0$.

title: Cosine of Half Angle for Spherical Triangles
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\cos \dfrac A 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {\sin s \, \map \sin {s - a} } {\sin b \sin c} }$ where $s = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$.

title: Cosine of Half Angle in Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Let $s$ denote the semiperimeter of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $\cos \dfrac C 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {s \paren {s - c} } {a b} }$

title: Cosine of Half Side for Spherical Triangles
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\cos \dfrac a 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {\map \cos {S - B} \, \map \cos {S - C} } {\sin B \sin C} }$ where $S = \dfrac {A + B + C} 2$.

title: Coslice Category is Isomorphic to Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ denote the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Let $\mathbf 1$ denote the category one. Let $G: \mathbf 1\to \mathbf C$ be the functor defined by: $G* = C$ and $G \operatorname{id}_* = \operatorname{id}_C$ Let $C / \mathbf C$ denote the coslice category $\mathbf C$ under $C$. Let $\paren {G \downarrow \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$.

title: Cotangent Additive Formula
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ where $\N_{>0}$ denotes the non-zero natural numbers. Let $z \in \C$ such that $\map \sin {n z} \ne 0$ Then: $\ds \map \cot {n z} = \frac 1 n \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \map \cot {z + \frac {k \pi} n}$ where $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

title: Count of Binary Operations Without Identity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. The number $N$ of possible different binary operations which do not have an identity element that can be applied to $S$ is given by: $N = n^{\paren {\paren {n - 1}^2 + 1} } \paren {n^{2 \paren {n - 1} } - 1}$

snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. The number $N$ of possible different commutative binary operations that can be applied to $S$ is given by: $N = n^{\frac {n \paren {n + 1} } 2}$

title: Count of Commutative Binary Operations with Fixed Identity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. Let $x \in S$. The number $N$ of possible different commutative binary operations such that $x$ is an identity element that can be applied to $S$ is given by: $N = n^{\frac {n \paren {n - 1} } 2}$

title: Count of Commutative Binary Operations with Identity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. The number $N$ of possible different commutative binary operations that can be applied to $S$ which have an identity element is given by: $N = n^{\frac {n \paren {n - 1} } 2 + 1}$

title: Count of Commutative Operations on Finite Set which are Closed on Every Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set with $n$ elements. There are $2^{n \paren {n - 1} / 2}$ commutative binary operations on $S$ which are closed on all subsets of $S$.

title: Count of Commutative Quasigroups on Set given Count of Commutative Algebra Loops
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$. Let $e \in S$. Let there be $m$ commutative operations $\oplus$ on $S$ such that $\struct {S, \oplus}$ is an algebra loop whose identity is $e$. Then there are $n! m$ commutative binary operations $\otimes$ on $S$ such that $\struct {S, \otimes}$ is a quasigroup.

title: Count of Distinct Homomorphisms between Additive Groups of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. The number of distinct homomorphisms $\phi: \struct {\Z_m, +} \to \struct {\Z_n, +}$ is $\gcd \set {m, n}$.

title: Count of Operations on Finite Set which are Closed on Every Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set with $n$ elements. There are $2^{n \paren {n - 1} }$ binary operations on $S$ which are closed on all subsets of $S$.

title: Count of Rows of Truth Table
snippet: Let $P$ be a WFF of propositional logic. Suppose $\PP$ is of finite size such that it contains $n$ different letters. Then a truth table constructed to express $P$ will contain $2^n$ rows.

title: Count of Subsets with Even Cardinality
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. Then the number of subsets of $S$ whose cardinality is even is $2^{n-1}$.

title: Count of Subsets with Odd Cardinality
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is $n$. Then the number of subsets of $S$ whose cardinality is odd is $2^{n-1}$.

title: Count of Truth Functions
snippet: There are $2^{\paren {2^k} }$ distinct truth functions on $k$ variables.

title: Count of a's and b's in Fibonacci String
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci string. Then for $n \ge 3$, $S_n$ has: $F_{n - 2}$ instances of $\text a$ $F_{n - 1}$ instances of $\text b$.

title: Countability Axioms Preserved under Open Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a surjective open mapping which is also continuous. If $T_A$ has one of the following properties, then $T_B$ has the same property: First-Countability Second-Countability

title: Countability Properties Preserved under Projection Mapping
snippet: Let $\sequence {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }$ be a sequence of topological spaces. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\sequence {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }$. Let $\pr_\alpha: \struct {S, \tau} \to \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ denote the projection on the $\alpha$ coordinate. Then $\pr_\alpha$ preserves the following countability properties. That is, if $\struct {S, \tau}$ has one of the following properties, then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ has the same property.

title: Countable Anticompact Space has Countable K-Network
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable anticompact topological space. Then $T$ has a countable $k$-network.

title: Countable Basis for P-adic Numbers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. For any $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ and $a \in \Q_p$ let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$. Then: $\BB_p = \set {\map {B_{p^{-n} } } q : q \in \Q, n \in \Z}$ is a countable basis for $\struct{\Q_p, \tau_p}$.

title: Countable Basis of Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\BB$ be the set of subsets of $\R$ defined as: $\BB = \set {\openint a b: a, b \in \Q,\ a < b}$ That is, $\BB$ is the set of open intervals of $\R$ whose endpoints are rational numbers. Then $\BB$ forms a countable basis of $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$

title: Countable Closed Ordinal Space is Metrizable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ is a metrizable space.

title: Countable Closed Ordinal Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ is a second-countable space.

title: Countable Compactness is Preserved under Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous surjection. If $T_A$ is countably compact, then $T_B$ is also countably compact.

title: Countable Complement Space Satisfies Countable Chain Condition
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ satisfies the countable chain condition.

title: Countable Complement Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is a connected space.

title: Countable Complement Space is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is an irreducible space.

title: Countable Complement Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

title: Countable Complement Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is a locally connected space.

title: Countable Complement Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is pseudocompact.

title: Countable Complement Space is T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a countably compact space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not Countably Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not countably metacompact.

title: Countable Complement Space is not First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a first-countable space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a separable space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $\sigma$-compact space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_2$ space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_4$ space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not a $T_5$ space.

title: Countable Complement Space is not Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then $T$ is not weakly countably compact.

title: Countable Complement Topology is Expansion of Finite Complement Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the countable complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Let $T' = \struct {S, \tau'}$ be the finite complement topology on the same infinite set $S$. Then $\tau$ is an expansion of $\tau'$.

title: Countable Complement Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable complement space. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $T$.

title: Countable Cover is Point Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a countable cover of $S$. Then $\CC$ is a point countable cover of $S$.

title: Countable Discrete Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

title: Countable Discrete Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is second-countable.

title: Countable Discrete Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is separable.

title: Countable Discrete Space is Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is $\sigma$-compact.

title: Countable Discrete Space is not Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable discrete space. Then $T$ is not weakly countably compact.

title: Countable Excluded Point Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be a countable excluded point space. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

title: Countable Excluded Point Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be a countable excluded point space. Then $T$ is a separable space.

title: Countable Finite Complement Space is not Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable finite complement topology. Then $T$ is not locally path-connected.

title: Countable Finite Complement Space is not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable finite complement topology. Then $T$ is not path-connected.

title: Countable Fort Space is Metrizable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a metrizable space.

title: Countable Fort Space is Perfectly Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a perfectly normal space.

title: Countable Fort Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

title: Countable Fort Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on a countably infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a separable space.

title: Countable Function on Power Set of Sample Space is Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space such that $\Sigma$ is the power set of $\Omega$. Let $f: \Omega \to \R$ be a function such that $\Img f$ is countable. Then $f$ is a discrete random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$.

title: Countable Hypothesis Set has Finished Tableau
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\mathbf H$ be a countable set of WFFs of propositional logic. Then there exists a finished tableau whose root node is $\mathbf H$.

title: Countable Infinite Product of Real Number Spaces is Homeomorphic to Fréchet Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ denote the real number line under the Euclidean topology. Let $T = \struct {\R^\omega, \tau} = \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in \N} \struct {\R, \tau_d}$ denote the countable-dimensional real Cartesian space under the product topology $\tau$. Let $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ be the Fréchet product space on $\R^\omega$, where: $\map d {x, y} = \ds \sum_{i \mathop \in \N} \dfrac {2^{-i} \size {x_i - y_i} } {1 + \size {x_i - y_i} }$ Then the topology induced by $d$ is exactly the product topology $\tau$.

title: Countable Intersection of Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $\quad A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \Sigma \implies \ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty A_i \in \Sigma$ That is, the countable intersection of events is also an event.

title: Countable Local Basis in Compact Complement Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the compact complement topology on $\R$. Let $p \in \R$. Then sets of the form: $\openint \gets {-n} \cup \openint {p - \dfrac 1 n} {p + \dfrac 1 n} \cup \openint n \to$ form a countable local basis for $p$.

title: Countable Open Covers Condition for Separated Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ For all $X \subseteq S$, let $X^-$ denote the closure of $X$ in $T$. Let: $\UU = \set {U_n : n \in \N}$ be a countable open cover of $A : \forall n \in \N : {U_n}^- \cap B = \O$ Let: $\VV = \set {V_n : n \in \N}$ be a countable open cover of $B : \forall n \in \N : {V_n}^- \cap A = \O$ Then: $A$ and $B$ can be separated in $T$

title: Countable Open Ordinal Space is Metrizable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ is a metrizable space.

title: Countable Open Ordinal Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal which strictly precedes $\Omega$. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ is a second-countable space.

title: Countable Particular Point Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a countable particular point space. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf apace.

title: Countable Product of First-Countable Spaces is First-Countable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be first-countable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also first-countable.

title: Countable Product of Second-Countable Spaces is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be second-countable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also second-countable.

title: Countable Product of Separable Spaces is Separable
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be separable. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also separable.

title: Countable Product of Sequentially Compact Spaces is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with countable cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be sequentially compact. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also sequentially compact.

title: Countable Set equals Range of Sequence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is countable there exists a sequence $\sequence {s_i}_{i \mathop \in N}$ where $N$ is a subset of $\N$ such that $S$ equals the range of $\sequence {s_i}_{i \mathop \in N}$.

title: Countable Set has Choice Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Let $\mathbb S = \powerset S \setminus \set \O$ be the power set of $S$ excluding the empty set $\O$. Then there exists a choice function $C$ for $S$: $\forall x \in \mathbb S: \map C x \in x$

title: Countable Set has Measure Zero
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Then the measure of $S$ is $\map m S = 0$.

title: Countable Set is Null Set under Lebesgue Measure
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a countable set. Then $\map \lambda S = 0$, where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure. That is, $S$ is a $\lambda$-null set.

title: Countable Set is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Then $S$ is well-orderable.

title: Countable Set may have Uncountable Limit Points
snippet: Let $S$ be an uncountable set. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a countable subset of $S$. Let $T = \struct {H, \tau}$ be a topological space on the underlying set $H$. Then despite the fact that $H$ is countable, the set of limit points of $T$ may be uncountable.

title: Countable Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space where $S$ is a countable set. Then $T$ is a separable space.

title: Countable Space is Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countable topological space. Then $T$ is $\sigma$-compact.

title: Countable Stability implies Stability for All Infinite Cardinalities
snippet: Let $T$ be a complete $\LL$-theory whose language $\LL$ is countable. If $T$ is $\omega$-stable, then $T$ is $\kappa$-stable for all infinite $\kappa$.

title: Countable Subset of Minimal Uncountable Well-Ordered Set Has Upper Bound
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the minimal uncountable well-ordered set. Let $\omega$ be a countable subset of $\Omega$. Then $\omega$ has an upper bound in $\Omega$.

title: Countable Union of Countable Sets is Countable
snippet: Let the be accepted. Then it can be proved that a countable union of countable sets is countable.

title: Countable Union of Finite Sets is Countable
snippet: in $\mathrm{ZF}^-$: The holds. The union of any countable set of finite sets is countable. {{explain|What is $\mathrm{ZF}^-$? See talk page for a discussion on this.}}

title: Countable Union of Meager Sets is Meager
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {A_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a countable set of meager subsets of $X$. Let: $\ds A = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n$ Then $A$ is meager in $X$.

title: Countable Union of Measurable Sets as Disjoint Union of Measurable Sets
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {A_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable sets. Then there exists a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable pairwise disjoint sets $\sequence {B_n}_{n \in \N}$ such that: $\ds \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty A_n = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty B_n$ That is: any countable union of $\Sigma$-measurable sets can be rewritten as the countable union of pairwise disjoint $\Sigma$-measurable sets.

title: Countable iff Cardinality not greater than Aleph Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be set. $X$ is countable : $\card X \le \aleph_0$ where: $\card X$ denotes the cardinality of $X$ $\aleph_0 = \card \N$ by Aleph Zero equals Cardinality of Naturals.

title: Countably Additive Function Dichotomy by Empty Set
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a function be a countably additive function. Then the exactly one of the following is true: $\paren 1$: $\map f \O = 0$ $\paren 2$: $\map f \O = + \infty$. Moreover, $\map f A = + \infty$ for all $A \in \AA$. $\paren 3$: $\map f \O = - \infty$. Moreover, $\map f A = - \infty$ for all $A \in \AA$.

title: Countably Additive Function also Finitely Additive
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a countably additive function. Then $f$ is a finitely additive function.

title: Countably Additive Function of Null Set
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\overline \R$ denote the extended set of real numbers. Let $f: \AA \to \overline \R$ be a function be a countably additive function. Suppose that there exists at least one $A \in \AA$ where $\map f A$ is a finite number. Then: $\map f \O = 0$

title: Countably Compact First-Countable Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: A countably compact first-countable topological space is also sequentially compact.

title: Countably Compact Lindelöf Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then: $T$ is a compact space $T$ is both: a Lindelöf space a countably compact space.

title: Countably Compact Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $\struct {X, d}$ is bounded.

title: Countably Compact Metric Space is Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be countably compact. Then $M$ is compact.

title: Countably Compact Metric Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is second-countable.

title: Countably Compact Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is separable.

title: Countably Compact Metric Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $M$ be a countably compact metric space. Then $M$ is sequentially compact.

title: Countably Compact Second-Countable Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact second-countable space. Then $T$ is compact.

title: Countably Compact Space is Countably Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact space. Then $T$ is countably paracompact.

title: Countably Compact Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact space. Then $T$ is a pseudocompact space.

title: Countably Compact Space is Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Every countably compact space is a weakly countably compact space.

title: Countably Compact Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: A countably compact topological space is not necessarily also a compact space.

title: Countably Compact Space is not necessarily Metacompact
snippet: A countably compact topological space is not necessarily also a metacompact space.

title: Countably Compact Space is not necessarily Sequentially Compact
snippet: A countably compact topological space is not necessarily also a sequentially compact space.

title: Countably Compact Space satisfies Countable Finite Intersection Axiom
Countably Infinite Set has Enumeration
snippet: Let $S$ be a countably inifnite set. Then there exists a countably infinite enumeration $\set{s_1, s_2, s_3, \ldots}$ of $S$.

title: Countably Infinite Set has Uncountable Family of Subsets with Finite Intersection
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a countably infinite set. Then there exists an uncountable family $\SS \subseteq \powerset \CC$ such that for each $A, B \in \SS$, we have that: $A \cap B$ is finite.

title: Countably Infinite Set in Countably Compact Space has Omega-Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a countably compact topological space. Let $A \subseteq X$ be countably infinite. Then $A$ has an $\omega$-accumulation point in $X$.

title: Countably Metacompact Lindelöf Space is Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Lindelöf space which is also countably metacompact. Then $T$ is metacompact.

title: Countably Metacompact Space is not necessarily Metacompact
snippet: A countably metacompact topological space is not necessarily also a metacompact space.

title: Countably Paracompact Lindelöf Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Lindelöf space which is also countably paracompact. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Countably Paracompact Space is Countably Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably paracompact space. Then $T$ is countably metacompact.

title: Countably Paracompact Space is not necessarily Paracompact
snippet: A countably paracompact topological space is not necessarily also a paracompact space.

title: Counting Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Then the counting measure $\size {\,\cdot\,}$ on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ is a measure.

title: Counting Measure on Natural Numbers is Sigma-Finite
snippet: Let $\mu$ be the counting measure on $\struct {\N, \powerset \N}$. Then $\mu$ is $\sigma$-finite.

title: Counting Theorem
snippet: Every well-ordered set is order isomorphic to a unique ordinal.

title: Couriers' Meeting
snippet: == Classic Problem == The Holy Father sent a courier from Rome to Venice, commanding him that he reach Venice in $7$ days. The Most Illustrious Signorina of Venice sent a courier from Venice to Rome, directing him to reach Rome in $9$ days. It is $250$ miles between Rome and Venice. It so happened that both couriers started at exactly the same time. In how many days do they meet?

title: Covariance as Expectation of Product minus Product of Expectations
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the expectations of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then the covariance of $X$ and $Y$ is given by: $\cov {X, Y} = \expect {X Y} - \expect X \expect Y$

title: Covariance is Symmetric
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Suppose the covariance $\cov {X, Y}$ exists. Then $\cov {X, Y} = \cov {Y, X}$.

title: Covariance of Independent Random Variables is Zero
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent random variables. Let the expectations of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then the covariance of $X$ and $Y$ is $0$.

title: Covariance of Linear Combination of Random Variables with Another
snippet: Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Then: $\cov {a X + b Y, Z} = a \cov {X, Z} + b \cov {Y, Z}$

title: Covariance of Multiples of Random Variables
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be random variables. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Then: $\cov {a X, b Y} = a b \cov {X, Y}$

title: Covariance of Random Variable with Itself
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Then $\cov {X, X} = \var X$.

title: Covariance of Sums of Random Variables
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\sequence {X_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n}$, $\sequence {Y_j}_{1 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be sequences of random variables. Then: $\ds \cov {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i, \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n Y_j} = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \cov {X_i, Y_j}$

title: Covariant Hom Functor is Continuous
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$, and let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {C, \cdot}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf{Set}$ be the covariant hom functor based at $C$. Then $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {C, \cdot}$ is a continuous functor.

title: Cowen's Theorem
snippet: Let $g$ be a progressing mapping. Let $x$ be a set. Let $\powerset x$ denote the power set of $x$. Let $M_x$ denote the intersection of the $x$-special subsets of $\powerset x$ $g$. Let $M$ be the class of all $x$ such that $x \in M_x$. Then $M$ is minimally superinductive under $g$.

title: Cowen-Engeler Lemma
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $M$ be a set of mappings from subsets of $X$ to $Y$. Thus each element of $M$ is a partial mapping from $X$ to $Y$. Define a mapping: $\Phi: X \to \powerset Y$ thus: $\map \Phi x = \set {\map f x: f \in M \text{ and } x \in \Dom f}$ That is: $\map \Phi x = \set {y \in Y: \exists f \in M: \tuple {x, y} \in f}$ Suppose that the following hold: Then there exists an element of $M$ with domain $X$.

title: Cramer's Rule
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be real numbers. Let $\mathbf b = \tuple {b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n}^\intercal$. Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n$ be real numbers. Let $\mathbf x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n}^\intercal$. Let $A$ be a nonsingular $n \times n$ matrix whose elements are in $\R$. For each $i \in \set {1, \dots, n}$, let $A_i$ be the matrix obtained by replacing the $i$th column with $\mathbf b$. Let: $A \mathbf x = \mathbf b$ Then: $\mathbf x_i = \dfrac {\map \det {A_i} } {\map \det A}$ for each $i \in \set {1, \dots, n}$.

title: Creation of Orthogonal Vector from Independent Vectors
snippet: Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space. Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be vectors of $\mathbf V$ such that $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ form a linearly independent set. Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be expressed as column vectors. Let $\mathbf b'$ be calculated as: $\mathbf b' = \mathbf b - \dfrac {\mathbf a^\intercal \mathbf b} {\mathbf a^\intercal \mathbf a} \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a^\intercal$ denotes the transpose of $\mathbf a$. Then $\mathbf b'$ is orthogonal to $\mathbf a$.

title: Cross-Relation Equivalence Classes on Natural Numbers are Cancellable for Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ be the semigroup of natural numbers under addition. Let $\boxtimes$ be the cross-relation defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ Let $\eqclass {x, y} {}$ denote the equivalence class of $\tuple {x, y}$ under $\boxtimes$.

title: Cross-Relation on Natural Numbers is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ be the semigroup of natural numbers under addition. Let $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$ be the (external) direct product of $\struct {\N, +}$ with itself, where $\oplus$ is the operation on $\N \times \N$ induced by $+$ on $\N$. The relation $\boxtimes$ defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ is an equivalence relation on $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function as Integral of Probability Density Function
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable. Let $f_X$ be a probability density function for $X$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function for $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Then: $\ds \map {F_X} x = \int_{-\infty}^x f_X \rd \lambda$ for each $x \in \R$, where $\ds \int_{-\infty}^x f_X \rd \lambda$ denotes the Lebesgue integral of $f$ over $\hointl {-\infty} x$.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function for Discrete Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then the cumulative distribution function of $X$ is given by: $\map F x = \ds \sum_{x_i \mathop \le x} \map \Pr {X = x_i}$

title: Cumulative Distribution Function is Increasing

title: Cumulative Distribution Function of Binomial Distribution
snippet: The cumulative distribution function of a binomially distributed random variable $X$ is equal to: $\map \Phi x = \ds \sum_{t \mathop \le x} \dbinom n t p^t \paren {1 - p}^{n - t}$ where: $n$ is the number of trials $p$ is the probability of success such that $0 \le p \le 1$.

title: Cumulative Distribution Function of Logistic Distribution

title: Curl Operator Distributes over Addition
snippet: Let $\map {\R^3} {x, y, z}$ denote the real Cartesian space of $3$ dimensions.. Let $\tuple {\mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k}$ be the standard ordered basis on $\R^3$. Let $\mathbf f$ and $\mathbf g: \R^3 \to \R^3$ be vector-valued functions on $\R^3$: $\mathbf f := \tuple {\map {f_x} {\mathbf x}, \map {f_y} {\mathbf x}, \map {f_z} {\mathbf x} }$ $\mathbf g := \tuple {\map {g_x} {\mathbf x}, \map {g_y} {\mathbf x}, \map {g_z} {\mathbf x} }$ Let $\nabla \times \mathbf f$ denote the curl of $f$.

title: Curry's Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Let $P$ be an arbitrary proposition. Let a proposition $C$ be defined: $C \implies P$ that $\neg C$. Then $C \implies P$ is vacuously true. By definition, $C$ is true, a contradiction. This contradiction shows $C$ to be true. By definition, $C \implies P$. By Modus Ponendo Ponens, we conclude $P$, where $P$ is arbitrary. But this means that any proof system expressing the above is inconsistent.

snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $1^*$ denote the rational cut (rational) number $1$. Then: $\alpha 1^* = \alpha$ where $\alpha 1^*$ denote the product of $\alpha$ and $1^*$.

title: Cycle Decomposition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cycle Decompositions ==

title: Cycle Decomposition of Conjugate
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi, \rho \in S_n$. The cycle decomposition of the permutation $\pi \rho \pi^{-1}$ can be obtained from that of $\rho$ by replacing each $i$ in the cycle decomposition of $\rho$ with $\map \pi i$.

title: Cycle Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cycle Graphs == The following illustrations are of cycle graphs: 700px It is noted that: $C_1$ is a loop-graph and $C_2$ is a multigraph. $C_n$ is a simple graph only for $n \ge 3$. Category:Examples of Cycle Graphs

title: Cycle Graph is 2-Regular
snippet: Let $G$ be a cycle graph. Then $G$ is regular.

title: Cycle Graph is Bipartite iff Order is Even
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $C_n$ be the cycle graph of order $n$. Then $C_n$ is a bipartite graph $n$ is even.

title: Cycle Graph is Connected
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a cycle graph. Then $G$ is connected.

title: Cycle Graph is Eulerian
snippet: Let $G$ be a cycle graph. Then $G$ is Eulerian.

title: Cycle Graph is Hamiltonian
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n \ge 3$. Let $C_n$ denote the cycle graph of order $n$. Then $C_n$ is Hamiltonian.

title: Cycle Graph of Order 1 is Loop-Graph
snippet: Let $C_1$ denote the cycle graph of order $1$. Then $C_1$ is a loop-graph.

title: Cycle Graph of Order 2 is Multigraph
snippet: Let $C_2$ denote the cycle graph of order $2$. Then $C_2$ is a multigraph.

title: Cycle Graph of Order 3 is Complete Graph
snippet: Let $C_3$ denote the cycle graph of order $2$. Then $C_3$ is the complete graph of of order $3$.

title: Cycle Matroid is Matroid
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a graph. Let $\struct {E, \mathscr I}$ be the cycle matroid of $G$. Then $\struct {E, \mathscr I}$ is a matroid.

title: Cycle Notation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cycle Notation ==

title: Cycle does not Contain Subcycles
snippet: Let $G$ be a cycle graph. Then the only cycle graph that is a subgraph of $G$ is $G$ itself.

title: Cycle in Balanced Signed Graph
snippet: Let $G$ be a balanced signed graph. Let $C$ be a cycle in $G$. Then $C$ has an even number of negative edges.

title: Cycle of Subsets implies Set Equality
snippet: Let $A_1, A_2, \dotsc, A_n$ be sets. Let: $\forall k \in \set {2, 3, \dotsc, n}: A_{k - 1} \subseteq A_k$ and: $A_n \subseteq A_1$ Then: $\forall j, k \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: A_j = A_k$

title: Cyclic Group/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cyclic Groups ==

title: Cyclic Group/Group Presentation
snippet: == Generator of the Cyclic Group of Order $n$ == The presentation of a finite cyclic group of order $n$ is: $C_n = \gen {a: a^n = e}$

title: Cyclic Group Elements whose Powers equal Identity
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group whose identity is $e$ and whose order is $n$. Let $d \divides n$. Then there exist exactly $d$ elements $x \in G$ satisfying the equation $x^d = e$. These are the elements of the group $G_d$ generated by $g^{n / d}$: $G_d = \gen {g^{n / d} }$

title: Cyclic Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Then $G$ is abelian.

title: Cyclic Group is Finitely Generated
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a cyclic group. Then $\CC$ is finitely generated.

title: Cyclic Group is Simple iff Prime
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Then $G$ is simple $G$ is a prime group.

title: Cyclic Group of Order 6
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. Then: $C_2 \times C_3 \cong C_6$ $C_6$ is the internal group direct product of $C_2$ and $C_3$.

title: Cyclic Group of Order 8 is not isomorphic to Group of Units of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be an integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \cdot}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$. Let $C_8$ denote the cyclic group of order $8$ Then: $U$ and $C_8$ are not isomorphic.

title: Cyclic Groups of Same Order are Isomorphic
snippet: Two cyclic groups of the same order are isomorphic to each other.

title: Cyclic Permutation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Cyclic Permutations ==

title: Cyclic Permutation of Kaprekar Number
snippet: Let $n$ be a Kaprekar number of $k$ digits. Let $m$ be an integer formed from a cyclic permutation of the digits of $n$. Let $m$ be squared and the result split into $2$ parts, where the $2$nd part is of $k$ digits. Let these two parts be added, in the way of operating on a Kaprekar number. If the result is more than $k$ digits long, split that into $2$ parts, where the $2$nd part is of $k$ digits, and add the parts. The result will be another cyclic permutation of the digits of $n$.

title: Cyclic Permutations of 5-Digit Multiples of 41
snippet: Let $n$ be a multiple of $41$ with $5$ digits. Let $m$ be an integer formed by cyclically permuting the digits of $n$. Then $m$ is a multiple of $41$.

title: Cyclicity Condition for Units of Ring of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \times}$. Then $U$ is cyclic either: $n = p^\alpha$ or: $n = 2 p^\alpha$ where $p \ge 3$ is prime and $\alpha \ge 0$.

title: Cycloid has Tautochrone Property
snippet: Let a wire $AB$ be curved into the shape of an arc of a cycloid such that: $A$ is at the cusp $B$ is the highest point of the arc and inverted so that its cusps are uppermost and on the same horizontal line. Thus $B$ is the lowest point of the arc. Let $AB$ be embedded in a constant and uniform gravitational field where Acceleration Due to Gravity is $g$. Let a bead $P$ be released from anywhere on the wire between $A$ and $B$ to slide down without friction to $B$.

title: Cycloid is Best Shape for Arch
snippet: The optimal shape for an arch is a cycloid.

title: Cyclotomic Polynomial has Integer Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Then the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial $\map {\Phi_n} x$ has integer coefficients.

title: Cyclotomic Polynomial of Index Power of Two
snippet: Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Then the $2^n$th cyclotomic polynomial is: $\map {\Phi_{2^n} } x = x^{2^{n - 1} } + 1$

title: Cyclotomic Polynomial of Index times Prime Power
snippet: Let $n, k \ge 1$ be natural numbers. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\Phi_n$ denote the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. Then $\map {\Phi_{p^k n}} x = \begin{cases} \map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^k}} & \text{if } p \divides n\\ \dfrac {\map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^k}}} {\map {\Phi_n} {x^{p^{k - 1}}}} & \text{if } p \nmid n \end{cases}$

title: Cyclotomic Polynomial of Prime Index
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. The $p$th cyclotomic polynomial is: $\map {\Phi_p} x = x^{p - 1} + x^{p - 2} + \cdots + x + 1$

snippet: == Famous False Conjecture == Every odd number greater than $1$ can be expressed as the sum of a power of $2$ and a prime.

title: De Polignac's Formula
snippet: Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Let $p$ be a prime number. Then $p^\mu$ is a divisor of $n!$, and $p^{\mu + 1}$ is not, where: $\ds \mu = \sum_{k \mathop > 0} \floor {\frac n {p^k} }$ where $\floor {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function.

title: De Rham Cohomology of Sphere
snippet: Let $S^n$ denote the $n$-Sphere. Then the de Rham Cohomology of $S^n$ are: $\map {H^k} {S^n} = \begin {cases} \Z^2 & : k = 0, n = 0 \\ \Z & : k = 0 \text { or } k = n, n > 0 \\ 0 & : 0 < k < n \end {cases}$ and Higher de Rham Cohomology Vanishes.

title: Decay Equation
snippet: The first order ordinary differential equation: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = k \paren {y_a - y}$ where $k \in \R: k > 0$ has the general solution: $y = y_a + C e^{-k x}$ where $C$ is an arbitrary constant. If $y = y_0$ at $x = 0$, then: $y = y_a + \paren {y_0 - y_a} e^{-k x}$ This differential equation is known as the decay equation.

title: Decoding Received Word using Coset Decoding Table
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear code. Let $v$ be a received word, which may have transmission errors. To find out the transmitted codeword $u$ corresponding to $v$: $(1): \quad$ Find $v$ in the coset decoding table for $C$. $(2): \quad$ The corresponding transmitted codeword $u$ will be found at the top of the column where $v$ can be found.

title: Decomposition into Even-Odd Integers is not always Unique
snippet: For every even integer $n$ such that $n > 1$, if $n$ can be expressed as the product of one or more even-times odd integers, it is not necessarily the case that this product is unique.

title: Decomposition into Product of Power of 2 and Odd Integer is Unique
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $n$ can be decomposed into the product of a power of $2$ and an odd integer.

title: Decomposition of 2-Form on 4-Dimensional Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $M$ be a $4$-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $\omega$ be a $2$-form on $M$. Then $\omega$ can be written uniquely as a sum of a self-dual $2$-form and an anti-self-dual $2$-form.

title: Decomposition of Complex Measure into Finite Signed Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Then there exists unique finite signed measures $\mu_R$ and $\mu_I$ such that: $\mu = \mu_R + i \mu_I$

title: Decomposition of Distribution Function of Finite Signed Borel Measure
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a finite signed Borel measure on $\R$. Let $\tuple {\mu^+, \mu^-}$ be the Jordan decomposition of $\mu$. Then: $F_\mu = F_{\mu^+} - F_{\mu^-}$ where: $F_\mu$ is the distribution function of $\mu$ $F_{\mu^+}$ and $F_{\mu^-}$ are the distribution functions of $\mu^+$ and $\mu^-$ respectively.

title: Decomposition of Field Extension as Separable Extension followed by Purely Inseparable
snippet: Let $E / F$ be an algebraic field extension. Then the relative separable closure $K = F^{sep}$ in $E$ is the unique intermediate field with the following properties: $K / F$ is separable $E / K$ is purely inseparable.

title: Decomposition of Matrix Exponential
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix of order $m$ for some $m \in \Z_{\ge 1}$. Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf P$ be a nonsingular matrix of order $m$. Then: $e^{\mathbf P \mathbf A \mathbf P^{-1} t} = \mathbf P e^{\mathbf A t} \mathbf P^{-1}$ {{explain|Review what is meant by $e^{\mathbf A}$. We have only got $e^{\mathbf A t}$ defined.}}

title: Decomposition of Mean Squared Error
snippet: Let $\theta$ be a population parameter of some stochastic model. Let $\hat \theta$ be an estimator of $\theta$. We then have: $\map {\operatorname {MSE} } {\hat \theta} = \var {\hat \theta} + \paren {\map {\operatorname {bias}} {\hat \theta} }^2 $ where: $\map {\operatorname {MSE} } {\hat \theta}$ denotes the Mean Squared Error of $\hat \theta$. $\var {\hat \theta}$ denotes the variance of $\hat \theta$. $\map {\operatorname {bias} } {\hat \theta}$ denotes the bias of $\hat \theta$.

title: Decomposition of Probability Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, P}$ be a probability space. Suppose that for every $\omega \in \Omega$, it holds that: $\set \omega \in \Sigma$ that is, that $\Sigma$ contains all singletons. Then there exist a unique diffuse measure $\mu$ and a unique discrete measure $\nu$ such that: $P = \mu + \nu$

title: Dedekind's Theorem
snippet: Let $\tuple {L, R}$ be a Dedekind cut of the set of real numbers $\R$. Then there exists a unique real number which is a producer of $\tuple {L, R}$. Thus it is proved that the totally ordered set $\R$ is Dedekind complete, and that is why it is referred to as the continuum.

title: Dedekind-Complete Bounded Ordered Set is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $L$ have a lower bound $\bot$ and an upper bound $\top$. Let $\struct {L, \preceq}$ be Dedekind-complete. Then $\struct {L, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice.

title: Dedekind Completeness is Self-Dual
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is Dedekind complete every non-empty subset of $S$ that is bounded below admits an infimum in $S$. That is, an ordered set is Dedekind complete its dual is Dedekind complete.

title: Dedekind Completion is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $S$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {X, f}$ and $\struct {Y, g}$ be Dedekind completions of $S$. Then there exists a unique order isomorphism $\phi: X \to Y$ such that $\phi \circ f = g$.

title: Deduction Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathscr H$ be instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system. Then the deduction rule: $\dfrac{U,\mathbf A \vdash \mathbf B}{U \vdash \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B}$ is a derived rule for $\mathscr H$.

title: Deduction Theorem for Hilbert Proof System for Predicate Logic
snippet: Let $\mathscr H$ be instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system for predicate logic. Then the deduction rule: $\dfrac{U,\mathbf A \vdash \mathbf B}{U \vdash \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B}$ is a derived rule for provable consequences in $\mathscr H$.

title: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Convergent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt[n] x - 1}$ Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is pointwise convergent.

title: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Strictly Decreasing
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt [n] x - 1}$ Then $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \sequence {\map {f_n} x}$ is strictly decreasing.

title: Defining Sequence of Natural Logarithm is Uniformly Convergent on Compact Sets
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be the sequence of mappings $f_n : \R_{>0} \to \R$ defined as: $\map {f_n} x = n \paren {\sqrt [n] x - 1}$ Let $K \subseteq \R_{>0}$ be compact. Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

title: Definite Integral/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Definite Integrals ==

title: Definite Integral from -a to a of Power of a plus x by Power of a minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \paren {a + x}^{m - 1} \paren {a - x}^{n - 1} \rd x = \paren {2 a}^{m + n - 1} \frac {\map \Gamma m \map \Gamma n} {\map \Gamma {m + n} }$ where: $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function $a$, $m$ and $n$ are positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Arcsine of x by Arccosine of x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\arcsin x \arccos x } x \rd x = \dfrac 7 8 \map \zeta 3$ where $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Arcsine of x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\arcsin x} x = \frac \pi 2 \ln 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Arctangent of x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\arctan x} x \rd x = G$ where $G$ denotes Catalan's constant.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Difference of Powers of x over Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {x^m - x^n} {\ln x} \rd x = \map \ln {\frac {m + 1} {n + 1} }$ where $m$ and $n$ are real numbers with $m, n > -1$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Even Powers of Logarithm of 1 - x over x
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. $\ds \int_0^1 \map {\ln^{2n} } {\dfrac {1 - x} x} \rd x = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} B_{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 2} \pi^{2 n}$ where $B_{2 n}$ is the $2 n$th Bernoulli number.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of One minus x over x
