title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x by Logarithm of One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \ln x \map \ln {1 - x} \rd x = 2 - \frac {\pi^2} 6$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x by Logarithm of One minus x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \dfrac {\ln x \map \ln {1 - x} } {\paren {1 - x} } \rd x = \map \zeta 3$ where $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x by Logarithm of One plus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \ln x \map \ln {1 + x} \rd x = 2 - 2 \ln 2 - \frac {\pi^2} {12}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\ln x} {1 - x} \rd x = -\frac {\pi^2} 6$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Logarithm of x over One plus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \frac {\ln x} {1 + x} \rd x = -\frac {\pi^2} {12}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Power of u over 1 + Power of u
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^1 \dfrac {u^{a - 1} \rd u} {1 + u^d} | r = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^j} {a + j d} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 a - \frac 1 {a + d} + \frac 1 {a + 2 d} - \frac 1 {a + 3 d} + \cdots | c = }} where $a, d > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Power of x by Power of Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 x^m \paren {\ln x}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {-1}^n \map \Gamma {n + 1} } {\paren {m + 1}^{n + 1} }$ where: $n$ is a non-negative integer $m$ is a real number with $m > -1$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of Zeta of 2 minus Dilogarithm of x over One minus x
snippet: $\ds \int_{\to 0}^{\to 1} \dfrac {\paren {\map \zeta 2 - \map {\Li_2} x } } {1 - x} \rd x = 2 \map \zeta 3$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the Dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\map \zeta 3$ is Apéry's constant: the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $3$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of x^4 (1 - x)^4 over (1 + x^2)
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^1 \dfrac {x^4 \paren {1 - x}^4} {1 + x^2} \rd x | r = \dfrac {22} 7 - \pi | c = }}

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of x to the minus x
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^1 x^{-x} \rd x | r = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty n^{-n} }}

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 1 of x to the x
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^1 x^x \rd x | r = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n + 1} } {n^n} }} {{eqn | r = -\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {-n}^{-n} }}

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Logarithm of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \map \ln {a + b \cos x} \rd x = 2 \pi \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } 2}$ where: $b$ is a real number $a$ is a positive real number with $a \ge \size b$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of One minus 2 a Cosine x plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {1 - 2 a \cos x + a^2} = \frac {2 \pi} {1 - a^2}$ where $a$ is a real number with $0 < a < 1$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of Square of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + b \cos x}^2} = \frac {2 \pi a} {\paren {a^2 - b^2}^{3/2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of Square of a plus b Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {\paren {a + b \sin x}^2} = \frac {2 \pi a} {\paren {a^2 - b^2}^{3/2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to 2 Pi of Reciprocal of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{2 \pi} \frac {\d x} {a + b \cos x} = \frac {2 \pi} {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Even Power of Cosine x
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\ds \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \cos^{2 n} x \rd x = \dfrac {\paren {2 n}!} {\paren {2^n n!}^2} \dfrac \pi 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Even Power of Sine x
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^{2 n} x \rd x | r = \dfrac {\paren {2 n}!} {\paren {2^n n!}^2} \dfrac \pi 2 | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 \cdots \paren {2 n - 1} } {2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 \cdots 2 n} \dfrac \pi 2 | c = }} for $n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Logarithm of Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \map \ln {\cos x} \rd x = -\frac \pi 2 \ln 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Logarithm of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \map \ln {\sin x} \rd x = -\frac \pi 2 \ln 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Logarithm of Sine x by Cosine of 2nx
snippet: For $n \in \N_{>0}$: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \map \ln {\sin x} \cos 2 n x \rd x = -\frac \pi {4 n}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Odd Power of Cosine x
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\ds \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \cos^{2 n + 1} x \rd x = \dfrac {\paren {2^n n!}^2} {\paren {2 n + 1}!}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Odd Power of Sine x
snippet: {{eqn | l = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^{2 n + 1} x \rd x | r = \dfrac {\paren {2^n n!}^2} {\paren {2 n + 1}!} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {2 \cdot 4 \cdot 6 \cdots 2 n} {3 \cdot 5 \cdot 7 \cdots \paren {2 n + 1} } | c = }} for $n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Reciprocal of One plus Power of Tan x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac {\d x} {1 + \tan^m x} = \frac \pi 4$ where $m$ is a real number.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Reciprocal of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac 1 {a + b \cos x} \rd x = \frac 1 {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } \map \arccos {\frac b a}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > b > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Sine x by Logarithm of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin x \map \ln {\sin x} \rd x = \ln 2 - 1$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Square of Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \cos^2 x \rd x = \frac \pi 4$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Square of Logarithm of Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \paren {\map \ln {\cos x} }^2 \rd x = \frac \pi 2 \paren {\ln 2}^2 + \frac {\pi^3} {24}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Square of Logarithm of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \paren {\map \ln {\sin x} }^2 \rd x = \frac \pi 2 \paren {\ln 2}^2 + \frac {\pi^3} {24}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Square of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^2 x \rd x = \frac \pi 4$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of x over Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac x {\sin x} \rd x = 2 G$ where $G$ is Catalan's constant.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Infinity of x^m over (x^n + a^n)^r
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x^m \rd x} {\paren {a^n + x^n}^r} = \frac {\paren {-1}^{r - 1} \pi a^{m + 1 - n r} \, \map \Gamma {\frac {m + 1} n} } {n \sin \frac {\paren {m + 1} \pi} n \paren {r - 1}! \, \map \Gamma {\frac {m + 1} n - r + 1} }$ for: $0 0}$ $r \in \N_{>0}$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Cosine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \dfrac \pi 2 & : m = n \end {cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_0^\pi \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \dfrac \pi 2 \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Logarithm of a plus b Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\pi \map \ln {a + b \cos x} \rd x = \pi \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } 2}$ where: $b$ is a real number $a$ is a positive real number with $a \ge \size b$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sec x by Logarithm of One plus b Cosine x over One plus a Cosine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/2} \sec x \map \ln {\frac {1 + b \cos x} {1 + a \cos x} } \rd x = \frac 1 2 \paren {\paren {\arccos a}^2 - \paren {\arccos b}^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $-1 < a, b < 1$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \cos n x \rd x = \begin{cases} 0 & : m + n \text { even} \\ \dfrac {2 m} {m^2 - n^2} & : m + n \text { odd} \end{cases}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of Sine of m x by Sine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \begin{cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \dfrac \pi 2 & : m = n \end{cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_0^\pi \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \dfrac \pi 2 \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of a Squared minus 2 a b Cosine x plus b Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\pi \map \ln {a^2 - 2 a b \cos x + b^2} \rd x = \begin{cases}2 \pi \ln a & a \ge b > 0 \\ 2 \pi \ln b & b \ge a > 0\end{cases}$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Pi of x by Logarithm of Sine x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\pi x \map \ln {\sin x} \rd x = -\frac {\pi^2} 2 \ln 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to Quarter Pi of Logarithm of One plus Tan x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{\pi/4} \map \ln {1 + \tan x} \rd x = \frac \pi 8 \ln 2$

title: Definite Integral from 0 to a of Reciprocal of Root of a Squared minus x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^a \dfrac {\d x} {\sqrt {a^2 - x^2} } = \frac \pi 2$ for $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to a of Root of a Squared minus x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^a \sqrt {a^2 - x^2} \rd x = \frac {\pi a^2} 4$ for $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral from 0 to a of x^m by (a^n - x^n)^p
snippet: $\ds \int_0^a x^m \paren {a^n - x^n}^p \rd x = \frac {a^{m + 1 + n p} \, \map \Gamma {\frac {m + 1} n} \map \Gamma {p + 1} } {n \map \Gamma {\frac {m + 1} n + p + 1} }$

title: Definite Integral of Constant/Corollary
snippet: == Corollary to Definite Integral of Constant == $\ds \int_a^b \rd x = b - a$

title: Definite Integral of Constant Multiple of Real Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $c \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \int_a^b c \map f x \rd x = c \int_a^b \map f x \rd x$

title: Definite Integral of Even Function
snippet: Let $f$ be an even function with a primitive on the closedinterval $\closedint {-a} a$, where $a > 0$. Then: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \map f x \rd x = 2 \int_0^a \map f x \rd x$

title: Definite Integral of Exponential of minus a x squared from 0 to Infinity
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-a x^2} \rd x = \dfrac 1 2 \sqrt {\dfrac \pi a}$ for $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral of Fourier Series at Ends of Interval
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function defined in the open interval $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Let $f$ fulfil the Dirichlet conditions in $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Let $a_0, a_1, \dotsc; b_1, \dotsc$ be the Fourier coefficients of $f$ in $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Consider the real function: $\map F x = \ds \int_{-\pi}^x \map f t \rd t - \dfrac {a_0} 2 x$ Then: $\map F \pi = \map F {-\pi} = \dfrac {a_0 \pi} 2$

title: Definite Integral of Function plus Constant
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $c$ be a constant. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \paren {\map f t + c} \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t + c \paren {b - a}$

title: Definite Integral of Function satisfying Dirichlet Conditions is Continuous
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function defined in the open interval $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Let $f$ fulfil the Dirichlet conditions in $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Let $a_0, a_1, \dotsc; b_1, \dotsc$ be the Fourier coefficients of $f$ in $\openint {-\pi} \pi$. Then the real function: $\map F x = \ds \int_{-\pi}^x \map f t \rd t - \dfrac {a_0} 2 x$ is continuous on $\openint {-\pi} \pi$.

title: Definite Integral of Limit of Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Integrable Functions
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ with $a < b$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of Riemann integrable real functions $\closedint a b \to \R$ converging uniformly to $f : \closedint a b \to \R$. Then $f$ is integrable, and: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int_a^b \map {f_n} x \rd x$

title: Definite Integral of Odd Function
snippet: Let $f$ be an odd function with a primitive on the open interval $\closedint {-a} a$, where $a > 0$. Then: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \map f x \rd x = 0$

title: Definite Integral of Partial Derivative
snippet: Let $\map f {x, y}$ and $\map {\dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x} } {x, y}$ be continuous functions of $x$ and $y$ on $D = \closedint {x_1} {x_2} \times \closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \frac \d {\d x} \int_a^b \map f {x, y} \rd y = \int_a^b \map {\frac {\partial f} {\partial x} } {x, y} \rd y$ for $x \in \closedint {x_1} {x_2}$.

title: Definite Integral of Periodic Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a Darboux integrable periodic function with period $L$. Let $\alpha \in \R$ and $n \in \Z$. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + n L} \map f x \d x = n \int_0^L \map f x \d x$

title: Definite Integral of Reciprocal of Root of a Squared minus x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^x \frac {\d t} {\sqrt{1 - t^2} } = \arcsin x$

title: Definite Integral of Step Function
snippet: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be a real numbers such that $\alpha < \beta$. Let $\map f x$ be a step function defined on the interval $\closedint \alpha \beta$: $\map f x = \lambda_1 \chi_{\mathbb I_1} + \lambda_2 \chi_{\mathbb I_2} + \cdots + \lambda_n \chi_{\mathbb I_n}$ where: $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n$ are real constants $\mathbb I_1, \mathbb I_2, \ldots, \mathbb I_n$ are intervals, where these intervals partition $\closedint \alpha \beta$ $\chi_{\mathbb I_1}, \chi_{\mathbb I_2}, \ldots, \chi_{\mathbb I_n}$ are characteristic functions of $\mathbb I_1, \mathbb I_2, \ldots,…

title: Definite Integral of Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let each of $\sequence {f_n}$ be continuous on the interval $\hointr a b$. Let the series: $\ds \map f x := \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {f_n} x$ be uniformly convergent for all $x \in \closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \int_a^b \map {f_n} x \rd x$

title: Definite Integral on Zero Interval
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is defined on the closed interval $\Bbb I := \closedint a b$, where $a < b$. Then: $\ds \forall c \in \Bbb I: \int_c^c \map f t \rd t = 0$

title: Definite Integral over Reals of Exponential of -(a x^2 plus b x plus c)
snippet: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map \exp {-\paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } \rd x = \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {\frac {b^2 - 4 a c} {4 a} }$ where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral over Unit Square of Logarithm of x minus Logarithm of y over x minus y
snippet: $\ds \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \frac {\ln x - \ln y} {x - y} \rd x \rd y = 2 \map \zeta 2$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Arctangent of p x minus Arctangent of q x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\arctan p x - \arctan q x} x \rd x = \frac \pi 2 \ln \frac p q$ where $p$ and $q$ are strictly positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine m x over x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos m x} {x^2 + a^2} \rd x = \frac \pi {2 a} e^{-m a}$ where $m$ and $a$ are positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine of a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \cos {a x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi {2 a} }$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine of a x over Hyperbolic Cosine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos a x} {\cosh b x} \rd x = \frac \pi {2 b} \sech \frac {a \pi} {2 b}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine p x minus Cosine q x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos p x - \cos q x} {x^2} \rd x = \frac {\pi \paren {\size q - \size p} } 2$ where $p, q$ are real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cosine x over Root x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos x} {\sqrt x} \rd x = \sqrt {\frac \pi 2}$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Cube of Sine x over x Cubed
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin^3 x} {x^3} \rd x = \frac {3 \pi} 8$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -(a x^2 plus b over x^2)
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-\paren {a x^2 + \frac b {x^2} } } \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {-2 \sqrt {a b} }$ where $a$ and $b$ are strictly positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -(a x^2 plus b x plus c)
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-\paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {\frac {b^2 - 4 a c} {4 a} } \map \erfc {\frac b {2 \sqrt a} }$ where: $\erfc$ denotes the complementary error function $a$, $b$ and $c$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi a}$ where $a$ is a strictly positive real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x^2 by Cosine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x^2} \cos b x \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi a} \map \exp {-\frac {b^2} {4 a} }$ where $a$ is a strictly positive real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Cosine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x} \cos b x \rd x = \frac a {a^2 + b^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by One minus Cosine x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} \paren {1 - \cos x} } {x^2} \rd x = \arccot a - \frac a 2 \map \ln {a^2 + 1} + a \ln a$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Sine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-a x} \sin b x \rd x = \frac b {a^2 + b^2}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers with $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x by Sine of b x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} \sin b x} x \rd x = \map \arctan {\frac b a}$ where $a$ and $b$ are real number with $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } x \rd x = \ln \frac b a$ where $a$ and $b$ are strictly positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x by Cosecant of p x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } {x \csc p x} \rd x = \arctan \frac b p - \arctan \frac a p$ where: $a$ and $b$ are non-negative real numbers $p$ is a non-zero real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -a x minus Exponential of -b x over x by Secant of p x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {e^{-a x} - e^{-b x} } {x \sec p x} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \map \ln {\frac {b^2 + p^2} {a^2 + p^2} }$ where: $a$ and $b$ are non-negative real numbers $p$ is a real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -i x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-i x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi 2} \paren {1 - i}$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -x^2 by Logarithm of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-x^2} \ln x \rd x = -\frac {\sqrt \pi} 4 \paren {\gamma + 2 \ln 2}$ where $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -x by Logarithm of x
snippet: Let $\ln t$ denote the natural logarithm function for real $t > 0$. Let $e^{-t}$ denote the real exponential. Then: $\ds \int_{0^+}^{\mathop \to +\infty} \ln t \, e^{-t} \rd t = - \gamma$ where the is an improper integral, and $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni Constant.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Hyperbolic Sine of a x over Exponential of b x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sinh a x} {e^{b x} - 1} \rd x = \frac 1 {2 a} - \frac \pi {2 b} \cot \frac {a \pi} b$ where: $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers with $b > a$ $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Hyperbolic Sine of a x over Exponential of b x plus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sinh a x} {e^{b x} + 1} \rd x = \frac \pi {2 b} \csc \frac {a \pi} b - \frac 1 {2 a}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers with $b > a$ $\csc$ is the cosecant function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Logarithm of Exponential of x plus One over Exponential of x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \ln {\frac {e^x + 1} {e^x - 1} } \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} 4$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x by Exponential of -a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty x^m e^{-a x^2} \rd x = \frac {\map \Gamma {\paren {m + 1}/2} } {2 a^{\paren {m + 1}/2} }$ where $m$ and $a$ are real numbers with $m > -1$ and $a > 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x by Logarithm of x over One plus x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x^{p - 1} \ln x} {1 + x} \rd x = -\pi^2 \csc p \pi \cot p \pi$ where: $p$ is a real number with $0 < p < 1$ $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x over 1 + 2 x Cosine Beta + x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {x^m \rd x} {1 + 2 x \cos \beta + x^2} = \frac \pi {\sin m x} \frac {\sin m \beta} {\sin \beta}$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x over 1 + x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {x^{p - 1} \rd x} {1 + x} = \frac \pi {\sin \pi p}$ for $0 < p < 1$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x over Hyperbolic Sine of a x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x^n} {\sinh a x} \rd x = \frac {2^{n + 1} - 1} {2^n a^{n + 1} } \map \Gamma {n + 1} \map \zeta {n + 1}$ where: $a$ and $n$ are positive real numbers $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Power of x over Power of x plus Power of a
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {x^m \rd x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac {\pi a^{m + 1 - n} } {n \map \sin {\paren {m + 1} \frac \pi n} }$ for $0 < m + 1 < n$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of 1 plus Power of x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac 1 {1 + x^n} \rd x = \frac \pi n \map \csc {\frac \pi n}$ where: $n$ is a real number greater than 1 $\csc$ is the cosecant function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of Exponential of x minus One minus Exponential of -x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \paren {\frac 1 {e^x - 1} - \frac {e^{-x} } x} \rd x = \gamma$ where $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {\d x} {x^2 + a^2} = \frac \pi {2 a}$ for $a \ne 0$.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine m x over x by x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin m x} {x \paren {x^2 + a^2} } \rd x = \frac \pi {2 a^2} \paren {1 - e^{-m a} }$ where: $a$ is a positive real number $m$ is a non-negative real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine of a x^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \sin {a x^2} \rd x = \frac 1 2 \sqrt {\frac \pi {2 a} }$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine of a x over Hyperbolic Sine of b x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin a x} {\sinh b x} \rd x = \frac \pi {2 b} \tanh \frac {a \pi} {2 b}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers $\tanh$ denotes the hyperbolic cotangent function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine of m x over Exponential of 2 Pi x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin m x} {e^{2 \pi x} - 1} \rd x = \frac 1 4 \coth \frac m 2 - \frac 1 {2 m}$ where: $m$ is a non-zero real number $\coth$ is the hyperbolic cotangent function.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of Sine x over Root x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin x} {\sqrt x} \rd x = \sqrt {\frac \pi 2}$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of x by Sine m x over x Squared plus a Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {x \sin m x} {x^2 + a^2} \rd x = \frac \pi 2 e^{-m a}$ where $m$ and $a$ are positive real numbers.

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of x over Exponential of x minus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac x {e^x - 1} \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} 6$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of x over Exponential of x plus One
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac x {e^x + 1} \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} {12}$

title: Definite Integral to Infinity of x over Hyperbolic Sine of a x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac x {\sinh a x} \rd x = \frac {\pi^2} {4 a^2}$ where $a$ is a positive real number.

title: Definition:(1-3) Parastrophe
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, *}$ be magmas on $S$. $\struct {S, *}$ is a $(1-3)$ parastrophe of $\struct {S, \circ}$ : $\forall x_1, x_2, x_3 \in S: x_1 \circ x_2 = x_3 \iff x_3 * x_2 = x_1$

title: Definition:(2-3) Parastrophe
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, *}$ be magmas on $S$. $\struct {S, *}$ is a $(2-3)$ parastrophe of $\struct {S, \circ}$ : $\forall x_1, x_2, x_3 \in S: x_1 \circ x_2 = x_3 \iff x_1 * x_3 = x_2$

title: Definition:*-Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be an algebra over $\C$. Let $\ast$ be an involution on $A$. We call $\struct {A, \ast}$ a $\ast$-algebra.

title: Definition:*-Algebra Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ and $\struct {B, \diamond}$ be $\ast$-algebras. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be an algebra homomorphism. We say that $\phi$ is a $\ast$-algebra homomorphism : $\map \phi {a^\ast} = \paren {\map \phi a}^\diamond$ for each $a \in A$.

title: Definition:*-Algebra Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ and $\struct {B, \diamond}$ be $\ast$-algebras. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be an *-algebra homomorphism. We say that $\phi$ is a $\ast$-algebra isomorphism $\phi$ is a bijection.

title: Definition:*-Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a self-adjoint subalgebra of $A$. We say that $B$ is a $\ast$-subalgebra of $A$.

title: Definition:1-Form
snippet: A $1$-form is an expression that can, locally, be written as $\map f z \rd z$, where $f$ is an analytic function.

title: Definition:1-Form/Closed 1-Forms
snippet: There is an operation called exterior differentiation taking a 1-form $ω$ to a 2-form $\rdω$. We say $ω$ is closed if $\rdω = 0$

title: Definition:1-Form/Holomorphic 1-Forms
snippet: A $C^{\infty}$ $1$-form $\omega$ on $X$ is called holomorphic if it can be written locally in the form $f(z)\rd z$ for some complex coordinate $z$ and holomorphic function $f$.

title: Definition:ARIMA Model/ARIMA Operator
snippet: Let $S$ be a stochastic process based on an equispaced time series. Let the values of $S$ at timestamps $t, t - 1, t - 2, \dotsc$ be $z_t, z_{t - 1}, z_{t - 2}, \dotsc$ Let $a_t, a_{t - 1}, a_{t - 2}, \dotsc$ be a sequence of independent shocks at timestamps $t, t - 1, t - 2, \dotsc$ Let: $w_t = \nabla^d z_t$ where $\nabla^d$ denotes the $d$th iteration of the backward difference operator.

title: Definition:ARIMA Model/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on ARIMA Model == The I in the acronym ARIMA stands for integrated. This arises because the relationship which is the inverse of the backward difference operator: $w_t = \map {\nabla^d} {z_t}$ is: $z_t = S^d w_T$ where $S$ is the summation operator, defined as: $S = \nabla^{-1} = \paren {1 - B}^{-1}$ so that: $\map S {w_t} = \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^\infty w_{t - j} = w_t + w_{t - 1} + w_{t - 2} + \dotsb$ Hence the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) process can be generated by summing or integrating the ARMA process a total of $d$ times.

title: Definition:ARIMA Model/Motivation
snippet: == ARIMA Model: Motivation == Suppose $S$ is a stochastic process which is non-stationary, and in particular does not have a constant mean level. $S$ may still have some sort of homogeneous behaviour. Although the general level about which there are deviations may change over time, the overall behaviour of $S$ may be the same if these changes are taken into account. It may be possible to model such behaviour using a variant of an autoregressive operator $\map \varphi B$ such that the polynomial $\map \varphi B$ has one or more of its roots actually lying on the unit circle.

title: Definition:A Posteriori (Logic)
snippet: A posteriori knowledge is the sort of knowledge which cannot be known without experience. That is, it cannot be determined by using logic and reasoning from definitions alone.

title: Definition:A Priori (Logic)
snippet: A priori knowledge is the sort of knowledge which comes from reason alone. That is, it does not require the exercise of experience to know it. Thus the truth value of a statement can be decided by a logical argument whose premises are definitions.

title: Definition:Abacism
snippet: Abacism means the process of doing arithmetic using an abacus.

title: Definition:Abacism/Abacist
snippet: An abacist is an arithmetician who uses an abacus to do arithmetic, as opposed to an algorist who calculates using algorism.

title: Definition:Abacus
snippet: An abacus is a tool for performing arithmetical calculations. It consists of: a series of lines (for example: grooves in sand, or wires on a frame), upon which are: a number of items (for example: pebbles in the grooves, or beads on the wires), which are manipulated by hand so as to represent number.

title: Definition:Abacus/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on the Abacus == The abacus is the earliest known machine for mathematics, and can be regarded as the earliest ancestor of the electronic computer. Category:Historical Notes

title: Definition:Abampere
snippet: The abampere is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic base unit of electric current. It is defined as being: The constant current which will produce a force of attraction whose value is $2$ dynes per centimetre of length between two straight, parallel conductors of infinite length and of infinitesimal circular cross-section placed one centimetre apart in a vacuum.

title: Definition:Abampere/Also known as
snippet: == Abampere: Also known as == The abampere is also known as: {{item||the electromagnetic unit, abbreviated $\mathrm {e.m.u.}$}} {{item||the biot, abbreviated $\mathrm {Bi}$, for .}}

snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abampere == The word abampere is a shortened form of absolute ampere, as evolved from its original full name absolute electromagnetic cgs unit of current. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic
snippet: The WFFs of propositional logic can be made more readable by allowing them to be abbreviated. The resulting strings are not actually WFFs as such, but can be translated back uniquely into full WFFs.

title: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic/Justification
snippet: == Justification for Abbreviation of WFFs == The abbreviation of WFFs of propositional logic stems from their semantics. It is only because we "know how binary connectives work" that we are able to allow these abbreviation rules to be defined. In particular, note that the ability to remove brackets from around repeated $\land$ and $\lor$ connectives stems from the Rule of Association which (at the stage of construction of the formal system that is PropLog) has not even been suggested, let alone proved.

title: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic/Limitation
snippet: == Limitation of Abbreviation of WFFs == The question needs to be answered: why can we not replace $\paren {\mathbf A \land \paren {\mathbf B \land \mathbf C} }$ with $\paren {\mathbf A \land \mathbf B \land \mathbf C}$? Is this not essentially what the Rule of Association states? Either way, the statement is only true if all three are true. This is indeed the case.

title: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic/Rules
snippet: == Rules for Abbreviation of WFFs == The following rules allow WFFs of propositional logic to be abbreviated so as to make them more readable. {{item|(3):|In the case of repeated $\land$ or $\lor$ connectives, we can replace: $\paren {\paren {\mathbf A \land \mathbf B} \land \mathbf C}$ with $\paren {\mathbf A \land \mathbf B \land \mathbf C}$ but not: $\paren {\mathbf A \land \paren {\mathbf B \land \mathbf C} }$ with $\paren {\mathbf A \land \mathbf B \land \mathbf C}$ (there is a reason for this).}} Any string obtained from a WFF $\mathbf A$ by applying any of the above rules is called an…

title: Definition:Abbreviation of WFF of Propositional Logic/Standard Abbreviation
snippet: The string obtained by applying as many of the rules for abbreviation of WFFs to a WFF $\mathbf A$ as possible is known as the standard abbreviation of $\mathbf A$. Thus it can be seen that there may be several abbreviations of a given WFF, but only one standard abbreviation.

title: Definition:Abcoulomb
snippet: The abcoulomb is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic base unit of electric charge. The abcoulomb is the charge flowing in $1$ second given a current of $1$ abampere.

title: Definition:Abcoulomb/Also known as

title: Definition:Abel's Integral Equation
snippet: Abel's integral equation is an integral equation whose purpose is to solve Abel's mechanical problem, which finds how long it will take a bead to slide down a wire. The purpose of Abel's integral equation is to find the shape of the curve into which the wire is bent in order to yield that result: Let $\map T y$ be a function which specifies the total time of descent for a given starting height.

title: Definition:Abel's Integral Equation/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abel's Integral Equation == devised what is now known as Abel's Integral Equation as a tool by which to solve the Tautochrone Problem in $1823$.

title: Definition:Abel Summation Method
snippet: The series: $\ds \sum a_n$ can be summed by the Abel method ($A$-method) to the number $S$ if, for any real $x$ such that $0 < x < 1$, the series: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k$ is convergent and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 1^-} \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty a_k x^k = S$ $\ds \map f x = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n e^{-n x} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n z^n$ where $z = \map \exp {−x}$. Then the limit of $\map f x$ as $x$ approaches $0$ through positive reals is the limit of the power series for $\map f z$ as $z$ approaches $1$ from below through positive reals.

title: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 1
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which: every monomorphism is a kernel every epimorphism is a cokernel

title: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 2
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which: every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel

title: Definition:Abelian Category/Definition 3
snippet: An abelian category is a pre-abelian category in which for every morphism $f$, the canonical morphism from its coimage to its image $\map {\operatorname {coim} } f \to \Img f$ is an isomorphism.

title: Definition:Abelian Function
snippet: An Abelian function is an inverse function of an Abelian integral.

title: Definition:Abelian Function/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abelian Function == The foundations for the theory of Abelian functions were laid in 's paper . studied Abelian functions by applying Dirichlet's Principle for Harmonic Functions combined with geometric reasoning. The work on extending our understanding of them continued with , working alone with no contact with other mathematicians. He took up their study as his life's work.

title: Definition:Abelian Group/Also known as
snippet: The usual way of spelling abelian group is without a capital letter, but Abelian is frequently seen. The term commutative group can occasionally be seen.

title: Definition:Abelian Group/Definition 1
snippet: An abelian group is a group $G$ where: $\forall a, b \in G: a b = b a$ That is, every element in $G$ commutes with every other element in $G$.

title: Definition:Abelian Group/Definition 2
snippet: An abelian group is a group $G$ : $G = \map Z G$ where $\map Z G$ is the center of $G$.

title: Definition:Abelian Group/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abelian Group == The importance of abelian groups was discovered by during the course of his investigations into the theory of equations.

title: Definition:Abelian Group/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abelian Group == The pronunciation of abelian in the term abelian group is usually either a-bee-lee-an or a-bell-ee-an, putting the emphasis on the second syllable. Note that the term abelian has thus phonetically lost the connection to its eponym (correctly pronounced aah-bl). Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Abelian Integral
snippet: An Abelian integral is a complex Riemann integral of the form: $\ds \int_{z_0}^z \map R {x, w} \rd x$ where $\map R {x, w}$ is an arbitrary rational function of the two variables $x$ and $w$. These variables are related by the equation: $\map F {x, w} = 0$ where $\map F {x, w}$ is an irreducible polynomial in $w$: $\map F {x, w} \equiv \map {\phi_n} x w^n + \cdots + \map {\phi_1} x w + \map {\phi_0} x$ whose coefficients $\map {\phi_j} x, j = 0, 1, \ldots, n$ are rational functions of $x$.

title: Definition:Abelian Integral/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abelian Integral == The foundations for the theory of Abelian integrals were laid in 's paper .

title: Definition:Abelianization of Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. The abelianization of $G$ is the quotient of $G$ by its derived subgroup: $G^{\mathrm {ab} } = G / \sqbrk {G, G}$

title: Definition:Abfarad
snippet: The abfarad is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic unit of capacitance. It is defined as being the amount of capacitance of a capacitor between the plates of which an electric potential of $1$ abvolt appears when it stores $1$ abcoulomb of electric charge.

title: Definition:Abfarad/Also known as
snippet: == Abfarad: Also known as == The abfarad is also known as the electromagnetic unit of capacitance, abbreviated $\mathrm {e.m.u.}$.

title: Definition:Abfarad/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abfarad == The word abfarad is a shortened form of absolute farad, as evolved from its original full name absolute electromagnetic cgs unit of resistance. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Abhenry
snippet: The abhenry is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic unit of inductance. It is defined as being the amount of inductance of a closed electronic circuit that produces $1$ maxwell of magnetic flux per abampere.

title: Definition:Abhenry/Also known as
snippet: == Abhenry: Also known as == The abhenry is also known as the electromagnetic unit of inductance, abbreviated $\mathrm {e.m.u.}$. In older texts, the unit may be rendered as the centimetre, reflecting its dimension in the CGS-EMU (electromagnetic cgs) absolute system of units .

title: Definition:Abhenry/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abhenry == The word abhenry is a shortened form of absolute henry, as evolved from its original full name absolute electromagnetic cgs unit of resistance. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Abnormal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is an abnormal subgroup : $\forall g \in G: g \in \gen {H, H^g}$ where $\gen {H, H^g}$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by $H$ and the conjugate of $H$ by $g$.

title: Definition:Abohm
snippet: The abohm is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic unit of electrical resistance. It is defined as being the electrical resistance between two points of an electrical conductor when a constant electric potential of $1$ abvolt, applied to these points, produces in the conductor an electric current of $1$ abampere, the conductor not being the seat of any electromotive force.

title: Definition:Abohm/Also known as
snippet: == Abohm: Also known as == The abohm is also known as the electromagnetic unit of resistance, abbreviated $\mathrm {e.m.u.}$.

title: Definition:Abohm/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abohm == The word abohm is a shortened form of absolute ohm, as evolved from its original full name absolute electromagnetic cgs unit of resistance. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Above
snippet: Numbers: Number $a$ is above number $b$ $a$ is greater than $b$. Solid Geometry: Point $a$ is above point $b$ the height of $a$ a given frame of reference $R$ is greater than the height of $b$ $R$. Plane Geometry: Point $a$ is above point $b$ the $y$ coordinate of $a$ is greater than the $y$ coordinate of $b$.

title: Definition:Above (Number)
snippet: In the context of numbers, above means greater than. Note that this applies to: the natural numbers $\N$ the integers $\Z$ the rational numbers $\Q$ the real numbers $\R$ but specifically not the complex numbers $\C$ because the complex numbers do not have a usual ordering.

title: Definition:Above (Plane Geometry)
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be points in the cartesian plane $\R^2$. Then: $a$ is above $b$ the $y$ coordinate of $a$ is greater than the $y$ coordinate of $b$.

title: Definition:Above (Solid Geometry)
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be points in $3$-dimensional Euclidean space $\R^3$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary plane embedded in $S$ be distinguished and defined as horizontal. Then: $a$ is above $b$ the height of $a$ $P$ is greater than the height of $b$ $P$.

title: Definition:Abridged Multiplication
snippet: Abridged multiplication is multiplication using only so many significant figures as are required to obtain a product with sufficient precision. Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be real numbers such that $x y = z$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $z$ be required to be rounded to the nearest $n$th power of $10$. Let $x$ and $y$ be reported to the nearest $n - r$th and $n - s$th power of $10$ respectively.

title: Definition:Abscissa
snippet: Consider the graph $y = \map f x$ of a real function $f$ embedded in a Cartesian plane. 500px The $x$ coordinate of a point $P = \tuple {x, y}$ on $f$ is known as the abscissa of $P$.

title: Definition:Abscissa/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abscissa == The term abscissa was used by in his $1220$ work Practica Geometriae. Some sources suggest that the word descends from translations of by . Its use in the modern sense, as meaning the $x$ coordinate of a point in a Cartesian plane, may have been due to in his $1659$ work Miscellaneum Hyperbolicum, et Parabolicum. The term entered the mathematical mainstream via the works of , and some suggest that he may even have coined it.

title: Definition:Abscissa/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abscissa == The term abscissa comes from the Latin term linea abscissa, which means a line cut off. The same source gives the word . Some sources suggest that the word descends from translations of by , where the Greek word ἀποτεμνομέναις (apotemnomenais) appears. The word is rarely used nowadays except in the context of the history of mathematics. Its plural is correctly abscissae or (to be even more strictly classically correct) abscissæ. However, the plural form of the term (when it is used at all) is commonly abscissas.

title: Definition:Abscissa of Convergence
snippet: Let $\map f s$ be a Dirichlet series The abscissa of convergence of $f$ is the extended real number $\sigma_0 \in \overline \R$ defined by: $\ds \sigma_0 = \inf \set {\map \Re s: s \in \C, \map f s \text{ converges} }$ where $\inf \O = +\infty$.

title: Definition:Absolute Continuity/Complex Measure
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $
u$ be a complex measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\size

title: Definition:Absolute Continuity/Measure
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be measures on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. We say that $
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$ and write: $
u \ll \mu$ $\ds  orall A \in \Sigma : \map \mu A = 0 \implies \map 
u A = 0$

title: Definition:Absolute Continuity/Real Function
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. A real function $f: I \to \R$ is said to be absolutely continuous it satisfies the following property: For every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that the following property holds: For every finite set of pairwise disjoint closed real intervals $\closedint {a_1} {b_1}, \dotsc, \closedint {a_n} {b_n} \subseteq I$ such that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {b_i - a_i} < \delta$ it holds that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {\map f {b_i} - \map f {a_i} } < \epsilon$

title: Definition:Absolute Continuity/Signed Measure
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $
u$ be a signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\size 
u$ be the variation of $
u$. We say that $
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$ : $\size 
u$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$. We write: $
u \ll \mu$

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence
snippet: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series Definition:Absolutely Convergent Product Definition:Absolute Convergence of Generalized Sum Definition:Absolutely Convergent Integral

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \size {a_n} }$ is convergent.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence of complex numbers. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Numbers/Definition 3
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent there exists $n_0 \in \N$ such that: $a_n \ne -1$ for $n > n_0$ The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = n_0 + 1}^\infty \log \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent where $\log$ denotes the complex logarithm.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \norm {a_n} }$ is convergent.

title: Definition:Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ is absolutely convergent the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent.

title: Definition:Absolute Difference
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. The absolute difference between $a$ and $b$ is defined and denoted as: $\size {a - b}$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ is the absolute value function. That is, the result of the smaller number subtracted from the larger.

title: Definition:Absolute Difference/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Difference: Also known as == The absolute difference between two real numbers is usually referred to just as their difference. However, this usage is ambiguous, so is deprecated on .

title: Definition:Absolute Error/Also defined as
snippet: == Absolute Error: Also defined as == Let $x_0$ be an approximation to a (true) value $x$. The absolute error of $x_0$ in $x$ can also be seen defined as: {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \Delta x | o = := | r = \size {x_0 - x} }} where $\size {x_0 - x}$ denotes the absolute value of $x_0 - x$.

title: Definition:Absolute Error/Correction
snippet: Let $x_0$ be an approximation to a (true) value $x$. Let $\Delta x$ denote the absolute error of $x_0$. The correction to $x$ is the quantity that needs to be added to $x_0$ to change it to $x$. That is, the correction to $x$ is defined as $-\Delta x$.

title: Definition:Absolute Galois Group
snippet: == Definition == Let $K$ be a field.

title: Definition:Absolute Galois Group/Definition 1
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. The absolute Galois group of $K$ is the Galois group $\Gal {K^{\operatorname{sep} } \mid K}$ of its separable closure.

title: Definition:Absolute Galois Group/Definition 2
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. The absolute Galois group of $K$ is the automorphism group $\Aut {\overline K \mid K}$ of its algebraic closure.

title: Definition:Absolute Geometry
snippet: Absolute geometry is the study of Euclidean geometry without the parallel postulate.

title: Definition:Absolute Geometry/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Geometry: Also known as == Absolute geometry is also known as neutral geometry.

title: Definition:Absolute Maximum/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Maximum: Also known as == An absolute maximum is also known as a maximum value, or just a maximum if there is no need to distinguish it from a local maximum. Some sources use the term global maximum

title: Definition:Absolute Measure of Dispersion
snippet: An absolute measure of dispersion is a measure of dispersion that indicates how spread out or scattered a set of observations with respect to the actual values of those observations.

title: Definition:Absolute Minimum/Also known as
snippet: An absolute minimum is also known as a minimum value, or just a minimum if there is no need to distinguish it from a local minimum.

title: Definition:Absolute Number
snippet: An absolute number is a number in an expression which has a single value. It is either expressed using actual figures, in an agreed number system, or by a symbol which is understood to represent that specific number.

title: Definition:Absolute Polar
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq E$ be non-empty. We define the absolute polar $A^\circ$ of $A$ by: $A^\circ = \set {f \in F : \cmod {\innerprod x f} \le 1 \text { for all } x \in A}$

title: Definition:Absolute Prepolar
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $B \subseteq F$ be non-empty. We define the absolute prepolar $B_\circ$ of $B$ by: $B_\circ = \set {x \in E : \cmod {\innerprod x f} \le 1 \text { for all } f \in B}$

title: Definition:Absolute Real Vector Ordering
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be elements of the real vector space $\R^n$. The absolute real vector ordering is the partial ordering $\ge$ defined on the real vector space $\R^n$ as: $\forall x, y \in \R^n: x \ge y \iff \forall i \in \left\{ {1, 2, \ldots, n}\right\}: x_i \ge y_i$

title: Definition:Absolute Real Vector Ordering/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Absolute Real Vector Ordering ==

title: Definition:Absolute Real Vector Strict Ordering
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be elements of the real vector space $\R^n$. The absolute real vector strict ordering is the strict partial ordering $\ge$ defined on the real vector space $\R^n$ as: $\forall x, y \in \R^n: x \ge y \iff \forall i \in \left\{ {1, 2, \ldots, n}\right\}: x_i \ge y_i$

title: Definition:Absolute Real Vector Strict Ordering/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Absolute Real Vector Strict Ordering ==

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Also known as
snippet: == Absolute Value: Also known as == The absolute value of $x$ is sometimes called the modulus or magnitude of $x$, but note that modulus has a more specialized definition in the domain of complex numbers, and that magnitude has a more specialized definition in the context of vectors. Some sources refer to it as the size of $x$. Some sources call it the numerical value. Some call it just the value, but that term is too broad to be reliable.

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 1
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The absolute value of $x$ is denoted $\size x$, and is defined using the usual ordering on the real numbers as follows: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x > 0 \\ 0 & : x = 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 1/Also presented as
snippet: == Absolute Value: Also presented as == Because $0 = -0$, the value of $\size x$ at $x = 0$ is often included in one of the other two cases, most commonly: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x < 0 \end{cases}$ but this can be argued as being less symmetrically aesthetic. This form can also be found: $\size x = \begin{cases} x & : x \ge 0 \\ -x & : x \le 0 \end{cases}$

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Definition 2
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. The absolute value of $x$ is denoted $\size x$, and is defined as: $\size x = +\sqrt {x^2}$ where $+\sqrt {x^2}$ is the positive square root of $x^2$.

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Graphical Illustration
snippet: == Graphical Illustration == The graph of the absolute value function can be presented as: 500px

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Number Classes
snippet: The absolute value function applies to the various number classes as follows: Natural numbers $\N$: All elements of $\N$ are greater than or equal to zero, so the concept is irrelevant. Integers $\Z$: As defined here. Rational numbers $\Q$: As defined here. Real numbers $\R$: As defined here. Complex numbers $\C$: As $\C$ is not an ordered set, the definition of the absolute value function based upon whether a complex number is greater than or less than zero cannot be applied. The notation $\cmod z$, where $z \in \C$, is defined as the modulus of $z$ and has a different meaning.

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Then for all $a \in D$, the absolute value of $a$ is defined as: $\size a = \begin {cases} a & : 0_D \le a \\ -a & : a 0_D$ denotes that $\neg \paren {a \le 0_D}$.

title: Definition:Absolute Value/Technical Note
snippet: == Technical Note == has a $\LaTeX$ shortcut for the symbol used to denote absolute value: {{LatexFor|for = \size {x} }} If the argument of the \size command is $1$ character, then the braces {} are usually omitted. Category:Definitions/Absolute Value Function Category:Technical Notes

title: Definition:Absolute Value of Complex Differential
snippet: Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to \C$ be a smooth path in $\C$. Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a complex function. Let the contour integral of $f$ along $\gamma$ exist. In other words: $\ds \int_\gamma \map f z \rd z$ or: $\ds \int_I \map f {\map \gamma t} \map {\gamma'} t \rd t$ exists. Then: $\cmod {\d z} = \cmod {\map {\gamma'} t} \rd t$

title: Definition:Absolute Value of Cut
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. The absolute value of $\alpha$ is denoted and defined as: $\size \alpha = \begin {cases} \alpha & : \alpha \ge 0^* \\ -\alpha & : \alpha < 0^* \end {cases}$ where: $0^*$ denotes the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$ $\ge$ denotes the ordering on cuts.

title: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping
snippet: Let $D$ be an ordered integral domain. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}_D$ denote the absolute value function on $D$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to D$ be a mapping. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f_D: S \to D$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f_D} s := \size {\map f s}_D$ Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on a mapping.

title: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping/Extended Real-Valued Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set, and let $f: S \to \overline \R$ be an extended real-valued function. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f: S \to \overline \R$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f} s := \size {\map f s}$ where $\size {\map f s}$ denotes the extended absolute value function on $\overline \R$. Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on extended real-valued functions. Since extended absolute value coincides on $\R$ with the standard ordering, this definition incorporates the definition for real-valued functions.

title: Definition:Absolute Value of Mapping/Real-Valued Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Then the absolute value of $f$, denoted $\size f: S \to \R$, is defined as: $\forall s \in S: \map {\size f} s := \size {\map f s}$ where $\size {\map f s}$ denotes the absolute value function on $\R$. Absolute value thence is an instance of a pointwise operation on real-valued functions.

title: Definition:Absolute Zero
snippet: Absolute zero is the lowest temperature which can theoretically be achieved. It is the temperature where all motion due to thermal effects stops. Before that temperature can be reached, quantum effects come into play.

title: Definition:Absolutely Consistent Proof System
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr P$ be a consistent proof system for $\LL$. Then $\mathscr P$ is absolutely consistent not all WFF of $\mathscr P$ is a theorem.

title: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Also known as
snippet: == Absolutely Continuous Random Variable: Also known as == Often, particularly in elementary discussions of probability theory, the term continuous random variable is used to mean absolutely continuous random variable as defined here. On we seek to avoid this ambiguity, and it should be made explicit whether a result applies only to absolutely continuous random variables, or general continuous random variables. Category:Definitions/Absolutely Continuous Random Variables

title: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. We say that $X$ is an absolutely continuous random variable : $P_X$ is an absolutely continuous measure with respect to $\lambda$.

title: Definition:Absolutely Continuous Random Variable/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function of $X$. We say that $X$ is an absolutely continuous random variable : $F_X$ is an absolutely continuous real function.

title: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Integral
snippet: Let $I = \ds \int_S \map f x \rd x$ be an improper integral, where $S$ is an unbounded closed interval. $I$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \int_S \size {\map f x} \rd x$ converges. Category:Definitions/Absolute Convergence Category:Definitions/Improper Integrals

title: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/Also known as
snippet: == Absolutely Convergent Series: Also known as == An absolutely convergent series is also referred to as absolutely summable.

title: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $S = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in the complex number field $\C$. Then $S$ is absolutely convergent : $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \cmod {a_n}$ is convergent where $\cmod {a_n}$ denotes the complex modulus of $a_n$.

title: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/General
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in $V$. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ in $V$ is absolutely convergent $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \norm {a_n}$ is a convergent series in $\R$.

title: Definition:Absolutely Convergent Series/Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a series in the real number field $\R$. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is absolutely convergent : $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {a_n}$ is convergent where $\size {a_n}$ denotes the absolute value of $a_n$.

title: Definition:Absolutely Convex Set
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $A \subseteq X$. We say that $A$ is absolutely convex : $A$ is convex and balanced.

title: Definition:Absolutely Integrable Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. $\map f x$ is absolutely integrable on $S \subseteq \R$ its absolute value of $f$ is an integrable function on $S$. That is, the definite integral of the absolute value of $f$ over any interval $\openint \alpha \beta \subseteq S$ is bounded. Category:Definitions/Integral Calculus

title: Definition:Absolutely Normal Number
snippet: A real number $r$ is absolutely normal if it is normal every number base $b$. That is, its basis expansion in every number base $b$ is such that: no finite sequence of digits of $r$ of length $n$ occurs more frequently than any other such finite sequence of length $n$. In particular, for every number base $b$, all digits of $r$ have the same natural density in the basis expansion of $r$.

title: Definition:Absolutely Symmetric Function/Also known as
snippet: == Absolutely Symmetric Function: Also known as == An absolutely symmetric function is also known as a totally symmetric function. Some sources use the term symmetric function,

title: Definition:Absolutely Symmetric Function/Definition 1
snippet: Let $f: \R^n \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Let $f$ be such that, for every pair $\tuple {x_i, x_j}$ in $\R^2$: $\map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_i, \ldots, x_j, \ldots, x_n} = \map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_j, \ldots, x_i, \ldots, x_n}$ Then $f$ is an absolutely symmetric function.

title: Definition:Absolutely Symmetric Function/Definition 2
snippet: Let $f: \R^n \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Let $f$ be such that, for all $\mathbf x := \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \in \R^n$: $\map f {\mathbf x} = \map f {\mathbf y}$ where $\mathbf y$ is a permutation of $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$. Then $f$ is an absolutely symmetric function.

title: Definition:Absorbent Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$. Let $W \subseteq V$ be a subset of $V$. Let the set $a \cdot W$ be defined as: $a \cdot W := \set {a \cdot y: y \in W}$ where: $a \in K$ $a \cdot y$ denotes the scalar multiplication. Then $W$ is an absorbent set in $V$ : $\ds \bigcup_{a \mathop \in K} a \cdot W = V$ which symbolically can be represented as: $K \cdot W = V$

title: Definition:Absorbent Set/Also known as
snippet: == Absorbent Set: Also known as == An absorbent set is also known as an absorbing set. Some sources use the term radial set. This reflects the idea that $W$ will generate all the elements of $V$ in the sense that any $v \in V$ can be written as $v = \alpha \cdot w$ for some $w \in W$ and $\alpha \in K$.

title: Definition:Absorbing Set
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $A \subseteq X$. We say that $A$ is absorbing : for all $x \in X$ there exists $t \in \R_{> 0}$ such that $x \in \alpha C$ for $\cmod \alpha \ge t$ where $t A$ denotes the dilation of $A$ by $t$.

title: Definition:Absorbing State
snippet: Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \mathop \ge 0}$ be a Markov chain on a state space $S$. Let $i \in S$ be an element of the state space $S$. Then $i$ is an absorbing state of $\sequence {X_n}$ : $X_k = i \implies X_{k + 1} = i$ That is, it is an element of $S$ such that if $\sequence {X_n}$ reaches $i$, it stays there.

title: Definition:Absorbing State/Also defined as
snippet: == Absorbing State: Also defined as == Some sources define an absorbing state on a random walk only. Some sources separate the definitions of absorbing state and absorbing barrier, using the former for a Markov chain and the latter for a random walk.

title: Definition:Absorbing State/Also known as
snippet: == Absorbing State: Also known as == An absorbing state can also be seen referred to as an absorbing barrier.

title: Definition:Absorption Law
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, *}$ be an algebraic structure. Let both $\circ$ and $*$ be commutative. Then $\circ$ absorbs $*$ : $\forall a, b \in S: a \circ \paren {a * b} = a$ This equality is called the absorption law of $\circ$ for $*$.

title: Definition:Abstract
snippet: Abstract Algebra Abstract Geometry In the field of Mathematical Logic and Automata Theory: Abstract Machine

title: Definition:Abstract Algebra
snippet: Abstract algebra is a branch of mathematics which studies algebraic structures and algebraic systems. It can be roughly described as the study of sets equipped with operations.

title: Definition:Abstract Algebra/Also known as
snippet: == Abstract Algebra: Also known as == Abstract algebra is also sometimes referred to as modern algebra, particularly in older texts.

title: Definition:Abstract Geometry
snippet: Let $P$ be a set and $L$ be a set of subsets of $P$. Then $\struct {P, L}$ is an abstract geometry $\struct {P, L}$ satisfies the abstract geometry axioms:

title: Definition:Abstract Geometry/Line
snippet: Let $\struct {P, L}$ be an abstract geometry. The elements of $L$ are referred to as lines.

title: Definition:Abstract Geometry/Point
snippet: Let $\struct {P, L}$ be an abstract geometry. The elements of $P$ are referred to as points.

title: Definition:Abstract Machine
snippet: An abstract machine is a hypothetical computing machine defined in terms of the operations it performs rather than its internal physical structure.

title: Definition:Abstract Space
snippet: An abstract space is: a set of objects together with: a set of axioms which define operations on and relations between those objects.

title: Definition:Abstract Space/Also known as
snippet: == Abstract Space: Also known as == An abstract space is also known as just a space, but this has multiple meanings in a number of different contexts. Hence its use here is not recommended on .

title: Definition:Abstraction
snippet: Abstraction is the process of making a general statement from a collection of particular statements so as to summarise a property that applies to the subject of those particular statements.

title: Definition:Abstraction (Mathematical Logic)
snippet: An abstraction is an operator that forms a class name or predicate from a given expression.

title: Definition:Absurd
snippet: Absurd is a word used mainly in logic meaning either meaningless, contradictory or internally inconsistent.

title: Definition:Abundance
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\map {\sigma_1} n$ be the divisor sum function of $n$. That is, let $\map {\sigma_1} n$ be the sum of all positive divisors of $n$. Then the abundance of $n$ is defined as $\map A n = \map {\sigma_1} n - 2 n$.

title: Definition:Abundance/Also known as
snippet: == Abundance: Also known as == There may possibly be a vanishingly tiny usage which refers to abundance as the excedent function. Category:Definitions/Abundance

title: Definition:Abundance/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Abundance == The concepts of abundant and deficient appear to have originated with the Neo-Pythagorean school, in particular , who wrote fancifully on the subject in his Ἀριθμητικὴ εἰσαγωγή (). Category:Historical Notes

title: Definition:Abundancy Index
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $\map {\sigma_1} n$ be the divisor sum function of $n$. That is, let $\map {\sigma_1} n$ be the sum of all positive divisors of $n$. Then the abundancy index of $n$ is defined as $\dfrac {\map {\sigma_1} n} n$.

title: Definition:Abundant Number
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer.

title: Definition:Abundant Number/Definition 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\map A n$ denote the abundance of $n$. $n$ is abundant $\map A n > 0$.

title: Definition:Abundant Number/Definition 2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\map {\sigma_1} n$ be the divisor sum function of $n$. $n$ is abundant $\dfrac {\map {\sigma_1} n} n > 2$.

title: Definition:Abundant Number/Definition 3
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. $n$ is abundant it is smaller than its aliquot sum.

title: Definition:Abuse of Notation
snippet: Mathematical notation can be considered in two ways: As an aid to mathematical understanding, no more and no less than a useful convention to encapsulate more or less complicated ideas in a completely unambiguous format; As the reason for mathematical effort, so as to encapsulate a truth as a documented piece of aesthetic beauty in its own right. Abuse of notation is a technique of using a system of symbology in a way different from that for which it was originally defined.

title: Definition:Abvolt
snippet: The abvolt is the CGS unrationalised electromagnetic unit of electromotive force and electric potential. It is defined as being: The electric potential which will drive $1$ abampere of electric current through a resistance of $1$ abohm.

title: Definition:Abvolt/Also known as
snippet: == Abvolt: Also known as == The abvolt is also known as the electromagnetic unit of potential, abbreviated $\mathrm {e.m.u.}$.

title: Definition:Abvolt/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Abvolt == The word abvolt is a shortened form of absolute volt, as evolved from its original full name absolute electromagnetic cgs unit of potential. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Académie Parisienne
snippet: The Académie Parisienne was an informal academic society established in $1635$ by the Franciscan friar , sponsored and encouraged by . It consisted of some $140$ correspondents from around Europe, and formed a hub of mathematical interaction through which the leading minds of the time could communicate with each other. 's copious correspondence held it all together. It was to form the nucleus of the later more formal , which was chartered in $1666$.

title: Definition:Acceleration
snippet: The acceleration $\mathbf a$ of a body $M$ is defined as the first derivative of the velocity $\mathbf v$ of $M$ relative to a given point of reference time $t$: $\mathbf a = \dfrac {\d \mathbf v} {\d t}$ Colloquially, it is described as the rate of change of velocity. It is important to note that as velocity is a vector quantity, then it follows by definition of derivative of a vector that so is acceleration.

title: Definition:Acceleration-Time Graph
snippet: An acceleration-time graph is a graph which shows: acceleration on the $y$-axis plotted against: time on the $x$-axis for a particle moving in a straight line.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Dimension
snippet: Acceleration has dimension $\mathsf {L T}^{-2}$.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Acceleration == The first person to study the acceleration of a particle moving along a general curve was first studied by . He was also the first to treat acceleration as a vector.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Acceleration == The word acceleration comes from the Latin for to add speed. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Acceleration/Straight Line
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle in motion along a straight line $\LL$ with acceleration $\map {\mathbf a} t$ as a function of time $t$. It is conventional to align $\LL$ along the $x$-axis of a Cartesian coordinate system such that the $\mathbf a$ can be expressed as $a \mathbf i$. Then the unit vector of the component vector $a \mathbf i$ is suppressed, and $\map {\mathbf a} t$ is treated as a scalar quantity $\map a t$.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Symbol
snippet: == Acceleration: Symbol == The usual symbol used to denote the acceleration of a body is $\mathbf a$.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Unit
snippet: The SI unit of acceleration is the metre per second squared: $\mathrm {m \, s^{-2} }$. The CGS unit of acceleration is the gal: $\mathrm {Gal}$. The FPS unit of acceleration is the foot per second squared $\mathrm {ft \, s^{-2} }$.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Unit/Foot per Second Squared
snippet: == FPS unit of Acceleration == The FPS unit of acceleration is the foot per second squared.

title: Definition:Acceleration/Unit/Gal
snippet: == CGS unit of Acceleration == The CGS unit of acceleration is the gal. $1$ gal is defined as $1$ centimetre per second squared: $1 \, \mathrm {Gal} = 1 \, \mathrm {cm \, s^{-2} }$

title: Definition:Acceleration/Unit/Metre per Second Squared
snippet: == SI unit of Acceleration == The SI unit of acceleration is the metre per second squared.

title: Definition:Acceleration (Continuum Mechanics)
snippet: In the context of continuum mechanics, the acceleration of a point $P$ in a body $B$ is the material derivative of the velocity of $P$ evaluated at $P$.

title: Definition:Acceleration of Smooth Curve
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an interval. Let $\gamma: \R \to \R^n$ be a smooth curve, written in standard coordinates as: $\map \gamma t = \tuple {\map {\gamma^1} t, \ldots, \map {\gamma^n} t}$. The acceleration of $\gamma$ at $t \in I$ is defined as: $\map {\gamma} t = \valueat{\map {\ddot \gamma^1} t \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x^1} } {\map \gamma t} + \ldots + \valueat {\map {\ddot \gamma^n} t \dfrac {\partial}{\partial x^n} } {\map \gamma t}$

title: Definition:Acceleration of Smooth Curve on Smooth Manifold
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with or without boundary. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be a smooth curve on $M$. Let $\gamma'$ be the velocity of $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$. Then $D_t \gamma'$ is called the acceleration of $\gamma$ on $M$.

title: Definition:Acceptance Region
snippet: Let $\theta$ be a population parameter of some population $P$. Let $\Omega$ be the parameter space of $\theta$. Let $\mathbf X$ be a random sample from $P$. Let $T = \map f {\mathbf X}$ be a sample statistic. Let $\delta$ be a hypothesis test of the form: accept $H_0$ if $T \in A$ for some null hypothesis $H_0$ and some $A \subset \Omega$. We refer to $A$ as the acceptance region of $\delta$.

title: Definition:Acceptance Sampling
snippet: Acceptance sampling is a procedure in quality control in which: $(1): \quad$ a sample is taken from a batch and measured $(2): \quad$ the number of defectives is counted $(3): \quad$ a decision is made to accept or reject the batch based on the count of those defectives. The most simple method is to have a single criterion to accept or reject the batch based on the number of defectives. A more sophisticated approach is to take further samples if the count of defectives is borderline.

title: Definition:Acceptance Sampling/Motivation
snippet: == Motivation for Acceptance Sampling == Every batch of items of merchandise may contain defectives. The consumer will not accept a batch with a large number of defectives. On the other hand, the producer does not want to reject a batch with a small number of defectives. A producer does not want to test everything produced, as that is impractical and inefficient, and (in cases where testing necessarily destroys the merchandise in some way) unfeasible. Hence a sample is tested.

title: Definition:Accessibility
snippet: Let $G$ be a connected graph. Let $v$ be a vertex of $G$. The accessibility of $v$ in $G$ is the sum of the distances between $v$ and all the other vertices of $G$. The smaller the sum, the more accessible the vertex.

title: Definition:Accounting
snippet: Accounting is the branch of mathematics concerned with processing of information about economic entities, such as businesses and corporations.

title: Definition:Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$.

title: Definition:Accumulation Point/Also known as
snippet: == Accumulation Point: Also known as == An accumulation point is also known as a cluster point, but that term has a number of different meanings. Some sources refer to an accumulation point as a limit point, but prefers to maintain a distinction between the two concepts.

title: Definition:Accumulation Point/Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an infinite sequence in $A$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x \in S$ is an accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}$ : $\forall U \in \tau: x \in U \implies \set {n \in \N: x_n \in U}$ is infinite

title: Definition:Accumulation Point/Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is an accumulation point of $A$ : $x \in \map \cl {A \setminus \set x}$ where $\cl$ denotes the (topological) closure of a set.

title: Definition:Accuracy
snippet: Accuracy is a measure of how closely a reported number matches the true value of that number.

title: Definition:Accuracy/Also known as
snippet: == Accuracy: Also known as == In the same way one can refer to a value as being accurate to $n$ decimal places or to $n$ significant figures, one can also say correct to $n$ decimal places or $n$ significant figures.

title: Definition:Accuracy/Decimal Places
snippet: A representation $y$ in decimal notation of a number $x$ is: accurate to $n$ decimal places the number $n$ of digits after the decimal point of $x$ match the first $n$ digits after the decimal point of $y$, without rounding.

title: Definition:Accuracy/Significant Figures
snippet: A representation $y$ in decimal notation of a number $x$ is accurate to $n$ significant figures the first $n$ digits of $x$ match, after rounding, the first $n$ digits of $y$. In this context it is usual for $y$ to be expressed only by $n$ digits.

title: Definition:Accurate to n Decimal Places/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == accurate (correct) to $n$ decimal places

title: Definition:Ackermann-Péter Function
snippet: The Ackermann-Péter function $A: \Z_{\ge 0} \times \Z_{\ge 0} \to \Z_{> 0}$ is an integer-valued function defined on the set of ordered pairs of positive integers as: $\map A {m, n} = \begin{cases} n + 1 & : m = 0 \\ \map A {m - 1, 1} & : m > 0, n = 0 \\ \map A {m - 1, \map A {m, n - 1} } & : \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$

title: Definition:Acnode
snippet: An acnode is a singular point of the locus of an equation describing a curve which is not actually on that curve.

title: Definition:Acnode/Also known as
snippet: == Acnode: Also known as == An acnode is also known as an isolated point, but the latter term has a wider application in the field of topology, of which the acnode is an example.

title: Definition:Acoustics
snippet: Acoustics is the branch of physics which studies the properties of sound.

snippet: == Acre: Conversion Factors ==
