title: Definition:Right Coset/Also defined as
snippet: == Right Coset: Also defined as == It is usual for the algebraic structure $S$ in fact to be a group. Hence, when $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group, the right coset of $H$ by $x$ is the equivalence class of $x$ defined by right congruence modulo $H$. Some sources (see , for example) order the operands in the opposite direction, and hence $x \circ H$ is a right coset.

title: Definition:Right Coset Space/Also known as
snippet: == Right Coset Space: Also known as == Some sources refer to the right coset space as the right quotient set. Other terms which may be encountered are: the right coset family. the right coset decomposition. Some sources use a hyphen: right-coset space or right-coset family, and so on.

title: Definition:Right Cylinder
snippet: A right cylinder is a cylinder whose bases are perpendicular to the generatrices.

title: Definition:Right Derived Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives. Let $\mathbf B$ be an abelian category. Let $F: \mathbf A \to \mathbf B$ be a left exact functor. Let $X$ and $Y$ be objects of $\mathbf A$. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathbf A$. Let $I$ be an arbitrary injective resolution of $X$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary injective resolution of $Y$. Let $\tilde f : I \to J$ be a morphism of cochain complexes induced by $f$. Let $\map F I$ denote the cochain complex defined by applying the functor on cochains induced by $F$ to $I$. Let $i \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a non-negative integer.

title: Definition:Right Elliptical Cylinder
snippet: A right elliptical cylinder is an elliptical cylinder which is also a right cylinder. That is, it is a cylinder with bases are: ellipses perpendicular to the generatrices.

title: Definition:Right Elliptical Cylinder/Also known as
snippet: == Right Elliptical Cylinder: Also known as == A right elliptical cylinder is also known as a right elliptic cylinder. Some sources assume rightness, and merely refer to an elliptic cylinder or elliptical cylinder.

title: Definition:Right Exact Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf A \to \mathbf B$ be a functor. Then $F$ is right exact $F$ preserves finite colimits.

title: Definition:Right Half-Open Interval/Also known as
snippet: == Right Half-Open Interval: Also known as == A right half-open interval is also called: a half-open interval on the right a real interval half-open to the right a left half-closed interval a half-closed interval on the left.

title: Definition:Right Half-Open Interval/Technical Note
snippet: == Technical Note on Right Half-Open Interval == {{LatexFor|for = \hointr {a} {b} }} This is a custom command designed to implement Wirth interval notation. The name is derived from half-open interval on the right. Category:Technical Notes

title: Definition:Right Hand Side
snippet: In an equation: $\text {Expression $1$} = \text {Expression $2$}$ the term $\text {Expression $2$}$ is the right hand side.

title: Definition:Right Identity/Also known as
snippet: == Right Identity: Also known as == A right identity is also known as: a right neutral element a right unit (particularly in the context of the ring product of a ring).

title: Definition:Right Inverse
snippet: Mapping Theory: Right Inverse Mapping Abstract Algebra: Right Inverse Element Matrix Theory: Right Inverse Matrix

title: Definition:Right Inverse Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets where $S \ne \O$, that is, $S$ is not empty. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $g: T \to S$ be a mapping such that: $f \circ g = I_T$ where: $f \circ g$ denotes the composite mapping $g$ followed by $f$ $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$. Then $g: T \to S$ is called a right inverse (mapping) of $f$.

title: Definition:Right Module over Group/Also known as
snippet: == Right Module over Group: Also known as == A right module over a group $G$ is also known as a right $G$-module. Category:Definitions/Right Modules over Groups

title: Definition:Right Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. A right module over $R$ is an $R$-algebraic structure $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ with one operation $\ast: G \times R \to G$, the (right) ring action, which satisfies the right module axioms:

title: Definition:Right Naturally Totally Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a positively totally ordered semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ is a right naturally totally ordered semigroup : $\forall a, b \in S: a \prec b \implies \exists x \in S: b = a \circ x$

title: Definition:Right Normal Element of Relation
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $A$. An element $x$ of $A$ is right normal with respect to $\RR$ : $\forall y \in A: \map \RR {y, x}$ holds.

title: Definition:Right Operation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. For any $x, y \in S$, the right operation on $S$ is the binary operation defined as: $\forall x, y \in S: x \to y = y$

title: Definition:Right Order Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\tau$ be the topology on $S$ generated by the basis sets of the form: $S_a = \set {x: a \prec x}$ for $a \in S$. Then the topological space $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq, \tau}$ is known as the right order topology on $S$.

title: Definition:Right Order Topology on Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\tau$ be the subset of the power set $\powerset {\R}$ be defined as: $\tau := \O \cup \set {\openint a \infty: a \in \R} \cup \R$ Then $\tau$ is the right order topology on $\R$. Hence the topological space $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ can be referred to as the right order space on $\R$.

title: Definition:Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. For $n \in \Z_{>0}$, let $O_n$ denote the set defined as: $O_n := \set {x \in \Z_{>0}: x \ge n}$ Let $\tau$ be the subset of the power set $\powerset {\Z_{>0} }$ be defined as: $\tau := \O \cup \set {O_n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Then $\tau$ is the right order topology on $\Z_{>0}$. Hence the topological space $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ can be referred to as the right order space on $\Z_{>0}$.

title: Definition:Right Parabolic Segment/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Right Parabolic Segment == Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Right Prism
snippet: A right prism is a prism whose lateral edges are perpendicular to the bases. That is, whose lateral faces are rectangles.

title: Definition:Right Quasi-Reflexive Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$.

title: Definition:Right Quasi-Reflexive Relation/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. $\RR$ is right quasi-reflexive : $\forall x, y \in S: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \implies \tuple {y, y} \in \RR$

title: Definition:Right Quasi-Reflexive Relation/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. $\RR$ is right quasi-reflexive : $\forall y \in \Img \RR: \tuple {y, y} \in \RR$ where $\Img \RR$ denotes the image set of $\RR$.

title: Definition:Right R-Algebraic Structure/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Right $R$-Algebraic Structures ==

title: Definition:Right R-Algebraic Structure/Examples/1 Operation
snippet: == Example of Right R-Algebraic Structure == A right $R$-algebraic structure with $1$ operation is a right $R$-algebraic structure such that the underlying structure is an algebraic structure with $1$ operation: $\struct {S, \circ, \ast}_R$ Thus it is constructed from: a ring $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ an algebraic structure with $1$ operation: $\struct {S, \circ}$ a right ring action $\ast: S \times R \to S$

title: Definition:Right R-Algebraic Structure/Examples/2 Operations
snippet: == Example of Right R-Algebraic Structure == A right $R$-algebraic structure with $2$ operations is a right $R$-algebraic structure such that the underlying structure is an algebraic structure with $2$ operations: $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ast}_R$ Thus it is constructed from: a ring $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ an algebraic structure with $2$ operations: $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2}$ a right ring action $\ast: S \times R \to S$

title: Definition:Right Regular Representation/Also known as
snippet: == Right Regular Representation: Also known as == For the right regular representation, some sources use a hyphen: right-regular representation. However, this can be confusing: when the term right appears hyphenated in this manner, it usually has the meaning of perpendicular or orthogonal. Some sources refer to the right regular representation as right multiplication.

title: Definition:Right Ring Action Defined by Ring Antirepresentation
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an abelian group. Let $\rho: R \to \map {\operatorname {End} } M$ be a ring antirepresentation. The associated right ring action is the right linear ring action: $M \times R \to M$: $\tuple {m, r} \mapsto \map \rho r \paren m$

title: Definition:Right Shift Operator
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sequence spaces. Let $x := \tuple {x_1, x_2, x_3, \ldots} \in X$. The right shift operator, denoted by $R$, is the mapping $R : X \to Y$ such that: $\map R {x_1, x_2, x_3, \ldots} = \tuple {0, x_1, x_2, \ldots}$

title: Definition:Right Singular Vector of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix of order $m \times n$. Let $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf V$ be a singular value decomposition of $\mathbf A$. The columns of $\mathbf V$ are known as the right singular vectors of $\mathbf A$.

title: Definition:Right Spherical Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle. Let one of the angles of $\triangle ABC$ be a right angle: $\dfrac \pi 2$. 500px Then $\triangle ABC$ is known as a right spherical triangle.

title: Definition:Right Vector Space/Definition 1
snippet: A right vector space is a unitary right module whose scalar ring is a division ring.

title: Definition:Right Vector Space/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a division ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. A right vector space over $R$ is an $R$-algebraic structure $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ with one operation $\ast: G \times R \to G$, which satisfies the right vector space axioms:

title: Definition:Right Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. An element $z_R \in S$ is called a right zero element (or just right zero) : $\forall x \in S: x \circ z_R = z_R$

title: Definition:Right Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. A right zero divisor (in $R$) is an element $x \in R$ such that: $\exists y \in R^*: y \circ x = 0_R$ where $R^*$ is defined as $R \setminus \set {0_R}$.

title: Definition:Rigid Body/Also known as
snippet: == Rigid Body: Also known as == A rigid body is also known as a stiff body. Oh stop sniggering, for goodness sake. Category:Definitions/Rigid Bodies

title: Definition:Rigidity Modulus
snippet: The rigidity modulus of a body or a substance is an elastic modulus used in relation to shear. It is the ratio of shear stress to the resulting shear strain of the body.

title: Definition:Rigidity Modulus/Also known as
snippet: == Rigidity Modulus: Also known as == The rigidity modulus of a body is also known as its modulus of rigidity. Category:Definitions/Rigidity Modulus

title: Definition:Ring
snippet: Abstract Algebra: Ring Boolean Ring Set Theory: Ring of Sets Topology: Topological Ring Geometry: Ring, also known as an annulus

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)
snippet: A ring $\struct {R, *, \circ}$ is a semiring in which $\struct {R, *}$ forms an abelian group. That is, in addition to $\struct {R, *}$ being closed, associative and commutative under $*$, it also has an identity, and each element has an inverse.

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Addition
snippet: The distributand $*$ of a ring $\struct {R, *, \circ}$ is referred to as ring addition. The conventional symbol for this operation is $+$, and thus a general ring is usually denoted $\struct {R, +, \circ}$.

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Also defined as
snippet: == Ring: Also known as == Some sources insist on another criterion which a semiring $\struct {S, *, \circ}$ must satisfy to be classified as a ring: Such sources then use the term rng (pronounced rung): for a ring without an identity. However, defines a ring as any structure fulfilling axioms $\text A 0$ - $\text A 4$, $\text M 0$ - $\text M 1$ and $\text D$, whether or not it has a unity. The more specific structure which does have a unity is termed a ring with unity.

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Also known as
snippet: == Ring: Also known as == Earlier sources, that is, dating to the early $20$th century, refer to a ring as an annulus, but the word ring (at least in this context) is now generally ubiquitous.

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Binding Priority
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. In order to simplify expressions involving both $+$ and $\circ$, it is the convention that ring product has a higher precedence than ring addition: $a \circ b + c := \paren {a \circ b} + c$ Category:Definitions/Ring Theory

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Historical Note
snippet: According to , in his of $2004$, the ring axioms were first formulated by in $1893$. Category:Historical Notes

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Product
snippet: Let $\struct {R, *, \circ}$ be a ring. The distributive operation $\circ$ in $\struct {R, *, \circ}$ is known as the ring product.

title: Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)/Ring Less Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {R, *, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0$. It is convenient to have a symbol for $R \setminus \set 0$, that is, the set of all elements of the ring without the zero. Thus we usually use: $R_{\ne 0} = R \setminus \set 0$

title: Definition:Ring Action/Also known as
snippet: == Ring Action: Also known as == A ring action is also often presented as an $R$-action, where $R$ is chosen to match the symbol used to denote the scalar ring under discussion. Sources which explore the concept of an $R$-algebraic structure in order to provide an abstract underpinning of the foundations of linear algebra often refer to an $R$-action as scalar multiplication.

title: Definition:Ring Action/Left
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n, \ast}_R$ be a left $R$-algebraic structure with $n$ operations. The binary operation $\ast: R \times S \to S$ is known as the left ring action on $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n, \ast}_R$.

title: Definition:Ring Action/Right
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n, \ast}_R$ be a right $R$-algebraic structure with $n$ operations. The binary operation $\ast: S \times R \to S$ is known as the right ring action on $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n, \ast}_R$.

title: Definition:Ring Action Defined by Ring Representation
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an abelian group. Let $\rho : R \to \map {\operatorname {End} } M$ be a ring representation. The associated (left) ring action is the linear ring action: $R \times M \to M$: $\tuple {r, m} \mapsto \map {\map \rho r} m$

title: Definition:Ring Addition/Also known as
snippet: == Ring Addition: Also known as == The operation of ring addition is also known as just addition, if there is no likelihood of ambiguity or misinterpretation.

title: Definition:Ring Antirepresentation
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an abelian group. A ring antirepresentation of $R$ on $M$ is a ring antihomomorphism to the endomorphism ring of $M$.

title: Definition:Ring Automorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\phi: R \to R$ be a (ring) isomorphism. Then $\phi$ is a ring automorphism. That is, a ring automorphism is a (ring) isomorphism from a ring to itself.

title: Definition:Ring Direct Product/Finite Case
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \ldots, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be rings. Let: $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ be the external direct product on two operations, such that: $(1):\quad$ The operation $+$ induced on $R$ by $+_1, \ldots, +_n$ is defined as: $\tuple {s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n} + \tuple {t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n} = \tuple {s_1 +_1 t_1, s_2 +_2 t_2, \ldots, s_n +_n t_n}$ $(2):\quad$ The operation $\circ $ induced on $R$ by $\circ_1, \ldots, \circ_n$ is defined as: $\tuple {s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n} \circ…

title: Definition:Ring Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\phi: R \to R$ be a (ring) homomorphism from $R$ to itself. Then $\phi$ is a ring endomorphism.

title: Definition:Ring Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, \oplus, *}$ be rings. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a (ring) homomorphism. Then $\phi$ is a ring epimorphism $\phi$ is a surjection.

title: Definition:Ring Extension
snippet: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $\phi : R \to S$ be a ring monomorphism. Then $\phi : R \to S$ is a ring extension of $R$. Alternatively, we can define $S$ to be a ring extension of $R$ if $R$ is a subring of $S$ (provided we insist that a subring inherits the multiplicative identity from its parent ring). These definitions are equivalent up to isomorphism, for if $R \subseteq S$ is a subring, then the identity $\operatorname{id} : R \to S$ is a monomorphism. Conversely if $\phi : R \to S$ is a monomorphism, then $\operatorname{im}\phi \subseteq S$ is a subring of $S$.

title: Definition:Ring Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, \oplus, *}$ be rings. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a mapping such that both $+$ and $\circ$ have the morphism property under $\phi$. That is, $\forall a, b \in R$: {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \map \phi {a + b} | r = \map \phi a \oplus \map \phi b }} {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \map \phi {a \circ b} | r = \map \phi a * \map \phi b }} Then $\phi: \struct {R, +, \circ} \to \struct {S, \oplus, *}$ is a ring homomorphism.

title: Definition:Ring Homomorphism/Also defined as
snippet: == Ring Homomorphism: Also defined as == Sources dealing only with rings with unity may define a ring homomorphism as a unital ring homomorphism.

title: Definition:Ring Homomorphism/Also known as
snippet: == Ring Homomorphism: Also known as == A ring homomorphism is also known as a (ring) representation, but that is reserved on for a more specialised definition. Some sources hyphenate: ring-homomorphism.

title: Definition:Ring Less Zero/Also denoted as
snippet: == Ring Less Zero: Also denoted as == Most sources use $R^*$ to denote the set of elements of a ring without the zero. However, this is also used by some sources to mean the group of units of such a ring $R$. Hence prefers the more explicit notation $\R_{\ne 0}$.

title: Definition:Ring Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, \oplus, *}$ be rings. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a (ring) homomorphism. Then $\phi$ is a ring monomorphism $\phi$ is an injection.

title: Definition:Ring Negative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $x \in R$. The inverse of $x$ with respect to the addition operation $+$ in the additive group $\struct {R, +}$ of $R$ is referred to as the (ring) negative of $x$ and is denoted $-x$. That is, the (ring) negative of $x$ is the element $-x$ of $R$ such that: $x + \paren {-x} = 0_R$

title: Definition:Ring Product/Also known as
snippet: == Ring Product: Also known as == The operation of ring product is also known as multiplication. However, on it is preferred that multiplication is kept to the conventional meaning as applied to multiplication of numbers. Hence, in the context of the general ring, the word product is mandatory, except in specific cases (for example, the case of matrix multiplication) where the term multiplication is established.

title: Definition:Ring Representation
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an abelian group. A ring representation of $R$ on $M$ is a ring homomorphism from $R$ to the endomorphism ring $\map {\operatorname {End} } M$.

title: Definition:Ring Representation/Unital
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be an abelian group. A unital ring representation of $R$ on $M$ is a ring representation $R \to \map \End M$ which is unital. That is, it is a unital ring homomorphism from $R$ to the endomorphism ring $\map \End M$.

title: Definition:Ring Representation Defined by Ring Action
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an abelian group. Let $\phi : R \times M \to M$ be a left linear ring action. The associated ring representation is the ring representation $\rho: R \to \map {\operatorname {End} } M$ with: $\map {\map \rho r} m = \map \phi {r, m}$

title: Definition:Ring Theory
snippet: Ring Theory is a branch of abstract algebra which studies rings and other related algebraic structures.

title: Definition:Ring Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. The identity for ring addition is called the ring zero (of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$). It is denoted $0_R$ (or just $0$ if there is no danger of ambiguity).

title: Definition:Ring of Arithmetic Functions
snippet: Let $\AA$ be the set of all arithmetic functions. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution, and $+$ the pointwise sum of functions. The ring of arithmetic functions is the ring $\struct {\AA, +, *}$.

title: Definition:Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. The ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$, denoted $\map {C^*} {S, \R}$, is the set of all bounded continuous mappings in $\map C {S, \R}$ with (pointwise) ring operations $+$ and $*$ restricted to $\map {C^*} {S, R}$.

title: Definition:Ring of Cauchy Sequences
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. Let $\CC$ be the set of Cauchy sequences on $R$. The ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$ is the subring $\struct {\CC, +', \circ'}$ of $R^\N$ with unity. The (pointwise) ring operations on the ring of Cauchy sequences over $R$ are defined as: $\forall \sequence {x_n}, \sequence {y_n} \in R^\N: \sequence {x_n} +' \sequence {y_n} = \sequence {x_n + y_n}$ $\forall \sequence {x_n}, \sequence {y_n} \in R^\N: \sequence {x_n} \circ' \sequence {y_n} =…

title: Definition:Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring. Let $\struct {R^S, +, *}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. The ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$, denoted $\map C {S, R}$, is the set of all continuous mappings in $R^S$ with (pointwise) ring operations $+$ and $*$ restricted to $\map C {S, R}$.

title: Definition:Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau }$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. The ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $\R$, denoted $\map C {S, \R}$, is called the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. The (pointwise) ring operations on the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$ are defined as: $\forall f, g \in \map C {S, \R} : f + g : S \to \R$ is defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f + g}} s = \map f x + \map g s$ $\forall f, g \in \map C {S, \R} : f g : S \to \R$ is defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f g}} s = \map f x \map g s$

title: Definition:Ring of Eisenstein Integers
snippet: The ring of Eisenstein integers $\struct {\Z \sqbrk \omega, +, \times}$ is the algebraic structure formed from: the set of Eisenstein integers $\Z \sqbrk \omega$, where $\omega = e^{2 \pi i / 3}$ the operation of complex addition the operation of complex multiplication.

title: Definition:Ring of Endomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $*: \mathbb G \times \mathbb G \to \mathbb G$ be the operation defined as: $\forall u, v \in \mathbb G: u * v = u \circ v$ where $u \circ v$ is defined as composition of mappings. Then $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is called the ring of endomorphisms of the abelian group $\struct {G, \oplus}$.

title: Definition:Ring of Formal Dirichlet Series
snippet: The ring of formal Dirichlet series is the topological ring $\struct {\AA, \tau}$ where: $\AA$ is the ring of arithmetic functions $\tau$ is the topology on formal dirichlet series Category:Definitions/Dirichlet Series

title: Definition:Ring of Formal Laurent Series
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity.

title: Definition:Ring of Formal Power Series
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity.

title: Definition:Ring of Gaussian Integers
snippet: The ring of Gaussian integers $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ is the algebraic structure formed from: the set of Gaussian integers $\Z \sqbrk i$ the operation of complex addition the operation of complex multiplication.

title: Definition:Ring of Idempotents
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $A$ be the set of all idempotent elements of $R$ under $\circ$: $A = \set {x \in R: x \circ x = x}$ Define a binary operation $\circ$ on $A$ by: $\forall x, y \in A: x \oplus y := x + y - 2 x \circ y$ Denote also with $\circ$ the restriction of $\circ$ to $A$. The algebraic structure $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ is called the ring of idempotents of $R$. It is an idempotent ring, as shown on Ring of Idempotents is Idempotent Ring.

title: Definition:Ring of Integers
snippet: The ring of integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ is the set of integers under the two operations of integer addition and integer multiplication.

title: Definition:Ring of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$. Let $+_m$ and $\times_m$ denote addition modulo $m$ and multiplication modulo $m$ respectively. The algebraic structure $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ is the ring of integers modulo $m$.

title: Definition:Ring of Integers of Number Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a number field. The ring of integers of $K$, usually denoted $\OO_K$ or $\mathfrak o_K$, is the integral closure of $\Z$ in $K$.

title: Definition:Ring of Integers of Number Field/Also defined as
snippet: Some sources define a ring of integers specifically on an algebraic number field. The motivation behind this decision is that some mathematicians are not very interested in the general case. However, this point of view goes against the inclusivist philosophical position endorsed by .

title: Definition:Ring of Linear Operators
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $G$ be an $R$-module. Let $\map {\LL_R} G$ denote the set of all linear operators on $G$. Let $+$ and $\circ$ be the binary operations on $\map {\LL_R} G$ defined such that: $+$ denotes pointwise addition $\circ$ denotes composition of linear operators. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\map {\LL_R} G, +, \circ}$ is a ring is known as the ring of linear operators on $G$.

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $R^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $R$. The ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ is the algebraic structure $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ where $+'$ and $\circ'$ are the (pointwise) operations induced on $R^S$ by $+$ and $\circ$. From Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring, $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring.

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Additive Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. From Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring, $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring. The additive inverse in the ring of mappings is defined by: $\forall f \in R^S : -f \in R^S : \forall s \in S : \map {\paren {-f} } x = -\map f x$

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. From Structure Induced by Commutative Ring Operations is Commutative Ring, the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ is a commutative ring.

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Pointwise Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. The pointwise operation $+'$ induced by $+$ on the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ is called pointwise addition and is defined as: $\forall f, g \in R^S: f +’ g \in R^S$ $\forall s \in S: \map {\paren {f +’ g} } x = \map f x + \map g x$

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Pointwise Multiplication
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. The pointwise operation $\circ'$ induced by $\circ$ on the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ is called pointwise multiplication and is defined as: $\forall f, g \in R^S: f \circ’ g \in R^S$ $\forall s \in S: \map {\paren {f \circ’ g} } x = \map f x \circ \map g x$

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. Let $f : S \to U_R$ is a mapping into the set of units $U_R$ of $R$. From Unit of Ring of Mappings iff Image is Subset of Ring Units: $f$ is a unit in the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ and: the inverse of $f$ is the mapping defined by: $f^{-1} \in R^S : \forall x \in S: \map {\paren {f^{-1} } } x = \map f x^{-1}$

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. From Structure Induced by Ring with Unity Operations is Ring with Unity, the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$ is a ring with unity whose unity is the constant mapping $f_1: S \to R$ defined as: $\quad \forall s \in S : \map {f_1} x = 1$

title: Definition:Ring of Mappings/Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. From Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring, $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring. The zero of the ring of mappings is the constant mapping $f_0 : S \to R$ defined by: $\quad \forall s \in S : \map {f_0} x = 0$ where $0$ is the zero in $R$

title: Definition:Ring of Polynomial Forms
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $I$ be a set Let $\family {X_i: i \in I}$ be an indexed set. Let $A = R \sqbrk {\family {X_i: i \in I} }$ be the set of all polynomial forms over $R$ in $\family {X_i: i \in I}$. Let $+$ and $\circ$ denote the standard addition and multiplication of polynomial forms. The ring of polynomial forms is the ordered triple $\struct {A, +, \circ}$.

title: Definition:Ring of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $R \sqbrk {\set {X_j: j \in J} }$ be the ring of polynomial forms over $R$ in the indeterminates $\set {X_j: j \in J}$. Let $R^J$ be the free module on $J$. Let $A$ be the set of all polynomial functions $R^J \to R$. Then the operations $+$ and $\circ$ on $R$ induce pointwise operations on $A$.

title: Definition:Ring of Polynomials in Ring Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $x \in R$. The subring of $R$ consisting of all the polynomials in $x$ over $D$ is called the ring of polynomials over $D$ and is denoted $D \sqbrk x$.

title: Definition:Ring of Quaternions
snippet: The ring of quaternions $\struct {\H, +, \times}$ is the set of quaternions under the two operations of quaternion addition and quaternion multiplication.

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Given the natural numbers $\N$, the ring of sequences over $R$ is the ring of mappings $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ where: $(1): \quad R^\N$ is the set of sequences in $R$ $(2): \quad +'$ and $\circ'$ are the (pointwise) operations induced by $+$ and $\circ$. From Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring, $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ is a ring.

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Additive Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. From Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring, $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ is a ring. The additive inverse in the ring of sequences is defined by: $\forall \sequence {x_n} \in R^\N: -\sequence {x_n} = \sequence {-x_n}$

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. From Structure Induced by Commutative Ring Operations is Commutative Ring, the ring of sequences over $R$ is a commutative ring.

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Pointwise Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. The pointwise operation $+'$ induced by $+$ on the ring of sequences is called pointwise addition and is defined as: $\forall \sequence {x_n}, \sequence {y_n} \in R^\N: \sequence {x_n} +' \sequence {y_n} = \sequence {x_n + y_n}$

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Pointwise Multiplication
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. The pointwise operation $\circ'$ induced by $\circ$ on the ring of sequences is called pointwise multiplication and is defined as: $\forall \sequence {x_n}, \sequence {y_n} \in R^{\N}: \sequence {x_n} \circ' \sequence {y_n} = \sequence {x_n \circ y_n}$

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1$. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence over the set of units $U_R$ of $R$. From Unit of Ring of Mappings iff Image is Subset of Ring Units: $\sequence {x_n}$ is a unit in the ring of sequences over $R$ and: the inverse of $\sequence {x_n}$ is the sequence defined by: $\sequence {x_n}^{-1} \in R^\N : \sequence {x_n}^{-1} = \sequence {x_n^{-1}}$

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1$. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. From Structure Induced by Ring with Unity Operations is Ring with Unity, the ring of sequences is a ring with unity; namely the constant sequence $\tuple {1, 1, 1, \dots}$, where $1$ is the unity in $R$.

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences/Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R^\N, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of sequences over $R$. The zero of the ring of sequences is the constant sequence $\tuple {0, 0, 0, \dots}$, where $0$ is the zero of $R$.

title: Definition:Ring of Sequences of Finite Support
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $P \sqbrk R$ be the set of all sequences in $R$ whose domain is $\N$: $P \sqbrk R = \set {\sequence {r_0, r_1, r_2, \ldots} }$ and whose support is finite. Let the operations $\oplus$ and $\odot$ on $P \sqbrk R$ be defined as follows: The ring of sequences of finite support over $R$ is the ring $\struct {P \sqbrk R, \oplus, \odot}$.
