snippet: Consider the functional $J \sqbrk {\mathbf y}$, such that: $\ds J \sqbrk {\mathbf y} = \int_a^b \map F {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf y'} \rd x$ Let the momenta of $J$ be: $\mathbf p = \nabla_{\mathbf y'} \map F {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf y'}$ Let the following boundary conditions hold: $\map {\mathbf y'} a = \bigvalueat {\map {\boldsymbol \psi} {\mathbf y} } {x \mathop = a}$ If: $\exists \map g {x, \mathbf y}: \bigvalueat {\map {\mathbf p} {x, \mathbf y, \map {\boldsymbol \psi} {\mathbf y} } } {x \mathop = a} = \bigvalueat {\nabla_{\mathbf y'} \map g {x, \mathbf y} } {x \mathop = a}$ then the boundary…

title: Definition:Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a densely defined linear operator on $\HH$ Let $\struct {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast}$ be the adjoint of $\struct {\map D T, T}$. We say that $\struct {\map D T, T}$ is self-adjoint : $\struct {\map D {T^\ast}, T^\ast} = \struct {\map D T, T}$

title: Definition:Self-Adjoint Subset of *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$ such that: for each $a \in S$ we have $a^\ast \in S$. We say that $S$ is a self-adjoint subset of $A$.

title: Definition:Self-Conjugate Triangle
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $\triangle PQR$ be a triangle such that: $PR$ is the polar of $Q$ $QR$ is the polar of $P$ with respect to $\CC$. Then $\triangle PQR$ is said to be a self-conjugate triangle with respect to $\CC$.

title: Definition:Self-Distributive Operation
snippet: Let $\circ$ be a binary operation on the set $S$. $\circ$ is self-distributive : $(1): \quad \circ$ is left self-distributive and: $(2): \quad \circ$ is right self-distributive.

title: Definition:Self-Distributive Operation/Left
snippet: Let $\circ$ be a binary operation on the set $S$. $\circ$ is left self-distributive : $\forall a, b, c \in S: a \circ \paren {b \circ c} = \paren {a \circ b} \circ \paren {a \circ c}$

title: Definition:Self-Distributive Operation/Right
snippet: Let $\circ$ be a binary operation on the set $S$. $\circ$ is right self-distributive : $\forall a, b, c \in S: \paren {a \circ b} \circ c = \paren {a \circ c} \circ \paren {b \circ c}$

title: Definition:Self-Distributive Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure such that $\circ$ is a self-distributive operation. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is known as a self-distributive structure.

title: Definition:Self-Dual
snippet: Definition:Self-Dual (Order Theory)

title: Definition:Self-Dual (Order Theory)
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. If $S$ is dual to $S$, then $S$ is self-dual.

title: Definition:Self-Dual 2-Form
snippet: Let $M$ be a $4$-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $\omega$ be a $2$-form on $M$. Let $*$ be the Hodge star operator. Suppose: $* \omega = \omega$ Then $\omega$ is known as the self-dual $2$-form.

title: Definition:Self-Inverse Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e_S$. Let $x \in S$ be an element of $S$.

title: Definition:Self-Inverse Element/Also known as
snippet: The definition of a self-inverse element is usually made in the context of a group. Some sources refer to such an element as an involution. Category:Definitions/Self-Inverse Elements

title: Definition:Self-Inverse Element/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e_S$. Let $x \in S$ be an element of $S$. $x$ is a self-inverse element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ $x \circ x = e_S$.

title: Definition:Self-Inverse Element/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e$. Let $x \in S$ be an element of $S$. $x$ is a self-inverse element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ : $x$ is invertible and: $x = x^{-1}$, where $x^{-1}$ is the inverse of $x$.

title: Definition:Self-Locating Number in Pi
snippet: A natural number $n$ is self-locating in $\pi$ if it can be found starting at the $n$th decimal place in the decimal expansion of $\pi$.

title: Definition:Self-Map
snippet: A self-map is a mapping whose domain is equal to its codomain: $\Dom f = \Cdm f$

title: Definition:Self-Map/Also known as
snippet: == Self-Map: Also known as == Some sources refer to a self-map as a transformation.

title: Definition:Self-Normalizing Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is a self-normalizing subgroup : $\map {N_G} H = H$ where $\map {N_G} H$ is the normalizer of $H$ in $G$.

title: Definition:Self-Orthogonal Trajectories
snippet: Let $\map f {x, y, c}$ define a one-parameter family of curves $F$. Let the family of orthogonal trajectories of $F$ be $F$ itself. Then $\map f {x, y, c}$ is self-orthogonal.

title: Definition:Self-Similarity
snippet: Let $S$ be a geometric object. $S$ has the property of self-similarity : every point of $S$ is contained in a copy of $S$ at a smaller scale.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence
snippet: Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for a formal language $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be a collection of WFFs of $\LL$. Let $\map {\mathscr M} \FF$ be the formal semantics obtained from $\mathscr M$ by retaining only the structures of $\mathscr M$ that are models of $\FF$. Let $\phi$ be a tautology for $\map {\mathscr M} \FF$.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Also known as
snippet: == Semantic Consequence: Also known as == For semantic consequence, one also says that $\FF$ semantically entails $\phi$, in particular if $\FF$ comprises just one WFF. The term formal consequence is also sometimes encountered. Another common term used is logical consequence, but this is mainly used more generally in the context of logical implication. Correspondingly, the term logical entailment can also be found. However, the adjective "logical" is heavily used and prone to ambiguity, so these terms should not be used on .

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a collection of WFFs of propositional logic. Then a WFF $\mathbf A$ is a semantic consequence of $\FF$ : $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \FF$ implies $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf A$ where $\models_{\mathrm{BI}}$ is the models relation.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Boolean Interpretations/Single Formula
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Boolean Interpretations/Single Formula/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ is a semantic consequence of $\mathbf B$ : $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf B$ implies $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf A$ for all boolean interpretations $v$. Here, $\models_{\mathrm{BI}}$ is the models relation.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Boolean Interpretations/Single Formula/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ is a semantic consequence of $\mathbf B$ : $\mathbf A \implies \mathbf B$ is a tautology where $\implies$ is the conditional connective.

title: Definition:Semantic Consequence/Predicate Logic
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a collection of WFFs of predicate logic. Then a WFF $\mathbf A$ is a semantic consequence of $\FF$ : $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \FF$ implies $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \mathbf A$ for all structures $\AA$, where $\models_{\mathrm{PL} }$ is the models relation.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence
snippet: Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for a formal language $\LL$. Let $\phi, \psi$ be $\LL$-WFFs. Then $\phi$ and $\psi$ are $\mathscr M$-semantically equivalent : $\phi \models_{\mathscr M} \psi$ and $\psi \models_{\mathscr M} \phi$ that is, they are $\mathscr M$-semantic consequences of one another. Equivalently, $\phi$ and $\psi$ are $\mathscr M$-semantically equivalent , for each $\mathscr M$-structure $\MM$: $\MM \models_{\mathscr M} \phi$ $\MM \models_{\mathscr M} \psi$

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Boolean Interpretations/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent for boolean interpretations : $\mathbf A \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf B$ and $\mathbf B \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf A$ that is, each is a semantic consequence of the other. That is to say, $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent : $\map v {\mathbf A} = T$ $\map v {\mathbf B} = T$ for all boolean interpretations $v$.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Boolean Interpretations/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent for boolean interpretations : $\map v {\mathbf A} = \map v {\mathbf B}$ for all boolean interpretations $v$.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Boolean Interpretations/Definition 3
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent for boolean interpretations : $\mathbf A \iff \mathbf B$ is a tautology where $\iff$ is the biconditional connective.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Predicate Logic
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of predicate logic.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Predicate Logic/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of predicate logic. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent : $\mathbf A \models_{\mathrm{PL_A}} \mathbf B$ and $\mathbf B \models_{\mathrm{PL_A}} \mathbf A$ that is, each is a semantic consequence of the other. That is to say, $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent , for all structures $\AA$ and assignments $\sigma$: $\AA, \sigma \models_{\mathrm{PL_A}} \mathbf A$ $\AA, \sigma \models_{\mathrm{PL_A}} \mathbf B$ where $\models_{\mathrm{PL_A}}$ denotes the models relation.

title: Definition:Semantic Equivalence/Predicate Logic/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be WFFs of predicate logic. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are (semantically) equivalent : $\mathbf A \iff \mathbf B$ is a tautology where $\iff$ is the biconditional connective.

title: Definition:Semantic Tableau
snippet: Semantic tableaus are the labeled trees which can be obtained in the course of executing the Semantic Tableau Algorithm.

title: Definition:Semantic Tableau/Closed
snippet: Let $T$ be a semantic tableau. Then $T$ is closed all of its leaves are marked closed.

title: Definition:Semantic Tableau/Completed
snippet: Let $T$ be a semantic tableau. Then $T$ is completed all of its leaves are marked.

title: Definition:Semantic Tableau/Open
snippet: Let $T$ be a semantic tableau. Then $T$ is open all of its leaves are marked open.

title: Definition:Semantics
snippet: The semantics of a language (either natural or formal) is its meaning in a linguistic sense. Hence in the context of logic, semantics is the study of the relationships between the expressions of a formal language and a logical domain. Semantics, therefore, includes the study of interpretations.

title: Definition:Semantics of Conjunction/Warning
snippet: == Semantics of Conjunction: Warning == Beware of the usage of and in natural language which has the following form: He fell out of bed and broke his leg which does not mean the same as: He broke his leg and fell out of bed. This use of and actually means and then, as it is implicit that the two occurrences are neither simultaneous nor independent, but that the second occurrence happens as a result of the first.

title: Definition:Semi-/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Semi- == The prefix semi- can be found in the following contexts: semicircle: one of the halves of a circle which has been bisected through its diameter by a straight line semiprime number: an integer which is the product of two (not necessarily distinct) primes Category:Definitions/Number Prefixes

title: Definition:Semi-/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Semi- == The prefix semi- derives from the Latin semi-, meaning half. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Semi-Decidable/Predicate
snippet: In the context of computability theory, a predicate is semi-decidable there exists an algorithm which, in every possible case:

title: Definition:Semi-Eulerian Graph
snippet: A graph is called semi-Eulerian it contains an Eulerian trail. Note that the definition of graph here includes: Simple graph Loop-graph Multigraph Loop-multigraph. Note that an Eulerian graph is also semi-Eulerian, as an Eulerian circuit is still a path, and therefore an Eulerian trail.

title: Definition:Semi-Eulerian Graph/Also known as
snippet: == Semi-Eulerian Graph: Also known as == A semi-Eulerian graph is also called a traversable graph. Some sources have transversable graph but it is suspected that this is a mistake.

title: Definition:Semi-Great Circle
snippet: Let $S$ be a sphere. A semi-great circle on $S$ is a semicircle consisting of half of a great circle on $S$.

title: Definition:Semi-Hamiltonian Graph
snippet: A semi-Hamiltonian graph is a graph that contains a Hamiltonian path, but not a Hamilton cycle.

title: Definition:Semi-Inner Product/Complex Field
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a complex subfield $\GF$. A (complex) semi-inner product is a mapping $\innerprod \cdot \cdot: V \times V \to \GF$ that satisfies the (complex) semi-inner product axioms:

title: Definition:Semi-Inner Product/Real Field
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a real subfield $\GF$. A (real) semi-inner product is a mapping $\innerprod \cdot \cdot: V \times V \to \GF$ that satisfies the real semi-inner product axioms:

title: Definition:Semi-Inner Product Space
snippet: A semi-inner product space is a vector space together with an associated semi-inner product.

title: Definition:Semi-Inner Product Space/Complex Field
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a complex subfield $\GF$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot : V \times V \to \GF$ be an complex semi-inner product on $V$. We say that $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ is a (complex) semi-inner product space. That is, a (complex) semi-inner product space is a vector space over a complex subfield together with an associated complex semi-inner product.

title: Definition:Semi-Inner Product Space/Real Field
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a real subfield $\GF$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot : V \times V \to \GF$ be an real semi-inner product on $V$. We say that $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ is a (real) semi-inner product space. That is, a (real) semi-inner product space is a vector space over a real subfield together with an associated real semi-inner product.

title: Definition:Semi-Interquartile Range
snippet: The semi-interquartile range is a measure of dispersion in statistics. Let $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ be first quartile and third quartile respectively. The semi-interquartile range is defined as: $\dfrac {Q_3 - Q_1} 2$ That is, half the interquartile range.

title: Definition:Semi-Interquartile Range/Also known as
snippet: == Semi-Interquartile Range: Also known as == A semi-interquartile range is also known as a quartile deviation.

title: Definition:Semi-Local Ring
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Then $A$ is semi-local $A$ has a finite number of maximal ideals.

title: Definition:Semi-Magic Square
snippet: A semi-magic square is an arrangement of $n^2$ numbers into an $n \times n$ square array such that: the sum of the elements of each row the sum of the elements in each column are the same. Hence a semi-magic square is like a magic square, but without the property that the sum of the elements along each diagonal are the same as those of the rows and columns.

title: Definition:Semi-Magic Square/Also known as
snippet: == Semi-Magic Square: Also known as == A semi-magic square is also seen unhyphenated: semimagic square. Some sources refer to a semi-magic square as a magic square, and a true magic square as a diagonally magic square. So let's be careful out there.

title: Definition:Semiaxis
snippet: A semiaxis is a line segment consisting of one of the two halves of an axis of a conic section.

title: Definition:Semiaxis/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Semiaxis == The plural of semiaxis is semiaxes. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Semicircle/Also known as
snippet: == Semicircle: Also known as == A semicircle is also seen referred to as a hemicycle, but this is uncommon.

title: Definition:Semiconjugate Axis of Hyperbola
snippet: A semiconjugate axis of a hyperbola is one of the halves of the conjugate axis from the center to one of the covertices.

title: Definition:Semicubical Parabola
snippet: The semicubical parabola is the plane curve whose locus can be described with the equation: $y^2 = a^2 x^3$ 500px

title: Definition:Semicubical Parabola/Also known as
snippet: == Semicubical Parabola: Also known as == The semicubical parabola is also known as: Neile's parabola, after the cuspidal cubic.

title: Definition:Semicubical Parabola/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Semicubical Parabola == The semicubical parabola was discovered and rectified by , who published his findings in $1657$. In $1659$, published the method he had used, giving full credit. It was the first curve to be rectified, apart from conic sections and some of the spirals.

title: Definition:Semidirect Product/Inner
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $H$ and $N$ be complementary. Then $G$ is the inner semidirect product of $N$ and $H$. This is denoted $G = N \rtimes H$ or $G = H \ltimes N$.

title: Definition:Semidirect Product/Outer
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \ast}$ and $\struct {H, \cdot}$ be groups. Let $\Aut G$ denote the automorphism group of $G$. Let $\phi: H \to \Aut G$ be a group homomorphism, that is, let $H$ act on $G$. The outer semidirect product of $G$ and $H$ with respect to $\phi$ is the group $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ where: $G \times H$ is the cartesian product of $G$ with $H$ $\circ$ is the group operation defined as: $\tuple {g_1, h_1} \circ \tuple {g_2, h_2} = \tuple {g_1 \ast \map {\phi_{h_1} } {g_2}, h_1 \cdot h_2}$ where $\map {\phi_{h_1} } {g_2}$ is the action of $h_1$ on $g_2$ under $\phi$.

title: Definition:Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a semigroup $\circ$ is associative on $S$. That is: A semigroup is an algebraic structure which is closed and whose operation is associative.

title: Definition:Semigroup/Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup whose operation is addition. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an additive semigroup. It is implicit in this definition that the elements of $S$ are numbers, or objects derived from numbers upon which the concept of addition is applicable.

title: Definition:Semigroup/Also defined as
snippet: == Semigroup: Also defined as == Some sources specify that a semigroup must be non-empty, thus denying the possibility of $S = \O$ for such a structure.

title: Definition:Semigroup/Also known as
snippet: == Semigroup: Also known as == Some older texts hyphenate semigroup as semi-group. A semigroup is also known as an associative algebraic structure. Some sources call this a monoid, but this term usually (and on ) has a different meaning. Make sure you understand which is being used.

title: Definition:Semigroup/Multiplicative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup whose operation is multiplication. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a multiplicative semigroup. It is implicit in this definition that the elements of $S$ are numbers, or objects derived from numbers upon which the concept of multiplication is applicable.

title: Definition:Semigroup Automorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\phi: S \to S$ be a (semigroup) isomorphism from $S$ to itself. Then $\phi$ is a semigroup automorphism.

title: Definition:Semigroup Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroups. Let $\phi: S \to S$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism from $S$ to itself. Then $\phi$ is a semigroup endomorphism.

title: Definition:Semigroup Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism. Then $\phi$ is a semigroup epimorphism $\phi$ is a surjection.

title: Definition:Semigroup Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping such that $\circ$ has the morphism property under $\phi$. That is, $\forall a, b \in S$: $\map \phi {a \circ b} = \map \phi a * \map \phi b$ Then $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ is a semigroup homomorphism.

title: Definition:Semigroup Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism. Then $\phi$ is a semigroup monomorphism $\phi$ is an injection.

title: Definition:Semigroup of Bounded Linear Operators
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a $\hointr 0 \infty$-indexed family of bounded linear transformations $\map T t : X \to X$. We say that $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ is a semigroup of bounded linear operators : $(1): \quad$ $\map T 0 = I$ $(2): \quad$ for $t, s \ge 0$ we have $\map T {t + s} = \map T t \map T s$

title: Definition:Semigroup with respect to Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $C$ be a class. Let $\thickapprox$ be an equivalence relation on $C$. Let $\struct {C, \cdot}$ be a large magma. Then $\struct {C, \cdot}$ is a semigroup with respect to $\thickapprox$ : $\forall x, y,z \in C: \paren {x \cdot y} \cdot z \thickapprox x \cdot \paren {y \cdot z}$

title: Definition:Semihereditary Ring
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. We say that $A$ is semihereditary if for every module $M$ over $A$, if $M$ is projective, then so is each finitely generated submodule of $M$.

title: Definition:Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is called a semilattice $\circ$ is a commutative and idempotent operation. Thus an algebraic structure is a semilattice it satisfies the semilattice axioms:

title: Definition:Semilattice/Also known as
snippet: == Semilattice: Also known as == Some sources hyphenate the word semilattice as semi-lattice.

title: Definition:Semilattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semilattices. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping such that $\circ$ has the morphism property under $\phi$. That is, $\forall a, b \in S$: $\map \phi {a \circ b} = \map \phi a * \map \phi b$ Then $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ is a semilattice homomorphism.

title: Definition:Semilogarithmic Graph Paper
snippet: Semilogarithmic graph paper is graph paper in which one, but not both, coordinate axes are marked with a logarithmic scale.

title: Definition:Semilogarithmic Graph Paper/Also known as
snippet: == Semilogarithmic Graph Paper: Also known as == Semilogarithmic graph paper is also known as logarithmic graph paper. Hence note that what on is defined as logarithmic graph paper would then be referred to as log-log graph paper. Category:Definitions/Semilogarithmic Graph Paper

title: Definition:Semimajor Axis of Ellipse/Also known as
snippet: == Semimajor Axis of Ellipse: Also known as == Some sources hyphenate: semi-major axis. Category:Definitions/Semimajor Axis of Ellipse

title: Definition:Semimajor Axis of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. A semimajor axis of $\EE$ is one of the two halves of the major axis of $\EE$ divided by its midpoint.

title: Definition:Semimean Axis of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. A semimean axis of $\EE$ is one of the two halves of the minor axis of $\EE$ divided by its midpoint.

title: Definition:Semiminor Axis of Ellipse/Also known as
snippet: == Semiminor Axis of Ellipse: Also known as == Some sources hyphenate: semi-minor axis. Category:Definitions/Semiminor Axis of Ellipse

title: Definition:Semiminor Axis of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. A semiminor axis of $\EE$ is one of the two halves of the minor axis of $\EE$ divided by its midpoint.

title: Definition:Seminorm (Scalar Product Space)
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a scalar product space. Let $v \in V$ be a vector. Then the seminorm of $v$ is defined as: $\norm v :=\sqrt {\innerprod v v}$

title: Definition:Seminorm on Vector Space induced by Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $Y$. Define: $\map q x = \map p {T x}$ for each $x \in X$. We say that $q$ is the seminorm on $X$ induced by $T$.

title: Definition:Semiperfect Number
snippet: A semiperfect number is a positive integer which is equal to the sum of some or all of its aliquot parts.

It is possible this is a mistake in , as the author of this page has not been able to corroborate this definition with any sources elsewhere.

title: Definition:Semiprime Number
snippet: A semiprime (number) is an integer which is the product of two (not necessarily distinct) primes.

title: Definition:Semiregular Polyhedron
snippet: A semiregular polyhedron is a polyhedron with the following properties: $(1): \quad$ Each of its faces is a regular polygon $(2): \quad$ It is isogonal $(3): \quad$ The faces are not all congruent.

title: Definition:Semiregular Polyhedron/Also known as
snippet: == Semiregular Polyhedron: Also known as == Many sources present semiregular polyhedron as semi-regular, but prefers the simplicity of the unhyphenated version of this term.

title: Definition:Semiregular Tessellation
snippet: A semiregular tessellation $T$ is a tessellation which uses regular polygons of more than one kind, arranged so that every vertex of $T$ is congruent to every other vertex of $T$.

title: Definition:Semiring (Abstract Algebra)/Also defined as
snippet: == Semiring in context of Abstract Algebra: Also defined as == There are various other conventions on what constitutes a semiring. Some of these have a distinguished, different name on , for example: An additive semiring is a semiring whose distributand is commutative. A rig is a semiring whose distributand forms a commutative monoid. Still, some sources impose further that there be a identity element for the distributor, that is, that $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Such a structure could be referred to as a rig with unity, consistent with the definition of ring with unity.

title: Definition:Semiring of Natural Numbers
snippet: The semiring of natural numbers is the semiring $\struct {\N, +, \times}$ where: $\N$ is the set of natural numbers $+$ is the addition $\times$ is the multiplication.

title: Definition:Semitransverse Axis of Hyperbola
snippet: A semitransverse axis of a hyperbola is one of the halves of the transverse axis from the center to one of the vertices.

title: Definition:Senary Notation
snippet: Senary notation is the positional number system whose base is $6$. That is, every number $x \in \R$ is expressed in the form: $\ds x = \sum_{j \mathop \in \Z} r_j 6^j$ where: $\forall j \in \Z: r_j \in \set {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}$ Category:Definitions/Positional Number Systems

title: Definition:Sensitive Dependence on Initial Conditions
snippet: Let a dynamical system be such that the orbits of adjacent points evolve in ways which are markedly different. Such a dynamical system exhibits sensitive dependence on initial conditions.

title: Definition:Sensitive Dependence on Initial Conditions/Also known as
snippet: == Sensitive Dependence on Initial Conditions: Also known as == The phenomenon of sensitive dependence on initial conditions is also known as the butterfly effect.

title: Definition:Separable
snippet: Topology: Separable space Completely separable space or perfectly separable space, otherwise known as a second-countable space Field Theory: Separable element Separable extension Separable polynomial Differential Equations: Separable differential equation

title: Definition:Separable Closure
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. A separable closure of $K$ is a separably closed algebraic field extension of $F$. It may be defined as the relative separable closure of $F$ in its algebraic closure.

title: Definition:Separable Degree
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a field extension.

title: Definition:Separable Degree/Definition 1
snippet: Let $S \subseteq E$ be the separable closure of $F$ in $E$. The separable degree $\index E F_{\operatorname {sep} }$ of $E / F$ is the degree $\index S F$.

title: Definition:Separable Degree/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\bar F$ be the algebraic closure of $F$. The separable degree $\index E F_{\operatorname {sep} }$ of $E / F$ is the number of embeddings of $E$ into $\bar F$ that fix $F$.

title: Definition:Separable Degree/Definition 3
snippet: Let $K$ be a normal extension of $F$ that contains $E$. The separable degree $\index E F_{\operatorname {sep} }$ of $E / F$ is the number of embeddings of $E$ into $K$ that fix $F$.

title: Definition:Separable Differential Equation
snippet: A first order ordinary differential equation which can be expressed in the form: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map g x \map h y$ is known as a separable differential equation. Its general solution is found by solving the integration: $\ds \int \frac {\d y} {\map h y} = \int \map g x \rd x + C$

title: Definition:Separable Differential Equation/Also known as
snippet: == Separable Differential Equation: Also known as == A separable differential equation is also known as a differential equation with separable variables. Some sources refer to it as a variables separable differential equation.

title: Definition:Separable Differential Equation/Also presented as
snippet: == Separable Differential Equation: Also presented as == Some sources present this as an equation in the form: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \dfrac {\map g x} {\map h y}$ or: $\map h y \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map g x$ whose general solution is found by solving the integration: $\ds \int \map h y \rd y = \int \map g x \rd x + C$ Other sources have: $\map g x + \map h y \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0$ whose general solution is found by solving the integration: $\ds \int \map g x \rd x = -\int \map h y \rd y + C$

title: Definition:Separable Differential Equation/General Form
snippet: A first order ordinary differential equation which can be expressed in the form: $\map {g_1} x \map {h_1} y + \map {g_2} x \map {h_2} y \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0$ is known as a separable differential equation. Its general solution is found by solving the integration: $\ds \int \frac {\map {g_1} x} {\map {g_2} x} \rd x + \int \frac {\map {h_2} y} {\map {h_1} y} \rd y = C$

title: Definition:Separable Element
snippet: Let $L/K$ be a field extension. Let $\alpha\in L$. Then $\alpha$ is separable over $K$ its minimal polynomial over $K$ is separable.

title: Definition:Separable Extension
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $L/K$ be an algebraic field extension. Then $L/K$ is a separable extension every $\alpha\in L$ is separable over $K$. That is: For every $\alpha \in L$, its minimal polynomial over $K$ is separable.

title: Definition:Separable Polynomial
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $\map P X \in K \sqbrk X$ be a polynomial of degree $n$.

title: Definition:Separable Polynomial/Definition 1
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $\map P X \in K \sqbrk X$ be a polynomial of degree $n$. $P$ is separable its roots are distinct in an algebraic closure of $K$. Category:Definitions/Separable Polynomials

title: Definition:Separable Polynomial/Definition 2
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $\map P X \in K \sqbrk X$ be a polynomial of degree $n$. $P$ is separable it has no double roots in every field extension of $K$. Category:Definitions/Separable Polynomials

title: Definition:Separable Polynomial/Definition 3
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $\map P X \in K \sqbrk X$ be a polynomial of degree $n$. $P$ is separable it has $n$ distinct roots in every field extension where $P$ splits. Category:Definitions/Separable Polynomials

title: Definition:Separable Space
snippet: A topological space $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ is separable there exists a countable subset of $S$ which is everywhere dense in $T$.

title: Definition:Separable Space/Also known as
snippet: == Separable Space: Also known as == A separable space is also known as a density $\le \aleph_0$ space.

title: Definition:Separable Space/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Separable Space == The thinking behind applying the word separable to the concept of a separable space arises from the idea of denseness in the context of the real number line. For example, a subset $S \subseteq \R$ is dense any two distinct real numbers $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$ can be separated by an element of $S$ in the sense that there exists $s \in S$ such that $a < s < b$. The term seems to have been coined by in $1906$.

title: Definition:Separable Space/Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a subset of $X$. Let $Y$ be countable set and (everywhere) dense in $X$. In other words, suppose $Y = \set {y_i : i \in \N}$ such that: $\forall x \in X : \forall \epsilon \in \R_{> 0} : \exists y_{n \mathop \in \N} \in Y : \norm {y_n - x} < \epsilon$ Then $X$ is separable.

title: Definition:Separably Closed Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Then $K$ is separably closed

title: Definition:Separably Injective Banach Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. We say that $Y$ is separably injective : for each separable Banach space $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ with closed linear subspace $E$ and bounded linear transformation $T : E \to Y$: there exists a bounded linear transformation $\widetilde T : X \to Y$ extending $T$.

title: Definition:Separated Morphism of Schemes
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \OO_Y}$ be schemes. Let $f : \struct {X, \OO_X} \to \struct {Y, \OO_Y}$ be a morphism of schemes. $f$ is separated $f$ the diagonal morphism $\Delta_f : X \times_Y X \to Y$ is a closed immersion.
