title: Definition:Unbounded Closed Real Interval/Also known as
snippet: == Unbounded Closed Real Interval: Also known as == Some sources refer to the unbounded closed real intervals as half-open infinite (real) intervals. Some sources use the term semi-infinite (closed) intervals.

title: Definition:Unbounded Divergent Sequence/Complex Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}$ be a sequence in $\C$. Then $\sequence {z_n}$ tends to $\infty$ or diverges to $\infty$ : $\forall H > 0: \exists N: \forall n > N: \cmod {z_n} > H$ where $\cmod {z_n}$ denotes the modulus of $z_n$. We write: $x_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Definition:Unbounded Divergent Sequence/Real Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$.

title: Definition:Unbounded Divergent Sequence/Real Sequence/Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. $\sequence {x_n}$ diverges to $\infty$ : $\forall H > 0: \exists N: \forall n > N: \size {x_n} > H$

title: Definition:Unbounded Divergent Sequence/Real Sequence/Negative Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. $\sequence {x_n}$ diverges to $-\infty$ : $\forall H \in \R_{>0}: \exists N: \forall n > N: x_n < -H$ That is, whatever positive real number $H$ you choose, for sufficiently large $n$, $x_n$ will be less than $-H$. We write: $x_n \to -\infty$ as $n \to \infty$ or: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n \to -\infty$

title: Definition:Unbounded Divergent Sequence/Real Sequence/Positive Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. $\sequence {x_n}$ diverges to $+\infty$ : $\forall H \in \R_{>0}: \exists N: \forall n > N: x_n > H$ That is, whatever positive real number $H$ you choose, for sufficiently large $n$, $x_n$ will exceed $H$. We write: $x_n \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$ or: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n \to +\infty$

title: Definition:Unbounded Mapping/Also known as
snippet: == Unbounded Mapping: Also known as == An unbounded mapping is also known as an unbounded function.

title: Definition:Unbounded Open Real Interval/Also known as
snippet: == Unbounded Open Real Interval: Also known as == Some sources refer to the unbounded open real intervals as open infinite (real) intervals. Some sources use the term semi-infinite intervals.

title: Definition:Unbounded Real-Valued Function/Definition 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to \R$ be a real-valued function. $f$ is unbounded it is either unbounded above or unbounded below.

title: Definition:Unbounded Real-Valued Function/Definition 2
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to \R$ be a real-valued function. $f$ is unbounded : for every positive real number $M$ there exists $x_M \in \R$ such that: $\size {\map f {x_M} } > M$

title: Definition:Unbounded Real Interval/Also known as
snippet: == Unbounded Real Interval: Also known as == Some sources refer to an unbounded real Interval as an infinite (real) interval.

title: Definition:Uncertainty
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable. Let $X$ take a finite number of values with probabilities $p_1, p_2, \dotsc, p_n$. The uncertainty of $X$ is defined as: $\map H X = \ds -\sum_k p_k \lg p_k$ where: $\lg$ denotes logarithm base $2$ the summation is over those $k$ where $p_k > 0$.

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Also defined as
snippet: == Uncertainty: Also defined as == In their definition of uncertainty, some sources do not specify the condition that the summation is over those $k$ where $p_k > 0$, but instead define, or implicitly assume, $0 \lg 0 = 0$. This is justified, as: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0^+} x \lg x = 0$ from .

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Also known as
snippet: == Uncertainty: Also known as == The uncertainty of a random variable is also known as its entropy. Some sources refer to it as Shannon entropy, for .

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Incomplete Knowledge
snippet: Uncertainty caused by incomplete knowledge is caused by physical conditions that are not fully understood.

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Randomness
snippet: Uncertainty caused by randomness is caused by physical conditions that cannot be controlled.

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Sources
snippet: There are two main sources of uncertainty:

title: Definition:Uncertainty/Units
snippet: The unit of measurement used to quantify uncertainty is the bit. Category:Definitions/Uncertainty

title: Definition:Uncia/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Uncia == The uncia continued to be used as a unit of mass in Europe after the fall of Rome, evolving into the ounce. It is understood to be of the same mass as the apothecaries' ounce and troy ounce, and is about $10 \%$ heavier than the ounce avoirdupois. Category:Historical Notes

title: Definition:Uncia/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Uncia == The word uncia literally means twelfth part, that is: $\dfrac 1 {12}$. The name derives from the fact that an uncia was $\dfrac 1 {12}$ of a libra. The plural is unciae. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Unclosed Surface
snippet: Let $S$ be a surface in ordinary $3$-space. $S$ is an unclosed surface if $S$ is not a closed surface. Category:Definitions/Surfaces

title: Definition:Unconditional Inequality
snippet: An unconditional inequality is an inequality which is true for all values of the variables.

title: Definition:Unconditionally Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence such that the infinite series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ converges. We say that $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ converges unconditionally : $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_{\map \pi n}$ converges for each permutation $\pi : \N \to \N$.

title: Definition:Unconstrained Optimization
snippet: An unconstrained optimization problem is a problem of optimization theory in which the variables have no restrictions or constraints on their values.

title: Definition:Uncorrelated Data
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the Pearson correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y$ be equal to $0$. Then $X$ and $Y$ are described as being uncorrelated.

title: Definition:Uncountable/Also known as
snippet: An uncountable collection can also be seen as: non-denumerable or nondenumerable non-countable.

title: Definition:Uncountable/Class
snippet: A class which is neither countably infinite nor finite is described as uncountable.

title: Definition:Uncountable/Set
snippet: A set which is infinite but not countable is described as uncountable.

title: Definition:Uncountable Cartesian Product of Closed Unit Interval
snippet: Let $\Bbb I^\Bbb I$ be the uncountable Cartesian product of the closed unit interval $\Bbb I := \closedint 0 1$: $\ds \Bbb I^\Bbb I := \prod_{i \mathop \in \Bbb I} \Bbb I_i$ This object is referred to on as the uncountable cartesian product of the closed unit interval.

title: Definition:Uncountable Discrete Ordinal Space
snippet: Let $\Omega$ denote the first uncountable ordinal. Let $\hointr 0 \Omega$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Omega$. Let $S$ be the set of points of $\hointr 0 \Omega$ of the form $\alpha + 1$, where $\alpha$ is a limit ordinal. Let $\tau$ be the subspace topology induced by the order topology on $\hointr 0 \Omega$. $\struct {S, \tau}$ is known as the uncountable discrete ordinal space.

title: Definition:Uncountable Ordinal
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then $\alpha$ is said to be uncountable it is an uncountable set.

title: Definition:Uncountable Product Space of Positive Integers
snippet: Let $Z = \struct {\Z_{\ge 0}, \tau_d}$ denote the positive integers with the discrete topology. Let $A$ be an uncountable set with cardinality $\lambda$. Let $X_\lambda = \ds \struct {\prod_{\alpha \mathop \in A} Z_\alpha, \tau}$ be the space formed on the countable Cartesian product of instances of $Z$ such that $\tau$ is the Tychonoff product topology. Then $X$ is known as the uncountable product space of $Z_{\ge 0}$. Thus $\tau$ can be referred to as the uncountable product topology of $Z_{\ge 0}$. {{Proofread|Completely out of my depth here.

title: Definition:Uncountable Sum
snippet: Let $X$ be an uncountable set. Let $f: X \to \closedint 0 \to$ be an extended real-valued function. The uncountable sum of $f$ over $X$ is defined to be the supremum of the finite sums: $\ds \sum_{x \mathop \in X} \map f x := \sup \set {\sum_{x \mathop \in F} \map f x: F \subseteq X, F \text{ finite} }$

title: Definition:Uncountable Topological Space
snippet: An uncountable topological space is a topological space whose underlying set is uncountable.

title: Definition:Undecidable Statement
snippet: An undecidable statement is a statement which, in the context of a given deductive apparatus, cannot be assigned a definitive truth value.

title: Definition:Undecimal Notation
snippet: Undecimal notation is the technique of expressing numbers in base $11$. Every number $x \in \R$ is expressed in the form: $\ds x = \sum_{j \mathop \in \Z} r_j 11^j$ where: $\forall j \in \Z: r_j \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, 9, 10}$ In order to be able to represent numbers in such a format conveniently and readably, it is necessary to render the digit $10$ using a single character. Category:Definitions/Number Bases

title: Definition:Undefined
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets Let $H \subsetneqq S$ be a proper subset of $S$. Let $f: H \to T$ be a mapping on $H$. Let $x \in S \setminus H$ be an element of $S$ which is not in $H$. Then $x$ is undefined for the mapping $f$. Category:Definitions/Mapping Theory Category:Definitions/Language Definitions

title: Definition:Undefined Term
snippet: For a definition to not be circular, the definer must use already defined terms. However, this process cannot go on indefinitely. If we were to insist on everything being defined only using previously defined terms, we would enter an infinite regress. Concepts that are not defined in terms of previously defined concepts are called undefined terms. An undefined term is frequently explained by using an ostensive definition: that is, a statement that shows what something is, rather than explains.

title: Definition:Underdamped
snippet: Consider a physical system $S$ whose behaviour can be described with the second order ODE in the form: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d t^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d x} {\d t} + a^2 x = 0$ for $a, b \in \R_{>0}$. Let $b < a$, so that the solution of $(1)$ is in the form: $x = e^{-b t} \paren {C_1 \cos \alpha t + C_2 \sin \alpha t}$ where $\alpha = \sqrt {a^2 - b^2}$. Then $S$ is described as being underdamped. 600px

title: Definition:Underdamped/Also known as
snippet: == Underdamped: Also known as == An underdamped system is also known as: lightly damped, or undergoing light damping weakly damped, or undergoing weak damping.

title: Definition:Underlying Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $M: = \struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be a module over $R$. The underlying abelian group of $M$ is the abelian group $\struct {G, +_G}$. Such an underlying abelian group satisfies the underlying group axioms:

title: Definition:Underlying Abelian Group/Also defined as
snippet: == Underlying Abelian Group: Also known as == Sources which do not explore module theory at its most general may define an underlying abelian group only in the context of vector spaces. Hence, in such an exposition, $\struct {G, +_G}$ would then be defined as the underlying (abelian) group of a vector space $V := \struct {G, +_G, \times}_R$. The notation may of course vary accordingly.

title: Definition:Underlying Abelian Group/Also known as
snippet: == Underlying Abelian Group: Also known as == The underlying abelian group of a module or vector space is also referred to just as the underlying group, its abelian nature being taken for granted.

title: Definition:Underlying Graph
snippet: Let $N = \struct {V, E, f}$ be a network where $f: E \to \R$ is the mapping from the edge set $E$ to the real numbers $\R$. The underlying graph of $N$ is the graph $G = \struct {V, E}$ consisting only of the vertex set $V$ and the edge set $E$. Category:Definitions/Network Theory Category:Definitions/Graph Theory

title: Definition:Underlying Module of Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A, *}$ be an algebra over $R$. Its underlying module is the $R$-module $A$.

title: Definition:Underlying Ring of Associative Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A, *}$ be an associative algebra over $R$. Let $A = \struct {M, +, \circ}$ be the underlying module of $\struct {A, *}$. The underlying ring of $\struct {A, *}$ is the ring $\struct {A, +, *}$.

title: Definition:Underlying Set/Abstract Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then the underlying set of $\struct {S, \circ}$ is the set $S$.

title: Definition:Underlying Set/Metric Space
snippet: The underlying set of a metric space $M = \struct {A, d}$ is the set $A$.

title: Definition:Underlying Set/Relational Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Then the underlying set of $\struct {S, \RR}$ is the set $S$.

title: Definition:Underlying Set/Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the underlying set of $T$ is the set $S$.

title: Definition:Underlying Set Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory with: A collection of sets as objects; A collection of mappings as morphisms. The underlying set functor $\size {\, \cdot \,}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ is defined in the following cases.

title: Definition:Underlying Set Functor/Category of Monoids
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf {Mon}$ be the category of monoids. The underlying set functor $\size {\, \cdot \,}: \mathbf {Mon} \to \mathbf {Set}$ is the functor defined by: {{DefineFunctor |ob = $\size {\struct {M, \circ} } := M$ |mor = $\size f := f$ }} The underlying set functor thus comes down to deleting the information that $\struct {M, \circ}$ is a monoid, and that $f$ is a monoid homomorphism. It is thus seen to be an example of a forgetful functor.

title: Definition:Undetermined
snippet: In the Łukasiewicz system of three-valued logic, a statement has a truth value of undetermined it cannot be stated (at the moment, at least) that it is either true or false.

title: Definition:Undetermined/Symbol
snippet: == Undetermined: Symbol == The symbol used to denote that a statement has a truth value of undetermined is $\U$.

title: Definition:Undirected Graph
snippet: An undirected graph is a graph whose edge set considered as a relation is symmetric. That is, if $G$ is an undirected graph and $e = u v$ is an edge in $G$, then $v u$ is also an edge in $G$. In other words, if you can "go from $u$ to $v$", you can also "go from $v$ to $u$".

title: Definition:Undistributed Term of Categorical Syllogism
snippet: A term in a syllogism is undistributed the categorical statement in which it occurs does not refer to the whole of the class designated by the term.

title: Definition:Undistributed Term of Categorical Syllogism/Predicate
snippet: Let $\map {\mathbf \Phi} {S, P}$ be a categorical statement, expressed in abbreviated form. Let $\mathbf \Phi$ be an affirmative categorical statement. Then $P$ is described as being undistributed.

title: Definition:Undistributed Term of Categorical Syllogism/Subject
snippet: Let $\map {\mathbf \Phi} {S, P}$ be a categorical statement, expressed in abbreviated form. Let $\mathbf \Phi$ be a particular categorical statement. Then $S$ is described as being undistributed.

title: Definition:Uniform
snippet: Let $B$ be an object. Let $P$ be a property of $B$. Then $P$ is said to be uniform $P$ is constant throughout the whole of $B$.

title: Definition:Uniform/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Uniformity ==

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {V, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n: S \to V$. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly absolutely the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \norm {f_n}$ converges uniformly.

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \C$.

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Functions/Definition 1
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + f_n}$ converges uniformly absolutely the sequence of partial products of $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \size {f_n} }$ converges uniformly. Category:Definitions/Complex Analysis Category:Definitions/Uniform Convergence Category:Definitions/Infinite Products

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Functions/Definition 2
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + f_n}$ converges uniformly absolutely the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly absolutely. Category:Definitions/Complex Analysis Category:Definitions/Uniform Convergence Category:Definitions/Infinite Products

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/Complex Functions/Definition 3
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \C$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + f_n}$ converges uniformly absolutely there exists $n_0 \in \N$ such that: $(1): \quad \map {f_n} x \ne -1$ for $n \ge n_0$ and $x \in X$ and: $(2): \quad$ The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = n_0}^\infty \map \log {1 + f_n}$ is uniformly absolutely convergent. Category:Definitions/Complex Analysis Category:Definitions/Uniform Convergence Category:Definitions/Infinite Products

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n} $ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$.

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 1
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n} $ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + f_n}$ converges uniformly absolutely the sequence of partial products of $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + \norm {f_n} }$ converges uniformly. Category:Definitions/Uniform Convergence Category:Definitions/Infinite Products

title: Definition:Uniform Absolute Convergence of Product/General Definition/Definition 2
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + f_n}$ converges uniformly absolutely the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly absolutely. Category:Definitions/Uniform Convergence Category:Definitions/Infinite Products

title: Definition:Uniform Antiprism
snippet: A uniform antiprism is an antiprism: $(1): \quad$ whose bases are both congruent regular polygons $(2): \quad$ whose lateral faces are all equilateral triangles.

title: Definition:Uniform Antiprism/Also known as
snippet: == Uniform Antiprism: Also known as == A uniform antiprism is also known as a regular antiprism. Category:Definitions/Uniform Antiprisms

title: Definition:Uniform Cauchy Criterion
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \mathbb R$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $S \to \R$. We say that $\sequence {f_n}$ satisfies the uniform Cauchy criterion or is uniformly Cauchy on $S$ if for all $\varepsilon \in \R_{> 0}$, there exists $N \in \N$ such that: $\size {\map {f_n} x - \map {f_m} x} N$. By Sequence of Functions is Uniformly Cauchy iff Uniformly Convergent, this criterion gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a sequence of real functions to be uniformly convergent.

title: Definition:Uniform Continuity/Metric Space
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Then a mapping $f: A_1 \to A_2$ is uniformly continuous on $A_1$ : $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \exists \delta \in \R_{>0}: \forall x, y \in A_1: \map {d_1} {x, y} 0}$ denotes the set of all strictly positive real numbers.

title: Definition:Uniform Continuity/Real Function
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. A real function $f: I \to \R$ is said to be uniformly continuous on $I$ : for every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that the following property holds: for every $x, y \in I$ such that $\size {x - y} 0: \exists \delta > 0: \paren {x, y \in I, \size {x - y} < \delta \implies \size {\map f x - \map f y} < \epsilon}$ It can be seen that this says exactly the same thing as the definition for metric spaces if $\R$ is considered a metric space under the Euclidean metric.

title: Definition:Uniform Contraction Mapping
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be metric spaces. Let $f : M \times N \to M$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a uniform contraction there exists $K<1$ such that for all $x,y\in M$ and $t\in N$: $d(f(x,t), f(y,t)) \leq K\cdot d(x,y)$.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence/Also defined as
snippet: == Uniform Convergence: Also defined as == In definining uniform convergence, some sources insist that $N \in \N$, but this is unnecessary and makes proofs more cumbersome.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Uniform Convergence == The concept of uniform convergence was created by during his investigation of power series.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence/Infinite Series
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $S \to \R$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be sequence of real functions $S \to \R$ with: $\ds \map {s_n} x = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \map {f_n} x$ for each $n \in \N$ and $x \in S$. We say that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly to a real function $f: S \to \R$ on $S$ $\sequence {s_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ on $S$.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence/Metric Space
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n: S \to A$. Let: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \exists N \in \R: \forall n \ge N, \forall x \in S: \map d {\map {f_n} x, \map f x} < \epsilon$ Then $\sequence {f_n}$ converges to $f$ uniformly on $S$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence/Real Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions defined on $D \subseteq \R$. Let: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \exists N \in \R: \forall n \ge N, \forall x \in D: \size {\map {f_n} x - \map f x} < \epsilon$ Then $\sequence {f_n}$ converges to $f$ uniformly on $D$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Definition:Uniform Convergence of Product/Compact Space
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a complete valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly there exists $n_0 \in \N$ such that the sequence of partial products of $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = n_0}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly and is nonzero.

title: Definition:Uniform Density
snippet: A body has uniform density its density is constant. The type of density, that is: mass density, electric charge density, and so on, will be clarified in context.

title: Definition:Uniform Distribution/Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. $X$ is said to be uniformly distributed on the closed real interval $\closedint a b$ it has probability density function: $\map {f_X} x = \begin{cases} \dfrac 1 {b - a} & a \le x \le b \\ \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$ This is written: $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$

title: Definition:Uniform Distribution/Discrete
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on a probability space. Then $X$ has a discrete uniform distribution with parameter $n$ : $\Img X = \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ $\map \Pr {X = k} = \dfrac 1 n$ That is, there is a number of outcomes with an equal probability of occurrence. This is written: $X \sim \DiscreteUniform n$

title: Definition:Uniform Equivalence/Metric Spaces
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Then the mapping $f: A_1 \to A_2$ is a uniform equivalence of $M_1$ with $M_2$ $f$ is a bijection such that $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are both uniformly continuous.

title: Definition:Uniform Equivalence/Metrics
snippet: Let $A$ be a set on which there are two metrics imposed: $d_1$ and $d_2$. Then $d_1$ and $d_2$ are uniformly equivalent the identity mapping of $A$ is uniformly $\tuple {d_1, d_2}$-continuous and also uniformly $\tuple {d_2, d_1}$-continuous.

title: Definition:Uniform Gravitational Field
snippet: A uniform gravitational field is a gravitational field in which identical particles experience the same forces, independent of their position.

title: Definition:Uniform Matroid
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$. Let $\mathscr I_{k, n}$ be the set of all subsets of $S$ of cardinality less than or equal to $k$. Then the ordered pair $\struct {S, \mathscr I_{k, n} }$ is called the uniform matroid of rank $k$ and is denoted $U_{k, n}$.

title: Definition:Uniform Motion
snippet: Uniform motion is motion with constant velocity, speed or acceleration.

title: Definition:Uniform Operator Topology
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm{\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. Then the topology induced by $\struct {\map {CL} {X, Y}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}}$ is called the uniform operator topology.

title: Definition:Uniform Polyhedron
snippet: A uniform polyhedron is a polyhedron: $(1): \quad$ which is isogonal $(2): \quad$ whose faces are all regular polygons (but not necessarily all of the same type).

title: Definition:Uniform Prism
snippet: A uniform prism is a regular prism whose lateral faces are square.

title: Definition:Uniform Prism/Also known as
snippet: == Uniform Prism: Also known as == A uniform prism is also known as a semi-regular prism, which can also be rendered semiregular prism.

title: Definition:Uniform Space
snippet: Let $\UU$ be a uniformity on a set $S$. The quasiuniform space $\struct {\struct {S, \UU}, \tau}$ induced by $\UU$ is a uniform space.

title: Definition:Uniform Tubular Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $P \subseteq M$ be an embedded submanifold. Let $U \subseteq M$ be the tubular neighborhood of $P$ in $M$ with $\map \delta x = \epsilon$ where $\epsilon \in \R_{> 0}$. Then $U$ is called the uniform tubular neighborhood (or $\epsilon$-tubular neighborhood) of $P$ in $M$.

title: Definition:Uniformity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. A uniformity on $S$ is a set of subsets $\UU$ of the cartesian product $S \times S$ satisfying the quasiuniformity axioms: and also: $(\text U 5): \forall u \in \UU: u^{-1} \in \UU$ where $u^{-1}$ is defined as: $u^{-1} := \set {\tuple {y, x}: \tuple {x, y} \in u}$ That is, all elements of $\UU$ are symmetric. These five axioms are together known as the uniformity axioms.

title: Definition:Uniformity/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == Part $\text I$: Basic Definitions Section $5$. Metric Spaces Uniformities

title: Definition:Uniformizable Space/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Uniformizable == The British English spelling for uniformizable is uniformisable. Category:Linguistic Notes

title: Definition:Uniformly Bounded
snippet: Let $X$ be a set and let $Y = \left({A, d}\right)$ be a metric space. Let $\FF = \family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings $f_i: X \to Y$. Then $\FF$ is said to be uniformly bounded every mapping $f \in \FF$ can be bounded by the same constant. That is, there exists some $M \in \R$ such that: $\forall x, y \in X, i \in I : \map d {\map {f_i} x, \map {f_i} y} \le M$ Category:Definitions/Metric Spaces Category:Definitions/Boundedness

title: Definition:Uniformly Continuous Semigroup
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a $\hointr 0 \infty$-indexed family of bounded linear transformations $\map T t : X \to X$. Let $\struct {\map B X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations equipped with the canonical norm. We say that $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ is uniformly continuous : $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to 0^+} \norm {\map T t - I}_{\map B X} = 0$

title: Definition:Uniformly Convex Normed Vector Space
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. We say that $X$ is uniformly convex : for every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that: whenever $x, y \in X$ have $
orm x = 
orm y = 1$ and $
orm {x - y} > \epsilon$, we have: $\ds 
orm { rac {x + y} 2} < 1 - \delta$

title: Definition:Uniformly Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $X = \struct {A, d}$ and $Y = \struct {B, \rho}$ be metric spaces. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings $f_i: X \to Y$. Then $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ is said to be uniformly equicontinuous on $S \subseteq A$ : $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0} : \exists \delta \in \R_{>0}: \forall i \in I: \forall x, y \in S : \map d {x, y} < \delta \implies \map \rho {\map {f_i} x, \map {f_i} y} < \epsilon$

title: Definition:Uniformly Equicontinuous Mappings
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $\family {f_i: M_1 \to M_2}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings, where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\family {f_i}$ have the property that: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \exists \delta \in \R_{>0}: \forall x, y \in A_1: \map {d_1} {x, y} < \delta \implies \map {d_2} {\map {f_i} x, \map {f_i} y} < \epsilon$ for all $i \in I$. Then $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ is a family of uniformly equicontinuous mappings.

title: Definition:Uniformly Integrable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\FF \subseteq \map \MM \Sigma$ be a collection of measurable functions. Then $\FF$ is said to be uniformly integrable (with respect to $\mu$) : $\ds \forall \epsilon > 0: \exists g_\epsilon \in \map {\LL^1_+} \mu: \sup_{f \mathop \in \FF} \int_{\set {\size f \mathop > g_\epsilon} } \size f \rd \mu g_\epsilon}$ is short for $\set {x \in X: \size {\map f x} > \map {g_\epsilon} x}$

title: Definition:Uniformly Normal Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $W \subseteq M$ be a subset. Let $U_p = \map {\exp_p} {\map {B_\delta^-} 0 }$ be a closed geodesic ball around $p \in M$. Suppose there exists $\delta \in \R_{> 0}$ such that: $\forall p \in W : W \subseteq U_p$ Then $W$ is called uniformly normal (or uniformly $\delta$-normal).

title: Definition:Unilateral Surface
snippet: A unilateral surface is a surface with only one side.

title: Definition:Unimodal Distribution
snippet: A unimodal distribution is a probability distribution which has only one mode. For a discrete probability distribution $X$, if two adjacent values both have the same probability or frequency, and this is the modal value, then it is usual to regard this as a unimodal distribution.

title: Definition:Unimodular Matrix
snippet: A unimodular matrix is a square matrix whose determinant equals $1$.

title: Definition:Union
snippet: Definition:Set Union Definition:Union of Mappings Definition:Union of Relations Definition:Union Mapping Definition:Union Relation Definition:Union of Family Definition:Union of Adjacent Open Intervals

title: Definition:Union Mapping
snippet: Let: $(1): \quad f_1: S_1 \to T_1$ be a mapping from $S_1$ to $T_1$ $(2): \quad f_2: S_2 \to T_2$ be a mapping from $S_2$ to $T_2$ Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be combinable, that is, that they agree on $S_1 \cap S_2$. Then the union mapping $f = f_1 \cup f_2$ of $f_1$ and $f_2$ is: $f: S_1 \cup S_2 \to T_1 \cup T_2: \map f s = \begin{cases} \map {f_1} s : & s \in S_1 \\ \map {f_2} s : & s \in S_2 \end{cases}$

title: Definition:Union Mapping/Family
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $F = \family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of mappings indexed by $I$ The union mapping $f$ of $F$ is defined when: $\forall i, j \in I: f_i$ and $f_j$ are combinable and is defined as: $\forall x \in \ds \bigcup \set {\Dom {f_i}: i \in I} x \in \Dom {f_i} \implies f = \map {f_i} x$

title: Definition:Union Mapping/Finite Set
snippet: Let $S = \set {f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n}$ denote a finite set of mappings. The union mapping $f$ of $S$ is defined when: $\forall i, j \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: f_i$ and $f_j$ are combinable and is defined as: $\forall x \in \ds \bigcup \set {\Dom {f_i}: i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n} } x \in \Dom {f_i} \implies f = \map {f_i} x$

title: Definition:Union Relation
snippet: Let: $(1): \quad \RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times T_1$ be a relation on $S_1 \times T_1$ $(2): \quad \RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times T_2$ be a relation on $S_2 \times T_2$ Let $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ be combinable, that is, that they agree on $S_1 \cap S_2$. Then the union relation (or combined relation) $\RR$ of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ is: $\RR \subseteq \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cup T_2}: \map \RR s = \begin{cases} \map {\RR_1} s : & s \in S_1 \\ \map {\RR_2} s : & s \in S_2 \end{cases}$

title: Definition:Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line $\R$ under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Let $a, b, c \in \R$ where $a < b < c$. Let $S$ be the union of the two open intervals: $S := \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Let $T := \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the subspace composed of $S$ with the subspace topology induced on $S$ by $\tau_d$. Then $T$ is the union of adjacent open intervals.

title: Definition:Union of Family/Also denoted as
snippet: == Union of Family: Also denoted as == The set $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ can also be seen denoted as: $\ds \bigcup_I S_i$ or, if the indexing set is clear from context: $\ds \bigcup_i S_i$ Some sources use the form: $\bigcup \set {S_i: i \in I}$

title: Definition:Union of Relations
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ be relations on $S \times T$. The union of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ is the relation $\QQ$ defined by: $\QQ := \RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ where $\cup$ denotes set union. Explicitly, for $s \in S$ and $t \in T$, we have: $s \mathrel \QQ t$ $s \mathrel {\RR_1} t$ or $s \mathrel {\RR_2} t$

title: Definition:Union of Relations/General Definition
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\mathscr R$ be a collection of relations on $S \times T$. The union of $\mathscr R$ is the relation $\RR$ defined by: $\ds \RR = \bigcup \mathscr R$ where $\bigcup$ denotes set union. Explicitly, for $s \in S$ and $t \in T$: $s \mathrel \RR t$ for some $\QQ \in \mathscr R$, $s \mathrel \QQ t$

title: Definition:Union of Set of Sets/Also denoted as
snippet: == Union of Set of Sets: Also denoted as == The symbol $\bigcup$ is rendered in display mode as $\ds \bigcup$. Some sources denote $\bigcup \mathbb S$ as $\ds \bigcup_{S \mathop \in \mathbb S} S$.

title: Definition:Unique
snippet: Suppose $A$ and $B$ are two objects whose definition is in terms of a given set of properties. If it can be demonstrated that, in order for both $A$ and $B$ to fulfil those properties, it is necessary for $A$ to be equal to $B$, then $A$ (and indeed $B$) is unique. Equivalently, there is one and only one, or exactly one, such object. Thus, intuitively, an object is unique if there is precisely one such object.

title: Definition:Unique Factorization Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain. If, for all $x \in D$ such that $x$ is non-zero and not a unit of $D$: $(1): \quad x$ possesses a complete factorization in $D$ $(2): \quad$ Any two complete factorizations of $x$ in $D$ are equivalent then $D$ is a unique factorization domain.

title: Definition:Unique Parsability
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a formal language. Let every WFF of $\LL$ result from a unique rule of formation. Then $\LL$ has unique parsability.

title: Definition:Unique Period Prime
snippet: Let $b \in \N_{>1}$ be a natural number. A unique period prime base $b$ is a prime number $p$ whose reciprocal expressed base $b$ has a period shared with no other prime. If $b$ is not specified, then decimal notation (that is, base $10$) is assumed.

title: Definition:Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $S \subseteq \map {\operatorname {Ob} } {\mathbf C}$ be a subclass of its objects. The class $S$ is unique up to isomorphism for all objects $s, t \in S$ there is a isomorphism from $s$ to $t$.

title: Definition:Unique up to Unique Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $S \subseteq \map {\operatorname {Ob} } {\mathbf C}$ be a subclass of its objects. The class $S$ is unique up to unique isomorphism for all objects $s, t \in S$ there exists a unique isomorphism from $s$ to $t$.

title: Definition:Unique up to Unique Morphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $S \subseteq \map {\operatorname {Ob} } {\mathbf C}$ be a subclass of its objects.

title: Definition:Uniquely Complemented Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \vee, \preceq}$ be a complemented lattice. Let $L$ be such that each element of $S$ has exactly one complement. Then $L$ is a uniquely complemented lattice.

title: Definition:Uniqueness Theorem
snippet: A uniqueness theorem is a theorem which asserts that only one particular type of object exists.

title: Definition:Unit
snippet: Arithmetic and so on: Numbers: An instance of the number $1$ (one). Abstract Algebra: Unit of Ring Set Systems: Unit of System of Sets. Set Theory: Unit set: another word for singleton Algebras: Unit of a unitary algebra The concepts are related: it is apparent that the unit of an algebra of sets $\SS$ is the unity of $\SS$ considered as a ring $\struct {\SS, *, \cap}$. Unit may also refer to: Unit of Measurement: A definite magnitude of a physical quantity which is agreed by convention. Experimental Unit: A subject of an experimental design to which a treatment is to be applied.

title: Definition:Unit-Speed Curve
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : \R \to M$ be a smooth curve. Suppose the speed of $\gamma$ is equal to $1$: $\size {\map {\gamma'} t}_g = 1$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}_g$ is the Riemannian inner product norm. Then $\gamma$ is a unit-speed curve.

title: Definition:Unit/Also known as
snippet: == Unit: Also known as == In older writings, a unit is often rendered as an unit; the rules of grammar have since evolved.

title: Definition:Unit (One)
snippet: A numerical quantity whose cardinality corresponds to the number $1$ (one) is called a unit. '

title: Definition:Unit (One)/Naturally Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $S^*$ be the zero complement of $S$. By Zero Complement is Not Empty, $S^*$ is not empty. Therefore, by , $\struct {S^*, \circ, \preceq}$ has a smallest element for $\preceq$. This smallest element is called one and denoted $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Arithmetic Function
snippet: The unit arithmetic function $u: S \to \Z$ is defined by $u \left({n}\right) = 1$ for all $n$: $\forall n \in S: u \left({n}\right) = 1$ where $S$ is (in theory) any set, but in this context is usually one of the standard number sets $\Z, \Q, \R, \C$.

title: Definition:Unit Ball
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$. The closed unit ball of $V$, denoted $\operatorname {ball} V$, is the set: $\set {v \in V: \norm v_V \mathop \le 1}$

title: Definition:Unit Circle
snippet: The unit circle is a circle with radius equal to $1$. 400px

title: Definition:Unit Conversion
snippet: Unit conversion is the process which converts a measurement of a physical quantity from one unit of measurement to another.

title: Definition:Unit Cube
snippet: A unit cube is a cube each of whose edges is one unit long.

title: Definition:Unit Diagonal
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. $\mathbf A$ has a unit diagonal all of the diagonal elements of $\mathbf A$ are $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Disk
snippet: A unit disk is a disk whose radius is equal to $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Fraction
snippet: A unit fraction is a fraction whose numerator is $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Ideal
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Its unit ideal is $A$ itself.

title: Definition:Unit Ideal of Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Its unit ideal is the ideal $R$.

title: Definition:Unit Length
snippet: A unit length is a straight line segment of arbitrary length can defined as having a length of $1$ (one). During the course of the exposition arising from the definition a unit length $L$, all subsequent lengths can then be expressed as multiples of $L$. Category:Definitions/Geometry

title: Definition:Unit Matrix
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ be the ring of order $n$ square matrices over $R$. Then the unit matrix (of order $n$) of $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ is defined as: $\mathbf I_n := \sqbrk a_n: a_{i j} = \delta_{i j}$ where $\delta_{i j}$ is the Kronecker delta for $\map {\MM_R} n$. That is, it is the square matrix where every element on the diagonal is equal to $1_R$, and whose other entries all are $0_R$.

title: Definition:Unit Matrix/Also known as
snippet: == Unit Matrix: Also known as == Some sources refer to the unit matrix as the identity matrix, as it is the identity element of the ring of order $n$ square matrices over $R$. There are several variants of $\mathbf I_n$ which can frequently be found, for example: $\mathbf 1$ $\mathbf 1_n$ $\mathbb I_n$ In physics and mechanics it is common to see $\mathbf I$ used specifically to denote the $3 \times 3$ unit matrix.

title: Definition:Unit Matrix/Examples/3 x 3
snippet: The $3 \times 3$ unit matrix is as follows: $\mathbf I_3 = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \end{bmatrix}$

title: Definition:Unit Normal
snippet: Let $S$ be a surface in ordinary $3$-space. Let $P$ be a point of $S$. Let $\mathbf n$ be a normal to $S$ at $P$ such that $\mathbf n$ is a unit vector. Then $\mathbf n$ is known as a unit normal.

title: Definition:Unit Sphere
snippet: A unit sphere is a sphere whose radius equals $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Sphere/Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $x \in X$. The $n$-dimensional unit sphere, or unit $n$-sphere, is the $n$-sphere of radius $1$: $\map {\Bbb S^n} x = \set {y \in \R^{n + 1} : \norm {x - y} = 1}$ Category:Definitions/Unit Spheres Category:Definitions/Normed Vector Spaces

title: Definition:Unit Sphere/Topology
snippet: The $n$-dimensional unit sphere, or unit $n$-sphere, is the $n$-sphere of radius $1$ and center the origin: $\Bbb S^n = \set {x \in \R^{n + 1} : \size x = 1}$ Intuitively, it is the skin of the open $1$-ball of $\mathbb 0$ in $\R^{n + 1}$.

title: Definition:Unit Square
snippet: A unit square is a square of side of unit length.

title: Definition:Unit Square under Lexicographic Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be the unit square in the (real) Cartesian plane: {{eqn | l = S | r = \set {\tuple {x, y}: x, y \in \R, 0 \le x \le 1, 0 \le y \le 1} | c = }} Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ denote the lexicographic ordering applied to $S$: $\forall \tuple {x_1, y_1}, \tuple {x_2, y_2} \in S: \tuple {x_1, y_1} \preccurlyeq_l \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff \begin {cases} x_1 < x_2 \\ x_1 = x_2 \land y_1 \le y_2 \end {cases}$ Let $\tau$ be the order topology be applied to the ordered structure $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq_l}$.

title: Definition:Unit Tangent Bundle
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $T M$ be the tangent bundle of $\struct {M, g}$. Let $p \in M$ be a point in $M$. Let $\tuple {p, v}$ be a geometric tangent vector. The unit tangent bundle $UTM \subseteq TM$ is the subset of unit vectors: $UTM = \set {\tuple {p, v} \in TM : \norm v_g = 1}$

title: Definition:Unit Tangent Vector of Curve Parameterized by Arc Length/3-Dimensional Real Vector Space
snippet: Let $\alpha : I \to \R^3$ be a (smooth) curve parameterized by arc length. The unit tangent vector of $\alpha$ at $s$ is defined as: $\map t s := \map {\alpha '} s$ where: $\alpha '$ denotes the derivative of $\alpha$

title: Definition:Unit Vector
snippet: A unit vector is a vector quantity which has a magnitude of $1$.

title: Definition:Unit Vector/Dimension
snippet: The unit vector has no dimension. This is because it consists of a quantity (of a dimension $D$) divided by another instance of that same quantity (also of dimension $D$), leaving no dimension. Category:Definitions/Vectors

title: Definition:Unit n-Cube
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. The unit $n$-cube $I^n$ is the Cartesian product of $n$ instances of the closed real interval $\set {x \in \R: 0 \le x \le 1}$: $I^n = \closedint 0 1^n$

title: Definition:Unit of Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. The unit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ is the natural transformation $\eta: \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D} \to GF$ where: for each $D$ of $\mathbf D: \eta_{_D} = \map {\alpha_{\tuple{D, F D}}} {\operatorname {id}_{FD}}$ where $\alpha_{\tuple{D, F D}} : \map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {F D, F D} \to \map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf D} } {D, GF D}$ is the bijection from the adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ $\operatorname {id}_{F D}$ is the…

title: Definition:Unit of Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$ be a unital algebra over $R$. The unit of $\struct {A_R, \oplus}$, denoted $1_A$, is the identity element of the operation $\oplus$: $\forall a \in A_R: a \oplus 1_A = 1_A \oplus a = a$ It is usually denoted $1$ when there is no source of confusion with the identity elements of the underlying structures of the algebra.

title: Definition:Unit of Measurement
snippet: A unit of measurement is a specified magnitude of a given physical quantity, defined by convention. It is used as a standard for measurement of that physical quantity. Any other value of the physical quantity can be expressed as a multiple of that unit of measurement.

title: Definition:Unit of Measurement/Also known as
snippet: == Definiend: Also known as == Some sources refer to a unit of measurement as a unit of measure.

title: Definition:Unit of Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$.

title: Definition:Unit of Ring/Also known as
snippet: == Unit of Ring: Also known as == Some sources use the term invertible element for unit of ring. Category:Definitions/Units of Rings

title: Definition:Unit of Ring/Definition 1
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. An element $x \in R$ is a unit of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ $x$ is invertible under $\circ$. That is, a unit of $R$ is an element of $R$ which has an inverse. $\exists y \in R: x \circ y = 1_R = y \circ x$

title: Definition:Unit of Ring/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. An element $x \in R$ is a unit of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ $x$ is divisor of $1_R$.

title: Definition:Unit of System of Sets
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a system of sets. Let $U \in \SS$ such that: $\forall A \in \SS: A \cap U = A$ Then $U$ is the unit of $\SS$.

title: Definition:Unital Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A, *}$ be an algebra over $R$. Then $\struct {A, *}$ is a unital algebra the algebraic structure $\struct {A, \oplus}$ has an identity element. That is: $\exists 1_A \in A: \forall a \in A: a * 1_A = 1_A * a = a$

title: Definition:Unital Algebra Homomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A, *}$ and $\struct {B, \times}$ be unital algebras over $R$ with units $1_A$ and $1_B$. A unital algebra homomorphism $f : A \to B$ is a algebra homomorphism such that $\map f {1_A} = 1_B$.

title: Definition:Unital Associative Commutative Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity.

title: Definition:Unital Associative Commutative Algebra/Definition 1
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. A unital associative commutative algebra over $R$ is an algebra $\struct {A, *}$ over $R$ that is unital, associative and commutative and whose underlying module is unitary.

title: Definition:Unital Associative Commutative Algebra/Definition 2
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. A unital associative commutative algebra over $R$ is a ring under $A$, that is, an ordered pair $\struct {A, f}$ where: $A$ is a commutative ring with unity $f : R \to A$ is a unital ring homomorphism.

title: Definition:Unital Associative Commutative Algebra Homomorphism
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $B$ and $C$ be $A$-algebras.

title: Definition:Unital Magma
snippet: A unital magma is a magma that has an identity element.

title: Definition:Unital Normed Algebra
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\Bbb F$ that is unital as an algebra. Let $\mathbf 1_A$ be the identity element of $A$. We say that $A$ is a unital normed algebra : $\norm {\mathbf 1_A} = 1$

title: Definition:Unital Ring Homomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ and $S$ be rings with unities $1_R$ and $1_S$ respectively. A unital ring homomorphism is a ring homomorphism $f: R \to S$ such that $\map f {1_R} = 1_S$.

title: Definition:Unital Subalgebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A_R, *}$ be an unital algebra over $R$ whose unit is $1_A$. Let $\struct {B_R, *}$ be a subalgebra of $A_R$.

title: Definition:Unital Subalgebra/Definition 1
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A_R, *}$ be an unital algebra over $R$ whose unit is $1_A$. Let $\struct {B_R, *}$ be a subalgebra of $A_R$. $\struct {B_R, *}$ is a unital subalgebra of $A_R$ $1_A \in B$.

title: Definition:Unital Subalgebra/Definition 2
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A_R, *}$ be an unital algebra over $R$ whose unit is $1_A$. Let $\struct {B_R, *}$ be a subalgebra of $A_R$. $\struct {B_R, *}$ is a unital subalgebra of $A_R$ : $(1) \quad B_R$ is unital $(2) \quad$ Its unit is $1_A$. That is, a unital subalgebra of $A_R$ must not only have a unit, but that unit must also be the same unit as that of $A_R$.

title: Definition:Unital Subalgebra/Warning
snippet: == Unital Subalgebra: Warning == It is possible for $B_R \subseteq A_R$ to be a subalgebra of $A_R$ such that it has a unit $1_B$ such that $1_B \ne 1_A$. Such a subalgebra is a unital algebra, but is not a unital subalgebra of $A_R$.

title: Definition:Unitary Division Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a division algebra. Then $\struct {A_F, \oplus}$ is a unitary division algebra it has an identity element $1_{A_F}$ called a unit for $\oplus$, that is: $\exists 1_{A_F} \in A_F: \forall a \in A_F: a \oplus 1_{A_F} = 1_{A_F} \oplus a = a$ The unit is usually denoted $1$ when there is no source of confusion with the identity elements of the underlying structures of the division algebra.

title: Definition:Unitary Division Algebra/Also known as
snippet: == Unitary Division Algebra: Also known as == Some refer to a unitary division algebra just as a division algebra. That is, its unitary nature is subsumed in the definition.

title: Definition:Unitary Divisor
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $d \in \Z$ be such that: $d$ is a divisor of $n$ $d$ and $\dfrac n d$ are coprime. Then $d$ is a unitary divisor of $n$.

title: Definition:Unitary Element of Unital *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a unital $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $a \in A$. Let $\mathbf 1_A$ be the identity element of $A$. We say that $a$ is unitary $a^\ast a = a a^\ast = \mathbf 1_A$.

title: Definition:Unitary Group
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. The unitary group $\operatorname U_n$ is the group of all $n \times n$ unitary matrices under (conventional) matrix multiplication.

title: Definition:Unitary Group/Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. The unitary group of $\HH$ is the group consisting of the unitary operators of $\HH$.

title: Definition:Unitary Left Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a unitary ring whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. A unitary left module over $R$ is an $R$-algebraic structure $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ with one operation $\ast: R \times G \to G$, which satisfies the unitary left module axioms:

title: Definition:Unitary Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf U$ be a nonsingular square matrix over the complex numbers $\C$. Then $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix : $\mathbf U^{-1} = \mathbf U^\dagger$ where: $\mathbf U^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\mathbf U$ $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$.

title: Definition:Unitary Matrix/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == unitary matrix

title: Definition:Unitary Method
snippet: The unitary method is a technique for solving problems in proportion in which one of the variables is reduced to $1$.

title: Definition:Unitary Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. A unitary module over $R$ is an $R$-algebraic structure with one operation $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ which is either a unitary left module or a unitary right module, depending upon whether $\ast$ is defined as: $\ast: R \times G \to G$ or: $\ast: G \times R \to G$ respectively. As follows:

title: Definition:Unitary Module over Ring/Also known as
snippet: == Unitary Module over Ring: Also known as == A unitary module over $R$ can also be referred to as a unitary $R$-module. A unitary module is also known as a unital module.

title: Definition:Unitary Operator
snippet: A unitary operator is an isomorphism from a Hilbert space $\HH$ to itself.

title: Definition:Unitary Perfect Number
snippet: A unitary perfect number is a positive integer which equals the sum of its positive unitary divisors apart from itself.

title: Definition:Unitary Perfect Number/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of unitary perfect numbers begins: $6, 60, 90, 87 \, 360, 146 \, 361 \, 946 \, 186 \, 458 \, 562 \, 560 \, 000, \ldots$ It is not known whether this sequence is complete.

title: Definition:Unitary Ratio
snippet: A unitary ratio is a ratio such that either its antecedent or its consequent is equal to $1$.

title: Definition:Unitary Right Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a unitary ring whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. A unitary right module over $R$ is an $R$-algebraic structure $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ with one operation $\ast: G \times R \to G$ which satisfies the unitary right module axioms:

title: Definition:Unitary Similarity
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be square matrices over $\C$. Then, $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are unitarily similar there exists a unitary matrix $\mathbf U$ such that: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U^{-1} \mathbf B \mathbf U$ That is, $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are related by a unitary transformation.

title: Definition:Unitary Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be square matrices over the complex numbers $\C$. An unitary transformation is an operation of changing $\mathbf B$ to $\mathbf A$ by multiplying $\mathbf B$ by an unitary matrix $\mathbf Y$ and its inverse $\mathbf Y^{-1}$ such that: $\mathbf A = \mathbf Y^{-1} \mathbf B \mathbf Y$

title: Definition:United States Customary System
snippet: The United States customary system is a system of measurement based on the imperial system and adapted by the emergent .

title: Definition:Unitization of Algebra over Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $A_+ = A \times K$ be the direct product of $A$ and $K$ as vector spaces over $K$ with vector addition $+_{A \times K}$ and scalar multiplication $\cdot_{A \times K}$. Define multiplication $\circ_{A \times K}$ on $A \times K$ by: $\tuple {a, \lambda} \circ_{A \times K} \tuple {b, \mu} = \tuple {a b + \lambda b + \mu a, \lambda \mu}$ for each $\tuple {a, \lambda}, \tuple {b, \mu} \in A \times K$.

title: Definition:Unity
snippet: Abstract Algebra: The concept of a unity, which is the abstraction of the concept of the number $1$ (one) The unity of a ring The unity of a field Another name (not recommended) for the identity element of a group Arithmetic, Number Theory, and so on: Another word for the number $1$ (one), when it is important to call attention to its numeric properties.

title: Definition:Unity (Abstract Algebra)/Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. If the semigroup $\struct {R, \circ}$ has an identity, this identity is referred to as the unity of the ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. It is (usually) denoted $1_R$, where the subscript denotes the particular ring to which $1_R$ belongs (or often $1$ if there is no danger of ambiguity). The ring $R$ itself is then referred to as a ring with unity.

title: Definition:Univalent Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $\RR$ is univalent : $\RR \circ \RR^{-1} \subseteq \Delta_S$ That is, $\RR$ composed with its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is a subset of the diagonal relation on $S$.

title: Definition:Universal
snippet: Set Theory and Class Theory: Universal Set Universal Class Category Theory: Universal Object Universal Property Universal Morphism Universal Enveloping Algebra Topology: Universal Cover

title: Definition:Universal Affirmative
snippet: A universal affirmative is a categorical statement of the form: Every $S$ is $P$ where $S$ and $P$ are predicates. In the language of predicate logic, this can be expressed as: $\forall x: \map S x \implies \map P x$ Its meaning can be amplified in natural language as: Every object which has the property of being $S$ also has the property of being $P$.

title: Definition:Universal Affirmative/Also denoted as
snippet: == Universal Affirmative: Also denoted as == Traditional logic abbreviated the universal affirmative as $\mathbf A$. Thus, when examining the categorical syllogism, the universal affirmative $\forall x: \map S x \implies \map P x$ is often abbreviated: $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P}$

title: Definition:Universal Affirmative/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Universal Affirmative == The abbreviation $\mathbf A$ for a universal affirmative originates from the first vowel in the Latin word Affirmo, meaning I affirm.

title: Definition:Universal Affirmative/Set Theory
snippet: The universal affirmative $\forall x: \map S x \implies \map P x$ can be expressed in set language as: $\set {x: \map S x} \subseteq \set {x: \map P x}$ or, more compactly: $S \subseteq P$

title: Definition:Universal Bounds
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $S$ have a smallest element, $\bot$. Let $S$ have a greatest element, $\top$. Then $\bot$ and $\top$ are the universal bounds of $S$.

title: Definition:Universal Class
snippet: The universal class is the class of which all sets are elements. The universal class is defined most commonly in literature as: $V = \set {x: x = x}$ where $x$ ranges over all sets. It can be briefly defined as the class of all sets.

title: Definition:Universal Class/Notation
snippet: == Universal Class: Notation == The use of $V$ as the symbol used to denote the universal class follows the presentation by and , in their . Much of the literature uses $U$ and its variants, for example $\Bbb U$. However, as $U$ is often used to denote the universal set, prefers to use $V$ for the universal class in order to reduce confusion between the two. The symbol $\mathfrak A$ is also seen in older literature; however, the number of those who still like using this awkward and difficult-to-read Germanic font is decreasing. Category:Definitions/Universal Class

title: Definition:Universal Class/Zermelo-Fraenkel Theory
snippet: == Universal Class in Zermelo-Fraenkel Set Theory == If the universal class is allowed to be a set in ZFC, then a contradiction can be derived. One equivalent of the states that: $\forall z: \forall A: \paren {A \subseteq z \implies A \in V}$ Since the universal class contains all classes, then if we assume that it is the value of some variable $z$, then all classes become elements of the universe. However, due to Russell's Paradox, this cannot be the case. Therefore, comprehension of the universal set leads to a contradiction and cannot be a value of a variable in ZF set theory.

title: Definition:Universal Closure of Well-Formed Formula
snippet: Let $\LL_1$ be the language of predicate logic. Let $\mathbf A$ be a well-formed formula of $\LL_1$. A universal closure of $\mathbf A$ is a sentence $\mathbf B$ of $\LL_1$ of the form: $\forall x_1: \cdots \forall x_n: \mathbf A$ By definition of sentence, this means that at least the variables occurring freely in $\mathbf A$ should be quantified over.

title: Definition:Universal Cover
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $C = \struct {X, \phi}$ be a covering space for $T$. Then $C$ is a universal cover for $T$ $C$ is simply connected.

title: Definition:Universal Cover/Also known as
snippet: == Universal Cover: Also known as == A universal cover is also known as a universal covering space.

title: Definition:Universal Gas Constant
snippet: The universal gas constant is a constant of proportion that relates the average relative thermal energy of a mole of gas with the thermodynamic temperature of the gas. It is defined as Avogadro's number multiplied by Boltzmann's constant: $R = N_{\mathrm A} k$

title: Definition:Universal Gas Constant/Also known as
snippet: == Universal Gas Constant: Also known as == The universal gas constant is also known as: the molar gas constant the ideal gas constant the gas constant.

title: Definition:Universal Gas Constant/Dimension
snippet: == Dimension of Universal Gas Constant == The universal gas constant has the dimension $\mathsf {M L^2 T^{-2} \Theta^{-1} N^{-1} }$. Category:Definitions/Universal Gas Constant Category:Definitions/Dimensions of Measurement

title: Definition:Universal Gas Constant/Units
snippet: The SI unit for the universal gas constant is given as joules per kelvin per mole: $\mathrm {J \, K^{-1} \, mol^{-1} }$ where: $\mathrm J$ denotes the joule $\mathrm K$ denotes the kelvin $\mathrm {mol}$ denotes the mole. Category:Definitions/Units of Measurement Category:Definitions/Universal Gas Constant

title: Definition:Universal Graph
snippet: Let $\Bbb G$ be a set of graphs. A universal graph in $\Bbb G$ is a graph $K$ in which every element of $\Bbb G$ can be embedded in $K$. Note that $K$ need not itself be an element of $\Bbb G$.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant
snippet: == Physical Constant == The universal gravitational constant is the physical constant which is the constant of proportion in Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation. Its value in SI units is referred to as $G$ and is approximately equal to $6.674 \times 10^{-11} \, \mathrm N \, \mathrm m^2 \, \mathrm{kg}^{-2}$.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Also known as
snippet: == Universal Gravitational Constant: Also known as == The universal gravitational constant can also be seen referred to as the gravitational constant, but this is ambiguous. The more wordy term universal constant of gravitation can also be seen.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Dimension
snippet: == Dimension of Universal Gravitational Constant == The universal gravitational constant has the dimension $\mathsf {M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2} }$.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Universal Gravitational Constant == When formulated his Law of Universal Gravitation, he did not know, and had no immediate means to determine, what the universal gravitational constant $G$ actually is. The value of $G$ was determined in $1789$ by in what is now known as the Cavendish experiment.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Symbol
snippet: == Universal Gravitational Constant: Symbol == The symbol for the universal gravitational constant is $G$.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Symbol/Also denoted as
snippet: == Universal Gravitational Constant: Symbol == The symbol for the universal gravitational constant can be presented as $\gamma$.

title: Definition:Universal Gravitational Constant/Units
snippet: The SI unit for the universal gravitational Constant is given as newton square metres per kilogram squared: $\mathrm {N \, m^2 \, kg^{-2} }$ where: $\mathrm N$ denotes the newton $\mathrm m$ denotes the metre $\mathrm {kg}$ denotes the kilogram. Category:Definitions/Units of Measurement Category:Definitions/Universal Gravitational Constant

title: Definition:Universal Mapping Property (Category Theory)
snippet: A universal mapping property (or UMP) in category theory is a property that defines how morphisms from or to objects factor uniquely through a unique morphism and object.

title: Definition:Universal Model
snippet: Let $T$ be an $\LL$-theory. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite cardinal. A model $\MM$ of $T$ is $\kappa$-universal : for every model $\NN$ of $T$ whose universe has cardinality strictly less than $\kappa$, there is an elementary embedding of $\NN$ into $\MM$. That is, $\MM$ is $\kappa$-universal : for all models $\NN \models T$ with cardinality $\card \NN < \kappa$, there is an elementary embedding $j: \NN \to \MM$. We say $\MM$ is universal it is $\kappa^+$-universal where $\kappa$ is the cardinality of the universe of $\MM$ and $\kappa^+$ is the successor cardinal of $\kappa$.

title: Definition:Universal Morphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor.

title: Definition:Universal Morphism from Functor to Object

title: Definition:Universal Morphism from Functor to Object/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let the pair $\tuple{R, v}$ consist of an object $R$ of $\mathbf D$ and a morphism $v: FR \to C$ in $\mathbf C$. The pair $\tuple{R, v}$ is called a universal morphism from $F$ to $C$ : $\tuple{R, v}$ is a terminal object of the comma category $\paren{F \downarrow C}$ of $F$ over $C$

title: Definition:Universal Morphism from Object to Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let the pair $\tuple{R, u}$ consist of an object $R$ of $\mathbf D$ and a morphism $u: C \to FR$ in $\mathbf C$.

Let the pair $\tuple{R, u}$ consist of an object $R$ of $\mathbf D$ and a morphism $u: C \to FR$ in $\mathbf C$. The pair $\tuple{R, u}$ is called a universal morphism from $C$ to $F$ : for every pair $\tuple{D, f}$ consisting of an object $D$ of $\mathbf D$ and a morphism $f: C \to FD$ in $\mathbf C$: there exists a unique morphism $f': R \to D$ with $Ff' \circ u = f$ as in the commutative diagram: $\begin{xy} +{C} = "C", +{F R} = "FR", +{F D} =…

title: Definition:Universal Morphism from Object to Functor/Definition 2
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let the pair $\tuple{R, u}$ consist of an object $R$ of $\mathbf D$ and a morphism $u: C \to FR$ in $C$. The pair $\tuple{R, u}$ is called a universal morphism from $C$ to $F$ : $\tuple{R, u}$ is an initial object of the comma category $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ of $F$ under $C$

title: Definition:Universal Negative
snippet: A universal negative is a categorical statement of the form: No $S$ is $P$ where $S$ and $P$ are predicates. In the language of predicate logic, this can be expressed as: $\forall x: \map S x \implies \neg \map P x$ Its meaning can be amplified in natural language as: Every object which has the property of being $S$ does not have the property of being $P$.

title: Definition:Universal Negative/Also denoted as
snippet: == Universal Negative: Also denoted as == Traditional logic abbreviated the universal negative as $\mathbf E$. Thus, when examining the categorical syllogism, the universal negative $\forall x: \map S x \implies \neg \map P x$ is often abbreviated: $\map {\mathbf E} {S, P}$

title: Definition:Universal Negative/Linguistic Note
snippet: == Linguistic Note on Universal Negative == The abbreviation $\mathbf E$ for a universal negative originates from the first vowel in the Latin word nEgo, meaning I deny.

title: Definition:Universal Negative/Set Theory
snippet: The universal negative $\forall x: \map S x \implies \neg \map P x$ can be expressed in set language as: $\set {x: \map S x} \implies \set {x: \map P x} = \O$ or, more compactly: $S \subseteq \map \complement P$

title: Definition:Universal Net
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $H$ be a set directed by $\preceq$. Let $f: H \to S$ be a net in $S$. Then $f$ is a universal net for each subset $A \subseteq S$, $f$ is eventually in $A$ or $f$ is eventually in $S \setminus A$. Category:Definitions/Set Theory Category:Definitions/Topology

title: Definition:Universal Object
snippet: Let $C$ be a category. A universal object of $C$ is an object that is initial or terminal.

title: Definition:Universal Quantifier
snippet: The symbol $\forall$ is called the universal quantifier. It expresses the fact that, in a particular universe of discourse, all objects have a particular property. That is: $\forall x:$ means: For all objects $x$, it is true that ... In the language of set theory, this can be formally defined: $\forall x \in S: \map P x := \set {x \in S: \map P x} = S$ where $S$ is some set and $\map P x$ is a propositional function on $S$.

title: Definition:Universal Quantifier/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Universal Quantifier == The symbol $\forall$ for the universal quantifier was first used by in . He invented it in analogy with the existential quantifier symbol $\exists$ which he borrowed from . himself used the notation $\paren x$ for for all $x$. See his .
