title: Diagonals of Rhombus Bisect Each Other at Right Angles
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a rhombus. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of $ABCD$ bisect each other at right angles.

title: Diagonals of Rhombus Intersect at Right Angles
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a rhombus. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of $ABCD$ intersect each other at right angles.

title: Diameter of Circle is Axis of Bilateral Symmetry
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle. Let $D$ be a diameter of $C$. Then $O$ is an axis of bilateral symmetry for $C$.

title: Diameter of Closure of Subset is Diameter of Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $S \subseteq A$ be bounded in $M$. Then: $\map \diam S = \map \diam {S^-}$ where $\map \diam S$ denotes the diameter of $S$, and $S^-$ denotes the closure of $S$ in $M$.

title: Diameter of N-Cube
snippet: Let $Q_n = \closedint {c - R} {c + R}^n$ be an $n$-cube in Euclidean $n$-Space equipped with the usual metric. Then the diameter of $Q_n$ is given by: $\map \diam {Q_n} = 2 R \sqrt n$

title: Diameters of Circle are all Equal
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle of radius $r$. Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be arbitrary diameters of $\CC$. Then: $D_1 = D_2 = 2 r$ That is, all diameters of $\CC$ are the same length and equal to twice the radius.

title: Diameters of Parallelogram Bisect each other
snippet: Let $\Box ABCD$ be a parallelogram with diameters $AC$ and $BD$. Let $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$. Then $E$ is the midpoint of both $AC$ and $BD$.

title: Diameters of Sphere are all Equal
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a sphere of radius $r$. Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be arbitrary diameters of $\SS$. Then: $D_1 = D_2 = 2 r$ That is, all diameters of $\SS$ are the same length and equal to twice the radius.

title: Dichotomy Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Motion is impossible. Suppose $B$ is a body which is to move from $P$ to $Q$. Before $B$ can reach $Q$, it must first move halfway to $Q$. But before it can reach the midpoint between $P$ and $Q$, it must first move halfway to that midpoint. And before it can reach the point half way to the midpoint, it has to move halfway to that point too. So on, indefinitely. It is therefore impossible for motion to happen, because you cannot even get started. Every time you try to reach a point, you have to reach the point half way before it first.

title: Dicyclic Group Dic3/Matrix Representation
snippet: == Matrix Representation of Dicyclic Group $\Dic 3$ == Let $\omega$ denote the complex number $\map \exp {\dfrac {2 \pi i} 6}$, so that $\omega^6 = 1$. Let $\mathbf X$ be the matrix defined as: $\mathbf X = \begin{bmatrix} \omega & 0 \\ 0 & \omega^{-1} \end{bmatrix}$ Let $\mathbf Y$ be the matrix defined such that: $\mathbf X \mathbf Y = \mathbf Y \mathbf X^{-1}$ and: $\mathbf Y^2 = \mathbf X^3$ Then the set: $G = \set {\mathbf X^i, \mathbf Y \mathbf X^j: 1 \le i, j \le 6}$ defines the dicyclic group $\Dic 3$.

title: Dicyclic Group is Non-Abelian Group
snippet: The dicyclic group $\Dic n$ is a non-abelian group on two generators.

title: Dido's Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == The new is to be founded. Its area is to be determined by enclosing as much land as possible within a line whose length is fixed. What shape should it be to make sure the area is a maximum?

title: Dieudonné Plank is Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Dieudonné plank. Then $T$ is metacompact.

title: Dieudonné Plank is not Countably Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Dieudonné plank. Then $T$ is not countably paracompact.

title: Dieudonné Plank is not Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Dieudonné plank. Then $T$ is not paracompact.

title: Difference Between Adjacent Polygonal Numbers is Triangular Number
snippet: Let $\map P {k, n}$ be the $n$th $k$-gonal number. Then: $\map P {k + 1, n} - \map P {k, n} = T_{n - 1}$ where $T_n$ is the $n$th triangular number.

title: Difference Between Adjacent Square Roots Converges
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as $x_n = \sqrt {n + 1} - \sqrt n$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to a zero limit.

title: Difference Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Difference Equations ==

title: Difference Sequence of Quadratic Sequence is Arithmetic Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {u_n}$ be a quadratic sequence. Then its difference sequence is an arithmetic sequence.

title: Difference Triangle for Sequence of Fifth Powers
snippet: The difference triangle for the sequence of fifth powers ends on the fifth line with instances of $5!$, where $!$ denotes factorial.

title: Difference between 2 Consecutive Cubes is Odd
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be consecutive integers. Then $b^3 - a^3$ is odd.

title: Difference between Adjacent Convergents But One of Simple Continued Fraction
snippet: Let $n \in \N \cup \set \infty$ be an extended natural number. Let $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$ be a continued fraction in $\R$ of length $n$. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Let $C_0, C_1, C_2, \ldots$ be the convergents of $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$. For $k \ge 2$: $p_k q_{k - 2} - p_{k - 2} q_k = \paren {-1}^k a_k$ That is: $C_k - C_{k-2} = \dfrac {p_k} {q_k} - \dfrac {p_{k - 2} } {q_{k - 2} } = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^k a_k} {q_k q_{k - 2} }$

title: Difference between Adjacent Convergents of Simple Continued Fraction
snippet: Let $n \in \N \cup \set \infty$ be an extended natural number. Let $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$ be a continued fraction in $\R$ of length $n$. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Let $C_0, C_1, C_2, \ldots$ be the convergents of $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$. Then for $k \ge 1$: $p_k q_{k - 1} - p_{k - 1} q_k = \paren {-1}^{k + 1}$ That is: $C_k - C_{k - 1} = \dfrac {p_k} {q_k} - \dfrac {p_{k - 1} } {q_{k - 1} } = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^{k + 1} } {q_k q_{k - 1} }$

title: Difference between Adjacent Terms of Farey Sequence
snippet: == Theroem == Let $F_n$ be a Farey sequence of order $n$. Let $\dfrac a b$ and $\dfrac c d$ be consecutive terms of $F_n$ such that $\dfrac a b < \dfrac c d$. Then: $\dfrac c d - \dfrac a b = \dfrac 1 {b d}$ or equivalently: $b c - a d = 1$

title: Difference between Distances from Point on Hyperbola to Foci is Constant
snippet: Let $K$ be a hyperbola. Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the foci of $K$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $K$. Then the distance from $P$ to $F_1$ minus the distance from $P$ to $F_2$ is constant for all $P$ on $K$.

title: Difference between Kaprekar Number and Square is Multiple of Repunit
snippet: Let $n$ be a Kaprekar number of $m$ digits. Then: $n^2 - n = k R_m$ where: $R_m$ is the $m$-digit repunit $k$ is an integer.

title: Difference between Odd Squares is Divisible by 8
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be odd integers. Then $a^2 - b^2$ is divisible by $8$.

title: Difference between Summation of Natural Logarithms and Summation of Harmonic Numbers
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k - \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \map \ln {n!} \approx \gamma n + \dfrac {\ln n} 2 + 0 \cdotp 158$ where: $H_k$ denotes the $k$th harmonic number $n!$ denotes the $n$th factorial $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Difference between Terms of Wythoff Pair
snippet: Let $\tuple {\floor {k \phi}, \floor {k \phi^2} }$ be a Wythoff pair. The difference between the coordinates of this Wythoff pair is $k$. That is: $\floor {k \phi^2} - \floor {k \phi} = k$

title: Difference between Two Squares equal to Repdigit
snippet: Some differences of two squares that each make a repdigit number include:

title: Difference between Two Squares equal to Repunit
snippet: The sequence of differences of two squares that each make a repunit begins:

title: Difference in Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $n, m \in S$ such that $m \preceq n$. Then there exists a unique difference $n - m$ of $m$ and $n$.

title: Difference is Rational is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Define $\sim$ as the relation on real numbers given by: $x \sim y \iff x - y \in \Q$ That is, that the difference between $x$ and $y$ is rational. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Difference of Abscissae of Convergence
snippet: Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$ be a Dirichlet series. Suppose that $\map f s$ has finite Abscissa of Convergence $\sigma_c$. Then the Abscissa of Absolute Convergence $\sigma_a$ is finite, and: $0 \le \sigma_a - \sigma_c \le 1$

title: Difference of Absolutely Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ be two real or complex series that are absolutely convergent. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {a_n - b_n}$ is absolutely convergent, and: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {a_n - b_n} = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n - \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$

title: Difference of Arccotangents
snippet: $\arccot a - \arccot b = \arccot \dfrac {a b + 1} {a - b}$ where $\arccot$ denotes the arccotangent.

title: Difference of Arctangents
snippet: Let $\arctan a - \arctan b \in \openint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ Then: $\arctan a - \arctan b = \arctan \dfrac {a - b} {1 + a b}$ where $\arctan$ denotes the arctangent.

title: Difference of Complex Conjugates
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of the complex number $z$. Then: $\overline {z_1 - z_2} = \overline {z_1} - \overline {z_2}$

title: Difference of Complex Number with Conjugate
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Let $\map \Im z$ be the imaginary part of $z$. Then $z - \overline z = 2 i \, \map \Im z$

title: Difference of Consecutive terms of Coherent Sequence
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ be a coherent sequence. Then: for all $n \in \N_{>0}$ there exists $c_n \in \N$ such that: $0 \le c_n < p$ $\alpha_n - \alpha_{n - 1} = c_n p^n$

title: Difference of Even Powers of z + a and z - a
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer such that $m > 1$. Then for all complex number $z$: $\paren {z + a}^{2 m} - \paren {z - a}^{2 m} = 4 m a z \ds \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^{m - 1} \paren {z^2 + a^2 \cot^2 \dfrac {k \pi} {2 m} }$

title: Difference of Fourth Powers of Cosine and Sine
snippet: $\sin^4 x - \cos^4 x = \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x$ where $\sin$ and $\cos$ denote sine and cosine respectively.

title: Difference of Fourth Powers of Secant and Tangent
snippet: $\sec^4 x - \tan^4 x = \sec^2 x + \tan^2 x$

title: Difference of Functions of Bounded Variation is of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f, g : \closedint a b \to \R$ be functions of bounded variation. Let $\map {V_f} {\closedint a b}$ and $\map {V_g} {\closedint a b}$ be the total variations of $f$ and $g$ respectively, on $\closedint a b$. Then $f - g$ is of bounded variation with: $\map {V_{f - g} } {\closedint a b} \le \map {V_f} {\closedint a b} + \map {V_g} {\closedint a b}$ where $V_{f - g}$ denotes the total variation of $f - g$ on $\closedint a b$.

title: Difference of Images under Mapping not necessarily equal to Image of Difference
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. The image of the set difference of two subsets of $S$ is not necessarily equal to the set difference of the images. That is: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then it is not always the case that: $f \sqbrk {S_1} \setminus f \sqbrk {S_2} = f \sqbrk {S_1 \setminus S_2}$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Difference of Logarithms
snippet: Let $x, y, b \in \R$ be strictly positive real numbers such that $b > 1$. Then: $\log_b x - \log_b y = \map {\log_b} {\dfrac x y}$ where $\log_b$ denotes the logarithm to base $b$.

title: Difference of Positive and Negative Parts
snippet: Let $X$ be a set, and let $f: X \to \overline{\R}$ be an extended real-valued function. Let $f^+$, $f^-: X \to \overline{\R}$ be the positive and negative parts of $f$, respectively. Then $f = f^+ - f^-$.

title: Difference of Projections
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $P, Q$ be projections.

title: Difference of Reciprocals of One Plus and Minus Sine
snippet: $\ds \frac 1 {1 - \sin x} - \frac 1 {1 + \sin x} = 2 \tan x \sec x$

title: Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent/Also presented as
snippet: == Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent: Also presented as == Difference of Squares of Cosecant and Cotangent can also be presented as: $\csc^2 x = 1 + \cot^2 x \quad \text{(when $\sin x \ne 0$)}$ or: $\cot^2 x = \csc^2 x - 1 \quad \text{(when $\sin x \ne 0$)}$

title: Difference of Squares of Hyperbolic Cosine and Sine
snippet: $\cosh^2 x - \sinh^2 x = 1$ where $\cosh$ and $\sinh$ are hyperbolic cosine and hyperbolic sine.

title: Difference of Squares of Hyperbolic Cotangent and Cosecant
snippet: $\coth^2 x - \csch^2 x = 1$ where $\coth$ and $\csch$ are hyperbolic cotangent and hyperbolic cosecant.

title: Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent/Also presented as
snippet: == Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent: Also presented as == Difference of Squares of Secant and Tangent can also be presented as: $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x \quad \text {(when $\cos x \ne 0$)}$ or: $\tan^2 x = \sec^2 x - 1 \quad \text {(when $\cos x \ne 0$)}$

title: Difference of Squares of Sines
snippet: $\sin^2 A - \sin^2 B = \map \sin {A + B} \map \sin {A - B}$

title: Difference of Squares of Sum and Difference
snippet: $\forall a, b \in \R: \paren {a + b}^2 - \paren {a - b}^2 = 4 a b$

title: Difference of Two Even-Times Odd Powers
snippet: Let $\F$ be one of the standard number systems, that is $\Z, \Q, \R$ and so on. Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive odd integer. Then: {{eqn | l = a^{2 n} - b^{2 n} | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a + b} \paren {\sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} a^{n - j - 1} b^j} \paren {\sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {-1}^j a^{n - j - 1} b^j} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a + b} \paren {a^{n - 1} + a^{n - 2} b + a^{n - 3} b^2 + \dotsb + a b^{n - 2} + b^{n - 1} } \paren {a^{n - 1} - a^{n - 2} b + a^{n - 3} b^2 - \dotsb - a b^{n - 2} + b^{n - 1} } | c = }}

title: Difference of Two Even Powers
snippet: Let $\GF$ denote one of the standard number systems, that is $\Z$, $\Q$, $\R$ and $\C$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then for all $a, b \in \GF$: {{eqn | l = a^{2 n} - b^{2 n} | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a + b} \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} a^{2 \paren {n - j - 1} } b^{2 j} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a + b} \paren {a^{2 n - 2} + a^{2 n - 4} b^2 + a^{2 n - 6} b^4 + \dotsb + a^2 b^{2 n - 4} + b^{2 n - 2} } | c = }}

title: Difference of Two Fifth Powers
snippet: $x^5 - y^5 = \paren {x - y} \paren {x^4 + x^3 y + x^2 y^2 + x y^3 + y^4}$

title: Difference of Two Fourth Powers
snippet: $x^4 - y^4 = \paren {x - y} \paren {x + y} \paren {x^2 + y^2}$

title: Difference of Two Odd Powers
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ denote one of the standard number systems, that is $\Z$, $\Q$, $\R$ and $\C$. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb F$: {{eqn | l = a^{2 n + 1} - b^{2 n + 1} | r = \paren {a - b} \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{2 n} a^{2 n - j} b^j | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a^{2 n} + a^{2 n - 1} b + a^{2 n - 2} b^2 + \dotsb + a b^{2 n - 1} + b^{2 n} } | c = }}

title: Difference of Two Powers
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ denote one of the standard number systems, that is $\Z$, $\Q$, $\R$ and $\C$. Let $n \in \N$ such that $n \ge 2$. Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb F$: {{eqn | l = a^n - b^n | r = \paren {a - b} \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} a^{n - j - 1} b^j | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {a - b} \paren {a^{n - 1} + a^{n - 2} b + a^{n - 3} b^2 + \dotsb + a b^{n - 2} + b^{n - 1} } | c = }} For convenience of applicability, these results are sometimes separated into two cases for odd and even indices:

title: Difference of Two Sixth Powers
snippet: $x^6 - y^6 = \paren {x - y} \paren {x + y} \paren {x^2 + x y + y^2} \paren {x^2 - x y + y^2}$

title: Difference of Two Squares
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $x, y \in R$. Then: $x \circ x + \paren {- \paren {y \circ y} } = \paren {x + y} \circ \paren {x + \paren {-y} }$ When $R$ is one of the standard sets of numbers, that is $\Z, \Q, \R$, and so on, then this translates into: $x^2 - y^2 = \paren {x + y} \paren {x - y}$

title: Difference of Two Squares cannot equal 2 modulo 4
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be of the form $4 k + 2$ for some $k \in \Z$. Then $n$ cannot be expressed in the form: $n = a^2 - b^2$ for $a, b \in \Z$.

title: Difference of Unbounded Closed Intervals
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ have $a < b$. Then: $\hointl {-\infty} b \setminus \hointl {-\infty} a = \hointl a b$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Difference of Unions is Subset of Union of Differences
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $S_\alpha, T_\alpha$ be sets, for all $\alpha \in I$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha} \setminus \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} T_\alpha} \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \paren {S_\alpha \setminus T_\alpha}$ where $S_\alpha \setminus T_\alpha$ denotes set difference.

title: Different Latitude and Longitude on Same Meridian
snippet: == Problem == There are $3$ remarkable places on the globe that differ in latitude, as well as in longitude; and yet, all of them lie under the same meridian.

title: Different Representations to Number Base represent Different Integers
snippet: Let $k \in \Z$ such that $k \ge 2$. Let $a$ and $b$ be representations of integers in base $k$ notation: $a = \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^r a_j k^j$ $b = \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^s b_j k^j$ such that either: $r \ne s$ or: $\exists j \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, r}: a_j \ne b_j$ Then $a$ and $b$ represent different integers.

title: Differentiability Class/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Differentiability Classes ==

title: Differentiability Class is Subset of Differentiability Class of Lower Order
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $f$ be an element of differentiability class $C^n$. Then: $\forall k \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, n - 1}: f \in C^k$ That is, $f$ is in all differentiability classes of order less than $n$.

title: Differentiability of Function at Essential Singularity
snippet: Let $f$ be a complex function with an essential singularity at $z_0 \in \C$. Then $\map f z \paren {z - z_0}^n$ is not differentiable at $z_0$ for all $n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Differentiability of Function with Translation Property
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $f$ have the translation property. Let $c$ be a real number. Let $\map {f'} c$ exist. Then: $f'$ exists $f'$ is a constant function

title: Differentiability under Integral Sign
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\openint a b$ be a non-empty open interval. Let $f: \openint a b \times X \to \R$ be a mapping satisfying: $(1): \quad$ For all $t \in \openint a b$, the mapping $x \mapsto \map f {t, x}$ is $\mu$-integrable $(2): \quad$ For all $x \in X$, the mapping $t \mapsto \map f {t, x}$ is differentiable $(3): \quad$ There exists a $\mu$-integrable $g: X \to \R$ such that: $\ds \forall \tuple {t, x} \in \openint a b \times X: \size {\frac \partial {\partial t} \map f {t, x} } \le \map g x$ Then the mapping $h: \openint a b \to \R$ defined by: $\ds…

title: Differentiable Bounded Concave Real Function is Constant
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is: $(1): \quad$ differentiable on $\R$ $(2): \quad$ bounded on $\R$ $(3): \quad$ concave on $\R$. Then $f$ is constant.

title: Differentiable Bounded Convex Real Function is Constant
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is: $(1): \quad$ differentiable on $\R$ $(2): \quad$ bounded on $\R$ $(3): \quad$ convex on $\R$. Then $f$ is constant.

title: Differentiable Function as Distribution
snippet: Let $T \in \map {\DD'} \R$ be a Schwartz distribution. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a continuously differentiable real function. Suppose $T_f$ is a Schwartz distribution identified with $f$. Then $T_f' = T_{f'}$.

title: Differentiable Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $I$. Let $x_0 \in I$ such that $f$ is differentiable at $x_0$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x_0$.

title: Differentiable Function of Bounded Variation may not have Bounded Derivative
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a continuous function of bounded variation. Let $f$ be differentiable on $\openint a b$. Then $f'$ is not necessarily bounded.

title: Differentiable Function with Bounded Derivative is Absolutely Continuous
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a continuous function. Let $f$ be differentiable on $\openint a b$, with bounded derivative. Then $f$ is absolutely continuous.

title: Differentiable Function with Bounded Derivative is of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a continuous function. Let $f$ be differentiable on $\openint a b$, with bounded derivative. Then $f$ is of bounded variation.

title: Differentiable Operator-Valued Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $f : I \to X$ be a map defined on an interval $I$. Let $x_0 \in I$ such that $f$ is differentiable at $x_0$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x_0$.

title: Differentiable Structure Contains Unique Maximal Atlas
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological space. Let $k$ and $d$ be natural numbers. Let $S$ be a $d$-dimensional differentiable structure of class $C^k$ on $M$. Then $S$ contains a unique maximal $C^k$-atlas.

title: Differential Entropy of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$ for some $a, b \in \R$, $a \ne b$, where $\operatorname U$ is the continuous uniform distribution. Then the differential entropy of $X$, $\map h X$, is given by: $\map h X = \map \ln {b - a}$

title: Differential Entropy of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable of the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$ for some $\beta \in \R_{> 0}$. Then the differential entropy of $X$, $\map h X$, is given by: $\map h X = 1 + \map \ln \beta$

title: Differential Entropy of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution. Then the differential entropy $\map h X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map h X = \map \ln {\sigma \sqrt {2 \pi} } + \dfrac 1 2$

title: Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Differential Equations ==

title: Differential Equation defining Confocal Conics
snippet: Consider the equation: $(1): \quad \dfrac {x^2} {a^2 + \lambda} + \dfrac {y^2} {b^2 + \lambda} = 1$ where $a^2 > b^2$ and $-\lambda < a^2$. defining the set of confocal conics whose foci are at $\tuple {\pm \sqrt {a^2 - b^2}, 0}$. The differential equation defining these confocal conics is: $x y \paren {\paren {y'}^2 - 1} + \paren {x^2 - y^2 - a^2 + b^2} y' = 0$

title: Differential Equation governing First-Order Reaction
snippet: Let a substance decompose spontaneously in a first-order reaction. The differential equation which governs this reaction is given by: $-\dfrac {\d x} {\d t} = k x$ where: $x$ determines the quantity of substance at time $t$. $k \in \R_{>0}$.

title: Differential Equation governing Simple Harmonic Motion
snippet: Let $B$ be a body undergoing simple harmonic motion in a straight line. Then its motion can be described using the equation: $\dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d x^2} = -\omega^2 x$

title: Differential Equation of Family of Linear Combination of Functions is Linear
snippet: Consider the one-parameter family of curves: $(1): \quad y = C \map f x + \map g x$ The differential equation that describes $(1)$ is linear and of first order.

title: Differential Equation of Perpendicular Pursuit Curve
snippet: == Therorem == Let a $R$ be situated at the origin of a cartesian plane. Let a $D$ be situated at the point $\tuple {c, 0}$. Let $R$ start running up the $y$-axis with speed $a$. At the same instant, let $D$ start pursuing $R$ by running directly towards it at speed $b$. Then the differential equation describing the path taken by $D$ is: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \dfrac 1 2 \paren {\paren {\dfrac x c}^k - \paren {\dfrac c x}^k}$ where $k = \dfrac a b$.

title: Differential Equation satisfied by Weierstrass's Elliptic Function
snippet: The differential equation: $\paren {\dfrac {\d f} {\d z} }^2 = 4 f^3 - g_2 f - g_3$ where: $\ds g_2 = 60 \sum_{\tuple {n, m} \mathop \in \Z^2 \setminus \tuple {0, 0} } \frac 1 {\paren {2 m \omega_1 + 2 n \omega_2}^4}$ and: $\ds g_3 = 140 \sum_{\tuple {n, m} \mathop \in \Z^2 \setminus \tuple {0, 0} } \frac 1 {\paren {2 m \omega_1 + 2 n \omega_2}^6}$ has the general solution: $\map f z = \map \wp {z + C; \omega_1, \omega_2}$ where: $\wp$ is Weierstrass's elliptic function $C$ is an arbitrary constant $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$ are constants independent of $z$.

title: Differential Equations for Shortest Path on 3d Sphere/Cartesian Coordinates
snippet: Let $M$ be a $3$-dimensional Euclidean space. Let $S$ be a sphere embedded in $M$. Let $\gamma$ be a curve on $S$. Let the chosen coordinate system be Cartesian. Let $\gamma$ begin at $\paren {x_0, y_0, z_0}$ and terminate at $\paren {x_1, y_1, z_1}$. Let $\map y x$, $\map z x$ be real functions. Let $\gamma$ connecting both endpoints be of minimum length. Then $\gamma$ satisfies the following equations of motion: $2 y \map \lambda x - \dfrac \d {\d x} \dfrac {y'} {\sqrt {1 + y'^2 + z'^2} } = 0$ $2 z \map \lambda x - \dfrac \d {\d x} \dfrac {z'} {\sqrt {1 + y'^2 + z'^2} } = 0$

title: Differential Form/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Differential Forms ==

title: Differential Form of Arc Length on Curved Surface
snippet: The first fundamental form for the element of arc length on a curved surface is given by: $\d s^2 = E \rd u^2 + 2 F \d u \rd v + G \rd v^2$ where $E$, $F$ and $G$ are the coefficients of the first fundamental form.

title: Differential Geometry/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Differential Geometry ==

title: Differential of Arctangent of Quotient
snippet: $\map \d {\arctan \dfrac x y} = \dfrac {y \rd x - x \rd y} {x^2 + y^2}$

title: Differential of Differentiable Functional is Unique
snippet: The differential of a differentiable functional is unique.

title: Differential of Logarithm of Quotient
snippet: $\map \d {\ln \dfrac x y} = \dfrac {y \rd x - x \rd y} {x y}$

title: Differential of Real-Valued Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Differentials of Real-Valued Functions ==

title: Differential of Sum of Squares
snippet: $\map \d {x^2 + y^2} = 2 \paren {x \map \rd x + y \map \rd y}$

title: Differentiation of Exponential of a x by Cosine of b x and Exponential of a x by Sine of b x wrt x as Nonsingular Matrix
snippet: Let $a, b, x \in \R$ be real numbers. Suppose $a \ne 0 \ne b$. Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be the real functions defined as: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \R | l = \map {f_1} x | r = \map \exp {a x} \map \cos {b x} }} {{eqn | l = \map {f_2} x | r = \map \exp {a x} \map \sin {b x} }} Let $\map \CC \R$ be the space of continuous real-valued functions. Let $\struct {\map {\CC^1} \R, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the vector space of continuously differentiable real-valued functions. Let $S = \span \set {f_1, f_2} \subset \map {\CC^1} \R$ be a vector space. Let $D : S \to S$ be the derivative $x$.

title: Differentiation of Polynomials induces Well-Founded Relation
snippet: Let $P$ be the set of all polynomials over $\R$ in one variable with real coefficients. Let $\DD$ be a relation on $P$ defined as: $\forall p_0, p_1 \in P: \tuple {p_0, p_1} \in \DD$ $p_0$ is the derivative of $p_1$. Then $\DD$ is a well-founded relation on $P$.

title: Differentiation of Real Power Series
snippet: Let $\xi \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $\ds \sum_{m \mathop \ge 0} a_m \paren {x - \xi}^m$ be the power series in $x$ about the point $\xi$. Then within the interval of convergence: $\ds \frac {\d^n} {\d x^n} \sum_{m \mathop \ge 0} a_m \paren {x - \xi}^m = \sum_{m \mathop \ge n} a_m m^{\underline n} \paren {x - \xi}^{m - n}$ where $m^{\underline n}$ denotes the falling factorial.

title: Differentiation of Vector-Valued Function Componentwise
snippet: Let: $\mathbf r: t \mapsto \tuple {\map {r_1} t, \map {r_2} t, \ldots, \map {r_n} t}$ be a differentiable vector-valued function. The derivative of a vector-valued function can be calculated by differentiating each of its component functions: $\dfrac {\d \map {\mathbf r} t} {\d t} = \tuple {\dfrac \d {\d t} \map {r_1} t, \dfrac \d {\d t} \map {r_2} t, \ldots, \dfrac \d {\d t} \map {r_n} t}$

title: Differentiation on Polynomials is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\map P \R$ be the vector space of all polynomial functions on the real number line $\R$. Then the differentiation operator $D$ on $\map P \R$ is a linear operator.

title: Diffuse Measure of Countable Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Suppose that for all $x \in X$, the singleton $\set x$ is in $\Sigma$. Suppose further that $\mu$ is a diffuse measure. Let $E \in \Sigma$ be a countable measurable set. Then $\map \mu E = 0$.

title: Digamma Additive Formula
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ where $\N_{>0}$ denotes the non-zero natural numbers. Let $z \in \C \cap z \notin \set {-\dfrac m n: m \in \N}$ Then: $\ds \map \psi {n z} = \frac 1 n \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \map \psi {z + \frac k n} + \ln n$ where: $\psi$ is the digamma function $\ln$ is the complex natural logarithm.

title: Digamma Function in terms of General Harmonic Number
Digamma Function of Five Sixths
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 5 6} = -\gamma - 2 \ln 2 - \dfrac 3 2 \ln 3 + \dfrac {\pi \sqrt 3} 2$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of Four Fifths
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 4 5} = -\gamma - \dfrac 5 4 \ln 5 + \dfrac \pi 2 5^{-\frac 1 4} \phi^{\frac 3 2} + \paren {\dfrac 1 2 - \phi} \ln \phi$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One
snippet: $\map \psi 1 = -\gamma$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One Fifth
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 1 5} = -\gamma - \dfrac 5 4 \ln 5 - \dfrac \pi 2 5^{-\frac 1 4} \phi^{\frac 3 2} + \paren {\dfrac 1 2 - \phi} \ln \phi$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One Fourth
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 1 4} = -\gamma - 3 \ln 2 - \dfrac \pi 2$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One Half
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 1 2} = -\gamma - 2 \ln 2$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One Sixth
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 1 6} = -\gamma - 2 \ln 2 - \dfrac 3 2 \ln 3 - \dfrac {\pi \sqrt 3} 2$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of One Third
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 1 3} = -\gamma - \dfrac 3 2 \ln 3 - \dfrac \pi {2 \sqrt 3}$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of Three Fifths
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 3 5} = -\gamma - \dfrac 5 4 \ln 5 + \dfrac \pi 2 5^{-\frac 1 4} \phi^{-\frac 3 2} + \paren {\phi - \dfrac 1 2} \ln \phi$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of Three Fourths
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 3 4} = -\gamma - 3 \ln 2 + \dfrac \pi 2$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of Two Fifths
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 2 5} = -\gamma - \dfrac 5 4 \ln 5 - \dfrac \pi 2 5^{-\frac 1 4} \phi^{-\frac 3 2} + \paren {\phi - \dfrac 1 2} \ln \phi$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Function of Two Thirds
snippet: $\map \psi {\dfrac 2 3} = -\gamma - \dfrac 3 2 \ln 3 + \dfrac \pi {2 \sqrt 3}$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Digamma Reflection Formula
snippet: Let $z \in \C \setminus \Z$. Let $\psi$ denote the digamma function. Then: $\map \psi z - \map \psi {1 - z} = -\pi \cot \pi z$

title: Digital Root of 3 Consecutive Numbers ending in Multiple of 3
snippet: Let $n$, $n + 1$ and $n + 2$ be positive integers such that $n + 2$ is a multiple of $3$. Let $m = n + \paren {n + 1} + \paren {n + 2}$. Then the digital root of $m$ is $6$.

title: Digital Root of Square
snippet: Let $n^2$ be a square number. Then the digital root of $n^2$ is $1$, $4$, $7$ or $9$.

title: Digits of Permutable Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a permutable prime with more than $1$ digit. Then $p$ contains only digits from the set: $\left\{ {1, 3, 7, 9}\right\}$

title: Dihedral Group/Group Presentation
snippet: The dihedral group $D_n$ has the group presentation: $D_n = \gen {\alpha, \beta: \alpha^n = \beta^2 = e, \beta \alpha \beta = \alpha^{−1} }$ That is, the dihedral group $D_n$ is generated by two elements $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that: $(1): \quad \alpha^n = e$ $(2): \quad \beta^2 = e$ $(3): \quad \beta \alpha = \alpha^{n - 1} \beta$

title: Dihedral Group D3/Cayley Table

title: Dihedral Group D3/Group Presentation
snippet: == Group Presentation of Dihedral Group $D_3$ == The group presentation of the dihedral group $D_3$ is given by: $D_3 = \gen {a, b: a^3 = b^2 = e, a b = b a^{-1} }$

title: Dihedral Group D4/Center
snippet: == Center of the Dihedral Group $D_4$ == Let $D_4$ denote the dihedral group $D_4$, whose group presentation is given as: The center of $D_4$ is given by: $\map Z {D_4} = \set {e, a^2}$

title: Dihedral Group D4/Group Presentation
snippet: == Group Presentation of Dihedral Group $D_4$ == The group presentation of the dihedral group $D_4$ is given by: $D_4 = \gen {a, b: a^4 = b^2 = e, a b = b a^{-1} }$

title: Dihedral Group D4 is not Internal Group Product
snippet: The dihedral group $D_4$ is not an internal group product of any $2$ of its proper subgroups.

title: Dihedral Group D6 is Internal Direct Product of C2 with D3
snippet: The dihedral group $D_6$ is an internal direct product of the cyclic group $C_2$ of order $2$ and the dihedral group $D_3$: $D_6 = C_2 \times D_3$

title: Dihedral Group is Group
snippet: Let $D_n$ be the dihedral group of order $2 n$. Then $D_n$ is indeed a group.

title: Dihedral Group is Non-Abelian
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number such that $n > 2$. Let $D_n$ denote the dihedral group of order $2 n$. Then $D_n$ is not abelian.

title: Dilation Mapping on Topological Vector Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +_K, \circ_K, \tau_K}$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, +_X, \circ_X, \tau_X}$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $\lambda \in K$. Let $c_\lambda$ be the dilation by $\lambda$ mapping. Then $c_\lambda$ is continuous.

title: Dilation Mapping on Topological Vector Space is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\lambda \in K \setminus \set {0_K}$. Let $c_\lambda$ be the dilation by $\lambda$ mapping. Then $c_\lambda$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Dilation of Closed Set in Topological Vector Space is Closed Set
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $F$ be a closed set in $X$. Let $\lambda \in K \setminus \set {0_K}$. Then $\lambda F$ is a closed set in $X$.

title: Dilation of Closed Unit Ball in Normed Vector Space Decomposes as Sum of Dilations
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\lambda, \mu > 0$. Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball in $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Then: $\paren {\lambda + \mu} B_X^- = \lambda B_X^- + \mu B_X^-$

title: Dilation of Closure of Set in Topological Vector Space is Closure of Dilation
snippet: Let $F$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $F$. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $\lambda \in F \setminus \set {0_F}$. Then we have: $\lambda A^- = \paren {\lambda A}^-$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$.

title: Dilation of Compact Set in Topological Vector Space is Compact
snippet: Let $k$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $X$. Let $K$ be a compact subset of $X$. Let $t \in k \setminus \set {0_k}$. Then $t K$ is compact.

title: Dilation of Complement of Set in Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $F \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then: $X \setminus \paren {\lambda F} = \lambda \paren {X \setminus F}$

title: Dilation of Convex Set containing Zero Vector by Real Number between 0 and 1
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $C$ be a convex set with ${\mathbf 0}_X \in C$. Let $t \in \closedint 0 1$. Then: $t C \subseteq C$

title: Dilation of Convex Set in Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex subset of $X$. Let $\alpha \in \Bbb F$. Then $\alpha C$ is convex.

title: Dilation of Interior of Set in Topological Vector Space is Interior of Dilation
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $\lambda \in K \setminus \set 0$. Then we have: $\lambda A^\circ = \paren {\lambda A}^\circ$ where $A^\circ$ denotes the interior of $A$.

title: Dilation of Intersection of Subsets of Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $\family {E_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of $X$. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then: $\ds \lambda \bigcap_{\alpha \mathop \in I} E_\alpha = \bigcap_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \paren {\lambda E_\alpha}$ where $\lambda E_\alpha$ denotes the dilation of $E_\alpha$ by $\lambda$.

title: Dilation of Open Set in Normed Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $U \subseteq X$ be an open set. Let $\lambda \in \Bbb F \setminus \set 0$. Then: $\lambda U$ is open.

title: Dilation of Open Set in Topological Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\lambda \in K \setminus \set {0_K}$. Let $U$ be a open set in $X$. Then $\lambda U$, the dilation of $U$ by $\lambda$ is open.

title: Dilation of Subset of Vector Space Distributes over Sum
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$.

title: Dilation of Union of Subsets of Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $\family {E_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of $X$. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then: $\ds \lambda \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} E_\alpha = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \paren {\lambda E_\alpha}$ where $\lambda E_\alpha$ denotes the dilation of $E_\alpha$ by $\lambda$.

title: Dilations of von Neumann-Bounded Neighborhood of Origin in Topological Vector Space form Local Basis for Origin
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\sequence {\delta_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a strictly decreasing real sequence with $\delta_n \to 0$. Let $V$ be a von Neumann-bounded open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Then: $\BB = \set {\delta_n V : n \in \N}$ is a local basis for ${\mathbf 0}_X$.

title: Dilogarithm Reflection Formula
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} z + \map {\Li_2} {1 - z} = \map \zeta 2 - \map \ln z \map \ln {1 - z}$ where: $\map {\Li_2} z$ is the Dilogarithm function of $z$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$.

title: Dilogarithm of Minus Golden Mean
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {-\phi} = -\dfrac 3 5 \map \zeta 2 - \paren {\map \ln \phi}^2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Dilogarithm of Minus One
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {-1} = -\dfrac 1 2 \map \zeta 2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$.

title: Dilogarithm of Minus Reciprocal of Golden Mean
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {-\dfrac 1 \phi} = -\dfrac 2 5 \map \zeta 2 + \dfrac 1 2 \paren {\map \ln \phi}^2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Dilogarithm of Minus Z Plus Dilogarithm of Minus Reciprocal of Z
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {-z} + \map {\Li_2} {-\dfrac 1 z} = -\map \zeta 2 - \dfrac 1 2 \map {\ln^2} z$ where: $\map {\Li_2} z$ is the dilogarithm function of $z$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$.

title: Dilogarithm of One
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} 1 = \map \zeta 2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$.

title: Dilogarithm of One Half
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {\dfrac 1 2} = \dfrac 1 2 \paren {\map \zeta 2 - \paren {\map \ln 2}^2}$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$.

title: Dilogarithm of One Minus Reciprocal of Golden Mean
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {1 - \dfrac 1 \phi} = \dfrac 2 5 \map \zeta 2 - \paren {\map \ln \phi}^2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Dilogarithm of One Minus Z Plus Dilogarithm of One Minus Reciprocal of Z
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {1 - z} + \map {\Li_2} {1 - \dfrac 1 z} = -\dfrac 1 2 \map {\ln^2} z$ where: $\map {\Li_2} z$ is the Dilogarithm function of $z$ $z \in \C$ and $z < 1$.

title: Dilogarithm of Reciprocal of Golden Mean
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} {\dfrac 1 \phi} = \dfrac 3 5 \map \zeta 2 - \paren {\map \ln \phi}^2$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$ $\map \zeta 2$ is the Riemann $\zeta$ function of $2$ $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Dilogarithm of Square
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} z + \map {\Li_2} {-z} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\Li_2} {z^2}$ where $\Li_2$ denotes the dilogarithm function.

title: Dilogarithm of Zero
snippet: $\map {\Li_2} 0 = 0$ where: $\map {\Li_2} x$ is the dilogarithm function of $x$

title: Dilworth's Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a finite ordered set. Then the maximal size of an antichain is equal to the minimal number of pairwise disjoint chains in $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ that partition $S$. That is: $\min \set {k : \exists C_1, \dots C_k \subseteq S \text { chains such that } C_1 \mathop {\dot \cup} \dots \mathop {\dot \cup} C_k = S} = \max \set {\card A: A \subseteq S \text { is an antichain} }$ where $\dot \cup$ denotes disjoint union.

title: Dimension of Affine Algebraic Set is Dimension of Affine Coordinate Ring
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $Y \subseteq k^n$ be an affine algebraic set. Let $\map A Y$ be the affine coordinate ring. Then: $\map \dim Y = \map \dim {\map A Y}$ where: $\map \dim Y$ is the Krull dimension of $Y$ with respect to Zariski topology $\map \dim {\map A Y}$ is the Krull dimension of $\map A Y$

title: Dimension of Algebraic Dual
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional $R$-module. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Then $G^*$ is also $n$-dimensional.

title: Dimension of Annihilator on Algebraic Dual
snippet: Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $M$ be an $m$-dimensional subspace of $G$. Let $M^\circ$ be the annihilator of $M$. Then: $M^\circ$ is an $\paren {n - m}$-dimensional subspace of $G^*$.

title: Dimension of Bohr Radius
snippet: The Bohr radius has the dimension $\mathsf L$.

title: Dimension of Direct Product of Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let: $\ds X = \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^n X_j$ be the direct product of $X_1, \ldots, X_n$. Then: $\ds \dim X = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \map \dim {X_j}$

title: Dimension of Double Dual
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional $R$-module. Let $G^{**}$ be the double dual of $G$. Then $G^{**}$ is also $n$-dimensional.

title: Dimension of Free Vector Space on Set
snippet: Let $k$ be a division ring. Let $X$ be a set. Let $k^{\paren X}$ be the free vector space on $X$. The vector space $k^{\paren X}$ has dimension the cardinality of $X$.

title: Dimension of Hilbert Space is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Then the dimension $\dim H$ of $H$ is well-defined. That is to say, any two bases of $H$ have the same cardinality.

title: Dimension of Image of Vector Space under Linear Transformation is Bounded Above by Dimension of Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then: $\dim T \sqbrk X \le \dim X$

title: Dimension of Measurement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Dimensions of Measurement == Displacement has dimension $\mathsf L$. Velocity has dimension $\mathsf {L T}^{-1}$ (change in displacement, that is length traveled, per unit of time). Acceleration has dimension $\mathsf {L T}^{-2}$ (change in velocity per unit of time). Force has dimension $\mathsf {M L T}^{-2}$ (mass times acceleration, from Newton's Second Law of Motion). Category:Dimensions of Measurement

title: Dimension of Orthogonal Complement With Respect to Bilinear Form
snippet: Let $\mathbb K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K$ of finite dimension. Let $f$ be a nondegenerate bilinear form on $V$. Let $U\subset V$ be a subspace. Let $U^\perp$ be its orthogonal complement. Then: $\map \dim U + \map \dim U^\perp = \map \dim V$

title: Dimension of Proper Subspace is Less Than its Superspace
snippet: Let $G$ be a vector space whose dimension is $n$. Let $H$ be a subspace of $G$. Then $H$ is finite dimensional, and $\map \dim H \le \map \dim G$. If $H$ is a proper subspace of $G$, then $\map \dim H < \map \dim G$.

title: Dimension of Quotient Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $Y$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/Y$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $Y$. Then we have: $\dim Y + \map \dim {X/Y} = \dim X$ Hence $X$ is finite-dimensional both $Y$ and $X/Y$ are.

title: Dimension of R-Module R is 1
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}_R$ denote the $R$-module $R$. Then the dimension of $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}_R$ is $1$.

title: Dimension of Radical of Bilinear Form
snippet: Let $\mathbb K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K$ of finite dimension $n > 0$. Let $f$ be a bilinear form on $V$. Let $\map \Rad V$ denote the radical of $V$. Let $\map {\operatorname {rk} } f$ be the rank of $f$. Then: $\map \dim {\map \Rad V} = n - \map {\operatorname {rk} } f$ where $\dim$ denotes dimension.

title: Dimension of Rydberg Constant
snippet: The Rydberg constant has the dimension $\mathsf {L^{-1} }$.

title: Dimension of Set of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module such that $\map \dim G = n$. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module such that $\map \dim H = m$. Let $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$ be the set of all linear transformations from $G$ to $H$. Then: $\map \dim {\map {\LL_R} {G, H} } = n m$ where $\map \dim {\map {\LL_R} {G, H} }$ denotes the dimension of $\map {\LL_R} {G, H}$.

title: Dimension of Spring Force Constant
snippet: The dimension of a spring force constant is $\mathsf {M T}^{-2}$.

title: Dimension of Universal Gravitational Constant
snippet: The dimension of the universal gravitational constant $G$ is $M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}$.

title: Dimension of Vector Space of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1_F$. Let $F_n \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials over $F$ whose degree is less than $n$. Then the dimension of the vector space $F_n \sqbrk X$ is $n$.

title: Dimension of Vector Space on Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a division ring. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $\mathbf V := \struct {K^n, +, \times}_K$ be the $K$-vector space $K^n$. Then the dimension of $\mathbf V$ is $n$.

title: Dini's Theorem

Suppose that: $\forall x \in K : \sequence {\map {f_n} x}$ is monotone. Then the convergence of $\sequence {f_n}$ to $f$ is uniform.

title: Dipper Operation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Dipper Operations == Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers such that $m \ge 0, n > 0$. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $+_{m, n}$ be the dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ defined as: $\forall a, b \in \N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }: a +_{m, n} b = \begin{cases} a + b & : a + b < m \\ a + b - k n & : a + b \ge m \end{cases}$ where $k$ is the largest integer satisfying: $m + k n \le a + b$

title: Dipper Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers such that $m \ge 0, n > 0$. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is associative.

title: Dipper Operation is Closed on Initial Segment
snippet: Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $+_{m, n}$ denote the dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$: $\forall a, b \in \N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }: a +_{m, n} b = \begin{cases} a + b & : a + b < m \\ a + b - k n & : a + b \ge m \end{cases}$ where $k$ is the largest integer satisfying: $m + k n \le a + b$ Then $+_{m, n}$ is closed on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$.

title: Dipper Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers such that $m \ge 0, n > 0$. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is commutative.

title: Dipper Relation is Congruence for Addition
snippet: Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\RR_{m, n}$ be the dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N: x \mathrel {\RR_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR_{m, n}$ is a congruence relation for addition.

title: Dipper Relation is Congruence for Multiplication
snippet: Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\RR_{m, n}$ be the dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N: x \mathrel {\RR_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR_{m, n}$ is a congruence relation for multiplication.

title: Dipper Relation is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\RR_{m, n}$ be the dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N: x \mathrel {\RR_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR_{m, n}$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Dipper Semigroup is Commutative Semigroup
snippet: The dipper semigroup is a commutative semigroup.

title: Dirac's Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a connected simple graph with $n$ vertices such that $n > 3$. Let the degree of each vertex be at least $\dfrac n 2$. Then $G$ is Hamiltonian.

title: Dirac Bra Grouping is Conjugate Linear
snippet: Let $\bra \alpha$ and $\bra \beta$ be bras in some dual space. Let $h$ and $k$ be scalars. Then: $\bra {h \alpha + k \beta} = \bra \alpha h^\dagger + \bra \beta k^\dagger$ where $h^\dagger$ is the complex conjugate of $h$.

title: Dirac Comb is Distribution
snippet: Let $\phi \in \map \DD \R$ be a test function. Suppose $\map {\operatorname {III} } 0$ is a Dirac comb such that: $\ds \map {\map {\operatorname {III} } 0} \phi := \sum_{n \mathop \in \Z} \map \phi n$ Then $\map {\operatorname {III} } 0$ is a Schwartz distribution. {{explain|Dirac comb currently leads to Definition:Sampling Function, but the notation does not quote tally.

title: Dirac Delta Distribution is Tempered Distribution
snippet: Let $\delta$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Let $\map {\SS'} \R$ be the tempered distribution space. Then: $\delta \in \map {\SS'} \R$

title: Dirac Inner Product is Conjugate Linear in First Argument
snippet: Let $\ket \alpha$, $\ket \beta$, and $\ket \gamma$ be kets. Let $k$ be a scalar. Then: $\braket {k \alpha + \beta} \gamma = \bar k \braket \alpha \gamma + \braket \beta \gamma$

title: Dirac Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $x \in X$, and let $\delta_x$ be the Dirac measure at $x$. Then $\delta_x$ is a measure.

title: Dirac Measure is Probability Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \AA}$ be a measurable space. Let $x \in X$, and let $\delta_x$ be the Dirac measure at $x$. Then $\delta_x$ is a probability measure.

title: Direct Image Mapping is Bijection iff Mapping is Bijection
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$. Then $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ is a bijection $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ is a bijection.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Domain is Image Set of Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\powerset S$ and $\powerset T$ be their power sets. Let $f \subseteq S \times T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$: $\forall X \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} X = \begin {cases} \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \map f s = t} & : X \ne \O \\ \O & : X = \O \end {cases}$ Then: $\map {f^\to} S = \Img f$ where $\Img f$ is the image set of $f$.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Domain is Image Set of Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\powerset S$ and $\powerset T$ be their power sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$: $\forall X \in \powerset S: \map {\RR^\to} X = \begin {cases} \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \tuple {x, t} \in \RR} & : X \ne \O \\ \O & : X = \O \end {cases}$ Then: $\map {\RR^\to} {\Dom \RR} = \Img \RR$ where: $\Dom \RR$ is the domain of $\RR$ $\Img \RR$ is the image set of $\RR$.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Identity is Identity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $I_S : S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Let $\paren{I_S}^\to : \powerset S \to \powerset S$ be the direct image mapping of $I_S$. Then: $\paren{I_S}^\to = I_{\powerset S}$ where $I_{\powerset S} :\powerset S \to \powerset S$ denotes the identity mapping on $\powerset S$.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Left-Total Relation is Empty iff Argument is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR: S \to T$ be a left-total relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$: $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T: \map {\RR^\to} X = \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \tuple {s, t} \in \RR}$ Then: $\map {\RR^\to} X = \O \iff X = \O$

title: Direct Image Mapping of Mapping is Empty iff Argument is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $f^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $f$: $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T: \map {f^\to} X = \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \map f s = t}$ Then: $\map {f^\to} X = \O \iff X = \O$

title: Direct Image Mapping of Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping on $S \times T$. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$: $\forall X \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} X = \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \map f s = t}$ Then $f^\to$ is indeed a mapping.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Relation is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$: $\forall X \in \powerset S: \map {\RR^\to} X = \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \tuple {s, t} \in \RR}$ Then $\RR^\to$ is indeed a mapping.

title: Direct Image Mapping of Surjection is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a surjection. Then the direct image mapping of $f$: $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ is a surjection.

title: Direct Image of Intersection with Inverse Image
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let: $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping of $f$ $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping of $f$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then: $\forall A \in \powerset S, B \in \powerset T: \map {f^\to} {A \cap \map {f^\gets} B} = \map {f^\to} A \cap B$

title: Direct Image of Inverse Image of Direct Image equals Direct Image Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let: $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping of $f$ $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping of $f$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then: $f^\to \circ f^\gets \circ f^\to = f^\to$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Direct Product of *-Algebras is *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\tuple {A, \square}$ and $\tuple {B, \diamond}$ be $\ast$-algebras over $\C$. Let $A \times B$ be the direct product of $A$ and $B$. Define $\ast : A \times B \to A \times B$ by: $\tuple {a, b}^\ast = \tuple {a^\square, b^\diamond}$ for each $\tuple {a, b} \in A \times B$. Then $\tuple {A \times B, \ast}$ is a $\ast$-algebra.

title: Direct Product of Algebras is Algebra
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ and $B$ be algebras over $K$. Let $\tuple {A \times B, +_{A \times B}, \cdot_{A \times B} }$ be the direct product of $A$ and $B$ as vector spaces. Define $\cdot_{A \times B} : A \times B \to A \times B$ by: $\tuple {a, b} \tuple {a', b'} = \tuple {a a', b b'}$ for each $\tuple {a, b}, \tuple {a', b'} \in A \times B$. Then $\tuple {A \times B, +_{A \times B}, \cdot_{A \times B}, \circ_{A \times B} }$ is an algebra.

title: Direct Product of Central Subgroup with Inverse Isomorphism is Central Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $\map Z G$ denote the center of $G$. Let $Z$ and $W$ be central subgroups of $G$ and $H$ respectively. Let: $Z \cong W$ where $\cong$ denotes isomorphism. Let such a group isomorphism be $\theta: Z \to W$. Let $X$ be the set defined as: $X = \set {\tuple {x, \map \theta x^{-1} }: x \in Z}$ Then $X$ is a central subgroup of $G \times H$.

title: Direct Product of Central Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $Z$ and $W$ be central subgroups of $G$ and $H$ respectively. Then $Z \times W$ is a central subgroup of $G \times H$.

title: Direct Product of Group Homomorphisms is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}, \struct {H_1, *_1}$ and $\struct {H_2, *_2}$ be groups. Let $\struct {H_1 \times H_2, *}$ be the group direct product of $H_1$ and $H_2$. Let $f_1: G \to H_1$ and $f_2: G \to H_2$ be group homomorphisms. Let $f_1 \times f_2: g \to H_1 \times H_2$ be the direct product of $f_1$ and $f_2$. Then $f_1 \times f_2$ is a group homomorphism.

title: Direct Product of Locally Convex Spaces is Locally Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a non-empty set. For each $\alpha \in I$, let $\struct {X_\alpha, \PP_\alpha}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ with standard topology $\tau_\alpha$. That is, $\struct {X_\alpha, \PP_\alpha}$ is a locally convex topological vector space. Let: $\ds X = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} X_\alpha$ be the direct product of $\family {X_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let $\tau$ be the product topology on $X$. Then $\tau$ is the standard topology of a locally convex space $\struct {X, \PP}$.

title: Direct Product of Modules is Module
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\family {\struct {M_i, +_i, \circ_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of $R$-modules. Let $\struct {M, +, \circ}$ be their direct product. Then $\struct {M, +, \circ}$ is a module.

title: Direct Product of Normal Subgroups is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ and $G'$ be groups. Let: $H \lhd G$ $H' \lhd G'$ where $\lhd$ denotes the relation of being a normal subgroup. Then: $\paren {H \times H'} \lhd \paren {G \times G'}$ where $H \times H'$ denotes the group direct product of $H$ and $H'$

title: Direct Product of Normed Algebras is Normed Algebra with Direct Product Norm
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A,

title: Direct Product of Solvable Groups is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups which are solvable. Then their (external) direct product $G \times H$ is also solvable.

title: Direct Product of Sylow p-Subgroups is Sylow p-Subgroup
snippet: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be groups. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subgroups of $G_1$ and $G_2$ respectively. Let $H_1$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_1$. Let $H_2$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_2$. Then $H_1 \times H_2$ is a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_1 \times G_2$.

title: Direct Product of Topological Vector Spaces is Hausdorff iff Hausdorff Factor Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\family {X_i}_{i \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological vector spaces over $K$. Let: $\ds X = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the direct product of $\family {X_i}_{i \in I}$. Equip $X$ with the product topology. Then $X$ is Hausdorff $X_i$ is Hausdorff for each $i \in I$.

title: Direct Product of Topological Vector Spaces is Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\family {X_i}_{i \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of topological vector spaces over $K$. Let: $\ds X = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the direct product of $\family {X_i}_{i \in I}$. Equip $X$ with the product topology. Then $X$ is a topological vector space.

title: Direct Product of Unique Sylow p-Subgroups is Unique Sylow p-Subgroup
snippet: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be groups. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subgroups of $G_1$ and $G_2$ respectively. Let $G_1$ be such that $H_1$ is the unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_1$. Let $G_2$ be such that $H_2$ is the unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_2$. Then $H_1 \times H_2$ is the unique Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G_1 \times G_2$.

title: Direct Product of Unitary Modules is Unitary Module
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\family {\struct {M_i, +_i, \circ_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of unitary $R$-modules. Let $\struct {M, +, \circ}$ be their direct product. Then $\struct {M, +, \circ}$ is a unitary $R$-module.

title: Direct Product of Vector Spaces is Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_n$ be $K$-vector spaces. Let $\struct {V, + , \circ}_K$ be their direct product. Then $\struct {V, + , \circ}_K$ is a $K$-vector space.

snippet: Both versions of the Directed Hamilton Cycle problem are NP-complete.

title: Directed Set has Strict Successors iff Unbounded Above
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \le}$ be a directed set. Then every element of $S$ has a strict successor in $S$ $S$ has no upper bound in $S$.

title: Directed Smooth Curve Relation is Equivalence
snippet: Let $\sim$ denote a relation on the set of all smooth paths: $\set {\gamma: I \to \C : \text{$I$ is a closed real interval, $\gamma$ is a smooth path} }$. Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \C$ and $\sigma : \closedint c d \to \C$ be smooth paths. Define $\sim$ as follows: $\gamma \sim \sigma$ there exists a bijective differentiable strictly increasing real function $\phi: \closedint c d \to \closedint a b$ such that $\sigma = \gamma \circ \phi$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation on the set of all smooth paths.

title: Directed Suprema Preserving Mapping at Element is Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \precsim}$ be bounded below continuous lattices. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that $f$ preserves directed suprema. Let $x \in S$. Then: $\map f x = \sup \set {\map f w: w \in S \land w \ll x}$

title: Directed Suprema Preserving Mapping is Increasing
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $f: S \to S$ be a mapping that preserves directed suprema. Then $f$ is an increasing mapping.

title: Directed iff Filtered in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preceq_2}$ be a dual ordered set of $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ Let $X \subseteq S$. Then: $X$ is directed in $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ $X$ is filtered in $\struct {S, \preceq_2}$.

title: Directed iff Finite Subsets have Upper Bounds
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \precsim}$ be a preordered set. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $H$ is directed : for every finite subset $A$ of $H$: $\exists h \in H: \forall a \in A: a \precsim h$

title: Directed iff Lower Closure Directed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \precsim}$ be a preordered set. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $H$ is directed : $H^\precsim$ is directed where $H^\precsim$ denotes the lower closure of $H$ with respect to $\precsim$.

title: Directed in Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $H$ be a non-empty lower section of $S$. Then $H$ is directed $\forall x, y \in H: x \vee y \in H$

title: Directed in Join Semilattice with Finite Suprema
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $H$ be a non-empty lower section of $S$. Then $H$ is directed for every non-empty finite subset $A$ of $H$, $\sup A \in H$

title: Direction Angle of 2D Vector in Terms of Arctangent
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector quantity embedded in a Cartesian plane $P$ expressed in component form as: $\mathbf a = x \mathbf i + y \mathbf j$ Let $\theta$ denote the direction of $\mathbf a$. Then: $\theta = \begin{cases} \map \arctan {\dfrac y x} & : x > 0 \\ \map \arctan {\dfrac y x} + \pi & : x 0 \\ -\dfrac \pi 2 & : x = 0 \text{ and } y where: $\arctan$ denotes the real arctangent function, defined on the real interval $\openint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ $\theta$ is conventionally measured from the positive direction of the $x$-axis in the interval $\hointl {-\pi} \pi$.

title: Direction Cosines/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Direction Cosines ==

title: Direction of Electric Field caused by Point Charge
snippet: Let $q$ be a point charge. Let $\map {\mathbf E} {\mathbf r}$ be the electric field strength due to $q$ at a point $P$ whose position vector is $\mathbf r$. The direction of the electric field due to $q$ at $P$ is: for positive $q$, directly away from $q$ for negative $q$, directly towards $q$.

title: Direction of Line of Electric Force
snippet: Let $\mathbf E$ be an electric field. Let $L$ be a line of force within $\mathbf E$. Then $L$ has one of the following properties: $(1): \quad$ Begins on a positively charged body and ends on a negatively charged body $(2): \quad$ Begins on a positively charged body and goes to infinity without terminating $(3): \quad$ Comes from infinity without a start point and ends on a negatively charged body.

title: Direction of Rotation of Plane of Oscillation of Foucault's Pendulum
snippet: Let $P$ be a Foucault pendulum. The rotation $\alpha$ of the plane of oscillation of $P$ is: clockwise in the northern hemisphere anticlockwise in the southern hemisphere.

title: Directional Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Directional Data ==

title: Dirichlet's Approximation Theorem
snippet: Let $\alpha, x \in \R$. Then there exist integers $a, q$ such that: $\gcd \set {a, q} = 1$ $1 \le q \le x$ and: $\size {\alpha - \dfrac a q} \le \dfrac 1 {q x}$

title: Dirichlet's Box Principle
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set whose cardinality is $n$. Let $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_k$ be a partition of $S$ into $k$ subsets. Then: at least one subset $S_i$ of $S$ contains at least $\ceiling {\dfrac n k}$ elements where $\ceiling {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the ceiling function.

title: Dirichlet's Integral Form of Digamma Function
snippet: Let $z$ be a complex number with a positive real part. Then: $\ds \map \psi z = \int_0^\infty \paren {\frac {e^{-t} } t - \frac 1 {t \paren {1 + t}^z } } \rd t$ where $\psi$ is the digamma function.

title: Dirichlet's Principle for Harmonic Functions
snippet: Let the function $\map u x$ be the particular solution to Poisson's equation: $\Delta u + f = 0$ on a domain $\Omega$ of $\R^n$ with boundary condition: $u = g$ on $\partial \Omega$ Then $u$ can be obtained as the minimizer of the Dirichlet's energy: $\ds E \sqbrk {\map v x} = \int_\Omega \paren {\frac 1 2 \cmod {\nabla v}^2 - v f} \rd x$ amongst all twice differentiable functions $v$ such that $v = g$ on $\partial \Omega$ . This result holds provided that there exists at least one function which makes the Dirichlet Integral finite.

title: Dirichlet's Test for Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $D$ be a set. Let $\struct {V, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $a_i, b_i$ be mappings from $D \to M$. Let the following conditions be satisfied: $(1): \quad$ The sequence of partial sums of $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {a_n} x$ be bounded on $D$ $(2): \quad \sequence {\map {b_n} x}$ be monotonic for each $x \in D$ $(3): \quad \map {b_n} x \to 0$ converge uniformly on $D$. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {a_n} x \map {b_n} x$ converges uniformly on $D$.

title: Dirichlet's Theorem on Arithmetic Sequences
snippet: Let $a, q$ be coprime integers. Let $\PP_{a, q}$ be the set of primes $p$ such that $p \equiv a \pmod q$. Then $\PP_{a, q}$ has Dirichlet density: $\map \phi q^{-1}$ where $\phi$ is Euler's phi function. In particular, $\PP_{a, q}$ is infinite.

title: Dirichlet Beta Function at Odd Positive Integers
snippet: {{eqn | l = \map \beta {2 n + 1} | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^k} {\paren {2 k + 1}^{2 n + 1} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 {1^{2 n + 1} } - \frac 1 {3^{2 n + 1} } + \frac 1 {5^{2 n + 1} } - \frac 1 {7^{2 n + 1} } + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {-1}^n \dfrac {E_{2 n} \pi^{2 n + 1} } {4^{n + 1} \paren {2 n}!} | c = }} where: $\beta$ denotes the Dirichlet beta function $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number $n$ is a non-negative integer.

title: Dirichlet Beta Function in terms of Hurwitz Zeta Function
snippet: $\map \beta s = \dfrac 1 {4^s} \paren {\map \zeta {s, \dfrac 1 4} - \map \zeta {s, \dfrac 3 4} }$ where: $\map \beta s$ is the Dirichlet beta function $\map \zeta {s, x}$ is the Hurwitz zeta function $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > 1$

title: Dirichlet Conditions/Examples/Reciprocal of 4 minus x squared
snippet: == Example of Dirichlet Conditions == The function: $\map f x = \dfrac 1 {4 - x^2}$ does not satisfy the Dirichlet conditions on the real interval $\openint 0 {2 \pi}$.

title: Dirichlet Conditions/Examples/Sine of Reciprocal of x - 1
snippet: == Example of Dirichlet Conditions == The function: $\map f x = \map \sin {\dfrac 1 {x - 1} }$ does not satisfy the Dirichlet conditions on the real interval $\openint 0 {2 \pi}$.

title: Dirichlet Convolution Preserves Multiplicativity
snippet: Let $f, g: \N \to \C$ be multiplicative arithmetic functions. Then their Dirichlet convolution $f * g$ is again multiplicative.

title: Dirichlet Convolution is Associative
snippet: Let $f, g, h$ be arithmetic functions. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution. Then: $\paren {f * g} * h = f * \paren {g * h}$

title: Dirichlet Convolution is Commutative
snippet: Let $f, g$ be arithmetic functions. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution. Then: $f * g = g * f$

title: Dirichlet Eigenvalue is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with non-empty boundary $\partial M$. Let $\lambda$ be a Dirichlet eigenvalue of $M$. Then $\lambda$ is strictly positive.

title: Dirichlet Eta Function at Non-Positive Integers
snippet: Let $n \ge 0$ be a integer. Then: $\map \eta {-n} = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^{n + 1} \paren {2^{n + 1 } - 1} B_{n + 1} } {n + 1}$ where: $B_n$ is the $n$th Bernoulli number $\eta$ is the Dirichlet eta function

title: Dirichlet Function has no Period
snippet: The Dirichlet functions are periodic by Dirichlet Function is Periodic. However, they do not admit a period. That is, there does not exist a smallest value $L \in \R_{> 0}$ such that: $\forall x \in \R: \map D x = \map D {x + L}$

title: Dirichlet Function is Discontinuous
snippet: Let $D: \R \to \R$ denote the Dirichlet function: $\forall x \in \R: \map D x = \begin {cases} c & : x \in \Q \\ d & : x \notin \Q \end {cases}$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Then $D$ is discontinuous at every $x \in \R$.

title: Dirichlet Function is Periodic
snippet: Let $D: \R \to \R$ be a Dirichlet function: $\forall x \in \R: \map D x = \begin{cases} c & : x \in \Q \\ d & : x \notin \Q \end{cases}$ Then $D$ is periodic. Namely, every non-zero rational number is a periodic element of $D$.

title: Dirichlet Function is not Darboux Integrable
snippet: Let $D: \R \to \R$ denote the Dirichlet function: $\forall x \in \R: \map D x = \begin {cases} c & : x \in \Q \\ d & : x \notin \Q \end {cases}$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Then $D$ is not a Darboux integrable function.

title: Dirichlet Integral
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin x} x \rd x = \frac \pi 2$

title: Dirichlet L-Function from Trivial Character
snippet: Let $\chi_0$ be the trivial Dirichlet character modulo $q$. Let $\map L {s, \chi_0}$ be the Dirichlet $L$-function associated to $\chi_0$. Let $\map \zeta s$ be the Riemann zeta function. Then: $\ds \map L {s, \chi_0} = \map \zeta s \cdot \prod_{p \mathop \divides q} \paren {1 - p^{-s} }$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

title: Dirichlet Series/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Dirichlet Series == The Riemann zeta function is the (ordinary) Dirichlet series with $a_n = 1$ for all $n$. Category:Examples of Dirichlet Series

title: Dirichlet Series Absolute Convergence Lemma
snippet: Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a_n} {n^s}$ be a Dirichlet series. Suppose that $f$ converges absolutely at $s_0 = \sigma_0 + i t_0 \in \C$. Then $f$ converges absolutely at all points $s = \sigma + i t \in \C$ with $\sigma \ge \sigma_0$.

title: Dirichlet Series Convergence Lemma
snippet: Let $\ds \map f s = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a_n} {n^s}$ be a Dirichlet series. Let $\map f s$ converge at $s_0 = \sigma_0 + i t_0$. Then $\map f s$ converge for all $s = \sigma + i t$ where $\sigma > \sigma_0$.

title: Dirichlet Series is Analytic
snippet: Let $(a_n)$ be sequence of complex numbers. Let: $\ds \map f z = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {a_n} {n^z}$ be the associated Dirichlet Series, which is defined at the points where the series converges. Then $f$ is analytic in every open set such that the sum converges in the set.

title: Dirichlet Series of Convolution of Arithmetic Functions
snippet: Let $f, g: \N \to \C$ be arithmetic functions. Let $h = f * g$ be their Dirichlet convolution. Let $F, G, H$ be their Dirichlet series. Let $s$ be a complex number such that $\map F s$ and $\map G s$ converge absolutely. Then $\map H s$ converges absolutely to $\map F s \times \map G s$.

title: Dirichlet Series of Inverse of Arithmetic Function
snippet: Let $f : \N \to\C$ be an arithmetic function. Let $g : \N \to \C$ be an Dirichlet inverse of $f$. Let $F, G$ be their Dirichlet series. Let $s \in \C$ such that both $\map F s$ and $\map G s$ converge absolutely. Then $\map F s \cdot \map G s = 1$.

title: Discontinuity of Monotonic Function is Jump Discontinuity
snippet: Let $X$ be an open set of $\R$. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a monotone real function. Then $f$ is discontinuous at a point $c \in X$ $c$ is a jump discontinuity of $f$.

title: Discrepancy between Gregorian Year and Tropical Year
snippet: The Gregorian year and the tropical year differ such that the Gregorian calendar becomes $1$ day further out approximately every $3319$ years.

title: Discrepancy between Julian Year and Tropical Year
snippet: The Julian year and the tropical year differ such that the Julian calendar becomes $1$ day further out approximately every $128$ years.

title: Discrete Category is Order Category
snippet: Let $\map {\mathbf{Dis} } S$ be a discrete category. Then $\map {\mathbf{Dis} } S$ is also an order category.

title: Discrete Category on Set is Discrete Category
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map {\mathbf {Dis} } S$ be the discrete category on $S$. Then $\map {\mathbf {Dis} } S$ determines a unique (up to isomorphism) discrete category $\map {\mathbf {Dis} } S$ whose objects precisely comprise $S$. {{explain|What is unique up to isomorphism in this context? This is the definition of $\map {\mathbf {Dis} } S$, isn't it?}} {{expand|That is, $\mathbf {Dis}: \mathbf {Set} \to \mathbf {Cat}$ is a functor (with left inverse $\mathbf {ob}$) }}

title: Discrete Fourier Transform on Abelian Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Let $G^*$ be the dual group of characters $G \to \C^\times$. Let $\eta: G \to \C$ be a mapping from $G$ to the set of complex numbers. Then for all $x \in G$: $\ds \map \eta x = \frac 1 {\map \phi q} \sum_{\chi \mathop \in G^*} \innerprod \eta \chi_G \map \chi x$ where: $\ds \innerprod \eta \chi_G = \sum_{x \mathop \in G} \map \eta x \map {\overline \chi} x$

title: Discrete Group Acts Continuously iff Acts by Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $G$ be a discrete group acting on a topological space $X$. $G$ acts continuously $G$ acts by homeomorphisms

title: Discrete Normal Subgroup of Connected Group is Contained in Center
snippet: Let $G$ be a connected topological group. Let $\map Z G$ be the center of $G$. Let $N$ be a discrete normal subgroup of $G$. Then: $N \subseteq \map Z G$

title: Discrete Random Variable is Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then $X$ fulfils the condition: $\forall x \in \R: \set {\omega \in \Omega: \map X \omega \le x} \in \Sigma$ That is, $X$ fulfils the condition for it to be a random variable.
