title: Envelope Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Suppose you are given one of two sealed containing money. You do not know how much money there is in these , but you do know that the money in one of them is twice the money in the other. You are given the option of exchanging one for the other. Should you change ? By symmetry, it seems apparent that there is no benefit in swapping . However, consider the following. Let $x$ be the amount in your . Then in the other there is either $2 x$ or $\dfrac x 2$. So you have: a $50 \%$ probability of gaining $x$ a $50 \%$ probability of losing $\dfrac x 2$.

title: Epic Equalizer is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $e: E \to C$ be the equalizer of two morphisms $f, g: C \to D$. Let $e$ be an epimorphism. Then $e$ is an isomorphism.

title: Epicycloid is Closed iff Ratio of Radii of Generators is Rational
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an epicycloid whose generators are the circles $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$. Let the radii of $\CC_1$ and $\CC_2$ be $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively. Then $\EE$ forms a closed curve $\dfrac {r_1} {r_2}$ is rational.

title: Epicycloid whose Ratio of Generating Circle Radii is Rational is Closed Curve
snippet: Consider the epicycloid $E$ generated by a epicycle $C_1$ of radius $b$ rolling within a deferent $C_2$ of radius $a$. Let $k = \dfrac a b$ be a rational number. Then $E$ is a closed curve.

title: Epimenides Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == famously stated: All Cretans are liars. As himself was a Cretan, then naturally he would have been telling a lie when he said it. That would mean all Cretans are not liars, which would mean (as was a Cretan) he would have been telling the truth. This would then mean was a liar. Hence this statement contradicts itself.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Associativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\circ$ be an associative operation. Then $*$ is also an associative operation.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\circ$ be a commutative operation. Then $*$ is also a commutative operation.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Distributivity
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: R_1 \to R_2$ be an epimorphism. If $\circ_1$ is left distributive over $+_1$, then $\circ_2$ is left distributive over $+_2$. If $\circ_1$ is right distributive over $+_1$, then $\circ_2$ is right distributive over $+_2$. Consequently, if $\circ_1$ is distributive over $+_1$, then $\circ_2$ is distributive over $+_2$. That is, epimorphism preserves distributivity.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Groups
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a group. Then $\struct {T, *}$ is also a group.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity element $e_S$. Then $\struct {T, *}$ has the identity element $\map \phi {e_S}$.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $x^{-1}$ be an inverse element of $x$ for $\circ$. Then $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse element of $\map \phi x$ for $*$. That is: $\map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$

title: Epimorphism Preserves Modules
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-algebraic structure. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be an epimorphism. Then $H$ is an $R$-module.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Rings
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ be a ring, and $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a closed algebraic structure. Let $\phi: R_1 \to R_2$ be an epimorphism. Then $\struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ is a ring.

title: Epimorphism Preserves Semigroups
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then $\struct {T, *}$ is also a semigroup.

title: Epimorphism from Division Ring to Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a division ring whose zero is $0_K$. Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\phi: K \to R$ be a ring epimorphism. Then one of the following applies: $(1): \quad R$ is a null ring $(2): \quad R$ is a division ring and $\phi$ is a ring isomorphism.

title: Epimorphism from Integers to Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $\gen a = \struct {G, \circ}$ be a cyclic group. Let $f: \Z \to G$ be a mapping defined as: $\forall n \in \Z: \map f n = a^n$. Then $f$ is a (group) epimorphism from $\struct {\Z, +}$ onto $\gen a$.

title: Epimorphism from Polynomial Forms to Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $D$ be an integral domain. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in $X$ over $D$. Let $\map P D$ be the ring of polynomial functions over $D$. The mapping $\kappa: D \sqbrk X \to \map P D$ given by: $\ds \map \kappa {\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n {a_k \circ X^k} } = f$ where $\ds f = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n {a_k \circ x^k}, x \in D$ is a ring epimorphism.

title: Epimorphism from Real Numbers to Circle Group
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \times}$ be the circle group, that is: $K = \set {z \in \C: \cmod z = 1}$ under complex multiplication. Let $f: \R \to K$ be the mapping from the real numbers to $K$ defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \cos x + i \sin x$ Then $f: \struct {\R, +} \to \struct {K, \times}$ is a group epimorphism. Its kernel is: $\map \ker f = \set {2 \pi n: n \in \Z}$

title: Epimorphism iff Monomorphism in Dual Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$ be the dual category of $\mathbf C$. Let $f$ be an morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is a epimorphism in $\mathbf C$ $f^{\operatorname{op}}$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$.

title: Epimorphism in Isomorphic Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be an isomorphism of categories. Let $f$ be a morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is an epimorphism in $\mathbf C$ $Ff$ is an epimorphism in $\mathbf D$.

title: Epimorphism into Projective Object Splits
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $P \in \mathbf C_0$ be a projective object of $\mathbf C$. Let $e: E \twoheadrightarrow P$ be an epimorphism. Then $e$ is a split epimorphism, i.e. it admits a retraction $f: P \to E$.

title: Epimorphism that is Split Monomorphism is Split Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f: C \to D$ be a epimorphism and a split monomorphism. Then $f: C \to D$ is a split epimorphism.

title: Epitaph of Diophantus
snippet: == Classic Problem == This tomb holds . Ah, how great a marvel! the tomb tells scientifically the measure of his life. God granted him to be a boy for the sixth part of his life, and adding a twelfth part to this, he clothed his cheeks with down; He lit him the light of wedlock after a seventh part, and five years after his marriage He granted him a son. Alas! late-born wretched child; after attaining the measure of half his father's life, chill Fate took him. After consoling his grief by this science of numbers for four years he ended his life.

title: Epsilon-Function Differentiability Condition
snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be a continuous function, where $D \subseteq \R$ is an open set. Let $x \in \R$. Then $f$ is differentiable at $x$ there exist $\alpha \in \R$ and $r \in \R_{>0}$ such that for all $h \in \openint {-r} r \setminus \set 0$: $\map f {x + h} = \map f x + h \paren {\alpha + \map \epsilon h}$ where: $\openint {-r} r$ denotes an open interval of $0$ $\epsilon: \openint {-r} r \setminus \set 0 \to \R$ is a real function with $\ds \lim_{h \mathop \to 0} \map \epsilon h = 0$.

title: Epsilon-Neighborhood (Real Number Line)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Epsilon-Neighborhoods ==

title: Epsilon Relation is Proper
snippet: Let $\mathbb U$ be the universal class. Let $\Epsilon$ be the epsilon relation. Then $\struct {\mathbb U, \Epsilon}$ is a proper relational structure.

title: Epsilon Relation is Strictly Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\Epsilon$ denote the epsilon relation. Then $\Epsilon$ is a strictly well-founded relation on every class $A$.

title: Equal Alternate Angles implies Parallel Lines
snippet: Given two infinite straight lines which are cut by a transversal, if the alternate angles are equal, then the lines are parallel.

title: Equal Angles in Equal Circles
snippet: In equal circles, equal angles stand on equal arcs, whether at the center or at the circumference of those circles.

title: Equal Arcs of Circles Subtended by Equal Straight Lines
Equal Chords in Circle
snippet: In a circle, equal chords are equally distant from the center, and chords that are equally distant from the center are equal in length.

title: Equal Consecutive Prime Number Gaps are Multiples of Six
snippet: If you list the gaps between consecutive primes greater than $5$: $2, 4, 2, 4, 2, 4, 6, 2, 6, 4, 2, 4, \ldots$ you will notice that consecutive gaps that are equal are of the form $6 x$. This is always the case.

title: Equal Corresponding Angles implies Parallel Lines
snippet: Given two infinite straight lines which are cut by a transversal, if the corresponding angles are equal, then the lines are parallel.

title: Equal Corresponding Angles or Supplementary Interior Angles implies Parallel Lines
Equal Elements of Field of Quotients
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be the field of quotients of $\struct {D, +, \circ}$. Let $x = \dfrac p q \in K$. Then: $\forall k \in D^*: x = \dfrac {p \circ k} {q \circ k}$ where: $D^* := D \setminus \set {0_D}$ that is, $D$ with its zero removed.

title: Equal Images of Mappings to Hausdorff Space form Closed Set
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $T_B$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $f, g: T_A \to T_B$ be continuous mappings. Let $W$ be the set defined as: $W = \set {x \in T_A: \map f x = \map g x}$ Then $W$ is closed in $T_A$.

title: Equal Numbers are Congruent
snippet: $\forall x, y, z \in \R: x = y \implies x \equiv y \pmod z$ where $x \equiv y \pmod z$ denotes congruence modulo $z$.

title: Equal Order Elements may not be Conjugate
snippet: Let $G$ be a group Let $x, y \in G$ be elements of $G$ such that: $\order x = \order y$ where $\order x$ denotes the order of $x$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $x$ and $y$ are conjugates.

title: Equal Powers of Finite Order Element
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Let $\order g = k$. Then: $g^r = g^s \iff k \divides \paren {r - s}$

title: Equal Powers of Group Element implies Finite Order
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $g \in G$ such that $g^r = g^s$ where $r, s \in \Z: r \ne s$. Then there exists $m \in \Z_{>0}$ such that: $(1): \quad g^m = e$ $(2): \quad 0 \le i < j < m \implies g^i \ne g^j$

title: Equal Relative Complements iff Equal Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\relcomp S B = \relcomp S A \iff A = B$ where $\complement_S$ denotes the complement relative to $S$.

title: Equal Set Differences iff Equal Intersections
snippet: $R \setminus S = R \setminus T \iff R \cap S = R \cap T$

title: Equal Sized Triangles on Equal Base have Same Height
snippet: Triangles of equal area which are on equal bases, and on the same side of it, are also in the same parallels.

title: Equal Sized Triangles on Same Base have Same Height
snippet: Triangles of equal area which are on the same base, and on the same side of it, are also in the same parallels.

title: Equal Surfaces do not Intersect
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of space, which may be the interior of a body. Let there exist a point-function $F$ on $R$ giving rise to a scalar field. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be equal surfaces in $R$ upon which the value of $F$ on $S_1$ is different from the value of $F$ on $S_2$. Then $S_1$ and $S_2$ do not intersect.

title: Equality Relation is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The relation $\operatorname{eq} \subseteq \N^2$, defined as: $\map {\operatorname {eq} } {n, m} \iff n = m$ is primitive recursive.

title: Equality implies Substitution
snippet: Let $\map P x$ denote a Well-Formed Formula which contains $x$ as a free variable. Then the following are tautologies: $\forall x: \paren {\map P x \iff \exists y: \paren {y = x \land \map P y} }$ $\forall x: \paren {\map P x \iff \forall y: \paren {y = x \implies \map P y} }$ Note that when $y$ is substituted for $x$ in either formula, it is false in general; compare Confusion of Bound Variables.

title: Equality is Reflexive
snippet: Equality is reflexive. That is: $\forall a: a = a$

title: Equality is Symmetric
snippet: Equality is symmetric. That is: $\forall a, b: a = b \implies b = a$

title: Equality is Transitive
snippet: Equality is transitive: $\forall a, b, c: \paren {a = b} \land \paren {b = c} \implies a = c$

title: Equality of Algebraic Structures
snippet: Two algebraic structures $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ are equal : $S = T$ $\forall a, b \in S: a \circ b = a * b$

title: Equality of Cartesian Products
snippet: Let $A, B, C, D$ be nonempty sets. Then: $A \times B = C \times D \iff A = C \land B = D$ where $\times$ denotes cartesian product.

title: Equality of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1 := a_1 + i b_1$ and $z_2 := a_2 + i b_2$ be complex numbers. Then $z_1 = z_2$ $a_1 = a_2$ and $b_1 = b_2$.

title: Equality of Cycles
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters, realised as the permutations of $\set {1, \ldots, n}$. Let: $\rho = \begin {bmatrix} a_0 & \cdots & a_{k - 1} \end {bmatrix} \in S_n$ $\sigma = \begin {bmatrix} b_0 & \cdots & b_{k - 1} \end {bmatrix} \in S_n$ be $k$-cycles of $S_n$. For $d \in \Z$, by Integer is Congruent to Integer less than Modulus we can associate to $d$ a unique integer $\tilde d \in \set {0, \ldots, k - 1}$ such that: $d \equiv \tilde d \pmod k$ Define $a_d$ and $b_d$ for any $d \in \Z$ by $a_d = a_{\tilde d}$ and $b_d = b_{\tilde d}$ Choose $i, j \in \set {1, \ldots,…

title: Equality of Division Products
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {U_R, \circ}$ be the group of units of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $a, b \in R, c, d \in U_R$. Then: $\dfrac a c = \dfrac b d \iff a \circ d = b \circ c$ where $\dfrac x z$ is defined as $x \circ \paren {z^{-1} }$, that is, $x$ divided by $z$.

title: Equality of Elements in Range of Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\exists y \in \Rng f: \tuple {x_1, y} \in f \land \tuple {x_2, y} \in f \iff \map f {x_1} = \map f {x_2}$

title: Equality of Integers to the Power of Each Other
snippet: $2$ and $4$ are the only pair of positive integers $m, n$ such that $m \ne n$ such that: $m^n = n^m$ Thus: $2^4 = 4^2 = 16$

title: Equality of Mappings
snippet: Two mappings $f_1: S_1 \to T_1, f_2: S_2 \to T_2$ are equal : $(1): \quad S_1 = S_2$ $(2): \quad T_1 = T_2$ $(3): \quad \forall x \in S_1: \map {f_1} x = \map {f_2} x$

title: Equality of Monomials of Polynomial Ring
Equality of Monomials of Polynomial Ring in Multiple Variables
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $I$ be a set. Let $R \sqbrk {\sequence {x_i}_{i \mathop \in I} }$ be a polynomial ring in $I$ variables $\sequence {x_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ over $R$. Let $a, b : I \to \N$ be distinct mappings with finite support. Then the monomials $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i^{a_i}$ and $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i^{b_i}$ are distinct, where: $X_i^k$ denotes the $k$th power of $X_i$ $\prod$ denotes product with finite support

title: Equality of Monomials of Polynomial Ring in One Variable
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $R \sqbrk X$ be a polynomial ring in one variable $X$ over $R$. Let $k, l \in \N$ be distinct natural numbers. Then the mononomials $X^k$ and $X^l$ are distinct, where $X^k$ denotes the $k$th power of $X$.

title: Equality of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N$. Then: $\N_m \sim \N_n \iff m = n$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence and $\N_n$ denotes the set of all natural numbers less than $n$.

title: Equality of Open Balls does not imply Equality of Centers
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x, y \in A$ and $r, s \in \R$ such that: $\map {B_r} x = \map {B_s} y$ Then it is not necessarily the case that their centers $x$ and $y$ are equal.

title: Equality of Open Balls does not imply Equality of Radii
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x, y \in A$ and $r, s \in \R$ such that: $\map {B_r} x = \map {B_s} y$ Then it is not necessarily the case that their radii $r$ and $s$ are equal.

title: Equality of Ordered Pairs
snippet: Two ordered pairs are equal corresponding coordinates are equal: $\tuple {a, b} = \tuple {c, d} \iff a = c \land b = d$

title: Equality of Ordered Triples/Proof 1
snippet: == Example of Equality of Ordered Tuples ==

title: Equality of Ordered Triples/Proof 2
snippet: == Example of Equality of Ordered Tuples ==

title: Equality of Ordered Tuples
snippet: Let $a = \tuple {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n}$ and $b = \tuple {b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n}$ be ordered tuples. Then: $a = b \iff \forall i: 1 \le i \le n: a_i = b_i$ That is, for two ordered tuples to be equal, all the corresponding elements have to be equal.

title: Equality of Polynomials
snippet: $f$ and $g$ are equal as polynomials $f$ and $g$ are equal as functions. Thus we can say $f = g$ without ambiguity as to what it means.

title: Equality of Radial Distance Function to Riemannian Distance
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a connected Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p = \map {\exp_p} {\map {B_\epsilon} 0 }$ be an open or closed geodesic ball around $p \in M$. Let $r : U_p \to \R$ be the radial distance function. Let $d_g$ be the Riemannian distance. Then: $\forall p \in M : \forall x \in U_p : \map r x = \map {d_g} {p, x}$

title: Equality of Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d$ be integers, with $b$ and $d$ nonzero. $(1): \quad$ The rational numbers $\dfrac a b$ and $\dfrac c d$ are equal. $(2): \quad$ The integers $a d$ and $b c$ are equal.

title: Equality of Ratios Ex Aequali
snippet: That is, if: $a : b = d : e$ $b : c = e : f$ then: $a : c = d : f$

title: Equality of Ratios in Perturbed Proportion
snippet: That is, if: $a : b = e : f$ $b : c = d : e$ then: $a : c = d : f$

title: Equality of Ratios is Transitive
snippet: That is: $A : B = C : D, C : D = E : F \implies A : B = E : F$

title: Equality of Real Numbers/Examples
snippet: == Examples on Equality of Real Numbers ==

title: Equality of Relations
snippet: Let $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ be relations on $S_1 \times T_1$ and $S_2 \times T_2$ respectively. Then $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ are equal : $S_1 = S_2$ $T_1 = T_2$ $\tuple {s, t} \in \RR_1 \iff \tuple {s, t} \in \RR_2$ It is worth labouring the point that for two relations to be equal, not only must their domains be equal, but so must their codomains.

title: Equality of Squares Modulo Integer is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\RR_n$ be the relation on the set of integers $\Z$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x \mathrel {\RR_n} y \iff x^2 \equiv y^2 \pmod n$ Then $\RR_n$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Equality of Successors
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$. Then, $x = y \iff x^+ = y^+$

title: Equality of Successors implies Equality of Ordinals
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Then: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \On: \alpha^+ = \beta^+ \implies \alpha = \beta$

title: Equality of Terms of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be terms in the language of arithmetic containing no variables. Let $A = B$ when interpreted over the natural numbers $\N$. Then there is a formal proof of $A = B$ in minimal arithmetic.

title: Equality of Towers in Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a non-empty set. Let $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be towers in $X$. Then either: $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_1} = \struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ or: $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is an initial segment of $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ or: $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is an initial segment of $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$

title: Equality of Vector Quantities
snippet: Two vector quantities are equal they have the same magnitude and direction. That is: $\mathbf a = \mathbf b \iff \paren {\size {\mathbf a} = \size {\mathbf b} \land \hat {\mathbf a} = \hat {\mathbf b} }$ where: $\hat {\mathbf a}$ denotes the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf a$ $\size {\mathbf a}$ denotes the magnitude of $\mathbf a$.

title: Equality to Initial Segment Imposes Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\AA$ be the set of all ordered pairs $\struct {A, <}$ such that $A$ is a subset of $X$ and $<$ is a strict well-ordering of $A$. Define $\prec$ as: $\struct {A, <} \prec \struct {A', <'}$ $\struct {A, <}$ equals an initial segment of $\struct {A', <'}$. Let $\BB$ be a set of ordered pairs in $\AA$ such that $\BB$ is ordered by $\prec$. Let $B'$ be the union of the sets $B$ for all $\struct {B, <} \in \BB$. Let $<'$ be the union of the relations $<$ for all $\struct {B, <}$. Then $\struct {B', <'}$ is strictly well-ordered set.

title: Equalizer as Limit
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f_1, f_2: C_1 \to C_2$ be morphisms of $\mathbf C$. Let their equalizer $e: E \to C_1$ exist in $\mathbf C$. Define $\tilde e : E \to C_2$ by: $\tilde e = f_1 e = f_2 e$ Then $\struct {E, \sequence {e, \tilde e} }$ is the limit of the diagram $D: \mathbf J \to \mathbf C$ defined by: $\begin{xy}\xymatrix@+1em@L+3px{ \mathbf{J}: & \ast \ar[r] \ar[r] & \star }\end{xy}$ $\begin{xy}\xymatrix@+1em@L+3px{ D: & C_1 \ar[r]^*+{f_1} \ar[r]_*+{f_2} & C_2 }\end{xy}$

title: Equalizer is Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $e: E \to C$ be the equalizer of two morphisms $f, g: C \to D$. Then $e$ is a monomorphism.

title: Equating Coefficients/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Equating Coefficients ==

title: Equation for Line through Two Points in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $L$ be a straight line through $z_1$ and $z_2$ in the complex plane.

title: Equation for Perpendicular Bisector of Two Points
snippet: Let $\tuple {x_1, y_1}$ and $\tuple {y_1, y_2}$ be two points in the cartesian plane. Let $L$ be the perpendicular bisector of the straight line through $z_1$ and $z_2$ in the complex plane. $L$ can be expressed by the equation: $y - \dfrac {y_1 + y_2} 2 = \dfrac {x_1 - x_2} {y_2 - y_1} \paren {x - \dfrac {x_1 + x_2} 2}$

title: Equation for Perpendicular Bisector of Two Points in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $L$ be the perpendicular bisector of the straight line through $z_1$ and $z_2$ in the complex plane.

title: Equation of Astroid
snippet: Let $H$ be the astroid generated by the epicycle $C_1$ of radius $b$ rolling without slipping around the inside of a deferent $C_2$ of radius $a = 4 b$. Let $C_2$ be embedded in a cartesian plane with its center $O$ located at the origin. Let $P$ be a point on the circumference of $C_1$. Let $C_1$ be initially positioned so that $P$ is its point of tangency to $C_2$, located at point $A = \tuple {a, 0}$ on the $x$-axis. Let $\tuple {x, y}$ be the coordinates of $P$ as it travels over the plane.

title: Equation of Chord of Contact on Circle Centered at Origin
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle whose radius is $r$ and whose center is at the origin of a Cartesian plane. Let $P = \tuple {x_0, y_0}$ be a point which is outside the boundary of $\CC$. Let $UV$ be the chord of contact on $\CC$ with respect to $P$. Then $UV$ can be defined by the equation: $x x_0 + y y_0 = r^2$

title: Equation of Chord of Contact on Ellipse in Reduced Form
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipse embedded in a Cartesian plane in reduced form with the equation: $\dfrac {x^2} {a^2} + \dfrac {y^2} {b^2} = 1$ Let $P = \tuple {x_0, y_0}$ be a point which is outside the boundary of $\EE$. Let $UV$ be the chord of contact on $\EE$ with respect to $P$. Then $UV$ can be defined by the equation: $\dfrac {x x_0} {a^2} + \dfrac {y y_0} {b^2} = 1$

title: Equation of Circle center Origin
snippet: The circle with radius $R$ whose center is at the origin expressed in Cartesian coordinates is given by the equation: $x^2 + y^2 = R^2$

title: Equation of Circle in Complex Plane
Equation of Circular Arc in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $a, b \in \C$ be complex constants representing the points $A$ and $B$ respectively in the complex plane. Let $z \in \C$ be a complex variable representing the point $Z$ in the complex plane. Let $\lambda \in \R$ be a real constant such that $-\pi < \lambda < \pi$. Then the equation: $\arg \dfrac {z - b} {z - a} = \lambda$ represents the arc of a circle with $AB$ as a chord subtending an angle $\lambda$ at $Z$ on the circumference.

title: Equation of Circular Cylinder in Cylindrical Coordinates
snippet: The equation of a circular cylindrical surface with radius $R$ can be expressed in cylindrical coordinates as: $r = R$

title: Equation of Circular Helix/Parametric Form
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a circular helix embedded in Cartesian $3$-space whose axis coincides with the $z$-axis. $\HH$ can be described by the parametric equation: $\begin {cases} x & = a \cos t \\ y & = a \sin t \\ z & = b t \\ \end {cases}$ where $t$ is the parameter.

title: Equation of Cissoid of Diocles
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle of radius $a$ whose circumference passes through the origin $O$ and whose diameter through $O$ lies on the horizontal.

title: Equation of Conic in Cartesian Coordinates is Quadratic
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a conic section. Then $\CC$ can be expressed by an quadratic equation in $2$ variables.

title: Equation of Cornu Spiral/Parametric
snippet: Let $K$ be a Cornu spiral embedded in a Cartesian coordinate plane such that the origin coincides with the point at which $s = 0$. Then $K$ can be expressed by the parametric equations: $\begin {cases} x = a \sqrt 2 \map {\operatorname C} {\dfrac s {a \sqrt 2} } \\ \\ y = a \sqrt 2 \map {\operatorname S} {\dfrac s {a \sqrt 2} } \end {cases}$ where: $\operatorname C$ denotes the Fresnel cosine integral function $\operatorname S$ denotes the Fresnel sine integral function.

title: Equation of Cycloid
snippet: Consider a circle of radius $a$ rolling without slipping along the x-axis of a cartesian plane. Consider the point $P$ on the circumference of this circle which is at the origin when its center is on the y-axis. Consider the cycloid traced out by the point $P$. title: Equation of Cycloid in Cartesian Coordinates

Let $\tuple {x, y}$ be the coordinates of $P$ as it travels over the plane. The point $P = \tuple {x, y}$ is described by the equation: $a \sin^{-1} \paren {\dfrac {\sqrt {2 a y - y^2} } a} = \sqrt {2 a y - y^2} + x$

title: Equation of Ellipse in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $\C$ be the complex plane. Let $E$ be an ellipse in $\C$ whose major axis is $d \in \R_{>0}$ and whose foci are at $\alpha, \beta \in \C$. Then $C$ may be written as: $\cmod {z - \alpha} + \cmod {z - \beta} = d$ where $\cmod {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes complex modulus.

title: Equation of Ellipse in Reduced Form

title: Equation of Hyperboloid of Two Sheets

title: Equation of Plane Shear

title: Equation of Polar of Point with respect to Ellipse

title: Equation of Rectangular Hyperbola in Standard Form/Parametric Form

title: Equation of Right Circular Cone/Cartesian

title: Equation of Straight Line Tangent to Circle

The equation of a non-vertical tangent line $\TT$ to $\CC$ is given by: $y - y_n = \dfrac {a - x_n} {y_n - b} \paren {x - x_n}$ The equations of the vertical tangent lines to $\CC$ are: $x = r - a$ for $P = \tuple {r - a, b}$ $x = a - r$ for $P = \tuple {a - r, b}$

title: Equation of Tangent to Ellipse in Reduced Form

title: Equation of Tangents to Circle from Point

title: Equation of Trochoid

snippet: Let $\set {S_1, \ldots, S_m}, \set {T_1, \ldots, T_m}$ be sets of sets in $\R^n$ such that: for each $k \in \set {1, \dots, m}, S_k$ and $T_k$ are equidecomposable. Then the set $\ds S = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^m S_i$ is equidecomposable with $\ds T = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^m T_i$.

title: Equivalence Classes induced by Derivative Function on Set of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be the set of real functions $f: \R \to \R$ which possess continuous derivatives. snippet: Let $\struct {A, \oplus}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on $\struct {A, \oplus}$. Let $\SS$ be a congruence relation on the quotient structure $\struct {A / \RR, \oplus_\RR}$ defined by $\RR$. Let $\TT$ be the relation on $A$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in A: x \mathrel \TT y \iff \eqclass x \RR \mathrel \SS \eqclass y \RR$ Then: $\TT$ is a congruence relation on $\struct {A, \oplus}$ and: there exists a unique isomorphism $\phi$ from $\paren {A / \RR} / \SS$ to $A / \TT$ which satisfies: $\phi \circ q_\SS \circ q_\RR = q_\TT$ where $q_\SS$, $q_\RR$ and $q_\TT$…

title: Equivalence Relation inducing Closed Quotient Set of Magma is Congruence Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\circ_\PP$ be the operation induced by $\circ$ on $\powerset S$, the power set of $S$. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $S / \RR$ denote the quotient set of $S$ induced by $\RR$. Let the algebraic structure $\struct {S / \RR, \circ_\PP}$ be closed. Then: $\RR$ is a congruence relation for $\circ$ and: the operation $\circ_\RR$ induced on $S / \RR$ by $\circ$ is the operation induced on $S / \RR$ by $\circ_\PP$.

title: Equivalence Relation is Circular
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation. Then $\RR$ is also a circular relation.

title: Equivalence Relation is Congruence for Constant Operation
snippet: Every equivalence relation is a congruence relation for the constant operation.

title: Equivalence Relation is Congruence for Left Operation
snippet: Every equivalence relation is a congruence for the left operation $\leftarrow$.

title: Equivalence Relation is Congruence for Right Operation
snippet: Every equivalence relation is a congruence for the right operation $\rightarrow$.

title: Equivalence Relation is Congruence iff Compatible with Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a congruence relation for $\circ$ : {{eqn | q = \forall x, y, z \in S | l = x \mathrel \RR y | o = \implies | r = \paren {x \circ z} \mathrel \RR \paren {y \circ z} }} {{eqn | l = x \mathrel \RR y | o = \implies | r = \paren {z \circ x} \mathrel \RR \paren {z \circ y} }} That is, $\RR$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Equivalence Relation on Cauchy Sequences
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\CC \sqbrk X$ denote the set of all Cauchy sequences of elements from $X$. Let a relation $\sim$ be defined on $\CC \sqbrk X$ by: $\ds \sequence {x_n} \sim \sequence {y_n} \iff \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map d {x_n, y_n} = 0$ Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation on $\CC \sqbrk X$.

title: Equivalence Relation on Integers Modulo 5 induced by Squaring
snippet: Let $\beta$ denote the relation defined on the integers $\Z$ by: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x \mathrel \beta y \iff x^2 \equiv y^2 \pmod 5$ Then $\beta$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Equivalence Relation on Natural Numbers such that Quotient is Power of Two
snippet: Let $\alpha$ denote the relation defined on the natural numbers $\N$ by: $\forall x, y \in \N: x \mathrel \alpha y \iff \exists n \in \Z: x = 2^n y$ Then $\alpha$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Equivalence Relation on Power Set induced by Intersection with Subset
snippet: Let $A, T$ be sets such that $A \subseteq T$. Let $S = \powerset T$ denote the power set of $T$. Let $\alpha$ denote the relation defined on $S$ by: $\forall X, Y \in S: X \mathrel \alpha Y \iff X \cap A = Y \cap A$ Then $\alpha$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Equivalence Relation on Square Matrices induced by Positive Integer Powers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $S$ be the set of all square matrices of order $n$. Let $\alpha$ denote the relation defined on $S$ by: $\forall \mathbf A, \mathbf B \in S: \mathbf A \mathrel \alpha \mathbf B \iff \exists r, s \in \N: \mathbf A^r = \mathbf B^s$ Then $\alpha$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Equivalence Relation on Symmetric Group by Image of n is Congruence Modulo Subgroup
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters $\set {1, \dots, n}$. Let $\sim$ be the relation on $S_n$ defined as: $\forall \pi, \tau \in S_n: \pi \sim \tau \iff \map \pi n = \map \tau n$ Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation which is congruence modulo a subgroup.

title: Equivalence iff Diagonal and Inverse Composite
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$ : $\Delta_S \subseteq \RR$ and: $\RR = \RR \circ \RR^{-1}$

Then the following statements are equivalent: $T_f = T_g$ For almost all $\mathbf x \in \R^d$ we have $\map f {\mathbf x} = \map g {\mathbf x}$.

Principle of Complete Finite Induction: Given a subset $S \subseteq \N$ of the natural numbers which has these properties: $0 \in S$ $\set {0, 1, \ldots, n} \subseteq S \implies n + 1 \in S$ then $S = \N$. title: Equivocation of Nothing
snippet: == Fallacy == This is a fallacy in the following form. Consider a universe of discourse $\mathbb U$ whose elements are strictly ordered by a relation, here denoted better. Let $M \in \mathbb U$ be a maximal element with respect to better. Let $m \in \mathbb U$ be any other element. The fallacy of equivocation of nothing goes as follows: $m$ is better than nothing. Nothing is better than $M$. Therefore, $m$ is better than $M$. As $M$ is maximal, this is a contradiction.

snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be a Euclidean domain whose unity is $1$. Let $a, b, c \in D$. Let $a \divides b \times c$, where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Let $a \perp b$, where $\perp$ denotes relative primeness. Then $a \divides c$.

title: Euclid's Lemma for Irreducible Elements
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be a Euclidean domain whose unity is $1$. Let $p$ be an irreducible element of $D$. Let $a, b \in D$ such that: $p \divides a \times b$ where $\divides$ means is a divisor of. Then $p \divides a$ or $p \divides b$.

title: Euclid's Lemma for Unique Factorization Domain
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be a unique factorization domain. Let $p$ be an irreducible element of $D$. Let $a, b \in D$ such that: $p \divides a \times b$ where $\divides$ means is a divisor of. Then $p \divides a$ or $p \divides b$.

title: Euclid's Theorem
snippet: For any finite set of prime numbers, there exists a prime number not in that set.

title: Euclidean Algorithm
snippet:
== Algorithm == The Euclidean algorithm is a method for finding the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers $a$ and $b$. Let $a, b \in \Z$ and $a 
e 0 \lor b 
e 0$. The steps are: $(1): \quad$ Start with $	uple {a, b}$ such that $\size a \ge \size b$. If $b = 0$ then the task is complete and the GCD is $a$. $(2): \quad$ If $b 
e 0$ then you take the remainder $r$ of $\dfrac a b$. $(3): \quad$ Set $a \gets b, b \gets r$ (and thus $\size a \ge \size b$ again). $(4): \quad$ Repeat these steps until $b = 0$.

title: Euclidean Borel Sigma-Algebra Closed under Scalar Multiplication
snippet: Let $\map \BB {\R^n}$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\R^n$. Let $B \in \BB$, and let $t \in \R_{>0}$. Then also $t \cdot B := \set {t \mathbf b: \mathbf b \in B} \in \BB$.

snippet: == Examples of Use of Euclidean Algorithm in Euclidean Domain ==

title: Euclidean Domain/Examples

title: Euclidean Domain is GCD Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be a Euclidean domain. Then any two elements $a, b \in D$ have a greatest common divisor $d$ such that: $d \divides a \land d \divides b$ $x \divides a \land x \divides b \implies x \divides d$ and $d$ is written $\gcd \set {a, b}$. For any $a, b \in D$: $\exists s, t \in D: s a + t b = d$ Any two greatest common divisors of any $a, b$ are associates.

title: Euclidean Domain is Principal Ideal Domain
snippet: A Euclidean domain is a principal ideal domain.

title: Euclidean Domain is UFD
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be a Euclidean domain. Then $\struct {D, +, \times}$ is a unique factorization domain.

title: Euclidean Metric and Chebyshev Distance on Real Metric Space give rise to Same Topological Space
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be an Euclidean space. Let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Let $T_2 = \struct {\R^n, \tau_2}$ denote the topological space which is induced by $d_2$. Let $T_\infty = \struct {\R^n, \tau_\infty}$ denote the topological space which is induced by $d_\infty$. Then $T_2$ and $T_\infty$ are the same. That is: $\tau_2 = \tau_\infty$

title: Euclidean Metric induces Product Topology
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $d$ be the Euclidean metric on $M_1 \times M_2$. The topology induced by $d$ on $M_1 \times M_2$ is the product topology on $M_1 \times M_2$.

title: Euclidean Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $M_{1'} = \struct {A_{1'}, d_{1'} }, M_{2'} = \struct {A_{2'}, d_{2'} }, \ldots, M_{n'} = \struct {A_{n'}, d_{n'} }$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_{i'}$ be the cartesian product of $A_{1'}, A_{2'}, \ldots, A_{n'}$. The Euclidean metric on $\AA$ is a metric.

title: Euclidean Metric on Real Number Line is Metric
snippet: The Euclidean metric on the real number line $\R$ is a metric.

title: Euclidean Metric on Real Number Plane is Rotation Invariant
snippet: Let $r_\alpha: \R^2 \to \R^2$ denote the rotation of the Euclidean plane about the origin through an angle of $\alpha$. Let $d_2$ denote the Euclidean metric on $\R^2$. Then $d_2$ is unchanged by application of $r_\alpha$: $\forall x, y \in \R^2: \map {d_2} {\map {r_\alpha} x, \map {r_\alpha} y} = \map {d_2} {x, y}$

title: Euclidean Metric on Real Number Space is Translation Invariant
snippet: Let $\tau_{\mathbf t}: \R^n \to \R^n$ denote the translation of the real Euclidean space of $n$ dimensions by the vector $\mathbf t = \tuple {t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n}$. Let $d_2$ denote the Euclidean metric on $\R^n$. Then $d_2$ is unchanged by application of $\tau$: $\forall \mathbf x, \mathbf y \in \R^n: \map {d_2} {\map \tau {\mathbf x}, \map \tau {\mathbf y} } = \map {d_2} {\mathbf x, \mathbf y}$

title: Euclidean Metric on Real Vector Space is Metric
snippet: The Euclidean metric on a real vector space $\R^n$ is a metric.

title: Euclidean Plane is Abstract Geometry
snippet: The Euclidean plane $\struct {\R^2, L_E}$ is an abstract geometry.

title: Euclidean Plus Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $d: \R \times \R \to \R$ be the Euclidean plus metric: $\map d {x, y} := \size {x - y} + \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty 2^{-i} \map \inf {1, \size {\max_{j \mathop \le i} \frac 1 {\size {x - r_j}} - \max_{j \mathop \le i} \frac 1 {\size {y - r_j} } } }$ Then $d$ is indeed a metric.

title: Euclidean Space is Banach Space
snippet: Let $m$ be a positive integer. Then the Euclidean space $\R^m$, along with the Euclidean norm, forms a Banach space over $\R$.

title: Euclidean Space is Complete Metric Space
snippet: Let $m$ be a positive integer. Then the Euclidean space $\R^m$, along with the Euclidean metric, forms a complete metric space.

title: Euclidean Space is Normed Vector Space
snippet: The real Euclidean space $\R^n$ is a normed vector space.

title: Euclidean Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space for $n \in \N$ a natural number. Then $\R^n$ is path-connected.

title: Euclidean Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $\struct {\R^n, \tau_d}$ $n$-dimensional real Euclidean space with the usual topology. Then, $\struct {\R^n, \tau_d}$ is a second-countable space.

title: Euclidean Space is Subspace of Extended Real Number Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\overline \R, \tau}$ be the extended real number space. Then $\tau {\restriction_\R}$, the subspace topology on $\R$, is the Euclidean topology. That is, Euclidean $1$-space is a subspace of the extended real number space.

title: Euclidean Space without Origin is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n \ge 2$. Let $\R^n$ be the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. Let $\R^n \setminus \set {\mathbf 0}$ be $\R^n$ with the origin removed. Then $\R^n \setminus \set {\mathbf 0}$ is path-connected.

title: Euclidean Topology is Product Topology
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {\R, \tau_1}$ be the topological space such that $\tau_1$ is the Euclidean topology on $\R$. Let $T_n = \struct {\R^n, \tau_n}$ be the topological space such that $\tau_n$ is the product topology on the cartesian product $\ds \R_n = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \R$. Then the Euclidean topology on $\R^n$ and the product topology on $\R^n$ are the same.

snippet: Let a rigid body $B$ rotate about an axis $\AA$ which is fixed in relation to $B$ and parallel to the principal axis of inertia of $B$. title: Euler's Number:Limit of Sequence implies Base of Logarithm
snippet: Let $e$ be Euler's number defined by: $\ds e := \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {1 + \frac 1 n}^n$ Then $e$ is the unique solution to the equation $\map \ln x = 1$. That is: $\map \ln x = 1 \iff x = e$

title: Euler's Number:Limit of Sequence implies Limit of Series
snippet: Let Euler's number $e$ be defined as: $\ds e := \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {1 + \frac 1 n}^n$ Then: $\ds e = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac 1 {k!}$ That is: $e = \dfrac 1 {0!} + \dfrac 1 {1!} + \dfrac 1 {2!} + \dfrac 1 {3!} + \dfrac 1 {4!} \cdots$

title: Euler's Number as Limit of 1 + Reciprocal of n to nth Power
snippet: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {1 + \frac 1 n}^n = e$ where $e$ denotes Euler's number.

title: Euler's Number as Limit of n over nth Root of n Factorial
snippet: $\ds e = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac n {\sqrt [n] {n!} }$ where: $e$ denotes Euler's number $n!$ denotes $n$ factorial.

title: Euler's Number as Sum of Egyptian Fractions
snippet: The reciprocal of Euler's number $e$ can be approximated by the following sequence of Egyptian fractions: $\dfrac 1 e = \dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 1 {29} + \dfrac 1 {15 \, 786} + \dfrac 1 {513 \, 429 \, 610} + \cdots$

title: Euler's Theorem for Planar Graphs
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a connected planar graph with $V$ vertices and $E$ edges. Let $F$ be the number of faces of $G$. Then: $V - E + F = 2$

title: Euler Lucky Number Function for n equals p

title: Euler Method
snippet: == Proof Technique == Consider the first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' = \map f {x, y}$ subject to the initial condition $\map y {x_0} = y_0$ where $\map f {x, y}$ is a continuous real function. Let $\map y x$ be the particular solution of $(1)$. For all $n \in \N_{>0}$, we define: $x_n = x_{n - 1} + h$ where $h \in \R_{>0}$. Then for all $n \in \N_{>0}$ such that $x_n$ is in the domain of $y$: $y_{n + 1} = y_n + h \map f {x_n, y_n}$ is an approximation to $\map y {x_{n + 1} }$.

title: Euler Number for Odd Index is Zero

title: Euler Phi Function by Argument is Injective
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \N$ be the arithmetic function defined as: $\map f n = n \map \phi n$ where $\map \phi n$ is the Euler Phi function (which is not injective). Then $f$ is injective.

title: Euler Phi Function in terms of Möbius Function
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map \mu d \frac n d = \map \phi n$ where: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n}$ denotes the sum over all of the divisors of $n$ $\map \phi n$ is the Euler $\phi$ function, the number of integers less than $n$ that are prime to $n$ $\map \mu d$ is the Möbius function. Equivalently, this says that: $\phi = \mu * I_{\Z_{>0} }$ where: $*$ denotes Dirichlet convolution $I_{\Z_{>0} }$ denotes the identity mapping on $\Z_{>0}$, that is: $\forall n \in \Z_{>0}: I_{\Z_{>0} }: n \mapsto n$

title: Euler Phi Function is Even for Argument greater than 2

title: Euler Phi Function is Multiplicative
snippet: The Euler $\phi$ function is a multiplicative function: $m \perp n \implies \map \phi {m n} = \map \phi m \map \phi n$ where $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Euler Phi Function is not Completely Multiplicative
snippet: The Euler $\phi$ function is not a completely multiplicative function. That is, it is not always the case that: $\map \phi {m n} = \map \phi m \map \phi n$ where $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Euler Phi Function of Integer
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$, that is, a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\phi: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the Euler $\phi$ function. Then for any $n \in \Z_{>0}$, we have: $\map \phi n = n \paren {1 - \dfrac 1 {p_1} } \paren {1 - \dfrac 1 {p_2} } \cdots \paren {1 - \dfrac 1 {p_r} }$ where $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_r$ are the distinct primes dividing $n$. Or, more compactly: $\ds \map \phi n = n \prod_{p \mathop \divides n} \paren {1 - \frac 1 p}$ where $p \divides n$ denotes the primes which divide $n$.

title: Euler Phi Function of Non-Square Semiprime
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a semiprime with distinct prime factors $p$ and $q$. Let $\map \phi n$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function. Then: $\map \phi n = \paren {p - 1} \paren {q - 1}$

title: Euler Phi Function of Power Minus One is Divisible by Exponent
snippet: Let $a, n \in \Z$ with $a \ge 2$ and $n \ge 1$. Then: $n \divides \map \phi {a^n - 1}$ where $\phi$ is the Euler phi function.

title: Euler Phi Function of Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then: $\map \phi p = p - 1$ where $\phi: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ is the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Euler Phi Function of Prime Power
snippet: Let $p^n$ be a prime power for some prime number $p > 1$. Then: $\map \phi {p^n} = p^n \paren {1 - \dfrac 1 p} = \paren {p - 1} p^{n - 1}$ where $\phi: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ is the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Euler Phi Function of Product
snippet: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers. Let $d$ be the greatest common divisor of $m$ and $n$. Then: $\map \phi {m n} = \map \phi m \map \phi n \paren {\dfrac d {\map \phi d} }$ where $\phi$ is the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Euler Phi Function of Product with Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be prime and $n \in \Z: n \ge 1$. Then: $\map \phi {p n} = \begin{cases} \paren {p - 1} \map \phi n & : p \nmid n \\ p \map \phi n & : p \divides n \end{cases}$ where: $\map \phi n$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function of $n$ $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Thus for all $n \ge 1$ and for any prime $p$, we have that $\map \phi n$ divides $\map \phi {p n}$.

title: Euler Phi Function of Square-Free Integer
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that $n \ge 2$. Let $n$ be square-free. Let $\map \phi n$ be the Euler $\phi$ function of $n$. That is, let $\map \phi n$ be the count of strictly positive integers less than or equal to $n$ which are prime to $n$. Then: $\map \phi n = \ds \prod_{\substack {p \mathop \divides n \\ p \mathop > 2} } \paren {p - 1}$ where $p \divides n$ denotes the primes which divide $n$.

title: Euler Phi Function of n equal to Euler Phi Function of n+3
snippet: Let $\phi$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function. The only solutions to the equation: $\map \phi n = \map \phi {n + 3}$ less than $1 \, 000 \, 000$ are: $\map \phi 3 = \map \phi 6 = 2$ $\map \phi 5 = \map \phi 8 = 4$

title: Euler Phi Function preserves Divisibility
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\map \phi n$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function of $n$. Then: $d \divides n \implies \map \phi d \divides \map \phi n$ where $d \divides n$ denotes that $d$ is a divisor of $n$.

title: Euler Polyhedron Formula
snippet: For any convex polyhedron with $V$ vertices, $E$ edges, and $F$ faces: $V - E + F = 2$

title: Euler Theorem on Curvature of Surface
snippet: Let $S$ be a surface in space. The principal directions of the curvature of $S$ are perpendicular to each other.

title: Euler Triangle Formula
snippet: Let $d$ be the distance between the incenter and the circumcenter of a triangle. Then: $d^2 = R \paren {R - 2 \rho}$ where: $R$ is the circumradius $\rho$ is the inradius.

snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 2$. Let $\map \Li x$ denote the Eulerian logarithmic integral of $x$. Let $\map \pi x$ denote the prime-counting function of $x$. Then $\map \Li x$ is asymptotically equal to $\map \pi x$.

title: Eulerian Logarithmic Integral is less than Prime-Counting Function for Infinite Number of Integers
snippet: Let $\map \Li x$ denote the Eulerian logarithmic integral for $x \in \Z$. Let $\map \pi x$ denote the prime-counting function for $x \in \Z$. Then there exist an infinite set of integers $x$ such that: $\map \Li x < \map \pi x$

title: Evaluation Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be a unitary $R$-module whose dimension is finite. Then the evaluation linear transformation $J: G \to G^{**}$ is an isomorphism.

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation is Bilinear
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $G$ be an $R$-module. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $\innerprod x t$ be the evaluation linear transformation from $G$ to $G^{**}$. Then the mapping $\phi: G \times G^* \to R$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, t} \in G \times G^*: \map \phi {x, t} = \innerprod x t$ satisfies the following bilinearity properties: {{eqn | n = 1 | q = \forall x, y \in G: \forall t \in G^* | l = \innerprod {x + y} t | r = \innerprod x t + \innerprod y t }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall x \in G: \forall s, t \in G^* | l = \innerprod x {s + t} | r = \innerprod x s +…

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be an $R$-module. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $G^{**}$ be the double dual of $G^*$. Let the mapping $J: G \to G^{**}$ be the evaluation linear transformation from $G$ into $G^{**}$ defined as: $\forall x \in G: \map J x = x^\wedge$ where for each $x \in G$, $x^\wedge: G^* \to R$ is defined as: $\forall t \in G^*: \map {x^\wedge} t = \map t x$ Then $J$ is a linear transformation.

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation on Normed Vector Space is Linear Isometry
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm \cdot_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the second normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$. Let $J : X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation for $X$. Then: $J$ is a linear isometry.

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation on Normed Vector Space is Linear Transformation from Space to Second Normed Dual
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm \cdot_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$. Let $\map L {X^\ast, \Bbb F}$ be the set of linear functionals on $X^\ast$. For each $x \in X$, define $x^\wedge : X^\ast 	o \Bbb F$ by: $\map {x^\wedge} f = \map f x$ Define $J : X 	o \map L {X^\ast, \Bbb F}$ by: $\map J x = x^\wedge$ for each $x \in X$. Then: $J$ is a linear transformation $X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$. where $X^{\ast \ast}$ denotes the second normed dual.

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation on Normed Vector Space is Weak to Weak-* Continuous Embedding into Second Normed Dual
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual of $X$. Let $X^{\ast \ast}$ be the second normed dual of $X$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^{\ast \ast}$. Let $\iota : X \to X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation. Then $\iota$ is $\struct {w, w^\ast}$-continuous.

title: Evaluation Linear Transformation on Normed Vector Space is Weak to Weak-* Homeomorphism onto Image
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual of $X$. Let $X^{\ast \ast}$ be the second normed dual of $X$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^{\ast \ast}$. Let $\iota : X \to X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation. Then $\iota : \struct {X, w} \to \struct {\iota X, w^\ast}$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Evaluation Mapping is Injective iff Mappings Separate Points
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for some indexing set $I$. Let $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of continuous mappings. Let $\ds Y = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} Y_i$ be the product space of $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be the evaluation mapping induced by $\family{f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $f$ is an injection $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ separates points

title: Evaluation Mapping on T1 Space is Embedding if Mappings Separate Points from Closed Sets
snippet: Let $X$ be a $T_1$ topological space. Let $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for some indexing set $I$. Let $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of continuous mappings. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ separate points from closed sets. Let $\ds Y = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} Y_i$ be the product space of $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be the evaluation mapping induced by $\family{f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $f$ is an embedding

title: Evaluation of Integral using Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\ds \int_0^{\to \infty} \map f t \rd t = \map F 0$ assuming the integral is convergent.

title: Even Convergent of Simple Continued Fraction is Strictly Smaller than Odd Convergent
snippet: Let $n \in \N \cup \set \infty$ be an extended natural number. Let $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, \ldots}$ be a simple continued fraction in $\R$ of length $n$. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Let $\sequence {C_0, C_1, \ldots}$ be its sequence of convergents. Every even convergent is strictly smaller than every odd convergent.

title: Even Convergents of Simple Continued Fraction are Strictly Increasing
snippet: Let $n \in \N \cup \set \infty$ be an extended natural number. Let $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, \ldots}$ be a simple continued fraction in $\R$ of length $n$. Let $p_0, p_1, p_2, \ldots$ and $q_0, q_1, q_2, \ldots$ be its numerators and denominators. Let $\sequence {C_0, C_1, \ldots}$ be its sequence of convergents. The even convergents satisfy $C_0 < C_2 < C_4 \cdots$.

title: Even Derivatives of Cotangent of Pi Z at One Fourth
snippet: $ \ds \valueat {\dfrac {\d^{2 n} } {\d z^{2 n} } \cot \pi z} {z \mathop = \frac 1 4} = \paren {-1}^n \paren {2 \pi}^{2 n} E_{2 n}$ where: $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number $n$ is a non-negative integer.

title: Even Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Even Functions ==

title: Even Function Times Even Function is Even
snippet: Let $X \subset \R$ be a symmetric set of real numbers: $\forall x \in X: -x \in X$ Let $f, g: X \to \R$ be two even functions. Let $f \cdot g$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then $\paren {f \cdot g}: X \to \R$ is also an even function.

title: Even Functions in 2-Lebesgue Space form Closed Subspace of 2-Lebesgue Space
snippet: Let $\map {\LL^2} \R$ be the Lebesgue $2$-space. For all $f \in \map {\LL^2} \R$ denote $\map {\check f} x = \map f {-x}$. Let $Y = \set {f \in \map {\LL^2} \R : f = \check f}$ be the set of all even functions in $\map {\LL^2} \R$. Then $Y$ is a closed subspace of $\map {\LL^2} \R$.

title: Even Impulse Pair is Fourier Transform of Cosine Function
snippet: Consider the (real) cosine function $\map \cos x: \R \to \R$. $\map f x = \map \cos {\pi x}$ Then: {{eqn | l = \map {\hat f} s | r = \dfrac 1 2 \map \delta {s - \dfrac 1 2} + \dfrac 1 2 \map \delta {s + \dfrac 1 2} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \map {\operatorname {II} } s | c = }} where: $\map {\hat f} s$ is the Fourier transform of $\map f x$. $\operatorname {II}$ denotes the even impulse pair function.

title: Even Integer Plus 5 is Odd
snippet: Let $x \in \Z$ be an even integer. Then $x + 5$ is odd.

title: Even Integer with Abundancy Index greater than 9
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ have an abundancy index greater than $9$. Then $n$ has at least $35$ distinct prime factors.

title: Even Integers do not form Integral Domain
snippet: Let $2 \Z$ be the set of even integers. Then $\struct {2 \Z, +, \times}$ is not an integral domain.

title: Even Integers form Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $2 \Z$ be the set of even integers. Then $\struct {2 \Z, +, \times}$ is a commutative ring. However, $\struct {2 \Z, +, \times}$ is not an integral domain.

title: Even Integers not Expressible as Sum of 3, 5 or 7 with Prime
snippet: The even integers that cannot be expressed as the sum of $2$ prime numbers where one of those primes is $3$, $5$ or $7$ begins: $98, 122, 124, 126, 128, 148, 150, \ldots$

title: Even Integers not Sum of 2 Twin Primes
snippet: The following even integers cannot be expressed as the sum of $2$ prime numbers which are each one of a pair of twin primes: $2, 4, 94, 96, 98, 400, 402, 404, \ldots$

title: Even Integers not Sum of Two Abundant Numbers
snippet: The even integers which are not the sum of $2$ abundant numbers are: All even integers less than $24$; $26, 28, 34, 46$

title: Even Multiple Angle Formula for Cosine
snippet: $\ds \cos 2 n \theta = \paren {-1}^n \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {1 - \frac {\cos^2 \theta} {\map {\cos^2} {\frac {\paren {2 k - 1} \pi} {4 n} } } }$

title: Even Natural Numbers are Infinite
snippet: The set of even natural numbers is infinite.

title: Even Number minus Even Number is Even
Even Number minus Odd Number is Odd
Even Order Derivative of Odd Function Vanishes at Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be a symmetric subset of $\R$ containing $0$. Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $f:X \to \R$ be an odd function. Let $f$ be at least $\paren {2 n}$-times differentiable. Then: $\map {f^{\paren {2 n} } } 0 = 0$

title: Even Order Group has Odd Number of Order 2 Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $G$ be of even order. Then $G$ has an odd number of elements of order $2$.

title: Even Order Group has Order 2 Element
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $G$ be of even order. Then: $\exists x \in G: \order x = 2$ That is: $\exists x \in G: x \ne e: x^2 = e$

title: Even Perfect Number ends in 6 or 28 preceded by Odd Digit
snippet: Let $n$ be an even perfect number. Then $n$ ends either in $6$ or $28$ preceded by an odd digit.

title: Even Perfect Number except 6 is Congruent to 1 Modulo 9
snippet: Let $n$ be an even perfect number, but not $6$. Then: $n \equiv 1 \pmod 9$

title: Even Perfect Number is Hexagonal
snippet: All perfect numbers which are even are hexagonal.

title: Even Perfect Number is Sum of Successive Odd Cubes except 6
snippet: Let $n$ be an even perfect number such that $n \ne 6$. Then: $\ds n = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^m \paren {2 k - 1}^3 = 1^3 + 3^3 + \cdots + \paren {2 m - 1}^3$ for some $m \in \Z_{>0}$. That is, every even perfect number apart from $6$ is the sum of the sequence of the first $m$ odd cubes, for some $m$.

title: Even Perfect Number is Triangular
snippet: All perfect numbers which are even are triangular.

title: Even Permutation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Even Permutations ==

title: Even Permutation is Product of 3-Cycles
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ such that $n \ge 3$. Let $\pi: \N_n \to \N_n$ be a permutation on $n$ letters. Let $\pi$ be an even permutation. Then $\pi$ can be expressed as the composition of cyclic permutations of length $3$.

title: Even Power is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n \in \Z$ be an even integer. Then $x^n \ge 0$. That is, all even powers are positive.

title: Even Power of 3 as Sum of Consecutive Positive Integers
snippet: Take the positive integers and group them in sets such that the $n$th set contains the next $3^n$ positive integers: $\set 1, \set {2, 3, 4}, \set {5, 6, \ldots, 13}, \set {14, 15, \cdots, 40}, \ldots$ Let the $n$th such set be denoted $S_{n - 1}$, that is, letting $S_0 := \set 1$ be considered as the zeroth. Then the sum of all the elements of $S_n$ is $3^{2 n}$.

title: Even Power of Negative Real Number
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n \in \Z$ be an even integer. Then: $\paren {-x}^n = x^n$

title: Even Vertex of Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Even Vertices ==

title: Even and Odd Integers form Partition of Integers
snippet: The odd integers and even integers form a partition of the integers.

title: Evenly Spaced Integer Space is Countably Infinite
snippet: The evenly spaced integer space is a countably infinite topological space.

title: Evenly Spaced Integer Space is Sigma-Compact
snippet: The evenly spaced integer space is a $\sigma$-compact space.

title: Evenly Spaced Integer Space is not Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: The evenly spaced integer space is not a weakly locally compact space.

title: Evenly Spaced Integer Space is not Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact
snippet: The evenly spaced integer space is not a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact space.

title: Event/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Events ==

title: Event Independence is Symmetric
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be events in a probability space. Let $A$ be independent of $B$. Then $B$ is independent of $A$. That is, is independent of is a symmetric relation.

title: Event Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Event Spaces ==

title: Event Space contains Empty Set
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $\O \in \Sigma$ That is, the empty set is in the event space.

title: Event Space contains Sample Space
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $\Omega \in \Sigma$ where $\Omega$ is the sample space of $\EE$.

title: Event Space from Single Subset of Sample Space
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment whose sample space is $\Omega$. Let $\O \subsetneqq A \subsetneqq \Omega$. Then $\Sigma := \set {\O, A, \Omega \setminus A, \Omega}$ is an event space of $\EE$.

title: Event Space of Experiment with Final Sample Space has Even Cardinality
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\Omega$ be a finite set. Then the event space $\Sigma$ consists of an even number of subsets of $\Omega$.

title: Event of Stopping Time Equal to Infinity is Measurable in Limit of Filtration
Events One of Which equals Intersection
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A, B \in \Sigma$ be events of $\EE$, so that $A \subseteq \Omega$ and $B \subseteq \Omega$. Let $A$ and $B$ be such that: $A \cap B = A$ Then whenever $A$ occurs, it is always the case that $B$ occurs as well.

title: Events One of Which equals Union
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A, B \in \Sigma$ be events of $\EE$, so that $A \subseteq \Omega$ and $B \subseteq \Omega$. Let $A$ and $B$ be such that: $A \cup B = A$ Then whenever $B$ occurs, it is always the case that $A$ occurs as well.

title: Eventually Constant Sequence Converges to Constant
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a normed division ring. Let $\lambda \in R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $R$ such that: $\exists N \in \R_{>0} : \forall n \ge N: x_n = \lambda$ Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n = \lambda$

title: Every Element is Directed and Every Two Elements are Included in Third Element implies Union is Directed
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\forall X \in A: X$ is directed. Let $\forall X, Y \in A: \exists Z \in A: X \cup Y \subseteq Z$ Then $\bigcup A$ is directed.

title: Every Element is Lower implies Union is Lower
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\forall X \in A: X$ is a lower section. Then $\bigcup A$ is a lower section.

title: Every Filter has Adherent Point implies Every Ultrafilter Converges
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let every filter on $S$ have a adherent point in $S$. Then every ultrafilter on $S$ converges to a point in $S$.

title: Every Operation is Distributive over Left Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\gets$ denote the left operation on $S$. Then $\circ$ is distributive over $\gets$.

title: Every Operation is Distributive over Right Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\to$ denote the right operation on $S$. Then $\circ$ is distributive over $\to$.

title: Every Point except Endpoint in Connected Linearly Ordered Space is Cut Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a connected space. Let $p \in A$ be a point of $A$ which is not an endpoint of $A$. Then $p$ is a cut point of $A$.

title: Every Pseudoprime Element is Prime implies Lattice is Arithmetic
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below algebraic distributive lattice. Assume that for every element $p$ of $S$ if $p$ is pseudoprime element, then $p$ is prime element. Then $L$ is arithmetic.

title: Every Triangle has 2 Equal Sides
snippet: == Fallacy == Every triangle has $2$ sides that are equal in length. That is, all triangles are isosceles.

title: Every Ultrafilter Converges implies Every Filter has Adherent Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let every ultrafilter on $S$ be convergent. Then every filter on $S$ has a adherent point.

title: Everywhere Dense Set determines Adjoint Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_Y}$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $\DD$ be an everywhere dense subset of $Y$. Let $T : X \to Y$ and $S : Y \to X$ be bounded linear transformations such that: $\innerprod {T x} y_Y = \innerprod x {S y}_X$ for each $x \in X$ and $y \in \DD$. Then $S = T^\ast$.

title: Everywhere Dense Subset of Countable Hilbert Space Direct Sum in terms of Everywhere Dense Subsets of Summands
snippet: Let $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of Hilbert spaces over $\C$. For each $n \in \N$, let $\family {e^{(n)}_\alpha}_{\alpha \in \map J n}$ be an everywhere dense subset of $\HH_n$. Let $\tuple {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\family {\tuple {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$.

title: Everywhere Dense iff Interior of Complement is Empty
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subset S$. Then $A$ is everywhere dense : $\paren {\relcomp S A}^\circ = \O$ where $A^\circ$ is the interior of $A$.

title: Evolute/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Evolutes ==

title: Evolute of Circle is its Center
snippet: The evolute of a circle is a single point: its center.

title: Evolute of Cycloid is Cycloid
snippet: The evolute of a cycloid is another cycloid.

title: Evolute of Ellipse
snippet: Let $E$ be an ellipse embedded in a Cartesian plane with the equation: $\dfrac {x^2} {a^2} + \dfrac {y^2} {b^2} = 1$

title: Evolute of Parabola
snippet: The evolute of the parabola $y = x^2$ is the curve: $27 X^2 = 16 \paren {Y - \dfrac 1 2}^3$

title: Exact Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exact Differential Equation == This page gathers examples of exact differential equations of the first order: $\map M {x, y} \rd x + \map N {x, y} \rd y = 0$ where there exists a function $\map f {x, y}$ such that: $\dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x} = M, \dfrac {\partial f} {\partial y} = N$ such that the second partial derivatives of $f$ exist and are continuous.

title: Exact Divisor/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exact Divisors ==

title: Exact Form of Prime-Counting Function
snippet: Let: $\ds \map \Pi x = \map \Li x - \sum_\rho \map \Li {x^\rho} - \map \ln 2 + \int_x^\infty \frac {\d t} {t \paren {t^2 - 1} \map \ln t}$ where: $\map \Li x$ is the offset logarithmic integral the sum $\ds \sum_\rho$ is taken over all $0 < \rho \in \R$ such that the zeta function $\map \zeta {\alpha + i \rho} = 0$ for some $\alpha \in \R$. Then the prime-counting function is precisely: $\ds \map \pi x = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\frac {\map \mu n} n \map \Pi {x^{1 / n} } }$ where $\map \mu n$ denotes the Möbius function.

title: Example:Antiassociative Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {\R_{>0}, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure where $\R_{>0}$ denotes the strictly positive real numbers. Define: $\forall x, y \in \R_{>0}: x \circ y = x y + y$ Then $\circ$ is antiassociative on $\R_{>0}$: $\forall x, y, z \in \R_{>0}: \paren {x \circ y} \circ z \ne x \circ \paren {y \circ z}$ and so $\struct {\R_{>0}, \circ}$ is an antiassociative structure.
