title: Existence of Unique Difference between Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Then there exists exactly one cut $\gamma$ such that: $\alpha + \gamma = \beta$

title: Existence of Unique Inverse Element for Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Then there exists a unique cut $\beta$ such that: $\alpha + \beta = 0^*$ where $+$ denotes the operation of addition of cuts.

title: Existence of Unique Inverse Element for Multiplication of Cuts
snippet: Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Let $\alpha$ be a cut such that $\alpha \ne 0^*$. Then for every cut $\beta$, there exists a unique cut $\gamma$ such that: $\alpha \gamma = \beta$ where $\alpha \gamma$ denotes the operation of product of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$. In this context, $\gamma$ can be expressed as $\beta / \alpha$.

title: Existence of Unique Subgroup Generated by Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\O \subset S \subseteq G$. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be the subgroup generated by $S$. Then $H = \gen S$ exists and is unique. Also, $\struct {H, \circ}$ is the intersection of all of the subgroups of $G$ which contain the set $S$: $\ds \gen S = \bigcap_i {H_i}: S \subseteq H_i \le G$

title: Existence of Unique Subsemigroup Generated by Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\O \subset X \subseteq S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup generated by $X$. Then $T = \gen X$ exists and is unique.

title: Existence of Unitization of C*-Algebra
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra that is not unital as an algebra. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$ as an algebra. Define: $	uple {x, \lambda}^\ast = 	uple {x^\ast, \overline \lambda}$ for each $	uple {x, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then there exists a unique algebra norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast$ such that $\struct {A_+, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast}$ is a unital $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Further, $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\ast$ extends $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$.

title: Existence of Universal Class
snippet: There exists a unique class $V$ such that: $\forall u: u \in V$ That is, the universal class exists and is unique.

title: Existence of Upper Bound of Finite Subset of Directed Set
snippet: Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\FF \subseteq \Lambda$ be a finite subset. Then $\FF$ has an upper bound in $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$.

title: Existence of Upper and Lower Numbers of Cut whose Difference equal Given Rational
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $r \in \Q_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive rational number. Then there exist rational numbers $p$ and $q$ such that: $p \in \alpha, q \notin \alpha$ $q - p = r$ such that $q$ is not the smallest upper number of $\alpha$.

title: Existence of Urysohn Function does not guarantee Normal Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space. Let $T$ have the property that: For all closed sets $A, B \subseteq S$ of $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$, there exists an Urysohn function for $A$ and $B$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a normal space.

title: Existence of Vector Space Bases implies Axiom of Choice
snippet: The supposition that every vector space has a basis, along with the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms, implies that the holds.

title: Existence of Vitali Set implies Subset of Unit Interval with Inner Measure Zero and Outer Measure 1
snippet: Let us posit the existence of a Vitali set. Then there exists a subset of the closed unit interval which has an inner measure of $0$ and an outer measure of $1$.

title: Existence of n such that M - 2^n or M + 2^n has no Prime factors less than 331
snippet: Let $M \in \Z$ be an integer. Then there exists a positive integer $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ such that either $M - 2^n$ or $M + 2^n$ has no prime factors less than $331$.

title: Existence of q for which j - qk is Positive
snippet: Let $j, k \in \Z$ be integers such that $k > 0$. Then there exist $q \in \Z$ such that $j - q k > 0$.

title: Existential Import/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Existential Import ==

title: Existential Quantification of Provable Arithmetic Formula is Provable
snippet: Let $\map \phi x$ be a WFF in the language of arithmetic with $1$ free variable. Let $\sqbrk a$ denote the unary representation of $a$. Suppose that, for every $n \in \N$ such that $\N \models \map \phi {x \gets \sqbrk n}$: $\map \phi {x \gets \sqbrk n}$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic. Suppose also that: $\N \models \exists x: \map \phi x$ Then: $\exists x: \map \phi x$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

title: Existential Quantifier Distributes over Conjunction
snippet: Let $\map \phi x, \map \psi x$ be WFFs of the free variable $x$. Then: $\exists x: \paren {\map \phi x \land \map \psi x} \vdash \paren {\exists x: \map \phi x} \land \paren {\exists x: \map \psi x}$

title: Existential Quantifier Distributes over Disjunction
snippet: Let $\map \phi x, \map \psi x$ be WFFs of the free variable $x$. Then: $\exists x: \paren {\map \phi x \lor \map \psi x} \dashv \vdash \paren {\exists x: \map \phi x} \lor \paren {\exists x: \map \psi x}$

title: Existential Statement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Existential Statements ==

title: Exists Bijection to a Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then there exists a bijection from $T$ onto a set $T'$ disjoint from $S$.

title: Exists Divisor in Set of n+1 Natural Numbers no greater than 2n
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of $n + 1$ non-non-zero natural numbers all less than or equal to $2 n$. Then there exists $a, b \in S$ such that $a \divides b$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

title: Exists Element Not in Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $\exists x: x \notin S$ That is, for any set, there exists some element which is not in that set.

title: Exists Ordinal Greater than Set of Ordinals
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of ordinals. Then there exists an ordinal greater than every element of $S$: If $S$ contains a greatest ordinal $\alpha$, then $\alpha^+$ is greater than every element of $S$ If $S$ does not contain a greatest ordinal, then $\bigcup S$ is greater than every element of $S$.

title: Exists Rational Cut Between two Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Let $\alpha < \beta$, where $<$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts. Then there exists a rational cut $r^*$ associated with the rational number $r$ such that: $\alpha < r^* < \beta$

title: Exists Subset which is not Element
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists at least one subset of $S$ which is not an element of $S$.

title: Exogenous Variable/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exogenous Variables == An example of an exogenous variable is the occurrence and quantity of rainfall. Depending on the economic model under analysis, it may be the case that the demand for certain products, for example, may be affected by the weather.

title: Exp (-x^2) is Schwartz Test Function
snippet: $\map \exp {-x^2}$ is a Schwartz test function.

title: Expanded Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Expanded Numbers ==

title: Expansion of Associated Reduced Quadratic Irrational
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\alpha$ be a reduced quadratic irrational which is associated to $n$. Let $\alpha$ be transformed into its integer part and fractional part via: $\alpha = \left \lfloor {\alpha} \right \rfloor + \dfrac 1{\alpha'}$ Then the resulting quadratic irrational $\alpha'$ is also reduced and associated to $n$.

title: Expansion of Characteristic Polynomial of Matrix
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $R \sqbrk x$ be the polynomial ring in one variable over $R$. Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $R$ of order $n > 0$. Let $\map {p_{\mathbf A} } x$ be the characteristic polynomial of $\mathbf A$. Then $\map {p_{\mathbf A} } x$ can be expressed as: $\map {p_{\mathbf A} } x = x^n + a_{n - 1} x^{n - 1} + \cdots + a_0$ where: {{eqn | l = a_{n - 1} | r = -\map \tr {\mathbf A} | c = where $\map \tr {\mathbf A}$ denotes the trace of $\mathbf A$ }} {{eqn | l = a_0 | r = \paren {-1}^n \map \det {\mathbf A} | c = where $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ denotes…

title: Expansion of Included Set Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A_1 \subseteq S$ and $A_2 \subseteq S$. Let $T_1 = \struct {S, \tau_{A_1} }$ and $T_2 = \struct {S, \tau_{A_2} }$ be included set spaces on $S$. Then: $(1): \quad T_1 \ge T_2 \iff A_1 \subseteq A_2$ $(2): \quad T_1 > T_2 \iff A_1 \subsetneq A_2$ where: $T_1 \ge T_2$ denotes that $T_1$ is finer than $T_2$ $T_1 > T_2$ denotes that $T_1$ is strictly finer than $T_2$.

title: Expectation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Expectation ==

title: Expectation Preserves Inequality
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ be random variables. Let $\map \Pr {X \ge Y} = 1$. Then: $\expect X \ge \expect Y$

title: Expectation and Variance of Poisson Distribution equal its Parameter
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the expectation of $X$ equals the variance of $X$, that is, $\lambda$ itself.

title: Expectation is Linear
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\expect X$ denote the expectation of $X$. Then: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \R: \expect {\alpha X + \beta Y} = \alpha \, \expect X + \beta \, \expect Y$

title: Expectation is Monotone
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables such that: $\forall \omega \in \Omega: \map X \omega \le \map Y \omega$ Then: $\expect X \le \expect Y$

title: Expectation of Almost Surely Constant Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be an almost surely constant random variable. That is, there exists some $c \in \R$ such that: $\map \Pr {X = c} = 1$ Then: $\expect X = c$

title: Expectation of Bernoulli Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $p$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = p$

title: Expectation of Beta Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \BetaDist \alpha \beta$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\operatorname {Beta}$ denotes the beta distribution. Then: $\expect X = \dfrac \alpha {\alpha + \beta}$

title: Expectation of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$ for some $n \in \N$ and $0 \le p \le 1$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = n p$

title: Expectation of Bounded Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $b \ge a$. Let: $\map \Pr {a \le X \le b} = 1$ Then: $a \le \expect X \le b$ where $\expect X$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

title: Expectation of Chi-Squared Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim \chi_n^2$ where $\chi_n^2$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = n$

title: Expectation of Chi Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim \chi_n$ where $\chi_n$ is the chi distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \sqrt 2 \dfrac {\map \Gamma {\paren {n + 1} / 2} } {\map \Gamma {n / 2} }$ where $\Gamma$ is the gamma function.

title: Expectation of Conditional Expectation
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra. Let $X$ be a integrable random variable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Then: $\expect {\expect {X \mid \GG} } = \expect X$

title: Expectation of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a < b$. Let $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$ be the continuous uniform distribution over $\closedint a b$. Then: $\expect X = \dfrac {a + b} 2$

title: Expectation of Discrete Random Variable from PGF
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable whose probability generating function is $\map {\Pi_X} s$. Then the expectation of $X$ is the value of the first derivative of $\map {\Pi_X} s$ $s$ at $s = 1$. That is: $\expect X = \map {\Pi'_X} 1$

title: Expectation of Discrete Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the discrete uniform distribution with parameter $n$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac {n + 1} 2$

title: Expectation of Erlang Distribution
snippet: Let $k$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\lambda$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with an Erlang distribution with parameters $k$ and $\lambda$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac k \lambda$

title: Expectation of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable of the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$ for some $\beta \in \R_{> 0}$ Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \beta$

title: Expectation of Function of Continuous Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable. Let $\expect X$ be the expectation of $X$. Let $g: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\ds \expect {g \sqbrk X} = \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map g x \map f x $

title: Expectation of Function of Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable. Let $\expect X$ be the expectation of $X$. Let $g: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\ds \expect {g \sqbrk X} = \sum_{x \mathop \in \Omega_X} \map g x \, \map \Pr {X = x}$ whenever the sum is absolutely convergent.

title: Expectation of Function of Joint Probability Mass Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\expect X$ be the expectation of $X$. Let $g: \R^2 \to \R$ be a real-valued function Let $p_{X, Y}$ be the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y$. $\ds \expect {\map g {X, Y} } = \sum_{x \mathop \in \Omega_X} \sum_{y \mathop \in \Omega_Y} \map g {x, y} \map {p_{X, Y} } {x, y}$ whenever the sum is absolutely convergent.

title: Expectation of Gamma Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution. The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac \alpha \beta$

title: Expectation of Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the geometric distribution with parameter $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$.

title: Expectation of Hat-Check Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Hat-Check distribution with parameter $n$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = n - 1$

title: Expectation of Linear Transformation of Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $a, b$ be real numbers. Let $\expect X$ denote the expectation of $X$. Then we have: $\expect {a X + b} = a \expect X + b$ if that expectation exists.

title: Expectation of Log Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the Log Normal distribution with $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$. The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \exp {\paren {\mu + \dfrac {\sigma^2 } 2 } }$

title: Expectation of Logistic Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which satisfies the logistic distribution: $X \sim \map {\operatorname {Logistic} } {\mu, s}$ The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \mu$

title: Expectation of Negative Binomial Distribution (Type 2)/Also defined as
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the type $2$ negative binomial distribution with parameters $r$ and $p$. Let $X$ use the definition as the number of failures before $r$ successes have occurred. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac {r q} p$ where $q = 1 - p$.

title: Expectation of Non-Negative Random Variable is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $\map \Pr {X \ge 0} = 1$. Then: $\expect X \ge 0$ where $\expect X$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

title: Expectation of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim N \paren {\mu, \sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution. Then: $\expect X = \mu$ where $\mu$ denotes the expectation of $X$.

title: Expectation of Pareto Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the Pareto distribution with $a, b \in \R_{> 0}$. The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \begin {cases} \dfrac {a b} {a - 1} & 1 < a \\ \text {does not exist} & 1 \ge a \end {cases}$

title: Expectation of Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \lambda$

title: Expectation of Power of Gamma Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution. Then: $\expect {X^n} = \dfrac {\alpha^{\overline n} } {\beta^n}$ where: $\expect {X^n}$ denotes the expectation of $X^n$ $\alpha^{\overline n}$ denotes the $n$th rising factorial of $\alpha$.

title: Expectation of Product of Independent Random Variables is Product of Expectations
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be non-negative real-valued random variables that are independent. Then: $\expect {X Y} = \expect X \expect Y$

title: Expectation of Random Variable as Integral with respect to Probability Distribution
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an integrable real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Then: $\ds \expect X = \int_\R x \map {\rd P_X} x$ where $\expect X$ is the expected value of $X$.

title: Expectation of Real-Valued Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a discrete real-valued random variable. Then $X$ is integrable : $\ds \sum_{x \in \Img X} \size x \map \Pr {X = x} < \infty$ in which case: $\ds \expect X = \sum_{x \in \Img X} x \map \Pr {X = x}$

title: Expectation of Real-Valued Measurable Function composed with Absolutely Continuous Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $P_X$ be the probability distribution of $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\R$. Let $h : \R \to \R$ be a $\map \BB \R$-measurable function. Let $f_X$ be a probability density function for $X$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$.

title: Expectation of Sample Distribution Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of ordinal data. Let $\map {S_n} x$ denote the sample distribution function on $S$. Then: $\expect {\map {S_n} x} = \map F x$ where: $\expect {\map {S_n} x}$ denotes the expectation of $\map {S_n} x$ $\map F x$ denotes the cumulative distribution function of the population from which $S$ was taken.

title: Expectation of Shifted Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the shifted geometric distribution with parameter $p$. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac 1 p$

title: Expectation of Snedecor's F-Distribution
snippet: Let $n, m$ be strictly positive integers. Let $X \sim F_{n, m}$ where $F_{n, m}$ is Snedecor's $F$-distribution with $\tuple {n, m}$ degrees of freedom. Then the expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \dfrac m {m - 2}$ for $m > 2$, and does not exist otherwise.

title: Expectation of Square of Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable whose probability generating function is $\map {\Pi_X} s$. Then the square of the expectation of $X$ is given by the expression: $\expect {X^2} = \map { {\Pi_X}} 1 + \map { {\Pi_X}'} 1$ where $\map { {\Pi_X}} 1$ and $\map { {\Pi_X}'} 1$ denote the second and first derivative respectively of the PGF $\map {\Pi_X} s$ evaluated at $1$.

title: Expectation of Student's t-Distribution
snippet: Let $k$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim t_k$ where $t_k$ is the $t$-distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom. Then the expectation of $X$ is equal to $0$ for $k > 1$, and does not exist otherwise.

title: Expectation of Truncated Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a probability distribution. Let $x_0$ be a given value of $X$. Let $Y$ be a truncated distribution formed from $X$ by ignoring the part either to the left or right of $x_0$. Then the expectation of $Y$ is dependent upon $X$ and $x_0$.

title: Expectation of Weibull Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the Weibull distribution with $\alpha, \beta \in \R_{> 0}$. The expectation of $X$ is given by: $\expect X = \beta \, \map \Gamma {1 + \dfrac 1 \alpha}$ where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function.

title: Expected-Utility Maximization Theorem
snippet: Let $P$ be a rational decision-maker. Let $A$ be a set of possible moves available to $P$. Then there exists a way of assigning values to a payoff function $u: A \to \R$ so that $P$ will always choose the move such that $u$ is a maximum.

title: Expected Monetary Value/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Expected Monetary Value ==

title: Expected Number of Cards Drawn Before First Ace
snippet: Consider a standard deck of $52$ cards. We draw cards from the deck at uniform random without replacement. The expected number of cards drawn before the first ace is $9.6$. Hence the expected number of cards drawn before and including the first ace is $10.6$.

title: Expected Number of Rolls until Two Consecutive Heads
snippet: Let $0 < p \le 1$. Consider a coin such that we toss a head with probability $p$. We repeatedly toss this coin until we observe two consecutive heads. The expected number of tosses until we observe two consecutive heads is: $\ds \frac 1 p + \frac 1 {p^2}$ In particular, for a fair coin, the expected value is $6$. {{explain|Does this generalize? That is, until $n$ consecutive heads is it $\ds \sum_{k \mathop 1}^n \dfrac 1 {p^k}$? be nice if it did}}

title: Expected Number of Trials Until N Consecutive Successes
snippet: Let $0 < p \le 1$. Let $N$ be a positive integer. We conduct an experiment with probability of success $p$. We run this experiment until we see $N$ consecutive successes. Then the expected number of trials until we see $N$ consecutive successes is: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^N p^{-k} = \frac 1 p + \frac 1 {p^2} + \ldots + \frac 1 {p^N}$

title: Expected Sum of Randomly Drawn Subset
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $\sqbrk n = \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ be the set of integers between $1$ and $n$. Equip $\powerset {\sqbrk n}$ with the discrete uniform distribution. Let $\map \Sigma S$ be the sum of a subset $S \in \powerset {\sqbrk n}$. Then: $\ds \expect {\map \Sigma S} = \frac {n \paren {n + 1} } 4$

title: Expected Value of Martingale is Constant in Time
Expected Value of Submartingale Greater Than or Equal To Initial Expected Value
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be a submartingale. Then: $\expect {X_n} \ge \expect {X_0}$ for each $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.

title: Expected Value of Submartingale is Increasing in Time
Expected Value of Supermartingale Less Than or Equal To Initial Expected Value
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be a supermartingale. Then: $\expect {X_n} \le \expect {X_0}$ for each $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.

title: Explicit Form for Generated C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S \subseteq A$. Define: $S^\ast = \set {x^\ast : x \in A}$ Let $\map {\text C^\ast} S$ be the $\text C^\ast$-algebra generated by $S$. Then: $\ds \map {\text C^\ast} S = \span \set {x_1^{k_1} x_2^{k_2} \ldots x_n^{k_n} : x_1, \ldots, x_n \in S \cup S^\ast, \, k_1, \ldots, k_n \ge 0}^-$ where $\paren {\cdot}^-$ denotes closure in $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$.

title: Explicit Form for Generated Subalgebra
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a non-empty set. Let $K \sqbrk S$ be the subalgebra generated by $A$. Then: $\ds K \sqbrk S = \span \set {x_1^{k_1} x_2^{k_2} \ldots x_n^{k_n} : x_1, \ldots, x_n \in S, \, k_1, \ldots, k_n \ge 1}$

title: Exponent/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exponents ==

title: Exponent Base of One
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $1^x = 1$

title: Exponent Combination Laws
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R_{>0}$ be strictly positive real numbers. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $a^x$ be defined as $a$ to the power of $x$. Then:

title: Exponent Not Equal to Zero
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x \ne 0$. Then: $x^y \ne 0$

title: Exponent of Convergence is Less Than Order
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $\omega$ be its order. Let $\tau$ be its exponent of convergence. Then $\tau \le \omega$.

title: Exponential Distribution in terms of Beta Distribution
snippet: Let $\sequence {X_n}$ be a sequence of independent random variables with: $X_n \sim \BetaDist 1 n$ for each natural number $n$, where $\BetaDist 1 n$ denotes the beta distribution with parameters $1$ and $n$. Then: $n X_n \xrightarrow d X$ with: $X \sim \Exponential 1$ where: $\Exponential 1$ denotes the exponential distribution with parameter $1$, $\xrightarrow d$ denotes convergence in distribution.

title: Exponential Distribution in terms of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \mathrm U \hointl 0 1$ where $\mathrm U \hointl 0 1$ is the continuous uniform distribution on $\hointl 0 1$. Let $\beta$ be a positive real number. Then: $-\beta \ln X \sim \Exponential \lambda$ where $\Exponential \cdot$ is the exponential distribution.

title: Exponential Distribution is Special Case of Gamma Distribution
snippet: The exponential distribution is a special case of the gamma distribution.

title: Exponential Dominates Polynomial
snippet: Let $\exp$ denote the real exponential function. Let $k \in \N$. Let $\alpha \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists N \in \N: \forall x \in \R_{>N}: \map \exp {\alpha x} > x^k$

title: Exponential Form of Complex Conjugate
snippet: Let $z := r e^{i \theta} \in \C$ be a complex number expressed in exponential form. Then: $\overline z = r e^{-i \theta}$ where $\overline z$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z$.

title: Exponential Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Exponential Function ==

title: Exponential Function as Limit of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\ds e^x = \lim_{p \mathop \to \infty} \map F {1, p; 1; \dfrac x p}$ where $x$ is a real number.

title: Exponential Function in terms of Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $e^x = \map { {}_1 \operatorname F_1} {p; p; x}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \in \R$ $e^x$ denotes the exponential function $\map { {}_1 \operatorname F_1} {a; b; x}$ is the generalized hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} } { b^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

title: Exponential Function is Solution of Constant Coefficient Homogeneous LSOODE iff Index is Root of Auxiliary Equation
snippet: Let: $(1): \quad y' ' + p y' + q y = 0$ be a constant coefficient homogeneous linear second order ODE. Then: $y = e^{m_1 x}$ is a solution to $(1)$ $m_1$ is a root of the auxiliary equation $m^2 + p m + q = 0$

title: Exponential Function is Superfunction
snippet: The function $f : \C \to \C$, defined as: $\map f z = c^z$ is a superfunction for any complex number $c$.

title: Exponential Function is Well-Defined/Real
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then $\exp x$ is well-defined.

title: Exponential Generating Function for Boubaker Polynomials
snippet: The Boubaker polynomials, defined as: $\map {B_n} x = \begin {cases} 1 & : n = 0 \\ x & : n = 1 \\ x^2 + 2 & : n = 2 \\ x \map {B_{n - 1} } x - \map {B_{n - 2} } x & : n > 2 \end {cases}$ have as an exponential generating function: $\ds \map {f_{B_n, \operatorname {EXP} } } {x, t} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \map {B_n} x \frac {t^n} {n!} = 4 x e^{t \frac x 2} \frac {\map \sin {t \sqrt {1 - \paren {\frac x 2}^2} } } {\sqrt {1 - \paren {\frac x 2}^2} } - 2 e^{t \frac x 2} \map \cos {t \sqrt {1 - \paren {\frac x 2}^2} } - 3$

title: Exponential Growth Equation/Special Case
snippet: All solutions of the differential equation $y' = y$ take the form $y = C e^x$.

title: Exponential Sequence Converges Compactly
snippet: For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : \C \to \C$ be defined as: $\map {f_n} z = \paren {1 + \dfrac z n}^n$ Then, $\sequence {f_n}$ converges compactly to the complex exponential function.

title: Exponential Sequence is Eventually Increasing
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}$ be the sequence of real functions $E_n: \R \to \R$ defined as: $\map {E_n} x = \paren {1 + \dfrac x n}^n$ Then, for sufficiently large $n \in \N$, $\sequence {\map {E_n} x}$ is increasing $n$. That is: $\forall x \in \R: \forall n \in \N: n \ge \ceiling {\size x} \implies \map {E_n} x \le \map {E_{n + 1} } x$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Exponential Sequence is Eventually Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $\sequence {E_n}$ be the sequence of real functions $E_n: \R \to \R$ defined as: $\map {E_n} x = \paren {1 + \dfrac x n}^n$ Then, for each $x \in \R$ and for sufficiently large $n \in \N$, $\map {E_n} x$ is positive. That is: $\forall x \in \R: \forall n \in \N: n \ge \ceiling {\size x} \implies \map {E_n} x > 0$ where $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$.

title: Exponential Sequence is Uniformly Convergent on Compact Sets
snippet: Let $\EE = \sequence {E_n}$ denote the sequence of complex functions $E_n: \C \to \C$ defined as: $\map {E_n} z = \paren {1 + \dfrac z n}^n$ Let $K$ be a compact subset of $\C$. Then $\EE$ is uniformly convergent on $K$.

title: Exponential Tends to Zero and Infinity
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp x \to +\infty$ as $x \to +\infty$ $\exp x \to 0$ as $x \to -\infty$ Thus the exponential function has domain $\R$ and image $\openint 0 \infty$.

title: Exponential Time/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Exponential Time ==

title: Exponential is Strictly Convex
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: The function $f \left({x}\right) = \exp x$ is strictly convex.

title: Exponential is Strictly Increasing
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: The function $\map f x = \exp x$ is strictly increasing.

title: Exponential is of Exponential Order Real Part of Index
snippet: Let $\map f t = e^{\psi t}$ be the complex exponential function, where $t \in \R, \psi \in \C$. Let $a = \map \Re \psi$. Then $e^{\psi t}$ is of exponential order $a$.

title: Exponential of 2 m i Arccotangent of p
snippet: $\map \exp {2 m i \arccot p} \paren {\dfrac {p i + 1} {p i - 1} }^m = 1$

title: Exponential of Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $B$ and $C$ be sets. Let $C^B$ be the set of all mappings from $B$ to $C$. Define a mapping $\epsilon : C^B \times B \to C$ by: $\map \epsilon {f,b} = \map f b$ where $C^B \times B$ denotes the Cartesian product of $C^B$ and $B$. Then $\struct {C^B,\epsilon}$ is an exponential of $C$ by $B$. Moreover, the transpose $\tilde f : A \to C^B$ of $f : A\times B \to C$ is given by: $\map {\tilde f} a = \map f {a, \cdot}$

title: Exponential of Complex Number plus 2 pi i
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\map \exp {z + 2 \pi i} = \map \exp z$

title: Exponential of Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\forall x > 0: \map \exp {\ln x} = x$ $\forall x \in \R: \map \ln {\exp x} = x$

title: Exponential of Negative of Exponential Random Variable has Beta Distribution
snippet: Let $\beta$ be a positive real number. Let $X \sim \Exponential \beta$ where $\Exponential \beta$ is the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$. Then: $e^{-X} \sim \BetaDist {\dfrac 1 \beta} 1$

title: Exponential of One
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp 1 = e$ where $e$ is Euler's number: $e = 2.718281828\ldots$

title: Exponential of Product
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\map \exp {x y} = \paren {\exp y}^x$

title: Exponential of Rational Number is Irrational
snippet: Let $r$ be a rational number such that $r \ne 0$. Then: $e^r$ is irrational where $e$ is Euler's number.

title: Exponential of Real Number is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Let $\exp$ denote the (real) exponential function. Then: $\forall x \in \R : \exp x > 0$

title: Exponential of Series Equals Infinite Product
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}$ be a sequence of complex numbers. Suppose $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty z_n$ converges to $z \in \C$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map \exp {z_n}$ converges to $\exp z$.

title: Exponential of Sum of Real Numbers/Corollary
snippet: == Corollary to Exponential of Sum of Real Numbers == Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\map \exp {x - y} = \dfrac {\exp x} {\exp y}$

title: Exponential of Zero
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then: $\exp 0 = 1$

title: Exponential of Zero and One
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential of $x$. Then:

title: Exponential of a x by Cosine of b x and Exponential of a x by Sine of b x are Linearly Independent
snippet: Let $x, a, b \in \R$. Then $e^{a x} \map \cos {b x}$ and $e^{b x} \map \sin {b x}$ are linearly independent.

title: Exponential of x not less than 1+x
snippet: $e^x \ge 1 + x$ for all $x \in \R$.

title: Exponential on Complex Plane is Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of complex numbers. Let $\exp: \struct {\C, +} \to \struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the mapping: $x \mapsto \map \exp x$ where $\exp$ is the complex exponential function. Then $\exp$ is a group homomorphism.

title: Exponential on Real Numbers is Group Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of positive real numbers. Let $\exp: \struct {\R, +} \to \struct {\R_{> 0}, \times}$ be the mapping: $x \mapsto \map \exp x$ where $\exp$ is the exponential function. Then $\exp$ is a group isomorphism.

title: Exponential on Real Numbers is Injection
snippet: Let $\exp: \R \to \R$ be the exponential function: $\map \exp x = e^x$ Then $\exp$ is an injection.

title: Exponentiation Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a Cartesian closed metacategory. Let $A$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\left({-}\right)^A: \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ be the exponentiation functor. Then $\left({-}\right)^A$ is a functor.

title: Exponentiation is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The function $\exp: \N^2 \to \N$, defined as: $\map \exp {n, m} = n^m$ is primitive recursive‎.

title: Exponents of Primes in Prime Decomposition are Less iff Divisor
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$. Then $a \divides b$ : $(1): \quad$ every prime $p_i$ in the prime decomposition of $a$ appears in the prime decomposition of $b$ and: $(2): \quad$ the exponent of each $p_i$ in $a$ is less than or equal to its exponent in $b$.

title: Exportation and Self-Conditional
snippet: $p \land q \implies r \dashv \vdash \paren {p \implies q} \implies \paren {p \implies r}$

title: Expression for Balanced Hull
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty.. Then the balanced hull $\map {\operatorname {bal} } A$ is well-defined and: $\ds \map {\operatorname {bal} } A = \bigcup_{\lambda \in \GF : \cmod \lambda \le 1} \lambda A$

title: Expression for Closure of Set in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $\mathcal V$ be the set of open neighborhoods of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Then: $\ds A^- = \bigcap_{V \in \mathcal V} \paren {A + V}$ where $A^-$ is the closure of $A$.

title: Expression for Integer as Product of Primes is Unique
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Then the expression for $n$ as the product of one or more primes is unique up to the order in which they appear.

title: Expression for Integers as Powers of Same Primes
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. title: Expression for Set of Points at which Sequence of Functions does not Converge to Given Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a real function. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a real function. Then we have: $\ds \set {x \in X : \sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \in \N} \text { does not converge to } \map f x} = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcap_{N \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcup_{n \mathop = N}^\infty \set {x \in X : \size {\map {f_n} x - \map f x} \ge \frac 1 k}$

title: Expression for bilinear function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function of two independent variables, $f \in \R \times \R \to \R$. Then: $\map f {x, y}$ is a linear function of $x$ when $y$ is equal to a real constant $\map f {x, y}$ is a linear function of $y$ when $x$ is equal to a real constant $f$ has the form: $\exists a, b, c, d \in \R: \forall {x, y} \in \R: \map f {x, y} = a x y + b x + c y + d$

title: Expression of Vector as Linear Combination from Basis is Unique
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space of dimension $n$. Let $\BB = \set {\mathbf x_1, \mathbf x_2, \ldots, \mathbf x_n}$ be a basis for $V$. Let $\mathbf x \in V$ be any vector of $V$. Then $\mathbf x$ can be expressed as a unique linear combination of elements of $\BB$.

title: Exradius of Triangle in Terms of Circumradius
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Let $\rho_a$ be the exradius of $\triangle ABC$ $a$. Let $R$ be the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $\rho_a = 4 R \sin \dfrac A 2 \cos \dfrac B 2 \cos \dfrac C 2$

title: Extend Theory to Satisfy Witness Property
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a language of predicate logic. Let $T$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. Then there exists a language $\LL^*$ and a set of $\LL^*$-sentences $T^*$ satisfying the following properties: $T^*$ is finitely satisfiable $T$ is finitely satisfiable. If $T^*$ is satisfiable, then $T$ is also. For every $\LL^*$-WFF of $1$ free variable $\map \phi x$, there exists some constant $c_\phi$ such that: $T^* \models \paren {\exists x: \map \phi x} \implies \map \phi {x := c_\phi}$ $T^*$ satisfies the witness property.

title: Extendability Theorem for Derivatives Continuous on Open Intervals
snippet: Let $f$ be a continuous real function defined on an interval $\closedint a b$ where $a < b$. Then $f$ is continuously differentiable on $\closedint a b$ : $f$ is continuously differentiable on $\openint a b$ and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map {f'} x$ and $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to b^-} \map {f'} x$ exist.

title: Extendability Theorem for Function Continuous on Open Interval
snippet: Let $f$ be a continuous real function that is defined on an open interval $\openint a b$. Let $g$ be a real function that satisfies: $g$ is defined on $\closedint a b$ $g$ is continuous on $\closedint a b$ $g = f$ on $\openint a b$. Then $g$ exists $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map f x$ and $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to b^-} \map f x$ exist.

title: Extendability Theorem for Intersection Numbers
snippet: Let $X = \partial W$ be a smooth manifold which is the boundary of a smooth compact manifold $W$. Let: $Y$ be a smooth manifold $Z$ be a closed smooth submanifold of $Y$ $f: X \to Y$ be a smooth mapping. Let there exist a smooth mapping $g: W \to Y$ such that $g \restriction_X = f$. Then: $\map I {f, Z} = 0$ where $\map I {f, Z}$ is the intersection number. {{explain|what $\map I {f, Z}$ is the intersection number of: presumably the words will go something like "... the intersection number of $f$ with respect to $Z$", or something.}}

title: Extended Completeness Theorem for Propositional Tableaux and Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Tableau proofs (in terms of propositional tableaux) are a strongly complete proof system for boolean interpretations. More precisely, for every countable collection $\mathbf H$ of WFFs of propositional logic and every WFF $\mathbf A$: $\mathbf H \models_{\mathrm{BI} } \mathbf A$ implies $\mathbf H \vdash_{\mathrm{PT} } \mathbf A$

title: Extended Euclidean Algorithm
snippet: == Algorithm == The extended Euclidean algorithm is a method for: finding the greatest common divisor (GCD) $d$ of two strictly positive integers $m$ and $n$ computing two integers $a$ and $b$ such that $a m + b n = d$. Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$. $\mathbf 1:$ Initialise. Set $a' \gets b \gets 1, a \gets b\,' \gets 0, c \gets m, d \gets n$. $\mathbf 2:$ Divide. Let $q$ and $r$ be the quotient and remainder respectively of $ c / d$. (Thus we have $c = q d + r$ such that $0 \le r < d$.) $\mathbf 3:$ Remainder zero? If $r = 0$, the algorithm terminates.

title: Extended Mean Value Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f'$ be the derivative of $f$. Let $f'$ also be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then: $\exists \xi \in \openint a b: \map f b = \map f a + \paren {b - a} \map {f'} a + \dfrac 1 {2!} \paren {b - a}^2 \map {f' '} \xi$

title: Extended Real Addition is Associative
snippet: Extended real addition $+_{\overline{\R}}$ is commutative. That is, for all $x, y, z \in \overline \R$: $(1): \quad x +_{\overline \R} \paren {y +_{\overline \R} z} = \paren {x +_{\overline \R} y} +_{\overline \R} z$ whenever at least one of the sides is defined.

title: Extended Real Addition is Commutative
snippet: Extended real addition $+_{\overline{\R}}$ is commutative. That is, for all $x, y \in \overline{\R}$: $x +_{\overline{\R}} y = y +_{\overline{\R}} x$ whenever at least one of the sides is defined.

title: Extended Real Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Extended real multiplication $\cdot_{\overline \R}$ is commutative. That is, for all $x, y, z \in \overline \R$: $(1): \quad x \cdot_{\overline \R} \left({y \cdot_{\overline \R} z}\right) = \left({x \cdot_{\overline \R} y}\right) \cdot_{\overline \R} z$

title: Extended Real Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: Extended real multiplication $\times_{\overline \R}$ is commutative. That is, for all $x, y \in \overline \R$: $x \times_{\overline \R} y = y \times_{\overline \R} x$

title: Extended Real Number Space is Compact
snippet: The extended real number space is compact.

title: Extended Real Numbers under Multiplication form Commutative Monoid
snippet: Denote with $\overline \R$ the extended real numbers. Denote with $\cdot_{\overline \R}$ the extended real multiplication. The algebraic structure $\struct {\overline \R, \cdot_{\overline \R} }$ is a commutative monoid.

title: Extended Real Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: Denote with $\overline \R$ the extended real numbers. Denote with $\cdot_{\overline \R}$ the extended real multiplication. The algebraic structure $\struct {\overline \R, \cdot_{\overline \R} }$ is a monoid.

title: Extended Real Sigma-Algebra Induces Borel Sigma-Algebra on Reals
snippet: Let $\overline \BB$ be the extended real $\sigma$-algebra. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\R$. Then: $\overline \BB_\R = \map \BB \R$ where $\overline \BB_\R$ denotes a trace $\sigma$-algebra.

title: Extended Rolle's Theorem
snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be differentiable on a closed interval $I \subseteq \R$. Let $x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n \in I$. Let $\map f {x_i} = 0$ for $i = 0, \ldots, n$. Then for all $i = 0, \ldots, n-1$: $\exists \xi_i \in \openint {x_i} {x_{i + 1} }: \map {f'} {\xi_i} = 0$

title: Extended Rule of Implication
snippet: Any sequent can be expressed as a theorem. That is: $P_1, P_2, P_3, \ldots, P_n \vdash Q$ means the same thing as: $\vdash P_1 \implies \paren {P_2 \implies \paren {P_3 \implies \paren {\ldots \implies \paren {P_n \implies Q} \ldots} } }$ The latter expression is known as the corresponding conditional of the former. Thus every sequent containing the symbol $\vdash$ can, if so desired, be expressed in the form of a theorem which has $\implies$.

title: Extended Soundness Theorem for Propositional Tableaux and Boolean Interpretations
snippet: Tableau proofs (in terms of propositional tableaux) are a strongly sound proof system for boolean interpretations. That is, for every collection $\mathbf H$ of WFFs of propositional logic and every WFF $\mathbf A$: $\mathbf H \vdash_{\mathrm{PT}} \mathbf A$ implies $\mathbf H \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf A$

title: Extended Topologist's Sine Curve is Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the extended topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is injectively path-connected.

title: Extended Topologist's Sine Curve is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the extended topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is path-connected.

title: Extended Topologist's Sine Curve is not Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the extended topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is not locally injectively path-connected.

title: Extended Topologist's Sine Curve is not Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be the extended topologist's sine curve. Then $T$ is not locally path-connected.

title: Extending Operation is a Slowly Progressing Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ denote the class of all ordinal sequences. Let $E: S \to S$ be an extending operation on $S$. Then $E$ is a slowly progressing mapping.

title: Extending Operation is a Strictly Progressing Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ denote the class of all ordinal sequences. Let $E: S \to S$ be an extending operation on $S$. Then $E$ is a strictly progressing mapping.

title: Extension Realizing All Types
snippet: Let $\MM$ be an $\LL$-structure. Let $M$ be its universe. There is an elementary extension $\NN$ of $\MM$ such that every type over $M$ (relative to $\MM$) is realized in $\NN$.

title: Extension Theorem for Homomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup with cancellable elements Let $\struct {C, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup of all cancellable elements of $S$ Let $\struct {S', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Let $\phi$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into a semigroup $\struct {T, *}$ such that $\map \phi y$ is invertible for all $y \in C$.

title: Extension Theorem for Isomorphisms
snippet: Let the following conditions be fulfilled: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup with cancellable elements Let $\phi$ be an isomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into a semigroup $\struct {T, *}$ Let $\struct {S', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Let $\struct {T', \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {T, \circ}$. Then there is a unique isomorphism $\phi': S' \to T'$ extending $\phi$.

title: Extension Theorem for Positive Linear Functional defined on Cofinal Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \succeq}$ be a preordered vector space over $\R$. Let $Y$ be a linear subspace of $X$ that is cofinal in $\struct {X, \succeq}$. Let $f_0 : Y \to \R$ be a positive linear functional. Then there exists a positive linear functional $f : X \to \R$ such that: $\map f y = \map {f_0} y$ for each $y \in Y$.

title: Extension Theorem for Total Orderings
snippet: Let the following conditions be fulfilled: $(1):\quad$ Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered commutative semigroup $(2):\quad$ Let all the elements of $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be cancellable $(3):\quad$ Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$. title: Extension of Bounded Linear Transformation from Closed Subspace of Hilbert Space to Whole Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH_1, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_1}$ and $\struct {\HH_2, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_2}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\GF$. Let $\KK_1$ and $\KK_2$ be closed linear subspaces of $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ respectively. Let $T_1 : \KK_1 \to \KK_2$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $\KK_1^\bot$ of $\KK_2^\bot$ be the orthocomplements of $\KK_1$ and $\KK_2$ respectively. Let $T_2 : \KK_1^\bot \to \KK_2^\bot$ be a bounded linear transformation. Define $T : \HH_1 \to \HH_2$ by: $\map T {u + v} = T_1 u + T_2 v$ for each $u \in \KK_1$ and $v \in \KK_1^\bot$.

title: Extension of Continuous Complex-Valued Function Vanishing at Infinity to Alexandroff Extension is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $X^\ast = X \cup \set p$ be the Alexandroff extension of $X$. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a continuous complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Define $f^\ast : X^\ast \to \C$ by taking: $\map {f^\ast} x = \begin{cases}\map f x & x \in X \\ 0 & x = p\end{cases}$ for each $x \in X^\ast$. Then $f^\ast$ is continuous.

title: Extension of Continuous Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T_H = \struct{H, \tau_H}$ be a topological subspace of $T_2$ where $H \subseteq S_2$. Let $f: S_1 \to H$ be a $\tuple { \tau_1 , \tau_H}$-continuous mapping. Define a mapping $g: S_1 \to S_2$ by: $\forall x \in S_1 : \map g x = \map f x$ Then $g$ is $\tuple { \tau_1 , \tau_2}$-continuous.

title: Extension of Contraction of Extension of Ideal is Extension
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $f : A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\mathfrak a$ be an ideal of $A$. Let ${\mathfrak a}^e$ be the extension of $\mathfrak a$ by $f$. Let ${\mathfrak a}^{ec}$ be the contraction of ${\mathfrak a}^e$ by $f$. Let ${\mathfrak a}^{ece}$ be the extension of ${\mathfrak a}^{ec}$ by $f$. Then: ${\mathfrak a}^e = {\mathfrak a}^{ece}$

title: Extension of Contradictory Branch is Contradictory
snippet: Let $T$ be a propositional tableau. Let $\Gamma$ be a contradictory branch of $T$. Let $\Gamma'$ be an extension of $\Gamma$. Then $\Gamma'$ is also contradictory.

title: Extension of Directed Suprema Preserving Mapping to Complete Lattice Preserves Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $L_3 = \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be a complete lattice. Suppose that $L_2$ is directed suprema inheriting ordered subset of $L_3$. Let $f:S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping such that $f$ preserves directed suprema. Then $f:S_1 \to S_3$ preserves directed suprema.

title: Extension of Extension of Mapping is Extension
snippet: Let $A, B, C, S$ be sets such that $A \subseteq B \subseteq C$. Let $f: A \to S$, $g: B \to S$ and $h: C \to S$ be mappings such that: $g$ is an extension of $f$ to $B$ $h$ is an extension of $g$ to $C$. Then $h$ is an extension of $f$ to $C$.

snippet: Let $\map f x$ be a real function defined on the interval $\openint 0 \lambda$. Let $\map f x$ be represented by the half-range Fourier cosine series $\map S x$: $\map f x \sim \map S x = \dfrac {a_0} 2 + \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n \cos \frac {n \pi x} \lambda$ where for all $n \in \Z_{> 0}$: $a_n = \ds \frac 2 \lambda \int_0^\lambda \map f x \cos \frac {n \pi x} \lambda \rd x$ Then $\map S x$ also represents the extension to the even function $g: \openint {-\lambda} \lambda \to \R$ of $f$, defined as: $\forall x \in \openint {-\lambda} \lambda: \map g x = \begin {cases} \map f x & :…

title: Extension of Half-Range Fourier Sine Function to Symmetric Range
snippet: Let $\map f x$ be a real function defined on the interval $\openint 0 \lambda$. Let $\map f x$ be represented by the half-range Fourier sine series $\map S x$: $\map f x \sim \map S x = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n \sin \frac {n \pi x} \lambda$ where for all $n \in \Z_{> 0}$: $b_n = \ds \frac 2 \lambda \int_0^\lambda \map f x \sin \frac {n \pi x} \lambda \rd x$ Then $\map S x$ also represents the extension $g: \openint {-\lambda} \lambda \to \R$ of $f$, defined as: $\forall x \in \openint {-\lambda} \lambda: \map g x = \begin {cases} \map f x & : x > 0 \\ -\map f {-x} & : x < 0 \\ 0 &…

title: Extension of Harmonic Number to Non-Integer Argument
snippet: Let $\map H x$ be the real function defined as: $\map H x = \gamma + \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} {x + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x + 1} }$ where: $\map \Gamma x$ denotes the Gamma function $\map {\Gamma'} x$ denotes the derivative of the Gamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant. Then $H$ is an extension of the mapping $H: \N \to \Q$ defined as: $\forall n \in \N: \map H n = H_n$ where $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number.

title: Extension of Infima Preserving Mapping to Complete Lattice Preserves Infima
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $L_3 = \struct {S_3, \preceq_3}$ be a complete lattice. Suppose that. $L_2$ is an infima inheriting ordered subset of $L_3$. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping such that: $f$ preserves infima. Then $f: S_1 \to S_3$ preserves infima.

title: Exterior Angle of Regular Polygon
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular polygon with $n$ sides. Then each of the exterior angles of $P$ is equal to $\dfrac {360 \degrees} n$.

title: Exterior of Exterior in Sorgenfrey Line is not necessarily Interior
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the Sorgenfrey line. Let $A \subseteq \R$. Let $A^e$ denote the exterior of $A$ in $T$. Let $A^\circ$ denote the interior of $A$ in $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $A^\circ = A^{ee}$ that is, that the interior of $A$ is equal to the exterior of the exterior of $A$.

title: Exterior of Exterior of Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $A$ be the union of the adjacent open intervals: $A := \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Then: $A^{ee} = \openint a c$ where $A^e$ is the exterior of $A$.

title: Exterior of Finite Union equals Intersection of Exteriors
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Let $\forall i \in \closedint 1 n: H_i \subseteq S$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}^e = \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i^e$ where $H_i^e$ denotes the exterior of $H_i$.

title: Exterior of Intersection contains Union of Exteriors
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\mathbb H$ be a set of subsets of $TS$. That is, let $\mathbb H \subseteq \powerset S$ where $\powerset S$ is the power set of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} H^e \subseteq \paren {\bigcap_{H \mathop \in \mathbb H} H}^e$ where $H^e$ denotes the exterior of $H$.

title: Exterior of Union of Singleton Rationals is Empty
snippet: Let $B_\alpha$ be the singleton containing the rational number $\alpha$. Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Then the exterior in $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ of the union of all $B_\alpha$ is the empty set: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in \Q} B_\alpha}^e = \O$

title: External Angle of Triangle equals Sum of other Internal Angles
snippet: The external angle of a triangle equals the sum of the other two internal angles.

title: External Angle of Triangle is Greater than Internal Opposite
snippet: The external angle of a triangle is greater than either of the opposite internal angles.

title: External Center of Similitude of Circles with respect to Radii
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be the centers of two circles $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ whose radii are $r$ and $R$ respectively, $r \ne R$. Let $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ be such that neither is completely enclosed inside the other. Let $T$ be the external center of similitude of $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points on the circumference of $\bigcirc Ar$ and $\bigcirc BR$ respectively. Then: the radii $AP$ and $QR$ are parallel $T$, $P$ and $Q$ are collinear.

title: External Direct Product Associativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ be the external direct product of the two algebraic structures $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$. Then: $\circ_1$ and $\circ_2$ are associative $\circ$ is associative.

title: External Direct Product Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ be the external direct product of $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$. Then: $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$ be closed $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ is also closed.

title: External Direct Product Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ be the external direct product of the two algebraic structures $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$. Then: $\circ_1$ and $\circ_2$ are commutative $\circ$ is commutative.

title: External Direct Product Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ be the external direct product of two algebraic structures $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$. Then: $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ has identity element $e_S$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$ has identity element $e_T$ $\tuple {e_S, e_T}$ is the identity element for $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$.

title: External Direct Product Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ be the external direct product of the two algebraic structures $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$. Then: $s^{-1}$ and $t^{-1}$ are inverse elements of $s \in \struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $t \in \struct {T, \circ_2}$ respectively $\tuple {s^{-1}, t^{-1} }$ is an inverse element of $\tuple {s, t} \in \struct {S \times T, \circ}$.

title: External Direct Product of Abelian Groups is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$ be groups. Then the group direct product $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ is abelian both $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$ are abelian.

title: External Direct Product of Congruence Relations
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \odot}$ and $\struct {B, \circledast}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be congruence relations on $\struct {A, \odot}$ and $\struct {B, \circledast}$ respectively. Let $\struct {A / \RR, \odot_\RR}$ and $\struct {B / \SS, \circledast_\SS}$ denote the quotient structures defined by $\RR$ and $\SS$ respectively. Let $\struct {A \times B, \otimes}$ be the external direct product of $\struct {A, \odot}$ and $\struct {B, \circledast}$.

title: External Direct Product of Groups is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be groups whose identity elements are $e_1$ and $e_2$ respectively. Let $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ be the external direct product of $G_1$ and $G_2$. Then $\struct {G_1 \times G_2, \circ}$ is a group whose identity element is $\tuple {e_1, e_2}$.

title: External Direct Product of Projection with Canonical Injection
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures with identity elements $e_1$ and $e_2$ respectively. Let $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ}$ be the external direct product of $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ Let: $\pr_1: \struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ} \to \struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ be the first projection from $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ $\pr_2: \struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ} \to \struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ be the second projection from $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$.

title: External Direct Product of Ringoids is Ringoid
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \ldots, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be ringoids. Let $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ be their external direct product. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ is a ringoid.

title: External Direct Product of Semigroups
snippet: The external direct product of two semigroups is itself a semigroup.

title: External Direct Sum of Rings is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \ldots, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be rings. Then their (external) direct product: $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ is a ring.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an extremally disconnected Hausdorff space. Then $T$ is totally separated.

snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space which is extremally disconnected. Then $M$ is the discrete topology.

snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ with its standard topology. Let $K$ be a non-empty compact convex subset of $X$. Let $E$ be an extreme set of $K$. Then $E$ contains an extreme point of $K$.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $X$ be an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $X$ is a closed set of $T$.

title: F-Sigma Sets Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F, F'$ be $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then their intersection $F \cap F'$ is also a $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

title: F-Sigma Sets Closed under Union
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $F, F'$ be $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then their union $F \cup F'$ is also an $F_\sigma$ set of $T$.

title: F-Sigma Sets form Lattice
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be the collection of all $F_\sigma$ sets of $T$. Then $\struct {\FF, \subseteq}$ is a lattice, where $\subseteq$ denotes the subset relation.

title: F-Sigma Sets in Indiscrete Topology
snippet: $H \subseteq S$ is an $F_\sigma$ ($F$-sigma) set of an indiscrete topological space $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ either $H = S$ or $H = \O$.

title: F-Sigma and G-Delta Subsets of Uncountable Finite Complement Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Then countably infinite subsets of $S$ are $F_\sigma$ sets and are neither open nor closed sets. Their relative complements in $S$ are $G_\delta$ sets, and are also neither open nor closed sets.

title: Factor Spaces are Completely Normal if Product Space is Completely Normal

Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a completely normal space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a completely normal space.

title: Factor Spaces are Normal if Product Space is Normal
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\SS$. Let $T$ be a normal space. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a normal space.

title: Factor Spaces are T4 if Product Space is T4
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct{S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces for $\alpha$ in some indexing set $I$. Then each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Factor Spaces are T5 if Product Space is T5

title: Factor of Mersenne Number Mp equivalent to 1 mod p
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $q$ is a divisor of the Mersenne number $M_p$. Then: $q \equiv 1 \pmod p$

title: Factor of Mersenne Number Mp is of form 2kp + 1
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $q$ is a divisor of the Mersenne number $M_p$. Then: $q = 2 k p + 1$ for some integer $k$.

title: Factor of Mersenne Number equivalent to +-1 mod 8
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $q$ is a divisor of the Mersenne number $M_p$. Then: $q \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 8$

title: Factorial Divides Product of Successive Numbers
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{\ge 1}$ be natural numbers Let $m^{\overline n}$ be $m$ to the power of $n$ rising. Then: $m^{\overline n} \equiv 0 \bmod n!$ That is, the factorial of $n$ divides the product of $n$ successive numbers.

title: Factorial Divisible by Binary Root
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n \ge 1$. Let $n$ be expressed in binary notation: $n = 2^{e_1} + 2^{e_2} + \cdots + 2^{e_r}$ where $e_1 > e_2 > \cdots > e_r \ge 0$. Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Then $n!$ is divisible by $2^{n - r}$, but not by $2^{n - r + 1}$.

title: Factorial Divisible by Prime Power
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n \ge 1$. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n$ be expressed in base $p$ notation: $\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m r_j p^j$ where $0 \le r_j < p$. Let $n!$ be the factorial of $n$. Let $p^\mu$ be the largest power of $p$ which divides $n!$, that is: $p^\mu \divides n!$ $p^{\mu + 1} \nmid n!$ Then: $\mu = \dfrac {n - \map {s_p} n} {p - 1}$ where $\map {s_p} n$ is the digit sum of $n$ to base $p$.

title: Factoring Mapping into Quotient and Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then $f$ can be uniquely factored into a quotient mapping, followed by an injection. Thus: $f = h \circ q_{\RR_f}$ where: $q_{\RR_f}: S \to S / \RR_f: \map {q_{\RR_f} } s = \eqclass s {\RR_f}$ $h: S / \RR_f \to T: \map h {\eqclass s {\RR_f} } = \map f s$ $\eqclass s {\RR_f}$ denotes the equivalence class of $s$ with respect to the equivalence relation $\RR$ induced on $S$ by $f$.

title: Factoring Mapping into Surjection and Inclusion
snippet: Every mapping $f:S \to T$ can be uniquely factored into a surjection $g$ followed by the inclusion mapping $i_T$. That is, $f = i_T \circ g$ where: $g: S \to \Img f: \map g x = \map f x$ $i_T: \Img f \to T: \map {i_T} x = x$ This can be illustrated using a commutative diagram as follows: $\quad\quad \begin{xy}\xymatrix@L+2mu@+1em { S \ar@{-->}[r]^*{g} \ar[rd]_*{f = i_T \circ g} & \Img f \ar@{-->}[d]^*{i_T} \\ & T }\end{xy}$

title: Factorisation of z^(2n+1)+1 in Real Domain

title: Factorisation of z^n+a
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $z^n + a = \ds \prod_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {z - \alpha_k b}$ where: $\alpha_k$ are the complex $n$th roots of negative unity $b$ is any complex number such that $b^n = a$.

title: Factorization of Continuous Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_X}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$ with $N \subseteq \ker T$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then $T$ is continuous : there exists a continuous linear transformation $\Lambda : X/N \to Y$ such that: $T x = \map \Lambda {\map \pi x}$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Factorization of Limit Ordinals
snippet: Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Then: $x = \paren {\omega \times y}$ for some $y \in \On$ where $\omega$ is the minimally inductive set.

title: Factorization of Natural Numbers within 4 n + 1 not Unique
snippet: Let: $S = \set {4 n + 1: n \in \N} = \set {1, 5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots}$ be the set of natural numbers of the form $4 n + 1$. Then not all elements of $S$ have a complete factorization by other elements of $S$ which is unique.

title: Factorization of Open Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_X}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$ with $N \subseteq \ker T$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then $T$ is open : there exists a open linear transformation $\Lambda : X/N \to Y$ such that: $T x = \map \Lambda {\map \pi x}$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Factors in Absolutely Convergent Product Converge to One
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 + a_n}$ be absolutely convergent. Then: $a_n \to 0$

title: Factors in Convergent Product Converge to One
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be convergent. Then $a_n \to 1$.

title: Factors in Uniformly Convergent Product Converge Uniformly to One
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly on $X$. Then $f_n$ converges uniformly to $1$.

snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $\HH$ be a composition series of $G$. Then all factor groups of $\HH$ must be prime.

title: Faithful Functor Reflects Monomorphisms
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a faithful functor. Let $x$ and $y$ be objects in $\mathbf C$. Let $f: x \to y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf C$. Let $\map F f : \map F x \to \map F y$ be a monomorphism in $\mathbf D$. Then $f$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf C$.

title: Falling Factorial as Quotient of Factorials
snippet: Let $x \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $x^{\underline n} = \dfrac {x!} {\paren {x - n}!} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {x + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x - n + 1} }$ where: $x^{\underline n}$ denotes the $n$th falling factorial power of $x$. $\map \Gamma x$ denotes the Gamma function of $x$.

title: Falling Factorial of Complex Number as Summation of Unsigned Stirling Numbers of First Kind
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number whose real part is positive. Then: $z^{\underline r} = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^m{r \brack r - k} \paren {-1}^k z^{r - k} + \map \OO {z^{r - m - 1} }$ where: $\ds {r \brack r - k}$ denotes the extension of the unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind to the complex plane $z^{\underline r}$ denotes $z$ to the $r$ falling $\map \OO {z^{r - m - 1} }$ denotes big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Falling Factorial of Sum of Integers
snippet: Let $r \in \R$ be a real number. Let $a, b \in \Z$ be (positive) integers. Then: $r^{\underline {a + b} } = r^{\underline a} \paren {r - a}^{\underline b}$ where $r^{\underline a}$ denotes the $a$th falling factorial of $r$.

title: Family of Lipschitz Continuous Functions with same Lipschitz Constant is Uniformly Equicontinuous

title: Fan-Glicksberg-Hoffman Concave Alternative
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_m : C \to \R$ be concave functions. Then exactly one of the following is true: $(1): \quad$ there exists $x \in C$ such that $\map {f_i} x > 0$ for each $1 \le i \le n$ $(2): \quad$ there exists $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$, not all zero, such that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_i \map {f_i} x \le 0$ for each $x \in C$.

title: Feit-Thompson Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == There exist no distinct prime numbers $p$ and $q$ such that: $\dfrac {p^q - 1} {p - 1}$ divides $\dfrac {q^p - 1} {q - 1}$

title: Feit-Thompson Theorem
snippet: All finite groups of odd order are solvable. That is, every non-abelian finite simple group is of even order.

title: Fekete's Subadditive Lemma
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be a subadditive sequence. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \frac {a_n} n = \inf_{n \mathop \ge 1} \frac {a_n} n$

title: Fencepost Mistake
snippet: == Common Mistake == Let $F$ be a fence of length $n$ units, with fenceposts at either end and spaced $1$ unit apart. How many fenceposts are there? To answer $n$ is to make the fencepost mistake. There are $n + 1$ fenceposts.

title: Fermat's Last Theorem
snippet: $\forall a, b, c, n \in \Z_{>0}: n > 2$, the equation $a^n + b^n = c^n$ has no solutions.

title: Fermat's Little Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer such that $p$ is not a divisor of $n$. Then: $n^{p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod p$

title: Fermat's Marginal Notes

title: Fermat's Right Triangle Theorem
snippet: $x^4 + y^4 = z^2$ has no solutions in the (strictly) positive integers.

title: Fermat's Two Squares Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Then $p$ can be expressed as the sum of two squares either: $p = 2$ or: $p \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ The expression of a prime of the form $4 k + 1$ as the sum of two squares is unique except for the order of the two summands.

title: Fermat Number whose Index is Sum of Integers
snippet: Let $F_n = 2^{\left({2^n}\right)} + 1$ be the $n$th Fermat number. Let $k \in \Z_{>0}$. Then: $F_{n + k} - 1 = \left({F_n - 1}\right)^{2^k}$

title: Fermat Problem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle Let the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ all have angles less than $120 \degrees$. Let $\triangle ABG$, $\triangle BCE$ and $\triangle ACF$ be equilateral triangles constructed on the sides of $ABC$. Let $AE$, $BF$ and $CG$ be constructed. Let $P$ be the point at which $AE$, $BF$ and $CG$ meet. 500px Then $P$ is the Fermat-Torricelli point of $\triangle ABC$. If one of vertices of $\triangle ABC$ be of $120 \degrees$ or more, then that vertex is itself the Fermat-Torricelli point of $\triangle ABC$.

title: Fermat Pseudoprime/Base 3/Examples/91
snippet: The smallest Fermat pseudoprime to base $3$ is $91$: $3^{91} \equiv 3 \pmod {91}$ despite the fact that $91$ is not prime: $91 = 7 \times 13$

title: Fermat Quotient of 2 wrt p is Square iff p is 3 or 7
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. The Fermat quotient of $2$ with respect to $p$: $\map {q_p} 2 = \dfrac {2^{p - 1} - 1} p$ is a square $p = 3$ or $p = 7$.

title: Fermat Set cannot be Extended to Diophantine Quintuple
snippet: The Fermat set $F = \set {1, 3, 8, 120}$ cannot be extended to a Diophantine quintuple.

title: Fermat Set is Diophantine Quadruple
snippet: The Fermat set $F = \left\{{1, 3, 8, 120}\right\}$ is a Diophantine quadruple: $\forall a, b \in F: a \ne b: a b + 1 = n^2$ for some $n \in \Z$.

title: Ferrari's Method
snippet: Let $P$ be the quartic equation: $a x^4 + b x^3 + c x^2 + d x + e = 0$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then $P$ has solutions: $x = \dfrac {-p \pm \sqrt {p^2 - 8 q} } 4$ where: {{eqn | l = p | r = \dfrac b a \pm \sqrt {\dfrac {b^2} {a^2} - \dfrac {4 c} a + 4 y_1} }} {{eqn | l = q | r = y_1 \mp \sqrt { {y_1}^2 - \dfrac {4 e} a} }} where $y_1$ is a real solution to the cubic: $y^3 - \dfrac c a y^2 + \paren {\dfrac {b d} {a^2} - \dfrac {4 e} a} y + \paren {\dfrac {4 c e} {a^2} - \dfrac {b^2 e} {a^3} - \dfrac {d^2} {a^2} } = 0$ Ferrari's Method is a technique for solving this quartic.

title: Fibonacci Number by Golden Mean plus Fibonacci Number of Index One Less
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$. Then: $\phi^n = F_n \phi + F_{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Fibonacci Number by One Minus Golden Mean plus Fibonacci Number of Index One Less
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$. Then: $\hat \phi^n = F_n \hat \phi + F_{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number $\hat \phi$ denotes the $1$ minus the golden mean: $\hat \phi := 1 - \phi$

title: Fibonacci Number greater than Golden Section to Power less Two
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{\ge 2}$: $F_n \ge \phi^{n - 2}$ where: $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden section: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

title: Fibonacci Number in terms of Larger Fibonacci Numbers

title: Fibonacci Number is not Product of Two Smaller Fibonacci Numbers

title: Fibonacci Number less than Golden Section to Power less One

title: Fibonacci Number plus Binomial Coefficient in terms of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be the sequence defined as: $a_n = \begin{cases} 0 & : n = 0 \\ 1 & : n = 1 \\ a_{n - 2} + a_{n - 1} + \dbinom {n - 2} m & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ where $\dbinom {n - 2} m$ denotes a binonial coefficient. title: Fibonacci Number plus Constant in terms of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $c$ be a number. Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be the sequence defined as: $b_n = \begin{cases} 0 & : n = 0 \\ 1 & : n = 1 \\ b_{n - 2} + b_{n - 1} + c & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then $\sequence {b_n}$ can be expressed in Fibonacci numbers as: $b_n = c F_{n - 1} + \paren {c + 1} F_n - c$

title: Fibonacci Number whose Index is Plus or Minus Prime p is Multiple of p

title: Field Adjoined Set
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Let $S \subseteq F$ be a subset of $F$. Let $K \le F$ be a subfield of $F$. The subring $K \sqbrk S$ of $F$ generated by $K \cup S$ is the set of all finite linear combinations of powers of elements of $S$ with coefficients in $K$. The subfield $\map K S$ of $F$ generated by $K \cup S$ is the set of all $x y^{-1} \in F$ with $a, b \in K \sqbrk S$, $b \ne 0$. $\map K S$ is isomorphic to the field of quotients $Q$ of $K \sqbrk S$.

title: Field Generated by Macroscopic Charge Density
snippet: Let $B$ be a body of matter. Let $P$ be a point inside $B$ whose position vector is $\mathbf r$. The electric field at $P$ generated by the macroscopic charge density within $B$ is given by: $\ds \map {\mathbf E} {\mathbf r} = \dfrac 1 {4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \int_{\text {all space} } \dfrac {\paren {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'} \map \rho {\mathbf r'} } {\size {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'}^3} \rd V'$ where: $\d V'$ is an infinitesimal volume element $\mathbf r'$ is the position vector of $\d V'$ $\map \rho {\mathbf r'}$ is the macroscopic charge density of the macroscopic electric field at $\mathbf r'$…

title: Field Generated by Surface Charge Density
snippet: Let $B$ be a body of matter. Let $P$ be a point inside $B$ whose position vector is $\mathbf r$. The electric field at $P$ generated by the surface charge density over $B$ is given by: $\ds \map {\mathbf E} {\mathbf r} = \dfrac 1 {4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \int_{\text {all surfaces} } \dfrac {\paren {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'} \map \sigma {\mathbf r'} } {\size {\mathbf r - \mathbf r'}^3} \rd S'$ where: $\d S'$ is an infinitesimal area element $\mathbf r'$ is the position vector of $\d S'$ $\map \sigma {\mathbf r'}$ is the surface charge density at $\mathbf r'$ $\varepsilon_0$ denotes the vacuum…

title: Field Homomorphism Preserves Product Inverses
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {F_1, +_1, \times_1} \to \struct {F_2, +_2, \times_2}$ be a field homomorphism. Then: $\forall x \in F_1^*: \map \phi {x^{-1} } = \map \phi x^{-1}$

title: Field Homomorphism Preserves Subfields
snippet: Let $\struct {F_1, +_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {F_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be fields. Let $\phi: F_1 \to F_2$ be a field homomorphism such that $\phi$ is not the trivial homomorphism. If $K$ is a subfield of $F_1$, then $\phi \sqbrk K$ is a subfield of $F_2$.

title: Field Homomorphism Preserves Unity
