snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C e^{-x}$ where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

title: First Order ODE/y' - f (y) phi' (x) over f' (y) = phi (x) phi' (x) over f' (y)
snippet: Let $\map f y$ and $\map \phi x$ be known real functions of $y$ and $x$ respectively. The general solution of: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - \dfrac {\map f y} {\map {f'} y} \map {\phi'} x = \dfrac {\map \phi x \map {\phi'} x} {\map {f'} y}$ is: $\map f y = C e^{\map \phi x} - \map \phi x - 1$

title: First Order ODE/y' = (x + y)^2
snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \paren {x + y}^2$ has the general solution: $x + y = \map \tan {x + C}$

title: First Order ODE/y' = e^x
snippet: The first order ODE: $y' = e^x$ has the general solution: $y = e^x + C$ where $C$ is an arbitrary constant.

title: First Order ODE/y' = sin^2 (x - y + 1)
snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map {\sin^2} {x - y + 1}^2$ has the general solution: $\map \tan {x - y + 1} = x + C$

title: First Order ODE/y' = x
snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = x$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {x^2} 2 + C$

title: First Order ODE/y' ln (x - y) = 1 + ln (x - y)
snippet: The first order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} \map \ln {x - y} \d x = 1 + \map \ln {x - y}$ is an exact differential equation with solution: $\paren {x - y} \map \ln {x - y} = C - y$

title: First Order ODE/y - x y' = y' y^2 exp y
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y - x y' = y' y^2 e^y$ has the general solution: $x y^2 = e^y + C$

title: First Order ODE/y dx + (x^2 y - x) dy = 0
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y \rd x + \paren {x^2 y - x} \rd y = 0$ has the general solution: $\dfrac {y^2} 2 - \dfrac y x = C$ This can also be presented in the form: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \dfrac y {x^2 y - x}$

title: First Order ODE/y dx + x dy + 3 x^3 y^4 dy
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y \rd x + x \rd y + 3 x^3 y^4 \rd y = 0$ has the general solution: $-\dfrac 1 {2 x^2 y^2} + \dfrac {3 y^2} 2 = C$

title: First Order ODE/y dx + x dy = 0
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y \rd x + x \rd y = 0$ has the general solution: $x y = C$

title: First Order ODE/y dx - x dy = x y^3 dy
snippet: The first order ODE: $(1): \quad y \rd x - x \rd y = x y^3 \rd y$ has the general solution: $\ln \dfrac x y = \dfrac {y^3} 3 + C$

title: First Order ODE/y dy = k dx
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The first order ODE: $y \, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = k$ has the general solution: $y^2 = 2 k x + C$

title: First Order ODE/y dy = k x dx
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The first order ODE: $y \rd y = k x \rd x$ has the general solution: $y^2 = k x^2 + C$

title: First Order ODE in form y' = F ((a x + b y + c) over (d x + e y + f))
snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map F {\dfrac {a x + b y + c} {d x + e y + f} }$ such that: $ a e \ne b d$ can be solved by substituting: $x := z - h$ $y := w - k$ where: $h = \dfrac {c e - b f} {a e - b d}$ $k = \dfrac {a f - c d} {a e - b d}$ to obtain: $\dfrac {\d w} {\d z} = \map F {\dfrac {a z + b w} {d z + e w} }$ which can be solved by the technique of Solution to Homogeneous Differential Equation.

title: First Order ODE in form y' = F ((a x + b y + c) over (d x + e y + f)) where a e = b d
First Order ODE in form y' = f (a x + b y + c)
snippet: The first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map f {a x + b y + c}$ can be solved by substituting: $z := a x + b y + c$ to obtain: $\ds x = \int \frac {\d z} {b \map f z + a}$

title: First Order Ordinary Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of First Order Ordinary Differential Equation ==

title: First Pappus-Guldinus Theorem
snippet: Let $C$ be a plane figure that lies entirely on one side of a straight line $\LL$. Let $S$ be the solid of revolution generated by $C$ around $\LL$. Then the volume of $S$ is equal to the area of $C$ multiplied by the distance travelled by the centroid of $C$ around $\LL$ when generating $S$.

title: First Power of Element in B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\left({X, \circ}\right)$ be a $B$-algebra. Then: $\forall x \in X: x^1 = x$ where $x^k$ for $k \in \N$ denotes the $k$th power of the element $x$.

title: First Price Auction/Analysis
snippet: == Analysis of First Price Auction == Let $G$ denote the game under analysis, that is, the first price auction under discussion. Let $F$ be the object being bid for. As in the formal definition of the sealed-bid auction, let the players be labelled in order of their valuations of $F$: $v_1 > v_2 > \cdots > v_n > 0$ In this context, a move by player $i$ is the bid that $i$ places on $F$. Let $b$ be the profile of moves made by all players. Let player $i$ win the auction by move $b_i$. By hypothesis, player $i$'s valuation for $F$ is $v_i$. Hence $i$'s payoff is $v_i - b_i$.

title: First Principle of Transfinite Induction
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be a well-ordering on $A$. Let $P$ be a property that satisfies the following condition: For all $x \in A$, if $P$ holds for every $y \prec x$, then $P$ holds for $x$. Then $P$ holds for all $x \in A$.

title: First Principles/Examples
snippet: == Examples of First Principles ==

title: First Projection on Ordered Pair of Sets
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Let $w = \tuple {a, b}$ denote the ordered pair of $a$ and $b$. Let $\map {\pr_1} w$ denote the first projection on $w$. Then: $\ds \map {\pr_1} w = \bigcup \bigcap w$ where $\ds \bigcup$ and $\ds \bigcap$ denote union and intersection respectively.

title: First Ring Isomorphism Theorem/Also known as
snippet: == First Ring Isomorphism Theorem: Also known as == The First Ring Isomorphism Theorem is also referred to as the First Fundamental Theorem on Ring Homomorphisms. It can also be called the First Isomorphism Theorem for Rings.

title: First Sequence of Three Consecutive Strictly Decreasing Euler Phi Values
snippet: The first sequence of $3$ consecutive positive integers whose Euler $\phi$ values are strictly decreasing is: $\map \phi {523} > \map \phi {524} > \map \phi {525}$

title: First Socratic Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == was supposed to have said: I know nothing at all. In which case, how does Socrates know that he knows nothing?

title: First Subsequence Rule
snippet: Let $T = \struct {A, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $T$. Suppose $\sequence {x_n}$ has two convergent subsequences with different limits. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is divergent.

title: First Supplement to Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
snippet: $\quad \paren {\dfrac {-1} p} = \paren {-1}^{\paren {p - 1} / 2} = \begin {cases} +1 & : p \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \\ -1 & : p \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \end {cases}$ where $\paren {\dfrac {-1} p}$ is defined as the Legendre symbol.

title: First Sylow Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a group such that: $\order G = k p^n$ where: $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$ $p$ is not a divisor of $k$. Then $G$ has at least one Sylow $p$-subgroup.

title: First Translation Property of Laplace Transforms
snippet: Let $\map f t: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a function of exponential order $a$ for some constant $a \in \R$. Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ be the Laplace transform of $f$. Let $e^t$ be the exponential function. Then: $\laptrans {e^{a t} \map f t} = \map F {s - a}$ everywhere that $\laptrans f$ exists, for $\map \Re s > a$

title: First Variation Formula
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $J$ be an open real interval. Suppose $\gamma : I \to M$ is a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be a variation of $\gamma$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $V : M \to T_\gamma M$ be the variation field of $\Gamma$. Let $L_g$ be the Riemannian length of an admissible curve. Let $\gamma'$ be the velocity of $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$. Let $\tuple {a_0, \ldots, a_k}$ be an admissible subdivision for $\gamma$.

title: First Variation Formula for Proper Variation
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $J$ be an open real interval. Suppose $\gamma : I \to M$ is a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $\Gamma : J \times I \to M$ be a proper variation of $\gamma$. Let $T_p M$ be the tangent space at $p \in M$. Let $V : M \to T_\gamma M$ be the variation field of $\Gamma$. Let $L_g$ be the Riemannian length of an admissible curve. Let $\gamma'$ be the velocity of $\gamma$. Let $D_t$ be the covariant derivative along $\gamma$.

title: Fisher's Inequality
snippet: For a BIBD $\struct {v, k, \lambda}$, the number of blocks $b$ must be greater than or equal to the number of points $v$: $ b \ge v$

title: Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko Theorem
snippet: In general, for iid $\set {X_i} _{i\mathop = 1}^n$ with cdf $\map F x$ we have $\mathbb P \sqbrk {\max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {X_i} > x} = \map {F^n} x$. Let $x_* := \sup \set {x: \map F x 0, b_n$ such that: $\dfrac {\ds \max_{i \mathop = 1, \mathop \ldots, n} \set {X_i} - b_n} {a_n} \stackrel {dis} {\to} X_*$ for some non-degenerate $X_*$ with distribution $\map G x$. We have the following three possible limits Frechet: If $x > 0$, $\map G x = \map \exp {-x^{-a} }$ for some $a > 0$. If $x \le 0$, $\map G x = 0$.

title: Fitting Chord Into Circle
snippet: Into a given circle, it is possible to fit a chord equal to a given line segment which is not greater than the diameter of the circle.

title: Five Color Theorem
snippet: A planar graph $G$ can be assigned a proper vertex $k$-coloring such that $k \le 5$.

title: Five Cube Theorem
snippet: Every integer can be expressed as a sum of five cube numbers.

title: Five Eighths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 5 8$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Five Lemma
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let: $\begin{xy}\xymatrix@L+2mu@+1em{ M_1 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_1} \ar[d]^*{\phi_1} & M_2 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_2} \ar[d]^*{\phi_2} & M_3 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_3} \ar[d]^*{\phi_3} & M_4 \ar[r]^*{\alpha_4} \ar[d]^*{\phi_4} & M_5 \ar[d]^*{\phi_5} \\ N_1 \ar[r]_*{\beta_1} & N_2 \ar[r]_*{\beta_2} & N_3 \ar[r]_*{\beta_3} & N_4 \ar[r]_*{\beta_4} & N_5 }\end{xy}$ be a commutative diagram of $A$-modules. Suppose that the rows are exact. Then: If $\phi_2$ and $\phi_4$ are surjective and $\phi_5$ is injective then $\phi_3$ is surjective.

title: Five Ninths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 5 9$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Five Platonic Solids
snippet: There exist exactly five platonic solids:

title: Five Ramanujan-Nagell Numbers
snippet: There exist exactly $5$ Ramanujan-Nagell numbers: positive integers of the form $2^m - 1$ which are triangular: $0, 1, 3, 15, 4095$

title: Five Sevenths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 5 7$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Five Sixths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 5 6$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Fixed-Point Property is Topological
snippet: Let $T \sim T'$ be homeomorphic topological spaces. Suppose every continuous $f : T \to T$ has a fixed point. Then, every continuous $g : T' \to T'$ also has a fixed point.

title: Fixed-Point Representation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Fixed-Point Representation ==

title: Fixed Compass drawing Smaller Circle
snippet: == Problem == How can a rusty compass be used to draw a circle whose radius is smaller than that of the compass opening?

title: Fixed Elements form 1-Cycles
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$. Let $\Fix \pi$ be the set of elements fixed by $\pi$. For any $\pi \in S_n$, all the elements of $\Fix \pi$ form $1$-cycles.

title: Fixed Point Formulation of Explicit ODE
snippet: Let $x' = \map f {t, x}$ with $\map x {t_0} = x_0$ be an explicit ODE of dimension $n$. For $a, b \in \R$, let $\XX = \map {\CC} {\closedint a b; \R^n}$ be the space of continuous functions on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $T: \XX \to \XX$ be the map defined by: $\ds \map {\paren {T x} } t = x_0 + \int_{t_0}^t \map f {s, \map x s} \rd s$ {{explain|Definition of $\paren {T x}$}} Then a fixed point of $T$ in $\XX$ is a solution to the above ODE.

title: Fixed Point Set of Continuous Self-Map on Hausdorff Space is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $f: T \to T$ be a continuous mapping on $T$. Let $W$ be the set defined as: $W = \set {x \in T: \map f x = x}$ Then $W$ is closed in $T$.

title: Fixed Point of Composition of Inflationary Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be inflationary mappings. Let $x \in S$. Then: $x$ is a fixed point of $f \circ g$ $x$ is a fixed point of both $f$ and $g$.

title: Fixed Point of Idempotent Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an idempotent mapping. Let $\Img f$ be the image of $f$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is a fixed point of $f$ $x \in \Img f$.

title: Fixed Point of Mappings is Fixed Point of Composition
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be mappings. Let $x \in S$ be a fixed point of both $f$ and $g$. Then $x$ is also a fixed point of $f \circ g$, the composition of $f$ and $g$.

title: Fixed Point of Permutation is Fixed Point of Power
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\sigma \in S_n$. Let $i \in \Fix \sigma$, where $\Fix \sigma$ denotes the set of fixed elements of $\sigma$. Then for all $m \in \Z$: $i \in \Fix {\sigma^m}$

title: Fixed Point of Progressing Mapping on Minimally Closed Class is Greatest Element
snippet: $g$ has no fixed point, unless possibly the greatest element, if there is one.

title: Fixed Point of Progressing Mapping on Minimally Inductive Class is Greatest Element
snippet: Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$. Let $x$ be a fixed point of $g$. Then $x$ is the greatest element of $M$.

title: Fixed Point of g-Tower is Greatest Element
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Let $x = \map g x$. Then $x$ is the greatest element (under the subset relation) of $M$.

title: Fixed Points of Idempotent Operator
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space. Let $T : X \to X$ be an idempotent operator. Then the set of fixed points of $T$ is precisely the range $\Rng T$.

title: Fixed Points of Orthogonal Projection
snippet: Let $\struct {H, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\norm \cdot$ be the inner product norm of $H$. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Let $h \in H$. Then: $\map {P_K} h = h$ $h \in K$.

title: Fixed Points of Projection in Plane
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be distinct lines in the plane. 420px Let $\pr_{M, N}$ be the projection on $M$ along $N$: $\forall x \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{M, N} } x =$ the intersection of $M$ with the line through $x$ parallel to $N$. Then $M$ is the set of fixed points of $\pr_{M, N}$ in the sense that: $x \in M$ $\map {\pr_{M, N} } x = x$

title: Floor Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Floor Function == === Floor of $0 \cdotp 99999$ ===

title: Floor Function is Continuous on Right at Integer
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\map f x = \floor x$ where $\floor{\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $\map f x$ is continuous on the right at $n$.

title: Floor Function is Idempotent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Then: $\floor {\floor x} = \floor x$ That is, the floor function is idempotent.

title: Floor Function is Integer
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then the floor function of $x$ is an integer: $\floor x \in \Z$

title: Floor Function is Not Continuous on Left at Integer
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\map f x = \floor x$ where $\floor{\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $\map f x$ is not continuous on the left at $n$.

title: Floor Function is Replicative
snippet: The floor function is a replicative function in the sense that: $\ds \forall n \in \Z_{> 0}: \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \floor {x + \frac k n} = \floor {n x}$

title: Floor defines Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor function of $x$. Let $\RR$ be the relation defined on $\R$ such that: $\forall x, y, \in \R: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \floor x = \floor y$ Then $\RR$ is an equivalence, and $\forall n \in \Z$, the $\RR$-class of $n$ is the half-open interval $\hointr n {n + 1}$.

title: Floor equals Ceiling iff Integer
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ denote the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor x = \begin {cases} \ceiling x & : x \in \Z \\ \ceiling x - 1 & : x \notin \Z \\ \end {cases}$ or equivalently: $\ceiling x = \begin {cases} \floor x & : x \in \Z \\ \floor x + 1 & : x \notin \Z \\ \end {cases}$ where $\Z$ is the set of integers.

title: Floor is between Number and One Less
snippet: $x - 1 < \floor x \le x$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

title: Floor of Ceiling is Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor {\ceiling x} = \ceiling x$ That is, the floor of the ceiling is the ceiling.

title: Floor of Half of n+m plus Floor of Half of n-m+1
snippet: Let $n, m \in \Z$ be integers. $\floor {\dfrac {n + m} 2} + \floor {\dfrac {n - m + 1} 2} = n$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

title: Floor of Negative equals Negative of Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$, and $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then: $\floor {-x} = -\ceiling x$

title: Floor of Non-Integer
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $x \notin \Z$. Then: $\floor x < x$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

title: Floor of Number plus Integer
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z: \floor x + n = \floor {x + n}$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

title: Floor of Root of Floor equals Floor of Root
snippet: Let $x \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Then: $\ds \floor {\sqrt {\floor x} } = \floor {\sqrt x}$

title: Floor of Simple Finite Continued Fraction
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}_{k \mathop \ge 0}$ be a simple finite continued fraction of length $n \ge 0$. Let $x = \sqbrk {a_0, \ldots, a_n}$ be its value. Then the floor of $x$ is the partial denominator $a_0$: $\floor x = a_0$ unless $n = 1$ and $a_1 = 1$, in which case: $\floor x = x = a_0 + 1$

title: Floor of m+n-1 over n
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$. Then: $\floor {\dfrac {m + n - 1} n} = \ceiling {\dfrac m n}$ The identity does not necessarily apply for $n < 0$.

title: Floor of x+m over n
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$. Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\floor {\dfrac {x + m} n} = \floor {\dfrac {\floor x + m} n}$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$.

title: Floor plus One
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\floor {x + 1} = \floor x + 1$ where $\floor x$ is the floor function of $x$.

title: Floquet's Theorem
snippet: Let $\mathbf A \left({t}\right)$ be a continuous matrix function with period $T$. Let $\Phi \left({t}\right)$ be a fundamental matrix of the Floquet system $\mathbf x' = \mathbf A \left({t}\right) \mathbf x$. Then $\Phi \left({t + T}\right)$ is also a fundamental matrix. Moreover, there exists: A nonsingular, continuously differentiable matrix function $\mathbf P \left({t}\right)$ with period $T$ A constant (possibly complex) matrix $\mathbf B$ such that: $\Phi \left({t}\right) = \mathbf P \left({t}\right) e^{\mathbf Bt}$

title: Flow in Terms of Complex Potential
snippet: Let $\map u z$ be an inviscid, incompressible and irrotational flow in the complex plane. Let the velocity potential of $\map u z$ be $\varphi$. Let the stream function of $\map u z$ be $\psi$. Let the complex potential of $\map u z$ be: $w := \varphi + i \psi$ where: $\varphi$ denotes the velocity potential of $\map u z$ $\psi$ denotes the stream function of $\map u z$. Then: $\map u z = \overline {\paren {\dfrac {\d w} {\d z} } }$ where $\overline z$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z$.

title: Focal Property of Conic Section
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a conic section. Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be the foci of $\KK$. Let $P$ be a point on $\KK$. Let $\TT$ be the tangent to $\KK$ at $P$. Let $\LL_1$ be the straight line through $F_1$ to $P$. Let $\LL_2$ be the straight line through $P$ which makes the same angle with $\TT$ as does $\LL_1$. Then $\LL_2$ passes through $F_2$.

title: Focal Property of Ellipse
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipse. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $\EE$. Let $APB$ be a tangent to $\EE$ at $P$. Then: $\angle APF_1 = \angle BPF_2$ where $F_1$ and $F_2$ are the foci of $\EE$. 400px

title: Focal Property of Hyperbola
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a hyperbola. Let $APB$ be a tangent to $\KK$ at $P$. Then: $\angle APF_1 = \angle BPF_2$ where $F_1$ and $F_2$ are the foci of $\KK$.

title: Focal Property of Parabola
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a parabola whose focus is at $F$ and whose directrix is $D$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $\KK$. The tangent to $\KK$ at $P$ bisects the angle between the straight line $PF$ and the straight line through $P$ perpendicular to $D$. 500px

title: Focus of Hyperbola from Transverse and Conjugate Axis
snippet: Let $K$ be a hyperbola whose transverse axis is $2 a$ and whose conjugate axis is $2 b$. Let $c$ be the distance of the foci of $K$ from the center. Then: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2$

title: For Complete Ritz Sequence Continuous Functional approaches its Minimal Value
snippet: Let $J$ be a continuous functional. Let $\sequence {\phi_n}$ be a complete Ritz sequence. {{explain|The concept of $\sequence {\phi_n}$ does not appear to be related in any way to the statement of the theorem.}} Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \mu_n = \mu$ where $\ds \mu = \inf_y J \sqbrk y$.

title: Force Field is Conservative iff Potential Energy Exists
snippet: Let $\map {\mathbf F} {\mathbf r}$ be a force field. Then a potential energy function $\map P {\mathbf r}$ exists for $\map {\mathbf F} {\mathbf r}$ $\map {\mathbf F} {\mathbf r}$ is conservative.

title: Force between Infinite Parallel Straight Conductors carrying Steady Current
snippet: Let $s_1$ and $s_2$ be wires in a vacuum carrying steady currents $I_1$ and $I_2$. Let $s_1$ and $s_2$ be parallel and (effectively) infinitely long. Then the magnitude of the force per unit distance between $s_1$ and $s_2$ is given by: $\dfrac {\d F} {\d l} = \dfrac {\mu_0 I_1 I_2} {2 \pi r}$ where: $r$ denotes the distance between $s_1$ and $s_2$ $\mu_0$ denotes the vacuum permeability $\d l$ is an infinitesimal distance along one of the wires. Furthermore, if the currents are in the same direction, the force is attractive. Otherwise, it is repulsive.

Forking is Local
snippet: Let $T$ be a complete $\LL$-theory. Let $\mathfrak C$ be a monster model for $T$. Let $A\subseteq B$ be subsets of the universe of $\mathfrak C$. Let $\map \pi {\bar x}$ be an $n$-type over $B$. $\pi$ forks over $A$ a finite subset of $\pi$ forks over $A$.

title: Form of Elements of Inductive Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an inductive semigroup. Then the elements of $S$ are of the form: $\alpha \circ \beta \circ \beta \circ \cdots \circ \beta$

title: Form of Geometric Sequence of Integers
snippet: Let $P = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence of length $n + 1$ consisting of integers only. Then the $j$th term of $P$ is given by: $a_j = k p^{n - j} q^j$ where: the common ratio of $P$ expressed in canonical form is $\dfrac q p$ $k$ is an integer.

title: Form of Geometric Sequence of Integers from One
snippet: Let $Q_n = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence consisting of integers only. Let $a_0 = 1$. Then the $j$th term of $Q_n$ is given by: $a_j = a^j$ where: the common ratio of $Q_n$ is $a$ $a = a_1$. Thus: $Q_n = \tuple {1, a, a^2, \ldots, a^n}$

title: Form of Geometric Sequence of Integers in Lowest Terms
snippet: Let $G_n = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence of length $n$ consisting of positive integers only. Let $r$ be the common ratio of $G_n$. Let the elements of $G_n$ be the smallest positive integers such that $G_n$ has common ratio $r$. Then the $j$th term of $G_n$ is given by: $a_j = p^{n - j} q^j$ where $r = \dfrac q p$. That is: $G_n = \tuple {p^n, p^{n - 1} q, p^{n - 2} q^2, \ldots, p q^{n - 1}, q^n}$

title: Form of Geometric Sequence of Integers with Coprime Extremes
snippet: Let $Q_n = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence of length $n$ consisting of positive integers only. Let $a_1$ and $a_n$ be coprime. Then the $j$th term of $Q_n$ is given by: $a_j = q^j p^{n - j}$

title: Form of Logit for Logistic Curve
snippet: Let $p$ denote the probability of the occurrence of an event. Let $p$ satisfy a logistic relationship with an explanatory variable $x$ of the form: $p = \dfrac 1 {1 + \map \exp {-\paren {\alpha + \beta x} } }$ Let $Y$ be the logit of $p$. Then: $Y = \alpha + \beta x$

title: Form of Prime Sierpiński Number of the First Kind
snippet: Suppose $S_n = n^n + 1$ is a prime Sierpiński number of the first kind. Then: $n = 2^{2^k}$ for some integer $k$.

title: Form of Spherical Harmonic
snippet: A spherical harmonic has the form: $r^n \paren {a_n \map {P_n} {\cos \theta} + \ds \sum_{m \mathop = 1}^n \paren { {a_n}^m \cos m \phi + {b_n}^m \sin m \phi} \map { {P_n}^m} {\cos \theta} }$ where: $P_n$ denotes a Legendre polynomial ${P_n}^m$ denotes an associated Legendre function.

title: Formal Derivative of Polynomials Satisfies Leibniz's Rule
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $R \sqbrk X$ be the polynomial ring over $R$. Let $f, g \in R \sqbrk X$ be polynomials. Let $f'$ and $g'$ denote their formal derivatives. Then: $\paren {f g}' = f g' + f' g$

title: Formula and its Negation Cannot Both Cause Forking
snippet: Let $T$ be a complete $\LL$-theory. Let $\mathfrak C$ be a monster model for $T$. Let $A \subseteq B$ be subsets of the universe of $\mathfrak C$. Let $\map \pi {\bar x}$ be an $n$-type over $B$. If $\pi$ does not fork over $A$, then for any formula $\map \phi {\bar x, \bar b}$, either $\pi \cup \set \phi$ or $\pi \cup \set {\neg \phi}$ does not fork over $A$.

title: Formula for Aerodynamic Drag
snippet: The following formula can be used in aerodynamics to calculate an estimate of the aerodynamic drag on a body $B$ passing through a fluid $F$ (usually air): $D = \dfrac 1 2 k \rho A v^2$ where: $D$ is the drag on $B$ $A$ is a representative area of cross-section of $B$ $\rho$ is the density of $F$ $v$ is the speed of $B$ through $F$ $k$ is a coefficient which depends on the conditions, and is a function of the Reynolds number.

title: Formula for Compound Interest
snippet: Let $P$ be a principal. Let $r$ be the interest rate for a given conversion period. Let $n$ be the number of conversion periods. The amount of compound interest paid on $P$ at the end of $n$ conversion periods is given by: $I = P \paren {\paren {1 + r}^n - 1}$

title: Formula for Hydrodynamic Lift
snippet: The following formula can be used in hydrodynamics to calculate an estimate of the (hydrodynamic) lift on a body $B$ passing through a fluid $F$ (usually air): $L = c \rho A v^2$ where: $L$ is the lift on $B$ $A$ is a representative area of $B$, such as the area of a wing or hydrofoil $\rho$ is the density of $F$ $v$ is the speed of $B$ through $F$ $c$ is a coefficient which depends on the circulation of $F$ around $B$, and is a function of the Reynolds number.

title: Formula for Nth Prime

title: Formula for Radiocarbon Dating
snippet: Let $Q$ be a quantity of a sample of dead organic material (usually wood) whose time of death is to be determined. Let $t$ years be the age of $Q$ which is to be determined. Let $r$ denote the ratio of the quantity of carbon-14 remaining in $Q$ after time $t$ to the quantity of carbon-14 in $Q$ at the time of its death. Then the number of years that have elapsed since the death of $Q$ is given by: $t = -8060 \ln r$

title: Formula for Spearman's Rank Correlation Coefficient
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of entities. Let $\sequence {x_i}$ and $\sequence {y_i}$ be rankings of $S$ based on an arbitrary property of the elements of $S$. Let there be no tied ranks in either $\sequence {x_i}$ or $\sequence {y_i}$. The Spearman's rank correlation coefficient may be calculated using the formula: $r_S = 1 - \dfrac {6 T} {n \paren {n^2 - 1} }$ where $T$ denotes the sum of squares of the differences between the ranks for each of the pairs $\tuple {x_1, y_1}$

title: Formula for Total Variation of Continuously Differentiable Function
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a continuously differentiable function. Let $\map {V_} {\closedint a b}$ be the total variation of $f$ on $\closedint a b$. Then: $\ds V_f = \int_a^b \size {\map {f'} x} \rd x$

title: Formulation 1 Rank Axioms Implies Rank Function of Matroid
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\rho : \powerset S \to \Z$ be a mapping from the power set of $S$ to the integers. Let $\rho$ satisfy formulation 1 of the rank axioms: Then $\rho$ is the rank function of a matroid on $S$.

snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on an infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a compact space.

title: Fort Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a Fort space on an infinite set $S$. Then $T$ is a completely normal space. Consequently, $T$ satisfies all weaker separation axioms.

title: Forward-Backward Induction
snippet: Let $P$ be a propositional function on the natural numbers $\N$. Suppose that: $(1): \quad \forall n \in \N: \map P {2^n}$ holds. $(2): \quad \map P n \implies \map P {n - 1}$. Then $\map P n$ holds for all $\forall n \in \N$. The proof technique based on this result is called forward-backward induction.

title: Forward Difference of Falling Factorial
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $\Delta$ denote the forward difference operator. Let $x^{\underline m}$ be the $m$th falling factorial of $x$ Then: $\map \Delta {x^{\underline m} } = m x^{\underline {m - 1} }$

title: Forward Difference of Harmonic Number Function
snippet: Let $H_x$ denote the harmonic number function. Then: $\Delta H_x = \dfrac 1 {x + 1}$ where $\Delta H_x$ denotes the forward difference operator.

title: Forward Difference of Power

title: Four-Line Locus
snippet: Let $4$ straight lines in the plane be given. The problem is to find the locus of a point $P$ such that the product of the distances from $P$ to any $2$ of them is proportional to the product of the distances to the other $2$.

title: Four-Parts Formula
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. We have: $\cos a \cos C = \sin a \cot b - \sin C \cot B$ That is: $\map \cos {\text {inner side} } \cdot \map \cos {\text {inner angle} } = \map \sin {\text {inner side} } \cdot \map \cot {\text {other side} } - \map \sin {\text {inner angle} } \cdot \map \cot {\text {other angle} }$ This is known as the four-parts formula, as it defines the relationship between…

title: Four Color Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a planar graph. Then: $\map \chi G \le 4$ where the $\map \chi G$ denotes the chromatic number of $G$. That is, $G$ can be assigned a proper vertex $k$-coloring such that $k \le 4$.

title: Four Color Theorem for Finite Maps implies Four Color Theorem for Infinite Maps
snippet: Suppose that any finite planar graph can be assigned a proper vertex $k$-coloring such that $k \le 4$. Then the same is true of any infinite planar graph.

Fourier's Law
snippet: == Physical Law == Fourier's law is used when modeling the flow of heat through a given substance $\SS$. It states: $\mathbf q = -k \nabla T$ where: $\mathbf q$ denotes heat flux $k$ denotes the thermal conductivity of $\SS$ $T$ denotes the temperature at a given point in $\SS$ $\nabla T$ denotes the gradient operator on $T$

title: Fourier Series over General Range from Specific
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a function such that $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x$ converges absolutely. Then $f$ can be expressed by a Fourier series of the form: $\ds \frac {A_0} 2 + \sum_{m \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {A_m \cos \frac {2 m \pi \paren {x - a} } {b - a} + B_m \sin \frac {2 m \pi \paren {x - a} } {b - a} }$ where: {{eqn | l = A_m | r = \dfrac 2 {b - a} \int_a^b \map f x \cos \frac {2 m \pi \paren {x - a} } {b - a} \rd x }} {{eqn | l = B_m | r = \dfrac 2 {b - a} \int_a^b \map f x \sin \frac {2 m \pi \paren {x - a} } {b - a} \rd x }}

title: Fourier Transform of 1
snippet: Let: $\map f x = 1$ Then: $\map {\hat f} s = \map \delta s$ where $\map {\hat f} s$ is the Fourier transform of $\map f x$.

title: Fourier Transform of 1-Lebesgue Space Function is Bounded
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $\map {L^1} {\R^n}$ be the complex-valued Lebesgue $1$-space with respect to the Lebesgue measure. Let $f \in \map {L^1} {\R^n}$. Let $\hat f$ be the Fourier transform of $f$. Then: $\ds \sup_{\mathbf s \mathop \in \R^n} \cmod {\map {\hat f} {\mathbf s} } \le \norm f_{\map {L^1} {\R^n} }$

title: Fourier Transform of Derivative of Tempered Distribution
snippet: Let $T \in \map {\SS'} \R$ be a tempered distribution. Let $\xi \in \R$ be a real number. Let the hat denote the Fourier transform. Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\hat {\paren{T'} } = 2 \pi i \xi \hat T$

title: Fourier Transform of Dirac Delta Distribution
snippet: Let $\delta \in \map {\SS'} \R$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Let $\mathbf 1 : \map \SS \R \to \R$ be the constant tempered distribution such that for all $\phi \in \map \SS \R$ we have: $\ds \map {\mathbf 1} \phi = \int_{-\infty}^\infty 1 \cdot \map \phi x \rd x$ Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\hat \delta = \mathbf 1$ where the hat denotes the Fourier transform of a tempered distribution.

title: Fourier Transform of Exponential Function
snippet: Let $\map f x$ be defined as the real exponential function where the absolute value of the input is used in the exponent and the exponent is scaled by a factor of $-2 \pi a$: $\map f x = e^{-2 \pi a \size x}: \R \to \R$ Then: $\map {\hat f} s = \dfrac 1 \pi \dfrac a {a^2 + s^2}$ where $\map {\hat f} s$ is the Fourier transform of $\map f x$.

title: Fourier Transform of Normal Function
snippet: Let $\map f x$ be defined as $\sqrt \pi$ times the normal probability density function where $\mu = 0$ and $\sigma = \dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2$: {{eqn | l = \map f x | r = \dfrac {\sqrt {\pi} } {\dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2 \sqrt {2 \pi} } \map \exp {-\dfrac {\paren {x - 0}^2} {2 \paren {\dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2 }^2} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = e^{-x^2} | c = }} Then: $\map {\hat f} s = \sqrt \pi e^{-\paren {\pi s }^2}$ where $\map {\hat f} s$ is the Fourier transform of $\map f x$.

title: Fourier Transform of Tempered Distribution on 1-Lebesgue Space equals Tempered Distribution of Fourier Transform of defining Function
snippet: Let $\map {L^1} \R$ be the Lebesgue $1$-space. Let $f \in \map {L^1} \R$. Let $T_f \in \map {\SS'} \R$ be a tempered distribution associated with $f$. Then: $\hat T_f = T_{\hat f}$ where: $\hat T_f$ denotes the Fourier transform of the tempered distribution $T_f$ $\hat f$ denotes the Fourier transform of the real function $f$.

title: Fourth Apotome/Example
snippet: == Example of Fourth Apotome== Let $a, b \in \set {x \in \R_{>0} : x^2 \in \Q}$ be two rationally expressible numbers such that $a - b$ is an apotome. By definition, $a - b$ is a fourth apotome : $(1): \quad a \in \Q$ $(2): \quad \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} a \notin \Q$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Let $a = 3$ and $b = \sqrt 2$. Then: {{eqn | l = \frac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a | r = \frac {\sqrt {9 - 2} } 3 }} {{eqn | r = \frac {\sqrt 7} 3 | rr= \notin \Q }} Therefore $3 - \sqrt 2$ is a fourth apotome. Category:Examples of Apotome

title: Fourth Hyperoperation is Tetration Operation
snippet: The $4$th hyperoperation is the tetration operation restricted to the positive integers: $\forall x, y \in \Z_{\ge 0}: H_4 \left({x, y}\right) = x \uparrow \uparrow y$ where $\uparrow \uparrow$ denotes tetration: $x \uparrow \uparrow n := \begin{cases} 1 & : n = 0 \\ x \uparrow \left({x \uparrow \uparrow \left({n - 1}\right)}\right) & : n > 0 \\ \end{cases}$ In this context, $x \uparrow y$ is the Knuth notation for powers: $x \uparrow y := x^y$

title: Fourth Isomorphism Theorem
snippet: Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $K = \map \ker \phi$ be the kernel of $\phi$. Let $\mathbb K$ be the set of all subrings of $R$ which contain $K$ as a subset. Let $\mathbb S$ be the set of all subrings of $\Img \phi$. Let $\phi^\to: \powerset R \to \powerset S$ be the direct image mapping of $\phi$. Then its restriction $\phi^\to: \mathbb K \to \mathbb S$ is a bijection. Also: $(1): \quad \phi^\to$ and its inverse both preserve subsets.

title: Fourth Power Modulo 5
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $n^4 \equiv m \pmod 5$ where $m \in \set {0, 1}$.

title: Fourth Power as Summation of Groups of Consecutive Integers
snippet: Take the positive integers and group them in sets such that the $m$th set contains the next $m$ positive integers: $\set 1, \set {2, 3}, \set {4, 5, 6}, \set {7, 8, 9, 10}, \set {11, 12, 13, 14, 15}, \ldots$ Remove all the sets with an even number of elements. Then the sum of all the integers in the first $n$ sets remaining equals $n^4$.

title: Fourth Power expressible as Sum of 6 Fourth Powers
snippet: $28 \, 561$ can be expressed as the sum of $6$ fourth powers: $28 \, 561 = 13^4 = 12^4 + 8^4 + 7^4 + 6^4 + 2^4 + 2^4$

title: Fourth Power is Sum of 2 Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\exists a, b \in \Z_{\ge 0}: n^4 = T_a + T_b$ where $T_a$ and $T_b$ are triangular numbers. That is, the $4$th power of an integer equals the sum of two triangular numbers.

title: Fourth Power of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Then its fourth power is given by: $z^4 = a^4 - 6 a^2 b^2 + b^4 + i \paren {4 a^3 b - 4 a b^3}$

title: Fourth Powers which are Sum of 4 Fourth Powers
snippet: The following positive integers are such that their fourth powers can be expressed as the sum of the fourth powers of $4$ other positive integers with no common factors: $353, 651, 2487, 2501, 2829, \ldots$

title: Fourth Sylow Theorem
snippet: The number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1 \pmod p$.

title: Fraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Fractions == $(1): \quad \dfrac 1 2$ is a proper fraction. $(2): \quad \dfrac 5 2$ is an improper fraction. It can be expressed as a mixed fraction as follows: $\dfrac 5 2 = \dfrac {4 + 1} 2 = \dfrac 4 2 + \dfrac 1 2 = 2 \frac 1 2$ $(3): \quad \dfrac {24} {36}$ is a proper fraction, although not in canonical form. It is found that when $\dfrac {24} {36}$ is expressed in canonical form: $\dfrac {24} {36} = \dfrac {12 \times 2} {12 \times 3} = \dfrac 2 3$ its denominator is not $1$. Hence $\dfrac {24} {36}$ is indeed a vulgar fraction. Category:Examples of Fractions

title: Fractional Sobolev Embedding Theorem
snippet: Let $S'$ denote the space of tempered distributions. Let $\FF : S' \to S'$ denote the Fourier transform. For each $s \in \R$ and $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$, let: $\map {W^{s, p} } {\R^n} = \set {u \in S': \sequence \xi^s \hat u \in \map {L^p} {\R^n} }$ where: $\sequence \xi = \paren {1 + \size \xi^2}^\frac 1 2$ Then: $(1): \quad$ If $s > t$ then $\map {W^{s, p} } {\R^n}$ embeds continuously into $\map {W^{t, q} } {\R^n}$ where $q$ is given by $\dfrac 1 q = \dfrac 1 p - \dfrac {s - t} n$. Category:Fourier Analysis

title: Frame-Homogeneous Riemannian Manifold is Homogeneous and Isotropic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Suppose $M$ is frame-homogeneous. Then $M$ is homogeneous and isotropic.

title: Frame Homomorphism Onto Two Induced by Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\struct{\mathbf 2, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ denote the (Boolean Lattice) $\mathbf 2$. Let $p$ be a completely prime filter of $L$. Let $\phi_p : L \to \mathbf 2$ be the mapping defined by: $\forall a \in L : \map {\phi_p} a = \begin{cases} \top & : a \in p\\ \bot & : a \notin p \end{cases}$ Then: $\phi_p$ is a frame homomorphism

title: Frame Homomorphism Preserves Greatest Element
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame homomophism. Let $\top_1$ and $\top_2$ denote the greatest elelment of $L_1$ and $L_2$ respectively. Then: $\map \phi \top_1 = \top_2$

title: Frame Homomorphism Preserves Smallest Element
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame homomophism. Let $\bot_1$ and $\bot_2$ denote the smallest elelment of $L_1$ and $L_2$ respectively. Then: $\map \phi \bot_1 = \bot_2$

title: Frame Homomorphism is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame homomorphism. Then: $\phi: \struct{S_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct{S_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ is a lattice homomorphism where: $\wedge_1, \vee_1$ denote the meet and join on $L_1$ $\wedge_2, \vee_2$ denote the meet and join on $L_2$

title: Frame Homomorphism is Lower Adjoint of Galois Connection
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}, L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $f : L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame homomorphism. Then there exists a Galois connection $g = \tuple {\upperadjoint g, \loweradjoint g}$: the lower adjoint $\loweradjoint g = f$

title: Frame Homomorphism of Continuous Mapping is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{S_1, \tau_1}, T_2 = \struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f : T_1 \to T_2$ be a continuous mapping. Let $\map \Omega {T_1} = \struct{\tau_1, \subseteq}$ and $\map \Omega {T_2} = \struct{\tau_2, \subseteq}$ denote the frames of $T_1$ and $T_2$ respectively. Let $\map \Omega f : \map \Omega {T_2} \to \map \Omega {T_1}$ be the frame homomorphism of $f$ Then: $\map \Omega f : \map \Omega {T_2} \to \map \Omega {T_1}$ is a frame homomorphism

title: Frame Isomorphism is Isomorphism in Category Frm
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Frm}$ denote the category of frames. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a morphism of $\mathbf{Frm}$. Then: $\phi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbf{Frm}$ $\phi$ is a complete lattice isomorphsm

title: Frame Spectrum Functor is Contravariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Frm}$ denote the category of frames. Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Then: the frame spectrum functor $\mathbf {\operatorname {Sp}} : \mathbf{Frm} \to \mathbf{Top}$ is a contravariant functor

title: Frame is Distributive Lattice
snippet: Let $L= \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Then: $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ is a distributive lattice where $\vee$ and $\wedge$ denote the join and meet operations on $S$, respectively.

title: Frame of Open Sets Functor is Contravariant
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Let $\mathbf{Frm}$ denote the category of frames. Then: the open sets functor $\mathbf \Omega : \mathbf{Top} \to \mathbf{Frm}$ is a contravariant functor

title: Frame of Reference/Examples/Coordinate System
snippet: == Example of Frame of Reference == An elementary example of a frame of reference is a coordinate system established in the plane or in space in order for a mathematical model to be implemented.

title: Frame of Reference moving at Constant Velocity relative to Inertial Frame is Inertial Frame
snippet: Let $F_1$ be a frame of reference. Let $F_2$ be an inertial frame of reference. Let $F_1$ be moving at constant velocity relative to $F_2$. Then $F_1$ is an inertial frame of reference.

title: Frame of Topological Space is Frame
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\map \Omega T$ denote the frame of topological space $T$. Then: $\map \Omega T$ is a frame

title: Frattini's Argument
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $K$ be a finite normal subgroup of $G$, and $p$ a prime which divides the order of $K$. Let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $K$, and $\map {N_G} P$ the normalizer of $P$ in $G$. Then: $G = \map {N_G} P \circ K = K \circ \map {N_G} P$

title: Free Commutative Monoid is Commutative Monoid
snippet: The free commutative monoid on a set $\family {X_j: j \in J}$ is a commutative monoid.

title: Free Commutative Monoid on One Element is Isomorphic to Natural Numbers under Addition
snippet: Let $X = \set x$ be a singleton. Let $M$ be the free commutative monoid on $X$. Then $M$ is isomorphic to the additive monoid of natural numbers.

title: Free Matroid is Matroid
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\struct {S, \powerset S}$ be the free matroid of $S$. Then $\struct {S, \powerset S}$ is a matroid.

title: Free Module is Isomorphic to Free Module on Set
snippet: Let $M$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $\BB = \family {b_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of $M$. Let $\Psi: R^{\paren I} \to M$ be the morphism given by Universal Property of Free Module on Set.

title: Free Module on Set is Free
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $I$ be a set. Let $R^{\paren I}$ be the free $R$-module on $I$. Then $R^{\paren I}$ is a free $R$-module.

title: Free Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {M, i}$ and $\struct {N, j}$ be free monoids over $S$. Then there is a unique monoid isomorphism $f: M \to N$ such that: $\size f \circ i = j$ $\size {f^{-1} } \circ j = i$ where $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the underlying set functor on $\mathbf{Mon}$.

snippet: The system of axiomatic set theory that is Frege set theory is inconsistent.

title: Frequency of Beats
snippet: Let $W_1$ and $W_2$ be harmonic waves whose frequencies are $f_1$ and $f_2$. Let the superpositon of $W_1$ onto $W_2$ exhibit the phenomenon of beats. The frequency $f_b$ of those beats is: $f_b = \size {f_2 - f_1}$

title: Frequency of Harmonic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = a \map \cos {\omega \paren {x - c t} }$ The frequency $\nu$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\nu = \dfrac 1 \tau$ where $\tau$ is the period of $\phi$.

title: Frequency of Periodic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a periodic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = \map f {x - c t}$ The frequency $\nu$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\nu = \dfrac 1 \tau$ where $\tau$ is the period of $\phi$.

title: Freshman's Dream
snippet: == Mistake == The freshman's dream is a name for the mistake: $\paren {x + y}^n = x^n + y^n$ where $n$ is a real number. The correct result is given by the Binomial Theorem.

title: Fresnel Cosine Integral Function is Odd
snippet: $\map {\operatorname C} {-x} = -\map {\operatorname C} x$ where: $\operatorname C$ denotes the Fresnel cosine integral function $x$ is a real number.

title: Fresnel Cosine Integral Function of Zero
snippet: $\map {\operatorname C} 0 = 0$ where $\operatorname C$ denotes the Fresnel cosine integral function.

title: Fresnel Sine Integral Function is Odd
snippet: $\map {\operatorname S} {-x} = -\map {\operatorname S} x$ where: $\operatorname S$ denotes the Fresnel sine integral function $x$ is a real number.

title: Fresnel Sine Integral Function of Zero
snippet: $\map {\operatorname S} 0 = 0$ where $\operatorname S$ denotes the Fresnel sine integral function.

title: Freyd-Mitchell Embedding Theorem
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a small abelian category. Then there exists a ring with unity $R$ and a fully faithful and exact functor $F : \AA \to R \text{-} \mathbf{Mod}$ to the category of left $R$-modules.

title: Friction is Independent of Area of Contact
snippet: == Physical Law == Let $B$ be a body resting on a rough surface $S$. The friction between $B$ and $S$ does not depend on the area of contact between $B$ and $S$.

title: Frictional Couple/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Frictional Couples ==

title: Frictional Force is in Opposite Direction to Direction of Motion
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be bodies in contact. Let the contact between $A$ and $B$ be rough. Let $A$ and $B$ be moving relative to each other. Then the frictional force between $A$ and $B$ is in the opposite direction to the direction of motion.

title: Friendship Theorem
snippet: Let there be a group of $6$ people. The traditional setting is that these $6$ people are at a party. Then (at least) one of the following $2$ statements is true: $(1): \quad$ At least $3$ of these $6$ people have all met each other before $(2): \quad$ At least $3$ of these $6$ people have never met each other before. That is, either there exists a set of $3$ mutual acquaintances, or there exists a set of $3$ mutual strangers.

title: Frink's Metrization Theorem
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then: $T$ is metrizable for all $s \in S$ there exists a countable neighborhood basis, denoted $\set {U_{s, n} : n \in \N}$, such that: $(1): \quad \forall s \in S, n \in \N : U_{s, n + 1} \subseteq U_{s, n}$ $(2): \quad \forall s \in S, n \in \N : \exists m > n : \forall t \in S : U_{t, m} \cap U_{s ,m} \ne \O \implies U_{t, m} \subseteq U_{s, n}$

title: Frobenius's Theorem
snippet: An algebraic associative real division algebra $A$ is isomorphic to $\R, \C$ or $\Bbb H$.

title: Frobenius Endomorphism is Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity with prime characteristic $p$. Let $\phi: R \to R$ denote the Frobenius endomorphism on $R$: $\forall x \in R: \map \phi x = x^p$ Then $\phi$ is an additive function in the sense that: $\forall x, y \in R: \map \phi {x + y} = \map \phi x + \map \phi y$

title: Frobenius Endomorphism is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity with prime characteristic $p$. Let $\phi: R \to R$ denote the Frobenius endomorphism on $R$: $\forall x \in R: \map \phi x = x^p$ Then $\phi$ is a multiplicative function in the sense that: $\forall x, y \in R: \map \phi {x \circ y} = \map \phi x \circ \map \phi y$

title: Frobenius Endomorphism on Field is Injective
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p$. Then the Frobenius endomorphism $\Frob: F \to F$ is injective.

title: From Medial Straight Line arises Infinite Number of Irrational Straight Lines
Frullani's Integral
snippet: Let $a, b > 0$. Let $f$ be a function continuously differentiable on the non-negative real numbers. Suppose that $\ds \map f \infty = \lim_{x \mathop\to \infty} \map f x$ exists, and is finite. Then: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\map f {a x} - \map f {b x} } x \rd x = \paren {\map f \infty - \map f 0} \ln \frac a b$

title: Fréchet-Darmois-Cramér-Rao Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of $n$ observations from a probability distribution with frequency function $\map f {x, \theta}$. Let it be assumed that certain regularity conditions apply. Let it also be assumed that the extremes do not depend on $\theta$. The lower bound of the variance of an estimator $T$ of a parameter $\theta$ is given by $\dfrac 1 I$ where: $I = -n \map E {\dfrac {\partial^2 \ln f} {\partial \theta^2} }$

title: Fréchet Filter is Filter
snippet: Let $S$ be an infinite set. Let $\FF$ be the Fréchet filter on $S$. Then $\FF$ is a filter on $S$.

title: Fréchet Product Space is Complete Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ be the Fréchet product space on $\R^\omega$. Then $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ is a complete metric space.

title: Fréchet Product Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ be the Fréchet product space on $\R^\omega$. Then $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ is a metric space.

snippet: A full rook matrix is nonsingular.

title: Fully Characteristic Subgroup is Characteristic
snippet: Let $G$ a group. Let $H$ a fully characteristic subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is a characteristic subgroup of $G$.

title: Fully Normal Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a fully normal space. Then $T$ is a normal space.

title: Fully Normal Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a fully normal space. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Fully T4 Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a fully $T_4$ space. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Fully T4 Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a fully $T_4$ space. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Functions ==

title: Function A.E. Equal to Measurable Function in Complete Measure Space is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a complete measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $g : X \to \overline \R$ be a function such that: $f = g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Then $g$ is $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Function Measurable iff Positive and Negative Parts Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be an extended real-valued function. Let $f^+, f^-: X \to \overline \R$ be the positive and negative parts of $f$. Then $f$ is $\Sigma$-measurable both $f^+$ and $f^-$ are $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Function Measurable with respect to Power Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \powerset X}$ be a measurable space, where $\powerset X$ is the power set of $X$. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a function. Then $f$ is $\powerset X$-measurable function.

title: Function Obtained by Minimization from URM Computable Functions
snippet: Let the function $f: \N^{k+1} \to \N$ be a URM computable function. Let $g: \N^k \to \N$ be the function obtained by minimization from $f$ thus: $\map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} \approx \map {\mu y} {\map f {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y} = 0}$ Then $g$ is also URM computable.

title: Function Obtained by Minimization from URM Computable Relations
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a URM computable $k+1$-ary relation on $\N^{k + 1}$. Let the function $f: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be a URM computable function. Let $g: \N^k \to \N$ be the function obtained by minimization from $f$ thus: $\map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} \approx \mu y \map \RR {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y}$ Then $g$ is also URM computable.

title: Function Obtained by Primitive Recursion from URM Computable Functions
snippet: Let the functions $f: \N^k \to \N$ and $g: \N^{k + 2} \to \N$ be URM computable functions. Let $h: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be obtained from $f$ and $g$ by primitive recursion. Then $h$ is also URM computable.

title: Function Obtained by Substitution from URM Computable Functions
snippet: Let the functions $f: \N^t \to \N, g_1: \N^k \to \N, g_2: \N^k \to \N, \ldots, g_t: \N^k \to \N$ all be URM computable functions. Let $h: \N^k \to \N$ be defined from $f, g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_t$ by substitution. Then $h$ is also URM computable.

title: Function Simple iff Positive and Negative Parts Simple
snippet: Let $\left({X, \Sigma}\right)$ be a measurable space. Let $g: X \to \overline{\R}$ be an extended real-valued function. Then $g$ is a simple function its positive part $g^+$ and negative part $g^-$ are simple functions.

title: Function f is Big-O of g iff g is Big-Omega of f
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \R, g: \N \to \R$ be two real sequences, expressed here as real-valued functions on the set of natural numbers $\N$. Then: $\map f n \in \map \OO {\map g n}$ $\map g n \in \map \Omega {\map f n}$ where: $\OO$ denotes big-$\OO$ notation $\Omega$ denotes big-$\Omega$ notation.

title: Function in Differentiability Class 1 is also in Continuity Class
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $f$ be an element of differentiability class $C^1$. Then $f$ is also an element of the class $C$ of continuous real functions.

title: Function is Concave iff Hypograph is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {hypo} } f$ be the hypograph of $f$. Then $f$ is concave $\map {\operatorname {hypo} } f$ is convex in $X \times \GF$.

title: Function is Concave iff Strict Hypograph is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {hypo} } f$ be the hypograph of $f$. Then $f$ is convex $\map {\operatorname {hypo} } f$ is convex in $X \times \GF$.

title: Function is Convex iff Epigraph is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$. Let $f : C \to \overline \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {epi} } f$ be the epigraph of $f$. Then $f$ is convex $\map {\operatorname {epi} } f$ is convex in $X \times \GF$.

title: Function is Convex iff Strict Epigraph is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {epi}_S} f$ be the strict epigraph of $f$. Then $f$ is convex $\map {\operatorname {epi}_S} f$ is convex in $X \times \GF$.

title: Function is Odd Iff Inverse is Odd
snippet: Let $f$ be an odd real function with an inverse $f^{-1}$. Then $f^{-1}$ is also odd.

title: Function is Upper Semicontinuous iff Negative is Lower Semicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f : S \to \overline \R$ be an extended real valued function. Let $x_0 \in S$. Then $f$ is upper semicontinuous at $x_0$ $-f$ is lower semicontinuous at $x_0$.

title: Function of Bounded Variation is Bounded
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a function of bounded variation. Then $f$ is bounded.

title: Function of Discrete Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on the probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $g: \R \to \R$ be any real function. Then $Y = g \sqbrk X$, defined as: $\forall \omega \in \Omega: \map Y \omega = g \sqbrk {\map X \omega}$ is also a discrete random variable.

title: Function of Exponential Order of Scalar Multiple
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \F$ be a function, where $\F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\lambda$ be a real constant. Let $\map f t$ be of exponential order $a$. Then the function defined by $t \mapsto \map f {\lambda t}$ is of exponential order $a\lambda$.

title: Function of Two Discrete Random Variables
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $g: \R^2 \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Then $Z = \map g {X, Y}$, defined as: $\forall \omega \in \Omega: \map Z \omega = \map g {\map X \omega, \map Y \omega}$ is also a discrete random variable.

title: Function that Satisfies Axioms of Uncertainty
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $p_1, p_2, \dotsc, p_n$ be real numbers such that: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: p_i \ge 0$ $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n p_i = 1$ Let $\map H {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n}$ be a real-valued function which satisfies the axioms of uncertainty. Then: $\ds \map H {p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n} = -\lambda \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n p_i \log_b p_i$ where: $\lambda \in \R_{>0}$ $b \in \R_{>1}$ Thus the uncertainty function satisfies these axioms.

title: Function which is Zero except on Countable Set of Points is Null
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a subset of $\R$ such that $S$ is countable, either finite or countably infinite. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function such that: $\forall x \in \R \setminus S: \map f x = 0$ That is, except perhaps for the elements of $S$, the value of $f$ is zero. Then $f$ is a null function.

title: Function with Limit at Infinity of Exponential Order Zero
snippet: Let $f: \hointr 0 \to \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be continuous everywhere on their domains, except possibly for some finite number of discontinuities of the first kind in every finite subinterval of $\hointr 0 \to$. Let $f$ have a (finite) limit at infinity. Then $f$ is of exponential order $0$.

title: Functional/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Functionals ==

title: Functional Completeness over Finite Number of Arguments
snippet: Every truth function is definable from the set of Binary Truth Functions.

title: Functional Equation for Completed Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: Let $\xi : \C \to \C$ be the completed Riemann zeta function. Let $s\in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\map \xi s = \map \xi {1 - s}$

title: Functional Equation for Dirichlet L-Functions
snippet: Let $\chi$ be a primitive Dirichlet character to the modulus $q \geq 1$. Let $\map \Lambda {s, \chi}$ be the completed $L$-function for $\chi$. Let $\map \tau \chi$ denote the Gaussian sum. Then for all $s \in \C$: $\map \Lambda {s, \chi} = i^{-\kappa} \dfrac {\map \tau \chi} {\sqrt q} \map \Lambda {1 - s, \overline \chi}$ where $\kappa = \dfrac 1 2 \paren {1 - \map \chi {-1} }$.

title: Functional Equation for Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $\map \zeta s$ have an analytic continuation for $\map \Re s > 0$. Then: $\pi^{-s/2 } \map \Gamma {\dfrac s 2} \map \zeta s = \pi^{\paren {s/2 - 1/2 } } \map \Gamma {\dfrac {1 - s} 2} \map \zeta {1 - s}$ where $\Gamma$ is the gamma function

title: Functionally Complete Logical Connectives
snippet: These sets of logical connectives are functionally complete:

title: Functionally Complete Singleton Sets
snippet: The only binary logical connectives that form singleton sets which are functionally complete are NAND and NOR.

title: Functionally Incomplete Logical Connectives
snippet: These sets of logical connectives are not functionally complete.

title: Functions A.E. Equal iff Positive and Negative Parts A.E. Equal
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be extended real-valued functions. Then $f = g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere : $f^+ = g^+$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and $f^- = g^-$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. where: $f^+$ and $g^+$ denote the positive parts of $f$ and $g$ respectively $f^-$ and $g^-$ denote the negative parts of $f$ and $g$ respectively.

title: Functions in Vector Space of Real-Valued Functions Continuously Differentiable on Closed Interval vanish at Endpoints
snippet: Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\struct {\map {C^1} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the continuously differentiable on closed interval real function vector space. Let $S := \set {x \in \map {C^1} I : \map x a = y_a, \map x b = y_b}$. Then $S$ is a vector subspace of $\struct {\map {C^1} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ $y_a = y_b = 0$.

title: Functions of Independent Random Variables are Independent
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent random variables on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $g$ and $h$ be real-valued functions defined on the codomains of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Then $\map g X$ and $\map h Y$ are independent random variables.

title: Functor Category is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Then the functor category $\map {\operatorname {Funct} } {\mathbf C, \mathbf D}$ is a metacategory.

title: Functor Induced on Opposite Categories

title: Functor Over Object Comma Category is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $G : \mathbf E \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\paren{G \downarrow C}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $C$. Then: $\paren{G \downarrow C}$ is a metacategory

title: Functor Over Object Comma Category is Isomorphic to Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $G : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\mathbf 1$ denote the category one. Let $F: \mathbf 1\to \mathbf C$ be the functor defined by: {{DefineFunctor |ob = $F* = C$ |mor = $F \operatorname{id}_* = \operatorname{id}_C$ }} Let $\paren{G \downarrow C}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $C$. Let $\paren{G \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $F$.

title: Functor Under Object Comma Category is Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $F$ under $C$. Then: $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ is a metacategory.

title: Functor Under Object Comma Category is Isomorphic to Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\mathbf 1$ denote the category one. Let $G: \mathbf 1\to \mathbf C$ be the functor defined by: {{DefineFunctor |ob = $G* = C$ |mor = $G \operatorname{id}_* = \operatorname{id}_C$ }} Let $\paren{C \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $F$ under $C$. Let $\paren{G \downarrow F}$ denote the comma category $G$ over $F$.

title: Functor between Monoid Categories
snippet: Let $\left({S, \circ}\right)$ and $\left({T, *}\right)$ be monoids. Let $\mathbf S$ and $\mathbf T$ be the associated monoid categories. Let $F: \mathbf S \to \mathbf T$ be a functor. Then the morphism functor $F_1$ of $F$ is a monoid homomorphism.

title: Functor between Order Categories
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $\mathbf S$ and $\mathbf T$ be their associated order categories, respectively. Let $F: \mathbf S \to \mathbf T$ be a functor. Then its object functor $F: S \to T$ is a monotone mapping.

title: Fundamental Group is Independent of Base Point for Path-Connected Space
snippet: Let $X$ be a path-connected space. For $x \in X$, let $\map {\pi_1}{X, x}$ denote the fundamental group. For $x, y \in X$, there is an isomorphism: $\phi: \map {\pi_1} {X, x} \to \map {\pi_1} {X, y}$

title: Fundamental Group of Circle is Set of Integers
snippet: The fundamental group of a circle is the set of integers $\Z$.

title: Fundamental Law of Universal Class
snippet: $\forall x: x \in \Bbb U$ where: $\Bbb U$ denotes the universal class $x$ denotes a set.

title: Fundamental Principle of Counting
snippet: Let $A$ be a finite set. Let $\sequence {B_n}$ be a sequence of distinct finite subsets of $A$ which form a partition of $A$. Let $p_k = \size {B_k}$ for each $k \in \closedint 1 n$. Then: $\ds \size A = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n p_k$ That is, the sum of the numbers of elements in the subsets of a partition of a set is equal to the total number of elements in the set.
