title: Hexagonal Number as 4 times Triangular Number plus n
snippet: Let $H_n$ be the $n$th hexagonal number. Then: $H_n = 4 T_{n - 1} + n$ where $T_{n - 1}$ is the $n - 1$th triangular number.

title: Hexagonal Number is Triangular Number
snippet: Let $H_n$ be the $n$th hexagonal number. Then $H_n$ is the $2 n - 1$th triangular number.

title: Hexominoes cannot form Rectangle
snippet: While there are a total of $210$ squares in a complete set of hexominoes, it is impossible to build them into a rectangle of side lengths $a$ and $b$ where $a \times b = 210$.

title: Higher-Aleph Complement Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an $\aleph_n$ complement space. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $T$.

title: Higher Derivatives/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Higher Derivatives ==

title: Higher Derivatives of Exponential Function
snippet: Let $\exp x$ be the exponential function. Then: $\map {\dfrac {\d^n} {\d x^n} } {\exp x} = \exp x$

title: Higher Dimensional Hausdorff Measure than Euclidean Space is Zero
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be the $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. Let $s \in \R_{>n}$. Then: $\map {\HH ^s} {\R^n} = 0$ where $\map {\HH^s} \cdot$ denotes the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\R^n$

title: Higher Homotopy Groups are Abelian
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $x_0 \in S$. Let $n \ge 2$ be a integer. Let $\pi_n \left({T, x_0}\right)$ be the $n$th homotopy group with base point $x_0$. Then $\pi_n \left({T, x_0}\right)$ is abelian.

title: Higher Order Derivatives of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le A$. Let $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial s}$, the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $s$, exist and be continuous on said intervals. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then, everywhere that $\laptrans f$ exists and is $n$ times differentiable: $\dfrac {\d^n} {\d s^n} \laptrans {\map f t} = \paren {-1}^n \laptrans {t^n \, \map f t}$

title: Highest Power of 2 Dividing Numerator of Sum of Odd Reciprocals
snippet: Let: $S = \dfrac p q = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac 1 {2 k - 1}$ where $\dfrac p q$ is the canonical form of $S$. Let $n = 2^k m$ where $m$ is odd. Then the largest power of $2$ that divides $p$ is $2^{2 k}$.

title: Highly Composite Number/Examples/1
snippet: == Example of Highly Composite Number == $1$ is a highly composite number, being the smallest positive integer with $1$ divisor or more.

title: Highly Composite Number/Examples/2
snippet: == Example of Highly Composite Number == $2$ is a highly composite number, being the smallest positive integer with $2$ divisors or more.

title: Highly Composite Number/Examples/60
snippet: == Example of Highly Composite Number == $60$ is a highly composite number, being the smallest positive integer with $12$ divisors or more.

title: Hilbert's Basis Theorem
snippet: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $A \sqbrk x$ be the ring of polynomial forms over $A$ in the single indeterminate $x$. Then $A \sqbrk x$ is also a Noetherian ring.

title: Hilbert's Basis Theorem for Finitely Generated Algebras
snippet: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring. Let $B$ be a finitely generated algebra over $A$. Then $B$ is a Noetherian ring.

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz
snippet: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $n \geq 0$ be an natural number. Let $k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Then for every ideal $J \subseteq k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$, the associated ideal of its zero-locus equals its radical: $\map I {\map Z J} = \map \Rad J$

title: Hilbert-Waring Theorem
snippet: For each $k \in \Z: k \ge 2$, there exists a positive integer $\map g k$ such that every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of at most $\map g k$ positive $k$th powers.

title: Hilbert Cube is Compact
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a compact space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a completely normal space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Homeomorphic to Countable Infinite Product of Real Number Unit Intervals
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube: $M_1 = \ds \prod_{k \mathop \in \N} \closedint 0 {\dfrac 1 k}$ under the same metric as that of the Hilbert sequence space: $\ds \forall x = \sequence {x_i}, y = \sequence {y_i} \in I^\omega: \map {d_2} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} \paren {x_k - y_k}^2}^{\frac 1 2}$ Let $M_2$ be the metric space defined as: $M_2 = \ds \prod_{k \mathop \in \N} \closedint 0 1$ under the product topology. Then $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic.

title: Hilbert Cube is Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is an injectively path-connected space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a locally injectively path-connected space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a metric space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a second-countable space.

title: Hilbert Cube is Separable
snippet: Let $M = \struct {I^\omega, d_2}$ be the Hilbert cube. Then $M$ is a separable space.

title: Hilbert Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Hilbert Matrices ==

title: Hilbert Matrix is Cauchy Matrix
snippet: A Hilbert matrix is a special case of a Cauchy matrix.

title: Hilbert Matrix is Positive Definite
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a Hilbert matrix. Then $\mathbf A$ is positive definite

title: Hilbert Proof System Instance 2 Independence Results
snippet: Let $\mathscr H_2$ be Instance 2 of the Hilbert proof systems. Then the following independence results hold:

title: Hilbert Proof System Instance 2 is Consistent
snippet: Instance 2 of the Hilbert proof systems $\mathscr H_2$ is consistent.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Complete Metric Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\left\langle{x_i}\right\rangle$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^\infty x_i^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a complete metric space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Homeomorphic to Countable Infinite Product of Real Number Spaces
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ denote the real number line under the Euclidean topology. Let $\R^\omega = \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in \N} \struct {\R, \tau_d}$ denote the countable-dimensional real Cartesian space under the product topology. Then $\ell^2$ is homeomorphic to $\R^\omega$.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is injectively path-connected.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $\ell^2$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a Lindelöf space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a metric space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\ell^2$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a second-countable space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is Separable
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} x_i^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a separable space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is not Locally Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is not a locally compact Hausdorff space.

title: Hilbert Sequence Space is not Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} x_i^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is not $\sigma$-compact.

title: Hilbert Space Direct Sum is Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\sequence {H_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a $I$-indexed family of Hilbert spaces over $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $H = \ds \bigoplus_{i \mathop \in I} H_i$ be their Hilbert space direct sum. Then $H$ is a Hilbert space.

title: Hilbert Space Direct Sum of Countably Many Separable Hilbert Spaces is Separable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. For each $n \in \N$, let $\struct {\HH_n, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_n}$ be a separable Hilbert space over $\GF$. Let: $\ds \HH = \bigoplus_{n \mathop \in \N} \HH_n$ be the direct sum of $\sequence {\HH_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then $\HH$ is separable.

title: Hilbert Space Isomorphism is Bijection
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Denote by $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_H$ and $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_K$ their respective inner products. Let $U: H \to K$ be an isomorphism. Then $U$ is a bijection.

title: Hilbert Space Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Hilbert space isomorphism is an equivalence relation.

title: Hilbert Space Isomorphism preserves Orthocomplements
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $T : \HH \to \KK$ be a Hilbert space isomorphism. Let $U \subseteq \HH$. Then: $T \sqbrk {U^\bot} = \paren {T \sqbrk U}^\bot$

title: Hilbert Space Projection is *-Algebra Projection
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\map B \HH$ be the space of bounded linear operators on $\HH$ understood as a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $P : \HH \to \HH$ be a Hilbert space projection. Then $P$ is a $\ast$-algebra projection.

title: Hilbert Space Projections with Zero Product are Pointwise Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $P, Q : \HH \to \HH$ be projections (in the Hilbert space sense) such that: $P Q = 0$ Then: $\innerprod {Q x} {P y} = 0$ for each $x, y \in \HH$.

title: Hilbert Space Separable iff Countable Dimension
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Then $H$ is a separable space it has countable dimension.

title: Hilbert Space is Hausdorff Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {H, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $d: H \times H \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the metric induced by the inner product norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ on $H$. Let $\tau$ be the the topology on $H$ induced by the metric $d$. Then $\struct {H, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space.

title: Hilbert Spaces Isomorphic iff Same Dimension
snippet: Two Hilbert spaces are isomorphic iff they have the same dimension.

title: Hinge Theorem
snippet: If two triangles have two pairs of sides which are the same length, the triangle with the larger included angle also has the larger third side.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is T0
snippet: Let $T$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is a $T_0$ space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is T4
snippet: Let $T$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is T5
snippet: Let $T$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is a $T_5$ space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is not Regular
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is not a regular space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is not a $T_1$ space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Hjalmar Ekdal Space is not T3.5
snippet: Let $T$ be a Hjalmar Ekdal space. Then $T$ is not a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Hodge Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == It is conjectured that: For projective algebraic varieties, Hodge cycles are rational linear combinations of algebraic cycles.

title: Holomorphic 1-forms are closed
snippet: Holomorphic 1-forms are closed.

title: Holomorphic Branch/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Holomorphic Branches ==

title: Holomorphic Elliptic Function is Constant
snippet: Let $\phi: \C \to \C$ be an elliptic function. Let $\phi$ in addition be a holomorphic function. Then $\phi$ is constant

title: Holomorphic Function is Analytic
snippet: Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $r > 0$ be a real number. Let $f$ be a function holomorphic on some open disk $D = \map B {a, r}$. Then $f$ is complex analytic on $D$.

title: Holomorphic Function is Conformal if Derivative is Non-Zero
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a holomorphic function. Let $a \in \C$ be a point in the domain of $f$. Then $f$ is conformal at $a$ if the derivative of $f$ at $a$ is non-zero.

title: Holomorphic Function is Continuously Differentiable
snippet: Let $U \subseteq \C$ be an open set. Let $f : U \to \C$ be a holomorphic function. Then $f$ is continuously differentiable in $U$.

title: Holomorphic Function is Identified by Real or Imaginary Part
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be an open subset of the set of complex numbers $\C$. Let $f, g : D \to \C$ be holomorphic functions such that either: $\map \Re f = \map \Re g$ or: $\map \Im f = \map \Im g$ Then $f = g$.

title: Holomorphic Function with Constant Imaginary Part is Constant
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be an open subset of the set of complex numbers $\C$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a holomorphic function such that $\map \Im f$ is constant. Then $f$ is constant.

title: Hom Bifunctor With Left Functor is Covariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $L : \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {L-, -} : \mathbf D^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor with left functor. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {L-, -}$ is a covariant functor.

title: Hom Bifunctor With Left Identity Functor is Hom Bifunctor
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} : \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ denote the identity functor. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}-, -} : \mathbf C^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor with left functor $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {-, -} : \mathbf C^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor.

title: Hom Bifunctor With Right Functor is Covariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $R : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf D} } {-, R-} : \mathbf D^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor with right functor. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf D} } {-, R-}$ is a covariant functor.

title: Hom Bifunctor With Right Identity Functor is Hom Bifunctor
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} : \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ denote the identity functor. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {-, \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}-} : \mathbf C^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor with right functor $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$. Let $\map {\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {-, -} : \mathbf C^{\text{op} } \times \mathbf C \to \mathbf {Set}$ denote the hom bifunctor.

title: Homeomorphic Image of Local Basis is Local Basis
snippet: Let $T_\alpha = \struct{S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ and $T_\beta = \struct{S_\beta, \tau_\beta}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_\alpha \to T_\beta$ be a homeomorphism. Let $s \in S_\alpha$. Let $\BB$ be a local basis of $s$ in $T_\alpha$. Then: $\BB' = \set{ \phi \sqbrk B : B \in \BB}$ is a local basis of $\map \phi s$ in $T_\beta$

title: Homeomorphic Image of Meager Set is Meager
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homeomorphism. Let $A \subseteq X$ be meager in $X$. Then $f \sqbrk A$ is meager in $Y$.

title: Homeomorphic Image of Neighborhood Basis is Neighborhood Basis
snippet: Let $T_\alpha = \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ and $T_\beta = \struct {S_\beta, \tau_\beta}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_\alpha \to T_\beta$ be a homeomorphism. Let $s \in S_\alpha$. Let $\NN$ be a neighborhood basis of $s$ in $T_\alpha$. Then: $\NN' = \set {\phi \sqbrk N : N \in \NN}$ is a neighborhood basis of $\map \phi s$ in $T_\beta$.

title: Homeomorphic Image of Nowhere Dense Set is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a homeomorphism. Let $A$ be a nowhere dense subset of $X$. Then $f \sqbrk A$ is a nowhere dense subset of $Y$.

title: Homeomorphic Image of Sub-Basis is Sub-Basis
snippet: Let $T_\alpha = \struct{X_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}, T_\beta = \struct{X_\beta, \tau_\beta}$ be topological spaces. Let $\SS_\alpha \subseteq \tau_\alpha$ be a sub-basis for $\tau_\alpha$. Let $\phi: T_\alpha \to T_\beta$ be a homeomorphism. Let $\SS_\beta = \set{\phi \sqbrk S : S \in \SS_\alpha}$. Then: $\SS_\beta$ is a sub-basis for $\tau_\beta$

title: Homeomorphic Metric Spaces are not necessarily Isometric
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be homeomorphic. Then it is not necessarily the case that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are isometric.

title: Homeomorphic Non-Comparable Particular Point Topologies
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with at least two elements. Let $p, q \in S: p \ne q$. Let $\tau_p$ and $\tau_q$ be the particular point topologies on $S$ by $p$ and $q$ respectively. Then the topological spaces $T_p = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ and $T_q = \struct {S, \tau_q}$ are homeomorphic. However, $\tau_p$ and $\tau_q$ are not comparable.

title: Homeomorphic Topologies on Same Set may not be Identical
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ both be topologies on $S$ such that the topological spaces $\struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {S, \tau_2}$ are homeomorphic. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau_1} = \struct {S, \tau_2}$.

title: Homeomorphic Topology of Initial Topology is Initial Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {X_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}, \struct {X_\beta, \tau_\beta}$ be topological spaces. Let $\ds \family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds \family {f_i: X_\beta \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau_\beta$ be the initial topology on $X_\beta$ with respect to $\ds \family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $\phi : \struct {X_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} \to \struct {X_\beta, \tau_\beta}$ be a homeomorphism.

title: Homeomorphism Preserves Sobriety
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ be a sober space. Let $T_2 = \struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be a topological space. Let $f : T_1 \to T_2$ be a homeomorphism. Then: $T_2$ is a sober space.

title: Homeomorphism Preserves System of Open Neighborhoods
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f : T_1 \to T_2$ be a homeomorphism between $T_1$ and $T_2$. Let $f^\to : \powerset{S_1}\to \powerset{S_2}$ denote the direct image mapping of $f : S_1 \to S_2$. Then: $\forall x \in S_1 : f^\to \sqbrk {\map \UU x} = \map \UU {\map f x}$ where $\map \UU x$ and $\map \UU {\map f x}$ denote the systems of open neighborhoods of $x$ and $\map f x$ respectively.

title: Homeomorphism Relation is Equivalence
snippet: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $T_1 \sim T_2$ denote that $T_1$ and $T_2$ are homeomorphic. The relation $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Homeomorphism between Topological Spaces may not be Unique
snippet: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $f$ be a homeomorphism from $T_1$ to $T_2$. Then $f$ may not necessarily be unique.

title: Homeomorphism iff Image of Closure equals Closure of Image
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a bijection. Then $f$ is a homeomorphism : $\forall H \subseteq T_1: f \sqbrk {H^-} = \paren {f \sqbrk H}^-$ where $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Homeomorphism may Exist between Non-Comparable Topologies
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_1 = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces defined on the underlying set $S$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be non-comparable. Then it may possibly be the case that $T_1$ and $T_2$ are homeomorphic.

title: Homeomorphism of Metric Spaces is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1 \sim M_2$ denote that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic. The relation $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Homeomorphism yields Topologically Equivalent Metric
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be a homeomorphism. Let $d_3: A^2 \to \R$ be a mapping defined as: $\map {d_3} {x, y} := \map {d_2} {\map f x, \map f y}$ Then $d_3$ yields a metric on $M_1$ which is topologically equivalent to $d_1$.

title: Homogeneity of Space implies Conservation of Linear Momentum
snippet: Because space is homogeneous in an inertial frame of reference, linear momentum is conserved if the system is closed.

title: Homogeneous Cartesian Coordinates/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Homogeneous Cartesian Coordinates ==

title: Homogeneous Cartesian Coordinates represent Unique Finite Point
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the Cartesian plane. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point in $\CC$ which is not the point at infinity. Let $Z \in \R_{\ne 0}$ be fixed. Then $P$ can be expressed uniquely in homogeneous Cartesian coordinates as: $P = \tuple {X, Y, Z}$

title: Homogeneous Cyclotomic Polynomial is Symmetric
snippet: Let $n>1$ be a natural number. Let $\Phi_n(x,y)$ be the $n$th homogeneous cyclotomic polynomial. Then $\Phi_n(x,y) = \Phi_n(y,x)$, that is, $\Phi_n(x,y)$ is symmetric.

title: Homogeneous Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: This page gathers examples of homogeneous differential equations of the first order: $\map M {x, y} + \map N {x, y} \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0$ where both $M$ and $N$ are homogeneous functions of the same degree.

snippet: == Examples of Homogeneous Equations ==

title: Homogeneous Quadratic Equation for Straight Lines Parallel to those Passing through Origin
snippet: Let $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ represent $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane which are represented by a quadratic equation $E$ in two variables: $a x^2 + b y^2 + 2 h x y + 2 g x + 2 f y + c = 0$ Then $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ are parallel respectively to the $2$ straight lines through the origin represented by the homogeneous quadratic equation: $a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2$

title: Homogeneous Quadratic Equation representing Coincident Straight Lines
snippet: Let $E$ be a homogeneous quadratic equation in two variables: $E: \quad a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2$ Let $h^2 - a b = 0$. Then Then $E$ represents $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane which completely coincide:

title: Homogeneous Quadratic Equation representing Imaginary Straight Lines
snippet: Let $E$ be a homogeneous quadratic equation in two variables: $E: \quad a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2$ Let $h^2 - a b < 0$. Then Then $E$ represents a conjugate pair of imaginary straight lines in the Cartesian plane:

title: Homogeneous Quadratic Equation represents Two Straight Lines through Origin
snippet: Let $E$ be a homogeneous quadratic equation in two variables: $E: \quad a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2 = 0$ Then $E$ represents $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane: $y = \dfrac {h \pm \sqrt {h^2 - a b} } b x$

title: Homogeneous Simultaneous Linear Equations with More Unknowns than Equations
snippet: Let $\alpha_{ij}$ be elements of a field $F$, where $1 \le i \le m, 1 \le j \le n$. Let $n > m$. Then there exist $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in F$ not all zero, such that: $\ds \forall i: 1 \le i \le m: \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_{ij} x_j = 0$ where $0$ denotes the zero of $F$.

title: Homogeneous System has Zero Vector as Solution
snippet: Every homogeneous system of linear equations has the zero vector as a solution.

title: Homology Group/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Homology Groups ==

title: Homology Group is Group
snippet: The $p$th singular homology group of a space $X$ is a group.

title: Homomorphic Image of Cyclic Group is Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group with generator $g$. Let $H$ be a group. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a (group) homomorphism. Let $\Img G$ denote the homomorphic image of $G$ under $\phi$. Then $\Img G$ is a cyclic group with generator $\map \phi g$. That is: $\phi \sqbrk {\gen g} = \gen {\map \phi g}$

title: Homomorphic Image of Group Element is Coset
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group homomorphism. Let $\map \ker \phi$ be the kernel of $\phi$. Let $h \in H$. Then $\Preimg h$ is either the empty set or a coset of $\map \ker \phi$.

title: Homomorphic Image of Quotient Group under Epimorphism
snippet: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be groups whose identities are $e_{G_1}$ and $e_{G_2}$ respectively. Let $\phi: G_1 \to G_2$ be a group epimorphism. Let $K := \map \ker \phi$ be the kernel of $\phi$. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G_1$ such that $K \subseteq N$. Then: $\dfrac {G_1} N \cong \dfrac {G_2} {\map \phi N}$ where $\dfrac {G_1} N$ denotes the quotient group of $G_1$ by $N$.

title: Homomorphic Image of R-Module is R-Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be an $R$-algebraic structure. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a homomorphism. Then the homomorphic image of $\phi$ is an $R$-module.

title: Homomorphic Image of Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +_K, \times_K}$ be a division ring. Let $\struct {V, +_V, \circ_V}_K$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $\struct {W, +_W, \circ_W}_K$ be a $K$-algebraic structure. Let $\phi: V \to W$ be a homomorphism, that is, a linear transformation. Then the homomorphic image of $\phi$ is a $K$-vector space.

title: Homomorphism Preserves Subsemigroups
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $S'$ be a subsemigroup of $S$. Then $\phi \paren {S'}$ is a subsemigroup of $T$.

title: Homomorphism from Group of Cube Roots of Unity to Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {U_3, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of the complex cube roots of unity. Here, $U_3 = \set {1, \omega, \omega^2}$ where $\omega = e^{2 i \pi / 3}$. Let $\phi: U_3 \to U_3$ be defined as: $\forall z \in U_3: \map \phi z = \begin{cases} 1 & : z = 1 \\ \omega^2 & : z = \omega \\ \omega & : z = \omega^2 \end{cases}$ Then $\phi$ is a group homomorphism.

title: Homomorphism from Integers into Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the characteristic of $R$ be $p$. Let $g_a: \Z \to R$ be the mapping from the integers into $R$ defined as: $\forall n \in \Z:\forall a \in R: \map {g_a} n = n \cdot a$ where $\cdot$ denotes the multiple operation. Then the following hold:

title: Homomorphism from Reals to Circle Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $\struct {K, \times}$ be the circle group. Let $\phi: \struct {\R, +} \to \struct {K, \times}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map \phi x = e^{i x}$ Then $\phi$ is a (group) homomorphism.

title: Homomorphism of Chain Complexes induces Homomorphism of Homology
snippet: Let $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$ be chain complexes of abelian groups. Let $f: A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ be a homomorphism. Then for every $n$, $f$ induces a morphism $\map {H_n} {A_\bullet} \to \map {H_n} {B_\bullet}$ of homology groups.

title: Homomorphism of External Direct Products
snippet: Let: $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \circ}$ be the external direct product of two algebraic structures $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ $\struct {T_1 \times T_2, *}$ be the external direct product of two algebraic structures $\struct {T_1, *_1}$ and $\struct {T_2, *_2}$ $\phi_1$ be a homomorphism from $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ onto $\struct {T_1, *_1}$ $\phi_2$ be a homomorphism from $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ onto $\struct {T_2, *_2}$.

title: Homomorphism of Generated Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, \circ}$ be groups. Let $\phi: G \to H$ and $\psi: G \to H$ be homomorphisms. Let $\gen S = G$ be the group generated by $S$. Let: $\forall x \in S: \map \phi x = \map \psi x$ Then: $\phi = \psi$

title: Homomorphism of Power of Group Element
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, \ast}$ be groups. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a group homomorphism. Then: $\forall n \in \Z: \forall g \in G: \map \phi {g^n} = \paren {\map \phi g}^n$

title: Homomorphism of Powers
snippet: Let $\struct {T_1, \odot}$ and $\struct {T_2, \oplus}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {T_1, \odot} \to \struct {T_2, \oplus}$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism.

title: Homomorphism of Ring Subtraction
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Then: $\forall a, b \in R_1: \map \phi {a -_1 b} = \map \phi a -_2 \map \phi b$ where $a -_1 b$ denotes subtraction of $b$ from $a$.

title: Homomorphism on Induced Structure to Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \oplus}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $T^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Let $f$ and $g$ be homomorphisms from $S$ into $T$. Let $f \oplus' g$ be the pointwise operation on $T^S$ induced by $\oplus$. Then $f \oplus' g$ is a homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, \oplus}$.

title: Homomorphism to Group Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, *}$ be a group. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Then: $\map \phi {e_S} = e_T$

title: Homomorphism to Group Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, *}$ be a group. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $x^{-1}$ be an inverse of $x$ for $\circ$. Then $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse of $\map \phi x$ for $*$.

title: Homomorphism with Cancellable Codomain Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, *}$ have an identity $e_T$. Let every element of $\struct {T, *}$ be cancellable. Then $\map \phi {e_S}$ is the identity $e_T$.

title: Homomorphism with Identity Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, *}$ also have an identity $e_T = \map \phi {e_S}$. If $x^{-1}$ is an inverse of $x$ for $\circ$, then $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse of $\map \phi x$ for $*$. That is: $\map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$

title: Homotopic Chain Maps Induce Equal Maps on Homology
snippet: Let $A_\bullet$, $B_\bullet$ be chain complexes of abelian groups. Let $f, g: A_\bullet \to B_\bullet$ be chain maps which are homotopic. Then $f$ and $g$ induce equal maps on homology.

title: Homotopic Paths Implies Homotopic Composition
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $f_1, f_2, g_1, g_2: \left[{0 \,.\,.\, 1}\right] \to S$ be paths in $T$. Let $f_1$ be homotopic to $f_2$ and $g_1$ be homotopic to $g_2$. Then the concatenated paths $f_1 * g_1$ and $f_2 * g_2$ are homotopic.

title: Homotopic Paths have Same Endpoints
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $f, g: \closedint 0 1 \to X$ be paths. Let $f$ and $g$ be homotopic. Then $f$ and $g$ have the same endpoints. That is: $\map f 0 = \map g 0$ and $\map f 1 = \map g 1$.

title: Homotopy-Class of Curves in Complete Connected Riemannian Manifold contains Minimal Geodesic of Class
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a complete connected Riemannian manifold. Let $H_{p q}$ homotopy class of segments from $p \in M$ to $q \in M$. Let $\gamma_{p q}$ be a geodesic from $p \in M$ to $q \in M$ such that $\gamma_{p q} \in H_{p q}$. Let $y_{p q} \in H_{p q}$ be an admissible curve. Let $L_g$ be the Riemannian length. Then in every $H_{p q}$ there is a $\gamma_{pq}$ which is minimizing among all $y_{p q} \in H_{p q}$: $\forall p, q \in M : \exists \gamma_{pq} \in H_{p q} : \forall y_{p q} \in H_{p q} : \map {L_g} {\gamma_{p q} } \le \map {L_g} {y_{p q} }$

title: Homotopy Group is Group
snippet: The set of all homotopy classes of continuous mappings: $c: \closedint 0 1^n \to X$ satisfying: $\map c {\partial \closedint 0 1^n} = x_0$ in a space $X$ at a base point $x_0$, under the operation of concatenation on class members, forms a group. This group is called the $n$th homotopy group.

title: Homotopy Group is Homeomorphism Invariant
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be two topological spaces. Let $\phi: X \to Y$ be a homeomorphism. Let $x_0 \in X$, $y_0 \in Y$. Then for all $n \in \N$ the induced mapping: $\phi_* : \pi_n \left({X, x_0}\right) \to \pi_n \left({Y, y_0}\right):$ $\left[{\!\left[{\, c \,}\right]\!}\right] \mapsto \left[{\!\left[{\, \phi \circ c \,}\right]\!}\right]$ is an isomorphism, where $\pi_n$ denotes the $n$th homotopy group.

title: Honsberger's Identity
snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{>0}: F_{m + n} = F_{m - 1} F_n + F_m F_{n + 1}$

title: Hooke's Law
snippet: == Physical Law == Hooke's Law applies to an ideal spring: $\mathbf F = -k \mathbf x$ where: $\mathbf F$ is the force caused by a displacement $\mathbf x$ $k$ is the spring force constant. The negative sign indicates that the force pulls in the opposite direction to that of the displacement imposed. The strain is proportional to the stress.

title: Hopf-Rinow Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a connected Riemannian manifold. Then $M$ is metrically complete it is geodesically complete.

title: Horizontal Point of Inflection is Stationary Point
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is differentiable on an interval $\Bbb I \subseteq \R$. Let $\xi \in \Bbb I$ be such that $\xi$ has a point of inflection at $\xi$ such that the tangent to $f$ at $\xi$ is parallel to the $x$-axis. Then $\xi$ is a stationary point.

title: Horizontal Section of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq X$ and $B \subseteq Y$, so that $A \times B \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\paren {A \times B}^y = \begin{cases}A & y \in B \\ \O & y \not \in B\end{cases}$ where $\paren {A \times B}^y$ is a horizontal section of $A \times B$.

title: Horizontal Section of Characteristic Function is Characteristic Function of Horizontal Section
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E \subseteq X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\paren {\chi_E}^y = \chi_{E^y}$ where: $E^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E$ $\chi_E$ and $\chi_{E^y}$ are the characteristic functions of $E$ and $E^y$ as subsets of $X \times Y$ respectively $\paren {\chi_E}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal function of $\chi_E$.

title: Horizontal Section of Continuous Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $T$ be topological spaces. Equip the Cartesian product $X \times Y$ with the product topology. Let $f : X \times Y \to T$ be a continuous mapping. Let $y \in Y$. Then the $y$-horizontal section $f^y : X \to T$ is continuous.

title: Horizontal Section of Empty Set
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\O^y = \O$ where $\O$ is the empty set and $\O^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $\O$.

title: Horizontal Section of Linear Combination of Functions is Linear Combination of Horizontal Sections
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ be functions. Let $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n$ be real numbers. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_k f_k}^y = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_k \paren {f_k}^y$ where $f^y$ denotes the $y$-horizontal section of the function $f$.

title: Horizontal Section of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $f : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$-measurable function where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $f^y$ is $\Sigma_X$-measurable where $f^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $f$.

title: Horizontal Section of Measurable Set is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $E \in \Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $E^y \in \Sigma_X$ where $E^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E$.

title: Horizontal Section of Simple Function is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $\struct {X \times Y, \Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y}$ be the product measurable space of $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$. Let $f : X \times Y \to \R$ be a simple function. Let $y \in Y$. Then $f^y : X \to \R$ is a simple function, where $f^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $f$.

title: Horizontal Section preserves Increasing Sequences of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an increasing sequence of real-valued functions with $f_i : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ for each $i$. Let $y \in Y$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\paren {f_n}^y}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing, where $\paren {f_n}^y$ denotes the $y$-horizontal section of $f_n$.

title: Horizontal Section preserves Increasing Sequences of Sets
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sequence {A_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an increasing sequence in $X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\sequence {\paren {A_n}^y}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is an increasing sequence.

title: Horizontal Section preserves Pointwise Limits of Sequences of Functions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $f : X \times Y \to \overline \R$ be a function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of functions converging pointwise to $f$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\paren {f_n}^y \to f^y$ pointwise, where: $\paren {f_n}^y$ denotes the $y$-horizontal section of $f_n$ $f^y$ denotes the $y$-horizontal section of $f$.

title: Horizontal Section preserves Subsets
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq B$ be subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $A^y \subseteq B^y$ where $A^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $A$ and $B^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $B$.

title: Hyperbolic Cosine Function is Even

title: Hyperbolic Cosine in terms of Cosine

title: Hyperbolic Cotangent Function is Odd

title: Hyperbolic Cotangent in terms of Cotangent
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\coth z = -\cot \paren {i z}$ where: $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function $\coth$ denotes the hyperbolic cotangent $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Hyperbolic Secant Function is Even
snippet: Let $\sech: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic secant function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\sech$ is even: $\map \sech {-x} = \sech x$

title: Hyperbolic Secant in terms of Secant
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\sech z = \sec \paren {i z}$ where: $\sec$ denotes the secant function $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Hyperbolic Secant of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\sech \paren {a + b i} = \dfrac {\cosh a \cos b - i \sinh a \sin b} {\cosh^2 a \cos^2 b + \sinh^2 a \sin^2 b}$ where: $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant function. $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

title: Hyperbolic Sine Function in terms of Hypergeometric Function

title: Hyperbolic Sine Function is Odd
snippet: Let $\sinh: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic sine function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\sinh$ is odd: $\map \sinh {-x} = -\sinh x$

title: Hyperbolic Sine in terms of Sine
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \sinh z = \map \sin {i z}$ where: $\sin$ denotes the complex sine $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Hyperbolic Sine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\sinh \paren {a + b i} = \sinh a \cos b + i \cosh a \sin b$ where: $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function.

title: Hyperbolic Sine of Sum
snippet: $\map \sinh {a + b} = \sinh a \cosh b + \cosh a \sinh b$ where $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine and $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine.

title: Hyperbolic Sine of Zero is Zero

title: Hyperbolic Tangent Function is Odd

title: Hypergeometric Distribution approaches Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable which obeys a hypergeometric distribution over a population consisting of $M$ satisfactory units and $N$ unsatisfactory units: $\map \Pr {X = r} = \dfrac {\dbinom M r \dbinom N {n - r} } {\dbinom {M + N} r}$ where: $n$ is the number of trials $r$ is the number of satisfactory units drawn from the population without replacement. When $M$ and $N$ are large compared to $n$, $X$ approaches the binomial distribution $\Binomial n p$ where: $p = \dfrac M {M + N}$

Let $p, q \in \R_{>0}$ such that $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$. {{improve|the assumption should read $p,q\in\R_{>0}\cup\set{+\infty}$.Suggestion: make a page for defining $p,q$ as satisfying this relation, including the pair $\tuple{1,\infty}$}} Let $f \in \map {\LL^p} \mu, f: X \to \R$, and $g \in \map {\LL^q} \mu, g: X \to \R$, where $\LL$ denotes Lebesgue space.

title: Hölder Mean for Exponent -1 is Harmonic Mean
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be real numbers. For $p \in \R_{\ne 0}$, let $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ denote the Hölder mean with exponent $p$ of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $\map {M_{-1} } {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} = \dfrac 1 {\dfrac 1 n \paren {\dfrac 1 {x_1} + \dfrac 1 {x_2} + \cdots + \dfrac 1 {x_n} } }$ which is the harmonic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.

title: Hölder Mean for Exponent 1 is Arithmetic Mean
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be real numbers. For $p \in \R_{\ne 0}$, let $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ denote the Hölder mean with exponent $p$ of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $\map {M_1} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} = \dfrac {x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_n} n$ which is the arithmetic mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.

title: Ideal Contained in Finite Union of Prime Ideals
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak p_1, \ldots, \mathfrak p_n$ be prime ideals. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n \mathfrak p_i$ be an ideal contained in their union. Then $\mathfrak a \subseteq \mathfrak p_i$ for some $i \in \{1, \ldots, n\}$.

title: Ideal Contains Extension of Contraction
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $f : A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\mathfrak b \subseteq B$ be an ideal. Then $\mathfrak b$ contains the extension of its contraction by $f$: $\mathfrak b^{ce} \subseteq \mathfrak b$

title: Ideal Quotient is Ideal
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a, \mathfrak b$ be ideals of $R$. Then the ideal quotient $\ideal {\mathfrak a : \mathfrak b}$ is indeed an ideal.

title: Ideal and Zero Locus are Order Reversing
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \ge 0$ be a natural number. Let $P := k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Then, the associate ideal and zero-locus are inclusion reversing. That is: $(1): \quad$ if: $X \subseteq Y \subseteq k^n$ then: $\map I Y \subseteq \map I X$ $(2): \quad$ if: $I \subseteq J \subseteq k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ are ideals of $k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ then: $\map Z J \subseteq \map Z I$

title: Ideal induced by Congruence Relation defines that Congruence
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\EE$ be a congruence relation on $R$. Let $J = \eqclass {0_R} \EE$ be the ideal induced by $\EE$. Then the equivalence defined by the coset space $\struct {R, +} / \struct {J, +}$ is $\EE$ itself.

title: Ideal induces Congruence Relation on Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$ Then $J$ induces a congruence relation $\EE_J$ on $R$ such that $\struct {R / J, +, \circ}$ is a quotient ring.

title: Ideal is Additive Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Then $\left({J, +}\right)$ is a normal subgroup of $\left({R, +}\right)$.

title: Ideal is Bimodule over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $J \subseteq R$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\circ_l : R \times J \to J$ be the restriction of $\times$ to $R \times J$. Let $\circ_r : J \times R \to J$ be the restriction of $\times$ to $J \times R$. Then $\struct {J, +, \circ_l, \circ_r}$ is a bimodule over $\struct {R, +, \times}$.

title: Ideal is Contained in Contraction of Extension
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $f : A \to B$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq A$ be an ideal. Then $\mathfrak a$ is contained in the contraction of its extension by $f$: $\mathfrak a \subseteq \mathfrak a^{ec}$

title: Ideal is Dual of Filter (Order Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. The following are dual statements: $T$ is a filter of $\struct {S, \preceq}$ $T$ is an ideal of $\struct {S, \preceq}$

title: Ideal is Filter in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is ideal in $P$ $X$ is filter in $P^{-1}$ where $P^{-1} = \struct {S, \succeq}$ denotes the dual of $P$.

title: Ideal is Subring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring, and let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Then $J$ is a subring of $R$.

title: Ideal is Unit Ideal iff Includes Unity
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a$ be an ideal of $A$. Then: $\mathfrak a = A \iff 1 \in \mathfrak a$ where $1$ denotes the unity of $A$.

title: Ideal of Algebra over Field Embeds into Unitization as Ideal
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$ that is not unital. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Let: $I_0 = \set {\tuple {x, 0_K} : x \in I}$ Then $I_0$ is an ideal of $A_+$.

title: Ideal of External Direct Sum of Rings
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \ldots, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be rings. Let $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ be their direct product. For each $k \in \closedint 1 n$, let: ${R_k}' = \set {\tuple {x_1, \ldots, x_n} \in R: \forall j \ne k: x_j = 0}$ Then: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: {R_k}'$ is an ideal of $R$.

title: Ideal of Ring/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ideals of Rings ==

title: Ideal of Ring is Contained in Radical
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq A$ be an ideal. Then $\mathfrak a$ is contained in its radical: $\mathfrak a \subseteq \operatorname{Rad} \left({\mathfrak a}\right)$

title: Ideal of Ring of Polynomials over Field has Unique Monic Polynomial forming Principal Ideal
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Let $F \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $F$. Let $J$ be a non-null ideal of $F \sqbrk X$. Then there exists exactly one monic polynomial $f \in F \sqbrk X$ such that: $J = \ideal f$ where $\ideal f$ is the principal ideal generated by $f$ in $F \sqbrk X$.

title: Ideal of Unit is Whole Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. If $J$ contains a unit of $R$, then $J = R$.

title: Ideal of Unital Algebra is Modular
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A$ be a unital $R$-algebra. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Then $I$ is a modular ideal of $A$.

title: Ideals Containing Ideal Form Lattice
snippet: Let $J$ be an ideal of a ring $R$. Let $\mathbb L_J$ be the set of all ideals of $R$ which contain $J$. Then the ordered set $\struct {\mathbb L_J, \subseteq}$ is a lattice.

title: Ideals Containing Ideal Isomorphic to Quotient Ring
snippet: Let $J$ be an ideal of a ring $R$. Let $\mathbb L_J$ be the set of all ideals of $R$ which contain $J$. Let the ordered set $\struct {\map {\mathbb L} {R / J}, \subseteq}$ be the set of all ideals of $R / J$. Let the mapping $\Phi_J: \struct {\mathbb L_J, \subseteq} \to \struct {\map {\mathbb L} {R / J}, \subseteq}$ be defined as: $\forall a \in \mathbb L_J: \map {\Phi_J} a = \map {q_J} a$ where $q_J: a \to a / J$ is the quotient epimorphism from $a$ to $a / J$ from the definition of quotient ring. Then $\Phi_J$ is an isomorphism.

title: Ideals are Continuous Lattice Subframe of Power Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $I = \paren {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set where $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L$ denotes the set of all ideals in $L$, $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L \times \map {\operatorname{Ids} } L}$ Let $P = \struct {\powerset S, \precsim'}$ be an inclusion ordered set where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$, $\mathord \precsim' = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\powerset S \times \powerset S}$ Then $I$ is continuous lattice…

title: Ideals equal Filters in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be an ordered set. Let $L_2 = \struct {S, \preceq_2}$ be a dual ordered set of $L_1$. Then $\map {\mathit {Ids} } {L_1} = \map {\mathit {Filt} } {L_2}$ where $\map {\mathit {Filt} } {L_2}$ denotes the set of all filters of $L_2$ $\map {\mathit {Ids} } {L_1}$ denotes the set of all ideals of $L_1$.

title: Ideals form Algebraic Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $I = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set where $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L$ denotes the set of all ideals in $L$ $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L \times \map {\operatorname{Ids} } L}$ Then $I$ is an algebraic lattice.

title: Ideals form Arithmetic Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below lattice. Let $I = \struct {\map {\mathit {Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an inclusion ordered set, where: $\map {\mathit {Ids} } L$ denotes the set of all ideals in $L$ $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\map {\mathit {Ids} } L \times \map {\mathit {Ids} } L}$ Then $I$ is an arithmetic lattice.

title: Ideals form Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\II = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L, \subseteq}$ be an inclusion ordered set, where $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L$ denotes the set of all ideals in $L$. Then $\II$ is complete lattice.

title: Ideals of Division Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a division ring whose zero is $0_R$. The only ideals of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are $\set {0_R}$ and $R$ itself. That is, $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ has no non-null proper ideals.

title: Ideals of Field
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ is a field the only ideals of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ and $\set {0_R}$.

title: Ideals of P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers for some prime $p$. Then the ideals of $\Z_p$ are the principal ideals: $\text a) \quad \set 0$ $\text b) \quad \forall k \in \N: p^k \Z_p$

title: Ideals of Ring of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ denote the ring of integers modulo $m$. The ideals of $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ are of the form: $d \Z / m \Z$ where $d$ is a divisor of $m$.

title: Ideals with Coprime Radicals are Coprime
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a, \mathfrak b \subseteq A$ be ideals. Let their radicals be coprime: $\map \Rad {\mathfrak a} + \map \Rad {\mathfrak b} = \ideal 1$ Then $\mathfrak a$ and $\mathfrak b$ are coprime: $\mathfrak a + \mathfrak b = \ideal 1$

title: Idempotent Element/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Idempotent Elements ==

title: Idempotent Elements for Integer Multiplication
snippet: There are exactly two integers which are idempotent with respect to multiplication: $0 \times 0 = 0$ $1 \times 1 = 1$

title: Idempotent Elements form Submonoid of Commutative Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $e \in S$ be the identity element of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $I$ be the set of all elements of $S$ that are idempotent under $\circ$. That is: $I = \set {x \in S: x \circ x = x}$ Then $\struct {I, \circ}$ is a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$ with identity $e$.

title: Idempotent Elements form Subsemigroup of Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup such that $\circ$ is commutative. Let $I$ be the set of all elements of $S$ that are idempotent under $\circ$. That is: $I = \set {x \in S: x \circ x = x}$ Then $\struct {I, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Idempotent Elements of Ring with No Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null ring with no (proper) zero divisors. Let $x \in R$. Then: $x \circ x = x \iff x \in \set {0_R, 1_R}$ That is, the only elements of $\struct {R, \circ}$ that are idempotent are zero and unity.

title: Idempotent Magma Element forms Singleton Submagma
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $x \in S$ be an idempotent element of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\struct {\set x, \circ}$ is a submagma of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Idempotent Non-Trivial Quasigroup is Not a Loop
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an idempotent quasigroup whose underlying set $S$ comprises more than one element. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is not an algebra loop, that is, it has no identity element.

title: Idempotent Ring has Characteristic Two
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be an idempotent non-null ring. Denote with $0_R$ the zero of $R$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ has characteristic $2$.

title: Idempotent Ring is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be an idempotent ring. Denote with $0_R$ the zero of $R$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ is a commutative ring.

title: Idempotent Semigroup/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Idempotent Semigroups ==

title: Identification Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then the identification mapping $f$ is continuous.

title: Identification Topology equals Quotient Topology on Induced Equivalence
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a surjective mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$: $\tau_2 = \set {V \subseteq S_2 : f^{-1} \sqbrk V \in \tau_1}$ Let $\RR_f \subseteq S_1 \times S_1$ be the equivalence on $S_1$ induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $q_{\RR_f}$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$.

title: Identification Topology is Finest Topology for Mapping to be Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 := \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Let $T_2 := \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be the resulting topological space. Then $\tau_2$ is the finest topology on $S_2$ such that $f: T_1 \to T_2$ is continuous.

title: Identification Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then $\tau_2$ is a topology on $S_2$.

title: Identities of Boolean Algebra are also Zeroes
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \neg}$ be a Boolean algebra, defined as in Definition 1. Let the identity for $\vee$ be $\bot$ and the identity for $\wedge$ be $\top$. Then: That is: $\bot$ is a zero element for $\wedge$ $\top$ is a zero element for $\vee$.

title: Identity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Identity Elements ==

title: Identity (Equation)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Identities in context of Equations ==

title: Identity Element for Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Then: $\alpha + 0^* = \alpha$ where $+$ denotes the operation of addition of cuts.

title: Identity Element for Dirichlet Convolution
snippet: Let $f$ be an arithmetic function. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution. Let $\iota$ be the identity arithmetic function. Then: $\iota * f = f$

title: Identity Element for Power Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma whose underlying set $S$ is non-empty. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then: a subset $J$ of $S$ is an identity element of $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ there exists an identity element $e$ of $\struct {S, \circ}$, such that $J = \set e$.

title: Identity Element in Unital *-Algebra is Hermitian
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a unital $\ast$-algebra. Let ${\mathbf 1}_A$ be the identity element of $A$. Then we have: ${\mathbf 1}_A^\ast = {\mathbf 1}_A$

title: Identity Element is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $e \in S$ be an identity with respect to $\circ$. Then $e$ is idempotent under $\circ$.

title: Identity Element is Order Unit on Set of Hermitian Elements of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le$ be the canonical preordering on $A$. Let $A_{\mathbf {SA}}$ be the set of Hermitian elements of $A$. Then ${\mathbf 1}_A$ is an order unit for $\tuple {A_{\mathbf{SA}}, \le}$.

title: Identity Element of Addition on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the identity element of addition is zero ($0$).

title: Identity Element of Multiplication on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the identity element of multiplication is one ($1$).

title: Identity Element of Natural Number Addition is Zero
snippet: The identity element for the natural numbers under addition is zero ($0$): $\forall n \in \N: 0 + n = n$

title: Identity Element of Natural Number Multiplication is One
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $1$ be the element one of $\N$. Then $1$ is the identity element of multiplication: $\forall n \in \N: n \times 1 = n = 1 \times n$

title: Identity Elements occupy Diagonal of Cayley Table in Inverse Row Form
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a finite group. Let $\CC$ be a Cayley table for $\struct {G, \circ}$ presented in inverse row form. Then all the entries in the main diagonal of $\CC$ are instances of the identity element.

title: Identity Function is Completely Multiplicative
snippet: Let $I_{\Z_{>0}}: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the identity function: $\forall n \in \Z_{>0}: I_{\Z_{>0}} \left({n}\right) = n$ Then $I_{\Z_{>0}}$ is completely multiplicative. {{Questionable|Completely multiplicativity is defined for fields but $\Z_{>0}$ is not a field}}

title: Identity Function is Computable Real Function
snippet: Let $I_\R : \R \to \R$ denote the identity function on $\R$. Then $I_\R$ is a computable real function.

title: Identity Function is Computably Uniformly Continuous Real Function
snippet: Let $I_\R : \R \to \R$ denote the identity function on $\R$. Then, $I_\R$ is a computably uniformly continuous real function.

title: Identity Function is Odd Function
snippet: Let $I_\R: \R \to \R$ denote the identity function on $\R$. Then $I_\R$ is an odd function.

title: Identity Function is Sequentially Computable Real Function
snippet: Let $I_\R : \R \to \R$ denote the identity function on $\R$. Then $I_\R$ is a sequentially computable real function.

title: Identity Functor is Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}: \mathbf C \to \mathbf C$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ is a functor.

title: Identity Functor is Left Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a functor, and let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D}$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf D$. Then the composite functor $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D} F$ satisfies: $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf D} F = F$

title: Identity Functor is Right Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a functor, and let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ be the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Then the composite functor $F \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ satisfies: $F \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} = F$

title: Identity Mapping between Metrics separated by Scale Factor is Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$. Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be such that: $\forall x, y \in A: \map {d_2} {x, y} \le K \map {d_2} {x, y}$ Let $I_A: A \to A$ be the identity mapping on $A$. Then $I_A$ is continuous from $M_1$ to $M_2$.

title: Identity Mapping forms Galois Connection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered sets. Let $\operatorname{id}_S : S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then: $\tuple {\operatorname{id}_S, \operatorname{id}_S}$ is a Galois connection.

title: Identity Mapping is Automorphism
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ on the algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an automorphism. Its image is $S$.

title: Identity Mapping is Bijection
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ on the set $S$ is a bijection.

title: Identity Mapping is Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{A, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a complete lattice homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

title: Identity Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {I_S} x = x$ is a continuous mapping.

title: Identity Mapping is Frame Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\operatorname{id}_S$ denote the identity mapping on $S$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_S$ is a frame homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

title: Identity Mapping is Frame Isomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $\operatorname{id}_S$ denote the identity mapping on $S$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_S$ is a frame isomorphism of $L$ to $L$

title: Identity Mapping is Group Endomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Then $I_G: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {G, \circ}$ is a group endomorphism.

title: Identity Mapping is Hermitian
snippet: The identity mapping is Hermitian.

title: Identity Mapping is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_T: T \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in T: \map {I_T} x = x$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Identity Mapping is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $I_S: S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then $I_S$ is idempotent: $I_S \circ I_S = I_S$

title: Identity Mapping is Injection
snippet: On any set $S$, the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is an injection.

title: Identity Mapping is Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L = \struct{A, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a lattice homomorphism of $L$ to $L$

title: Identity Mapping is Left Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $I_T \circ f = f$ where $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

title: Identity Mapping is Localic Mapping
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\operatorname{id}_S : S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_S : L \to L$ is a localic mapping.

title: Identity Mapping is Normal
snippet: The identity mapping is normal.

title: Identity Mapping is Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. The identity mapping $I_S$ is an order isomorphism from $\struct {S, \preceq}$ to itself.

title: Identity Mapping is Ordered Ring Automorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, +, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered ring. Then the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is an ordered ring automorphism.

title: Identity Mapping is Permutation
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ on the set $S$ is a permutation.

title: Identity Mapping is Relation Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Then the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is a relation isomorphism from $\struct {S, \RR}$ to itself.

title: Identity Mapping is Right Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $f \circ I_S = f$ where $I_S$ is the identity mapping on $S$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

title: Identity Mapping is Semilattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $S = \struct{A, \circ}$ be a semilattice. Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a semilattice homomorphism of $S$ to $S$

title: Identity Mapping is Surjection
snippet: On any set $S$, the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is a surjection.

title: Identity Mapping on Metric Space is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. The identity mapping $I_A: M \to M$ defined as: $\forall x \in A: \map {I_A} x = x$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Identity Mapping on Normed Vector Space is Bounded Linear Operator
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $I : X 	o X$ be the identity mapping on $X$. Then $I$ is a bounded linear operator. Further: Let $\map B X$, be the space of bounded linear operators on $X$. Then: $
orm I_{\map B X} = 1$ where $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X}$ denotes the norm on $\map B X$.

title: Identity Mapping on Real Vector Space from Chebyshev to Euclidean Metric is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Let $I: \R^n \to \R^n$ be the identity mapping from $\R^n$ to itself. Then the mapping: $I: \struct {\R^n, d_\infty} \to \struct {\R^n, d_2}$ is $\tuple {d_\infty, d_2}$-continuous.

title: Identity Mapping on Real Vector Space from Euclidean to Chebyshev Distance is Continuous
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Let $I: \R^n \to \R^n$ be the identity mapping from $\R^n$ to itself. Then the mapping: $I: \struct {\R^n, d_2} \to \struct {\R^n, d_\infty}$ is $\tuple {d_2, d_\infty}$-continuous.

title: Identity Mapping on Symmetric Group is Even Permutation
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $e \in S_n$ be the identity permutation on $S_n$. Then $e$ is an even permutation on $S_n$.

title: Identity Mapping to Coarser Topology is Continuous
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on $S$. That is, let $T_1 = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $I_S: \struct {S, \tau_1} \to \struct {S, \tau_2}$ denote the identity mapping on $S$: $\forall x \in S: \map {I_S} x = x$ Then: $I_S: T_1 \to T_2$ is a continuous mapping $\tau_2$ is coarser than $\tau_1$.

title: Identity Mapping to Expansion is Closed
snippet: Let $S$ be a set on which $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ are topologies such that: $\tau_1 \subseteq \tau_2$ that is, such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. Let $I_S: \struct {S, \tau_1} \to \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be the identity mapping from $\struct {S, \tau_1}$ to $\struct {S, \tau_2}$. Then $I_S$ is closed.

title: Identity Matrix from Upper Triangular Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_{m n}$ be an upper triangular matrix of order $m \times n$ with no zero diagonal elements. Let $k = \min \set {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf A$ can be transformed into a matrix such that the first $k$ rows and columns form the unit matrix of order $k$.

title: Identity Matrix is Permutation Matrix
snippet: An identity matrix is an example of a permutation matrix.

title: Identity Minus Compact Linear Operator on Banach Space has Index Zero
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $I : X \to X$ be the identity mapping. Let $C : X \to X$ be a compact linear operator. Then $I - C$ is a Fredholm operator with the index: $\map {\mathrm{ind} } {I - C} = 0$

title: Identity Morphism is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_X : X \to X$ denote the identity morphism of $X$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_X \circ \operatorname{id}_X = \operatorname{id}_X$

title: Identity Morphism is Initial Object in Coslice Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory, and let $C \in \mathbf C_0$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C$ be the identity morphism for $C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_C$ is an initial object in the coslice category $C / \mathbf C$.

title: Identity Morphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $X$ be an object in $\mathbf C$. Then: the identity morphism $\operatorname{id}_X$ of $X$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf C$.

title: Identity Morphism is Terminal Object in Slice Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory, and let $C \in \mathbf C_0$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_C: C \to C$ be the identity morphism for $C$. Then $\operatorname{id}_C$ is a terminal object in the slice category $\mathbf C \mathop / C$.

title: Identity Morphism is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Then the identity morphism $\operatorname{id}_X : X \to X$ is unique.

title: Identity Morphism of Coproduct
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$, and let $C \sqcup D$ be a binary coproduct for $C$ and $D$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_{\paren {C \mathop \sqcup D} } = \operatorname{id}_C \sqcup \operatorname{id}_D$ where $\operatorname{id}$ denotes an identity morphism, and $\sqcup$ signifies a coproduct of morphisms.

title: Identity Morphism of Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$, and let $C \times D$ be a binary product for $C$ and $D$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_{\paren {C \mathop \times D} } = \operatorname{id}_C \times \operatorname{id}_D$ where $\operatorname{id}$ denotes an identity morphism, and $\times$ signifies a product of morphisms.

title: Identity Natural Transformation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F$ denote the identity natural transformation on $F$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_F \circ \operatorname{id}_F = \operatorname{id}_F$ where $\operatorname{id}_F \circ \operatorname{id}_F$ denotes the vertical composition of $\operatorname{id}_F$ with itself.

title: Identity Natural Transformation is Left Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation from $F$ to $G$. Let $\operatorname{id}_G$ denote the identity natural transformation on $G$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_G \mathop \circ \eta = \eta$ where $\operatorname{id}_G \mathop \circ \eta$ denotes the verictal composition of $\eta$ and $\operatorname{id}_G$.

title: Identity Natural Transformation is Natural Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F: F \to F$ denote the identity natural transformation Then: $\operatorname{id}_F$ is a natural isomorphism

title: Identity Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be a covariant functor. Let $\operatorname{id}_F: F \to F$ denote the identity natural transformation Then: $\operatorname{id}_F$ is a natural transformation.

title: Identity Natural Transformation is Right Identity
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation from $F$ to $G$. Let $\operatorname{id}_F$ denote the identity natural transformation on $F$. Then: $\eta \circ \operatorname{id}_F = \eta$

title: Identity Operator is Compact iff Finite-Dimensional Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $I : X \to X$ be the identity operator. Then $I$ is compact $X$ is finite-dimensional.

title: Identity Permutation is Disjoint from All
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $e \in S_n$ be the identity permutation on $S_n$. Then $e$ is disjoint from every permutation $\pi$ on $S_n$ (including itself).

title: Identity Property in Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $s \in S$ be such that: $\forall a \in S: \exists x, y \in S: s \circ x = a = y \circ s$ Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ has an identity.

title: Identity Theorem
snippet: Let $U$ be an open connected subset of the complex plane $\C$. Let $f$ and $g$ be complex functions whose domain is $U$. Let $S = \set {z \in U: \map f z = \map g z}$. Let $f$ and $g$ be analytic on $U$. Let $S$ have a limit point in $U$. Then: $\forall z \in U: \map f z = \map g z$

title: Identity is Only Group Element of Order 1
snippet: In every group, the identity, and only the identity, has order $1$.

title: Identity is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure that has an identity element $e \in S$. Then $e$ is unique.

title: Identity is in Kernel of Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $e_G$ and $e_H$ be the identity elements of $G$ and $H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a (group) homomorphism from $G$ to $H$. Then: $e_G \in \map \ker \phi$ where $\map \ker \phi$ is the kernel of $\phi$.

title: Identity is of Exponential Order Epsilon
snippet: Let $I_\R: t \mapsto t$ be the identity mapping on $\R_{\ge 0}$. Then $I_\R$ is of exponential order $\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small in magnitude.

title: Identity is only Idempotent Cancellable Element
snippet: Let $e_S$ be the identity of an algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $e_S$ is the only cancellable element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ that is idempotent.

title: Identity is only Idempotent Element in Group
snippet: Every group has exactly one idempotent element: the identity.

title: Identity of Affine Group of One Dimension
snippet: Let $\map {\mathrm {Af}_1} \R$ denote the $1$-dimensional affine group on $\R$. Then $\map {\mathrm {Af}_1} \R$ has $f_{1, 0}$ as an identity element.

title: Identity of Algebraic Structure is Preserved in Substructure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure with identity $e$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a algebraic substructure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. That is, let $T \subseteq S$. Let $e \in T$. Then $e$ is an identity of $\struct {T, \circ}$.

title: Identity of Cancellable Monoid is Identity of Submonoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid, all of whose elements are cancellable. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the identity of $\struct {T, \circ}$ is the same element as the identity of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Identity of Cardinal Product is One
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a cardinal. Then: $\bsone \mathbf a = \mathbf a$ where $\bsone \mathbf a$ denotes the product of the (cardinal) one and $\mathbf a$. That is, $\bsone$ is the identity element of the product operation on cardinals.

title: Identity of Cardinal Sum is Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a cardinal. Then: $\mathbf a + \mathbf 0 = \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a + \mathbf 0$ denotes the sum of the zero cardinal and $\mathbf a$. That is, $\mathbf 0$ is the identity element of the sum operation on cardinals.

title: Identity of Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of the two groups $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$. Let $e_G$ be the identity for $\struct {G, \circ_1}$. Let $e_H$ be the identity for $\struct {H, \circ_2}$. Then $\tuple {e_G, e_H}$ is the identity for $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$.

title: Identity of Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which has an identity element $e \in G$. Then $e$ is unique.

title: Identity of Group is in Center
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $e$ be the identity of $G$. Then $e$ is in the center of $G$: $e \in \map Z G$
