title: Inconsistent Proof System has no Model
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr P$ be a proof system for $\LL$ which is inconsistent. Then $\mathscr P$ has no model.

title: Increasing Alternating Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n \paren {-1}^{n + 1} j \binom n j = 0$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is: $1 \dbinom n 1 - 2 \dbinom n 2 + 3 \dbinom n 3 - \cdots + \paren {-1}^{n + 1} n \dbinom n n = 0$

title: Increasing Mapping Preserves Lower Bounds
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$, $L' = \left({S', \preceq'}\right)$ be ordered sets. Let $f:S \to S'$ be an increasing mapping. Let $x \in S$, $X \subseteq S$ such that $x$ is lower bound for $X$. Then $f \left({x}\right)$ is lower bound for $f \left[{X}\right]$.

title: Increasing Mapping Preserves Upper Bounds
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$, $L' = \left({S', \preceq'}\right)$ be ordered sets. Let $f:S \to S'$ be an increasing mapping. Let $x \in S$, $X \subseteq S$ such that $x$ is upper bound for $X$. Then $f\left({x}\right)$ is upper bound for $f\left[{X}\right]$.

title: Increasing Mappings Satisfying Inclusion in Lower Closure is Isomorphic to Auxiliary Relations
snippet: Let $R = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R$ be the set of all ideals in $R$. Let $L = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq\restriction_{\map {\operatorname{Ids} } R \times \map {\operatorname{Ids} } R}$. Let $M = \struct {F, \preccurlyeq}$ be the ordered set of increasing mappings $g:S \to \map {\operatorname{Ids} } R$ satisfying $\forall x \in S: \map g x \subseteq x^\preceq$. Let $\map {\operatorname{Aux} } R$ be the set of all auxiliary relations on $S$.

title: Increasing Martingale Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a probability space. Let $f$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Given sub-$\sigma$-algebra $\CC \subseteq \Sigma$, let $\expect {f \mid \CC}$ denote the conditional expectation of $f$ on $\CC$. Let $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a filtration of $\Sigma$. Let $\FF_\infty$ be the limit of $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \expect {f \mid \FF_n} = \expect {f \mid \FF_\infty}$ holds in $L^1$ norm, and $\mu$-almost surely.

title: Increasing Real Function has Countably Many Discontinuities
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an increasing real function. Then $f$ has at most countably many discontinuities.

title: Increasing Real Sequence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Increasing Real Sequence ==

title: Increasing Second Argument of Ackermann-Péter Function is Not Greater than Increasing First Argument
snippet: For all $x, y \in \N$: $\map A {x + 1, y} \ge \map A {x, y + 1}$ where $A$ is the Ackermann-Péter function.

title: Increasing Sequence in Ordered Set Terminates iff Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {P, \le}$ be an ordered set. $(1): \quad$ Every increasing sequence $x_1 \le x_2 \le x_3 \le \cdots$ with $x_i \in P$ eventually terminates: there is $n \in \N$ such that $x_n = x_{n + 1} = \cdots$. $(2): \quad$ Every non-empty subset of $P$ has a maximal element.

title: Increasing Sequence of Sets forms Nest
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be an increasing sequence of sets: $\forall k \in \N: S_k \subseteq S_{k + 1}$ Let $c = \set {a_1, a_1, \ldots, a_n, a_{n + 1}, \ldots}$ be the class of all terms of $\sequence {a_n}$. Then $c$ is a nest.

title: Increasing Sequence of Sets induces Partition on Limit
snippet: Let $\sequence {S_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \uparrow S$ be an increasing sequence of sets with limit $S$. Define $T_1 = S_1$, and, for $n \in \N$, $T_{n + 1} = S_{n + 1} \setminus S_n$, where $\setminus$ denotes set difference. Then $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a countable partition of $S$.

title: Increasing Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n j \binom n j = n 2^{n - 1}$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is: $1 \dbinom n 1 + 2 \dbinom n 2 + 3 \dbinom n 3 + \dotsb + n \dbinom n n = n 2^{n - 1}$

title: Increasing Sum of Squares of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: $\ds \sum_{r \mathop = 1}^n r \binom n r^2 = \dfrac {\paren {2 n - 1}!} {\paren {\paren {n - 1}!}^2}$ where $\dbinom n r$ denotes the binomial coefficient: $\dbinom n r = \dfrac {n!} {r! \paren {n - r} }$

title: Increasing Union of Ideals is Ideal
Increasing Union of Subrings is Subring
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $S_0 \subseteq S_1 \subseteq S_2 \subseteq \ldots \subseteq S_i \subseteq \ldots$ be subrings of $R$. Then the increasing union $S$: $\ds S = \bigcup_{i \mathop \in \N} S_i$ is a subring of $R$.

title: Increasing and Ordering on Mappings implies Mapping is Composition
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}, R = \struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered sets. Let $g: S \to T, d: T \to S$ be mappings such that $g$ and $d$ are increasing mappings and $d \circ g \preceq I_S$ and $I_T \preccurlyeq g \circ d$ where $\preceq, \preccurlyeq$ denotes the orderings on mappings. Then $d = d \circ \paren {g \circ d}$ and $g = \paren {g \circ d} \circ g$

title: Indecomposable Lattice of Subgroups does not necessarily form Totally Ordered Set
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a Group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by the subset ordering on $\mathbb G$. Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an indecomposable group. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ is totally ordered.

title: Independence System Induced from Set of Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr A$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr I = \set {X \subseteq S : \exists A \in \mathscr A : X \subseteq A}$. Then $\struct {S, \mathscr I}$ is an independence system.

title: Independent Equations/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Independent Equations ==

title: Independent Events are Independent of Complement
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be events in a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Then $A$ and $B$ are independent $A$ and $\Omega \setminus B$ are independent.

title: Independent Set can be Augmented by Larger Independent Set
snippet: Let $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $X, Y \in \mathscr I$ such that: $\size X < \size Y$ Then there exists non-empty $Z \subseteq Y \setminus X$ such that: $X \cup Z \in \mathscr I$ $\size {X \cup Z} = \size Y$

title: Independent Sets of Dual Matroid
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\mathscr B$ be the set of bases of the matroid $M$. Then the independent subsets of the dual $M^*$ of $M$ is: $\mathscr I^* = \set{X \subseteq S : \exists B \in \mathscr B : X \subseteq \paren{S \setminus B}}$

title: Independent Subset Contains No Dependent Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $X \subseteq S$ be any independent subset of $M$. Then: No dependent subset $D$ of $M$ is a subset of $X$.

title: Independent Subset is Base if Cardinality Equals Rank of Matroid
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\rho: \powerset S \to \Z$ be the rank function of $M$. Let $B \in \mathscr I$ such that: $\size B = \map \rho S$ Then: $B$ is a base of $M$.

title: Independent Subset is Contained in Base
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $\mathscr B$ denote the set of all bases of $M$. Let $A \in \mathscr I$. Then: $\exists B \in \mathscr B : A \subseteq B$

title: Independent Subset is Contained in Maximal Independent Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $X \in \mathscr I$ such that $X \subseteq A$. Then: $\exists Y \in \mathscr I : X \subseteq Y \subseteq A : \size Y = \map \rho A$ where $\rho$ is the rank function on $M$.

title: Indeterminate Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indeterminate Equations ==

title: Indeterminate System of Simultaneous Equations/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indeterminate Systems of Simultaneous Equations ==

title: Index Laws for Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \circ}$ be a field with zero $0_F$ and unity $1_F$. Let $F^* = F \setminus {0_F}$ denote the set of elements of $F$ without the zero $0_F$. Then the following hold:

title: Index Laws for Monoids
snippet: These results are an extension of the results in Index Laws for Semigroup in which the domain of the indices is extended to include all integers. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in S$ be invertible for $\circ$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $a^n$ be the $n$th power of $a$: $a^n = \begin{cases} e : & n = 0 \\ a^{n - 1} \circ a : & n > 0 \\ \paren {a^{-n}}^{-1} : & n < 0 \end{cases}$ Then we have the following results:

title: Index Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Index Numbers == Examples of economic indicators that are often assigned an index number include: magnitude of business activity wages cost of living share prices imports and so on.

title: Index in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H, K$ be subgroups of finite index of $G$. Then: $\index H {H \cap K} \le \index G K$ where $\index G K$ denotes the index of $K$ in $G$. Equality happens $G = H K$.

title: Index is One iff Subgroup equals Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity element is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\index G H = 1 \iff G = H$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$.

title: Index of Intersection of Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H, K$ be subgroups of finite index of $G$. Then: $\index G {H \cap K} \le \index G H \index G K$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$. Note that here the symbol $\le$ is being used with its meaning less than or equal to. Equality holds $H K = \set {h k: h \in H, k \in K} = G$.

title: Index of Proper Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number such that $n > 4$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $A_n$ denote the alternating group on $n$ letters. $A_n$ is the only proper subgroup of $S_n$ whose index is less than $n$.

title: Index of Refraction of Atmosphere for Radio Waves
snippet: The index of refraction of the atmosphere of Earth for radio waves of frequency less than $3 \times 10^{10} \, \mathrm {Hz}$ is given by: $\paren {n - 1} 10^6 = \dfrac {77 \cdotp 6} t \paren {p + \dfrac {4810 e} t}$ where: $n$ denotes the index of refraction of the atmosphere $t$ denotes the temperature in kelvin $p$ denotes the total atmospheric pressure in millibars $e$ denotes the water vapor partial pressure in millibars.

title: Index of Root/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indices of Roots ==

title: Index of Square Triangular Number from Preceding
snippet: Let $T_n$ be the $n$th triangular number. Let $T_n$ be square. Then $T_{4 n \paren {n + 1} }$ is also square.

title: Index of Subgroup equals Index of Conjugate
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\index G H = \index G {a H a^{-1} }$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$.

title: Index of Subsequence not Less than its Index
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be a sequence in a set $S$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then: $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: n_r \ge r$

title: Index of Trivial Subgroup is Cardinality of Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity element is $e$. Let $\set e$ be the trivial subgroup of $G$. Then: $\index G {\set e} = \order G$ where: $\index G {\set e}$ denotes the index of $\set e$ in $G$ $\order G$ denotes the cardinality of $G$.

title: Indexed Cartesian Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indexed Cartesian Spaces ==

title: Indexed Cartesian Space is Set of all Mappings
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} S$ denote the cartesian space of $S$ indexed by $I$. Then $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} S$ is the set of all mappings from $I$ to $S$, and hence the notation: $S^I := \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} S$

title: Indexed Family/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indexed Families ==

title: Indexed Iterated Operation does not Change under Permutation
snippet: Let $G$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $a, b \in\Z$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to G$ be a mapping. Let $\sigma: \closedint a b \to \closedint a b$ be a permutation.

title: Indexed Summation does not Change under Permutation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\sigma: \closedint a b \to \closedint a b$ be a permutation. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f {\map \sigma i}$

title: Indexed Summation of Multiple of Mapping
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\lambda \in \mathbb A$. Let $g = \lambda \cdot f$ be the product of $f$ with $\lambda$. Then we have the equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map g i = \lambda \cdot \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i$

title: Indexed Summation of Sum of Mappings
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f, g: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be mappings. Let $h = f + g$ be their pointwise sum. Then we have the equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map h i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i + \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map g i$

title: Indexed Summation over Adjacent Intervals
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b, c$ be integers. Let $\closedint a c$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $c$. Let $b \in \closedint {a - 1} c$. Let $f : \closedint a c \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^c \map f i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i + \sum_{i \mathop = b + 1}^c \map f i$

title: Indexed Summation over Interval of Length One
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $f: \set a \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping on the singleton $\set a$. Then the indexed summation: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^a \map f i = \map f a$

title: Indexed Summation over Interval of Length Two
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $f: \set {a, a + 1} \to \mathbb A$ be a real-valued function. Then the indexed summation: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^{a + 1} \map f i = \map f a + \map f {a + 1}$

title: Indexed Summation over Translated Interval
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $c\in\Z$ be an integer. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b f(i) = \sum_{i \mathop = a + c}^{b + c} \map f {i - c}$

title: Indexed Summation without First Term
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers with $a \le b$. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i = \map f a + \sum_{i \mathop = a + 1}^b \map f {\map \sigma i}$

title: Indexed Union Equality
snippet: Let $A$, $B_x$, and $C_x$ be classes. Then: $\ds \forall x \in A: B_x = C_x \implies \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} B_x = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} C_x$ {{MissingLinks|$\bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} B_x$ and $\bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} C_x$}}

title: Indexed Union Subset
snippet: Let $A$, $B_x$ and $C_x$ be classes. Then: $\ds \forall x \in A: B_x \subseteq C_x \implies \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} B_x \subseteq \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} C_x$ {{MissingLinks|$\bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} B_x$ and $\bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} C_x$}}

title: Indicator is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group, and $a \in G$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then the indicator of $a$ in $H$ is well defined.

title: Indices of Complete Bipartite Graph Commute
snippet: Let $G = \struct {A \mid B, E} =: K_{m, n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $m$ vertices in $A$ and $n$ vertices in $B$. Then: $K_{m, n}$ is isomorphic to $K_{n, m}$ for all $m, n \in \N$.

title: Indirect Isometry/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indirect Isometries ==

title: Indirect Proof
snippet: Let $P$ be a proposition whose truth value is to be proved (either true or false). An indirect proof has one of the following two argument forms:

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is T0
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is a $T_0$ space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is T1
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not Completely Normal
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a completely normal space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not Normal
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a normal space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not Regular
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a regular space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not T3
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not T4
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_4$ space.

title: Indiscrete Extension of Reals is not T5
snippet: Let $T$ be an indiscrete extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_5$ space.

title: Indiscrete Non-Singleton Space is not T0
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space which has more than one element. Then $T$ is not a $T_0$ space.

title: Indiscrete Non-Singleton Space is not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space which has more than one element. Then $T$ is not a $T_1$ space.

title: Indiscrete Non-Singleton Space is not T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space which has more than one element. Then $T$ is not a $T_2$ space.

title: Indiscrete Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Indiscrete Space ==

title: Indiscrete Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is connected.

title: Indiscrete Space is Injectively Path-Connected iff Uncountable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is injectively path-connected $S$ is an uncountable set.

title: Indiscrete Space is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is irreducible.

title: Indiscrete Space is Noetherian
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is Noetherian.

title: Indiscrete Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is non-meager.

title: Indiscrete Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is path-connected.

title: Indiscrete Space is Pseudometrizable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is pseudometrizable.

title: Indiscrete Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is a second-countable space.

title: Indiscrete Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space such that $S$ has more than one element. Then $T$ is separable.

title: Indiscrete Space is T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space . Then $T$ is a $T_3$ space.

title: Indiscrete Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Indiscrete Space is T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is a $T_5$ space.

title: Indiscrete Space is Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Then $T$ is ultraconnected.

title: Indiscrete Topology is Coarsest Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an indiscrete topological space. $\tau$ is the coarsest topology on $S$. Hence it is comparable with all other topologies on $S$.

title: Indiscrete Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau$ be the indiscrete topology on $S$. $\tau$ is a topology on $S$.

title: Indiscrete Topology is not Metrizable
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with more than one element. The indiscrete topology on $S$ is not metrizable.

title: Induced Algebra Homomorphism on Unitization
snippet: Let $A, B$ be algebras over $\C$. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be an algebra homomorphism. Let $A_+$ and $B_+$ be the unitizations of $A$ and $B$ respectively. Define $\psi : A_+ \to B_+$ by: $\map \psi {a, \lambda} = \tuple {\map \phi a, \lambda}$ for each $\tuple {a, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then $\psi$ is a unital algebra homomorphism.

title: Induced Group Product is Homomorphism iff Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H_1, H_2$ be subgroups of $G$. Let $\phi: H_1 \times H_2 \to G$ be defined such that: $\forall \tuple {h_1, h_2} \in H_1 \times H_2: \map \phi {h_1, h_2} = h_1 \circ h_2$ Then $\phi$ is a homomorphism every element of $H_1$ commutes with every element of $H_2$.

title: Induced Homomorphism of Polynomial Forms
snippet: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $R \sqbrk X$ and $S \sqbrk X$ be the rings of polynomial forms over $R$ and $S$ respectively in the indeterminate $X$. Then the map $\overline \phi: R \sqbrk X \to S \sqbrk X$ given by: $\map {\overline \phi} {a_0 + a_1 X + \cdots + a_n X^n} = \map \phi {a_0} + \map \phi {a_1} X + \cdots + \map \phi {a_n} X^n$ is a ring homomorphism.

title: Induced Metric on Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^3, d}$ be the Euclidean space. Let $S_C \subseteq \R^3$ be the surface of revolution. Let the smooth local parametrization of $C$ be: $\map \gamma t = \tuple {\map x t, \map y t}$ Then the induced metric on $S_C$ is: $g = \paren {\map {x'} t^2 + \map {y'} t^2} d t^2 + \map y t^2 d \theta^2$

title: Induced Neighborhood Space is Neighborhood Space
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau$ be a topology on $S$, thus forming the topological space $\struct {S, \tau}$. Let $\struct {S, \NN}$ be the neighborhood space induced by $\struct {S, \tau}$. Then $\struct {S, \NN}$ is a neighborhood space.

title: Induced Outer Measure Restricted to Semiring is Pre-Measure
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a semiring over a set $X$. Let $\mu: \SS \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a pre-measure on $\SS$, where $\overline \R_{\ge 0}$ denotes the set of positive extended real numbers. Let $\mu^*: \powerset X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be the outer measure induced by $\mu$. Then: $\ds \mu^*\restriction_\SS \, = \mu$ where $\restriction$ denotes restriction.

title: Induced Relation Generates Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {A_1, \preceq_1}$ be an ordered set. Let $\phi: A_1 \to A_2$ be a bijection. Let: $\preceq_2 \mathop{:=} \set {\tuple {\map \phi x, \map \phi y}: x \in A_1 \land y \in A_1 \land x \mathop{\preceq_1} y}$ Then $\phi: \struct {A_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct {A_2, \preceq_2}$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Induced Solution to Homogeneous Linear Second Order ODE is Linearly Independent with Inducing Solution
snippet: Let $\map {y_1} x$ be a particular solution to the homogeneous linear second order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + \map P x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map Q x y = 0$ such that $y_1$ is not the trivial solution. Let $\map {y_2} x$ be the real function defined as: $\map {y_2} x = \map v x \map {y_1} x$ where: $\ds v = \int \dfrac 1 { {y_1}^2} e^{-\int P \rd x} \rd x$ Then $y_2$ and $y_1$ are linearly independent.

title: Induced Structure Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $e$ be an identity for $\circ$. Then the constant mapping $f_e: S \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {f_e} x = e$ is the identity for the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$.

title: Induced Structure from Doubleton is Isomorphic to External Direct Product with Self
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $S^A$ denote the set of mappings from $A$ to $S$. Let $\struct {S^A, \odot}$ denote the algebraic structure on $S^A$ induced by $\odot$. Then $\struct {S^A, \odot}$ is isomorphic to the external direct product of $\struct {S, \odot}$ with itself.

title: Induced Topology on Subspace of Subspace Coincides with Induced Topology on Subspace
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space Let $S_2 \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $S_3 \subseteq S_2$ be a subset of $S_2$. Let $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be the topological subspace of $T_1$ such that $\tau_2$ is the subspace topology on $T_2$ induced by $\tau_1$. Let $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be the topological subspace of $T_1$ such that $\tau_3$ is the subspace topology on $T_3$ induced by $\tau_1$. Then $\tau_3$ is the same set of subsets of $S_1$ as is the subspace topology on $T_3$ induced by $\tau_2$.

title: Induction of Finite Set
snippet: == Theorem Scheme == Let $A$ be finite set. Let $\map P -$ be a predicate. Let $\map P \O$. Let $\forall B \subseteq A, x \in A: \paren {\map P B \implies \map P {B \cup \set x} }$ Then: $\map P A$

title: Induction on Well-Formed Formulas
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a formal language with a bottom-up grammar. Let $\Phi$ be a proposition about the well-formed formulas of $\FF$. Suppose that $\Phi$ is true for all letters of $\FF$. Suppose further that every rule of formation preserves $\Phi$, i.e. when fed well-formed formulas satisfying $\Phi$, it yields new well-formed formulas satisfying $\Phi$. Then all well-formed formulas of $\FF$ satisfy $\Phi$.

title: Inductive Argument/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inductive Arguments ==

title: Inductive Construction of Natural Numbers fulfils Peano's Axiom of Injectivity
snippet: Let $P$ denote the set of natural numbers by definition as an inductive set. Then $P$ fulfils: where $s$ denotes the successor mapping.

title: Inductive Construction of Natural Numbers fulfils Peano's Axioms
snippet: Let $P$ denote the set of natural numbers by definition as an inductive set. Then $P$ fulfils Peano's axioms.

title: Inductive Construction of Sigma-Algebra Generated by Collection of Subsets
snippet: Let $\EE$ be a set of sets which are subsets of some set $X$. Let $\map \sigma \EE$ be the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\EE$. Then $\map \sigma \EE$ can be constructed inductively. The construction is as follows: Let $\Omega$ denote the minimal uncountable well-ordered set. Let $\alpha$ be an arbitrary initial segment in $\Omega$.

title: Inductive Definition of Sequence
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $h \in \N$. Let $a_i \in X$ for all $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, h}$. Let $S$ be the set of all finite sequences whose codomains are in $X$. Let $G: S \to X$ be a mapping. Then there is a unique sequence $f$ whose codomain is in $X$ such that: $f_i = \begin{cases} a_i & : i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, h} \\ \map G {f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_{i - 1} } & : i \ge h + 1 \end{cases}$

title: Inductive Semigroup whose Inductive Elements Commute is Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let there exist $\alpha, \beta \in S$ which fulfil the condition for $\struct {S, \circ}$ to be an inductive semigroup: the only subset of $S$ containing both $\alpha$ and $x \circ \beta$ whenever it contains $x$ is $S$ itself. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ commute. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a commutative semigroup.

title: Inductive Set/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inductive Sets ==

title: Inductive Set under Mapping has Minimally Inductive Subset
snippet: Let $A$ be an inductive class under a mapping $g$. Let $A$ be a set. Then there exists some subset $S$ of $A$ such that $S$ is minimally inductive under $g$.

title: Inequalities Concerning Roots
snippet: Let $\closedint X Y$ be a closed real interval such that $0 0}: X Y^{1/n} \size {x - y} \le n X Y \size {x^{1/n} - y^{1/n} } \le Y X^{1/n} \size {x - y}$

title: Inequality Rule for Absolutely Convergent Generalized Sums
Inequality Rule for Real Convergent Nets
snippet: Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ and $\family {y_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be indexed families of elements in $\R$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ and $\family {y_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be convergent to the following limits: $\ds \lim_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} x_\lambda = l$ $\ds \lim_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} y_\lambda = m$ Let there exist $\lambda \in \Lambda$ such that: $\forall \mu \in \Lambda : \lambda \preceq \mu: x_\mu \le y_\mu$ Then: $l \le m$

title: Inequality Rule for Real Sequences
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be sequences in $\R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be convergent to the following limits: {{eqn | l = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n | r = l }} {{eqn | l = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} y_n | r = m }} Let there exist $N \in \N$ such that: $\forall n \ge N: x_n \le y_n$ Then: $l \le m$

title: Inequality for Ordinal Exponentiation
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal and let $y > 0$. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} \times b_i}^y \le x^{a_1 \mathop \times y} \times \paren {b_1 + 1}$

title: Inequality of Height of Proper Ideal
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $I$ be a proper ideal in $A$. Then: $\map {\operatorname {dim_{Krull} } } {A / I} + \map {\operatorname {ht} } I \le \map {\operatorname {dim_{Krull} } } A$ where: $A/I$ is the quotient ring of $A$ by $I$ $\operatorname {dim_{Krull} }$ denotes the Krull dimension $\map {\operatorname {ht} } I$ is the height of $I$

title: Inequality of Hölder Means
snippet: Let $p, q \in \overline \R$ be extended real numbers such that $p 0$. Then the Hölder mean satisfies the inequality: $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map {M_q} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ Equality holds : $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots = x_n$ or: $q < 0$ and $x_k = 0$ for at least one $k \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Note that in particular: $\forall p \in \R: \map {M_{-\infty} } {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ and: $\forall p \in \R: \map {M_\infty} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \ge \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$

title: Inequality of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$ be natural numbers. Suppose $x \ne y$. Let $\sqbrk a$ denote the unary representation of $a \in \N$. Then $\sqbrk x \ne \sqbrk y$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

title: Inequality of Product of Unequal Numbers
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$. Then: $0 < a < b \land 0 < c < d \implies 0 < a c < b d$

title: Inequality with Meet Operation is Equivalent to Inequality with Relative Pseudocomplement in Brouwerian Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be s Brouwerian lattice. Let $a, x, y \in S$. Then $a \wedge x \preceq y$ $x \preceq a \to y$

title: Inertia Principle
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $a_n \to l$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $c \in \R$: such that $c < l$. Then $\exists N \in \N$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: n \ge N \implies c < a_n$

title: Inertial Force/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inertial Forces ==

title: Infima Inheriting Ordered Subset of Complete Lattice is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {X, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $S = \struct {T, \precsim}$ be an infima inheriting ordered subset of $L$. Then $S$ is a complete lattice.

title: Infima Preserving Mapping on Filters Preserves Filtered Infima
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$, $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. For every filter $F$ in $\struct {S, \preceq}$, let $f$ preserve the infimum on $F$. Then $f$ preserves filtered infima.

title: Infima Preserving Mapping on Filters is Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$, $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. For every filter $F$ in $\struct {S, \preceq}$, let $f$ preserve the infimum on $F$. Then $f$ is increasing.

title: Infima in Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $x, y, z \in G$ be arbitrary. Let any one of the sets $\set {x, y}$, $\set {x \circ z, y \circ z}$ or $\set {z \circ x, z \circ y}$ admit an infimum. Then all three sets admit an infimum, and: {{eqn | l = \inf \set {x \circ z, y \circ z} | r = \inf \set {x, y} \circ z }} {{eqn | l = \inf \set {z \circ x, z \circ y} | r = z \circ \inf \set {x, y} }}

title: Infima of two Real Sets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets of real numbers. Let $S$ and $T$ admit infima. Then: $\inf S \ge \inf T \iff \forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \forall s \in S: \exists t \in T: s + \epsilon > t$

title: Infimum Plus Constant
snippet: Let $T$ be a subset of the set of real numbers. Let $T$ be bounded below. Let $\xi \in \R$. Then: $\ds \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } {x + \xi} = \xi + \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } x$ where $\inf$ denotes infimum.

title: Infimum Precedes Coarser Infimum
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$ such that $Y$ is coarser than $X$. Then $\inf X \preceq \inf Y$ where $\inf X$ denotes the infimum of $X$.

title: Infimum and Supremum of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by $\mathbb G$ and $\subseteq$. Let $H, K \in \mathbb G$.

title: Infimum in Ordered Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $R = \struct {T, \preceq'}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Let $X \subseteq T$ such that $X$ admits an infimum in $L$. Then $\inf_L X \in T$ $X$ admits an infimum in $R$ and $\inf_R X = \inf_L X$

title: Infimum is Product in Order Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf P$ be an order category whose ordering is $\preceq$. Let $p, q \in \mathbf P_0$, and suppose that they have some infimum $r = \inf \set {p, q}$. Then $r$ is a binary product of $p$ and $q$ in $\mathbf P$.

title: Infimum is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $T$ has at most one infimum in $S$.

title: Infimum is not necessarily Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ admit a infimum in $S$. Then the infimum of $T$ in $S$ is not necessarily the smallest element of $T$.

title: Infimum of Bounded Below Set of Reals is in Closure
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean} metric. Let $H \subseteq \R$ be a bounded below subset of $\R$ such that $H \ne \O$. Let $l = \map \inf H$ be the infimum of $H$. Then: $l \in \map \cl H$ where $\map \cl H$ denotes the closure of $H$ in $\R$.

title: Infimum of Empty Set is Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Suppose that $\map \inf \O$, the infimum of the empty set, exists in $S$. Then $\forall s \in S: s \preceq \map \inf \O$. That is, $\map \inf \O$ is the greatest element of $S$.

title: Infimum of Image of Upper Closure of Element under Increasing Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an increasing mapping. Let $x \in S$. Then $\map \inf {f \sqbrk {x^\succeq} } = \map f x$

title: Infimum of Infima
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $\mathbb T$ be a collection of subsets of $S$. Suppose all $T \in \mathbb T$ admit an infimum $\inf T$ in $S$. Then: $\inf \bigcup \mathbb T = \inf \left\{{\inf T: T \in \mathbb T}\right\}$ as soon as one of these two quantities exists.

title: Infimum of Intersection of Upper Closures equals Join Operands
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $\map \inf {x^\succeq \cap y^\succeq} = x \vee y$

title: Infimum of Open Set is Way Below Element in Complete Scott Topological Lattice
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete topological lattice with Scott topology. Let $X$ be an open subset of $S$, Let $x \in X$. Then $\inf X \ll x$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

title: Infimum of Power Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\powerset S$ by the relation $\subseteq$. (From Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering, this is an ordered set.) Then the infimum of $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is the empty set $\O$.

title: Infimum of Real Subset
snippet: == Lemma == Let $S$ be a set of extended real numbers. Let $S$ be bounded below in $\R$. Let $T = S \cap \R$. Then: $S$ admits an infimum in $\R$ $T$ admits an infimum in $\R$ and, if $\inf S$ and $\inf T$ exist as real numbers: $\inf S = \inf T$

title: Infimum of Set of Integers equals Smallest Element
snippet: Let $S \subset \Z$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers. Let $S$ be bounded below in the set of real numbers $\R$. Then $S$ has a smallest element, and it is equal to the infimum $\sup S$.

title: Infimum of Set of Integers is Integer
snippet: Let $S \subset \Z$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers. Let $S$ be bounded below in the set of real numbers. Then its infimum $\inf S$ is an integer.

title: Infimum of Set of Oscillations on Set
snippet: == Lemma == Let $f: D \to \R$ be a real function where $D \subseteq \R$. Let $x$ be a point in $D$. Let $S_x$ be a set of real sets that contain (as an element) $x$. Let: $\map {\omega_f} x = \inf \set {\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}: I \in S_x}$ where $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$ denotes the oscillation of $f$ on the set $I \cap D$: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \sup \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}$ Then: $\map {\omega_f} x \in \R$ $\set {\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}: I \in S_x}$ contains a real number.

title: Infimum of Set of Oscillations on Set is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: == Lemma == Let $f: D \to \R$ be a real function where $D \subseteq \R$. Let $x$ be a point in $D$. Let $S_x$ be a set of real sets that contain (as an element) $x$. Let: $\map {\omega_f} x = \ds \inf \set {\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}: I \in S_x}$ where $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$ is the oscillation of $f$ on a real set $I \cap D$: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \ds \sup \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}$ Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Let $\map {\omega_f} x \in \R$. Then an $I \in S_x$ exists such that: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} - \map {\omega_f} x < \epsilon$

title: Infimum of Set of Reciprocals of Positive Integers
snippet: Let $S$ be the subset of the set of real numbers defined as: $S = \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Then: $\inf S = 0$ where $\inf S$ denotes the infimum of $S$.

title: Infimum of Singleton
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then for all $a \in S$: $\inf \set a = a$ where $\inf$ denotes infimum.

title: Infimum of Subgroups in Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by $\mathbb G$ and $\subseteq$. Let $H, K \in \mathbb G$. Then: $\inf \set {H, K} = H \cap K$

title: Infimum of Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {U, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $S \subseteq U$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ admit an infimum in $U$. If $T$ also admits an infimum in $U$, then $\map \inf S \preceq \map \inf T$.

title: Infimum of Subset Product in Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered group. Let subsets $A$ and $B$ of $G$ admit infima in $G$. Then: $\map \inf {A \circ_\PP B} = \inf A \circ \inf B$ where $\circ_\PP$ denotes subset product.

title: Infimum of Subset of Bounded Below Set of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded below. Then: $\inf A \ge \inf B$ where $\inf$ denotes the infimum.

title: Infimum of Subset of Extended Real Numbers is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \overline \R$ be a subset of the extended real numbers. Let $b$ be an infimum (in $\R$) of $A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists x \in A \cap \R: x - b < \epsilon$

title: Infimum of Subset of Real Numbers/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Infima of Subsets of Real Numbers ==

title: Infimum of Subset of Real Numbers May or May Not be in Subset
snippet: Let $S \subset \R$ be a proper subset of the set $\R$ of real numbers. Let $S$ admit an infimum $m$. Then $m$ may or may not be an element of $S$.

title: Infimum of Subset of Real Numbers is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers. Let $b$ be an infimum of $A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists x \in A: x - b < \epsilon$

title: Infimum of Union of Bounded Below Sets of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ both be bounded below. Then: $\map \inf {A \cup B} = \min \set {\inf A, \inf B}$ where $\inf$ denotes the infimum.

title: Infimum of Upper Closure of Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $s$ be an element of $S$. Then: $\map \inf {s^\succeq} = s$ where $s^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $s$.

title: Infimum of Upper Closure of Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $U = T^\succeq$ be the upper closure of $T$ in $S$. Let $s \in S$. Then $s$ is the infimum of $T$ it is the infimum of $U$.

title: Infimum of Upper Sums Never Smaller than Lower Sum
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f$ be a bounded real function defined on $\closedint a b$. Let $S$ be a finite subdivision of $\closedint a b$. Let $\map L S$ be the lower Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to $S$. Let $\map U P$ be the upper Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to a finite subdivision $P$. Then: $\inf_P \map U P \ge \map L S$

title: Infinite-Dimensional Banach Space contains Basic Sequence with Basis Constant Arbitrarily Close to 1
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\GF$. Then for each $\epsilon > 0$, $X$ contains a basic sequence with basis constant at most $1 + \epsilon$.

title: Infinite-Dimensional Banach Space has Uncountable Dimension
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $B$ be a Hamel basis for $X$. Then $B$ is uncountable. That is, $\dim X > \aleph_0$.

title: Infinite-Dimensional Normed Vector Space contains Weakly Null Net with Unbounded Tails
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$ that is infinite-dimensional. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Then there exists a directed set $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ and a net $ amily {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ such that: $x_\lambda 	o {\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, w}$ and: $\ds \sup \set {
orm {x_\lambda}_X : \lambda \succeq \lambda_0}$ for each $\lambda_0 \in \Lambda$.

title: Infinite-Dimensional Vector Subspace of P-Sequence Space contains Topologically Complemented Subspace Linearly Isomorphic to Whole Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \hointr 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $Y$ be an infinite-dimensional closed vector subspace of $\map {\ell_p} \GF$. Then there exists a closed vector subspace $Z$ of $\map {\ell_p} \GF$ that is topologically complemented in $\map {\ell_p} \GF$ and linearly isomorphic to $\map {\ell_p} \GF$.

title: Infinite Cyclic Group is Isomorphic to Integers
snippet: Let $G$ be an infinite cyclic group. Then $G$ is isomorphic to the additive group of integers: $G \cong \struct {\Z, +}$.

title: Infinite Cyclic Group is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: All infinite cyclic groups are isomorphic. That is, up to isomorphism, there is only one infinite cyclic group.

title: Infinite Discontinuity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Infinite Discontinuities ==

title: Infinite Group has Infinite Number of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an infinite group. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ has an infinite number of distinct subgroups.

title: Infinite Intersection of Open Sets of Metric Space may not be Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {U_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an infinite sequence of open sets of $M$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\ds \bigcap_{n \mathop \in \N} U_n$ is itself an open set of $M$.

title: Infinite Lexicographic Order on Well-Ordered Sets is not Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered set. Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ be the lexicographic order on the set $T$ of all ordered tuples of $S$: $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_m} \prec \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n}$ : $\exists k: 1 \le k \le \map \min {m, n}$ such that $\forall 1 \le j < k: x_j = y_j$ but $x_k \prec y_k$ in $S$ or: $m < n$ and $\forall 1 \le j < m: x_j = y_j$. Then $\preccurlyeq_l$ is not a well-ordering on $T$.

title: Infinite Limit Operator is Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $c$ be the space of convergent sequences. Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $L : c \to \R$ be the infinite limit operator. Then $L$ is a linear mapping.

Let $f$ be a real function of $x$ of the form $\map f x = \dfrac {\map g x} {\map h x}$ Further, let $g$ and $h$ be continuous on some open interval $\mathbb I$, where $c$ is a constant in $\mathbb I$. If: $(1): \quad \map g c 
e 0$ $(2): \quad \map h c = 0$ $(3): \quad  orall x \in \mathbb I: x 
e c \implies \map h x 
e 0$ then the limit of $f$ as $x 	o c$ will not exist, and: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop 	o c^+} \map f x = +\infty$ or $-\infty$ $\ds \lim_{x \mathop 	o c^-} \map f x = +\infty$ or $-\infty$

title: Infinite Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Then the infinite measure $\mu$ on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ is a measure.

title: Infinite Number of Chen Primes
snippet: There exists an infinite number of Chen primes. That is, there exists an infinite number of pairs: $\set {p, p + 2}$ where: $p$ is a prime $p + 2$ is either a prime or a semiprime.

title: Infinite Number of Even Fermat Pseudoprimes
snippet: Despite their relative rarity, there exist an infinite number of even Fermat pseudoprimes.

title: Infinite Number of Integers which are Sum of 3 Sixth Powers in 2 Ways
snippet: There exist an infinite number of positive integers which can be expressed as the sum of $3$ sixth powers in $2$ different ways.

title: Infinite Number of Primes of form 4n - 1
snippet: There are infinitely many prime numbers of the form $4 n - 1$.

title: Infinite Ordinal can be expressed Uniquely as Sum of Limit Ordinal plus Finite Ordinal
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Suppose $x$ satisfies $\omega \subseteq x$. Then $x$ has a unique representation as $\paren {y + z}$ where $y$ is a limit ordinal and $z$ is a finite ordinal.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not compact.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Countably Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not countably metacompact.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Countably Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not countably paracompact.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not metacompact.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not strongly locally compact.

title: Infinite Particular Point Space is not Weakly Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an infinite particular point space. Then $T$ is not weakly countably compact.

title: Infinite Product of Analytic Functions
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open connected set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n: D \to \C$ that are not identically zero. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {f_n - 1}$ converge locally uniformly absolutely on $D$. Then: $(1): \quad f = \ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges locally uniformly absolutely on $D$ $(2): \quad f$ is analytic $(3): \quad$ For each $z \in D$, $\map {f_n} z = 0$ for finitely many $n \in \N$ $(4): \quad$ For each $z \in D$, $\map {\operatorname {mult}_z} f = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {\operatorname {mult}_z}…

title: Infinite Product of Analytic Functions is Analytic
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n: D \to \C$. Let $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge locally uniformly to $f$. Then $f$ is analytic.

snippet: $\ds \prod_{n \mathop \ge 1} \dfrac {\paren {n + \alpha_1} \cdots \paren {n + \alpha_k} } {\paren {n + \beta_1} \cdots \paren {n + \beta_k} } = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {1 + \beta_1} \cdots \map \Gamma {1 + \beta_k} } {\map \Gamma {1 + \alpha_1} \cdots \map \Gamma {1 + \alpha_k} }$ where: $\alpha_1 + \cdots + \alpha_k = \beta_1 + \cdots + \beta_k$ none of the $\beta$s is a negative integer.

title: Infinite Product of Sigma-Compact Spaces is not always Sigma-Compact
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with infinite cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be $\sigma$-compact. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also $\sigma$-compact.

title: Infinite Product of Weakly Locally Compact Spaces is not always Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set with infinite cardinality. Let $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\ds \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Let each of $\struct {S_\alpha, \tau_\alpha}$ be weakly locally compact-compact. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also weakly locally compact.

title: Infinite Ramsey's Theorem
snippet: Let $k, n \in \N$. For any set $S$, let $S^{\paren n}$ denote the set $\set {\set {s_1, \ldots, s_n}: \text{each } s_i \in S}$ of cardinality $n$ subsets of $S$. Let $X$ be an infinite set. Then: for every partition $P$ of $X^{\paren n}$ into $k$ many components there is an infinite subset $Y \subseteq X$ such that: each member of $Y^{\paren n}$ is in the same component of $P$.

title: Infinite Ramsey's Theorem implies Finite Ramsey's Theorem
snippet: $\forall l, n, r \in \N: \exists m \in \N: m \to \left({l}\right)_r^n$ where $\alpha \to \left({\beta}\right)^n_r$ means that: for any assignment of $r$-colors to the $n$-subsets of $\alpha$ there is a particular color $\gamma$ and a subset $X$ of $\alpha$ of size $\beta$ such that all $n$-subsets of $X$ are $\gamma$.

title: Infinite Sequence Property of Strictly Well-Founded Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Then $\RR$ is a strictly well-founded relation there is no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n$

title: Infinite Sequence Property of Well-Founded Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Then $\RR$ is a well-founded relation there exists no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: \paren {a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n} \text { and } \paren {a_{n + 1} \ne a_n}$

title: Infinite Sequence in Countably Compact Space has Accumulation Point
snippet: == Corollary to Countably Infinite Set in Countably Compact Space has Omega-Accumulation Point == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a countably compact topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an infinite sequence in $S$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ has an accumulation point in $T$.

title: Infinite Series of Functions is Uniformly Convergent iff Sequence of Partial Sums is Uniformly Cauchy
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $S \to \R$. Then the infinite series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly on $S$ for all $\varepsilon \in \R_{> 0}$ there exists $N \in \N$ such that: $\ds \size {\sum_{k \mathop = m + 1}^n \map {f_k} x} m > N$.

title: Infinite Series of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions $f_n : X \to \overline \R$ such that: for each $N \in \N$ and $x \in X$, the summation $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^N \map {f_n} x$ is well-defined. Then: the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ is $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Infinite Series preserves Strict Inequality
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be real sequences such that: $x_n \le y_n$ for all $n \in \N$ and: $x_m < y_m$ for at least one $m \in \N$. Suppose that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty y_n$ both converge. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n < \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty y_n$

title: Infinite Set has Countably Infinite Subset
snippet: Every infinite set has a countably infinite subset.

title: Infinite Set in Compact Space has Omega-Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a compact topological space. Let $A \subseteq X$ be infinite. Then $A$ has an $\omega$-accumulation point in $X$.

title: Infinite Set is Equivalent to Proper Subset
snippet: A set is infinite it is equivalent to one of its proper subsets.

title: Infinite Set of Natural Numbers is Countably Infinite
snippet: Let $\N$ be the set of natural numbers. Let $S$ be an infinite subset of $\N$. Then $S$ is countably infinite. That is, there is a bijection $f: \N \to S$.

title: Infinite Subseries of Unconditionally Convergent Series is Unconditionally Convergent
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ such that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is unconditionally convergent. Let $A \subseteq \N$ be infinite. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \in A} x_n = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {\chi_A} n x_n$ is unconditionally convergent where $\chi_A$ is the indicator function of $A$.

title: Infinite Subset of Finite Complement Space Intersects Open Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Let $H \subseteq S$ be an infinite subset of $S$. Then the intersection of $H$ with any non-empty open set of $T$ is infinite.

title: Infinite Union of Closed Sets of Metric Space may not be Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $V_1, V_2, V_3, \ldots$ be an infinite set of closed sets of $M$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\ds \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} V_n$ is itself a closed set of $M$.

title: Infinite if Injection from Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let there exist an injection $\phi: \N \to S$ from the natural numbers to $S$. Then $S$ is infinite.

title: Infinitely Many Programs for URM Computable Function
snippet: Let $g: \N^k \to \N$ be a URM computable function. Then there is an infinite number of URM programs which compute $g$.

title: Infinity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Infinity ==

title: Information Contained in Letter of Alphabet
snippet: Let $\psi$ be a letter of the English alphabet. To a first degree of approximation, the quantity of information contained in $\psi$ is $4 \cdotp 7$. That is, there is approximately $4 \cdotp 7$ times as much information conveyed by transmission of a single letter as a single bit.

title: Information of Sample from Given Distribution
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of $n$ observations from a probability distribution with frequency function $\map f {x, \theta}$. The information $I$ is given by: $I = n \map E {\paren {\dfrac {\partial \ln f} {\partial \theta} }^2}$

title: Information of Sample from Given Distribution under Regularity Conditions
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of $n$ observations from a probability distribution with frequency function $\map f {x, \theta}$. Let it be assumed that certain regularity conditions apply. Let it also be assumed that the extremes do not depend on $\theta$. The information $I$ is given by: $I = -n \map E {\dfrac {\partial^2 \ln f} {\partial \theta^2} }$

title: Ingham's Theorem on Convergent Dirichlet Series
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n} \le 1$ For a complex number $z \in \C$, let $\map \Re z$ denote the real part of $z$. Form the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n n^{-z}$ which converges to an analytic function $\map F z$ for $\map \Re z > 1$. {{explain|We have "$\map \Re z > 1$" used here and below to mean $\set {z \in \C: \map \Re z > 1}$? In which case, rather than just call it "$\map \Re z > 1$", which is unwieldy and suboptimal, it might be better and clearer to give it a single-symbol identifier.}} Let $\map F z$ be analytic throughout $\map \Re z \ge 1$.

title: Initial Object is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $0$ and $0'$ be two initial objects of $\mathbf C$. Then there is a unique isomorphism $u: 0 \to 0'$. Hence, initial objects are unique up to unique isomorphism.

title: Initial Segment Determined by Smallest Element is Empty
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set, where $S$ is non-empty. Let $s_0 = \min S$, the smallest element of $S$. Then the initial segment determined by $s_0$, $S_{s_0}$, is empty.

title: Initial Segment of Canonical Order is Set
snippet: Let $R_0$ denote the canonical ordering of $\paren {\On \times \On}$. Then, for all $\tuple {x, y} \in \paren {\On \times \On}$, the $R_0$-initial segment is a set.

title: Initial Segment of Natural Numbers determined by Zero is Empty
snippet: Let $\N_k$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers determined by $k$: $\N_k = \set {0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, k - 1}$ Then $\N_0 = \O$.

title: Initial Segment of Natural Numbers forms Complete Residue System
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ne 0}$ be a non-zero integer. Let $\N_m = \set {0, 1, 2, \ldots, m - 1}$ denote the initial segment of $\N$ Then $\N_m$ is a complete residue system modulo $m$.

title: Initial Segment of One-Based Natural Numbers determined by Zero is Empty
snippet: Let $\N^*_k$ denote the initial segment of the one-based natural numbers determined by $k$: $\N^*_k = \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots, k - 1, k}$ Then $\N^*_0 = \O$.

title: Initial Segment of Ordinal is Ordinal
snippet: Let $S$ be an ordinal. Let $a \in S$. Then the initial segment $S_a = a$ of $S$ determined by $a$ is also an ordinal. In other words, every element of a (non-empty) ordinal is also an ordinal.

title: Initial Segment of Ordinals under Lexicographic Order
snippet: Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ denote the lexicographic order for the set $\paren {\On \times \On}$. Let the ordinal number $1$ denote the successor of $\O$. Then the initial segment of $\tuple {1, \O}$ with respect to the lexicographic order $\preccurlyeq_l$ is a proper class. This initial segment shall be denoted $\paren {\On \times \On}_{\tuple {1, \O} }$.

title: Initial Topology Generated by Countable Family of Functions Separating Points is Metrizable
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. For each $n \in \N$, let $\struct {Y_n, d_n}$ be a metric space. Let $\family {f_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a indexed family of functions $X \to Y_n$ that separates points. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ generated by $\family {f_n}_{n \in \N}$. Then $\tau$ is metrizable.

title: Initial Topology on Hausdorff Locally Convex Space is Weak Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a Hausdorff locally convex space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $X$. Let $w$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $X^\ast$. Then $w$ is the weak topology on $X$.

title: Initial Topology on Normed Vector Space is Weak Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $w$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $X^\ast$. Then $w$ is the weak topology on $X$.

title: Initial Topology on Vector Space Generated by Linear Functionals is Locally Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $F$ be a set of linear functionals on $X$ that form a vector space over $\GF$. That is, for each $\lambda, \mu \in \GF$ and $f, g \in F$, we have: $\lambda f + \mu g \in F$ Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ generated by $F$. For each $f \in F$, define $p_f : X \to \R_{\ge 0}$ by: $\map {p_f} x = \cmod {\map f x}$ and let: $\PP = \set {p_f : f \in F}$ Then the standard topology on the locally convex space $\struct {X, \PP}$ is precisely $\tau$.

title: Initial Topology with respect to Mapping equals Set of Preimages
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a topological space. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_X$ be the initial topology on $X$ $f$. Then: $\tau_X = \set {f^{-1} \sqbrk U: U \in \tau_Y}$

title: Initial Topology with respect to Point-Separating Family of Mappings onto Hausdorff Spaces is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of Hausdorff topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$ that separate the points of $X$ in the sense that: for each $x, y \in X$ with $x \ne y$, there exists $i \in I$ such that $\map {f_i} x \ne \map {f_i} y$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then $\struct {X, \tau}$ is Hausdorff.

title: Initial Value Theorem of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to 0} \map f t = \lim_{s \mathop \to \infty} s \, \map F s$ if those limits exist.

title: Injection/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Injections ==

title: Injection Induces Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({T, \le}\right)$ be a totally ordered set, and let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\le_f$, the ordering induced by $f$, is a total ordering.

title: Injection Induces Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({T, \le}\right)$ be a well-ordered set. Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\le_f$, the ordering induced by $f$, is a well-ordering.

title: Injection from Finite Set to Itself is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Then $f$ is also a surjection.

title: Injection from Proper Class to Class
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $P$ be a proper class. Let $f: P \to A$ be an injection. Then $A$ is proper.

title: Injection from Set to Power Set
snippet: For every set $S$, there exists an injection from $S$ to its power set $\powerset S$.

title: Injection from Subset to Superset
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $A \subseteq B$. Then there is an injection $f: A \to B$.

title: Injection has Surjective Left Inverse Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \ne \O$. Let $f: S \to T$ be a injection. Then there exists a surjection $g: T \to S$ such that: $g \circ f = I_S$

title: Injection if Composite is Injection
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be mappings such that their composite $g \circ f$ is an injection. Then $f$ is an injection.

title: Injection iff Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $\card T$ denote the cardinal number of $T$. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \sim \card S$ and $T \sim \card T$. Then: $\card S \le \card T $ there exists an injection $f: S \to T$.

title: Injection iff Left Cancellable
snippet: A mapping $f$ is an injection $f$ is left cancellable.

title: Injection iff Left Inverse
snippet: A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is an injection : $\exists g: T \to S: g \circ f = I_S$ where $g$ is a mapping. That is, $f$ has a left inverse.

title: Injection iff Monomorphism in Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{Set}$, that is, a mapping. Then $f$ is an injection it is a monomorphism.

title: Injection implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $\card T$ denote the cardinal number of $T$. Let: $T \sim \card T$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence Then: $\card S \le \card T$

title: Injection is Bijection iff Inverse is Injection
snippet: Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\phi$ is a bijection its inverse $\phi^{-1}$ is also an injection.

title: Injection is Open Mapping iff Image of Sub-Basis Set is Open
snippet: Let $\struct {X_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {X_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\SS \subseteq \powerset {X_1}$ be a sub-basis of $\tau_1$. Let $f: X_1 \to X_2$ be an injection. Then: $f$ is an open mapping $\forall U \in \SS: f \sqbrk U \in \tau_2$

title: Injection to Image is Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \rightarrowtail T$ be an injection. Let $X \subseteq T$ be the image of $f$. Then the restriction $f {\restriction_{S \times X}}: S \to X$ of $f$ to the image of $f$ is a bijection of $S$ onto $X$.

title: Injective Closed Subspace of Banach Space is Topologically Complemented
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $E$ be a closed vector subspace of $X$ that is injective. Then $E$ is topologically complemented in $X$.

title: Injective Linear Transformation between Normed Vector Spaces sends Closed Unit Ball to Closed Unit Ball iff Isometric Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a injective linear transformation. Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball of $X$. Let $B_Y^-$ be the closed unit ball of $Y$. Then $T$ is an isometric isomorphism : $T \sqbrk {B_X^-} = B_Y^-$

title: Injective Module over Dedekind Domain
snippet: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain. Let $M$ be a $D$-module. Then $M$ is injective it is divisible.

title: Injective Module over Principal Ideal Domain
snippet: Let $D$ be a principal ideal domain. Let $M$ be a $D$-module. Then $M$ is injective it is divisible.

title: Injective Path-Connectedness in Uncountable Finite Complement Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on a uncountable set $S$. If the Continuum Hypothesis is accepted as true, then: $T$ is injectively path-connected $T$ is locally injectively path-connected.

title: Injective Path-Connectedness is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $a \sim b $ denote the relation: $a \sim b \iff a$ is injectively path-connected to $b$ where $a, b \in S$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Injective Path in Topological Space is Path
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f$ be an injective path in $T$. Then $f$ is a path in $T$.

title: Injective Quotient Mapping Equals Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Then: $f$ is an injective quotient mapping $f$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Injective Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator has Everywhere Dense Image
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a self-adjoint densely defined linear operator that is injective. Then $\Img T$ is everywhere dense in $\HH$.

title: Injective Separable Banach Space is Isometrically Isomorphic to Topologically Complemented Subspace of Space of Bounded Sequences
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a injective separable Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of bounded sequences. Then there exists a topologically complemented subspace $E$ of $\map {\ell_\infty} \GF$ that is isometrically isomorphic to $X$.

title: Injective iff Projective in Dual Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an abelian category. Let $X$ be an object in $\mathbf A$. Then: $X$ is injective in $\mathbf A$ $X$ is projective in the dual category $\mathbf A^{\mathrm{op}}$ of $\mathbf A$.

title: Injectively Path-Connected Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is injectively path-connected. Then $T$ is path-connected.

title: Injectively Path-Connected Space is not necessarily Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is injectively path-connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also locally arc-connected.

title: Injectivity Radius of Compact Riemannian Manifold is Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a compact Riemannian manifold. Let $\map {\operatorname{inj} } M$ be the injectivity radius of $M$. Then $\map {\operatorname{inj} } M > 0$.

title: Injectivity of Fourier transform over Lebesgue integrable functions
snippet: Fourier transform is injective over the space $\map {\mathrm L^1} {\R^N}$ {{explain|what is $\map {\mathrm L^1} {\R^N}$?}}

title: Injectivity of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $f$, $g$ be functions from $\R_{\ge 0} \to K$ of a real variable $t$, where $K \in \set {\R, \C}$. Further let $f$ and $g$ be continuous everywhere on their domains. Let $f$ and $g$ both admit Laplace transforms. Suppose that the Laplace transforms $\laptrans f$ and $\laptrans g$ satisfy: $\forall t \in \R_{\ge 0}: \laptrans {\map f t} = \laptrans {\map g t}$ Then $f = g$ everywhere on $\R_{\ge 0}$.

title: Inner Automorphism Group is Isomorphic to Quotient Group with Center
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\Inn G$ be the inner automorphism group of $G$. Let $\map Z G$ be the center of $G$. Let $G / \map Z G$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $\map Z G$. Then $G / \map Z G \cong \Inn G$.

title: Inner Automorphism Maps Subgroup to Itself iff Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. For $x \in G$, let $\kappa_x$ denote the inner automorphism of $x$ in $G$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\forall x \in G: \kappa_x \sqbrk H = H$ $H$ is a normal subgroup of $G$.

title: Inner Automorphism is Automorphism
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $x \in G$. Let $\kappa_x$ be the inner automorphism of $x$ in $G$. Then $\kappa_x$ is an automorphism of $G$.

title: Inner Automorphisms form Normal Subgroup of Automorphism Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Then the set $\Inn G$ of all inner automorphisms of $G$ is a normal subgroup of the automorphism group $\Aut G$ of $G$: $\Inn G \lhd \Aut G$

title: Inner Automorphisms form Subgroup of Automorphism Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Then the set $\Inn G$ of all inner automorphisms of $G$ forms a normal subgroup of the automorphism group $\Aut G$ of $G$: $\Inn G \le \Aut G$

title: Inner Automorphisms form Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma G, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $G$. Let $\Inn G$ denote the inner automorphism group of $G$. Then: $\Inn G \le \struct {\map \Gamma G, \circ}$ where $\le$ denotes the relation of being a subgroup.

title: Inner Jordan Content is Monotone
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \R^n$ be bounded subspaces of Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose that $A \subseteq B$. Then: $\map {m_*} A \le \map {m_*} B$ where $m_*$ denotes the inner Jordan content.

title: Inner Jordan Content is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subspace of Euclidean $n$-space. Let: {{eqn | l = R | r = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \closedint {a_i} {b_i} }} {{eqn | l = R' | r = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \closedint {a'_i} {b'_i} }} be closed $n$-rectangles that contain $M$. Then: $\map V R - \map {m^*} {R \setminus M} = \map V {R'} - \map {m^*} {R' \setminus M}$ where $\map V R$ denotes the content of a rectangle. Therefore, the inner Jordan content of $M$ is independent of the rectangle $R$ used to define it.

title: Inner Limit in Hausdorff Space by Open Neighborhoods
snippet: Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in a Hausdorff topological space $\struct {\XX, \tau}$. Let $x \in \XX$. Let $\map \mho x := \set {V \in \tau:\ x \in V}$ denote the set of open neighborhoods of $x$. Let $\NN_\infty$ denote the set of cofinite subsets of $\N$: $\NN_\infty := \set {N \subset \N: \N \setminus N \text{ is finite} }$ Then the inner limit of $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set {x \in \XX: \forall V \in \map \mho x: \exists N \in \NN_\infty: \forall n \in N: C_n \cap V \ne \O}$ or equivalently: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set…

title: Inner Limit in Hausdorff Space by Set Closures
snippet: Let $\struct {\XX, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in $\XX$. Then: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \bigcap_{N \mathop \in \NN_\infty^\#} \map \cl {\bigcup_{n \mathop \in N} C_n}$ where: $\cl$ denotes set closure $\NN_\infty^\#$ denotes the set of cofinal subsets of $\N$.

title: Inner Limit in Normed Spaces by Open Balls
snippet: Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in a normed vector space $\struct {\XX, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then the inner limit of $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set {x: \forall \epsilon > 0: \exists N \in \NN_\infty: \forall n \in N: x \in C_n + B_\epsilon}$ where $B_\epsilon$ denotes the open $\epsilon$-ball of the space.

title: Inner Limit is Closed Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff topological space. Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in $S$. Then the inner limit $\liminf_n C_n$ is a closed set.

title: Inner Limit of Sequence of Sets in Normed Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\XX, \norm {\, \cdot \, } }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in $\XX$. The inner limit of $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set {x \in X: \lim_n \map d {x, C_n} = 0}$ where $d$ stands for the point-to-set distance mapping.

title: Inner Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inner Products ==

title: Inner Product Induced by Positive Linear Operator is Inner Product
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a positive linear operator on $\HH$. Define $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_T : \map D T \times \map D T \to \C$ by: $\innerprod x y_T = \innerprod {\paren {T + I} x} y$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in \map D T \times \map D T$. Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_T$ is an inner product.

title: Inner Product Norm is Norm
snippet: Let $V$ be an inner product space over a subfield $\Bbb F$ of $\C$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ denote the inner product norm on $V$. Then $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ is a norm on $V$.

title: Inner Product Space is Uniformly Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Then $V$ is uniformly convex.

title: Inner Product is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a inner product space. Let $\norm \cdot$ be the inner product norm on $V$. Let $x, y \in V$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be sequences converging in $\struct {V, \norm \cdot}$ to $x$ and $y$ respectively. Then we have: $\innerprod {x_n} {y_n} \to \innerprod x y$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Inner Product is Sesquilinear
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $V$ be a inner product space over $V$ with inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$. Define the $f : V \times V \to \mathbb F$ by: $\map f {x, y} = \innerprod x y$ for each $x, y \in V$. Then $f$ is sesquilinear.

title: Inner Product on Space of Square Summable Mappings is Complex Inner Product
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\map {\ell^2} I$ be the space of square summable mappings over $I$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot: \map {\ell^2} I \times \map {\ell^2} I \to \GF$ be the inner product on $\map {\ell^2} I$. Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a complex inner product.

title: Inner Product with Vector is Bounded Linear Functional
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space over $\GF$. Let $v_0 \in V$. Then the mapping $L: V \to \GF$ defined by: $\map L v := \innerprod v {v_0}$ is a bounded linear functional with norm equal to $\norm {v_0}$.

title: Inner Product with Vector is Linear Functional
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct{ V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot }$ be an inner product space over $\GF$. Let $v_0 \in V$. Then the mapping $L: V \to \GF$ defined by: $\map L v := \innerprod v {v_0}$ is a linear functional.

title: Inner Product with Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $0_V$ be the zero vector of $V$. Then: $\innerprod {0_V} x = \innerprod x {0_V} = 0$ for all $x \in V$.
