title: Inradius in Terms of Circumradius
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Let $r$ denote the inradius of $\triangle ABC$. Let $R$ denote the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $r = 4 R \sin \dfrac A 2 \sin \dfrac B 2 \sin \dfrac C 2$

title: Inradius of Pythagorean Triangle is Integer
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a Pythagorean triangle. Let $r$ be the inradius of $\triangle ABC$. Then $r$ is an integer.

title: Inradius of Triangle in Terms of Exradii
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Then we have the following relation: $\dfrac 1 r = \dfrac 1 {\rho_a} + \dfrac 1 {\rho_b} + \dfrac 1 {\rho_c}$ where: $r$ is the inradius $\rho_a$, $\rho_b$ and $\rho_c$ are the exradii of $\triangle ABC$ $a$, $b$ and $c$ respectively.

title: Inscribe Square in Circle using Compasses Alone
snippet: == Problem == To inscribe a square in a given circle, by means of compass alone, supposing the center to be known.

title: Inscribed Angle Theorem
snippet: An inscribed angle is equal to half the angle that is subtended by that arc. 300px Thus, in the figure above: $\angle ABC = \frac 1 2 \angle ADC$ In a circle the angle at the center is double of the angle at the circumference, when the angles have the same circumference as base.

title: Inscribed Squares in Right-Angled Triangle
snippet: For any right-angled triangle, two squares can be inscribed inside it. One square would share a vertex with the right-angled vertex of the right-angled triangle: 200px The other square would have a side lying on the hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle: 400px

title: Inscribing Circle in Regular Pentagon
snippet: In any given regular pentagon it is possible to inscribe a circle.

snippet: Let $\Box ABCD$ be a square. It is required that $\triangle DGH$ be an equilateral triangle inscribed within $\Box ABCD$ such that vertex $D$ of $\triangle DGH$ coincides with vertex $D$ of $\Box ABCD$.

title: Inscribing Regular 15-gon in Circle
snippet: In a given circle, it is possible to inscribe a regular 15-gon.

title: Inscribing Regular Hexagon in Circle
snippet: In a given circle, it is possible to inscribe a regular hexagon.

title: Inscribing Regular Pentagon in Circle
snippet: In a given circle, it is possible to inscribe a regular pentagon.

Integer Addition Identity is Zero
snippet: The identity of integer addition is $0$: $\exists 0 \in \Z: \forall a \in \Z: a + 0 = a = 0 + a$

title: Integer Addition is Associative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x + \paren {y + z} = \paren {x + y} + z$

title: Integer Addition is Cancellable
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is cancellable: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x + z = y + z \implies x = y$

title: Integer Addition is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under addition: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a + b \in \Z$

title: Integer Addition is Commutative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is commutative: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x + y = y + x$

title: Integer Addition is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ be the semigroup of natural numbers under addition. Let $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$ be the (external) direct product of $\struct {\N, +}$ with itself, where $\oplus$ is the operation on $\N \times \N$ induced by $+$ on $\N$. Let $\boxtimes$ be the cross-relation defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ Let $\eqclass {x, y} {}$ denote the equivalence class of $\tuple {x, y}$ under $\boxtimes$. Let: $\paren {\N \times \N} / \boxtimes$ be the quotient set induced by $\boxtimes$.

title: Integer Arbitrarily Close to Rational in Valuation Ring of P-adic Norm
snippet:
Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime number $p$. Let $x \in \Q$ such that $
orm x_p \le 1$. Then for all $i \in \N$ there exists $\alpha \in \Z$ such that: $
orm {x - \alpha}_p \le p^{-i}$

title: Integer Combination of Coprime Integers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers, not both zero. Then: $a$ and $b$ are coprime there exists an integer combination of them equal to $1$: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a \perp b \iff \exists m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = 1$ In such an integer combination $m a + n b = 1$, the integers $m$ and $n$ are also coprime.

title: Integer Coprime to Factors is Coprime to Whole
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \Z$ be integers. Let: $a \perp b$ $a \perp c$ where $\perp$ denotes coprimality. Then: $a \perp b c$

title: Integer Coprime to Modulus iff Linear Congruence to 1 exists
snippet: Let $a, m \in \Z$. The linear congruence: $a x \equiv 1 \pmod m$ has a solution $x$ $a$ and $m$ are coprime.

title: Integer Coprime to all Factors is Coprime to Whole
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$. Let $\ds b = \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^r b_j$ Let $a$ be coprime to each of $b_1, \ldots, b_r$. Then $a$ is coprime to $b$.

title: Integer Divided by Divisor is Integer
snippet: Let $a, b \in \N$. Then: $b \divides a \implies \dfrac 1 b \times a \in \N$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibilty.

title: Integer Division/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Integer Division ==

title: Integer Divisor Results
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Let $m \divides n$ denote that $m$ is a divisor of $n$. The following results all hold:

title: Integer Divisor is Equivalent to Subset of Ideal
snippet: Let $\Z$ be the set of all integers. Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ and let $n \in \Z$. Let $\ideal m$ be the principal ideal of $\Z$ generated by $m$. Then: $m \divides n \iff \ideal n \subseteq \ideal m$

title: Integer Greater than 121 is Sum of Distinct Primes of form 4 n + 1
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $121$. Then $n$ can be expressed as the sum of distinct prime numbers of the form $4 n + 1$.

title: Integer Greater than 205 is Sum of Distinct Primes of form 6 n + 1
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $205$. Then $n$ can be expressed as the sum of distinct prime numbers of the form $6 n + 1$.

title: Integer Heronian Triangle can be Scaled so Area equals Perimeter
snippet: Let $T_1$ be an integer Heronian triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$. Then there exists a rational number $k$ such that the Heronian triangle $T_2$ whose sides are $k a$, $k b$ and $k c$ such that the perimeter of $T$ is equal to the area of $T$.

title: Integer Lattice/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Integer Lattices ==

title: Integer Less One divides Power Less One
snippet: Let $q, n \in \Z_{>0}$. Then: $\paren {q - 1} \divides \paren {q^n - 1}$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

title: Integer Multiple of Integer Combination is Integer Combination
snippet: == Lemma == Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $S = \set {a x + b y: x, y \in \Z}$ be the set of integer combinations of $a$ and $b$. Let $u \in S$. Let $n \in \Z$. Then $n u \in S$.

title: Integer Multiples Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {n \Z, +}$ is closed under addition.

title: Integer Multiples Closed under Multiplication
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {n \Z, \times}$ is closed under multiplication.

title: Integer Multiples Greater than Positive Integer Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Let $p \in \Z: p \ge 0$ be a positive integer. Let $S \subseteq n \Z$ be defined as: $S := \set {x \in n \Z: x > p}$ that is, the set of integer multiples of $n$ greater than $p$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, +}$ is closed under addition.

title: Integer Multiples Greater than Positive Integer Closed under Multiplication
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Let $p \in \Z: p \ge 0$ be a positive integer. Let $S \subseteq n \Z$ be defined as: $S := \set {x \in n \Z: x > p}$ that is, the set of integer multiples of $n$ greater than $p$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, \times}$ is closed under multiplication.

title: Integer Multiples form Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, +, \times}$ is a commutative ring. Unless $n = 1$, $\struct {n \Z, +, \times}$ is not a ring with unity.

title: Integer Multiples under Addition form Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, +}$ is a countably infinite cyclic group. It is generated by $n$ and $-n$: $n \Z = \gen n$ $n \Z = \gen {-n}$ Hence $\struct {n \Z, +}$ can be justifiably referred to as the additive group of integer multiples.

title: Integer Multiples under Addition form Subgroup of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$. Hence $\struct {n \Z, +}$ can be justifiably referred to as the additive group of integer multiples.

title: Integer Multiples under Multiplication form Semigroup
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, \times}$ is a semigroup. If $\size n > 1$ then $\struct {n \Z, \times}$ has no identity.

title: Integer Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is distributive over addition: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x \times \paren {y + z} = \paren {x \times y} + \paren {x \times z}$ $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: \paren {y + z} \times x = \paren {y \times x} + \paren {z \times x}$

title: Integer Multiplication Identity is One
snippet: The identity of integer multiplication is $1$: $\exists 1 \in \Z: \forall a \in \Z: a \times 1 = a = 1 \times a$

title: Integer Multiplication has Zero
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ has a zero element, which is $0$.

title: Integer Multiplication is Associative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x \times \paren {y \times z} = \paren {x \times y} \times z$

title: Integer Multiplication is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under multiplication: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a \times b \in \Z$

title: Integer Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is commutative: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x \times y = y \times x$

title: Integer Multiplication is Well-Defined
snippet: Integer multiplication is well-defined.

title: Integer Power Function is Bijective iff Index is Odd
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $f_n: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\map {f_n} x = x^n$ Then $f_n$ is a bijection $n$ is odd.

title: Integer Power of Root of Unity is Root of Unity
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $F$ be a field. Let $\alpha$ be an $n$-th root of unity. Let $k \in \Z$. Then: $\alpha^k$ is an $n$-th root of unity.

title: Integer Powers of 2 under Multiplication form Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of integers defined as: $S = \set {2^k: k \in \Z}$ Then $\struct {S, \times}$ is an infinite abelian group.

title: Integer Reciprocal Space contains Cauchy Sequence with no Limit
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $A$ has a Cauchy sequence which has no limit in $A$.

title: Integer Reciprocal Space is Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line $\R$ under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Then the integer reciprocal space $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ is a topological space.

title: Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero is Totally Separated
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $A$ is totally separated.

title: Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero is not Extremally Disconnected
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $A$ is not extremally disconnected.

title: Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero is not Locally Connected
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $A$ is not locally connected.

title: Integer Square Function is not Injective
snippet: == Example of Mapping which is Not an Injection == Let $f: \Z \to \Z$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \Z: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is not an injection.

title: Integer Square Function is not Surjective
snippet: == Example of Mapping which is Not a Surjection == Let $f: \Z \to \Z$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \Z: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is not a surjection.

title: Integer Subtraction is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under subtraction: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a - b \in \Z$

title: Integer and Fifth Power have same Last Digit
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $n^5$ has the same last digit as $n$ when both are expressed in conventional decimal notation.

title: Integer and its Double forming Pandigital Pair
snippet: $6729$ and its double contain all the digits from $1$ to $9$ between them.

title: Integer as Difference between Two Squares
Integer as Sum of 27 Primes
snippet: Every positive integer greater than $1$ can be expressed as the sum of no more than $27$ primes.

title: Integer as Sum of 2 Cubes in 3 Ways
snippet: $728$ is the smallest natural number which can be expressed as the sum of $2$ cubes in $3$ different ways: {{eqn | r = \paren {-1}^3 + 9^3 | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {-10}^3 + 12^3 | c = }}

title: Integer as Sum of 4 Cubes
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $n \not \equiv 4 \pmod 9$ and $n \not \equiv 5 \pmod 9$. Then it is possible to express $n$ as the sum of no more than $4$ cubes which may be either positive or negative.

title: Integer as Sum of 5 Non-Zero Squares
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 33$. Then $n$ can be expressed as the sum of $5$ non-zero squares.

title: Integer as Sum of Polygonal Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then $n$ is: $(1): \quad$ Either triangular or the sum of $2$ or $3$ triangular numbers $(2): \quad$ Either square or the sum of $2$, $3$ or $4$ square numbers $(3): \quad$ Either pentagonal or the sum of $2$, $3$, $4$ or $5$ pentagonal numbers and so on. That is: for all $k \ge 3$, $n$ is the sum of no more than $k$ polygonal numbers of order $k$.

title: Integer as Sum of Seven Positive Cubes
snippet: Every sufficiently large integer can be expressed as the sum of no more than $7$ positive cubes.

title: Integer as Sum of Three Odd Squares
snippet: Let $r$ be a positive integer. Then: $r \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ $r$ is the sum of $3$ odd squares.

title: Integer as Sum of Three Squares
snippet: Let $r$ be a positive integer. Then $r$ can be expressed as the sum of three squares it is not of the form: $4^n \paren {8 m + 7}$ for some $m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.

title: Integer as Sum of Two Squares
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Then: $n$ can be expressed as the sum of two squares each of its prime divisors of the form $4 k + 3$ (if any) occur to an even power.

title: Integer as Sums and Differences of Consecutive Squares
snippet: Every integer $k$ can be represented in infinitely many ways in the form: $k = \pm 1^2 \pm 2^2 \pm 3^3 \pm \dots \pm m^2$ for some (strictly) positive integer $m$ and some choice of signs $+$ or $-$.

title: Integer both Square and Triangular
snippet: Consider a pair of (strictly) positive integers $m$ and $n$ such that $n < m$. Then: $\dfrac m n$ is a best rational approximation to the square root of $2$ $\paren {m n}^2$ is both square and triangular.

title: Integer equals Ceiling iff Number between Integer and One Less
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ceiling x = n \iff n - 1 < x \le n$

title: Integer equals Ceiling iff between Number and One More
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ceiling x = n \iff x \le n < x + 1$

title: Integer equals Floor iff Number between Integer and One More
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\floor x = n \iff n \le x < n + 1$

title: Integer equals Floor iff between Number and One Less
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\floor x = n \iff x - 1 < n \le x$

title: Integer has Multiplicative Order Modulo n iff Coprime to n
snippet: Let $a$ and $n$ be integers. Let the multiplicative order of $a$ modulo $n$ exist. Then: $a \perp n$ that is, $a$ and $n$ are coprime.

title: Integer is Congruent Modulo Divisor to Remainder
snippet: Let $a \in \Z$. Let $a$ have a remainder $r$ on division by $m$. Then: $a \equiv r \pmod m$ where the notation denotes that $a$ and $r$ are congruent modulo $m$.

title: Integer is Congruent to Integer less than Modulus
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$. Then each integer is congruent (modulo $m$) to precisely one of the integers $0, 1, \ldots, m - 1$.

title: Integer is Coprime to 1
snippet: Every integer is coprime to $1$. That is: $\forall n \in \Z: n \perp 1$

title: Integer is Divisor Modulo m of Every Integer iff Coprime to m
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $n$ is coprime to $m$ $n$ is a divisor modulo $m$ to every integer.

title: Integer is Expressible as Product of Primes
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Then $n$ can be expressed as the product of one or more primes.

title: Integer is Sum of Three Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Then $n$ is the sum of $3$ triangular numbers.

title: Integer of form 6k + 5 is of form 3k + 2 but not Conversely
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer of the form: $n = 6 k + 5$ where $k \in \Z$. Then $n$ can also be expressed in the form: $n = 3 k + 2$ for some other $k \in \Z$. However it is not necessarily the case that if $n$ can be expressed in the form: $n = 3 k + 2$ then it can also be expressed in the form: $n = 6 k + 5$

title: Integer to Power of Itself Falling is Factorial
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. $n^{\underline n} = n!$ where: $n^{\underline n}$ denotes the falling factorial $n!$ denotes the factorial.

title: Integer to Power of Itself Less One Falling is Factorial
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. $n^{\underline {n - 1} } = n!$ where: $n^{\underline {n - 1} }$ denotes the falling factorial $n!$ denotes the factorial.

title: Integer to Power of Multiple of Order
snippet: Let $a$ and $n$ be integers. Let $a \perp n$, that is, let $a$ and $b$ be coprime. Let $c \in \Z_{>0}$ be the multiplicative order of $a$ modulo $n$. Then $a^k \equiv 1 \pmod n$ $k$ is a multiple of $c$.

title: Integer to Power of p-1 over 2 Modulo p
snippet: Let $a \in \Z$. Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $b = a^{\frac {\paren {p - 1} } 2}$. Then one of the following cases holds: $b \bmod p = 0$ which happens exactly when $a \equiv 0 \pmod p$, or: $b \bmod p = 1$ or: $b \bmod p = p - 1$ where: $b \bmod p$ denotes the modulo operation $x \equiv y \pmod p$ denotes that $x$ is congruent modulo $p$ to $y$.

title: Integer to Rational Power is Irrational iff not Integer or Reciprocal
snippet: Let $m$ be a rational number. Let $n$ be a positive integer. Then $n^m$ is an irrational number $n^{\size m}$ is not an integer.

title: Integer which is Multiplied by 9 when moving Last Digit to First
snippet: Let $N$ be the positive integer: $N = 10 \, 112 \, 359 \, 550 \, 561 \, 797 \, 752 \, 808 \, 988 \, 764 \, 044 \, 943 \, 820 \, 224 \, 719$ $N$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that if you move the last digit to the front, the result is the positive integer $9 N$.

title: Integer which is Multiplied by Last Digit when moving Last Digit to First
snippet: Let $N$ be a positive integer expressed in decimal notation in the form: $N = \sqbrk {a_k a_{k - 1} a_{k - 2} \ldots a_2 a_1}_{10}$ Let $N$ be such that when you multiply it by $a_1$, you get: $a_1 N = \sqbrk {a_1 a_k a_{k - 1} \ldots a_3 a_2}_{10}$ Then at least one such $N$ is equal to the recurring part of the fraction: $q = \dfrac {a_1} {10 a_1 - 1}$

title: Integer which is Sum of 3 Fourth Powers in 2 Ways and Products of Those Roots
snippet: The positive integer $256 \, 103 \, 393$ can be expressed as the sum of $3$ fourth powers in $2$ different ways: Also note that:

title: Integer whose Digits when Grouped in 3s add to Multiple of 999 is Divisible by 999
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer which has at least $3$ digits when expressed in decimal notation. Let the digits of $n$ be divided into groups of $3$, counting from the right, and those groups added. Then the result is equal to a multiple of $999$ $n$ is divisible by $999$.

title: Integers Coprime to Zero
snippet: The only integers which are coprime to zero are $1$ and $-1$. That is: $n \in \Z: n \perp 0 \iff n \in \set {1, -1}$ In particular, note that two integers which are coprime to each other cannot both be $0$.

title: Integers Differing by 2 with Same Divisor Sum
snippet: Let $\sigma_1: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the divisor sum function, defined on the strictly positive integers. The equation: $\map {\sigma_1} n = \map {\sigma_1} {n + 2}$ is satisfied by integers in the sequence: $33, 54, 284, 366, 834, 848, 918, 1240, 1504, 2910, 2913, 3304, \ldots$

title: Integers Divided by GCD are Coprime
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers which are not both zero. Let $d$ be a common divisor of $a$ and $b$, that is: $\dfrac a d, \dfrac b d \in \Z$ Then: $\gcd \set {a, b} = d$ $\gcd \set {\dfrac a d, \dfrac b d} = 1$ that is: $\dfrac a {\gcd \set {a, b} } \perp \dfrac b {\gcd \set {a, b} }$ where: $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor $\perp$ denotes coprimality.

title: Integers Modulo m under Addition form Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ is the set of integers modulo $m$ Let $+_m$ be the operation of addition modulo $m$. Then the structure $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ is an abelian group.

title: Integers Modulo m under Addition form Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$. Let $+_m$ be the operation of addition modulo $m$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. Then $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ is a cyclic group of order $m$, generated by the element $\eqclass 1 m \in \Z_m$.

title: Integers Modulo m under Max Operation form Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ denote the set of integers modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {0, 1, \ldots, m - 1}$ Let $\vee_m$ be the operation on $\Z_m$ defined as: $\forall a, b \in \Z_m: a \vee_m b = \max \set {a, b}$ Then the ordered algebraic structure $\struct {\Z_m, \vee_m, \le}$ is an ordered semigroup.

title: Integers Modulo m under Multiplication form Commutative Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_m, \times_m}$ denote the algebraic structure such that: $\Z_m$ is the set of integers modulo $m$ $\times_m$ denotes the operation of multiplication modulo $m$. Then $\struct {\Z_m, \times_m}$ is a commutative monoid.

title: Integers Representable as Product of both 3 and 4 Consecutive Integers
snippet: There are $3$ integers which can be expressed as both $x \paren {x + 1} \paren {x + 2} \paren {x + 3}$ for some $x$, and $y \paren {y + 1} \paren {y + 2}$ for some $y$: $24, 120, 175 \, 560$

title: Integers are Arbitrarily Close to P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Z_p$. Then for $n \in \N$ there exists unique $\alpha \in \Z$: $(1): \quad 0 \le \alpha \le p^n - 1$ $(2): \quad \norm { x -\alpha}_p \le p^{-n}$

title: Integers are Coprime iff Powers are Coprime
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Then: $a \perp b \iff \forall n \in \N: a^n \perp b^n$ That is, two integers are coprime all their positive integer powers are coprime.

title: Integers are Countably Infinite
snippet: The set $\Z$ of integers is countably infinite.

title: Integers are Dense in P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $d_p$ be the metric induced by the norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ restricted to the $p$-adic integers. The integers $\Z$ are dense in the metric space $\struct{\Z_p, d_p}$.

title: Integers are Euclidean Domain
snippet: The integers $\Z$ with the mapping $\nu: \Z \to \Z$ defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \nu x = \size x$ form a Euclidean domain.

title: Integers are not Densely Ordered
snippet: The integers $\Z$ are not densely ordered. That is: $\forall n \in \Z: \not \exists m \in \Z: n < m < n + 1$

title: Integers as Sum of Three Pairwise Coprime Integers
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer greater than $17$. Then $n$ is the sum of $3$ integers greater than $1$ which are pairwise coprime.

title: Integers do not form Field
snippet: == Corollary of Invertible Integers under Multiplication == The integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ do not form a field.

title: Integers for which Divisor Sum of Phi equals Divisor Sum
snippet: The following positive integers have the property that the divisor sum of their Euler $\phi$ value equals their divisor sum: $\map {\sigma_1} {\map \phi n} = \map {\sigma_1} n$ $1, 87, 362, 1257, 1798, 5002, 9374, \ldots$

title: Integers form Commutative Ring
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ forms a commutative ring under addition and multiplication.

title: Integers form Commutative Ring with Unity
snippet: The integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ form a commutative ring with unity under addition and multiplication.

title: Integers form Integral Domain
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ form an integral domain under addition and multiplication.

title: Integers form Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: The integers $\Z$ form an ordered integral domain under addition and multiplication.

title: Integers form Subdomain of Rationals
snippet: The integral domain of integers $\left({\Z, +, \times}\right)$ forms a subdomain of the field of rational numbers.

title: Integers form Subdomain of Reals
snippet: The integral domain of integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ forms a subdomain of the field of real numbers.

title: Integers form Subring of Reals
snippet: The ring of integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ forms a subring of the field of real numbers.

title: Integers form Totally Ordered Ring
snippet: The structure $\struct {\Z, +, \times, \le}$ is a totally ordered ring.

title: Integers form Unique Factorization Domain
snippet: The integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ form a unique factorization domain.

title: Integers not Expressible as Sum of Distinct Primes of form 6n-1
snippet: $161$ is the largest integer that cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct primes of the form $6 n - 1$. The following integers cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct primes of the form $6 n - 1$: $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30, 31, 32, 35, 36, 37, 38, 42, 43, 44, 48, 49, 50,$ $54, 55, 60, 61, 65, 66, 67, 72, 73, 77, 78, 79, 84, 90, 91, 95, 96, 102, 108, 114, 119, 120, 125, 143, 155, 161$

title: Integers not Sum of Distinct Triangular Numbers
snippet: The sequence of integers which cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct triangular numbers is: $2, 5, 8, 12, 23, 33$

title: Integers such that Difference with Power of 2 is always Prime
snippet: == Unproven Hypothesis == The following positive integers are believed to be the only values of $n$ such that: $\forall k > 0: n - 2^k$ is prime whenever $n - 2^k$ is (strictly) positive: $4, 7, 15, 21, 45, 75, 105$

title: Integers such that all Coprime and Less are Prime
snippet: The following positive integers have the property that all positive integers less than and coprime to it, excluding $1$, are prime: $1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 18, 24, 30$ There are no other positive integers with this property.

title: Integers under Addition form Abelian Group
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms an abelian group.

title: Integers under Addition form Group
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms a group.

title: Integers under Addition form Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: The additive group of integers $\struct {\Z, +}$ is an infinite cyclic group which is generated by the element $1 \in \Z$.

title: Integers under Addition form Monoid
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms a monoid.

title: Integers under Addition form Semigroup
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms a semigroup.

title: Integers under Addition form Totally Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Let $\le$ be the usual ordering on $\Z$. Then the ordered structure $\struct {\Z, +, \le}$ is a totally ordered group.

title: Integers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ does not form a group.

title: Integers under Multiplication form Countably Infinite Commutative Monoid
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a countably infinite commutative monoid.

title: Integers under Multiplication form Countably Infinite Semigroup
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a countably infinite semigroup.

title: Integers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a monoid.

title: Integers under Multiplication form Semigroup
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a semigroup.

title: Integers under Subtraction do not form Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, -}$ denote the algebraic structure formed by the set of integers under the operation of subtraction. Then $\struct {\Z, -}$ is not a group.

title: Integers under Subtraction do not form Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, -}$ denote the algebraic structure formed by the set of integers under the operation of subtraction. Then $\struct {\Z, -}$ is not a semigroup.

title: Integers under Subtraction form Magma
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ under the operation of subtraction forms a magma.

title: Integers which are Divisor Sum for 3 Integers
snippet: The sequence of integers which are the divisor sum of $3$ different integers begins: $24, 42, 48, 60, 84, 90, \ldots$

title: Integers whose Divisor Count equals Cube Root
snippet: There are $3$ positive integers whose divisor count function equals its cube root: {{eqn | l = 1 = 1^3 | o = : | r = \map {\sigma_0} 1 = 1 | c = }} {{eqn | l = 21 \, 952 = 28^3 | o = : | r = \map {\sigma_0} {21 \, 952} = 28 | c = }} {{eqn | l = 64 \, 000 = 40^3 | o = : | r = \map {\sigma_0} {64 \, 000} = 40 | c = }}

title: Integers whose Divisor Sum equals Half Phi times Divisor Count
snippet: The following positive integers $n$ have the property where: $\map {\sigma_1} n = \dfrac {\map \phi n \times \map {\sigma_0} n} 2$ where: $\map {\sigma_1} n$ denotes the divisor sum function: the sum of the divisors of $n$ $\map \phi n$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function: the count of positive integers smaller than of $n$ which are coprime to $n$ $\map {\sigma_0} n$ denotes the divisor count function: the count of the divisors of $n$: These positive integers are: $35, 105, \ldots$

title: Integers whose Divisor Sum is Cube
snippet: The following positive integers are those whose divisor sum is a cube: $1, 7, 102, 110, 142, 159, 187, 381, 690, 714, 770, 994, 1034, \ldots$

title: Integers whose Number of Representations as Sum of Two Primes is Maximum
snippet: $210$ is the largest integer which can be represented as the sum of two primes in the maximum number of ways. The full list of such numbers is as follows: $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 60, 90, 210$ The list contains: $n \le 8$ $n \le 18$ where $2 \divides n$ $n \le 48$ where $2 \times 3 \divides n$ $n \le 90$ where $2 \times 3 \times 5 \divides n$ $210 = 2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7$

title: Integers whose Phi times Divisor Count equal Divisor Sum
snippet: The positive integers whose Euler $\phi$ function multiplied by its divisor count function equals its divisor sum are: $1, 3, 14, 42$

title: Integers whose Ratio between Divisor Sum and Phi is Square
snippet: The sequence of integers whose divisor sum divided by its Euler $\phi$ value is a square begins: $1, 14, 30, 105, 248, 264, 418, 714, 1485, 3080, \ldots$

title: Integers whose Squares end in 444
snippet: The sequence of positive integers whose square ends in $444$ begins: $38, 462, 538, 962, 1038, 1462, 1538, 1962, 2038, 2462, 2538, 2962, 3038, 3462, \ldots$

title: Integers with Metric Induced by P-adic Valuation
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $d: \Z^2 \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \map d {x, y} = \begin {cases} 0 & : x = y \\ \dfrac 1 r & : x - y = p^{r - 1} k: r \in \N_{>0}, k \in \Z, p \nmid k \end {cases}$ Then $d$ is a metric on $\Z$.

title: Integers with Prime Values of Divisor Sum
snippet: The sequence of integers whose divisor sum is prime begins: {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} 2 | r = 3 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} 4 | r = 7 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} 6 | r = 13 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} {16} | r = 31 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} {25} | r = 31 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} {64} | r = 127 }} {{eqn | l = \map {\sigma_1} {289} | r = 307 }}

title: Integrability Theorem for Functions Continuous on Open Intervals
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on a closed interval $\closedint a b$ such that $a < b$. Let $f$ be continuous on $\openint a b$. Let the one-sided limits $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map f x$ and $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to b^-} \map f x$ exist. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable on $\closedint a b$.

title: Integrable Function is A.E. Real-Valued
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then $\map f x \in \R$ for almost all $x \in X$.

title: Integrable Function with Zero Integral on Sub-Sigma-Algebra is A.E. Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\GG$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\GG$-integrable function. Suppose that, for all $G \in \GG$: $\ds \int_G f \rd \mu = 0$ Then $f = 0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

title: Integrable Functions with Equal Integrals on Sub-Sigma-Algebra are A.E. Equal
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\GG$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\GG$-integrable functions. Suppose that, for all $G \in \GG$: $\ds \int_G f \rd \mu = \int_G g \rd \mu$ Then $f = g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

title: Integral Closure is Integrally Closed
snippet: Let $A \subseteq B$ be an extension of commutative rings with unity. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$. Then $C$ is integrally closed.

title: Integral Closure is Subring
snippet: Let $A$ be an extension of a commutative ring with unity $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $A$. Then $C$ is a subring of $A$.

title: Integral Domain/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Integral Domains ==

title: Integral Domain iff Zero Ideal is Prime
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. $(1): \quad A$ is an integral domain $(2): \quad$ the zero ideal $\ideal 0 \subseteq A$ is prime

title: Integral Domain is Reduced Ring
snippet: Let $\left({D, +, \circ}\right)$ be an integral domain. Then $D$ is reduced.

title: Integral Domain of Prime Order is Field
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_p, +_p, \times_p}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $p$. {{item|(2):|$\struct {\Z_p, +_p, \times_p}$ is an integral domain.}} {{item|(3):|$\struct {\Z_p, +_p, \times_p}$ is a field.}}

title: Integral Domain with Characteristic Zero
snippet: In an integral domain with characteristic zero, every non-zero element has infinite order under ring addition.

title: Integral Expression of Harmonic Number
snippet: Let $\sequence {H_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the harmonic numbers. Then: $\ds H_n = 1 + \int_1 ^n \dfrac {\floor u} {u^2} \rd u$ where $\floor u$ denotes the floor of $u$.

title: Integral Form of Gamma Function equivalent to Euler Form
Integral Form of Polygamma Function
snippet: Let $z$ be a complex number with a positive real part. Then: $\ds \map {\psi_n} z = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} \int_0^\infty \frac {t^n e^{-z t} } {1 - e^{-t} } \rd t$ where $\map {\psi_n} z$ denotes the $n$th polygamma function.

title: Integral Form of Ramanujan Phi Function
snippet: $\ds \map \phi x = \int_{\to 0}^{\to 1} \paren {\dfrac {u^{x - 2} \paren {1 - u}^2} {1 - u^x} } \rd u + 1$ where: $\map \phi x$ denotes the Ramanujan phi function $x \in \C$ $\map \Re x > 1$

title: Integral Ideal iff Set of Integer Multiples
snippet: Let $J$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers $\Z$. Then: $J$ is an integral ideal $\exists m \in \Z: J = m \Z$.

title: Integral Ideal is Ideal of Ring
snippet: Let $J$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers $\Z$. Then: $J$ is an integral ideal $J$ is an ideal of the ring of integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$.

title: Integral Ideal is Set of Integer Multiples
snippet: Let $J$ be an integral ideal. Then $J$ is in the form of a set of integer multiples $m \Z$ for some $m \in \Z$.

title: Integral Multiple Distributes over Ring Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring, or a field. Let $a, b \in R$ and $m, n \in \Z$. Then: $(1): \quad \paren {m + n} \cdot a = \paren {m \cdot a} + \paren {n \cdot a}$ $(2): \quad m \cdot \paren {a + b} = \paren {m \cdot a} + \paren {m \cdot b}$ where $m \cdot a$ is as defined in integral multiple.

title: Integral Multiple of Integral Multiple
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field. Let $a \in F$ and $m, n \in \Z$. Then: $\paren {m n} \cdot a = m \cdot \paren {n \cdot a}$ where $n \cdot a$ is as defined in integral multiple.

title: Integral Multiple of Ring Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $n \cdot x$ be an integral multiple of $x$: $n \cdot x = \begin {cases} 0_R & : n = 0 \\ x & : n = 1 \\ \paren {n - 1} \cdot x + x & : n > 1 \end {cases}$ that is: $n \cdot x = \underbrace {x + x + \cdots + x}_{\text {$n$ times} }$ For $n < 0$ we use: $n \cdot x = \paren{-n} \cdot \paren {-x}$ Then: $\forall n \in \Z: \forall x \in R: \paren {n \cdot x} \circ x = n \cdot \paren {x \circ x} = x \circ \paren {n \cdot x}$

title: Integral Multiple of an Algebraic Number
snippet: Let $K$ be a number field and $\alpha \in K$. Then there exists a positive $n \in \Z$ such that $n \alpha \in \OO_K$. In this context, $ \OO_K$ denotes the algebraic integers in $K$.

title: Integral Operator is Linear
snippet: Let $T$ be an integral operator. Let $f$ and $g$ be integrable real functions on a domain appropriate to $T$. Then $T$ is a linear operator: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \R: \map T {\alpha f + \beta g} = \alpha \map T f + \beta \map T g$

title: Integral Points of Elliptic Curve y^2 = x^3+3x
snippet: 200px The elliptic curve: $y^2 = x^3 + 3 x$ has exactly $7$ lattice points: $\tuple {0, 0}, \tuple {1, \pm 2}, \tuple {3, \pm 6}, \tuple {12, \pm 42}$

title: Integral Representation of Bernoulli Number
snippet: Bernoulli numbers can be expressed in integral form as follows: $\ds \size {B_{2 n} } = 4 n \int_0^\infty \frac {t^{2 n - 1} } {e^{2 \pi t} - 1} \rd t$ where: $B_n$ are the Bernoulli numbers $n$ is a positive integer.

title: Integral Representation of Bessel Function of the First Kind
snippet: Let $\map {J_n} x$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$.

title: Integral Representation of Dirichlet Beta Function in terms of Gamma Function
snippet: $\ds \map \beta s = \frac 1 {\map \Gamma s} \int_0^\infty \frac {x^{s - 1} e^{-x} } {1 + e^{-2 x} } \rd x$ where: $\beta$ denotes the Dirichlet beta function $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > 0$.

title: Integral Representation of Dirichlet Eta Function in terms of Gamma Function
snippet: $\ds \map \eta s = \frac 1 {\map \Gamma s} \int_0^\infty \frac {x^{s - 1} } {e^x + 1} \rd x$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > 0$ $\eta$ denotes the Dirichlet eta function $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function.

title: Integral Representation of Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Fractional Part
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\sigma > 1$. Then $\ds \map \zeta s = \frac s {s - 1} - s \int_1^\infty \fractpart x x^{-s - 1} \rd x$ where $\fractpart x$ denotes the fractional part of $x$.

title: Integral Representation of Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Gamma Function
snippet: For $\Re \paren s > 1$, the Riemann Zeta function is given by: $\ds \map \zeta s = \frac 1 {\map \Gamma s} \int_0^\infty \frac {t^{s - 1}} {e^t - 1} \rd t$ where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function.

title: Integral Representation of Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Jacobi Theta Function
snippet: Let $s \in \C: \map \Re s > 1$. Let $x \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\ds \pi^{-s / 2} \map \Gamma {\frac s 2} \map \zeta s = -\frac 1 {s \paren {1 - s} } + \dfrac 1 2 \int_1^\infty \paren {x^{s / 2 - 1} + x^{-\paren {s + 1} / 2} } \paren {\map {\vartheta_3} {0, e^{-\pi x} } - 1} \rd x$ where: $\map \Gamma s$ is the gamma function $\map \zeta s$ is the Riemann zeta function $\ds \map {\vartheta_3} {0, e^{-\pi x} }$ is the Jacobi theta function of the third type.

title: Integral Resulting in Arcsecant
snippet: $\ds \int \frac 1 {x \sqrt {x^2 - a^2} } \rd x = \begin{cases} \dfrac 1 {\size a} \arcsec \dfrac x {\size a} + C & : x > \size a \\ -\dfrac 1 {\size a} \arcsec \dfrac x {\size a} + C & : x where $a$ is a constant.

title: Integral Transform is Mapping
snippet: Let $\map F p$ be an integral transform: $\map F p = \ds \int_a^b \map f x \map K {p, x} \rd x$ Let $T$ be the integral operator associated with $\map F p$. Then $T$ is a mapping from the domain of $T$ to its image. That is, for every $\map f x$ there exists a unique $\map F p$.

title: Integral between Limits is Independent of Direction
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is integrable on the interval $\openint a b$. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \int_a^b \map f {a + b - x} \rd x$

title: Integral from 0 to 1 of Complete Elliptic Integral of First Kind
snippet: Let $G$ denote Catalan's constant. Then: $2 G = \ds \int_0^1 \map K k \rd k$ where $\map K k$ denotes the complete elliptic integral of the first kind: $\map K k = \ds \int \limits_0^{\pi / 2} \dfrac {\d \phi} {\sqrt {1 - k^2 \sin^2 \phi} }$

title: Integral of Arcsine Function
snippet: $\ds \int \arcsin x \rd x = x \arcsin x + \sqrt {1 - x^2} + C$ for $x \in \closedint {-1} 1$.

title: Integral of Bounded Measurable Function with respect to Finite Signed Measure is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\mu$ be a finite signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\tuple {\mu^+, \mu^-}$ be the Jordan decomposition of $\mu$. Then the $\mu$-integral of $f$ defined by: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu^+ - \int f \rd \mu^-$ is well-defined.

title: Integral of Characteristic Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $E \in \Sigma$ be a measurable set, and let $\chi_E: X \to \R$ be its characteristic function. Then $\map {I_\mu} {\chi_E} = \map \mu E$, where $\map {I_\mu} {\chi_E}$ is the $\mu$-integral of $\chi_E$.

title: Integral of Compactly Supported Function
snippet: Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a continuous real function. Let $K \subset \R$ be a compact subset, say, $\closedint a b$. Let $K$ be the support of $f$: $\map \supp f = K$. Then: $\ds \int_{- \infty}^\infty \map f x \rd x = \int_a^b \map f x \rd x$

title: Integral of Constant
snippet: Let $c$ be a constant.

title: Integral of Dirac Delta Function by Continuous Function over Reals
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Let $g$ be a continuous real function. Then: $\ds \int_{- \infty}^{+ \infty} \map \delta x \map g x \rd x = \map g 0$

title: Integral of Dirac Delta Function over Reals
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Then: $\ds \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \map \delta x \rd x = 1$

title: Integral of Distribution Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space and $f$ be a $\mu$-measurable function. Let $p > 0, r \geq 0$. For $\lambda > 0$, let $E_\lambda = \set {x \in X: \size {\map f x} > \lambda}$, so that $\map m \lambda = \map \mu {E_\lambda}$ is the distribution function of $f$. Then: $\ds \int_0^\infty p \lambda^{p - 1} \int_{E_\lambda} \size f^r \rd \mu \rd \lambda = \int_X \size f^{p + r} \rd \mu$ and in particular: $\ds \int_0^\infty p \lambda^{p - 1} \map m \lambda \rd \lambda = \int_X \size f^p \rd \mu$

title: Integral of Exponent of Half Square over Reals
snippet: $\ds \int_{\mathop \to -\infty}^{\mathop \to +\infty} e^{- x^2 / 2} \rd x = \sqrt {2 \pi}$

title: Integral of Generating Function
snippet: Let $\map G z$ be the generating function for the sequence $\sequence {a_n}$. Then: {{eqn | l = \int_0^z \map G t \rd t | r = \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \dfrac {a_{k - 1} z^k} k | c = }} {{eqn | r = a_0 z + \dfrac {a_1 z^2} 2 + \dfrac {a_2 z^3} 3 + \dfrac {a_3 z^4} 4 + \cdots | c = }}

title: Integral of Horizontal Section of Measurable Function gives Measurable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X, \mu}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y, \nu}$ be $\sigma$-finite measure spaces. Let $f : X \times Y \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$-measurable function, where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Define the function $g : X \to \overline \R$ by: $\ds \map g y = \int f^y \rd \mu$ where $f^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $f$. Then: $g$ is $\Sigma_Y$-measurable.

title: Integral of Increasing Function Composed with Measurable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space. Let $f: X \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive measurable function. Let $\phi: \R_{\ge 0} \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be a continuously differentiable, increasing function such that $\map \phi 0 = 0$. Then: $\ds \int \phi \circ f \rd \mu = \int_0^\infty \map {\phi'} t \map F t \rd t$ where: $F$ is the survival function of $f$ $\ds \int_0^\infty$ denotes an improper integral.

title: Integral of Integrable Function is Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $f + g$ is $\mu$-integrable, with: $\ds \int \paren {f + g} \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu + \int g \rd \mu$

title: Integral of Integrable Function is Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Let $\lambda \in \R$. Let $\lambda f$ be the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$. Then $\lambda f$ is $\mu$-integrable, and: $\ds \int \lambda f \rd \mu = \lambda \int f \rd \mu$

title: Integral of Integrable Function is Monotone
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Suppose that $f \le g$ pointwise. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu \le \int g \rd \mu$

title: Integral of Integrable Function over Measurable Set is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $E \in \Sigma$. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then the $\mu$-integral of $f$ over $E$: $\ds \int_E f \rd \mu = \int f \cdot \chi_E \rd \mu$ is well-defined.

title: Integral of Integrable Function over Null Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Let $N$ be a $\mu$-null set. Then: $\ds \int_N f \rd \mu = 0$ where $\ds \int_N$ signifies an integral over $N$.

title: Integral of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le A$. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then: $\ds \laptrans {\dfrac {\map f t} t} = \int_s^{\to \infty} \map F u \rd u$ wherever $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to 0} \dfrac {\map f t} t$ and $\laptrans f$ exist.

title: Integral of Modulus of Continuous Real Function is Zero iff Zero Function
snippet: Let $I$ be an open interval. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $I$. Let $f : I \to \R$ be a continuous real function such that: $\ds \int_I \size f \rd \lambda = 0$ Then $f = 0$.

title: Integral of Positive Function with respect to Counting Measure on Natural Numbers
snippet: Consider the measure space $\struct {\N, \powerset \N, \mu}$ where $\mu$ is the counting measure on $\struct {\N, \powerset \N}$. Let $f : \N \to \R$ be a function. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map f n$

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function Extends Integral of Positive Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \R, f \in \EE^+$ be a positive simple function. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \map {I_\mu} f$ where: $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ denotes the $\mu$-integral of positive measurable functions $I_\mu$ denotes the $\mu$-integral of positive simple functions. That is: $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu \restriction_{\EE^+} = I_\mu$ using the notion of restriction, $\restriction$.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function as Limit of Integrals of Positive Simple Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a positive simple function, such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n = f$ and: for each $x \in X$, the sequence $\sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing where $\lim$ denotes a pointwise limit. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the integral signs denote $\mu$-integration.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ and $g : X \to \overline \R$ be positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then: $\ds \int \paren {f + g} \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu + \int g \rd \mu$ where: $f + g$ is the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$ the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration This can be summarized by saying that $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ is additive.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Monotone
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Suppose that $f \le g$, where $\le$ denotes pointwise inequality. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu \le \int g \rd \mu$ where the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration. This can be summarized by saying that $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ is monotone.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Positive Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\lambda \in \overline \R$ be an extended real number with $\lambda \ge 0$. Then: $\ds \int \lambda f \rd \mu = \lambda \int f \rd \mu$ where: $\lambda f$ is the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$ The integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration This can be summarized by saying that $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ is positive homogeneous.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function over Disjoint Union
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\sequence {D_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of pairwise disjoint $\Sigma$-measurable sets. Let: $\ds D = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty D_n$ Then: $\ds \int_D f \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \int_{D_n} f \rd \mu$

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function over Measurable Set is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $A \in \Sigma$. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then the $\mu$-integral of $f$ over $A$ defined by: $\ds \int_A f \rd \mu = \int \paren {\chi_A \cdot f} \rd \mu$ is well-defined.

title: Integral of Positive Measurable Function with respect to Restricted Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\GG \subseteq \Sigma$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Let $\mu \restriction_\GG$ be the restriction of $\mu$ to $\GG$. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\GG$-measurable function. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu \restriction_\GG$

title: Integral of Positive Simple Function is Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \R$, $f, g \in \EE^+$ be positive simple functions. Then $\map {I_\mu} {f + g} = \map {I_\mu} f + \map {I_\mu} g$, where: $f + g$ is the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$ $I_\mu$ denotes $\mu$-integration This can be summarized by saying that $I_\mu$ is additive.

title: Integral of Positive Simple Function is Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \R$, $f, g \in \EE^+$ be positive simple functions. Suppose that: $f \le g$ where $\le$ denotes pointwise inequality. Then: $\map {I_\mu} f \le \map {I_\mu} g$ where $I_\mu$ denotes $\mu$-integration This can be summarized by saying that $I_\mu$ is an increasing mapping.

title: Integral of Positive Simple Function is Positive Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \R, f \in \EE^+$ be a positive simple function. Let $\lambda \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive real number. Then: $\map {I_\mu} {\lambda \cdot f} = \map {\lambda \cdot I_\mu} f$ where: $\lambda \cdot f$ is the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$ $I_\mu$ denotes $\mu$-integration. This can be summarized by saying that $I_\mu$ is positive homogeneous.

title: Integral of Positive Simple Function is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \R, f \in \EE^+$ be a positive simple function. Then the $\mu$-integral of $f$, $\map {I_\mu} f$, is well-defined. That is, for any two standard representations for $f$, say: $\ds f = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n a_i \chi_{E_i} = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m b_j \chi_{F_j}$ it holds that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n a_i \map \mu {E_i} = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m b_j \map \mu {F_j}$

title: Integral of Power
snippet: $\ds \forall n \in \R_{\ne -1}: \int_0^b x^n \rd x = \frac {b^{n + 1} } {n + 1}$

title: Integral of Probability Density Function over the Reals is Equal to One
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be an absolutely continuous random variable. Let $f_X$ be a probability density function for $X$. Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Then: $\ds \int_\R f_X \rd \lambda = 1$ where $\ds \int_\R f_X \rd \lambda$ denotes the Lebesgue integral of $f_X$.

title: Integral of Product of Exponential with Sine or Cosine
Integral of Series of Positive Measurable Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of positive measurable functions. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be the pointwise series of the $f_n$. Then: $\ds \int \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration.

title: Integral of Survival Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space. Let $f: X \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $F_f : \R \to \R$ be the survival function of $f$. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \int_{\openint 0 \to} F_f \rd \lambda$ where $\lambda$ is Lebesgue measure.

title: Integral of Vertical Section of Measurable Function gives Measurable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X, \mu}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y, \nu}$ be $\sigma$-finite measure spaces. Let $f : X \times Y \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$-measurable function, where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Define the function $g : X \to \overline \R$ by: $\ds \map g x = \int f_x \rd \nu$ where $f_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $f$. Then: $g$ is $\Sigma_X$-measurable.

title: Integral on L-1 Space is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {L^1} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be the $L^1$ space of $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Let $E \in \map {L^1} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Then the $\mu$-integral of $E$ is well-defined.

title: Integral over 2 pi of Cosine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\alpha \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \pi & : m = n \end {cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \cos m x \cos n x \rd x = \pi \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Integral over 2 pi of Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \cos m x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne 0 \\ 2 \pi & : m = 0 \end {cases}$

title: Integral over 2 pi of Sine of m x by Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\alpha \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \sin m x \cos n x \rd x = 0$

title: Integral over 2 pi of Sine of m x by Sine of n x
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\alpha \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne n \\ \pi & : m = n \end {cases}$ That is: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \sin m x \sin n x \rd x = \pi \delta_{m n}$ where $\delta_{m n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Integral over 2 pi of Sine of n x
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \sin m x \rd x = 0$

title: Integral to Infinity of Bessel Function of First Kind order Zero
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map {J_0} t \rd t = 1$ where $J_0$ denotes the Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$.

title: Integral to Infinity of Cosine p x minus Cosine q x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\cos p x - \cos q x} x \rd x = \ln \frac q p$ where $p$ and $q$ are strictly positive real numbers.

title: Integral to Infinity of Dirac Delta Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Then: $\ds \int_0^{+ \infty} \map \delta x \rd x = 1$

title: Integral to Infinity of Dirac Delta Function by Continuous Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Let $g$ be a continuous real function. Then: $\ds \int_0^{+ \infty} \map \delta x \map g x \rd x = \map g 0$

title: Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -t^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-t^2} \rd t = \dfrac {\sqrt \pi} 2$

title: Integral to Infinity of Function over Argument
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le A$. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then: $\ds \int_0^\infty {\dfrac {\map f t} t} = \int_0^{\to \infty} \map F u \rd u$ provided the integrals converge.

title: Integral to Infinity of One minus Cosine p x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {1 - \cos p x} {x^2} \rd x = \frac {\pi \size p} 2$ where $p$ is a real number.

title: Integral to Infinity of Reciprocal of Power of x
snippet: The improper integral $\ds \int_1^\infty \dfrac {\d t} {t^x}$ exists $x > 1$.

title: Integral to Infinity of Shifted Dirac Delta Function by Continuous Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta x$ denote the Dirac delta function. Let $g$ be a continuous real function. Let $a \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive real number. Then: $\ds \int_0^{+ \infty} \map \delta {x - a} \, \map g x \rd x = \map g a$

title: Integral to Infinity of Sine p x Cosine q x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin p x \cos q x} x \rd x = \begin {cases} \dfrac \pi 2 & : p > q > 0 \\ \\ 0 & : 0 0 \end {cases}$

title: Integral to Infinity of Sine p x Sine q x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin p x \sin q x} {x^2} \rd x = \begin {cases} \dfrac {\pi p} 2 & : 0 0 \end {cases}$

title: Integral to Infinity of Sine p x over x
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin p x} x \rd x = \begin {cases} \dfrac \pi 2 & : p > 0 \\ \\ 0 & : p = 0 \\ \\ -\dfrac \pi 2 & : p < 0 \end {cases}$

title: Integral to Infinity of Square of Sine p x over x Squared
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \paren {\frac {\sin p x} x}^2 \rd x = \frac {\pi \size p} 2$ where $p$ is a real number.

title: Integral to Infinity of e^-t by Gauss Error Function of Root t
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty e^{-t} \erf \sqrt t \rd t = \dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2$ where $\erf$ denotes the Gauss error function.

title: Integral with respect to Dirac Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $x \in X$, and let $\delta_x$ be the Dirac measure at $x$. Let $f \in \MM _{\overline \R}, f: X \to \overline \R$ be a measurable function. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \delta_x = \map f x$ where the integral sign denotes the $\delta_x$-integral.

title: Integral with respect to Discrete Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Let $\ds \mu = \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \lambda_n \delta_{x_n}$ be a discrete measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $f \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+, f: X \to \overline \R$ be a positive measurable function. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \lambda_n \map f {x_n}$ where the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration.

title: Integral with respect to Kernel Transformation of Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $N: X \times \Sigma \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a kernel. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a positive measurable function. Then: $\ds \int f \map \rd {\mu N} = \int N f \rd \mu$ where: The integral sign denotes integration with respect to a measure $\mu N$ is the transformation of $\mu$ by $N$ $N f$ is the transformation of $f$ by $N$ Writing $\map \mu f$ in place of $\ds \int f \rd \mu$, the theorem statement can be conveniently expressed as: $\map {\mu N} f = \map \mu {N f}$

title: Integral with respect to Pushforward Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\struct {X', \Sigma'}$ be a measurable space. Let $T: X \to X'$ be a $\Sigma \, / \, \Sigma'$-measurable mapping. Let $f: X' \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma'$-measurable function. Let $\map T \mu$ be the pushforward measure of $\mu$ under $T$. Then $f \circ T: X \to \overline \R$ is positive and $\Sigma$-measurable with: $\ds \int_{X'} f \rd \map T \mu = \int_X f \circ T \rd \mu$

title: Integral with respect to Restriction of Measure to Trace Sigma-Algebra of Measurable Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $A \in \Sigma$. Let $\Sigma_A$ be the trace $\sigma$-algebra of $A$ in $\Sigma$. Let $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A}$ be the restriction of $\mu$ to $\Sigma_A$. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive measurable function. Let $f \restriction_A$ be the restriction of $f$ to $A$. Define $f^\ast : X \to \overline \R$ by: $\ds \map {f^\ast} x = \begin{cases}\map f x & x \in A \\ 0 & x \not \in A\end{cases}$ for each $x \in X$. Then, we have: $\ds \int \paren {f \restriction_A} \rd \paren {\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A} } = \int f^\ast \rd \mu$

title: Integral with respect to Series of Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\ds \mu := \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \lambda_n \mu_n$ be a series of measures on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Then for all positive measurable functions $f: X \to \overline \R, f \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+$: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \lambda_n \int f \rd \mu_n$ where the integral signs denote integration with respect to a measure.

title: Integrally Closed is Local Property
snippet: Let $A$ be an integral domain. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, let $A_{\mathfrak p}$ denote the localization at $S = A \divides \mathfrak p$. {{item|(2):|$A_{\mathfrak p}$ is integrally closed for all prime ideals $\mathfrak p$}} {{item|(3):|$A_{\mathfrak m}$ is integrally closed for all maximal ideals $\mathfrak m$}}

title: Integrated Linear Differential Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $C^1 \closedint a b := \map {C^1} {\closedint a b, \R}$ be the space of real functions of differentiability class $C^1$. Let $S$ be the set of differentiable functions on closed real interval vanishing at their endpoints: $S := \set {\mathbf h \in C^1 \closedint a b : \map {\mathbf h} a = \map {\mathbf h} b = 0}$ Let $S \subseteq C^1 \closedint a b$ be equiped with the $C^1$ norm. Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B \in C \closedint a b$ be continuous real functions.

title: Integrating Factor for First Order ODE
snippet: Let the first order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad \map M {x, y} + \map N {x, y} \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0$ be non-homogeneous and not exact. By Existence of Integrating Factor, if $(1)$ has a general solution, there exists an integrating factor $\map \mu {x, y}$ such that: $\ds \map \mu {x, y} \paren {\map M {x, y} + \map N {x, y} \frac {\d y} {\d x} } = 0$ is an exact differential equation.

title: Integration by Inversion
snippet: $\ds \int_0^{+\infty} \map f x \rd x = \int_0^{+\infty} \dfrac {\map f {\frac 1 x} } {x^2} \rd x$

title: Integration by Partial Fractions
snippet: Let $\map R x = \dfrac {\map P x} {\map Q x}$ be a rational function over $\R$ such that the degree of the polynomial $P$ is strictly smaller than the degree of the polynomial $Q$. Consider the primitive: $\ds \int \map R x \rd x$ Let $\map R x$ be expressible by the partial fractions expansion: $\map R x = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \dfrac {\map {p_k} x} {\map {q_k} x}$ where: each of the $\map {p_k} x$ are polynomial functions the degree of $\map {p_k} x$ is strictly less than the degree of $\map {q_k} x$ for all $k$.

title: Integration by Substitution
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a real function which has a derivative on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $I$ be an open interval which contains the image of $\closedint a b$ under $\phi$. Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on $I$.

title: Integration on Polynomials is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\map P \R$ be the vector space of all polynomial functions on the real number line $\R$. Let $S$ be the mapping defined as: $\ds \forall p \in \map P \R: \forall x \in \R: \map S {\map p x} = \int_0^x \map p t \rd t$ Then $S$ is a linear operator on $\map P \R$.
