title: Inverse Element/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Elements ==

title: Inverse Element in Inverse Completion of Commutative Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $\struct {C, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup of cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $\struct {T, \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the inverse of an element of $S$ which is invertible for $\circ$ is also its inverse for $\circ'$.

title: Inverse Element is Power of Order Less 1
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Then: $\order g = n \implies g^{n - 1} = g^{-1}$

title: Inverse Element of Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Then: $\map {f^{-1} } y = x \iff \map f x = y$ where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse mapping of $f$.

title: Inverse Element of Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then: $\map {f^{-1} } y = x \iff \map f x = y$

title: Inverse Elements of Right Transversal is Left Transversal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $S \subseteq G$ be a right transversal for $H$ in $G$. Let $T$ be the set defined as: $T := \set {x^{-1}: x \in S}$ where $x^{-1}$ is the inverse of $x$ in $G$. Then $T$ is a left transversal for $H$ in $G$.

title: Inverse Evaluation Isomorphism of Annihilator
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be a module over $R$ whose dimension is finite. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $G^{**}$ be the algebraic dual of $G^*$. Let $N$ be a submodule of $G^*$. Let $J$ be the evaluation isomorphism from $G$ onto $G^{**}$. Let $N^\circ$ be the annihilator of $N$. Then: $J^{-1} \sqbrk {N^\circ} = \set {x \in G: \forall t \in N: \map t x = 0}$ where $J^{-1} \sqbrk {N^\circ}$ denotes the preimage of $N^\circ$ under $J$.

title: Inverse Function Theorem
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $f: \R^n \to \R^n$ be a mapping on the real Cartesian space of $n$ dimensions. Let $\mathbf x \in \R^n$ be an element of $\R^n$. Let the Jacobian matrix of $f$ be nonsingular in the locality of $\mathbf x$. Then there exists a local single-valued differentiable inverse for $f$ at the locality of $\mathbf x$.

title: Inverse Function Theorem for Real Functions
snippet: Let $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be natural numbers. Let $\Omega \subset \R^n$ be open. Let $f: \Omega \to \R^n$ be a vector-valued function of class $C^k$. Let $a \in \Omega$. Let the differential $D \map f a$ of $f$ at $a$ be invertible. Then there exist open sets $U \subset \Omega$ and $V \subset \R^n$ such that: $a \in U$ the restriction of $f$ to $U$ is a $C^k$-diffeomorphism $f: U \to V$.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cosecant is Odd Function
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\map {\csch^{-1} } {-x} = -\csch^{-1} x$ where $\map {\csch^{-1} } {-x}$ denotes the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cosecant of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\csch^{-1} } {i x} = -i \csc^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cosine of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\cosh^{-1} x = \pm \, i \cos^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent is Odd Function
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\map {\coth^{-1} } {-x} = -\coth^{-1} x$ where $\map {\coth^{-1} } {-x}$ denotes the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\coth^{-1} } {i x} = i \cot^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Secant of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\sech^{-1} x = \pm \, i \sec^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Sine Logarithmic Formulation
snippet: {{finish|The true story is more complicated than this. The inverse hyperbolic sine is a multifunction. So is $\ln$ in the complex plane. And $\sqrt {z^2 + 1}$ has two values, pos and neg, so you need to justify which one is taken. The best context to put this page is probably into Definition:Inverse Hyperbolic Sine/Complex/Principal Branch, where an explanation needs to be made as to why the principal value is taken thus.}} For any complex number $z \in \C$: $\arsinh z = \map \ln {z + \sqrt {z^2 + 1} }$ where $\arsinh z$ is the inverse hyperbolic sine.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Sine is Odd Function
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\map \arsinh {-x} = -\arsinh x$ where $\arsinh$ denotes the inverse hyperbolic sine function.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Sine of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\sinh^{-1} } {i x} = i \sin^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent ==

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent is Odd Function
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\map {\tanh^{-1} } {-x} = -\tanh^{-1} x$ where $\map {\tanh^{-1} } {-x}$ denotes the inverse hyperbolic tangent function.

title: Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\tanh^{-1} } {i x} = i \tan^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Image Mapping Induced by Projection
snippet: Let $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of sets. Let $\ds S = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ be the Cartesian product of $\family {S_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. For each $j \in I$, let $\pr_j: S \to S_j$ denote the $j$-th projection. For each $j \in I$ let $\pr_j^\gets: \powerset {S_i} \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping induced by $\pr_j$ Then for all $j \in I$, $\pr_j^\gets$ is the mapping defined by: $\ds \forall T \subseteq S_i: \map {\pr_j^\gets} T = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} T_i$ where: $T_i = \begin {cases} T & i = j \\ S_i & i \ne j \end {cases}$

title: Inverse Image Mapping is Lower Adjoint to Composite Involving Direct Image Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^\to : \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping. Let $f^\gets : \powerset T \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping. Let $\complement_S: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ denote the relative complement mapping on the power set of $S$. Let $\complement_T: \powerset T \to \powerset T$ denote the relative complement mapping on the power set of $T$.

title: Inverse Image Mapping is Upper Adjoint to Direct Image Mapping
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^\to : \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping. Let $f^\gets : \powerset T \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping. Then: $f^\gets : \powerset T \to \powerset S$ is the upper adjoint to $f^\to : \powerset S \to \powerset T$ That is: $\forall A \subseteq S, B \subseteq T : A \subseteq \map {f^\gets} B$ $\map {f^\to} A \subseteq B$

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Bijection is Inverse of Direct Image Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f :S \to T$ be a bijection. Let $f^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Let $f^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$. Then: $\paren {f^\to}^{-1} = f^\gets$ where $\paren {f^\to}^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $f^\to$.

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Codomain is Preimage Set of Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\powerset S$ and $\powerset T$ be their power sets. Let $f \subseteq S \times T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$: $\forall Y \in \powerset T: \map {f^\gets} Y = \begin {cases} \set {s \in S: \exists t \in Y: \map f s = t} & : \Img f \cap Y \ne \O \\ \O & : \Img f \cap Y = \O \end {cases}$ Then: $\map {f^\gets} T = \Preimg f$ where $\Preimg f$ is the preimage set of $f$.

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Codomain is Preimage Set of Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\powerset S$ and $\powerset T$ be their power sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $\RR$: $\forall X \in \powerset S: \map {\RR^\to} X = \begin {cases} \set {t \in T: \exists s \in X: \tuple {x, t} \in \RR} & : X \ne \O \\ \O & : X = \O \end {cases}$ Then: $\map {\RR^\gets} T = \Preimg \RR$ where $\Preimg \RR$ is the preimage of $\RR$.

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Frame Homomorphism Preserves Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi : L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame homomorphism. Let $\phi^\gets$ denote the inverse image mapping of $\phi$. Let $F$ be a completely prime filter of $L_2$. Then: $\map {\phi^\gets} F$ is a completely prime filter of $L_1$

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Identity is Identity
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $\paren{I_S}^\gets = I_{\powerset S}$ where: $I_S$ denotes the identity mapping on $S$ $\paren{I_S}^\gets$ denotes the inverse image mapping of $I_S$ $\powerset S$ denotes the powerset of $S$ $I_{\powerset S}$ denotes the identity mapping on $\powerset S$

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Injection is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a injection. Let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$. Then $f^\gets$ is a surjection.

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $f^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$: $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S: \map {f^\gets} Y = f^{-1} \sqbrk Y$ Then $f^\gets$ is indeed a mapping.

title: Inverse Image Mapping of Relation is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $\RR$: $\RR^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S: \map {\RR^\gets} Y = \RR^{-1} \sqbrk Y$ Then $\RR^\gets$ is indeed a mapping.

title: Inverse Image of Direct Image of Inverse Image equals Inverse Image Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let: $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ denote the direct image mapping of $f$ $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ denote the inverse image mapping of $f$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then: $f^\gets \circ f^\to \circ f^\gets = f^\gets$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Inverse Image of Order-Convex Set under Monotone Mapping is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \le}$ and $\struct {Y, \preceq}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a monotone mapping. Let $C$ be a order-convex subset of $Y$. Then $f^{-1} \sqbrk C$ is order-convex in $X$.

title: Inverse Image of Set under Set-Like Relation is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a set-like endorelation on $A$. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a set. Then $\map {\RR^{-1} } B$, the inverse image of $B$ under $\RR$, is also a set.

title: Inverse Image under Embedding of Image under Relation of Image of Point
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR_S$ and $\RR_t$ be relations on $S$ and $T$, respectively. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping with the property that: $\forall p, q \in S: \paren {p \mathrel {\RR_S} q \iff \map \phi p \mathrel {\RR_T} \map \phi q}$ Then for each $p \in S$: $\map {\RR_S} p = \phi^{-1} \sqbrk {\map {\RR_T} {\map \phi p} }$

title: Inverse Image under Order Embedding of Strict Upper Closure of Image of Point
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an order embedding of $\struct {S, \preceq}$ into $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ Let $p \in S$. Then: $\map {\phi^{-1} } {\map \phi p^{\succ'} } = p^\succ$ where $\cdot^\succ$ and $\cdot^{\succ'}$ represent strict upper closure with respect to $\preceq$ and $\preceq'$, respectively.

title: Inverse Integral Operator is Linear if Unique
snippet: Let $T$ be an integral operator. Let $f$ be an integrable real function on a domain appropriate to $T$. Let $F = \map T f$ and $G = \map T g$. Let $T$ have a unique inverse $T^{-1}$. Then $T^{-1}$ is a linear operator: $\forall p, q \in \R: \map {T^{-1} } {p F + q G} = p \map {T^{-1} } F + q \map {T^{-1} } G$

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of 1 over (s^2 + a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\paren {3 - a^2 t^2} \sin a t - 3 a t \cos a t} {8 a^5} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {e^{-b t} - e^{-a t} } {2 \paren {b - a} \sqrt {\pi t^3} } } } s = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {s + a} + \sqrt {s + b} }$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers such that $a \ne b$ $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of 1 over s^3 - a^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {e^{-a t / 2} } {3 a^2} \paren {e^{3 a t / 2} - \cos \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 2 a t - \sqrt 3 \sin \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 2 a t} } } s = \dfrac 1 {s^3 - a^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of 1 over s^4 + 4 a^4
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac 1 {4 a^3} \paren {\sin a t \cosh a t - \cos a t \sinh a t} } } s = \dfrac 1 {s^4 + 4 a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac 1 {2 a^3} \paren {\sinh a t - \sin a t} } } s = \dfrac 1 {s^4 - a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of Function of Logarithm of s over s by Logarithm of s
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac {\map F {\ln s} } {s \ln s} } = \ds \int_0^\infty \dfrac {t^u \map f u} {\map \Gamma {u + 1} } \rd u$ where: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac {\map F {\ln s} } {s \ln s} }$ denotes the inverse Laplace transform of $\dfrac {\map F {\ln s} } {s \ln s}$ $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of Function of Reciprocal by Reciprocal
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 s \map F {\dfrac 1 s} } = \ds \int _0^\infty \map {J_0} {2 \sqrt {u t} } \map f u \rd u$ where: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 s \map F {\dfrac 1 s} }$ denotes the inverse Laplace transform of $\dfrac 1 s \map F {\dfrac 1 s}$ $J_0$ denotes the Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of Function of Reciprocal by Reciprocal of Power
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 {s^{n + 1} } \map F {\dfrac 1 s} } = t^{n / 2} \ds \int_0^\infty u^{-n / 2} \map {J_n} {2 \sqrt {u t} } \map f u \rd u$ where: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 {s^{n + 1} } \map F {\dfrac 1 s} }$ denotes the inverse Laplace transform of $\dfrac 1 {s^{n + 1} } \map F {\dfrac 1 s}$ $J_n$ denotes the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of Function of Root by Reciprocal
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac {\map F {\sqrt s} } s} = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {\pi t} } \ds \int _0^\infty e^{-{u^2} / 4 t} \map f u \rd u$ where $\invlaptrans {\map F {\sqrt s} }$ denotes the inverse Laplace transform of $\map F {\sqrt s}$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of Function of s + 1 over s by Reciprocal of s^2 + 1
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 {s^2 + 1} \map F {\dfrac {s + 1} s} } = \ds \int_0^t \map {J_0} {2 \sqrt {u \paren {t - u} } } \map f u \rd u$ where: $\invlaptrans {\dfrac 1 {s^2 + 1} \map F {\dfrac {s + 1} s} }$ denotes the inverse Laplace transform of $\dfrac 1 {s^2 + 1} \map F {\dfrac {s + 1} s}$ $J_0$ denotes the Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^2 over s^4 + 4 a^4
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac 1 {2 a} \paren {\sin a t \cosh a t + \cos a t \sinh a t} } } s = \dfrac {s^2} {s^4 + 4 a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^2 over s^4 - a^4
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac 1 {2 a} \paren {\sinh a t + \sin a t} } } s = \dfrac {s^2} {s^4 - a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^3 over (s^2 + a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {3 t \sin a t + a t^2 \cos a t} {8 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^3} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^3 over (s^2 - a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {3 t \sinh a t + a t^2 \cosh a t} {8 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^3} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^4 over (s^2 - a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\paren {3 + a^2 t^2} \sinh a t + 5 a t \cosh a t} {8 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^4} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^5 over (s^2 + a^2)^3

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s^5 over (s^2 - a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\paren {8 + a^2 t^2} \cosh a t + 7 a t \sinh a t} 8} } s = \dfrac {s^5} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s over (s^2 + a^2)^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t \sin a t - a t^2 \cos a t} {8 a^3} } } s = \dfrac s {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s over (s^2 - a^2)^3

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s over s^3 + a^3

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s over s^4 + 4 a^4
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\sin a t \sinh a t} {2 a^2} } } s = \dfrac s {s^4 + 4 a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Laplace Transform of s over s^4 - a^4
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac 1 {2 a^2} \paren {\cosh a t - \cos a t} } } s = \dfrac s {s^4 - a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Inverse Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Mappings ==

title: Inverse Mapping in Induced Structure of Homomorphism to Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $f$ be a homomorphism from $S$ into $T$. Let $f^*$ be the pointwise inverse of $f$. Then $f^*$ is a homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, \oplus}$.

title: Inverse Mapping is Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ and $g: T \to S$ be inverse mappings of each other. Then $f$ and $g$ are bijections.

title: Inverse Mapping is Unique
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. If $f$ has an inverse mapping, then that inverse mapping is unique. That is, if: $f$ and $g$ are inverse mappings of each other and $f$ and $h$ are inverse mappings of each other then $g = h$.

title: Inverse Mapping on Group of Units in Unital Banach Algebra is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra. Let $\map G A$ be the group of units of $A$. Define $\phi : \map G A \to \map G A$ by: $\map \phi x = x^{-1}$ for each $x \in \map G A$. Then $\phi$ is continuous.

title: Inverse Morphism is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $f: C \to D$ be an isomorphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ admits a unique inverse morphism $g: D \to C$.

title: Inverse Probability/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Probability ==

title: Inverse Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverse Relations ==

title: Inverse Relation Equal iff Subset
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. If $\RR$ is a subset or superset of its inverse, then it equals its inverse. {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \RR | o = \subseteq | r = \RR^{-1} }} {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \RR^{-1} | o = \subseteq | r = \RR }} {{eqn | n = 3 | l = \RR | r = \RR^{-1} }}

title: Inverse Relation Functor is Contravariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Rel}$ be the category of relations. Let $C: \mathbf{Rel} \to \mathbf{Rel}$ be the inverse relation functor. Then $C$ is a contravariant functor.

title: Inverse Relation Properties
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ has any of the properties: Reflexive Antireflexive Non-reflexive Symmetric Asymmetric Antisymmetric Non-symmetric Transitive Antitransitive Non-transitive then its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ has the same properties.

title: Inverse Relation is Left and Right Inverse iff Bijection
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on a cartesian product $S \times T$. Let: $I_S$ be the identity mapping on $S$ $I_T$ be the identity mapping on $T$. Let $\RR^{-1}$ be the inverse relation of $\RR$. Then $\RR$ is a bijection : $\RR^{-1} \circ \RR = I_S$ and $\RR \circ \RR^{-1} = I_T$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of relations.

title: Inverse Relational Structures of Isomorphic Structures are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let ${\RR_1}^{-1}$ and ${\RR_2}^{-1}$ be the inverses of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ respectively. Let $f: \struct {S, \RR_1} \to \struct {T, \RR_2}$ be a relation isomorphism. Then $f: \struct {S, {\RR_1}^{-1} } \to \struct {T, {\RR_2}^{-1} } $ is also a relation isomorphism.

snippet: == Examples of Inverse Row form of Cayley Table for Group ==

snippet: $\sec^{-1} x = \pm i \sech^{-1} x$

snippet: Everywhere that the function is defined: $\map \arcsin {-x} = -\arcsin x$

title: Inverse Sine of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\sin^{-1} } {i x} = i \sinh^{-1} x$
