title: Inverse Tangent is Odd Function
snippet: Everywhere that the function is defined: $\map \arctan {-x} = -\arctan x$

title: Inverse Tangent of Imaginary Number
snippet: $\map {\tan^{-1} } {i x} = i \tanh^{-1} x$

title: Inverse Tangent of i
snippet: The inverse tangent of $i$ is not defined.

title: Inverse Trigonometric Function of Reciprocal
snippet: For all $x \in \R$ for which the expressions above are defined:

title: Inverse for Complex Addition
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $-z = -x - i y \in \C$ be the negative of $z$. Then $-z$ is the inverse element of $z$ under the operation of complex addition: $\forall z \in \C: \exists -z \in \C: z + \paren {-z} = 0 = \paren {-z} + z$

title: Inverse for Complex Multiplication
Inverse for Integer Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of integers $\Z$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of integer addition: $\forall x \in \Z: \exists -x \in \Z: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

title: Inverse for Rational Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of rational numbers $\Q$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of rational number addition: $\forall x \in \Q: \exists -x \in \Q: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

title: Inverse for Rational Multiplication
Inverse for Real Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of real numbers $\R$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of real number addition: $\forall x \in \R: \exists -x \in \R: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

title: Inverse for Real Multiplication
Inverse in Affine Group of One Dimension
snippet: Let $\map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R$ denote the $1$-dimensional affine group on $\R$. Let $f_{a b} \in \map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R$. Let $c = \dfrac 1 a$ and $d = \dfrac {-b} a$. Then $f_{c d} \in \map {\operatorname {Af}_1} \R$ is the inverse of $f_{a b}$.

title: Inverse in Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then every element $x \in G$ has exactly one inverse: $\forall x \in G: \exists_1 x^{-1} \in G: x \circ x^{-1} = e^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ x$ where $e$ is the identity element of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

title: Inverse in Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Then an element $x \in S$ can have at most one inverse for $\circ$.

title: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then $f$ is an injection.

title: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Injection and Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then: $(1): \quad f$ is an injection $(2): \quad f$ is a surjection.

title: Inverse is Mapping implies Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let the inverse $f^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ itself be a mapping. Then $f$ is a surjection.

title: Inverse not always Unique for Non-Associative Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be a non-associative operation. Then for any $x \in S$, it is possible for $x$ to have more than one inverse element.

title: Inverse of Algebraic Structure Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, *} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Antireflexive Relation is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is antireflexive, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Antisymmetric Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is antisymmetric, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Antitransitive Relation is Antitransitive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is antitransitive, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Asymmetric Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is asymmetric, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Bijection is Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection in the sense that: $(1): \quad f$ is an injection $(2): \quad f$ is a surjection. Then the inverse $f^{-1}$ of $f$ is itself a bijection by the same definition.

title: Inverse of Bijective Complete Lattice Homomorphism is Bijective Complete Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a bijective complete lattice homomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a bijective complete lattice homomorphism.

title: Inverse of Bijective Lattice Homomorphism is Bijective Lattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ be lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a bijective lattice homomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a bijective lattice homomorphism

title: Inverse of Cantor Pairing Function
snippet: Let $\pi : \N^2 \to \N$ be the Cantor pairing function. Define $k : \N \to \N$ as: $\map k z$ is the largest $k$ such that $T_k \le z$ where $T_k$ is the $k$-th triangular number. Let $\pi_1 : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\ds \map {\pi_1} z = z - T_{\map k z}$ Let $\pi_2 : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\map {\pi_2} z = \map k z - \map {\pi_1} z$ Then: $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are well-defined For every $z \in \N$: $\map \pi {\map {\pi_1} z, \map {\pi_2} z} = z$ For every $x, y \in \N$: $\map {\pi_1} {\map \pi {x, y}} = x$ $\map {\pi_2} {\map \pi {x, y}} = y$

title: Inverse of Cantor Pairing Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Define $k : \N \to \N$ as: $\map k z$ is the largest $k$ such that $T_k \le z$ where $T_k$ is the $k$-th triangular number. Let $\pi_1 : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\ds \map {\pi_1} z = z - T_{\map k z}$ Let $\pi_2 : \N \to \N$ be defined as: $\map {\pi_2} z = \map k z - \map {\pi_1} z$ Then, $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are primitive recursive functions.

title: Inverse of Cauchy Matrix
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the square Cauchy matrix of order $n$: $C_n = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_1 + y_n} \\ \dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_2 + y_n} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ \dfrac 1 {x_n + y_1} & \dfrac 1 {x_n + y_2} & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {x_n + y_n} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse $C_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as: $\begin{bmatrix} b_{ij} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac {\ds \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x_j + y_k} \paren {x_k + y_i} } {\ds \paren {x_j + y_i} \paren…

title: Inverse of Central Unit of Ring is in Center
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\map Z R$ denote the center of $R$. Let $u \in R$ be a unit of $R$. Then: $u \in \map Z R \implies u^{-1} \in \map Z R$

title: Inverse of Circle Not Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle in the plane on center $O$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $\CC$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Let $K$ be an arbitrary circle distinct from $\CC$ and not through $O$. Then the image under $T$ of all the points on $K$ lie on the same circle, distinct from both $K$ and $\CC$.

title: Inverse of Circle Through Inversion Center is Straight Line Not Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let an arbitrary circle $K$ be drawn in the plane. Let $A'$ and $P'$ be arbitrary points on $K$. Let $T$ be an inversive transformation such that: the inversion center of $T$ is $O$ the inversion circle $O$ for $T$ is chosen such that $OA'$ is a diameter of $K$ the radius of $O$ is $r$. Let $A$ and $P$ be the images of $A'$ and $P'$ under $T$ respectively. Let $L$ be a straight line drawn perpendicular to the extension of $OA'$ at point $A$. Then $P$ lies on $L$.

title: Inverse of Combinatorial Matrix
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the combinatorial matrix of order $n$ given by: $C_n = \begin{bmatrix} x + y & y & \cdots & y \\ y & x + y & \cdots & y \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ y & y & \cdots & x + y \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse $C_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as: $b_{i j} = \dfrac {-y + \delta_{i j} \paren {x + n y} } {x \paren {x + n y} }$ where $\delta_{i j}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Inverse of Commuting Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x$ and $y$ are both invertible. Then $x$ commutes with $y$ : $\struct {x \circ y}^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ y^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Complete Lattice Isomorphism is Complete Lattice Isomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \preceq_2}$ be complete lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a complete lattice isomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a complete lattice isomorphism

title: Inverse of Composite Bijection
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be bijections such that $\Dom g = \Cdm f$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f}^{-1} = f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}$ and $f^{-1} \circ g^{-1}$ is itself a bijection.

title: Inverse of Composite Relation
snippet: Let $\RR_2 \circ \RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times S_3$ be the composite of the two relations $\RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times S_2$ and $\RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times S_3$. Then: $\paren {\RR_2 \circ \RR_1}^{-1} = \RR_1^{-1} \circ \RR_2^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Composition of Subsets of Topological Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \odot, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $A, B \subseteq G$. Then: $\paren {A \odot B}^{-1} = B^{-1} \odot A^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Conditional is Contrapositive of Converse
snippet: Let $p \implies q$ be a conditional. Then the inverse of $p \implies q$ is the contrapositive of its converse.

title: Inverse of Conditional is Converse of Contrapositive
snippet: Let $p \implies q$ be a conditional. Then the inverse of $p \implies q$ is the converse of its contrapositive.

title: Inverse of Curve under Inversive Transformation
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle embedded in a Cartesian plane $\EE$ whose center $O$ is at the origin $\tuple {0, 0}$ and whose radius is $r$. Let $f$ be the inversive transformation of $\EE$ $\CC$. Let $P = \tuple {x, y}$ be an arbitrary point of $\CC$. The inverse point $P' = \tuple {x', y'}$ of $P$ under $f$ is given by: {{eqn | l = x' | r = \dfrac {r^2 x} {x^2 + y^2} }} {{eqn | l = y' | r = \dfrac {r^2 y} {x^2 + y^2} }}

title: Inverse of Diagonal Matrix
snippet: Let: $\mathbf D = \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ be an $n \times n$ diagonal matrix. Then its inverse is given by: $\mathbf D^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 {a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac 1 {a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {a_{nn}} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ provided that none of the diagonal elements are zero. If any of the diagonal elements are zero, $\mathbf D$ is singular.

title: Inverse of Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\Delta_S$ denote the diagonal relation on $S$. Let ${\Delta_S}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\Delta_S$. Then: ${\Delta_S}^{-1} = \Delta_S$

title: Inverse of Direct Image Mapping does not necessarily equal Inverse Image Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $\RR^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $\RR$. Let $\RR^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $\RR$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\paren {\RR^\to}^{-1} = \RR^\gets$ where $\paren {\RR^\to}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\RR^\to$. That is, the inverse of the direct image mapping of $\RR$ does not always equal the inverse image mapping of $\RR$.

title: Inverse of Direct Image Mapping is Direct Image Mapping of Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f :S \to T$ be a bijection. Let $f^\to$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Then: $\paren {f^\to}^{-1} = \paren {f^{-1} }^{\to}$ where $f^{-1}$ and $\paren{f^\to}^{-1}$ denote the inverses of $f$ and $f^\to$ respectively

title: Inverse of Division Product
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {U_R, \circ}$ be the group of units of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $a, b \in U_R$. Then: $\paren {\dfrac a b}^{-1} = \dfrac {1_R} {\paren {a / b}} = \dfrac b a$ where $\dfrac x z$ is defined as $x \circ \paren {z^{-1} }$, that is, $x$ divided by $z$.

title: Inverse of Element in Semidirect Product
snippet: Let $N$ and $H$ be groups. Let $H$ act by automorphisms on $N$ via $\phi$. Let $N \rtimes_\phi H$ be the corresponding (outer) semidirect product. Let $\tuple {n, h} \in N \rtimes_\phi H$. Then: {{eqn | l = \tuple {n, h}^{-1} | r = \tuple {\map {\phi_{h^{-1} } } {n^{-1} }, h^{-1} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \tuple {\paren {\map {\phi_{h^{-1} } } n}^{-1}, h^{-1} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \tuple {\map { {\phi_h}^{-1} } {n^{-1} }, h^{-1} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \tuple {\paren {\map { {\phi_h}^{-1} } n}^{-1}, h^{-1} } | c = }}

title: Inverse of Field Product
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $a, b \in F$ such that $a \ne 0$ and $b \ne 0$. Then: $\paren {a \times b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \times a^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Field Product with Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$ and whose unity is $1$. Let $a, b \in F$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then: $\paren {a \times b^{-1} }^{-1} = b \times a^{-1}$ This can also be expressed using the notation of division as: $1 / \paren {a / b} = b / a$

title: Inverse of Frame Isomorphism is Frame Isomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be frames. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a frame isomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : S_2 \to S_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : S_1 \to S_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a frame isomorphism

title: Inverse of Generator of Cyclic Group is Generator
snippet: Let $\gen g = G$ be a cyclic group. Then: $G = \gen {g^{-1} }$ where $g^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $g$. Thus, in general, a generator of a cyclic group is not unique.

title: Inverse of Group Commutator
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\sqbrk {g, h}$ denote the commutator of $g$ and $h$. Then $\sqbrk {g, h}$ is the inverse of $\sqbrk {h, g}$: $\sqbrk {g, h} = \sqbrk {h, g}^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Group Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $g \in G$, with inverse $g^{-1}$. Then: $\paren {g^{-1} }^{-1} = g$

title: Inverse of Group Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {H, *} \to \struct {G, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Group Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $a, b \in G$, with inverses $a^{-1}, b^{-1}$. Then: $\paren {a \circ b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \circ a^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Hilbert Matrix
snippet: Let $H_n$ be the Hilbert matrix of order $n$: $\begin{bmatrix} a_{i j} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 {i + j - 1} \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse $H_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as: $\begin{bmatrix} b_{i j} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac {\paren {-1}^{i + j} \paren {i + n - 1}! \paren {j + n - 1}!} {\paren {\paren {i - 1}!}^2 \paren {\paren {j - 1}!}^2 \paren {n - j}! \paren {n - i}! \paren {i + j - 1} } \end{bmatrix}$

title: Inverse of Homeomorphism between Metric Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be a homeomorphism. Then $f^{-1}: M_2 \to M_1$ is also a homeomorphism.

title: Inverse of Homeomorphism is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T, T'$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T \to T'$ be a homeomorphism. Then $f^{-1}: T' \to T$ is also a homeomorphism.

title: Inverse of Identity Element is Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure with an identity element $e$. Let the inverse of $e$ be $e^{-1}$. Then: $e^{-1} = e$ That is, $e$ is self-inverse.

title: Inverse of Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $I_S: S \to S$ be the identity mapping on $S$. Then the inverse of $I_S$ is itself: $\paren {I_S}^{-1} = I_S$

title: Inverse of Increasing Bijection need not be Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a bijection which is increasing. Then $\phi^{-1}: T \to S$ is not necessarily also increasing.

title: Inverse of Infimum in Ordered Group is Supremum of Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $x, y \in G$. Then: $\set {x, y}$ admits an infimum in $G$ $\set {x^{-1}, y^{-1} }$ admits a supremum in $G$ in which case: $\paren {\inf \set {x, y} }^{-1} = \sup \set {x^{-1}, y^{-1} }$

title: Inverse of Injection is Many-to-One Relation
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $f^{-1}: T \to S$ be the inverse relation of $f$. Then $f^{-1}$ is many-to-one.

title: Inverse of Injection is One-to-One Relation
snippet: Let $f$ be an injective mapping. Then its inverse $f^{-1}$ is a one-to-one relation.

title: Inverse of Injective and Surjective Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that: $(1): \quad f$ is an injection $(2): \quad f$ is a surjection. Then the inverse $f^{-1}$ of $f$ is itself a mapping.

title: Inverse of Inner Automorphism
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $x \in G$. Let $\kappa_x$ be the inner automorphism of $G$ given by $x$. Then: $\paren {\kappa_x}^{-1} = \kappa_{x^{-1} }$

title: Inverse of Inverse Relation
snippet: The inverse of an inverse relation is the relation itself: $\paren {\RR^{-1} }^{-1} = \RR$

title: Inverse of Inverse of Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Then: $\paren {f^{-1} }^{-1} = f$ where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse of $f$.

title: Inverse of Inverse of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a nonsingular matrix. Then: $\paren {\mathbf A^{-1} }^{-1} = \mathbf A$ That is, a nonsingular matrix equals the inverse of its inverse.

title: Inverse of Inverse of Subset of Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $X \subseteq G$. Then: $\paren {X^{-1} }^{-1} = X$. where $X^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $X$.

title: Inverse of Isometric Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_R}$ and $\struct {S, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_S}$ be normed division rings. Let $\phi:R \to S$ be a mapping. Then $\phi:R \to S$ is an isometric isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: S \to R$ is also an isometric isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Lattice Isomorphism is Lattice Isomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {A_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {A_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ be lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a lattice isomorphism. Let $\phi^{-1} : A_2 \to A_1$ be the inverse of $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$. Then: $\phi^{-1} : L_2 \to L_1$ is a lattice isomorphism

title: Inverse of Left-Total Relation is Right-Total
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ be the inverse of $\RR$. Then: $\RR$ is left-total $\RR^{-1}$ is right-total.

title: Inverse of Linear Function on Real Numbers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ be real numbers such that $a \ne 0$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = a x + b$ Then the inverse of $f$ is given by: $\forall y \in \R: \map {f^{-1} } y = \dfrac {y - b} a$

title: Inverse of Linear Isometry is Linear Isometry
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear isometry with inverse $T^{-1} : Y \to X$. Then $T^{-1}$ is a linear isometry.

title: Inverse of Linear Operator is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space. Let $A : X \to X$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear transformation with inverse mapping $A^{-1} : X \to X$. Then $A^{-1}$ is a linear operator.

title: Inverse of Linear Transformation is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ and $U$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $A : V \to U$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear transformation with inverse mapping $A^{-1} : U \to V$. Then $A^{-1}$ is a linear transformation.

title: Inverse of Many-to-One Relation is One-to-Many
snippet: The inverse of a many-to-one relation is a one-to-many relation, and vice versa.

title: Inverse of Mapping is One-to-Many Relation
snippet: Let $f$ be a mapping. Then its inverse $f^{-1}$ is a one-to-many relation. Hence $f^{-1}$ is not necessarily a mapping itself.

title: Inverse of Mapping is Right-Total Relation
snippet: Let $f$ be a mapping. Then its inverse $f^{-1}$ is a right-total relation.

title: Inverse of Mapping to Annihilator on Algebraic Dual is Bijection
snippet: Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over a field. Let $J: G \to G^{**}$ be the evaluation isomorphism. Let $G^*$ be the algebraic dual of $G$. Let $M$ be an $m$-dimensional subspace of $G$. Let $M^\circ$ be the annihilator of $M$. Let $N$ be a $p$-dimensional subspace of $G^*$. Let $G_m$ denote the set of all $m$-dimensional subspaces of $G$. Let ${G^*}_{n - m}$ denote the set of all $n - m$-dimensional subspaces of $G^*$.

title: Inverse of Matrix Exponential
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\paren {e^{\mathbf A t} }^{-1} = e^{-\mathbf A t}$ where $\paren {e^{\mathbf A t} }^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $e^{\mathbf A t}$.

title: Inverse of Matrix Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf {A, B}$ be square matrices of order $n$ Let $\mathbf I$ be the $n \times n$ unit matrix. Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be nonsingular. Then the matrix product $\mathbf {AB}$ is also nonsingular, and: $\paren {\mathbf A \mathbf B}^{-1} = \mathbf B^{-1} \mathbf A^{-1}$

title: Inverse of Matrix is Scalar Product of Adjugate by Reciprocal of Determinant
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a nonsingular square matrix of order $n$. Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$. Let $\adj {\mathbf A}$ be the adjugate of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\mathbf A^{-1} = \dfrac 1 {\map \det {\mathbf A} } \cdot \adj {\mathbf A}$ where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathbf A$

title: Inverse of Multiplicative Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $a \in F$ such that $a \ne 0_F$. Let $a^{-1}$ be the multiplicative inverse of $a$. Then $\paren {a^{-1} }^{-1} = a$.

title: Inverse of Neighborhood of Diagonal Point is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological Space. Let $\tau_{X \times X}$ denote the product topology on the cartesian product $X \times X$. Let $x \in X$. Let $R$ be a neighborhood of $\tuple{x,x}$ in the product space $\struct{X \times X, \tau_{X \times X}}$. Let $R^{-1}$ denote the inverse relation of $R$ where $R$ is viewed as a relation on $X \times X$. Then: $R^{-1}$ is a neighborhood of $\tuple{x,x}$ in $\struct{X \times X, \tau_{X \times X}}$.

title: Inverse of Non-Reflexive Relation is Non-Reflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is non-reflexive, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Non-Symmetric Relation is Non-Symmetric
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is non-symmetric, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Non-Transitive Relation is Non-Transitive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is non-transitive, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Nonsingular 2 x 2 Real Square Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an nonsingular $2 \times 2$ real square matrix defined as: $\mathbf A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf A^{-1}$ is: $\mathbf A^{-1} = \dfrac 1 {\map \det {\mathbf A} } \begin {pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end {pmatrix} = \dfrac 1 {a d - b c} \begin {pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end {pmatrix}$

title: Inverse of One-to-One Relation is One-to-One
snippet: The inverse of a one-to-one relation is a one-to-one relation.

title: Inverse of Open Set in Product Space is Open in Inverse Product Space
snippet: Let $\struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\tau_{S_1 \times S_2}$ be the product topology on the Cartesian product $S_1 \times S_2$. Let $\tau_{S_2 \times S_1}$ be the product topology on the Cartesian product $S_2 \times S_1$. Let $V \subseteq S_1 \times S_2$. Let $V^{-1} \subseteq S_2 \times S_1$ denote the inverse of $V$ viewed as a relation on $S_1 \times S_2$. Then: $V$ is open in $\struct{S_1 \times S_2, \tau_{S_1 \times S_2}}$ $V^{-1}$ is open in $\struct{S_2 \times S_1, \tau_{S_2 \times S_1}}$

title: Inverse of Order Isomorphism is Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi$ be a bijection from $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ to $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$. Then: $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$ is an order isomorphism : $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, \preceq_2} \to \struct {S, \preceq_1}$ is also an order isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Ordered Ring Isomorphism is Ordered Ring Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, +, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \oplus, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered rings. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an ordered ring isomorphism. Then $\phi^{-1}: T \to S$ is also an ordered ring isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Ordered Semigroup Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} \to \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be a mapping. Then: $\phi$ is an ordered semigroup isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq} \to \struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ is also an ordered semigroup isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Orthogonal Matrix is Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an orthogonal matrix. Then its inverse $\mathbf A^{-1}$ is also orthogonal.

title: Inverse of Pascal's Triangle expressed as Matrix
snippet: Consider Pascal's triangle expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf M$, with the top left element holding $\dbinom 0 0$. $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 3 & 3 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 4 & 6 & 4 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 5 & 10 & 10 & 5 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 6 & 15 & 20 & 15 & 6 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 7 & 21 & 35 & 35 & 21 & 7 & 1 & 0 & \cdots \\ 1 & 8 & 28 & 56 & 70 & 56 & 28 & 8 & 1 & \cdots \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots…

title: Inverse of Permutation is Permutation
snippet: If $f$ is a permutation of $S$, then so is its inverse $f^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Plane Reflection Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf R$ be the matrix associated with a reflection in the plane. $\mathbf R = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 2\alpha & \sin 2\alpha \\ \sin 2\alpha & -\cos 2\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf R^{-1}$ is itself.

title: Inverse of Plane Rotation Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf R$ be the matrix associated with a rotation of the plane about the origin through an angle of $\alpha$: $\mathbf R = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse matrix $\mathbf R^{-1}$ is: $\mathbf R^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \alpha & \sin \alpha \\ -\sin \alpha & \cos \alpha \end{bmatrix}$

title: Inverse of Product of Subsets of Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $X, Y \subseteq G$. Then: $\paren {X \circ Y}^{-1} = Y^{-1} \circ X^{-1}$ where $X^{-1}$ is the inverse of $X$.

title: Inverse of Proper Orthogonal Matrix is Proper Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a proper orthogonal matrix. Then its inverse $\mathbf A^{-1}$ is also proper orthogonal.

title: Inverse of Real Square Function on Positive Reals
snippet: Let $f: \R_{\ge 0} \to R_{\ge 0}$ be the restriction of the real square function to the positive real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$. The inverse of $f$ is $f^{-1}: \R_{\ge 0} \times R_{\ge 0}$ defined as: $\forall x \in \R_{\ge 0}: \map {f^{-1} } x = \sqrt x$ where $\sqrt x$ is the positive square root of $x$.

title: Inverse of Reflexive Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is reflexive, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Relation Compatible with Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a closed algebraic structure. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$ which is compatible with $\circ$. Let $\QQ$ be the inverse relation of $\RR$. Then $\QQ$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Inverse of Relation Isomorphism is Relation Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \RR_1} \to \struct {T, \RR_2}$ be a bijection. Then: $\phi: \struct {S, \RR_1} \to \struct {T, \RR_2}$ is a relation isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, \RR_2} \to \struct {S, \RR_1}$ is also a relation isomorphism.

title: Inverse of Rescaling Matrix
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $r \in R$ be a unit in $R$. Let $r \, \mathbf I_n$ be the $n \times n$ rescaling matrix of $r$. Then: $\paren {r \, \mathbf I_n}^{-1} = r^{-1} \, \mathbf I_n$

title: Inverse of Right-Total Relation is Left-Total
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ be the inverse of $\RR$. Then: $\RR$ is right-total $\RR^{-1}$ is left-total.

title: Inverse of Similarity Mapping
snippet: Let $G$ be a vector space over a field $K$. Let $\beta \in K$ such that $\beta \ne 0$. Let $s_\beta: G \to G$ be the similarity on $G$ defined as: $\forall \mathbf x \in G: \map {s_\beta} {\mathbf x} = \beta \mathbf x$ Let $\paren {s_\beta}^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $s_\beta$. Then: $\paren {s_\beta}^{-1} = s_{\beta^{-1} }$ where $\beta^{-1}$ is the multiplicative inverse in $K$ of $\beta$.

title: Inverse of Small Relation is Small
snippet: Let $a$ be a small class. Let $a$ also be a relation. Then the inverse relation of $a$ is small.

title: Inverse of Square Matrix over Field is Unique
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a field, usually one of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$ or $\C$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map \MM n$ denote the matrix space of order $n$ square matrices over $\Bbb F$. Let $\mathbf B$ be an inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf B$ is the only inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$.

title: Inverse of Star of Element in Unital *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a unital $\ast$-algebra. Let $a \in A$ be invertible. Then $a^\ast$ is invertible and: $\paren {a^\ast}^{-1} = \paren {a^{-1} }^\ast$

title: Inverse of Stirling's Triangle expressed as Matrix
snippet: Consider Stirling's triangle of the first kind (signed) expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf A$, with the top left element holding $\map s {0, 0}$. $\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & -1 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 1 & 0 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & -6 & 11 & -6 & 1 & 0 & \cdots \\ 0 & 24 & -50 & 35 & -10 & 1 & \cdots \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots \\ \end{pmatrix}$ Then consider Stirling's triangle of the second kind expressed as a (square) matrix $\mathbf B$, with the top left element…

title: Inverse of Straight Line Not Through Inversion Center is Circle Through Inversion Center
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle on center $O$ in the plane. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $C$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Let $L$ be an arbitrary straight line not containing $O$. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point on $L$. Let $P'$ be the image of $P$ under $T$. Then $P'$ lies on a circle through $O$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Concave Real Function is Concave
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is concave on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \left[{I}\right]$. If $f$ be strictly decreasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is concave on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Convex Real Function is Convex
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is convex on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \left[{I}\right]$. If $f$ be strictly decreasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is convex on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Strictly Concave Real Function is Strictly Concave
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is strictly concave on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ be strictly decreasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is strictly concave on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Strictly Convex Real Function is Strictly Convex
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is strictly convex on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ be strictly decreasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is strictly convex on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Increasing Concave Real Function is Convex
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is concave on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ is strictly increasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is convex on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Increasing Convex Real Function is Concave
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is convex on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ be strictly increasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is concave on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Increasing Strictly Concave Real Function is Strictly Convex
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is strictly concave on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ be strictly increasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is strictly convex on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Increasing Strictly Convex Real Function is Strictly Concave
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is strictly convex on the open interval $I$. Let $J = f \sqbrk I$. If $f$ be strictly increasing on $I$, then $f^{-1}$ is strictly concave on $J$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Monotone Continuous Real Function is Strictly Monotone and Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a continuous real function which is defined on the closed interval $I := \closedint a b$. Let $f$ be strictly monotone on $I$. Then $f$ has an inverse function $f^{-1}$ which is continuous and strictly monotone on $f \sqbrk I$.

title: Inverse of Strictly Monotone Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is defined on $I \subseteq \R$. Let $f$ be strictly monotone on $I$. Let the image of $f$ be $J$. Then $f$ always has an inverse function $f^{-1}$ and: if $f$ is strictly increasing then so is $f^{-1}$ if $f$ is strictly decreasing then so is $f^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $H^{-1} = H$ where $H^{-1}$ is the inverse of $H$.

title: Inverse of Subset/Group/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Inverses of Subsets of Groups ==

title: Inverse of Subset of Relation is Subset of Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets Let $\RR_1 = S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR_2 \subseteq \RR_1$. Then: $\RR_2^{-1} \subseteq \RR_1^{-1}$ where $\RR_1^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\RR_1$.

title: Inverse of Supremum in Ordered Group is Infimum of Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $x, y \in G$. Then: $\set {x, y}$ admits a supremum in $G$ $\set {x^{-1}, y^{-1} }$ admits an infimum in $G$ in which case: $\paren {\sup \set {x, y} }^{-1} = \inf \set {x^{-1}, y^{-1} }$

title: Inverse of Surjection is Relation both Left-Total and Right-Total
snippet: Let $f$ be an surjective mapping. Then its inverse $f^{-1}$ is a relation which is both left-total and right-total.

title: Inverse of Symmetric Relation is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. If $\RR$ is symmetric, then so is $\RR^{-1}$.

title: Inverse of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR$ be transitive. Then its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is also transitive.

title: Inverse of Transpose of Matrix is Transpose of Inverse
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix over a field. Let $\mathbf A^\intercal$ denote the transpose of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf A$ be an nonsingular matrix. Then $\mathbf A^\intercal$ is also nonsingular and: $\paren {\mathbf A^\intercal}^{-1} = \paren {\mathbf A^{-1} }^\intercal$ where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\mathbf A$.

title: Inverse of Unit in Centralizer of Ring is in Centralizer
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a subset of $R$. Let $\map {C_R} S$ denote the centralizer of $S$ in $R$ Let $u \in R$ be a unit of $R$. Then: $u \in \map {C_R} S \implies u^{-1} \in \map {C_R} S$

title: Inverse of Vandermonde Matrix
snippet: Let $V_n$ be the Vandermonde matrix of order $n$ given by: $V_n = \begin {bmatrix} x_1 & x_2 & \cdots & x_n \\ x_1^2 & x_2^2 & \cdots & x_n^2 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ x_1^n & x_2^n & \cdots & x_n^n \end{bmatrix}$ Then its inverse $V_n^{-1} = \sqbrk b_n$ can be specified as: $b_{i j} = \begin {cases} \paren {-1}^{j - 1} \paren {\dfrac {\ds \sum_{\substack {1 \mathop \le m_1 \mathop

title: Inverse of a Line Through Circle Center is a Line
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle in the plane on center $O$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Let $L$ be an arbitrary ray through $O$. Let $P$ be an otherwise arbitrary point, but lying on $L$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be an inversive transformation with $C$ as the inversion circle. Then $O$ is the inversion center. Then the image of $P$ under $T$ also lies on $L$.

title: Inverse reverses Preorder of Positive Invertible Elements of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\le_A$ be the canonical preordering on $A$. Let $a, b \in A$ be positive and invertible such that: $a \le_A b$ Then we have: $0 \le_A b^{-1} \le_A a^{-1}$

title: Inverses in Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G \times H, \circ}$ be the group direct product of the two groups $\struct {G, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {H, \circ_2}$. Let $g^{-1}$ be an inverse of $g \in \struct {G, \circ_1}$. Let $h^{-1}$ be an inverse of $h \in \struct {H, \circ_2}$. Then $\tuple {g^{-1}, h^{-1} }$ is the inverse of $\tuple {g, h} \in \struct {G \times H, \circ}$.

title: Inverses in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then for each $h \in H$, the inverse of $h$ in $H$ is the same as the inverse of $h$ in $G$.

title: Inverses of Elements Related by Compatible Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR$ be a relation compatible with $\circ$. Then: $\forall x, y \in G: x \mathrel \RR y \iff y^{-1} \mathrel \RR x^{-1}$

title: Inverses of Right-Total and Left-Total Relations
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^{-1} \subseteq T \times S$ be the inverse of $\RR$. Then:

title: Inversion Mapping Reverses Ordering in Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $\prec$ be the reflexive reduction of $\preceq$. Then the following equivalences hold: {{eqn | q = \forall x, y \in G | l = x \preccurlyeq y | o = \iff | r = e \prec y^{-1} \preccurlyeq x^{-1} }} {{eqn | q = \forall x, y \in S | l = x \prec y | o = \iff | r = y^{-1} \prec x^{-1} }}

title: Inversion Mapping is Automorphism iff Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$, defined as: $\forall g \in G: \map \iota g = g^{-1}$ Then $\iota$ is an automorphism $G$ is abelian.

title: Inversion Mapping is Involution
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping. Then $\iota$ is an involution. That is: $\forall g \in G: \map \iota {\map \iota g} = g$

title: Inversion Mapping is Isomorphism from Ordered Abelian Group to its Dual
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered Abelian group. Let $\struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ be the dual of $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq} \to \struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ be the inversion mapping from $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ to $\struct {G, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ defined as: $\forall x \in G: \map \phi x = x^{-1}$ where $x^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $x$ in $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

title: Inversion Mapping is Isomorphism to Opposite Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be its opposite group. That is: $\forall g, h \in G: g \circ h = h * g$ Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping for $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then $\iota: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {G, *}$ is a group isomorphism.

title: Inversion Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$. Then $\iota$ is indeed a mapping.

title: Inversion Mapping is Permutation
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping on $G$. Then $\iota$ is a permutation on $G$.

title: Inversion Mapping on Ordered Group is Dual Order-Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered group. Let $\iota: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping, defined by $\map \phi x = x^{-1}$. Then $\iota$ is a dual order-isomorphism.

title: Inversion Mapping on Topological Group is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T = \struct {G, \circ, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $\phi: G \to G$ be the inversion mapping of $T$. Then $\phi$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Inversive Transformation in Euclidean Space is Conformal
snippet: Let $f$ be an inversive transformation in Euclidean space. Then $f$ is a conformal transformation.

title: Inversive Transformation is Conformal Transformation
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle embedded in a Cartesian plane $\EE$ whose center $O$ is at the origin $\tuple {0, 0}$ and whose radius is $r$. Let $f$ be the inversive transformation of $\EE$ $\CC$. Then $f$ is a conformal transformation.

title: Invertibility of Arithmetic Functions
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \C$ be an arithmetic function. Then $f$ has a Dirichlet inverse : $\map f 1 \ne 0$

title: Invertibility of Identity Minus Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator such that: $\norm T_{\map \BB X} < 1$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB X}$ denotes the norm of a bounded linear operator. Then $I - T$ is invertible as a bounded linear operator. In particular: $\ds \paren {I - T}^{-1} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty T^n$

title: Invertibility of Identity Transformation Plus Product of Two Continuous Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm{, \cdot ,} }$ be the normed vector space. Let $I : X \to X$ be the identity mapping. Let $\map {CL} X := \map {CL} {X, X}$ be the continuous linear transformation space on $X$. Suppose $I + A \circ B$ is invertible, where $\circ$ denotes the composition of mappings. Then $I + B \circ A$ is invertible, with the inverse given by: $\paren {I + B \circ A}^{-1} = I - B \circ \paren {I + A \circ B}^{-1} \circ A$

title: Invertible Bounded Linear Transformation with Norm and Norm of Inverse Bounded Above by One is Isometric Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $\struct {\map \BB {X, Y}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {X, Y} } }$ and $\struct {\map \BB {Y, X}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {X, Y} } }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $X 	o Y$ and $Y 	o X$ respectively. Let $T : X 	o Y$ be an invertible bounded linear transformation such that: $
orm T_{\map \BB {X, Y} } \le 1$ and: $
orm {T^{-1} }_{\map \BB {Y, X} } \le 1$ Then $T$ is an isometric isomorphism.

title: Invertible Continuous Linear Operator has Unique Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the normed vector space. Let $\map {CL} X := \map {CL} {X, X}$ be a continuous linear transformation space. Let $I \in \map {CL} X$ be the identity element. Suppose $A \in \map {CL} X$ is invertible. Then there is a unique $B \in \map {CL} X$ such that $A \circ B = B \circ A = I$.

title: Invertible Continuous Linear Operator is Bijective
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the normed vector space. Let $\map {CL} X := \map {CL} {X, X}$ be a continuous linear transformation space. Let $I \in \map {CL} X$ be the identity element. Suppose $A \in \map {CL} X$ is invertible. Then $A$ is bijective.

title: Invertible Element containing Identity in Power Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let identity element $e \in S$ be an identity element of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $X \subseteq S$ such that: $e \in X$ $X$ is invertible for $\circ_PP$. Then $X = \set e$.

title: Invertible Element of Associative Structure is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure where $\circ$ is associative. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity element $e_S$. An element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ which is invertible is also cancellable.

title: Invertible Elements of Monoid form Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity element is $e$. Let $U \subseteq S$ be the subset of $S$ consisting of the invertible elements of $S$. Then $\struct {U, \circ}$ forms a subgroup of $S$.

title: Invertible Elements of Monoid form Subgroup of Cancellable Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $C$ be the set of all cancellable elements of $S$. Let $T$ be the set of all invertible elements of $S$. Then $\struct {T, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {C, \circ}$.

title: Invertible Elements under Natural Number Multiplication
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $\times$ denote multiplication. Then the only invertible element of $\N$ for $\times$ is $1$.

title: Invertible Integers under Multiplication
snippet: The only invertible elements of $\Z$ for multiplication (that is, units of $\Z$) are $1$ and $-1$.

title: Invertible Matrix Corresponds with Change of Basis
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be an $n$-dimensional unitary $R$-module. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be an ordered basis of $G$. Let $\mathbf P = \sqbrk \alpha_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$ over $R$. Let $\ds \forall j \in \closedint 1 n: b_j = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_{i j} a_i$. Then $\sequence {b_n}$ is an ordered basis of $G$ $\mathbf P$ is nonsingular.

title: Involution is Permutation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an involution. Then $f$ is a permutation.

title: Irrational Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irrational Numbers ==

title: Irrational Number Space is Completely Metrizable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is completely metrizable.

title: Irrational Number Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is a completely normal space.

title: Irrational Number Space is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is dense-in-itself.

title: Irrational Number Space is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is non-meager.

title: Irrational Number Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is paracompact.

title: Irrational Number Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is second-countable.

title: Irrational Number Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is separable.

title: Irrational Number Space is Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space formed by the irrational numbers $\R \setminus \Q$ under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Then $\tau_d$ forms a topology.

title: Irrational Number Space is Totally Separated
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is totally separated.

title: Irrational Number Space is Zero Dimensional
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is zero dimensional.

title: Irrational Number Space is not Locally Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is not a locally compact Hausdorff Space.

title: Irrational Number Space is not Scattered
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is not scattered.

title: Irrational Number Space is not Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ be the irrational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then $\struct {\R \setminus \Q, \tau_d}$ is not weakly $\sigma$-locally compact.

title: Irrational Number divided by Rational Number is Irrational
snippet: Let $x$ be a irrational number. Let $y$ be a non-zero rational number. Then: $\dfrac x y$ is irrational.

title: Irrational Number has Periodic Continued Fraction iff Quadratic
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number. Then $x$ is a quadratic irrational its continued fraction expansion is periodic.

title: Irrational Number is Limit of Unique Simple Infinite Continued Fraction
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number. Then the continued fraction expansion of $x$ is the unique simple infinite continued fraction that converges to $x$.

title: Irrational Numbers are Uncountably Infinite
snippet: The set $\R \setminus \Q$ of irrational numbers is uncountable.

title: Irrational Numbers form G-Delta Set in Reals
snippet: Let $\R \setminus \Q$ denote the set of irrational numbers. Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\R \setminus \Q$ forms a $G_\delta$ set in $\R$.

title: Irrational Numbers form Metric Space
snippet: Let $\mathbb I = \R \setminus \Q$ be the set of all irrational numbers. Let $d: \mathbb I \times \mathbb I \to \R$ be defined as: $\map d {x_1, x_2} = \size {x_1 - x_2}$ where $\size x$ is the absolute value of $x$. Then $d$ is a metric on $\mathbb I$ and so $\struct {\mathbb I, d}$ is a metric space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is T0
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is a $T_0$ space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is T1
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is T2
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not Normal
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a normal space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not Regular
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a regular space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not T2.5
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not T3
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not T4
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a $T_4$ space.

title: Irrational Slope Space is not T5
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is not a $T_5$ space.

title: Irrationality of Logarithm
snippet: Let $a, b \in \N_{>0}$ such that both $\nexists m, n \in \N_{>0}: a^m = b^n$. Then $\log_b a$ is irrational.

title: Irrationals are Everywhere Dense in Reals
Irreducible Component is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be an irreducible component of $T$. Then $Y$ is closed in $T$.

title: Irreducible Components of Hausdorff Space are Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty Hausdorff space. Then the irreducible components of $T$ are the singleton sets.

title: Irreducible Elements of 5th Cyclotomic Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ denote the $5$th cyclotomic ring. The following elements of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ are irreducible: $2$ $3$ $1 + i \sqrt 5$ $1 - i \sqrt 5$

title: Irreducible Elements of Ring of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers. The irreducible elements of $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ are the prime numbers and their negatives.

title: Irreducible Fraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irreducible Fractions ==

title: Irreducible Hausdorff Space is Singleton
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space which is irreducible and Hausdorff. Then $S$ is a singleton.

title: Irreducible Polynomial/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irreducible Polynomials ==

title: Irreducible Radical/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Irreducible Radicals ==

title: Irreducible Representations of Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a finite abelian group. Let $V$ be a non-null vector space over an algebraically closed field $K$. Let $\rho: G \to \GL V$ be a linear representation. Then $\rho$ is irreducible $\map {\dim_K} V = 1$, where, $\dim_K$ denotes dimension.

title: Irreducible Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is connected.

title: Irreducible Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is locally connected.

title: Irreducible Space is Pseudocompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is pseudocompact.

title: Irreducible Space is not necessarily Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is not necessarily path-connected.

title: Irreducible Space is not necessarily Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is ultraconnected.

title: Irreducible Space with Finitely Many Open Sets is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an irreducible topological space. Let its topology $\tau$ be finite. Then $T$ is path-connected.

title: Irreducible Subspace is Contained in Irreducible Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S_1, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space. Let $S_2$ be an irreducible subset of $S_1$. Then there exists an irreducible component $S_3$ of $T$ such that $S_2 \subseteq S_3$.

title: Is 2 to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $2$ to the power of Euler's number $e$: $2^e$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is 2 to the power of Pi Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $2$ to the power of $\pi$ (pi): $2^\pi$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is Apéry's Constant Transcendental?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Apéry's constant $\map \zeta 3$ is transcendental or not.

title: Is Catalan's Constant Irrational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Catalan's constant is rational or irrational.

title: Is Euler's Number Normal?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's Number $e$ is normal.

title: Is Euler's Number to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's number $e$ to the power of itself: $e^e$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is Euler's Number to the power of Pi Squared Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether Euler's number $e$ to the power of $\pi$ (pi) squared: $e^{\pi^2}$ is rational or irrational. Category:Open Questions

title: Is Euler-Mascheroni Constant Irrational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not even known whether the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\gamma$ is irrational, let alone whether it is transcendental or not.

title: Is Log of Pi Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the logarithm of $\pi$ (pi): $\ln \pi$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is Pi Normal?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $\pi$ (pi) is normal.

title: Is Pi multiplied by Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the product of $\pi$ (pi) and Euler's number $e$: $\pi \times e$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is Pi plus Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the sum of $\pi$ (pi) and Euler's number $e$: $\pi + e$ is rational or irrational.

title: Is Pi to the power of Euler's Number Rational?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether $\pi$(pi) to the power of Euler's number $e$: $\pi^e$ is rational or irrational. Its decimal expansion gives its value to be approximately: $\pi^e \approx 22 \cdotp 45915 \, 77183 \, 61045 \, 47342 \, 7152 \ldots$

title: Is the Mandelbrot Set Locally Connected?
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether the Mandelbrot set is locally connected in the complex plane $\C$.

title: Is there a Limit to the Multiplicative Persistence of a Number?
snippet: It has been conjectured that there may be an upper limit to the multiplicative persistence of a natural number.

title: Is there an Infinite Number of Palindromic Primes?
snippet: == Open Question == Is there an infinite number of palindromic primes?

title: Is there an Infinite Number of Primes of Form n^2 + 1?
snippet: == Open Question == Is there an infinite number of prime numbers of the form $n^2 + 1$?

snippet: == Open Question == Is there an infinite number of repunit primes?

title: Island and Lake Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == An island is a body of land surrounded entirely by water. A lake is a body of water surrounded entirely by land. What if you had a planet whose northern hemisphere was all land, and whose southern hemisphere was all water? Would you call the northern hemisphere an island, or would you call the southern hemisphere a lake? Or would you say: there is an island in the middle of a lake which is in the middle of an island which is in the middle of a lake which is in the middle of an island $\ldots$ ?

title: Island in English Channel Further from France than England
snippet: == Problem == There is a certain island, situated between and , and yet, that island is farther from than is.

title: Isolated Point in Metric Space iff Isolated Point in Topological Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $T = \struct {A, \tau}$ be the topological space with the topology induced by $d$. Let $H \subseteq A$. Let $x \in H$ Then: $x$ is an isolated point of $H$ in $M$ $x$ is an isolated point of $H$ in $T$

title: Isolated Point of Closure of Subset is Isolated Point of Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$. Let $\map \cl H$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $x \in \map \cl H$ be an isolated point of $\map \cl H$. Then $x$ is also an isolated point of $H$.

title: Isolated Points in Arens-Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the Arens-Fort space. Let $q \in S: q \ne \tuple {0, 0}$. Then $q$ is an isolated point of $T$.

title: Isolated Points in Subsets of Modified Fort Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Let $H \subseteq S$ contain more than two points. Then $H$ contains an isolated point.

title: Isometric Image of Cauchy Sequence is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, d_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be an isometry. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $S_1$. Let $\sequence {y_n} = \sequence {\map f {x_n} }$ be the image of $\sequence {x_n}$ under $f$. Then $\sequence {y_n}$ is a Cauchy sequence.

orm x_R $

title: Isometric Metric Spaces/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Isometric Metric Spaces ==

title: Isometric Metric Spaces are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be isometric. Then $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic.
