title: Lagrange's Formula
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions. Then: $\mathbf a \times \paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf c} = \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf c} \mathbf b - \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b} \mathbf c$

title: Lagrange's Four Square Theorem
snippet: Every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of four squares.

title: Lagrange's Identity

title: Lagrange's Theorem
snippet: Lagrange's Theorem (Number Theory), about the number of solutions of an integral polynomial in $\Z_p$. Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory), concerning the order of a subgroup. Lagrange's Four Square Theorem: every positive integer can be expressed as the sum of four squares of integers.

title: Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\order H$ divides $\order G$ where $\order G$ and $\order H$ are the order of $G$ and $H$ respectively. In fact: $\index G H = \dfrac {\order G} {\order H}$ where $\index G H$ is the index of $H$ in $G$. When $G$ is an infinite group, we can still interpret this theorem sensibly: A subgroup of finite index in an infinite group is itself an infinite group. A finite subgroup of an infinite group has infinite index.

title: Lagrange's Theorem (Number Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_p, +_p, \times_p}$ be the ring of integers modulo $p$ for some prime $p$. Let $f$ be a polynomial in one variable of degree $n$ over $\Z_p$. Then $f$ has at most $n$ roots in $\Z_p$.

title: Lagrange Polynomial Approximation
snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be $n + 1$ times differentiable in an interval $I \subseteq \R$. Let $x_0, \dotsc, x_n \in I$ be pairwise distinct points. Let $P$ be the Lagrange Interpolation Formula of degree at most $n$ such that: $\forall i \in \set {0, \dotsc, n}: \map P {x_i} = \map f {x_i}$ Let $\map R x = \map f x - \map P x$. Then, for every $x \in I$, there exists $\xi$ in the interval spanned by $x$ and $x_i$, $i = 0, \dotsc, n$, such that: $\map R x = \dfrac {\paren {x - x_0} \paren {x - x_1} \dotsm \paren {x - x_n} \map {f^{\paren {n + 1} } } \xi} {\paren {n + 1}!}$

title: Lambert W of Non-Zero Algebraic Number is Transcendental
snippet: Let $W$ denote the (general) Lambert $W$ function. Let $a$ be a non-zero algebraic number. Then $\map W a$ is transcendental.

title: Lambert W of Zero is Zero
snippet: Let $W_0$ denote principal branch of the Lambert W function. Then: $W_0 \left({0}\right) = 0$

title: Lami's Theorem
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in static equilibrium. Let the only forces acting on $B$ be $F_a$, $F_b$ and $F_c$. Let $F_a$, $F_b$ and $F_c$ be represented by the vectors $V_a$, $V_b$ and $V_c$ respectively, such that the magnitudes and directions of each force corresponds to the magnitudes and directions of each vectors. Let the directions of $V_a$, $V_b$ and $V_c$ be non-parallel.

title: Lamé's Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $c$ and $d$ be the number of digits in $a$ and $b$ respectively when expressed in decimal notation. Let the Euclidean Algorithm be employed to find the GCD of $a$ and $b$. Then it will take fewer than $5 \times \min \set {c, d}$ integer divisions to find $\gcd \set {a, b}$.

title: Landau's Theorem
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a holomorphic function in the unit disk $\cmod z \le 1$. Let $\cmod {\map {f'} 0} = 1$. Then there exists: a disk $D$ of radius $B$ an analytic function $\phi$ in $D$ such that $\map f {\map \phi z} = z$ for all $z$ in $D$ such that $L$ is an absolute constant where: $L > B$ where $B$ is Bloch's constant.

title: Language of Predicate Logic has Unique Parsability
snippet: Each WFF of predicate logic which starts with a left bracket or a negation sign has exactly one main connective.

title: Language of Propositional Logic has Unique Parsability
snippet: The language of propositional logic $\LL_0$ has unique parsability.

title: Laplace's Expansion Theorem
snippet: Let $D$ be the determinant of order $n$. Let $r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_k$ be integers such that: $1 \le k < n$ $1 \le r_1 < r_2 < \cdots < r_k \le n$ Let $\map D {r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_k \mid u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_k}$ be an order-$k$ minor of $D$. Let $\map {\tilde D} {r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_k \mid u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_k}$ be the cofactor of $\map D {r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_k \mid u_1, u_2, \ldots, u_k}$.

title: Laplace Expansion Theorem for Determinants
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $D = \map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$: $\ds \map \det {\mathbf A} := \sum_{\lambda} \paren {\map \sgn \lambda \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_{k \map \lambda k} } = \sum_\lambda \map \sgn \lambda a_{1 \map \lambda 1} a_{2 \map \lambda 2} \cdots a_{n \map \lambda n}$ where: the summation $\ds \sum_\lambda$ goes over all the $n!$ permutations of $\set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ $\map \sgn \lambda$ is the sign of the permutation $\lambda$. Let $a_{p q}$ be an element of $\mathbf A$.

title: Laplace Transform/Graphical Interpretation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Graphical Interpretation of Laplace Transforms == The following are three examples of the contours defined by the integrand defining the Laplace transform of $\map \cos t$.

title: Laplace Transform Determination
snippet: == Solution Techniques for Laplace Transforms == The following techniques may be used to find the Laplace transform $\laptrans f$ of a function $f$.

title: Laplace Transform Exists if Function Piecewise Continuous and of Exponential Order
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is: piecewise continuous in every closed interval $\closedint 0 N$ of exponential order $\gamma$ for $t > N$. Then the Laplace transform $\map F s$ of $\map f t$ exists for all $s > \gamma$.

title: Laplace Transform of 1
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the function defined as: $\forall t \in \R: \map f t = 1$ Then the Laplace transform of $\map f t$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map f t} = \dfrac 1 s$ for $\map \Re s > 0$.

title: Laplace Transform of Bessel Function of the First Kind
snippet: Let $J_n$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$. Then the Laplace transform of $J_n$ is given as: $\laptrans {\map {J_n} {a t} } = \dfrac {\paren {\sqrt {s^2 + a^2} - s}^n} {a^n \sqrt {s^2 + a^2} }$

title: Laplace Transform of Bessel Function of the First Kind of Order One
snippet: Let $J_1$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $1$. Then the Laplace transform of $J_1$ is given as: $\laptrans {\map {J_1} t} = \dfrac {\sqrt {s^2 + 1} - s} {\sqrt {s^2 + 1} }$

title: Laplace Transform of Bessel Function of the First Kind of Order Zero
snippet: Let $J_0$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$. Then the Laplace transform of $J_0$ is given as: $\laptrans {\map {J_0} t} = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {s^2 + 1} }$

title: Laplace Transform of Complex Power
snippet: Let $q$ be a constant complex number with $\map \Re q > -1$. Let $t^q$ be the the principal branch of the $q$-th complex power whose domain contains the half-plane $\map \Re s > 0$. Then $t^q$ has a Laplace transform given by: $\laptrans {t^q} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {q + 1} } {s^{q + 1} }$ where $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function.

title: Laplace Transform of Constant Mapping
snippet: Let $a \in \R$ be a real constant. Let $f_a: \R \to \R$ or $\C$ be the constant mapping, defined as: $\forall t \in \R: \map {f_a} t = a$ Let $\laptrans {f_a}$ be the Laplace transform of $f_a$. Then: $\laptrans {\map {f_a} t} = \dfrac a s$ for $\map \Re s > a$.

title: Laplace Transform of Cosine
snippet: Let $\cos$ be the real cosine function. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\cos a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 + a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

title: Laplace Transform of Cosine Integral Function
snippet: $\laptrans {\map \Ci t} = \dfrac {\map \ln {s^2 + 1} } {2 s}$ where: $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$ $\Ci$ denotes the cosine integral function.

title: Laplace Transform of Cosine of Root over Root
snippet: $\laptrans {\dfrac {\cos \sqrt t} {\sqrt t} } = \sqrt {\dfrac \pi s} \, \map \exp {-\dfrac 1 {4 s} }$ where $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$.

title: Laplace Transform of Derivative
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function, differentiable on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le A$. Let $f$ be of exponential order $a$. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Let $f'$ be piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Then $\laptrans f$ exists for $\map \Re s > a$, and: $\laptrans {\map {f'} t} = s \laptrans {\map f t} - \map f 0$

title: Laplace Transform of Derivative with Finite Discontinuities
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function, differentiable on any interval of the form $0 < t \le A$. Let $f$ be of exponential order $a$. Let $f'$ be piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Let $f$ have a finite number of jump discontinuities at $t = a_i$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$. Then: $\laptrans {\map {f'} t} = s \laptrans {\map f t} - \map f 0 - \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n e^{-a_i s} \paren {\map f {a_i^+} - \map f {a_i^-} }$

title: Laplace Transform of Difference between Exponentials
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {e^{b t} - e^{a t} } {b - a} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} }$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers such that $a \ne b$ $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of Dirac Delta Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta t$ denote the Dirac delta function. The Laplace transform of $\map \delta t$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map \delta t} = 1$

title: Laplace Transform of Dirac Delta Function by Function
snippet: Let $\map f t: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a function. Let $\map \delta t$ denote the Dirac delta function. Let $c$ be a positive constant real number. Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\map \delta {t - c} \map f t} = e^{- s c} \map f c$

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential
snippet: {{expand|three theorems: $\laptrans {e^{a t} }$ for $a \in \R$; $\laptrans {e^{i b t} }$ for $b \in \R$; $\laptrans {e^{\psi t} }$ for $\psi \in \C$In progress: this page has been renamed, and a master page created. The pages for the second two instances need to be written. In due course, unless someone gets there before me.}}

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential Integral Function
snippet: Let $\Ei: \R_{>0} \to \R$ denote the exponential integral function: $\map \Ei x = \ds \int_{t \mathop = x}^{t \mathop \to +\infty} \frac {e^{-t} } t \rd t$ Then: $\laptrans {\map \Ei t} = \dfrac {\map \ln {s + 1} } s$ where $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Cosine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {s - b} {\paren {s - b}^2 + a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Hyperbolic Cosine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {s - b} {\paren {s - b}^2 - a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Hyperbolic Sine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \sinh a t} } s = \dfrac a {\paren {s - b}^2 - a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Sine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \sin a t} } s = \dfrac a {\paren {s - b}^2 + a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of Function of Constant Multiple
snippet: Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of a real function $f$. Let $a \in \C$ or $\R$ be constant. Then: $a \laptrans {\map f {a t} } = \map F {\dfrac s a}$

title: Laplace Transform of Function of Square of t
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: $\laptrans {\map f {t^2} } = \ds \dfrac 1 {2 \sqrt \pi} \int_0^\infty u^{3 / 2} e^{-s^2 / 4 u} \map F u \rd u$ where $\laptrans {\map f {t^2} }$ denotes the Laplace transform of $\map f {t^2}$.

title: Laplace Transform of Gauss Error Function
snippet: $\laptrans {\map \erf t} = \dfrac 1 s \map \exp {\dfrac {s^2} 4} \map \erfc {\dfrac s 2}$ where: $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$ $\erf$ denotes the Gauss error function $\erfc$ denotes the complementary error function $\exp$ denotes the exponential function.

title: Laplace Transform of Gauss Error Function of Root
snippet: $\laptrans {\map \erf {\sqrt t} } = \dfrac 1 {s \sqrt {s + 1} }$ where: $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$ $\erf$ denotes the Gauss error function

title: Laplace Transform of Generating Function of Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence{a_n}$ be a sequence which has a generating function which is convergent. Let $\map G z$ be the generating function for $\sequence{a_n}$. Let $\map f x$ be the step function: $\map f x = \ds \sum_{k \mathop \in \Z} a_k \sqbrk{0 \le k \le x}$ where $\sqbrk{0 \le k \le x}$ is Iverson's convention. Then the Laplace transform of $\map f x$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map f s} = \dfrac {\map G {e^{-s} }} s$

title: Laplace Transform of Half Wave Rectified Sine Curve
snippet: Consider the half wave rectified sine curve: $\map f t = \begin {cases} \sin t & : 2 n \pi \le t \le \paren {2 n + 1} \pi \\ 0 & : \paren {2 n + 1} \pi \le t \le \paren {2 n + 2} \pi \end {cases}$ The Laplace transform of $\map f t$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map f t} = \dfrac 1 {\paren {1 - e^{-\pi s} } \paren {s^2 + 1} }$

title: Laplace Transform of Heaviside Step Function
snippet: Let $\map {u_c} t$ denote the Heaviside step function: $\map {u_c} t = \begin {cases} 1 & : t > c \\ 0 & : t The Laplace transform of $\map {u_c} t$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map {u_c} t} = \dfrac {e^{-s c} } s$ for $\map \Re s > c$.

title: Laplace Transform of Heaviside Step Function times Function
snippet: Let $\map f t: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a function of exponential order $a$ for some constant $a \in \R$. Let $f$ be piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on any closed interval of the form $\closedint 0 b$ where $b > 0$. Let $\map {u_c} t$ be the Heaviside step function. Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\map {u_c} t \, \map f {t - c} } = e^{-s c} \map F s$ for $\map \Re s > a$.

title: Laplace Transform of Higher Order Derivatives
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le a$. Let $f$ be $n$ times differentiable on said intervals. Let $f, f', \ldots, f^{\paren {n - 1} }$ be continuous and $f^{\paren n}$ piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Let $f, f', \ldots, f^{\paren {n - 1} }$ be of exponential order. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$.

title: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Cosine
snippet: Let $\cosh t$ be the hyperbolic cosine, where $t$ is real. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\cosh a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 - a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

title: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Sine
snippet: Let $\sinh t$ be the hyperbolic sine, where $t$ is real. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\sinh a t} = \dfrac a {s^2 - a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

title: Laplace Transform of Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$. Let $\map {I_\R} t$ denote the identity mapping on $\R$ for $t > 0$. Then: $\laptrans {\map {I_\R} t} = \dfrac 1 {s^2}$ for $\map \Re s > 0$.

title: Laplace Transform of Integral
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a function. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then: $\ds \laptrans {\int_0^t \map f u \rd u} = \dfrac {\map F s} s$ wherever $\laptrans f$ exists.

title: Laplace Transform of Multiple Integral
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a function. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then for all $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$: $\ds \laptrans {\underbrace {\int_0^t \dotsm \int_0^t}_{\text {$n$ times} } \map f u \rd u^n} = \dfrac {\map F s} {s^n}$ wherever $\laptrans f$ exists.

title: Laplace Transform of Natural Logarithm
snippet: $\laptrans {\ln t} = \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} 1 - \ln s} s = -\dfrac {\gamma + \ln s} s$ where: $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$ $\Gamma$ denotes the Gamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Laplace Transform of Null Function
snippet: Let $\NN: \R \to \R$ be a null function. The Laplace transform of $\map \NN t$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map \NN t} = 0$

title: Laplace Transform of Periodic Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be periodic, that is: $\exists T \in \R_{\ne 0}: \forall x \in \R: \map f x = \map f {x + T}$ Then: $\laptrans {\map f t} = \dfrac 1 {1 - e^{-s T} } \ds \int_0^T e^{-s t} \map f t \rd t$ where $\laptrans {\map f t}$ denotes the Laplace transform.

title: Laplace Transform of Positive Integer Power
snippet: Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$. Let $t^n: \R \to \R$ be $t$ to the $n$th power for some $n \in \N_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\laptrans {t^n} = \dfrac {n!} {s^{n + 1} }$ for $\map \Re s > 0$.

title: Laplace Transform of Positive Integer Power times Exponential
snippet: Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$. Let $e^x$ be the real exponential. Then: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^{n - 1} e^{a t} } {\paren {n - 1}!} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s - a}^n}$ where: $a \in \R$ is constant $\map \Re s > \map \Re a$ $n \in \N_{>0}$

title: Laplace Transform of Positive Real Power times Exponential
snippet: Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$. Let $e^x$ be the real exponential. Then: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^{n - 1} e^{a t} } {\map \Gamma n} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s - a}^n}$ where: $a \in \R$ is constant $\map \Re s > \map \Re a$ $n \in \R_{>0}$

title: Laplace Transform of Real Power
snippet: Let $n$ be a constant real number such that $n > -1$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\map f t = t^n$ Then $f$ has a Laplace transform given by: {{eqn | l = \laptrans {\map f t} | r = \int_0^\infty e^{-s t} t^n \rd t }} {{eqn | r = \frac {\map \Gamma {n + 1} } {s^{n + 1} } }} where $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function.

title: Laplace Transform of Reciprocal of Square Root
snippet: $\forall t \in \R_{\ne 0}: \laptrans {\dfrac 1 {\sqrt t} } = \sqrt {\dfrac \pi s}$ where $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the real function $f$.

title: Laplace Transform of Second Derivative
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le a$. Let $f$ be twice differentiable. Let $f'$ be continuous and $f' '$ piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Let $f$ and $f'$ be of exponential order. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then $\laptrans {f' '}$ exists for $\map \Re s > a$, and: $\laptrans {\map {f' '} t} = s^2 \laptrans {\map f t} - s \, \map f 0 - \map {f'} 0$

title: Laplace Transform of Shifted Dirac Delta Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta t$ denote the Dirac delta function. The Laplace transform of $\map \delta {t - a}$ is given by: $\laptrans {\map \delta {t - a} } = e^{-a s}$

title: Laplace Transform of Sine
snippet: Let $\sin$ denote the real sine function. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\sin at} = \dfrac a {s^2 + a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > 0$.

title: Laplace Transform of Sine Integral Function
snippet: $\laptrans {\map \Si t} = \dfrac 1 s \arctan \dfrac 1 s$ where: $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$ $\Si$ denotes the sine integral function

title: Laplace Transform of Sine of Root
snippet: $\laptrans {\sin \sqrt t} = \dfrac {\sqrt \pi} {2 s^{3/2} } \map \exp {-\dfrac 1 {4 s} }$ where $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of the function $f$.

title: Laplace Transform of Sine of t over t
snippet: Let $\sin$ denote the real sine function. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\dfrac {\sin t} t} = \arctan \dfrac 1 s$

title: Laplace Transform of a t cosh a t - sinh a t over 2 a^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {a t \cosh a t - \sinh a t} {2 a^3} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of b e^bt - a e^at over b - a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {b e^{b t} - a e^{a t} } {b - a} } } s = \dfrac s {\paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} }$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers such that $a \ne b$ $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of cos a t by cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\cos a t \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {s^3} {s^4 + 4 a^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of cosh a t + half a t sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\cosh a t + \dfrac 1 2 a t \sinh a t} } s = \dfrac {s^3} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of cosine a t - half a t sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\cos a t - \dfrac 1 2 a t \sin a t} } s = \dfrac {s^3} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of sine a t + a t cosine a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\sin a t + a t \cos a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of sine a t - a t cosine a t over 2 a^3
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\sin a t - a t \cos a t} {2 a^3} } } s = \dfrac 1 {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of sinh a t + a t cosh a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {\sinh a t + a t \cosh a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {2 s \paren {s^2 + 3 a^2} } {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosh a t over 2
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^2 \cosh a t} 2} } s = \dfrac {s^3 + 3 a^2 s} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {2 s \paren {s^2 - 3 a^2} } {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosine a t over 2
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^2 \cos a t} 2} } s = \dfrac {s^3 - 3 a^2 s} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \sin a t} } s = 2 a \paren {\dfrac {3 s^2 - a^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3} }$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 sine a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^2 \sin a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac {3 s^2 - a^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \sinh a t} } s = 2 a \paren {\dfrac {3 s^2 + a^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3} }$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^2 sinh a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^2 \sinh a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac {3 s^2 + a^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^3 \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {6 \paren {s^4 + 6 a^2 s^2 + a^4} } {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 cosh a t over 6
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^3 \cosh a t} 6} } s = \dfrac {s^4 + 6 a^2 s^2 + a^4} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 cosine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^3 \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {6 \paren {s^4 - 6 a^2 s^2 + a^4} } {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 cosine a t over 6
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^3 \cos a t} 6} } s = \dfrac {s^4 - 6 a^2 s^2 + a^4} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^3 \sin a t} } s = \dfrac {24 a s \paren {s^2 - a^2} } {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 sine a t over 24 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^3 \sin a t} {24 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^3 - a^2 s} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^3 \sinh a t} } s = \dfrac {24 a s \paren {s^2 + a^2} } {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t^3 sinh a t over 24 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t^3 \sinh a t} {24 a} } } s = \dfrac {s^3 + a^2 s} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^4}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {s^2 + a^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t cosine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {s^2 - a^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \sin a t} } s = \dfrac {2 a s} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t sine a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t \sin a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac s {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \sinh a t} } s = \dfrac {2 a s} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplace Transform of t sinh a t over 2 a
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {\dfrac {t \sinh a t} {2 a} } } s = \dfrac s {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

title: Laplacian of Function in Orthogonal Curvilinear Coordinates
snippet: Let $\map \psi {q_1, q_2, q_3}$ denote a real-valued function embedded in an orthogonal curvilinear coordinate system. Then the Laplacian of $\psi$ can be expressed as: $\nabla^2 \psi = \dfrac 1 {h_1 h_2 h_3} \paren {\map {\dfrac \partial {\partial q_1} } {\dfrac {h_2 h_3} {h_1} \dfrac {\partial \psi} {\partial q_1} } + \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial q_2} } {\dfrac {h_3 h_1} {h_2} \dfrac {\partial \psi} {\partial q_2} } + \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial q_3} } {\dfrac {h_1 h_2} {h_3} \dfrac {\partial \psi} {\partial q_3} } }$ where: ${h_i}^2 = \paren {\dfrac {\partial x} {\partial q_i} }^2 +…

title: Laplacian on Scalar Field is Divergence of Gradient
snippet: Let $\R^n$ denote the real Cartesian space of $n$ dimensions. Let $U$ be a scalar field over $\R^n$. Let $\nabla^2 U$ denote the laplacian on $U$. Then: $\nabla^2 U = \operatorname {div} \grad U$ where: $\operatorname {div}$ denotes the divergence operator $\grad$ denotes the gradient operator.

title: Larger Set has Larger Set Difference
snippet: Let $U, V$ be finite sets. Let $\card V < \card U$. Then: $\card {V \setminus U} < \card {U \setminus V}$

title: Largest 9-Digit Prime Number
snippet: The largest prime number with $9$ digits is $999 \, 999 \, 937$.

title: Largest Even Integer not expressible as Sum of 2 k Odd Composite Integers
snippet: Let $k \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. The largest even integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of $2 k$ odd positive composite integers is $18 k + 20$.

title: Largest Integer Expressible by 3 Digits
snippet: The largest integer that can be represented using no more than $3$ digits, with no additional symbols, is: $9^{9^9} = 9^{387 \, 420 \, 489}$ and (at $369 \, 693 \, 100$ digits, is too large to be calculated on a conventional calculator. Note that this does not include the notation for tetration: ${}^9 9$.

title: Largest Integer Not Expressible as Sum of Distinct 4th Powers
snippet: The largest integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct $4$th powers is $5 \, 134 \, 240$.

title: Largest Integer not Sum of Two Abundant Numbers
snippet: The largest integer which is not the sum of $2$ abundant numbers is $20 \, 161$.

title: Largest Integer whose Digits taken in Pairs all form Distinct Primes
snippet: The largest integer which has the property that every pair of its digits taken together is a distinct prime number is $619 \, 737 \, 131 \, 179$.

title: Largest Known Lead by 4n+1 in Prime Number Race
snippet: In the prime number race between prime numbers of the form $4 n - 1$ and $4 n + 1$, the highest known stretch of integers where $4 n + 1$ is not less than $4 n - 1$ is between $18 \, 465 \, 126 \, 293$ and $19 \, 033 \, 524 \, 538$.

title: Largest Mutually Coprime Subset of Initial Segment of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Consider the set $\N_n$ defined as: $\N_n = \closedint 1 n = \set {1, 2, \ldots n}$ Let $Q_n$ be the largest subset of $\N_n$ such that no element of $Q_n$ is the divisor of another element of $Q_n$. Let $\map f n$ be the cardinality of $Q_n$. Then for sufficiently large $n$: $0 \cdotp 6725 \ldots \le \dfrac {\map f n} n \le 0 \cdotp 6736 \ldots$

title: Largest Number Not Expressible as Sum of Fewer than 8 Cubes
snippet: $8042$ is (probably) the largest positive integer that cannot be expressed as the sum of fewer than $8$ cubes.

title: Largest Number not Expressible as Sum of Less than 32 Positive Fifth Powers
snippet: The largest positive integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of less than $32$ positive fifth powers is $466$: $466 = 18 \times 1^5 + 14 \times 2^5$

title: Largest Number not Expressible as Sum of Less than 37 Positive Fifth Powers
snippet: The largest positive integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of less than $37$ positive fifth powers is $223$: $223 = 31 \times 1^5 + 6 \times 2^5$

title: Largest Number not Expressible as Sum of Multiples of 23 and 28
snippet: The largest integer $n$ that cannot be expressed in the form: $n = 23 x + 28 y$ for $x, y \in \Z_{>0}$ is $593$.

title: Largest Number not Expressible as Sum of Multiples of Coprime Integers
snippet: Let $a, b$ be coprime integers, each greater than $1$. Then the largest number not expressible as a sum of multiples of $a$ and $b$ (possibly zero) is the number: $a b - a - b = \paren {a - 1} \paren {b - 1} - 1$

title: Largest Number not Sum of Squares of Distinct Primes
snippet: The largest positive integer which cannot be expressed as the sum of the squares of distinct prime numbers is $17 \, 163$.

title: Largest Pandigital Square
snippet: The largest pandigital square (in the sense where pandigital includes the zero) is $9 \, 814 \, 072 \, 356$: $9 \, 814 \, 072 \, 356 = 99 \, 066^2$

title: Largest Parallelogram Contained in Triangle
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle. Let $P$ be a parallelogram contained within $T$. Let $P$ have the largest area possible for the conditions given. Then: $(1): \quad$ One side of $P$ is coincident with part of one side of $T$, and hence two vertices lie on that side of $T$ $(2): \quad$ The other two vertices of $P$ bisect the other two sides of $T$ $(3): \quad$ The area of $P$ is equal to half the area of $T$.

title: Largest Penholodigital Square
snippet: The largest penholodigital square is $923 \, 187 \, 456$: $923 \, 187 \, 456 = 30 \, 384^2$

title: Largest Positive Integer not Sum of Distinct Cubes
snippet: $12 \, 758$ is the largest positive integer that cannot be expressed as the sum of distinct cubes.

title: Largest Prime Factor of Euler Phi Function
snippet: Let $\phi: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the Euler $\phi$ function. Then the largest prime factor of $\map\phi n$ is less than the largest prime factor of $n$,

title: Largest Prime Factor of n squared plus 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be greater than $239$. Then the largest prime factor of $n^2 + 1$ is at least $17$.

title: Largest Product of Pandigital Factors
snippet: The largest integer that can be obtained by multiplying $2$ integers which between them use all the digits from $1$ to $9$ is: $843 \, 973 \, 902 = 9642 \times 87531$

title: Largest Rectangle Contained in Triangle
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle. Let $R$ be a rectangle contained within $T$. Let $R$ have the largest area possible for the conditions given. Then: $(1): \quad$ One side of $R$ is coincident with part of one side of $T$, and hence two vertices lie on that side of $T$ $(2): \quad$ The other two vertices of $R$ bisect the other two sides of $T$ $(3): \quad$ The area of $R$ is equal to half the area of $T$.

title: Largest Rectangle with Given Perimeter is Square
snippet: Let $\SS$ be the set of all rectangles with a given perimeter $L$. The element of $\SS$ with the largest area is the square with length of side $\dfrac L 4$.

title: Largest Right-Truncatable Primes allowing 1
snippet: Let $1$ be temporarily considered to be a prime number. Under that consideration, the largest right-truncatable prime numbers are: $1 \, 979 \, 339 \, 333$ $1 \, 979 \, 339 \, 339$

title: Largest n such that 1 to n can be Partitioned for no Element to be Sum of 2 Elements in Same Set
snippet: $44$ is the largest integer $n$ such that the set of integers from $1$ to $n$ can be partitioned into $4$ subsets such that no integer in any of these subsets is the sum of $2$ other integers in the same subset: $\set {1, 3, 5, 15, 17, 19, 26, 28, 40, 42, 44}$ $\set {2, 7, 8, 18, 21, 24, 27, 33, 37, 38, 43}$ $\set {4, 6, 13, 20, 22, 23, 25, 30, 32, 39, 41}$ $\set {9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 29, 31, 34, 35, 36}$

title: Last Digit of Perfect Numbers Alternates between 6 and 8
snippet: == Conjecture == The last digit of the sequence of perfect numbers alternates between $6$ and $8$: $6$ $28$ $496$ $8128$

title: Last Element of Geometric Sequence with Coprime Extremes has no Integer Proportional as First to Second
snippet: Let $G_n = \sequence {a_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ be a geometric sequence of integers such that $a_0 \ne 1$. Let $a_0 \perp a_n$, where $\perp$ denotes coprimality. Then there does not exist an integer $b$ such that: $\dfrac {a_0} {a_1} = \dfrac {a_n} b$

title: Lateral Face of Prismatoid is Triangle, Trapezium or Parallelogram
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a prismatoid. Let $\FF$ be a lateral face of $\PP$. Then $\FF$ is one of the following: a triangle a trapezium a parallelogram.

title: Lateral Surface Area of Circular Cylinder
Lateral Surface Area of Frustum of Right Circular Cone
snippet: Let $F$ be a frustum of a right circular cone. The area $\AA$ of the lateral surface of $F$ is given as: {{eqn | l = \AA | r = \pi \paren {r_1 + r_2} \sqrt {h^2 + \paren {r_2 - r_1}^2} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \pi \paren {r_1 + r_2} s | c = }} where: $r_1$ and $r_2$ are the radii of the bases of $F$ $h$ is the altitude of $F$. $s$ is the slant height of $F$. 300px

title: Lateral Surface Area of Right Circular Cone
snippet: Let $K$ be a right circular cone. Let $r$ be the radius of the base of $K$. Let $s$ be the slant height of $K$. Then the area $\AA$ of the lateral surface of $K$ is given by: $\AA = \pi r s$

title: Lateral Surface Area of Right Circular Cylinder
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a right circular cylinder: whose bases are circles of radius $r$ and whose height is $h$. The area $\AA$ of the lateral surface of $\CC$ is given by the formula: $\AA = 2 \pi r h$

title: Latin Square/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Latin Squares ==

title: Latin Square is not necessarily Cayley Table of Group
snippet: While it is true that the Cayley table of a (finite) group is in the form of a Latin square it is not necessarily the case that a Latin square is the Cayley table of a group.

title: Latitudes on Mercator's Projection get Further Apart
snippet: Let $\MM$ be a Mercator's projection of Earth's surface such that the cylinder circumscribing Earth intersects it along the equator. Then equally spaced lines of latitude on Earth map to parallel lines on $\MM$, but the further from the equator they are, the further apart they get..

title: Lattice (Ordered Set)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Lattices in context of Ordered Sets ==

title: Lattice Homomorphism is Both Meet and Join Semilattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ be lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a lattice homomorphsm between $L_1$ and $L_2$. Then: $\phi: \struct{S_1, \vee_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct{S_2, \vee_2, \preceq_2}$ $\phi: \struct{S_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct{S_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ are semilattice homomorphisms

title: Lattice Homomorphism is Order-Preserving
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \vee_1, \wedge_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \vee_2, \wedge_2, \preceq_2}$ be lattices. Let $\phi: L_1 \to L_2$ be a lattice homomorphsm between $L_1$ and $L_2$. Then: $\phi: \struct{S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ is order-preserving

title: Lattice Isomorphism is Isomorphism in Category Lat
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Lat}$ denote the category of lattices. Let $f : L_1 \to L_2$ be a morphism of $\mathbf{Lat}$. Then: $f$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbf{Lat}$ $f$ is a lattice isomorphsm

title: Lattice Ordering/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Lattice Orderings ==

title: Lattice and Ring of Real-Valued Functions forms Ordered Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\R^S, +, \times}$ be the ring of real-valued functions from $S$ to $\R$. Let $\struct {\R^S, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of real-valued functions from $S$ to $\R$. Then: $\struct {\R^S, +, \times, \le}$ is an ordered ring

title: Lattice is Complete iff it Admits All Suprema
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice $\forall X \subseteq S: X$ admits a supremum.

title: Lattice of Bounded Continuous Functions is Sublattice of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau }$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ is a sublattice of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$

title: Lattice of Continuous Functions is Sublattice of All Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau }$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\R^S, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, R}, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ is a sublattice of $\struct {\R^S, \vee, \wedge, \le}$

title: Lattice of Power Set is Algebraic
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \preceq}$ be the lattice of power set of $X$ where $\mathord \preceq = \mathord \subseteq \cap \paren {\powerset X \times \powerset X}$ Then $L$ is algebraic.

title: Lattice of Power Set is Arithmetic
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $P = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \subseteq}$ be a lattice of power set. Then $P$ is an arithmetic ordered set.

title: Lattice of Real-Valued Functions forms Distributive Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\R^S, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ be the lattice of real-valued functions from $S$ where: $\forall f, g \in \R^S : f \vee g : S \to \R$ is defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f \vee g}} s = \max \set{\map f s, \map g s}$ $\forall f, g \in \R^S : f \wedge g : S \to \R$ is defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f \wedge g}} s = \min \set{\map f s, \map g s}$ $\forall f, g \in \R^S : f \le g$ : $\forall x \in S : \map f x \le \map g x$ Then: $\struct {\R^S, \vee, \wedge, \le}$ is a…

title: Lattice of Subgroups forming Totally Ordered Set is Indecomposable
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a Group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by the subset ordering on $\mathbb G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be totally ordered. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is an indecomposable group.

title: Laurent Expansion of Function about Pole
snippet: Let $f$ be a complex function with a pole at $z_0 \in \C$ of order $k$. The Laurent expansion of $f$ about $z_0$ can be expressed as: $\map f z = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = -k}^\infty a_n \paren {z - z_0}^n$

title: Laurent Expansion of Isolated Essential Singularity
snippet: Let $f$ be a complex function with an essential singularity at $z_0 \in \C$. Let $z_0$ also be an isolated singularity. Then there exists a Laurent expansion for $f$ at $z_0$ with a principal part with infinitely many terms.

title: Laurent Series Expansion for Cotangent Function
snippet: {{eqn | l = \pi \cot \pi z | r = \frac 1 z - 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map \zeta {2 n} z^{2 n - 1} }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 z - 2 \paren {\dfrac {\pi^2 } 6 z + \dfrac {\pi^4 } {90 } z^3 + \dfrac {\pi^6 } {945 } z^5 + \cdots} }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 z - \dfrac {\pi^2 } 3 z - \dfrac {\pi^4 } {45 } z^3 - \dfrac {2 \pi^6 } {945 } z^5 - \cdots }} where: $z \in \C$ such that $\cmod z < 1$ $\zeta$ is the Riemann Zeta function.

title: Law of Cosines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 a b \cos C$

title: Law of Division
snippet: Let $\mathbb F$ denote one of the following number systems: rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ Let $a, b \in \mathbb F$ such that $a \ne 0$. Then there exists a unique $x$ such that: $a x = b$ $x$ is then defined and denoted: $x := b / a$

title: Law of Excluded Middle
snippet: == Proof Rule == The law of (the) excluded middle is a valid argument in certain types of logic dealing with disjunction $\lor$ and negation $\neg$. This includes classical propositional logic and predicate logic, and in particular natural deduction, but for example not intuitionistic propositional logic.

title: Law of Excluded Middle for Two Variables
snippet: $\vdash (p \land q) \lor (\lnot p \land q) \lor (p \land \lnot q) \lor (\lnot p \land \lnot q)$

title: Law of Excluded Middle implies Peirce's Law
snippet: From the Law of Excluded Middle follows Peirce's Law: $\paren {p \lor \neg p} \vdash \paren {\paren {p \implies q} \implies p} \implies p$

title: Law of Identity
snippet: Every proposition entails itself:

title: Law of Inverses (Modulo Arithmetic)
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$. Then: $\exists n' \in \Z: n n' \equiv d \pmod m$ where $d = \gcd \set {m, n}$.

title: Law of Mass Action
snippet: Let $\AA$ and $\BB$ be two chemical substances in a solution $C$ which are involved in a second-order reaction. Let $x$ grams of $\CC$ contain $a x$ grams of $\AA$ and $b x$ grams of $\BB$, where $a + b = 1$. Let there be $a A$ grams of $\AA$ and $b B$ grams of $\BB$ at time $t = t_0$, at which time $x = 0$. Then: $x = \begin{cases} \dfrac {k A^2 a b t} {k A a b t + 1} & : A = B \\ & \\ \dfrac {A B e^{-k \paren {A - B} a b t}} {A - B e^{-k \paren {A - B} a b t}} & : A \ne B \end{cases}$ for some positive real constant $k$. This is known as the law of mass action.

title: Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes. Then: $\paren {\dfrac p q} \paren {\dfrac q p} = \paren {-1}^{\dfrac {\paren {p - 1} \paren {q - 1} } 4}$ where $\paren {\dfrac p q}$ and $\paren {\dfrac q p}$ are defined as the Legendre symbol. An alternative formulation is: $\paren {\dfrac p q} = \begin{cases} \quad \paren {\dfrac q p} & : p \equiv 1 \lor q \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \\ -\paren {\dfrac q p} & : p \equiv q \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \end{cases}$ The fact that these formulations are equivalent is immediate. This fact is known as the Law of Quadratic Reciprocity, or LQR for short.

title: Law of Simple Conversion of E
snippet: Consider the universal negative categorical statement No $S$ is $P$: $\map {\mathbf E} {S, P}: \forall x: \map S x \implies \neg \map P x$ Then No $P$ is $S$: $\map {\mathbf E} {P, S}$

title: Law of Simple Conversion of I
snippet: Consider the particular affirmative categorical statement Some $S$ is $P$: $\map {\mathbf I} {S, P}: \exists x: \map S x \land \map P x$ Then Some $P$ is $S$: $\map {\mathbf I} {P, S}$

title: Law of Sines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $\dfrac a {\sin A} = \dfrac b {\sin B} = \dfrac c {\sin C} = 2 R$ where $R$ is the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$.

title: Law of Species
snippet: Let $T$ be a right spherical triangle whose angles are $A$, $B$ and $C$ and whose respective sides opposite those angles are $a$, $b$ and $c$. Let $C$ be the right angle of $T$. Then: $(1): \quad$ $A$ and $a$ are of the same species, and $B$ and $b$ are of the same species $(2): \quad$ if $c 90 \degrees$, then $a$ and $b$ are of the opposite species, as are $A$ and $B$.

title: Law of Subtraction
snippet: On the following number systems: integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ there exists a unique $x$ such that: $a + x = b$ for every given $a$ and $b$. $x$ is then defined and denoted: $x := b - a$

title: Law of Tangents
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $\dfrac {a + b} {a - b} = \dfrac {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A + B} } {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A - B} }$

title: Laws of Logarithms
snippet: Let $x, y, b \in \R_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive real numbers. Let $a \in \R$ be any real number such that $a > 0$ and $a \ne 1$. Let $\log_a$ denote the logarithm to base $a$. Then:

title: Leading Coefficient of Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Leading Coefficient of Matrix == Consider: $\mathbf A = \begin {bmatrix} 1 & 5 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & 6 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end {bmatrix}$ The leading coefficient of row $1$ is $1$. The leading coefficient of row $2$ is $5$. The leading coefficient of row $3$ is $6$. Row $4$ has no leading coefficient. Category:Leading Coefficients of Matrices

title: Leading Coefficient of Product of Polynomials over Integral Domain
snippet: Let $R$ be an integral domain. Let $f, g \in R \sqbrk x$ be polynomials. Let $c$ and $d$ be their leading coefficients. Then $f g$ has leading coefficient $c d$.

title: Leaf Node/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Leaf Nodes ==

title: Leaf of Rooted Tree is on One Branch
snippet: Let $T$ be a rooted tree with root node $r_T$. Let $t$ be a leaf node of $T$. Then there exists a unique branch $\Gamma$ of $T$ such that $t \in \Gamma$.

title: Least Fixed Point of Enumeration Operator
snippet: Let $\psi : \powerset \N \to \powerset \N$ be an enumeration operator. Let $A_i$ be defined recursively as: {{eqn | l = A_{n + 1} | r = \map \psi {A_n} }} Let $A = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in \N} A_i$. Then: $A$ is a fixed point of $\psi$ Every fixed point of $\psi$ is a superset of $A$

title: Least Fixed Point of Enumeration Operator is Recursively Enumerable
snippet: Let $\psi : \powerset \N \to \powerset \N$ be an enumeration operator. Then there exists a recursively enumerable set $A$ such that: $A$ is a fixed point of $\psi$ Every fixed point of $\psi$ is a superset of $A$

title: Least Number with Three Given Fractions
Least Time at which Discrete-Time Adapted Stochastic Process equals or exceeds Real Number is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be a discrete-time $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-adapted stochastic process. Let $\lambda \in \R$. Let: $T = \inf \set {n \in \Z_{\ge 0} : X_n \ge \lambda}$ Then $T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Least Upper Bound Property
snippet: Let $S \subset \R$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers such that $S$ is bounded above. Then $S$ admits a supremum in $\R$. This is known as the least upper bound property of the real numbers.

title: Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $g : X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions $f_n : X \to \overline \R$ such that: $\ds \map f x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} x$ and: $\size {\map {f_n} x} \le \map g x$ hold for $\mu$-almost all $x \in X$. Then: $f$ is $\mu$-integrable and $f_n$ is $\mu$-integrable for each $n \in \N$ and: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$

title: Lebesgue 1-Space is Subset of Tempered Distribution Space
snippet: Let $\map {L^1} \R$ be the Lebesgue $1$-space. Let $\map {\SS'} \R$ be the tempered distribution space. Then in the distributional sense: $\map {L^1} \R \subseteq \map {\SS'} \R$ That is: $T_f \subseteq \map {\SS'} \R$ where $f \in \map {L^1} \R$.

title: Lebesgue Decomposition Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

title: Lebesgue Decomposition of Finite Borel Measure
snippet: Let $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of the real number line $\R$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Let $\mu$ be a finite Borel measure on $\struct {\R, \map \BB \R}$. Then there exists: a discrete measure $\mu_{pp}$ a measure $\mu_{sc}$ that is continuous and mutually singular with respect to $\lambda$ a measure $\mu_{ac}$ that is absolutely continuous with respect to $\lambda$ such that $\mu = \mu_{pp} + \mu_{sc} + \mu_{ac}$.

title: Lebesgue Infinity-Space is Subset of Tempered Distribution Space
snippet: Let $\map {L^\infty} \R$ be the Lebesgue infinity-space. Let $\map {\SS'} \R$ be the tempered distribution space. Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\map {L^\infty} \R \subseteq \map {\SS'} \R$ That is, every Schwartz distribution defined by an element of $\map {L^\infty} \R$ is a tempered distribution.

title: Lebesgue Integrable Function is not necessarily Riemann Integrable
snippet: Let $f$ be a Lebesgue integrable function. Then $f$ is not necessarily therefore a Riemann integrable function.

title: Lebesgue Integrable Functions which Agree Almost Everywhere have Equal Integrals
snippet: Let $\lambda^n$ be a Lebesgue measure on $\R^n$ for some $n > 0$. Let $f, g: \R^n \to \overline \R$ be Lebesgue integrable functions. Let $f$ and $g$ be such that $f = g$ $\lambda^n$-almost everywhere. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \lambda^n = \ds \int g \rd \lambda^n$ That is, their Lebesgue integrals are equal.

title: Lebesgue Integral is Extension of Darboux Integral
snippet: Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a Darboux integrable function. Then it is also Lebesgue integrable, and furthermore: $\ds R \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = \int_{\closedint a b} f \rd \lambda$ where $\ds R \int_a^b$ is the Darboux integral and $\ds \int_{\closedint a b}$ is the Lebesgue integral.

title: Lebesgue Integral of Dirichlet Function
snippet: The Lebesgue integral of a Dirichlet function is zero.

title: Lebesgue Measure Invariant under Orthogonal Group
snippet: Let $M \in \map {\mathrm O} {n, \R}$ be an orthogonal matrix. Let $\lambda^n$ be $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then the pushforward measure $M_* \lambda^n$ equals $\lambda^n$.

title: Lebesgue Measure Space is Complete
snippet: Let $\map {\operatorname {Leb} } {\R^n}$ be the Lebesgue $\sigma$-algebra on $\R^n$. Let $\lambda$ be the Lebesgue measure on $\R^n$. Then $\struct {\R^n, \map {\operatorname {Leb} } {\R^n}, \lambda}$ is a complete measure space.

title: Lebesgue Measure is Diffuse
snippet: Let $\lambda^n$ be Lebesgue measure on $\R^n$. Then $\lambda^n$ is a diffuse measure.

title: Lebesgue Measure is Invariant under Translations
snippet: Let $\lambda^n$ be the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on $\R^n$ equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\map \BB {\R^n}$. Let $\mathbf x \in \R^n$. Then $\lambda^n$ is translation invariant; that is, for all $B \in \map \BB {\R^n}$, have: $\map {\lambda^n} {\mathbf x + B} = \map {\lambda^n} B$ where $\mathbf x + B$ is the set $\set {\mathbf x + \mathbf b: \mathbf b \in B}$.

title: Lebesgue Measure of Scalar Multiple
snippet: Let $\lambda^n$ be the $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure on $\R^n$ equipped with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\map \BB {\R^n}$. Let $B \in \BB$. Let $t \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\map {\lambda^n} {t B} = t^n \map {\lambda^n} B$ where $t B = \set {t \mathbf b: \mathbf b \in B}$ is the dilation of $B$ by $t$.

title: Lebesgue Pre-Measure is Pre-Measure
snippet: The Lebesgue pre-measure $\lambda^n$ on the half-open $n$-rectangles $\JJ_{ho}^n$ is a pre-measure.

title: Lebesgue Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space and let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be Lebesgue $p$-space on $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Then $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ is a vector subspace of $\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R}$, the space of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions on $X$. In particular, it is a vector space over $\R$.

title: Lefschetz Principle (First-Order)
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a sentence in the language $\LL_r = \set {0, 1, +, -, \cdot}$ for rings, where $0, 1$ are constants and $+, -, \cdot$ are binary functions. $(1): \quad \phi$ is true in every algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. $(2): \quad \phi$ is true in some algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. $(3): \quad \phi$ is true in algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$ for arbitrarily large primes $p$. $(4): \quad \phi$ is true in algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$ for sufficiently large primes $p$.

title: Left-Hand Differentiable Function is Left-Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $I$. Let $a$ be a point in $I$ where $f$ is left-hand differentiable. Then $f$ is left-continuous at $a$.

title: Left-Hand and Right-Hand Differentiable Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $I$. Let $a$ be a point in $I$ where $f$ is left- and right-hand differentiable. Then $f$ is continuous at $a$.

title: Left-Truncatable Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Left-Truncatable Primes ==

title: Left-Truncatable Prime/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of left-truncatable primes begins: $2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 23, 37, 43, 47, 53, 67, 73, 83, 97, 113, 137, 167, 173, 197, \ldots$ Category:Left-Truncatable Primes

title: Left-Truncated Automorphic Number is Automorphic
snippet: Let $n$ be an automorphic number, expressed in some conventional number base. Let any number of digits be removed from the left-hand end of $n$. Then what remains is also an automorphic number.

title: Left Adjoint Functor is Unique up to Natural Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Then: the left adjoint functor $F$ of $G$ is unique up to isomorphism in the functor category $\operatorname{Funct} \tuple{C, D}$. That is: left adjoint functor $F$ is unique up to natural isomorphism.

title: Left Cancellable Commutative Operation is Right Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be left cancellable and also commutative. Then $\circ$ is also right cancellable.

title: Left Cancellable Element is Left Cancellable in Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$. Let $x \in T$ be left cancellable in $S$. Then $x$ is also left cancellable in $T$.

title: Left Cancellable Elements of Semigroup form Subsemigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $C_\lambda$ be the set of left cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\struct {C_\lambda, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Left Cancellable iff Left Regular Representation Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then $a \in S$ is left cancellable the left regular representation $\map {\lambda_a} x$ is injective.

title: Left Composition of Banach Space-Valued Simple Function with Function Fixing Origin is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$. Let $f : I \to X$ be a simple function. Let $g : X \to Y$ be a function such that $\map g { {\mathbf 0}_X} = {\mathbf 0}_Y$. Then $g \circ f$ is a simple function.

title: Left Congruence Class Modulo Subgroup is Left Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $\RR^l_H$ be the equivalence defined as left congruence modulo $H$. The equivalence class $\eqclass g {\RR^l_H}$ of an element $g \in G$ is the left coset $g H$. This is known as the left congruence class of $g \bmod H$.

title: Left Congruence Modulo Subgroup is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x \equiv^l y \pmod H$ denote the relation that $x$ is left congruent modulo $H$ to $y$. Then the relation $\equiv^l$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Left Coset Equals Subgroup iff Element in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x \in G$. Let $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $x H = H \iff x \in H$

title: Left Coset Space forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. The left coset space of $H$ forms a partition of its group $G$, and hence: {{eqn | l = \neg \paren {x \equiv^l y} \pmod H | o = \iff | r = x H \cap y H = \O }}

title: Left Coset by Identity
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $e H = H$ where $e H$ is the left coset of $H$ by $e$.

title: Left Coset of Stabilizer in Group of Transformations
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $G$ be a group of permutations of $S$. Let $t \in G$. Let $G_t$ be the set defined as: $G_t = \set {g \in G: \map g t = t}$ Then each left coset of $G_t$ in $G$ consists of the elements of $G$ that map $t$ to some element of $S$.

title: Left Cosets are Equal iff Element in Other Left Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $x H = y H \iff x \in y H$

title: Left Cosets are Equal iff Product with Inverse in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $x H = y H \iff x^{-1} y \in H$

title: Left Distributive Law for Natural Numbers
snippet: The operation of multiplication is left distributive over addition on the set of natural numbers $\N$: $\forall x, y, n \in \N_{> 0}: n \times \paren {x + y} = \paren {n \times x} + \paren {n \times y}$

title: Left Distributive and Commutative implies Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, *}$ be an algebraic structure. Let the operation $\circ$ be left distributive over the operation $*$. Let $\circ$ be commutative. Then $\circ$ is distributive over $*$.

title: Left Ideal is Left Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $J \subseteq R$ be a left ideal of $R$. Let $\circ : R \times J \to J$ be the restriction of $\times$ to $R \times J$. Then $\struct {J, +, \circ}$ is a left module over $\struct {R, +, \times}$.

title: Left Identity Element is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $e_L \in S$ be a left identity with respect to $\circ$. Then $e_L$ is idempotent under $\circ$.

title: Left Identity in Semigroup may not be Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $e_L$ be a left identity of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $e_L$ is unique.

title: Left Identity while exists Left Inverse for All is Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup with a left identity $e_L$ such that: $\forall x \in S: \exists x_L: x_L \circ x = e_L$ That is, every element of $S$ has a left inverse with respect to the left identity. Then $e_L$ is also a right identity, that is, is an identity.

title: Left Inverse Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Left Inverse Mappings ==

title: Left Inverse Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $g: T \to S$ be a left inverse of $f$. Then $g$ is a surjection.

title: Left Inverse and Right Inverse is Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid with identity element $e_S$. Let $x \in S$ such that $x$ has both a left inverse and a right inverse. That is: $\exists x_L \in S: x_L \circ x = e_S$ $\exists x_R \in S: x \circ x_R = e_S$ Then $x_L = x_R$, that is, $x$ has an inverse. Furthermore, that element is the only inverse (both right and left) for $x$

title: Left Inverse for All is Right Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup with a left identity $e_L$ such that: $\forall x \in S: \exists x_L: x_L \circ x = e_L$ That is, every element of $S$ has a left inverse with respect to the left identity. Then $x \circ x_L = e_L$, that is, $x_L$ is also a right inverse with respect to the left identity.

title: Left Limit of Distribution Function of Finite Borel Measure
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a finite Borel measure. Let $F_\mu$ be the distribution function of $\mu$. Then we have: $\ds \lim_{y \mathop \to x^-} \map {F_\mu} y = \map \mu {\openint {-\infty} x}$

title: Left Module Does Not Necessarily Induce Right Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : G \times R \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ' \lambda = \lambda \circ x$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ'}$ is not necessarily a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$

title: Left Module induces Right Module over same Ring iff Actions are Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}$ be a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ': G \times R \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ' \lambda = \lambda \circ x$ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ : $\forall \lambda, \mu \in R: \forall x \in G: \paren {\lambda \times_R \mu} \circ x = \paren {\mu \times_R \lambda} \circ x$

title: Left Module over Commutative Ring induces Bimodule
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : G \times R \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ' \lambda = \lambda \circ x$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ, \circ'}$ is a bimodule over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$.

title: Left Module over Commutative Ring induces Right Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}$ be a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : G \times R \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ' \lambda = \lambda \circ x$ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$.

title: Left Module over Ring Induces Right Module over Opposite Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R, +_R, *_R}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : G \times R \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ’ \lambda = \lambda \circ x$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, *_R}$.

title: Left Operation has no Left Identities
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with more than $1$ element. Let $\struct {S, \gets}$ be an algebraic structure in which the operation $\gets$ is the left operation. Then $\struct {S, \gets}$ has no left identities.

title: Left Operation is Anticommutative
snippet: The left operation is anticommutative: $\forall x, y: x \leftarrow y = y \leftarrow x \iff x = y$

title: Left Operation is Associative
snippet: The left operation is associative: $\forall x, y, z: \paren {x \gets y} \gets z = x \gets \paren {y \gets z}$

title: Left Operation is Closed for All Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\leftarrow$ be the left operation on $S$. That is: $\forall x, y \in S: x \leftarrow y = x$ Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Then for all $T \in \powerset S$, $\leftarrow$ is closed on $T$. That is, for all $T \in \powerset S$: $\struct {T, \leftarrow}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \leftarrow}$.

title: Left Operation is Distributive over Idempotent Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \leftarrow}$ be an algebraic structure where: $\leftarrow$ is the left operation $\circ$ is any arbitrary binary operation. Then: $\leftarrow$ is distributive over $\circ$ $\circ$ is idempotent.

title: Left Operation is Entropic
snippet: The left operation is entropic: $\forall a, b, c, d: \paren {a \gets b} \gets \paren {c \gets d} = \paren {a \gets c} \gets \paren {b \gets d}$

title: Left Operation is Idempotent
snippet: The left operation is idempotent: $\forall x: x \leftarrow x = x$

title: Left Operation is Right Distributive over All Operations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \leftarrow}$ be an algebraic structure where: $\leftarrow$ is the left operation $\circ$ is any arbitrary binary operation. Then $\leftarrow$ is right distributive over $\circ$.

title: Left Operation is not Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\leftarrow$ denote the left operation on $S$. Then $\leftarrow$ is not commutative on $S$ unless $S$ is a singleton.

title: Left Quasigroup if (2-3) Parastrophe of Magma is Magma
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma, where $S$ is a set $\circ : S \times S \to S$ is a binary operation on $S$ Let the $\paren {2 - 3}$ parastrophe of $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a left quasigroup.

title: Left Regular Representation is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the operation: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\lambda_g} h$ where $\lambda_g$ is the left regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a group action.

title: Left Regular Representation is Transitive Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the group action: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\lambda_g} h$ where $\lambda_g$ is the left regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a transitive group action.

title: Left Regular Representation of Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\lambda_a: S \to S$ be the left regular representation of $S$ with respect to $a$. Then: $\lambda_a \sqbrk T = \set a \circ T = a \circ T$ where $a \circ T$ denotes subset product with a singleton.

title: Left Regular Representation wrt Left Cancellable Element on Finite Semigroup is Bijection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a finite semigroup. Let $a \in S$ be left cancellable. Then the left regular representation $\lambda_a$ of $\struct {S, \circ}$ with respect to $a$ is a bijection.

title: Left Self-Distributive Operation with Right Identity is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be left self-distributive. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have a right identity. Then $\circ$ is an idempotent operation.

title: Left Shift Operator is Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $X = Y = \ell^2$ be 2-sequence spaces over real numbers. Let $L : X \to Y$ be the left shift operator. Then $L$ is a linear mapping.

title: Left Shift Operator on 2-Sequence Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the $2$-sequence space with $2$-norm. Let $L : \ell^2 \to \ell^2$ be the left shift operator. Then $L$ is continuous on $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$.

title: Left Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Double-sided Whiskered Composite
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf B$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $H : \mathbf B \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\eta H: F \circ H \to G \circ H$ denote the left whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $H$.

title: Left Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf B$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $H : \mathbf B \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\eta H: F \circ H \to G \circ H$ denote the left whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $H$. Then: $\eta H$ is a natural transformation.

title: Left Zero Divisor of Commutative Ring is Right Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $x \in R$ be a left zero divisor of $R$. Then $x$ is also a right zero divisor of $R$.

title: Left and Right Coset Spaces are Equivalent
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let: $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$ $H y$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $y$. Then: $\order {\set {x H: x \in G} } = \order {\set {H y: y \in G} }$ That is: The number of right cosets is the same as the number of left cosets of $G$ with respect to $H$. The left and right coset spaces are equivalent.

title: Left and Right Identity are the Same
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $e_L \in S$ be a left identity, and $e_R \in S$ be a right identity. Then: $e_L = e_R$ that is, both the left identity and right identity are the same, and are therefore an identity $e$. Furthermore, $e$ is the only left identity and right identity for $\circ$.

title: Left and Right Inverse Mappings Implies Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f$ be such that: $\exists g_1: T \to S: g_1 \circ f = I_S$ $\exists g_2: T \to S: f \circ g_2 = I_T$ where both $g_1$ and $g_2$ are mappings. Then $f$ is a bijection.

title: Left and Right Inverse Relations Implies Bijection
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on a cartesian product $S \times T$. Let: $I_S$ be the identity mapping on $S$ $I_T$ be the identity mapping on $T$. Let $\RR^{-1}$ be the inverse relation of $\RR$. Let $\RR$ be such that: $\RR^{-1} \circ \RR = I_S$ and $\RR \circ \RR^{-1} = I_T$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of relations. Then $\RR$ is a bijection.

title: Left and Right Inverses of Mapping are Inverse Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping such that: $(1): \quad \exists g_1: T \to S: g_1 \circ f = I_S$ $(2): \quad \exists g_2: T \to S: f \circ g_2 = I_T$ Then: $g_1 = g_2 = f^{-1}$ where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse of $f$.

title: Left and Right Inverses of Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $x, y \in S$. Let: $(1): \quad x \circ y$ have a left inverse for $\circ$ $(2): \quad y \circ x$ have a right inverse for $\circ$. Then both $x$ and $y$ are invertible for $\circ$.

title: Left and Right Inverses of Square Matrix over Field are Equal
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a field, usually one of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$ or $\C$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map \MM n$ denote the matrix space of order $n$ square matrices over $\Bbb F$. Let $\mathbf B$ be a left inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf B$ is also a right inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$. Similarly, let $\mathbf B$ be a right inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf B$ is also a right inverse matrix of $\mathbf A$.

title: Left and Right Operation are Closed for All Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let: $\leftarrow$ be the left operation on $S$ $\rightarrow$ be the right operation on $S$. That is: $\forall x, y \in S: x \leftarrow y = x$ $\forall x, y \in S: x \rightarrow y = y$ Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Then for all $T \in \powerset S$, both $\leftarrow$ and $\rightarrow$ are closed on $T$. That is, for all $T \in \powerset S$:

title: Left and Right Zero are the Same
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $z_L \in S$ be a left zero, and $z_R \in S$ be a right zero. Then $z_L = z_R$, that is, both the left and right zero are the same, and are therefore a zero $z$. Furthermore, $z$ is the only left and right zero for $\circ$.

title: Left or Right Inverse of Matrix is Inverse
snippet: Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf B$ be square matrices of order $n$ over a commutative ring with unity $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Suppose that: $\mathbf A \mathbf B = \mathbf I_n$ where $\mathbf I_n$ is the unit matrix of order $n$. Then $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ are nonsingular matrices, and furthermore: $\mathbf B = \mathbf A^{-1}$ where $\mathbf A^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\mathbf A$.

title: Legendre's Condition
snippet: Let $y =\map y x$ be a real function, such that: $\map y a = A,\quad \map y b = B$ Let $J \sqbrk y$ be a functional, such that: $\ds J \sqbrk y = \int_a^b \map F {x, y, y'} \rd x$ where $F \in C^2 \closedint a b$ all its variables, and $C$ stands for differentiability class. Then a necessary condition for $J \sqbrk y$ to have a minimum at $y = \hat y$ is: $\bigintlimits {F_{y'y'} } {y \mathop = \hat y} {} \ge 0 \quad \forall x \in \closedint a b$

title: Legendre's Conjecture
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether: $\exists n \in \N_{>1}: \map \pi {n^2 + 2 n + 1} = \map \pi {n^2}$ where $\pi$ denotes the prime-counting function. That is: Is there always a prime number between consecutive squares?

title: Legendre's Differential Equation/(1 - x^2) y'' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0
snippet: The special case of Legendre's differential equation: $(1): \quad \paren {1 - x^2} y' ' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + C_2 \paren {\dfrac x 2 \, \map \ln {\dfrac {1 + x} {1 - x} } - 1}$

title: Legendre's Duplication Formula
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote the gamma function. Then: $\forall z \notin \set {-\dfrac n 2: n \in \N}: \map \Gamma z \map \Gamma {z + \dfrac 1 2} = 2^{1 - 2 z} \sqrt \pi \, \map \Gamma {2 z}$ where $\N$ denotes the natural numbers.

title: Legendre's Theorem
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n$ be expressed in base $p$ representation. Let $r$ be the digit sum of the representation of $n$ in base $p$. Then $n!$ is divisible by $p^\mu$ but not by $p^{\mu + 1}$, where: $\mu = \dfrac {n - r} {p - 1}$
