title: Linear Eccentricity of Ellipse from Major and Minor Axis
snippet: Let $K$ be an ellipse whose major axis is $2 a$ and whose minor axis is $2 b$. Let $c$ be the linear eccentricity of $K$. Then: $a^2 = b^2 + c^2$

title: Linear Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Linear Equations ==

title: Linear First Order ODE/(1 + x^2) dy + 2 x y dx = cotangent x dx
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {1 + x^2} \rd y + 2 x y \rd x = \cot x \rd x$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {\map \ln {\sin x} } {1 + x^2} + \dfrac C {1 + x^2}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/(1 + x^2) y' + 2 x y = 4 x^3
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $\paren {1 + x^2} \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + 2 x y = 4 x^3$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {x^4} {1 + x^2} + \dfrac C {1 + x^2}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/(2 y - x^3) dx = x dy
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {2 y - x^3} \rd x = x \rd y$ has the general solution: $y = -x^3 + C x^2$

title: Linear First Order ODE/(x^2 + y) dx = x dy
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 + y} \rd x = x \rd y$ has the general solution: $y = x^2 + C x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/dy = f(x) dx
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an integrable real function. The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = \map f x$ has the general solution: $y = \ds \int \map f x \rd x + C$ where $\ds \int \map f x \rd x$ denotes the primitive of $f$.

title: Linear First Order ODE/x dy + y dx = x cosine x dx
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $x \rd y + y \rd x = x \cos x \rd x$ has the general solution: $x y = x \sin x + \cos x + C$

title: Linear First Order ODE/x y' + y = f (x)
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad x \, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + y = \map f x$ has the general solution: $\ds x y = \int \map f x \rd x + C$

title: Linear First Order ODE/x y' + y = x^2 cosine x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $x \, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + y = x^2 \cos x$ has the general solution: $y = 2 \cos x + x \sin x - \dfrac 2 x \sin x + \dfrac C x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/x y' - 3 y = x^4
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - 3y = x^4$ has the general solution: $y = x^4 + \dfrac C {x^3}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + (y over x) = 3 x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \dfrac y x = 3 x$ has the general solution: $x y = x^3 + C$ or: $y = x^2 + \dfrac C x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + (y over x) = k x^n
snippet: Let $k, n \in \R$ be real numbers. The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \dfrac y x = k x^n$ has the general solution: $y = \begin{cases} \dfrac {k x^{n + 1} } {n + 2} + \dfrac C x & : n \ne -2 \\ & \\ \dfrac {k \ln x} x + \dfrac C x & : n = -2 \end{cases}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + 2 x y = exp -x^2
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + 2 x y = \map \exp {-x^2}$ has the general solution: $y = \paren {x + C} \map \exp {-x^2}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + 2y = cos x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + 2 y = \cos x$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {2 \cos x + \sin x} 5 + C e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + y = 1 over (1 + exp 2 x)
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' + y = \dfrac 1 {1 + e^{2 x} }$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \map \arctan {e^x} + C e^{-x}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + y = 2 x exp -x + x^2
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' + y = 2 x e^{-x} + x^2$ has the general solution: $y = x^2 e^{-x} + x^2 - 2 x + 2 + C e^{-x}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + y = sech x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + y = \sech x$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C + \map \ln {e^{2 x} + 1} }$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' + y cot x = 2 x cosec x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad y' + y \cot x = 2 x \csc x$ has the general solution: $y = x^2 \csc x + C \csc x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' - (y over x) = 3 x
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - \dfrac y x = 3 x$ has the general solution: $\dfrac y x = 3 x + C$ or: $y = 3 x^2 + C x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' - (y over x) = k x
snippet: Let $k \in \R$ be a real number. The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - \dfrac y x = k x$ has the general solution: $\dfrac y x = k x + C$ or: $y = k x^2 + C x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' - y = 3
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - y = 3$ has the general solution: $y = C e^x - 3$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' - y = e^x/y(0) = 0
snippet: Consider the linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - y = e^x$ subject to the initial condition: $\map y 0 = 0$ $(1)$ has the particular solution: $y = x e^x$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' - y = x^2
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - y = x^2$ has the general solution: $y = C e^x - \paren {x^2 + 2 x + 2}$

title: Linear First Order ODE/y' = x + y
snippet: The linear first order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = x + y$ has the general solution: $y = C e^x - x - 1$

title: Linear Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a linear real function: $\map f x = \alpha x + \beta$ for all $x \in \R$. Then $f$ is continuous at every real number $c \in \R$.

title: Linear Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The function $f: \N \to \N$, defined as: $\map f n = a n + b$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants, is primitive recursive‎.

title: Linear Function on Real Numbers is Bijection
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = a x + b$ Then $f$ is a bijection $a \ne 0$.

title: Linear Function on Stationary Stochastic Model is Stationary
snippet: Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence of $n$ successive values of $T$: $\sequence {s_n} = \tuple {z_1, z_2, \dotsb, z_n}$ Let $L_t$ be a linear function of $\sequence {s_n}$: $L_t = l_1 z_t + l_2 z_{t - 1} + \dotsb + l_n z_{t - n + 1}$ Then $L_t$ is itself stationary.

title: Linear Functional on *-Algebra Real-Valued at Hermitian Elements preserves Star
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $f : A \to \C$ be a linear functional such that: for each $x \in A$ Hermitian, we have $\map \phi x \in \R$. Then: $\overline {\map \phi x} = \map \phi {x^\ast}$ for each $x \in A$.

title: Linear Functional on Complex Vector Space is Uniquely Determined by Real Part
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\C$. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a linear functional. Define a function $g : X \to \R$: $\map g x = \map \Re {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Then: $\map f x = \map g x - i \map g {i x}$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Linear Functional on Vector Space is Zero or Surjective
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $f : X \to K$ be a linear functional. Then either: $\map f x = 0$ for each $x \in X$ or: $f$ is surjective.

title: Linear Hypothesis/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Linear Hypotheses ==

title: Linear Integral Bounded Operator is Continuous
snippet: Let $I = \closedint 0 1$ be a closed real interval. Let $A : I \times I \to \R$ be a real function such that: $\ds \int_0^1 \int_0^1 \paren {\map A {t, \tau} }^2 \rd t \rd \tau < \infty$ where $\times$ denotes the cartesian product. Let $T_A : \map {L^2} I \to \map {L^2} I$ be an integral operator such that: $\ds \map {\paren {T_A \mathbf x} } t := \int_0^1 \map A {t, \tau} \map {\mathbf x} \tau \rd \tau$ where $\mathbf x \in \map {L^2} I$, and $\map {L^2} I$ is the Lebesgue $2$-space. Then $T_A$ is a continuous transformation.

title: Linear Interval Scale/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Linear Interval Scales ==

title: Linear Isometry is Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear isometry. Then $T$ is injective.

title: Linear Isomorphic Image of Complemented Subspace of Banach Space is Complemented
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be Banach spaces over $\GF$ such that: there exists a linear isomorphism $T : X \to Y$. Let $X_1$ be a complemented subspace of $X$ with topological complement $X_2$. Then $T \sqbrk {X_1}$ is a complemented subspace of $Y$ with topological complement $T \sqbrk {X_2}$.

title: Linear Mappings between Vector Spaces form Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1_F$. Let $X, Y$ be vector spaces over the same field $\struct {F, +, \times}$. Let $\map \LL {X, Y}$ be the set of linear mappings. Let $x \in X$. Define pointwise addition $T + S \in \map \LL {X, Y}$ such that: $\forall x \in X: \map {\paren {T + S} } x := \map T x + \map S x$ For $\alpha \in F$, define pointwise scalar multiplication $\alpha \cdot T$ such that: $\forall x \in X: \map {\paren {\alpha \cdot T} } x := \alpha \cdot \map T x$ Let $\mathbf 0: X \to Y$ be the zero mapping.

title: Linear Operator is Diagonalizable iff it has Eigenbasis
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $K$. Let $A: V \to V$ be a linear operator on $V$. Then $A$ is diagonalizable $A$ has an eigenbasis.

title: Linear Operator is Sum of Real and Imaginary Parts
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $A \in \map B \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $B$ and $C$ be the real and imaginary parts of $A$, respectively. Then $A = B + i C$.

title: Linear Operator on General Logarithm
snippet: Let $\phi: \R^\R \to \R^\R, y \mapsto \map \phi y$ be a linear operator on the space of functions from $\R\to\R$. Let $y$ be a real function such that: $\forall x \in \R: \map y x > \map \bszero x = 0$. Let $\log_a y$ be the logarithm of $y$ to base $a$. Then: $\map \phi {\log_a y} = \dfrac 1 {\ln a} \paren {\map \phi {\ln y} }$ where $\ln$ is the natural logarithm.

title: Linear Operator on the Plane
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a linear operator on the real vector space of two dimensions $\R^2$. Then $\phi$ is completely determined by an ordered tuple of $4$ real numbers.

title: Linear Second Order ODE/(1 + x^2) y'' + x y' = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $\paren {1 + x^2} y' ' + x y' = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \map \ln {x + \sqrt {x^2 + 1} } + C_2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/(x^2 + x) y'' + (2 - x^2) y' - (2 + x) y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 + x} y' ' + \paren {2 - x^2} y' - \paren {2 + x} y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + \dfrac {C_2} x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/(x^2 + x) y'' + (2 - x^2) y' - (2 + x) y = x (x + 1)^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 + x} y' ' + \paren {2 - x^2} y' - \paren {2 + x} y = x \paren {x + 1}^2$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + \dfrac {C_2} x - x - 1 - \dfrac {x^2} 3$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/(x^2 - 1) y'' - 2 x y' + 2 y = (x^2 - 1)^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 - 1} y' ' - 2 x y' + 2 y = \paren {x^2 - 1}^2$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + C_2 \paren {x^2 + 1} + \dfrac {x^4} 6 - \dfrac {x^2} 2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/(x - 1) y'' - y' + y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x - 1} y' ' - x y' + y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + C_2 e^x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/2 x^2 y'' + 10 x y' + 8 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad 2 x^2 y' ' + 10 x y' + 8 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x^{-2} + C_2 x^{-2} \ln x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/2 y'' + 2 y' + 3 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad 2 y' ' + 2 y' + 3 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x/2} \paren {C_1 \cos \dfrac {\sqrt 5} 2 x + C_2 \sin \dfrac {\sqrt 5} 2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/2 y'' - 4 y' + 8 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad 2 y' ' - 4 y + 8 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^x \paren {C_1 \cos \sqrt 3 x + C_2 \sin \sqrt 3 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + 2 x y' - 12 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y + 2 x y' - 12 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x^3 + C_2 x^{-4}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + 2 x y' - 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y + 2 x y' - 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + \dfrac {C_2} {x^2}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + 3 x y' + 10 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y + 3 x y' + 10 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac 1 x \paren {C_1 \map \cos {\ln x^3} + C_2 \map \sin {\ln x^3} }$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + x y' - 4 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y + x y' - 4 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x^2 + \dfrac {C_2} {x^2}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + x y' - y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y + x y' - y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + \dfrac {C_2} x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x^2 y' ' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + C_2 x^2$ on any closed real interval which does not contain $0$.

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 10 y' + 25 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 10 y' + 25 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{-5 x} + C_2 x e^{-5 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 10 y' + 25 y = 14 exp -5 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 10 y' + 25 y = 14 e^{-5 x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x + \sin x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 b y' + a^2 y = 0/b less than a
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 b y' + a^2 y = 0$ where $b^2 < a^2$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-b x} \paren {C_1 \, \map \cos {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } x + C_2 \, \map \sin {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 b y' + a^2 y = K cosine omega x/b less than a
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 b y' + a^2 y = K \cos \omega x$ where $b^2 < a^2$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-b x} \paren {C_1 \cos \alpha x + C_2 \sin \alpha x} + \dfrac K {\sqrt {4 b^2 \omega^2 + \paren {a^2 - \omega^2}^2} } \map \cos {\omega x - \phi}$ where: $\alpha = \sqrt {a^2 - b^2}$ $\phi = \map \arctan {\dfrac {2 b \omega} {a^2 - \omega^2} }$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + 10 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + 10 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C_1 \cos 3 x + C_2 \sin 3 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {A \cos x + B \sin x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + 5 y = exp -x secant 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + 5 y = e^{-x} \sec 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x} + \dfrac {x e^{-x} \sin 2 x} 2 + \dfrac {e^{-x} \cos 2 x \ln \cos 2 x} 4$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + 5 y = x sin x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + 5 y = x \sin x$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x} + \ldots$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{-x} + C_2 x e^{-x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + y = exp -x log x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + y = e^{-x} \ln x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{-x} + C_2 x e^{-x} - \dfrac {x^2 e^{-x} \ln x} 2 - \dfrac 3 4 x^2 e^{-x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 y' + y = x exp -x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 y' + y = x e^{-x}$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-x} \paren {C_1 + C_2 x + \dfrac {x^3} 6}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 3 y' - 10 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 3 y' - 10 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-5 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 3 y' - 10 y = 6 exp 4 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 3 y' - 10 y = 6 e^{4 x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-5 x} + \dfrac {e^{4 x} } 3$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y' + 4 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y' + 4 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = \paren {C_1 + C_2 x} e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y' + 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y' + 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-2 x} \paren {C_1 \cos x + C_2 \sin x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y' + 5 y = 2 exp -2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + 4 y' + 5 y = 2 e^{-2 x}$ has the general solution: $y = e^{-2 x} \paren {C_1 \cos x + C_2 \sin x + 2}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 3 sin 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 3 \sin 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin k x + C_2 \cos k x - \dfrac 3 4 x \cos 2 x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 3 sine x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 3 \sin x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x + \sin x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 4 cosine 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 4 \cos 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin 2 x + C_2 \cos 2 x + x \sin 2 x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 4 cosine 2 x + 6 cosine x + 8 x^2 - 4 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 4 \cos 2 x + 6 \cos x + 8 x^2 - 4 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin 2 x + C_2 \cos 2 x + x \sin 2 x + 2 \cos x - 1 - x + 2 x^2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 6 cosine x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + 4 y = 6 \cos x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin 2 x + C_2 \cos 2 x + 2 \cos x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = 8 x^2 - 4 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 4 y = 8 x^2 - 4 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin 2 x + C_2 \cos 2 x - 1 - x + 2 x^2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 4 y = tan 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + 4 y = \tan 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x - \dfrac 1 4 \cos 2 x \map \ln {\sec 2 x + \tan 2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + 8 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 8 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \cos 2 \sqrt 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 \sqrt 2 x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + k^2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + k^2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = A \, \map \sin {k x + B}$ or can be expressed as: $y = C_1 \sin k x + C_2 \cos k x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + k^2 y = sine b x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + k^2 y = \sin b x$ has the general solution: $y = \begin{cases} C_1 \sin k x + C_2 \cos k x + \dfrac {\sin b x} {k^2 - b^2} & : b \ne k \\ C_1 \sin k x + C_2 \cos k x - \dfrac {x \cos k x} {2 k} & : b = k \end{cases}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y' - 12 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + y' - 12 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-4 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y' - 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + y' - 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y' - 6 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + y' - 6 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-3 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = 2 cosine x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + y = 2 \cos x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x + x \cos x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = K
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + y = K$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x + K$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = cosecant x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + y = \csc x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x - x \cos x + \sin x \map \ln {\sin x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' + y = exp -x cos x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y + y = e^{-x} \cos x$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {e^{-x} } 5 \paren {\cos x - 2 \sin x} + C_1 \sin x + C_2 \cos x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' + 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = e^x \paren {C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + 5 y = 25 x^2 + 12
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 2 y' + 5 y = 25 x^2 + 12$ has the general solution: $y = e^x \paren {C_1 \cos 2 x + C_2 \sin 2 x} + 2 + 4 x + 5 x^2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' + y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 x e^x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + y = 1 over 1 + e^x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 2 y' + y = \dfrac 1 {1 + e^x}$ has a particular solution: $y = 1 + e^x \ds \int \map \ln {1 + e^{-x} } \rd x$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + y = 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' + y = 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 x e^x + 2 x + 4$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' + y = exp x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 2 y' + y = e^x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 x e^x + \dfrac {x^2 e^x} 2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' - 3 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' - 3 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' - 3 y = 64 x exp -x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' - 3 y = 64 x e^{-x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-x} - x e^{-x} \paren {8 x + 4}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' - 3 y = e^(-x)
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' - 3 y = e^{-x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-x} - \dfrac {x e^{-x} } 4$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' - 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' - 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \map \exp {\paren {1 + \sqrt 6} x} + C_2 \map \exp {\paren {1 - \sqrt 6} x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' - 5 y = 2 cos 3 x - sin 3 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 2 y' - 5 y = 2 \cos 3 x - \sin 3 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \map \exp {\paren {1 + \sqrt 6} x} + C_2 \map \exp {\paren {1 - \sqrt 6} x} + \dfrac 1 {116} \paren {\sin 3 x - 17 \cos 3 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 2 y' = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 + C_2 e^{2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 2 y' = 12 x - 10
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 2 y' = 12 x - 10$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 + C_2 e^{2 x} + 2 x - 3 x^2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 3 y' + 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 3 y' + 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 3 y' + 2 y = 14 sine 2 x - 18 cosine 2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 3 y' + 2 y = 14 \sin 2 x - 18 \cos 2 x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x} - 4 x e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 3 y' + 2 y = 5 exp 3 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 3 y' + 2 y = 5 e^{3 x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{2 x} + \dfrac {5 e^{3 x} } 2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y' + 4 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 4 y' + 4 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 x e^{2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y' - 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 4 y' - 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{5 x} + C_2 e^{-x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y' - 5 y = x^2/y(0) = 1, y'(0) = -1
snippet: Consider the second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 4 y' - 5 y = x^2$ whose initial conditions are: $y = 1$ when $x = 0$ $y' = -1$ when $x = 0$ $(1)$ has the particular solution: $y = \dfrac {e^{5 x} } {375} + \dfrac {4 e^{-x} } 3 - \dfrac {x^2} 5 + \dfrac {8 x} {25} - \dfrac {42} {125}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 4 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 4 y = x^2 - 3 x - 4
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 4 y = x^2 - 3 x - 4$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x} - \dfrac {x^2} 4 + \dfrac {3 x} 4 + \dfrac 7 8$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 5 y' + 6 y = 0
snippet: The linear second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 5 y' + 6 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{3 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 5 y' + 6 y = cos x + sin x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 5 y' + 6 y = \cos x + \sin x$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{2 x} + C_2 e^{3 x} + \dfrac {\cos x} 5$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 7 y' - 5 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 7 y' - 5 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \, \map \exp {\paren {\dfrac 7 2 + \dfrac {\sqrt {69} } 2} x} + C_2 \, \map \exp {\paren {\dfrac 7 2 - \dfrac {\sqrt {69} } 2} x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 7 y' - 5 y = x^3 - 1
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - 7 y' - 5 y = x^3 - 1$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 \, \map \exp {\paren {\dfrac 7 2 + \dfrac {\sqrt {69} } 2} x} + C_2 \, \map \exp {\paren {\dfrac 7 2 - \dfrac {\sqrt {69} } 2} x} + \dfrac 1 {625} \paren {-125 x^3 + 525 x^2 - 1620 x + 2603}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - 9 y' + 20 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - 9 y' + 20 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{4 x} + C_2 e^{5 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - k^2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - k^2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{k x} + C_2 e^{-k x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y' - 6 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - y' - 6 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y' - 6 y = 20 exp -2 x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - y' - 6 y = 20 e^{-2 x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x} - 4 x e^{-2 x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y' - 6 y = exp -x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - y' - 6 y = e^{-x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^{3 x} + C_2 e^{-2 x} - \dfrac {e^{-x} } 4$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{-x}$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' - y = 3 exp -x
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y - y = 3 e^{-x}$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^{-x} - \dfrac {3 x e^{-x} } 2$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' = 1 over 1 - x^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' = \dfrac 1 {1 - x^2}$ has the general solution: $y = x \tanh^{-1} x + \map \ln {1 - x^2} + C x + D$

title: Linear Second Order ODE/y'' = y'
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y = y'$ has the general solution: $y = A_1 e^x + A_2$

title: Linear Span is Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a division ring $K$. Let $S \subseteq V$ be a subset of $V$. Then the linear span $\map \span S$ is a subspace of $V$.

title: Linear Span of Self-Adjoint Subset of *-Algebra is Self-Adjoint
snippet: Let $\tuple {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be self-adjoint. Then $\map \span S$ is self-adjoint.

title: Linear Subspace Dense iff Zero Orthocomplement
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $K$ be a linear subspace of $H$. Then $K$ is everywhere dense $K^\perp = \paren 0$, where $K^\perp$ is the orthocomplement of $K$, and $\paren 0$ denotes the zero subspace.

title: Linear Subspace is Convex Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over $\R$ or $\C$, and let $L$ be a linear subspace of $V$. Then $L$ is a convex set.

title: Linear Subspace is Subset of Double Annihilator
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $N$ be a linear subspace of $X^\ast$. Then: $N \subseteq \paren { {}^\bot N}^\bot$ where: ${}^\bot N$ denotes the annihilator of $N \subseteq X^\ast$ $\paren { {}^\bot N}^\bot$ denotes the annihilator of ${}^\bot N \subseteq X$.

title: Linear Subspaces Closed under Setwise Addition
snippet: Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $M, N$ be linear subspaces of $V$. Then $L := M + N$ is also a linear subspace of $V$, where $+$ denotes setwise addition.

title: Linear Transform on Dirac Bra
snippet: Let $\bra x$ be a bra in some dual space. Let $T$ be a linear transform. Then: $\bra x T = \bra {T^* x}$

title: Linear Transformation Compact iff Adjoint Compact
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $T: H \to K$ be a linear transformation. Then $T$ is compact its adjoint $T^*$ is.

title: Linear Transformation Defined from Basis
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $\BB = \set {e_\alpha : \alpha \in I}$ be a basis for $X$. For each $\alpha \in I$, let $c_\alpha \in Y$. Then there exists a linear transformation $T : X \to Y$ with $T e_\alpha = c_\alpha$ for each $\alpha \in I$. This allows us to define a linear transformation $T$ by specifying its action on a basis and then "extending linearly".

title: Linear Transformation Maps Zero Vector to Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0$. Likewise let $\mathbf V\,'$ be another vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0'$. Let $T: \mathbf V \to \mathbf V\,'$ be a linear transformation. Then: $T: \mathbf 0 \mapsto \mathbf 0'$

title: Linear Transformation as Matrix Product
snippet: Let $T: \R^n \to \R^m, \mathbf x \mapsto \map T {\mathbf x}$ be a linear transformation. Then: $\map T {\mathbf x} = \mathbf A_T \mathbf x$ where $\mathbf A_T$ is the $m \times n$ matrix defined as: $\mathbf A_T = \begin {bmatrix} \map T {\mathbf e_1} & \map T {\mathbf e_2} & \cdots & \map T {\mathbf e_n} \end {bmatrix}$ where $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \cdots, \mathbf e_n}$ is the standard ordered basis of $\R^n$.

title: Linear Transformation between Normed Vector Spaces is Bounded iff Bounded as Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be linear transformations. Then $T$ is bounded as a linear transformation between normed vector spaces it is bounded as a linear transformation between topological vector spaces.

title: Linear Transformation between Normed Vector Spaces is Open iff Image of Open Unit Ball is Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $B_X^O$ be the open unit ball of $X$. Then $T$ is open $T \sqbrk {B_X^O}$ is open.

title: Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces Continuous iff Continuous at Origin
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $T$ is everywhere continuous it is continuous at ${\mathbf 0}_X$.

title: Linear Transformation between Topological Vector Spaces is Open iff Interior of Image of Open Neighborhood contains Zero Vector
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $T$ is open : for each open neighborhood $U$ of ${\mathbf 0}_X$, we have ${\mathbf 0}_Y \in T \sqbrk U^\circ$.

title: Linear Transformation defined from Graph
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $X \times Y$ be the direct product of $X$ and $Y$. Let $U$ be a vector subspace of $X \times Y$ such that: whenever $\tuple { {\mathbf 0}_X, y} \in U$, we have $y = {\mathbf 0}_Y$ Define: $\map D T = \set {x \in X : \tuple {x, y} \in U \text { for some } y \in Y}$ Then there exists a linear transformation $T : \map D T \to Y$ with graph $\map \GG T = U$.

title: Linear Transformation from Banach *-Algebra is Bounded if Bounded on Hermitian Elements
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ be a Banach $\ast$-algebra. Let $\struct {B, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be a normed vector space over $\C$. Let $T : A 	o B$ be a linear transformation such that there exists $M > 0$ with: $
orm {T x}_B \le M 
orm x_A$ for each $x \in A$ Hermitian. Then $T$ is bounded.

title: Linear Transformation from C*-Algebra is Bounded if Bounded on Positive Elements
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_A}$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\struct {B, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_B}$ be a normed vector space over $\C$. Let $T : A 	o B$ be a linear transformation such that there exists $M > 0$ with: $
orm {T x}_B \le M 
orm x_A$ for each $x \in A$ positive. Then $T$ is bounded.

title: Linear Transformation from Cartesian Space on Hausdorff Topological Field to Topological Vector Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $K^n$ be the $n$-Cartesian space as a topological vector space with its product topology. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $f : K^n \to X$ be a linear transformation. Then $f$ is continuous.

title: Linear Transformation from Center of Scalar Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Let $\map Z R$ be the center of the scalar ring $R$. Let $\lambda \in \map Z R$. Then $\lambda \circ \phi$ is a linear transformation.

title: Linear Transformation from Finite-Dimensional Vector Space is Injective iff Surjective
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a finite dimensional vector space over $K$. Let $f: V \to V$ be a linear transformation on $V$. Then $f$ is an injection $f$ is a surjection.

title: Linear Transformation from Ordered Basis less Kernel
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be unitary $R$-modules. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a non-zero linear transformation. Let $G$ be $n$-dimensional. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be any ordered basis of $G$ such that $\set {a_k: r + 1 \le k \le n}$ is the basis of the kernel of $\phi$. Then $\sequence {\map \phi {a_r} }$ is an ordered basis of the image of $\phi$.

title: Linear Transformation has Finite Rank iff Domain Quotiented by Kernel is Finite Dimensional
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $\ker T$ be the kernel of $T$. Let $X/\ker T$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $\ker T$. Then $T$ has finite rank $X/\ker T$ is finite dimensional.

title: Linear Transformation is Fredholm Operator iff Pseudoinverse exists
snippet: Let $U, V$ be vector spaces. Let $T: U \to V$ be a linear transformation. Then $T$ is a Fredholm operator $T$ has a pseudoinverse.

title: Linear Transformation is Injective iff Kernel Contains Only Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf V, \mathbf V'$ be vector spaces, with respective zeroes $\mathbf 0, \mathbf 0'$. Let $T: \mathbf V \to \mathbf V'$ be a linear transformation. Then: $T$ is injective $\map \ker T = \set {\mathbf 0}$ where: $\mathbf 0$ is the zero of the domain of $T$ $\map \ker T$ is the kernel of $T$.

title: Linear Transformation is Isomorphism iff Inverse Equals Adjoint
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $U : \HH \to \KK$ be a bounded linear transformation. {{item|(2):|$U$ is invertible and $U^{-1} U^*$, where $U^*$ denotes the adjoint of $U$}}

title: Linear Transformation of Arithmetic Mean
snippet: Let $D = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ be a set of real data describing a quantitative variable. Let $\overline x$ be the arithmetic mean of the data in $D$. Let $T: \R \to \R$ be a linear transformation such that: $\forall i \in \set {0, 1, \ldots, n}: \map T {x_i} = \lambda x_i + \gamma$ Let $T \sqbrk D$ be the image of $D$ under $T$. Then the arithmetic mean of the data in $T \sqbrk D$ is given by: $\map T {\overline x} = \lambda \overline x + \gamma$

title: Linear Transformation of Continuous Random Variable is Continuous Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $a$ be a non-zero real number. Let $b$ be a real number. Let $X$ be a continuous real variable. Let $F_X$ be the cumulative distribution function of $X$. Then $a X + b$ is a continuous real variable. Further, if $a > 0$, the cumulative distribution function of $a X + b$, $F_{a X + b}$. is given by: $\ds \map {F_{a X + b} } x = \map {F_X} {\frac {x - b} a}$ for each $x \in \R$. If $a < 0$, $F_{a X + b}$ is given by: $\ds \map {F_{a X + b} } x = 1 - \map {F_X} {\frac {x - b} a}$ for each $x \in \R$.

title: Linear Transformation of Generated Module
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $G$ and $H$ be $R$-modules. Let $\phi$ and $\psi$ be linear transformations from $G$ into $H$. Let $S$ be a generator for $G$. Suppose that: $\forall x \in S: \map \phi x = \map \psi x$ Then $\phi = \psi$.

title: Linear Transformation of Normal Random Variable
snippet: Let $\mu$, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be real numbers. Let $\sigma$ be a positive real number. Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ where $\Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ is the normal distribution with parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$. Then: $\alpha X + \beta \sim \Gaussian {\alpha \mu + \beta} {\alpha^2 \sigma^2}$

title: Linear Transformation of Real-Valued Random Variable is Real-Valued Random Variable
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ be a real-valued random variable on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Then: $a X + b$ is a real-valued random variable.

title: Linear Transformation of Submodule
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation.

title: Linear Transformation of Vector Space Equivalent Statements
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be $n$-dimensional vector spaces. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. $(1): \quad \phi$ is an isomorphism. $(2): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism. $(3): \quad \phi$ is an epimorphism. $(4): \quad \map \phi B$ is a basis of $H$ for every basis $B$ of $G$. $(5): \quad \map \phi B$ is a basis of $H$ for some basis $B$ of $G$.

title: Linear Transformation of Vector Space Monomorphism
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Then $\phi$ is a monomorphism for every linearly independent sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of vectors of $G$, $\sequence {\map \phi {a_n} }$ is a linearly independent sequence of vectors of $H$.

title: Linear Transformations between Finite-Dimensional Normed Vector Spaces are Continuous
snippet: Linear transformations between finite-dimensional normed vector spaces are continuous.

title: Linearity of Function defined using Function with Translation Property
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $f$ have the translation property. Let $x$ and $l$ be real numbers. Define: $\map {f_x} l = \map f {x + l} - \map f x$ Then: $\forall q \in \Q: \map {f_x} {q l} = q \map {f_x} l$

title: Linearity of Function with Translation Property
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $c$ be a real number. Then: $f$ has the translation property $\map {f'} c$ exists $f$ is linear

title: Linearly Dependent Sequence of Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +}$ be a group whose identity is $\mathbf 0$. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_K$ be a $K$-vector space. Let $\sequence {a_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be a sequence of distinct non-zero vectors of $G$. Then $\sequence {a_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ is linearly dependent : $\exists p \in \closedint 2 n: a_p$ is a linear combination of $\sequence {a_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le p - 1}$

title: Linearly Independent Set is Contained in some Basis
Linearly Independent Solutions of y'' - y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - y = 0$ has solutions: $y_1 = e^x$ $y_2 = e^{-x}$ which are linearly independent.

title: Linearly Independent Solutions to 1st Order Systems
snippet: The 1st-order homogeneous linear system of differential equations $x' = A \left({t}\right) x$, expressed with the vectors $x', x: \R \to \R^n$ and the matrix function $A: \R \to M_{n \times n} \left({\R}\right)$, has $n$ linearly independent solutions, and if $ \phi_1 , \phi_2, \dots, \phi_n$ are $n$ linearly independent solutions, then $c_1 \phi_1 + c_2 \phi_2 + \cdots + c_n \phi_n$, where $c_i$ are constants, is a general solution.

title: Linearly Independent Subset also Independent in Generated Subspace
snippet: Let $G$ be a finitely generated $K$-vector space. Let $S$ be a linearly independent subset of $G$. Let $M$ be the subspace of $G$ generated by $S$. If $M \ne G$, then $\forall b \in G: b \notin M$, the set $S \cup \set b$ is linearly independent.

title: Linearly Independent over the Rational Numbers iff Linearly Independent over the Integers
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ be complex numbers. Then: $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ are linearly independent over the rational numbers $\Q$ $z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n$ are linearly independent over the integers $\Z$.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Compact iff Complete
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $T$ is a compact space it is complete.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $T$ is a completely normal space.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Connected iff Linear Continuum
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $S$ is a connected space it is a linear continuum.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $\struct {X, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff space.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is normal.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is Regular
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is regular.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: Linearly Ordered Space is T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Then $T$ is a $T_5$ space.

title: Linearly Ordered Space on Order-Convex Subset is Subspace Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq,\tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a order-convex set in $S$. Let $\upsilon$ be the order topology on $A$. Let $\tau'$ be the $\tau$-relative subspace topology on $A$. Then $\upsilon = \tau'$.

title: Lines Joining Equal and Parallel Straight Lines are Parallel
snippet: The straight lines joining equal and parallel straight lines at their endpoints, in the same direction, are themselves equal and parallel.

title: Lines Parallel to Same Line not in Same Plane are Parallel to each other
Lines Through Endpoints of One Side of Triangle to Point Inside Triangle is Less than Sum of Other Sides
snippet: Given a triangle and a point inside it, the sum of the lengths of the line segments from the endpoints of one side of the triangle to the point is less than the sum of the other two sides of the triangle.

title: Lines are Subspaces of Plane
snippet: The one-dimensional subspaces of $\R^2$ are precisely the homogeneous lines of plane analytic geometry.

title: Lines of Electric Force do not Cross
snippet: Let $\mathbf E$ be an electric field. Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be lines of force within $\mathbf E$. Then $L_1$ and $L_2$ do not cross over each other.

title: Lines of Electric Force due to Dipole
snippet: Let $\pm q$ denote an electric dipole. Then the lines of force of the electric field brought about by $\pm q$ have the following form:

title: Lines through Center Square of Order 3 Magic Square are in Arithmetic Sequence
snippet: Consider the order 3 magic square: Each of the lines through the center cell contain $3$ integers in arithmetic sequence.

title: Liouville's Constant is Transcendental
snippet: Liouville's constant: {{eqn | l = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \dfrac 1 {10^{n!} } | r = \frac 1 {10^1} + \frac 1 {10^2} + \frac 1 {10^6} + \frac 1 {10^{24} } + \cdots | c = }} is transcendental.

title: Liouville's Theorem
snippet: Liouville's Lemma: concerning diophantine approximations. Liouville's Theorem (Hamiltonian Mechanics): the phase-space distribution function is constant along the trajectories of the system. Liouville's Theorem (Number Theory): concerning the transcendental nature of Liouville numbers. Liouville's Theorem (Differential Algebra): how to tell whether an elementary function has an elementary integral. Liouville's Theorem (Conformal Mappings): a conformal mapping is a Möbius transformation. Liouville's Theorem (Complex Analysis): a bounded entire complex function is constant.

title: Liouville's Theorem (Complex Analysis)
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a bounded entire function. Then $f$ is constant.

title: Liouville's Theorem (Differential Equations)
snippet: Let $\map \Phi t$ be a solution to the matrix differential equation: $X' = \map A t X$ with $\map A t$ continuous on the interval $I$ such that $t_0 \in I$. Then: $\ds \det \map \Phi t = \map \exp {\int_{t_0}^t \map \tr {\map A s} \rd s} \det \map \Phi {t_0}$

title: Liouville's Theorem (Hamiltonian Mechanics)
snippet: Consider a Hamiltonian system characterised by the Hamiltonian $\map \HH {t, \mathbf q, \mathbf p}$, where the state of the system, $\mathbf r$, is described by generalized coordinates $\mathbf q$ and $\mathbf p$, which correspond to $N$ generalized positions and $N$ generalized momenta, respectively. Let the trajectory, $\map {\mathbf r} t$, be the solution of the intial-value problem given by Hamilton's equations together with the initial condition. Consider the Hamiltonian system's joint distribution function $\map f {t, \map {\mathbf r} t}$.

title: Liouville's Theorem (Number Theory)
snippet: Let $x$ be an irrational number that is algebraic of degree $n$. Then there exists a constant $c > 0$ (which can depend on $x$) such that: $\size {x - \dfrac p q} \ge \dfrac c {q^n}$ for every pair $p, q \in \Z$ with $q \ne 0$.

title: Liouville Numbers are Irrational
snippet: Liouville numbers are irrational.

title: Lipschitz Condition implies Uniform Continuity
snippet: Let $\struct {M_1, d_1}$ and $\struct {M_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $g: M_1 \to M_2$ satisfy the Lipschitz condition. Then $g$ is uniformly continuous on $M_1$.

title: Lipschitz Continuous Real Function is Absolutely Continuous
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f$ be Lipschitz continuous on $I$. Then $f$ is absolutely continuous on $I$.

title: Lipschitz Equivalence is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\DD$ be the set of all metrics on $A$. Let $\sim$ be the relation on $\DD$ defined as: $\forall d_1, d_2 \in \DD: d_1 \sim d_2 \iff d_1$ is Lipschitz equivalent to $d_2$ Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Lipschitz Equivalence yields Lipschitz Equivalent Metric
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$. Let $f: M_1 \to M_2$ be a Lipschitz equivalence. Let $d_3: A^2 \to \R$ be a mapping defined as: $\map {d_3} {x, y} := \map {d_2} {\map f x, \map f y}$ Then $d_3$ yields a metric on $M_1$ which is Lipschitz equivalent to $d_1$.

title: Lipschitz Equivalent Metric Spaces are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be Lipschitz equivalent. Then $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic.

title: Lipschitz Equivalent Metrics are Topologically Equivalent
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be metric spaces on the same underlying set $A$. Let $d_1$ and $d_2$ be Lipschitz equivalent. Then $d_1$ and $d_2$ are topologically equivalent.

title: Lissajous-Bowditch Figure/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Lissajous-Bowditch Figures ==

title: List of Elements in Finite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in G$ have finite order $\order a = k$. Let $\gen a$ be the cyclic subgroup generated by $a$. Then: $\set {a^0, a^1, a^2, \ldots, a^{k - 1} }$ is a complete repetition-free list of the elements of $\gen a$ That is, let $\closedint 0 {k - 1}$ be the integer interval from $0$ to $k - 1$. Then the mapping: $\closedint 0 {k - 1} \to \gen a$: $n \mapsto g^n$ is a bijection.

title: List of Elements in Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $\gen a$ be the infinite cyclic subgroup generated by $a$. Then: $\set {\ldots, a^{-2}, a^{-1}, a^0, a^1, a^2, \ldots}$ is a complete repetition-free list of the elements of $\gen a$. That is: $G = \set {a^n: n \in \Z}$

title: List of Fundamental Groups for 2-Manifolds
snippet: For the following two-manifolds, the fundamental group for any point in $X$, written $\map {\pi_1} X$ is isomorphic to the listed group: $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^1 \times \closedint 0 1} = \Z$ $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^2} = \set e$, the trivial group. $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb T^2} = \map {\pi_1} {\Bbb S^1 \times \Bbb S^1} = \Z \times \Z$ $\map {\pi_1} {\Bbb {RP}^2} = \Z_2$

title: Little-O Estimate for Real Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Little-$\oo$ Estimates for Real Functions ==

title: Little Bézout Theorem
snippet: Let $\map {P_n} x$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ in $x$. Let $a$ be a constant. Then the remainder of $\map {P_n} x$ when divided by $x - a$ is equal to $\map {P_n} a$.

title: Little Picard Theorem
snippet: A non-constant entire function $f: \C \to \C$ omits at most one complex value $a \in \C$.

title: Lituus is Asymptotic to Polar Axis
snippet: Let $L$ be a lituus expressed in polar coordinates as: $r^2 = \dfrac {a^2} \theta$ Then the polar axis is an asymptote to $L$.

title: Lobachevsky Integral Formula
snippet: Let $f$ be a continuous real function, periodic with period $\pi$. Then: $\ds \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin x} x \map f x \rd x = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \map f x \rd x$

title: Local Basis Generated from Neighborhood Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x$ be an element of $S$. Let $\BB$ be a neighborhood basis of $x$. For any subset $A \subseteq S$, let $A^\circ$ denote the interior of $A$. Then the set: $\BB' = \set {H^\circ: H \in \BB}$ is a local basis of $x$.

title: Local Basis Test
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\BB$ be a local basis for $x$ in $\struct {S, \tau}$. Let $\CC$ be a set of open neighborhoods of $x$. Then: $\CC$ is a local basis : $\forall B \in \BB \implies \exists C \in \CC: C \subseteq B$

title: Local Basis Test for Adherent Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\BB_x$ be a local basis of $x$. Then $x \in S$ is an adherent point of $H$ : $\forall U \in \BB_x : H \cap U \ne \O$

title: Local Basis Test for Isolated Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $x \in H$. Let $\BB_x$ be a local basis of $x$. Then $x$ is an isolated point of $H$ : $\exists U \in \BB_x : U \cap H = \set x$

title: Local Basis Test for Limit Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\BB_x$ be a local basis of $x$. Then $x \in S$ is a limit point of $H$ : $\forall U \in \BB_x : H \cap U \setminus \set x \ne \O$

title: Local Basis for Point in Union of Adjacent Open Intervals
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals considered as a topological space: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ Let $x \in S$ be arbitrary. Let $\BB = \set {\openint s t: a < s < x < t < b} \cup \set {\openint s t: c < s < x < t < d}$ Then $\BB$ is a local basis for $x$ in $T$.

title: Local Basis for Point on Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line under the Euclidean topology. Let $x \in \R$ be arbitrary. Let $\BB = \set {\openint a b: a, b \in \R: a < x < b}$ Then $\BB$ is a local basis for $x$ in $\R$.

title: Local Basis of Open Real Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line under the Euclidean topology. Let $I = \openint a b \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $T = \struct {I, \tau}$ be the subspace of $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ with the subspace topology on $I$ induced by $\tau_d$. Let $x \in I$ be arbitrary. Let $\BB = \set {\openint c d: a < c < x < d < b}$ Then $\BB$ is a local basis for $x$ in $T$.

title: Local Basis of Open Subspace iff Local Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U \subseteq S$ be an open subset Let $\tau_U$ denote the subspace topology on $U$. Let $s \in U$. Let $\BB \subseteq \powerset U$. Then: $\BB$ is a local basis of $s$ in $\struct {U, \tau_U}$ $\BB$ is a local basis of $s$ in $\struct {S, \tau}$.

title: Local Basis of P-adic Number
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Then the set of open balls $\set {\map {B_{p^{-n} } } a : n \in Z}$ is a local basis of $a$ consisting of clopen sets.

title: Local Basis of Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\XX, \tau}$ be a topological vector space. Let $0_\XX$ denote the zero vector of $\XX$. Then there exists a local basis $\BB$ of $0_\XX$ with the following properties: $(1): \quad \forall W \in \BB: \exists V \in \BB$ such that $V + V \subseteq W$ (where the addition $V + V$ is meant in the sense of the Minkowski sum) $(2): \quad$ Every $W \in \BB$ is star-shaped (balanced) $(3): \quad$ Every $W \in \BB$ is absorbent. $(4): \quad \ds \bigcap_\BB W = \set {0_\XX}$.

title: Local Compactness Properties which are Hereditary
snippet: The following local compactness properties are hereditary:

title: Local Compactness Properties which are Weakly Hereditary
snippet: The following local compactness properties are weakly hereditary:

title: Local Compactness is Preserved under Open Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \left({S_A, \tau_A}\right)$ and $T_B = \left({S_B, \tau_B}\right)$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous mapping which is also an open mapping and a surjection. If $T_A$ is locally compact, then $T_B$ is also locally compact.

title: Local Connectedness is not Preserved under Continuous Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {B, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: A \to B$ be a continuous mapping. Let $\struct {\Img f, \tau_3}$ be the image of $f$ with the subspace topology of $B$. Let $\struct {A, \tau_1}$ be locally connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {\Img f, \tau_3}$ is also locally connected.

title: Local Connectedness is not Preserved under Infinite Product
snippet: The property of local connectedness is not preserved under the operation of forming an infinite product space.

title: Local Criterion for Continuity of Convex Real Function
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set with non-empty interior $\Int C$. Let $x \in \Int C$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $x$ in $\Int C$. Let $f : C \to \R$ be a convex real function such that: $\ds \sup_{z \mathop \in U} \map f z < \infty$ Then $f$ is continuous at $x$.

title: Local Expression for Metric of Product Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $\struct {M_1, g_1}$ and $\struct {M_2, g_2}$ be Riemannian manifolds. Let their smooth local coordinates be $\tuple {x^1, \dots, x^n}$ and $\tuple {x^{n + 1}, \dots, x^{n + m}}$ respectively. Let $M_1 \times M_2$ be the product Riemannian manifold with smooth local coordinates $\tuple {x^1, \dots, x^{n + m}}$.

title: Local Maxima of Number of Goldbach Decompositions
snippet: Let $\mathbb E$ be the set of even positive integers. Let $G: \mathbb E \to \N$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall n \in \mathbb E: \map G n =$ the number of Goldbach decompositions of $n$. Then $G$ has local maxima when $n$ is a multiple of $6$.

title: Local Membership of Equalizer
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $e: E \to C$ be the equalizer of $f, g : C \to D$. Then a variable element $z: Z \to C$ is a local member of $e$ $f \circ z = g \circ z$: $z \in_C e \iff f \circ z = g \circ z$

title: Local Minimum of Gamma Function on Positive Domain
snippet: The local minimum of the Gamma function on the positive real numbers occurs at the point: $\tuple {1 \cdotp 46163 21449 68362 34126 26595, 0 \cdotp 88560 31944 10888 70027 88159}$

title: Local Normal Form for Immersions
snippet: Let $\Omega\subset\R^k$ be open. Let $f: \Omega \to \R^n$ be an immersion. Let $p \in \Omega$. Then: $k \le n$ and there exists a local diffeomorphism $\phi$ around $\map f p$ such that: $\phi \circ \map f x = \tuple {x, 0}$ for all $x$ in a neighborhood of $p$.

title: Local Normal Form for Submersions
snippet: Let $\Omega\subset\R^n$ be open. Let $f : \Omega \to \R^k$ be an submersion. Let $p\in\Omega$. Then $n\geq k$, and there exists a local diffeomorphism $\phi$ around $f(p)$ such that $\phi\circ f (x, y) = x$ for all $(x, y)$ in a neighborhood of $p$.

title: Local Orthonormal Coframe defines Riemannian Density
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $\tuple {\epsilon^i}$ be an local orthonormal coframe. Let $\mu$ be a Riemannian density. Then there exists $\mu$ such that: $\mu = \size {\epsilon^1 \wedge \ldots \wedge \epsilon^n}$ where $\wedge$ denotes the wedge product.

title: Local Orthonormal Frame and Coframe related by Index Raising
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $\tuple {E_i}$ be the local frame of $M$. Let $\tuple {\epsilon^i}$ the local coframe dual to $\tuple {E_i}$. Let $\sharp$ be the sharp operator. {{item|(1):|$\tuple {E_i}$ is orthonormal.}} {{item|(2):|$\tuple {\epsilon^i}$ is orthonormal.}} {{item|(3):|$\forall i \in \N_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n}: \tuple {\epsilon^i}^\sharp E_i$}}

title: Local Uniform Convergence Implies Compact Convergence
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n : X \to M$. Let $f_n$ converge locally uniformly to $f : X \to M$. Then $f_n$ converges compactly to $f$.

title: Locale Isomorphism is Isomorphism in Loc
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Loc}$ denote the category of locales. Let $L_1 = \struct{S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct{S_2, \preceq_2}$ be locales. Let $f:S_1 \to S_2$ be a continuous map of $\mathbf{Loc}$. Then: $f$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbf{Loc}$ $f$ is a locale isomorphism.

title: Locale of Open Sets Functor is Covariant
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Let $\mathbf{Loc}$ denote the category of locales. Then the open sets functor $\mathbf \Omega : \mathbf{Top} \to \mathbf{Loc}$ is a covariant functor.

title: Locale of Topological Space is Locale
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\map \Omega T$ denote the locale of $T$. Then: $\map \Omega T$ is a locale

title: Localic Functor is Covariant
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Let $\mathbf{Loc_*}$ denote the category of locales with localic mappings. Then: the localic functor $\mathbf {Lc} : \mathbf{Top} \to \mathbf{Loc_*}$ is a covariant functor

title: Localic Spectrum Functor is Covariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Loc_*}$ denote the category of locales with localic mappings. Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Then: the localic spectrum functor $\operatorname {Sp} : \mathbf{Loc_*} \to \mathbf{Top}$ is a covariant functor

title: Localization Preserves Integral Closure
snippet: Let $A \subseteq B$ be an extension of commutative rings with unity. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. Then $C_S$ is the integral closure of $A_S$ in $B_S$, where subscript $S$ indicates the localization at $S$.

title: Localization of Module Homomorphism is Exact
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. Let $S^{-1}A$ be the localization of $A$ at $S$. Let: $M_1 \stackrel {f_1} \longrightarrow M_2 \stackrel {f_2} \longrightarrow M_3$ be an exact sequence of $A$-modules. For $i=1,2,3$, let $\struct { S^{-1}M_i, \iota_i}$ be the localization of $M_i$ at $S$.

title: Localization of Module Homomorphism is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. Let $S^{-1}A$ be the localization of $A$ at $S$. Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be $A$-homomorphisms: $M_1 \stackrel {f_1} \longrightarrow M_2 \stackrel {f_2} \longrightarrow M_3$ For $i=1,2,3$, let $\struct { S^{-1}M_i, \iota_i}$ be the localization of $M_i$ at $S$.

title: Localization of Ring Exists
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset with $0 \notin S$. Then there exists a localization $\struct {A_S, \iota}$ of $A$ at $S$.

title: Localization of Ring is Unique
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. Let $\struct {A_S, \iota}$ and $\struct {\tilde A_S, \tilde \iota}$ both satisfy the definition of the localization of $A$ at $S$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $\phi: A_S \to \tilde A_S$.

title: Locally Bounded Hausdorff Topological Vector Space with Heine-Borel Property has Finite Dimension
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally bounded Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$ with the Heine-Borel property. Then $X$ is a finite dimensional vector space.

title: Locally Compact Hausdorff Topological Vector Space has Finite Dimension
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$. Then $X$ is a finite dimensional vector space.

title: Locally Compact Space is Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a locally compact topological space. Then $T$ is weakly locally compact.

title: Locally Compact iff Open Neighborhood contains Compact Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then: $T$ is locally compact $\forall U \in \tau, x \in U: \exists K \subseteq S: x \in K^\circ \land K \subseteq U \land K$ is compact where $K^\circ$ denotes the interior of $K$.

title: Locally Connected Separable Topological Space has Countably Many Components
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally connected separable topological space. Let $\CC$ be the set of components of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $\CC$ is countable.

title: Locally Connected Space is not necessarily Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also a connected space.

title: Locally Connected Space is not necessarily Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also an locally path-connected space.

title: Locally Convex Space is Hausdorff iff induces Hausdorff Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \mathcal P}$ be a locally convex space. Let $\tau$ be the standard topology on $\struct {X, \mathcal P}$. Then $\struct {X, \mathcal P}$ is Hausdorff $\struct {X, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff topological space.

title: Locally Convex Space is Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ equipped with the standard topology $\tau$. Then $\struct {X, \tau}$ is a topological vector space.

title: Locally Euclidean Space has Countable Local Basis Homeomorphic to Open Balls
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Let $m \in M$. Then: there exists a countable local basis $\family{U_n}_{n \in \N}$ of $m$ where each $U_n$ is the homeomorphic image of an open ball of $\R^d$

title: Locally Euclidean Space has Countable Neighborhood Basis Homeomorphic to Closed Balls
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Let $m \in M$. Then: there exists a countable neighborhood basis $\family{N_n}_{n \in \N}$ of $m$ where each $N_n$ is the homeomorphic image of a closed ball of $\R^d$

title: Locally Euclidean Space is First-Countable
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Then $M$ is first-countable.

title: Locally Euclidean Space is Locally Compact
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Then $M$ is locally compact.

title: Locally Euclidean Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Then $M$ is locally connected.

title: Locally Euclidean Space is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $M$ be a locally Euclidean space of some dimension $d$. Then $M$ is locally path-connected.

title: Locally Euclidean Subspace of Euclidean Space is Manifold
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an Euclidean space for $n \in \N$. Let $M = \struct{H, \tau_H}$ be a subspace of $\R^n$, where $H \subseteq \R^n$. Let $M$ be locally Euclidean of dimension $d$. Then $M$ is a $d$-manifold.

title: Locally Euclidean iff has C0-Atlas
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad$ $M$ is locally euclidean. $(2): \quad$ There exists a $C^0$-atlas on $M$.

title: Locally Finite Connected Graph is Countable
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a graph which is connected and locally finite. Then $G$ has countably many vertices and countably many edges.

title: Locally Finite Refinement is Point Finite
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a cover of a topological space $T = \struct {S, \tau}$. Let $\UU$ be a locally finite refinement of $\CC$. Then $\UU$ is also a point finite refinement of $\CC$.

title: Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Sigma-Locally Finite Set of Subsets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\AA$ be a locally finite set of subsets. Then: $\AA$ is a $\sigma$-locally finite set of subsets.

title: Locally Injectively Path-Connected Space is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally injectively path-connected. Then $T$ is also locally path-connected.

title: Locally Injectively Path-Connected Space is not necessarily Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally injectively path-connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also injectively path-connected.

title: Locally Integrable (f(x+ct) + f(x-ct))/2 is Weak Solution to Wave Equation
snippet: Consider the wave equation: $\dfrac {\partial^2 u} {\partial t^2} - c^2 \dfrac {\partial^2 u} {\partial x^2} = 0$ with the initial conditions: $\map u {x, 0} = \map f x$ $\map {\dfrac {\partial u} {\partial t}} {x, 0} = 0$ and $c \in \R$. Then it has a weak solution of the form: $\map u {x, t} := \dfrac {\map f {x + ct} + \map f {x - ct}} 2$ where $f \in \map {L^1_{loc} } \R$ is a locally integrable function.

title: Locally Integrable Function defines Distribution
snippet: Let $f \in \map {L^1_{loc}} {\R^d}$ be a locally integrable function. Let $\map \DD {\R^d}$ be the test function space. Let $T_f : \map \DD {\R^d} \to \C$ be a mapping. Then $T_f$ is a Schwartz distribution.

title: Locally Integrable f(x+ct) is Weak Solution to Transport Equation
snippet: Consider the transport equation: $\dfrac {\partial u} {\partial t} - c \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} = 0$ with the initial condition: $\map u {x, 0} = \map f x$ where $c \in \R$. Then it has a weak solution of the form: $\map u {x, t} := \map f {x + ct}$ where $f \in \map {L^1_{loc} } \R$ is a locally integrable function.

title: Locally Path-Connected Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally path-connected. Then $T$ is also locally connected.

title: Locally Path-Connected Space is not necessarily Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally path-connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also a locally injectively path-connected space.

title: Locally Path-Connected Space is not necessarily Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally path-connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also path-connected.

title: Locally Pseudometrizable Space is First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally pseudometrizable. Then $T$ is first-countable.

title: Locker Problem
snippet: == Problem == There is a school with $100$ students, and correspondingly $100$ lockers, all of which start off closed. The first student opens every locker. The second student closes every other locker, starting with the second. The third student changes the state of every third locker, starting with the third. That is, if the locker is open, he or she closes it, and if it is closed, he or she opens it. This continues similarly until all $100$ students have passed along the lockers. After the $100$th student has finished, which lockers are open and which are closed?

title: Locus of Midpoints of Parallel Chords of Central Conic passes through Center
snippet: Let $\KK$ be a central conic. Let $\DD$ be the locus of the midpoints of a system of parallel chords of $\KK$. Then $\DD$ passes through the center of $\KK$.

snippet: == Examples of Log Tables ==

title: Log of Gamma Function is Convex on Positive Reals
snippet: Let $\Gamma: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be the Gamma function, restricted to the strictly positive real numbers. Let $\ln$ denote the natural logarithm function. Then the composite mapping $\ln \circ \operatorname \Gamma$ is a convex function.

title: Logarithm Base 10 of 2 is Irrational
snippet: The common logarithm of $2$: $\log_{10} 2 \approx 0.30102 \, 99956 \, 63981 \, 19521 \, 37389 \ldots$ is irrational.

title: Logarithm Tends to Infinity
snippet: Let $x \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\ln x \to +\infty$ as $x \to +\infty$

title: Logarithm Tends to Negative Infinity
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\ln x \to -\infty$ as $x \to 0^+$

title: Logarithm is Strictly Concave
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\ln x: x > 0$ strictly concave.

title: Logarithm is Strictly Increasing
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $x > 0$. Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$. Then: $\ln x: x > 0$ is strictly increasing.

title: Logarithm of Absolute Value of 2 times Sine of pi x is Replicative Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \log \, \size {2 \sin \pi x}$ Then $f$ is a replicative function.

title: Logarithm of Base
snippet: Let $b \in \R_{>0}$ such that $b \ne 1$. Then: $\log_b b = 1$ where $\log_b$ denotes the logarithm to base $b$.

title: Logarithm of Beta Function is Convex on Positive Reals
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\map \Beta {x, y}$ be the Beta function: $\ds \map \Beta {x, y} := \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} t^{x - 1} \paren {1 - t}^{y - 1} \rd t$ Let $y \in \R_{>0}$ be given. Then $\map \ln {\map \Beta {x, y} }$ is a convex function of $x$ on $\R_{>0}$.

title: Logarithm of Convergent Product of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence of strictly positive real numbers. $(1): \quad$ The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converges to $a \in \R_{\ne 0}$. $(2): \quad$ The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \ln a_n$ converges to $\ln a$.

title: Logarithm of Dirichlet L-Functions
snippet: Let $\chi$ be a Dirichlet character modulo $q$. The Dirichlet series: $\map f s = \ds \sum_{n \mathop \ge 1} \sum_p \frac {\map \chi p^n} {n p^{n s} }$ converges absolutely to an analytic function, where $p$ ranges over the primes. Moreover, $\map f s$ defines a branch of $\ln \map L {s, \chi}$.

title: Logarithm of Divergent Product of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\left\langle{a_n}\right\rangle$ be a sequence of strictly positive real numbers.

title: Logarithm of Factorial
snippet: {{eqn | l = \ln n! | r = \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} a_{k + 1} n^{\underline k} | c = }} {{eqn | r = a_1 n + a_2 n \paren {n - 1} + a_3 n \paren {n - 1} \paren {n - 2} + \cdots | c = }} where: $\ds a_m = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^m} {m!} \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \paren {-1}^k \binom {m - 1} {k - 1} \ln k$

title: Logarithm of Infinite Product of Complex Functions
snippet: Let $X$ be a weakly locally compact topological space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of everywhere nonzero continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \C$. {{item|(1):|The product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop 1}^\infty f_n$ converges locally uniformly to $f$}} {{item|(2):|The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop 1}^\infty \ln f_n$ converges locally uniformly to $\ln f + 2 k \pi i$ for some mapping $k: K\to\Z$}}

title: Logarithm of Infinite Product of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $\sequence {z_n}$ be a sequence of nonzero complex numbers. {{item|(1):|The infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop 1}^\infty z_n$ converges to $z \in \C_{\ne 0}$.}} {{item|(2):|The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop 1}^\infty \log z_n$ converges to $\log z + 2 k \pi i$ for some integer $k \in \Z$.}}

title: Logarithm of Infinite Product of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $(a_n)$ be a sequence of strictly positive real numbers.

title: Logarithm of Logarithm in terms of Natural Logarithms
snippet: Let $b, x \in \R_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive real numbers. Then: $\map {\log_b} {\log_b x} = \dfrac {\map \ln {\ln x} - \map \ln {\ln b} } {\ln b}$ where $\ln x$ denotes the natural logarithm of $x$.

title: Logarithm of One plus x in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac {a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } {c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\map \ln {1 + x} = x \map F {1, 1; 2; -x}$ where $x$ is a real number such that $\size x < 1$/

title: Logarithm of One plus x over One minus x in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $\map \ln {\dfrac {1 + x} {1 - x} } = 2 x \map F {\dfrac 1 2, 1; \dfrac 3 2; x^2}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $\size x < 1$ $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

title: Logarithm of Reciprocal
snippet: Let $x, b \in \R$ be strictly positive real numbers such that $b > 1$. Then: $\map {\log_b} {\dfrac 1 x} = -\log_b x$ where $\log_b$ denotes the logarithm to base $b$.

title: Logarithm on Positive Real Numbers is Group Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\R_{>0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of positive real numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $b$ be any real number such that $b > 1$. Let $\log_b: \struct {\R_{>0}, \times} \to \struct {\R, +}$ be the mapping: $x \mapsto \map {\log_b} x$ where $\log_b$ is the logarithm to base $b$. Then $\log_b$ is a group isomorphism.

title: Logarithm to Own Base equals 1
snippet: Let $b \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number such that $b \ne 1$. Let $\log_b$ denote the logarithm to base $b$. Then: $\log_b b = 1$

title: Logarithmic Approximation of Error Term of Stirling's Formula for Gamma Function
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ with a strictly positive real part and $\size {\arg z} < \dfrac \pi 2$. Then: $\ds \map \Ln {\map \Gamma z} = \paren {z - \dfrac 1 2} \map \Ln z - z + \dfrac {\ln 2 \pi} 2 + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^d \frac {B_{2 n} } {2 n \paren {2 n - 1} z^{2 n - 1} } + \OO \paren {\dfrac 1 {z^{2 d + 1} } }$ where: $\Gamma$ is the gamma function $\Ln$ is the principal branch of the complex logarithm $B_{2 n}$ is the $2 n$th Bernoulli number $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Logarithmic Derivative of Infinite Product of Analytic Functions
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be open. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n: D \to \C$. Let none of the $f_n$ be identically zero on any open subset of $D$. Let the product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge locally uniformly to $f$. Then: $\ds \dfrac {f'} f = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {f_n'} {f_n}$ and the series converges locally uniformly in $D \setminus \set {z \in D : \map f z = 0}$.

title: Logarithmic Derivative of Product of Analytic Functions
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be open. Let $f, g: D \to \C$ be analytic. Let $f g$ be their pointwise product. Let $z \in D$ with $\map f z \ne 0 \ne \map g z$. Then: $\dfrac {\map {\paren {f g}' } z} {\map {\paren {f g} } z} = \dfrac{\map {f'} z} {\map f z} + \dfrac {\map {g'} z} {\map g z}$

title: Logarithmic Derivative of Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function: $\ds \forall s \in \C: \map \Re s > 1: \map \zeta s = \sum_{n \mathop \ge 1} n^{-s}$ Then for all $s \in \C$ with $\map \Re s > 1$: $\ds -\frac {\map {\zeta'} s} {\map \zeta s} = \sum_{n \mathop \ge 1} \map \Lambda n n^{-s}$ where $\Lambda$ is von Mangoldt's function.
