title: Minimal Polynomial of Square Matrix is Divisor of Characteristic Polynomial
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix of order $n$. The minimal polynomial of $\mathbf A$ is a divisor of the characteristic polynomial of $\mathbf A$.

title: Minimal Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Minimal Primes == $881$ is a minimal prime in base $10$ because there is no prime among the proper subsequences of the digits: $8$, $1$, $88$, $81$. The subsequence does not have to consist of consecutive digits. Hence $149$ is not a minimal prime in base $10$, because $19$ is prime. However, by the definition of subsequence, the digits do have to be in the same order. So, for example, $991$ is still a minimal prime in base $10$, even though a subset of the digits can form the shorter prime $19$ by changing the order. Category:Minimal Primes

title: Minimal Ring Generated by System of Sets
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a non-empty system of sets. Then there is a unique ring of sets $\map \RR \SS$ which: $(1): \quad$ contains $\SS$ $(2): \quad$ is contained by every ring of sets which also contains $\SS$. This ring of sets $\map \RR \SS$ is called the minimal ring generated by $\SS$.

title: Minimal Smooth Surface Spanned by Contour
snippet: Let $\map z {x, y}: \R^2 \to \R$ be a real-valued function. Let $\Gamma$ be a closed contour in $3$-dimensional Euclidean space. Then the smooth surface of least area spanned by the contour $\Gamma$ has to satisfy the following Euler's equation: $r \paren {1 + q^2} - 2 s p q + t \paren {1 + p^2} = 0$ where: {{eqn | l = r | r = z_{xx} }} {{eqn | l = s | r = z_{xy} }} {{eqn | l = t | r = z_{yy} }} with subscript denoting respective partial derivatives. In other words, its mean curvature has to vanish.

title: Minimal Smooth Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\map y x$ be a real mapping in 2-dimensional real Euclidean space. Let $y$ pass through the points $\tuple {x_0, y_0}$ and $\tuple {x_1, y_1}$. Consider a surface of revolution constructed by rotating $y$ around the $x$-axis. Suppose this surface is smooth for any $x$ between $x_0$ and $x_1$. Then its surface area is minimized by the following curve, known as a catenoid: $y = C \map \cosh {\dfrac {x + C_1} C}$ Furthermore, its area is: $A = \paren {x_1 - x_0} C \pi + \dfrac {\pi C^2} 2 \paren {\map \sinh {\dfrac {2 \paren {x_1 + C_1} } C} - \map \sinh {\dfrac {2 \paren {x_0 + C_1} } C} }$

title: Minimal Surface/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Minimal Surfaces ==

title: Minimal Surface Bounded by Coaxial Rings is Catenoid
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be coaxial rings of wire between which a minimal surface is stretched. The minimal surface is in the shape of a catenoid.

title: Minimal Uncountable Well-Ordered Set Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\Omega, \Omega'$ be minimal uncountable well-ordered sets. Then $\Omega$ is order isomorphic to $\Omega'$. That is, the minimal uncountable well-ordered set is unique up to order isomorphism.

title: Minimal WRT Restriction
snippet: Let $A$ be a set or class. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $A$. Let $B$ be a subset or subclass of $A$. Let $\RR'$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $B$. Let $m \in B$. Then: $m$ is a strictly minimal element under $\RR$ in $B$ $m$ is a strictly minimal element under $\RR'$ in $B$.

title: Minimally Closed Class under Progressing Mapping
snippet: Statement of Conditions: Then the following results hold:

title: Minimally Closed Class under Progressing Mapping induces Nest
snippet: For all $x, y \in N$: either $\map g x \subseteq y$ or $y \subseteq x$ and $N$ forms a nest: $\forall x, y \in N: x \subseteq y$ or $y \subseteq x$

title: Minimally Closed Class under Progressing Mapping is Well-Ordered
snippet: $N$ is well-ordered under the subset relation.

title: Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping induces Nest
snippet: Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$. Then $M$ is a nest in which: $\forall x, y \in M: \map g x \subseteq y \lor y \subseteq x$

title: Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping is Well-Ordered under Subset Relation
snippet: Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$. Let $x$ be a fixed point of $g$. Then $M$ is well-ordered under the subset relation.

title: Minimally Inductive Class under Progressing Mapping with Fixed Element is Finite
snippet: Let $M$ be a class which is minimally inductive under a progressing mapping $g$. Let there exist an element $x \in M$ such that $x = \map g x$. Then $M$ is a finite class.

title: Minimally Inductive Class under Slowly Progressing Mapping is Nest
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a slowly progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a minimally inductive class under $g$. Then $M$ is a nest.

title: Minimally Inductive Set Exists
snippet: There exists a minimally inductive set $\omega$ that is a subset of every other inductive set.

title: Minimally Inductive Set forms Peano Structure
snippet: Let $\omega$ be the minimally inductive set. Let $\cdot^+: \omega \to \omega$ be the mapping assigning to a set its successor set: $n^+ := n \cup \set n$ Let $\O \in \omega$ be the empty set. Then $\struct {\omega, \cdot^+, \O}$ is a Peano structure.

title: Minimally Inductive Set is Infinite Cardinal
snippet: $\omega$, the minimally inductive set, is an element of the class of infinite cardinals $\NN'$.

title: Minimally Inductive Set is Limit Ordinal
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the minimally inductive set. Then $\omega$ is a limit ordinal.

title: Minimally Inductive Set is Minimal
snippet: The minimally inductive set $\omega$ is a subset of every inductive set.

title: Minimally Inductive Set is Ordinal
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the minimally inductive set. Then $\omega$ is an ordinal.

title: Minimally Inductive Set is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $\omega$ be the minimally inductive set. Then $\omega$ is well-ordered by $\subseteq$.

title: Minimally Superinductive Class is Well-Ordered under Subset Relation
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be minimally superinductive under $g$. Then $M$ is well-ordered under the subset relation.

title: Minimization of Arithmetically Definable Function is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be a partial function. Let $g: \N^k \to \N$ be the partial function defined as: $\map g {x_1, \dotsc, x_k} \approx \map {\mu z} {\map f {x_1, \dotsc, x_k, z} }$ where $\mu$ is minimization. Suppose that there exists a $\Sigma_1$ WFF of $k + 2$ free variables: $\map {\phi_f} {y, x_1, \dotsc, x_k, z}$ such that: $y = \map f {x_1, \dotsc, x_k, z} \iff \N \models \map {\phi_f} {\sqbrk y, \sqbrk {x_1}, \dotsc, \sqbrk {x_k}, \sqbrk z}$ where $\sqbrk a$ denotes the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Minimization on Relation Equivalent to Minimization on Function
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a $k + 1$-ary relation on $\N^{k + 1}$. Then the function $g: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ defined as: $\map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, z} = \mu y \ \map \RR {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y}$ where $\mu y \ \map \RR {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, y}$ is the minimization operation on $\RR$ is equivalent to minimization on a total function.

title: Minimum Area of Triangle whose Vertices are Lattice Points
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle embedded in a cartesian plane. Let the vertices of $T$ be lattice points which are not all on the same straight line. Then the area of $T$ is such that: $\map \Area T \ge \dfrac 1 2$

title: Minimum Connector Problem
snippet: == Problem == Given a weighted graph $G$, the object is to find a minimum spanning tree for $G$.

title: Minimum Degree Bound for Simple Planar Graph
snippet: Let $G$ be a simple connected planar graph. Then: $\map \delta G \le 5$ where $\map \delta G$ denotes the minimum degree of vertices of $G$.

title: Minimum Degree is at Least Connectivity
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a simple graph. Then: $\map \delta G \ge \map \kappa G$ That is, the minimum degree of $G$ is at least its connectivity.

title: Minimum Distance of Linear Code is Smallest Weight of Non-Zero Codeword
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear $\tuple {n, k}$-code whose master code is $\map V {n, p}$. Let $\map d C$ denote the minimum distance of $C$. Then: $\map d C = \ds \min_{u \mathop \in C} \map w u$ where $\map w u$ denotes the weight of $u$.

title: Minimum Function in terms of Absolute Value
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers. Then: $\ds \min \set {x, y} = \frac 1 2 \paren {\paren {x + y} - \size {x - y} }$

title: Minimum Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The minimum function $\min: \N^2 \to \N$, defined as: $\map \min {n, m} = \begin{cases} n: & n \le m \\ m: & m \le n \end{cases}$ is primitive recursive‎.

title: Minimum Rule for Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f, g: S \to \R$ be continuous real-valued functions. Let $\min \set {f, g}: S \to \R$ denote the pointwise minimum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\min \set {f, g}$ is continuous.

title: Minimum Rule for Real Sequences
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be sequences in $\R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be convergent to the following limits: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n = l$ $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} y_n = m$ Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \min \set {x_n, y_n} = \min \set {l, m}$

title: Minimum Value of Real Quadratic Function
snippet: Let $a \in \R_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Consider the quadratic function: $\map Q x = a x^2 + b x + c$ $\map Q x$ achieves a minimum at $x = -\dfrac b {2 a}$, at which point $\map Q x = c - \dfrac {b^2} {4 a}$.

title: Minimum is Less than or Equal to Geometric Mean
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be positive real numbers. Let $p \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\map G {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ denote the geometric mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $\min \set {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map G {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ Equality holds : $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots x_n$ or $x_k = 0$ for some $k \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$.

title: Minimum is Less than or Equal to Hölder Mean
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be positive real numbers. Let $p \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ denote the Hölder mean with exponent $p$ of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $\min \set {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ Equality holds : $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots x_n$ or: $p < 0$ and $x_k = 0$ for some $k \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$.

title: Minimum of Exponential Random Variables has Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $\beta_1, \beta_2, \ldots, \beta_n$ be positive real numbers. Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be independent random variables. For each $i$, let $X_i \sim \Exponential {\beta_i}$, where $\Exponential {\beta_i}$ is the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta_i$. Let: $\ds M = \map {\min_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n} } {X_i} $ Then: $\ds M \sim \Exponential {\paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \frac 1 {\beta_i} }^{-1} }$

title: Minimum of Finitely Many Continuous Real Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number. Let $X \subseteq \R$. Let $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n$ be functions $X \to \R$. Define the function $m : X \to \R$ by: $\ds \map m x = \min_i \map {f_i} x$ for all $x \in X$. Then $m$ is continuous.

title: Minimum of Real Hyperbolic Cosine Function
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then: $\cosh x \ge 1$ where $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function.

title: Minkowski's Inequality for Integrals
snippet: Let $f, g$ be (Darboux) integrable functions. Let $p \in \R$ such that $p > 1$. Then: $\ds \paren {\int_a^b \size {\map f x + \map g x}^p \rd x}^{1/p} \le \paren {\int_a^b \size {\map f x}^p \rd x}^{1 / p} + \paren {\int_a^b \size {\map g x}^p \rd x}^{1 / p}$

title: Minkowski's Inequality for Sums
snippet: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n, b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be non-negative real numbers. Let $p \in \R$, $p \ne 0$ be a real number. If $p 1$, then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {a_k + b_k}^p}^{1/p} \le \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^p}^{1/p} + \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n b_k^p}^{1/p}$ If $p < 1$, $p \ne 0$, then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {a_k + b_k}^p}^{1/p} \ge \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^p}^{1/p} + \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n b_k^p}^{1/p}$

title: Minkowski's Theorem
snippet: Let $L$ be a lattice in $\R^n$. Let $d$ be the covolume of $L$. Let $\mu$ be a translation invariant measure on $\R^n$ Let $S$ be a convex subset of $\R^n$ that is symmetric about the origin: $\forall p \in S : -p \in S$ Let the volume of $S$ be greater than $2^n d$. Then $S$ contains a non-zero point of $L$.

title: Minkowski Functional of Balanced Convex Absorbing Set in Vector Space is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be a set that is balanced, convex and absorbing. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then $\mu_A$ is a seminorm.

title: Minkowski Functional of Convex Absorbing Set is Finite
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be a convex absorbing set. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then for each $x \in X$, $\map {\mu_A} x$ is a finite extended real number. That is: $\forall x \in X: \map {\mu_A} x < \infty$

title: Minkowski Functional of Convex Absorbing Set is Positive Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A$ be a convex absorbing set. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then $\mu_A$ is positive homogeneous. That is, for each $t \ge 0$ we have: $\map {\mu_A} {t x} = t \map {\mu_A} x$

title: Minkowski Functional of Convex Absorbing Set is Sublinear
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Let $A$ be a convex absorbing set. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then for each $x, y \in X$ we have: $\map {\mu_A} {x + y} \le \map {\mu_A} x + \map {\mu_A} y$

title: Minkowski Functional of Convex Absorbing Set is Sublinear Functional
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A$ be a convex absorbing set. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then $\mu_A$ is a sublinear functional.

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Ball with respect to Seminorm is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Let: $B = \set {x \in X : \map p x < 1}$ be the open ball centred at ${\mathbf 0}_X$ with radius $1$ in the pseudometric induced by $p$. Let $\mu_B$ the Minkowski functional of $B$. Then $p = \mu_B$.

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Convex Set containing Zero Vector in Topological Vector Space recovers Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be an open convex set with ${\mathbf 0}_X \in C$. From Convex Subset of Topological Vector Space containing Zero Vector in Interior is Absorbing Set, $C$ is absorbing. Let $\mu_C$ be the Minkowski functional of $C$. Then we have: $C = \set {x \in X : \map {\mu_C} x < 1}$

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Convex Set in Normed Vector Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $C$ be an open convex subset of $X$ with $0 \in C$. Let $p_C$ be the Minkowski functional for $C$. Then there exists a real number $c > 0$ such that: $0 \le \map {p_C} x \le c \norm x$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Convex Set in Normed Vector Space is Sublinear Functional
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\R$. Let $C$ be an open convex subset of $X$ with $0 \in C$. Let $p_C$ be the Minkowski functional for $C$. Then $p_C$ is a sublinear functional.

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Convex Set in Normed Vector Space is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $C$ be an open convex subset of $X$ with $0 \in C$. Then, for each $x \in X$: $\set {t > 0 : t^{-1} x \in C} \ne \O$ and so the Minkowski functional of $C$ is well-defined.

title: Minkowski Functional of Open Convex Set in Normed Vector Space recovers Set
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $C$ be an open convex subset of $X$ with $0 \in C$. Let $p_C$ be the Minkowski functional for $C$. Then: $C = \set {x \in X : \map {p_C} x < 1}$

title: Minkowski Functional of Symmetric Convex Absorbing Set in Real Vector Space is Seminorm
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be a set that is symmetric, convex and absorbing. Let $\mu_A$ be the Minkowski functional of $A$. Then $\mu_A$ is a seminorm.

title: Minor Axis of Ellipse is Axis of Symmetry
snippet: Let $K$ be an ellipse. The minor axis of $K$ is an axis of bilateral symmetry of $K$.

title: Minor Axis of Ellipsoid is Axis of Symmetry
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid. The minor axis of $\EE$ is an axis of symmetry of $\EE$.

title: Minus One is Less than Zero
snippet: == Theorem == $-1 < 0$

title: Mittag-Leffler's Expansion Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a meromorphic function that: has only simple poles is continuous, or has a removable singularity, at $0$. Let $X$ be the set of poles of $f$. For $N \in \N$, let $C_N$ be a disk, centred at the origin, of radius $R_N$ where: $R_N \to \infty$ as $N \to \infty$ $\partial C_N$ contains no poles of $f$ for any $N$. there exists a real number $M > 0$ independent of $N$ such that for all $z \in \partial C_N$, $\cmod {\map f z} < M$ , for all $N \in \N$.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Cosecant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \cosec \pi z = \frac 1 z + 2\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {-1}^n \frac z {z^2 - n^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not an integer $\cosec$ is the cosecant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Cotangent Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \cot \pi z = \frac 1 z + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac z {z^2 - n^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not an integer $\cot$ is the cotangent function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Hyperbolic Cosecant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \csch {\pi z} = \frac 1 z + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {-1}^n \frac z {z^2 + n^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not an integer multiple of $i$ $\csch$ is the hyperbolic cosecant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Hyperbolic Cotangent Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \coth {\pi z} = \frac 1 z + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac z {z^2 + n^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not an integer multiple of $i$ $\coth$ is the hyperbolic cotangent function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Hyperbolic Secant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \sech {\pi z} = 4 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {-1}^n \frac {2 n + 1} {\paren {2 n + 1}^2 + 4 z^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not a half-integer multiple of $i$ $\sech$ is the hyperbolic secant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Hyperbolic Tangent Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \tanh {\pi z} = 8 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac z {4 z^2 + \paren {2 n + 1}^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not a half-integer multiple of $i$ $\tanh$ is the hyperbolic tangent function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Real Cotangent Function
snippet: Let $\alpha \in \R$ be a real number which is specifically not an integer. Then: $\ds \dfrac 1 \alpha + \sum_{n \mathop \ge 1} \dfrac {2 \alpha} {\alpha^2 - n^2} = \pi \cot \pi \alpha$

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Secant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \sec {\pi z} = 4 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {-1}^n \frac {2 n + 1} {\paren {2 n + 1}^2 - 4 z^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not a half-integer $\sec$ is the secant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Square of Cosecant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi^2 \map {\csc^2} {\pi z} = \frac 1 {z^2} + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {z^2 + n^2} {\paren {z^2 - n^2}^2}$ where: $z$ is a complex number that is not a integer $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Square of Secant Function
snippet: $\ds \pi^2 \map {\sec^2} {\pi z} = 8 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {2 n + 1} + 4 z^2} {\paren {\paren {2 n + 1}^2 - 4 z^2}^2}$ where: $z$ is a complex number that is not a half-integer $\sec$ denotes the secant function.

title: Mittag-Leffler Expansion for Tangent Function
snippet: $\ds \pi \map \tan {\pi z} = 8 \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac z {\paren {2 n + 1}^2 - 4 z^2}$ where: $z \in \C$ is not a half-integer $\tan$ is the tangent function.

title: Mixed Partial Derivative of Heaviside Step Function
snippet: Let $\tuple {x, y} \stackrel u {\longrightarrow} \map u {x, y}: \R^2 \to \R$ be the Heaviside step function. Let $u := T_u$ be the Schwartz distribution associated with $u$. Let $\delta_{\tuple {0, 0} } \in \map {\DD'} {\R^2}$ be the Dirac delta distribution. Then in the distributional sense: $\dfrac {\partial^2 u} {\partial x \partial y} = \delta_{\tuple {0, 0}}$

title: Modal Logic is Intensional
snippet: Modal logic is intensional, in the sense that: the truth value of a WFF $\AA$ does not determine the truth value of $\map \nec \AA$.

title: Mode of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a real number. Let $\sigma$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ where $\Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ is the normal distribution with parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$. Then the mode $M$ of $X$ is equal to $\mu$.

title: Model for Air Resistance under Laminar Flow
snippet: Let $B$ be a body passing through air such that the flow is laminar. Then the scenario can be modeled by assuming that the magnitude of the air resistance is proportional to the speed of $B$ through the air.

title: Model for Air Resistance under Turbulent Motion
snippet: Let $B$ be a body passing through air such that the motion of the air is turbulent. Then the scenario can be modeled by assuming that the magnitude of the air resistance is proportional to the square of the speed of $B$ through the air.

title: Model of Root of Propositional Tableau is Model of Branch
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \mathbf H, \Phi}$ be a propositional tableau. Let $v: \LL_0 \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a boolean interpretation such that: $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \mathbf H$ that is, such that $v$ is a model for the root $\mathbf H$ of $T$. Then there exists a branch $\Gamma$ of $T$ such that: $v \models_{\mathrm{BI}} \Phi \sqbrk \Gamma$ where $\Phi \sqbrk \Gamma$ denotes the image of $\Gamma$ under $\Phi$.

title: Models for Propositional Logic
snippet: This page gathers together some useful results that can be used in the derivation of proofs by propositional tableau. Let $\MM$ be a model for propositional logic, and let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be WFFs of propositional logic. Then the following results hold. The symbol $\models$ is used throughout to denote semantic consequence.

title: Modified Fort Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Then $T$ is a compact space.

title: Modified Fort Space is Scattered
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{a, b} }$ be a modified Fort space. Then $T$ is scattered.

title: Modified Fort Space is Sequentially Compact

title: Modulo Addition/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Modulo Addition == The additive group of integers modulo $m$ can be described by showing its Cayley table.

title: Modulo Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Modulo Addition ==

title: Modulo Addition has Identity
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then addition modulo $m$ has an identity: $\forall \eqclass x m \in \Z_m: \eqclass x m +_m \eqclass 0 m = \eqclass x m = \eqclass 0 m +_m \eqclass x m$ That is: $\forall a \in \Z: a + 0 \equiv a \equiv 0 + a \pmod m$

title: Modulo Addition has Inverses
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then addition modulo $m$ has inverses: For each element $\eqclass x m \in \Z_m$, there exists the element $\eqclass {-x} m \in \Z_m$ with the property: $\eqclass x m +_m \eqclass {-x} m = \eqclass 0 m = \eqclass {-x} m +_m \eqclass x m$ where $\Z_m$ is the set of integers modulo $m$. That is: $\forall a \in \Z: a + \paren {-a} \equiv 0 \equiv \paren {-a} + a \pmod m$

title: Modulo Addition is Associative
snippet: Addition modulo $m$ is associative: $\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m, \eqclass z m \in \Z_m: \paren {\eqclass x m +_m \eqclass y m} +_m \eqclass z m = \eqclass x m +_m \paren {\eqclass y m +_m \eqclass z m}$ where $\Z_m$ is the set of integers modulo $m$. That is: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: \paren {x + y} + z \equiv x + \paren {y + z} \pmod m$

title: Modulo Addition is Commutative
snippet: Modulo addition is commutative: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x + y \pmod m = y + x \pmod m$

title: Modulo Addition is Linear
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{> 0}$. Let $x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2, c_1, c_2 \in \Z$. Let: $x_1 \equiv y_1 \pmod m$ $x_2 \equiv y_2 \pmod m$ Then: $c_1 x_1 + c_2 x_2 \equiv c_1 y_1 + c_2 y_2 \pmod m$

title: Modulo Addition is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$. Let $\eqclass a m$ denote the equivalence class on $\Z_m$, for some $a \in \Z$. The modulo addition operation on $\Z_m$, defined by the rule: $\eqclass a m +_m \eqclass b m = \eqclass {a + b} m$ is a well-defined operation. That is: If $a \equiv b \pmod m$ and $x \equiv y \pmod m$, then $a + x \equiv b + y \pmod m$.

title: Modulo Division is not generally Well-Defined
snippet: The operation of division modulo $m$ operation on $\Z_m$, the set of integers modulo $m$, defined by the rule: $a \div_m b$ equals the integer $q \in \Z_m$ such that $b \times_m q \equiv a \pmod m$ is not in general a well-defined operation. That is: If $a \equiv b \pmod m$ and $x \equiv y \pmod m$, then it is not always the case that $a \div_m x \equiv b \div_m y \pmod m$.

title: Modulo Multiplication/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Modulo Multiplication == The multiplicative monoid of integers modulo $m$ can be described by showing its Cayley table.

title: Modulo Multiplication/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Modulo Multiplication ==

title: Modulo Multiplication Distributes over Modulo Addition
snippet: Multiplication modulo $m$ is distributive over addition modulo $m$: $\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m, \eqclass z m \in \Z_m$: $\eqclass x m \times_m \paren {\eqclass y m +_m \eqclass z m} = \paren {\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m} +_m \paren {\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass z m}$ $\paren {\eqclass x m +_m \eqclass y m} \times_m \eqclass z m = \paren {\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass z m} +_m \paren {\eqclass y m \times_m \eqclass z m}$ where $\Z_m$ is the set of integers modulo $m$.

title: Modulo Multiplication has Identity
snippet: Multiplication modulo $m$ has an identity: $\forall \eqclass x m \in \Z_m: \eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass 1 m = \eqclass x m = \eqclass 1 m \times_m \eqclass x m$

title: Modulo Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Multiplication modulo $m$ is associative: $\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m, \eqclass z m \in \Z_m: \paren {\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m} \times_m \eqclass z m = \eqclass x m \times_m \paren {\eqclass y m \times_m \eqclass z m}$ That is: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z_m: \paren {x \cdot_m y} \cdot_m z = x \cdot_m \paren {y \cdot_m z}$

title: Modulo Multiplication is Closed
snippet: Multiplication modulo $m$ is closed on the set of integers modulo $m$: $\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m \in \Z_m: \eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m \in \Z_m$.

title: Modulo Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: Multiplication modulo $m$ is commutative: $\forall \eqclass x m, \eqclass y m \in \Z_m: \eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m = \eqclass y m \times_m \eqclass x m$

title: Modulo Multiplication is Well-Defined
snippet: The multiplication modulo $m$ operation on $\Z_m$, the set of integers modulo $m$, defined by the rule: $\eqclass x m \times_m \eqclass y m = \eqclass {x y} m$ is a well-defined operation. That is: If $a \equiv b \pmod m$ and $x \equiv y \pmod m$, then $a x \equiv b y \pmod m$.

title: Modulo Multiplication on Reduced Residue System is Cancellable
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Z'_m$ be the reduced residue system modulo $m$: $\Z'_m = \set {\eqclass k m \in \Z_m: k \perp m}$ Let $S = \struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of $\Z'_m$ under modulo multiplication. Then $\times_m$ is cancellable, in the sense that: $\forall a, b, c \in \Z'_m: a \times_m c = b \times_m c \implies a = b$ and: $\forall a, b, c \in \Z'_m: c \times_m a = c \times_m b \implies a = b$

title: Modulo Multiplication on Reduced Residue System is Closed
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Z'_m$ be the reduced residue system modulo $m$: $\Z'_m = \set {\eqclass k m \in \Z_m: k \perp m}$ Let $S = \struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of $\Z'_m$ under the modulo multiplication. Then $S$ is closed, in the sense that: $\forall a, b \in \Z'_m: a \times_m b \in \Z'_m$

title: Modulo Subtraction is Well-Defined

title: Modulus and Argument of Complex Exponential
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\hointr a {a + 2 \pi}$ be a half open interval of length $2 \pi$. Let $r \in \hointr 0 {+\infty}$ and $\theta \in \hointr a {a + 2 \pi}$. Then: $r = \cmod z$ and $\theta = \map \arg z$ $z = r e^{i \theta}$ where: $\cmod z$ denotes the modulus of $z$ $\map \arg z$ denotes the argument of $z$ $x \mapsto e^x$ is the complex exponential function. If $z = 0$ or $r = 0$, then $\theta$ may be any number in $\hointr a {a + 2 \pi}$.

title: Modulus in Terms of Conjugate
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Let $\overline z$ be the conjugate of $z$. Then: $\cmod z = \sqrt {z \overline z}$

title: Modulus of Complex Root of Unity equals 1

title: Modulus of Exponential is Exponential of Real Part
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\exp z$ denote the complex exponential function. Let $\cmod {\, \cdot \,}$ denote the complex modulus Then: $\cmod {\exp z} = \map \exp {\map \Re z}$ where $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$.

title: Modulus of Exponential of Imaginary Number is One
snippet: Let $\cmod z$ denote the modulus of a complex number $z$. Let $e^z$ be the complex exponential of $z$. Let $x$ be wholly real. Then: $\cmod {e^{i x} } = 1$

title: Modulus of Exponential of i z where z is on Circle
snippet: Let $C$ be the circle embedded in the complex plane given by the equation: $z = R e^{i \theta}$ Then: $\cmod {e^{i z} } = e^{-R \sin \theta}$

title: Modulus of Gamma Function of Imaginary Number
snippet: Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\cmod {\map \Gamma {i t} } = \sqrt {\dfrac {\pi \csch \pi t} t}$ where: $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function $\csch$ is the hyperbolic cosecant function.

title: Modulus of Gamma Function of One Half plus Imaginary Number
snippet: Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\cmod {\map \Gamma {\dfrac 1 2 + i t} } = \sqrt {\pi \map \sech {\pi t} }$ where: $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function $\sech$ is the hyperbolic secant function.

title: Modulus of Limit
snippet: Let $X$ be one of the standard number fields $\Q, \R, \C$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be convergent to the limit $l$. That is, let $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n = l$. Then $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \cmod {x_n} = \cmod l$ where $\cmod {x_n}$ is the modulus of $x_n$.

title: Modulus of Linear Functional on Vector Space is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $f : X \to \GF$ be a linear functional. Define $p_f : X \to \R_{\ge 0}$ by: $\map {p_f} x = \cmod {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Then $p_f$ is a seminorm.

title: Modulus of Positive Real Number to Complex Power is Positive Real Number to Power of Real Part
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $t > 0$ be wholly real. Let $t^z$ be $t$ to the power of $z$ defined on its principal branch. Then: $\cmod {t^z} = t^{\map \Re z}$

title: Modulus of Sine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number, where $x, y \in \R$. Let $\sin z$ denote the complex sine function. Then: $\cmod {\sin z} = \sqrt {\sin^2 x + \sinh^2 y}$ where: $\cmod z$ denotes the modulus of a complex number $z$ $\sin x$ denotes the real sine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function.

title: Modulus of Sine of x Less Than or Equal To Absolute Value of x
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then: $\size {\sin x} \le \size x$

title: Modulus of Sum equals Modulus of Distance implies Quotient is Imaginary
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers such that: $\cmod {z_1 + z_2} = \cmod {z_1 - z_2}$ Then $\dfrac {z_2} {z_1}$ is wholly imaginary.

title: Modulus z - 1 Less than Modulus z + 1 iff Real z Greater than Zero
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\cmod {z - 1} 0$

title: Modus Ponendo Ponens
snippet: == Proof Rule == Modus ponendo ponens is a valid argument in types of logic dealing with conditionals $\implies$. This includes propositional logic and predicate logic, and in particular natural deduction.

title: Modus Ponendo Ponens for Semantic Consequence in Predicate Logic
snippet: Let $\mathrm{PL}$ be the formal semantics of structures for predicate logic. Denote with $\models_{\mathrm{PL}}$ $\mathrm{PL}$-semantic consequence. Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be sentences. Let $\FF$ be a set of sentences. Suppose that: $\FF \models_{\mathrm{PL}} \mathbf A$ $\FF \models_{\mathrm{PL}} \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B$ Then: $\FF \models_{\mathrm{PL}} \mathbf B$ establishing Modus Ponendo Ponens in $\mathrm{PL}$.

title: Mollweide's Projection is Equiareal

title: Moment Generating Function Uniquely Characterizes Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. The probability distribution of $X$ is uniquely characterized by the moment generating function of $X$.

title: Moment Generating Function of Bernoulli Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $p$ for some $0 \le p \le 1$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = q + p e^t$ where $q = 1 - p$.

title: Moment Generating Function of Beta Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \BetaDist \alpha \beta$ denote the Beta distribution fior some $\alpha, \beta > 0$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\ds \map {M_X} t = 1 + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\prod_{r \mathop = 0}^{k - 1} \frac {\alpha + r} {\alpha + \beta + r} } \frac {t^k} {k!}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$ for some $n \in \N$ and $0 \le p \le 1$: $X \sim \Binomial n p$ Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \paren {1 - p + p e^t}^n$

title: Moment Generating Function of Chi-Squared Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim \chi^2_n$ where $\chi^2_n$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then the moment generating function of $X$, $M_X$, is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \begin{cases} \paren {1 - 2 t}^{-n / 2} & : t < \dfrac 1 2 \\ \text{does not exist} & : t \ge \dfrac 1 2 \end{cases}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Continuous Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \ContinuousUniform a b$ for some $a, b \in \R$ denote the continuous uniform distribution on the interval $\closedint a b$. Then the moment generating function of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \begin {cases} \dfrac {e^{t b} - e^{t a} } {t \paren {b - a} } & t \ne 0 \\ 1 & t = 0 \end{cases}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Discrete Uniform Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a discrete uniform distribution with parameter $n$ for some $n \in \N$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \dfrac {e^t \paren {1 - e^{n t} } } {n \paren {1 - e^t} }$

title: Moment Generating Function of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with an exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$ for some $\beta \in \R_{> 0}$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \dfrac 1 {1 - \beta t}$ for $t < \dfrac 1 \beta$, and is undefined otherwise.

title: Moment Generating Function of Gamma Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \map \Gamma {\alpha, \beta}$ for some $\alpha, \beta > 0$, where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma distribution. Then the moment generating function of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \begin {cases} \paren {1 - \dfrac t \beta}^{-\alpha} & t < \beta \\ \text {does not exist} & t \ge \beta \end {cases}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Geometric Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a geometric distribution with parameter $p$ for some $0 < p < 1$.

title: Moment Generating Function of Linear Combination of Independent Random Variables
snippet: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be independent random variables. Let $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_n$ be real numbers. Let: $\ds X = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n k_i X_i$ Let $M_{X_i}$ be the moment generating function of $X_i$ for $1 \le i \le n$. Then: $\ds \map {M_X} t = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map {M_{X_i}} {k_i t}$ for all $t$ such that $M_{X_i}$ exists for all $1 \le i \le n$.

title: Moment Generating Function of Linear Transformation of Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be real numbers. Let $Z = \alpha X + \beta$. Let $M_X$ be the moment generating function of $X$. Then the moment generating function of $Z$, $M_Z$, is given by: $\map {M_Z} t = e^{\beta t} \map {M_X} {\alpha t}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Logistic Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable which satisfies the logistic distribution: $X \sim \map {\operatorname {Logistic} } {\mu, s}$ for some $\mu \in \R, s \in \R_{> 0}$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \begin {cases} \map \exp {\mu t} \map \Beta {\paren {1 - s t}, \paren {1 + s t} } & \size t < \dfrac 1 s \\ \text {does not exist} & \size t \ge \dfrac 1 s \end {cases}$ where $\Beta$ denotes the beta function

title: Moment Generating Function of Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ for some $\mu \in \R, \sigma \in \R_{> 0}$, where $N$ is the normal distribution. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \map \exp {\mu t + \dfrac 1 2 \sigma^2 t^2}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Pareto Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with a Pareto distribution with parameters a and b for $a, b \in \R_{> 0}$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = \begin {cases} a \paren {-b t}^a \map \Gamma {-a, -b t} & t 0 \end {cases}$

title: Moment Generating Function of Poisson Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with a Poisson distribution with parameter $\lambda$ for some $\lambda \in \R_{> 0}$. Then the moment generating function $M_X$ of $X$ is given by: $\map {M_X} t = e^{\lambda \paren {e^t - 1} }$

title: Moment in terms of Moment Generating Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $M_X$ be the moment generating function of $X$. Then: $\expect {X^n} = \map { {M_X}^{\paren n} } 0$ where: $n$ is a non-negative integer ${M_X}^{\paren n}$ denotes the $n$th derivative of $M_X$ $\expect {X^n}$ denotes the expectation of $X^n$.

title: Moment of Couple is Invariant over Plane of Forces
snippet: A couple has the same moment about any arbitrary point in the plane of the two forces that compose it.

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Circular Lamina about Diameter
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a circle whose radius is $a$. Let $\DD$ be the straight line through a diameter of $\DD$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M a^2} 4$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Circular Lamina through Midpoint about Perpendicular Axis
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a circle whose radius is $a$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through the centroid of $\LL$ perpendicular to $\LL$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M a^2} 2$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Cylindrical Shell about Axis
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a uniform lamina in the shape of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder whose mass is $M$ and whose radius is $r$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through the axis of $\CC$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\CC$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = M r^2$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Ellipsoid about Axis of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be a solid ellipsoid of uniform density of mass $M$ whose axes are of length $2 a$, $2 b$ and $2 c$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coinciding with the axis of $\EE$ of length $2 c$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\EE$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M \paren {a^2 + b^2} } 5$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Ellipsoidal Shell about Axis of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of the surface of an ellipsoid whose axes are of length $2 a$, $2 b$ and $2 c$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coincident with the axis of $\EE$ of length $2 c$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\SS$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M \paren {a^2 + b^2} } 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Elliptical Lamina about Axis of Ellipse
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a ellipse whose axes are of length $2 a$ and $2 b$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coinciding with the axis of $\LL$ of length $2 a$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M b^2} 4$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Elliptical Lamina through Midpoint about Perpendicular Axis
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a ellipse whose axes are of length $2 a$ and $2 b$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through the centroid of $\LL$ perpendicular to $\LL$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M \paren {a^2 + b^2} } 4$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Hoop about Axis
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a hoop of uniform density of radius $r$ and mass $M$. Let $\AA$ be the axis of $\HH$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\HH$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = M r^2$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Hoop about Diameter
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a hoop of uniform density of radius $r$ and mass $M$. Let $\DD$ be a straight line through a diameter of $\HH$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\HH$ about $\DD$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M r^2} 2$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Rectangular Lamina about Axis in Plane Bisecting Lamina
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a rectangle whose sides are of length $2 a$ and $2 b$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line: through the centroid of $\LL$ in the plane of $\LL$ perpendicular to the side of $\LL$ of length $2 a$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M a^2} 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Rectangular Lamina about Edge
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a rectangle whose sides are of length $2 a$ and $2 b$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line passing through the side of $\LL$ of length $2 b$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {4 M a^2} 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Rectangular Lamina through Midpoint about Perpendicular Axis
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of a rectangle whose sides are of length $2 a$ and $2 b$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through the centroid of $\LL$ perpendicular to $\LL$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\LL$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M \paren {a^2 + b^2} } 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Rod through Endpoint
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a uniform rod of length $2 a$ and mass $M$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through one of the endpoints of $\RR$ perpendicular to $\RR$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\RR$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {4 M a^2} 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Rod through Midpoint
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a uniform rod of length $2 a$ and mass $M$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line through the midpoint of $\RR$ perpendicular to $\RR$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\RR$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M a^2} 3$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Solid Cylinder about Axis
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a (right circular) cylinder of uniform density of mass $M$ whose radius is $r$. Let $\AA$ be the axis of $\CC$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\CC$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {M r^2} 2$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Solid Right Circular Cone about Axis
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a solid right circular cone of uniform density of mass $M$ whose base is of radius $a$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coinciding with the axis of $\CC$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\CC$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {3 M a^2 } {10}$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Solid Sphere about Diameter
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a solid sphere of uniform density of mass $M$ and radius $a$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coincident with an arbitrary diameter of $\SS$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\SS$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {2 M a^2} 5$

title: Moment of Inertia of Uniform Spherical Shell about Diameter
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a uniform lamina of mass $M$ in the shape of the surface of a sphere of radius $a$. Let $\AA$ be the straight line coincident with an arbitrary diameter of $\SS$. Then the moment of inertia $\II$ of $\SS$ about $\AA$ is given by: $\II = \dfrac {2 M a^2} 3$

title: Moment of Sum of Couples is Vector Sum of Moments
snippet: Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be couple. The sum of $C_1$ and $C_2$ is a third couple whose moment is the sum of the moments of $C_1$ and $C_2$.

title: Monochromatic Electromagnetic Plane Wave satisfies Maxwell's Equations
snippet: Let $W$ be a monochromatic electromagnetic plane wave. Then $W$ satisfies Maxwell's Equations in a vacuum.

title: Monochromatic Electromagnetic Plane Wave satisfies Wave Equation
snippet: Let $W$ be a monochromatic electromagnetic plane wave. Then $W$ satisfies the wave equation.

title: Monoid/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Monoids ==

title: Monoid Category is Category
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid with identity $e_S$. Let $\mathbf S$ be the associated monoid category. Then $\mathbf S$ is a category.

title: Monoid Ring of Commutative Monoid over Commutative Ring is Commutative
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $G$ be a commutative monoid. Let $\sqbrk R G$ be the monoid ring of $G$ over $R$. Then $\sqbrk R G$ is commutative.

title: Monoid is not Empty
snippet: A monoid cannot be empty.

title: Monoid of Self-Inverse Elements is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid such that: $\forall x \in S: x \circ x = e$ where $e$ is the identity element of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an abelian group.

title: Monomials form Basis of Polynomial Ring
Monomials of Polynomial Ring are Linearly Independent
Monomorphism Image is Isomorphic to Domain
snippet: The image of a monomorphism is isomorphic to its domain. That is, if $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ is a monomorphism, then: $\phi: S_1 \to \Img \phi$ is an isomorphism.

title: Monomorphism from Rational Numbers to Totally Ordered Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \circ, \le}$ be a totally ordered field. There is one and only one (ring) monomorphism from the totally ordered field $\Q$ onto $F$. Its image is the prime subfield of $F$.

title: Monomorphism from Total Ordering
snippet: Let the following conditions hold: $(1): \quad$ Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered semigroups. $(2): \quad$ Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping. $(3): \quad$ Let $\preceq$ be a total ordering on $S$. Then $\phi \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} \to \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ is a (structure) monomorphism : $(1): \quad \phi$ is strictly increasing from $\struct {S, \preceq}$ into $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ $(2): \quad \phi$ is a homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, *}$.

title: Monomorphism iff Epimorphism in Dual Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$ be the dual category of $\mathbf C$. Let $f$ be a morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf C$ $f^{\operatorname{op}}$ is an epimorphism in $\mathbf C^{\operatorname{op}}$.

title: Monomorphism in Isomorphic Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be an isomorphism of categories. Let $f$ be a morphism of $\mathbf C$. Then $f$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf C$ $Ff$ is a monomorphism in $\mathbf D$.

title: Monomorphism that is Split Epimorphism is Split Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be a morphism in $\mathbf C$ such that $f$ is a monomorphism and a split epimorphism. Then $f: C \to D$ is a split monomorphism.

title: Monotone Additive Function is Linear
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a monotone real function which is additive, that is: $\forall x, y \in \R: \map f {x + y} = \map f x + \map f y$ Then: $\exists a \in \R: \forall x \in \R: \map f x = a x$ That is, $f$ is a linear function.

title: Monotone Convergence Theorem (Measure Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $u : X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\sequence {u_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be an sequence of positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions $u_n : X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ such that: $\map {u_i} x \le \map {u_j} x$ for all $i \le j$ and: $\ds \map u x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {u_n} x$ hold for $\mu$-almost all $x \in X$. Then: $\ds \int u \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int u_n \rd \mu$

title: Monotone Convergence Theorem (Real Analysis)
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a bounded monotone sequence sequence in $\R$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is convergent.

title: Monotone Convergence Theorem for Positive Simple Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \R$ be a positive simple function. Let $\EE^+$ be the space of positive simple functions. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a positive simple function, such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n = f$ and: for each $x \in X$, the sequence $\sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing where $\lim$ denotes a pointwise limit. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the integral signs denote $\mu$-integration.

title: Monotone Function is of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a monotone function. Then $f$ is of bounded variation.

title: Monotone Real Function is Darboux Integrable
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval, where $a < b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a monotone real function. Then $f$ is Darboux integrable over $\closedint a b$.

title: Monotone Real Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open interval. Let $\map \BB I$ and $\map \BB \R$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebras of $I$ and $\R$ respectively. Let $F : \R \to \R$ be a monotone function. Then $F$ is $\map \BB I/\map \BB \R$-measurable.

title: Monotone Real Function with Everywhere Dense Image is Continuous
snippet: Let $I$ and $J$ be real intervals. Let $f: I \to J$ be a monotone real function. Let $f \sqbrk I$ be everywhere dense in $J$, where $f \sqbrk I$ denotes the image of $I$ under $f$. Then $f$ is continuous on $I$.

title: Monotonic Sequence Characterization of Left Limit of Function
snippet: Let $\hointl a b$ be a real interval. Let $x \in \hointl a b$. Let $f : \hointl a b \to \R$ be a real function. Let $L \in \R$. Then: $\ds \lim_{y \mathop \to x^-} \map f y = L$ for all monotone sequences $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, with $x_n < x$ for each $n$, that converge to $x$ we have: $\map f {x_n} \to L$

title: Monotonic Sequential Right-Continuity is Equivalent to Right-Continuity in the Reals
snippet: Let $\hointr a b$ be a real interval. Let $x \in \hointr a b$. Let $f : \hointr a b \to \R$ be a real function. Then $f$ is right-continuous at $x$ : for all monotone sequences $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, with $x_n > x$ for each $n$, that converge to $x$ we have: $\map f {x_n} \to \map f x$

snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces. Let $S$ be a subspace of $X$. Let $c$ be a limit point of $S$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n : X \to Y$. Suppose that: $(1): \quad \sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on $S$ $(2): \quad \ds \forall n \in \N : \lim_{x \mathop \to c} \map {f_n} x$ exists Then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to c} \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \lim_{x \mathop \to c} \map {f_n} x$ {{questionable|The may diverge, since $\lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} x $ is not assumed to converge for $x \not \in S$.

title: Mordell's Theorem
snippet: Let $C$ be an elliptic curve over $\Q$. Then the group of rational points on $C$ is a finitely generated abelian group.

title: More than One Right Zero then No Left Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. If $\struct {S, \circ}$ has more than one left zero, then it has no right zero. Likewise, if $\struct {S, \circ}$ has more than one right zero, then it has no left zero.

title: More than one Left Identity then no Right Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. If $\struct {S, \circ}$ has more than one left identity, then it has no right identity.

title: More than one Right Identity then no Left Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. If $\struct {S, \circ}$ has more than one right identity, then it has no left identity.

title: Morera's Theorem
snippet: Let $D$ be a simply connected domain in $\C$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a continuous function. Let $f$ be such that: $\ds \int_\gamma \map f z \rd z = 0$ for every simple closed contour $\gamma$ in $D$ Then $f$ is analytic on $D$.

title: Morley's Formula

title: Morley's Trisector Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let the internal angles of $\triangle ABC$ be trisected. Let the points where these angle trisectors first intersect be $D$, $E$ and $F$. 500px Then $\triangle EDF$ is equilateral.

title: Morphism Category is Isomorphic to Comma Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ denote the identity functor on $\mathbf C$. Let $\mathbf C^\to$ denote the morphism category on $\mathbf C$. Let $\paren{\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C} \downarrow \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}}$ denote the comma category $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$ over $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}$.

title: Morphism Class Equivalence is Equivalence
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\map {\mathbf {Sub}_{\mathbf C} } C$ be the category of subobjects of $C$. Let $\sim$ denote morphism class equivalence on the morphisms of $\map {\mathbf {Sub}_{\mathbf C} } C$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence.

title: Morphism Property Preserves Cancellability
snippet: Let: $\phi: \struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {T, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ be a mapping from one algebraic structure: $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ to another: $\struct {T, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ Let $\circ_k$ have the morphism property under $\phi$ for some operation $\circ_k$ in $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$. Then if an element $a \in S$ is either left cancellable or right cancellable under $\circ_k$, then $\map \phi a$ is correspondingly left cancellable or right cancellable under $*_k$.

title: Morphism Property Preserves Closure
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n} \to \struct {T, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$ be a mapping from one algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$ to another $\struct {T, *_1, *_2, \ldots, *_n}$. Let $\circ_k$ have the morphism property under $\phi$ for some operation $\circ_k$ in $\struct {S, \circ_1, \circ_2, \ldots, \circ_n}$.

title: Morphism from Integers to Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$. Let $\phi: \Z \to G$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall n \in \Z: \map \phi n = g^n$. Then: If $g$ has infinite order, then $\phi$ is a group isomorphism from $\struct {\Z, +}$ to $\gen g$. If $g$ has finite order such that $\order g = m$, then $\phi$ is a group epimorphism from $\struct {\Z, +}$ to $\gen g$ whose kernel is the principal ideal $\paren m$. Thus $\gen g$ is isomorphic to $\struct {\Z, +}$, and $m$ is the smallest (strictly) positive integer such that $g^m = e$.

Morphism from Ring with Unity to Module
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Then for every $m \in M$ there exists a unique $R$-module morphism: $\psi: R \to M$ that sends $1$ to $m$.

title: Morphism in Preorder Category is Epic
snippet: Let $\mathbf P$ be a preorder category. Let $f \in \mathbf P_1$ be a morphism. Then $f$ is epic.

title: Morphism in Preorder Category is Monic
snippet: Let $\mathbf P$ be a preorder category. Let $f \in \mathbf P_1$ be a morphism. Then $f$ is monic.

title: Morphism of Counit of Adjunction is Universal
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Let $\xi: FG \to \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf C}$ be the counit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ Then: for each object $C$ in $\mathbf C$ the morphism $\xi_C$ is a universal morphism from $F$ to $GC$

title: Morphism of Unit of Adjunction is Universal
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Let $\eta: \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D} \to GF$ be the unit of adjunction $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ Then: for each object $D$ in $\mathbf D$ the morphism $\eta_D$ is a universal morphism from $FD$ to $G$

title: Morphisms-Only Metacategory Induces Metacategory

Then $\mathbf C$ induces a metacategory $\mathbf C'$, as follows (phrased to fit with Characterization of Metacategory via Equations): Define $\mathbf C'_1$ to be the collection $\mathbf C_1$ of morphisms of $\mathbf C$. Define $\mathbf C'_0$ to be the image of the operation $\operatorname{dom}$ on $\mathbf C_1$. Define $\operatorname{id}$ to be the identity on $\mathbf C'_0$, and take $\operatorname{dom}$ and $\operatorname{cod}$ as in $\mathbf C$.

title: Morse-Sard Theorem
snippet: Let $f: X \to Y$ be any smooth map of manifolds. Then almost every point in $Y$ is a regular value of $f$.

title: Motion of Body Falling through Air
snippet: The motion of a body $B$ falling through air can be described using the following differential equation: $m \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d t^2} = m g - k \dfrac {d y} {d t}$ where: $m$ denotes mass of $B$ $y$ denotes the height of $B$ from an arbitrary reference $t$ denotes time elapsed from an arbitrary reference $g$ denotes the local gravitational constant acting on $B$ $k$ denotes the coefficient of resistive force exerted on $B$ by the air (assumed to be proportional to the speed of $B$)

title: Motion of Body with Constant Mass
snippet: Let $B$ be a body with constant mass $m$ undergoing a force $\mathbf F$. Then the equation of motion of $B$ is given by: $\mathbf F = m \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a$ is the acceleration of $B$.

title: Motion of Body with Variable Mass
snippet: Let $B$ be a body undergoing a force $\mathbf F$. Let $B$ be travelling at a velocity $\mathbf v$ at time $t$. Let mass travelling at a velocity $\mathbf v + \mathbf w$ be added to $B$ at a rate of $\dfrac {\d m} {\d t}$. Let $m$ be the mass of $B$ at time $t$. Then the equation of motion of $B$ is given by: $\mathbf w \dfrac {\d m} {\d t} + \mathbf F = m \dfrac {\d \mathbf v} {\d t}$

Let $\mathbf F$ be expressed as: $\mathbf F = F_r \mathbf u_r + F_\theta \mathbf u_\theta$ where: $\mathbf u_r$ is the unit vector in the direction of the radial coordinate of $p$ $\mathbf u_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of the angular coordinate of $p$ $F_r$ and $F_\theta$ are the magnitudes of the components of $\mathbf F$ in the directions of $\mathbf u_r$ and $\mathbf u_\theta$…

title: Motion of Rocket in Outer Space
snippet: Let $B$ be a rocket travelling in outer space. Let the velocity of $B$ at time $t$ be $\mathbf v$. Let the mass of $B$ at time $t$ be $m$. Let the exhaust velocity of $B$ be constant at $\mathbf b$. Then the equation of motion of $B$ is given by: $m \dfrac {\d \mathbf v} {\d t} = - \mathbf b \dfrac {\d m} {\d t}$

title: Motion of Simple Pendulum
snippet: Consider a simple pendulum consisting of a bob whose mass is $m$, at the end of a rod of negligible mass of length $a$. Let the bob be pulled to one side so that the rod is at an angle $\alpha$ from the vertical and then released. Let $T$ be the time period of the simple pendulum, that is, the time through which the bob takes to travel from one end of its path to the other, and back again. Then: $T = 4 \sqrt {\dfrac a g} \map K k$ where: $k = \map \sin {\dfrac \alpha 2}$ $\map K k$ is the complete elliptic integral of the first kind.
