snippet: Let $G$ be a multigraph. Let the vertex set of $G$ be finite. Then it is not necessarily the case that $G$ is also finite.

title: Multiindices under Addition form Commutative Monoid
snippet: Let $Z$ be the set of multiindices. Let $+$ denote the addition of multiindices. Then $\left({Z, +}\right)$ is a commutative monoid.

title: Multilinear Mapping from Free Modules is Determined by Bases
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $M_1, \ldots, M_n$ be free $R$-modules. Let $B_1, \ldots, B_n$ be bases of $M_1, \ldots, M_n$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Let $f: B_1 \times \cdots \times B_n \to N$ be a mapping. Then there exists a unique multilinear map $\phi: M_1 \times \cdots \times M_n \to N$ such that $\map \phi b = \map f b$ for all $b \in B_1 \times \cdots \times B_n$.

title: Multinomial Coefficient/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multinomial Coefficients ==

title: Multinomial Coefficient expressed as Product of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: $\dbinom {k_1 + k_2 + \cdots + k_m} {k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_m} = \dbinom {k_1 + k_2} {k_1} \dbinom {k_1 + k_2 + k_3} {k_1 + k_2} \cdots \dbinom {k_1 + k_2 + \cdots + k_m} {k_1 + k_2 + \cdots + k_{m - 1} }$ where: $\dbinom {k_1 + k_2 + \cdots + k_m} {k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_m}$ denotes a multinomial coefficient $\dbinom {k_1 + k_2} {k_1}$ etc. denotes binomial coefficients.

title: Multinomial Theorem
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k \in F$, where $F$ is a field. Then: $\ds \paren {x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_m}^n = \sum_{k_1 \mathop + k_2 \mathop + \mathop \cdots \mathop + k_m \mathop = n} \binom n {k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_m} {x_1}^{k_1} {x_2}^{k_2} \cdots {x_m}^{k_m}$ where: $m \in \Z_{> 0}$ is a positive integer $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ is a non-negative integer $\dbinom n {k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_m} = \dfrac {n!} {k_1! \, k_2! \, \cdots k_m!}$ denotes a multinomial coefficient.

title: Multiple Angle Formula for Sine
snippet: $\ds \frac {\map \sin {n z} } {\sin z} = 2^{n - 1} \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^{n - 1} \paren {\cos z - \cos \frac {k \pi} n}$ for $\sin z \ne 0$.

title: Multiple Angle Formula for Tangent
snippet: $\ds \map \tan {n \theta} = \frac {\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^{\floor{\frac {n - 1} 2} } \paren {-1}^i \binom n {2 i + 1} \tan^{2 i + 1}\theta} {\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^{\floor {\frac n 2} } \paren {-1}^i \binom n {2 i} \tan^{2 i}\theta}$

title: Multiple Angle Formulas
snippet: == Trigonometric Identities ==

title: Multiple Correlation Coefficient has Highest Correlation
snippet: Let $\expect y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 \cdots$ Let $R$ denote the multiple correlation coefficient. No other linear function of the $x_i$ has a higher correlation with the $y_i$ than $R$.

title: Multiple Equilibrium Points all have Equal Payoffs
snippet: Let $G$ be a two-person zero-sum game. Let $G$ have more than one equilibrium point. Then every equilibrium point of $G$ has the same payoff.

title: Multiple Function on Ring is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $g_a: \Z \to R$ be the mapping from the integers into $R$ defined as: $\forall n \in \Z:\forall a \in R: \map {g_a} n = n \cdot a$ where $\cdot$ denotes the multiple operation. Then: $g_a$ is a group homomorphism from $\struct {\Z, +}$ to $\struct {R, +}$.

title: Multiple Function on Ring is Zero iff Characteristic is Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the characteristic of $R$ be $p$. Let $a \in R$ such that $a$ is not a zero divisor of $R$. Then: $n \cdot a = 0_R$ $p \divides n$ where $\cdot$ denotes the multiple operation.

title: Multiple Linear Regression/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multiple Linear Regression ==

title: Multiple Root/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multiple Roots ==

title: Multiple Root is Root of First Derivative of Equation
snippet: Let $\EE$ be the equation: $\map f x = 0$ where $f: \R \to \R$ is a real function. Let $\xi$ be a multiple root of $\EE$. Then $\xi$ is also a root of the equation: $\map {f'} x = 0$ where $f': \R \to \R$ is the first derivative of $f$ $x$.

title: Multiple Rule for Sequence in Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ converging to $x$. Let $\lambda \in \Bbb F$. Then: $\lambda x_n \to \lambda x$

title: Multiple of 6 is Semiperfect
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a multiple of $6$. Then $n$ is semiperfect.

title: Multiple of 999 can be Split into Groups of 3 Digits which Add to 999/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == The Dictionary $999$ The Dictionary $999$

title: Multiple of Absolutely Continuous Function is Absolutely Continuous
snippet: Let $k$ be a real number. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f : I \to \R$ be an absolutely continuous real function. Then $k f$ is absolutely continuous.

title: Multiple of Abundant Number is Abundant
snippet: Let $n$ be an abundant number. Let $m$ be a positive integer such that $m > 1$. Then $m n$ is abundant.

title: Multiple of Chi-Squared Random Variable has Gamma Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $k > 0$ be a real number. Let $X \sim \chi^2_n$ where $\chi^2_n$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then: $k X \sim \map \Gamma {\dfrac n 2, \dfrac 1 {2 k}}$ where $\map \Gamma {\dfrac n 2, \dfrac 1 {2 k}}$ is the gamma distribution with parameters $\dfrac n 2$ and $\dfrac 1 {2 k}$.

title: Multiple of Codeword in Linear Code/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multiples of Codewords in Linear Codes ==

title: Multiple of Column Added to Column of Determinant
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \begin {bmatrix} a_{1 1} & \cdots & a_{1 r} & \cdots & a_{1 s} & \cdots & a_{1 n} \\ a_{2 1} & \cdots & a_{2 r} & \cdots & a_{2 s} & \cdots & a_{2 n} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ a_{n 1} & \cdots & a_{n r} & \cdots & a_{n s} & \cdots & a_{n n} \\ \end {bmatrix}$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ denote the determinant of $\mathbf A$.

title: Multiple of Divisor Divides Multiple
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \Z$. Let: $a \divides b$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then: $a c \divides b c$

title: Multiple of Divisor in Integral Domain Divides Multiple
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Let $a, b, c \in D$. Let $a \divides b$, where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then $a \times c$ is a divisor of $b \times c$.

title: Multiple of Exponential Random Variable has Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $\beta, k$ be real numbers with $\beta > 0$. Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $X \sim \Exponential \beta$, where $\Exponential \beta$ is the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$. Then: $k X \sim \Exponential {k \beta}$

title: Multiple of Function of Bounded Variation is of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b, k$ be real numbers with $a < b$. Let $f : \closedint a b \to \R$ be a functions of bounded variation. Let the total variation of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ be $\map {V_f} {\closedint a b}$. Then $k f$ is of bounded variation with: $\map {V_{k f} } {\closedint a b} = \size k \map {V_f} {\closedint a b}$ where $\map {V_{k f} } {\closedint a b}$ is the total variation of $k f$ on $\closedint a b$.

title: Multiple of Identity Element of Unital C*-Algebra is Positive iff Coefficient is Non-Negative Real Number
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\lambda \in \C$. Then $\lambda {\mathbf 1}_A$ is positive $\lambda \in \R_{\ge 0}$.

title: Multiple of Infimum
snippet: Let $T \subseteq \R: T \ne \O$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $T$ be bounded below. Let $z \in \R: z > 0$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Then: $\ds \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } {z x} = z \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } x$ where $\inf$ denotes infimum.

title: Multiple of Metric forms Metric
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $d_1: A^2 \to \R$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in A^2: \map {d_1} {x, y} = k \map d {x, y}$ for some strictly positive $k \in \R_{>0}$. Then $d_1$ is a metric for $A$.

title: Multiple of Perfect Number is Abundant
snippet: Let $n$ be a perfect number. Let $m$ be a positive integer such that $m > 1$. Then $m n$ is abundant.

title: Multiple of Pi as Infinite Product
snippet: {{eqn | l = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\frac n {n - \frac 1 2} }^2 \paren {\frac {n - 1 + z} {n + z} } | r = \paren {\frac 1 {1 - \frac 1 2} }^2 \paren {\frac {1 - 1 + z} {1 + z} } \times \paren {\frac 2 {2 - \frac 1 2} }^2 \paren {\frac {2 - 1 + z} {2 + z} } \times \paren {\frac 3 {3 - \frac 1 2} }^2 \paren {\frac {3 - 1 + z} {3 + z} } \times \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {\frac 2 1 }^2 \paren {\frac z {1 + z} } \times \paren {\frac 4 3 }^2 \paren {\frac {1 + z} {2 + z} } \times \paren {\frac 6 5 }^2 \paren {\frac {2 + z} {3 + z} } \times \cdots | c = }}

title: Multiple of Repdigit Base minus 1
snippet: Let $b \in \Z_{>1}$ be an integer greater than $1$. Let $n$ be a repdigit number of $k$ instances of the digit $b - 1$ for some integer $k$ such that $k \ge 1$. Let $m \in \Z_{>1}$ be an integer such that $1 < m < b$. Then $m \times n$, when expressed in base $b$, is of the form: $m n = \sqbrk {r d d \cdots d s}_b$ where: $d = b - 1$ $r = m - 1$ $s = b - m$ there are $k - 1$ occurrences of $d$.

title: Multiple of Ring Product
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $x, y \in \struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then: $\forall n \in \Z_{> 0}: \paren {n \cdot x} \circ y = n \cdot \paren {x \circ y} = x \circ \paren {n \cdot y}$ where $n \cdot x$ denotes the $n$th multiple of $x$.

title: Multiple of Row Added to Row of Determinant
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \begin {bmatrix} a_{1 1} & a_{1 2} & \cdots & a_{1 n} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ a_{r 1} & a_{r 2} & \cdots & a_{r n} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ a_{s 1} & a_{s 2} & \cdots & a_{s n} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ a_{n 1} & a_{n 2} & \cdots & a_{n n} \\ \end {bmatrix}$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ denote the determinant of $\mathbf A$.

title: Multiple of Semiperfect Number is Semiperfect
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a semiperfect number. Let $k \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then $k n$ is also a semiperfect number.

title: Multiple of Sine plus Multiple of Cosine
Multiple of Supremum
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R: S \ne \O$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $S$ be bounded above. Let $z \in \R: z > 0$ be a positive real number. Then: $\ds \map {\sup_{x \mathop \in S} } {z x} = z \map {\sup_{x \mathop \in S} } x$

title: Multiple of Vector in Topological Vector Space Converges
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space. Let $x \in X$. Let $\lambda \in K$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $K$ such that $\lambda_n \to \lambda$. Then: $\lambda_n x \to \lambda x$

title: Multiples of Alternate Ratios of Equal Fractions
Multiples of Divisors obey Distributive Law
snippet: In modern algebraic language: $a = \dfrac m n b, c = \dfrac m n d \implies a + c = \dfrac m n \paren {b + d}$

title: Multiples of Factorial Plus One are Coprime
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $\sequence {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_n}$ be a sequence of natural numbers such that: $\forall i: 1 \le i \le n: x_i = 1 + i \times a!$ where $a!$ denotes the factorial of $a$. Let $a \ge n - 1$. Then $\set {x_i}$ are pairwise coprime.

title: Multiples of Homogeneous Cartesian Coordinates represent Same Point
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the Cartesian plane. Let $P$ be an arbitrary point in $\CC$. Let $P$ be expressed in homogeneous Cartesian coordinates as: $P = \tuple {X, Y, Z}$ Then $P$ can also be expressed as: $P = \tuple {\rho X, \rho Y, \rho Z}$ where $\rho \in \R$ is an arbitrary real number such that $\rho \ne 0$.

title: Multiples of Reciprocals with Maximum Period form Magic Square
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number whose reciprocal has a decimal expansion which has the maximum period, that is, $p - 1$. Let the first $p - 1$ digits of $\dfrac 1 p$ be expressed as an integer $n$ (with one or more leading zeroes as it is presented). Then the first $p - 1$ multiples of $n$, when listed in order of size, arrange themselves as a magic square such that: the sum of the elements of each row the sum of the elements in each column are the same.

title: Multiples of Terms in Equal Ratios
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d$ be quantities. Let $a : b = c : d$ where $a : b$ denotes the ratio between $a$ and $b$. Then for any numbers $m$ and $n$: $m a : n b = m c : n d$

title: Multiplication Function on Ring with Unity is Zero if Characteristic is Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the characteristic of $R$ be $p$. Let $g_a: \Z \to R$ be the mapping from the integers into $R$ defined as: $\forall n \in \Z:\forall a \in R: \map {g_a} n = n \cdot a$ where $\cdot$ denotes the multiple operation. Then: $p \divides n \implies n \cdot a = 0_R$ where $p \divides n$ denotes that $p$ is a divisor of $n$.

title: Multiplication Property of Characteristic Functions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent random variables on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $\phi_X$ and $\phi_Y$ denote the characteristic functions of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Then: $\phi_{X + Y} = \phi_X \phi_Y$

title: Multiplication by 2 over 3 in Egyptian Fractions
snippet: Let $\dfrac 1 n$ be an Egyptian fraction not equal to $\dfrac 2 3$. In order to multiply $\dfrac 1 n$ by $\dfrac 2 3$ and have it that $\dfrac 1 n \times \dfrac 2 3$ is also expressed in Egyptian form, we have: $\dfrac 1 n \times \dfrac 2 3 = \dfrac 1 {2 n} + \dfrac 1 {6 n}$

title: Multiplication by Imaginary Unit is Equivalent to Rotation through Right Angle
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $z$ be interpreted as a vector in the complex plane. Let $w \in \C$ be the complex number defined as $z$ multiplied by the imaginary unit $i$: $w = i z$ Then $w$ can be interpreted as the vector $z$ after being rotated through a right angle in an anticlockwise direction.

title: Multiplication by Negative Real Number
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: x \times \paren {-y} = -\paren {x \times y} = \paren {-x} \times y$

title: Multiplication by Power of 10 by Moving Decimal Point
snippet: Let $n \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n$ be expressed in decimal notation. Let $10^d$ denote a power of $10$ for some integer $d$ Then $n \times 10^d$ can be expressed in decimal notation by shifting the decimal point $d$ places to the right. Thus, if $d$ is negative, and so $10^d = 10^{-e}$ for some $e \in \Z_{>0}$, $n \times 10^d$ can be expressed in decimal notation by shifting the decimal point $e$ places to the left.

title: Multiplication is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^2 \to \N$ be defined as: $\map f {x, y} = x \times y$ Then there exists a WFF $\map \phi {z, x, y}$ of $3$ free variables and containing no quantifiers such that: $z = \map f {x, y} \iff \N \models \map \phi {\sqbrk z, \sqbrk x, \sqbrk y}$ where $\sqbrk a$ is the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Multiplication is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The function $\operatorname{mult}: \N^2 \to \N$, defined as: $\map \Mult {n, m} = n \times m$ is primitive recursive‎.

title: Multiplication is Superfunction
snippet: The function $f: \C \to \C$, defined as: $\map f z = z \times c$ is a superfunction for any complex number $c$.

title: Multiplication of Complex Number by -1 is Equivalent to Rotation through Two Right Angles
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $z$ be interpreted as a vector in the complex plane. Let $w \in \C$ be the complex number defined as $z$ multiplied by $-1$: $w = \left({-1}\right) z$ Then $w$ can be interpreted as the vector $z$ after being rotated through two right angles. The direction of rotation is usually interpreted as being anticlockwise, but a rotated through two right angles is the same whichever direction the rotation is performed.

title: Multiplication of Cross-Relation Equivalence Classes on Natural Numbers is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ be the semigroup of natural numbers under addition. Let $\struct {\N \times \N, \oplus}$ be the (external) direct product of $\struct {\N, +}$ with itself, where $\oplus$ is the operation on $\N \times \N$ induced by $+$ on $\N$. Let $\boxtimes$ be the cross-relation defined on $\N \times \N$ by: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \boxtimes \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 + y_2 = x_2 + y_1$ Let $\eqclass {x, y} {}$ denote the equivalence class of $\tuple {x, y}$ under $\boxtimes$.

title: Multiplication of Cuts Distributes over Addition
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let: $\alpha + \beta$ denote the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. $\alpha \beta$ denote the product of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\alpha \paren {\beta + \gamma} = \alpha \beta + \alpha \gamma$

title: Multiplication of Cuts is Associative
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let $\alpha \beta$ denote the product of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\paren {\alpha \beta} \gamma = \alpha \paren {\beta \gamma}$

title: Multiplication of Cuts is Commutative
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Let the $\alpha \beta$ be the product of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then: $\alpha \beta = \beta \alpha$

title: Multiplication of Distribution induced by Locally Integrable Function by Smooth Function
snippet: Let $f \in \map {L^1_{loc} } {\R^d}$ be a locally integrable function. Let $\alpha \in \map {C^\infty} {\R^d}$ be a smooth function. Let $T_f \in \map {\DD'} {\R^d}$ be a Schwartz distribution induced by $f$. Then in the distributional sense it holds that: $\alpha T_f = T_{\alpha f}$

title: Multiplication of Fractions
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ such that $b d \ne 0$. Then: $\dfrac a b \times \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a c} {b d}$

title: Multiplication of Integers is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $t : \N^2 \to \N$ be defined as: $\map t {m, n} = p$ where: $m$ is the code number for the integer $k$ $n$ is the code number for the integer $\ell$ $p$ is the code number for the integer $k \times \ell$ Then $t$ is a primitive recursive function.

title: Multiplication of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$ be natural numbers. Then there exists a formal proof of: $\sqbrk x \times \sqbrk y = \sqbrk {x \times y}$ in minimal arithmetic, where $\sqbrk a$ is the unary representation of $a$.

title: Multiplication of Numbers is Left Distributive over Addition
snippet: That is, if $m a$, $m b$, $m c$ etc. be any equimultiples of $a$, $b$, $c$ etc., then: $m a + m b + m c + \cdots = m \paren {a + b + c + \cdots }$

title: Multiplication of Numbers is Right Distributive over Addition
snippet: That is: $m a + n a + p a + \cdots = \paren {m + n + p + \cdots} a$

title: Multiplication of Polynomials Distributes over Addition
snippet: Multiplication of polynomials is left- and right- distributive over addition.

title: Multiplication of Polynomials is Associative
snippet: Multiplication of polynomials is associative.

title: Multiplication of Polynomials is Commutative
snippet: Multiplication of polynomials is commutative.

title: Multiplication of Positive Cuts preserves Ordering
snippet: Let $0^*$ denote the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$. Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts such that: $0^* < \alpha < \beta$ $0^* < \gamma$ where $<$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts. Then $\alpha \gamma < \beta \gamma$ where $\alpha \gamma$ denotes the product of $\alpha$ and $\gamma$.

title: Multiplication of Positive Number by Real Number Greater than One
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be real numbers. Let $x > 1$. Let $y > 0$. Then $\dfrac y x < y$.

title: Multiplication of Real Numbers Distributes over Subtraction
Multiplication of Real Numbers is Left Distributive over Subtraction
snippet: That is, for any numbers $a, b$ and for any integer $m$: $m a - m b = m \paren {a - b}$

title: Multiplication of Real Numbers is Right Distributive over Subtraction
snippet: That is, for any number $a$ and for any integers $m, n$: $m a - n a = \paren {m - n} a$

title: Multiplication of Real and Imaginary Parts
snippet: Let $w, z \in \C$ be complex numbers. $(1)$ If $w$ is wholly real, then: $\map \Re {w z} = w \, \map \Re z$ and: $\map \Im {w z} = w \, \map \Im z$ $(2)$ If $w$ is wholly imaginary, then: $\map \Re {w z} = -\map \Im w \, \map \Im z$ and: $\map \Im {w z} = \map \Im w \, \map \Re z$ Here, $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$, and $\map \Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of $z$.

title: Multiplication on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $\times$ be multiplication on $\N_{>0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a \times c = b \times c \implies a = b$ $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a \times b = a \times c \implies b = c$ That is, $\times$ is cancellable on $\N_{>0}$.

title: Multiplication on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Cancellable for Ordering
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $\times$ be multiplication on $\N_{>0}$. Let $0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in \N_{>0}: a \times c 0}: a \times b 0}$ for $<$.

title: Multiplication on Normed Algebra is Continuous
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\GF$. Let $\struct {A^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{A^2} }$ be the direct product of $A$ with itself equipped with the direct product norm. Define $m : A^2 \to A$ by: $\map m {a, b} = a b$ for each $\tuple {a, b} \in A^2$. Then $m$ is continuous.

title: Multiplication using Parabola
snippet: thumb Let the parabola $P$ defined as $y = x^2$ be plotted on the Cartesian plane. Let $A = \tuple {x_a, y_a}$ and $B = \tuple {x_b, y_b}$ be points on the curve $\map f x$ so that $x_a < x_b$. Then the line segment joining $A B$ will cross the $y$-axis at $-x_a x_b$. Thus $P$ can be used as a nomogram to calculate the product of two numbers $x_a$ and $x_b$, as follows: $(1) \quad$ Find the points $-x_a$ and $x_b$ on the $x$-axis. $(2) \quad$ Find the points $A$ and $B$ where the lines $x = -x_a$ and $x = x_b$ cut $P$.

title: Multiplicative Auxiliary Relation iff Congruent
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below lattice. Let $\RR$ be an auxiliary relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is multiplicative : $\forall a, b, x, y \in S: \tuple {a, x}, \tuple {b, y} \in \RR \implies \tuple {a \wedge b, x \wedge y} \in \RR$ That is $\RR$ is a congruence relation for $\wedge$.

title: Multiplicative Auxiliary Relation iff Images are Filtered
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below lattice. Let $\RR$ be an auxiliary relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is multiplicative : for all $x \in S$: $\map \RR x$ is filtered where $\map \RR x$ denotes the $\RR$-image of $x$.

title: Multiplicative Function that Converges to Zero on Prime Powers
snippet: Let $f$ be a multiplicative function such that: $\ds \lim_{p^k \mathop \to \infty} \map f {p^k} = 0$ where $p^k$ runs though all prime powers. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f n = 0$ where $n$ runs through the integers.

title: Multiplicative Group of Complex Numbers is not Direct Product of Reals with Reals
Multiplicative Group of Complex Numbers is not Isomorphic to Additive Group of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ is not isomorphic to $\struct {\C, +}$.

title: Multiplicative Group of Complex Numbers is not Isomorphic to Additive Group of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Then $\struct {\C_{\ne 0}, \times}$ is not isomorphic to $\struct {\R, +}$.

title: Multiplicative Group of Complex Numbers is not Isomorphic to Multiplicative Group of Real Numbers
Multiplicative Group of Complex Roots of Unity is Subgroup of Circle Group
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 0$. Let $\struct {U_n, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of complex $n$th roots of unity. Let $\struct {K, \times}$ denote the circle group. Then $\struct {U_n, \times}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {K, \times}$.

title: Multiplicative Group of Field is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field. Let $F^* := F \setminus \set 0$ be the set $F$ less its zero. The algebraic structure $\struct {F^*, \times}$ is an abelian group.

title: Multiplicative Group of Galois Field is Cyclic
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a Galois field of order $q$. Then its multiplicative group is cyclic of order $q-1$: $\GF^\times \cong C_{q - 1}$

title: Multiplicative Group of Positive Rationals is Non-Cyclic
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q_{>0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of positive rational numbers. Then $\struct {\Q_{>0}, \times}$ is not a cyclic group.

title: Multiplicative Group of Rationals is Normal Subgroup of Complex
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of rational numbers. Let $\struct {\C, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of complex numbers. Then $\struct {\Q, \times}$ is a normal subgroup of $\struct {\C, \times}$.

title: Multiplicative Group of Rationals is Normal Subgroup of Reals
Multiplicative Group of Reals is Normal Subgroup of Complex
Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Groups of Reduced Residues ==

title: Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 5/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 5 == The multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $5$: $\struct {\Z'_5, \times_5} = \set {\eqclass 1 5, \eqclass 2 5, \eqclass 3 5, \eqclass 4 5}$ can be described completely by showing its Cayley table: $\quad \begin {array} {r|rrrr} \times_5 & \eqclass 1 5 & \eqclass 2 5 & \eqclass 3 5 & \eqclass 4 5 \\ \hline \eqclass 1 5 & \eqclass 1 5 & \eqclass 2 5 & \eqclass 3 5 & \eqclass 4 5 \\ \eqclass 2 5 & \eqclass 2 5 & \eqclass 4 5 & \eqclass 1 5 & \eqclass 3 5 \\ \eqclass 3 5 & \eqclass 3 5 & \eqclass 1 5 & \eqclass 4 5…

title: Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 7/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 7 == The multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $7$: $\Z'_7 = \set {\eqclass 1 7, \eqclass 2 7, \eqclass 3 7, \eqclass 4 7}, \eqclass 5 7, \eqclass 6 7$ can be described completely by showing its Cayley table: $\quad \begin {array} {r|rrrr} \times_5 & \eqclass 1 7 & \eqclass 2 7 & \eqclass 3 7 & \eqclass 4 7 & \eqclass 5 7 & \eqclass 6 7 \\ \hline \eqclass 1 7 & \eqclass 1 7 & \eqclass 2 7 & \eqclass 3 7 & \eqclass 4 7 & \eqclass 5 7 & \eqclass 6 7 \\ \eqclass 2 7 & \eqclass 2 7 & \eqclass 4 7 & \eqclass 6 7 &…

title: Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 7 is Cyclic
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z'_7, \times_7}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $7$. Then $\struct {\Z'_7, \times_7}$ is cyclic.

title: Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 8/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 8 == The multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $8$: $\Z'_8 = \set {\eqclass 1 8, \eqclass 3 8, \eqclass 5 8, \eqclass 7 8}$ can be described completely by showing its Cayley table: $\quad \begin {array} {r|rrrr} \times_8 & \eqclass 1 8 & \eqclass 3 8 & \eqclass 5 8 & \eqclass 7 8 \\ \hline \eqclass 1 8 & \eqclass 1 8 & \eqclass 3 8 & \eqclass 5 8 & \eqclass 7 8 \\ \eqclass 3 8 & \eqclass 3 8 & \eqclass 1 8 & \eqclass 7 8 & \eqclass 5 8 \\ \eqclass 5 8 & \eqclass 5 8 & \eqclass 7 8 & \eqclass 1 8 & \eqclass 3 8 \\…

title: Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues Modulo 8 is Klein Four-Group
snippet: Let $K_4$ denote the Klein $4$-group. Let $R_4$ be the multiplicative group of reduced residues Modulo $8$. Then $K_4$ and $R_4$ are isomorphic algebraic structures.

title: Multiplicative Identity for Quaternions
snippet: In the set of quaternions $\mathbb H$, the element: $\mathbf 1 + 0 \mathbf i + 0 \mathbf j + 0 \mathbf k$ serves as the identity element for quaternion multiplication. This element is written $\mathbf 1$.

title: Multiplicative Identity is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field. Then the multiplicative identity $1_F$ of $F$ is unique.

title: Multiplicative Inverse in Field is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $a \in F$ such that $a \ne 0_F$. Then the multiplicative inverse $a^{-1}$ of $a$ is unique.

title: Multiplicative Inverse in Monoid of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_m, \times_m}$ be the multiplicative monoid of integers modulo $m$. Then: $\eqclass k m \in \Z_m$ has an inverse in $\struct {\Z_m, \times_m}$ $k \perp m$

title: Multiplicative Inverse in Nicely Normed Star-Algebra
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a nicely normed $*$-algebra whose conjugation is denoted $*$. Let $a \in A$. Then the multiplicative inverse of $a$ is given by: $a^{-1} = \dfrac {a^*} {\norm a^2}$ where: $a^*$ is the conjugate of $a$ $\norm a$ is the norm of $a$.

title: Multiplicative Inverse in Ring of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Then $\eqclass k m \in \Z_m$ has an inverse in $\struct {\Z_m, \times_m}$ $k \perp m$.

title: Multiplicative Inverse of Quaternion
snippet: Let $\mathbf x = a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k$ be a quaternion such that $\mathbf x \ne \mathbf 0$. Then $\mathbf x$ has an inverse $\mathbf x^{-1}$ under the operation of quaternion multiplication: $\mathbf x^{-1} = \lambda \overline {\mathbf x}$ where: $\lambda = \dfrac 1 {a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2} \mathbf 1$

title: Multiplicative Magic Square/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Magic Squares ==

title: Multiplicative Magic Square from 9 Terms of Geometric Sequence from 1, 2, 4
snippet: == Problem == With the first $9$ terms of the geometric sequence $1, 2, 4, \ldots$, form a product of $4096$ each way. That is, form a multiplicative magic square whose magic constant is $4096$.

title: Multiplicative Order of Roots of Cyclotomic Polynomial Modulo Prime
snippet: Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Let $\Phi_n$ be the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $n = p^\alpha q$ where $\alpha = \map {\nu_p} n$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $n$. Let $a \in \Z$ with $\map {\Phi_n} a \equiv 0 \pmod p$. Then the order of $a$ modulo $p$ is $q$: $\map {\operatorname{ord}_p} a = q$.

title: Multiplicative Ordering on Integers
snippet: Let $x, y, z \in \Z$ such that $z > 0$. Then: $x < y \iff z x < z y$ $x \le y \iff z x \le z y$

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/10
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Persistence == $10$ is the smallest positive integer which has a multiplicative persistence of $1$.

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/25
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Persistence == $25$ is the smallest positive integer which has a multiplicative persistence of $2$.

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/277,777,788,888,899
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Persistence == $277 \, 777 \, 788 \, 888 \, 899$ is the smallest positive integer which has a multiplicative persistence of $11$.

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/39

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/679
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Persistence == $679$ is the smallest positive integer which has a multiplicative persistence of $5$.

title: Multiplicative Persistence/Examples/77
snippet: == Examples of Multiplicative Persistence == $77$ is the smallest positive integer which has a multiplicative persistence of $4$.

title: Multiplicative Regular Representations of Units of Topological Ring are Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct{R, + , \circ, \tau}$ be a topological ring with unity $1_R$. For all $y \in R$, let $\lambda_y$ and $\rho_y$ denote the left and right regular representations of $\struct{R, \circ}$ with respect to $y$. Let $x \in R$ be a unit of $R$ with product inverse $x^{-1}$. Then $\lambda_x, \, \rho_x: \struct{R, \tau} \to \struct{R, \tau}$ are homeomorphisms with inverse mappings $\lambda_{x^{-1} }, \, \rho_{x^{-1} }: \struct{R, \tau} \to \struct{R, \tau}$ respectively.

title: Multiplicatively Closed Subset is Saturated iff Complement is Union of Prime Ideals
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a multiplicatively closed subset. {{item|(2):|$\relcomp A S \bigcup \set {\mathfrak p \in \Spec A: \mathfrak p \cap S \O}$}} where: $\relcomp A S$ denotes the complement of $S$ $\Spec A$ denotes the prime spectrum of $A$

title: Multiplicity of 720 in 720 Factorial
snippet: The multiplicity of $720$ in $720!$ is $178$. That is: $720^{178} \divides 720!$ but: $720^{179} \nmid 720!$ where: $720!$ denotes $720$ factorial $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\nmid$ denotes non-divisibility.

title: Multiplier Algebra is Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $\map M A$ be the set of double centralizers of $A$. Define: $\tuple {L_1, R_1} +_{\map M A} \tuple {L_2, R_2} = \tuple {L_1 +_{\map B A} L_2, R_1 +_{\map B A} R_2}$ $\lambda \circ_{\map M A} \tuple {L_1, R_1} = \tuple {\lambda \circ_{\map B A} L_1, \lambda \circ_{\map B A} R_1}$ $\tuple {L_1, R_1} \times_{\map M A} \tuple {L_2, R_2} = \tuple {L_1 L_2, R_2 R_1}$ where $+_{\map B A}$ and $\circ_{\map B A}$ are the respective operations on the space of bounded linear transformations $\map B A$.

title: Multiply Perfect Number of Order 6
snippet: The number defined as: $n = 2^{36} \times 3^8 \times 5^5 \times 7^7 \times 11 \times 13^2 \times 19 \times 31^2$ $\times \ 43 \times 61 \times 83 \times 223 \times 331 \times 379 \times 601 \times 757 \times 1201$ $\times \ 7019 \times 112 \, 303 \times 898 \, 423 \times 616 \, 318 \, 177$ is multiply perfect of order $6$.

title: Multiply Perfect Number of Order 8
snippet: The number defined as: $n = 2^{65} \times 3^{23} \times 5^9 \times 7^{12} \times 11^3 \times 13^3 \times 17^2 \times 19^2 \times 23 \times 29^2 \times 31^2$ ${} \times 37 \times 41 \times 53 \times 61 \times 67^2 \times 71^2 \times 73 \times 83 \times 89 \times 103 \times 127 \times 131$ ${} \times 149 \times 211 \times 307 \times 331 \times 463 \times 521 \times 683 \times 709 \times 1279 \times 2141 \times 2557 \times 5113$ ${} \times 6481 \times 10 \, 429 \times 20 \, 857 \times 110 \, 563 \times 599 \, 479 \times 16 \, 148 \, 168 \, 401$ is multiply perfect of order $8$.

title: Multitape Turing Machine Reduces to Turing Machine
snippet: Let $T$ be a multitape Turing machine. Then, there exists a Turing machine $T'$ that accepts precisely the same language as $T$, and halts on exactly the inputs that $T$ does.

title: Multivariate Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Multivariate Data ==

title: Mutual Order Embedding does not imply Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let it be possible for: $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ to be embedded in $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ to be embedded in $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ are isomorphic.

title: Möbius Function/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Möbius Function ==

title: Möbius Function is Multiplicative
snippet: The Möbius function $\mu$ is a multiplicative function: $m \perp n \implies \map \mu {m n} = \map \mu m \map \mu n$ where $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Möbius Inversion Formula
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be arithmetic functions. Then: $(1): \quad \ds \map f n = \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map g d$ $(2): \quad \ds \map g n = \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f d \, \map \mu {\frac n d}$ where: $d \divides n$ denotes that $d$ is a divisor of $n$ $\mu$ is the Möbius function.

title: Möbius Inversion Formula for Cyclotomic Polynomials
snippet: Let $n > 0$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Phi_n$ be the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial. Then: $\map {\Phi_n} x = \ds \prod_{d \mathop \divides n} \paren {x^d - 1}^{\map \mu {n / d} }$ where: the product runs over all divisors of $n$ $\mu$ is the Möbius function.

title: Möbius Strip has Euler Characteristic Zero
snippet: Let $M$ be a Möbius Strip. Then: $\map \chi M = 0$ where $\map \chi M$ denotes the Euler characteristic of the graph $M$.

title: Möbius Strip is Fiber Bundle
snippet: The Möbius strip is an example of a fiber bundle.

title: Möbius Transformation is Bijection
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $f: \overline \C \to \overline \C$ be the Möbius transformation: $\map f z = \begin {cases} \dfrac {a z + b} {c z + d} & : z \ne -\dfrac d c \\ \infty & : z = -\dfrac d c \\ \dfrac a c & : z = \infty \\ \infty & : z = \infty \text { and } c = 0 \end {cases}$ where $\overline \C$ denotes the extended complex plane. Then: $f: \overline \C \to \overline \C$ is a bijection $a c - b d \ne 0$

title: Möbius Transformations form Group under Composition
snippet: Let $G$ be the set of Möbius transformations. Let $\circ$ denote the composition of mappings. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is a group.

title: N-Tuple Root is Root of n-1th Derivatives of Equation but not nth Derivative
snippet: Let $\EE$ be the equation: $\map f x = 0$ where $f: \R \to \R$ is a real function. Let $\xi$ be a multiple root of $\EE$ with a multiplicity of $n$. Then for all $k \in \N: k < n$: $\xi$ is a root of the equation $\map {f^{\paren k} } x = 0$ $\xi$ is not a root of the equation $\map {f^{\paren n} } x = 0$ where $f^{\paren k}: \R \to \R$ is the $k$th derivative of $f$ $x$.

title: NAND and NOR are Functionally Complete
snippet: The NAND and NOR operators are each functionally complete. That is, NAND and NOR are Sheffer operators.

title: NAND as Disjunction of Negations
snippet: $p \uparrow q \dashv \vdash \neg p \lor \neg q$

title: NAND is Commutative
snippet: Let $\uparrow$ signify the NAND operation. Then, for any two propositions $p$ and $q$: $p \uparrow q \dashv \vdash q \uparrow p$ That is, NAND is commutative.

title: NAND is not Associative
snippet: Let $\uparrow$ signify the NAND operation. Then there exist propositions $p, q, r$ such that: $p \uparrow \paren {q \uparrow r} \not \vdash \paren {p \uparrow q} \uparrow r$ That is, NAND is not associative.

title: NAND with Equal Arguments
snippet: Let $\uparrow$ signify the NAND operation. Then, for any proposition $p$: $p \uparrow p \dashv \vdash \neg p$ That is, the NAND of a proposition with itself corresponds to the negation operation.

title: NOR is Commutative
snippet: Let $\downarrow$ signify the NOR operation. Then, for any two propositions $p$ and $q$: $p \downarrow q \dashv \vdash q \downarrow p$ That is, NOR is commutative.

title: NOR is not Associative
snippet: Let $\downarrow$ signify the NOR operation. Then there exist propositions $p,q,r$ such that: $p \downarrow \paren {q \downarrow r} \not \vdash \paren {p \downarrow q} \downarrow r$ That is, NOR is not associative.

title: NOR with Equal Arguments
snippet: Let $\downarrow$ signify the NOR operation. Then for any proposition $p$: $p \downarrow p \dashv \vdash \neg p$ That is, the NOR of a proposition with itself corresponds to the negation operator.

title: NP-Complete Problems are all Equally Hard
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a decision problem which is NP-complete. Suppose $\LL$ can be shown to be solvable by an algorithm running in polynomial time. Then, in theory, so should all decision problems which are NP-complete

title: N (n + 1) (2n + 1) over 6 is Integer
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $\dfrac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {2 n + 1} } 6$ is also an integer.

title: N Choose Negative Number is Zero
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $k \in \Z_{<0}$ be a (strictly) negative integer. Then: $\dbinom n k = 0$

title: N Choose k is not greater than n^k
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z, k \in \Z: 1 \le k \le n: \dbinom n k < n^k$ where $\dbinom n k$ is a binomial coefficient. Equality holds when $k = 0$ and $k = 1$.

title: N less than M to the N
snippet: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{>0}: m > 1 \implies n < m^n$

title: N over 2 times Reciprocal of 1 Plus n Squared x Squared to the Power of 3 over 2 Delta Sequence
snippet: The graph of the $\ds \frac n 2 \frac 1 {\paren{1 + n^2 x^2}^{3 / 2}}$ delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the graph becomes thinner and taller. The area under each graph is equal to $1$. Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a sequence such that: $\ds \map {\delta_n} x := \frac n 2 \frac 1 {\paren{1 + n^2 x^2}^{3 / 2} }$ Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a delta sequence.

title: N over Pi times Reciprocal of 1 Plus n Squared x Squared Delta Sequence
snippet: The graph of the $\ds \frac n \pi \frac 1 {1 + n^2 x^2}$ delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the graph becomes thinner and taller. The area under each graph is equal to $1$. Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a sequence such that: $\map {\delta_n} x := \frac n \pi \frac 1 {1 + n^2 x^2}$ Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a delta sequence.

title: Nagata-Smirnov Metrization Theorem
snippet: A topological space $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ is metrizable $T$ is regular and has a basis that is $\sigma$-locally finite.

title: Nakayama's Lemma
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module. Let $\map {\operatorname{Jac} } A$ be the Jacobson radical of $A$. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq \map {\operatorname{Jac} } A$ be an ideal of $A$. Suppose $\mathfrak a M = M$. Then: $M = 0$

title: Napier's Analogies
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively.

title: Napier's Cosine Rule for Quadrantal Triangles
snippet: 500px Let $\triangle ABC$ be a quadrantal triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Let the side $c$ be a right angle. Let the remaining parts of $\triangle ABC$ be arranged according to the exterior of this circle, where the symbol $\Box$ denotes a right angle. 410px Let one of the parts of this circle be called a middle part. Let the two neighboring parts of the middle part be called adjacent parts.

title: Napier's Cosine Rule for Right Spherical Triangles

Let the remaining parts of $\triangle ABC$ be arranged according to the interior of this circle, where the symbol $\Box$ denotes a right angle. 410px Let one of the parts of this circle be called a middle part. Let the two parts which do not neighbor the middle part be called opposite parts.

title: Napoleon's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an arbitrary triangle. Let $\triangle ABF$, $\triangle BCD$ and $\triangle ACE$ be equilateral triangles constructed on $AB$, $BC$ and $AC$ respectively on the exterior of $\triangle ABC$. Let $O_1$, $O_2$ and $O_3$ be the incenters of $\triangle ABF$, $\triangle BCD$ and $\triangle ACE$. Then $\triangle O_1 O_2 O_3$ is an equilateral triangle. 400px

title: Natural Basis of Product Topology
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $X$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$: $\ds X := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ Then the natural basis on $X$ is the set $\BB$ of cartesian products of the form $\ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} U_i$ where: for all $i \in I : U_i \in \tau_i$ for all but finitely many indices $i : U_i = X_i$

title: Natural Frequency of Underdamped Cart attached to Wall by Spring
Natural Frequency of Underdamped System
snippet: Consider a physical system $S$ whose behaviour can be described with the second order ODE in the form: $\dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d t^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d x} {\d t} + a^2 x = 0$ for $a, b \in \R_{>0}$. Let $b < a$, so as to make $S$ underdamped. Then the natural frequency of $S$ is given by: $\nu = \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } {2 \pi}$

title: Natural Logarithm/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Natural Logarithm ==

title: Natural Logarithm Function is Differentiable
snippet: The (real) natural logarithm function is differentiable.

title: Natural Logarithm as Derivative of Exponential at Zero
snippet: Let $\ln: \R_{>0}$ denote the real natural logarithm. Then: $\ds \forall x \in \R_{>0}: \ln x = \lim_{h \mathop \to 0} \frac {x^h - 1} h$

title: Natural Logarithm of 1 is 0
snippet: $\ln 1 = 0$ where $\ln 1$ denotes the natural logarithm of $1$.

title: Natural Logarithm of 2 is Greater than One Half
snippet: == Lemma == $\ln 2 \ge \dfrac 1 2$ where $\ln$ denotes the natural logarithm function.

title: Natural Logarithm of e is 1
snippet: $\ln e = 1$ where $\ln$ is the natural logarithm, $e$ is Euler's number, and $1$ is the identity element of multiplication.

title: Natural Number Addition Commutativity with Successor
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Then: $\forall m, n \in \N: m^+ + n = \paren {m + n}^+$

title: Natural Number Addition Commutes with Zero
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Then: $\forall n \in \N: 0 + n = n = n + 0$

title: Natural Number Addition is Associative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of natural numbers $\N$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \N: x + \paren {y + z} = \paren {x + y} + z$

title: Natural Number Addition is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $+$ be addition on $\N$. Then: That is, $+$ is cancellable on $\N$.

title: Natural Number Addition is Cancellable for Ordering
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $0}: a + c 0}: a + b < a + c \implies b < c$ That is, $+$ is cancellable on $\N$ for $<$.

title: Natural Number Addition is Closed
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of natural numbers $\N$ is closed: $\forall x, y \in \N: x + y \in \N$

title: Natural Number Addition is Commutative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of natural numbers $\N$ is commutative: $\forall m, n \in \N: m + n = n + m$

title: Natural Number Commutes with 1 under Addition
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{> 0}$ be a natural number. Then $n$ commutes with $1$ under the operation of addition: $\forall n \in \N_{> 0}: n + 1 = 1 + n$

title: Natural Number Functions are Uncountable
snippet: The set of all natural number one-variable functions $\set {f: \N \to \N}$ is uncountably infinite.

title: Natural Number Less than or Equal to Successor of Another
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $m, n \in \N$ such that $m \le n^+$. Then either: $(1): \quad m \le n$ or: $(2): \quad m = n^+$

title: Natural Number Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: The operation of multiplication is distributive over addition on the set of natural numbers $\N$: $\forall x, y, z \in \N:$ $\paren {x + y} \times z = \paren {x \times z} + \paren {y \times z}$ $z \times \paren {x + y} = \paren {z \times x} + \paren {z \times y}$

title: Natural Number Multiplication by Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Natural Number Multiplication by Addition ==

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Associative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of natural numbers $\N$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \N: \paren {x \times y} \times z = x \times \paren {y \times z}$

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $\times$ be multiplication on $\N$. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in \N_{>0}: x \times z = y \times z \implies x = y$ $\forall x, y, z \in \N_{>0}: x \times y = x \times z \implies y = z$ That is, $\times$ is cancellable on $\N_{>0}$.

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Cancellable for Ordering
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $\times$ be multiplication on $\N$. Let $<$ be the strict ordering on $\N$. Then: $\forall a, b, c \in \N: a \times c < b \times c \implies a < b$ $\forall a, b, c \in \N: a \times b < a \times c \implies b < c$ That is, $\times$ is cancellable on $\N$ for $<$.

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Closed
snippet: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers. Then: $m \times n \in \N$ where $\times$ denotes natural number multiplication.

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of natural numbers $\N$ is commutative: $\forall x, y \in \N: x \times y = y \times x$

title: Natural Number Multiplication is Unique
snippet: Let $\N$ denote the natural numbers. Let $M: \N \times \N \to \N$ be the mapping defined as the multiplication operation: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in \N \times \N: \map M {x, y} = \begin {cases} 0 & : y = 0 \\ \paren {\map M {x, r} } + r & : y = r + 1 \end {cases}$ where $+$ denotes natural number addition. Then $M$ exists and is unique.

title: Natural Number Ordering is Preserved by Successor Mapping
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $m, n \in \N$. Then: $n \le m \implies n^+ \le m^+$

title: Natural Number Ordering is Transitive
snippet: Let $m, n, k \in \N$ where $\N$ is the set of natural numbers. Let $<$ be the relation defined on $\N$ such that: $m < n \iff m \in n$ where $\N$ is defined as the minimally inductive set $\omega$. Then: $k < m, m < n \implies k < n$ That is: $<$ is a transitive relation.

title: Natural Number Power is of Exponential Order Epsilon
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Then: $t \mapsto t^n$ is of exponential order $\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small in magnitude.

title: Natural Number Subtraction is not Closed
snippet: The operation of subtraction on the natural numbers is not closed.

title: Natural Number has Same Prime Factors as Integer Power
snippet: Let $x$ be a natural number such that $x > 1$. Let $n \ge 1$ be a (strictly) positive integer. The $n$th power of $x$ has the same prime factors as $x$.

title: Natural Number is Divisor or Multiple of Divisor of Another
Natural Number is Not Equal to Successor
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers: $\N_{> 0} = \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots}$ Then: $\forall n \in \N_{> 0}: n \ne n + 1$

title: Natural Number is Ordinal
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Then $n$ is an ordinal.

title: Natural Number is Ordinary Set
snippet: Let $n$ be a natural number. Then $n$ is an ordinary set. That is: $n \notin n$

title: Natural Number is Prime or has Prime Factor
snippet: Let $a$ be a natural number greater than $1$. Then either: $a$ is a prime number or: there exists a prime number $p \ne a$ such that $p \divides a$ where $\divides$ denotes is a divisor of.

title: Natural Number is Superset of its Union
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number as defined by the von Neumann construction. Then: $\bigcup n \subseteq n$

title: Natural Number is Transitive Set
snippet: Let $n$ be a natural number. Then $n$ is a transitive set.

title: Natural Number is Union of its Successor
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number as defined by the von Neumann construction. Then: $\map \bigcup {n^+} = n$

title: Natural Number is not Subset of its Union
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number as defined by the von Neumann construction. Then, except in the degenerate case where $n = 0$, it is not the case that: $n \subseteq \bigcup n$

title: Natural Number m is Less than n iff m is an Element of n
snippet: Let $\omega$ be the set of natural numbers defined as the von Neumann construction. Let $m, n \in \omega$. Then: $m < n \iff m \in n$ That is, every natural number is the set of all smaller natural numbers.

title: Natural Number m is Less than n implies n is not Greater than Successor of n
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $m, n \in \N$. Then: $m < n \implies m + 1 \le n$

title: Natural Numbers Bounded Below under Addition form Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $m \in \N$ where $\N$ is the set of natural numbers. Let $M \subseteq \N$ be defined as: $M := \set {x \in \N: x \ge m}$ That is, $M$ is the set of all natural numbers greater than or equal to $m$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {M, +}$ is a commutative semigroup.

title: Natural Numbers Set Equivalent to Ideals of Integers
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of all ideals of $\Z$. Let the mapping $\psi: \N \to S$ be defined as: $\forall b \in \N: \map \psi b = \ideal b$ where $\ideal b$ is the principal ideal of $\Z$ generated by $b$. Then $\psi$ is a bijection.

title: Natural Numbers and Eigenvalues of Pseudo-differential Operator
snippet: The natural numbers $\N$ are eigenvalues of psedo-differential operator (distribution generalization of differential operator with integral kernel), called response or Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda$. Let $\map \Lambda {\map f \theta} = \map g \phi$ be the response pseudo-differential operator on the boundary circle of interior unit disc $D$ for Laplace's equation.

title: Natural Numbers are Comparable
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $m, n \in \N$. Then $m$ and $n$ are comparable by the ordering relation $\le$. That is, either: $(1): \quad m \le n$ or: $(2): \quad n \le m$ or possibly both.

title: Natural Numbers are Infinite
snippet: The set $\N$ of natural numbers is infinite.

title: Natural Numbers are Non-Negative Integers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$. Then: $(1): \quad m \in \N \iff 0 \le m$ $(2): \quad m \in \N_{> 0} \iff 0 0}$ That is, the natural numbers are precisely those integers which are greater than or equal to zero.

title: Natural Numbers as Cardinals
snippet: The natural numbers $\N = \set {0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots}$ can be defined as the set of cardinals.

title: Natural Numbers cannot be Elements of Each Other
snippet: Let $m$ and $n$ be natural numbers. Then it cannot be the case that both $m \in n$ and $n \in m$.

title: Natural Numbers form Commutative Semiring
snippet: The semiring of natural numbers $\struct {\N, +, \times}$ forms a commutative semiring.

title: Natural Numbers form Inductive Set
snippet: Let $\N$ denote the natural numbers as subset of the real numbers $\R$. Then $\N$ is an inductive set.

title: Natural Numbers form Subsemiring of Integers
snippet: The semiring of natural numbers $\struct {\N, +, \times}$ forms a subsemiring of the ring of integers $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$.

title: Natural Numbers have No Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Then for all $m, n \in \N$: $m \times n = 0 \iff m = 0 \lor n = 0$ That is, $\N$ has no proper zero divisors.

title: Natural Numbers under Addition do not form Group
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\N, +}$ consisting of the set of natural numbers $\N$ under addition $+$ is not a group.

title: Natural Numbers under Addition form Commutative Monoid
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\N, +}$ consisting of the set of natural numbers $\N$ under addition $+$ is a commutative monoid whose identity is zero.

title: Natural Numbers under Addition form Commutative Semigroup
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\N, +}$ consisting of the set of natural numbers $\N$ under addition $+$ is a commutative semigroup.

title: Natural Numbers under Addition form Inductive but not Strictly Inductive Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, +}$ denote the algebraic structure consisting of the set of natural numbers $\N$ under addition $+$. Then $\struct {\N, +}$ forms an inductive semigroup, but not a strictly inductive semigroup

title: Natural Numbers under Min Operation forms Total Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, \wedge}$ denote the set of natural numbers $\N$ under the min operation: $\forall a, b \in \N: a \wedge b := \min \set {a, b}$ Then $\struct {\N, \wedge}$ forms a total semilattice.

title: Natural Numbers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\N, \times}$ consisting of the set of natural numbers $\N$ under multiplication $\times$ is not a group.

title: Natural Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of natural numbers under multiplication $\struct {\N, \times}$ is a monoid.

title: Natural Numbers under Multiplication form Ordered Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $\times$ be multiplication. Let $\le$ be the ordering on $\N$. Then $\struct {\N, \times, \le}$ is an ordered commutative semigroup.

title: Natural Numbers under Multiplication form Semigroup
snippet: Let $\N$ be the set of natural numbers. Let $\times$ denote the operation of multiplication on $\N$. The structure $\struct {\N, \times}$ forms a semigroup.

title: Natural Numbers under Multiplication form Subsemigroup of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\N, \times}$ denote the set of natural numbers under multiplication. Let $\struct {\Z, \times}$ denote the set of integers under multiplication. Then $\struct {\N, \times}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {\Z, \times}$.

title: Natural Numbers under Subtraction do not form Magma
snippet: The set of natural numbers $\N$ under the operation of subtraction does not form a magma.

title: Natural Numbers with Extension fulfil Naturally Ordered Semigroup Axioms 1, 3 and 4
Natural Numbers without 1 fulfil Naturally Ordered Semigroup Axioms 1, 2 and 4
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be the subset of the natural numbers defined as: $S = \N \setminus \set 1 = \set {0, 2, 3, 4, \ldots}$ Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {S, +, \le}$ is an ordered semigroup which fulfils the axioms: but: does not fulfil $\struct {S, +}$ is not isomorphic to $\struct {\N, +}$.

title: Naturality of Yoneda Lemma for Covariant Functors
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $\sqbrk {\mathbf C, \mathbf {Set} }$ be the covariant functor category. Let $\mathbf C \times \sqbrk {\mathbf C, \mathbf {Set} }$ be the product category. Let $\mathbf C \times \sqbrk {\mathbf C, \mathbf {Set} } \to \mathbf {Set}: \tuple {A, F} \mapsto \map {\operatorname {Nat} } {h^A, F}$ be the covariant functor defined as the composition of the hom bifunctor and the product of the contravariant Yoneda functor $h^-$ and the identity functor $\operatorname{id}_{\sqbrk {\mathbf C, \mathbf {Set} } }$.

title: Naturally Ordered Semigroup Axioms are Independent
snippet: Consider the naturally ordered semigroup axioms: Each of the naturally ordered semigroup axioms is independent of all the others. That is, you cannot drop any one of them and still uniquely define a naturally ordered semigroup.

title: Naturally Ordered Semigroup Axioms imply Commutativity
snippet: Consider the naturally ordered semigroup axioms: Axioms $\text {NO} 1$, $\text {NO} 2$ and $\text {NO} 3$ together imply the commutativity of the naturally ordered semigroup $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$.

title: Naturally Ordered Semigroup Exists
snippet: Let the Zermelo-Fraenkel axioms be accepted as axiomatic. Then there exists a naturally ordered semigroup.

title: Naturally Ordered Semigroup forms Peano Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $0 \in S$ be the zero of $S$. Let $1 \in S$ be the one of $S$. Let $s: S \to S$ be the mapping defined as: $\map s n := n \circ 1$ Then $\struct {S, 0, s}$ is a Peano structure.

title: Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {S', \circ', \preceq'}$ be naturally ordered semigroups. Let: $0'$ be the smallest element of $S'$ $1'$ be the smallest element of $S' \setminus \set {0'} = S'^*$. Then the mapping $g: S \to S'$ defined as: $\forall a \in S: \map g a = \circ'^a 1'$ is an isomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ to $\struct {S', \circ', \preceq'}$. This isomorphism is unique. Thus, up to isomorphism, there is only one naturally ordered semigroup.

title: Necessary Condition for Existence of BIBD
snippet: Let there exist a BIBD with parameters $v, b, r, k, \lambda$. Then the following are true: $(1): \quad b k = r v$ $(2): \quad \lambda \paren {v - 1} = r \paren {k - 1}$ $(3): \quad b \dbinom k 2 = \lambda \dbinom v 2$ $(4): \quad k \lambda$ All of $v, b, r, k, \lambda$ are integers. Some sources prefer to report $(3)$ as: $b = \dfrac {\dbinom v 2} {\dbinom k 2} \lambda$ which is less appealing visually, and typographically horrendous.

title: Necessary Condition for Existence of Complete Matching
snippet: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph. Let there exist a complete matching on $G$. Then it is a necessary condition for the partite sets of $G$ to have the same number of vertices.

title: Necessary Condition for Standardized Random Variable to have Standard Normal Distribution
snippet: Let $Z$ be the standardized random variable of a random variable $X$: $Z = \dfrac {X - \mu} \sigma$ where: $\mu$ denotes the expectation of $X$ $\sigma$ denotes the standard deviation of $X$. snippet: A Skolem sequence of order $n$ can only exist if $n \equiv 0, 1 \pmod 4$.

title: Necessary Proposition is Strictly Implied by Every Proposition
snippet: Let $P$ be a proposition of modal logic. Let $P$ be necessarily true. Then: $\forall Q: Q \implies P$ where $Q$ is an arbitrary proposition in the universe of discourse.
