title: One Perfect Number for Each Number of Digits
snippet: == Conjecture == There is one perfect number for each number of digits: $1$ digit: $6$ $2$ digits: $28$ $3$ digits: $496$ $4$ digits: $8128$

title: One Plus Reciprocal to the Nth
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as $x_n = \paren {1 + \dfrac 1 n}^n$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to a limit as $n$ increases without bound.

title: One Plus Tangent Half Angle over One Minus Tangent Half Angle
snippet: $\dfrac {1 + \tan \frac x 2} {1 - \tan \frac x 2} = \sec x + \tan x$

snippet: There are $7$ ways $\dfrac 1 7$ can be expressed as a pandigital fraction: $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {2394} {16 \, 758}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {2637} {18 \, 459}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {4527} {31 \, 689}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {5274} {36 \, 918}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {5418} {37 \, 926}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {5976} {41 \, 832}$ $\dfrac 1 7 = \dfrac {7614} {53 \, 298}$

title: One Succeeds Zero in Well-Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be a well-ordered integral domain. Let $0$ and $1$ be the zero and unity respectively of $D$. Then $0$ is the immediate predecessor of $1$: $0 < 1$ $\neg \exists a \in D: 0 < a < 1$

title: One Third as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: There are $2$ ways $\dfrac 1 3$ can be expressed as a pandigital fraction: {{eqn | l = \dfrac 1 3 | r = \dfrac {5823} {17469} }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac 1 3 | r = \dfrac {5832} {17496} }}

title: One Third as Quotient of Sequences of Odd Numbers
snippet: $\dfrac 1 3 = \dfrac {1 + 3} {5 + 7} = \dfrac {1 + 3 + 5} {7 + 9 + 11} = \dfrac {1 + 3 + 5 + 7} {9 + 11 + 13 + 15} = \cdots$ That is: $\forall n \in \Z_{> 0}: \dfrac 1 3 = \dfrac {\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \paren {2 k - 1} } {\ds \sum_{k \mathop = n + 1}^{2 n} \paren {2 k - 1} }$

title: One and Minus One form Subgroup of Multiplicative Group of Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q_{\ne 0}, \times}$ be the multiplicative group of rational numbers. Let $S \subseteq \Q$ where $S = \set {1, -1}$. Then $\struct {S, \times}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\Q_{\ne 0}, \times}$.

title: One is Common Divisor of Integers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Then $1$ is a common divisor of $a$ and $b$.

title: One is not Prime
snippet: The integer $1$ (one) is not a prime number.

title: One of 4 Consecutive Numbers Greater than 11 is Divisible by Prime Greater than 11
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n > 11$. Then at least one of the set: $\set {n, n + 1, n + 2, n + 3}$ is divisible by a prime number greater than $11$.

title: One to Integer Rising is Integer Factorial
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. $1^{\overline n} = n!$ where: $1^{\overline n}$ denotes the rising factorial $n!$ denotes the factorial.

title: Only Number Twice Sum of Digits is 18
snippet: There exists only one (strictly) positive integer that is exactly twice the sum of its digits.

title: Only Number which is Sum of 3 Factors is 6
snippet: The only positive integer which is the sum of exactly $3$ of its distinct coprime divisors is $6$.

title: Open Ball Centred at Origin in Normed Vector Space is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $\map B {0, r}$ be the open ball in $X$ centered at $0$ with radius $r$. Then $\map B {0, r}$ is symmetric.

title: Open Ball Contains Open Ball Less Than Half Its Radius
snippet: == Therorem == Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a, b \in A$. Let $\epsilon, \delta \in \R_{>0}$ such that $\delta \le \dfrac \epsilon 2$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball on $a$. Let $\map {B_\delta} b$ be the open $\delta$-ball on $b$. Let $a \in \map {B_\delta} b$. Then: $\map {B_\delta} b \subseteq \map {B_\epsilon} a$

title: Open Ball contains Smaller Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct{A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon, \delta \in \R_{>0}$ such that $\epsilon \le \delta$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball on $a$. Let $\map {B_\delta} a$ be the open $\delta$-ball on $a$. Then: $\map {B_\epsilon} a \subseteq \map {B_\delta} a$

title: Open Ball contains Strictly Smaller Closed Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon, \delta \in \R_{>0}$ such that $\epsilon < \delta$. Let $\map {B^-_\epsilon} a$ be the closed $\epsilon$-ball on $a$. Let $\map {B_\delta} a$ be the open $\delta$-ball on $a$. Then: $\map {B^-_\epsilon} a \subseteq \map {B_\delta} a$

title: Open Ball in Cartesian Product under Chebyshev Distance
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}, \ldots, M_n = \struct {A_n, d_n}$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i$ be the cartesian product of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$. Let $d_\infty: \AA \times \AA \to \R$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_\infty} {x, y} = \max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {\map {d_i} {x_i, y_i} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. Let $a = \tuple {a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n} \in \AA$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$.

title: Open Ball in Euclidean 3-Space is Interior of Sphere
snippet: Let $\R^3$ be the real Euclidean $3$-space considered as a metric space under the usual metric. Let $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, x_3} \in \R^3$ be a point in $\R^3$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball at $x$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ is the interior of the sphere whose center is $x$ and whose radius is $\epsilon$.

title: Open Ball in Euclidean Plane is Interior of Circle
snippet: Let $\R^2$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2} \in \R^2$ be a point in $\R^2$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball at $x$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ is the interior of the circle whose center is $x$ and whose radius is $\epsilon$.

title: Open Ball in Euclidean Plus Metric is Subset of Equivalent Ball in Euclidean Metric
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $d: \R \times \R \to \R$ be the Euclidean plus metric: $\map d {x, y} := \size {x - y} + \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty 2^{-i} \map \inf {1, \size {\max_{j \mathop \le i} \frac 1 {\size {x - r_j} } - \max_{j \mathop \le i} \frac 1 {\size {y - r_j} } } }$ Let $d': \R \times \R \to \R$ be the Euclidean metric. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} {p; d}$ be an open $\epsilon$-ball of $p$ in $\R$ on $d$. Let $\map {B'_\epsilon} {p; d'}$ be an open $\epsilon$-ball of $p$ in $\R$ on $d'$.

title: Open Ball in Infinite-Dimensional Normed Vector Space is not Weakly Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Suppose that $\dim X = \infty$. Let $\map {B_r} x$ be the open ball in $X$ with radius $r > 0$ and center $x \in X$. Then $\map {B_r} x$ is not weakly open.

title: Open Ball in Normed Division Ring is Open Ball in Induced Metric
Open Ball in Normed Vector Space is Connected
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. An open ball in the metric induced by $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ is connected.

title: Open Ball in Normed Vector Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. An open ball in the metric induced by $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ is path-connected.

title: Open Ball in P-adic Numbers is Closed Ball
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$: Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ Let $\map {B^-_\epsilon} a$ denote the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$. Then: $\forall n \in \Z : \map {B_{p^{-n} } } a = \map {B^-_{p^{-\paren {n + 1} } } } a$

title: Open Ball in Real Number Line is Open Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, d}$ denote the real number line $\R$ with the usual (Euclidean) metric $d$. Let $x \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball at $x$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ is the open interval $\openint {x - \epsilon} {x + \epsilon}$.

title: Open Ball in Real Number Plane under Chebyshev Distance
snippet: Let $\R^2$ be the real number plane. Let $d_\infty: \R^2 \times \R^2 \to \R$ be the Chebyshev Distance on $\R^2$: $\ds \map {d_\infty} {x, y} := \max \set {\size {x_1 - y_1}, \size {x_2 - y_2} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2} \in \R^2$. For $a \in \R^2$, let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball at $a$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ is the interior of the square centered at $a$ and whose sides are of length $2 \epsilon$ parallel to the coordinate axes.

title: Open Ball in Standard Discrete Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $d$ be the standard discrete metric on $M$. Let $a \in A$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} {a; d}$ be an open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Then: $\map {B_\epsilon} {a; d} = \begin {cases} \set a & : \epsilon \le 1 \\ A & : \epsilon > 1 \end {cases}$

title: Open Ball is Convex Set
snippet: Let $V$ be a normed vector space with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. An open ball in the metric induced by $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ is a convex set.

title: Open Ball is Neighborhood of all Points Inside
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ be an open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Let $x \in \map {B_\epsilon} a$. Then $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $M$.

title: Open Ball is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $d: V \times V \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the metric induced by the norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ on $V$. Let $\tau$ be the the topology on $V$ induced by the metric $d$. Let $v \in V$ and $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} v$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball of $v$. Let $\tau_B$ be the subspace topology on $\map {B_\epsilon} v$ induced by $\tau$. Then $\struct{ \map {B_\epsilon} v, \tau_B }$ is simply connected.

title: Open Ball is Subset of Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x, y$ be points of $A$. Then: $\epsilon-\delta \ge \map d {x, y} \implies \map {B_\delta} y \subseteq \map {B_\epsilon} x$ where $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ denotes the open $\epsilon$-ball in $M = \struct {A, d}$.

title: Open Ball of Metric Space/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Open Balls of Metric Spaces ==

title: Open Ball of Point Inside Open Ball
Open Ball with respect to Seminorm is Convex, Balanced and Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Let $d_p$ be the pseudometric induced by $p$. Let $B$ be the open unit ball in $\struct {X, d_p}$. That is: $B = \set {x \in X : \map p x < 1}$ Then $B$ is convex, balanced and absorbing.

title: Open Balls form Basis for Open Sets of Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\BB$ be the set of all open balls of $M$. Then $\BB$ is a basis for the open sets of $M$.

title: Open Balls form Local Basis for Point of Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x \in A$. Let $\BB_x$ be the set of all open balls of $M$ centered on $x$. That is: $\BB_x = \set {\map {B_\epsilon} x : \epsilon \in \R_{>0}}$ Then $\BB$ is a local basis of $x$.

title: Open Balls form Local Basis of Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\tau$ be the topology on $M$ induced by $d$. Let $x \in X$. For each $\epsilon > 0$, let $\map {B_\epsilon} x$ be the open $\epsilon$-ball around $x$. Let $\BB_x = \set {\map {B_\epsilon} x : \epsilon > 0}$. Then $\BB_x$ is a local basis at $x$.

title: Open Balls of P-adic Number
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$, let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open ball of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. Then: $\forall n \in Z : \map {B_{p^{-n} } } a = a + p^{n + 1} \Z_p$

title: Open Balls of Same Radius form Open Cover
Open Balls of Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions on Closed Interval
snippet: Let $\mathscr C \closedint a b$ be the set of all continuous functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$. Let $d: \mathscr C^2 \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $\mathscr C \closedint a b$ defined as: $\ds \forall f, g \in \mathscr C \closedint a b: \map d {f, g} := \sup_{x \mathop \in \closedint a b} \size {\map f x - \map g x}$ where $\sup$ denotes the supremum. Let $f, g \in \mathscr C \closedint a b$ be such that: $\forall x \in \closedint a b: \map f x 0}: \map g x := \map f x + c$ That is, $f$ and $g$ differ by a constant.

title: Open Balls on Rational Centers form Basis for Usual Topology on Plane
snippet: Let $\R^2$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $S$ be the set defined as: $S = \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: x, y \in \Q}$ That is, let $S$ be the set of all points in $\R^2$ whose coordinates are rational numbers. Let $\BB$ denote the set defined as: $\BB = \set {\map {B_q} s: s \in S, q \in \Q}$ That is, let $\BB$ be the set of all open $q$-balls with centers in $S$ and rational radius. Then $\BB$ forms a basis for $\R^2$.

title: Open Balls whose Distance between Centers is Twice Radius are Disjoint
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $x, y \in A$ such that $\map d {x, y} = 2 r > 0$. Let $\map {B_r} x$ denote the open $r$-ball of $x$ in $M$. Then $\map {B_r} x$ and $\map {B_r} y$ are disjoint.

title: Open Continuous Image of Paracompact Space is not always Countably Metacompact
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {X_A, \tau_A}$ be a topological space which is paracompact. Let $T_B = \struct {X_B, \tau_B}$ be another topological space. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a mapping which is both continuous and open. Then it is not necessarily even the case that $T_B$ is countably metacompact, let alone paracompact.

title: Open Continuous Injection is Embedding
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be an open and continuous injection. Then $f$ is an embedding of $T_1$ into $T_2$.

title: Open Convex Set in Hausdorff Locally Convex Space is Separated from Points outside Set by Continuous Linear Functional
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a Hausdorff locally convex space over $\GF$ equipped with its standard topology. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual of $X$. Let $C$ be an open convex set such that ${\mathbf 0}_X \in C$. Let $x_0 \in X \setminus C$. Then there exists $f \in X^\ast$ such that: $\map \Re {\map f x} < \map \Re {\map f {x_0} }$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Open Cover may not have Lebesgue Number
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\CC$ be an open cover of $M$. Then it may not necessarily be the case that $\CC$ has a Lebesgue number.

title: Open Cover with Closed Locally Finite Refinement is Even Cover
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological Space. Let $\UU$ be an open cover of $T$ with a closed locally finite refinement. Then: $\UU$ is an even cover.

title: Open Domain is Connected iff it is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be a open subset of the set of complex numbers. Then $D$ is connected $D$ is path-connected.

title: Open Extension Space is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is a compact space.

title: Open Extension Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is a connected space.

title: Open Extension Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is path-connected.

title: Open Extension Space is Ultraconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is ultraconnected.

title: Open Extension Topology is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Open Extension Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\tau^*_{\bar p}$ be the open extension topology of $\tau$. Then $\tau^*_{\bar p}$ is a topology on $S^*_p = S \cup \set p$.

title: Open Extension Topology is not Perfectly T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is not a perfectly $T_4$ space.

title: Open Extension Topology is not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is not a $T_1$ space.

title: Open Extension Topology is not T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T^*_{\bar p} = \struct {S^*_p, \tau^*_{\bar p} }$ be the open extension space of $T$. Then $T^*_{\bar p}$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Open Extension of Double Pointed Countable Complement Topology is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be a countable complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Let $D = \struct {\set {0, 1}, \tau_D}$ be the indiscrete topology on two points. Let $T \times D$ be the double pointed topology on $T$. Let $\paren {T \times D}^*_{\bar p}$ be the open extension topology on $S \times \set {0, 1} \cup \set p$ where $p \notin S \times \set {0, 1}$. Then $\paren {T \times D}^*_{\bar p}$ is a $T_4$ space, and no other separation axioms are fulfilled. That is, $\paren {T \times D}^*_{\bar p}$ is not a $T_0$ space, $T_1$ space, $T_2$ space, $T_3$ space or $T_5$ space.

title: Open Extension of Non-Trivial Particular Point Space is T0
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space such that $S$ is not a singleton or a doubleton. Let $T^*_{\bar q} = \struct {S^*_q, \tau^*_{\bar q} }$ be an open extension space of $T$. $T^*_{\bar q}$ is a $T_0$ space.

title: Open Extension of Non-Trivial Particular Point Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space such that $S$ is not a singleton or a doubleton. Let $T^*_{\bar q} = \struct {S^*_q, \tau^*_{\bar q} }$ be an open extension space of $T$. $T^*_{\bar q}$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Open Extension of Non-Trivial Particular Point Space is not T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space such that $S$ is not a singleton or a doubleton. Let $T^*_{\bar q} = \struct {S^*_q, \tau^*_{\bar q} }$ be an open extension space of $T$. $T^*_{\bar q}$ is not a $T_1$ space.

title: Open Extension of Non-Trivial Particular Point Space is not T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space such that $S$ is not a singleton or a doubleton. Let $T^*_{\bar q} = \struct {S^*_q, \tau^*_{\bar q} }$ be an open extension space of $T$. $T^*_{\bar q}$ is not a $T_5$ space.

title: Open Interval Defined by Absolute Value
snippet: Let $\xi, \delta \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $\delta > 0$. Then: $\set {x \in \R: \size {\xi - x} < \delta} = \openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ where $\openint {\xi - \delta} {\xi + \delta}$ is the open real interval between $\xi - \delta$ and $\xi + \delta$.

title: Open Mapping is not necessarily Closed Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T_1 \to T_2$ be a mapping which is not a bijection. Let $f$ be an open mapping. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f$ is also a closed mapping.

title: Open Neighborhood contains Affine Open Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ be a scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset. Let $x \in U$. Then there exists an open subset $V \subset U$ with $x \in V$, such that the restriction $\struct {V, \OO_X {\restriction_V}}$ of $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ to $V$ is an affine scheme.

title: Open Neighborhood of Dilation of Point in Topological Vector Space contains Pointwise Scalar Multiplication of Open Neighborhood of Scalar with Open Neighborhood of Vector
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\lambda \in K$ and $x \in X$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $\lambda x$. Then there exists an open neighborhood $D$ of $\lambda$ in $K$ and an open neighborhood $V$ in $X$ such that: $D V \subseteq U$ where: $D V = \set {\mu y : \mu \in D, \, y \in V}$

title: Open Neighborhood of Element of Set with no Limit Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ which has no limit points in $T$. Let $x \in H$ be an arbitrary point of $H$. Then there exists an open neighborhood $\NN_x$ of $x$ such that: $\NN_x \cap H = \set x$

title: Open Neighborhood of Origin in Topological Vector Space contains Balanced Open Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let ${\mathbf 0}_X$ be the origin of $X$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Then there exists a balanced open neighborhood $W$ of ${\mathbf 0}_X$ with $W \subseteq U$.

title: Open Neighborhood of Origin in Topological Vector Space is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $U$ is absorbing.

title: Open Neighborhood of Point in Topological Vector Space contains Sum of Open Neighborhoods
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $a, b \in X$. Let $W$ be an open neighborhood of $a + b$. Then there exists an open neighborhood $W_1$ of $a$ and an open neighborhood $W_2$ of $b$ such that: $W_1 + W_2 \subseteq W$ where $W_1 + W_2$ denotes the sum of $W_1$ and $W_2$.

title: Open Neighborhoods of Point form Directed Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct{ S, \tau }$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\NN \subseteq \tau$ be the set of open neighborhoods of $x$. Then $\supseteq$, the ordering of $\NN$ by reverse inclusion, is a directed ordering on $\NN$.

title: Open Ordinal Space is not Compact Space
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be a limit ordinal. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Consider the compact subspace $\hointr 0 \Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ is not compact in $\closedint 0 \Gamma$.

title: Open Projection and Closed Graph Implies Quotient is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq X \times X$ be an equivalence relation on a topological space $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $X / \RR$ be the quotient space. Let $p$ denote the quotient mapping. Let: $\RR$ be closed in $X \times X$ $p$ be an open mapping. Then $X / \RR$ is Hausdorff.

title: Open Rational-Number Balls form Neighborhood Basis in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $\BB_a$ be defined as: $\BB_a := \set {\map {B_\epsilon} a: \epsilon \in \Q_{>0} }$ that is, the set of all open $\epsilon$-balls of $a$ for rational $\epsilon$. Then the $\BB_a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

title: Open Ray is Dual to Open Ray
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $R$ be an open ray in $\struct {S, \preceq}$. Then $R$ is an open ray in $\struct {S, \succeq}$, where $\succeq$ is the dual ordering of $\preceq$.

title: Open Ray is Open in GO-Space
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq, \tau}\right)$ be a generalized ordered space. Let $p \in S$. Then: $p^\prec$ and $p^\succ$ are $\tau$-open where: $p^\prec$ is the strict lower closure of $p$ $p^\succ$ is the strict upper closure of $p$.

title: Open Real Interval/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Open Real Intervals ==

title: Open Real Interval is Homeomorphic to Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the Euclidean topology. Let $I := \openint a b$ be a non-empty open real interval. Then $I$ and $\R$ are homeomorphic.

title: Open Real Interval is Open Ball
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $I := \openint a b \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Then $I$ is the open $\epsilon$-ball $\map {B_\epsilon} \alpha$ of some $\alpha \in \R$.

title: Open Real Interval is Open Set
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $\openint a b \subset \R$ be an open interval of $\R$. Then $\openint a b$ is an open set of $\R$.

title: Open Real Interval is Regular Open
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\openint a b$ be an open interval of $\R$. Then $\openint a b$ is regular open in $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$.

title: Open Real Interval is Subset of Closed Real Interval
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ be real numbers. Then: $\openint a b \subseteq \closedint a b$ where: $\openint a b$ is the open interval between $a$ and $b$ $\closedint a b$ is the closed interval between $a$ and $b$.

title: Open Real Interval is not Closed Set
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $I = \openint a b$ be an open real interval. Then $I$ is not a closed set of $\R$.

title: Open Real Interval is not Compact
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $I = \openint a b$ be an open real interval. Then $I$ is not compact.

title: Open Real Interval is not Homeomorphic to Half-Open Real Interval
snippet: Let $I_o$ denote the open real interval $\openint 0 1$. Let $I_h$ denote the half-open real interval $\hointl 0 1$. Then $I_o$ and $I_h$ are not homeomorphic.

title: Open Real Intervals are Homeomorphic
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the Euclidean topology. Let $I_1 := \openint a b$ and $I_2 := \openint c d$ be non-empty open real intervals. Then $I_1$ and $I_2$ are homeomorphic.

title: Open Reciprocal-N Balls form Neighborhood Basis in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $\BB_a$ be defined as: $\BB_a := \set {\map {B_\epsilon} a: \epsilon \in \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \N} }$ that is, the set of all open $\epsilon$-balls of $a$ for $\epsilon$ which are reciprocals of integers. Then $\BB_a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

title: Open Rectangles Closed under Intersection
snippet: Let $\paren {\openint {\mathbf a} {\mathbf b} }$ and $\paren {\openint {\mathbf c} {\mathbf d} }$ be open $n$-rectangles. Then $\paren {\openint {\mathbf a} {\mathbf b} } \cap \paren {\openint {\mathbf c} {\mathbf d} }$ is also an open $n$-rectangle.

title: Open Region/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Open Regions ==

title: Open Set/Complex Analysis/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Open Sets in the context of Complex Analysis ==

title: Open Set Characterization of Denseness
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $S \subseteq X$. Then $S$ is (everywhere) dense in $X$ every non-empty ($\tau$-)open set contains an element of $S$.

title: Open Set Disjoint from Set is Disjoint from Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $B$ be an open set of $T$ disjoint from $A$. Then: $A^- \cap B = \O$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$.

title: Open Set Less One Point is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $U \subseteq M$ be an open set of $M$. Let $\alpha \in U$. Then $U \setminus \set \alpha$ is open in $M$.

title: Open Set Not in System of Open Neighborhoods Iff Subset of Complement of Singleton Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map \UU x$ denote the system of open neighborhoods of $x$. Let $\set x^-$ denote the topological closure of $\set x$. Then for all $U \in \tau$: $U \notin \map \UU x$ $U \subseteq S \setminus \set x^-$

title: Open Set in Initial Topology on Vector Space Induced by Linear Functionals
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $E$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $E^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $E$. Let $F \subseteq E^\#$ be a vector subspace. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $E$ induced by $F$. Let $U \subseteq E$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X, \tau}$ for each $x \in X$ there exists $\epsilon > 0$ and $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in F$ such that: $\set {y \in X : \cmod {\map {f_i} x - \map {f_i} y} < \epsilon \text { for each } 1 \le i \le n} \subseteq U$

title: Open Set in Open Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct{X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T_U = \struct{U, \tau_U}$ be a subspace of $T$ where $U \subseteq X$ is open. Let $V \subseteq U$ be a subset. Then $V$ is open in $T_U$ $V$ is open in $T$.

title: Open Set in Partition Topology is Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a partition topological space. Then each of its open sets is a component of $T$.

title: Open Set in Quotient Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $N$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\tau_N$ be the quotient topology on $X/N$. Let $U \subseteq X/N$. Then we have $U \in \tau_N$ there exists $V \in \tau$ such that $U = \pi \sqbrk V$.

title: Open Set in T3 Space is Union of Regular Open Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space. Then every open set of $T$ can be expressed as the union of regular open sets.

title: Open Set is G-Delta Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U$ be an open set of $T$. Then $U$ is a $G_\delta$ set of $T$.

title: Open Set is Union of Elements of Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $B$ be a basis of $T$. Let $V$ be an open subset of $S$. Then $V = \bigcup \set {G \in B: G \subseteq V}$

title: Open Set may not be Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $U \subseteq M$ be an open set of $M$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $U$ is an open ball of some $x \in A$.

title: Open Set minus Closed Set is Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. For $A \subseteq S$ denote by $\relcomp S A$ the relative complement of $A$ in $S$. Let $U \in \tau$ and $\relcomp S V \in \tau$. Then: $U \setminus V \in \tau$ and: $\relcomp S {V \setminus U} \in \tau$

title: Open Set of Irreducible Space is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an irreducible topological space. Let $U$ be a non-empty open set of $T$. Then $U$ is irreducible in its induced subspace topology.

title: Open Set of Uncountable Finite Complement Topology is not F-Sigma
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an uncountable set $S$. Let $U \in \tau$ be an open set of $T$. Then $U$ is not an $F_\sigma$ set.

title: Open Sets in Indiscrete Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. $H$ is an open set of $T$ either $H = S$ or $H = \O$.

title: Open Sets in Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Then $\O$ and $A$ are both open in $M$.

title: Open Sets in Pseudometric Space
snippet: Let $P = \struct {A, d}$ be a pseudometric space. Then $\O$ and $A$ are both open in $P$.

title: Open Sets in Real Number Line
snippet: Every non-empty open set $I \subseteq \R$ can be expressed as a countable union of pairwise disjoint open intervals. If: $\ds I = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} J_n$ $\ds I = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} K_n$ are two such expressions, then there exists a permutation $\sigma$ of $\N$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: J_n = K_{\map \sigma n}$

title: Open Sets in Standard Topology of Locally Convex Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$. Let $\tau$ be the standard topology on $\struct {X, \PP}$. Let $U \subseteq X$. Then $U \in \tau$ for each $x \in U$ there exists $n \in \N$, $p_1, \ldots, p_n \in \PP$ and $\epsilon > 0$ such that: $\set {y \in X : \map {p_k} {y - x} < \epsilon \text { for each } 1 \le k \le n} \subseteq U$

title: Open Sets in Vector Spaces with Equivalent Norms Coincide
snippet:
Let $M_a = \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a}$ and $M_b = \struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $U \subseteq X$ be an open set in $M_a$. Suppose, $
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a$ and $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b$ are equivalent norms, i.e. $
orm {\, \cdot \, }_a \sim 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_b$. Then $U$ is also open in $M_b$.

title: Open Sets in Weak-* Topology of Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Let $U \subseteq X$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ for each $f \in X^\ast$ there exists $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in X$ and $\epsilon > 0$ such that: $\set {g \in X^\ast : \cmod {\map f {x_i} - \map g {x_i} } < \epsilon \text { for each } 1 \le i \le n}$

title: Open Sets in Weak Topology of Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Let $U \subseteq X$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X, w}$ for each $x \in U$ there exists $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n \in X^\ast$ and $\epsilon > 0$ such that: $\set {y \in X : \cmod {\map {f_i} {y - x} } < \epsilon \text { for each } 1 \le i \le n} \subseteq U$

title: Open Sets of Cartesian Product of Metric Spaces under Chebyshev Distance
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}, M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}, \ldots, M_n = \struct {A_n, d_n}$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i$ be the cartesian product of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$. Let $d_\infty: \AA \times \AA \to \R$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_\infty} {x, y} = \max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {\map {d_i} {x_i, y_i} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. For $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$, let $U_i$ be open in $M_i$. Then $\ds \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n U_i$ is open in $M = \struct {\AA, d_\infty}$.

title: Open Sets of Double Pointed Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_S}$ be a topological space. Let $D$ be a doubleton endowed with the indiscrete topology. Let $\struct {S \times D, \tau}$ be the double pointed topology on $S$. Then $X \subseteq S \times D$ is open in $\tau$ for some $U \in \tau$: $X = U \times D$

title: Open Sets of Overlapping Interval Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the overlapping interval space. Then the open sets of $T$ are of the form: {{axiom | n = 2 | m = \hointr {-1} b | rc= where $0 < b \le 1$ }} {{axiom | n = 4 | m = \O \text { and } \closedint {-1} 1 | rc= }}

title: Open Star Convex Set Minus Countable Set is Path-Connected in Real Euclidean Space
snippet: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number. Let $A \subset \R^k$ be a star convex set, with star center $a \in A$. Let $G \subset \R^k$ be finite or countable. Suppose $a \notin G$. Then $A \setminus G$ is path-connected.

title: Open Statement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Open Statements ==

title: Open Subgroup is Closed
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $H\leq G$ be an open subgroup. Then $H$ is closed.

title: Open Subscheme is Scheme
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ be a scheme. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset. Then the open subscheme $\struct {U, \OO_X {\restriction U}}$ defined by $U$ is a scheme.

title: Open Subset is Lower Section in Lower Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a transitive relational structure with lower topology. Let $A \subseteq S$ such that $A$ is open. Then $A$ is a lower section of $S$.

title: Open Subset of Locally Compact Hausdorff Space is Locally Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be open. Let $\tau_Y$ be the subspace topology on $Y$ inherited from $\struct {X, \tau_X}$. Then $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space.

title: Open Subset of Locally Connected Space is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a locally connected topological space. Let $U \subseteq S$ be open in $T$. Then $U$ is locally connected.

title: Open Subset of Locally Path-Connected Space is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a locally path-connected topological space. Let $U \subset S$ be open in $T$. Then $U$ is locally path-connected in $T$.

title: Open Subspace of Polish Space is Polish Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a Polish space. Let $d$ be a metric on $X$ that induces $\tau$ and is such that $\struct {X, d}$ is a complete metric space. Let $U \subseteq X$ be open. Let $\tau_U$ be the subspace topology on $U$ induced by $\tau$. Then $\struct {U, \tau_U}$ is a Polish space.

title: Open Superset is Open Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U \in \tau$ be an open set of $T$. Let $H \subseteq U$. Then $U$ is an open neighborhood of $H$.

title: Open Unit Interval is Proper Subset of Closed Unit Interval
snippet: The open unit interval: $I_o = \openint 0 1$ is a proper subset of the closed unit interval: $I_c = \closedint 0 1$

title: Open Unit Interval on Rational Number Space is Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then: $\openint 0 1 \cap \Q$ is totally bounded in $T$ where $\openint 0 1$ is the open unit interval.

title: Open Unit Interval on Rational Number Space is not Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Then: $\openint 0 1 \cap \Q$ is not compact in $T$ where $\openint 0 1$ is the open unit interval.

title: Open and Closed Balls in P-adic Numbers are Clopen in P-adic Metric
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $n \in \Z$. Then the open ball $\map {B_{p^{-n}}} a$ and closed ball $\map {B^-_{p^{-n}}} a$ are clopen in the $p$-adic metric.

title: Open and Closed Balls in P-adic Numbers are Compact Subspaces
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $n \in \Z$. Then the open ball $\map {B_{p^{-n} } } a$ and closed ball $\map {B^-_{p^{-n}}} a$ are compact.

title: Open and Closed Balls in P-adic Numbers are Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $n \in \Z$. Then the open ball $\map {B_{p^{-n} } } a$ and closed ball $\map {B^-_{p^{-n} } } a$ are totally bounded subspaces.

title: Open and Closed Sets in Indiscrete Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$.

title: Open and Closed Sets in Multiple Pointed Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a finite set whose cardinality is greater than $1$. Let $D = \struct {A, \set {\O, A} }$ be the indiscrete space on $A$. Let $T \times D$ be a multiple pointed topological space generated from $T$ and $D$. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then: $H \times A$ is open in $T \times D$ $H$ is open in $T$ $H \times A$ is closed in $T \times D$ $H$ is closed in $T$ $H \times \O$ is both open and closed in $T \times D$ Let $\O \subsetneqq H_A \subsetneqq A$, that is, let $H_A$ be a non-empty proper subset of $A$.

title: Open and Closed Sets in Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $S$ and $\O$ are both both open and closed in $T$.

title: Open iff Upper and with Property (S) in Scott Topological Lattice
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be an up-complete topological lattice. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then $A$ is open $A$ is upper and with property (S).

title: Open implies There Exists Way Below Element
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a continuous topological lattice with Scott topology. Let $p \in S, A \subseteq S$ such that: $A$ is open and $p \in A$. Then: $\exists q \in A: q \ll p$ where $q \ll p$ denotes $q$ is way below $p$.

title: Openness Relation on Topological Spaces is Transitive
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space Let $S_2 \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $S_3 \subseteq S_2$ be a subset of $S_2$. Let $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be the topological subspace of $T_1$ such that $\tau_2$ is the subspace topology induced by $\tau_1$. Let $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be the topological subspace of $T_2$ such that $\tau_3$ is the subspace topology induced by $\tau_2$. Let: $S_2$ be an open set of $T_1$ $S_3$ be an open set of $T_2$. Then: $S_3$ is an open set of $T_1$.

title: Operand is Upper Bound of Way Below Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $x$ is upper bound for $x^\ll$ where $x^\ll$ denotes the way below closure of $x$.

title: Operating on Ordered Group Inequalities
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $\prec$ be the reflexive reduction of $\preceq$. Let $x, y, z, w \in \struct {G, \circ, \preceq}$. Then the following implications hold: If $x \prec y$ and $z \prec w$, then $x \circ z \prec y \circ w$. If $x \prec y$ and $z \preccurlyeq w$, then $x \circ z \prec y \circ w$. If $x \preccurlyeq y$ and $z \prec w$, then $x \circ z \prec y \circ w$. If $x \preccurlyeq y$ and $z \preccurlyeq w$, then $x \circ z \preccurlyeq y \circ w$.

title: Operating on Transitive Relationships Compatible with Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\RR$ be a transitive relation on $S$ which is compatible with $\circ$. Let $\RR^=$ be the reflexive closure of $\RR$. Let $x, y, z, w \in S$. Then the following implications hold: $(1): \quad$ If $x \mathrel \RR y$ and $z \mathrel \RR w$, then $x \circ z \mathrel \RR y \circ w$. $(2): \quad$ If $x \mathrel \RR y$ and $z \mathrel {\RR^=} w$, then $x \circ z \mathrel \RR y \circ w$. $(3): \quad$ If $x \mathrel {\RR^=} y$ and $z \mathrel \RR w$, then $x \circ z \mathrel \RR y \circ w$.

title: Operation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Operations ==

title: Operation Induced by Permutation on Magma is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\circ_\sigma$ be the operation on $S$ induced by $\sigma$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\circ_\sigma$ is closed on $S$

title: Operation Induced by Permutation on Semigroup is not necessarily Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\circ_\sigma$ be the operation on $S$ induced by $\sigma$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\circ_\sigma$ is not necessarily associative on $S$.

title: Operation is Isomorphic to Power Structure Operation on Set of Singleton Subsets
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $S'$ denote the set of singleton elements of $\powerset S$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {S', \circ_\PP}$.

title: Operation is Left Operation iff Anticommutative with Right Cancellable Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an semigroup. Then: $\circ$ is the left operation $\circ$ is anticommutative and has a right cancellable element.

title: Operation is Right Operation iff Anticommutative with Left Cancellable Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then: $\circ$ is the right operation $\circ$ is anticommutative and has a left cancellable element.

title: Operation on Set for which Every Equivalence Relation is Congruence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with at least $3$ elements. Let $\circ$ be an operation on $S$ such that every equivalence relation on $S$ is a congruence relation for $\circ$. Then $\circ$ is one of the following: the right operation $\to$ the left operation $\gets$ the constant operation $\sqbrk c$ for some $c \in S$.

title: Operation on Structure of Cardinality 4+ where Every Permutation is Automorphism is Left or Right Operation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is at least $4$. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure on $S$ such that every permutation on $S$ is an automorphism on $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\circ$ is either the left operation or the right operation.

title: Operation over which Every Commutative Associative Operation is Distributive is either Left or Right Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be such that every operation on $S$ which is both commutative and associative is distributive over $\circ$. Then $\circ$ is either the left operation $\gets$ or the right operation $\to$.

title: Operation which is Left Distributive over Every Commutative Associative Operation is Right Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ have the property that: for every arbitrary operation $*$ on $S$ which is both commutative and associative, $\circ$ is left distributive over $*$. Then $\circ$ is the right operation $\to$: $\forall a, b \in S: a \to b = b$

title: Operation which is Right Distributive over Every Commutative Associative Operation is Left Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ have the property that: for every arbitrary operation $*$ on $S$ which is both commutative and associative, $\circ$ is right distributive over $*$. Then $\circ$ is the left operation $\gets$: $\forall a, b \in S: a \gets b = a$

title: Operations of Boolean Algebra are Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \neg}$ be a Boolean algebra, defined as in Definition 1. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c \in S | l = \paren {a \wedge b} \wedge c | r = a \wedge \paren {b \wedge c} }} {{eqn | q = \forall a, b, c \in S | l = \paren {a \vee b} \vee c | r = a \vee \paren {b \vee c} }} That is, both $\vee$ and $\wedge$ are associative operations.

title: Operations of Boolean Algebra are Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge}$ be a Boolean algebra. Then: $\forall x \in S: x \wedge x = x = x \vee x$ That is, both $\vee$ and $\wedge$ are idempotent operations.

title: Operations with Identities which Distribute over each other are Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\odot$ and $\otimes$ be operations on $S$ which have identity elements $e$ and $u$ respectively. Let $\odot$ and $\otimes$ be distributive over each other. Then $\odot$ and $\otimes$ are both idempotent.

title: Operator/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Operator == Examples of operator include: the differentiation operator: $\dfrac \d {\d x}$ the square root operator: $\sqrt {\ \ }$

title: Operator Commuting with Diagonalizable Operator
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\ds A = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} \alpha_i P_i$ be a diagonalizable operator on $H$. Let $B \in \map B H$ be a bounded linear operator. {{item|(2):|For all $i \in I$, $\Rng {P_i}$ is a reducing subspace for $B$}} where $\Rng {P_i}$ denotes range.

title: Operator Diagonalizable iff Basis of Eigenvectors
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A: \HH \to \HH$ be a linear operator on $\HH$. Then $A$ is diagonalizable there exists a basis $E$ of $\HH$, consisting of eigenvectors for $A$.

title: Operator Generated by Closure System Preserves Directed Suprema iff Closure System Inherits Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {X, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $S = \struct {Y, \precsim}$ be a closure system on $L$. Then $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S$ preserves directed suprema $S$ inherits directed suprema. where $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S$ denotes the operator generated by $S$.

title: Operator Generated by Closure System is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $L = \left({X, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Let $S = \left({T, \precsim}\right)$ be a closure system of $L$. Then $\operatorname{operator}\left({S}\right)$ is closure operator, where $\operatorname{operator}\left({S}\right)$ denotes the operator generated by $S$.

title: Operator Generated by Image of Closure Operator is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $c: S \to S$ be a closure operator on $L$. Then $\map {\operatorname {operator} } {\struct {c \sqbrk S, \precsim} } = c$ where $\mathord \precsim = \mathord \preceq \cap \paren {c \sqbrk S \times c \sqbrk S}$ $\map {\operatorname {operator} } {\struct {c \sqbrk S, \precsim} }$ denotes the operator generated by $\struct {c \sqbrk S, \precsim}$

title: Operator Norm of Quotient Mapping in Quotient Normed Vector Space is 1
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\struct {X/N, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N} }$ be the normed quotient vector space associated with quotient vector space $X/N$. Let $\pi : X 	o X/N$ be the quotient mapping associated with $X/N$. Then: $
orm \pi_{\map B {X, X/N} } = 1$ where $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {X, X/N} }$ denotes the norm on the space of bounded linear transformations.

title: Operator Zero iff Inner Product Zero
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $A: \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Then: $\forall h \in \HH: \innerprod {A h} h_\HH = 0$ $A$ is the zero operator.

title: Operator is Hermitian iff Numerical Range is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $A : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map W A$ be the numerical range of $A$. Then $A$ is Hermitian : $\map W A \subseteq \R$ That is: $\forall h \in \HH: \innerprod {A h} h_\HH \mathop \in \R$

title: Operator is Normal iff Operator Minus Multiple of Identity Operator is Normal
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\mathbf T: \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\lambda$ be a scalar under $\HH$. Let $\mathbf I$ be the identity operator. Then $\mathbf T$ is normal $\mathbf T - \lambda \mathbf I$ is normal.

title: Operator of Integrated Weighted Derivatives is Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\map {a_i} x : I \to \R$ be Riemann integrable functions. Let $f, g \in \map {C^n} I$ be Riemann integrable real-valued functions of differentiability class $k$. Let $L : \map {C^n} I \to \R$ be the operator of integrated weighted derivatives. Then $L$ is a linear mapping.

title: Operator with Zero Numerical Range is Zero Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the inner product norm on $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator on $\HH$ such that: $\map W T = \set 0$ where $\map W T$ is the numerical range of $T$. Then $T = 0$.

title: Opposite Angles of Cyclic Quadrilateral sum to Two Right Angles
Opposite Group is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be the opposite group to $G$. Then $\struct {G, *}$ is a group.

title: Opposite Group of Opposite Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {G, *}$ be the opposite group to $\struct {G, \circ}$. Let $\struct {G, \circ'}$ be the opposite group to $\struct {G, *}$. Then: $\struct {G, \circ} = \struct {G, \circ'}$

title: Opposite Planes of Solid contained by Parallel Planes are Equal Parallelograms
Opposite Ring is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R, +, *}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +, \times}$. Then $\struct {R, +, *}$ is a ring.

title: Opposite Ring of Opposite Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R, +, *}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +, \times}$. Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +, *}$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ} = \struct {R, +, \times}$.

title: Opposite Sides Equal implies Parallelogram
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB = CD$ and $BC = AD$. Then $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

title: Opposite Sides and Angles of Parallelogram are Equal
snippet: The opposite sides and angles of a parallelogram are equal to one another, and either of its diameters bisects its area.

title: Opposites Theorem
snippet: {{eqn | l = \map \sin {-\theta} | r = -\sin \theta }} {{eqn | l = \map \cos {-\theta} | r = \cos \theta }} {{eqn | l = \map \tan {-\theta} | r = -\tan \theta }}

title: Optimal Strategy for Fibonacci Nim
snippet: Consider a game of Fibonacci nim with $n$ counters. Let it be the turn of player $\text A$. Let the maximum number of counters that can be taken by $\text A$ be $q$. Let $n$ be expressed in Zeckendorf representation as: $n = F_{k_1} + F_{k_2} + \cdots + F_{k_r}$ Then $\text A$ can force a win : $F_{k_r} \le q$ and by taking those $F_{k_r}$ counters.

title: Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a group which acts on a finite set $X$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\Orb x$ denote the orbit of $x$. Let $\Stab x$ denote the stabilizer of $x$ by $G$. Let $\index G {\Stab x}$ denote the index of $\Stab x$ in $G$. Then: $\order {\Orb x} = \index G {\Stab x} = \dfrac {\order G} {\order {\Stab x} }$

title: Orbit of Conjugacy Action on Subgroup is Set of Conjugate Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $X$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Let $*$ be the conjugacy action on $H$ defined as: $\forall g \in G, H \in X: g * H = g \circ H \circ g^{-1}$ Then the orbit $\Orb H$ of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is the set of subgroups of $G$ conjugate to $H$.

title: Orbit of Dynamical System/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orbits of Dynamical Systems ==

title: Orbit of Element of Group Acting on Itself is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*$ be the group action of $\struct {G, \circ}$ on itself by the rule: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h$ Then the orbit of an element $x \in G$ is given by: $\Orb x = G$

title: Orbit of Element under Conjugacy Action is Conjugacy Class
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*$ be the conjugacy group action on $G$: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h \circ g^{-1}$ Let $x \in G$. Then the orbit of $x$ under this group action is: $\Orb x = \conjclass x$ where $\conjclass x$ is the conjugacy class of $x$.

title: Orbit of Group Action on Subgroup by Right Regular Representation is Right Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a proper subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the group action defined as: $\forall \tuple {h, g} \in H \times G: h * g = \map {\rho_{h^{-1} } } g$ where $\map {\rho_{h^{-1} } } g$ is the right regular representation of $g$ by $h^{-1}$. Let $x \in G$. Then the orbit of $x$ under $*$ is given by: $\forall x \in G: \Orb x = H x$ where $H x$ is the right coset of $H$ by $x$.

title: Orbit of Subgroup Action is Coset
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the subgroup action defined for all $h \in H, g \in G$ as: $\forall h \in H, g \in G: h * g := h \circ g$ The orbit of $x \in G$ is the right coset by $x$ of $H$: $\Orb x = H x$

title: Orbit of Subgroup under Coset Action is Coset Space
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $G$. Let $H \in \powerset G$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*$ be the group action on $H$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: g * H = g \circ H$ where $g \circ H$ is the (left) coset of $g$ by $H$. Then the orbit of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is the (left) coset space of $H$: $\Orb H = G / H^l$

title: Orbit of Trivial Group Action is Singleton
snippet: Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $*: G \times S \to S$ be the trivial group action: $\forall \left({g, s}\right) \in G \times S: g * s = s$ Let $s \in S$. Then the orbit of $s$ under $*$ is $\left\{{s}\right\}$.
