Let $\mathbb S = \set {S \subseteq G: \order S = p^n}$ Let $G$ act on $\mathbb S$ by the group action defined in Group Action on Sets with k Elements: $\forall S \in \mathbb S: g * S = g S = \set {x \in G: x = g s: s \in S}$ Then:

title: Orchard Planting Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == A given number $n$ of trees are to be planted in an orchard so as to make the number of rows of $k$ trees the largest number possible. That is: $n$ points are to be configured in the plane so that the number of straight lines that can be drawn through exactly $k$ of these points is maximised.

title: Order-Convex Set Characterization
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be an ordered set. Let $C \subseteq S$.

title: Order-Convex Subset of Ordered Set is not necessarily Interval
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $C$ be an order-convex subset of $S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $C$ is an interval of $S$.

title: Order-Extension Principle
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\preceq$ be an ordering on $S$. Then there exists a total ordering $\le$ on $S$ such that: $\forall a, b \in S: \paren {a \preceq b \implies a \le b}$

title: Order-Preserving Bijection on Wosets is Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be well-ordered sets. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a bijection such that $\phi: S \to T$ is order-preserving: $\forall x, y \in S: x \preceq_1 y \implies \map \phi x \preceq_2 \map \phi y$ Then: $\forall x, y \in S: \map \phi x \preceq_2 \map \phi y \implies x \preceq_1 y$ That is, $\phi: S \to T$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Order-Preserving Identity Mapping between Ordered Structures not necessarily Isomorphism
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$ such that: $\forall a, b \in A: a \mathrel \RR b \implies a \mathrel \SS b$ Let $I_A$ denote the identity mapping on $A$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $I_A$ is an order isomorphism from the ordered structures $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {A, \SS}$.

title: Order-Preserving Mapping Not Always Semilattice Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semilattices. Let $\preceq_1$ be the ordering on $S$ defined by: $a \preceq_1 b \iff \paren {a \circ b} = b$ Let $\preceq_2$ be the ordering on $T$ defined by: $x \preceq_2 y \iff \paren {x * y} = y$ Let $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be an order-preserving mapping. Then: $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ may not be a semilattice homomorphism

title: Order 1 Simple Graph is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $G_1 = \struct {\map V {G_1}, \map E {G_1} }$ and $G_2 = \struct {\map V {G_2}, \map E {G_2} }$ be simple graphs of order $1$. Then $G_1$ and $G_2$ are isomorphic.

title: Order 2 Square Matrices with Zero Diagonals do not form Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of square matrices of order $2$ whose diagonal elements are zero. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {S, +, \times}$ is not a ring. Note that $\times$ denotes conventional matrix multiplication.

title: Order 3 Magic Hexagon/Historical Note
snippet: == Historical Note on Order $3$ Magic Hexagon == The order $3$ magic hexagon was published by in $1897$. It continues to appear sporadically in works of recreational mathematics. Category:Historical Notes

title: Order Automorphism on Well-Ordered Class is Forward Moving
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered class. Let $\phi$ be an order isomorphism on $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$. Then: $\forall a \in A: a \preccurlyeq \map \phi a$

title: Order Automorphism on Well-Ordered Class is Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered class. Let $\phi$ be an order isomorphism on $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$. Then $\phi$ is the identity mapping: $\forall a \in A: \map \phi a = a$

title: Order Completion is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ be an ordered set. Suppose that both $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ and $\struct {T', \preceq_{T'} }$ are order completions for $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$. Then there exists a unique order isomorphism $\psi: T \to T'$. In particular, $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ and $\struct {T', \preceq_{T'} }$ are isomorphic.

title: Order Embedding/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Embeddings ==

title: Order Embedding between Quotient Fields is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1, \le_1}$ and $\struct {S, +_2, \circ_2, \le_2}$ be totally ordered integral domains. Let $K, L$ be totally ordered fields of quotients of $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1, \le_1}$ and $\struct {S, +_2, \circ_2, \le_2}$ respectively. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a order embedding. Then there exists exactly one order embedding $\psi: K \to L$ extending $\phi$. Also: $\forall x \in R, y \in R_{\ne 0}: \map \psi {\dfrac x y} = \dfrac {\map \phi x} {\map \phi y}$ If $\phi: R \to S$ is an order isomorphism, then so is $\psi$.

title: Order Embedding into Image is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $S'$ be the image of a mapping $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$. Then: $\phi$ is an order embedding from $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ into $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ $\phi$ is an order isomorphism from $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ into $\struct {S', \preceq_2 \restriction_{S'} }$.

title: Order Embedding is Increasing Mapping
snippet: Let $\left({S_1, \preceq_1}\right)$, $\left({S_2, \preceq_2}\right)$ be ordered sets. Let $f:S_1 \to S_2$ be an order embedding. Then $f$ is increasing mapping.

title: Order Embedding is Injection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an order embedding. That is: $\forall x, y \in S: x \preceq_1 y \iff \map \phi x \preceq_2 \map \phi y$ Then $\phi$ is an injection.

title: Order Generating Subset Includes Completely Irreducible Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X \subseteq S$ be an order generating subset of $S$. Let $x \in S$ be a completely irreducible element of $S$. Then $x \in X$.

title: Order Generating iff Every Element is Infimum
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall x \in S: \exists Y \subseteq X: x = \inf Y$

title: Order Generating iff Every Superset Closed on Infima is Whole Space
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall Y \subseteq S: Y \supseteq X \land \paren {\forall Z \subseteq Y: \inf Z \in Y} \implies Y = S$

title: Order Generating iff Not Preceding implies There Exists Element Preceding and Not Preceding
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is order generating $\forall x, y \in S: \paren {y \npreceq x \implies \exists p \in X: x \preceq p \land y \npreceq p}$

title: Order Isomorphic Sets are Equivalent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be order isomorphic. Then $S$ and $T$ are equivalent.

title: Order Isomorphism/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Isomorphisms ==

title: Order Isomorphism Preserves Infima and Suprema
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ and $L' = \struct {S', \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to S'$ be an order isomorphism between $L$ and $L'$. Then $f$ preserves infima and suprema.

title: Order Isomorphism Preserves Initial Segments
snippet: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be classes. Let $\prec_1$ and $\prec_2$ be strict orderings. Let $\phi: A_1 \to A_2$ create an order isomorphism between $\struct {A_1, \prec_1}$ and $\struct {A_2, \prec_2}$. Suppose $x \in A_1$. Then $\phi$ maps the $\prec_1$-initial segment of $x$ to the $\prec_2$-initial segment of $\map \phi x$.

title: Order Isomorphism Preserves Lower Bounds
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$, $L' = \struct {S', \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to S'$ be an order isomorphism between $L$ and $L'$. Let $x \in S$, $X \subseteq S$. Then $x$ is lower bound for $X$ $\map f x$ is lower bound for $f \sqbrk X$.

title: Order Isomorphism Preserves Strictly Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be classes. Let $\prec_1$ and $\prec_2$ be relations. Let $\phi : A_1 \to A_2$ create an order isomorphism between $\struct {A_1, \prec_1}$ and $\struct {A_1, \prec_2}$. Let $B \subseteq A_1$. Then $\phi$ maps the strictly minimal elements under $\prec_1$ of $B$ to the strictly minimal elements under $\prec_2$ of $\phi \sqbrk B$.

title: Order Isomorphism Preserves Upper Bounds
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$, $L' = \struct {S', \preceq'}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to S'$ be an order isomorphism between $L$ and $L'$. Let $x \in S$, $X \subseteq S$. Then: $x$ is an upper bound for $X$ $\map f x$ is an upper bound for $f \sqbrk X$.

title: Order Isomorphism between Linearly Ordered Spaces is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \le_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \le_2, \tau_2}$ be linearly ordered spaces. Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ be an order isomorphism from $\struct {S_1, \le_1}$ to $\struct {S_2, \le_2}$. Then $\phi$ is a homeomorphism from $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ to $\struct {S_2, \tau_2}$.

title: Order Isomorphism between Ordinals and Proper Class
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \prec}$ be a strict well-ordering. Let $A$ be a proper class. Let the initial segment of $x$ be a set for every $x \in A$. Then we may make the following definitions: Set $G$ equal to the collection of ordered pairs $\tuple {x, y}$ such that: $y \in A \setminus \Img x$ $\paren {A \setminus \Img x} \cap A_y = \O$ Use the First Principle of Transfinite Recursion to construct a mapping $F$ such that: The domain of $F$ is the class of all ordinals $\On$ For all ordinals $x$, $\map F x = \map G {F {\restriction_x} }$ Then $F: \On \to A$ is an order isomorphism between $\struct…

title: Order Isomorphism between Tosets is not necessarily Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be tosets. Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \cong \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$, that is, let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be order isomorphic. Then it is not necessarily the case that there is exactly one mapping $f: S_1 \to S_2$ such that $f$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Order Isomorphism between Wosets is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be wosets. Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \cong \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$, that is, let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be order isomorphic. Then there is exactly one mapping $f: S_1 \to S_2$ such that $f$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Order Isomorphism forms Galois Connection
snippet: Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$, $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $f:S_1 \to S_2$ be an order isomorphism between $L_1$ and $L_2$. Then $\struct {f, f^{-1} }$ is a Galois connection.

title: Order Isomorphism from Woset onto Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a woset. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $f: S \to T$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\forall x \in S: x \preceq \map f x$.

title: Order Isomorphism iff Strictly Increasing Surjection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be totally ordered sets. A mapping $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$ is an order isomorphism : $(1): \quad \phi$ is a surjection $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x \mathop {\prec_1} y \implies \map \phi x \mathop {\prec_2} \map \phi y$

title: Order Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Order isomorphism between ordered sets is an equivalence relation. So any given family of ordered sets can be partitioned into disjoint classes of isomorphic sets.

title: Order Isomorphism is Preserved by Antilexicographic Order
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_{1'} }$ and $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$ be ordered sets such that: $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_{1'} }$ $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$ Then the antilexicographic order $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \otimes^a \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} } \otimes^a \struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$.

title: Order Isomorphism is Preserved by Order Sum
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_{1'} }$ and $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$ be ordered sets such that: $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_1, \preccurlyeq_{1'} }$ $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$ Then the order sum $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \oplus \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} } \oplus \struct {T_2, \preccurlyeq_{2'} }$.

title: Order Isomorphism is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ is isomorphic to itself.

title: Order Isomorphism is Surjective Order Embedding
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is an order isomorphism : $(1): \quad f$ is a surjection $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x \preceq_1 y \iff \map f x \preceq_2 \map f y$ That is, $f$ is an order embedding which is also a surjection.

title: Order Isomorphism is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ be isomorphic to $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$. Then $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$.

title: Order Isomorphism is Transitive
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$, $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ and $\struct {S_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ be isomorphic to $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$. Let $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be isomorphic to $\struct {S_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$. Then $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {S_3, \preccurlyeq_3}$.

title: Order Isomorphism on Lattice preserves Lattice Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1} \to \struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is a lattice $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also a lattice.

title: Order Isomorphism on Strictly Well-Founded Relation preserves Strictly Well-Founded Structure
snippet: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be classes. Let $\prec_1$ and $\prec_2$ be relations. Let $\phi: \struct {A_1, \prec_1} \to \struct {A_2, \prec_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {A_1, \prec_1}$ is a strictly well-founded structure $\struct {A_2, \prec_2}$ is also a strictly well-founded structure.

title: Order Isomorphism on Totally Ordered Set preserves Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1} \to \struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is a totally ordered set $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also a totally ordered set.

title: Order Isomorphism on Well-Ordered Set preserves Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\phi: \struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \to \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be an order isomorphism. Then $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ is a well-ordered set $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also a well-ordered set.

title: Order Modulo n of Power of Integer
snippet: Let $a$ have multiplicative order $c$ modulo $n$. Then for any $k \ge 1$, $a^k$ has multiplicative order $\dfrac c {\gcd \set {c, k}}$ modulo $n$.

title: Order Statistic/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order Statistics ==

title: Order Sum of Ordered Sets is Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Then the order sum $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \oplus \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ of $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also an ordered set.

title: Order Sum of Totally Ordered Sets is Totally Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be totally ordered sets. Then the order sum $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \oplus \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ of $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also a totally ordered set.

title: Order Sum of Well-Founded Orderings is Well-Founded Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\preccurlyeq_1$ and $\preccurlyeq_2$ be well-founded. Then the order sum $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} \oplus \struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ of $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ is also well-founded.

title: Order Topology equals Dual Order Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\tau$ be the $\preceq$-order topology on $S$. Let $\tau'$ be the $\succeq$-order topology on $S$, where $\succeq$ is the dual ordering of $\preceq$. Then $\tau' = \tau$.

title: Order Topology on Natural Numbers is Discrete Topology
snippet: Let $\le$ be the standard ordering on the natural numbers $\N$. Then the order topology $\tau$ on $\N$ is the discrete topology.

title: Order Type Addition is Associative
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be order types of ordered sets. Then: $\paren {\alpha + \beta} + \gamma = \alpha + \paren {\beta + \gamma}$ where $+$ denotes order type addition.

title: Order Type Addition is Well-Defined Operation
snippet: The addition operation on order types is well-defined.

title: Order Type Addition is not Commutative
snippet: The operation of order type addition is not commutative.

title: Order Type Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be order types of ordered sets. Then: $\alpha \cdot \paren {\beta + \gamma} = \paren {\alpha \cdot \beta} + \paren {\alpha \cdot \gamma}$ where: $+$ denotes order type addition $\cdot$ denotes order type multiplication.

title: Order Type Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be order types of ordered sets. Then: $\paren {\alpha \cdot \beta} \cdot \gamma = \alpha \cdot \paren {\beta \cdot \gamma}$ where $\cdot$ denotes order type multiplication.

title: Order Type Multiplication is Well-Defined Operation
snippet: The multiplication operation on order types is well-defined.

title: Order Type of Integers under Usual Ordering
snippet: Consider the ordered structure $\struct {\Z, \le}$ that is the set of integers under the usual ordering. Then: $\map \ot {\Z, \le} = \omega^* + \omega$ where: $\ot$ denotes order type $\omega$ denotes the order type of the natural numbers $\N$ $\omega^*$ denotes the dual of $\omega$ $+$ denotes addition of order types.

title: Order Types of Duals of Isomorphic Sets are Equal
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let: $\map \ot {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1} = \map \ot {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$ where $\ot$ denotes the order type operator. Let $\struct {S_1, \succcurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \succcurlyeq_2}$ denote the dual ordered sets of $\struct {S_1, \preccurlyeq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preccurlyeq_2}$. Then: $\map \ot {S_1, \succcurlyeq_1} = \map \ot {S_2, \succcurlyeq_2}$

title: Order and Size of Graph do not determine Degrees of Vertices
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a simple graph. Let both the order $\card V$ and size $\card E$ of $G$ be given. Then it is not always possible to determine the degrees of each of the vertices of $G$.

title: Order is Maximum of Exponent of Convergence and Degree
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $\omega$ be its order. Let $\tau$ be its exponent of convergence. Let $h$ be the degree of the polynomial in its canonical factorization. Then: $\omega = \map \max {\tau, h}$

title: Order is Preserved on Positive Reals by Squaring
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R: x > 0, y >0$. Then: $x < y \iff x^2 < y^2$

title: Order of 5 in Units of Ring of Integers Modulo 2^n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer and $n \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z / 2^n \Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers modulo $2^n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / 2^n \Z}^\times, \times}$ denote the group of units of $\struct {\Z / 2^n \Z, +, \times}$. The order of $5$ in $U$ is $2^{n - 2}$.

title: Order of Additive Group of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. The order of $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ is $m$.

title: Order of Alternating Group
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Let $A_n$ be the alternating group on $n$ letters. Then: $\order {A_n} = \dfrac {n!} 2$ where $\order {A_n}$ denotes the order of $A_n$.

title: Order of Automorphism Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group whose order is greater than $2$. Let $\Aut G$ be the automorphism group of $G$. Then the order of $\Aut G$ is greater than $1$.

title: Order of Automorphism Group of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $C_n$ denote the cyclic group of order $n$. Let $\Aut {C_n}$ denote the automorphism group of $C_n$. Then: $\order {\Aut {C_n} } = \map \phi n$ where: $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group $\map \phi n$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Order of Automorphism Group of Dihedral Group
snippet: Let $D_n$ denote the dihedral group of order $n$. Let $\Aut {D_n}$ denote the automorphism group of $D_n$. Then: $\order {\Aut {D_n} } = n \cdot \map \phi n$ where: $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group $\map \phi n$ is the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Order of Automorphism Group of Prime Group
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a group of order $p$. Let $\Aut G$ denote the automorphism group of $G$. Then: $\order {\Aut G} = p - 1$ where $\order {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the order of a group.

title: Order of Boolean Group is Power of 2
snippet: Let $G$ be a Boolean group. Let $\order G$ denote the order of $G$. Then: $\order G = 2^n$ where $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ is a positive integer.

title: Order of Conjugate Element equals Order of Element
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Then $\forall a, x \in \struct {G, \circ}: \order {x \circ a \circ x^{-1} } = \order a$ where $\order a$ denotes the order of $a$ in $G$.

title: Order of Conjugate of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that $H$ is of finite order. Then $\order {H^a} = \order H$.

title: Order of Contact/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orders of Contact ==

title: Order of Convergence Implies Convergence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be an real sequence that converges to $\alpha$ with order $p$, where $p \ge 1$. Then, $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to $\alpha$.

title: Order of Cycle is Length of Cycle
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$ be a cyclic permutation of length $k$. Then: $\order \pi = k$ where: $\order \pi$ denotes the order of $\pi$ in $S_n$.

title: Order of Cyclic Group equals Order of Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite cyclic group which is generated by $a \in G$. Then: $\order a = \order G$ where: $\order a$ denotes the order of $a$ in $G$ $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

title: Order of Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orders of Differential Equations ==

title: Order of Dihedral Group
snippet: The dihedral group $D_n$ is of order $2 n$.

title: Order of Divisor Count Function
snippet: For all $x \ge 1$: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \le x} \map {\sigma_0} n = x \log x + \paren {2 \gamma - 1} x + \map \OO {\sqrt x}$ where: $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant $\map {\sigma_0} n$ is the divisor count function.

title: Order of Element Divides Order of Finite Group
snippet: In a finite group, the order of a group element divides the order of its group: $\forall x \in G: \order x \divides \order G$

title: Order of Element divides Order of Centralizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $x \in G$ be an element of $G$. Let $\map {C_G} x$ denote the centralizer of $x$. Then: $\order x \divides \order {\map {C_G} x}$ where: $\order x$ denotes the order of $x$ in $G$ $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\order {\map {C_G} x}$ denotes the order of $\map {C_G} x$.

title: Order of Element in Group equals its Order in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$, where $\le$ denotes the property of being a subgroup. Let $x \in H$. Then the order of $x$ in $H$ equals the order of $x$ in $G$.

title: Order of Element in Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / H$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $H$. The order of $a H \in G / H$ divides the order of $a \in G$.

title: Order of Elements in Quaternion Group
snippet: Let $Q = \Dic 2$ be the quaternion group, whose group presentation is given by: $\Dic 2 = \gen {a, b: a^4 = e, b^2 = a^2, a b a = b}$ Then $\Dic 2$ has: $1$ element of order $2$ and: $6$ elements of order $4$.

title: Order of External Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {T, \circ_2}$ be algebraic structures. Then the order of $\struct {S \times T, \circ}$ is $\card S \times \card T$.

title: Order of Finite Abelian Group with p+ Order p Elements is Divisible by p^2
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $G$ be a finite abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $G$ have at least $p$ elements of order $p$. Then: $p^2 \divides \order G$ where: $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

title: Order of Finite p-Group is Power of p
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $p$ be a prime number. Let all elements of $G$ have order a power of $p$. Then $G$ is a $p$-group.

title: Order of Fischer-Griess Monster
snippet: The order of the Fischer-Griess Monster $\mathrm M$ is given as: {{eqn | l = \order {\mathrm M} | r = 2^{46} \times 3^{20} \times 5^9 \times 7^6 \times 11^2 \times 13^3 \times 17 \times 19 \times 23 \times 29 \times 31 \times 41 \times 47 \times 59 \times 71 | c = }}

title: Order of Floor Function
snippet: Let $\floor x$ denote the floor function of $x$. Then: $\floor x = x + \map \OO 1$ where $\OO$ is big-O notation.

title: Order of General Linear Group over Galois Field
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a Galois field with $p$ elements. Then the order of the general linear group $\GL {n, \GF}$ is: $\ds \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^n \paren {p^n - p^{j - 1} }$

title: Order of Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order of Graph ==

title: Order of Group Element/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Order of Group Element ==

title: Order of Group Element equals Order of Coprime Power
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $g$. Let $\order g$ denote the order of $g$ in $G$. Then: $\forall m \in \Z: \order {g^m} = \order g \iff m \perp \order g$ where: $g^m$ denotes the $m$th power of $g$ in $G$ $\perp$ denotes coprimality.

title: Order of Group Element equals Order of Inverse
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Then: $\forall x \in G: \order x = \order {x^{-1} }$ where $\order x$ denotes the order of $x$.

title: Order of Group Element in Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be finite groups. Let $g \in G: \order g = m, h \in H: \order h = n$. Then $\order {\tuple {g, h} }$ in $G \times H$ is $\lcm \set {m, n}$.

title: Order of Group Element not less than Order of Power
snippet: Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $g$. Let $\left\lvert{g}\right\rvert$ denote the order of $g$ in $G$. Then: $\forall m \in \Z: \left\lvert{g^m}\right\rvert \le \left\lvert{g}\right\rvert$ where $g^m$ denotes the $m$th power of $g$ in $G$.

title: Order of Group equals Sum of Squares of Degrees of Characters
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $S$ be a set of representatives of the conjugacy classes of $G$: one such representative from each conjugacy class. Let $n$ be defined as: $n = \ds \sum_{x \mathop \in S} \paren {\map \deg {\map {\chi_\rho} x} }^2$ where $\map \deg {\map {\chi_\rho} x}$ denotes the degree of the character of an arbitrary irreducible linear representation of $G$. Then: $n = \order G$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

title: Order of Group of Units of Integers Modulo n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be an integer. Let $\struct {\Z / n \Z, +, \cdot}$ be the ring of integers modulo $n$. Let $U = \struct {\paren {\Z / n \Z}^\times, \cdot}$ denote the group of units of this ring. Then: $\order U = \map \phi n$ where $\phi$ denotes the Euler $\phi$-function.

title: Order of Hadamard Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a Hadamard matrix. Then the order of $\mathbf A$ must either be $2$ or an integer multiple of $4$.

title: Order of Homomorphic Image of Group Element
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups whose identities are $e_G$ and $e_H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a homomorphism. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Then: $\forall g \in G: \order {\map \phi g} \divides \order g$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility.

title: Order of Monomorphic Image of Group Element
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups whose identities are $e_G$ and $e_H$ respectively. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a monomorphism. Let $g \in G$ be of finite order. Then: $\forall g \in G: \order {\map \phi g} = \order g$

title: Order of Multiplicative Group of Reduced Residues
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $m$. The order of $\struct {\Z'_m, \times_m}$ is $\map \phi m$, where $\phi$ denotes the Euler $\phi$ function.

title: Order of Möbius Function
snippet: Let $\mu$ denote the Möbius function . Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \le N} \map \mu n = \map o N$ where $o$ denotes little-o notation.

title: Order of Natural Logarithm Function
snippet: Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Then: $\ln x = \map \OO {x^\epsilon}$ as $x \to \infty$ and: $\ln x = \map \OO {x^{-\epsilon} }$ as $x \to 0^+$ where $\OO$ is big-O notation.

title: Order of Power of Group Element
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $G$ such that: $\order g = n$ where $\order g$ denotes the order of $g$. Then: $\forall m \in \Z: \order {g^m} = \dfrac n {\gcd \set {m, n} }$ where $\gcd \set {m, n}$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $m$ and $n$.

title: Order of Product of Abelian Group Elements Divides LCM of Orders of Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $a, b \in G$. Then: $\order {a b} \divides \lcm \set {\order a, \order b}$ where: $\order a$ denotes the order of $a$ $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\lcm$ denotes the lowest common multiple.

title: Order of Product of Commuting Group Elements of Coprime Order is Product of Orders
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $g_1, g_2 \in G$ be commuting elements such that: {{eqn | l = \order {g_1} | r = n_1 }} {{eqn | l = \order {g_2} | r = n_2 }} where $\order {g_1}$ denotes the order of $g_1$ in $G$. Let $n_1$ and $n_2$ be coprime. Then: $\order {g_1 g_2} = n_1 n_2$

title: Order of Product of Disjoint Permutations
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi$ be a product of disjoint permutations of orders $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r$. Then: $\order \pi = \lcm \set {k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r}$ where: $\order \pi$ denotes the order of $\pi$ in $S_n$ $\lcm$ denotes lowest common multiple.

title: Order of Product of Entire Function with Polynomial
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of order $\omega$. Let $P: \C \to \C$ be a nonzero polynomial. Then $f \cdot P$ has order $\omega$.

title: Order of Product of Entire Functions
snippet: Let $f, g: \C \to \C$ be entire functions of order $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then $f g$ has order at most $\map \max {\alpha, \beta}$.

title: Order of Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / N$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $N$. Then: $\dfrac {\order G} {\order N} = \order {G / N}$ where $\order G$ denotes the order of $G$.

title: Order of Real Numbers is Dual of Order of their Negatives
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: x > y \iff \paren {-x}< \paren {-y}$

title: Order of Reciprocal of Entire Function
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of order $\rho$. Let $f$ have no zeroes. Then $1/f$ has order $\rho$.

title: Order of Second Chebyshev Function
snippet: Let $x \ge 2$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \map \psi x = \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \ln p + \map \OO {\sqrt x \paren {\ln x}^2}$ where: $\OO$ is big-O notation $\psi$ is the Second Chebyshev Function the sum runs over the primes less than or equal to $x$.

title: Order of Shifted Entire Function
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of order $\alpha$. Let $a \in \C$. Then $\map f {z + a}$ has order $\alpha$.

title: Order of Simple Group divides Factorial of Index of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a simple group, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with index $n$. Then $|G|$ divides $n!$.

title: Order of Squares in Ordered Field
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered field whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Suppose that $\forall a \in R: 0 < a \implies 0 < a^{-1}$. Let $x, y \in \struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ such that $0_R \le x, y$. Then $x \le y \iff x \circ x \le y \circ y$. That is, the square function is an order embedding of $\struct {R_{\ge 0}, \le}$ into itself. When $R$ is one of the standard fields of numbers $\Q$ and $\R$, then this translates into: If $x, y$ are positive then $x \le y \iff x^2 \le y^2$.

title: Order of Squares in Ordered Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x, y \in \struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ such that $0_R \le x, y$. Then: $x \le y \implies x \circ x \le y \circ y$ When $R$ is one of the standard sets of numbers, that is $\Z, \Q, \R$, then this translates into: If $x, y$ are positive then $x \le y \implies x^2 \le y^2$.

title: Order of Squares in Totally Ordered Ring without Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be a totally ordered ring without proper zero divisors whose zero is $0_R$. Let $x, y \in R$ be positive, that is, $0_R \le x, y$. Then $x \le y \iff x \circ x \le y \circ y$. That is, the square mapping is an order embedding of $\struct {R_{\ge 0}, \le}$ into itself. When $R$ is one of the standard sets of numbers $\Z, \Q, \R$, then this translates into: If $x, y$ are positive, then $x \le y \iff x^2 \le y^2$.

title: Order of Strictly Positive Real Numbers is Dual of Order of their Reciprocals
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: x > y > 0 \implies \dfrac 1 x < \dfrac 1 y$

title: Order of Subgroup Product
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then: $\order {H K} = \dfrac {\order H \order K} {\order {H \cap K} }$ where: $H K$ denotes subset product $\order H$ denotes the order of $H$. {{questionable|The does not make sense if $\order {H \cap K} +\infty$, because it is then $\dfrac {+\infty}{+\infty}$. Can someone check the source?}}

title: Order of Subgroup of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $C_n = \gen g$ be the cyclic group of order $n$ which is generated by $g$ whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in C_n: a = g^i$. Let $H = \gen a$. Then: $\order H = \dfrac n {\gcd \set {n, i} }$ where: $\order H$ denotes the order of $H$ $\gcd \set {n, i}$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $n$ and $i$.

title: Order of Subset Product with Singleton
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $X, Y \subseteq \struct {G, \circ}$ such that $X$ is a singleton: $X = \set x$ Then: $\order {X \circ Y} = \order Y = \order {Y \circ X}$ where $\order S$ is defined as the order of $S$.

title: Order of Sum of Entire Functions
snippet: Let $f, g: \C \to \C$ be entire functions of order $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then $f + g$ has order at most $\map \max {\alpha, \beta}$, with equality if $\alpha \ne \beta$.

title: Order of Sum of Reciprocal of Primes
snippet: Let $x \ge 2$ be a real number. We have: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \frac 1 p = \map \ln {\ln x} + \map \OO 1$ where: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x}$ sums over the primes less than or equal to $x$ $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Order of Sum of Von Mangoldt Function of n over n
snippet: We have: $\ds \sum_{n \le x} \frac {\map \Lambda n} n = \ln x + \map \OO 1$ where: $\Lambda$ is the Von Mangoldt function $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Order of Sum over Primes of Logarithm of p over p
snippet: We have: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x} \frac {\ln p} p = \ln x + \map \OO 1$ where: $\ds \sum_{p \mathop \le x}$ sums over the primes less than or equal to $x$ $\OO$ is big-$\OO$ notation.

title: Order of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$. Then $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ has $n!$ elements (see factorial).

title: Ordered Basis for Coordinate Plane
snippet: Let $a_1, a_2 \in \R^2$ such that $\set {a_1, a_2}$ forms a linearly independent set. Then $\tuple {a_1, a_2}$ is an ordered basis for the $\R$-vector space $\R^2$. Hence the points on the plane can be uniquely identified by means of linear combinations of $a_1$ and $a_2$.

title: Ordered Field of Rational Cuts is Isomorphic to Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $\struct {\RR, +, \times, \le}$ denote the ordered field of rational cuts. Let $\struct {\Q, +, \times, \le}$ denote the field of rational numbers. Then $\struct {\RR, +, \times, \le}$ and $\struct {\Q, +, \times, \le}$ are isomorphic.

title: Ordered Field with Archimedean Property on which Monotone Convergence Theorem Holds has Continuum Property
snippet: Let $\FF$ be an ordered field on which the Archimedean property holds. Let $\FF$ be such that every sequence which is increasing and bounded above is convergent. Then every non-empty subset of $\FF$ which is bounded above has a supremum.

title: Ordered Group whose Doubletons with Identity admit Supremum is Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \odot, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group whose identity element is $e$. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be such that for all $x \in G$, $\set {x, e}$ admits a supremum. Then $\preccurlyeq$ is a lattice ordering.

title: Ordered Integral Domain is Totally Ordered Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain. Then $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ is a totally ordered ring.

title: Ordered Pair/Kuratowski Formalization/Motivation
snippet: The only reason for the Kuratowski formalization of ordered pairs: $\tuple {a, b} = \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ is so their existence can be justified in the strictures of the axiomatic set theory, in particular Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory (ZF). Once that has been demonstrated, there is no need to invoke it again. The fact that this formulation allows that: $\tuple {a, b} = \tuple {c, d} \iff a = c, b = d$ is its stated aim. The fact that $\set {a, b} \in \tuple {a, b}$ is an unfortunate side-effect brought about by means of the definition.

title: Ordered Pair/Kuratowski Formalization/Warning
snippet: == Warning == The weakness of the Kuratowski formalization of the ordered pair shows up when $a = b$: {{eqn | l = \tuple {a, a} | r = \set {\set a, \set {a, a} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \set {\set a, \set a} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \set {\set a} | c = }} Thus the ordered pair degenerates into the set $\set {\set a}$. Most works on this subject gloss over this point, and indeed, completely fail to mention it.

title: Ordered Semigroup Isomorphism is Surjective Monomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} \to \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an ordered semigroup isomorphism : $(1): \quad \phi$ is an ordered semigroup monomorphism $(2): \quad \phi$ is a surjection.

title: Ordered Semigroup Monomorphism into Image is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be ordered semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} \to \struct {T, *, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered semigroup monomorphism. Let $S'$ be the image of $\phi$. Then $\phi$ is an ordered semigroup isomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ into $\struct {S', * {\restriction_{S'} }, \preccurlyeq \restriction_{S'} }$. Here: $* {\restriction_{S'}}$ denotes the restriction of $*$ to $S' \times S'$ $\preccurlyeq \restriction_{S'}$ denotes the restriction of $\preccurlyeq$ to $S' \times S'$.

title: Ordered Set has Lower Bound iff has Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct{S,\preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then: $S$ has a lower bound in $\struct{S,\preceq}$ $\struct{S,\preceq}$ has a smallest element

title: Ordered Set has Upper Bound iff has Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\struct{S,\preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then: $S$ has an upper bound in $\struct{S,\preceq}$ $\struct{S,\preceq}$ has a greatest element

title: Ordered Set is Lower Section in Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $S$ is a lower section in $S$.

title: Ordered Set is Order-Convex in Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $S$ is an order-convex set in $S$.

title: Ordered Set is Upper Section in Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $S$ is an upper section in $S$.

title: Ordered Set may not have Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. It may be the case that $S$ has no maximal elements.

title: Ordered Set may not have Minimal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. It may be the case that $S$ has no minimal elements.

title: Ordered Set of All Mappings is Lattice iff Codomain is Lattice or Domain is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {T^S, \preccurlyeq}$ denote the ordered set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Then: $\struct {T^S, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice either: $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice or: $S = \O$

title: Ordered Set of All Mappings is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a set. Then $L^X$ is also an ordered set.

title: Ordered Set of Auxiliary Relations is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L$ be the set of all auxiliary relations on $S$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq \restriction_{\map {\operatorname {Aux} } L \times \map {\operatorname {Aux} } L}$ Then $P$ is a complete lattice.

title: Ordered Set of Closure Operators and Dual Ordered Set of Closure Systems are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a complete lattice. Then $\operatorname{Closure}\left({L}\right)$ and $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)^{-1}$ are order isomorphic where $\operatorname{Closure}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure operators of $L$, $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure systems oj $L$, $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)^{-1}$ denotes the dual to $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$.

title: Ordered Set of Closure Systems is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Then $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ is an ordered set, where $\operatorname{ClSystems}\left({L}\right)$ denotes the ordered set of closure systems.

title: Ordered Set with Greatest Element whose Subsets have Infimum is Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set such that: $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has a greatest element $u$ every non-empty subset of $S$ admits an infimum. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ is a complete lattice.

title: Ordered Set with Multiple Maximal Elements has no Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ have more than one maximal element. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has no greatest element.

title: Ordered Set with Multiple Minimal Elements has no Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ have more than one minimal element. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has no smallest element.

title: Ordered Set with Order Type of Natural Numbers plus Dual has Minimum Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered structure such that: $\map \ot {S, \preccurlyeq} = \omega + \omega^*$ where: $\ot$ denotes order type $\omega$ denotes the order type of the natural numbers $\N$ $\omega^*$ denotes the dual of $\omega$ $+$ denotes addition of order types. Then $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has a smallest element.

title: Ordered Subset of Ordered Set is Ordered Set
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S', \preceq'}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Then $\struct {S', \preceq'}$ is an ordered set.

title: Ordered Sum of Tosets is Totally Ordered Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be tosets. Let $S + T = \struct {S \cup T, \preceq}$ be the ordered sum of $S$ and $T$. Then $\struct {S \cup T, \preceq}$ is itself a toset.

title: Ordering/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Orderings ==

title: Ordering Compatible with Group Operation is Strongly Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group whose identity element is $e$. Let $\prec$ be the reflexive reduction of $\preccurlyeq$. The following hold:

title: Ordering Cycle implies Equality
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ be elements of $S$. Suppose that Then $x_1 = x_2 = x_3$.

title: Ordering Induced by Injection is Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({T, \le}\right)$ be an ordered set, and let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\le_f$, the ordering induced by $f$, is an ordering.

title: Ordering Induced by Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. By Join Semilattice is Semilattice, $\struct {S, \vee}$ is a semilattice. By Semilattice Induces Ordering, $\struct {S, \vee}$ induces an ordering $\preceq'$ on $S$, by: $a \preceq' b$ $a \vee b = b$ for all $a, b \in S$. The ordering $\preceq'$ coincides with the original ordering $\preceq$.

title: Ordering Induced by Preordering is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure such that $\RR$ is a preordering. Let $\sim_\RR$ denote the equivalence on $S$ induced by $\RR$: $x \sim_\RR y$ $x \mathrel \RR y$ and $y \mathrel \RR x$ Let $\preccurlyeq_\RR$ be the ordering on the quotient set $S / {\sim_\RR}$ by $\RR$: $\eqclass x {\sim_\RR} \preccurlyeq_\RR \eqclass y {\sim_\RR} \iff x \mathrel \RR y$ where $\eqclass x {\sim_\RR}$ denotes the equivalence class of $x$ under $\sim_\RR$. Then $\preccurlyeq_\RR$ is a well-defined relation.

title: Ordering Principle
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists a total ordering on $S$.

title: Ordering Relations are Primitive Recursive
snippet: The ordering relations on $\N^2$: $n m$ are all primitive recursive.

title: Ordering in terms of Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then $\forall m, n \in S$: $m \preceq n \iff \exists p \in S: m \circ p = n$

title: Ordering is Directed iff Composite with Inverse is Trivial Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be an ordered set. Then $\RR$ is a directed ordering : $\RR^{-1} \circ \RR = S \times S$ where: $\circ$ denotes composite relation $\RR^{-1}$ denotes inverse relation $S \times S$ denotes the trivial relation, that is, the Cartesian product of $S$ with itself.

title: Ordering is Equivalent to Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then there exists a set $\mathbb S$ of subsets of $S$ such that: $\struct {S, \preceq} \cong \struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ where: $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is the relational structure consisting of $\mathbb S$ and the subset relation $\cong$ denotes order isomorphism. Hence any ordering on a set can be modelled uniquely by a set of subsets of that set under the subset relation. Specifically: Let $\mathbb S := \set {a^\preceq: a \in S}$ where $a^\preceq$ is the lower closure of $a$.

title: Ordering is Preordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an ordering on $S$. Then $\RR$ is also a preordering on $S$.

title: Ordering is Preserved on Integers by Addition
snippet: The usual ordering on the integers is preserved by the operation of addition: $\forall a, b, c, d, \in \Z: a \le b, c \le d \implies a + c \le b + d$

title: Ordering of Cardinality of Sets is Well-Defined
snippet: The relation $\le$ in the context of cardinalities of sets is well-defined in the sense that: if $\card A = \card {A'}$ and $\card B = \card {B'}$, then there exists an injection from $A$ into $B$ there exists an injection from $A'$ into $B'$.

title: Ordering of Cardinals Compatible with Cardinal Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \le \mathbf b \implies \mathbf a \mathbf c \le \mathbf b \mathbf c$ where $\mathbf a \mathbf c$ denotes the product of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf c$.

title: Ordering of Cardinals Compatible with Cardinal Sum
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a \le \mathbf b \implies \mathbf a + \mathbf c \le \mathbf b + \mathbf c$ where $\mathbf a \mathbf c$ denotes the sum of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf c$.

title: Ordering of Integers is Reversed by Negation
snippet: Let $x, y \in \Z$ such that $x > y$. Then: $-x < -y$

title: Ordering of Inverses in Ordered Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $x, y \in S$ be invertible. Then: $x \prec y \iff y^{-1} \prec x^{-1}$

title: Ordering of Natural Numbers is Provable
snippet: Let $x, y \in \N$. Suppose $x < y$. Let $\sqbrk a$ denote the unary representation of $a \in \N$. Then $\sqbrk x < \sqbrk y$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

title: Ordering of Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Strongly Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then $\preceq$ is strongly compatible with $\circ$: $\forall m, n, p \in S: m \preceq n \iff m \circ p \preceq n \circ p$

title: Ordering of Rational Cuts preserves Ordering of Associated Rational Numbers
snippet: Let $p \in\ Q$ and $q \in \Q$ be rational numbers. Let $p^*$ and $q^*$ denote the rational cuts associated with $p$ and $q$. Then: $p^* < q^* \iff p < q$ where $p^* < q^*$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts defined as: $\beta < \gamma \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \beta, p \notin \gamma$

title: Ordering of Real Numbers is Reversed by Negation
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ in $\R$ be real numbers such that: $x \le y$ Then: $-y \le -x$ where $-y$ and $-x$ are the negatives of $y$ and $x$ respectively.

title: Ordering of Reciprocals
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers such that $x, y \in \openint 0 \to$ or $x, y \in \openint \gets 0$ Then: $x \le y \iff \dfrac 1 y \le \dfrac 1 x$

title: Ordering of Series of Ordered Sequences
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ and $\sequence {b_n}$ be two real sequences. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^{\infty} a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ be convergent series. For each $n \in \N$, let $a_n < b_n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a_n < \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty b_n$

title: Ordering on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Compatible with Addition
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $+$ denote addition on $\N_{>0}$. Let $0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, n \in \N_{>0}: a $ is compatible with $+$ on $\N_{>0}$.

title: Ordering on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Compatible with Multiplication
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $\times$ denote multiplication on $\N_{>0}$. Let $0}$. Then: $\forall a, b, n \in \N_{>0}: a 0}$.

title: Ordering on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $0}$. Then $<$ is a (strict) total ordering.

title: Ordering on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Transitive
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $0}$. Then $<$ is a transitive relation.

title: Ordering on 1-Based Natural Numbers is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the $1$-based natural numbers. Let $0}$. Then exactly one of the following is true: $(1): \quad a = b$ $(2): \quad a > b$ $(3): \quad a 0}$.

title: Ordering on Closure Operators iff Images are Including
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $f, g: S \to S$ be closure operators on $L$. Then: $f \preceq g$ $g \sqbrk S \subseteq f \sqbrk S$ where $\preceq$ denotes the ordering on mappings $f \sqbrk S$ denotes the image of $f$.

title: Ordering on Cuts is Compatible with Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let the operation of $\alpha + \beta$ be the sum of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Let $\beta < \gamma$ denotes the strict ordering on cuts defined as: $\beta < \gamma \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \beta, p \notin \gamma$ Then: $\beta < \gamma \implies \alpha + \beta < \alpha + \gamma$

title: Ordering on Cuts is Total
snippet: Let $\CC$ denote the set of cuts. Let $<$ denote the strict ordering on cuts defined as: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \CC: \alpha < \beta \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \alpha, p \notin \beta$ Then $<$ is a (strict) total ordering on $\CC$.

title: Ordering on Cuts is Transitive
snippet: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be cuts. Let: where $<$ denotes the strict ordering of cuts: $\alpha < \beta \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \alpha, p \notin \beta$ Then: $\alpha < \gamma$ Hence the ordering of cuts $\le$ is a transitive relation.

title: Ordering on Cuts satisfies Trichotomy Law
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be cuts. Then exactly one of the following applies: where $$ denote the strict ordering of cuts: $\alpha < \beta \iff \exists p \in \Q: p \in \alpha, p \notin \beta$ Hence the ordering of cuts $\le$ is a total ordering.

title: Ordering on Extended Real Numbers is Ordering
snippet: Denote with $\le$ the usual ordering on the extended real numbers $\overline \R$. Then $\le$ is an ordering, and so $\overline \R$ is an ordered set.

title: Ordering on Extended Real Numbers is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\le$ denote the ordering on the extended real numbers $\overline \R$. Then $\le$ is a total ordering, and so $\overline \R$ is a toset.

title: Ordering on Integers is Transitive
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \land | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \implies | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = \le | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} That is, ordering on the integers is transitive.

title: Ordering on Mappings Implies Galois Connection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$, $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $g: S \to T$ and $d: T \to S$ be mappings such that: $g$ and $d$ are increasing mappings and $d \circ g \preceq I_S$ and $I_T \precsim g \circ d$ Then $\struct {g, d}$ is Galois connection. where $\preceq, \precsim$ denote the orderings on mappings $I_S$ denotes the identity mapping of $S$ $\circ$ denotes the composition of mappings.

title: Ordering on Multiindices is Partial Order
snippet: Let $Z$ be the set of multiindices indexed by a set $J$. The ordering on $Z$ is a partial ordering.

title: Ordering on Natural Numbers is Compatible with Addition
snippet: Let $m, n, k \in \N$ where $\N$ is the set of natural numbers. Then: $m < n \iff m + k < n + k$

title: Ordering on Natural Numbers is Compatible with Multiplication
snippet: Let $m, n, k \in \N$ where $\N$ is the set of natural numbers. Let $k \ne 0$. Then: $m < n \iff m \times k < n \times k$

title: Ordering on Natural Numbers is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $ b$ $(3): \quad a < b$ That is, $<$ is a trichotomy on $\N$.

title: Ordering on Ordinal is Subset Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be an ordinal. Then $\forall x, y \in S:$ $x \in y \iff x \prec y \iff S_x \subsetneqq S_y \iff x \subsetneqq y$ where $S_x$ and $S_y$ are the initial segments of $S$ determined by $x$ and $y$ respectively. Thus there is no need to specify what the ordering on an ordinal is -- it is always the subset relation.

title: Ordering on Partition Determines Preordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\PP$ be a partition of $S$. Let $\phi: S \to \PP$ be the quotient mapping. Let $\preceq$ be a ordering of $\PP$. Define a relation $\precsim$ on $S$ by letting $p \precsim q$ : $\map \phi p \preceq \map \phi q$ Then: $\precsim$ is a preordering on $S$. $\precsim$ is the only preordering on $S$ that induces the $\preceq$ ordering on $\PP$.

title: Ordering on Positive Integers is Equivalent to Ordering on Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $u, v \in \Z_{>0}$ be natural numbers. Consider the mapping $\phi: \N_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ defined as: $\forall u \in \N_{>0}: \map \phi u = u'$ where $u' \in \Z$ denotes the (strictly) positive integer $\eqclass {b + u, b} {}$. Let $u', v' \in \Z_{>0}$ be strictly positive integers. Then: $u > v \iff u' > v'$

title: Ordering on Real Numbers from Decimal Expansion
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $x$ and $y$ be expressed by their decimal expansions: Let $\preccurlyeq_l$ be the lexicographic ordering on $\R$ defined as: $x \preccurlyeq_l y$ : $m \prec n$ or: $m = n$ and $\exists k \in \Z_{>0}: \paren {\forall j: 1 \le j 0}: d_j = e_j$. Then: $x \le y$ where $\le$ denotes the usual ordering on $\R$.

title: Ordering on Singleton is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $S = \set s$ be a singleton. Let $\RR$ be an ordering on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a total ordering on $S$.

title: Ordering where every Subclass has Smallest Element is Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be an ordering on $A$. Let $\RR$ be such that every subclass of $A$ has a smallest element under $\RR$. Then $\RR$ is a well-ordering.

title: Ordinal Addition/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Addition ==

title: Ordinal Addition by Zero
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $\O$ be the zero ordinal. Then: $x + \O = x = \O + x$ where $+$ denotes ordinal addition.

title: Ordinal Addition is Associative
snippet: Ordinal addition is associative, i.e.: $\paren {x + y} + z = x + \paren {y + z}$ holds for all ordinals $x$, $y$ and $z$.

title: Ordinal Addition is Closed
snippet: Let $\On$ be the class of all ordinals. Then: $\forall x, y \in \On: x + y \in \On$ That is: the sum $x+y$ is an ordinal.

title: Ordinal Addition is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {z + x} = \paren {z + y} \implies x = y$ That is, ordinal addition is left cancellable.

title: Ordinal Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Data ==

title: Ordinal Equal to Rank
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $S$ be a small class. Let $\map V x$ denote the von Neumann hierarchy on the ordinal $x$. Then $x$ equals the rank of $S$ $S \in \map V {x + 1} \land S \notin \map V x$.

title: Ordinal Exponentiation is Closed
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x^y \in \On$ That is, ordinal exponentiation is closed.

title: Ordinal Exponentiation of Terms
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $n$ be a finite ordinal. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Let $y, z, n$ all be greater than $0$. Then: $\paren {x^y \times n}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z} \times n$ if $z$ is not a limit ordinal $\paren {x^y \times n}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z}$ if $z$ is a limit ordinal.

title: Ordinal Exponentiation via Cantor Normal Form/Corollary
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal and let $y > 0$. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} \times b_i}^{x^y} = x^{a_1 \mathop \times x^y}$

title: Ordinal Exponentiation via Cantor Normal Form/Limit Exponents
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ and $y$ be limit ordinals. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Then: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{a_i} \times b_i}^y = x^{a_1 \mathop \times y}$

title: Ordinal Less than Successor Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $y < \aleph_{x + 1} \iff y < \aleph_x \lor y \sim \aleph_x$

title: Ordinal Membership is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $m$ and $n$ be ordinals. Then it is not the case that $m \in n$ and $n \in m$.

title: Ordinal Membership is Transitive
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Then: $\forall \alpha, \beta, \gamma \in \On: \paren {\alpha \in \beta} \land \paren {\beta \in \gamma} \implies \alpha \in \gamma$

title: Ordinal Membership is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {\alpha = \beta} \lor \paren {\alpha \in \beta} \lor \paren {\beta \in \alpha}$ where $\lor$ denotes logical or.

title: Ordinal Multiplication by One
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $1$ denote the ordinal one.

title: Ordinal Multiplication by Zero
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal.

title: Ordinal Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $\times$ denote ordinal multiplication. Then: $x \times \paren {y \times z} = \paren {x \times y} \times z$

title: Ordinal Multiplication is Closed
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. $x \cdot y \in \On$

title: Ordinal Multiplication is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Let $z \ne 0$. Then: $\ds \paren {z \cdot x} = \paren {z \cdot y} \implies x = y$ That is, ordinal multiplication is left cancellable.

title: Ordinal Multiplication is Left Distributive
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Let $\times$ denote ordinal multiplication. Let $+$ denote ordinal addition. Then: $x \times \paren {y + z} = \paren {x \times y} + \paren {x \times z}$

title: Ordinal Multiplication via Cantor Normal Form/Infinite Exponent
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x > 1$. Let $y \ge \omega$ where $\omega$ denotes the minimally inductive set. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals such that $0 < b_i < x$ for all $1 \le i \le n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x^{a_i} b_i} \times x^y = x^{a_1 \mathop + y}$

title: Ordinal Multiplication via Cantor Normal Form/Limit Base
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x$ be a limit ordinal. Let $y > 0$. Let $\sequence {a_i}$ be a sequence of ordinals that is strictly decreasing on $1 \le i \le n$. Let $\sequence {b_i}$ be a sequence of finite ordinals. Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {x^{a_i} b_i} \times x^y = x^{a_1 \mathop + y}$

title: Ordinal Number Equivalent to Cardinal Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $\card x$ denote the cardinal number of $x$. Then: $x \sim \card x$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence.

title: Ordinal Power of Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {x^y}^z = x^{y \mathop \times z}$

title: Ordinal Scale/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Scales ==

title: Ordinal Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote a limit ordinal. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ and $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ are both completely normal.

title: Ordinal Space is Regular
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote a limit ordinal. Let $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ denote the open ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Let $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ denote the closed ordinal space on $\Gamma$. Then $\hointr 0 \Gamma$ and $\closedint 0 \Gamma$ are both regular spaces.

title: Ordinal Space is Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T$ denote an ordinal space on a limit ordinal $\Gamma$. Then $T$ is a strongly locally compact space.

title: Ordinal Subset is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $S$ be a class. Let every element of $S$ be an ordinal. Then $\struct {S, \in}$ is a strict well-ordering.

title: Ordinal Subset of Ordinal is Initial Segment
snippet: Let $S$ be an ordinal. Let $T \subset S$ also be an ordinal. Then $\exists a \in S: T = S_a$, where $S_a$ is the initial segment of $S$ determined by $a$. That is, $T = S_a = a \in S$.

title: Ordinal Subtraction when Possible is Unique
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals such that $x \le y$. Then there exists a unique ordinal $z$ such that $x + z = y$. That is: $x \le y \implies \exists! z \in \On: x + z = y$

title: Ordinal Sum of Powers
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $x^y \times x^z = x^{y + z}$

title: Ordinal Variable/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Ordinal Variables ==

title: Ordinal equals Successor of its Union
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\bigcup \alpha^+ = \alpha$ where: $\alpha^+$ denotes the successor set of $\alpha$ $\bigcup \alpha^+$ denotes the union of $\alpha^+$.

title: Ordinal equals its Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $<$ denote the (strict) usual ordering of $\On$. Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then $\alpha$ is equal to its own initial segment: $\alpha = \set {\beta \in \On: \beta < \alpha}$

title: Ordinal in Aleph iff Cardinal in Aleph
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \in \aleph_y \iff \card x \in \aleph_y$ where $\aleph$ denotes the aleph mapping.

title: Ordinal is Finite iff Natural Number
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then $x$ is a finite set $x$ is an element of the minimally inductive set.

title: Ordinal is Less than Ordinal times Limit
snippet: Let $y$ be a limit ordinal. Let $x$ and $z$ be ordinals. Then: $z < x \times y \iff \exists w \in y: z < x \times w$

title: Ordinal is Less than Ordinal to Limit Power
snippet: Let $x$, $y$, and $z$ be ordinals. Let $z$ be a limit ordinal. Then: $x < y^z \iff \exists w \in z: x < y^w$

title: Ordinal is Less than Successor
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $x^+$ denote the successor of $x$. Then: $x \in x^+$ $x \subset x^+$

title: Ordinal is Less than Sum
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le \paren {x + y}$ $x \le \paren {y + x}$

title: Ordinal is Member of Class of All Ordinals
snippet: Let $A$ be an ordinal. Then: $A \in \On \lor A = \On$ where $\On$ denotes the class of all ordinals.

title: Ordinal is Proper Subset of Successor
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\alpha \subsetneqq \alpha^+$ where $\alpha^+$ denotes the successor set of $\alpha$. That is: $\alpha$ is a proper subset of $\alpha^+$.

title: Ordinal is Subset of Class of All Ordinals
snippet: Suppose $A$ is an ordinal. Then: $A \subseteq \On$ where $\On$ represents the class of all ordinals.

title: Ordinal is Subset of Rank of Small Class iff Not in Von Neumann Hierarchy
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $S$ be a small class. Let $\map V x$ denote the von Neumann hierarchy on the ordinal $x$. Then $x$ is a subset of the rank of $S$ $S \notin \map V x$.

title: Ordinal is Subset of Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $y^+$ denote the successor of $y$. Then: $x \subseteq y^+ \iff \left({x \subseteq y \lor x = y^+}\right)$

title: Ordinal is Transitive
snippet: Every ordinal is a transitive set.

title: Ordinal is not Element of Itself
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Then: $x \notin x$

title: Ordinals Isomorphic to the Same Well-Ordered Set
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be ordinals. Let $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be a strict well-ordering. Let $\left({\in, A}\right)$ and $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be order isomorphic. Let $\left({\in, B}\right)$ and $\left({\prec, S}\right)$ be order isomorphic. Then: $A = B$

title: Ordinals are Totally Ordered
snippet: The ordinals are totally ordered.

title: Ordinals are Well-Ordered
snippet: The ordinals are well-ordered.

title: Ordinals have No Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $\paren {x \cdot y} = 0 \iff \paren {x = 0 \lor y = 0}$

title: Ore's Theorem
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a simple graph of order $n \ge 3$. Let $G$ be an Ore graph, that is: For each pair of non-adjacent vertices $u, v \in V$: $(1): \quad \deg u + \deg v \ge n$ Then $G$ is Hamiltonian.

title: Ore Graph is Connected
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be an Ore graph. Then $G$ is connected.

title: Orientation of Contour is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $C$ be a contour in the complex plane $\C$. Let $D \subseteq \C$ be a connected domain. Let $\Img C \subseteq \partial D$, where $\Img C$ denotes the image of $C$, and $\partial D$ denotes the boundary of $D$. The orientation of $C$ with respect to $D$, if it exists, does not depend on the choice of parameterization of $C$.

title: Orientation of Simple Closed Contour is with Respect to Interior
snippet: Let $C$ be a simple closed contour in the complex plane $\C$. Let $\Int C$ denote the interior of $C$. $C$ is positively oriented, $C$ is positively oriented with respect to $\Int C$. $C$ is negatively oriented, $C$ is negatively oriented with respect to $\Int C$.

title: Orthic Triangle of Obtuse Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an obtuse triangle such that $A$ is the obtuse angle. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. Let $\triangle DEF$ be the orthic triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Then $\triangle DEF$ is also the orthic triangle of $\triangle HBC$, which is an acute triangle.

title: Orthocenter, Centroid and Circumcenter Coincide iff Triangle is Equilateral
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $O$ be the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$. Let $G$ be the centroid of $\triangle ABC$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. Then $O$, $G$ and $H$ are the same points $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral. If $\triangle ABC$ is not equilateral, then $O$, $G$ and $H$ are all distinct.

title: Orthocenter and Incenter Coincide if Triangle is Equilateral
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. Let $G$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle ABC$. Then: $G$ is the incenter of $\triangle ABC$.

title: Orthocenter of Self-Conjugate Triangle
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $\triangle PQR$ be a self-conjugate triangle with respect to $\CC$. Then the orthocenter of $\triangle PQR$ is the center of $\CC$.

title: Orthocomplement Reverses Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $V$ with $A \subseteq B$. Then: $B^\perp \subseteq A^\perp$ where $\perp$ denotes orthocomplementation.

title: Orthocomplement equal to Orthocomplement of Linear Span
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space over $\GF$. Let $S \subseteq V$ be non-empty. Then: $S^\bot = \paren {\map \span S}^\bot$ where $\bot$ denotes orthocomplement.

title: Orthocomplement is Closed Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $A \subseteq V$ be a subset of $V$. Then the orthocomplement $A^\perp$ of $A$ is a closed linear subspace of $H$.

title: Orthocomplement of Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $S \subseteq V$ be non-empty. Then: $S^\bot = \map \cl S^\bot$ where $\bot$ denotes orthocomplementation.

title: Orthocomplement of Subset of Orthocomplement is Superset
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $A, B \subseteq V$ be subsets of $V$ such that $B \subseteq A^\perp$, where $A^\perp$ is the orthocomplement of $A$. Then: $A \subseteq B^\perp$.

title: Orthogonal Difference is Closed Linear Subspace
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $M, N$ be closed linear subspaces of $H$. Then the orthogonal difference $M \ominus N$ is also a closed linear subspace of $H$.

title: Orthogonal Group is Group
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. The $n$th orthogonal group on $k$ is a group.

title: Orthogonal Group is Subgroup of General Linear Group
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $\map {\operatorname O} {n, k}$ be the $n$th orthogonal group on $k$. Let $\GL {n, k}$ be the $n$th general linear group on $k$. Then $\map {\operatorname O} {n, k}$ is a subgroup of $\GL {n, k}$.

title: Orthogonal Projection is Bounded
snippet:
Let $H$ be a Hilbert space with inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ and inner product norm $
orm \cdot$. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Then $P_K$ is bounded. That is: $
orm {\map {P_K} h} \le 
orm h$ for each $h \in H$.

title: Orthogonal Projection is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $H$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb F$ with inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Then $P_K$ is a linear transformation on $H$.

title: Orthogonal Projection is Mapping
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K: H \to H$ be the orthogonal projection on $K$. Then $P_K$ is a mapping.

title: Orthogonal Projection is Projection
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $K$. Then $P_K$ is a projection.

title: Orthogonal Projection onto Closed Linear Span
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space with inner product $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ and inner product norm $\norm \cdot$. Let $E = \set {e_1, \ldots, e_n}$ be an orthonormal subset of $H$. Let $M = \vee E$, where $\vee E$ is the closed linear span of $E$. Let $P$ be the orthogonal projection onto $M$. Then: $\forall h \in H: P h = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \innerprod h {e_k} e_k$

title: Orthogonal Projection onto Orthocomplement
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $A$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_A: H \to H$ be the orthogonal projection onto $A$. Let $P_{A^\perp}: H \to H$ be the orthogonal projection onto $A^\perp$, the orthocomplement of $A$. Let $I: H \to H$ be the identity operator on $H$. Then: $P_{A^\perp} = I - P_A$

snippet: Let $\map {T_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind of order $n$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \R | l = \map f x | r = \dfrac 1 2 A_0 \map {T_0} x + \sum_{k \mathop \in \N_{>0} } A_k \map {T_k} x | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac 1 2 A_0 \map {T_0} x + A_1 \map {T_1} x + A_2 \map {T_2} x + \cdots | c = }} where: $\ds A_k = \dfrac 2 \pi \int_{-1}^1 \dfrac {\map f x \map {T_k} x} {\sqrt {1 - x^2} } \rd x$

snippet: Let $\map {U_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind of order $n$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \R | l = \map f x | r = \sum_{k \mathop \in \N} A_k \map {U_k} x | c = }} {{eqn | r = A_0 \map {U_0} x + A_1 \map {U_1} x + A_2 \map {U_2} x + \cdots | c = }} where: $\ds A_k = \dfrac 2 \pi \int_{-1}^1 \sqrt {1 - x^2} \, \map f x \map {U_k} x \rd x$

title: Orthogonal Series of Hermite Polynomials
snippet: Let $\map {H_n} x$ denote the Hermite polynomial of order $n$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \R | l = \map f x | r = \sum_{k \mathop \in \N} A_k \map {H_k} x | c = }} {{eqn | r = A_0 \map {H_0} x + A_1 \map {H_1} x + A_2 \map {H_2} x + \cdots | c = }} where: $\ds A_k = \dfrac 1 {2^k k! \sqrt \pi} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \map f x \map {H_k} x \rd x$

title: Orthogonal Series of Legendre Polynomials
snippet: Let $\map {P_n} x$ denote the Legendre polynomial of order $n$. Let $f: \Bbb I \to \R$ be a real function where $I$ is the closed real interval $\closedint {-1} 1$. Then: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \Bbb I | l = \map f x | r = \sum_{k \mathop \in \N} A_k \map {P_k} x | c = }} {{eqn | r = A_0 \map {P_0} x + A_1 \map {P_1} x + A_2 \map {P_2} x + \cdots | c = }} where: $\ds A_k = \int_{-1}^1 \map f x \map {P_k} x \rd x$

title: Orthogonal Set is Linearly Independent Set

title: Orthogonality of Resolution of the Identity evaluated at Disjoint Sets
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\map B {\HH}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations on $\HH$. Let $\EE : \map \BB X \to \map B {\HH}$ be a resolution of the identity. Let $A, B \in \map \BB X$ be such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then: $\innerprod {\map \EE A x} {\map \EE B y} = 0$ for each $x, y \in \HH$.

title: Orthogonality of Solutions to the Sturm-Liouville Equation with Distinct Eigenvalues
snippet: Let $\map f x$ and $\map g x$ be solutions of the Sturm-Liouville equation: $(1): \quad -\map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\map p x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} } + \map q x y = \lambda \map w x y$ where $y$ is a function of the free variable $x$. The functions $\map p x$, $\map q x$ and $\map w x$ are specified. In the simplest cases they are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. In addition: $(1a): \quad \map p x > 0$ has a continuous derivative $(1b): \quad \map w x > 0$ $(1c): \quad y$ is typically required to satisfy some boundary conditions at $a$ and $b$.

title: Orthonormal Sequence in Hilbert Space Converges Weakly to Zero

Then: $e_n \weakconv 0$ where $\rightharpoonup$ denotes weak convergence.

Let $\map {\omega_f} x$ be the oscillation of $f$ at $x$ as defined by: $\map {\omega_f} x = \inf \set {\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}: I \in N_x}$ where $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$ is the oscillation of $f$ on a real set $I \cap D$: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \sup \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}$ Let $\map {\omega^L_f} x$ be the oscillation of $f$ at $x$ as defined by: $\map {\omega^L_f} x = \ds \lim_{h \mathop \to 0^+} \map {\omega_f}…
