snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be a real function where $D \subseteq \R$. Let $x$ be a point in $D$. Let $I$ be a real set that contains (as an element) $x$. Let $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$ be the oscillation of $f$ on $I \cap D$: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \sup \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}$ Then: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} \in \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ and: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \begin{cases} \text{a positive real number} & \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D} \text{is bounded above} \\ \infty & \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}…

title: Oscillation on Subset
snippet: Let $f: D \to \R$ be a real function where $D \subseteq \R$. Let $x$ be a point in $D$. Let $S_x$ be a set of real sets that contain (as an element) $x$. Let $I$ be an element of $S_x$. Let $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$ be the oscillation of $f$ on $I \cap D$: $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} = \sup \set {\size {\map f y - \map f z}: y, z \in I \cap D}$ Let $I \in S_x$. Let $\map {\omega_f} {I \cap D} \in \R$. Let $J \in S_x$ be a subset of $I$. Then: $\map {\omega_f} {J \cap D} \in \R$ $\map {\omega_f} {J \cap D} \le \map {\omega_f} {I \cap D}$

title: Ostrowski's Theorem
snippet: Every non-trivial norm on the rational numbers $\Q$ is equivalent to either: the $p$-adic norm $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ for some prime $p$ or: the absolute value, $\size {\, \cdot \,}$.

title: Outer Jordan Content Never Smaller than Inner Jordan Content
snippet: Let $M$ be a bounded subspace of Euclidean space. Then: $\map {m^*} M \ge \map {m_*} M$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $m_*$ denotes the inner Jordan content

title: Outer Jordan Content is Monotone
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \R^n$ be bounded subspaces of Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose that $A \subseteq B$. Then: $\map {m^*} A \le \map {m^*} B$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content is Subadditive
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \R^n$ be bounded subspaces of Euclidean $n$-space. Then: $\map {m^*} {A \cup B} \le \map {m^*} A + \map {m^*} B$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content of Closed Rectangle
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq \R^n$ be a closed $n$-rectangle. Then: $\map {m^*} \RR = \map V \RR$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $V$ denotes the content of a rectangle

title: Outer Jordan Content of Degenerate Set
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subset of Euclidean $n$-space. Suppose that, for every $\tuple {x_1, \dots, x_n} \in M$, we have that: $x_k = \gamma$ for some fixed $k \in \set {1, \dots, n}$ and $\gamma \in \R$. Then: $\map {m^*} M = 0$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content of Open Rectangle
snippet: Let: $\ds R = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \openint {a_i} {b_i}$ be an open $n$-rectangle, where: $a_i \le b_i$ for each $i \in \set {1, \dots, n}$. Then: $\ds \map {m^*} R = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {b_i - a_i}$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content of Right Triangle
snippet: Let $T \subseteq \R^2$ be defined as: $T = \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2 : x \ge 0 \land y \ge 0 \land x + y \le 1}$ Then: $\map {m^*} T = \dfrac 1 2$

title: Outer Jordan Content of Scaled Set
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subspace of Euclidean $n$-space. Let $c_1, c_2, \dotsc, c_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be non-negative real numbers. Let $M' \subseteq \R^n$ be defined as: $M' = \set {\tuple {c_1 x_1, c_2 x_2, \dotsc, c_n x_n} : \tuple {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_n} \in \R^n}$ Then: $\map {m^*} {M'} = c_1 c_2 \dotsm c_n \map {m^*} M$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content of Separated Union
snippet: Let $M \subseteq \R^n$ be a bounded subset of Euclidean $n$-space. Fix $k \in \set {1, 2, \dots, n}$ and $\gamma \in \R$. For $\vec x \in \R^n$, let $\vec x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n}$ Let: $A = \set {\vec x \in M : x_k \gamma}$ Then: $\map {m^*} M = \map {m^*} A + \map {m^*} B$ where $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content.

title: Outer Jordan Content of Subdivision
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq \R^n$ be a closed $n$-rectangle. Let $M \subseteq \RR$ be a subset. Let $P$ be a finite subdivision of $\RR$. Then: $\ds \map {m^*} M = \sum_{R \mathop \in P} \map {m^*} {M \cap R^\circ}$ where: $m^*$ denotes the outer Jordan content $R \in P$ denotes that $R$ is a subrectangle of $P$ $R^\circ$ denotes the interior of $R$

title: Outer Measure of Limit of Increasing Sequence of Sets
snippet: Let $\mu^*$ be an outer measure on a set $X$. Let $\sequence {S_n}$ be an increasing sequence of $\mu^*$-measurable sets, and let $S_n \uparrow S$ (as $n \to \infty$). Then for any subset $A \subseteq X$: $\ds \map {\mu^*} {A \cap S} = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {\mu^*} {A \cap S_n}$

title: P-Norm of Real Sequence is Strictly Decreasing Function of P
snippet: Let $p \ge 1$ be a real number. Let ${\ell^p}_\R$ denote the real $p$-sequence space. Let $\mathbf x = \sequence {x_n} \in {\ell^p}_\R$. Suppose $\mathbf x$ is not a sequence of zero elements. Let $\norm {\mathbf x}_p$ denote the $p$-norm of $\mathbf x$ where $p \ge 1$. Then the mapping $p \to \norm {\mathbf x}_p$ is strictly decreasing $p$.

title: P-Product Metric Induces Product Topology
snippet: Let $M_A = \struct{A, d_A}$ and $M_B = \struct{B, d_B}$ be metric spaces. Let $\tau_A$ and $\tau_B$ be the topologies on $A$ and $B$ induced by $d_A$ and $d_B$, respectively. Let $p \ge 1$ be an extended real number. Let $M = \struct{A \times B, d}$ be the $p$-product of $M_A$ and $M_B$. We have that $M$ is a metric space. Let $\tau$ be the topology on $A \times B$ induced by $d$. Then $\struct{A \times B, \tau}$ is the product space of $\struct{A, \tau_A}$ and $\struct{B, \tau_B}$.

title: P-Product Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $M_{1'} = \struct {A_{1'}, d_{1'} }, M_{2'} = \struct {A_{2'}, d_{2'} }, \ldots, M_{n'} = \struct {A_{n'}, d_{n'} }$ be metric spaces. Let $\ds \AA = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_{i'}$ be the cartesian product of $A_{1'}, A_{2'}, \ldots, A_{n'}$. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p: \AA \times \AA \to \R$ be the $p$-product metric on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_p} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {\map {d_{i'} } {x_i, y_i} }^p}^{\frac 1 p}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. Then $d_p$ is a metric.

title: P-Product Metric on Real Vector Space is Metric
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p: \R^n \times \R^n \to \R$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$: $\ds \map {d_p} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \size {x_i - y_i}^p}^{\frac 1 p}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \R^n$. Then $d_p$ is a metric.

title: P-Product Metrics are Lipschitz Equivalent
snippet: Let $M_A = \left({A, d_A}\right)$ and $M_B = \left({B, d_B}\right)$ be metric spaces. Let $\tau_A$ and $\tau_B$ be the topologies on $A$ and $B$ induced by $d_A$ and $d_B$, respectively. For all extended real numbers $p \ge 1$, let $M_p = \left({A \times B, d_p}\right)$ be the $p$-product of $M_A$ and $M_B$. Then all the metrics $\left\{{d_p: p \ge 1}\right\}$ are Lipschitz equivalent.

title: P-Product Metrics on Real Vector Space are Topologically Equivalent
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be an Euclidean space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Then $d_p$ and $d_\infty$ are topologically equivalent.

title: P-Seminorm is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p \in \hointr 1 \infty$. Let $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be the Lebesgue $p$-space on $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ be the $p$-seminorm on $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Then $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ is a seminorm on $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$.

title: P-Seminorm of Function Zero iff A.E. Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space and let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be the Lebesgue $p$-space. Let $f \in \map {\LL^p} {X, \Sigma, \mu}$. Then: $\norm f_p = 0$ $f = 0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere where $\norm \cdot_p$ is the $p$-seminorm.

title: P-Sequence Space admits Schauder Basis
snippet: Let $1 \le p < \infty$. Let $\ell^p$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {\mathbf e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N } \in \ell^p$ be a sequence such that: $\mathbf e_n = \tuple {\underbrace{0, \ldots, 0}_n, 1, 0, \ldots}$ Then $\set {\mathbf e_n : n \in \N}$ is a Schauder basis for $\ell^p$.

title: P-Sequence Space is Reflexive for Finite p Greater Than One
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \openint 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Then $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ is reflexive.

title: P-Sequence Space is Strictly Increasing in p
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p, q \in \hointr 1 \infty$ be such that $1 \le p < q$. Let $\map {\ell_p} {\N, \GF}$ and $\map {\ell_q} {\N, \GF}$ be the $p$ and $q$-sequence spaces. Then: $\map {\ell_p} {\N, \GF} \subsetneq \map {\ell_q} {\N, \GF}$

title: P-Sequence Space of Real Sequences is Metric Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} x_i^2$ is convergent. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-sequence metric on $\R$. Then $\ell^p := \struct {A, d_p}$ is a metric space.

title: P-Sequence Space with P-Norm forms Banach Space
snippet: Let $\ell^p$ be a p-sequence space. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ be a p-norm. Then $\struct {\ell^p, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ is a Banach space.

title: P-Sequence Space with P-Norm forms Normed Vector Space
snippet: A $p$-Sequence Space with a $p$-norm forms a normed vector space.

title: P-Sequence Space with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication on Ring of Sequences forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\ell^p$ be the p-sequence space. Let $\struct {\R, +_\R, \times_\R}$ be the field of real numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition on the ring of sequences. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise multiplication on the ring of sequences. Then $\struct {\ell^p, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ is a vector space.

title: P-Value/Examples
snippet: == Examples of $p$-Values ==

title: P-adic Closed Ball is Instance of Closed Ball of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $B \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $B$ is a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $B$ is a closed ball of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ That is, the definition of a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of a closed ball in a normed division ring.

title: P-adic Expansion Less Initial Zero Terms Represents Same P-adic Number
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ be a $p$-adic expansion that represents $a$. Let $l$ be the first index $i \ge m$ such that $d_i \ne 0$ Then the series: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = l}^\infty d_i p^i$ also represents $a$.

title: P-adic Expansion Representative of P-adic Number is Unique
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ and $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = k}^\infty e_i p^i$ be $p$-adic expansions that represent $a$. Then: $(1) \quad m = k$ $(2) \quad \forall i \ge m : d_i = e_i$ That is, the $p$-adic expansions $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = m}^\infty d_i p^i$ and $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = k}^\infty e_i p^i$ are identical.

title: P-adic Expansion is a Cauchy Sequence in P-adic Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals numbers $\Q$. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = m}^\infty d_n p^n$ be a $p$-adic expansion. Then the sequence of partial sums of the series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = m}^\infty d_n p^n$ is a Cauchy sequence in the valued field $\struct{\Q, \norm{\,\cdot\,}_p}$.

title: P-adic Expansion of P-adic Unit
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p$. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $a \in \Z_p$. Let $\ldots a_n \ldots a_3 a_2 a_1 a_0$ be the canonical expansion of $a$. Then: $a$ is a $p$-adic unit $a_0 \ne 0$

title: P-adic Integer has Unique Coherent Sequence Representative
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$ such that $\norm a _p \le 1$. Then $a$ has exactly one representative that is a coherent sequence.

title: P-adic Integer is Limit of Unique Coherent Sequence of Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Z_p$. Then there exists a unique coherent sequence $\sequence {\alpha_n}$: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \alpha_n = x$

title: P-adic Integer is Limit of Unique P-adic Expansion
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Z_p$. Then $x$ is the limit of a unique $p$-adic expansion of the form: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty d_n p^n$

title: P-adic Integers Form Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\Q_p$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p$. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then: $\Z_p$ is an integral domain

title: P-adic Integers is Metric Completion of Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $d$ be the subspace metric of the $p$-adic metric on the $p$-adic integers $\Z_p$. Then $\struct {\Z_p, d}$ is the metric completion of the integers $\Z$.

title: P-adic Integers is Valuation Ring Induced by P-adic Norm
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p$. Then: the $p$-adic integers, $\Z_p$, is the valuation ring induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$

title: P-adic Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p: \Q \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the $p$-adic norm on $\Q$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-adic metric on $\Q$: $\forall x, y \in \Q: \map {d_p} {x, y} = \norm{x - y}_p$ Then $d_p$ is a metric.

title: P-adic Metric on P-adic Numbers is Non-Archimedean Metric
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $\norm{\,\cdot\,}_p: \Q_p \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be the $p$-adic norm on the $p$-adic numbers $\Q_p$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-adic metric on $\Q_p$: $\forall x, y \in \Q_p: \map {d_p} {x, y} = \norm{x - y}_p$ Then $d_p$ is a non-Archimedean metric that extends the $p$-adic metric on the rationals $\Q$ to $\Q_p$.

title: P-adic Norm Characterisation of Divisibility by Power of p
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $\Q$ denote the rational numbers. Let $\norm{\,\cdot\,}$ denote the $p$-adic norm on $\Q$. Then: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a \equiv b \pmod {p^n} \iff \norm {a - b}_p \le p^{-n}$

P-adic Norm is Norm

title: P-adic Number has Unique P-adic Expansion Representative
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a$ be a $p$-adic number, that is left coset, in $\Q_p$. Then $a$ has exactly one representative that is a $p$-adic expansion.

title: P-adic Number is Limit of Unique P-adic Expansion
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then $x$ is the limit of a unique $p$-adic expansion.

title: P-adic Number is Power of p Times P-adic Unit

title: P-adic Number times Integer Power of p is P-adic Integer
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then: $\forall a \in \Q_p: \exists n \in \N: p^n a \in \Z_p$

title: P-adic Number times P-adic Norm is P-adic Unit
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p^\times$ be the $p$-adic units. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Then there exists $n \in \Z$ such that: $p^n a \in \Z_p^\times$ where $p^n = \norm a_p$

title: P-adic Numbers are Generated Ring Extension of P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Then: $Q_p = \Z_p \sqbrk {1 / p}$ where $\Z_p \sqbrk {1 / p}$ denotes the ring extension generated by $1 / p$.

title: P-adic Numbers are Uncountable
snippet: Let $p$ be any prime number. The set of $p$-adic numbers $\Q_p$ is an uncountable set.

title: P-adic Numbers form Completion of Rational Numbers with P-adic Norm

orm {\,\cdot\,}^\Q_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$. Let $\struct {\Q_p,

title: P-adic Numbers is Hausdorff Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct{\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is Hausdorff.

title: P-adic Numbers is Locally Compact Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is locally compact.

title: P-adic Numbers is Second Countable Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is second-countable.

title: P-adic Numbers is Totally Disconnected Topological Space
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\tau_p$ be the topology induced by the non-Archimedean norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$. Then the topological space $\struct {\Q_p, \tau_p}$ is totally disconnected.

title: P-adic Open Ball is Instance of Open Ball of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $B \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $B$ is an open ball in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $B$ is an open ball of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ . That is, the definition of an open ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of an open ball in a normed division ring.

title: P-adic Sphere is Instance of Sphere of a Norm
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $S \subseteq \Q_p$. Then: $S$ is a sphere in $p$-adic numbers with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ $S$ is a sphere of the normed division ring $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ with radius $\epsilon$ and centre $a$ That is, the definition of a closed ball in $p$-adic numbers is a specific instance of the general definition of a sphere in a normed division ring.

title: P-adic Unit has Norm Equal to One
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ denote the $p$-adic integers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then x is a $p$-adic unit $\norm x_p = 1$

P-adic Valuation of Rational Number is Well Defined

title: PDF of Cantor Distribution does not Exist
snippet: The probability density function of the Cantor distribution $C$ does not exist.

title: PGF of Sum of Independent Discrete Random Variables
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent discrete random variables on $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $Z$ be a discrete random variable such that $Z = X + Y$. Then: $\map {\Pi_Z} s = \map {\Pi_X} s \, \map {\Pi_Y} s$ where $\map {\Pi_Z} s$ is the probability generating function of $Z$.

title: PGF of Sum of Random Number of Independent Discrete Random Variables
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let: $N, X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be independent discrete random variables such that the $X$'s have the same probability distribution. Let: $\map {\Pi_N} s$ be the PGF of $N$ $\map {\Pi_X} s$ be the PGF of each of the $X$'s. Let: $Z = X_1 + X_2 + \ldots + X_N$ Then: $\map {\Pi_Z} s = \map {\Pi_N} {\map {\Pi_X} s}$

title: P versus NP
snippet: == Open Question == The class of problems for which an algorithm can find a solution in polynomial time is termed $P$. The class of problems for which an algorithm can verify a solution in nondeterministic polynomial time is termed $NP$. The $P$ versus $NP$ question is: Are all problems in $NP$ also in $P$?

title: Pack of Cards is Randomized by 7 Riffle Shuffles
snippet: A pack of cards is randomized by $7$ riffle shuffles.

title: Packing of Circles into Plane
snippet: The most space-efficient way to pack unit circles into the plane is to place their centers at the lattice points of the point lattice in $\R^n$ with a basis $\set {\tuple {2, 0}, \tuple {1, \sqrt 3} }$.

title: Padé Approximant/Examples

title: Pair of Consecutive Powerful Numbers whose First is Odd
snippet: The only known pair of consecutive integers which are both powerful numbers such that the first of the pair is odd is: $\tuple {675, 676}$

title: Pair of Large Twin Primes
snippet: The integers defined as: $1\,159\,142\,985 \times 2^{2304} \pm 1$ are a pair of twin primes each with $703$ digits.

title: Pair of Titanic Twin Primes
snippet: The integers defined as: $190 \, 116 \times 3003 \times 10^{5120} \pm 1$ are a pair of titanic twin primes. That is: $570 \, 918 \, 347 \paren 9_{5820}$ and: $570 \, 918 \, 348 \paren 0_{5819} 1$ where $\paren a_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string.

title: Pair of Ulam Numbers differing by One
snippet: == Open Question == The largest known pair of Ulam numbers which differ by $1$ are $47$ and $48$. It is not known whether there are any higher.

title: Pairs of Consecutive Integers with 6 Divisors
snippet: The following sequence of integers are those $n$ which fulfil the equation: $\map {\sigma_0} n = \map {\sigma_0} {n + 1} = 6$ where $\map {\sigma_0} n$ denotes the divisor count function. That is, they are the first of pairs of consecutive integers which each have $6$ divisors: $44, 75, 98, 116, 147, 171, 242, 243, 244, 332, \ldots$

title: Pairs of Integers whose Product with Divisor Count are Equal
snippet: Let $\map {\sigma_0} n$ denote the divisor count function: the number of divisors of $n$. The following pairs of integers $T$ have the property that $m \, \map {\sigma_0} m$ is equal for each $m \in T$: $\set {18, 27}$ $\set {24, 32}$ $\set {56, 64}$

title: Pairwise Disjoint Sets Partition Any Sets in Semiring
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\mathbb S$ be a semiring of sets. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ all belong to $\mathbb S$. Then there exists a finite system of pairwise disjoint sets: $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_t \in \mathbb S$ such that every $A_k$ where $k \in \closedint 1 n$ has a finite expansion: $\ds A_k = \bigcap_{s \mathop \in M_k} B_s$ where $M_k \subseteq \closedint 1 s$.

title: Pairwise Disjoint Subsets in Semiring Part of Partition
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\mathbb S$ be a semiring of sets. Let $A, A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ all belong to $\mathbb S$. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ all be pairwise disjoint subsets of $A$. Then there exists a finite expansion of $A$: $\ds \exists s \ge n: A = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^s A_k$ with $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ as its first $n$ elements, such that: $(1): \quad \forall k, 1 \le k \le s: A_k \in \mathbb S$ $(2): \quad \forall k, l, 1 \le k \le s, 1 \le l \le s: k \ne l \implies A_k \cap A_l = \O$.

title: Parabola is Mechanical Curve
snippet: The parabola is a mechanical curve. That is, it cannot be constructed using a compass and straightedge. However, as many points as is desired can be so constructed that lie on any given parabola.

title: Paracompactness is Preserved under Projections

title: Parallactic Angle in terms of Azimuth and Declination
snippet: Let $x$ be a point on the celestial sphere. Let $q$ denote the parallactic angle of $x$. Then: $\sin q := \dfrac {\cos \phi \sin A} {\sin \delta}$ where: $\phi$ is the terrestrial latitude $A$ is the azimuth $\delta$ is the declination.

title: Parameterization Theorem
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N$ be natural numbers. There exists a primitive recursive function $S^m_n : \N^{1 + m} \to \N$ such that, for $e, x_1, \dotsc, x_m$: If $e$ is not the code for a URM program, $\map {S^m_n} {e, x_1, \dotsc, x_m} = 0$ Otherwise, let $P$ be that program. Let $f$ be the $m + n$-arity function computed by $P$. Then $\map {S^m_n} {e, x_1, \dotsc, x_m}$ is the code for a URM program $P'$ computing a function $g : \N^n \to \N$, such that: $\map g {y_1, \dotsc, y_n} = \map f {x_1, \dotsc, x_m, y_1, \dotsc, y_n}$ whenever $f$ is defined, and undefined otherwise.

title: Parameterization of Unit Circle is Simple Loop

Let $p: \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be defined by: $\forall t \in \closedint 0 1 : \map p t = \tuple {\map \cos {2 \pi t}, \map \sin {2 \pi t} }$ Then $p$ is a simple loop with image equal to $\mathbb S^1$.

snippet: Let $\LL$ be a linear $\tuple {n, 2}$-code with a parity check. Then $\LL$ is such that one transmission error will be detected.

title: Parity Function is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$. Let $\map \sgn \pi$ be the sign of $\pi$. Let the parity function of $\pi$ be defined as: Parity of $\pi = \begin {cases} \mathrm {Even} & : \map \sgn \pi = 1 \\ \mathrm {Odd} & : \map \sgn \pi = -1 \end {cases}$ The mapping $\sgn: S_n \to C_2$, where $C_2$ is the cyclic group of order 2, is a homomorphism.

title: Parity Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $R := \struct {\set {\text{even}, \text{odd} }, +, \times}$ be the parity ring. The operation $\times$ is associative: $\forall a, b, c \in R: \paren {a \times b} \times c = a \times \paren {b \times c}$

title: Parity of Best Rational Approximations to Root 2
snippet: Consider the Sequence of Best Rational Approximations to Square Root of 2: $\sequence S := \dfrac 1 1, \dfrac 3 2, \dfrac 7 5, \dfrac {17} {12}, \dfrac {41} {29}, \dfrac {99} {70}, \dfrac {239} {169}, \dfrac {577} {408}, \ldots$ where $S_1 := \dfrac 1 1$. The numerators of the terms of $\sequence S$ are all odd. For all $n$, the parity of the denominator of term $S_n$ is the same as the parity of $n$.

title: Parity of Conjugate of Permutation
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Then: $\forall \pi, \rho \in S_n: \map \sgn {\pi \rho \pi^{-1} } = \map \sgn \rho$ where $\map \sgn \pi$ is the sign of $\pi$.

title: Parity of Integer equals Parity of Positive Power
snippet: Let $p \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Then $p$ is even $p^n$ is even. That is, the parity of an integer equals the parity of all its (strictly) positive powers.

title: Parity of Integer equals Parity of its Square
snippet: Let $p \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $p$ is even $p^2$ is even.

title: Parity of Inverse of Permutation
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Then: $\forall \pi \in S_n: \map \sgn \pi = \map \sgn {\pi^{-1} }$

title: Parity of K-Cycle
snippet: Let $\pi$ be a $k$-cycle. Then: $\map \sgn \pi = \begin{cases} 1 & : k \ \text {odd} \\ -1 & : k \ \text {even} \end{cases}$ Thus: $\map \sgn \pi = \paren {-1}^{k - 1}$ or equivalently: $\map \sgn \pi = \paren {-1}^{k + 1}$

title: Parity of Numbers in Amicable Pair
snippet: == Open Question == It is not known whether it is possible for the numbers in an amicable pair to have opposite parity. All known amicable pairs consist of numbers which are either both odd or both even.

title: Parity of Pell Numbers

title: Partial Denominators of Continued Fraction Expansion of Irrational Square Root
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ such that $n$ is not a square. Let the continued fraction expansion of $\sqrt n$ be expressed as: $\sqbrk {a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots}$ Then the partial denominators of this continued fraction expansion can be calculated as: $a_r = \floor {\dfrac {\floor {\sqrt n} + P_r} {Q_r} }$ where: $P_r = \begin{cases} 0 & : r = 0 \\ a_{r - 1} Q_{r - 1} - P_{r - 1} & : r > 0 \\ \end{cases}$ $Q_r = \begin{cases} 1 & : r = 0 \\ \dfrac {n - {P_r}^2} {Q_{r - 1} } & : r > 0 \\ \end{cases}$

title: Partial Derivative/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Partial Derivatives ==

title: Partial Derivative of Hamiltonian with respect to Displacement
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hamiltonian of a system: $\ds H = -F + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n y_i' F_{y_i'}$ where: $F$ is the Lagrangian of the system $y_i$ are the generalized coordinates $y_i'$ is the first derivative of $q_i$ time $p_i$ is the momentum of the system in those generalized coordinates: $p_i = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial q_i}$ Then the partial derivative of $H$ momentum is given by: $\dfrac {\partial H} {\partial y_i} = -p_i'$

title: Partial Derivative of Hamiltonian with respect to Momentum
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hamiltonian of a system: $\ds H = -F + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n y_i' F_{y_i'}$ where: $F$ is the Lagrangian of the system $y_i$ are the generalized coordinates $y_i'$ is the first derivative of $q_i$ time $p_i$ is the momentum of the system in those generalized coordinates: $p_i = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial q_i}$ Then the partial derivative of $H$ momentum is given by: $\dfrac {\partial H} {\partial p_i} = y_i'$

title: Partial Derivative of Hamiltonian with respect to Time
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hamiltonian of a system: $\ds H = -F + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n y_i' F_{y_i'}$ where: $F$ is the Lagrangian of the system $y_i$ are the generalized coordinates $y_i'$ is the first derivative of $q_i$ time $p_i$ is the momentum of the system in those generalized coordinates: $p_i = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial q_i}$ Then the partial derivative of $H$ time is given by: $\dfrac {\partial H} {\partial t} = \dfrac {\partial F} {\partial t}$

title: Partial Derivative wrt x of sin x y over cos (x + y)
snippet: $\dfrac \partial {\partial x} \dfrac {\sin x y} {\map \cos {x + y} } = \dfrac {y \map \cos {x + y} \cos x y + \map \sin {x + y} \sin x y} {\map {\cos^2} {x + y} }$

title: Partial Derivative wrt z of z^2 equals x^2 - 2 x y - 1 at (1, -2, -2)
snippet: Let $z^2 = x^2 - 2 x y - 1$. Then: $\valueat {\dfrac {\partial z} {\partial x} } {x \mathop = 1, y \mathop = -2, z \mathop = -2} = -\dfrac 3 2$

title: Partial Derivatives of Metric vanish at Origin of Normal Neighborhood
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Let $\struct {U_p, \tuple {x^i}}$ be a normal coordinate chart. Suppose $g_{ij}$ are the components of metric $g$ in coordinates $\tuple {x^i}$ at $p \in M$. Then all partial derivatives of $g_{ij}$ vanish at $p$: $\map {\dfrac {\partial g_{ij} }{\partial x^k} } {\map {x^r} p} = 0$

title: Partial Derivatives of Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi Equation are First Integrals of Euler's Equations
snippet: Let $\mathbf y = \sequence {y_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le n}$, $\bsalpha = \sequence {\alpha_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le m}$ be vectors, where $m \le n$. Let $S = \map S {x, \mathbf y, \bsalpha}$ be a solution of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, where $\bsalpha$ are parameters. Then each partial derivative: $\dfrac {\partial S} {\partial \alpha_i}$ is a first integral of canonical Euler's equations.

snippet: Let: $\map f {x, y} = \map {\tan^2} {x^2 - y^2}$ Then: {{eqn | l = \map {f_1} {x, y} | r = 4 x \map \tan {x^2 - y^2} \map {\sec^2} {x^2 - y^2} }} {{eqn | l = \map {f_2} {1, 2} | r = 8 \tan 3 \sec^2 3 }}

title: Partial Derivatives of u^2 + x^2 + y^2, u - v^3 + 3 x
snippet: Let: Then: {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} | r = -\dfrac x u }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial y} | r = -\dfrac y u }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial v} {\partial x} | r = \dfrac {x - 3 u} {3 u v^2} }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial v} {\partial y} | r = \dfrac y {3 u v^2} }}

title: Partial Derivatives of x^u + u^y
snippet: Let: $u = x^u + u^y$ Then: {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} | r = \frac {u^2} {x \paren {1 - u \ln x - y} } }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial y} | r = \frac {u \ln u} {1 - u \ln x - y} }}

title: Partial Derivatives of x^y^z
snippet: Let: $u = x^{\paren {y^z} }$ Then: {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} | r = y^z x^{\paren {y^z - 1} } }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial y} | r = x^{y^z} z y^{z - 1} \ln x }} {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial z} | r = x^{\paren {y^z} } y^z \ln x \ln y }}

title: Partial Derivatives of x ln y^2 + y e^z
snippet: Let: $\map f {x, y, z} = x \ln y^2 + y e^z$ Then: {{eqn | l = \map {f_1} {1, -1, 0} | r = 0 }} {{eqn | l = \map {f_2} {x, x y, y + z} | r = \dfrac 2 y + e^{y + z} }}

title: Partial Derivatives of x tan^-1 (x^2 + y)
snippet: Let: $\map f {x, y} = x \map \arctan {x^2 + y}$ Then: {{eqn | l = \map {f_1} {1, 0} | r = \dfrac \pi 4 + 1 }} {{eqn | l = \map {f_2} {x, y} | r = \dfrac x {1 + \paren {x^2 + y}^2} }}

title: Partial Difference of Integer Combinations is Integer Combination
snippet: == Lemma == Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $S = \set {a x + b y: x, y \in \Z}$ be the set of integer combinations of $a$ and $b$. Let $u \in S$ and $v \in S$. Then: $u \mathop {\dot -} v \in S$ where $\dot -$ denotes the extension of the partial subtraction operator to the integers.

title: Partial Gamma Function expressed as Integral
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{\ge 1}$. Let $\map {\Gamma_m} x$ denote the partial Gamma function, defined as: $\map {\Gamma_m} x := \dfrac {m^x m!} {x \paren {x + 1} \paren {x + 2} \cdots \paren {x + m} }$ Then: $\ds \map {\Gamma_m} x = \int_0^m \paren {1 - \frac t m}^m t^{x - 1} \rd t$ for $x > 0$.

title: Partial Ordering can be Expanded to compare Additional Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $a$ and $b$ be non-comparable elements of $S$. That is, let: $a \not\preceq b$ and: $b \not\preceq a$ Let ${\preceq'} = {\preceq} \cup \set {\tuple {a, b} }$. Let $\preceq'^+$ be the transitive closure of $\preceq'$. Then: $\preceq'^+$ is an ordering. $\preceq'^+$ can be defined by letting $p \preceq'^+ q$ : $p \preceq q$ or $p \preceq a$ and $b \preceq q$.

title: Partial Products of Uniformly Convergent Product Converge Uniformly
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly. Then the sequence of partial products converges uniformly.

title: Partial Sum Congruent to P-adic Integer Modulo Power of p
snippet: Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers for some prime $p$. Let $a \in \Z_p$. Let $\ds a = \sum_{j=0}^\infty d_j p^j$ be the $p$-adic expansion of $a$ For all $n \in \N$, let $\ds a_n = \sum_{j=0}^n d_j p^j$ be the $n$-th partial sum of the $p$-adic expansion of $a$ Then: $\forall n \in \N : a_n \equiv a \pmod{p^{n+1}\Z_p}$ where $a_n \equiv a \pmod{p^{n+1}\Z_p}$ denotes congruence modulo the ideal $\Z_p$.

title: Partial Sums of P-adic Expansion forms Coherent Sequence
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty d_n p^n$ be a $p$-adic expansion. Let $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ be the sequence of partial sums; that is: $\forall n \in \N :\alpha_n = \ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n d_i p^i$. Then $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ is a coherent sequence.

title: Partial Sums of Power Series with Fibonacci Coefficients
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n F_k x^k = \begin {cases} \dfrac {x^{n + 1} F_{n + 1} + x^{n + 2} F_n - x} {x^2 + x - 1} & : x^2 + x - 1 \ne 0 \\ \dfrac {\paren {n + 1} x^n F_{n + 1} + \paren {n + 2} x^{n + 1} F_n - 1} {2 x + 1} & : x^2 + x - 1 = 0 \end {cases}$ where $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number.

title: Particular Point Topology is Closed Extension Topology of Discrete Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $p \in S$. Let $\tau_p$ be the particular point topology on $S$. Let $T = \struct {S \setminus \set p, \vartheta}$ be the discrete topological space on $S \setminus \set p$. Then $T^* = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ is a closed extension space of $T$.

title: Particular Point Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Then $\tau_p$ is a topology on $S$, and $T$ is a topological space.

title: Particular Point Topology with Three Points is not T4

title: Particular Point of Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space is Dispersion Point
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\left({\Q, \tau_d}\right)$. Then $p$ is a dispersion point of $T^*$.

title: Particular Solution of Constant Coefficient Linear nth Order ODE
snippet: Consider the linear $n$th order ODE with constant coefficients: $(1): \quad \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n a_k \dfrac {\d^k y} {d x^k} = \map R x$ Let $(1)$ have the following $n$ initial conditions: $(2): \quad y = y_0, \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = y_1, \dotsc, \dfrac {\d^{n - 1} y} {\d x^{n - 1} } = y_{n - 1}$ when $x = x_0$. Then there exists exactly one particular solution of $(1)$ which satisfies $(2)$.

title: Particular Solution of System of Constant Coefficient Linear 1st Order ODEs
snippet: Consider the system of linear first order ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients: {{eqn | n = 1 | l = \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + a y + b z | r = 0 }} {{eqn | n = 2 | l = \dfrac {\d x} {\d z} + c y + d z | r = 0 }} Let $(1)$ and $(2)$ have the following $n$ initial conditions: $(3): \quad y = y_0, z = z_0$ when $x = x_0$. Then there exists exactly one particular solution of $(1)$ and $(2)$ which satisfies $(3)$.

title: Particular Solution to Homogeneous Linear Second Order ODE gives rise to Another
snippet: Let $\map {y_1} x$ be a particular solution to the homogeneous linear second order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + \map P x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map Q x y = 0$ such that $y_1$ is not the trivial solution. Then there exists a standard procedure to determine another particular solution $\map {y_2} x$ of $(1)$ such that $y_1$ and $y_2$ are linearly independent.

title: Partition of Non-Regular Prime Stellated Cyclic Polygons into Rotation Classes
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $C$ be a circle whose center is $O$. Consider the set $P$ of $p$ points on the circumference of $C$ dividing it into $p$ equal arcs. Let $S$ be the set of all non-regular stellated $p$-gons whose vertices are the elements of $P$. Let $\sim$ denote the equivalence relation on $S$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {a, b} \in S \times S: a \sim b \iff$ there exists a plane rotation about $O$ transforming $a$ to $b$. Then the $\sim$-equivalence classes of $S$ into which $S$ can thereby be partitioned all have cardinality $p$.

title: Partition of Singletons yields Discrete Topology

title: Partition of Spectrum of Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then: $\map \sigma T = \map {\sigma_p} T \cup \map {\sigma_s} T \cup \map {\sigma_r} T$ where: $\map {\sigma_p} T$ is the point spectrum of $T$ $\map {\sigma_s} T$ is the continuous spectrum of $T$. $\map {\sigma_r} T$ is the residual spectrum of $T$

title: Pascal's Rule
snippet: Let $\dbinom n k$ be a binomial coefficient. For positive integers $n, k$ with $1 \le k \le n$: $\dbinom n {k - 1} + \dbinom n k = \dbinom {n + 1} k$ This is also valid for the real number definition: $\forall r \in \R, k \in \Z: \dbinom r {k - 1} + \dbinom r k = \dbinom {r + 1} k$ Thus the binomial coefficients can be defined using the following recurrence relation: $\dbinom n k = \begin{cases} 1 & : k = 0 \\ 0 & : k > n \\ \dbinom {n - 1} {k - 1} + \dbinom {n - 1} k & : \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$

title: Pascal's Theorem
snippet: Let $ABCDEF$ be a hexagon whose $6$ vertices lie on a conic section and whose opposite sides are not parallel. Then the points of intersection of the opposite sides, when produced as necessary, all lie on a straight line.

title: Pascal's Wager
snippet: == Philosophical Argument == God either exists, or He does not. If God exists, then when I die, I will go either to Hell or to Heaven. If God does not exist, then when I die, my consciousness will simply vanish, and I will know nothing more. If God exists, and I do not believe in Him, then I will go to Hell. If God exists, and I do believe in Him, then I will go to Heaven. If God does not exist, then whether or not I believe in Him, I will vanish into oblivion. Therefore, if I do not believe in God, I will either vanish or go to Hell.

title: Pasch's Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d$ be points on a line. Let $\tuple {a, b, c}$ denote that $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$. Then $\tuple {a, b, c}$ and $\tuple {b, c, d}$ together imply that $\tuple {a, b, d}$. That is, if: $b$ is between $a$ and $c$ and: $c$ is between $b$ and $d$ then: $b$ is between $a$ and $d$.

title: Path-Connected Hausdorff Space is Arc-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff ($T_2$) topological space which is path-connected. Then $T$ is arc-connected.

title: Path-Connected Set in Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq B \subseteq S$. Let $T_B = \struct {B, \tau_B}$ be the topological space where $\tau_B$ is the subspace topology on $B$. Then $A$ is path-connected in $T_B$ $A$ is path-connected in $T$.

title: Path-Connected Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space which is path-connected. Then $T$ is connected.

title: Path-Connected Space is not necessarily Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is path-connected. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is also locally path-connected.

title: Path-Connected iff Path-Connected to Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $T$. Then $U$ is path-connected : $\exists p \in U: \forall q \in U: \exists f: \closedint 0 1 \to U: f$ continuous, $\map f 0 = p$ and $\map f 1 = q$

title: Path-Connectedness is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $a \sim b $ denote the relation: $a \sim b \iff a$ is path-connected to $b$ where $a, b \in S$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Path-Connectedness is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {T_1, \tau_1}, \struct {T_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_1 \to T_2$ be a homeomorphism. Let $S \subseteq T_1$ be a subset of $T_1$. Let $S$ be path-connected in $\struct {T_1, \tau_1}$. Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is path-connected in $\struct {T_2, \tau_2}$. That is, path-connectedness is a topological property.

title: Path-Homotopic Paths have Path Homotopy
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $f, g: \closedint 0 1 \to X$ be paths. Then $f$ and $g$ are path-homotopic, there exists a path homotopy between $f$ and $g$.

title: Path Component is not necessarily Injective Path Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $P$ be a path component of $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $P$ is also an injective path component of $T$.

title: Path Component of Locally Path-Connected Space is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a locally path-connected topological space. Let $G$ be a path component of $T$. Then $G$ is open in $T$.

title: Path Component of Locally Path-Connected Space is Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a locally path-connected topological space. Let $G$ be a path component of $T$. Then $G$ is open in $T$.

title: Path Components are Open iff Union of Open Path-Connected Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad$ The path components of $T$ are open. $(2): \quad S$ is a union of open path-connected sets of $T$.

title: Path Graph from Cycle Graph
snippet: Removing one edge from a cycle graph leaves a path graph.

title: Path Homotopy is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $p, q \in X$. Then path homotopy on the set of all paths in $X$ from $p$ to $q$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Path as Parameterization of Contour
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \C$ be a path. Let there exist $n \in \N$ and a subdivision $\set {a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n}$ of $\closedint a b$ such that: $\gamma {\restriction_{\closedint {a_{k - 1} } {a_k} } }$ is a smooth path for all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$ where $\gamma {\restriction_{\closedint {a_{k - 1} } {a_k} } }$ denotes the restriction of $\gamma$ to $\closedint {a_{k - 1} } {a_k}$. Then there exists a contour $C$ with parameterization $\gamma$.

snippet: Let $R = \closedint a b \times \closedint c d$ be a closed rectangle. Let $p, q : \closedint {-1} 1 \to R$ be paths in $R$. The path $q$ begins on the bottom edge of $R$, and ends on the top edge.

title: Paths of Minimal Length from Vertex form Tree
snippet: Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a simple graph. Let $r \in V$ be a vertex in $G$. Let $P$ be the set of minimal length paths beginning at $r$. Let $p, q \in P$. title: Perfect Number/Flow Chart
snippet: == Flow Chart for Calculation of Perfect Numbers == The following flow chart can be used to define an algorithm (not particularly efficient) for finding all perfect numbers under $500$: 400px

title: Perfect Number has at least Two Distinct Prime Factors
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a perfect number. Then $n$ has at least two distinct prime factors.

title: Perfect Number is Ore Number
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a perfect number. Then $n$ is an Ore number.

title: Perfect Number is Primitive Semiperfect
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a perfect number. Then $n$ is also a primitive semiperfect number.

title: Perfect Number which is Sum of Equal Powers of Two Numbers
snippet: $28$ is the only perfect number which is the sum of equal powers of exactly $2$ positive integers: $28 = 1^3 + 3^3$

title: Perfect Square Dissection of Lowest Order
snippet: The perfect square dissection of lowest order is of an integer square of side $112$ into $21$ parts.

title: Perfectly Normal Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a perfectly normal space. Then $T$ is also a completely normal space.

title: Perfectly T4 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a perfectly $T_4$ space. Then every subspace of $T$ is also perfectly $T_4$. That is, the property of being perfectly $T_4$ is hereditary.

title: Perfectly T4 Space is T5
snippet: Every perfectly $T_4$ space is a $T_5$ space.

title: Perimeter of Circle
snippet: The perimeter $C$ of a circle with radius $r$ is given by: $C = 2 \pi r$

title: Perimeter of Ellipse
snippet: Let $K$ be an ellipse whose major axis is of length $2 a$ and whose minor axis is of length $2 b$. The perimeter $\PP$ of $K$ is given by: $\PP = 4 a \map E e$ where: $\ds \map E e = \int_0^{\pi / 2} \sqrt{1 - e^2 \sin^2 \theta} \rd \theta$ is the complete elliptic integral of the second kind $e = \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a$ is the eccentricity of $K$.

title: Perimeter of Parallelogram
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram whose side lengths are $a$ and $b$. The perimeter of $ABCD$ is $2 a + 2 b$.

title: Perimeter of Rectangle
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a rectangle whose side lengths are $a$ and $b$. The perimeter of $ABCD$ is $2 a + 2 b$.

title: Perimeter of Regular Polygon
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-sided polygon whose side length is $b$. Then the perimeter $L$ of $P$ is given by: $L = n b$

title: Perimeter of Regular Polygon by Circumradius
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Let $C$ be a circumcircle of $P$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Then the perimeter $\PP$ of $P$ is given by: $\PP = 2 n r \sin \dfrac \pi n$

title: Perimeter of Regular Polygon by Inradius
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Let $C$ be an incircle of $P$. Let the radius of $C$ be $r$. Then the perimeter $\PP$ of $P$ is given by: $\PP = 2 n r \tan \dfrac \pi n$

title: Perimeter of Trapezium
snippet: 400px Let $ABCD$ be a trapezium: whose parallel sides are of lengths $a$ and $b$ whose height is $h$. and whose non-parallel sides are at angles $\theta$ and $\phi$ with the parallels. The perimeter $P$ of $ABCD$ is given by: $P = a + b + h \paren {\csc \theta + \csc \phi}$ where $\csc$ denotes cosecant.

title: Perimeter of Triangle
snippet: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Then the perimeter $P$ of $ABC$ is given by: $P = a + b + c$ where $a, b, c$ are the lengths of the sides of $ABC$.

title: Period of Complex Exponential Function
snippet: Let $z \in \C$, and let $k \in \Z$. Then: $\map \exp {z + 2 k \pi i} = \map \exp z$

title: Period of Harmonic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = a \map \cos {\omega \paren {x - c t} }$ The period $\tau$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\tau = \dfrac \lambda c$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

title: Period of Oscillation of Underdamped Cart attached to Wall by Spring
Period of Oscillation of Underdamped System is Regular
snippet: Consider a physical system $S$ whose behaviour can be described with the second order ODE in the form: $\dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d t^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d x} {\d t} + a^2 x = 0$ for $a, b \in \R_{>0}$. Let $b < a$, so as to make $S$ underdamped. Then the period of its movement is well-defined, in the sense that its zeroes are regularly spaced, and given by: $T = \dfrac {2 \pi} {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} }$

title: Period of Periodic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a periodic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = \map f {x - c t}$ The period $\tau$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\tau = \dfrac \lambda c$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

title: Period of Real Cosine Function
snippet: The period of the real cosine function is $2 \pi$. That is, $2 \pi$ is the smallest value $L \in \R_{>0}$ such that: $\forall x \in \R: \cos x = \map \cos {x + L}$

title: Period of Real Sine Function
snippet: The period of the real sine function is $2 \pi$. That is, $2 \pi$ is the smallest value $L \in \R_{>0}$ such that: $\forall x \in \R: \sin x = \map \sin {x + L}$

title: Period of Reciprocal of 43 is Odd
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of $43$ has an odd period, that is, $21$: $\dfrac 1 {43} = 0 \cdotp \dot 02325 \, 58139 \, 53488 \, 37209 \, \dot 3$

title: Period of Reciprocal of 53 is One Quarter of Maximal
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of $53$ has $\dfrac 1 4$ the maximum period, that is: $13$: $\dfrac 1 {53} = 0 \cdotp \dot 01886 \, 79245 \, 28 \dot 3$

title: Period of Reciprocal of 729 is 81
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of $729$ has $\dfrac 1 9$ the maximum period, that is, $81$: $\dfrac 1 {729} = 0 \cdotp \dot 00137 \, 17421 \, 12482 \, 85322 \, 35939 \, 64334 \, 70507 \, 54458 \, 16186 \, 55692 \, 72976 \, 68038 \, 40877 \, 91495 \, 19890 \, 26063 \, \dot 1$ The recurring part can be arranged in groups of $9$ digits each, revealing an interesting pattern: that is, each row (apart from the last) can be obtained from the previous one by adding $111 \, 111 \, 111$ to it.

title: Period of Reciprocal of 79 is One Sixth of Maximal
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of $79$ has $\dfrac 1 6$ the maximum period, that is: $13$: $\dfrac 1 {79} = 0 \cdotp \dot 01265 \, 82278 \, 48 \dot 1$

title: Period of Reciprocal of Prime
snippet: Consider the decimal expansion of the reciprocal $\dfrac 1 p$ of a prime $p$. If $p \nmid a$, the decimal expansion of $\dfrac 1 p$ is periodic in base $a$ and its period of recurrence is the order of $a$ modulo $p$. If $p \divides a$, the decimal expansion of $\dfrac 1 p$ in base $a$ terminates.

title: Period of Reciprocal of Repunit 1031 is 1031
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of the repunit prime $R_{1031}$ has a period of $1031$. $\dfrac 1 {R_{1031}} = 0 \cdotp \underbrace{\dot 000 \ldots 000}_{1030} \dot 9$ This is the only prime number to have a period of exactly $1031$.

title: Period of Revolution of Conical Pendulum
snippet: Let $P$ be a conical pendulum. Let $h$ be the height of the pivot of $P$ above the circle in which $P$ is moving. Then the period of revolution of $P$ around the circle is given by: $T = 2 \pi \sqrt {\dfrac h g}$ where $g$ is the acceleration on $P$ caused by the gravitational field in which $P$ is suspended.

title: Period of Rotation of Plane of Oscillation of Foucault's Pendulum
snippet: Let $P$ be a Foucault pendulum. The plane of oscillation of $P$ rotates through a full circle in time $T$, where: $T = \dfrac D {\sin \lambda}$ where: $\lambda$ denotes the latitude on Earth at which $P$ is located $D$ denotes the length of a sidereal day.

title: Periodic Element is Multiple of Antiperiod
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real anti-periodic function with anti-period $A$. Let $L$ be a periodic element of $f$. Then $A \divides L$.

title: Periodic Element is Multiple of Period
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real periodic function with period $P$. Let $L$ be a periodic element of $f$. Then $P \divides L$.

title: Periodic Function as Mapping from Unit Circle
snippet: Let $\SS$ denote the unit circle whose center is at the origin of the Cartesian plane $\R^2$. Let $p: \R \to \SS$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map p x = \tuple {\cos x, \sin x}$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a periodic real function whose period is $2 \pi$. Then there exists a well-defined real-valued function $f': \SS \to \R$ such that: $f = f' \circ p$ where $f' \circ p$ denotes the composition of $f'$ with $p$.

title: Periodic Function is Continuous iff Mapping from Unit Circle is Continuous
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a periodic real function whose period is $2 \pi$. Let $\SS$ denote the unit circle whose center is at the origin of the Cartesian plane $\R^2$. Let $p: \R \to \SS$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map p x = \tuple {\cos x, \sin x}$ Let $f': \SS \to \R$ be the well-defined real-valued function such that: $f = f' \circ p$ where $f' \circ p$ denotes the composition of $f'$ with $p$. Then $f$ is continuous $f'$ is continuous.

title: Periodic Function plus Constant

title: Permutation Group is Subgroup of Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$, where $\circ$ denotes the composition operation. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a set of permutations of $S$ which forms a group under $\circ$. Then $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$.

title: Permutation Induces Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi \in S_n$. Let $\RR_\pi$ be the relation defined by: $i \mathrel {\RR_\pi} j \iff \exists k \in \Z: \map {\pi^k} i = j$ Then $\RR_\pi$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Permutation Representation defines Group Action
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $X$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma X$ be the symmetric group of $X$. Let $\rho: G \to \map \Gamma X$ be a permutation representation, that is, a homomorphism. The mapping $\phi: G \times X \to X$ associated to $\rho$, defined by: $\map \phi {g, x} = \map {\map \rho g} x$ is a group action.

title: Permutation Test/Examples

title: Permutation is Cyclic iff At Most One Non-Trivial Orbit
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\rho: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Then: $\rho$ is a cyclic permutation $S$ has no more than one orbit under $\rho$ with more than one element.

title: Permutation is Product of Transpositions
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Every element of $S_n$ can be expressed as a product of transpositions.

title: Permutation of Cosets
snippet: Let $G$ be a group and let $H \le G$. Let $\mathbb S$ be the set of all distinct left cosets of $H$ in $G$. Then: $(1): \quad$ For any $g \in G$, the mapping $\theta_g: \mathbb S \to \mathbb S$ defined by $\map {\theta_g} {x H} = g x H$ is a permutation of $\mathbb S$. $(2): \quad$ The mapping $\theta$ defined by $\map \theta g = \theta_g$ is a homomorphism from $G$ into the symmetric group on $\mathbb S$. $(3): \quad$ The kernel of $\theta$ is the subgroup $\ds \bigcap_{x \mathop \in G} x H x^{-1}$.

title: Permutation of Determinant Indices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$ over a field. Let $\lambda: \N_{> 0} \to \N_{> 0}$ be any fixed permutation on $\N_{> 0}$. Let $\map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$. Let $\struct {S_n, \circ}$ be the symmetric group of $n$ letters. Then: $\ds \map \det {\mathbf A} = \sum_{\mu \mathop \in S_n} \paren {\map \sgn \mu \map \sgn \lambda \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_{\map \lambda k, \map \mu k} }$ $\ds \map \det {\mathbf A} = \sum_{\mu \mathop \in S_n} \paren {\map \sgn \mu \map \sgn \lambda \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_{\map \mu k, \map \lambda k} }$…

title: Permutation of Indices
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Let $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$. Then:

title: Permutation of Indices of Product
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j = \prod_{\map R {\map \pi j} } a_{\map \pi j}$ where: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j$ denotes the continued product over $a_j$ for all $j$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R j$ $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$.

title: Permutation of Indices of Summation
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j = \sum_{\map R {\map \pi j} } a_{\map \pi j}$ where: $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j$ denotes the summation over $a_j$ for all $j$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R j$ $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$.

title: Permutation of Indices of Supremum
snippet: Let $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of the non-negative real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$ indexed by $I$. Let $\map R i$ be a propositional functions of $i \in I$. Let $\ds \sup_{\map R i} a_i$ be the indexed supremum on $\family {a_i}$. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R i} a_i = \sum_{\map R {\map \pi i} } a_{\map \pi i}$ where $\pi$ is a permutation on the fiber of truth of $R$.

title: Permutation of Set is Automorphism of Set under Left Operation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \gets}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ under the left operation. Let $f$ be a permutation on $S$. Then $f$ is an automorphism of $f$.

title: Permutation of Set is Automorphism of Set under Right Operation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \to}$ be the algebraic structure formed from $S$ under the right operation. Let $f$ be a permutation on $S$. Then $f$ is an automorphism of $f$.

title: Permutation of Variables of Primitive Recursive Function
snippet: Let $f: \N^k \to \N$ be a primitive recursive function. Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\set {1, 2, \ldots, k}$. Then the function $h: \N^k \to \N$ defined as: $\map h {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} = \map f {n_{\map \sigma 1}, n_{\map \sigma 2}, \ldots, n_{\map \sigma k} }$ is also primitive recursive.

title: Permutation on Polynomial is Group Action
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 0$. Let $F_n$ be the set of all polynomials in $n$ variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$: $F = \set {\map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}: f \text{ is a polynomial in $n$ variables} }$ Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $*: S_n \times F \to F$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \pi \in S_n, f \in F: \pi * \map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} = \map f {x_{\map \pi 1}, x_{\map \pi 2}, \ldots, x_{\map \pi n} }$ Then $*$ is a group action.

title: Perpendicular Axes Theorem
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a lamina. Let $O_x$ and $O_y$ be axes of rotation in the plane of $\LL$ perpendicular to each other and intersecting at $O$. Let $O_z$ be an axis of rotation of $\LL$ through $O$ perpendicular to both $O_x$ and $O_y$. Let $I_x$, $I_y$ and $I_z$ be the moments of inertia of $\LL$ about $O_x$, $O_y$ and $O_z$ respectively. Then: $I_z = I_x + I_y$

title: Perpendicular Bisector is Locus of Points Equidistant from Endpoints
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line segment. The locus of points which are equidistant from $A$ and $B$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.

title: Perpendicular Bisector is Unique
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line segment in a Euclidean geometry. Let $\LL$ be the perpendicular bisector of $AB$. Then $\LL$ is unique.

title: Perpendicular Bisector of Chord Passes Through Center
snippet: The perpendicular bisector of any chord of any given circle must pass through the center of that circle.

title: Perpendicular Bisector of Triangle is Altitude of Medial Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $\triangle DEF$ be the medial triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Let a perpendicular bisector be constructed on $AC$ at $F$ to intersect $DE$ at $P$. Then $FP$ is an altitude of $\triangle DEF$.

title: Perpendicular Bisectors of Triangle Meet at Point
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. The perpendicular bisectors of $AB$, $BC$ and $AC$ all intersect at the same point.

title: Perpendicular Distance from Point to Plane
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a plane embedded in a cartesian $3$-space, given by the equation: $a x + b y + c z + d = 0$ Let $p$ be a point in the cartesian $3$-space whose coordinates are given by: $p = \tuple {x_0, y_0, z_0}$ Then the perpendicular distance $D$ from $p$ to $\PP$ is given by: $D = \dfrac {\size {a x_0 + b y_0 + c z_0 + d} } {\sqrt {a^2 + b^2 + c^2} }$

title: Perpendicular Distance from Straight Line in Plane to Origin
snippet: Let $L$ be the straight line embedded in the cartesian plane whose equation is given as: $a x + b y = c$ Then the perpendicular distance $d$ between $L$ and $\tuple {0, 0}$ is given by: $d = \size {\dfrac c {\sqrt {a^2 + b^2} } }$

Perpendicular is Shortest Straight Line from Point to Plane
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a plane. Let $C$ be a point which is not on $\PP$. Let $D$ be a point on $\PP$ such that $CD$ is perpendicular to $\PP$. Then the length of $CD$ is less than the length of all other line segments that can be drawn from $C$ to $\PP$.

title: Perpendicular is Shortest Straight Line from Point to Straight Line
snippet: Let $AB$ be a straight line. Let $C$ be a point which is not on $AB$. Let $D$ be a point on $AB$ such that $CD$ is perpendicular to $AB$. Then the length of $CD$ is less than the length of all other line segments that can be drawn from $C$ to $AB$.

title: Perpendicularity is Antireflexive Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \perp l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$. Then $\perp$ is an antireflexive relation on $S$.

title: Perpendicularity is Antitransitive Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \perp l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$. Then $\perp$ is an antitransitive relation on $S$.

title: Perpendicularity is Symmetric Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of straight lines in the plane. For $l_1, l_2 \in S$, let $l_1 \perp l_2$ denote that $l_1$ is perpendicular to $l_2$. Then $\perp$ is a symmetric relation on $S$.

title: Pfaff's Transformation
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \C$. Let $\size x \map \Re b > 0$. Then: $\ds \map F {a, b; c; x} = \paren {1 - x}^{-a} \map F {a, c - b; c; \dfrac x {x - 1} }$ where: $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ $x^{\overline k}$ denotes the $k$th rising factorial power of $x$ $\map \Gamma {n + 1} = n!$ is the Gamma function.

title: Pfaff-Saalschütz Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \C$. Let $n \in Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds \map { {}_3 \operatorname F_2} { { {a, b, -n} \atop {c, 1 + a + b - c - n} } \, \middle \vert \, 1} = \dfrac {\paren {c - a}^{\overline n} \paren {c - b}^{\overline n} } { c^{\overline n} \paren {c - a - b}^{\overline n} }$ where: ${}_3 \operatorname F_2$ is the generalized hypergeometric function $x^{\overline k}$ denotes the $k$th rising factorial power of $x$.

title: Phillips-Sobczyk Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of bounded sequences. title: Plane Angle between Lines from Center to Vertices of Tetrahedron
snippet: Let $T$ be a regular tetrahedron. Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ be straight lines constructed from the center of $T$ to two of the vertices of $T$. title: Plane Curve Classification Theorem
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma, \tilde \gamma: I \to \R^2$ be smooth unit-speed curves on a plane. Let $N$ and $\tilde N$ be their normal vector fields. Let $\map {\kappa_N} t$ and $\map {\kappa_{\tilde N}} t$ be curvatures at $\map \gamma t$ and $\map {\tilde \gamma} t$ respectively. Then $\gamma$ and $\tilde \gamma$ are congruent by a direction-preserving congruence iff: $\forall t \in I : \map {\kappa_N} t = \map {\kappa_{\tilde N}} t$

title: Plane Reflection is Space Rotation
