title: Pluperfect Digital Invariant has less than 61 Digits
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a pluperfect digital invariant. Then $n$ has less than $61$ digits.

title: Poincaré Conjecture
snippet: Let $\Sigma^m$ be a smooth $m$-manifold. Let $\Sigma^m$ satisfy: $H_0 \struct {\Sigma; \Z} = 0$ and: $H_m \struct {\Sigma; \Z} = \Z$ Then $\Sigma^m$ is homeomorphic to the $m$-sphere $\Bbb S^m$. {{explain|Definition of the notation $H_0 \struct {\Sigma; \Z}$, nature of $H_0$ and $H_m$}}

title: Poincaré Duality Theorem
snippet: Let $M$ be an $n$-manifold. Let its $n$th homology group $\map {H_n} M$ be infinite and cyclic (that is, that $M$ is an orientable manifold). Then $\map {H_r} M$ is homeomorphic to the $\paren {n - r}$th cohomology group $\map {H^{n - r} } M$ for all $r$.

title: Poincaré Plane is Abstract Geometry
snippet: The Poincaré plane $\struct {\H, L_H}$ is an abstract geometry.

title: Poincaré Recurrence Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \BB, \mu, T}$ be a measure-preserving dynamical system. Then for each $A \in \BB$: $\ds \map \mu {A \setminus \bigcap_{N \mathop = 1}^\infty \bigcup_{n \mathop = N}^\infty T^{-n} \sqbrk A} = 0$ That is, for $\mu$-almost all $x\in A$ there are integers $0 < n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ such that $\map {T^{n_i} }x \in A$.

title: Point Evaluations are Continuous Linear Functionals on Space of Complex-Valued Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map \CC K$ be the space of complex-valued continuous functions of compact Hausdorff space. For $k \in K$, define $\delta_k : \map \CC K \to \C$ by: $\map {\delta_k} f = \map f k$ for each $f \in \map \CC K$. Then $\delta_k$ is a continuous linear functional on $\map \CC K$ and further: $\norm {\delta_k}_{\map \CC {K}^\ast} = 1$

title: Point Finite Set of Open Sets in Separable Space is Countable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a separable space. Let $\FF$ be a point finite set of open sets of $X$. Then $\FF$ is countable.

title: Point Lattice/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Point Lattices ==

title: Point Spectrum of Densely-Defined Linear Operator consists of its Eigenvalues
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a densely-defined linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_p} T$ be the point spectrum of $T$. Then $\lambda \in \map {\sigma_p} T$ $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $T$.

title: Point Spectrum of Symmetric Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a symmetric densely-defined linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_p} T$ be the point spectrum of $\struct {\map D T, T}$. Then: $\map {\sigma_p} T \subseteq \R$

title: Point at Distance Zero from Closed Set is Element
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be an arbitrary subset of $A$. Let $x \in A$ be arbitrary. Let $\map d {x, H}$ denote the distance between $x$ and $H$: $\ds \map d {x, H} = \inf_{y \mathop \in H} \paren {\map d {x, y} }$ Let $H$ be closed in $M$. Then: $\map d {x, H} = 0$ $x \in H$.

title: Point at Infinity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Point at Infinity ==

title: Point at Infinity of Intersection of Parallel Lines
snippet: Let $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ be straight lines embedded in a cartesian plane $\CC$ such that $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ are parallel. By Condition for Straight Lines in Plane to be Parallel, $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ can be expressed as the general equations: The point at infinity of $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ can thence be expressed in homogeneous Cartesian coordinates as $\tuple {-m, l, 0}$.

title: Point at Zero Distance from Subset of Metric Space is Limit Point or Element
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be an arbitrary subset of $A$. Let $x \in A$ be arbitrary. Let $\map d {x, H}$ denote the distance between $x$ and $H$: $\ds \map d {x, H} = \inf_{y \mathop \in H} \paren {\map d {x, y} }$ Then: $\map d {x, H} = 0$ either $x \in H$ or $x$ is a limit point of $H$.

title: Point at which Prime-Counting Function becomes less than Eulerian Logarithmic Integral
snippet: Let $\map \pi n$ denote the prime-counting function. Let $a \uparrow b$ be interpreted as Knuth notation for $a^b$.

title: Point dividing Line Segment between Two Points in Given Ratio
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be points whose position vectors relative to an origin $O$ of a Euclidean space are $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$. Let $\mathbf r$ be the position vector of a point $R$ on $AB$ which divides $AB$ in the ratio $m : n$. 320px Then: $\mathbf r = \dfrac {n \mathbf a + m \mathbf b} {m + n}$

title: Point in Closure of Sequence in Metric Space is Term of Sequence or Subsequential Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Let $\cl$ be the closure taken in $X$. Let $x \in \map \cl {\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} }$. Then either there exists $n \in \N$ with $x = x_n$ or there exists a subsequence $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ converging to $x$.

title: Point in Closure of Subset of Metric Space iff Limit of Sequence
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$. Let $a \in A$. Then $a \in H^-$ there exists a sequence $\sequence {x_n}$ of points of $H$ which converges to the limit $a$.

title: Point in Convex Set is Extreme Point iff Singleton is Extreme Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $K$ be a convex subset of $X$. Let $a \in K$. Then $a$ is an extreme point of $K$ : $\set a$ is an extreme set in $K$.

title: Point in Discrete Space is Adherent Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Let $U \subseteq S$. Then $x$ is an adherent point of $U$ $x \in U$.

title: Point in Discrete Space is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then $\set x$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$.

title: Point in Finite Metric Space is Isolated
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $X \subseteq A$ such that $X$ is finite. Let $x \in X$. Then $x$ is isolated in $X$.

title: Point in Finite T2 Space is Isolated
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $X \subseteq S$ such that $X$ is finite. Let $x \in X$. Then $x$ is isolated in $X$.

title: Point in Hilbert Sequence Space has no Compact Neighborhood
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then no point of $\ell^2$ has a compact neighborhood.

title: Point in Metric Space has Countable Neighborhood Basis
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$. Then there exists a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$ which is countable.

title: Point in Metric Space has Neighborhood
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$ be a point in $M$. Then there exists some neighborhood of $a$ in $M$.

title: Point in Metric Space is Element of its Neighborhood
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$ be a point in $M$. Let $N$ be a neighborhood of $a$ in $M$. Then $a \in N$.

title: Point in Open Set of Particular Point Space is not Omega-Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $x \in S$ such that $x \ne p$. Let $H \subseteq S$ such that $p \in H$. Then $x$ is not an $\omega$-accumulation point of $H$.

title: Point in Plane is Constructible iff Coordinates in Extension of Degree Power of 2
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a Cartesian plane. Let $S$ be a set of points in $\CC$. Let $F$ be the smallest field containing all the coordinates of the points in $S$. Let $P = \tuple {a, b}$ be a point in $\CC$. Then: $P$ is constructible from $S$ using a compass and straightedge construction the coordinates of $P$ are contained in a finite extension $K$ of $F$ whose degree is given by: $\index K F = 2^m$ for some $m \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.

title: Point in Set Closure iff Limit of Filter
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\cl$ denote closure in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\FF$ be a filter on $X$. Let $E \subseteq X$. Let $x \in X$. We have that $x \in \map \cl E$ there exists a filter on $X$ such that: $\FF$ converges to $x$ and: $E \in \FF$

title: Point in Set Closure iff Limit of Net
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $E \subseteq X$ be a subset. Let $\map \cl E$ be the closure of $E$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $x \in \map \cl E$ there exists a directed set $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ and a net $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ in $E$ converging to $x$.

title: Point in Standard Discrete Metric Space is Isolated
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, d}$ be the standard discrete metric space on a set $A$. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\alpha \in H$. The $\alpha$ is an isolated point of $H$.

title: Point in T1 Space is Intersection of Open Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then: $T$ is a $T_1$ space for every point $x \in S$, the singleton $\set x$ is the intersection of every open set $U$ of $T$ such that $x \in U$: $\forall x \in S: \set x = \ds \bigcap_{x \mathop \in U} \set {U \in \tau}$

title: Point in Topological Space has Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then there exists in $T$ at least one neighborhood of $x$. That is: $\forall x \in S: \NN_x \ne \O$ where $\NN_x$ is the neighborhood filter of $x$.

title: Point in Topological Space is Element of its Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $N$ be a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. Then $a \in N$. That is: $\forall x \in S: \forall N \in \NN_x: x \in N$ where $\NN_x$ is the neighborhood filter of $x$.

title: Point in Topological Space is Open iff Isolated
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then $\left\{{x}\right\}$ is open in $T$ $x$ is an isolated point of $T$.

title: Point is Cluster Point of Net iff Adherent Point of Generated Filter
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net. Let $x \in X$. Let $\FF$ be the filter generated by $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Then $x$ is a cluster point of $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ $x$ is an adherent point of $\FF$.

title: Point is Cluster Point of Net iff Limit of Subnet
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net. Let $x \in X$. Then $x$ is a cluster point of $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ : there exists a directed set $\struct {A, \sqsubseteq}$ and an increasing cofinal mapping $\lambda : A \to \Lambda$ such that: $\family {x_{\map \phi \alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a subnet converging to $x$.

title: Point is Contained in Irreducible Component
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $x\in X$ be a point. Then $x$ is contained in some irreducible component of $X$.

title: Point is Isolated iff belongs to Set less Derivative
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $x \in S$. Then: $x$ is an isolated point in $H$ $x \in H \setminus H'$ where $H'$ denotes the derivative of $H$.

title: Point is Isolated iff not Accumulation Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$. Let $x \in H$. Then: $x$ is an isolated point in $H$ $x$ is not an accumulation point of $H$

title: Point is Path-Connected to Itself
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $a \in S$. Then $a$ is path-connected to itself.

title: Point not in Subset of Metric Space iff Distance from Elements is Greater than Zero
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be an arbitrary subset of $A$. Let $x \in A$ be arbitrary. Then: $x \notin H$ $\forall y \in H: \map d {x, y} > 0$

title: Point of Intersection with Line at Infinity
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a straight line embedded in a cartesian plane $\CC$ given in homogeneous Cartesian coordinates by the equation: $l X + m Y + n_1 Z = 0$ Then $\LL$ intersects the line at infinity at the point: $\tuple {-m, l, 0}$

title: Point of Perpendicular Intersection on Real Line from Points in Complex Plane
snippet: Let $a, b \in \C$ be complex numbers represented by the points $A$ and $B$ respectively in the complex plane. Let $x \in \R$ be a real number represented by the point $X$ on the real axis such that $AXB$ is a right triangle with $X$ as the right angle. Then: $x = \dfrac {a_x - b_x \pm \sqrt {a_x^2 + b_x^2 + 2 a_x b_x - 4 a_y b_y} } 2$ where: $a = a_x + a_y i, b = b_x + b_y i$

title: Point with Zero Second Derivative is not necessarily Point of Inflection
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $\map {f' '} \xi = 0$ where $\map {f' '} \xi$ denotes the second derivative of $f$ at $\xi \in \openint a b$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f$ has a point of inflection at $\xi$.

title: Pointed Extension of Reals is not T3
snippet: Let $T$ be an pointed extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_3$ space.

title: Pointed Extension of Reals is not T4
snippet: Let $T$ be an pointed extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_4$ space.

title: Pointed Extension of Reals is not T5
snippet: Let $T$ be an pointed extension of $\R$. Then $T$ is not a $T_5$ space.

title: Points Defined by Adjacent Pairs of Digits of Reciprocal of 13 lie on Hyperbola
snippet: Consider the digits that form the recurring part of the reciprocal of $13$: $\dfrac 1 {13} = 0 \cdotp \dot 07692 \dot 3$ Take the digits in ordered pairs, and treat them as coordinates of a Cartesian plane. It will be found that they all lie on a hyperbola: 600px

title: Points Defined by Adjacent Pairs of Digits of Reciprocal of 7 lie on Ellipse
snippet: Consider the digits that form the recurring part of the reciprocal of $7$: $\dfrac 1 7 = 0 \cdotp \dot 14285 \dot 7$ Take the digits in ordered pairs, and treat them as coordinates of a Cartesian plane. It will be found that they all lie on an ellipse: 400px

title: Points are Path-Connected iff Contained in Path-Connected Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x, y \in S$ Then: $x, y$ are path-connected points in $T$ there exists a path-connected set of $T$ containing $x$ and $y$.

title: Points in Product Spaces are Near Open Sets
snippet: Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces, where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $X = \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the product space of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $U$ be nonempty open subset of $X$. Let $x$ be a point in $X$. For each point $y$ in $X$, let $\map K y = \set {i \in I : y_i \ne x_i}$. Then there exists a point $u$ in $U$ such that $\map K u$ is finite.

title: Points of Riemannian Manifold are Contained in Geodesically Convex Geodesic Balls
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\epsilon_0 \in \R_{> 0}$. Then for all $p \in M$ there exists a closed geodesic ball or open geodesic ball centered at $p \in M$ of radius $\epsilon \le \epsilon_0$ which is also geodesically convex.

title: Pointwise Addition is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\Z, \Q, \R$ or $\C$. Let $f, g, h: S \to \mathbb F$ be functions. Let $f + g: S \to \mathbb F$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f + g} + h = f + \paren {g + h}$ That is, pointwise addition is associative.

title: Pointwise Addition is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\Z, \Q, \R$ or $\C$. Let $f, g: S \to \mathbb F$ be functions. Let $f + g: S \to \mathbb F$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f + g = g + f$ That is, pointwise addition is commutative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Complex-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \C$ be complex-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \C$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f + g} + h = f + \paren {g + h}$ That is, pointwise addition on complex-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Complex-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to \C$ be complex-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \C$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f + g = g + f$ That is, pointwise addition of complex-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Continuous Real Functions forms Group
snippet: Let $C$ be the set of all continuous real functions on the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $f, g \in C$. Let $f + g$ be the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$: $\forall x \in R: \map {\paren {f + g} } x = \map f x + \map g x$ Then $\struct {C, +}$, the algebraic structure on $C$ induced by $+$, forms a group.

title: Pointwise Addition on Continuous Real Functions on Closed Unit Interval forms Group
snippet: Let $J \subseteq \R$ denote the closed unit interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $\map {\mathscr C} J$ denote the set of all continuous real functions from $J$ to $\R$. Let $\R^J$ denote the set of all mappings from $J$ to $\R$. Let $\struct {\R^J, +}$ denote the algebraic structure on $\R^J$ induced by addition: $\forall f, g \in \R^J: \map {\paren {f + g} } x = \map f x + \map g x$ Then $\struct {\map {\mathscr C} J, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\R^J, +}$.

title: Pointwise Addition on Differentiable Real Functions on Closed Unit Interval forms Group
snippet: Let $J \subseteq \R$ denote the closed unit interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $\map {\mathscr D} J$ denote the set of all differentiable real functions from $J$ to $\R$. Let $\R^J$ denote the set of all mappings from $J$ to $\R$. Let $\struct {\R^J, +}$ denote the algebraic structure on $\R^J$ induced by addition: $\forall f, g \in \R^J: \map {\paren {f + g} } x = \map f x + \map g x$ Then $\struct {\map {\mathscr D} J, +}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\R^J, +}$.

title: Pointwise Addition on Integer-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \Z$ be integer-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \Z$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f + g} + h = f + \paren {g + h}$ That is, pointwise addition on integer-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Integer-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to \Z$ be integer-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \Z$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f + g = g + f$ That is, pointwise addition of integer-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Rational-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \Q$ be rational-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \Q$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f + g} + h = f + \paren {g + h}$ That is, pointwise addition on rational-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Rational-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to \Q$ be rational-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \Q$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f + g = g + f$ That is, pointwise addition of rational-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Real-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \R$ be real-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \R$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f + g} + h = f + \paren {g + h}$ That is, pointwise addition on real-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to \R$ be real-valued functions. Let $f + g: S \to \R$ denote the pointwise sum of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f + g = g + f$ That is, pointwise addition of real-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Addition on Space of Real-Valued Measurable Functions Identified by A.E. Equality is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$ be the set of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions on $X$. Let $\sim$ be the almost-everywhere equality relation on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ be the space of real-valued measurable functions identified by $\mu$-A.E. equality. Then pointwise addition on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ is well-defined.

title: Pointwise Addition preserves A.E. Equality
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g, F, G : X \to \overline \R$ be functions with: $f = F$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and: $g = G$ $\mu$-almost everywhere and the pointwise sums $f + g$ and $F + G$ well-defined. Then: $f + g = F + G$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

title: Pointwise Cauchyness of Sequence of Continuous Linear Transformations on Non-Meager Set implies Everywhere Pointwise Cauchyness
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological vector spaces. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of continuous linear transformations $T_n : X \to Y$ such that: the set $C$ of $x \in X$ such that $\sequence {T_n x}_{n \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence is non-meager. Then $C = X$, so that: $\sequence {T_n x}_{n \in \N}$ is Cauchy for each $x \in X$.

title: Pointwise Convergence Implies Convergence in Measure on Finite Measure Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a finite measure space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}, f_n : X \to \R$ be a sequence of measurable functions. Also, let $f: X \to \R$ be a measurable function. Suppose that $f$ is the pointwise limit of the $f_n$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Then $f_n$ converges in measure to $f$ (in $\mu$). That is: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} x \stackrel {a.e.} {=} \map f x \implies \operatorname {\mu-\!\lim\,} \limits_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n = f$

title: Pointwise Convergence implies Convergence Almost Everywhere
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. For each $n \mathop \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then: if $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges pointwise to $f$, it converges almost everywhere to $f$.

title: Pointwise Convergent Bounded Sequence in Lebesgue Space Converges in Norm
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}, f_n: X \to \R$ be a sequence in Lebesgue $p$-space $\map {\LL^p} \mu$. Suppose that the pointwise limit $f := \ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n$ exists $\mu$-almost everywhere. Suppose that for some $g \in \map {\LL^p} \mu$, the pointwise inequality $\size {f_n} \le g$ holds for all $n \in \N$. Then $f \in \map {\LL^p} \mu$, and: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \norm {f - f_n}_p = 0$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_p$ denotes the $p$-seminorm.

title: Pointwise Difference is Pointwise Addition with Negation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $f, g :S \to \R$ be real-valued functions. Let $f - g$ denote the pointwise difference of $f$ and $g$, that is, $f - g$ is the mapping defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {\paren{f - g} } s = \map f s - \map g s$ Then: $f - g = f + \paren{-g}$ where: $-g$ denotes the pointwise negation of $g$ $f + \paren{-g}$ denotes the pointwise addition of $f$ and $-g$

title: Pointwise Difference of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Assume that the pointwise difference $f - g: X \to \overline \R$ is well-defined. Then $f - g$ is a $\Sigma$-measurable function.

title: Pointwise Difference of Simple Functions is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f,g : X \to \R$ be simple functions. Let $f - g: X \to \R$ be the pointwise difference of $f$ and $g$: $\forall x \in X: \map {\paren {f - g} } x := \map f x - \map g x$ Then $f - g$ is also a simple function.

title: Pointwise Exponentiation preserves A.E. Equality
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space and let $p \in \hointr 0 \infty$. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions such that: $\size f = \size g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Then: $\size f^p = \size g^p$ $\mu$-almost everywhere.

title: Pointwise Infimum of Family of Concave Real Functions is Concave
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a non-empty convex set. Let $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of concave functions $f_\alpha : C \to \overline \R$. Let: $\ds f = \inf_{\alpha \mathop \in I} f_\alpha$ be the pointwise infimum of $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Then $f$ is concave.

title: Pointwise Infimum of Family of Upper Semicontinuous Functions is Upper Semicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a set of upper semicontinuous functions $f_\alpha : X \to \overline \R$. Define $f : X \to \overline \R$ by: $\ds \map f x = \liminf_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \map {f_\alpha} x$ for each $x \in X$. Then $f$ is upper semicontinuous.

title: Pointwise Infimum of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $I$ be a countable set. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$, $f_i: X \to \overline \R$ be an $I$-indexed family of $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise infimum $\ds \inf_{i \mathop \in I} f_i: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Infimum of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let: $\ds T = \inf_{n \in \N} T_n$ be the pointwise infimum of the $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$. Then $T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Inverse in Induced Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be a group whose identity is $e_G$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $G^S$ induced by $\oplus$. Let $f \in G^S$. Let $f^* \in G^S$ be the pointwise inverse of $f$: $\forall x \in S: \map {f^*} x = \paren {\map f x}^{-1}$ Then $f^*$ is the inverse of $f$ for the pointwise operation induced on $G^S$ by $\oplus$.

title: Pointwise Limit Inferior of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let: $\ds T = \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} T_n$ be the pointwise limit inferior of the $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$. Then $T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Limit Superior of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let: $\ds T = \limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} T_n$ be the pointwise limit superior of the $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$. Then $T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Limit of Increasing Functions is Increasing
snippet: Let $X \subseteq \R$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $X \to \R$ converging pointwise to a function $f : X \to \R$. Let $f_n$ be a increasing function for each $n$. Then $f$ is increasing.

title: Pointwise Limit of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise limit $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Limit of Sequence of Bounded Linear Transformations from Banach Space to Normed Vector Space is Bounded Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ be a Banach space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\struct {Y, \norm \cdot_Y}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a function. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of bounded linear transformations such that: $\ds T x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} T_n x$ for each $x \in X$. Then $T$ is a bounded linear transformation.

title: Pointwise Lower Limit of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise lower limit: $\ds \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Maximum of Finite Family of Seminorms is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_K}$ be a normed division ring. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $\II$ be a set of seminorms on $X$. Define: $\ds q =: \max_{p \mathop \in \II} p$ where $\max$ denotes the pointwise maximum over $\II$.

title: Pointwise Maximum of Integrable Functions is Integrable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $\map \max {f, g}$, the pointwise maximum of $f$ and $g$, is also a $\mu$-integrable function. That is, the space of $\mu$-integrable functions $\LL^1_{\overline \R}$ is closed under pointwise maximum.

title: Pointwise Maximum of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise maximum $\max \set {f, g}: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Maximum of Simple Functions is Simple
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be simple functions. Then the pointwise maximum $\max \set {f, g}: X \to \R$ is also simple function.

title: Pointwise Maximum of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $T$ and $S$ be stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $S \vee T$ be the pointwise maximum of $S$ and $T$. Then $S \vee T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Minimum of Integrable Functions is Integrable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $\map \min {f, g}$, the pointwise minimum of $f$ and $g$, is also a $\mu$-integrable function. That is, the space of $\mu$-integrable functions $\LL^1_{\overline \R}$ is closed under pointwise minimum.

title: Pointwise Minimum of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise minimum $\min \set {f, g}: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Minimum of Metric and Positive Real Number is Topologically Equivalent Metric
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $c > 0$ be a real number. For each $x, y \in X$, define: $\map {d'} {x, y} = \min \set {\map d {x, y}, c}$ Then $d'$ is a metric that is topologically equivalent to $d$.

title: Pointwise Minimum of Simple Functions is Simple
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be simple functions. Then the pointwise minimum $\min \set {f, g}: X \to \R$ is also simple function.

title: Pointwise Minimum of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $T$ and $S$ be stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $S \wedge T$ be the pointwise minimum of $S$ and $T$. Then $S \wedge T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Multiplication is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\Z, \Q, \R$ or $\C$. Let $f, g, h: S \to \mathbb F$ be functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \mathbb F$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f \times g} \times h = f \times \paren {g \times h}$ That is, pointwise multiplication is associative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $\mathbb F$ be one of the standard number sets: $\Z, \Q, \R$ or $\C$. Let $f, g, h: S \to \mathbb F$ be functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \mathbb F$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f \times g = g \times f$ That is, pointwise multiplication is commutative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Complex-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \C$ be complex-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \C$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f \times g} \times h = f \times \paren {g \times h}$ That is, pointwise multiplication on complex-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Complex-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g: S \to \C$ be complex-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \C$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f \times g = g \times f$ That is, pointwise multiplication of complex-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Integer-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \Z$ be integer-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \Z$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f \times g} \times h = f \times \paren {g \times h}$ That is, pointwise multiplication on integer-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Integer-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f, g: S \to \Z$ be integer-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \Z$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f \times g = g \times f$ That is, pointwise multiplication of integer-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Rational-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \Q$ be rational-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \Q$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f \times g} \times h = f \times \paren {g \times h}$ That is, pointwise multiplication on rational-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Rational-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g: S \to \Q$ be rational-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \Q$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f \times g = g \times f$ That is, pointwise multiplication of rational-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Real-Valued Functions is Associative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g, h: S \to \R$ be real-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \R$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $\paren {f \times g} \times h = f \times \paren {g \times h}$ That is, pointwise multiplication on real-valued functions is associative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Let $f, g: S \to \R$ be real-valued functions. Let $f \times g: S \to \R$ denote the pointwise product of $f$ and $g$. Then: $f \times g = g \times f$ That is, pointwise multiplication of real-valued functions is commutative.

title: Pointwise Multiplication on Space of Real-Valued Measurable Functions Identified by A.E. Equality is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$ be the set of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions on $X$. Let $\sim$ be the almost-everywhere equality equivalence relation on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ be the space of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions identified by $\sim$. Then pointwise scalar multiplication on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ is well-defined.

title: Pointwise Multiplication preserves A.E. Equality
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g, h : X \to \overline \R$ be functions with: $f = g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Then: $f \times h = g \times h$ $\mu$-almost everywhere where $f \times h$ and $g \times h$ are the pointwise products of $f$ and $h$, and $g$ and $h$ respectively.

title: Pointwise Operation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Pointwise Operations ==

title: Pointwise Operation is Composite of Operation with Mapping to Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, *}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Let the algebraic structure $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the algebraic structure on $T^S$ induced by $*$. Let $f, g \in T^S$, that is, let $f: S \to T$ and $g: S \to T$ be mappings. Let $f \times g : S \to T \times T$ be the mapping from $S$ to the cartesian product $T \times T$ defined by: $\forall x \in S : \map {\paren {f \times g}} x = \tuple {\map f x, \map g x}$ Then: $f \oplus g = * \circ \paren {f \times g}$ That is, $f \oplus g$ is the composition of the binary…

title: Pointwise Operation on Distributive Structure is Distributive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, +, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure with two operations $+$ and $\circ$. Let $T^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Let $\struct {T^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure induced on $T^S$ by $+$ and $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be distributive over $+$ in $T$. Then $\circ'$ is distributive over $+'$ in $T$.

title: Pointwise Product of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise product $f \cdot g: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Product of Simple Functions is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be simple functions. Then $f \cdot g: X \to \R, \map {\paren {f \cdot g} } x := \map f x \cdot \map g x$ is also a simple function.

title: Pointwise Scalar Multiple of Measurable Function is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\alpha \in \overline \R$ be an extended real number. Then the pointwise scalar multiple $\alpha f$ is $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Scalar Multiplication on Space of Real-Valued Measurable Functions Identified by A.E. Equality is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$ be the set of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions on $X$. Let $\sim$ be the $\mu$-almost-everywhere equality relation on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}$. Let $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ be the space of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions identified by $\sim$. Then pointwise scalar multiplication on $\map {\mathcal M} {X, \Sigma, \R}/\sim$ is well-defined.

title: Pointwise Scalar Multiplication preserves A.E. Equality
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be extended real-valued functions such that: $f = g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Let $\lambda \in \overline \R$. Then: $\lambda \cdot f = \lambda \cdot g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere where $\lambda \cdot f$ denotes pointwise scalar multiplication.

title: Pointwise Sum of Integrable Functions is Integrable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Suppose that their pointwise sum $f + g$ is well-defined. Then $f + g$ is also a $\mu$-integrable function. That is, the space of $\mu$-integrable functions $\LL^1_{\overline \R}$ is closed under pointwise addition.

title: Pointwise Sum of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Assume that the pointwise sum $f + g: X \to \overline \R$ is well-defined. Then $f + g$ is a $\Sigma$-measurable function.

title: Pointwise Sum of Simple Functions is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be simple functions. Then the pointwise sum $f + g: X \to \R$ of $f$ and $g$: $\forall x, y \in X: \map {\paren {f + g} } x := \map f x + \map g x$ is also a simple function.

title: Pointwise Supremum of Family of Convex Real Functions is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a non-empty convex set. Let $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of convex functions $f_\alpha : C \to \overline \R$. Let: $\ds f = \sup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} f_\alpha$ be the pointwise supremum of $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$. Then $f$ is convex.

title: Pointwise Supremum of Family of Lower Semicontinuous Functions is Lower Semicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {f_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a set of lower semicontinuous functions $f_\alpha : X \to \overline \R$. Define $f : X \to \overline \R$ by: $\ds \map f x = \limsup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \map {f_\alpha} x$ for each $x \in X$. Then $f$ is lower semicontinuous.

title: Pointwise Supremum of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space, and let $I$ be a countable set. Let $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$, $f_i: X \to \overline \R$ be an $I$-indexed collection of $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise supremum $\ds \sup_{i \mathop \in I} f_i: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Pointwise Supremum of Stopping Times is Stopping Time
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a sequence of stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let: $\ds T = \sup_{n \in \N} T_n$ be the pointwise supremum of the $\sequence {T_n}_{n \in \N}$. Then $T$ is a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$.

title: Pointwise Upper Limit of Measurable Functions is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Then the pointwise upper limit $\ds \limsup_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ is also $\Sigma$-measurable.

title: Poisson's Differential Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Poisson's Differential Equation ==

title: Poisson's Differential Equation for Rotational and Solenoidal Field
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of ordinary space. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field over $R$. Let $\mathbf V$ be both rotational and solenoidal. Let $\mathbf A$ be a vector field such that $\mathbf V = \curl \mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf V$ satisfies this version of Poisson's differential equation: $\curl \mathbf V = -\nabla^2 \mathbf A \ne \bszero$

title: Poisson Bracket satisfies Jacobi Identity
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let: $\map A {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf p}: \R^{2 n + 1} \to \R$ $\map B {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf p}: \R^{2 n + 1} \to \R$ be real functions, dependent on canonical variables. Let $\sqbrk {A, B}$ denote the Poisson bracket of $A$ and $B$. Then: $\sqbrk {A, \sqbrk {B, C} } + \sqbrk {B, \sqbrk {C, A} } + \sqbrk {C, \sqbrk {A, B} } = 0$ That is, the Poisson bracket operation satisfies the Jacobi identity.

snippet: Let $P$ be a classical particle embedded in a 2-dimensional Euclidean manifold.
