title: Projection from Product Topology is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are are continuous.

title: Projection from Product Topology is Open
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are open.

title: Projection from Product Topology is Open and Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then both $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are open and continuous.

title: Projection from Topological Product is Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $T = \struct {T_1 \times T_2, \tau}$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$, where $\tau$ is the product topology on $S$. Let $\pr_1: T \to T_1$ and $\pr_2: T \to T_2$ be the first and second projections from $T$ onto its factors. Then $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are identification mappings.

title: Projection in Plane between Lines passing through Origin is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $M$ and $N$ be distinct straight lines through the plane through the origin. Let $\pr_{M, N}$ be the projection on $M$ along $N$. Then $\pr_{M, N}$ is a linear operator.

title: Projection in Plane on X-Axis along Y-Axis
snippet: Let $\pr_{X, Y}$ denote the projection on the $x$-axis along the $y$-axis: $\forall P \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{X, Y} } P =$ the intersection of the $x$-axis with the line through $P$ parallel to the $y$-axis. Let $P = \tuple {\lambda_1, \lambda_2}$ be an arbitrary point in $\R^2$. Then: $\map {\pr_{X, Y} } {\lambda_1, \lambda_2} = \tuple {\lambda_1, 0}$

title: Projection in Plane on Y-Axis along X-Axis
snippet: Let $\pr_{Y, X}$ denote the projection on the $y$-axis along the $x$-axis: $\forall P \in \R^2: \map {\pr_{Y, X} } P =$ the intersection of the $y$-axis with the line through $P$ parallel to the $x$-axis. Let $P = \tuple {\lambda_1, \lambda_2}$ be an arbitrary point in $\R^2$. Then: $\map {\pr_{Y, X} } {\lambda_1, \lambda_2} = \tuple {0, \lambda_2}$

title: Projection is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ be the external direct product of the algebraic structures $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$. Then: $\pr_1$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_1, \circ_1}$ $\pr_2$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {\SS, \circ}$ to $\struct {S_2, \circ_2}$ where $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are the first and second projection respectively of $\struct {\SS, \circ}$.

title: Projection is Injection iff Factor is Singleton
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$ be non-empty sets. Let $\ds S = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n S_i$ be the cartesian product of $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$. Let $\pr_j: S \to S_j$ be the $j$th projection on $S$. Then $\pr_j$ is an injection $S_k$ is a singleton for all $k \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}$ where $k \ne j$.

title: Projection is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be non-empty sets. Let $S \times T$ be the Cartesian product of $S$ and $T$. Let $\pr_1: S \times T \to S$ and $\pr_2: S \times T \to T$ be the first projection and second projection respectively on $S \times T$. Then $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are both surjections.

title: Projection of Complement Contains Complement of Projection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be non-empty sets. Let $X \subseteq S \times T$ be a subset of the Cartesian product $S \times T$. Denote with $\pr_1, \pr_2$ and $\complement$ the first and second projections, and the complement operation, respectively. Then: {{eqn|l = \map \complement {\map {\pr_1} X} |o = \subseteq |r = \map {\pr_1} {\map \complement X} }} {{eqn|l = \map \complement {\map {\pr_2} X} |o = \subseteq |r = \map {\pr_2} {\map \complement X} }}

title: Projection of Conic Section is Conic Section
snippet: Let $K$ be a conic section. Let $K'$ be a projection of $K$. Then $K'$ is also a conic section.

title: Projection of Euclidean Space onto Euclidean Subspace is Riemannian Submersion
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^{n + k}, g^E_{n + k}}$, $\struct {\R^n, g^E_n}$ be the real vector spaces with Euclidean metrics. Let $\pi : \R^{n + k} \to \R^n$ be the projection onto the first $n$ coordinates. Then $\pi$ is a Riemannian submersion.

title: Projection of Product Manifold onto Factor Manifold is Riemannian Submersion
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g^M}$ and $\struct {N, g^N}$ be Riemannian manifolds. Let $M \times N$ be the product manifold endowed with the product metric $g = g^M \oplus g^N$. Let $\pi_M$, $\pi_N$ be projections such that: $\pi_M : M \times N \to M$ $\pi_N : M \times N \to N$ Then $\pi_M$ and $\pi_N$ are Riemannian submersions.

title: Projection of Subset is Open iff Saturation is Open
snippet: Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on a topological space $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $p$ denote the quotient mapping induced by $\sim$. Let $\tau_\sim$ be the quotient topology on $X / \sim$ by $p$. Let $\struct {X / \sim, \tau_\sim}$ be the quotient space of $X$ by $\sim$. Let $U \subset X$. {{item|(1):|$\map p U$ is open in $\struct {X / \sim, \tau_\sim}$}} {{item|(2):|The saturation of $U$ is open in $\struct {X, \tau}$}}

title: Projection of Warped Product Manifold onto Unwarped Factor Manifold is Riemannian Submersion
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g^M}$ and $\struct {N, g^N}$ be Riemannian manifolds. Let $f : M \to \R_{\mathop > 0}$ be a strictly positive smooth function. Let $M \times_f N$ be the warped product manifold endowed with the metric $g = g^M \oplus f^2 g^N$. Let $\pi_M$, $\pi_N$ be projections such that: $\pi_M : M \times_f N \to M$ $\pi_N : M \times_f N \to N$ Then $\pi_M$ is a Riemannian submersion, but $\pi_N$ is not necessarily so.

title: Projection on Cartesian Product of Modules
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be the cartesian product of a sequence $\sequence {\struct {G_n, +_n, \circ_n}_R}$ of $R$-modules. Then for each $j \in \closedint 1 n$, the projection $\pr_j$ on the $j$th co-ordinate is an epimorphism from $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ onto $\struct {G_j, +_j, \circ_j}_R$.

title: Projection on Group Direct Product is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ be groups. Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be the group direct product of $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$. Then: $\pr_1$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {G, \circ}$ to $\struct {G_1, \circ_1}$ $\pr_2$ is an epimorphism from $\struct {G, \circ}$ to $\struct {G_2, \circ_2}$ where $\pr_1$ and $\pr_2$ are the first and second projection respectively of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

title: Projection on Real Euclidean Plane is Open Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\rho: \R^2 \to \R$ be the first projection on $\R^2$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: \map \rho {x, y} = x$ Then $\rho$ is an open mapping. The same applies with the second projection on $\R^2$.

title: Projection on Real Euclidean Plane is not Closed Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\rho: \R^2 \to \R$ be the first projection on $\R^2$ defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: \map \rho {x, y} = x$ Then $\rho$ is not a closed mapping. The same applies with the second projection on $\R^2$.

title: Projection on Space of Complex-Valued Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\struct {\map \CC K, \overline \cdot, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the $\text C^\ast$-algebra of continuous functions on $K$. Let $p \in \map \CC K$ be a projection. Then there exists open sets (possibly empty) $U_0, U_1 \subseteq K$ such that: $U_0 \cap U_1 = \O$ and: $K = U_0 \cup U_1$ such that: $\ds \map p x = \begin{cases}1 & x \in U_1 \\ 0 & x \in U_0\end{cases}$

title: Projection onto Ideal of External Direct Sum of Rings
snippet: Let $\struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1}, \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}, \ldots, \struct {R_n, +_n, \circ_n}$ be rings. Let $\ds \struct {R, +, \circ} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n \struct {R_k, +_k, \circ_k}$ be their direct product. For each $k \in \closedint 1 n$, let: ${R_k}' = \set {\tuple {x_1, \ldots, x_n} \in R: \forall j \ne k: x_j = 0}$ Let $\pr_k: R \to {R_k}'$ be the projection on the $k$th coordinate of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ onto ${R_k}'$. Then $\pr_k$ is an epimorphism.

title: Projections Associated with Schauder Basis Converge to Identity in Strong Operator Topology
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Schauder basis for $X$. Let $\sequence {S_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the projections associated with $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then $\sequence {S_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges to the identity mapping in the strong operator topology.

title: Projections on Direct Product of Group Homomorphisms
snippet: Let $G, H_1$ and $H_2$ be groups. Let $H_1 \times H_2$ be the group direct product of $H_1$ and $H_2$. Let $f_1: G \to H_1$ and $f_2: G \to H_2$ be group homomorphisms. Let $f_1 \times f_2: g \to H_1 \times H_2$ be the direct product of $f_1$ and $f_2$. Let: $\pr_1: H_1 \times H_2 \to H_1$ be the first projection from $H_1 \times H_2$ to $H_1$ $\pr_2: H_1 \times H_2 \to H_2$ be the second projection from $H_1 \times H_2$ to $H_2$.

snippet: The finite projective plane of order $4$ is unique.

title: Projective Resolution Exists Iff Enough Projectives
snippet: Let $\AA$ be an abelian category. Then $\AA$ has enough projectives any object in $\AA$ has a projective resolution.

title: Proof by Contraposition
snippet: == Proof Technique == Proof by Contraposition is a rule of inference used in proofs. This rule infers a conditional statement from its contrapositive. It is based on the Rule of Transposition, which says that a conditional statement and its contrapositive have the same truth value: $p \implies q \dashv \vdash \neg q \implies \neg p$ In other words, the conclusion: if $A$, then $B$ is drawn from the single premise: if not $B$, then not $A$.

title: Proof by Counterexample
snippet: == Proof Technique == Consider the definition of a counterexample: Proving, or disproving, a statement in the form of $X$ by establishing the truth or falsehood of a statement in the form of $Y$ is known as the technique of proof by counterexample.

title: Proof of Theorem by Truth Table
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a propositional formula whose atoms are $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$. Let $l$ be the line number of any row in the truth table of $\phi$. Let $\hat {p_i}$ be defined as: $\hat {p_i} = \begin{cases} p_i & : \text {the entry in line } l \text { of } p_i \text { is } \T \\ \neg p_i & : \text {the entry in line } l \text { of } p_i \text { is } \F \end{cases}$ for all $i$ such that $1 \le i \ne n$.

title: Proper Class is not Element of Class
snippet: Let $\mathrm P$ be a proper class. Then $\mathrm P$ is not an element of any class. That is: $\neg \exists A : \mathrm P \in A$

title: Proper Closed Linear Subspace of Topological Vector Space is Meager
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $D$ be a proper closed linear subspace of $X$. Then $D$ is meager.

title: Proper Convex Combination of Interior of Convex Set and Closure of Convex Set is Contained in Interior of Set
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be a convex set with non-empty interior $\Int C$. Let $\map \cl C$ be the closure of $C$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $t \in \openint 0 1$. Then we have: $t \Int C + \paren {1 - t} \map \cl C \subseteq \Int C$

title: Proper Ideal iff Quotient Ring is Non-Null
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq A$ be an ideal. $(1): \quad \mathfrak a$ is a proper ideal of $A$. $(2): \quad$ The quotient ring $A / \mathfrak a$ is a non-null ring.

title: Proper Ideal is Prime iff Contains Element or Complement
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a boolean lattice. Let $I$ be a proper ideal on $S$. Then: $I$ is a prime ideal for every $a \in S$, either $a \in I$ or $\neg a \in I$.

title: Proper Ideal of Ring is Contained in Maximal Ideal
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a \subseteq A$ be a proper ideal. Then there exists a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ with $\mathfrak a \subseteq \mathfrak m$.

title: Proper Integer Heronian Triangle whose Area is 24
snippet: There exists exactly one proper integer Heronian triangle whose area equals $24$. That is, the obtuse triangle whose sides are of length $4$, $13$ and $15$.

title: Proper Linear Subspace of Topological Vector Space has Empty Interior
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $L$ be a proper linear subspace of $X$. Then: $L^\circ = \O$ where $L^\circ$ denotes the interior of $L$.

title: Proper Lower Section under Well-Ordering is Initial Segment
snippet: Let $A$ be a class under a well-ordering $\preccurlyeq$. Let $B$ be a proper lower section of $A$. Let $b$ be the smallest element of $A \setminus B$. Then $B$ is the initial segment of $b$ in $A$.

title: Proper Modular Ideal of Algebra is Contained in Maximal Ideal
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be an $R$-algebra. Let $\struct {J, \ast}$ be a proper modular ideal of $\struct {A, \ast}$. Then there exists a maximal ideal $M$ of $\struct {A, \ast}$ such that $J \subseteq M$.

title: Proper Subset of Finite Ordinal is Equivalent to Smaller Ordinal
snippet: Let $n$ be a finite ordinal. Let $x \subsetneq n$. Then for some finite ordinal $m < n$: $m \sim x$ where $m \sim x$ denotes that $m$ is (set) equivalent to $x$. That is, every proper subset of a finite ordinal $n$ is equivalent to some finite ordinal smaller than $n$.

title: Proper Subset of Matroid Circuit is Independent
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $C \subseteq S$ be a circuit of $M$. Then every proper subset $A$ of $C$ is independent.

title: Proper Subtower is Initial Segment

snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Suppose that the following is a commutative diagram in $\mathbf C$: $\begin{xy}\xymatrix@+1em@L+2px{ A' \ar[rr]^*{h_\alpha} \ar[dd]_*{\alpha'} & & A \ar[rd]^*{\gamma} \ar[dd]^(.4)*{\alpha} \\ & B' \ar[ld]^*{\beta'} \ar[rr] |{\hole} ^(.3)*{h_\beta} & & B \ar[ld]^*{\beta} \\ C' \ar[rr]_*{h} & & C }\end{xy}$ and that the two squares in it are pullback diagrams.

title: Pullback of Quotient Group Isomorphism/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Pullbacks of Quotient Group Isomorphisms ==

title: Pullback of Quotient Group Isomorphism is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity element is $e_G$. Let $\struct {H, *}$ be a group whose identity element is $e_H$. Let $N \lhd G, K \lhd H$ be normal subgroups of $G$ and $H$ respectively. Let: $G / N \cong H / K$ where: $G / N$ denotes the quotient of $G$ by $N$ $\cong$ denotes group isomorphism. Let $\theta: G / N \to H / K$ be such a group isomorphism. Let $G \times^\theta H$ be the pullback of $G$ and $H$ via $\theta$. Then $G \times^\theta H$ is a subgroup of $G \times H$.

title: Pullback of Riemannian Metric by Smooth Mapping is Riemannian Metric iff Mapping is Immersion
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with or without boundary. Let $F : M \to \tilde M$ be a smooth mapping. Let $F^* \tilde g$ be the pullback of $\tilde g$ by $F$. Let $g = F^* \tilde g$ be a smooth $2$-tensor field. Then $g$ is a Riemannian metric $F$ is an immersion.

title: Pullback of Subset Inclusion
snippet: Denote with $\mathbf{Set}$ the category of sets. Let $A, B$ be sets, and let $f: A \to B$ be a mapping. Let $V \subseteq B$ be a subset of $B$. Denote with $i: V \to B$ the inclusion mapping. Let $f^{-1} \left({V}\right) \subseteq A$ be the preimage of $V$ under $f$. Denote with $j: f^{-1} \left({V}\right) \to A$ the inclusion mapping. Denote with $\bar f = f \restriction_{f^{-1} \left({V}\right)}$ the restriction of $f$ to $f^{-1} \left({V}\right)$.

title: Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages
snippet: Let $\LL_3$ be the set of regular languages. Then the following holds: $\forall L \in \LL_3: \exists n_0 \in \N_0: \forall z \in L: \card z > n_0 \implies \exists u, v, w$ such that: $z = u \cdot v \cdot w$ $\card v > 0$ $\card {u v} < n_0$ $\forall i \in \N_0: u \cdot v^i \cdot w \in L$

title: Pursuit Curve of Boat in River
snippet: Consider a straight river $R$ whose parallel banks are aligned with the $y$-axis and the line $x = c$ of a cartesian plane. Let the current of $R$ have a constant and uniform speed $a$ in the negative $y$ direction. Let a boat $B$ be launched from the point $\tuple {c, 0}$ and headed directly towards the origin with speed $b$ relative to the water. The path of $B$ is defined by the equation: $c^k \paren {y + \sqrt {x^2 + x^2} } = x^{k + 1}$ where $k = \dfrac a b$.

title: Push Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the open interval $\openint a \to$, $a \in \R$, such that: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map f x = +\infty$ Let $g$ be a real function defined on some open interval $\openint b \to$ such that, for sufficiently large $x$: $\map g x > \map f x$ Then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map g x = +\infty$

title: Pushforward Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ and $\struct {X', \Sigma'}$ be measurable spaces. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $f: X \to X'$ be a $\Sigma \, / \, \Sigma'$-measurable mapping. Then the pushforward measure $f_* \mu: \Sigma' \to \overline \R$ is a measure.

title: Pushforward of Lebesgue Measure under General Linear Group
snippet: Let $M \in \GL {n, \R}$ be a nonsingular matrix. Let $\lambda^n$ be $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Then the pushforward measure $M_* \lambda^n$ satisfies: $M_* \lambda^n = \size {\det M^{-1} } \cdot \lambda^n$

title: Pythagoras's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a right triangle with $c$ as the hypotenuse. Then: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$

title: Pythagoras's Theorem (Inner Product Space)
snippet:
Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $
orm \cdot$ be the inner product norm on $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n \in V$ form an orthogonal set. Then: $\ds 
orm {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n f_i}^2 = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n 
orm {f_i}^2$

title: Pythagoras's Theorem for Parallelograms
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Let $ACDE$ and $BCFG$ be parallelograms constructed on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$. Let $DE$ and $FG$ be produced to intersect at $H$. Let $AJ$ and $BI$ be constructed on $A$ and $B$ parallel to and equal to $HC$. Then the area of the parallelogram $ABIJ$ equals the sum of the areas of the parallelograms $ACDE$ and $BCFG$.

title: Pythagorean Prime/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of Pythagorean primes begins: $\begin{array} {r | r | r} p & 4 n + 1 & a^2 + b^2 \\ \hline 5 & 4 \times 1 + 1 & 2^2 + 1^2 \\ 13 & 4 \times 3 + 1 & 3^2 + 2^2 \\ 17 & 4 \times 4 + 1 & 4^2 + 1^2 \\ 29 & 4 \times 7 + 1 & 5^2 + 2^2 \\ 37 & 4 \times 9 + 1 & 6^2 + 1^2 \\ 41 & 4 \times 10 + 1 & 5^2 + 4^2 \\ 53 & 4 \times 13 + 1 & 7^2 + 2^2 \\ \end{array}$

title: Pythagorean Triangle/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Pythagorean Triangles ==

title: Pythagorean Triangle cannot be Isosceles
snippet: Let $P$ be a Pythagorean triangle. Then $P$ is not isosceles.

title: Pythagorean Triangle from Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Take $4$ consecutive Fibonacci numbers: $F_n, F_{n + 1}, F_{n + 2}, F_{n + 3}$ Let: $a := F_n F_{n + 3}$ $b := 2 F_{n + 1} F_{n + 2}$ $c := F_{2 n + 3}$ Then: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ and: $\dfrac {a b} 2 = F_n \times F_{n + 1} \times F_{n + 2} \times F_{n + 3}$ That is, if the legs of a right triangle are the product of the outer terms and twice the inner terms, then: the hypotenuse is the Fibonacci number whose index is half the sum of the indices of the four given Fibonacci numbers. the area is the product of the four given Fibonacci numbers.

title: Pythagorean Triangle from Sum of Reciprocals of Consecutive Same Parity Integers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers such that they are consecutively of the same parity. Let $\dfrac p q = \dfrac 1 a + \dfrac 1 b$. Then $p$ and $q$ are the legs of a Pythagorean triangle.

title: Pythagorean Triangle whose Area is Half Perimeter
snippet: The $3-4-5$ triangle is the only Pythagorean triangle whose area is half its perimeter.

title: Pythagorean Triangle whose Hypotenuse and Leg differ by 1
snippet: Let $P$ be a Pythagorean triangle whose sides correspond to the Pythagorean triple $T$. Then: the hypotenuse of $P$ is $1$ greater than one of its legs the generator for $T$ is of the form $G = \tuple {n, n + 1}$ where $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ is a (strictly) positive integer.

title: Pythagorean Triangle with Sides in Arithmetic Sequence
snippet: The $3-4-5$ triangle is the only Pythagorean triangle such that: the lengths of whose sides are in arithmetic sequence and: the lengths of whose sides form a primitive Pythagorean triple.

title: Pythagorean Triangles whose Area equal their Perimeter
snippet: There exist exactly $2$ Pythagorean triples which define a Pythagorean triangle whose area equals its perimeter: $(1): \quad \tuple {6, 8, 10}$, leading to an area and perimeter of $24$ $(2): \quad \tuple {5, 12, 13}$, leading to an area and perimeter of $30$.

title: Pépin's Test
snippet: Let $F_n = 2^{2^n} + 1$ be a Fermat number. Then $F_n$ is prime : $3^{\paren {F_n - 1} / 2} \equiv -1 \pmod {F_n}$

title: Pólya-Vinogradov Inequality
snippet: Let $p$ be a positive odd prime. Then: $\forall m, n \in \N: \ds \size {\sum_{k \mathop = m}^{m + n} \paren {\frac k p} } < \sqrt p \, \ln p$ where $\paren {\dfrac k p}$ is the Legendre symbol.

title: Quadratic Equation for Parallel Straight Lines
snippet: Let $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ represent $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane which are represented by a quadratic equation $E$ in two variables: $a x^2 + b y^2 + 2 h x y + 2 g x + 2 f y + c = 0$ Let $\LL_1$ and $\LL_2$ be parallel. Then: $h^2 - a b = 0$

title: Quadratic Form (Polynomial Theory)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quadratic Forms ==

title: Quadratic Form in Three Variables represents Conicoid
snippet: A quadratic form in $3$ variables, when put equal to a constant, represents a conicoid.

title: Quadratic Form in Two Variables represents Conic Section
snippet: A quadratic form in $2$ variables, when put equal to a constant $a x^2 + b x y + c y^2 = r$ represents a conic section.

title: Quadratic Integers over 2 are Not a Field
snippet: Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $2$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Z}$ that is, all (real) numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are addition and multiplication on real numbers, is not a field.

title: Quadratic Integers over 2 form Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $2$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Z}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers, is an ordered integral domain.

title: Quadratic Integers over 2 form Subdomain of Reals
snippet: Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $2$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Z}$ That is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers, form an integral subdomain of the real numbers $\R$.

title: Quadratic Integers over 3 form Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the set of real numbers. Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 3} \subseteq \R$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $3$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 3} = \set {a + b \sqrt 3: a, b \in \Z}$ Then $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 3}, +, \times}$ is an integral domain.

title: Quadratic Irrational is Root of Quadratic Equation
snippet: Let $x$ be a quadratic irrational. Then $x$ is a solution to a quadratic equation with rational coefficients.

title: Quadratic Representation of Pair of Straight Lines
snippet: Consider the general quadratic equation in $2$ variables: $(1): \quad a x^2 + b x y + c y^2 + d x + e y + f = 0$ Then $(1)$ is the locus of $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane it can be expressed in the form: $\paren {l_1 x + m_1 y + n_1} \paren {l_2 x + m_2 y + n_2} = 0$ where $l_1$, $m_1$, $n_1$, $l_2$, $m_2$ and $n_2$ are real numbers.

title: Quadratic Residue/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quadratic Residues ==

title: Quadrature of Parabola
snippet: Let $T$ be a parabola. Consider the parabolic segment bounded by an arbitrary chord $AB$. Let $C$ be the point on $T$ where the tangent to $T$ is parallel to $AB$. Then the area $S$ of the parabolic segment $ABC$ of $T$ is given by: $S = \dfrac 4 3 \triangle ABC$

title: Quadric Surface/Examples

title: Quadrilateral Tessellates the Plane
snippet: Let $Q$ be a quadrilateral. Then $Q$ can tessellate the plane.

title: Quadrilateral in Complex Plane is Cyclic iff Cross Ratio of Vertices is Real
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ be distinct complex numbers. Then: $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4$ define the vertices of a cyclic quadrilateral their cross-ratio: $\paren {z_1, z_3; z_2, z_4} = \dfrac {\paren {z_1 - z_2} \paren {z_3 - z_4} } {\paren {z_1 - z_4} \paren {z_3 - z_2} }$ is wholly real.

title: Quadrilateral is Cyclic iff Opposite Angles sum to Two Right Angles
snippet: 500px Given $\Box ABCD$ with $A, B$ and $D$ on a circle. Let $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ADC$ add to two right angles. Then $C$ lies on the circle, and $\Box ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral.

title: Quadrilateral is Parallelogram iff Both Pairs of Opposite Angles are Equal
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Then: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram $\angle ABC = \angle ADC$ and $\angle BAD = \angle BCD$.

title: Quadrilateral is Parallelogram iff Both Pairs of Opposite Sides are Equal or Parallel
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Then: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram either $AB = CD$ and $AD = BC$ or $AB \parallel CD$ and $AD \parallel BC$ where $AB \parallel CD$ denotes that $AB$ is parallel to $CD$.

title: Quadrilateral is Parallelogram iff Diagonals Bisect each other
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Then: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram both: $AD$ is a bisector of $BC$ and: $BC$ is a bisector of $AD$.

title: Quadrilateral is Parallelogram iff One Pair of Opposite Sides is Equal and Parallel
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Then: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram $AB = CD$ and $AB \parallel CD$ where $AB \parallel CD$ denotes that $AB$ is parallel to $CD$.

title: Quadrilateral with Bisecting Diagonals is Parallelogram
snippet: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral. Let the diagonals of $ABCD$ bisect each other. Then $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

title: Quadruple Angle Formula for Sine/Corollary 1
snippet: == Corollary to Quadruple Angle Formula for Sine == For all $\theta$ such that $\theta \ne 0, \pm \pi, \pm 2 \pi \ldots$ $\dfrac {\sin 4 \theta} {\sin \theta} = 8 \cos^3 \theta - 4 \cos \theta$ where $\sin$ denotes sine and $\cos$ denotes cosine.

title: Quadruple Angle Formula for Sine/Corollary 2
snippet: == Corollary to Quadruple Angle Formula for Sine == For all $\theta$ such that $\theta \ne 0, \pm \pi, \pm 2 \pi \ldots$ $\dfrac {\sin 4 \theta} {\sin \theta} = 2 \cos 3 \theta + 2 \cos \theta$ where $\sin$ denotes sine and $\cos$ denotes cosine.

title: Quadruply Perfect Number/Examples/30,240
snippet: == Example of Quadruply Perfect Number == $30 \, 240$ is quadruply perfect: $\map {\sigma_1} {30 \, 240} = 120 \, 960 = 4 \times 30 \, 240$

title: Quantal Response/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quantal Responses ==

title: Quantifier-Free Formula of Arithmetic is Provable
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a sentence in the language of arithmetic. Suppose $\phi$ contains no quantifiers. Suppose also that $\N \models \phi$. That is, the natural numbers model $\phi$. Then $\phi$ is a theorem of minimal arithmetic.

title: Quantifier/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Use of Quantifiers ==

title: Quantifier Free Formula is Preserved by Superstructure
snippet: Let $\MM, \NN$ be $\LL$-structures such that $\MM$ is a substructure of $\NN$. Let $\map \phi {\bar x}$ be a quantifier-free $\LL$-formula, and let $\bar a \in\MM$. Then $\MM \models \map \phi {\bar a}$ $\NN \models \map \phi {\bar a}$.

title: Quantifier has Unique Scope
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of predicate logic. Let $Q$ be an occurrence of a quantifier in $\mathbf A$. Then there exists a unique well-formed part of $\mathbf A$ which (omitting outermost parentheses) begins with that occurrence $Q$. This unique well-formed part of $\mathbf A$ is called the scope of the occurrence of $Q$.

title: Quantity of Positive Integers Divisible by Particular Integer
snippet: Let $d$ be a positive integer. Let $x \ge 1$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \le x, \, d \divides n} 1 = \floor {\frac x d}$ That is: there are $\floor {\dfrac x d}$ natural numbers less than or equal to $x$ that are divisible by $d$.

title: Quantum-Charge Ratio
snippet: The ratio of Planck's constant to the elementary charge is given by: {{eqn | l = \dfrac h \E | o = \approx | r = 4 \cdotp 13566 \, 7697 \times 10^{-15} | c = joule seconds per coulombs | cc= }} {{eqn | o = \approx | r = 4 \cdotp 13566 \, 7697 \times 10^{-7} | c = erg seconds per abcoulomb }} {{eqn | o = \approx | r = 1 \cdotp 37951 \, 0386 \times 10^{-17} | c = erg seconds per statcoulomb }}

title: Quantum Mechanics Commutator satisfies Jacobi Identity
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be operators acting on the Hilbert Space of some quantum system. Let $\sqbrk {\, \cdot, \cdot \,}$ denotes the commutator of these operators. Then: $\sqbrk {A, \sqbrk {B, C} } + \sqbrk {B, \sqbrk {C, A} } + \sqbrk {C, \sqbrk {A, B} } = 0$ That is, the commutator satisfies the Jacobi identity.

title: Quasicomponent is Intersection of Clopen Sets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $p \in S$. Then the quasicomponent containing $p$ equals the intersection of all sets which are both open and closed which contain $p$.

title: Quasicomponent is not necessarily Component
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $Q$ be a quasicomponent of $T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $C$ is also a component of $T$.

title: Quasicomponent of Compact Hausdorff Space is Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $C$ be a quasicomponent of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $C$ is connected.

title: Quasicomponents and Components are Equal in Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Then for each $A \subseteq S$: $A$ is a component of $S$ $A$ is a quasicomponent of $S$.

title: Quasicomponents and Components are Equal in Locally Connected Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally connected. Then $A \subseteq S$ is a component of $T$ $A \subseteq S$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

title: Quasicomponents and Injective Path Components are Equal in Locally Injectively Path-Connected Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally injectively path-connected. Then $A \subseteq S$ is an injective path component of $T$ $A$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

title: Quasicomponents and Path Components are Equal in Locally Path-Connected Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is locally path-connected. Then $A \subseteq S$ is a path component of $T$ $A \subseteq S$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

title: Quasicomponents of Integer Reciprocal Space with Zero are Single Points
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set 0 \cup \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space with zero under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then the quasicomponents of $A$ are singletons.

title: Quasigroup is not necessarily B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a quasigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is not necessarily a $B$-algebra.

title: Quasiperfect Number is Square of Odd Integer
snippet: Let $n$ be a quasiperfect number. Then: $n = \paren {2 k + 1}^2$ for some $k \in \Z_{>0}$. That is, a quasiperfect number is the square of an odd integer.

title: Quasiuniformity Inducing Topology may not be Unique
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\UU$ be a quasiuniformity on a set $S$ such that $T$ is the topology induced by $\UU$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\UU$ is the only quasiuniformity that induces $T$.

title: Quaternion Addition forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\mathbb H$ be the set of quaternions. Then $\struct {\mathbb H, +}$, where $+$ denotes quaternion addition, is an abelian group.

title: Quaternion Conjugation is Involution

Thus the quotient group of $G$ by $N$ is: $G / N = \set {E, A, B, C}$ whose Cayley table can be presented as: $\begin{array}{c|cccc} & E & A & B & C \\ \hline E & E & A & B & C \\ A & A & E & C & B \\ B & B & C & E & A \\ C & C & B & A & E \\ \end{array}$ which is seen to be an example of the Klein $4$-group.

snippet: == Subgroups of the Quaternion Group == Let $Q$ denote the quaternion group, whose group presentation is given as: The subsets of $Q$ which form subgroups of $Q$ are: {{eqn | o = | r = \set {e, a^2} }} {{eqn | o = | r = \set {e, a, a^2, a^3} }} {{eqn | o = | r = \set {e, b, a^2, a^2 b} }} {{eqn | o = | r = \set {e, a b, a^2, a^3 b} }} From Quaternion Group is Hamiltonian we have that all of these subgroups of $Q$ are normal.

title: Quaternion Group has Normal Subgroup without Complement
snippet: Let $Q$ denote the quaternion group. There exists a normal subgroup of $Q$ which has no complement.

title: Quaternion Group is Hamiltonian
snippet: The quaternion group $Q$ is Hamiltonian.

title: Quaternion Group not Dihedral Group
snippet: Let $Q$ be the quaternion group. Then $Q$ is not isomorphic to the dihedral group $D_4$.

title: Quaternion Modulus in Terms of Conjugate
snippet: Let $\mathbf x = a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k$ be a quaternion. Let $\size {\mathbf x}$ be the modulus of $\mathbf x$. Let $\overline {\mathbf x}$ be the conjugate of $\mathbf x$. Then: $\size {\mathbf x}^2 \mathbf 1 = \mathbf x \overline {\mathbf x}$

title: Quaternion Modulus of Conjugate
snippet: Let $z = a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k$ be a quaternion. Let $\overline z$ be the conjugate of $z$. Let $\cmod z$ be the quaternion modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {\overline z} = \cmod z$

title: Quaternion Modulus of Product of Quaternions
snippet: Let $\mathbf x, \mathbf y$ be quaternions. Let $\size {\mathbf x}$ be the modulus of $\mathbf x$. Then: $\size {\mathbf {x y} } = \size {\mathbf x} \size {\mathbf y}$

title: Quaternion Multiplication
snippet: Let $\mathbf x_1 = a_1 \mathbf 1 + b_1 \mathbf i + c_1 \mathbf j + d_1 \mathbf k$ and $\mathbf x_2 = a_2 \mathbf 1 + b_2 \mathbf i + c_2 \mathbf j + d_2 \mathbf k$ be quaternions. title: Quaternion Multplication is not Commutative
snippet: The operation of multplication on the quaternions $H$ is not commutative.

title: Quaternions Defined by Ordered Pairs
snippet: Consider the quaternions $\Bbb H$ as numbers in the form: $a \mathbf 1 + b \mathbf i + c \mathbf j + d \mathbf k$ where: $a, b, c, d$ are real numbers; $\mathbf 1, \mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k$ are entities related to each other in the following way: Now consider the quaternions $\Bbb H$ defined as ordered pairs $\tuple {x, y}$ where $x, y \in \C$ are complex numbers, on which the operation of multiplication is defined as follows: Let $w = a_1 + b_1 i, x = c_1 + d_1 i, y = a_2 + b_2 i, z = c_2 + d_2 i$ be complex numbers.

title: Quaternions Subring of Complex Matrix Space
snippet: The Ring of Quaternions is a subring of the matrix space $\map {\MM_\C} 2$.

title: Quaternions form Algebra
snippet: The set of quaternions $\Bbb H$ forms an algebra over the field of real numbers. This algebra is: $(1): \quad$ An associative algebra, but not a commutative algebra. $(2): \quad$ A normed division algebra. $(3): \quad$ A nicely normed $*$-algebra.

title: Quaternions form Skew Field
snippet: The set $\H$ of quaternions forms a skew field under the operations of addition and multiplication.

title: Quaternions form Vector Space over Reals
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\H$ be the set of quaternions. Then the $\R$-module $\H$ is a vector space.

title: Quaternions form Vector Space over Themselves
snippet: The set of quaternions $\H$, with the operations of addition and multiplication, forms a vector space.

title: Queen's Tour
snippet: Consider a chessboard $\CC$ of size $n \times n$ such that $n > 2$. Then the shortest queen's tour on $\CC$ is of $2 n - 2$ moves. For $n < 5$ it is necessary for the queen to move outside the boundary of the chessboard in order for this to happen.

title: Quintic Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quintic Equations ==

title: Quintuplets of Consecutive Integers which are not Divisor Sum Values
snippet: The elements of the following $5$-tuples of consecutive integers have the property that they are not values of the divisor sum function $\map {\sigma_1} n$ for any $n$: $\tuple {49, 50, 51, 52, 53}$ $\tuple {115, 116, 117, 118, 119}$ $\tuple {145, 146, 147, 148, 149}$

title: Quotient Algebra is Algebra
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A$ be a $R$-algebra. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Let $A/I$ be the quotient module of $A$ modulo $I$. For $a, b \in A$, define $\ast : \paren {A/I}^2 \to A/I$ by: $\paren {a + I} \ast \paren {b + I} = a b + I$ Then $\ast$ is well-defined and $\struct {A/I, \ast}$ is an $R$-algebra.

title: Quotient Algebra is Unital iff Quotienting Ideal is Modular
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A$ be a $R$-algebra. Let $I$ be an proper ideal of $A$. Let $A/I$ be the quotient algebra of $A$ modulo $I$. Then $A/I$ is unital $I$ is modular.

title: Quotient Epimorphism Condition for Normal Subgroup Product to be Internal Group Direct Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \odot}$ be a group Let $\struct {H, \odot}$ and $\struct {K, \odot}$ be normal subgroups of $\struct {G, \odot}$. Then: $\struct {G, \odot}$ is the internal group direct product of $\struct {H, \odot}$ and $\struct {K, \odot}$ the restriction of the quotient epimorphism $q_H$ to $K$ is an isomorphism from $K$ onto the quotient group $G / H$ and: the restriction of the quotient epimorphism $q_K$ to $H$ is an isomorphism from $H$ onto the quotient group $G / K$

title: Quotient Epimorphism from Integers by Principal Ideal
snippet: Let $m$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\ideal m$ be the principal ideal of $\Z$ generated by $m$. The restriction to $\N_m$ of the quotient epimorphism $q_m$ from the ring $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ onto $\struct {\Z, +, \times} / \ideal m$ is an isomorphism from the ring $\struct {\N_m, +_m, \times_m}$ of integers modulo $m$ onto the quotient ring $\struct {\Z, +, \times} / \ideal m$. In particular, $\struct {\Z, +, \times} / \ideal m$ has $m$ elements.

title: Quotient Group by Intersection of Normal Subgroups not necessarily Cyclic if Quotient Groups are
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N$ and $K$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Let the quotient groups $G / N$ and $G / K$ be cyclic. Then the quotient group $G / \paren {N \cap K}$ is not necessarily cyclic.

title: Quotient Group is Abelian iff All Commutators in Divisor
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $G / N$ be the quotient group of $G$ by $N$. Then the quotient group $G / N$ is abelian : $\forall x, y \in G: \sqbrk {x, y} \in N$ where $\sqbrk {x, y}$ denotes the commutator of $x$ and $y$. That is, $x y x^{-1} y^{-1} \in N$ for all $x, y \in G$.

title: Quotient Group is Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then the quotient group $G / N$ is indeed a group.

title: Quotient Group is Subgroup of Power Structure of Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {N, \circ}$ be a normal subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Then $\struct {G / N, \circ_N}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {\powerset G, \circ_\PP}$, where: $\struct {G / N, \circ_N}$ is the quotient group of $G$ by $N$ $\struct {\powerset G, \circ_\PP}$ is the power structure of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

title: Quotient Group of Abelian Group is Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be an abelian group. Let $N \le G$. Then the quotient group $G / N$ is abelian.

title: Quotient Group of Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group which is generated by $g$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $g H$ generates $G / H$.

title: Quotient Group of Direct Products
snippet: Let $G$ and $G'$ be groups. Let: where $\lhd$ denotes the relation of being a normal subgroup. Then: $\paren {G \times G'} / \paren {H \times H'}$ is isomorphic to $\paren {G / H} \times \paren {G' / H'}$ where: $G \times G'$ denotes the group direct product of $H$ and $H'$ $G / H$ denotes the quotient group of $G$ by $H$.

title: Quotient Group of General Linear Group by Special Linear Group
snippet: Let $\GL {n, \R}$ denote the general linear group of degree $n$ over $\R$. Let $\SL {n, \R}$ denote the special linear group of degree $n$ over $\R$. Then the quotient group $\GL {n, \R} / \SL {n, \R}$ is the multiplicative group of real numbers $\struct {\R_{\ne 0}, \times}$.

title: Quotient Group of Ideal is Coset Space
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\struct {R / J, +}$ be the quotient group of $\struct {R, +}$ by $\struct {J, +}$. Then each element of $\struct {R / J, +}$ is a coset of $J$ in $R$, that is, is of the form $x + J = \set {x + j: j \in J}$ for some $x \in R$. The rule of addition of these cosets is: $\paren {x + J} + \paren {y + J} = \paren {x + y} + J$. The identity of $\struct {R / J, +}$ is $J$ and for each $x \in R$, the inverse of $x + J$ is $\paren {-x} + J$.

title: Quotient Group of Infinite Cyclic Group by Subgroup
snippet: Let $C_n$ be the cyclic group of order $n$. Then: $C_n \cong \dfrac {\struct {\Z, +} } {\struct {n \Z, +} } = \dfrac \Z {n \Z}$ where: $\Z$ is the additive group of integers $n \Z$ is the additive group of integer multiples $\Z / n \Z$ is the quotient group of $\Z$ by $n \Z$. Thus, every cyclic group is isomorphic to one of: $\Z, \dfrac \Z \Z, \dfrac \Z {2 \Z}, \dfrac \Z {3 \Z}, \dfrac \Z {4 \Z}, \ldots$

title: Quotient Group of Integers by Multiples
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {m \Z, +}$ be the additive group of integer multiples of $m$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ be the additive group of integers modulo $m$. Then the quotient group of $\struct {\Z, +}$ by $\struct {m \Z, +}$ is $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$. Thus: $\index \Z {m \Z} = m$

title: Quotient Group of Quadratic Residues Modulo 2 of 2-adic Units
snippet: Let $\Q_2$ be the $2$-adic numbers. Let $\Q_2^\times$ denote the set of invertible elements of $\Q_2$. Let $\paren{\Q_2^\times}^2 = \set{a^2 : a \in \Q_2^\times}$ Then the multiplicative quotient group $\Q_2^\times \mathop/ \paren{\Q_2^\times}^2$ has order $8$ with: $\set{1, -1, 5, -5, 2, -2, 10, -10}$ is a transversal

title: Quotient Group of Quadratic Residues Modulo p of P-adic Units
snippet: Let $\Q_p$ be the $p$-adic numbers for some prime $p \ne 2$. Let $\Q_p^\times$ denote the set of invertible elements of $\Q_p$. Let $\paren{\Q_p^\times}^2 = \set{a^2 : a \in \Q_p^\times}$ Then the multiplicative quotient group $\Q_p^\times \mathop/ \paren{\Q_p^\times}^2$ has order $4$: $\exists c \in \Q_p^\times \setminus \paren{\Q_p^\times}^2 : \set{1, p, c, cp}$ is a transversal

title: Quotient Group of Reals by Integers is Circle Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $K$ be the circle group. Then the quotient group of $\struct {\R, +}$ by $\struct {\Z, +}$ is isomorphic to $K$.

title: Quotient Group of Solvable Group is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then, $G / N$, the quotient group of $G$ by $N$ is solvable.

title: Quotient Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Quotient Mappings ==

title: Quotient Mapping Induces Homeomorphism between Quotient Space and Image
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a quotient mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S_1 \times S_1$ be the equivalence on $S_1$ induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $q_{\RR_f}: S_1 \to S_1 / \RR_f$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$. Let $\tau_{\RR_f}$ be the quotient topology on $S_1 / \RR_f$ by $q_{\RR_f}$. Then there exists a uniquely defined homeomorphism $\tilde f: S_1 / \RR_f \to S_2$ such that $f = \tilde f \circ q_{\RR_f}$.

title: Quotient Mapping Maps Unit Open Ball in Normed Vector Space to Unit Open Ball in Normed Quotient Vector Space
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\struct {X/N, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the normed quotient vector space associated with the quotient vector space $X/N$. Let $B_X$ be the unit open ball in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $B_{X/N}$ be the unit open ball in $\struct {X/N, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\pi$ be the quotient mapping associated with $X/N$. Then: $\map \pi {B_X} = B_{X/N}$

title: Quotient Mapping and Continuous Mapping Induces Continuous Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$, $T_3 = \struct {S_3, \tau_3}$ be topological spaces. Let $p: S_1 \to S_2$ be a quotient mapping. Let $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be a mapping such that for all $s_1, s_2 \in S_1$ with $\map p {s_1} = \map p {s_2}$, we have $\map g {s_1} = \map g {s_2}$. Then $g$ induces a mapping $f: S_2 \to S_3$ such that $f \circ p = g$. The induced mapping $f$ is a continuous mapping $g$ is a continuous mapping.

title: Quotient Mapping equals Surjective Identification Mapping
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a quotient mapping, : $f$ is surjective, and $\tau_2$ is the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $T_1$.

title: Quotient Mapping is Bounded in Normed Quotient Vector Space
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\struct {X/N, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N} }$ be the normed quotient vector space associated with quotient vector space $X/N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping associated with $X/N$. Then $\pi$ is a bounded linear transformation.

title: Quotient Mapping is Coequalizer
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $S$ be a Set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $r_1, r_2: \RR \to S$ be the projections corresponding to the inclusion mapping $\RR \hookrightarrow S \times S$. Let $q: S \to S / \RR$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR$. Then $q$ is a coequalizer of $r_1$ and $r_2$ in $\mathbf{Set}$.

title: Quotient Mapping is Injection iff Equality
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Then the quotient mapping $q_\RR: S \to S / \RR$ is an injection $\RR$ is the equality relation.

title: Quotient Mapping is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $M$ be a subspace of $V$. Let $V / M$ be the quotient vector space. Let $Q: V \to V / M$ be the quotient mapping. Then $Q$ is a linear transformation.

title: Quotient Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Then the quotient mapping $q_\RR: S \to S / \RR$ is a surjection.

title: Quotient Mapping of Inverse Completion
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of a commutative semigroup $\struct {S, \circ}$, where $C$ is the set of cancellable elements of $S$. Let $f: S \times C: T$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in S, y \in C: \map f {x, y} = x \circ' y^{-1}$ Let $\RR_f$ be the equivalence relation induced by $f$. Then: $\tuple {x_1, y_1} \mathrel {\RR_f} \tuple {x_2, y_2} \iff x_1 \circ y_2 = x_2 \circ y_1$

title: Quotient Mapping on Quotient Topological Vector Space is Open Mapping
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : \struct {X, \tau} \to \struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient mapping. Then $\pi$ is an open mapping.

title: Quotient Mapping on Structure is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation on an algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the quotient mapping from $\struct {S, \circ}$ to the quotient structure $\struct {S / \RR, \circ_\RR}$ is an epimorphism: $q_\RR: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {S / \RR, \circ_\RR}: \forall x, y \in S: \map {q_\RR} {x \circ y} = \map {q_\RR} x \circ_\RR \map {q_\RR} y$

title: Quotient Metric on Vector Space induces Quotient Topology
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric such that the induced topology $\tau$ makes $\struct {X, \tau}$ a topological vector space. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\struct {X/N, \tau_N}$ be the quotient topological vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ induces $\tau_N$.

title: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Invariant Metric iff Vector Subspace is Closed
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ is an invariant metric $N$ is closed.

title: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Invariant Pseudometric
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $d_N$ be the quotient metric on $X/N$ induced by $d$. Then $d_N$ is an invariant pseudometric.

title: Quotient Metric on Vector Space is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Let $N$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then the mapping $d_N : X/N \times X/N \to \hointr 0 \infty$ defined by: $\ds \map {d_N} {\map \pi x, \map \pi y} = \inf_{z \mathop \in N} \map d {x - y, z}$ for each $\map \pi x, \map \pi y \in X/N$, is well-defined.

title: Quotient Norm is Norm
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N}$ be the quotient norm on $X/N$. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X/N}$ is indeed a norm.
