title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is Regular
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a regular space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is Semiregular
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a semiregular space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T0
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_0$ space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T1
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_1$ space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T2
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T2.5
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T3

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T3.5

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T4
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is T5
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a $T_5$ space

title: Real Number Line with Euclidean Topology is Urysohn
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is an Urysohn space

title: Real Number Line with Off-Center Distance Function is Quasimetric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $\tau_d$ can be given by a quasimetric defined as: $\map d {x, y} = \begin {cases} y - x & : y \ge x \\ 2 \paren {x - y} & : y Thus $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ is a quasimetric space.

title: Real Number Line with Point Removed is Not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then $\R \setminus \set x$, where $\setminus$ denotes set difference, is not path-connected.

title: Real Number Multiplied by Complex Number
snippet: Let $a \in \R$ be a real number. Let $c + d i \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $a \times \paren {c + d i} = \paren {c + d i} \times a = a c + i a d$

title: Real Number Ordering is Compatible with Addition
snippet: $\forall a, b, c \in \R: a < b \implies a + c < b + c$ where $\R$ is the set of real numbers.

title: Real Number Ordering is Compatible with Multiplication
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the set of real numbers. Then:

title: Real Number Subtracted from Itself leaves Zero
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $x - x = 0$ where $x - x$ denotes the operation of real subtraction.

title: Real Number at Distance Zero from Closed Real Interval is In Interval
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\map d {x, S}$ be the distance between $x$ and $S$. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Then: $\map d {x, I} = 0 \implies x \in I$

title: Real Number between Zero and One is Greater than Power/Natural Number
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Let $0 < x < 1$. Let $n$ be a natural number. Then: $0 < x^n \le x$

title: Real Number between Zero and One is Greater than Square
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Let $0 < x < 1$. Then: $0 < x^2 < x$

title: Real Number is Ceiling minus Difference
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Let $n$ be a integer. $(1): \quad$ There exists $t \in \hointr 0 1$ such that $x = n - t$ $(2): \quad n = \ceiling x$

title: Real Number is Closed in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\alpha \in \R$ be a real number. Then $\set \alpha$ is closed in $\struct {\R, \tau}$.

title: Real Number is Floor plus Difference
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ be the floor of $x$. Then: There exists an integer $n \in \Z$ such that for some $t \in \hointr 0 1$: $x = n + t$ $n = \floor x$ where: $\hointr 0 1$ is the real interval half open on the right from $0$ to $1$ $\floor x$ is the floor of $x$

title: Real Number is Greater than Zero iff its Negative is Less than Zero
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: x > 0 \iff \paren {-x} < 0$

title: Real Number is Integer iff equals Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $x = \ceiling x \iff x \in \Z$ where $\ceiling x$ is the ceiling of $x$.

title: Real Number is Integer iff equals Floor
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $x = \floor x \iff x \in \Z$ where $\floor x$ is the floor of $x$.

title: Real Number is Limit Point of Rational Numbers in Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\Q$ be the set of rational numbers. Let $x \in \R$. Then $x$ is a limit point of $\Q$. Hence the interesting case of a $\Q$ is countable set $\Q$ whose set of limit points is uncountable.

title: Real Number is between Ceiling Functions
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: \ceiling {x - 1} \le x < \ceiling x$ where $\ceiling x$ is the ceiling of $x$.

title: Real Number is between Floor Functions
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: \floor x \le x < \floor {x + 1}$ where $\floor x$ is the floor of $x$.

title: Real Number is not necessarily Rational Number
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number. Then it is not necessarily the case that $x$ is also a rational number.

title: Real Number lies between Unique Pair of Consecutive Integers
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number.

title: Real Number minus Floor
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be any real number. Then: $x - \floor x \in \hointr 0 1$ where $\floor x$ is the floor of $x$. That is: $0 \le x - \floor x < 1$

title: Real Number to Negative Power
snippet: Let $r \in \R_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number.

title: Real Numbers Between Epsilons
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: a - \epsilon < b < a + \epsilon$. Then $a = b$.

title: Real Numbers are Densely Ordered
snippet: == Corollary to Between two Real Numbers exists Rational Number == $\forall a, b \in \R: a < b \implies \paren {\exists c \in \R: a < c < b}$ That is, the set of real numbers is densely ordered.

title: Real Numbers are Uncountably Infinite
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ is uncountably infinite.

title: Real Numbers are not Well-Ordered under Conventional Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \leqslant}$ be the ordered structure consisting of the real numbers under the usual ordering. Then $\struct {\R, \leqslant}$ is not a well-ordered set.

title: Real Numbers form Algebra
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms an algebra over the field of real numbers. This algebra is: $(1): \quad$ An associative algebra. $(2): \quad$ A commutative algebra. $(3): \quad$ A normed division algebra. $(4): \quad$ A nicely normed $*$-algebra whose $*$ operator is the identity mapping. $(5): \quad$ A real $*$-algebra.

title: Real Numbers form Field
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms a field under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times}$.

title: Real Numbers form Integral Domain
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms an integral domain under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times}$.

title: Real Numbers form Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms an ordered integral domain under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times, \le}$.

title: Real Numbers form Perfect Set
snippet: Consider the set of real numbers $\R$ as a (complete) metric space with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Then $\R$ forms a perfect set.

title: Real Numbers form Ring
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms a ring under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times}$.

title: Real Numbers form Subfield of Complex Numbers
snippet: The field of real numbers $\struct {\R, +, \times}$ forms a subfield of the field of complex numbers $\struct {\C, +, \times}$.

title: Real Numbers form Totally Ordered Field
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms a totally ordered field under addition and multiplication: $\struct {\R, +, \times, \le}$.

title: Real Numbers form Valued Field
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ forms a valued field under addition, multiplication and absolute value: $\struct {\R, +, \times, \size {\,\cdot\,} }$.

title: Real Numbers form Vector Space
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$, with the operations of addition and multiplication, forms a vector space.

title: Real Numbers form only Ordered Field which is Complete
snippet: The set of real numbers $\R$ is the only ordered field which also satisfies the Continuum Property.

title: Real Numbers of Type Rational a plus b root 2 form Field
snippet: Let $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set: $\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {x \in \R: x = a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Q}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are rational numbers. Then the algebraic structure: $\struct {\Q \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers, is a field.

title: Real Numbers under Addition Modulo 1 form Group
snippet: Let $S = \set {x \in \R: 0 \le x < 1}$. Let $\circ: S \times S \to S$ be the operation defined as: $x \circ y = x + y - \floor {x + y}$ That is, $\circ$ is defined as addition modulo $1$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

title: Real Numbers under Addition form Group
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. The structure $\struct {\R, +}$ is a group.

title: Real Numbers under Addition form Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. The structure $\struct {\R, +}$ is an infinite abelian group.

title: Real Numbers under Addition form Monoid
snippet: The set of real numbers under addition $\struct {\R, +}$ forms a monoid.

title: Real Numbers under Multiplication do not form Group
snippet: The algebraic structure $\struct {\R, \times}$ consisting of the set of real numbers $\R$ under multiplication $\times$ is not a group.

title: Real Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of real numbers under multiplication $\struct {\R, \times}$ forms a monoid.

title: Real Numbers under Subtraction do not form Semigroup
snippet: The set of real numbers under subtraction $\struct {\R, -}$ does not form a semigroup.

title: Real Numbers with Absolute Value form Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Let $\size {\, \cdot \,}$ be the absolute value. Then $\struct {\R, \size {\, \cdot \,}}$ is a normed vector space.

title: Real Ordering is not Compatible with Division
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \R$ be real numbers such that $a > b$ and $c > d$. Then it does not necessarily hold that: $\dfrac a c > \dfrac b d$ That is, the usual ordering is not compatible with division.

title: Real Ordering is not Compatible with Subtraction
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in R$ be real numbers such that $a > b$ and $c > d$. Then it does not necessarily hold that: $a - c > b - d$ That is, the usual ordering is not compatible with subtraction.

title: Real Orthogonal Matrix is Normal
snippet: All real orthogonal matrices are normal.

title: Real Orthogonal Matrix is Unitary
snippet: All real orthogonal matrices are unitary.

title: Real Part as Mapping is Endomorphism for Complex Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {\C, +}$ be the additive group of complex numbers. Let $\struct {\R, +}$ be the additive group of real numbers. Let $f: \C \to \R$ be the mapping from the complex numbers to the real numbers defined as: $\forall z \in \C: \map f z = \map \Re z$ where $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$. Then $f: \struct {\C, +} \to \struct {\R, +}$ is a group epimorphism. Its kernel is the set: $\map \ker f = \set {i x: x \in \R}$ of wholly imaginary numbers.

title: Real Part as Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \R$ be the projection from the complex numbers to the real numbers defined as: $\forall z \in \C: \map f z = \map \Re z$ where $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of $z$. Then $f$ is a surjection.

title: Real Part of Complex Exponential Function
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number, where $x, y \in \R$. Let $\exp z$ denote the complex exponential function. Then: $\map \Re {\exp z} = e^x \cos y$ where: $\Re z$ denotes the real part of a complex number $z$ $e^x$ denotes the real exponential function of $x$ $\cos y$ denotes the real cosine function of $y$.

title: Real Part of Complex Product
snippet: Let $z_1$ and $z_2$ be complex numbers. Then: $\map \Re {z_1 z_2} = \map \Re {z_1} \map \Re {z_2} - \map \Im {z_1} \map \Im {z_2}$

title: Real Part of Element of *-Algebra is Real Linear
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $x, y \in A$ and $\lambda \in \R$. Then we have: $\map \Re {x + \lambda y} = \map \Re x + \lambda \map \Re y$ where $\Re$ denotes real part.

title: Real Part of Imaginary Unit times Element of *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Then: $\map \Re {i x} = -\map \Im x$ where $\Re$ and $\Im$ denote the real and imaginary parts of $A$.

title: Real Part of Integer Power of Complex Number is Harmonic
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $z^n$ denote $z$ raised to the $n$th power. Then the real part $\map \Re {z^n}$ of $z^n$ is a harmonic polynomial.

title: Real Part of Linear Functional is Linear Functional
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\C$. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a linear functional. Define $g : X \to \R$ by: $\map g x = \map \Re {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Then $f$ is $\R$-linear.

title: Real Part of Sine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number, where $x, y \in \R$. Let $\sin z$ denote the complex sine function. Then: $\map \Re {\sin z} = \sin x \cosh y$ where: $\map \Re z$ denotes the real part of a complex number $z$ $\sin$ denotes the sine function (real and complex) $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function.

title: Real Plus Epsilon
snippet: Let $a, b \in \R$, such that: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: a 0}$ is the set of strictly positive real numbers. That is: $\epsilon > 0$ Then: $a \le b$

title: Real Polynomial Function is Continuous
snippet: A (real) polynomial function is continuous at every point. Thus a (real) polynomial function is continuous on every interval of $\R$.

title: Real Polynomial Function is Differentiable
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $f_n: \R \to \R$ be a real polynomial function. Then $f_n$ is differentiable over $\R$.

title: Real Power Function for Positive Integer Power is Continuous
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $f_n: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map {f_n} x = x^n$ Then $f_n$ is continuous on $\R$.

title: Real Power is of Exponential Order Epsilon
snippet: Let: $f: \hointr 0 \to \to \R: t \mapsto t^r$ be $t$ to the power of $r$, for $r \in \R, r > -1$. Then $f$ is of exponential order $\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small in magnitude.

title: Real Power of Strictly Positive Real Number is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $x$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $y$ be a real number. Then: $x^y > 0$ where $x^y$ denotes $x$ raised to the $y$th power.

title: Real Projective Plane is 2-Manifold
snippet: The real projective plane is a $2$-manifold. The real projective plane can be modelled as a square $ABCD$ whose opposite sides are identified after a half-twist: 400px That is: $AB$ is identified with $CD$ $DA$ is identified with $BC$

title: Real Projective Plane is Compactification of Plane
snippet: The real projective plane is a compactification of the plane.

title: Real Projective Plane is Homeomorphic to Möbius Strip Joined to Disc
snippet: The real projective plane is homeomorphic to the join of a Möbius strip with a disc along their boundaries.

title: Real Rational Function is Continuous
snippet: A real rational function is continuous at every point at which it is defined. Thus a real rational function is continuous on every interval of $\R$ not containing a root of the denominator of the function.

title: Real Semi-Inner Product Space is Complex Semi-Inner Product Space
snippet: Let $\struct{V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a real semi-inner product space. Then $\struct{V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ is a complex semi-inner product Space.

title: Real Semi-Inner Product is Complex Semi-Inner Product
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over a real subfield $\GF$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot: V \times V \to \GF$ be a real semi-inner product. Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a complex semi-inner product.

title: Real Sequence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Real Sequences ==

title: Real Sequence (1 + x over n)^n is Convergent
snippet: The sequence $\sequence {s_n}$ defined as: $s_n = \paren {1 + \dfrac x n}^n$ is convergent.

title: Real Sequence with Nonzero Limit is Eventually Nonzero
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a real sequence. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ converge to $a \ne 0$. Then: $\exists N \in \N: \forall n \ge N: x_n \ne 0$ That is, eventually every term of $\sequence {x_n}$ becomes non-zero.

title: Real Sequence with all Subsequences having Convergent Subsequence to Limit Converges to Same Limit
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence. Let $x \in \R$. Suppose that: every subsequence $\sequence {x_{n_j} }_{j \in \N}$ of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \mathop \N}$ has a subsequence $\sequence {x_{n_{j_k} } }_{k \in \N}$ such that: $x_{n_{j_k} } \to x$ Then: $x_n \to x$

title: Real Series is Unconditionally Convergent iff Absolutely Convergent
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a real sequence. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is unconditionally convergent it is absolutely convergent.

title: Real Sine Function is Bounded
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\size {\sin x} \le 1$

title: Real Sine Function is Continuous
snippet: The real sine function $\sin: \R \to \R$ is continuous on $\R$.

title: Real Sine Function is neither Injective nor Surjective
snippet: The real sine function is neither an injection nor a surjection.

title: Real Square Function is neither Injective nor Surjective
snippet: == Example of Mapping which is Not an Injection nor a Surjection == Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is neither an injection nor a surjection.

title: Real Square Function is not Bijective
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is not a bijection.

title: Real Square Function is not Injective
snippet: == Example of Mapping which is Not an Injection == Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is not an injection.

title: Real Square Function is not Surjective
snippet: == Example of Mapping which is Not a Surjection == Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^2$ Then $f$ is not a surjection.

title: Real Star-Algebra is Commutative
snippet: Let $A = \struct {A_F, \oplus}$ be a real $*$-algebra whose conjugation is denoted as $*$. Then: $\forall a, b \in A, a \oplus b = b \oplus a$ That is, real $*$-algebra is commutative.

title: Real Subtraction is Closed
snippet: The set of real numbers is closed under subtraction: $\forall a, b \in \R: a - b \in \R$

title: Real Symmetric Matrix is Hermitian
snippet: Every real symmetric matrix is Hermitian.

title: Real Symmetric Matrix is Normal
snippet: All real symmetric matrices are normal.

title: Real Symmetric Positive Definite Matrix has Positive Eigenvalues
snippet: Let $A$ be a symmetric positive definite matrix over $\mathbb R$. Let $\lambda$ be an eigenvalue of $A$. Then $\lambda$ is real with $\lambda > 0$.

title: Real Trigonometric Functions are Continuous
snippet: The trigonometric functions on the real numbers $\R$: sine cosine tangent cotangent secant cosecant are all continuous at every point of their domain.

title: Real Vector Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\R$ be the set of real numbers. Then the real vector space $\R^n$ is a vector space.

title: Real Vector Space under Chebyshev Distance is Homeomorphic to that under Euclidean Metric
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional real vector space. Let $d_\infty: \R^n \times \R^n \to \R$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Let $d_2: \R^n \times \R^n \to \R$ be the Euclidean metric on $\R^n$. Let $M_1 = \struct {\R^n, d_\infty}$ and $M_2 = \struct {\R^n, d_2}$ be the corresponding metric spaces. Then $M_1$ and $M_2$ are homeomorphic.

title: Real Vector Space with Dot Product is Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\R^d$ be a real vector space with $d$ dimensions. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ be the dot product on $\R^d$. Then $\R^d$ endowed with $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a Hilbert space.

title: Real Zero is Less than Real One
snippet: The real number $0$ is less than the real number $1$: $0 < 1$

title: Real Zero is Zero Element
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: 0 \times x = 0$

title: Real and Imaginary Part Projections are Continuous
snippet: Define the real-valued functions $x, y: \C \to \R$ by: $\forall z \in \C: \map x z = \map \Re z$ $\forall z \in \C: \map y z = \map \Im z$ Equip $\R$ with the usual Euclidean metric. Equip $\C$ with the usual Euclidean metric. Then both $x$ and $y$ are continuous functions.

title: Real and Imaginary Parts of Complex-Valued Function Vanishing at Infinity Vanish at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a complex-valued function vanishing at infinity. Then $\map \Re f$ and $\map \Im f$ vanish at infinity.

title: Real and Imaginary Parts of Holomorphic Function are Harmonic
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be an open subset of the set of complex numbers $\C$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a holomorphic complex function on $D$. Let $u, v: \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: x + i y = z \in D} \to \R$ be the two real-valued functions defined as: {{eqn | l = \map u {x, y} | r = \map \Re {\map f {x + i y} } }} {{eqn | l = \map v {x, y} | r = \map \Im {\map f {x + i y} } }} Then $u$ and $v$ are harmonic functions.

title: Real and Imaginary Parts of Integer Power of Complex Number are Harmonic
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $z^n$ denote $z$ raised to the $n$th power. Then both the real part $\map \Re {z^n}$ and the imaginary part $\map \Im {z^n}$ of $z^n$ are harmonic polynomials.

title: Realification of Normed Dual is Isometrically Isomorphic to the Normed Dual of Realification
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\C$. Let $\struct {X_\R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be the realification of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\struct {X^\ast_\R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast_\R} }$ be the normed dual of $\struct {X_\R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }_\R$ be the realification of $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$.

title: Realification of Topological Vector Space is Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\C$. Let $X_\R$ be the realification of $X$. Then $\struct {X_\R, \tau}$ is a topological vector space over $\R$. Further, $\struct {X, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space $\struct {X_\R, \tau}$ is a Hausdorff topological vector space.

title: Realism/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Realism ==

title: Realization of Stochastic Process/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Realizations of Stochastic Processes ==

title: Reals are Isomorphic to Dedekind Cuts
snippet: Let $\mathscr D$ be the set of all Dedekind cuts of the totally ordered set $\struct {\Q, \le}$. Define a mapping $f: \R \to \mathscr D$ as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \set {y \in \Q: y < x}$ Then $f$ is a bijection.

title: Rearrangement Operation as Replacement Operations
snippet: == Example of use of Replacement Operation == Let $\left({a, b, c, d}\right)$ be an ordered quadruple consisting of four variables whose values are to be rearranged into the order $\left({b, c, d, a}\right)$. This can be implemented using replacement operations. Let $t$ be a new variable which has been established for this purpose. Then the sequence of replacement operations: $t \gets a$ $a \gets b$ $b \gets c$ $c \gets d$ $d \gets t$ performs the task.

title: Rearrangement of Convergent Sequence Converges to Same Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence in $X$ with limit $x$. Let $\pi : \N \to \N$ be a permutation. Then $\sequence {x_{\map \pi n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges to $x$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Rearrangement of Unconditionally Convergent Series in Banach Space Converges to Same Value
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ such that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is unconditionally convergent. Let: $\ds x = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ Let $\pi : \N \to \N$ be a permutation. We have: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_{\map \pi n} = x$

title: Rearrangement of Variables in Total Differential Equation
snippet: In a total differential equation, any one of the variables can be regarded as an independent variable, while the remainder can be treated as dependent variables.

snippet: == Examples of Reciprocals ==

title: Reciprocal Curve/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Reciprocal Curves ==

title: Reciprocal Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Reciprocal Equations ==

title: Reciprocal Form of One Minus Golden Mean
snippet: $\hat \phi = - \dfrac 1 \phi$ where: $\phi$ denotes the golden mean $\hat \phi$ denotes one minus the golden mean: $\hat \phi = 1 - \phi$.

title: Reciprocal Function is Continuous on Real Numbers without Zero
Reciprocal Function is Discontinuous at Zero
snippet: Let $f$ be the real function defined as: $\map f x = \dfrac 1 x$ for $x \ne 0$ Then $\map f x$ cannot be extended to a real function $g$ on $\R$ such that $\map g x$ is continuous on $\openint {-1} 1$.

title: Reciprocal Function is Strictly Decreasing
snippet: The reciprocal function: $\operatorname{recip}: \R \setminus \set 0 \to \R$, $x \mapsto \dfrac 1 x$ is strictly decreasing: on the open interval $\openint 0 \to$ on the open interval $\openint \gets 0$

title: Reciprocal Function is Unbounded on Open Unit Interval
snippet: Let $A = \openint 0 1$ denote the open unit interval. Let $f: A \to \R$ be the reciprocal function: $\forall x \in A: \map f x := \dfrac 1 x$ Then $f$ is unbounded.

title: Reciprocal Property of Pole and Polar
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $P$ and $Q$ be points in the plane of $\CC$. Let $\PP$ and $\QQ$ be the polars of $P$ and $Q$ with respect to $\CC$ respectively. Let $Q$ lie on $\PP$ with respect to $\CC$. Then $P$ lies on $\QQ$. That is: if $P$ lies on the polar of $Q$, then $Q$ lies on the polar of $P$ if the pole of $\PP$ lies on $\QQ$, then the pole of $\QQ$ lies on $\PP$

title: Reciprocal Rule for Derivatives
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on the open interval $I$ such that: $\forall x \in I: \map f x \ne 0$ Let $h$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in I: \map h x = \dfrac 1 {\map f x}$ Let $\xi \in I$ be a point in $I$ at which both $f$ is differentiable. Then: $\map {h'} \xi = \dfrac {\map {f'} \xi} {\paren {\map f \xi}^2}$

title: Reciprocal Sequence is Strictly Decreasing
snippet: The reciprocal sequence: $\sequence {\operatorname {recip} }: \N_{>0} \to \R$: $n \mapsto \dfrac 1 n$ is strictly decreasing.

snippet: == Examples of Reciprocal Series ==

title: Reciprocal as Summation of Binomial Coefficients of Reciprocals
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z_{>0}: \dfrac 1 n = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {-1}^k \dbinom {n - 1} k \dfrac 1 {k + 1}$ where $\dbinom {n - 1} k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is, for example:

title: Reciprocal of 101
snippet: The decimal expansion of the reciprocal of $101$ is as follows: $\dfrac 1 {101} = 0 \cdotp \dot 009 \dot 9$

title: Reciprocal of 103

title: Reciprocal of Absolutely Convergent Product is Absolutely Convergent
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {1 + a_n}$ be a sequence of nonzero elements of $\mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \left({1 + a_n}\right)$ converge absolutely to $a \in \mathbb K \setminus \set 0$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {1 + a_n}$ converges absolutely to $1 / a$.

title: Reciprocal of Complex Exponential
snippet: Let $z \in \C$. Let $\exp$ denote the complex exponential function. Then: $\dfrac 1 {\map \exp z} = \map \exp {-z}$

title: Reciprocal of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. The reciprocal of $z$ is: $\dfrac 1 z = \dfrac {a - i b} {a^2 + b^2}$

title: Reciprocal of Complex Number in terms of Conjugate and Modulus
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. The reciprocal of $z$ can be expressed as: $\dfrac 1 z = \dfrac {\overline z} {\cmod z^2}$ where: $\overline z$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z$ $\cmod z^2$ denotes the modulus of $z$.

title: Reciprocal of Computable Rational Sequence is Computable
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a computable rational sequence. Suppose that, for all $n \in \N$: $x_n \ne 0$ Then: $\sequence {\dfrac 1 {x_n}}$ is a computable rational sequence.

title: Reciprocal of Computable Real Sequence is Computable
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_m}$ be a computable real sequence. Suppose that, for all $m \in \N$: $x_m \ne 0$ Then: $\sequence {\dfrac 1 {x_m}}$ is a computable real sequence.

title: Reciprocal of Continuous Complex-Valued Function Vanishing at Infinity does not Vanish at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a continuous function that vanishes at infinity such that: $\map f x \ne 0$ for each $x \in X$. Then $\dfrac 1 f : X \to \C$ does not vanish at infinity.

title: Reciprocal of Difference of Squares as Difference of Reciprocals
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {x^2 - y^2} = \dfrac 1 {2 y \paren {x - y} } - \dfrac 1 {2 y \paren {x + y} }$

title: Reciprocal of Difference of Squares as Sum of Reciprocals
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {x^2 - y^2} = \dfrac 1 {2 x \paren {x + y} } + \dfrac 1 {2 x \paren {x - y} }$

title: Reciprocal of Function of Bounded Variation Bounded away from Zero is of Bounded Variation
snippet: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $a 0$ for all $x \in \closedint a b$. Let $\map {V_f} {\closedint a b}$ be the total variation of $f$ on $\closedint a b$. Then: $\dfrac 1 f$ is of bounded variation with: $\map {V_{1 / f} } {\closedint a b} \le \dfrac {\map {V_f} {\closedint a b} } {M^2}$ where $\map {V_{1 / f} } {\closedint a b}$ denotes the total variation of $\dfrac 1 f$ on $\closedint a b$.

title: Reciprocal of Holomorphic Function
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a complex function. Let $U \subseteq \C$ be an open set such that $f$ has no zeros in $U$. Suppose further that $f$ is holomorphic in $U$. Then the complex function $\dfrac 1 {f_{\restriction U} } : U \to \C$ is holomorphic.

title: Reciprocal of Hyperbolic Cosine Minus One

title: Reciprocal of Hyperbolic Cosine Plus One
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {\cosh x + 1} = \dfrac 1 2 \sech^2 \dfrac x 2$

title: Reciprocal of Logarithm
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R_{> 0}$ be (strictly) positive real numbers. Then: $\dfrac 1 {\log_x y} = \log_y x$

title: Reciprocal of Null Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $\forall n \in \N: x_n > 0$. Then: $x_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ $\size {\dfrac 1 {x_n} } \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$

title: Reciprocal of One Minus Cosine
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {1 - \cos x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\csc^2} {\dfrac x 2}$

title: Reciprocal of One Minus Cosine plus Reciprocal of One Plus Cosine
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {1 - \cos x} + \dfrac 1 {1 + \cos x} = 2 \cosec^2 x$

title: Reciprocal of One Minus Secant
snippet: $\dfrac {\sin^2 x + 2 \cos x - 1} {\sin^2 x + 3 \cos x - 3} = \dfrac 1 {1 - \sec x}$

title: Reciprocal of One Minus Sine
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {1 - \sin x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\dfrac \pi 4 + \dfrac x 2}$

title: Reciprocal of One Plus Cosecant
snippet: $\dfrac {\cos^2 x + 3 \sin x - 1} {\cos^2 x + 2 \sin x + 2} = \dfrac 1 {1 + \csc x}$

title: Reciprocal of One Plus Cosine
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {1 + \cos x} = \dfrac 1 2 \sec^2 \dfrac x 2$

title: Reciprocal of One Plus Sine
snippet: $\dfrac 1 {1 + \sin x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\dfrac \pi 4 - \dfrac x 2}$

title: Reciprocal of One minus x in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac {a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } {c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\dfrac 1 {1 - x} = \map F {1, p; p; x}$ where $x$ and $p$ are real numbers such that $\size x < 1$.

title: Reciprocal of Power of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $z^n$ denote $z$ raised to the $n$th power. The reciprocal of $z^n$ can be expressed as: $\dfrac 1 {z^n} = \dfrac {\overline z^n} {\cmod z^{2 n} }$ where: $\overline z$ denotes the complex conjugate of $z$ $\cmod z^2$ denotes the modulus of $z$.

title: Reciprocal of Quotient of Real Numbers
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R_{\ne 0}: \dfrac 1 {x / y} = \dfrac y x$

title: Reciprocal of Random Variable with Snedecor's F-Distribution has Snedecor's F-Distribution
snippet: Let $n, m$ be strictly positive integers. Let $X \sim F_{n, m}$ where $F_{n, m}$ is the Snedecor's $F$-distribution with $\tuple {n, m}$ degrees of freedom. Then: $\dfrac 1 X \sim F_{m, n}$

title: Reciprocal of Real Exponential
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Let $\exp$ denotes the real exponential function. Then: $\dfrac 1 {\map \exp x} = \map \exp {-x}$

title: Reciprocal of Real Number is Non-Zero
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: x \ne 0 \implies \dfrac 1 x \ne 0$

title: Reciprocal of Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: For $\map \Re z > 1$: $\ds \frac 1 {\map \zeta z} = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac{\mu \left({k}\right)} {k^z}$ where: $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function $\mu$ is the Möbius function.

title: Reciprocal of Square of 1 Less than Number Base
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b > 2$. Let $n = \paren {b - 1}^2$. The reciprocal of $n$, expressed in base $b$, recurs with period $b - 1$: $\dfrac 1 n = \sqbrk {0 \cdotp \dot 012 \ldots c \dot d}_b = \sqbrk {0 \cdotp 012 \ldots cd012 \ldots}_b$ where: $c = b - 3$ $d = b - 1$

title: Reciprocal of Strictly Negative Real Number is Strictly Negative

title: Reciprocal of Strictly Positive Real Number is Strictly Positive
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: x > 0 \implies \dfrac 1 x > 0$

title: Reciprocal of i

title: Reciprocal times Derivative of Gamma Function
snippet: Let $z \in \C \setminus \Z_{\le 0}$. Then: $\ds \dfrac {\map {\Gamma'} z} {\map \Gamma z} = -\gamma + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\frac 1 n - \frac 1 {z + n - 1} }$ where: $\map \Gamma z$ denotes the Gamma function $\map {\Gamma'} z$ denotes the derivative of the Gamma function $\gamma$ denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

title: Reciprocals of Odd Numbers adding to 1

title: Rectangular Delta Sequence
snippet: The graph of the rectangular delta sequence. As $n$ grows, the rectangle becomes thinner and taller. The area of each rectangle is equal to $1$. Let $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}$ be a sequence such that: $\map {\delta_n} x := \begin {cases} 0 & : x \dfrac 1 {2 n} \end {cases}$ Then $\sequence {\map {\delta_n} x}_{n \mathop \in {\N_{>0} } }$ is a delta sequence.

title: Rectangular Formula for Definite Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $P = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n - 1}, x_n}$ form a normal subdivision of $\closedint a b$: $\forall r \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: x_r - x_{r - 1} = \dfrac {b - a} n$ Then the definite integral of $f$ $x$ from $a$ to $b$ can be approximated as: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x \approx \sum_{r \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} h \map f {x_r}$ where $h = \dfrac {b - a} n$.

title: Recurrence Formula for Associated Legendre Function of the First Kind
snippet: Let $\map { {P_n}^m} x$ denote an associated Legendre function of the first kind.

title: Recurrence Formula for Bessel Function of the First Kind
snippet: Let $\map {J_n} x$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$. Then: $\map {J_{n + 1} } x = \dfrac {2 n} x \map {J_n} x - \map {J_{n - 1} } x$ And: $\map {J_{n + 1} } x = -2 \map {J_n'} x + \map {J_{n - 1} } x$

title: Recurrence Formula for Chebyshev Polynomials of the First Kind
snippet: Let $\map {T_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind of order $n$. Then: $\map {T_n} x = \begin {cases} 1 & : n = 0 \\ x & : n = 1 \\ 2 x \, \map {T_{n - 1} } x - \map {T_{n - 2} } x & : n > 1 \end {cases}$

title: Recurrence Formula for Chebyshev Polynomials of the Second Kind
snippet: Let $\map {U_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind of order $n$. Then: $\map {U_n} x = \begin {cases} 1 & : n = 0 \\ 2 x & : n = 1 \\ 2 x \map {U_{n - 1} } x - \map {U_{n - 2} } x & : n > 1 \end {cases}$

title: Recurrence Formula for Hermite Polynomials
snippet: Let $\map {H_n} x$ denote the Hermite polynomial of order $n$. Then: $\map {H_{n + 1} } x = 2 x \map {H_n} x - 2 n \map {H_{n - 1} } x$

title: Recurrence Formula for Hermite Polynomials using Derivative
snippet: Let $\map {H_n} x$ denote the Hermite polynomial of order $n$. Then: $\dfrac \d {\d x} \map {H_n} x = 2 n \map {H_{n - 1} } x$

title: Recurrence Formula for Laguerre Polynomials
snippet: Let $\map {L_n} x$ denote the Laguerre polynomial of order $n$. Then: $\map {L_{n + 1} } x - \paren {2 n + 1 - x} \map {L_n} x + n^2 \map {L_{n - 1} } x = 0$

title: Recurrence Formula for Laguerre Polynomials using Derivative
snippet: Let $\map {L_n} x$ denote the Laguerre polynomial of order $n$. Then: $\dfrac \d {\d x} \map {L_n} x - n \dfrac \d {\d x} \map {L_{n - 1} } x + n \map {L_{n - 1} } x = 0$

title: Recurrence Formula for Sum of Sequence of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $g_n$ be the sum of the first $n$ Fibonacci numbers. Then: $\forall n \ge 2: g_n = g_{n - 1} + g_{n - 2} + 1$

title: Recurrence Relation for Bell Numbers
snippet: Let $B_n$ be the Bell number for $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $B_{n + 1} = \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n \dbinom n k B_k$ where $\dbinom n k$ are binomial coefficients.

title: Recurrence Relation for Digamma Function
snippet: $\map \psi {z + 1} = \map \psi z + \dfrac 1 z$ where: $\psi$ denotes the digamma function $z \in \C \setminus \Z_{\le 0}$.

title: Recurrence Relation for Euler Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: {{eqn | l = E_{2 n} | r = -\sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \dbinom {2 n} {2 k} E_{2 k} | c = }} {{eqn | r = -\paren {\binom {2 n} 0 E_0 + \binom {2 n} 2 E_2 + \binom {2 n} 4 E_4 + \cdots + \binom {2 n} {2 n - 2} E_{2 n - 2} } | c = }} where $E_n$ denotes the $n$th Euler number.

title: Recurrence Relation for Fibonomial Coefficients
snippet: $\dbinom n k_\FF = F_{k - 1} \dbinom {n - 1} k_\FF + F_{n - k + 1} \dbinom {n - 1} {k - 1}_\FF$ where: $\dbinom n k_\FF$ denotes a Fibonomial coefficient $F_{k - 1}$ etc. denote Fibonacci numbers.

title: Recurrence Relation for General Harmonic Numbers
snippet: $\harm r x = \harm r {x - 1} + \dfrac 1 {x^r}$ where: $\harm r x$ denotes the general harmonic number of order $r$ evaluated at $x$.

title: Recurrence Relation for Number of Derangements on Finite Set
snippet: The number of derangements $D_n$ on a finite set $S$ of cardinality $n$ is: $D_n = \paren {n - 1} \paren {D_{n - 1} + D_{n - 2} }$ where $D_1 = 0$, $D_2 = 1$.

title: Recurrence Relation for Polygamma Function
snippet: $\map {\psi_n} {z + 1} = \map {\psi_n} z + \paren {-1}^n n! z^{-n - 1}$ where: $\psi_n$ denote the $n$th polygamma function $z \in \C \setminus \Z_{\le 0}$.

title: Recurrence Relation for Polylogarithms
snippet: $\ds \map {\Li_{s + 1} } z = \int_0^z \dfrac {\map {\Li_s} t} t \rd t$ where: $\map {\Li_s} z$ denotes the polylogarithm.

title: Recurrence Relation for Sequence of mth Powers of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in \Z} \dbinom m k_\FF \paren {-1}^{\ceiling {\paren {m - k} / 2} } {F_{n + k} }^{m - 1} = 0$ where: $\dbinom m k_\FF$ denotes a Fibonomial coefficient $F_{n + k}$ denotes the $n + k$th Fibonacci number $\ceiling {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the ceiling function

title: Recurrence Relation where n+1th Term is A by nth term + B to the n
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be the sequence defined by the recurrence relation: $a_n = \begin {cases} 0 & : n = 0 \\ A a_{n - 1} + B^{n - 1} & : n > 0 \end {cases}$ for numbers $A$ and $B$. Then the closed form for $\sequence {a_n}$ is given by: $a_n = \begin {cases} \dfrac {A^n - B^n} {A - B} & : A \ne B \\ n A^{n - 1} & : A = B \end {cases}$

title: Recursion Property of Elementary Symmetric Function
snippet: Let $\set {z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_{n + 1} }$ be a set of $n + 1$ numbers, duplicate values permitted. Then for $1 \le m \le n$: $\map {e_m} {\set {z_1, \ldots, z_n, z_{n + 1} } } = z_{n + 1} \map {e_{m - 1} } {\set {z_1, \ldots, z_n} } + \map {e_m} {\set {z_1, \ldots, z_n} }$ where $\map {e_m} {\set {z_1, \ldots, z_n} }$ denotes the elementary symmetric function of degree $m$ on $\set {z_1, \ldots, z_n}$.

title: Recursive Construction of Transitive Closure
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation. The transitive closure $\RR^+$ of $\RR$ can be constructed as follows: Let: $\RR_n := \begin {cases} \RR & : n = 0 \\ \RR_{n - 1} \cup \set {\tuple {x_1, x_3}: \exists x_2: \tuple {x_1, x_2} \in \RR_{n-1} \land \tuple {x_2, x_3} \in \RR_{n - 1} } & : n > 0 \end{cases}$ Finally, let: $\ds \RR^+ = \bigcup_{i \mathop \in \N} \RR_i$ Then $R^+$ is the transitive closure of $R$.

title: Recursive Form of Generalized Termial
snippet: The termial function as defined on the real numbers fulfils the identity: $x? = x + \paren {x - 1}?$

title: Recursive Function is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^k \to \N$ be a recursive function. Then there exists a $\Sigma_1$ WFF of $k + 1$ free variables: $\map \phi {y, x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k}$ such that: $y = \map f {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k} \iff \N \models \map \phi {\sqbrk y, \sqbrk {x_1}, \sqbrk {x_2}, \dotsc, \sqbrk {x_k} }$ where $\sqbrk a$ denotes the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Recursive Function is URM Computable
snippet: Every recursive function‎ is URM computable.

title: Recursive Function uses One Minimization
snippet: Every recursive function can be obtained from the basic primitive recursive functions using: substitution primitive recursion at most one minimization on a function.

title: Recursive Relation is Turing Computable
snippet: Let $f: S \to \set {0, 1}$, where $S \subseteq \N^k$ be a recursive function. Let the encoding of some $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k} \in \N^k$ be the string: $1^{x_1} 0 1^{x_2} 0 1^{x_3} 0 \dotsm 0 1^{x_k}$ Then, there exists a Turing machine such that: The input symbols of the machine are $\set {0, 1}$ The accepted language is the set of encodings of $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k}$ such that $\map f {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k} = 1$ The machine halts on an input it is not in the correct format, or it is the encoding of some $\tuple {x_1, x_2, \dotsc, x_k}$ such that $\map f {x_1, x_2, \dotsc,…

title: Recursive Set is Turing Computable
snippet: Let $f: S \to \set {0, 1}$, where $S \subseteq \N$, be a recursive function. Let $\sqbrk x$ denote the reverse of the base-$2$ representation of $x$, possibly with additional $0$ at the end. That is, if the base-$2$ representation of $x$ is $\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \dotsm r_1 r_0}_2$ then $\sqbrk x$ is: $r_0 r_1 \dotsm r_{m - 1} r_m 0 \dotsm 0$ There exists a Turing machine such that: The input symbols of the machine are $\set {0, 1}$ The machine accepts the language $\set {\sqbrk x : \map f x = 1}$ The machine halts on $\sqbrk x$ $x \in S$

title: Recursively Defined Sequence/Examples/Minimum over k of Maximum of 1 plus Function of k and 2 plus Function of n-k

title: Recursively Defined Sequence/Examples/Term is Term of Index less 1 plus 6 times Term of Index less 2

title: Recursively Enumerable Set is Image of Primitive Recursive Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be recursively enumerable. Suppose $S$ is non-empty. Then there exists a primitive recursive function $f : \N^k \to \N$ such that: $\Img f = S$

title: Reduced Residue System Modulo Prime
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. The reduced residue system modulo $p$ contains $p - 1$ elements: $Z'_p = \set {\eqclass 1 m, \eqclass 2 m, \ldots, \eqclass {p - 1} m}$ and so can be defined as: $Z'_p = Z_p \setminus \set {\eqclass 0 m}$

title: Reduced Residue System is Subset of Set of All Residue Classes
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ be the set of set of residue classes modulo $m$. Let $\Z'_m$ be the reduced residue system modulo $m$. Then: $\forall m \in \Z_{> 1}: \O \subset \Z'_m \subset \Z_m$

title: Reduced Residue System under Multiplication forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ be the set of set of residue classes modulo $m$. Let $\struct {\Z'_m, \times}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $m$. Then $\struct {\Z'_m, \times}$ is an abelian group, precisely equal to the group of units of $\Z_m$.

title: Reduced Residues Modulo 5 under Multiplication form Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z'_5, \times_5}$ denote the multiplicative group of reduced residues modulo $5$. Then $\struct {\Z'_5, \times_5}$ is cyclic.

title: Reduction Formula (Trigonometry)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Reduction Formulae in context of Trigonometry ==

title: Reduction Formula for Definite Integral of Power of Cosine
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $I_n$ be defined as: $\ds I_n = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \cos^n x \rd x$ Then $\sequence {I_n}$ is a decreasing sequence of real numbers which satisfies: $n I_n = \paren {n - 1} I_{n - 2}$ Thus: $I_n = \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2}$ is a reduction formula for $I_n$.

title: Reduction Formula for Definite Integral of Power of Sine
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $I_n$ be defined as: $\ds I_n = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^n x \rd x$ Then $\sequence {I_n}$ is a decreasing sequence of real numbers which satisfies: $n I_n = \paren {n - 1} I_{n - 2}$ Thus: $I_n = \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2}$ is a reduction formula for $I_n$.

title: Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Cosine
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let: $I_n := \ds \int \cos^n x \rd x$ Then: $I_n = \dfrac {\cos^{n - 1} x \sin x} n + \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2}$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int \cos^n x \rd x$.

title: Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Sine
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let: $I_n := \ds \int \sin^n x \rd x$ Then: $I_n = \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2} - \dfrac {\sin^{n - 1} x \cos x} n$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int \sin^n x \rd x$.

title: Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Tangent
snippet: For all $n \in \Z_{> 1}$: Let: $I_n := \ds \int \tan^n x \rd x$ Then: $I_n = \dfrac {\tan^{n - 1} x} {n - 1} - I_{n - 2}$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int \tan^n x \rd x$.

title: Reduction Formula for Power of x by Exponential of a x
snippet: $\ds \int x^n e^{a x} \rd x = \frac {x^n e^{a x} } a - \dfrac n a \int x^{n - 1} e^{a x} \rd x$ for $n \in \Z_{>0}$, $a \in \R_{\ne 0}$.

title: Reduction Formula for Power of x by General Exponential of a x
snippet: $\ds \int x^n b^{a x} \rd x = \frac {x^n b^{a x} } {a \ln b} - \dfrac n {a \ln b} \int x^{n - 1} b^{a x} \rd x$ for $n \in \Z_{>0}$, $a \in \R_{\ne 0}$, $b > 0$, $b \ne 1$

title: Reduction Formula for Primitive of Product of Power with Exponential
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let: $I_n := \ds \int x^n e^x \rd x$ Then: $I_n = x^n e^x - n I_{n - 1}$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int x^n e^x \rd x$.

title: Reduction Formula for Primitive of Product of Power with Power of Quadratic
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ and $k \in \Z_{\ge 2}$. Let: $I_{n, k} := \ds \int x^k \paren {x^2 + A x + B}^n \rd x$ Then: $I_{n, k} = \dfrac {x^{k - 1} \paren {x^2 + A x + B}^{n + 1} } {k + 2 n + 1} - \dfrac {B \paren {k - 1} } {k + 2 n + 1} I_{n, k - 2} - \dfrac {A \paren {k + n} } {k + 2 n + 1} I_{n, k - 1}$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int x^k \paren {x^2 + A x + B}^n \rd x$.

title: Reduction Formula for Primitive of a x + b over Power of Quadratic
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 2}$. Let: $\map {I_n} {a, b} := \ds \int \dfrac {a x + b} {\paren {x^2 + A x + B}^n} \rd x$ Then: $\map {I_n} {a, b} = \dfrac {b A - 2 a B + \paren {2 b - a A} x} {\paren {n - 1} \paren {4 B - A^2} \paren {x^2 + A x + B}^n} + \dfrac {\paren {2 n - 3} \paren {2 b - a A} } {\paren {n - 1} \paren {4 B - A^2} } \map {I_{n - 1} }{0, 1}$ is a reduction formula for $\ds \int \dfrac {a x + b} {\paren {x^2 + A x + B}^n} \rd x$.

title: Reduction of Explicit ODE to First Order System
snippet: Let $\map {x^{\paren n} } t = \map F {t, x, x', \ldots, x^{\paren {n - 1} } }$, $\map x {t_0} = x_0$ be an explicit ODE with $x \in \R^m$. Let there exist $I \subseteq \R$ such that there exists a unique particular solution: $x: I \to \R^m$ to this ODE. Then there exists a system of first order ODEs: $y' = \map {\tilde F} {t, y}$ with $y = \tuple {y_1, \ldots, y_{m n} }^T \in \R^{m n}$ such that: $\tuple {\map {y_1} t, \ldots, \map {y_m} t} = \map x t$ for all $t \in I$ and $\map y {t_0} = x_0$.

title: Reduction of Riemann-Stieltjes Integral to Identity Integrator
snippet: Let $f, \alpha$ be real functions that are bounded on $\closedint a b$. Suppose that $f$ is Riemann-Stieltjes integrable with respect to $\alpha$ on $\closedint a b$. Also suppose that $\alpha$ is continuously differentiable on $\closedint a b$. Then, let $\alpha'$ be the derivative of $\alpha$ on $\closedint a b$. Let $g : \closedint a b \to \R$ be defined as: $\map g x = \map f x \map {\alpha'} x$ Let $\iota$ be the identity mapping on $\closedint a b$.

title: Refinement of Cover is not necessarily Subcover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover of $S$. Let $\RR$ be a refinement of $\CC$. Then $\RR$ is not necessarily a subcover of $\CC$.

title: Refinement of Open Cover has Greater Entropy
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\alpha, \beta$ be open covers of $X$. Let $\map H \alpha$ and $\map H \beta$ be their entropies. Suppose that $\beta$ is a refinement of $\alpha$. Then: $\map H \alpha \le \map H \beta$

title: Refinement of a Refinement is Refinement of Cover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\UU = \set {U_\alpha}$, $\VV = \set {V_\beta}$ and $\WW = \set {W_\gamma}$ be covers of $S$. Let $\VV$ be a refinement of $\UU$. Let $\WW$ be a refinement of $\VV$. Then: $\WW$ is a refinement of $\UU$

title: Reflection Formula (Geometry)
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $v, a, \in H$ be arbitrary elements of $H$. Let $A \subset H$ denote the hyperplane orthogonal to $a$. The reflection of $v$ through $A$ is given by: $\map {\operatorname {Ref}_a} v = v - 2 \dfrac {\langle v, a \rangle} {\langle a, a \rangle} a$

title: Reflection Rule for Gaussian Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $q \in \R_{\ne 1}, n \in \Z_{>0}, k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k_q = q^{k \paren {n - k} } \dbinom n k_{q^{-1} }$ where $\dbinom n k_q$ is a Gaussian binomial coefficient.

title: Reflection in Euclidean Space is Conformal
snippet: Let $f$ be an reflection in Euclidean space. Then $f$ is a conformal transformation.

title: Reflection is Isometry
snippet: Let $\Gamma = \R^n$ denote the real Euclidean space of $n$ dimensions, wher $n = 2$ or $n = 3$. Let $\phi$ be a reflection in $\Gamma$. Then $\phi$ is an isometry.

title: Reflection of Plane in Line through Origin is Linear Operator
snippet: Let $M$ be a straight line in the plane $\R^2$ passing through the origin. Let $s_M$ be the reflection of $\R^2$ in $M$. Then $s_M$ is a linear operator for every straight line $M$ through the origin.

title: Reflexive Banach Space is Schur Space iff Finite Dimensional
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a reflexive Banach space over $\GF$. Then $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ is a Schur space it is finite-dimensional.

title: Reflexive Banach Space is Weakly Sequentially Complete
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a reflexive Banach space over $\GF$. Then $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ is weakly sequentially complete.

title: Reflexive Bilinear Form is Symmetric or Alternating
snippet: Let $\mathbb K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K$. Let $f$ be a bilinear form on $V$. Let $f$ be reflexive. Then $f$ is symmetric or alternating.

title: Reflexive Circular Relation is Equivalence
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a reflexive and circular relation in $S$. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Reflexive Closure is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $R$ be the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the reflexive closure operator on $R$ is a closure operator.

title: Reflexive Closure is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $R$ denote the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the reflexive closure operator is an idempotent mapping on $R$. That is: $\forall \RR \in R: \RR^= = \paren {\RR^=}^=$ where $\RR^=$ denotes the reflexive closure of $\RR$.

title: Reflexive Closure is Inflationary
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $R$ denote the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the reflexive closure operator is an inflationary mapping on $R$.

title: Reflexive Closure is Order Preserving
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $R$ denote the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the reflexive closure operator is an order preserving mapping on $R$. That is: $\forall \RR, \SS \in R: \RR \subseteq \SS \implies \RR^= \subseteq \SS^=$ where $\RR^=$ and $\SS^=$ denote the reflexive closure of $\RR$ and $\SS$ respectively.

title: Reflexive Closure is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $\RR^=$, the reflexive closure of $\RR$, is reflexive.

title: Reflexive Closure of Antisymmetric Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $RR$ be an antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $\RR^=$ be the reflexive closure of $\RR$. Then $\RR^=$ is also antisymmetric.

title: Reflexive Closure of Relation Compatible with Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$ which is compatible with $\circ$. Let $\RR^=$ be the reflexive closure of $\prec$. That is, $\RR^=$ is defined as the union of $\RR$ with the diagonal relation for $S$. Then $\RR^=$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Reflexive Closure of Strict Ordering is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\prec$ be a strict ordering on $S$. Let $\preceq$ be the reflexive closure of $\prec$. Then $\preceq$ is an ordering.

title: Reflexive Closure of Strict Total Ordering is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\prec$ be a strict total ordering of $S$. Let $\preceq$ be the reflexive closure of $\prec$. Then $\preceq$ is an total ordering of $S$.

title: Reflexive Closure of Transitive Antisymmetric Relation is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\prec$ be a transitive, antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $\preceq$ be the reflexive closure of $\prec$. Then $\preceq$ is an ordering on $S$.

title: Reflexive Closure of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be a transitive relation. Let $\RR^=$ be the reflexive closure of $\RR$. Then $\RR^=$ is also transitive.

title: Reflexive Euclidean Relation is Equivalence
snippet: A relation is an equivalence it is either left-Euclidean or right-Euclidean, and also reflexive.

title: Reflexive Reduction is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR^\ne$ denote the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is antireflexive.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Antisymmetric Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is asymmetric.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Ordering is Strict Ordering
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an ordering on a set $S$. Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is a strict ordering on $S$.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Relation Compatible with Cancellable Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure such that $\circ$ is a cancellable operation. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$ which is compatible with $\circ$. Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Relation Compatible with Group Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$ which is compatible with $\circ$. Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Transitive Antisymmetric Relation is Strict Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be a transitive, antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $\RR^\ne$ denote the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is a strict ordering.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be a transitive relation on $S$. Let $\RR^\ne$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\ne$ is transitive.

title: Reflexive Reduction of Well-Founded Relation is Strictly Well-Founded Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $\RR^{\ne}$ be the reflexive reduction of $\RR$. Then $\RR^{\ne}$ is a strictly well-founded relation.

title: Reflexive Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Reflexive Relations ==

title: Reflexive Relation is Quasi-Reflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a reflexive relation on a set $S$. Then $\RR$ is a quasi-reflexive relation on $S$.

title: Reflexive Relation is Serial
snippet: Every reflexive relation is also a serial relation.

title: Reflexive Relation on Set of Cardinality 2 is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is equal to $2$: $\card S = 2$ Let $\odot \subseteq S \times S$ be a reflexive relation on $S$. Then $\odot$ is also transitive.

title: Reflexive Relation on Singleton is Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $S = \set s$ be a singleton. Let $\RR$ be a reflexive relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a well-ordering on $S$.

title: Reflexive Riesz Lemma
snippet: Let $X$ be a reflexive normed vector space. Let $Y$ be a proper closed linear subspace of $X$. Then $\exists x_\alpha \in X$ such that: $\norm {x_\alpha} = 1$ with: $\ds \map d {x_\alpha, Y} = 1$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set.

title: Reflexive Space is Banach Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a reflexive normed vector space. Then $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ is a Banach space.

title: Reflexive Transitive Closure/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Reflexive Transitive Closures ==

title: Reflexive and Symmetric Relation is not necessarily Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\alpha \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Let $\alpha$ be both reflexive and symmetric. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\alpha$ is also transitive.

title: Reflexive and Transitive Relation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR$ be both reflexive and transitive. Then $\RR$ is idempotent, in the sense that: $\RR \circ \RR = \RR$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of relations.

title: Reflexive and Transitive Relation is not necessarily Symmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\alpha \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Let $\alpha$ be both reflexive and transitive. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\alpha$ is also symmetric.

title: Regiomontanus' Angle Maximization Problem
snippet: Let $AB$ be a line segment. Let $AB$ be produced to $P$. Let $PQ$ be constructed perpendicular to $AB$. Then the angle $AQB$ is greatest when $PQ$ is tangent to a circle passing through $A$, $B$ and $Q$.

title: Region Less One Point is Region
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a dense-in-itself metric space. Let $R \subseteq M$ be a region of $M$. Let $x \in R$. Then $R \setminus \set x$ is also a region of $M$.

title: Regression/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Regression ==

title: Regression Coefficients of Normally Distributed Random Variable
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Let $x$ be a given value of $X$. Let $Y$ be a random variable with a normal distribution. Let the variance $\sigma^2$ of $Y$ (usually unknown) be independent of $x$. Let $S$ be a sample of $n$ independent pairs of observations $\tuple {x_i, y_i}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$.

title: Regular Closed Set is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be regular closed in $T$. Then $H$ is an closed set of $T$.

title: Regular Curve in Riemannian Manifold has Unit-Speed Forward Reparametrization
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be a regular curve. Then $\gamma$ has a unit-speed forward reparametrization.

title: Regular Dodecahedron is Dual of Regular Icosahedron
snippet: The regular dodecahedron is the dual of the regular icosahedron.

title: Regular Expression is Accepted by Finite State Machine
snippet: Let $R$ be a regular expression. Then there exists a finite state machine $F$ such that its accepted language $\map L F$ is exactly $\map L R$, the language defined by $R$.

title: Regular Graph/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Regular Graphs ==

title: Regular Graph is Tree iff Complete Graph of Order 2
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-edgeless regular graph. Then $G$ is a tree $G$ is $K_2$, the complete graph of order $2$.

title: Regular Heptagon is Smallest with no Compass and Straightedge Construction
snippet: The regular heptagon is the smallest regular polygon (smallest in the sense of having fewest sides) that cannot be constructed using a compass and straightedge construction.

title: Regular Hexagon is composed of Equilateral Triangles
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular hexagon. Let $O$ be the center of $P$. Then there exists a triangulation of $P$ into six congruent equilateral triangles. The three vertices of each triangle are $O$ and two adjacent vertices of $P$.

title: Regular Icosahedron as Pentagonal Antiprism with Pyramidal Endcaps
snippet: The regular icosahedron can be considered as a regular pentagonal antiprism with two regular pentagonal pyramid as end caps.

title: Regular Lindelöf Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular Lindelöf topological space. Then $T$ is a normal space.

title: Regular Lindelöf Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space which is also Lindelöf. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Regular Octahedron is Dual of Cube
snippet: The regular octahedron is the dual of the cube.

title: Regular Open Set is Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be regular open in $T$. Then $H$ is an open set of $T$.

title: Regular Paracompact Space is not necessarily Metrizable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is regular and paracompact. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is metrizable.

title: Regular Polygon can be Circumscribed around Circle
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular polygon. Then it is possible to circumscribe $P$ around a circle $C$, whose center is the same as the center of $P$.

title: Regular Polygon is Cyclic
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular polygon. Then $P$ is a cyclic polygon.

title: Regular Polygon is composed of Isosceles Triangles
snippet: Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon. Let $O$ be the center of $P$. Then there exists a triangulation of $P$ into $n$ congruent isosceles triangles. The three vertices of each triangle are $O$ and two adjacent vertices of $P$.

title: Regular Prism is Uniform Polyhedron/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == polyhedron

title: Regular Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a regular space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a regular space. That is: The property of being a regular space is hereditary.

title: Regular Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a regular space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: Regular Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a regular space, then so is $T_B$.

title: Regular Representation of Invertible Element is Permutation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Let $a \in S$ be invertible. Then the left regular representation $\lambda_a$ and the right regular representation $\rho_a$ are permutations of $S$.

title: Regular Representation on Subgroup is Bijection to Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$.

title: Regular Representation wrt Cancellable Element on Finite Semigroup is Bijection
snippet: Let $\left({S, \circ}\right)$ be a finite semigroup. Let $a \in S$ be cancellable. Then: the left regular representation $\lambda_a$ and: the right regular representation $\rho_a$ of $\left({S, \circ}\right)$ with respect to $a$ are both bijections.

title: Regular Representations in Group are Permutations
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $a \in G$ be any element of $G$. Then the left regular representation $\lambda_a$ and the right regular representation $\rho_a$ are permutations of $G$.

title: Regular Representations in Semigroup are Permutations then Structure is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. For $a \in S$, let $\lambda_a: S \to S$ and $\rho_a: S \to S$ denote the left regular representation and right regular representation with respect to $a$ respectively: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in S | l = \map {\lambda_a} x | r = a \circ x }} {{eqn | q = \forall x \in S | l = \map {\rho_a} x | r = x \circ a }} For all $a$ in $S$, let $\lambda_a$ be a permutation on $S$. Let there exist $b$ in $S$ such that $\rho_b$ is a permutation on $S$. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group.

title: Regular Representations wrt Element are Permutations then Element is Invertible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\lambda_a: S \to S$ and $\rho_a: S \to S$ be the left regular representation and right regular representation with respect to $a$ respectively: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in S | l = \map {\lambda_a} x | r = a \circ x }} {{eqn | q = \forall x \in S | l = \map {\rho_a} x | r = x \circ a }} Let both $\lambda_a$ and $\rho_a$ be permutations on $S$. Then there exists an identity element for $\circ$ and $a$ is invertible.

title: Regular Second-Countable Space is Homeomorphic to Subspace of Hilbert Cube
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is regular and second-countable. Then $T$ is homeomorphic to a subspace of the Hilbert cube.

title: Regular Space is Semiregular
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a semiregular space.

title: Regular Space is T2.5
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Regular Space is not necessarily Completely Regular
snippet: A topological space which is a regular space is not necessarily also a completely regular space.

title: Regular Space is not necessarily Normal
snippet: A topological space which is a regular space is not necessarily also a normal space.

title: Regular Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular space. Let there exist a $\sigma$-locally finite basis for $T$. Then: $T$ is a normal space

title: Regular Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Perfectly Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a regular topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis. Then: $T$ is a perfectly normal space.

snippet: == Examples of Regular Star Polygons ==

snippet: == Examples of Regular Stellated Polygons ==
