title: Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relations ==

title: Relation Between Bridges And Spanning Trees
Relation Between First and Second Form of Binet Form
snippet: Let $m \in \R$. Define: {{eqn | l = \Delta | r = \sqrt {m^2 + 4} }} {{eqn | l = \alpha | r = \frac {m + \Delta} 2 }} {{eqn | l = \beta | r = \frac {m - \Delta} 2 }}

title: Relation Between Rank and Exponent of Convergence
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $k$ be its rank and $\tau$ be its exponent of convergence. Then: $k=\tau=0$ if $f$ has finitely many zeroes. $k<\tau\leq k+1$ otherwise.

title: Relation Compatibility in Totally Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\left({S, \circ, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered semigroup such that: $(1): \quad$ All the elements of $\left({S, \circ, \preceq}\right)$ are cancellable for $\circ$ $(2): \quad \preceq$ is a total ordering. Then: $\forall x, y, z \in S: x \circ z \preceq y \circ z \iff x \preceq y$

title: Relation Compatible with Group Operation is Reflexive or Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $G$ that is compatible with $\circ$. Then $\RR$ is reflexive or antireflexive.

title: Relation Compatible with Group Operation is Strongly Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $G$ compatible with $\circ$. $\RR$ is strongly compatible with $\circ$: $\forall x, y, z \in G:$ $x \mathrel \RR y \iff x \circ z \mathrel \RR y \circ z$ $x \mathrel \RR y \iff z \circ x \mathrel \RR z \circ y$

title: Relation Contains Mapping is Equivalent to AoC
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Then: there exists a mapping $f \subseteq \RR$ whose domain is the same as the preimage of $\RR$ the axiom of choice holds.

title: Relation Induced by Mapping is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\RR_f \subseteq S \times S$ be the relation induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Then $\RR_f$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Relation Induced by Partition is Equivalence
snippet: Let $\mathbb S$ be a partition of a set $S$. Let $\RR$ be the relation induced by $\mathbb S$. Then: $(1): \quad \RR$ is unique $(2): \quad \RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$. Hence $\mathbb S$ is the quotient set of $S$ by $\RR$, that is: $\mathbb S = S / \RR$

title: Relation Induced by Quotient Set is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $S / \RR$ be the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR$. Let $\RR'$ be the equivalence relation induced by $S / \RR$ on $S$. Then $\RR' = \RR$.

title: Relation Induced by Strict Positivity Property is Asymmetric and Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property. Let the relation $<$ be defined on $D$ as: $\forall a, b \in D: a < b \iff \map P {-a + b}$ Then $<$ is asymmetric and antireflexive.

title: Relation Induced by Strict Positivity Property is Compatible with Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property. Let the relation $<$ be defined on $D$ as: $\forall a, b \in D: a < b \iff \map P {-a + b}$ Then $<$ is compatible with $+$, that is: $\forall x, y, z \in D: x < y \implies \paren {x + z} < \paren {y + z}$ $\forall x, y, z \in D: x < y \implies \paren {z + x} < \paren {z + y}$

title: Relation Induced by Strict Positivity Property is Compatible with Multiplication
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property. Let the relation $<$ be defined on $D$ as: $\forall a, b \in D: a < b \iff \map P {-a + b}$ Then $<$ is compatible with $\times$ in the following sense: $\forall x, y, z \in D: x < y, \map P z \implies \paren {z \times x} < \paren {z \times y}$ $\forall x, y, z \in D: x < y, \map P z \implies \paren {x \times z} < \paren {y \times z}$

title: Relation Induced by Strict Positivity Property is Transitive
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property. Let the relation $<$ be defined on $D$ as: $\forall a, b \in D: a < b \iff \map P {-a + b}$ Then $<$ is a transitive relation.

title: Relation Induced by Strict Positivity Property is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property. Let the relation $ b$ That is, $<$ is a trichotomy.

title: Relation Intersection Inverse is Greatest Symmetric Subset of Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\powerset \RR$ be the power set of $\RR$. By definition, $\powerset \RR$ is the set of all relations on $S$ that are subsets of $\RR$. Then the greatest element of $\powerset \RR$ that is symmetric is: $\RR \cap \RR^{-1}$

title: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Antisymmetry
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is an antisymmetric relation $\RR_2$ is also an antisymmetric relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Equivalence Relations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is an equivalence relation $\RR_2$ is also an equivalence relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Reflexivity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is a reflexive relation $\RR_2$ is also a reflexive relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Symmetry
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is a symmetric relation $\RR_2$ is also a symmetric relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism Preserves Transitivity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be relational structures. Let $\struct {S, \RR_1}$ and $\struct {T, \RR_2}$ be (relationally) isomorphic. Then $\RR_1$ is a transitive relation $\RR_2$ is a transitive relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Relation isomorphism is an equivalence relation.

title: Relation Isomorphism preserves Lattice Structure
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {B, \SS}$ be relational structures which are relationally isomorphic. Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be a lattice. Then $\struct {B, \SS}$ is also a lattice.

title: Relation Isomorphism preserves Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {B, \SS}$ be relational structures which are relationally isomorphic. Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {B, \SS}$ is also an ordered set.

title: Relation Isomorphism preserves Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {B, \SS}$ be relational structures which are relationally isomorphic. Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be a totally ordered set. Then $\struct {B, \SS}$ is also a totally ordered set.

title: Relation Isomorphism preserves Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ and $\struct {B, \SS}$ be relational structures which are relationally isomorphic. Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be a well-ordered set. Then $\struct {B, \SS}$ is also a well-ordered set.

title: Relation Partitions Set iff Equivalence
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $S$ can be partitioned into subsets by $\RR$ $\RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$. The partition of $S$ defined by $\RR$ is the quotient set $S / \RR$.

title: Relation Reflexivity
snippet: Every relation has exactly one of these properties: it is either: reflexive, antireflexive or non-reflexive.

title: Relation Segment is Increasing
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR, \QQ$ be relations on $S$ such that $\RR \subseteq \QQ$ Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\RR \subseteq x^\QQ$ where $x^\RR$ denotes the $\RR$-segment of $x$.

title: Relation Segment of Auxiliary Relation is Ideal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $R$ be auxiliary relation on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^R$ is ideal in $L$ where $x^R$ denotes the $R$-segment of $x$.

title: Relation Symmetry
snippet: Every non-null relation has exactly one of these properties: it is either: symmetric, asymmetric or non-symmetric.

title: Relation between Adjacent Best Rational Approximations to Root 2
snippet: Consider the Sequence of Best Rational Approximations to Square Root of 2: $\sequence S := \dfrac 1 1, \dfrac 3 2, \dfrac 7 5, \dfrac {17} {12}, \dfrac {41} {29}, \dfrac {99} {70}, \dfrac {239} {169}, \dfrac {577} {408}, \ldots$ Let $\dfrac {p_n} {q_n}$ and $\dfrac {p_{n + 1} } {q_{n + 1} }$ be adjacent terms of $\sequence S$. Then: $\dfrac {p_{n + 1} } {q_{n + 1} } = \dfrac {p_n + 2 q_n} {p_n + q_n}$

title: Relation between Direction Cosines
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a line embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $l$, $m$ and $n$ be the direction cosines of $\LL$ the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Then: $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$

title: Relation between Equations for Hypocycloid and Epicycloid
snippet: Consider the hypocycloid defined by the equations: $x = \paren {a - b} \cos \theta + b \map \cos {\paren {\dfrac {a - b} b} \theta}$ $y = \paren {a - b} \sin \theta - b \map \sin {\paren {\dfrac {a - b} b} \theta}$ By replacing $b$ with $-b$, this converts to the equations which define an epicycloid: $x = \paren {a + b} \cos \theta - b \map \cos {\paren {\dfrac {a + b} b} \theta}$ $y = \paren {a + b} \sin \theta - b \map \sin {\paren {\dfrac {a + b} b} \theta}$

title: Relation between Floor and Ceiling
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\left \lfloor {x}\right \rfloor$ be the floor of $x$, and $\left \lceil {x}\right \rceil$ be the ceiling of $x$. Then the following results apply:

title: Relation between Geodesic and Exponential Map
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g, \nabla}$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold without boundary endowed with the Levi-Civita connection. Let $TM$ be the tangent bundle of $M$. Let $\exp$ be the exponential map. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be an open real interval. Let $\gamma_v : I \to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic such that: $\map {\gamma '} 0 = v$ where $v \in TM$. Then: $\forall t \in I : \forall v \in TM : \map {\gamma_v} t = \map \exp {t v}$

title: Relation between Normal Neighborhood Charts on Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold. Let $\tuple {x^i}$ and $\tuple {\tilde x^j}$ be normal neighborhood charts on $M$. Let $\map O {n, \R}$ be the orthogonal group. Let $A^j_i \in \map O {n, \R}$ be a constant matrix. Then: $\forall \tuple {x^i} : \forall \tuple {\tilde x^i} : \exists A^j_i \in \map O {n, \R} : \tilde x^j = A^j_i x^i$

title: Relation between P-Product Metric and Chebyshev Distance on Real Vector Space
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be a Euclidean space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Then $\forall x, y \in \R^n: \map {d_\infty} {x, y} \le \map {d_p} {x, y} \le n^{1/p} \map {d_\infty} {x, y}$

title: Relation between Product and Box Topology
snippet: == Product and Box Topology ==

title: Relation between Signed and Unsigned Stirling Numbers of the First Kind
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be positive integers. Then: $\ds {n \brack m} = \paren {-1}^{n + m} \map s {n, m}$ where: $\ds {n \brack m}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\map s {n, m}$ denotes a signed Stirling number of the first kind.

title: Relation between Square of Fibonacci Number and Square of Lucas Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $L_n$ denote the $n$th Lucas number. Then: $5 {F_n}^2 + 4 \paren {-1}^n = {L_n}^2$

title: Relation between Two Ordinals
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be ordinals. Then either $S \subseteq T$ or $T \subseteq S$.

title: Relation between Volume Forms of Conformally Related Metrics on Oriented Riemannian Manifold
snippet: Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be conformally related Riemannian metrics. That is, suppose: $g_2 = f g_1$ where $f \in \map {C^\infty} M$ is a positive smooth real function. Let $\rd V_{g_1}$ and $\rd V_{g_2}$ be Riemannian volume forms associated with $g_1$ and $g_2$. Then: $\ds \rd V_{g_2} = f^{\frac n 2} \rd V_{g_1}$

title: Relation both Symmetric and Asymmetric is Null
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation in $S$ which is both symmetric and asymmetric. Then: $\RR = \O$

title: Relation is Antireflexive iff Disjoint from Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR$ is antireflexive $\Delta_S \cap \RR = \O$ where $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

title: Relation is Antisymmetric and Reflexive iff Intersection with Inverse equals Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on a set $S$. Then $\RR$ is both antisymmetric and reflexive : $\RR \cap \RR^{-1} = \Delta_S$ where $\Delta_S$ denotes the diagonal relation.

title: Relation is Antisymmetric iff Intersection with Inverse is Coreflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then: $\RR$ is antisymmetric $\RR \cap \RR^{-1}$ is coreflexive where $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$. That is, : $\RR \cap \RR^{-1} \subseteq \Delta_S$

title: Relation is Connected and Reflexive iff Total
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then: $\RR$ is both a connected relation and a reflexive relation $\RR$ is a total relation.

title: Relation is Connected iff Union with Inverse and Diagonal is Trivial Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a connected relation : $\RR \cup \RR^{-1} \cup \Delta_S = S \times S$ where $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$ and $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

title: Relation is Equivalence iff Reflexive and Circular
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is reflexive and circular $\RR$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Relation is Reflexive Symmetric and Antisymmetric iff Diagonal Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is reflexive, symmetric and antisymmetric $\RR$ is the diagonal relation $\Delta_S$.

title: Relation is Reflexive and Coreflexive iff Diagonal
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is reflexive and coreflexive : $\RR = \Delta_S$ where $\Delta_S$ is the diagonal relation.

title: Relation is Set implies Domain and Image are Sets
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $\RR \subseteq V \times V$ be a relation. Let $\RR$ be a set. Then $\Dom \RR$ and $\Img \RR$ are also sets.

title: Relation is Symmetric and Antisymmetric iff Coreflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$. Then: $\RR$ is both symmetric and antisymmetric $\RR$ is coreflexive.

title: Relation is Symmetric iff Inverse is Symmetric
snippet: A relation $\RR$ is symmetric its inverse $\RR^{-1}$ is also symmetric.

title: Relation is Total iff Union with Inverse is Trivial Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a total relation : $\RR \cup \RR^{-1} = S \times S$ where: $\RR^{-1}$ is the inverse of $\RR$. $S \times S$ is the trivial relation on $S$.

title: Relation of Boubaker Polynomials to Chebyshev Polynomials
snippet: The Boubaker polynomials are related to Chebyshev polynomials through the equations: $\map {B_n} {2 x} = \dfrac {4 x} n \dfrac \d {\d x} \map {T_n} x - 2 \map {T_n} x$ $\map {B_n} {2 x} = -2 \map {T_n} x + 4 x \map {U_{n - 1} } x$ where: $T_n$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind $U_n$ denotes the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind.

title: Relation of Boubaker Polynomials to Dickson Polynomials
snippet: The Boubaker polynomials $B_n$ are linked to the Dickson polynomials by the relations: $\map {B_{n + 1} } x \map {B_{n + j} } x - \map {B_{n + j + 1} } x \map {B_n} x = \paren {3 x^2 + 4} \map {D_{n + 1} } {x, \dfrac 1 4}$ $\map {B_n} x = \map {D_n} {2 x, \dfrac 1 4} + 4 \map {D_{n - 1} } {2 x, \dfrac 1 4}$

title: Relation of Boubaker Polynomials to Fermat Polynomials
snippet: The Boubaker polynomials are related to Fermat polynomials by: $\forall n \in \N: \map {B_n} x = \dfrac 1 {\paren {\sqrt 2}^n} \map {F_n} {\dfrac {2 \sqrt 2 x} 3} + \dfrac 3 {\paren {\sqrt 2}^{n - 2} } \map {F_{n - 2} } {\dfrac {2 \sqrt 2 x} 3}$

title: Relation of Ratios to Products
snippet: That is: $a : b = c : d \iff ad = bc$

title: Relation on Empty Set is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S = \O$, that is, the empty set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is the null relation and is an equivalence relation.

title: Relation on Set of Cardinality 1 is Symmetric and Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is equal to $1$: $\card S = 1$ Let $\odot \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then $\odot$ is both symmetric and transitive.

title: Relation on Set of Cardinality 2 cannot be Non-Symmetric and Non-Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is equal to $2$: $\card S = 2$ Let $\odot \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Then it is not possible for $\odot$ to be not symmetric and also not transitive.

title: Relation on Slowly Progressing Mapping which fulfils conditions of General Double Induction Principle
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a slowly progressing mapping on $M$. Let $\map \RR {x, y}$ be the relation on $M$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in M: \tuple {x, y} \in \R \iff x \subseteq y \lor y \subseteq x$ Then $\RR$ satisfies the conditions of the General Double Induction Principle: $({\text D'}_1): \quad \map \RR {x, 0}$ and $\map \RR {0, x}$ hold for every $x \in M$ $({\text D'}_2): \quad \forall x, y \in M: \paren {\map \RR {x, y} \land \map \RR {x, \map g y} \land \map \RR {\map g x, y} } \implies \map \RR {\map g x, \map g y}$

title: Relation to Empty Set is Mapping iff Domain is Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set Let $S \times \O$ denote the cartesian product of $S$ with the empty set $\O$. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times \O$ be a relation in $S$ to $\O$. Then $\RR$ is a mapping $S = \O$.

title: Relational Closure Exists for Set-Like Relation
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\prec$ be a relation on $A$. Furthermore, let $\map {\prec^{-1} } a$ be a small class for each $a \in A$. Let $S$ be a small class that is a subset of the class $A$. Let $G$ be a mapping such that: $\map G x = A \cap \paren {\map {\prec^{-1} } x}$ Let $F$ be defined using the Principle of Recursive Definition: $\map F 0 = S$ $\map F {n^+} = \map F n \cup \map G {\map F n}$ Let $\ds T = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \omega} \map F n$.

title: Relational Closure from Transitive Closure
snippet: Let $A$ be a set or class. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $A$. Let $\RR^+$ be the transitive closure of $\RR$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Let $B' = B \cup \inv {\paren {\RR^+} } B$. Let $C$ be an $\RR$-transitive subset or subclass of $A$ such that $B \subseteq C$. Then: $B'$ is $\RR$-transitive $B' \subseteq C$ If $B$ is a set and $\RR$ is set-like then $B'$ is a set. That is, $B'$ is the relational closure of $B$ under $\RR$.

title: Relational Structure admits Lower Topology
snippet: Let $R = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a relational structure. Then there exists a relational structure with lower topology $T = \left({S, \preceq, \tau}\right)$ such that $T$ is a topological space.

title: Relational Structure with Topology of Subsets with Property (S) is Topological Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a relational structure with topology where $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is an up-complete ordered set $\tau$ is the set of all subsets of $S$ with property (S). Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is topological space.

title: Relations Compatible with Group Form Complete Boolean Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a group. Let $C$ be the set of relations on $S$ which are compatible with $\circ$. Then $\struct {C, \cap, \cup, \subseteq}$ is a complete Boolean lattice.

title: Relations Compatible with Operation Form Complete Distributive Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $C$ be the set of relations on $S$ compatible with $\circ$. Then $\struct {C, \cap, \cup, \subseteq}$ is a complete distributive lattice.

title: Relations of Finite Partition and Finite Sub-Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\eta, \gamma$ be finite partitions of $\Omega$. Let $\BB, \CC \subseteq \Sigma$ be finite sub-$\sigma$-algebras. Let: $\map \xi \cdot$ denote the generated finite partition $\map \sigma \cdot$ denote the generated $\sigma$-algebra $\le$ denote the order by refinement of partition. Then the following results hold:

title: Relations with Combinations of Reflexivity, Symmetry and Transitivity Properties
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which has at least $3$ elements. Then it is possible to set up a relation $\circledcirc$ on $S$ which has any combination of the $3$ properties: Reflexivity Symmetry Transitivity but this is not possible for a set which has fewer than $3$ elements.

title: Relationship between Chebyshev Polynomial of the First and Second Kind
snippet: Let $\map {T_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of order $n$. Let $\map {U_n} x$ denote the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind of order $n$. Then:

title: Relationship between Component Types
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $p \in S$. Let: $A$ be the arc component of $p$ $J$ be the injective path component of $p$ $P$ be the path component of $p$ $C$ be the component of $p$ $Q$ be the quasicomponent of $p$. Then: $A \subseteq P \subseteq C \subseteq Q$ In general, the inclusions do not hold in the other direction.

title: Relationship between Limit Inferior and Lower Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f: S \to \R \cup \set {-\infty, \infty}$ be an extended real-valued function. Let $\sequence {s_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence in $S$ such that $s_n \to \bar s$. Then the lower limit of $f$ at $\bar s$ is bounded above by the limit inferior of $\sequence {\map f {s_n} }$: $\ds \liminf_{s \mathop \to \bar s} \map f s \le \liminf_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f {s_n}$

title: Relationship between Limit Point Types
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let: $C$ be the set of condensation points of $A$ $W$ be the set of $\omega$-accumulation points of $A$ $L$ be the set of limit points of $A$ $D$ be the set of adherent points of $A$. Then: $C \subseteq W \subseteq L \subseteq D$ That is: Every condensation point is an $\omega$-accumulation point Every $\omega$-accumulation point is a limit point Every limit point is an adherent point. In general, the inclusions do not hold in the other direction.

title: Relationship between Transitive Closure Definitions
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Let $a$ be the smallest set such that $x \in a$ and $a$ is transitive. Let $b$ be the smallest set such that $x \subseteq b$ and $b$ is transitive. Then $a = b \cup \set x$.

title: Relative Algebraic Closure with Algebraically Closed Extension is Algebraic Closure
snippet: Let $L$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $L/K$ be a field extension. Then the relative algebraic closure of $K$ contained in $L$ is an algebraic closure of $K$.

title: Relative Complement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relative Complement ==

title: Relative Complement Mapping on Powerset is Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\complement_S: \powerset S \to \powerset S$ denote the relative complement mapping on the power set of $S$. Then $\complement_S$ is a bijection. Thus each $T \subseteq S$ is in one-to-one correspondence with its relative complement.

title: Relative Complement inverts Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A \subseteq S, B \subseteq S$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq B \iff \relcomp S B \subseteq \relcomp S A$ where $\complement_S$ denotes the complement relative to $S$.

title: Relative Complement inverts Subsets of Relative Complement
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A \subseteq S, B \subseteq S$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq \relcomp S B \iff B \subseteq \relcomp S A$ where $\complement_S$ denotes the complement relative to $S$.

title: Relative Complement of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $X \subseteq A$ and $Y \subseteq B$. Then: $\relcomp {A \mathop \times B} {X \times Y} = \paren {A \times \relcomp B Y} \cup \paren {\relcomp A X \times B}$

title: Relative Complement of Decreasing Sequence of Sets is Increasing
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a decreasing sequence of sets in $X$. Then $\sequence {X \setminus E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is an increasing sequence of sets in $X$.

title: Relative Complement of Empty Set
snippet: The relative complement of the empty set is the set itself: $\relcomp S \O = S$

title: Relative Complement of Relative Complement
snippet: The relative complement of the relative complement of a set is itself: $\relcomp S {\relcomp S T} = T$ Thus, considered as a mapping on the power set of $S$: $\complement_S: \powerset S \to \powerset S: \relcomp S T = S \setminus T$ $\complement_S$ is an involution.

title: Relative Complement with Self is Empty Set
snippet: The relative complement of a set in itself is the empty set: $\relcomp S S = \O$

snippet: == Examples of Relative Cumulative Frequency ==

title: Relative Difference between Infinite Set and Finite Set is Infinite
snippet: Let $S$ be an infinite set. Let $T$ be a finite set. Then $S \setminus T$ is an infinite set.

snippet: == Examples of Relative Efficiency ==

title: Relative Frequency is Probability Measure
snippet: The relative frequency model is a probability measure.

title: Relative Homotopy is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $K \subseteq X$ be a (possibly empty) subset of $X$. Let $\map \CC {X, Y}$ be the set of all continuous mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Define a relation $\sim$ on $\map \CC {X, Y}$ as: $f \sim g$ $f$ and $g$ are homotopic relative to $K$. Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Relative Lengths of Chords of Circles
snippet: Of chords in a circle, the diameter is the greatest, and of the rest the nearer to the center is always greater than the more remote.

title: Relative Lengths of Lines Inside Circle
Relative Lengths of Lines Outside Circle
Relative Likelihood of n Sixes on 6n Dice
snippet: == Problem == Which is more likely: to throw at least $1$ six with $6$ dice to throw at least $2$ sixes with $12$ dice to throw at least $3$ six with $18$ dice?

title: Relative Matrix of Composition of Linear Transformations
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $M, N, P$ be free $R$-modules of finite dimension $m, n, p > 0$ respectively. Let $\AA, \BB, \CC$ be ordered bases of $M, N, P$. Let $f: M \to N$ and $g : N \to P$ be linear transformations, and $g \circ f$ be their composition. Let $\mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$ and $\mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB}$ be their matrices relative to $\AA, \BB$ and $\BB, \CC$ respectively. Then the matrix of $g \circ f$ relative to $\AA$ and $\CC$ is: $\mathbf M_{g \mathop \circ f, \CC, \AA} = \mathbf M_{g, \CC, \BB} \cdot \mathbf M_{f, \BB, \AA}$

title: Relative Matrix of Linear Transformation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relative Matrices of Linear Transformations ==

title: Relative Prime Modulo Tensor is Zero
snippet: Let $p \in \Z_{>0}$ and $q \in \Z_{>0}$ be positive coprime integers. Let $\Z / p \Z$ and $\Z / q \Z$ be $\Z$-modules. Then: $\Z / p \Z \otimes_\Z \Z / q\Z = 0$ where $\otimes_\Z$ denotes tensor product over integers.

title: Relative Pseudocomplement Preserves Order
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a Brouwerian lattice. Let $a, b, c \in S$. Let $b \preceq c$. Then $a \to b \preceq a \to c$ where $x \to y$ denotes the relative pseudocomplement of $x$ with respect to $y$.

title: Relative Pseudocomplement and Shift Mapping form Galois Connection in Brouwerian Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a Brouwerian lattice. Let $a$ be an element of $S$. Let $g, d: S \to S$ be mappings such that: $\forall s \in S: \map g s = a \to s$ and $\forall s \in S: \map d s = a \wedge s$ Then $\struct {g, d}$ is a Galois connection.

title: Relative Sizes of Angles in Segments
snippet: In a circle: the angle in a semicircle is right the angle in a segment greater than a semicircle is acute the angle in a segment less than a semicircle is obtuse. Further: the angle of a segment greater than a semicircle is obtuse the angle of a segment less than a semicircle is acute.

title: Relative Sizes of Components of Ratios
snippet: That is, if $a : b = c : d$ then: $a > c \implies b > d$ $a = c \implies b = d$ $a < c \implies b < d$

title: Relative Sizes of Definite Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$, where $a < b$. If: $\forall t \in \closedint a b: \map f t \le \map g t$ then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t \le \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$ Similarly, if: $\forall t \in \closedint a b: \map f t < \map g t$ then: $\ds \int_a^b \map f t \rd t < \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$

title: Relative Sizes of Elements in Perturbed Proportion
snippet: That is, let: $a : b = e : f$ $b : c = d : e$ Then: $a > c \implies d > f$ $a = c \implies d = f$ $a < c \implies d < f$

title: Relative Sizes of Magnitudes on Unequal Ratios
snippet: That is: $a : c > b : c \implies a > b$ $c : b > c : a \implies b < a$

title: Relative Sizes of Platonic Solids in Same Sphere
Relative Sizes of Proportional Magnitudes
snippet: That is: $a : b = c : d, c : d > e : f \implies a : b > e : f$

title: Relative Sizes of Ratios on Unequal Magnitudes
snippet: That is: $a > b \implies a : c > b : c$ $a > b \implies c : a < c : b$

title: Relative Sizes of Sides of Acute Triangle
Relative Sizes of Sides of Obtuse Triangle
Relative Sizes of Successive Ratios
snippet: That is, let: $a : b = d : e$ $b : c = e : f$ Then: $a > c \implies d > f$ $a = c \implies d = f$ $a < c \implies d < f$

title: Relatively Compact Subspace/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Relatively Compact Subspaces ==

title: Relativisation is Standard Model
snippet: Let $P$ be a well-formed formula. Let $A$ be a finite set such that $x \in A$ $x$ is a free variable in $P$. Then: $A \subseteq B \implies \paren {B \models P \iff P^B}$

title: Relativized Eberlein-Šmulian Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. $(1): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is relatively compact in $\struct {X, w}$ $(2): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is sequentially compact in $\struct {X, w}$ $(3): \quad$ $\struct {A, w}$ is relatively countably compact in $\struct {X, w}$.

title: Reliability in terms of Lifetime Distribution Function
snippet: Let $D$ be a device whose reliability as a function of time is $\map {\mathrm R} t$. Then: $\map {\mathrm R} t = 1 - \map {\mathrm F} t$ where $\map {\mathrm F} t$ is the lifetime distribution function of $D$ $t$.

title: Remainder Theorem
snippet: Chinese Remainder Theorem Polynomial Remainder Theorem, also known as the Little Bézout Theorem. Category:Chinese Remainder Theorem Category:Little Bézout Theorem Category:Named Theorems

title: Remainder is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $\operatorname{rem}: \N^2 \to \N$ be defined as: $\map \rem {n, m} = \begin{cases} \text{the remainder when } n \text{ is divided by } m & : m \ne 0 \\ 0 & : m = 0 \end{cases}$ where the $\text{remainder}$ is as defined in the Division Theorem: If $n = m q + r$, where $0 \le r < m$, then $r$ is the remainder. Then there exists a $\Sigma_1$ WFF of $3$ free variables: $\map \phi {r, n, m}$ such that: $r = \map \rem {n, m} \iff \N \models \map \phi {\sqbrk r, \sqbrk n, \sqbrk m}$ where $\sqbrk a$ denotes the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Remainder is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N$ be natural numbers. Let us define the function $\rem: \N^2 \to \N$: $\map \rem {n, m} = \begin{cases} \text{the remainder when } n \text{ is divided by } m & : m \ne 0 \\ 0 & : m = 0 \end{cases}$ where the $\text{remainder}$ is as defined in the Division Theorem: If $n = m q + r$, where $0 \le r < m$, then $r$ is the remainder. Then $\rem$ is primitive recursive.

title: Remainder of Fibonacci Number Divided by Fibonacci Number is Plus or Minus Fibonacci Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ and $F_m$ be Fibonacci numbers. By the Division Theorem, let: $F_n = q F_m + r$ where: $q \in \Z$ $r \in \Z: 0 \le r < \size {F_m}$ Then either $r$ or $\size {F_m} - r$, or both, is a Fibonacci number.

title: Remainder on Division is Least Positive Residue
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $a \ge 0$ and $b \ne 0$. Let $r$ be the remainder resulting from the operation of integer division of $a$ by $b$: $a = q b + r, 0 \le r < \size b$ Then $r$ is equal to the least positive residue of $a \pmod b$.

title: Removable Singularity at Infinity implies Constant Function
snippet: Let $f : \C \to \C$ be an entire function. Let $f$ have an removable singularity at $\infty$. Then $f$ is constant.

title: Renaming Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Renaming Mappings ==

title: Renaming Mapping from Set of Mappings on Single Element
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $E$ be the set of all mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Let $b \in X$. Let $\RR \subseteq E \times E$ be the relation on $E$ defined as: $\RR := \set {\tuple {f, g} \in \RR: \map f b = \map g b}$ Let $e_b: E / \RR \to Y$ be the renaming mapping induced by $\RR$. Then $e_b$ is a bijection.

title: Renaming Mapping is Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f$ be the renaming mapping, defined as: $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f: \map r {\eqclass x {\RR_f} } = \map f x$ where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by the mapping $f$ $S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR_f$ $\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR_f$. The renaming mapping is a bijection.

title: Renaming Mapping is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f$ be the renaming mapping, defined as: $r: S / \RR_f \to \Img f: \map r {\eqclass x {\RR_f} } = \map f x$ where: $\RR_f$ is the equivalence induced by the mapping $f$ $S / \RR_f$ is the quotient set of $S$ determined by $\RR_f$ $\eqclass x {\RR_f}$ is the equivalence class of $x$ under $\RR_f$. The renaming mapping is always well-defined.

title: Reparameterization of Contour is Contour
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ and $\closedint c d$ be closed real intervals. Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \C$ be a contour in $\C$. That is, there exists a subdivision $a_0, a_1 , \ldots, a_n$ of $\closedint a b$ such that $\gamma \restriction_{I_i}$ is a smooth path for all $i \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$, where $I_i = \closedint {a_{i - 1} } {a_i}$. Here, $\gamma \restriction_{I_i}$ denotes the restriction of $\gamma$ to $I_i$. Let $\phi: \closedint c d \to \closedint a b$ be a differentiable real function with $\map \phi c = a$, and $\map \phi d = b$.

title: Reparameterization of Directed Smooth Curve Maps Endpoints To Endpoints
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be a real cartesian space of $n$ dimensions. Let $\closedint a b$ and $\closedint c d$ be closed real intervals. Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \R^n$ be a smooth path in $\R^n$. Let $C$ be a directed smooth curve with parameterization $\gamma$. Suppose that $\sigma: \closedint c d \to \R^n$ is a reparameterization of $C$. Then the start points and end points of $\gamma$ and $\sigma$ are identical: $\map \gamma a = \map \sigma c$ $\map \gamma b = \map \sigma d$

title: Reparameterization of Directed Smooth Curve Preserves Image
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ and $\closedint c d$ be closed real intervals. Let $\gamma : \closedint a b \to \C$ be a smooth path. Let $C$ be a directed smooth curve with parameterization $\gamma$. Suppose that $\sigma : \closedint c d \to \C$ is a reparameterization of $C$. Then $\Img \gamma = \Img \sigma$, where $\Img \gamma$ denotes the image of $\gamma$.

title: Reparameterization of Directed Smooth Curve with Given Domain
snippet: Let $\gamma: \closedint a b \to \C$ be a smooth path in the complex plane. Let $C$ be a directed smooth curve with parameterization $\gamma$. Let $\closedint { a_0 }{ b_0 }$ be a closed real interval, where $a_0 < b_0$. Then there exists a smooth path $\gamma_0 : \closedint { a_0 }{ b_0 } \to \C$ that is a reparameterization of $C$.

title: Repdigit Number consisting of Instances of 9 is Kaprekar
snippet: A repdigit number that consists entirely of the digit $9$ is a Kaprekar number.

title: Repdigit Triangular Numbers
snippet: The only repdigit numbers which are also triangular are: $55, 66, 666$

title: Repeated Composition of Injection is Injection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Let the sequence of mappings: $f^0, f^1, f^2, \ldots, f^n, \ldots$ be defined as: $\forall n \in \N: \map {f^n} x = \begin {cases} x & : n = 0 \\ \map f x & : n = 1 \\ \map f {\map {f^{n - 1} } x} & : n > 1 \end{cases}$ Then for all $n \in \N$, $f^n$ is an injection.

title: Repeated Fourier Transform of Even Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an even real function which is Lebesgue integrable. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map f t} = \map F s = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i s t} \map f t \rd t$ be the Fourier transform of $f$. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map F s} = \map g t = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i t s} \map F s \rd s$ be the Fourier transform of $F$. Then: $\map g t = \map f t$

title: Repeated Fourier Transform of Odd Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be an odd real function which is Lebesgue integrable. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map f t} = \map F s = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i s t} \map f t \rd t$ be the Fourier transform of $f$. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map F s} = \map g t = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i t s} \map F s \rd s$ be the Fourier transform of $F$. Then: $\map g t = -\map f t$

title: Repeated Fourier Transform of Real Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function which is Lebesgue integrable. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map f t} = \map F s = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i s t} \map f t \rd t$ be the Fourier transform of $f$. Let $\ds \map \FF {\map F s} = \map g t = \int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-2 \pi i t s} \map F s \rd s$ be the Fourier transform of $F$. Then: $\map g t = \map f {-t}$

title: Repeated Simpson's Rule/Also known as
snippet: == Repeated Simpson's Rule: Also known as == The repeated Simpson's rule is also known as just Simpson's rule. It is also known as the parabolic formula. It can also be seen as Simpson's formula, but this may be confused with Simpson's formulas, which are a set of completely different results.

title: Repeated Sum of Cubes of Digits of Multiple of 3
snippet: Let $k \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let $f: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall m \in \Z_{>0}: \map f m = $ the sum of the cubes of the digits of $n$. Let $n_0 \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer which is a multiple of $3$. Consider the sequence: $s_n = \begin{cases} n_0 & : n = 0 \\ \map f {s_{n - 1} } & : n > 0 \end{cases}$ Then: $\exists r \in \N_{>0}: s_r = 153$ That is, by performing $f$ repeatedly on a multiple of $3$ eventually results in the pluperfect digital invariant $153$.

title: Repellor/Examples

snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be a replicative function. Let $g: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\map g x = \map f {x - \floor x}$ Then $g$ is also a replicative function.

snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a finite group. Let $\rho: G \to \GL V$ be a linear representation of $G$ on $V$ of degree $1$. Then $\rho$ is an irreducible linear representation.

snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. $n$ can be represented uniquely in balanced ternary: $\ds n = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m r_j 3^j$ $\sqbrk {r_m r_{m - 1} \ldots r_2 r_1 r_0}$ such that: where: $m \in \Z_{>0}$ is a strictly positive integer such that $3^m < \size {2 n} < 3^{m + 1}$ all the $r_j$ are such that $r_j \in \set {\underline 1, 0, 1}$, where $\underline 1 := -1$.

title: Representation of Number Base in that Base
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b > 1$. Then $b$ is expressed in base $b$ as $10$.

title: Representation of Ternary Expansions
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $x$ be represented in base $3$ notation. While it may be possible for $x$ to have two different such representations, for example: $\dfrac 1 3 = 0.100000 \ldots_3 = 0.022222 \ldots_3$ it is not possible for $x$ be written in more than one way without using the digit $1$.

title: Representations for 1 in Golden Mean Number System
snippet: Then there are infinitely many ways to express the number $1$ in the golden mean number system.

title: Representative of P-adic Number is Representative of Equivalence Class
snippet: Let $p$ be any prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $x \in \Q_p$. Then for any sequence $\sequence{y_n}$ of the rational numbers $\Q$: $\sequence{y_n}$ is a representative of the $p$-adic number $x$ $\sequence{y_n}$ is a representative of the equivalence class $x$.

title: Representatives of same P-adic Number iff Difference is Null Sequence
snippet:
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rational numbers $\Q$. Let $\struct {\Q_p, 
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\sequence{\alpha_n}$ and $\sequence{ eta_n}$ be Cauchy sequences in $\struct {Q, 
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$. Then: $\sequence {\alpha_n}$ and $\sequence { eta_n}$ are representatives of the same $p$-adic number in $\Q_p$ the sequence $\sequence {\alpha_n -  eta_n}$ is a null sequence.

title: Repunit 19 is Unique Period Prime with Period 19
snippet: The repunit prime $R_{19}$ is a unique period prime whose reciprocal has a period of $19$: $\dfrac 1 {1 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111 \, 111} = 0 \cdotp \dot 00000 \, 00000 \, 00000 \, 000 \dot 9$

title: Repunit Expressed using Power of 10
snippet: The repunit number $R_n$ can be expressed as: $R_n = \dfrac {10^n - 1} 9$

title: Repunit Integer as Product of Base - 1 by Increasing Digit Integer
snippet: That is: $\ds 9 \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n \paren {n - j} 10^j + n + 1 = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n 10^j$

title: Repunit Prime/Sequence

title: Repunit cannot be Cube
snippet: A repunit (apart from the trivial $1$) cannot be a cube.

title: Repunit cannot be Square
snippet: A repunit (apart from the trivial $1$) cannot be a square.

title: Repunit in Base 9 is Triangular
snippet: Let $m$ be a repunit base $9$. Then $m$ is a triangular number.

title: Repunit is Zuckerman Number
snippet: Let $n$ be a repunit. Then $n$ is also a Zuckerman number.

snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be a connected domain. Then $D$ is simply connected all paths in $D$ with the same initial points and end points are path-homotopic. That is, given two paths in $D$: $\gamma: \closedint a b \to D$ $\sigma: \closedint c d \to D$ with $\map \gamma a = \map \sigma c$ and $\map \gamma b = \map \sigma d$, there exists a continuous function $H: \closedint 0 1 \times \closedint 0 1 \to D$ such that: $\map H {s, 0} = \map \gamma s$ for all $s \in \closedint 0 1$ $\map H {s, 1} = \map \sigma s$ for all $s \in \closedint 0 1$ $\map H {t, 0} = \map \gamma t$ for all $t \in…

title: Rescaling is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {V, +, \ast}_R$ be an $R$-module. Then for any $r \in R$, the rescaling operator: $m_r: V \to V, v \mapsto r \ast v$ is a linear transformation.

title: Residue (Number Theory)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Residues in context of Number Theory ==

title: Residue Class/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Residue Classes ==

title: Residue Classes form Partition of Integers
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of residue classes modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {\eqclass 0 m, \eqclass 1 m, \dotsc, \eqclass {m - 1} m}$ Then $\Z_m$ forms a partition of $\Z$.

title: Residue Field of P-adic Norm on Rationals
snippet: Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime $p$. The induced residue field on $\struct {\Q,\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ is isomorphic to the field $\F_p$ of integers modulo $p$.

title: Residue at Multiple Pole
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a function meromorphic on some region, $D$, containing $a$. Let $f$ have a single pole in $D$, of order $N$, at $a$. Then the residue of $f$ at $a$ is given by: $\ds \Res f a = \frac 1 {\paren {N - 1}!} \lim_{z \mathop \to a} \frac {\d^{N - 1} } {\d z^{N - 1} } \paren {\paren {z - a}^N \map f z}$

title: Residue at Simple Pole
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be a function meromorphic on some region, $D$, containing $a$. Let $f$ have a simple pole at $a$. Then the residue of $f$ at $a$ is given by: $\ds \Res f a = \lim_{z \mathop \to a} \paren {z - a} \map f z$

title: Residue of Fibonacci Number Modulo Fibonacci Number
snippet: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$th Fibonacci number. Let $m, r$ be non-negative integers. Then: $F_{m n + r} \equiv \paren {\begin{cases} F_r & : m \bmod 4 = 0 \\ \paren {-1}^{r + 1} F_{n - r} & : m \bmod 4 = 1 \\ \paren {-1}^n F_r & : m \bmod 4 = 2 \\ \paren {-1}^{r + 1 + n} F_{n - r} & : m \bmod 4 = 3 \end{cases} } \pmod {F_n}$

title: Residue of Gamma Function
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be the Definition:Gamma Function. Let $n$ be a non-negative integer. Then: $\Res \Gamma {-n} = \dfrac {\paren {-1}^n} {n!}$

title: Residue of Quotient
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be functions holomorphic on some region containing $a$. Let $g$ have a zero of multiplicity $1$ at $a$. Then: $\Res {\dfrac f g} a = \dfrac {\map f a} {\map {g'} a}$

title: Resolvent Mapping Converges to 0 at Infinity
snippet: Let $B$ be a Banach space. Let $\map \LL {B, B}$ be the set of bounded linear operators from $B$ to itself. Let $T \in \map \LL {B, B}$. Let $\map \rho T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ in the complex plane. Then the resolvent mapping $f : \map \rho T \to \map \LL {B, B}$ given by $\map f z = \paren {T - z I}^{-1}$ is such that $\ds \lim_{z \mathop \to \infty} \norm {\map f z}_* = 0$.

title: Resolvent Set of Bounded Linear Operator equal to Resolvent Set as Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\rho_1} T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ as a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\rho_2} T$ be the resolvent set of $T$ as a densely-defined linear operator $\struct {\HH, T}$. Then: $\map {\rho_1} T = \map {\rho_2} T$

title: Resolvent Set of Bounded Linear Operator is Open
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map \rho T$ be the resolvent set of $T$. Then $\map \rho T$ is open.

title: Resolvent Set of Element in Banach Algebra has same Unique Unbounded Component as Resolvent Set of Element in Closed Subalgebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ both have unique unbounded component, and further these components coincide.

title: Resolvent Set of Element in Closed Unital Subalgebra of Banach Algebra is Clopen in Resolvent Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then $\map {\rho_B} x$ is clopen in $\map {\rho_A} x$.

title: Resolvent Set of Element in Subalgebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a Banach algebra. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then: $\map {\rho_B} x \subseteq \map {\rho_A} x$

title: Resolvent Set of Element of Banach Algebra is Open
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ be the resolvent set of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\rho_A} x$ is open.

title: Resonance Frequency is less than Natural Frequency
snippet: Consider a physical system $S$ whose behaviour is defined by the second order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + a^2 x = K \cos \omega x$ where: $K \in \R: k > 0$ $a, b \in \R_{>0}: b < a$ Then the resonance frequency of $S$ is smaller than the natural frequency of the associated second order ODE: $(2): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + 2 b \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + a^2 x = 0$

title: Restricted Dipper Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } \setminus \set 0$: $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {1, 2, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The restricted dipper operation $+^*_{m, n}$ on $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is associative.

title: Restricted Dipper Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } \setminus \set 0$: $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {1, 2, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ The restricted dipper operation $+^*_{m, n}$ on $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ is commutative.

title: Restricted Dipper Relation is Congruence for Addition
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\RR^*_{m, n}$ be the restricted dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N_{>0}: x \mathrel {\RR^*_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR^*_{m, n}$ is a congruence relation for addition.

title: Restricted Dipper Relation is Congruence for Multiplication
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\RR^*_{m, n}$ be the restricted dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N_{>0}: x \mathrel {\RR^*_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR^*_{m, n}$ is a congruence relation for multiplication.

title: Restricted Dipper Relation is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\RR^*_{m, n}$ be the restricted dipper relation on $\N$: $\forall x, y \in \N_{>0}: x \mathrel {\RR^*_{m, n} } y \iff \begin {cases} x = y \\ m \le x < y \text { and } n \divides \paren {y - x} \\ m \le y < x \text { and } n \divides \paren {x - y} \end {cases}$ Then $\RR^*_{m, n}$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Restricted Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\Sigma'$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Then the restricted measure $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma'}$ is a measure on the measurable space $\struct {X, \Sigma'}$.

title: Restricted P-adic Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $p \in \N$ be a prime. Let $d^\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic metric on $\Z$: $\forall x, y \in \Z: \map {d^\Z_p} {x, y} = \norm {x - y}_p$ where $\norm {x - y}_p$ denotes the $p$-adic norm. Then $d^\Z_p$ is a metric.

title: Restricted P-adic Valuation is Valuation
snippet: Let $\nu_p^\Z: \Z \to \Z \cup \set {+\infty}$ be the $p$-adic valuation restricted to the integers. Then $\nu_p^\Z$ is a valuation.

title: Restricting Measure Preserves Finiteness
snippet: Let $\left({X, \Sigma, \mu}\right)$ be a measure space. Let $\mu$ be a finite measure. Let $\Sigma'$ be a sub-$\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma$. Then the restricted measure $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma'}$ is also a finite measure.

title: Restriction/Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Restrictions of Mappings ==

title: Restriction is Subset of Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $X \subseteq S$. Then the restriction of $\RR$ to $X$ is a subset of $\RR$.

title: Restriction of Antireflexive Relation is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antireflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antireflexive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Antisymmetric Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antisymmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antisymmetric relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Antitransitive Relation is Antitransitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an antitransitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an antitransitive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Associative Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\circ_T$ denote the restriction of $\circ$ to $T$. Let the operation $\circ$ be associative on $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\circ_T$ is associative on $\struct {T, \circ_T}$.

title: Restriction of Asymmetric Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a asymmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a asymmetric relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Canonical Surjection to Restricted Dipper Semigroup is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{0}$ to the restricted dipper semigroup $\struct {\map {D^*} {m, n}, \oplus^*_{m, n} }$. Then $\phi^*_{m, n}$ is an isomorphism from $\struct {\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }, +^*_{m, n} }$ to $\struct {\map {D^*} {m, n}, \oplus^*_{m, n} }$.

title: Restriction of Commutative Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let the operation $\circ$ be commutative on $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the restriction $\circ {\restriction_T}$ of $\circ$ to $T$ is also commutative.

title: Restriction of Composition is Composition of Restriction
snippet: Let $X, Y, Z$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ and $g: Y \to Z$ be mappings. Let $S \subseteq X$. Then: $\paren {g \circ f} \restriction S = g \circ \paren {f \restriction S}$

title: Restriction of Congruence Relation is Congruence
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\RR$ be a congruence relation for $\circ$ on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a congruence relation for $\circ_T$ on $T$.

title: Restriction of Connected Relation is Connected
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a connected relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a connected relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Continuous Mapping is Continuous
Restriction of Dipper Operation to Non-Zero Initial Segment is Closed
snippet: Let $m, n \in \N_{>0}$ be non-zero natural numbers. Let $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the initial segment of the natural numbers: $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} } := \set {0, 1, \ldots, m + n - 1}$ Let $+_{m, n}$ denote the dipper operation on $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$: $\forall a, b \in \N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }: a +_{m, n} b = \begin{cases} a + b & : a + b < m \\ a + b - k n & : a + b \ge m \end{cases}$ where $k$ is the largest integer satisfying: $m + k n \le a + b$ Let $\N^*_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }$ denote the set defined as $\N_{< \paren {m \mathop + n} }…

title: Restriction of Equivalence Relation is Equivalence
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is an equivalence relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Homeomorphism is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$, $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a homeomorphism between $T_1$ and $T_2$. Let $S$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $f {\restriction_{S \times f \sqbrk S} } : S \to f \sqbrk S$ be the restriction of $f$ to $S \times f \sqbrk S$. Let $S$ and $f \sqbrk S$ bear their respective subspace topologies. Then $f {\restriction_{S \times f \sqbrk S} }$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Restriction of Homomorphism is Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, \odot}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a homomorphism. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then the restriction of $\phi$ to $A \times \Img A$ is also a homomorphism.

title: Restriction of Homomorphism to Image is Epimorphism
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a homomorphism. Then a surjective restriction of $\phi$ can be produced by limiting the codomain of $\phi$ to its image $\Img \phi$.

title: Restriction of Idempotent Operation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let the operation $\circ$ be idempotent. Then $\circ$ is also idempotent upon restriction to $\struct {T, \circ \restriction_T}$.

title: Restriction of Identity Mapping is Identity Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $A$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $I_S \restriction_{A \times A} = I_A$ where: $I_S$ denotes the identity mapping on $S$ $I_S \restriction_{A \times A}$ denotes the restriction of $I_S$ to $A \times A$ $I_A$ denotes the identity mapping on $A$

title: Restriction of Injection is Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $X \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $f \sqbrk X$ denote the image of $X$ under $f$. Let $Y \subseteq T$ be a subset of $T$ such that $f \sqbrk X \subseteq Y$. The restriction $f \restriction_{X \times Y}$ of $f$ to $X \times Y$ is an injection from $X$ to $Y$.

title: Restriction of Inverse is Inverse of Restriction
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a bijection. Let $S \subseteq S_1$ be a subset of $S_1$. Let $f \sqbrk S$ be the image of $S$ under $f$. Let $f^{-1}$ be the inverse of $f$. Let $f {\restriction_{S \mathop \times f \sqbrk S}}$ be the restriction of $f$ to $S \times f \sqbrk S$. Let $f^{-1} {\restriction_{f \sqbrk S \mathop \times S}}$ be the restriction of $f^{-1}$ to $f \sqbrk S \times S$.

title: Restriction of Mapping is Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $X \subseteq S$. Let $f \restriction_X$ be the restriction of $f$ to $X$. Then $f \restriction_X: X \to T$ is a mapping: whose domain is $X$ whose preimage is $X$.

title: Restriction of Mapping is Subclass of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe Let $f: V \to V$ be a mapping. Let $A$ be a class. Let $f \sqbrk A$ denote the image of $A$ under $f$. Let $f {\restriction} A$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $A$. Then $f {\restriction} A$ is a subclass of the cartesian product of $A$ with its image: $f {\restriction} A \subseteq A \times f \sqbrk A$

title: Restriction of Mapping is its Intersection with Cartesian Product of Subset with Image
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $X \subseteq S$. Let $f {\restriction_X}$ be the restriction of $f$ to $X$. Then: $f {\restriction_X} = f \cap \paren {X \times \Img f}$ where: $\Img f$ denotes the image of $f$, defined as: $\Img f = \set {t \in T: \exists s \in S: t = \map f s}$ $X \times \Img f$ denotes the cartesian product of $X$ with $\Img f$.

title: Restriction of Mapping to Image is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $g: S \to \Img f$ be the restriction of $f$ to $S \times \Img f$. Then $g$ is a surjective restriction of $f$.

title: Restriction of Mapping to Small Class is Small
snippet: Let $F$ be a mapping. Let $A$ be a small class. Then the restriction $F {\restriction_A}$ is a small class.

title: Restriction of Measurable Function is Measurable on Trace Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Let $E \in \Sigma$. Let $\Sigma_E$ be the trace $\sigma$-algebra of $E$ in $\Sigma$. Then the restriction $f \restriction_E$ is $\Sigma_E$-measurable.

title: Restriction of Measure to Trace Sigma-Algebra of Measurable Set is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $A \in \Sigma$. Let $\Sigma_A$ be the trace $\sigma$-algebra of $A$ in $\Sigma$. Let $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A}$ be the restriction of $\mu$ to $\Sigma_A$. Then $\mu \restriction_{\Sigma_A}$ is a measure on $\struct {A, \Sigma_A}$.

title: Restriction of Monotone Function is Monotone
snippet: The restriction of a monotone mapping is monotone.

title: Restriction of Non-Connected Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Connected
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-connected relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-connected relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Non-Continuous Mapping on Metric Space to Subspace may be Continuous
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be a metric spaces. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a mapping. Let $Y \subseteq A_1$. Let $f {\restriction_Y}: Y \to A_2$ be the restriction of $f$ to $Y$. Let $f {\restriction_Y}$ be $\tuple {d_Y, d_2}$-continuous. Then it is not necessarily the case that $f$ is also $\tuple {d_1, d_2}$-continuous.

title: Restriction of Non-Reflexive Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Reflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-reflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-reflexive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Non-Symmetric Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Symmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-symmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \ \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-symmetric relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Non-Transitive Relation is Not Necessarily Non-Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a non-transitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a non-transitive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Norm on Vector Space to Subspace is Norm
snippet:
Let $\Bbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $
orm \cdot_X : X 	o \hointr 0 \infty$ be a norm on $X$. Let $Y$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $

orm \cdot_Y$ is a norm on $Y$.

title: Restriction of Operation Distributivity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, *, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $T \subseteq S$. If the operation $\circ$ is distributive over $*$ in $\struct {S, *, \circ}$, then it is also distributive over $*$ on a restriction $\struct {T, * \restriction_T, \circ \restriction_T}$.

title: Restriction of Ordering is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\preceq$ be an ordering on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq \restriction_T$ is an ordering on $T$.

title: Restriction of Real Square Mapping to Positive Reals is Bijection
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real square function: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x^2$ Let $g: \R_{\ge 0} \to R_{\ge 0} := f {\restriction_{\R_{\ge 0} \times R_{\ge 0} } }$ be the restriction of $f$ to the positive real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$. Then $g$ is a bijective restriction of $f$.

title: Restriction of Reflexive Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a reflexive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a reflexive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Restriction is Restriction
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $X \subseteq S$, $Y \subseteq T$. Let $W \subseteq X$, $V \subseteq Y$. Then: $\paren{\RR {\restriction_{X \times Y} } } {\restriction_{W \times V} } = \RR {\restriction_{W \times V} }$ That is, the restriction of $\RR {\restriction_{X \times Y} }$ to $W \times V$ is the restriction of $\RR$ to $W \times V$

title: Restriction of Ringed Space to Open Set is Ringed Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ be a ringed space. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset of $X$. Let $\struct {U, \OO_X {\restriction_U}}$ denote the restriction of $\struct {X, \OO_X}$ to $U$. Then $\struct {U, \OO_X {\restriction_U}}$ is a ringed space.

title: Restriction of Serial Relation is Not Necessarily Serial
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a serial relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is not necessarily a serial relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Sheaf to Open Set is Sheaf
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a sheaf of sets on $X$. Let $U \subset X$ be an open subset. Then the restriction $\FF {\restriction_U}$ of $\FF$ to $U$ is a sheaf.

title: Restriction of Strict Total Ordering is Strict Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a strict total ordering. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\prec \restriction_T$ be the restriction of $\prec$ to $T$. Then $\prec \restriction_T$ is a strict total ordering of $T$.

title: Restriction of Strict Well-Ordering is Strict Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $R$ be a strict well-ordering of $A$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Then $R$ is a strict well-ordering of $B$.

title: Restriction of Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Strictly Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a strictly well-founded relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Symmetric Relation is Symmetric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a symmetric relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a symmetric relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Total Ordering is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a total ordering. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq \restriction_T$ is a total ordering of $T$.

title: Restriction of Transitive Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a transitive relation on $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\RR {\restriction_T} \subseteq T \times T$ be the restriction of $\RR$ to $T$. Then $\RR {\restriction_T}$ is a transitive relation on $T$.

title: Restriction of Union of Mappings which Agree Equals Mapping
snippet: Let $Y$ be a set. Let $\family {A_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of sets indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: A_i \to Y}$ be a family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $X = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} A_i$. Let $f = \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} f_i : X \to Y$ where $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} f_i$ is the union of relations. Let for all $i, j \in I$, $f_i$ and $f_j$ agree on $A_i \cap A_j$. Let $f \restriction_{A_i} : A_i \to Y$ denote the restriction of $f$ to $A_i$. Then: $\forall i \in I: f \restriction_{A_i} = f_i: A_i \to Y$.

title: Restriction of Well-Founded Ordering is Well-Founded

title: Restriction of Well-Founded Relation is Well-Founded

title: Restriction of Well-Ordering is Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set or class. Let $\preceq$ be a well-ordering of $S$. Let $T$ be a subset or subclass of $S$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $\preceq'$ is a well-ordering of $T$.

title: Restriction to Subset of Strict Total Ordering is Strict Total Ordering

title: Reversed Contour Reverses Orientation
snippet: Let $C$ be a contour in the complex plane $\C$. Let $D \subseteq \C$ be a connected domain. Let $\Img C \subseteq \partial D$, where $\Img C$ denotes the image of $C$, and $\partial D$ denotes the boundary of $D$. Let $-C$ be the reversed contour of $C$. If $C$ is positively oriented $D$, then $-C$ is negatively oriented $D$. If $C$ is negatively oriented $D$, then $-C$ is positively oriented $D$.

title: Reversed Directed Smooth Curve is Directed Smooth Curve

Then $\rho$ is a smooth path which parameterizes a directed smooth curve $-C$. The directed smooth curve $-C$ is independent of the parameterization $\gamma$.

title: Riemann-Hurwitz Formula
snippet: Now assume that $S$ and $S'$ are Riemann surfaces, and that the map $\pi$ is complex analytic. The map $\pi$ is said to be ramified at a point $P$ in $S'$ if there exist analytic coordinates near $P$ and $π(P)$ such that $π$ takes the form $π(z) = z^n$, and $n>1$. An equivalent way of thinking about this is that there exists a small neighborhood $U$ of $P$ such that $π(P)$ has exactly one preimage in $U$, but the image of any other point in $U$ has exactly $n$ preimages in $U$. The number $n$ is called the ramification index at $P$ and is denoted by $e_P$.
