snippet: For $n \in \Z_{> 0}$, the Riemann zeta function is given by: $\ds \map \zeta n = \int_{\closedint 0 1^n} \frac 1 {1 - \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n x_i} \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \rd x_i$ where $\closedint 0 1^n$ denotes the Cartesian $n$th power of the closed real interval $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Riemann Zeta Function at Even Integers
snippet: The Riemann $\zeta$ function can be calculated for even integers as follows: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta {2 n} | r = \paren {-1}^{n + 1} \dfrac {B_{2 n} 2^{2 n - 1} \pi^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 {1^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {2^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {3^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {4^{2 n} } + \cdots | c = }} where: $B_n$ are the Bernoulli numbers $n$ is a positive integer.

title: Riemann Zeta Function at Non-Positive Integers
snippet: Let $n \ge 0$ be a integer. Then: $\map \zeta {-n} = \paren {-1}^n \dfrac {B_{n + 1} } {n + 1}$ where: $B_n$ is the $n$th Bernoulli number $\zeta$ is the Riemann Zeta function

title: Riemann Zeta Function at Odd Integers
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == The value of the Riemann $\zeta$ function for odd integers has not been determined. For certain values it has been calculated to whatever number of places, but an exact expression has never been found.

title: Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Dirichlet Eta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $\eta$ be the Dirichlet eta function. Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\sigma > 1$. Then: $\map \zeta s = \dfrac 1 {1 - 2^{1 - s} } \map \eta s$

title: Riemann Zeta Function of 1000
snippet: To at least $100$ decimal places: $\map \zeta {1000} \approx 1$ where $\zeta$ denotes the Riemann zeta function.

title: Riemann Zeta Function of 4
snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $4$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 4 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^4} + \dfrac 1 {2^4} + \dfrac 1 {3^4} + \dfrac 1 {4^4} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^4} {90} | c = }}

title: Riemann Zeta Function of 6
snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $6$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 6 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^6} + \dfrac 1 {2^6} + \dfrac 1 {3^6} + \dfrac 1 {4^6} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^6} {945} | c = }}

title: Riemann Zeta Function of 8
snippet: The Riemann zeta function of $8$ is given by: {{eqn | l = \map \zeta 8 | r = \dfrac 1 {1^8} + \dfrac 1 {2^8} + \dfrac 1 {3^8} + \dfrac 1 {4^8} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^8} {9450} | c = }}

title: Riemann Zeta Has No Zeroes With Real Part One
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Then for all $t \in \R$: $\map \zeta {1 + i t} \ne 0$

title: Riemannian Geodesic is Locally Minimizing
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic. Then $\gamma$ is locally minimizing.

title: Riemannian Manifold as Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a connected Riemannian manifold with or without boundary. Let $d_g$ be the Riemannian distance. Then $\struct {M, d_g}$ is a metric space whose metric topology is the same as the given manifold topology.

title: Riemannian Manifold has Zero Gaussian Curvature iff Euclidean
snippet: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $2$. The Gaussian curvature on $M$ is zero the Riemannian metric on $M$ is the same as the Euclidean metric.

title: Riemannian Metric gives rise to Connection
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold. Let $g$ be a Riemannian metric on $M$. Then $g$ gives rise to a connection. It is not necessarily the case that a connection gives rise to a Riemannian metric.

title: Riemannian Volume Form of Orientable Hypersurface
snippet: Let $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold. Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an orientable hypersurface with an induced metric. Let $N$ be a unit global normal vector for $M$. Let $\rd V_g$ be the Riemannian volume form. Then Riemannian volume form is given by: $\rd V_g = \valueat {\paren {N \lrcorner \rd V_{\tilde g} } } M$ where $\lrcorner$ denotes the interior multiplicaiton.

title: Riemannian Volume Form under Orientation-Preserving Isometry
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ and $\struct {\tilde M, \tilde g}$ be oriented Riemannian manifolds. Let $\phi : M \to \tilde M$ be an orientation-preserving isometry. Let $\rd V_g$ be the Riemannian volume form. Then: $\phi^* \rd V_{\tilde g} = \rd V_g$

title: Riesel Problem
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == What is the smallest Riesel number?

title: Riesz's Convergence Theorem
Riesz's Lemma
snippet: Let $X$ be a normed vector space. Let $Y$ be a proper closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $\alpha \in \openint 0 1$. Then there exists $x_\alpha \in X$ such that: $\norm {x_\alpha} = 1$ with: $\norm {x_\alpha - y} > \alpha$ for all $y \in Y$.

title: Riesz-Fischer Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p \in \R$, $p \ge 1$. The Lebesgue $p$-space $\map {\LL^p} \mu$, endowed with the $p$-norm $\norm {\cdot}_p$, is a Banach space.

title: Riesz-Kakutani Representation Theorem
snippet:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff compact space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra on $X$. Let $\map C {X, \R}$ be the space of real-valued continuous functions. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $X$. Let $\struct {C', 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{C'} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {\map C {X, \R}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

title: Riesz-Markov-Kakutani Representation Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map {C_c} X$ be the space of continuous complex functions with compact support on $X$. Let $\Lambda$ be a positive linear functional on $\map {C_c} X$. There exists a $\sigma$-algebra $\MM$ over $X$ which contains the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\struct {X, \tau}$. There exists a unique complete Radon measure $\mu$ on $\MM$ such that: $\ds \forall f \in \map {C_c} X: \Lambda f = \int_X f \rd \mu$

title: Riesz Representation Theorem (Hilbert Spaces)
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $L$ be a bounded linear functional on $H$. Then there is a unique $h_0 \in H$ such that: $\forall h \in H: L h = \innerprod h {h_0}$

title: Right-Hand Derivative not Limit of Derivative from Right
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let the right-hand derivative $f'_+$ of $f$ exist. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\map {f'_+} a$ is the same thing as: $\map {f'} {a^+}$

title: Right-Hand Differentiable Function is Right-Continuous
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function defined on an interval $I$. Let $a$ be a point in $I$ where $f$ is right-hand differentiable. Then $f$ is right-continuous at $a$.

title: Right-Limits of Filtration of Sigma-Algebra form Filtration
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\family {\FF_t}_{t \mathop \ge 0}$ be a continuous-time filtration of $\Sigma$. For each $t \in \hointr 0 \infty$, let $\FF_{t^+}$ be the right-limit of $\family {\FF_t}_{t \mathop \ge 0}$ at $t$. Then $\family {\FF_{t^+} }_{t \ge 0}$ is a filtration of $\Sigma$.

title: Right-Truncatable Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Right-Truncatable Primes ==

title: Right-Truncatable Prime/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of right-truncatable primes begins: $2, 3, 5, 7, 23, 29, 31, 37, 53, 59, 71, 73, 79, 233, 239, 293, 311, 313, 317, 373, 379, \ldots$ Category:Right-Truncatable Primes

title: Right Adjoint Functor is Unique up to Natural Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $\tuple {F, G, \alpha}$ be an adjunction between $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$. Then: the right adjoint functor $G$ of $F$ is unique up to isomorphism in the functor category $\operatorname{Funct} \tuple{C, D}$. That is: right adjoint functor $G$ is unique up to natural isomorphism.

title: Right Angle to Tangent of Circle goes through Center
Right Cancellable Commutative Operation is Left Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be right cancellable and also commutative. Then $\circ$ is also left cancellable.

title: Right Cancellable Element is Right Cancellable in Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$. Let $x \in T$ be right cancellable in $S$. Then $x$ is also right cancellable in $T$.

title: Right Cancellable Elements of Semigroup form Subsemigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $C_\rho$ be the set of right cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\struct {C_\rho, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Right Cancellable iff Right Regular Representation Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then $a \in S$ is right cancellable the right regular representation $\map {\rho_a} x$ is injective.

title: Right Circular Cone has Axis of Symmetry
snippet: Let $C$ be a right circular cone. Let $A$ be the axis of $C$. Then $A$ is an axis of symmetry for $C$.

title: Right Congruence Class Modulo Subgroup is Right Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $\RR^r_H$ be the equivalence defined as right congruence modulo $H$. The equivalence class $\eqclass g {\RR^r_H}$ of an element $g \in G$ is the right coset $H g$. This is known as the right congruence class of $g \bmod H$.

title: Right Congruence Modulo Subgroup is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x \equiv^r y \pmod H$ denote the relation that $x$ is right congruent modulo $H$ to $y$ Then the relation $\equiv^r$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Right Coset Equals Subgroup iff Element in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x \in G$. Let $H x$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $H x = H \iff x \in H$

title: Right Coset Space forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. The right coset space of $H$ forms a partition of its group $G$: {{eqn | l = \neg \paren {x \equiv^r y} \pmod H | o = \iff | r = H x \cap H y = \O }}

title: Right Coset by Identity
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $H = H e$ where $H e$ is the right coset of $H$ by $e$.

title: Right Cosets are Equal iff Element in Other Right Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $H x$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $H x = H y \iff x \in H y$

title: Right Cosets are Equal iff Left Cosets by Inverse are Equal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $g_1, g_2 \in G$. Then: $H g_1 = H g_2 \iff {g_1}^{-1} H = {g_2}^{-1} H$ where: ${g_1}^{-1}$ and ${g_2}^{-1}$ denote the inverses of $g_1$ and $g_2$ in $G$ $H g_1$ and $H g_2$ denote the right cosets of $H$ by $g_1$ and $g_2$ respectively ${g_1}^{-1} H$ and ${g_2}^{-1} H$ denote the left cosets of $H$ by ${g_1}^{-1}$ and ${g_2}^{-1}$ respectively.

title: Right Cosets are Equal iff Product with Inverse in Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $H x$ denote the right coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $H x = H y \iff x y^{-1} \in H$

title: Right Distributive Law for Natural Numbers
snippet: The operation of multiplication is right distributive over addition on the set of natural numbers $\N_{> 0}$: $\forall x, y, n \in \N_{> 0}: \paren {x + y} \times n = \paren {x \times n} + \paren {y \times n}$

title: Right Ideal is Right Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $J \subseteq R$ be a right ideal of $R$. Let $\circ : J \times R \to J$ be the restriction of $\times$ to $J \times R$. Then $\struct {J, +, \circ}$ is a right module over $\struct {R, +, \times}$.

title: Right Identity Element is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $e_R \in S$ be a right identity with respect to $\circ$. Then $e_R$ is idempotent under $\circ$.

title: Right Identity in Semigroup may not be Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $e_R$ be a right identity of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $e_R$ is unique.

title: Right Identity while exists Right Inverse for All is Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup with a right identity $e_R$ such that: $\forall x \in S: \exists x_R: x \circ x_R = e_R$ That is, every element of $S$ has a right inverse with respect to the right identity. Then $e_R$ is also a left identity, that is, is an identity.

title: Right Inverse Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Right Inverse Mappings ==

title: Right Inverse Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $g: T \to S$ be a right inverse of $f$. Then $g$ is an injection.

title: Right Inverse for All is Left Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup with a right identity $e_R$ such that: $\forall x \in S: \exists x_R: x \circ x_R = e_R$ That is, every element of $S$ has a right inverse with respect to the right identity. Then $x_R \circ x = e_R$, that is, $x_R$ is also a left inverse with respect to the right identity.

title: Right Limit Function is Right-Continuous
snippet: Let $I$ be an open interval. Let $f : I \to \R$ be a real function such that: for each $x \in I$, the right limit: $\ds \lim_{y \mathop \to x^+} \map f y$ exists. Define $f_\leftarrow : I \to \R$ by: $\ds \map {f_\leftarrow} x = \lim_{y \mathop \to x^+} \map f y$ for each $x \in I$. Then $f_\leftarrow$ is right-continuous. Further, if $f$ is right-continuous at $x$, then $\map {f_\leftarrow} x = \map f x$.

title: Right Module Does Not Necessarily Induce Left Module over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ' x = x \circ \lambda$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ'}$ is not necessarily a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$

title: Right Module induces Left Module over same Ring iff Actions are Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ' x = x \circ \lambda $ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ : $\forall \lambda, \mu \in R: \forall x \in G: x \circ \paren{ \lambda \times_R \mu} = x \circ \paren {\mu \times_R \lambda}$

title: Right Module over Commutative Ring induces Bimodule
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ' x = x \circ \lambda $ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ', \circ}$ is a bimodule over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$.

title: Right Module over Commutative Ring induces Left Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ’ x = x \circ \lambda$ Then $\struct{G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$.

title: Right Module over Ring Induces Left Module over Opposite Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R, +_R, *_R}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\struct{G, +_G, \circ}$ be a right module over $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$. Let $\circ' : R \times G \to G$ be the binary operation defined by: $\forall \lambda \in R: \forall x \in G: \lambda \circ' x = x \circ \lambda$ Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ'}$ is a left module over $\struct {R, +_R, *_R}$.

title: Right Operation has no Right Identities
snippet: Let $S$ be a set with more than $1$ element. Let $\struct {S, \to}$ be an algebraic structure in which the operation $\to$ is the right operation. Then $\struct {S, \to}$ has no right identities.

title: Right Operation is Anticommutative
snippet: The right operation is anticommutative: $\forall x, y: x \rightarrow y = y \rightarrow x \iff x = y$

title: Right Operation is Associative
snippet: The right operation is associative: $\forall x, y, z: \paren {x \to y} \to z = x \to \paren {y \to z}$

title: Right Operation is Closed for All Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\rightarrow$ be the right operation on $S$. That is: $\forall x, y \in S: x \rightarrow y = y$ Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Then for all $T \in \powerset S$, $\rightarrow$ is closed on $T$. Thus, for all $T \in \powerset S$: $\struct {T, \rightarrow}$ is a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \rightarrow}$.

title: Right Operation is Distributive over Idempotent Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \rightarrow}$ be an algebraic structure where: $\rightarrow$ is the right operation $\circ$ is any arbitrary binary operation. Then: $\rightarrow$ is distributive over $\circ$ $\circ$ is idempotent.

title: Right Operation is Entropic
snippet: The right operation is entropic: $\forall a, b, c, d: \paren {a \to b} \to \paren {c \to d} = \paren {a \to c} \to \paren {b \to d}$

title: Right Operation is Idempotent
snippet: The right operation is idempotent: $\forall x: x \rightarrow x = x$

title: Right Operation is Left Distributive over All Operations
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \rightarrow}$ be an algebraic structure where: $\rightarrow$ is the right operation $\circ$ is any arbitrary binary operation. Then $\rightarrow$ is left distributive over $\circ$.

title: Right Operation is not Commutative
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\rightarrow$ denote the right operation on $S$. Then $\rightarrow$ is not commutative on $S$ unless $S$ is a singleton.

title: Right Order Topology on Real Numbers is Topology
snippet: Let $\tau$ be the right order topology on $\R$. Then $\tau$ forms a topology on $\R$. That is: $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ is a topological space.

title: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers as Neighborhood Space
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ denote the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Let $U \subseteq \Z_{>0}$ be defined as being a neighborhood of $n$ $\forall m \in \Z: m \ge n \implies m \in U$ Then the set $\NN$ of all $U$ for all $n \in \Z_{>0}$ forms a neighborhood space which is the same as the right order space on $\Z_{>0}$.

title: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers is Topology
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. Let $\tau$ be the right order topology on $\Z_{>0}$. Then $\tau$ forms a topology on $\Z_{>0}$. That is: $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ is a topological space.

title: Right Order Topology on Strictly Positive Integers is not Metrizable
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive integers. Let $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ denote the right order space on $\Z_{>0}$. Then $T = \struct {\Z_{>0}, \tau}$ is not a metrizable space.

title: Right Product with Degenerate Linear Transformation is Degenerate
snippet: Let $U, V, W$ be vector spaces over a field $K$. Let $G: U \to V$ be a degenerate linear transformation. Let $M: V \to W$ be a linear transformation. Then $M \circ G$ is degenerate.

title: Right Quasigroup if (1-3) Parastrophe of Magma is Magma
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let the $(1-3)$ parastrophe of $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a right quasigroup.

title: Right Regular Representation by Inverse is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the operation: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\rho_{g^{-1} } } h$ where $\rho_g$ is the right regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a group action.

title: Right Regular Representation by Inverse is Transitive Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*: G \times G \to G$ be the group action: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = \map {\rho_{g^{-1} } } h$ where $\rho_g$ is the right regular representation of $G$ with respect to $g$. Then $*$ is a transitive group action.

title: Right Regular Representation of 0 is Bijection in B-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \circ}$ be a $B$-algebra. Then the right regular representation of $\struct {X, \circ}$ $0$ is a bijection.

title: Right Regular Representation of Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\rho_a: S \to S$ be the right regular representation of $S$ with respect to $a$. Then: $\rho_a \sqbrk T = T \circ \set a = T \circ a$ where $T \circ a$ denotes subset product with a singleton.

title: Right Regular Representation wrt Right Cancellable Element on Finite Semigroup is Bijection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a finite semigroup. Let $a \in S$ be right cancellable. Then the right regular representation $\rho_a$ of $\struct {S, \circ}$ with respect to $a$ is a bijection.

title: Right Self-Distributive Operation with Left Identity is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\circ$ be right self-distributive. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have a left identity. Then $\circ$ is an idempotent operation.

title: Right Shift Operator is Linear Mapping
snippet: Let $X = Y = \ell^2$ be 2-sequence spaces over real numbers. Let $R : X \to Y$ be the right shift operator. Then $R$ is a linear mapping.

title: Right Shift Operator on 2-Sequence Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the $2$-sequence space with $2$-norm. Let $R : \ell^2 \to \ell^2$ be the right shift operator. Then $R$ is continuous on $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$.

title: Right Square Pyramid has Four Planes of Symmetry
snippet: Let $F$ be a right square pyramid. Then $F$ has $4$ planes of symmetry.

title: Right Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Double-sided Whiskered Composite
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $K : \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be a covariant functor. Let $K \eta: K \circ F \to K \circ G$ denote the right whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $K$.

title: Right Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf E$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $K : \mathbf D \to \mathbf E$ be a covariant functor. Let $K \eta : K \circ F \to K \circ G$ denote the right whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $K$. Then: $K \eta$ is a natural transformation.

title: Right Zero Divisor of Commutative Ring is Left Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $x \in R$ be a right zero divisor of $R$. Then $x$ is also a left zero divisor of $R$.

title: Right and Left Regular Representations in Topological Group are Homeomorphisms
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot, \tau}$ be a topological group. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $G$. Then the left and right regular representations with respect to $g$: $L_g: \struct {G, \tau} \to \struct {G, \tau}$ and: $R_g: \struct {G, \tau} \to \struct {G, \tau}$ are homeomorphisms.

title: Rigid Body Rotating about Fixed Axis has One Degree of Freedom
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis. Then $\BB$ has $1$ degree of freedom.

title: Rigid Body in General Motion has Six Degrees of Freedom
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a rigid body in general motion. Then $\BB$ has $6$ degrees of freedom: $3$ degrees of freedom to specify the position of the center of mass of $\BB$ $3$ degrees of freedom to specify the orientation of $\BB$.

title: Rigid Body under Action of Couple undergoes Rotation
snippet: Let $B$ be a rigid body in space. Let a couple $C$ act on $B$. Then $B$ will be subject to rotation.

title: Ring Direct Product of Modulo Integers is Isomorphic to Ring Modulo Product iff Coprime
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{>1}$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ and $\struct {\Z_n, +_n, \times_n}$ be the rings of integers modulo $m$ and $n$ respectively. Let $\struct {\Z_m \times \Z_n}$ be the direct product of $\Z_m$ and $\Z_n$. Let $\struct {\Z_{m n}, +_{m n}, \times_{m n} }$ be the ring of integers modulo $mn$. Then $\struct {\Z_m \times \Z_n}$ is isomorphic to $\struct {\Z_{m n}, +_{m n}, \times_{m n} }$ $m$ and $n$ are coprime.

title: Ring Element is Unit iff Unit in Integral Extension
snippet: let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $a \in A$. Let $B$ be an integral ring extension of $A$. $(1): \quad a$ is a unit of $A$ $(2): \quad a$ is a unit of $B$

title: Ring Element is Zero Divisor iff not Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring which is not null. Let $z \in R^*$. Then $z$ is a zero divisor $z$ is not cancellable for $\circ$.

title: Ring Epimorphism Preserves Ideals
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring epimorphism. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R_1$. Then $\phi \sqbrk J$ is an ideal of $R_2$.

title: Ring Epimorphism Preserves Subrings
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring epimorphism. Let $S$ be a subring of $R_1$. Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is a subring of $R_2$.

title: Ring Epimorphism Preserves Unity
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring with unity $1$. Let $B$ be a ring. Let $f: A \to B$ be a ring epimorphism. Then $\map f 1$ is a unity of $B$.

title: Ring Epimorphism from Integers to Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ be the ring of integers. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Let $\phi: \struct {\Z, +, \times} \to \struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \phi x = \eqclass x m$ where $\eqclass x m$ is the residue class modulo $m$. Then $\phi$ is a ring epimorphism, but specifically not a ring monomorphism. The image of $\phi$ is $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$. The kernel of $\phi$ is $m \Z$, the set of integer multiples of $m$.

title: Ring Epimorphism with Trivial Kernel is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring epimorphism. Let $K = \map \ker \phi$ be the kernel of $\phi$. $\phi$ is an isomorphism $K = \set {0_{R_1} }$.

title: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Negatives
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Then: $\forall x \in R_1: \map \phi {-x} = -\paren {\map \phi x}$

title: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Subrings
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $S$ be a subring of $R_1$. Then $\phi \sqbrk S$ is a subring of $R_2$.

title: Ring Homomorphism Preserves Zero
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Let: $0_{R_1}$ be the zero of $R_1$ $0_{R_2}$ be the zero of $R_2$. Then: $\map \phi {0_{R_1} } = 0_{R_2}$

title: Ring Homomorphism by Idempotent
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Let $e \in A$ be an idempotent element. Let $\ideal e$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by $e$. Then the mapping: $f: A \to \ideal e: a \mapsto e a$ is a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel the ideal $\ideal {1 - e}$ generated by $1 - e$.

title: Ring Homomorphism from Division Ring is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ}$ and $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be rings whose zeros are $0_R$ and $0_S$ respectively. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. If $R$ is a division ring, then either: $(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective) $(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in R: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

title: Ring Homomorphism from Field is Monomorphism or Zero Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +_F, \circ}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $\struct {S, +_S, *}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_S$. Let $\phi: F \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Then either: $(1): \quad \phi$ is a monomorphism (that is, $\phi$ is injective) or $(2): \quad \phi$ is the zero homomorphism (that is, $\forall a \in F: \map \phi a = 0_S$).

title: Ring Homomorphism from Ring with Unity to Integral Domain Preserves Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \circ_R}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {D, +_D, \circ_D}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$ and whose unity is $1_D$. Let $\phi: R \to D$ be a ring homomorphism such that: $\map \ker \phi \ne R$ where $\map \ker \phi$ denotes the kernel of $\phi$. Then $\map \phi {1_R} = 1_D$.

title: Ring Homomorphism of Addition is Group Homomorphism
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. Then $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2}$ is a group homomorphism.

title: Ring Homomorphism whose Kernel contains Ideal
snippet:
Let $R$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $
u: R 	o R / J$ be the quotient epimorphism. Let $\phi: R 	o S$ be a ring homomorphism such that: $J \subseteq \map \ker \phi$ where $\map \ker \phi$ is the kernel of $\phi$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism $\psi: R / J 	o S$ such that: $\phi = \psi \circ 
u$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. $ egin {xy} \xymatrix@L + 2mu@ + 1em { R \ar[rr]^*{
u} \ar[rdrd]_*{\phi} & & R / J \ar[dd]_*{\psi} \ \ & & S } \end {xy}$ Also: $\map \ker \psi = \map \ker \phi / J$

title: Ring Isomorphic to Polynomial Ring is Polynomial Ring
Ring Less Zero is Semigroup for Product iff No Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null ring. Then $R$ has no zero divisors $\struct {R^*, \circ}$ is a semigroup.

title: Ring Monomorphism from Integers to Rationals
snippet: Let $\phi: \Z \to \Q$ be the mapping from the integers $\Z$ to the rational numbers $\Q$ defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \phi x = \dfrac x 1$ Then $\phi$ is a (ring) monomorphism, but specifically not an epimorphism.

title: Ring Negative is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $a \in R$. Then the ring negative $-a$ of $a$ is unique.

title: Ring Operations on Coset Space of Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\powerset R$ be the power set of $R$. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be cosets of $J$. Let $X +_\PP Y$ be the sum of $X$ and $Y$, where $+_\PP$ is the operation induced on $\powerset R$ by $+$. Similarly, let $X \circ_\PP Y$ be the product of $X$ and $Y$, where $\circ_\PP$ is the operation induced on $\powerset R$ by $\circ$.

title: Ring Product preserves Inequalities on Positive Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring. Let $x, y, z, w \in R$. Let $0 < x < y$ and $0 < z < w$. Then: $0 < z \circ x < w \circ y$

title: Ring Product with Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Then: $\forall x \in R: 0_R \circ x = 0_R = x \circ 0_R$ That is, the zero is a zero element for the ring product, thereby justifying its name.

title: Ring Subtraction equals Zero iff Elements are Equal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$ Then: $\forall a, b \in R: a - b = 0_R \iff a = b$ where $a - b$ denotes ring subtraction.

title: Ring Without Unity may have Quotient Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $I$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\struct {R / I, +, \circ}$ be the associated quotient ring. Then $\struct {R / I, +, \circ}$ may have a unity even if $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ has not.

title: Ring Zero is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose ring zero is $0_R$. Then $0_R$ is an idempotent element of $R$ under the ring product $\circ$: $0_R \circ 0_R = 0_R$

title: Ring Zero is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Then the ring zero of $R$ is unique.

title: Ring Zero is not Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring which is not null. Let $0$ be the ring zero of $R$. Then $0$ is not a cancellable element for the ring product $\circ$.

title: Ring by Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $e$ be an idempotent element of $A$. Then the ideal $I := \ideal e$ generated by $e$ is a commutative ring with unity $\struct {I, +, \circ}$ with unity $e$.

title: Ring is Commutative iff Opposite Ring is Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {R, +, *}$ be the opposite ring of $\struct {R, +, \times}$. Then $\struct {R, +, \times}$ is a commutative ring : $\struct {R, +, \times} = \struct {R, +, *}$

title: Ring is Ideal of Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Then $R$ is an ideal of $R$.

title: Ring is Module over Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}_R$ is an $R$-module.

title: Ring is Subring of Itself
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Then $R$ is a subring of itself.

title: Ring is not Empty
snippet: A ring cannot be empty.

title: Ring of Algebraic Integers
snippet: Let $K / \Q$ be a number field. Let $\Z \sqbrk x$ denote the polynomial ring in one variable over $\Z$. Let $\OO_K$ denote the set of all elements of $K / \Q$ which are a root of some monic polynomial $P \in \Z \sqbrk x$. That is, let $\OO_K$ denote the algebraic integers over $K$. Then $\OO_K$ is a ring, called the Ring of Algebraic Integers.

title: Ring of Arithmetic Functions is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\AA$ be the set of all arithmetic functions. Let $*$ denote Dirichlet convolution, and $+$ the pointwise sum of functions. The ring of arithmetic functions $\struct {\AA, +, *}$ is a commutative ring with unity.

title: Ring of Bounded Continuous Functions is Ring of Continuous Functions for Compact Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \tau}$ be a compact space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *} = \struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$

title: Ring of Bounded Continuous Functions is Ring of Continuous Functions for Pseudocompact Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \tau}$ be a pseudocompact space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *} = \struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$

title: Ring of Bounded Continuous Functions is Subring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a subring of $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$

title: Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a commutative ring

title: Ring of Continuous Mappings is Subring of All Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring. Let $\struct {R^S, +, *}$ be the ring of mappings from $S$ to $R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is a subring of $\struct {R^S, +, *}$

title: Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a commutative ring

title: Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is a ring

title: Ring of Endomorphisms is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ denote the ring of endomorphisms on $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Then $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is a ring with unity.

title: Ring of Endomorphisms is not necessarily Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \oplus}$ be an abelian group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all group endomorphisms of $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ denote the ring of endomorphisms on $\struct {G, \oplus}$. Then $\struct {\mathbb G, \oplus, *}$ is not necessarily a commutative ring with unity.

title: Ring of Idempotents is Idempotent Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ be its ring of idempotents. Then $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ is an idempotent ring.

title: Ring of Idempotents of Commutative and Unitary Ring is Boolean Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative and unitary ring. Let $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ be its ring of idempotents. Then $\struct {A, \oplus, \circ}$ is a Boolean ring.

title: Ring of Integers Modulo Composite is not Integral Domain
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Let $m$ be a composite number. Then $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ is not an integral domain.

title: Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Field
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Then: $m$ is prime $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ is a field.

title: Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Integral Domain
snippet: == Corollary to Ring of Integers Modulo Prime is Field == Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Then: $m$ is prime $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ is an integral domain.

title: Ring of Integers Modulo m cannot be Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m \ge 2$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$‎ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Then $\struct {\Z_m, +, \times}$ cannot be an ordered integral domain.

title: Ring of Integers Modulo m is Ring
snippet: For all $m \in \N: m \ge 2$, the ring of integers modulo $m$: $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ is a commutative ring with unity $\eqclass 1 m$. The zero of $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ is $\eqclass 0 m$.

title: Ring of Integers has Characteristic Zero
snippet: The ring of integers has characteristic zero: $\Char {\Z, +, \times} = 0$

title: Ring of Integers has no Zero Divisors
snippet:
The integers have no zero divisors: $ orall x, y, \in \Z: x 	imes y = 0 \implies x = 0 \lor y = 0$ This can equivalently be expressed: $ orall x, y, \in \Z: x 
e 0 \land y 
e 0 \implies x 	imes y 
e 0$

title: Ring of Integers is Principal Ideal Domain
snippet: The integers $\Z$ form a principal ideal domain.

title: Ring of Integers of Algebraic Number Field is UFD iff Class Number is 1
snippet: Let $K$ be a field of algebraic numbers. Let $\OO_K$ be the ring of integers of $K$. Then $\OO_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD) the class number of $K$ is $1$.

title: Ring of Integers of Number Field is Dedekind Domain
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraic number field. Let $\OO_K$ be its ring of integers. Then $\OO_K$ is a Dedekind domain.

title: Ring of Integers of Number Field is Free Z-Module
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraic number field. Let $\OO_K$ be its ring of integers. Let $\sqbrk {K : \Q}$ denote the degree of field extension $K : \Q$. Then $\OO_K$ is a free $\Z$-module of dimension $\sqbrk {K : \Q}$.

title: Ring of Linear Operators is Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +}$ be an abelian group.. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\struct {\map {\LL_R} G, +, \circ}$ be the ring of linear operators on $G$, where: $+$ denotes pointwise addition $\circ$ denotes composition of linear operators. Then $\struct {\map {\LL_R} G, +, \circ}$ is a ring.

title: Ring of Polynomial Forms is Commutative Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $A = R \sqbrk {\set {X_j: j \in J} }$ be the set of all polynomial forms over $R$ in the indeterminates $\set {X_j: j \in J}$. Then $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ is a commutative ring with unity.

title: Ring of Polynomial Forms is Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $X \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $D$. Then $D \sqbrk X$ is an integral domain.

title: Ring of Polynomial Forms is not necessarily Isomorphic to Ring of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $D$ be an integral domain. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in $X$ over $D$. Let $\map P D$ be the ring of polynomial functions over $D$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $D \sqbrk X$ is isomorphic with $\map P D$.

title: Ring of Polynomial Forms over Field is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1_F$. Let $F \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials over $F$. Then $F \sqbrk X$ is a vector space over $F$.

title: Ring of Polynomial Forms over Integral Domain is Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Let $\struct {D \sqbrk X, \oplus, \odot}$ be the ring of polynomial forms over $D$ in the indeterminate $X$. Then $\struct {D \sqbrk X, \oplus, \odot}$ is an integral domain.

title: Ring of Polynomial Functions is Commutative Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $R \sqbrk {\set {X_j: j \in J} }$ be the ring of polynomial forms over $R$ in the indeterminates $\set {X_j: j \in J}$. Let $R^J$ be the free module on $J$. Let $A$ be the set of all polynomial functions $R^J \to R$. Let $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ be the ring of polynomial functions on $R$. Then $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ is a commutative ring with unity.

title: Ring of Polynomials over Reals is not Field
snippet: Let $\R \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in an indeterminate $X$ over $\R$. Then $\R \sqbrk X$ is not a field.

title: Ring of Quaternions is Ring
snippet: The set $\mathbb H$ of quaternions forms a ring under the operations of addition and multiplication.

title: Ring of Sets Generated by Semiring
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a semiring of sets. Let $\map \RR \SS$ be the minimal ring generated by $\SS$. Let $\LL$ be the system of sets $A$ with the finite expansions: $\ds A = \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^n A_k$ with respect to the sets $A_k \in \SS$. Then $\LL = \map \RR \SS$.

title: Ring of Sets is Closed under Finite Intersection
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a ring of sets. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \in \RR$. Then: $\ds \bigcap_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \RR$

title: Ring of Sets is Closed under Finite Union
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a ring of sets. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \in \RR$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \RR$

title: Ring of Sets is Commutative Ring
snippet: A ring of sets $\struct {\RR, \symdif, \cap}$ is a commutative ring whose zero is $\O$.

title: Ring of Sets is Semiring of Sets
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a ring of sets. Then $\RR$ is also a semiring of sets.

title: Ring of Square Matrices over Commutative Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ is a ring with unity. However, for $n \ge 2$, $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ is not a commutative ring.

title: Ring of Square Matrices over Field is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $F$ be a field. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_F} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $F$. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_F} n, +, \times}$ is a ring with unity, but is not a commutative ring.

title: Ring of Square Matrices over Real Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_\R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $\R$. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_\R} n, +, \times}$ is a ring with unity, but is not a commutative ring.

title: Ring of Square Matrices over Ring is Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ is a ring.

title: Ring of Square Matrices over Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Then $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ is a ring with unity.

title: Ring with Multiplicative Norm has No Proper Zero Divisors
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let its zero be denoted by $0_R$. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}$ be a multiplicative norm on $R$. Then $R$ has no proper zero divisors. That is: $\forall x, y \in R^*: x \circ y \ne 0_R$ where $R^*$ is defined as $R \setminus \set {0_R}$.

title: Ring with Unity/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Rings with Unity ==

title: Ring with Unity has Prime Ideal
snippet: Let $A$ be a non-trivial commutative ring with unity. Then $A$ has a prime ideal.

title: Ring with Unity is Module over Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}_R$ is a unitary $R$-module.

title: Rings of Polynomials in Ring Elements are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $R_1, R_2$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $D$ be an integral subdomain of both $R_1$ and $R_2$. Let $X_1, X_2 \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk {X_1}, D \sqbrk {X_2}$ be the rings of polynomials in $X_1$ and $X_2$ over $D$. Then $D \sqbrk {X_1}$ is isomorphic to $D \sqbrk {X_2}$.

title: Rising Factorial as Factorial by Binomial Coefficient
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. $x^{\overline n} = n! \dbinom {x + n - 1} n$ where: $x^{\overline n}$ denotes $x$ to the $n$ rising $n!$ denotes the factorial of $n$ $\dbinom {x + n - 1} n$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Rising Factorial as Quotient of Factorials
snippet: Let $x \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $x^{\overline n} = \dfrac {\paren {x + n - 1}!} {\paren {x - 1}!} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {x + n} } {\map \Gamma x}$ where: $x^{\overline n}$ denotes the $n$th rising factorial power of $x$ $\map \Gamma x$ denotes the Gamma function of $x$.

title: Rising Factorial in terms of Falling Factorial
snippet: $x^{\overline n} = \paren {x + n - 1}^{\underline n}$ where: $x^{\underline n}$ is the $n$th falling factorial power of $x$ $x^{\overline n}$ is the $n$th rising factorial power of $x$.

title: Rising Factorial in terms of Falling Factorial of Negative
snippet: $x^{\overline k} = \paren {-1}^k \paren {-x}^{\underline k}$ where: $x^{\underline k}$ is the $k$ to the $x$ falling $x^{\overline k}$ is the $k$ to the $x$ rising.

title: Rising Sum of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be positive integers. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^m \binom {n + j} n = \binom {n + m + 1} {n + 1} = \binom {n + m + 1} m$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient. That is: $\dbinom n n + \dbinom {n + 1} n + \dbinom {n + 2} n + \cdots + \dbinom {n + m} n = \dbinom {n + m + 1} {n + 1} = \dbinom {n + m + 1} m$

title: Ritz Method implies Not Worse Approximation with Increased Number of Functions
snippet: Consider the Ritz method. Let $\eta_n = \boldsymbol \alpha \boldsymbol \phi$. Let $J \sqbrk {\eta_n} = \mu_n$. Then: $\mu_n \ge \mu_{n + 1}$

title: Row Equivalence is Equivalence Relation

title: Row Equivalent Matrix for Homogeneous System has same Solutions
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix in the matrix space $\map {\MM_\R} {m, n}$ such that: $\mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$ represents a homogeneous system of linear equations. Let $\mathbf H$ be row equivalent to $\mathbf A$. Then the solution set of $\mathbf H \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$ equals the solution set of $\mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$. That is: $\mathbf A \sim \mathbf H \implies \set {\mathbf x: \mathbf A \mathbf x = \mathbf 0} = \set {\mathbf x: \mathbf H \mathbf x = \mathbf 0}$ where $\sim$ represents row equivalence.

title: Row Operation has Inverse
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists another row operation $\Gamma'$ which transforms $\mathbf B$ back to $\mathbf A$.

title: Row Operation is Equivalent to Pre-Multiplication by Product of Elementary Matrices
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists a unique nonsingular square matrix $\mathbf R$ of order $m$ such that: $\mathbf R \mathbf A = \mathbf B$ where $\mathbf R$ is the product of a finite sequence of elementary row matrices.

title: Row Operation to Clear First Column of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_{m n}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over a field $K$. Then there exists a row operation to convert $\mathbf A$ into another $m \times n$ matrix $\mathbf B = \sqbrk b_{m n}$ with the following properties: $(1): \quad$ Except possibly for element $b_{1 1}$, all the elements of column $1$ are $0$ $(2): \quad$ If $b_{1 1} \ne 0$, then $b_{1 1} = 1$. This process is referred to as clearing the first column.

title: Row Rank of Matrix equals Rank of Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix. The row rank of $\mathbf A$ is equal to the rank of $\mathbf A$.

title: Row and Column Sums of Adjacency Matrix of Undirected Graph equals Vertex Degree
snippet: Let $G$ be an undirected graph. Let $\mathbf M$ be the adjacency matrix for $G$. The row sums and column sums of the rows and columns of $\mathbf M$ are equal to the degrees of the corresponding vertices of $G$.

title: Rule for Extracting Random Variable from Conditional Expectation of Product

Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables such that: $X Y$ is integrable and: $Y$ is $\GG$-measurable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Let $\expect {X Y \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X Y$ given $\GG$. Then: $\expect {X Y \mid \GG} = Y \expect {X \mid \GG}$ almost everywhere.

title: Rule of Detachment/Linguistic Note

Let us assume: the truth of a conditional statement the truth of its antecedent clause Then the consequent clause will be true unconditionally. Hence we can detach the conditional part of the statement, leaving the consequent to stand alone without needing to be qualified.

title: Rule of Sequent Introduction
snippet: Let the statements $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_n$ be conclusions in a proof, on various assumptions. Let $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_n \vdash Q$ be a sequent for which we already have a proof. Then we may infer, at any stage of a proof (citing SI), the conclusion $Q$ of the sequent already proved. This conclusion depends upon the pool of assumptions upon which $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_n$ rest. This is called the rule of sequent introduction.

title: Rule of Substitution

title: Rule of Theorem Introduction

title: Same-Matrix Product of Matrix Exponentials
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Let $s, t \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Then: $e^{\mathbf A t} e^{\mathbf A s} = e^{\mathbf A \paren {t + s} }$

title: Same Degrees of Vertices does not imply Graph Isomorphism
snippet: Let $G = \struct {\map V G, \map E G}$ and $H = \struct {\map V H, \map E H}$ be graphs such that: $\card {\map V G} = \card {\map V H}$ where $\card {\map V G}$ denotes the order of $G$. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a mapping which preserves the degrees of the vertices: $\forall v \in \map V G: \map {\deg_H} {\map \phi v} = \map {\deg_G} v$ Then it is not necessarily the case that $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

title: Same Dimensional Vector Spaces are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $V$, $W$ be finite dimensional $K$-vector spaces. Suppose that $\dim_K V = \dim_K W$. Then: $V \cong W$ That is, $V$ and $W$ are isomorphic.

title: Sample Distribution Function is Consistent Estimator of Cumulative Distribution Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of ordinal data. Let $x \in S$ be arbitrary. Let $\map {S_n} x$ denote the sample distribution function on $S$. Let $\map F x$ denote the cumulative distribution function of the population from which $S$ was taken. Then $\map {S_n} x$ is a consistent estimator of $\map F x$.

title: Sample Distribution Function tends to Cumulative Distribution Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a sample of ordinal data. Let $\map {S_n} x$ denote the sample distribution function on $S$. Let $\map F x$ denote the cumulative distribution function of the population from which $S$ was taken. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {S_n} x = \map F x$

title: Sample Matrix Independence Test
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space of real or complex-valued functions on a set $J$. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ be functions in $V$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ from $J$ be given. Define the sample matrix: $S = \begin{bmatrix} \map {f_1} {x_1} & \cdots & \map {f_n} {x_1} \\ \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ \map {f_1} {x_n} & \cdots & \map {f_n} {x_n} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ Let $S$ be nonsingular. Then $f_1, \ldots, f_n$ are linearly independent in $V$.

title: Sample Mean is Unbiased Estimator of Population Mean
snippet: Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ form a random sample from a population with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$. Then: $\ds \bar X = \frac 1 n \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i$ is an unbiased estimator of $\mu$.

title: Sandwich Principle
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $g: A \to A$ be a mapping on $A$ such that: for all $x, y \in A$, either $\map g x \subseteq y$ or $y \subseteq x$. Then: $\forall x, y \in A: x \subseteq y \subseteq \map g x \implies x = y \lor y = \map g x$ That is, there is no element $y$ of $A$ such that: $x \subset y \subset \map g x$ where $\subset$ denotes a proper subset.

title: Sandwich Principle for G-Towers
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Let $x, y \in M$ be arbitrary. Then it cannot be the case that: $x \subsetneqq y \subsetneqq \map g x$

title: Sandwich Principle for Minimally Closed Class
snippet: Let $N$ be a class which is closed under a progressing mapping $g$. Let $b$ be an element of $N$ such that $N$ is minimally closed under $g$ with respect to $b$. Then for all $x, y \in N$: $x \subseteq y \subseteq \map g x \implies x = y \lor y = \map g x$

title: Sandwich Principle for Slowly Progressing Mapping
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a slowly progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a minimally inductive class under $g$. Then $x \subsetneqq y \subsetneqq \map g x$ can never hold.
