title: Satisfiability preserved in Supersignature
snippet: Let $\LL, \LL'$ be signatures for the language of predicate logic. Let $\LL'$ be a supersignature of $\LL$. Let $\Sigma$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ for some $\LL$-structure $\AA$ $\AA' \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ for some $\LL'$-structure $\AA'$ where $\models_{\mathrm{PL} }$ is the models relation. That is to say, the notion of satisfiability is preserved in passing to a supersignature.

title: Satisfiable Set Union Tautology is Satisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-satisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi$ be a tautology for $\mathscr M$. Then $\FF \cup \set \phi$ is also $\mathscr M$-satisfiable.

title: Satisfiable Set minus Formula is Satisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-satisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi \in \FF$. Then $\FF \setminus \set \phi$ is also $\mathscr M$-satisfiable.

title: Satisfiable iff Negation is Falsifiable
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ is satisfiable its negation $\neg \mathbf A$ is falsifiable.

title: Saturated Implies Universal
snippet: Let $\kappa$ be an infinite cardinal. Let $\MM$ be a model of the $\LL$-theory $T$. If $\MM$ is $\kappa$-saturated, then it is $\kappa^+$-universal, where $\kappa^+$ is the successor cardinal of $\kappa$.

title: Saturated Models of same Cardinality are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $T$ be an $\LL$-theory. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite cardinal. If $\MM$ and $\NN$ are saturated models of $T$ and the cardinality of the universes of $\MM$ and $\NN$ are both $\kappa$, then $\MM$ and $\NN$ are isomorphic.

title: Saturation Under Equivalence Relation in Terms of Graph
snippet: Let $\RR \subset S \times S$ be an equivalence relation on a set $S$. Let $\pr_1, \pr_2 : S \times S \to S$ denote the projections. Let $T\subset S$ be a subset. Let $\overline T$ denote its saturation. Then the following hold: $\overline T = \map {\pr_1} {\RR \cap \map {\pr_2^{-1} } T}$ $\overline T = \map {\pr_2} {\RR \cap \map {\pr_1^{-1} } T}$

title: Scalar-Valued Measure associated with Resolution of Identity is Positive Measure if Equal Vectors
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\map \BB X$ be the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $X$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\map B {\HH}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations on $\HH$. Let $\EE : \map \BB X \to \map B {\HH}$ be a resolution of the identity. For each $x, y \in \HH$, define $\EE_{x, y} : \map \BB X \to \C$ by: $\map {\EE_{x, y} } A = \innerprod {\map \EE A x} y$ for each $A \in \map \BB X$. If $x = y$, then $\EE_{x, y} := \EE_x$ is a measure with total variation $\norm x^2$.

title: Scalar Field (Physics)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Scalar Fields in the context of Physics ==

title: Scalar Multiple of Basic Sequence is Basic
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\GF$ with $\lambda_n 
e 0$ for each $n \in \N$. Then $\sequence {\lambda_n x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a basic sequence.

title: Scalar Multiple of Cauchy Sequence in Topological Vector Space is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $X$. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then $\sequence {\lambda x_n}_{n \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $X$.

title: Scalar Multiple of Convergent Net in Topological Vector Space is Convergent
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $x \in X$ and $\mu \in K$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ be a net converging to $x$. Then $\family {\mu x_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ converges to $\mu x$.

title: Scalar Multiple of Convergent Sequence in Topological Vector Space is Convergent
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence in $X$ with: $x_n \to x$ Let $\lambda \in K$. Then $\sequence {\lambda x_n}_{n \in \N}$ is a convergent sequence in $X$ with: $\lambda x_n \to \lambda x$.

title: Scalar Multiple of Function of Exponential Order
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \F$ be a function, where $\F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\lambda$ be a complex constant. Suppose $f$ is of exponential order $a$. Then $\lambda f$ is also of exponential order $a$.

title: Scalar Multiple of Integrable Function is Integrable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function, and let $\lambda \in \R$. Then $\lambda f: X \to \overline \R$, the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$, is also $\mu$-integrable. That is, the space of integrable functions $\LL^1_{\overline \R}$ is closed under pointwise $\R$-scalar multiplication.

title: Scalar Multiple of Schauder Basis is Schauder Basis
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\GF$ such that: $\lambda_n 
e 0$ for all $n \in \N$. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a Schauder basis for $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then $\sequence {\lambda_n e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Schauder basis for $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$.

title: Scalar Multiple of Simple Function is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $f: X \to \R$ be a simple function, and let $\lambda \in \R$. Then the pointwise scalar multiple $\lambda f: X \to \R$ of $f$ is also a simple function.

title: Scalar Multiple of Unconditionally Convergent Series is Unconditionally Convergent
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ such that: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is unconditionally convergent. Let $\lambda \in \GF$. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \lambda x_n$ is unconditionally convergent.

title: Scalar Multiplication Corresponds to Multiplication by 1x1 Matrix
snippet: Let $\map \MM 1$ denote the matrix space of square matrices of order $1$. Let $\map \MM {1, n}$ denote the matrix space of order $1 \times n$. Let $\mathbf A = \begin {pmatrix} a \end {pmatrix} \in \map \MM 1$ and $\mathbf B = \begin {pmatrix} b_1 & b_2 & \cdots & b_n \end{pmatrix} \in \map \MM {1, n}$. Let $\mathbf C = \mathbf A \mathbf B$ denote the (conventional) matrix product of $\mathbf A$ with $\mathbf B$. Let $\mathbf D = a \mathbf B$ denote the matrix scalar product of $a$ with $\mathbf B$. Then $\mathbf C = \mathbf D$.

title: Scalar Multiplication by Minus One reverses Preordering in Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\tuple {X, \le}$ be a preordered vector space over $\GF$. Let $x, y \in X$ be such that: $x \le y$ Then: $-y \le -x$

title: Scalar Multiplication by Zero gives Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector quantity. Let $0 \mathbf a$ denote the scalar product of $\mathbf a$ with $0$. Then: $0 \mathbf a = \bszero$ where $\bszero$ denotes the zero vector.

title: Scalar Multiplication is Continuous in Weak Topology
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$ with weak topology $w$. Define $m : K \times \struct {X, w} \to \struct {X, w}$ by: $\map m {\lambda, x} = \lambda x$ for each $\lambda \in K$, $x \in X$. Then $m$ is continuous. That is, scalar multiplication remains continuous when restricting to the weak topology.

title: Scalar Multiplication of Vectors is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector quantity. Let $m, n$ be scalar quantities. Then: $m \paren {n \mathbf a} = \paren {m n} \mathbf a = n \paren {m \mathbf a}$

title: Scalar Multiplication of Vectors is Distributive over Scalar Addition
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector quantity. Let $m, n$ be scalar quantities. Then: $\paren {m + n} \mathbf a = m \mathbf a + n \mathbf a$

title: Scalar Multiplication of Vectors is Distributive over Vector Addition
snippet: Let $\mathbf a, \mathbf b$ be a vector quantities. Let $m$ be a scalar quantity. Then: $m \paren {\mathbf a + \mathbf b} = m \mathbf a + m \mathbf b$

title: Scalar Multiplication on Locally Convex Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ equipped with the standard topolgoy. Let $\struct {\GF \times X, \tau}$ be the Cartesian product $\GF \times X$ equipped with the product topology. Let $\circ : \struct {\GF \times X, \tau} \to \struct {X, \PP}$ be the scalar multiplication defined on $X$. Then $\circ : \struct {\GF \times X, \tau} \to \struct {X, \PP}$ is a continuous mapping.

title: Scalar Multiplication on Normed Vector Space is Continuous
snippet:
Let $\struct { K, +, \circ_K }$ be a normed division ring with norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_K$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X }$ be a normed vector space over $K$. Let $\struct {K 	imes X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_P }$ be the direct product of $K$ and $X$ with the direct product norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_P$. Let $\circ : K 	imes X 	o X$ be the scalar multiplication defined on $X$. Then $\circ: K 	imes X 	o X$ is a continuous mapping.

title: Scalar Product of Magnitude by Unit Vector Quantity
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector quantity. Let $m$ be a scalar quantity. Then: $m \mathbf a = m \paren {\size {\mathbf a} \hat {\mathbf a} } = \paren {m \size {\mathbf a} } \hat {\mathbf a}$ where: $\size {\mathbf a}$ denotes the magnitude of $\mathbf a$ $\hat {\mathbf a}$ denotes the unit vector in the direction $\mathbf a$.

title: Scalar Product with Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $x \in G, \lambda \in R$. Then: $\lambda \ast e = 0_R \ast x = e$

title: Scalar Product with Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $x \in G, \lambda \in R$. Then: $\lambda \ast \struct {-x} = \struct {-\lambda} \ast x = -\struct {\lambda \ast x}$

title: Scalar Product with Inverse Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an unitary $R$-module. Let $x \in G$. Then: $\paren {-1_R} \circ x = - x$

title: Scalar Product with Multiple of Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an unitary $R$-module. Let $x \in G, n \in \Z$. Then: $\paren {n \cdot 1_R} \circ x = n \cdot x$ that is: $\paren {\map {\paren {+_R}^n} {1_R} } \circ x = \map {\paren {+_G}^n} x$

title: Scalar Product with Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $x \in G, \lambda \in R, n \in \Z$. Then: $\lambda \ast \paren {n \cdot x} = n \cdot \paren {\lambda \ast x} = \paren {n \cdot \lambda} \ast x$

title: Scalar Product with Sum
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \ast}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $x \in G, \lambda \in R$. Let $\sequence {x_m}$ be a sequence of elements of $G$. Then: $\ds \lambda \ast \paren {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^m x_k} = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^m \paren {\lambda \ast x_k}$

title: Scalar Triple Product as Product of Magnitudes
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be vectors in a Cartesian $3$-space: where $\tuple {\mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k}$ is the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Let $\sqbrk {\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c}$ be the scalar triple product of $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$. Then: $\sqbrk {\mathbf a, \mathbf b, \mathbf c} = \size {\mathbf a} \size {\mathbf b} \size {\mathbf c} \sin \theta \cos \alpha$ where: $\theta$ is the angle between $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ $\alpha$ is the angle between $\mathbf b \times \mathbf c$ and $\mathbf a$.

title: Scale Parameter of Cauchy Distribution is Half-Width at Half-Height
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with a Cauchy distribution: $\map {f_X} x = \dfrac 1 {\pi \lambda \paren {1 + \paren {\frac {x - \gamma} \lambda }^2} }$ for: $\lambda \in \R_{>0}$ $\gamma \in \R$ Then $\lambda$ can be referred to as the half-width at half-height: $\map \Pr {\gamma - \lambda < X \le \gamma + \lambda} = \dfrac 1 2$

title: Scaled Euclidean Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of (strictly) positive integers. Let $\delta: \R_{>0} \times \R_{>0} \to \R$ be the metric on $\R_{>0}$ defined as: $\forall x, y \in \R_{>0}: \map \delta {x, y} = \dfrac {\size {x - y} } {x y}$ Then $\delta$ is a metric.

title: Scaled Real Function that Decreases Without Bound
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $\lambda \in \R_{\ne 0}$ be a nonzero constant. Then: For $\lambda > 0$: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map f x = -\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \lambda \map f x = -\infty$ $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \map f x = -\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \lambda \map f x = -\infty$ For $\lambda < 0$: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map f x = -\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \lambda \map f x = +\infty$ $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \map f x = -\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \lambda \map f x…

title: Scaled Real Function that Increases Without Bound
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $\lambda \in \R_{\ne 0}$ be a nonzero constant. Then: For $\lambda > 0$: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map f x = +\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \lambda \map f x = +\infty$ $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \map f x = +\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \lambda \map f x = + \infty$ For $\lambda < 0$: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \map f x = +\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \lambda \map f x = -\infty$ $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \map f x = +\infty \implies \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \lambda \map f…

title: Scaled Sine Functions of Integer Multiples form Orthonormal Set
snippet: For all $n \in \Z_{>0}$, let $\map {\phi_n} x$ be the real function defined on the interval $\openint 0 \lambda$ as: $\map {\phi_n} x = \sqrt {\dfrac 2 \lambda} \sin \dfrac {n \pi x} \lambda$ Let $S$ be the set: $S = \set {\phi_n: n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Then $S$ is an orthonormal set.

title: Scalene Triangle Tessellates the Plane
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle, which can be any shape at all, even scalene. Then $T$ can tessellate the plane.

title: Scaling Property of Dirac Delta Function
snippet: Let $\map \delta t$ be the Dirac delta function. Let $a$ be a non zero constant real number. Then: $\map \delta {a t} = \dfrac {\map \delta t} {\size a}$

title: Scaling preserves Modulo Addition
snippet: Let $m \in \Z_{> 0}$. Let $x, y, c \in \Z$. Let $x \equiv y \pmod m$. Then: $c x \equiv c y \pmod m$

title: Scattered Space is T0
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a scattered topological space. Then $T$ is also a $T_0$ space.

title: Scattered Space is not necessarily T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a scattered topological space. Then $T$ is not necessarily a $T_1$ space.

title: Scattered T1 Space is Totally Disconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a scattered topological space which is also a $T_1$ space. Then $T$ is totally disconnected.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Let $z_1, \cdots, z_n$ be complex numbers that are linearly independent over the rational numbers $\Q$. Then: the extension field $\map \Q {z_1, \cdots, z_n, e^{z_1}, \cdots, e^{z_n} }$ has transcendence degree at least $n$ over $\Q$ where $e^z$ is the complex exponential of $z$. Category:Transcendental Number Theory Category:Unproven Hypotheses Category:Schanuel's Conjecture

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Algebraic Independence of Pi and Euler's Number over the Rationals
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $\pi$ (pi) and $e$ (Euler's number) are algebraically independent over the rational numbers $\Q$.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Algebraic Independence of Pi and Log of Pi over the Rationals
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $\pi$ (pi) and the logarithm of $\pi$ (pi): $\ln \pi$ are algebraically independent over the rational numbers $\Q$.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of 2 to the power of Euler's Number
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $2$ to the power of Euler's number $e$: $2^e$ is transcendental, where $e$ is Euler's number.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of Euler's Number to the power of Euler's Number
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then Euler's number $e$ to the power of itself: $e^e$ is transcendental.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of Log Pi
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then the logarithm of $\pi$ (pi): $\ln \pi$ is transcendental.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of Pi by Euler's Number
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $\pi \times e$ is transcendental.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of Pi plus Euler's Number
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $\pi + e$ is transcendental.

title: Schanuel's Conjecture Implies Transcendence of Pi to the power of Euler's Number
snippet: Let Schanuel's Conjecture be true. Then $\pi$(pi) to the power of Euler's number $e$: $\pi^e$ is transcendental.

title: Schatunowsky's Theorem
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\map w n$ denote the number of primes strictly less than $n$ which are not divisors of $n$. Let $\map \phi n$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function of $n$. Then $30$ is the largest integer $n$ such that: $\map w n = \map \phi n - 1$

title: Schauder Basis is Linearly Independent
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\set {e_n : n \in \N}$ be a Schauder basis for $X$. Then $\set {e_n : n \in \N}$ is linearly independent.

title: Scheffé's Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f_n$ be a sequence of $\mu$-integrable functions that converge almost everywhere to another $\mu$-integrable function $f$. Then $f_n$ converges to $f$ in $L^1$ $\ds \int_X \size {f_n} \rd \mu$ converges to $\ds \int_X \size f \rd \mu$.

title: Scheme of Abbreviation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Schemes of Abbreviation ==

title: Schreier-Zassenhaus Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ be two normal series for $G$. Then $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ have refinements of equal length whose factors are isomorphic.

title: Schröder Rule
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be relations on a set $S$. $(1): \quad A \circ B \subseteq C$ $(2): \quad A^{-1} \circ \overline C \subseteq \overline B$ $(3): \quad \overline C \circ B^{-1} \subseteq \overline A$ where: $\circ$ denotes relation composition $A^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $A$ $\overline A$ denotes the complement of $A$.

title: Schur's Inequality
snippet: Let $x, y, z \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be positive real numbers. Let $t \in \R, t > 0$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Then: $x^t \paren {x - y} \paren {x - z} + y^t \paren {y - z} \paren {y - x} + z^t \paren {z - x} \paren {z - y} \ge 0$ The equality holds either: $x = y = z$ Two of them are equal and the other is zero. When $t$ is a positive even integer, the inequality holds for all real numbers $x, y, z$.

title: Schur's Lemma
snippet: Schur's Lemma (Representation Theory) Schur's Lemma (Riemannian Geometry)

title: Schur's Lemma (Representation Theory)
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \cdot}$ be a finite group. Let $V$ and $V'$ be two irreducible $G$-modules. Let $f: V \to V'$ be a homomorphism of $G$-modules. Then either: $\map f v = 0$ for all $v \in V$ or: $f$ is an isomorphism.

title: Schur's Theorem
snippet: Schur-Zassenhaus Theorem Schur's Theorem (Ramsey Theory)

title: Schur's Theorem (Ramsey Theory)
snippet: Let $r$ be a positive integer. Then there exists a positive integer $S$ such that: for every partition of the integers $\set {1, \ldots, S}$ into $r$ parts, one of the parts contains integers $x$, $y$ and $z$ such that: $x + y = z$

title: Schur-Zassenhaus Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group and $N$ be a normal subgroup in $G$. Let $N$ be a Hall subgroup of $G$. Then there exists $H$, a complement of $N$, such that $G$ is the semidirect product of $N$ and $H$.

title: Schwartz Distribution/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Schwartz Distributions ==

title: Schwarz's Lemma
snippet: Let $D$ be the unit disk centred at $0$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a holomorphic function. Let $\map f 0 = 0$ and $\cmod {\map f z} \le 1$ for all $z \in D$. Then $\cmod {\map {f'} 0} \le 1$, and $\cmod {\map f z} \le \cmod z$ for all $z \in D$.

title: Schwarz-Pick Theorem
snippet: Let $\Bbb D$ be the unit disk in the complex plane centered at $0$. Let $f: \Bbb D \to \Bbb D$ be a holomorphic function. Then: $\forall z \in \Bbb D: \dfrac {\cmod {\map {f'} z} } {1 - \cmod {\map f z}^2} \le \dfrac 1 {1 - \cmod z^2}$ where $\cmod z$ denotes the modulus of $z$. Moreover, if there exists a $z_0 \in \Bbb D$ such that: $\dfrac {\cmod {\map {f'} {z_0} } } {1 - \cmod {\map {f'} {z_0} }^2} = \dfrac 1 {1 - \cmod {z_0}^2}$ then $f$ is a Möbius transformation.

title: Schönemann-Eisenstein Theorem
snippet: Let $\map f x = a_d x^d + a_{d - 1} x^{d - 1} + \dotsb + a_0 \in \Z \sqbrk x$ be a polynomial over the ring of integers $\Z$. Let $p$ be a prime such that: $(1): \quad p \divides a_i \iff i \ne d$ $(2): \quad p^2 \nmid a_0$ where $p \divides a_i$ signifies that $p$ is a divisor of $a_i$. Then $f$ is irreducible in $\Q \sqbrk x$.

title: Scientific Notation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Scientific Notation ==

title: Scope (Logic)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Scope in the context of Logic ==

title: Scott Topological Lattice is T0 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete topological lattice with Scott topology. Then $T$ is a $T_0$ space.

title: Scott Topology equals to Scott Sigma
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \preceq, \tau}$ be a up-complete topological lattice with Scott topology. Then $\tau = \map \sigma {T, \preceq}$ where $\map \sigma L$ denotes the Scott sigma of $L$.

title: Secant Function in terms of Gaussian Hypergeometric Function
snippet: Let $\map F {a, b; c; x}$ denote the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$ Then: $\sec x = \map F {\dfrac 1 2, 1; 1; \sin^2 x}$ where: $x$ is a real number such that $x \ne \dfrac {\paren {2 k + 1} \pi} 2$ for $k \in \Z$ $\sec$ denotes the secant function.

title: Secant Function is Even
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\sec x$ be the secant of $x$. Then, whenever $\sec x$ is defined: $\map \sec {-x} = \sec x$ That is, the secant function is even.

title: Secant Method can be derived from Newton-Raphson Method
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function which has a root which is to be found. The secant method can be derived from the Newton-Raphson method.

title: Secant Minus Cosine
snippet: $\sec x - \cos x = \sin x \tan x$

title: Secant Plus One over Secant Squared
snippet: $\dfrac {\sec x + 1} {\sec^2 x} = \dfrac {\sin^2 x} {\sec x - 1}$

title: Secant Secant Theorem
snippet: Let $C$ be a point external to a circle $ABED$. Let $CA$ and $CB$ be straight lines which cut the circle at $D$ and $E$ respectively. Then: $CA \cdot CD = CB \cdot CE$

title: Secant and Cosecant are Cofunctions
snippet: The secant and cosecant are cofunctions: {{eqn | n = 1 | q = \forall x \in \R, \cos x \ne 0 | l = \sec x | r = \map \csc {90 \degrees - x} }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall x \in \R, \sin x \ne 0 | l = \csc x | r = \map \sec {90 \degrees - x} }}

title: Secant in terms of Hyperbolic Secant
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\sec z = \map \sech {i z}$ where: $\sec$ denotes the secant function $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Secant in terms of Tangent
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number such that $\cos x \ne 0$. Then: {{eqn | l = \sec x | r = +\sqrt {\tan ^2 x + 1} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n - \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi$ }} {{eqn | l = \sec x | r = -\sqrt {\tan ^2 x + 1} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {2 n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {2 n + \dfrac 3 2} \pi$ }} where $\sec$ denotes the real secant function and $\tan$ denotes the real tangent function.

title: Secant is Reciprocal of Cosine
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\cos \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\sec \theta = \dfrac 1 {\cos \theta}$ where $\sec$ and $\cos$ mean secant and cosine respectively.

title: Secant of 105 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 105 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {7 \pi} {12} = -\paren {\sqrt 6 + \sqrt 2}$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 120 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 120 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {2 \pi} 3 = -2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 135 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 135 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {3 \pi} 4 = -\sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 150 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 150 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {5 \pi} 6 = -\dfrac {2 \sqrt 3} 3$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 15 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 15 \degrees = \sec \dfrac \pi {12} = \sqrt 6 - \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 165 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 165 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {11 \pi} {12} = -\paren {\sqrt 6 - \sqrt 2}$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 195 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 195 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {13 \pi} {12} = -\paren {\sqrt 6 - \sqrt 2}$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 210 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 210 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {7 \pi} 6 = -2 \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 225 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 225 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {5 \pi} 4 = -\sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 240 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 240 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {4 \pi} 3 = - 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 255 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 255 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {17 \pi} {12} = -\paren {\sqrt 6 + \sqrt 2}$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 285 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 285 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {19 \pi} {12} = \sqrt 6 + \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 300 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 300 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {5 \pi} 3 = 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 30 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 30 \degrees = \sec \dfrac \pi 6 = \dfrac {2 \sqrt 3} 3$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 315 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 315 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {7 \pi} 4 = \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 330 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 330 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {11 \pi} 6 = 2 \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 345 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 345 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {23 \pi} {12} = \sqrt 6 - \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 45 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 45 \degrees = \sec \dfrac \pi 4 = \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 60 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 60 \degrees = \sec \dfrac \pi 3 = 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of 75 Degrees
snippet: $\sec 75 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {5 \pi} {12} = \sqrt 6 + \sqrt 2$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of Angle in Cartesian Plane
snippet: Let $P = \tuple {x, y}$ be a point in the cartesian plane whose origin is at $O$. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the $x$-axis and the line $OP$. Let $r$ be the length of $OP$. Then: $\sec \theta = \dfrac r x$ where $\sec$ denotes the secant of $\theta$.

title: Secant of Angle plus Full Angle
snippet: $\sec \left({x + 2 \pi}\right) = \sec x$

title: Secant of Angle plus Right Angle
snippet: $\sec \left({x + \dfrac \pi 2}\right) = -\csc x$

title: Secant of Angle plus Straight Angle
snippet: $\map \sec {x + \pi} = -\sec x$

title: Secant of Angle plus Three Right Angles
snippet: $\map \sec {x + \dfrac {3 \pi} 2} = \csc x$

title: Secant of Complement equals Cosecant
snippet: $\map \sec {\dfrac \pi 2 - \theta} = \csc \theta$ for $\theta \ne n \pi$ where $\sec$ and $\csc$ are secant and cosecant respectively. That is, the cosecant of an angle is the secant of its complement. This relation is defined wherever $\sin \theta \ne 0$.

title: Secant of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\sec \paren {a + b i} = \dfrac {\cos a \cosh b + i \sin a \sinh b} {\cos^2 a \cosh^2 b + \sin^2 a \sinh^2 b}$ where: $\sec$ denotes the complex secant function. $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

title: Secant of Conjugate Angle
snippet: $\map \sec {2 \pi - \theta} = \sec \theta$ where $\sec$ denotes secant. That is, the secant of an angle equals its conjugate.

title: Secant of Full Angle
snippet: $\sec 360 \degrees = \sec 2 \pi = 1$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of Right Angle
snippet: $\sec 90 \degrees = \sec \dfrac \pi 2$ is undefined where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of Straight Angle
snippet: $\sec 180 \degrees = \sec \pi = -1$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of Supplementary Angle
snippet: $\map \sec {\pi - \theta} = -\sec \theta$ where $\sec$ denotes secant. That is, the secant of an angle is the negative of its supplement.

title: Secant of Three Right Angles
snippet: $\sec 270 \degrees = \sec \dfrac {3 \pi} 2$ is undefined where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of Three Right Angles less Angle
snippet: $\map \sec {\dfrac {3 \pi} 2 - \theta} = -\csc \theta$ where $\sec$ and $\csc$ are secant and cosecant respectively.

title: Secant of Zero
snippet: $\sec 0 = 0$ where $\sec$ denotes secant.

title: Secant of i
snippet: $\sec i = \dfrac {2 e} {e^2 + 1}$ where $\sec$ denotes the complex secant function and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

title: Second-Countability is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is second-countable. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is second-countable. That is, the property of second-countability is hereditary.

title: Second-Countability is Preserved under Open Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a surjective open mapping which is also continuous. If $T_A$ is second-countable, then $T_B$ is also second-countable.

title: Second-Countability is not Continuous Invariant
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous mapping. If $T_A$ is a second-countable space, then it does not necessarily follow that $T_B$ is also second-countable.

title: Second-Countable Metric Space is not necessarily Totally Bounded
snippet: A metric space which is second-countable is not necessarily also totally bounded.

title: Second-Countable Regular Space is Completely Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a second-countable space which is also regular. Then $T$ is a completely normal space.

title: Second-Countable Space is Compact iff Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a second-countable space. Then $T$ is compact $T$ is countably compact.

title: Second-Countable Space is First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a second-countable space. Then $T$ is also a first-countable space.

title: Second-Countable Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is second-countable. Then $T$ is also a Lindelöf space.

title: Second-Countable Space is Separable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a second-countable topological space. Then $T$ is also a separable space.

title: Second-Countable T3 Space is Lindelöf and T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a second-countable $T_3$ space. Then $T$ is both a Lindelöf space and a $T_5$ space.

title: Second-Countable T3 Space is T5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space which is also second-countable. Then $T$ is a $T_5$ space.

title: Second Apotome/Example
snippet: == Example of Second Apotome == Let $a = 2 \sqrt {3}$ and $b = 3$. Then: {{eqn | l = \frac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2} } a | r = \frac {\sqrt {12 - 9} } {2 \sqrt 3} }} {{eqn | r = \frac {\sqrt 3} {2 \sqrt 3} }} Therefore $2 \sqrt 3 - 3$ is a second apotome. Category:Examples of Apotome

Second Bimedial Straight Line is Divisible Uniquely
Second Chebyshev Function is Increasing
snippet: The second Chebyshev function $\psi$ is increasing.

title: Second Chebyshev Function is Theta of x
snippet: We have: $\map \psi x = \map \Theta x$ where: $\Theta$ is $\Theta$ notation $\psi$ is the second Chebyshev function.

title: Second Column and Diagonal of Pascal's Triangle consist of Triangular Numbers
snippet: The $2$nd column and $2$nd diagonal of Pascal's triangle consists of the set of triangular numbers.

snippet: == Source Work == Chapter $\text I$. The First Variation: $1.2$. Ordinary maximum and minimum theory

title: Second Derivative at Point of Inflection
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f$ have a point of inflection at $\xi \in \openint a b$. Then: $\map {f' '} \xi = 0$ where $\map {f' '} \xi$ denotes the second derivative of $f$ at $\xi$.

title: Second Derivative of Concave Real Function is Non-Positive
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then $f$ is concave on $\openint a b$ its second derivative $f \le 0$ on $\openint a b$.

title: Second Derivative of Convex Real Function is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then $f$ is convex on $\openint a b$ its second derivative $f' ' \ge 0$ on $\openint a b$.

title: Second Derivative of Inverse Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is of differentiability class $2$. Let $f$ have an inverse $f^{-1}$, likewise of differentiability class $2$. Then: $\dfrac {\d^2 x} {\d y^2} = -\dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} \paren {\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} }^{-3}$

title: Second Derivative of Laplace Transform
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function, twice differentiable on any closed interval $\closedint 0 a$. Let $\laptrans f = F$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Then, everywhere that $\dfrac {\d^2} {\d s^2} \laptrans f$ exists: $\dfrac {\d^2} {\d s^2} \laptrans {\map f t} = \laptrans {t^2 \, \map f t}$

title: Second Derivative of Locus of Cycloid
snippet: Consider a circle of radius $a$ rolling without slipping along the x-axis of a cartesian plane. Consider the point $P$ on the circumference of this circle which is at the origin when its center is on the y-axis. Consider the cycloid traced out by the point $P$. Let $\tuple {x, y}$ be the coordinates of $P$ as it travels over the plane. The second derivative of the locus of $P$ is given by: $y' ' = -\dfrac a {y^2}$

title: Second Derivative of Natural Logarithm Function
snippet: Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm function. Then: $\map {\dfrac {\d^2} {\d x^2} } {\ln x} = -\dfrac 1 {x^2}$

title: Second Derivative of PGF of Negative Binomial Distribution
Second Dual Operator Extends Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a bounded linear transformation. Let $X^{\ast \ast}$ and $Y^{\ast \ast}$ be the second normed duals of $X$ and $Y$ respectively. Let $\iota_X : X \to X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation on $X$. Let $\iota_Y : Y \to Y^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation on $Y$. Let $T^{\ast \ast} : X^{\ast \ast} \to Y^{\ast \ast}$ be the second dual operator of $T$. Then $T^{\ast \ast}$ extends $T$ in the sense that: $\map {T^{\ast \ast} } {\iota_X x} = \map {\iota_Y} {T x}$

title: Second Fontené Theorem/Also known as
snippet: == Second Fontené Theorem: Also known as == The second Fontené theorem is also known as Griffiths' theorem, for .

title: Second Hyperoperation is Multiplication Operation
snippet: The $2$nd hyperoperation is the multiplication operation restricted to the positive integers: $\forall x, y \in \Z_{\ge 0}: H_2 \left({x, y}\right) = x \times y$

title: Second Inversion Formula for Stirling Numbers
snippet: For all $m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$: $\ds \sum_k {n \brace k} {k \brack m} \paren {-1}^{n - k} = \delta_{m n}$ where: $\ds {n \brace k}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\ds {k \brack m}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\delta_{m n}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Second Order Fibonacci Number in terms of Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: The second order Fibonacci number $\FF_n$ can be expressed in terms of Fibonacci numbers as: $\dfrac {3 n + 3} 5 F_n - \dfrac n 5 F_{n + 1}$

title: Second Order ODE/(x^2 + 2 y') y'' + 2 x y' = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 + 2 y'} y' ' + 2 x y' = 0$ subject to the initial conditions: $y = 1$ and $y' = 0$ when $x = 0$ has the particular solution: $y = 1$ or: $3 y + x^3 = 3$

title: Second Order ODE/(x^2 - 1) y'' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad \paren {x^2 - 1} y' ' - 2 x y' + 2 y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 x + C_2 \paren {x^2 + 1}$

title: Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' + x y' = 1
snippet: The second order ODE: $x^2 y' ' + x y' = 1$ has the general solution: $y = \dfrac {\paren {\ln x}^2} 2 + C_1 \ln x + C_2$

title: Second Order ODE/x^2 y'' = 2 x y' + (y')^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $x^2 y' ' = 2 x y' + \paren {y'}^2$ has the general solution: $y = -\dfrac {x^2} 2 - C_1 x - {C_1}^2 \, \map \ln {x - C_1} + C_2$

title: Second Order ODE/x y'' + 3 y' = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x y' ' + 3 y' = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 + \dfrac {C_2} {x^2}$

title: Second Order ODE/x y'' - (2 x + 1) y' + (x + 1) y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x y' ' - \paren {2 x + 1} y' + \paren {x + 1} y = 0$ has the general solution: $y = C_1 e^x + C_2 x^2 e^x$

title: Second Order ODE/x y'' - y' = 3 x^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x y' ' - y' = 3 x^2$ has the general solution: $y = x^3 + \dfrac {C_1 x^2} 2 + C^2$

title: Second Order ODE/x y'' = y' + (y')^3
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad x y' ' = y' + \paren {y'}^3$ has the general solution: $x^2 + \paren {y - C_2}^2 = C_1^2$

title: Second Order ODE/y'' + 2 x (y')^2 = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' + 2 x \paren {y'}^2 = 0$ has the general solution: $C_1 \map \arctan {C_1 x} = y + C_2$

title: Second Order ODE/y'' - f(x) y' + (f(x) - 1) y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - \map f x y' + \paren {\map f x - 1} y = 0$ has the general solution: $\ds y = C_1 e^x + C_2 e^x \int e^{-2 x + \int \map f x \rd x} \rd x$

title: Second Order ODE/y'' - x f(x) y' + f(x) y = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' - x \, \map f x y' + \map f x y = 0$ has the general solution: $\ds y = C_1 x + C_2 x \int x^{-2} e^{\int x \, \map f x \rd x} \rd x$

title: Second Order ODE/y'' = 1 + (y')^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y' ' = 1 + \paren {y'}^2$ has the general solution: $y = \map {\ln \sec} {x + C_1} + C_2$

title: Second Order ODE/y'' = f(x)
snippet: The second order ODE: $\dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} = \map f x$ has the general solution: $\ds y = \iint \map f x \rd x \rd x + C_1 x + C_2$ where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are arbitrary constants.

title: Second Order ODE/y'' = f(y)
snippet: The second order ODE: $\dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} = \map f y$ has the general solution: $\dfrac {\sqrt 2} 2 \ds \int \dfrac {\d y} {\sqrt {\ds \int \map f y \rd y + C_1} } = x + C_2$ where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are arbitrary constants.

title: Second Order ODE/y y'' + (y')^2 - 2 y y' = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $y y' ' + \paren {y'}^2 - 2 y y' = 0$ has the general solution: $y^2 = C_2 e^{2 x} + C_1$

title: Second Order ODE/y y'' + (y')^2 = 0
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y y' ' + \paren {y'}^2 = 0$ has the general solution: $y^2 = C_1 x + C_2$

title: Second Order ODE/y y'' = (y')^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y y' ' = \paren {y'}^2$ has the general solution: $y = C_2 e^{C_1 x}$

title: Second Order ODE/y y'' = y^2 y' + (y')^2
snippet: The second order ODE: $(1): \quad y y' ' = y^2 y' + \paren {y'}^2$ subject to the initial conditions: $y = -\dfrac 1 2$ and $y' = 1$ when $x = 0$ has the particular solution: $2 y - 3 = 8 y \, \map \exp {\dfrac {3 x} 2}$

title: Second Order Weakly Stationary Gaussian Stochastic Process is Strictly Stationary
snippet: Let $S$ be a Gaussian stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Let $S$ be weakly stationary of order $2$. Then $S$ is strictly stationary.

title: Second Pappus-Guldinus Theorem
snippet: Let $C$ be a plane figure that lies entirely on one side of a straight line $L$. Let $S$ be the solid of revolution generated by $C$ around $L$. Then the surface area of $S$ is equal to the perimeter length of $C$ multiplied by the distance travelled by the centroid of $C$ around $L$ when generating $S$.

title: Second Pentagonal Number/Sequence
snippet: == Sequence of Second Pentagonal Numbers == The sequence of second pentagonal numbers, for $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$, begins: $0, 2, 7, 15, 26, 40, 57, 77, 100, 126, 155, 187, \ldots$

snippet: == Puzzle == Q: What is the volume of a whose radius is $z$ and whose thickness is $a$? A: From Volume of Right Circular Cylinder: $\text {pi} z z a$.

title: Second Price Auction/Analysis
snippet: == Analysis of Second Price Auction == Let $G$ denoted the game under analysis, that is, the second price auction under discussion. Let $F$ be the object being bid for. As in the formal definition of the sealed-bid auction, let the players be labelled in order of their valuations of $F$: $v_1 > v_2 > \cdots > v_n > 0$ In this context, a move by player $i$ is the bid that $i$ places on $F$. Let $b$ be the profile of moves made by all players. Let $\map m b$ be defined as the lowest $j$ such that $\ds b_j = \max_{k \mathop \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n} } b_k$.

title: Second Price Auction has Inefficient Equilibria
snippet: A second price auction has Nash equilibria which are inefficient.

title: Second Principle of Finite Induction
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \Z$ be a subset of the integers. Let $n_0 \in \Z$ be given. Suppose that: $(1): \quad n_0 \in S$ $(2): \quad \forall n \ge n_0: \paren {\forall k: n_0 \le k \le n \implies k \in S} \implies n + 1 \in S$ Then: $\forall n \ge n_0: n \in S$ The second principle of finite induction is usually stated and demonstrated for $n_0$ being either $0$ or $1$. This is often dependent upon whether the analysis of the fundamentals of mathematical logic are zero-based or one-based.

title: Second Principle of Mathematical Induction
snippet: Let $\map P n$ be a propositional function depending on $n \in \Z$. Let $n_0 \in \Z$ be given. Suppose that: $(1): \quad \map P {n_0}$ is true $(2): \quad \forall k \in \Z: k \ge n_0: \map P {n_0} \land \map P {n_0 + 1} \land \ldots \land \map P {k - 1} \land \map P k \implies \map P {k + 1}$ Then: $\map P n$ is true for all $n \ge n_0$. This process is called proof by (mathematical) induction. The Second Principle of Mathematical Induction is usually stated and demonstrated for $n_0$ being either $0$ or $1$.

title: Second Principle of Recursive Definition
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $T$ be a set. Let $a \in T$. For each $n \in \N_{>0}$, let $G_n: T^n \to T$ be a mapping. Then there exists exactly one mapping $f: \N \to T$ such that: $\forall x \in \N: \map f x = \begin{cases} a & : x = 0 \\ \map {G_n} {\map f 0, \ldots, \map f n} & : x = n + 1 \end{cases}$

title: Second Principle of Transfinite Induction
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be a well-ordering on $A$. Let $P$ be a property that satisfies the following $3$ conditions: $(1): \quad P$ holds for the smallest element of $A$. $(2): \quad$ For all $x \in A$ which have an immediate successor $\map S x$, if $P$ holds for $x$, then $P$ holds for $\map S x$. $(3): \quad$ For all limit element $y$ of $A$, if $P$ holds for all $x \prec y$, then $P$ holds for $y$. Then $P$ holds for all $x \in A$.

title: Second Projection on Ordered Pair of Sets
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be sets. Let $w = \tuple {a, b}$ denote the ordered pair of $a$ and $b$. Let $\map {\pr_2} w$ denote the second projection on $w$. Then: $\ds \map {\pr_2} w = \begin {cases} \ds \map \bigcup {\bigcup w \setminus \bigcap w} & : \ds \bigcup w \ne \bigcap w \\ \ds \bigcup \bigcup w & : \bigcup w = \ds \bigcap w \end {cases}$ where: $\ds \bigcup$ and $\ds \bigcap$ denote union and intersection respectively. $\setminus$ denotes the set difference operator.

title: Second Ring Isomorphism Theorem/Also known as
snippet: == Second Ring Isomorphism Theorem: Also known as == The Second Ring Isomorphism Theorem is also referred to by some sources as the First Ring Isomorphism Theorem. There is little consistency in the literature. It can also be called the Second Isomorphism Theorem for Rings. Because of the shape of its commutative diagram, this theorem is sometimes known as the Parallelogram Law. However, that name is usually applied to a result in vector algebra, so use in this context is not recommended. Category:Second Ring Isomorphism Theorem

title: Second Socratic Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == is supposed to have raised the question: Is the following statement in true or false? This statement in italics is false. Suppose the statement in italics is true. Then it is false. That is, what it says is different from the way things actually are. So, the sentence is not false. Therefore it is true. But it cannot be both. We can more formally demonstrate this as follows: Let $\map T P$ be a modal operator interpreted as "The proposition $P$ is true." Assume $P \iff \map T P$, or in other words, that declaring the proposition $P$ is equivalent to declaring that $P$ is true.

title: Second Standardized Moment is One
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable on some probability space with standard deviation $\sigma$. Then the second standardized moment $\alpha_2$ of $X$ is equal to $1$.

title: Second Subsequence Rule
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $M$. Suppose $\sequence {x_n}$ has a subsequence which is unbounded. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is divergent.

title: Second Supplement to Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
snippet: $\quad \paren {\dfrac 2 p} = \paren {-1}^{\paren {p^2 - 1} / 8} = \begin {cases} +1 & : p \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 8 \\ -1 & : p \equiv \pm 3 \pmod 8 \end {cases}$ where $\paren {\dfrac 2 p}$ is defined as the Legendre symbol.

title: Second Sylow Theorem
snippet: Let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of the finite group $G$. Let $Q$ be any $p$-subgroup of $G$. Then $Q$ is a subset of a conjugate of $P$.

title: Second Translation Property of Laplace Transforms
snippet: Let $f$ be a function such that $\laptrans f$ exists. Let $\laptrans {\map f t} = \map F s$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Let $a \in \C$ or $\R$ be constant. Let $g$ be the function defined as: $\map g t = \begin {cases} \map f {t - a} & : t > a \\ 0 & : t \le a \end {cases}$ Then: $\laptrans {\map g t} = e^{-a s} \map F s$

title: Secondary Data/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Secondary Data == Examples of secondary data include percentages means standard deviations.

title: Section Formula
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $P$ be collinear points. Let $P$ divide $AB$ externally in the ratio $1 : k$. Let the position vectors of $A$, $B$ and $P$ be $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf p$ respectively. Then: $\mathbf p = \dfrac {k \mathbf a - \mathbf b} {k - 1}$

title: Segment of Auxiliary Relation Mapping is Element of Increasing Mappings Satisfying Inclusion in Lower Closure
snippet: Let $R = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\map {\mathit {Ids} } R$ be the set of all ideals in $R$. Let $L = \struct {\map {\mathit {Ids} } R, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq {\restriction_{\map {\mathit {Ids} } R \times \map {\mathit {Ids} } R} }$. Let $r$ be an auxiliary relation on $S$. Let $M = \struct {F, \preccurlyeq}$ be the ordered set of increasing mappings $g$ satisfying $\forall x \in S: \map g x \subseteq x^\preceq$.

title: Segment of Auxiliary Relation Mapping is Increasing
snippet: Let $R = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let ${\it Ids}\left({R}\right)$ be the set of all ideals in $R$. Let $L = \left({ {\it Ids}\left({R}\right), \precsim}\right)$ be an ordered set where $\precsim \mathop = \subseteq\restriction_{ {\it Ids}\left({R}\right) \times {\it Ids}\left({R}\right)}$ Let $r$ be an auxiliary relation on $S$. Let $f: S \to {\it Ids}\left({R}\right)$ be a mapping such that $\forall x \in S: f\left({x}\right) = x^r$ where $x^r$ denotes the $r$-segment of $x$. Then $f$ is increasing mapping.

title: Segment of Auxiliary Relation is Subset of Lower Closure
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $R$ be auxiliary relation on $S$. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^R \subseteq x^\preceq$ where $x^R$ denotes the $R$-segment of $x$, $x^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $x$.

title: Segments of Rational Straight Line cut in Extreme and Mean Ratio are Apotome

snippet: The functor $\pi_1 : \mathbf{Top_\bullet} \to \mathbf{Grp}$ preserves pushouts of inclusions.

title: Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator has Empty Residual Spectrum
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a self-adjoint densely defined linear operator. Then the residual spectrum $\map {\sigma_r} T$ is empty.

title: Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Maximally Symmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a self-adjoint densely-defined linear operator. Then $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ is maximally symmetric.

title: Self-Conjugate Triangle needs Two Sides to be Specified
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $\triangle PQR$ be a triangle such that: $PR$ is the polar of $Q$ $QR$ is the polar of $P$ with respect to $\CC$. Then $PQ$ is the polar of $R$ and so $\triangle PQR$ is conjugate to itself. Hence a self-conjugate triangle requires just two sides to be specified as polars of their opposite vertices. The third side is the polar of its opposite vertex as a consequence.

title: Self-Distributive Quasigroup is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a self-distributive quasigroup. Then $\odot$ is an idempotent operation.

title: Self-Distributive Quasigroup with at least Two Elements has no Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a self-distributive quasigroup. Let $S$ have at least $2$ elements. Then $\struct {S, \odot}$ has no identity element.

title: Self-Distributive Quasigroup with at least Two Elements is not Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a self-distributive quasigroup. Let $S$ have at least $2$ elements. Then $\odot$ is not an associative operation.

title: Self-Inverse Element of Integral Domain is Unity or its Negative
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$ and whose unity is $1_D$. Let $x \in D$ such that $x^2 = 1_D$. Then either $x = 1_D$ or $x = -1_D$.

title: Self-Inverse Elements Commute iff Product is Self-Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $x, y \in \struct {G, \circ}$, such that $x$ and $y$ are self-inverse. Then $x$ and $y$ commute $x \circ y$ is also self-inverse.

title: Self-Product of Standard Ordered Basis Element equals 1
snippet: Let $\tuple {\mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k}$ be the standard ordered basis of Cartesian $3$-space $S$. Then: $\mathbf i^2 = \mathbf j^2 = \mathbf k^2 = 1$ where $\mathbf i^2$ and so on denotes the square of a vector quantity: $\mathbf i^2 := \mathbf i \cdot \mathbf i$

title: Semantic Consequence Union Negation
snippet: Let $U$ be a set of propositional formulas. Let $P$ be a propositional formula. Let $U \models P$ denote that $U$ is a semantic consequence $P$. Then: $U \models P$ iff: $U \cup \set {\neg P}$ has no models.

title: Semantic Consequence as Tautological Conditional
snippet: Let $\FF$ be a finite set of WFFs of propositional logic. Let $\mathbf A$ be another WFF. {{eqn | l = \FF | o = \models_{\mathrm {BI} } | r = \mathbf A }} {{eqn | o = \models_{\mathrm {BI} } | r = \bigwedge \FF \implies \mathbf A }} That is, $\mathbf A$ is a semantic consequence of $\FF$ $\ds \bigwedge \FF \implies \mathbf A$ is a tautology. Here, $\ds \bigwedge \FF$ is the conjunction of $\FF$.

title: Semantic Consequence is Transitive
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF, \GG$ and $\HH$ be sets of $\LL$-formulas. Suppose that: {{eqn | l = \FF | o = \models_{\mathscr M} | r = \GG }} {{eqn | l = \GG | o = \models_{\mathscr M} | r = \HH }} Then $\FF \models_{\mathscr M} \HH$.

title: Semantic Consequence of Set Union Formula
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be a set of logical formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi$ be an $\mathscr M$-semantic consequence of $\FF$. Let $\psi$ be another logical formula. Then: $\FF \cup \set \psi \models_{\mathscr M} \phi$ that is, $\phi$ is also a semantic consequence of $\FF \cup \set \psi$.

title: Semantic Consequence of Set minus Tautology
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be a set of logical formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi$ be an $\mathscr M$-semantic consequence of $\FF$. Let $\psi \in \FF$ be a tautology. Then: $\FF \setminus \set \psi \models_{\mathscr M} \phi$ that is, $\phi$ is also a semantic consequence of $\FF \setminus \set \psi$.

title: Semantic Consequence of Superset
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be a set of logical formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi$ be an $\mathscr M$-semantic consequence of $\FF$. Let $\FF'$ be another set of logical formulas. Then: $\FF \cup \FF' \models_{\mathscr M} \phi$ that is, $\phi$ is also a semantic consequence of $\FF \cup \FF'$.

title: Semantic Consequence preserved in Supersignature
snippet: Let $\LL, \LL'$ be signatures for the language of predicate logic. Let $\LL'$ be a supersignature of $\LL$. Let $\mathbf A$ be an $\LL$-sentence. Let $\Sigma$ be a set of $\LL$-sentences. $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \mathbf A$ for all $\LL$-structures $\AA$ for which $\AA \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ $\AA' \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \mathbf A$ for all $\LL'$-structures $\AA'$ for which $\AA' \models_{\mathrm{PL} } \Sigma$ where $\models_{\mathrm{PL} }$ denotes the models relation. That is to say, the notion of semantic consequence is preserved in passing to a supersignature.

title: Semantic Tableau Algorithm
snippet: == Algorithm == Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of propositional logic. The purpose of this algorithm is to create a completed semantic tableau $T$ for $\mathbf A$. Step 1: Start with a labeled tree $T$ comprising only a root node labeled with the singleton $\set {\mathbf A}$. Step 2: Choose a leaf node $t$ of $T$ that has not yet been marked. Let $\map U t$ be the set that labels $t$. Step 3: If $\map U t$ is a set of literals, mark $t$ as follows: a): If $\map U t$ contains a complementary pair, mark it closed, $\times$, and go to Step 2. b): Otherwise, mark it open, $\odot$, and go to Step 2.

title: Semantic Tableau Algorithm Terminates
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of propositional logic. Then the Semantic Tableau Algorithm for $\mathbf A$ terminates. Each leaf node of the resulting semantic tableau is marked.

title: Semantic Tableau Algorithm is Decision Procedure for Tautologies
snippet: The Semantic Tableau Algorithm is a decision procedure for tautologies.

title: Semantically Equivalent Terms are Equal
snippet: Let $\tau_1, \tau_2$ be terms. Suppose that they are semantically equivalent with respect to the empty set. Then $\tau_1 = \tau_2$.

title: Semi-Inner Product induces Inner Product on Quotient
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a semi-inner product space over $\GF$. Let: $N = \set {x \in V : \innerprod x x = 0}$ Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Define: $\innerprod {x + N} {y + N}_{X/N} = \innerprod x y$ for each $x, y \in X$. Then $\innerprod \cdot \cdot_{X/N}$ is an inner product on $X/N$.

title: Semi-Inner Product with Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a semi-inner product space. Let $\mathbf 0_V$ be the zero vector of $V$. Then for all $v \in V$: $\innerprod {\mathbf 0_V} v = \innerprod v {\mathbf 0_V} = 0$

title: Semicubical Parabola has Cusp at Origin
snippet: The semicubical parabola has a cusp at the origin.

title: Semidirect Product is Abelian iff Components are Abelian and Action is Trivial
snippet: Let $N$ and $H$ be groups. Let $H$ act by automorphisms on $N$ via $\phi$. Let $N \rtimes_\phi H$ be the corresponding (outer) semidirect product.

title: Semidirect Product of Groups is Group
snippet: Let $H$ and $N$ be groups. Let $\Aut N$ denote the automorphism group of $N$. Let $\phi : H\to \Aut N$ be a group homomorphism, that is, let $H$ act on $N$. Let $N \rtimes_\phi H$ be the (outer)semidirect product of $N$ and $H$ with respect to $\phi$, that is: $N \rtimes_\phi H = (N \times H, \circ)$ where $(n_1, h_1) \circ (n_2, h_2) = (n_1\cdot \phi(h_1)(n_2), h_1\cdot h_2)$ Then $N\rtimes_\phi H$ is a group.

title: Semidirect Product with Trivial Action is Direct Product
snippet: Let $H$ and $N$ be groups. Let $\Aut N$ denote the automorphism group of $N$. Let $\phi: H \to \Aut N$ be defined as: $\forall h \in H: \map \phi h = I_N$ for all $h \in H$ where $I_N$ denotes the identity mapping on $N$. Let $N \rtimes_\phi H$ be the corresponding semidirect product. Then $N \rtimes_\phi H$ is the direct product of $N$ and $H$.

title: Semigroup is Group Iff Latin Square Property Holds
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group for all $a, b \in S$ the Latin square property holds in $S$: $a \circ x = b$ $y \circ a = b$ for $x$ and $y$ each unique in $S$.

title: Semigroup is Subsemigroup of Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a subsemigroup of itself.

title: Semigroup of Bounded Linear Operators Uniformly Continuous iff Continuous as Map from Non-Negative Reals to Bounded Linear Operators
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a semigroup of bounded linear operators. Let $\struct {\map B X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations equipped with the canonical norm. Then $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ is uniformly continuous : the mapping $T : \hointr 0 \infty \to \map B X$ is continuous.

title: Semigroup of Bounded Linear Operators is C0 iff Point Evaluations Continuous
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a semigroup of bounded linear operators. For each $x \in X$, define $x^\wedge : \hointr 0 \infty \to X$ by: $\map {x^\wedge} t = \map T t x$ for each $t \in \hointr 0 \infty$. Then $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ is a $C_0$ semigroup $x^\wedge$ is continuous for each $x \in X$.

title: Semilattice Homomorphism is Order-Preserving
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be semilattices. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a semilattice homomorphism. Let $\preceq_1$ be the ordering on $S$ defined by: $a \preceq_1 b \iff \paren {a \circ b} = b$ Let $\preceq_2$ be the ordering on $T$ defined by: $x \preceq_2 y \iff \paren {x * y} = y$ Then: $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$ is order-preserving.

title: Semilattice Induces Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semilattice. Let $\RR$ be the relation on $S$ defined by, for all $a, b \in S$: $a \mathrel \RR b$ $a \circ b = b$ Then $\RR$ is an ordering.

title: Semilattice has Unique Ordering such that Operation is Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee}$ be a semilattice. Then there exists a unique ordering $\preccurlyeq$ on $S$ such that: $x \vee y = \sup \set {x, y}$ where $\sup \set {x, y}$ is the supremum of $\set {x, y}$ $\preccurlyeq$.

title: Seminorm Maps Zero Vector to Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \circ}$ be a division ring with norm $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_K$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\struct {K, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_K}$. Let $\mathbf 0_X$ be the zero vector of $X$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Then $\map p {\mathbf 0_X} = 0$.

title: Seminorm is Sublinear Functional
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $p : X \to \R$ be a seminorm on $X$. Then: $p$ is a sublinear functional.

title: Seminorm on Space of Bounded Operators induced by Vector is Seminorm
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $\map \BB {X, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $X 	o Y$. Let $x \in X$. Define: $\map {p_x} T = 
orm {T x}_Y$ for each $T \in \map \BB {X, Y}$. Then $p_x$ is a seminorm on $\map \BB {X, Y}$.

title: Seminorm on Vector Space induced by Linear Transformation is Seminorm
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $Y$. Define: $\map q x = \map p {T x}$ for each $x \in X$. Then $q$ is a seminorm on $X$.

title: Seminorm on Vector Space induces Norm on Quotient
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $p$ be a seminorm on $X$. Let: $N = \set {x \in X : \map p x = 0}$ From Set of Points for which Seminorm is Zero is Vector Subspace, $N$ is a vector subspace. Let $X/N$ be the quotient vector space of $X$ modulo $N$. Let $\pi : X \to X/N$ be the quotient mapping. Then the mapping $\norm {\, \cdot \,} : X/N \to \hointr 0 \infty$ defined by: $\norm {\map \pi x} = \map p x$ is well-defined and a norm on $X/N$.

title: Semiperfect Number is not Deficient
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a semiperfect number. Then $n$ is not deficient.

title: Semiperimeter of Integer Heronian Triangle is Composite
snippet: The semiperimeter of an integer Heronian triangle is always a composite number.

title: Semiregular Tessellation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Semiregular Tessellations ==

title: Semiregular Topological Space is not necessarily T2.5
snippet: A semiregular topological space is not necessarily a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Semiregular Topological Space is not necessarily T3
snippet: A semiregular topological space is not necessarily a $T_3$ space.

title: Semiregular Topological Space is not necessarily Urysohn
snippet: A semiregular topological space is not necessarily a Urysohn space.

title: Separability in Uncountable Particular Point Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be an uncountable particular point space. Let $H = S \setminus \set p$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference. Then $H$ is not separable.

title: Separability is Preserved only in Open Subspace
snippet: The property of separability is preserved only in subspaces which are open.

title: Separability is not Weakly Hereditary
snippet: The property of separability is not weakly hereditary.

title: Separability of Normed Vector Space preserved under Isometric Isomorphism
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ be a separable normed vector space. Let $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$ be a normed vector space that is isometrically isomorphic to $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$. Let $T : X 	o Y$ be an isometric isomorphism between $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$. Then $\struct {Y, 
orm \cdot_Y}$ is separable.

title: Separable Banach Space is Linearly Isomorphic to Quotient of 1-Sequence Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_1} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_1}$ be the $1$-sequence space. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space over $\GF$. Then there exists a closed vector subspace $M$ of $\map {\ell_1} \GF$ such that: $X$ is linearly isomorphic to the normed quotient vector space $\map {\ell_1} \GF/M$.

title: Separable C*-Algebra has Sequential Approximate Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a separable $\text C^\ast$ algebra. Then there exists a sequence $\family {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ forming an approximate identity of $A$.

title: Separable Degree is At Most Equal To Degree
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a finite field extension. Then $\index E F_s$ is finite, and: $\index E F_s \le \index E F$ where: $\index E F$ denotes the degree of $E / F$ $\index E F_s$ denotes the separable degree of $E / F$.

title: Separable Degree of Field Extensions is Multiplicative
snippet: Let $E / F / k$ be a tower of fields. Then $\index E k_s = \index E F_s \index F k_s$ where $\index E F_s$ denotes the separable degree of $E / F$.

title: Separable Discrete Space is Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Let $T$ be separable. Then $S$ is countable.

title: Separable Elements Form Field
snippet: Let $E / F$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $K$ be the relative separable closure of $F$ in $E$. Then $K$ is an intermediate field of $E / F$.

title: Separable Extension is Contained in Galois Extension
snippet: Let $E/F$ be a separable finite field extension. Then there exists a finite field extension $L/E$ such that $L/F$ is Galois.

title: Separable Meta-Lindelöf Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a separable meta-Lindelöf space. Then $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ is a Lindelöf space.

title: Separable Metacompact Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a separable topological space which is also metacompact. Then $T$ is a Lindelöf space.

title: Separable Metric Space is Homeomorphic to Subspace of Fréchet Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space whose induced topology is separable. Then $M$ is homeomorphic to a subspace of the Fréchet product space $\struct {\R^\omega, d}$ on the countable-dimensional real Cartesian space $\R^\omega$.

title: Separable Metric Space is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be separable. Then $M$ is second-countable.

title: Separable Normed Vector Space Isometrically Isomorphic to Linear Subspace of Space of Bounded Sequences
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a separable normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} {\Bbb F}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the normed vector space of bounded sequences. Then there exists a linear subspace $Y$ of $\map {\ell^\infty} {\Bbb F}$ such that: $X$ is isometrically isomorphic to $Y$.

title: Separable Space is not necessarily First-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is separable. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is first-countable.

title: Separable Space is not necessarily Second-Countable
snippet: A separable topological space is not necessarily also a second-countable space.

title: Separable Space satisfies Countable Chain Condition
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a separable topological space. Then $T$ satisfies the countable chain condition.

title: Separable Topological Space remains Separable in Coarser Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau_2}$ be a separable topological space. Let $\tau_1$ be a topology on $X$ such that: $\tau_1 \subseteq \tau_2$ That is, such that $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$. Then $\struct {X, \tau_1}$ is separable.

title: Separated Morphism is Quasi-Separated
snippet: Let $f$ be a separated morphism of schemes. Then $f$ is quasi-separated.

title: Separated Sets are Clopen in Union
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $A$ and $B$ be separated sets in $T$. Let $H = A \cup B$ be given the subspace topology. Then $A$ and $B$ are each both open and closed in $H$.

title: Separated Sets are Disjoint
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A$ and $B$ are separated in $T$. Then $A$ and $B$ are disjoint: $A \cap B = \O$

title: Separated Subsets of Linearly Ordered Space under Order Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $A$ and $B$ be separated sets of $T$. Let $A^*$ and $B^*$ be defined as: {{eqn | l = A^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in A, \closedint a b \cap B^- = \O} }} {{eqn | l = B^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in B, \closedint a b \cap A^- = \O} }} where $A^-$ and $B^-$ denote the closure of $A$ and $B$ in $T$. Then $A^*$ and $B^*$ are themselves separated sets of $T$.

title: Separation Axioms Preserved under Closed Bijection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}, T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a closed bijection.

title: Separation Axioms Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: The separation axioms are preserved under homeomorphism. Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}, T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism.

title: Separation Axioms on Double Pointed Topology
Separation Properties Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. These separation properties are not generally preserved under expansion:

title: Separation Properties Preserved in Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T_H$ be a subspace of $T$. The following separation axioms are hereditary. That is, if $T$ has one of the following properties then $T_H$ has the same property.

title: Separation Properties Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$.

title: Separation Properties Preserved under Topological Product
snippet: Let $\SS = \family {\struct {S_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds T = \struct {S, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \struct{S_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\SS$.

title: Separation Properties in Open Extension of Particular Point Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space such that $S$ is not a singleton or a doubleton. Let $T^*_{\bar q} = \struct {S^*_q, \tau^*_{\bar q} }$ be an open extension space of $T$.

title: Separation Properties of Alexandroff Extension of Rational Number Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the Euclidean topology $\tau_d$. Let $p$ be a new element not in $\Q$. Let $\Q^* := \Q \cup \set p$. Let $T^* = \struct {\Q^*, \tau^*}$ be the Alexandroff extension on $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$. Then $T^*$ satisfies no Tychonoff separation axioms higher than a $T_1$ space.

title: Separation of Non-Empty Set from Set containing Interior Point is Continuous and Proper
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\R$. Let $B \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $A \subseteq X$ have non-empty interior $\Int A$ such that there exists a linear functional $f : X \to \R$ and $\alpha \in \R$ with: $\map f b \le \alpha \le \map f a$ for each $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. That is, the affine hyperplane $\sqbrk {f = \alpha}$ separates $A$ and $B$. Then $f$ is continuous and the separation is proper.

title: Sequence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Sequences ==

title: Sequence Characterization of Open Sets
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $G \subseteq X$. {{item|(1):|$G \subseteq X$ is an open set of $\struct {X, d}$}} {{item|(2):|$\forall x \in G: \forall \sequence {x_n} \in X: x_n \to x: \exists n_0 \in \N: \forall n \ge n_0: \sequence {x_n} \in G$}}

title: Sequence Converges to Point Relative to Metric iff it Converges Relative to Induced Topology
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, d}$ be a metric space or a pseudometric space. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the topological space induced by $d$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a infinite sequence in $S$. Let $l \in S$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to $l$ relative to $d$ $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to $l$ relative to $\tau$.

title: Sequence Converges to Within Half Limit
Sequence in Banach Space Congruent to Basic Sequence is Basic

title: Sequence in Indiscrete Space converges to Every Point
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence in $T$. Then $\sequence {s_n}$ converges to every point of $S$.

title: Sequence in Metric Space with Summable Difference between Consecutive Terms is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\struct {X, d}$ such that: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \map d {x_k, x_{k + 1} } < \infty$ Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence.

title: Sequence in Normed Vector Space Convergent to Limit iff Norm of Sequence minus Limit is Null Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $x \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges to $x$ : $\norm {x_n - x} \to 0$

title: Sequence is Bounded in Norm iff Bounded in Metric
snippet:

title: Sequence of Binomial Coefficients is Strictly Decreasing from Half Upper Index
snippet: == Corollary to Sequence of Binomial Coefficients is Strictly Increasing to Half Upper Index == Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\dbinom n k$ be the binomial coefficient of $n$ over $k$ for a positive integer $k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $S_n = \left\langle{x_k}\right\rangle$ be the sequence defined as: $x_k = \dbinom n k$ Then $S_n$ is strictly decreasing exactly where $\dfrac n 2 < k \le n$.

title: Sequence of Binomial Coefficients is Strictly Increasing to Half Upper Index
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $\dbinom n k$ be the binomial coefficient of $n$ over $k$ for a positive integer $k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $S_n = \sequence {x_k}$ be the sequence defined as: $x_k = \dbinom n k$ Then $S_n$ is strictly increasing exactly where $0 \le k < \dfrac n 2$.

title: Sequence of Column Operations is Column Operation
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma_1$ be a column operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Let $\Gamma_2$ be a column operation which transforms $\mathbf B$ to another new matrix $\mathbf C \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists another column operation $\Gamma$ which transforms $\mathbf A$ back to $\mathbf C$ such that $\Gamma$ consists of $\Gamma_1$ followed by $\Gamma_2$.

title: Sequence of Natural Powers of Right Shift Operator in 2-Sequence Space Converges in Weak Operator Topology

title: Sequence of Powers of Number less than One
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as $x_n = x^n$. Then: $\size x < 1$ $\sequence {x_n}$ is a null sequence.

title: Sequence of Powers of Reciprocals is Null Sequence
snippet: Let $r \in \Q_{>0}$ be a strictly positive rational number. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as: $x_n = \dfrac 1 {n^r}$ Then $\sequence {x_n}$ is a null sequence.

snippet: For prime $p$, let $p \#$ denote the $p$th primorial, defined in the sense that $p \#$ is the product of all primes less than or equal to $p$. The sequence $\sequence p$ such that $p \# - 1$ is prime begins: $3, 5, 11, 13, 41, 89, 317, 337, 991, 1873, 2053, 2377, 4093, 4297, \ldots$

snippet: For prime $p$, let $p \#$ denote the $p$th primorial, defined in the sense that $p \#$ is the product of all primes less than or equal to $p$. title: Sequence of Record Peaks in Values of Divisor Sum
snippet: Let $d: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be the mapping defined as: $\map d n = \map {\sigma_1} n - \map {\sigma_1} {n'}$ where: $n$ denotes a highly abundant number $n'$ denotes the previous highly abundant number. The following $n \in \Z_{>0}$ have the property that they have a higher value of $\map d n$ than any smaller $n$: $\forall m \in \Z_{>0}: m < n \implies \map {\sigma_1} m < \map {\sigma_1} n$ That is, they are the peak divisor sums which exceed the previous peak by a higher number than any previous peak.

title: Sequence of Recursively Defined Terms forms Minimally Inductive Set
snippet: Let $g$ be a mapping. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence such that: $a_0 = \O$ and: $\forall n \in \N: a_{n + 1} = \map g {a_n}$ Then the set: $\set {a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n, a_{n + 1}, \ldots}$ is minimally inductive under $g$.

title: Sequence of Row Operations is Row Operation
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a metric space of order $m \times n$ over a field $K$. Let $\mathbf A \in \map \MM {m, n}$ be a matrix. Let $\Gamma_1$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf A$ to a new matrix $\mathbf B \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Let $\Gamma_2$ be a row operation which transforms $\mathbf B$ to another new matrix $\mathbf C \in \map \MM {m, n}$. Then there exists another row operation $\Gamma$ which transforms $\mathbf A$ back to $\mathbf C$ such that $\Gamma$ consists of $\Gamma_1$ followed by $\Gamma_2$.
