title: Sequence of Wythoff Pairs contains all Positive Integers exactly Once Each
snippet: Consider the sequence of Wythoff pairs arranged in sequential order: $\tuple {0, 0}, \tuple {1, 2}, \tuple {3, 5}, \tuple {4, 7}, \tuple {6, 10}, \tuple {8, 13}, \ldots$ Apart from the first Wythoff pair $\tuple {0, 0}$, every positive integer appears in this sequence exactly once.

title: Sequence on Product Space Converges to Point iff Projections Converge to Projections of Point
snippet: Let $I$ be an arbitrary index set. For all $i \in I$, let $T_i = \struct {X_i, \tau_i}$ be topological spaces. Let $\ds X = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $\tau$ be the product topology on $X$. Denote by $\pr_i : X \to X_i$ the projection from $X$ onto $X_i$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence on $X$ and let $x \in X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ converges to $x$ : for all $i \in I$ the sequence $\sequence {\map {\pr_i} {x_n} }$ converges to $\map {\pr_i} x$.

snippet: The following ordered quadruples of consecutive integers have divisor sums which are strictly decreasing: $44, 45, 46, 47$ $104, 105, 106, 107$

snippet: The following ordered quadruples of consecutive integers have divisor sum values which are strictly increasing: $61, 62, 63, 64$ $73, 74, 75, 76$

title: Sequences of Projections in 2-Sequence Space Converges in Strong Operator Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the $p$-sequence normed vector space. Let $\map {CL} {\ell^2} := \map {CL} {\ell^2, \ell^2}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. For $n \in \N$ let $P_n \in \map {CL} {\ell^2}$ be the projection operator over $\ell^2$. Let $\sequence {P_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence. Let $I \in \map {CL} {\ell^2}$ be the identity operator. Then $\sequence {P_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges to $I$ in the strong operator topology.

title: Sequences of Projections in 2-Sequence Space do not Converge in Uniform Operator Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the $p$-sequence normed vector space. Let $\map {CL} {\ell^2} := \map {CL} {\ell^2, \ell^2}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. For $n \in \N$ let $P_n \in \map {CL} {\ell^2}$ be the projection operator over $\ell^2$. Let $\sequence {P_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence. Let $I \in \map {CL} {\ell^2}$ be the identity operator. Then $\sequence {P_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ does not converge to $I$ in the uniform operator topology.

title: Sequences of Three Consecutive Strictly Increasing Euler Phi Values
snippet: The following sequences of $3$ consecutive positive integers have the property that their Euler $\phi$ values are strictly increasing: $\tuple {105, 106, 107}, \tuple {165, 166, 167}, \tuple {315, 316, 317}, \tuple {525, 526, 527}, \dots$

title: Sequential Characterization of Closed Linear Transformation
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be Banach spaces. Let $\map D T$ be a linear subspace of $X$. Let $T : \map D T 	o Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $T$ is closed : for each convergent sequence $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ valued in $\map D T$ such that $\sequence {T x_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges in $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$, we have: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} x_n \in \map D T$ and: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} T x_n = \map T {\lim_{n \mathop 	o \infty} x_n}$

title: Sequential Characterization of Limit at Minus Infinity of Real Function
snippet: Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $L$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \lim_{x \to -\infty} \map f x = L$ for all real sequences $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ with $x_n \to -\infty$ we have $\map f {x_n} \to L$ where: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to -\infty} \map f x$ denotes the limit at $-\infty$ of $f$.

title: Sequential Characterization of Limit at Positive Infinity of Real Function
snippet: Let $f : \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $L$ be a real number. Then: $\ds \lim_{x \to \infty} \map f x = L$ for all real sequences $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ with $x_n \to \infty$ we have $\map f {x_n} \to L$ where: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to \infty} \map f x$ denotes the limit at $+\infty$ of $f$.

title: Sequential Compactness is Preserved under Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous surjection. If $T_A$ is sequentially compact, then $T_B$ is also sequentially compact.

title: Sequential Continuity is Equivalent to Continuity in Metric Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ and $\struct {Y, e}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $x \in X$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$ $f$ is sequentially continuous at $x$.

title: Sequential Continuity is Equivalent to Continuity in the Reals
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers. Let $c \in A$. Let $f : A \to \R$ be a real function. Then $f$ is continuous at $c$ : for each sequence $\sequence {x_n}$ in $A$ that converges to $c$, the sequence $\sequence {\map f {x_n} }$ converges to $\map f c$.

title: Sequential Space is K2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is sequential. Then $T$ is a $k_2$-space.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Compact
snippet: A sequentially compact metric space is compact.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Complete
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space which is sequentially compact. Then $M$ is complete.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Lindelöf
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, d}$ be a sequentially compact metric space. Then $M$ is also a Lindelöf space. That is, from every open cover of $M$, it is possible to extract a countable subcover.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Second-Countable
snippet: A sequentially compact metric space is second-countable.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Separable
snippet: A sequentially compact metric space is separable.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Space is Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $M$ be sequentially compact. Then $M$ is totally bounded.

title: Sequentially Compact Metric Subspace is Sequentially Compact in Itself iff Closed
snippet: Let $M$ be a metric space. Let $C \subseteq M$ be a subspace of $M$ which is sequentially compact in $M$. Then $C$ is sequentially compact in itself $C$ is closed in $M$.

title: Sequentially Compact Space is Countably Compact
snippet: A sequentially compact topological space is also countably compact.

title: Sequentially Compact Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: A sequentially compact space is not necessarily also a compact space.

title: Serial Relation is not Null
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $S \ne \O$. Let $\RR$ be a serial relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is not a null relation.

title: Series Expansion for Pi Cosecant of Pi Lambda
snippet: Let $\lambda \in \R \setminus \Z$ be a real number which is not an integer. Then: $\ds \pi \csc \pi \lambda = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {-1}^n \paren {\frac 1 {n + \lambda} + \frac 1 {n - 1 - \lambda} }$

title: Series Expansion of Bessel Function of the First Kind
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a (strictly) non-negative integer. Let $\map {J_n} x$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$. Then: {{eqn | l = \map {J_n} x | r = \dfrac {x^n} {2^n \, \map \Gamma {n + 1} } \paren {1 - \dfrac {x^2} {2 \paren {2 n + 2} } + \dfrac {x^4} {2 \times 4 \paren {2 n + 2} \paren {2 n + 4} } - \cdots} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac {\paren {-1}^k} {k! \, \map \Gamma {n + k + 1} } \paren {\dfrac x 2}^{n + 2 k} | c = }}

title: Series Expansion of Function over Complete Orthonormal Set
snippet: Let $\map f x$ be a real function defined over the interval $\openint a b$. Let $\map f x$ be able to be expressed in terms of a complete orthonormal set of real functions $S := \family {\map {\phi_i} x}_{i \mathop \in I}$ for some indexing set $I$: $\map f x = \ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} a_i \map {\phi_i} x$ Then the coefficients $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ can be determined as: $\forall i \in I: a_i = \ds \int_a^b \map f x \map {\phi_i} x \rd x$

title: Series Expansion of Matrix Exponential
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Let $t \in \R$ be a real number. Let $e^{\mathbf A t}$ denote the matrix exponential of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\ds e^{\mathbf A t} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {t^n} {n!} \mathbf A^n$

snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a (strictly) non-negative integer. Let $\map {I_n} x$ denote the Modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $n$. Then: {{eqn | l = \map {I_n} x | r = \dfrac {x^n} {2^n \, \map \Gamma {n + 1} } \paren {1 + \dfrac {x^2} {2 \paren {2 n + 2} } + \dfrac {x^4} {2 \times 4 \paren {2 n + 2} \paren {2 n + 4} } + \cdots} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac 1 {k! \, \map \Gamma {n + k + 1} } \paren {\dfrac x 2}^{n + 2 k} | c = }}

title: Series Law for Extremal Length
snippet: Let $X$ be a Riemann surface. Let $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$ and $\Gamma$ be families of rectifiable curves (or, more generally, families of unions of rectifiable curves) on $X$. Let every $\gamma \in \Gamma$ contain a $\gamma_1 \in \Gamma_1$ and a $\gamma_2 \in \Gamma_2$ such that $\gamma_1 \cap \gamma_2 = \O$. Then the extremal lengths of $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$ and $\Gamma$ satisfy: $\map \lambda \Gamma \ge \map \lambda {\Gamma_1} + \map \lambda {\Gamma_2}$

title: Series is Weakly Unconditionally Cauchy iff Linear Transformation sending Schauder Basis of Space of Zero-Limit Sequences to Terms of Sequence is Bounded
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the Schauder basis for $\map {c_0} \GF$ given by Space of Zero-Limit Sequences admits Schauder Basis. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty x_n$ is weakly unconditionally Cauchy there exists a bounded linear transformation $T : \map {c_0} \GF \to X$ such that $T e_n = x_n$.

title: Series of Measures is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {\mu_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of measures on $\left({X, \Sigma}\right)$. Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \subseteq \R_{\ge 0}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers. Then the series of measures $\mu: \Sigma \to \overline \R$, defined by: $\ds \map \mu E := \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} a_n \map {\mu_n} E$ is also a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

title: Series of Positive Measurable Functions is Positive Measurable Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of positive measurable functions. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be the pointwise series of the $f_n$. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n$ is also a positive measurable function.

title: Series of Power over Factorial Converges
snippet: The series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {x^n} {n!}$ converges for all real values of $x$.

title: Series whose Terms Converge to Zero is not necessarily Convergent
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in any of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$, or $\C$. Suppose that $\sequence {a_n}$ converges to zero. Then it is not necessarily the case that the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ is itself convergent.

title: Serpent Climbing Out of a Well
snippet: == Classic Problem == A serpent lies at the bottom of a well $30$ length units deep. It starts to climb out of the well. Every day it climbs $\dfrac 2 3$ of a length unit, only to fall back $\dfrac 1 5$ of a length unit every night. How long does it take to climb out of the well?

snippet: The serpentine is the locus of an odd function: 600px

title: Set/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Sets ==

title: Set Closure Preserves Set Inclusion
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $B \subseteq A \subseteq S$. Then: $B^- \subseteq A^-$ where $A^-$ and $B^-$ are the set closures in $T$ of $A$ and $B$ respectively.

title: Set Closure as Intersection of Closed Sets
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Let the closure of $H$ (in $T$) be defined as: $H^- := H \cup H'$ where $H'$ is the derived set of $H$. Let $\mathbb K$ be defined as: $\mathbb K := \leftset {K \supseteq H: K}$ is closed in $\rightset T$ That is, let $\mathbb K$ be the set of all closed sets of $T$ which contain $H$. Then the closure of $H$ (in $T$) can be defined as: $\ds H^- := \bigcap \mathbb K$ that is, as the intersection of all the closed sets of $T$ which contain $H$.

title: Set Closure is Smallest Closed Set
Set Coarser than Upper Section is Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $A$ is coarser than $B$ and $B$ is an upper section. Then: $A \subseteq B$

title: Set Complement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Complement ==

title: Set Complement inverts Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $S \subseteq T \iff \map \complement T \subseteq \map \complement S$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $\complement$ denotes set complement.

title: Set Consisting of Empty Set is not Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be the set defined as: $S = \set \O$ Then $S$ is not the empty set. That is: $\O \ne \set \O$

title: Set Contained in Smallest Transitive Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists a transitive set $G$ such that: $S \subseteq G$ and: if $Q$ is any transitive set such that $S \subseteq Q$, then $G \subseteq Q$.

title: Set Containing Only Zero is Primitive Recursive
snippet: The subset $\left\{{0}\right\} \subset \N$ is primitive recursive.

title: Set Definition by Predicate/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Definition by Predicate ==

title: Set Difference/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Difference ==

title: Set Difference Equals First Set iff Sets are Disjoint
snippet: $S \setminus T = S \iff S \cap T = \O$

title: Set Difference Intersection with First Set is Set Difference
snippet: The intersection of the set difference with the first set is the set difference. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cap S = S \setminus T$

title: Set Difference Intersection with Second Set is Empty Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. The intersection of the set difference of $S$ and $T$ with $T$ is the empty set: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cap T = \O$

title: Set Difference Then Union Equals Union Then Set Difference
snippet: Let $S, A, B$ be sets. Let $A \cap B = \O$. Then: $\paren {S \setminus A} \cup B = \paren {S \cup B} \setminus A$

title: Set Difference Union First Set is First Set
snippet: The union of a set difference with the first set is the set itself: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cup S = S$

title: Set Difference Union Intersection
snippet: $S = \paren {S \setminus T} \cup \paren {S \cap T}$

title: Set Difference Union Second Set is Union
snippet: The union of a set difference with the second set is the union of the two sets. That is, let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cup T = S \cup T$

title: Set Difference and Intersection are Disjoint
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $S \setminus T$ and $S \cap T$ are disjoint where $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference and $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

title: Set Difference and Intersection form Partition
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that: $S \setminus T \ne \O$ $S \cap T \ne \O$ where $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference and $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection. Then $S \setminus T$ and $S \cap T$ form a partition of $S$.

title: Set Difference as Intersection with Complement
snippet: Set difference can be expressed as the intersection with the set complement: $A \setminus B = A \cap \map \complement B$

title: Set Difference as Intersection with Relative Complement
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq S$. Then the set difference between $A$ and $B$ can be expressed as the intersection with the relative complement with respect to $S$: $A \setminus B = A \cap \relcomp S B$

title: Set Difference as Symmetric Difference with Intersection
snippet: $S \setminus T = S \symdif \paren {S \cap T}$ where: $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference $S \symdif T$ denotes set symmetric difference $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

title: Set Difference is Anticommutative
snippet: Set difference is an anticommutative operation: $S = T \iff S \setminus T = T \setminus S = \O$

title: Set Difference is Disjoint with Reverse
snippet: $\paren {S \setminus T} \cap \paren {T \setminus S} = \O$

title: Set Difference is Right Distributive over Set Intersection
snippet: Let $A, B, C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \setminus C = \paren {A \setminus C} \cap \paren {B \setminus C}$ where: $A \cap B$ denotes set intersection $A \setminus C$ denotes set difference. That is, set difference is right distributive over set intersection.

title: Set Difference is Right Distributive over Union
snippet: Set difference is right distributive over union. Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \cup S} \setminus T = \paren {R \setminus T} \cup \paren {S \setminus T}$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cup T$ denotes set union.

title: Set Difference is Set
snippet: Let $x$ be a small class. Let $A$ be a class. Let $\map \MM B$ denote that $B$ is small. Then: $\map \MM {x \setminus A}$

title: Set Difference is Subset
snippet: Set difference is a subset of the first set: $S \setminus T \subseteq S$

title: Set Difference is Subset of Union of Differences
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus S \subseteq \paren {R \setminus T} \cup \paren {T \setminus S}$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes subset $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference $S \cup T$ denotes set union.

title: Set Difference is not Associative
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. The expression: $\paren {R \setminus S} \setminus T = R \setminus \paren {S \setminus T}$ holds exactly when $R \cap T = \O$. Here $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference. Thus, set difference is not associative.

title: Set Difference of Cartesian Products
snippet: $\paren {S_1 \times S_2} \setminus \paren {T_1 \times T_2} = \paren {S_1 \times \paren {S_2 \setminus T_2} } \cup \paren {\paren {S_1 \setminus T_1} \times S_2}$

title: Set Difference of Complements
snippet: $\map \complement S \setminus \map \complement T = T \setminus S$

title: Set Difference of Doubleton and Singleton is Singleton
snippet: Let $x, y$ be distinct objects. Then: $\set{x, y} \setminus \set x = \set y$

title: Set Difference of Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $A, B \in \Sigma \implies A \setminus B \in \Sigma$ That is, the difference of two events is also an event in the event space.

title: Set Difference of Intersection with Set is Empty Set
snippet: The set difference of the intersection of two sets with one of those sets is the empty set. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cap T} \setminus S = \O$ $\paren {S \cap T} \setminus T = \O$

title: Set Difference of Larger Set with Smaller is Not Empty
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $\card S > \card T$. Then: $S \setminus T \ne \O$

title: Set Difference of Matroid Dependent Set with Independent Set is Non-empty
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $I$ be an independent subset of $M$. Let $D$ be a dependent subset of $M$. Then: $D \setminus I \ne \O$

title: Set Difference of Relations Compatible with Group Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\RR, \QQ$ be relations on $G$ which are compatible with $\circ$. Then the difference $\RR \setminus \QQ$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Set Difference over Subset
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, and $S$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq B$. Then: $A \setminus S \subseteq B \setminus S$

title: Set Difference with Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $S \cap T = \O \iff S \setminus T = S$ where: $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection $\O$ denotes the empty set $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference.

title: Set Difference with Empty Set is Self
snippet: The set difference between a set and the empty set is the set itself: $S \setminus \O = S$

title: Set Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets.

title: Set Difference with Intersection is Difference
snippet: The set difference with the intersection is just the set difference. Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $S \setminus \paren {S \cap T} = S \setminus T$

title: Set Difference with Non-Empty Proper Subset is Non-Empty Proper Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subsetneq S$ be a non-empty proper subset of $S$. Let $S \setminus T$ denote the set difference between $S$ and $T$. Then: $S \setminus T$ is a non-empty proper subset of $S$

title: Set Difference with Proper Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subsetneq S$ be a proper subset of $S$. Let $S \setminus T$ denote the set difference between $S$ and $T$. Then: $S \setminus T \ne \O$ where $\O$ denotes the empty set.

title: Set Difference with Self is Empty Set
snippet: The set difference of a set with itself is the empty set: $S \setminus S = \O$

title: Set Difference with Set Difference
snippet: The set difference with the set difference of two sets is the intersection of the two sets: $S \setminus \paren {S \setminus T} = S \cap T = T \setminus \paren {T \setminus S}$

title: Set Difference with Set Difference is Union of Set Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus \paren {S \setminus T} = \paren {R \setminus S} \cup \paren {R \cap T}$ where: $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference $S \cup T$ denotes set union $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

title: Set Difference with Subset is Superset of Set Difference
snippet: Let $A, B, S$ be sets or classes. Suppose that $A \subseteq B$. Then: $S \setminus B \subseteq S \setminus A$ where $\setminus$ represents set difference.

title: Set Difference with Superset is Empty Set
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \setminus T = \O$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \setminus T$ denotes the set difference between $S$ and $T$ $\O$ denotes the empty set.

title: Set Difference with Union
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \setminus \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \cup T} \setminus \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \setminus S} \setminus T = \paren {R \setminus T} \setminus S$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cup T$ denotes set union.

title: Set Difference with Union is Set Difference
snippet: The set difference between two sets is the same as the set difference between their union and the second of the two sets: Let $S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cup T} \setminus T = S \setminus T$

title: Set Equality is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Set equality is an equivalence relation on the power set $\powerset S$ of $S$.

title: Set Equals Itself
snippet: All sets are equal to themselves: $\forall S: S = S$

title: Set Equation:Intersection
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Consider the set equation: $A \cap X = B$ The solution set of this is: $\O$ if $B \nsubseteq A$ $\set {B \cup Y: A \nsubseteq Y}$ otherwise.

title: Set Equation:Union
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Consider the set equation: $A \cup X = B$ The solution set of this is given by: $X = \begin {cases} \O & : A \nsubseteq B \\ \set {\paren {B \setminus A} \cup Y: Y \subseteq A} & : \text {otherwise} \end {cases}$

title: Set Equivalence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Set Equivalence ==

title: Set Equivalence Less One Element
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets which are equivalent: $S \sim T$ Let $a \in S$ and $b \in T$. Then: $S \setminus \set a \sim T \setminus \set b$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Set Equivalence behaves like Equivalence Relation
snippet: Set equivalence behaves like an equivalence relation. That is: where $S, T, S_1, S_2, S_3$ are sets.

title: Set Equivalence of Regular Representations
snippet: If $S$ is a finite subset of a group $G$, then: $\card {a \circ S} = \card S = \left|{S \circ a}\right|$ That is, $a \circ S$, $S$ and $S \circ a$ are equivalent: $a \circ S \sim S \sim S \circ a$.

title: Set Finite iff Injection to Initial Segment of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is finite for some $n \in \N$ there exists an injection $f: S \to \N_{< n}$. Here, $\N_{< n}$ denotes an initial segment of $\N$.

title: Set Finite iff Surjection from Initial Segment of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then $S$ is finite for some $n \in \N$ there exists a surjection $f: \N_{<n} \to S$. Here, $\N_{<n}$ denotes an initial segment of $\N$.

title: Set Inequality
snippet:
