orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ is a unital Banach algebra.

title: Space of Bounded Linear Operators on Hilbert Space is Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\map B \HH$ be the space of bounded linear operators. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B \HH}$ be the operator norm on $\map B \HH$. Let $\ast : \map B \HH \to \map B \HH$ denote the adjoint operation. Then $\struct {\map B \HH, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B \HH} }$ is a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

title: Space of Bounded Linear Transformations forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $\map B {X, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations from $X$ to $Y$. Let $+_B$ and $\circ_B$ be pointwise addition and pointwise scalar multiplication on $Y^X$. Then $\struct {\map B {X, Y}, +_B, \circ_B}_\GF$ is a vector space.

title: Space of Bounded Linear Transformations is Banach Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector spaces over $\GF$. Let $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\map B {X, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations from $X$ to $Y$ endowed with pointwise addition and ($\Bbb F$)-scalar multiplication. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {X, Y} }$ be the norm on the space of bounded linear transformations. Then $\struct {\map B {X, Y}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B {X, Y} } }$ is a Banach space.

title: Space of Bounded Sequences Supported on Subset of Natural Numbers is Closed Vector Subspace of Space of Bounded Sequences
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $A \subseteq \N$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of bounded sequences. Let: $\map {\ell_\infty} {A, \GF} = \set {\xi \in \map {\ell_\infty} \N : \map \xi n = 0 	ext { for } n \in \N \setminus A}$ Equip $\map {\ell_\infty} {A, \GF}$ with pointwise addition and pointwise scalar multiplication. Then $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} {A, \GF}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a closed vector subspace of $\struct {\map {\ell_\infty} {\N, \GF}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

title: Space of Bounded Sequences with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication on Ring of Sequences forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\map {\ell^\infty} \C$ be the space of bounded sequences on $\C$. Let $\struct {\C, +_\C, \times_\C}$ be the field of complex numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition on the ring of sequences. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise multiplication on the ring of sequences. Then $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} \C, +, \, \cdot \,}_\C$ is a vector space.

title: Space of Bounded Sequences with Supremum Norm forms Banach Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} \R, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the normed vector space of bounded sequences on $\R$. Then $\struct {\map {\ell^\infty} \R, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a Banach space.

title: Space of Bounded Sequences with Supremum Norm forms Normed Vector Space
snippet: The vector space of bounded sequences with the supremum norm forms a normed vector space.

title: Space of Compact Linear Transformations is Banach Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R,\C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be a Banach space oer $\GF$. Let $\map \KK {X, Y}$ be the space of compact linear transformations from $H$ to $K$. Now $\map \KK {X, Y} \subseteq Y^X$, where $Y^X$ is the set of mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Therefore, $\map \KK {X, Y}$ can be endowed with pointwise addition ($+$) and ($\GF$)-scalar multiplication ($\circ$). Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {X, Y} }$ denote the norm on bounded linear operators.

title: Space of Complex-Valued Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space is Separable iff Space is Metrizable
snippet: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map \CC K$ be the space of complex-valued continuous functions of compact Hausdorff space. Then $\map \CC K$ is separable the topology on $K$ is metrizable.

title: Space of Continuous Functions Vanishing at Infinity is C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\map {\CC_0} X$ be the set of continuous complex-valued functions vanishing at infinity. Equip $\map {\CC_0} X$ with pointwise addition, pointwise scalar multiplication and pointwise multiplication. For each $f \in \map {\CC_0} X$, define: $\map {\overline f} x = \overline {\map f x}$ for each $x \in X$. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\map {\CC_0} X$. Then $\tuple {\map {\CC_0} X, \overline {\, \cdot \,}, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a $\text C^\ast$-algebra.

title: Space of Continuous Functions on Locally Compact Hausdorff Space Vanishing at Infinity is Banach Space
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\struct {\map {\CC_0} X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of continuous functions on $X$ vanishing at infinity. Then $\struct {\map {\CC_0} X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a Banach space over $\C$.

title: Space of Continuous Functions on Locally Compact Hausdorff Space Vanishing in Neighborhood of Infinity is Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff space. Let $\struct {\map {\CC_{00} } X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of continuous functions on $X$ vanishing in a neighborhood of infinity. Then $\struct {\map {\CC_{00} } X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a normed vector space over $\C$.

title: Space of Continuous on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\map C I$ be the space of real-valued functions continuous on $I$. Let $\struct {\R, +_\R, \times_\R}$ be the field of real numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition of real-valued functions. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise scalar multiplication of real-valued functions. Then $\struct {\map C I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ is a vector space.

title: Space of Continuous on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with Supremum Norm forms Banach Space
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\map C I$ be the space of real-valued functions, continuous on $I$. Let $\norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on real-valued functions, continuous on $I$. Then $\struct {\map C I, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_\infty}$ is a Banach space.

title: Space of Continuous on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with Supremum Norm forms Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. The space of continuous real-valued functions on $I$ with supremum norm forms a normed vector space.

title: Space of Continuously Differentiable on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with C^1 Norm forms Normed Vector Space
snippet: Space of Continuously Differentiable on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with $C^1$ norm forms a normed vector space.

title: Space of Continuously Differentiable on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with C^1 Norm is Banach Space
snippet:
Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\map C I$ be the space of real-valued functions continuous on $I$. Let $\map {C^1} I$ be the space of real-valued functions, continuously differentiable on $I$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{1, \infty}$ be the $\CC^1$ norm. $\struct {\map {C^1} I, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{1, \infty} }$ be the normed space of real-valued functions, continuously differentiable on $I$. Then $\struct {\map {C^1} I, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{1, \infty} }$ is a Banach space.

title: Space of Continuously Differentiable on Closed Interval Real-Valued Functions with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $I := \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\map C I$ be a space of real-valued functions continuous on $I$. Let $\map {C^1} I$ be a space of continuously differentiable functions on $I$. Let $\struct {\R, +_\R, \times_\R}$ be the field of real numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition of real-valued functions. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise scalar multiplication of real-valued functions. Then $\struct {\map {C^1} I, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ is a vector space.

title: Space of Integrable Functions Under Pointwise Addition forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\LL^1} \mu$ be the space of real-valued $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $\map {\LL^1} \mu$, endowed with pointwise addition, forms an abelian group over $\map {\LL^1} \mu$.

title: Space of Integrable Functions is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\LL^1} \mu$ be the space of real-valued $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $\map {\LL^1} \mu$, endowed with pointwise $\R$-scalar multiplication and pointwise addition, forms a vector space over $\R$.

title: Space of Lipschitz Functions is Banach Space/Shift of Finite Type
snippet: Let $\struct {X _\mathbf A, \sigma_\mathbf A}$ be a shift of finite type. Let $\theta \in \openint 0 1$. Let $F_\theta$ be the Lipschitz space on $X _\mathbf A$. Let $\norm \cdot_\theta$ be the Lipschitz norm on $F_\theta$. Then $\struct {F_\theta, \norm \cdot_\theta}$ is a Banach space.

title: Space of Piecewise Linear Functions on Closed Interval is Dense in Space of Continuous Functions on Closed Interval
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b$. Let $\map \CC I$ be the set of continuous functions on $I$. Let $\map {\mathrm {PL} } I$ be the set of piecewise linear functions on $I$. Let $d$ be the metric induced by the supremum norm. Then $\map {\mathrm {PL} } I$ is dense in $\struct {\map \CC I, d}$.

title: Space of Real-Valued Measurable Functions Identified by A.E. Equality is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R}$ be the set of real-valued $\Sigma$-measurable functions on $X$. Let $\sim_\mu$ be the almost-everywhere equality relation on $\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R}$ with respect to $\mu$. Let $+$ denote pointwise addition on $\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R} / \sim_\mu$. Let $\cdot$ be pointwise scalar multiplication on $\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R} / \sim_\mu$. Then: $\struct {\map \MM {X, \Sigma, \R} / \sim_\mu, +, \cdot}_\R$ forms a vector space.

title: Space of Simple P-Integrable Functions is Everywhere Dense in Lebesgue Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p \in \R$, $p \ge 1$. Let $\map {\LL^p} \mu$ be Lebesgue $p$-space for $\mu$. Let $\map \EE \Sigma \cap \map {\LL^p} \mu$ be the space of $\Sigma$-simple, $p$-integrable functions. Then $\map \EE \Sigma \cap \map {\LL^p} \mu$ is everywhere dense in $\map {\LL^p} \mu$ with respect to the seminorm topology generated by the singleton $\set {\norm {\; \cdot \;}_p }$. That is, for all $f \in \map {\LL^p} \mu$ and $\epsilon > 0$ there exists a $g \in \map \EE \Sigma \cap \map {\LL^p} \mu$ such that: $\norm {f - g}_p < \epsilon$

title: Space of Somewhere Differentiable Continuous Functions on Closed Interval is Meager in Space of Continuous Functions on Closed Interval
snippet: Let $I = \closedint a b$. Let $\map \CC I$ be the set of continuous functions on $I$. Let $\map \DD I$ be the set of continuous functions on $I$ that are differentiable at a point. Let $d$ be the metric induced by the supremum norm. Then $\map \DD I$ is meager in $\struct {\map \CC I, d}$.

title: Space of Square Summable Mappings is Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\map {\ell^2} I$ be the space of square summable mappings over $I$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot: \map {\ell^2} I \times \map {\ell^2} I \to \GF$ be the inner product on $\map {\ell^2} I$. Then $\map {\ell^2} I$ endowed with $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a Hilbert space.

title: Space of Square Summable Mappings is L-2 Space
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\map {\ell^2} I$ be the space of square summable mappings over $I$. Then $\map {\ell^2} I$ is equal to the $L^2$ space $\map {L^2} {I, \powerset I, \mu}$, where $\mu$ is the counting measure on $I$.

title: Space of Square Summable Mappings is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $I$ be a set. Let $\map {\ell^2} I$ be the space of square summable mappings over $I$. Then $\map {\ell^2} I$ is a vector space.

title: Space of Zero-Limit Sequences admits Schauder Basis
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Define $e_n \in \map {c_0} \GF$ by: $\ds \map {e_n} k =  egin{cases}1 & n = k \ 0 & n 
e k\end{cases}$ Then $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Schauder basis for $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

title: Space of Zero-Limit Sequences is not Injective
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Then $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is not injective.

title: Space of Zero-Limit Sequences with Supremum Norm forms Banach Space
snippet: Let $c_0$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm. Then $\struct {c_0, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ is a Banach space.

title: Space such that Intersection of Open Sets containing Point is Singleton may not be Hausdorff
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$ be arbitrary. Let $T$ be such that the intersection of all open sets containing $x$ is $\set x$: $\ds \bigcap_{\substack {H \mathop \in \tau \\ x \mathop \in H} } = \set x$ Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Space which is T3 and T0 is also T2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is both a $T_3$ space and a $T_0$ space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Space with Open Point is Non-Meager
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$ be an open point. Then $T$ is a non-meager space.

title: Space with no Nontrivial Separation has no Nontrivial Clopen Subsets
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space.

title: Spaces of Continuous Functions on Homeomorphic Compact Hausdorff Spaces are Isometrically *-Algebra Isomorphic
snippet: Let $K, L$ be homeomorphic compact Hausdorff spaces. Let $\map \CC K$ and $\map \CC L$ be the spaces of continuous functions on $K$ and $L$ respectively. Then $\map \CC K$ and $\map \CC L$ are isometrically $\ast$-algebra isomorphic.

title: Spacing Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $X_{\paren i}$ be the $i$th ordered statistic of $N$ samples from a continuous random distribution with density function $\map {f_X} x$. Then the spacing between the ordered statistics given $X_{\paren i}$ converges in distribution to exponential for sufficiently large sampling according to: $N \paren {X_{\paren {i + 1} } - X_{\paren i} } \xrightarrow D \map \exp {\dfrac 1 {\map f { X_{\paren i} } } }$ as $N \to \infty$ for $i = 1, 2, 3, \dotsc, N - 1$.

title: Span of Exponential of a x by Cosine of b x and Exponential of a x by Sine of b x is preserved under Differentiation wrt x
snippet: Let $a, b, x, \alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in \R$ be real numbers. Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be the real functions defined as: {{eqn | q = \forall x \in \R | l = \map {f_1} x | r = \map \exp {a x} \map \cos {b x} }} {{eqn | l = \map {f_2} x | r = \map \exp {a x} \map \sin {b x} }} Let $\map \CC \R$ be the space of continuous real-valued functions. Let $\tuple {\map {\CC^1} \R, +, \, \cdot \,}_\R$ be the vector space of continuously differentiable real-valued functions. Let $S = \set {f_1, f_2} \subset \map {\CC^1} \R$ be a vector space. Let $\map \span S$ be the span of $S$.

title: Spanning Criterion of Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the vector space of bounded linear functionals on $X$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be a subset. Let $\vee A$ be the closed linear span of $A$, i.e. the closure of the linear span of $A$. Then $z \in \vee A$ : $\forall \ell \in X^\ast : \ell \restriction_A = 0 \implies \map \ell z = 0$ where $\ell \restriction_A$ denotes the restriction of $\ell$ to $A$.

title: Special Linear Group is Normal Subgroup of General Linear Group
snippet: Let $K$ be a field whose zero is $0_K$ and unity is $1_K$. Let $\SL {n, K}$ be the special linear group of order $n$ over $K$. Then $\SL {n, K}$ is a normal subgroup of the general linear group $\GL {n, K}$.

title: Special Linear Group is Subgroup of General Linear Group
snippet: Let $K$ be a field whose zero is $0_K$ and unity is $1_K$. Let $\SL {n, K}$ be the special linear group of order $n$ over $K$. Then $\SL {n, K}$ is a subgroup of the general linear group $\GL {n, K}$.

title: Special Linear Group is not Abelian
snippet: Let $K$ be a field whose zero is $0_K$ and unity is $1_K$. Let $\SL {n, K}$ be the special linear group of order $n$ over $K$. Then $\SL {n, K}$ is not an abelian group.

title: Special Orthogonal Group is Group
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. The $n$th orthogonal group on $k$ is a group.

title: Special Orthogonal Group is Subgroup of Orthogonal Group
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $\map {\operatorname O} {n, k}$ be the $n$th orthogonal group on $k$. Let $\map {\operatorname {SO} } {n, k}$ be the $n$th special orthogonal group on $k$. Then $\map {\operatorname {SO} } {n, k}$ is a subgroup of $\map {\operatorname O} {n, k}$.

title: Spectral Mapping Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be normal. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Let $\map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x}$ be the space of continuous functions on $\map {\sigma_A} x$. Let $f \in \map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x}$. Let $\map {\Theta_x} f = \map f x$ be the continuous functional calculus of $x$ applied to $f$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} {\map f x} = f \sqbrk {\map {\sigma_A} x}$

title: Spectral Mapping Theorem for Polynomials
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $p : \C \to \C$ be a polynomial with: $\ds \map p z = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n a_j z^j$ for all $z \in \C$, for some $a_0, \ldots, a_n \in \C$. Define: $\ds \map p y = a_0 {\mathbf 1}_A + \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n a_j y^j$ for each $y \in A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_A} {\map p x}$ be the spectrum of $x$ and $\map p x$ respectively. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} {\map p x} = p \sqbrk {\map {\sigma_A} x}$

title: Spectral Permanence Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a closed unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_B} x$ be the spectra of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $\map {\rho_A} x$ and $\map {\rho_B} x$ be the resolvent sets of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then there exists a indexed family $\family {U_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ of bounded components of $\map {\rho_A} x$ such that: $\ds \map {\sigma_B} x = \map {\sigma_A} x \cup \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} U_i$ Further, $I$ can be made countable.

title: Spectral Radius is Multiplicative on Commuting Elements in Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x, y \in A$ be commuting elements of $A$. Let $r_A$ denote spectral radius in $A$. Then we have: $\map {r_A} {x y} \le \map {r_A} x \map {r_A} y$

title: Spectral Radius is Subadditive on Commuting Elements in Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x, y \in A$ be commuting elements of $A$. Let $r_A$ denote spectral radius in $A$. Then we have: $\map {r_A} {x + y} \le \map {r_A} x + \map {r_A} y$

title: Spectral Radius of Element of Commutative Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a commutative Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\Phi_A$ be the spectrum of $A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$. Let $\map {r_A} x$ be the spectral radius of $x$. Then: $\ds \map {r_A} x = \sup_{\phi \in \Phi_A} \cmod {\map \phi x}$

title: Spectral Radius of Normal Element of C*-Algebra Equal to Norm
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $r_A$ be the spectral radius in $A$. Let $x \in A$ be normal. Then $\map {r_A} x = \norm x$.

title: Spectral Theorem
snippet: A spectral theorem is a statement about how certain types of matrix or linear operator can always be diagonalized.

title: Spectral Theorem for Anti-Hermitian Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $\mathbb C$. Then $\mathbf A$ is anti-Hermitian it is diagonalizable to an imaginary diagonal matrix via a unitary transformation. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where: $\mathbf D$ is an imaginary diagonal matrix $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$.

title: Spectral Theorem for Compact Hermitian Operators
snippet:
Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space. Let $T \in \map {B_0} \HH$ be a compact Hermitian operator. Then there exists a (possibly finite) sequence $\sequence {\lambda_n}$ of distinct nonzero eigenvalues of $T$ such that: $(1): \quad P_n P_m = P_m P_n = 0$ if $n 
e m$ $(2): \quad \ds \lim_{k \mathop 	o \infty} 
orm {T - \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^k \lambda_n P_n} = 0$, that is, $T = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \lambda_n P_n$ where: $P_n$ is the orthogonal projection onto the eigenspace of $\lambda_n$ $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the norm on bounded linear operators.

title: Spectral Theorem for Hermitian Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $\mathbb C$. Then $\mathbf A$ is Hermitian it is diagonalizable to a real diagonal matrix via a unitary transformation. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where: $\mathbf D$ is a real diagonal matrix $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$.

title: Spectral Theorem for Normal Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $\mathbb C$. Then $\mathbf A$ is normal it is diagonalizable by a unitary transformation. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf D$ is a diagonal matrix

title: Spectral Theorem for Real Anti-Symmetric Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $\R$. Then $\mathbf A$ is anti-symmetric it is diagonalizable to an imaginary diagonal matrix via a unitary transformation. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where: $\mathbf D$ is an imaginary diagonal matrix $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$.

title: Spectral Theorem for Real Orthogonal Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix over $\R$. Then, $\mathbf A$ is orthogonal it is diagonalizable via a unitary transformation to a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are of unit modulus which occur in conjugate pairs. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf D$ is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are of unit modulus which occur in conjugate pairs $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$

title: Spectral Theorem for Real Symmetric Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Then $\mathbf A$ is a real symmetric matrix it is diagonalizable to a real diagonal matrix via an orthogonal transformation. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\intercal$ where: $\mathbf D$ is a real diagonal matrix $\mathbf U$ is a real orthogonal matrix $\mathbf U^\intercal$ is the transpose of $\mathbf U$.

title: Spectral Theorem for Unitary Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix. Then, $\mathbf A$ is a unitary matrix it is diagonalizable via a unitary transformation to a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are of unit modulus. That is, we can write: $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf U^\dagger$ where $\mathbf U$ is a unitary matrix $\mathbf D$ is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal elements are of unit modulus $\mathbf U^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf U$

title: Spectrum Functor is Covariant Functor
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Loc}$ denote the category of locales. Let $\mathbf{Top}$ denote the category of topological spaces. Then: the spectrum functor $\operatorname {Sp} : \mathbf{Loc} \to \mathbf{Top}$ is a covariant functor

title: Spectrum of Adjoint of Bounded Linear Operator
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $T^\ast : X \to X$ be the adjoint of $T$. Let $\map \sigma T$ and $\map \sigma {T^\ast}$ be the spectrum of $T$ and $T^\ast$ respectively. Then: $\map \sigma {T^\ast} = \set {\overline \lambda : \lambda \in \map \sigma T}$ where $\overline \lambda$ denotes the complex conjugate of $\lambda$.

title: Spectrum of Banach Algebra is Weak-* Locally Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\struct {\Phi_A, w^\ast}$ be the spectrum of $A$. Then $\struct {\Phi_A, w^\ast}$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space.

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator contains Point Spectrum
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_p} T$ be the point spectrum of $T$. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then $\map {\sigma_p} T \subseteq \map \sigma T$.

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator equal to Spectrum as Densely-Defined Linear Operator
snippet: Let $\HH$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_1} T$ be the spectrum of $T$ as a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_2} T$ be the spectrum of $T$ as a densely-defined linear operator $\struct {\HH, T}$. Then: $\map {\sigma_1} T = \map {\sigma_2} T$

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot_X}$ be a Banach space over $\C$.. Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $X$. Then the spectrum $\map \sigma T$ of $T$ is a closed set in $\C$.

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator is Compact
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then $\map \sigma T$ is compact, and: $\map \sigma T \subseteq \set {\lambda \in \C : \cmod \lambda \le \norm T_{\map \BB X} }$

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $B$ be a Banach space over $\C$. Let $\map {\mathfrak L} {B, B}$ be the set of bounded linear operators from $B$ to itself. Let $T \in \map {\mathfrak L} {B, B}$. Then the spectrum $\map \sigma T$ of $T$ is non-empty.

title: Spectrum of Bounded Linear Operator on Finite-Dimensional Banach Space is equal to Point Spectrum
snippet: Let $X$ be a finite-dimensional Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. Let $\map {\sigma_p} T$ be the point spectrum of $T$. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then $\map \sigma T = \map {\sigma_p} T$.

snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a commutative $	ext C^\ast$-algebra such that: $A

title: Spectrum of Compact Linear Operator on Infinite-Dimensional Banach Space contains Zero
snippet: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space over $\C$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a compact linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then $0 \in \map \sigma T$. That is, $T$ is not invertible as a bounded linear operator.

title: Spectrum of Element in Maximal Commutative Subalgebra of Unital Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra. Let $C$ be a commutative subalgebra of $A$ that is maximal with respect to set inclusion. Let $x \in C$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_C} x$ be the spectra of $x$ in $A$ and $C$ respectively. Then: $\map {\sigma_C} x = \map {\sigma_A} x$

title: Spectrum of Element in Unital Subalgebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a unital algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a unital subalgebra of $A$. Let $x \in B$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_B} x$ be the spectra of $x$ in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \map {\sigma_B} x$

title: Spectrum of Element in Unitization of Unital Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a unital algebra over $\C$. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Let $a \in A$. Then: $\map {\sigma_{A_+} } {\tuple {a, 0} } = \map {\sigma_A} a \cup \set 0$ where $\sigma_{A_+}$ and $\sigma_A$ denote the spectrum in $A_+$ and $A$ respectively.

title: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is bounded, and in particular: $\cmod \lambda \le \norm x$ for all $\lambda \in \map {\sigma_A} x$

title: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is closed.

title: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is compact.

title: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \ne \O$.

title: Spectrum of Element of Space of Continuous Functions Vanishing at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $A = \map {\CC_0} X$ be the Banach algebra of continuous complex-valued functions vanishing at infinity. Let $f \in \map {\CC_0} X$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} f = f \sqbrk X \cup \set 0$ where $\sigma_A$ denotes the spectrum in $A$.

title: Spectrum of Element of Space of Continuous Functions on Compact Hausdorff Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $A = \map \CC K$ be the space of continuous functions on $K$ considered as a Banach algebra. Let $f \in \map \CC K$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} f = f \sqbrk K$ where $\sigma_A$ denotes spectrum in $A$.

title: Spectrum of Element of Unital C*-Subalgebra of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra with identity element ${\mathbf 1}_A$. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Let $\sigma_A$ and $\sigma_B$ be the spectrum in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $x \in B$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \map {\sigma_B} x$

title: Spectrum of Element of Unital Commutative Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a commutative unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\Phi_A$ be the spectrum of $A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \set {\map \phi x : \phi \in \Phi_A}$

title: Spectrum of Hermitian Element in Unital C*-Algebra is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be Hermitian. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \R$.

title: Spectrum of Idempotent in Algebra over Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ be an algebra over $\C$. Let $p \in A$ be idempotent, that is: $p^2 = p$ Let $\map {\sigma_A} p$ be the spectrum of $p$ in $A$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} p \subseteq \set {0, 1}$

title: Spectrum of Identity Element of Unital Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a unital algebra over $\C$ with at least two distinct elements. Let $\sigma_A$ be the spectrum in $A$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} { {\mathbf 1}_A} = \set 1$

title: Spectrum of Image of Element of Unital Algebra under Unital Algebra Homomorphism
snippet: Let $A, B$ be unital algebras over $\C$. Let $\phi : A \to B$ be a unital algebra homomorphism. Let $x \in A$. We then have: $\map {\sigma_B} {\map \phi x} \subseteq \map {\sigma_A} x$ where $\sigma_A$ and $\sigma_B$ denote spectra in $A$ and $B$ respectively. If $\phi$ is a unital algebra isomorphism, we further have $\map {\sigma_B} {\map \phi x} = \map {\sigma_A} x$.

title: Spectrum of Inverse of Element of Unital Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be an algebra over $\C$. Let $a \in A$ be invertible. Let $\sigma_A$ denote the spectrum in $A$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} {a^{-1} } = \set {\lambda^{-1} : \lambda \in \map {\sigma_A} a}$

title: Spectrum of Locale as Completely Prime Filters is Sober Space
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ denote the spectrum as completely prime filters of $L$. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ is a sober space.

title: Spectrum of Locale is Sober Space
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale. Let $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ denote the spectrum of $L$. Then: $\map {\operatorname{Sp}} L$ is a sober space.

title: Spectrum of Product of Elements of Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\sigma_A$ denote spectrum in $A$. Let $x, y \in A$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} {x y} \setminus \set 0 = \map {\sigma_A} {y x} \setminus \set 0$

title: Spectrum of Projection in *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $p$ be a projection on $A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} p$ be the spectrum of $p$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} p \subseteq \set {0, 1}$.

title: Spectrum of Ring is Nonempty
snippet: Let $A$ be a non-trivial commutative ring with unity. Then its prime spectrum is non-empty: $\Spec A \ne \O$

title: Spectrum of Self-Adjoint Bounded Linear Operator is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $T : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded self-adjoint operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $T$. Then: $\map \sigma T \subseteq \R$

title: Spectrum of Self-Adjoint Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Real and Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\map D T, T}$ be a self-adjoint densely-defined linear operator. Let $\map \sigma T$ be the spectrum of $\struct {\map D T, T}$. Then $\map \sigma T$ is a closed subset of $\C$ and: $\map \sigma T \subseteq \R$

title: Spectrum of Star of Element in *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a unital $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $a \in A$. Let $\sigma_A$ denote the spectrum. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} {a^\ast} = \set {\overline \lambda : \lambda \in \map {\sigma_A} a}$

title: Spectrum of Unitary Element in Unital C*-Algebra is Subset of Unit Circle
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be unitary. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \set {z \in \C : \cmod z = 1}$.

title: Spectrum of Zero Vector in Algebra
snippet: Let $A$ be an algebra over $\C$. Let ${\mathbf 0}_A$ be the zero vector of $A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} { {\mathbf 0}_A}$ be the spectrum of ${\mathbf 0}_A$ in $A$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} { {\mathbf 0}_A} = \set 0$ if $A \ne \set { {\mathbf 0}_A}$ $\map {\sigma_A} { {\mathbf 0}_A} = \O$ if $A = \set { {\mathbf 0}_A}$.

title: Speed of Body under Free Fall from Height
snippet: Let an object $B$ be released above ground from a point near the Earth's surface and allowed to fall freely. Let $B$ fall a distance $s$. Then: $v = \sqrt {2 g s}$ where: $v$ is the speed of $B$ after having fallen a distance $s$ $g$ is the Acceleration Due to Gravity at the height through which $B$ falls. It is supposed that the distance $s$ is small enough that $g$ can be considered constant throughout.

title: Speed of Hour Hand
snippet: Consider an analog clock $C$. The hour hand of $C$ rotates at $\dfrac 1 2$ of a degree per minute.

title: Speed of Minute Hand
snippet: Consider an analog clock $C$. The minute hand of $C$ rotates at $6$ degrees per minute.

title: Sphere in Normed Division Ring is Sphere in Induced Metric
Sphere is Disjoint Union of Open Balls in P-adic Numbers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $a \in \Q_p$. For all $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$: let $\map {S_\epsilon} a$ denote the sphere of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. let $\map {B_\epsilon} a$ denote the open ball of $a$ of radius $\epsilon$. Then: $\ds \forall n \in Z: \map {S_{p^{-n} } } a = \bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^{p - 1} \map {B_{p^{-n} } } {a + i p^n}$

title: Sphere is Locus of Equidistant Points from Point in Space
snippet: Let $P$ be a point in space. The locus of points which are equidistant from $P$ is the sphere whose center is $P$.

title: Sphere is Set Difference of Closed Ball with Open Ball
snippet: Let $M = \struct{A, d}$ be a metric space or pseudometric space. Let $a \in A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $\map {{B_\epsilon}^-} {a; d}$ denote the closed $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Let $\map {B_\epsilon} {a; d}$ denote the open $\epsilon$-ball of $a$ in $M$. Let $\map {S_\epsilon} {a; d}$ denote the $\epsilon$-sphere of $a$ in $M$. Then: $\map {S_\epsilon} {a; d} = \map { {B_\epsilon}^-} {a; d} \setminus \map {B_\epsilon} {a; d}$

title: Sphere is not Developable Surface
snippet: The sphere is not a developable surface.

title: Spheres in 24 Dimensions in Leech Lattice
snippet: Let a set of identical spheres in a $24$-dimensional space be arranged in a Leech lattice. Then each sphere will touch $196 \, 560$ other spheres. This is believed to be the densest possible sphere packing in $24$ dimensions.

title: Spherical Coordinate Form of Laplace's Equation
snippet: Laplace's equation can be expressed in spherical coordinates as: $\dfrac 1 {r^2} \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial r} } {r^2 \dfrac {\partial V} {\partial r} } + \dfrac 1 {r^2 \sin^2 \theta} \dfrac {\partial^2 V} {\partial \phi^2} + \dfrac 1 {r^2 \sin \theta} \map {\dfrac \partial {\partial \theta} } {\sin \theta \dfrac {\partial V} {\partial \theta} } = 0$

title: Spherical Law of Cosines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\cos a = \cos b \cos c + \sin b \sin c \cos A$

title: Spherical Law of Haversines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\hav a = \map \hav {b - c} + \sin b \sin c \hav A$ where $\hav$ denotes haversine.

title: Spherical Law of Sines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\dfrac {\sin a} {\sin A} = \dfrac {\sin b} {\sin B} = \dfrac {\sin c} {\sin C}$

title: Spherical Law of Tangents
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\dfrac {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A + B} } {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A - B} } = \dfrac {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {a + b} } {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {a - b} }$

title: Spherical Triangle is Polar Triangle of its Polar Triangle

Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Let $\triangle A'B'C'$ be the polar triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Then $\triangle ABC$ is the polar triangle of $\triangle A'B'C'$.

snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $C$ and $D$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $f: C \to D$ be a split epimorphism. Then $f: C \twoheadrightarrow D$ is epic.

title: Split Monomorphism is Monic

title: Sprague's Property of Root 2
snippet: Let $S = \sequence {s_n}$ be the sequence of fractions defined as follows: Let the numerator of $s_n$ be: $\floor {n \sqrt 2}$ where $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$. Let the denominators of the terms of $S$ be the (strictly) positive integers missing from the numerators of $S$: $S := \dfrac 1 3, \dfrac 2 6, \dfrac 4 {10}, \dfrac 5 {13}, \dfrac 7 {17}, \dfrac 8 {20}, \ldots$ Then the difference between the numerator and denominator of $s_n$ is equal to $2 n$.

title: Square-Bracing Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == Let there be an unlimited supply of rigid rods of unit length which may be joined together at their ends with a hinged joint. Let $4$ of these rods be used to construct a square. How many more of these rods are needed to make the square rigid?

title: Square-Summable Indexed Sets Closed Under Addition
snippet: Let $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}, \family {b_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be $I$-indexed families of real numbers. Let: {{eqn | l = \sum \set { {a_i}^2: i \in I} | o = < | r = \infty }} {{eqn | l = \sum \set { {b_i}^2: i \in I} | o = < | r = \infty }} where $\ds \sum$ denotes the generalized sums. Then: $\ds \sum \set {\paren {a_i + b_i}^2: i \in I} < \infty$

title: Square Cullen Numbers
snippet: The numbers: $1, 9, 25$ are Cullen numbers which are also square.

title: Square Divides Product of Multiples
snippet: Let $a, b, c, \in \Z$ be integers. Let: $a \divides b, a \divides c$ where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then: $a^2 \divides b c$

title: Square Fibonacci Number
snippet: After $1$, there exists exactly one Fibonacci number which is also square: $F_{12} = 144 = 12^2$ which is also coincidentally the square of its index.

title: Square Function is Even
snippet: The square function: $\map f x = x^2$ is an even function.

title: Square Inscribed in Circle is greater than Half Area of Circle
snippet: A square inscribed in a circle has an area greater than half that of the circle.

title: Square Matrices over Real Numbers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: Let $\map {\MM_\R} n$ be a $n \times n$ matrix space over the set of real numbers $\R$. Then the set of all $n \times n$ real matrices $\map {\MM_\R} n$ under matrix multiplication (conventional) forms a monoid.

title: Square Matrices with +1 or -1 Determinant under Multiplication forms Group
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $S$ be the set of square matrices of order $n$ of real numbers whose determinant is either $1$ or $-1$. Let $\struct {S, \times}$ denote the algebraic structure formed by $S$ whose operation is (conventional) matrix multiplication. Then $\struct {S, \times}$ is a group.

title: Square Matrix has Full Rank iff Nonsingular
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be an $n \times n$ square matrix. Then: $\mathbf A$ is of full rank $\mathbf A$ is nonsingular.

title: Square Matrix has Linearly Dependent Columns iff Determinant is Zero
snippet: Let $M$ be an $n \times n$ square matrix. Then: the columns of $M$ are linearly dependent $\map \det M = 0$

title: Square Matrix has Linearly Dependent Rows iff Determinant is Zero
snippet: Let $M$ be an $n \times n$ square matrix. Then: the rows of $M$ are linearly dependent $\map \det M = 0$

title: Square Matrix is Row Equivalent to Triangular Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$ over a commutative ring $R$. Then $\mathbf A$ can be converted to an upper or lower triangular matrix by elementary row operations.

title: Square Matrix with Duplicate Columns has Zero Determinant

title: Square Matrix with Duplicate Rows has Zero Determinant
snippet: If two rows of a square matrix over a commutative ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are the same, then its determinant is zero.

title: Square Modulo n Congruent to Square of Inverse Modulo n

title: Square Numbers which are Sum of Consecutive Powers
snippet: The only two square numbers which are the sum of consecutive powers of a positive integer are $121$ and $400$: $121 = 3^0 + 3^1 + 3^2 + 3^3 + 3^4 = 11^2$ $400 = 7^0 + 7^1 + 7^2 + 7^3 = 20^2$

title: Square Order 2 Matrices over Real Numbers form Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $S$ denote the set of square matrices of order $2$ whose entries are the set of real numbers. Then $S$ forms a non-commutative ring with unity whose unity is the matrix $\begin {pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end {pmatrix}$.

title: Square Product of Three Consecutive Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $T_n$ denote the $n$th triangular number for $n \in \Z_{>0}$ a (strictly) positive integer. Let $T_n \times T_{n + 1} \times T_{n + 2}$ be a square number. Then at least one value of $n$ fulfils this condition: $n = 3$

title: Square Root is Strictly Increasing
snippet: The positive square root function is strictly increasing, that is: $\forall x, y \in \R_{>0}: x < y \implies \sqrt x < \sqrt y$

title: Square Root is not Lipschitz Continuous
snippet: Let $\sqrt {\size x} : \R \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be a real function. $\sqrt {\size x}$ is not Lipschitz continuous.

title: Square Root is of Exponential Order Epsilon
snippet: The positive square root function: $t \mapsto \sqrt t$ is of exponential order $\epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$ arbitrarily small in magnitude.

snippet: Let $T_n$ denote the $n$th triangular number for $n \in \Z_{>0}$ a (strictly) positive integer. Let $T_n + T_{n + 1} + T_{n + 2}$ be a square number. Then at least one value of $n$ fulfils this condition: $n = 5$

title: Square and Tetrahedral Numbers
snippet: The only positive integers which are simultaneously tetrahedral and square are: $1, 4, 19 \, 600$

Square of 1 Less than Number Base
snippet: Let $b \in \Z$ be an integer such that $b > 2$. Let $n = b - 1$. The square of $n$ is expressed in base $b$ as: $n^2 = \left[{c1}\right]_b$ where $c = b - 2$.

title: Square of Chi Random Variable has Chi-Squared Distribution
snippet: Let $n$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim \chi_n$ where $\chi_n$ is the chi distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom. Then $X^2 \sim \chi^2_n$ where $\chi^2_n$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n$ degrees of freedom.

title: Square of Complex Conjugate is Complex Conjugate of Square
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of $z$. Then: $\overline {z^2} = \left({\overline z}\right)^2$

title: Square of Complex Modulus equals Complex Modulus of Square
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\cmod z$ be the modulus of $z$. Then: $\cmod {z^2} = \cmod z^2$

title: Square of Complex Number
snippet: Let $z = a + i b$ be a complex number. Then its square is given by: $z^2 = a^2 - b^2 + i \paren {2 a b}$

title: Square of Coprime Number is Coprime
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be coprime integers: $a, b \in \Z: a \perp b$ Then: $a^2 \perp b$

title: Square of Covariance is Less Than or Equal to Product of Variances
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the variances of $X$ and $Y$ exist and be finite. Then: $\paren {\cov {X, Y} }^2 \le \var X \, \var Y$ where $\cov {X, Y}$ denotes the covariance of $X$ and $Y$.

title: Square of Cube Number is Cube
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $a$ be a cube number. Then $a^2$ is also a cube number.

title: Square of Difference
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x - y}^2 = x^2 - 2 x y + y^2$

title: Square of Element Less than Unity in Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain. Let $x \in D$ such that $0 < x < 1$. Then: $0 < x \times x < x$

title: Square of Expectation of Product is Less Than or Equal to Product of Expectation of Squares
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be random variables. Let the expectation of $X Y$, $\expect {X Y}$, exist and be finite. Then: $\paren {\expect {X Y} }^2 \le \expect {X^2} \expect {Y^2}$

title: Square of Golden Mean equals One plus Golden Mean
snippet: $\phi^2 = \phi + 1$ where $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Square of Hypotenuse of Pythagorean Triangle is Difference of two Cubes/Refutation
snippet: Let $h$ be the hypotenuse of a Pythagorean triangle. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $h^2 = a^3 - b^3$ for some $a, b \in \Z_{>0}$.

title: Square of Inner Product Norm of Sum
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the inner product norm. Let $x, y \in X$. Then, we have: $
orm {x + y}^2 = 
orm x^2 + 2 \map \Re {\innerprod x y} + 
orm y^2$

title: Square of Metric does not necessarily form Metric
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $d_4: A^2 \to \R$ be the mapping defined as: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in A^2: \map {d_4} {x, y} = \paren {\map d {x, y} }^2$ Then $d_4$ may or may not be a metric for $A$.

title: Square of Modulo less One equals One
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$: $\Z_m = \set {\eqclass 0 m, \eqclass 1 m, \ldots, \eqclass {m - 1} m}$ Then: $\eqclass {m - 1} m \times_m \eqclass {m - 1} m = \eqclass 1 m$ where $\times_m$ denotes multiplication modulo $m$.

title: Square of Non-Zero Element of Ordered Integral Domain is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times, \le}$ be an ordered integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Then: $\forall x \in D: x \ne 0_D \iff \map P {x \times x}$ where $\map P {x \times x}$ denotes that $x \times x$ has the (strict) positivity property. That is, the square of any element of an ordered integral domain is (strictly) positive that element is non-zero.

title: Square of Non-Zero Real Number is Strictly Positive
snippet: $\forall x \in \R: x \ne 0 \implies x^2 > 0$

title: Square of Number Always Exists
snippet: Let $x$ be a number. Then its square $x^2$ is guaranteed to exist.

title: Square of Odd Multiple of 3 is Difference between Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $T_n$ denote the $n$th triangular number. Let $m = 2 n + 1$ be an odd integer Then: $\paren {3 m}^2 = T_{9 n + 4} - T_{3 n + 1}$

title: Square of Odd Number as Difference between Triangular Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\exists a, b \in \Z_{\ge 0}: \paren {2 n + 1}^2 = T_a - T_b$ where: $T_a$ and $T_b$ are triangular numbers $T_a$ and $T_b$ are coprime. That is, the square of every odd number is the difference between two coprime triangular numbers.

title: Square of Ones Matrix
snippet: Let $\mathbf J = \sqbrk 1_n$ be a square ones matrix of order $n$. Then $\mathbf J^2 = n \mathbf J$. That is: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & \cdots & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \cdots & 1 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 1 & 1 & \cdots & 1 \end{bmatrix}^2 = \begin{bmatrix} n & n & \cdots & n \\ n & n & \cdots & n \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ n & n & \cdots & n \end{bmatrix}$

title: Square of Pythagorean Prime is Hypotenuse of Pythagorean Triangle
snippet: Let $p$ be a Pythagorean prime. Then $p^2$ is the hypotenuse of a Pythagorean triangle.

title: Square of Quadratic Gauss Sum
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $a$ be an integer coprime to $p$. Let $\map g {a, p}$ denote the quadratic Gauss sum of $a$ and $p$. Then: $\map g {a, p}^2 = \paren {\dfrac {-1} p} \cdot p$

snippet: Let $k$ be a strictly positive integer. Let $X \sim t_k$ where $t_k$ is the $t$-distribution with $k$ degrees of freedom. Then: $X^2 \sim F_{1, k}$ where $F_{1, k}$ is Snedecor's $F$-distribution with $\tuple {1, k}$ degrees of freedom.

Then: $\paren {\mathbf a + \mathbf b}^2 = \mathbf a^2 + 2 \mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b + \mathbf b^2$ where: $\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b$ denotes dot product $\mathbf a^2$ denotes the square of $\mathbf a$, that is: $\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf a$.

title: Square of Sum with Double

title: Square of V Operator on Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\HH \times \HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH \times \HH} }$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\HH$ with itself. Define $V : \HH \times \HH \to \HH \times \HH$ by: $\map V {x, y} = \tuple {-y, x}$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in \HH \times \HH$. Then $V^2 = -I$.

title: Square of Vandermonde Matrix
snippet: The square of the Vandermonde matrix of order $n$: $\mathbf V = \begin{bmatrix} x_1 & x_2 & \cdots & x_n \\ x_1^2 & x_2^2 & \cdots & x_n^2 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ x_1^n & x_2^n & \cdots & x_n^n \end{bmatrix}$ is symmetrical in $x_1, \ldots, x_n$. {{questionable|The case $n 2$ left me clueless to what could possibly be intended here; only $\mathbf {V V}^T$ is trivially seen symmetric in the $x_n$, but this can hardly be called a square}}

title: Square of Vector Cross Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions. Let $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$ denote the vector cross product of $\mathbf a$ with $\mathbf b$. Then: $\paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b}^2 = \mathbf a^2 \mathbf b^2 - \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b}^2$ where: $\paren {\mathbf a \times \mathbf b}^2$ denotes the square of $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$ $\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b$ denotes the dot product of $\mathbf a \times \mathbf b$.

title: Square of Vector Quantity in Coordinate Form
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a vector in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $n$ dimensions: $\ds \mathbf a = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k \mathbf e_k$ where $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ is the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Then: $\ds \mathbf a^2 = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k^2$ where $\mathbf a^2$ denotes the square of $\mathbf a$.

title: Squares with All Odd Digits
snippet: The only squares whose digits (when written in base $10$ notation) are all odd are $1$ and $9$.

title: Squares with No More than 2 Distinct Digits
snippet: == Sequence == The sequence of square numbers which have no more than $2$ distinct digits and not ending in $0$ begins: $1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 121, 144, 225, 441, 484, 676, 1444, 7744, 11 \, 881, 29 \, 929, 44 \, 944, 55 \, 225, 69 \, 696, 9 \, 696 \, 996, 6 \, 661 \, 661 \, 161, \ldots$ It is not known whether there are any more.

title: Squaring the Circle
snippet: == Classic Problem == Squaring the Circle is creating a square with the same area as that of a given circle.

title: Squaring the Circle by Archimedean Spiral
snippet: Let $C$ be a circle. It is possible to construct a square of the same area as $C$ using an Archimedean spiral.

title: Squaring the Circle by Compass and Straightedge Construction is Impossible
snippet: There is no compass and straightedge construction to allow a square to be constructed whose area is equal to that of a given circle.

title: Squeeze Theorem for Absolutely Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\ds \sum \size {a_n}$ be an absolutely convergent series in $\R$. Suppose that: $\ds -\sum \size {a_n} = \sum \size {a_n}$ Then $\ds \sum a_n$ equals the above two series.

title: Squeeze Theorem for Filter Bases
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \le, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$ be filter bases in $S$. Let: $\forall T \in F_1: \exists M \in F_2: \forall x \in M: \exists y \in T: y \le x$ That is: for each $T \in F_1$, $F_2$ has an element $M$ such that all elements of $M$ succeed some element of $T$. Similarly, let: $\forall U \in F_3: \exists N \in F_2: \forall x \in N: \exists y \in U: x \le y$ That is: for each $U \in F_3$, $F_2$ has an element $N$ such that all elements of $N$ precede some element of $U$. Let $F_1$ and $F_3$ each converge to a point $p \in S$.

title: Squeeze Theorem for Real Sequences/Corollary
snippet: == Corollary to Squeeze Theorem for Real Sequences == Let $\sequence {y_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$ which is null, that is: $y_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ Let: $\forall n \in \N: \size {x_n - l} \le y_n$ Then $x_n \to l$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: St. Anselm's Ontological Argument
snippet: == Paradox == It is agreed that an atheist is a person who does not believe in the existence of God. But in order to disbelieve in God, they must be able to conceive of God in order to know what they deny the existence of. So, suppose that God does not exist. Then the atheist can still conceive of God as existing Thereby they can conceive of something greater than God. But, by definition, God is the entity of which nothing greater can be conceived. Hence the atheist's supposition leads to a contradiction. Therefore, God exists.

title: St. Ives Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == As I was going to I met a man with seven wives Every wife had seven sacks Every sack had seven cats Every cat had seven kits Kits, cats, sacks and wives How many were going to St. Ives?

title: St. Petersburg Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Let $A$ and $B$ be a players in a gambling game whose mechanics are as follows: $A$ tosses a coin until the first appearance of a head. Let this occur at the $k$th toss. $A$ then pays $2^k$ monetary units to $B$. For the game to be fair, $B$ must pay $A$ in advance the amount equal to the mean payment $A$ can expect to make to $B$. This mean payment in monetary units is: {{eqn | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \dfrac 1 {2^k} \times 2^k | r = 1 + 1 + 1 + \cdots | c = }} Hence it is not possible for $B$ to pay that amount, and a fair game is impossible.

title: Stabilizer in Group of Transformations
snippet: Let $X$ be any set with $n$ elements (where $n \in \Z_{>0}$). Consider the symmetric group on $n$ letters $S_n$ as a group of transformations on $X$. Let $x \in X$. Then the stabilizer of $x$ is isomorphic to $S_{n - 1}$.

title: Stabilizer is Normal iff Stabilizer of Each Element of Orbit
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ be a set. Let $*: G \times S \to S$ be a group action. Let $x \in S$. Let $\Stab x$ denote the stabilizer of $x$ under $*$. Let $\Orb x$ denote the orbit of $x$ under $*$. Then $\Stab x$ is normal in $G$ $\Stab x$ is also the stabilizer of every element in $\Orb x$.

title: Stabilizer is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which acts on a set $X$. Let $\Stab x$ be the stabilizer of $x$ by $G$. Then for each $x \in X$, $\Stab x$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Stabilizer of Cartesian Product of Group Actions
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $*_S: G \times S \to S$ and $*_T: G \times T \to T$ be group actions. Let the group action $*: G \times \paren {S \times T} \to S \times T$ be defined as: $\forall \tuple {g, \tuple {s, t} } \in G \times \paren {S \times T}: g * \tuple {s, t} = \tuple {g *_S s, g *_T t}$ Then the stabilizer of $\tuple {s, t} \in S \times T$ is given by: $\Stab {s, t} = \Stab s \cap \Stab t$ where $\Stab s$ and $\Stab t$ are the stabilizers of $s$ and $t$ under $*_S$ and $*_T$ respectively.

title: Stabilizer of Conjugacy Action on Subgroup is Normalizer
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $X$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Let $*$ be the conjugacy action on $H$: $\forall g \in G, H \in X: g * H = g \circ H \circ g^{-1}$ Then the stabilizer of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is given by: $\Stab H = \map {N_G} H$ where $\map {N_G} H$ is the normalizer of $H$ in $G$.

title: Stabilizer of Coset Action on Set of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ denote the power set of $G$. Let $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ denote the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $*$ be the subset product action on $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \forall H \in \HH: g * H = g \circ H$ where $g \circ H$ is the (left) coset of $g$ by $H$. Then the stabilizer of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is $H$ itself: $\Stab H = H$

title: Stabilizer of Coset under Group Action on Coset Space
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: G \times G / H \to G / H$ be the action on the (left) coset space: $\forall g \in G, \forall g' H \in G / H: g * \paren {g' H} := \paren {g g'} H$ Then the stabilizer of $a H$ under $*$ is given by: $\Stab {a H} = a H a^{-1}$

title: Stabilizer of Element after Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ be a set. Let $*_S: G \times S \to S$ be a group action. Let $x \in S, a \in G$. Then: $\Stab {a * x} = a^{-1} \circ \Stab x \circ a$

title: Stabilizer of Element of Group Acting on Itself is Trivial
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*$ be the group action of $\struct {G, \circ}$ on itself by the rule: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h$ Then the stabilizer of an element $x \in G$ is given by: $\Stab x = \set e$

title: Stabilizer of Element under Conjugacy Action is Centralizer
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $*$ be the conjugacy action on $G$ defined by the rule: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h \circ g^{-1}$ Let $x \in G$. Then the stabilizer of $x$ under this conjugacy action is: $\Stab x = \map {C_G} x$ where $\map {C_G} x$ is the centralizer of $x$ in $G$.

title: Stabilizer of Polynomial
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 0$. Let $\map f {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $\pi, \rho \in S_n$. Let the group action $\pi * f$ be defined as the permutation on the polynomial $f$ by $\pi$. Then the stabilizer of $f$ is the set of permutations on $n$ letters which fix $f$.

title: Stabilizer of Subgroup Action is Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the subgroup action defined for all $h \in H, g \in G$ as: $\forall h \in H, g \in G: h * g := h \circ g$ The stabilizer of $x \in G$ is $\set e$: $\Stab x = \set e$

title: Stabilizer of Subgroup Action on Left Coset Space
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$. Let $K$ act on the left coset space $G / H^l$ by: $\forall \tuple {k, g H} \in K \times G / H^l: k * \paren {g H} := \paren {k g} H$ The stabilizer of $g H$ is $K \cap H^g$, where $H^g$ denotes the $G$-conjugate of $H$ by $g$.

title: Stabilizer of Subset Product Action on Power Set
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $\struct {G, \circ}$. Let $*: G \times \powerset G \to \powerset G$ be the subset product action on $\powerset G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \forall S \in \powerset G: g * S = g \circ S$ where $g \circ S$ is the subset product $\set g \circ S$. Then the stabilizer of $S$ in $\powerset G$ is the set: $\Stab S = S$

title: Stabilizer of Subspace stabilizes Orthogonal Complement
snippet: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex Hilbert space (that is, inner product space). Let $t: H \to H$ be a normal operator on $H$. Let $t$ stabilize a subspace $V$. Then $t$ also stabilizes its orthogonal complement $V^\perp$.

title: Stabilizers of Elements in Same Orbit are Conjugate Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ be a group acting on a set $X$. Let: $y, z \in \Orb x$ where $\Orb x$ denotes the orbit of some $x \in X$. Then their stabilizers $\Stab y$ and $\Stab z$ are conjugate subgroups.

title: Stadium Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Consider three rows of bodies: $\begin{array} {ccccc} \text {(A)} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \text {(B)} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \text {(C)} & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}$ Let row $\text {(A)}$ be at rest, while row $\text {(B)}$ and row $\text {(C)}$ are travelling at the same speed in opposite directions.

title: Standard Bounded Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\bar d: A^2 \to \R$ be the standard bounded metric of $d$: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in A^2: \map {\bar d} {x, y} = \min \set {1, \map d {x, y} }$ Then $\bar d$ is a metric for $A$.

title: Standard Cauchy Distribution as Quotient of Normal Distributions
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $X$ and $Y$ have a normal distribution. Then the probability distribution $Z$ defined as: $Z = \dfrac X Y$ has a standard Cauchy distribution.

title: Standard Chessboard can be Tiled
snippet: <!-- There exists a perfect cover of a standard ($8 \times 8$) chessboard.

title: Standard Chessboard with Missing Square cannot be Tiled
snippet: There does not exist a perfect cover of a standard ($8 \times 8$) chessboard where a single square has been removed.

title: Standard Continuous Uniform Distribution in terms of Exponential Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent random variables. Let $\beta$ be a strictly positive real number. Let $X$ and $Y$ be random samples from the exponential distribution with parameter $\beta$. Then: $\dfrac X {X + Y} \sim \operatorname U \openint 0 1$ where $\operatorname U \openint 0 1$ is the uniform distribution on $\openint 0 1$.

title: Standard Discrete Metric/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Standard Discrete Metric ==

title: Standard Discrete Metric induces Discrete Topology
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be the (standard) discrete metric space on $A$. Then $d$ induces the discrete topology on $A$. Thus the discrete topology is metrizable.

title: Standard Discrete Metric is Metric
snippet: The standard discrete metric is a metric.

title: Standard Discrete Metric is not Topologically Equivalent to p-Product Metrics
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be an Euclidean space. Let $p \in \R_{\ge 1}$. Let $d_p$ be the $p$-product metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_0$ be the standard discrete metric on $\R^n$. Then $d_p$ and $d_0$ are not topologically equivalent.

title: Standard Equation of Ellipsoid
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an ellipsoid whose axes of symmetry coincide with the coordinate axes of a Cartesian $3$-space. Then $\EE$ can be expressed by the equation: $\dfrac {x^2} {a^2} + \dfrac {y^2} {b^2} + \dfrac {z^2} {c^2} = 1$

title: Standard Form of Equation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Standard Forms of Equations ==

title: Standard Machinery
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $\map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu$ be the space of $\mu$-integrable functions. Let $\map P {f_1, \ldots, f_n}$ be a proposition, where the variables $f_i$ denote $\mu$-measurable functions $f_i: X \to \overline \R$. Let every occurrence of an $f_i$ be of the form: $\ds \int \map \Phi {f_i} \rd \mu$ for a suitable index set $I$ and multilinear mapping $\Phi: \map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu^I \to \map {\LL^1_{\overline \R} } \mu$.

title: Standard Normal Random Variable as Transformation of Normal Random Variable
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a real number. Let $\sigma$ be a positive real number. Let $X \sim \Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ where $\Gaussian \mu {\sigma^2}$ is the normal distribution with parameters $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$. Then: $\dfrac {X - \mu} \sigma \sim \Gaussian 0 1$ where $\Gaussian 0 1$ is the standard normal distribution.

title: Standard Ordered Basis Vectors are Orthogonal
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_{\mathbb F}$ be a vector space over a field $\mathbb F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Let $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ be the standard ordered basis of $\mathbf V$. Let $\mathbf e_i$ and $\mathbf e_j$ be elements of $\tuple {\mathbf e_1, \mathbf e_2, \ldots, \mathbf e_n}$ such that $i \ne j$. $\mathbf e_i$ and $\mathbf e_j$ are orthogonal.

title: Standard Ordered Basis is Basis
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n$ be a positive integer. For each $j \in \closedint 1 n$, let $e_j$ be the ordered $n$-tuple of elements of $R$ whose $j$th entry is $1_R$ and all of whose other entries is $0_R$. Then $\sequence {e_n}$ is an ordered basis of the $R$-module $R^n$. This ordered basis is called the standard ordered basis of $R^n$. The corresponding set $\set {e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_n}$ is called the standard basis of $R^n$.

title: Standard Parity Check Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Standard Parity Check Matrices ==

title: Standard Schauder Basis in P-Sequence Space Multiplied by Bounded Sequence is Equivalent to Original Basis
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \hointr 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be the standard Schauder basis given by P-Sequence Space admits Schauder Basis. Let $m, M > 0$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\GF$ such that: $0 < m \le \cmod {\lambda_n} \le M$ Then $\sequence {\lambda_n e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is equivalent to $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$.

title: Standard Topology of Locally Convex Space has Local Basis of Balanced Convex Absorbing Sets
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space over $\GF$ with standard topology $\tau$. Then there exists a local basis $\BB$ for ${\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$ such that: each $A \in \BB$ is balanced, convex and absorbing.

title: Standard Topology on Locally Convex Space makes Seminorms Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a locally convex space. Let $\tau$ be the standard topology on $\struct {X, \PP}$. Let $p \in \PP$. Then $p$ is continuous as a function $\struct {X, \PP} \to \R$.

title: Standardized Random Variable/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Standardized Random Variables ==

title: Star-Finite Set is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\FF$ be a set of subsets of $S$ which is star-finite. Then $\FF$ is locally finite.

title: Star Convex Set is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a star convex subset of a topological vector space $V$ over $\R$ or $\C$. Then $A$ is path-connected.

title: Star Convex Set is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $A$ be a star convex subset of a topological vector space $\struct {V, \tau}$ over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $\tau_A$ be the subspace topology on $A$ induced by $\tau$. Then $\struct {A, \tau_A}$ is simply connected.

title: Star of Closed Subset of Banach *-Algebra is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $C \subseteq A$ be closed. Let: $C^\ast = \set {x^\ast : x \in C}$ Then $C^\ast$ is closed.

title: Star of Convergent Sequence in Banach *-Algebra Converges
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence in $A$ with: $x_n \to x$ Then: $x_n^\ast \to x^\ast$

title: Star of Ideal of *-Algebra is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $I$ be an ideal of $A$. Define: $I^\ast = \set {x^\ast : x \in I}$ Then $I^\ast$ is an ideal of $A$.

title: Star of Product of Elements in *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\tuple {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra. Let $n \ge 2$. Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in A$. Then: $\ds \paren {\prod_{j \mathop = 1}^n x_j}^\ast = \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^n x_{n - j + 1}^\ast$

title: Star of Vector Subspace of *-Algebra is Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a vector subspace of $A$. Define: $B^\ast = \set {x^\ast : x \in B}$ Then $B^\ast$ is a vector subspace of $A$.

title: State Code Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $k \in \N^*$. Let $e = \map \gamma P$ be the code number of a URM program $P$. Let $\tuple {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}$ be the input of $P$. Let $S_k: \N^{k + 2} \to \N$ be the function defined as: $\map {S_k} {e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, t}$ is the state code for $P$ at stage $t$ of computation of $P$. If $e$ does not code a URM Program then $S_k = 0$. Also, if $P$ terminates at stage $t_0$, then we put: $\forall t > t_0: \map {S_k} {e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, t} = \map {S_k} {e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, t_0}$ Then for all $k \ge 1$, the function $S_k$ is primitive recursive.

title: State Space of C*-Algebra is Weak-* Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S_A$ be the set of states on $A$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology. Then $\struct {S_A, w^\ast}$ is compact.

title: State Space of Unital C*-Algebra is Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $S_A$ be the set of states on $A$. Then $S_A$ is convex.

title: State on Unital C*-Subalgebra extends to whole C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $B$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Let $f_1 : B \to \C$ be a state. Then there exists a state $f : A \to \C$ extending $f_1$.

title: Stationary Point is Saddle Point iff Hessian is Negative
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a surface defined by the Cartesian equation $z = \map f {x, y}$. Let $P$ be a stationary point on $\SS$. Then $P$ is a saddle point of $\SS$ the Hessian of $\SS$ at $P$ is negative.

title: Steady-State Solution to Cart attached to Wall by Spring under Forced Vibration
Steiner's Calculus Problem
snippet: Let $f: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \map f x = x^{1/x}$ Then $\map f x$ reaches its maximum at $x = e$ where $e$ is Euler's number.

title: Steiner-Lehmus Theorem
snippet: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Denote the lengths of the angle bisectors through the vertices $A$ and $B$ by $\omega_\alpha$ and $\omega_\beta$. Let $\omega_\alpha = \omega_\beta$. Then $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle. 250px

title: Steiner Inellipse is Unique
snippet: For every triangle, there is one and only one Steiner inellipse.

title: Steiner Tree of Unit Cube
snippet: The length of the Steiner tree for the vertices of the unit cube is given approximately by: $L = 6 \cdotp 196 \ldots$

title: Steinitz's Theorem
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a finite field extension. $(1): \quad E / F$ is simple: there exists $\alpha \in E$ such that $E = \map F \alpha$ $(2): \quad$ there are only finitely many intermediate fields between $E$ and $F$.

title: Step Function satisfies Dirichlet Conditions
snippet: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \R$ be a real numbers such that $\alpha < \beta$. Let $\map f x$ be a step function defined on the interval $\openint \alpha \beta$. Then $f$ satisfies the Dirichlet conditions.

title: Stereographic Projection is Conformal Projection
snippet: A stereographic projection is an instance of a conformal projection.

title: Stewart's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with sides $a, b, c$. Let $CP$ be a cevian from $C$ to $P$. 400px Then: $a^2 \cdot AP + b^2 \cdot PB = c \paren {CP^2 + AP \cdot PB}$

title: Stieltjes Function of Measure is Stieltjes Function
snippet: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\R$ with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\map \BB \R$. Suppose that for every $n \in \N$: $\map \mu {\closedint {-n} n} < +\infty$ Then $F_\mu: \R \to \overline \R$, the Stieltjes function of $\mu$, is a Stieltjes function.

title: Stieltjes Function of Measure of Finite Stieltjes Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a finite Stieltjes function. Let $\mu_f$ be the measure of $f$. Let $f_{\mu_f}$ be the Stieltjes function of $\mu_f$. Then $f_{\mu_f} = f$.

title: Stirling's Formula
snippet: The factorial function can be approximated by the formula: $n! \sim \sqrt {2 \pi n} \paren {\dfrac n e}^n$ where $\sim$ denotes asymptotically equal.

title: Stirling's Formula for Gamma Function
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote the Gamma function. Let $z \in \C$ with a strictly positive real part and $\size {\arg z} < \dfrac \pi 2$. Then: $\map \Gamma {z + 1} = \sqrt {2 \pi z} \, z^z e^{-z} \paren {1 + \dfrac 1 {12 z} + \dfrac 1 {288 z^2} - \dfrac {139} {51 \, 840 z^3} - \dfrac {571} {2\, 488 \, 320 z^4} + \dfrac {163 \, 879} {209\, 018 \, 880 z^5} + \dfrac {5\, 246\, 819} {75\, 246\, 796\, 800 z^6} + \cdots}$

title: Stirling Number of Number with Greater
snippet: Let $n, k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $k > n$.

title: Stirling Number of n with n-m is Polynomial in n of Degree 2m
Stirling Number of the Second Kind of 0
snippet: $\ds {0 \brace n} = \delta_{0 n}$ where: $\ds {0 \brace n}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\delta_{0 n}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of 1
snippet: $\ds {1 \brace n} = \delta_{1 n}$ where: $\ds {1 \brace n}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\delta_{1 n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of Number with Greater
snippet: Let $n, k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $k > n$. Let $\ds {n \brace k}$ denote a Stirling number of the second kind. Then: $\ds {n \brace k} = 0$

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of Number with Self
snippet: $\ds {n \brace n} = 1$ where $\ds {n \brace n}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n+1 with 0
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brace 0} = 0$ where $\ds {n + 1 \brace 0}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n+1 with 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brace 1} = 1$ where $\ds {n + 1 \brace 1}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n+1 with 2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brace 2} = 2^n - 1$ where $\ds {n + 1 \brace 2}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 1}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 2}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $2$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 2} = \binom {n + 1} 4 + 2 \binom n 4$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 2}$ denotes an Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 4$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-3
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 3}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $3$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 3} = \binom {n + 2} 6 + 8 \binom {n + 1} 6 + 6 \binom n 6$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 3}$ denotes an Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 6$ denotes a binomial coefficient.
