title: Stokes's Law
snippet: == Physical Law == Stokes's Law is an empirical law for the drag exerted on a spherical body $\BB$ with a small Reynolds number in a viscous fluid $\FF$. It is formulated as: $\mathbf F_{\rm d} = 6 \pi \mu r \mathbf v$ where: $\mathbf F_{\rm d}$ is the Stokes's drag acting on the boundary between $\FF$ and $\BB$ in newtons $\mu$ is the dynamic viscosity in pascal-seconds $r$ is the radius of $\BB$ in metres $\mathbf v$ is the velocity of $\FF$ relative to $\BB$ in metres per second.

title: Stolz-Cesàro Theorem
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence. {{explain|Domain of $\sequence {a_n}$ -- $\R$ presumably but could it be $\C$?}} Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence of (strictly) positive real numbers such that: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^\infty b_n = \infty$ If: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac {a_n} {b_n} = L \in \R$ then also: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac {a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n} {b_1 + b_2 + \cdots + b_n} = L$

title: Stone's Representation Theorem for Boolean Algebras
snippet: Let $B$ be a Boolean algebra. Let $S$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then: The set of clopen sets in $S$ is a Boolean algebra under union, intersection, and complementation in $S$. That Boolean algebra is isomorphic to $B$.

title: Stone Space of Boolean Lattice is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $B = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be a Boolean lattice. Let $\map S B = \struct {U, \tau}$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then, $\map S B$ is a Hausdorff space.

title: Stone Space of Boolean Lattice is Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {B, \preceq, \wedge, \vee}$ be a Boolean lattice. Let $\struct {U, \tau}$ be the Stone space of $B$. Then $\struct {U, \tau}$ is a topological space.

title: Stopped Clock Paradox
snippet: == Paradox == Of two clocks, one is better than the other if it shows the absolutely correct time more often than the other. Consider: Clock $A$, which loses $1$ minute every day Clock $B$, which is stopped. Clock $A$ is $1$ minute slow after day $1$, and $2$ minutes slow after day $2$, and so on. There are $720$ minutes in $12$ hours. Hence it will be $720$ days, or nearly $2$ years, before it shows the right time again. On the other hand, clock $B$ shows the correct time every $12$ hours. Hence clock $B$, a stopped clock, is better than clock $A$, which loses but a minute a day.

title: Stopped Martingale is Martingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-martingale. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ be the stopped process. Then $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-martingale.

title: Stopped Process is Adapted Stochastic Process
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-adapted stochastic process. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-adapted process. Let $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ be the stopped process. Then $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-adapted process.

title: Stopped Sigma-Algebra is Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\FF_T$ be the stopped $\sigma$-algebra associated with $T$. Then $\FF_T$ is a $\sigma$-algebra.

title: Stopped Sigma-Algebra of Constant Stopping Time coincides with Filtration
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-adapted stochastic process. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $T$ be a stopping time such that: $\map T \omega = n$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. Let $\FF_T$ be the stopped $\sigma$-algebra associated with $T$. Then: $\FF_T = \FF_n$

title: Stopped Sigma-Algebra of Pointwise Minimum of Stopping Times
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a discrete-time filtered probability space. Let $T$ and $S$ be stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $S \wedge T$ be the pointwise minimum of $S$ and $T$. Then: $\FF_{S \wedge T} = \FF_S \cap \FF_T$ where $\FF_{\paren \cdot}$ denotes the stopped $\sigma$-algebra.

title: Stopped Sigma-Algebra preserves Inequality between Stopping Times
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $T$ and $S$ be stopping times with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$ such that: $\map S \omega \le \map T \omega$ for each $\omega \in \Omega$. Let $\FF_S$ and $\FF_T$ be the stopped $\sigma$-algebras associated with $S$ and $T$ respectively. Then: $\FF_S \subseteq \FF_T$

title: Stopped Submartingale is Submartingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-submartingale. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ be the stopped process. Then $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-submartingale.

title: Stopped Supermartingale is Supermartingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_n}_{n \ge 0}$ be an $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-supermartingale. Let $T$ be a stopping time with respect to $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$. Let $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ be the stopped process. Then $\sequence {X_n^T}_{n \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_n}_{n \ge 0}$-supermartingale.

title: Strict Hypograph of Continuous Real Function is Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Consider $X \times \GF$ as the direct product of $X$ and $\GF$ as topological vector spaces. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a function. Let $\map {\operatorname {hypo}_S} f$ be the strict hypograph of $f$. Then $\map {\operatorname {hypo}_S} f$ is open in $X \times \GF$.

title: Strict Lower Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$, and let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\prec T} = T \cap t^{\prec S}$ where: $t^{\prec T}$ is the strict lower closure of $t$ in $\left({T, \preceq \restriction_T}\right)$ $t^{\prec S}$ is the strict lower closure of $t$ in $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$.

title: Strict Lower Closure is Dual to Strict Upper Closure
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $a, b \in S$. The following are dual statements: $b \in a^\prec$, the strict lower closure of $a$ $b \in a^\succ$, the strict upper closure of $a$

title: Strict Lower Closure is Lower Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $p \in S$. Let $p^\prec$ denote the strict lower closure of $p$. Then $p^\prec$ is a lower section.

title: Strict Lower Closure of Element is Proper Lower Section
snippet: Let $A$ be a class under an ordering $\preccurlyeq$. Let $a \in A$. Let $a^\prec$ denote the strict lower closure of $a$ in $A$. Then $a^\prec$ is a proper lower section of $A$.

title: Strict Lower Closure of G-Tower is Set of Elements which are Proper Subsets
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Let $x \in M$. Then the strict lower closure of $x$ is the set of all elements of $M$ that are proper subsets of $M$.

title: Strict Lower Closure of Limit Element is Infinite
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be a well-ordering on $A$. Let $x \in A$ be a limit element of $A$ under $\preccurlyeq$. Let $x^\prec$ denotes the strict lower closure of $x$ in $A$ under $\preccurlyeq$. Then $x^\prec$ is an infinite set.

title: Strict Lower Closure of Sum with One
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then: $\forall n \in \struct {S, \circ, \preceq}: \paren {n \circ 1}^\prec = n^\prec \cup \set n$ where $n^\prec$ is defined as the strict lower closure of $n$, that is, the set of elements strictly preceding $n$.

title: Strict Negativity is equivalent to Strict Positivity of Negative
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain, whose (strict) positivity property is denoted $P$. Let $N$ be the (strict) negativity property on $D$: $\forall a \in D: \map N a \iff \map P {-a}$ Then for all $a \in D$: $\map P a \iff \map N {-a}$

title: Strict Negativity is equivalent to Strictly Preceding Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an ordered integral domain, whose (strict) positivity property is denoted $P$. Let $\le$ be the total ordering induced by $P$, and let $<$ be its strict total ordering counterpart. Let $N$ be the (strict) negativity property on $D$: $\forall a \in D: \map N a \iff \map P {-a}$ Then for all $a \in D$: $\map N a \iff a < 0$

title: Strict Ordering Preserved under Cancellability in Totally Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered semigroup. If either: $x \circ z \prec y \circ z$ or $z \circ x \prec z \circ y$ then $x \prec y$.

title: Strict Ordering Preserved under Product with Cancellable Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered semigroup. Let $x, y, z \in S$ be such that: $(1): \quad z$ is cancellable for $\circ$ $(2): \quad x \prec y$ Then: $x \circ z \prec y \circ z$ $z \circ x \prec z \circ y$

title: Strict Ordering Preserved under Product with Invertible Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered semigroup. Let $z \in S$ be invertible. Suppose that either $x \circ z \prec y \circ z$ or $z \circ x \prec z \circ y$. Then $x \prec y$.

title: Strict Ordering can be Expanded to Compare Additional Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be an ordered set. Let $a$ and $b$ be distinct, $\prec$-incomparable elements of $S$. That is, let: $a \nprec b$ and $b \nprec a$. Let $\prec' = {\prec} \cup \set {\tuple {a, b} }$. Define a relation $\prec'^+$ by letting $p \prec'^+ q$ : $p \prec q$ or: $p \preceq a$ and $b \preceq q$ where $\preceq$ is the reflexive closure of $\prec$. Then: $\prec'^+$ is a strict ordering $\prec^+$ is the transitive closure of $\prec'$.

title: Strict Ordering of Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Strongly Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then $\prec$ is strongly compatible with $\circ$: $\forall m, n, p \in S: m \prec n \iff m \circ p \prec n \circ p$

title: Strict Ordering of Ordinals is Equivalent to Membership Relation
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $<$ denote the (strict) usual ordering of $\On$. Then: $\forall \alpha, \beta \in \On: \alpha < \beta \iff \alpha \in \beta$

title: Strict Ordering on Integers is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \implies | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = \nless | r = \eqclass {a, b} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering on the integers is asymmetric.

title: Strict Ordering on Integers is Transitive
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | lo= \land | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \implies | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {e, f} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering on the integers is transitive.

title: Strict Ordering on Integers is Trichotomy
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ and $\eqclass {c, d} {}$ be integers, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Then exactly one of the following holds: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} That is, strict ordering is a trichotomy.

title: Strict Ordering on Integers is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\eqclass {a, b} {}$ denote an integer, as defined by the formal definition of integers. Let: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | r = \eqclass {a', b'} {} | c = }} {{eqn | l = \eqclass {c, d} {} | r = \eqclass {c', d'} {} | c = }} Then: {{eqn | l = \eqclass {a, b} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c, d} {} | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \leadstoandfrom | l = \eqclass {a', b'} {} | o = < | r = \eqclass {c', d'} {} | c = }}

title: Strict Positivity Property induces Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Let $D$ be endowed with a (strict) positivity property $P: D \to \set {\T, \F}$. Then there exists a total ordering $\le$ on $\struct {D, +, \times}$ induced by $P$ which is compatible with the ring structure of $\struct {D, +, \times}$.

title: Strict Upper Bound for Composition of Ackermann-Péter Functions
snippet: For all $x, y, z \in \N$: $\map A {x + y + 2, z} > \map A {x, \map A {y, z}}$ where $A$ is the Ackermann-Péter function.

title: Strict Upper Bound for Sum of Ackermann-Péter Functions
snippet: For all $x, y, z \in \N$: $\map A {\map \max {x, y} + 4, z} > \map A {x, z} + \map A {y, z}$ where $A$ is the Ackermann-Péter function.

title: Strict Upper Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$, and let $\preceq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\succ T} = T \cap t^{\succ S}$ where: $t^{\succ T}$ is the strict upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ $t^{\succ S}$ is the strict upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

title: Strict Upper Closure is Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $p \in S$. Let $p^\succ$ denote the strict upper closure of $p$. Then $p^\succ$ is an upper section.

title: Strict Weak Ordering Induces Partition
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a relational structure such that $\prec$ is a strict weak ordering on $S$. Then $S$ can be partitioned into equivalence classes whose equivalence relation is "is non-comparable". That is, each of the partitions $A$ of $S$ is a relational structure $\struct {\mathbb S, <}$ such that: $\mathbb S$ is the set of these partitions of $S$; $<$ is the strict total ordering on $\mathbb S$ induced by $\prec$.

title: Strict Well-Ordering Isomorphic to Unique Ordinal under Unique Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a strict well-ordering. Then there exists a unique ordinal $x$ and unique mapping $f$ such that $f: x \to S$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Strictly Decreasing Mapping is Decreasing

title: Strictly Increasing Infinite Sequence of Integers is Cofinal in Natural Numbers

title: Strictly Increasing Infinite Sequence of Positive Integers is Cofinal in Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $S = \sequence {x_n}$ be an infinite sequence of positive integers which is strictly increasing. Then $S$ is a cofinal subset of $\struct {\N, \le}$ where $\le$ is the usual ordering on the natural numbers.

title: Strictly Increasing Mapping Between Wosets Implies Order Isomorphism
snippet: Let $J$ and $E$ be well-ordered sets. Let there exist a mapping $k: J \to E$ which is strictly increasing. Then $J$ is order isomorphic to $E$ or an initial segment of $E$.

title: Strictly Increasing Mapping is Increasing
snippet: A mapping that is strictly increasing is an increasing mapping.

title: Strictly Increasing Mapping on Well-Ordered Class
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a strictly well-ordered class. Let $\struct {T, <}$ be a strictly ordered class. Let $f$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. For each $i \in S$ such that $i$ is not maximal in $S$, let: $\map f i < \map f {\map \Succ i}$ where $\map \Succ i$ is the immediate successor element of $i$. Let: $\forall i, j \in S: i \preceq j \implies \map f i \le \map f j$ Then for each $i, j \in S$ such that $i \prec j$: $\map f i < \map f j$

title: Strictly Increasing Sequence induces Partition
snippet: Let $\sequence {r_k}_{0 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be a strictly increasing finite sequence of natural numbers. Let: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: A_k := \closedint {r_{k - 1} + 1} {r_k}$ Then: $\set {A_k: k \in \closedint 1 n}$ is a partition of $\closedint {r_0 + 1} {r_n}$.

title: Strictly Increasing Sequence of Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $\N_{>0}$ be the set of natural numbers without zero: $\N_{>0} = \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots}$ Let $\sequence {n_r}$ be a strictly increasing sequence in $\N_{>0}$. Then: $\forall r \in \N_{>0}: n_r \ge r$

title: Strictly Increasing Sequence on Ordered Set
snippet: == Lemma == Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\sequence {r_k}_{p \mathop \le k \mathop \le q}$ be a finite sequence of elements of $\struct {S, \preceq}$. Then $\sequence {r_k}_{p \mathop \le k \mathop \le q}$ is strictly increasing : $\forall k \in \closedint {p + 1} q: r_{k - 1} \prec r_k$

title: Strictly Inductive Semigroup is Inductive Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a strictly inductive semigroup. Then $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an inductive semigroup.

title: Strictly Maximal Element is Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $m \in T$ be a strictly maximal element of $T$ under $\RR$. Then $m$ is a maximal element of $T$ under $\RR$.

title: Strictly Minimal Element is Minimal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $m \in T$ be a strictly minimal element of $T$ under $\RR$. Then $m$ is a minimal element of $T$ under $\RR$.

title: Strictly Monotone Mapping is Monotone
snippet: A mapping that is strictly monotone is a monotone mapping.

title: Strictly Monotone Mapping with Totally Ordered Domain is Injective
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be an ordered set. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \preceq_1} \to \struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be a strictly monotone mapping. Then $\phi$ is injective.

title: Strictly Monotone Real Function is Bijective
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is defined on $I \subseteq \R$. Let $f$ be strictly monotone on $I$. Let the image of $f$ be $J$. Then $f: I \to J$ is a bijection.

title: Strictly Order-Preserving and Order-Reversing Mapping on Strictly Totally Ordered Set is Injection
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec_1}$ and $\struct {T, \prec_2}$ be strictly totally ordered sets. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $\pi: S \to T$ be a mapping with the property that: $\forall x, y \in S: x \prec_1 y \iff \map \pi x \prec_2 \map \pi y$ Then $\pi$ is an injection.

title: Strictly Positive Hausdorff Measure implies Infinite Lower Dimensional Measure
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $F \subseteq \R^n$ be a subset of the real Euclidean space. Let $\map {\HH^s} \cdot$ denote the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Let $s \in \R_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\map {\HH^s} F > 0 \implies \forall t \in \hointr 0 s : \map {\HH^t} F = +\infty$

title: Strictly Positive Integer Power Function Strictly Succeeds Each Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring with unity. Let $\struct {R, \le}$ be a directed set with no upper bound. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $f: R \to R$ be defined by: $\forall x \in R: \map f x = \circ^n x$ Then the image of $f$ has elements strictly succeeding each elements of $R$.

title: Strictly Positive Integer Power Function is Unbounded Above
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real numbers with the usual ordering. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be defined by: $\map f x = x^n$ Then $f$ is unbounded above.

title: Strictly Positive Integers have same Cardinality as Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $\Z_{>0} := \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots}$ denote the set of strictly positive integers. Let $\N := \set {0, 1, 2, \ldots}$ denote the set of natural numbers. Then $\Z_{>0}$ has the same cardinality as $\N$.

title: Strictly Positive Power of Strictly Positive Element Greater than One Succeeds Element
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ, \le}$ be an ordered ring with unity. Let $x \in R$ with $x > 1$ and $x > 0$. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Then: $\circ^n x \ge x$

title: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers are Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $\Q_{>0}$ denote the set of strictly positive rational numbers: $\Q_{>0} := \set {x \in \Q: x > 0}$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. The algebraic structure $\struct {\Q_{>0}, +}$ is closed in the sense that: $\forall a, b \in \Q_{>0}: a + b \in \Q_{>0}$ where $+$ denotes rational addition.

title: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers are Closed under Multiplication
snippet: $\forall a, b \in \Q_{>0}: a b \in \Q_{>0}$

title: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers under Multiplication form Countably Infinite Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\Q_{> 0}$ be the set of strictly positive rational numbers, i.e. $\Q_{> 0} = \set {x \in \Q: x > 0}$. The structure $\struct {\Q_{> 0}, \times}$ is a countably infinite abelian group.

title: Strictly Positive Rational Numbers under Multiplication form Subgroup of Non-Zero Rational Numbers
Strictly Positive Real Numbers are Closed under Division
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is closed under division: $\forall a, b \in \R_{>0}: a \div b \in \R_{>0}$

title: Strictly Positive Real Numbers are Closed under Multiplication
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is closed under multiplication: $\forall a, b \in \R_{> 0}: a \times b \in \R_{> 0}$

title: Strictly Positive Real Numbers are not Closed under Subtraction
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is not closed under subtraction.

title: Strictly Positive Real Numbers under Multiplication form Subgroup of Non-Zero Real Numbers
Strictly Positive Real Numbers under Multiplication form Uncountable Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers: $\R_{>0} = \set {x \in \R: x > 0}$ The structure $\struct {\R_{>0}, \times}$ is an uncountable abelian group.

title: Strictly Precede and Step Condition and not Precede implies Joins are equal
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a join semilattice. Let $p, q, u \in S$ be such that: $p \prec q$ and $\paren {\forall s \in S: p \prec s \implies q \preceq s}$ and $u \npreceq p$ Then: $p \vee u = q \vee u$

title: Strictly Precedes is Strict Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\prec$ be the relation on $S$ defined as: $a \prec b \iff \paren {a \ne b} \land \paren {a \preceq b}$ That is, $a \prec b$ $a$ strictly precedes $b$. Then: $a \preceq b \iff \paren {a = b} \lor \paren {a \prec b}$ and $\prec$ is a strict ordering on $S$.

title: Strictly Stationary Stochastic Process/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Strictly Stationary Stochastic Processes == Let $S$ be a strictly stationary stochastic process giving rise to a time series $T$. Then the following conditions hold:

title: Strictly Succeed is Dual to Strictly Precede
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $a, b \in S$. The following are dual statements: $a$ strictly succeeds $b$ $a$ strictly precedes $b$

title: Strictly Well-Founded Relation determines Strictly Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $A$. Let $B$ be a nonempty class such that $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ has a strictly minimal element under $\RR$.

title: Strictly Well-Founded Relation has no Relational Loops
snippet: Let $\prec$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $A$ and let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in A$. Then: $\neg \paren {x_1 \prec x_2 \land x_3 \prec x_4 \cdots \land x_n \prec x_1}$ That is, there are no relational loops within $A$.

title: Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Antireflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation on a set or class $A$. Then $\RR$ is antireflexive.

title: Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Asymmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure, where $S$ is a set or a proper class. Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Then $\RR$ is asymmetric.

title: Strictly Well-Founded Relation is Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a strictly well-founded relation on $S$. Then $\RR$ is a well-founded relation on $S$.

title: String is Substring of Itself
snippet: Let $S$ be a string. Then $S$ is a substring of itself.

title: Strong Separation Theorem
snippet: Let $C \subset \R^\ell$ be closed and convex. Let $D = \set {\mathbf v} \subset C^c$. Then $C$ and $D$ can be strongly separated.

title: Strong Twin Prime Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == It is conjectured that the number of twin primes less than or equal to $N \in \N$ is asymptotically equal to: $2 C_2 \ds \int_2^N \dfrac {\d x} {\paren {\ln x}^2} = \dfrac {2 C_2 N} {\paren {\ln N}^2}$ The above is true only if the Twin Prime Conjecture holds.

title: Strongly Locally Compact Space is Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a strongly locally compact space. Then $T$ is weakly locally compact.

title: Strongly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: A strongly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a compact space.

title: Strongly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Lindelöf
snippet: A strongly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a Lindelöf space.

title: Strongly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Sigma-Compact
snippet: A strongly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a $\sigma$-compact space.

title: Strongly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact
snippet: A strongly locally compact space is not necessarily also a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact topological space.

title: Strongly Paracompact Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a strongly paracompact space. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: Structure Induced by Abelian Group Operation is Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $G^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ is an abelian group.

title: Structure Induced by Absorbing Operations is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ, *}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$ and $*$. Let $\circ$ and $*$ satisfy the absorption law: $\forall a, b \in S: a \circ \paren {a * b} = a$ Then the pointwise operations $\oplus$ and $\otimes$ on $T^S$ also satisfy the absorption law: $\forall f, g \in T^S: f \oplus \paren {f \otimes g} = f$

title: Structure Induced by Associative Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be associative. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also associative.

title: Structure Induced by Commutative Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be a commutative operation. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also commutative.

title: Structure Induced by Commutative Ring Operations is Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a commutative ring.

title: Structure Induced by Distributive Operation is Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S$: $a \times \paren {b + c} = \paren{a \times b} + \paren{a \times c}$ and: $\paren {b + c} \times a= \paren{b \times a} + \paren{c \times a}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S$: $f \otimes \paren {g \oplus h} = \paren{f \otimes g} \oplus \paren{f \otimes h}$ and: $\paren…

title: Structure Induced by Group Operation is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $G^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {G^S, \oplus}$ is a group.

title: Structure Induced by Idempotent Operation is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be an idempotent operation. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also idempotent.

title: Structure Induced by Lattice Operations is Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {L, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {L^S, \veebar, \barwedge}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\vee$ and $\wedge$. Let $\precsim$ be the ordering on $S$ defined by: $\forall f, g \in L^S: f \precsim g$ $f \veebar g = g$ as on Semilattice Induces Ordering. Then $\struct {L^S, \veebar, \barwedge, \precsim}$ is a lattice.

title: Structure Induced by Left Distributive Operation is Left Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be left distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S: a \times \paren {b + c} = \paren{a \times b} + \paren{a \times c}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is left distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S: f \otimes \paren {g \oplus h} = \paren{f \otimes g} \oplus \paren{f \otimes h}$

title: Structure Induced by Permutation on Algebra Loop is not necessarily Algebra Loop
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebra loop. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ be the structure induced by $\sigma$ on $\circ$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ is not necessarily also an algebra loop.

title: Structure Induced by Permutation on Commutative Quasigroup is Commutative Quasigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a quasigroup such that $\circ$ is a commutative operation. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ be the structure induced by $\sigma$ on $\circ$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ is also a quasigroup such that $\circ_\sigma$ is a commutative operation.

title: Structure Induced by Permutation on Quasigroup is Quasigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a quasigroup. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ be the structure induced by $\sigma$ on $\circ$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ is also a quasigroup.

title: Structure Induced by Permutation on Semigroup is not necessarily Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $\sigma: S \to S$ be a permutation on $S$. Let $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ be the structure induced by $\sigma$ on $\circ$: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ_\sigma y := \map \sigma {x \circ y}$ Then $\struct {S, \circ_\sigma}$ is not necessarily itself a semigroup.

title: Structure Induced by Right Distributive Operation is Right Distributive
snippet: Let $\struct {T, +, \times}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus, \otimes}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $+$ and $\times$. Let $\times$ be right distributive over $+$: $\forall a, b, c \in S: \paren {b + c} \times a= \paren{b \times a} + \paren{c \times a}$ Then the pointwise operation $\otimes$ is left distributive over the pointwise operation $\oplus$ on $T^S$: $\forall f, g, h \in T^S: \paren {g \oplus h} \otimes f = \paren{g \otimes f} \oplus \paren{h \otimes f}$

title: Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring, where $+'$ and $\circ'$ are the pointwise operations induced on $R^S$ by $+$ and $\circ$.

title: Structure Induced by Ring with Unity Operations is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring with unity whose unity is $f_{1_R}: S \to R$, defined by: $\forall s \in S: \map {f_{1_R} } s = 1_R$

title: Structure Induced by Semigroup Operation is Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ is a semigroup.

title: Structure Induced by Semilattice Operation is Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a semilattice. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Then $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ is a semilattice.

title: Structure Induced on Set of All Mappings to Ordered Semigroup is Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T, \odot, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered semigroup. Let $\struct {T^S, \otimes, \preccurlyeq}$ denote the algebraic structure on $T^S$ induced by $\odot$. Then $\struct {T^S, \otimes, \preccurlyeq}$ is an ordered semigroup.

title: Structure Induced on Set of Self-Maps on Entropic Structure is Entropic
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an entropic structure. Let $S^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself. Let $\struct {S^S, \oplus}$ denote the algebraic structure on $S^S$ induced by $\odot$. Then $\struct {S^S, \oplus}$ is an entropic structure.

title: Structure is Group iff Semigroup and Quasigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Then: $\struct {S, \circ}$ is a group $\struct {S, \circ}$ is both a semigroup and a quasigroup.

title: Structure of Cardinality 3+ where Every Permutation is Automorphism is Idempotent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set whose cardinality is at least $3$. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure on $S$ such that every permutation on $S$ is an automorphism on $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then $\circ$ is an idempotent operation.

title: Structure of Correlation Matrix
snippet: Let $\sequence a_n$ and $\sequence b_n$ be sequences of $n$ observations. Let $\mathbf C$ be the correlation matrix $\sequence a_n$ and $\sequence b_n$. Then $\mathbf C$ is symmetric with entries on the main diagonal all equal to $1$.

title: Structure of Inverse Completion of Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $\struct {C, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup of cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $\struct {T, \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then: $T = S \circ' C^{-1}$ where: $C^{-1}$ is the inverse of $C$ in $T$ $S \circ' C^{-1}$ is the subset product of $S$ with $C^{-1}$.

title: Structure of Moore-Penrose Pseudoinverse
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix of order $m \times n$ over the complex numbers $\C$. Let $\mathbf A^+$ be the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $\mathbf A$. Let $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf D \mathbf V^*$ be a singular value decomposition of $\mathbf A$. Then: $\mathbf A^+ = \mathbf V \mathbf D^+ \mathbf U^*$ where $\mathbf D^+$ is obtained by inverting the non-zero diagonal elements of $\mathbf D$. In the above, recall that $\mathbf V^*$ denotes the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf V$.

title: Structure of Recurring Decimal
snippet: Let $\dfrac 1 m$, when expressed as a decimal expansion, recur with a period of $p$ digits with no nonperiodic part. Let $\dfrac 1 n$, when expressed as a decimal expansion, terminate after $q$ digits. Then $\dfrac 1 {m n}$ has a nonperiodic part of $q$ digits, and a recurring part of $p$ digits.

title: Structure of Simple Algebraic Field Extension
snippet: Let $F / K$ be a field extension. Let $\alpha \in F$ be algebraic over $K$. Let $\mu_\alpha$ be the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $K$. Let $K \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial functions. Let $\gen {\mu_\alpha}$ be the ideal of $K \sqbrk X$ generated by $\mu_\alpha$. Let $K \sqbrk \alpha$ be the subring of $F$ generated by $K \cup \set \alpha$. Let $\map K \alpha$ be the subfield of $F$ generated by $K \cup \set \alpha$.

title: Structure of Simple Transcendental Field Extension
snippet: Let $F / K$ be a field extension and $\alpha \in F$. Let $\map K X$ be the Field of Rational Functions in an indeterminate $X$. If $\alpha$ is transcendental over $K$ then $\map K \alpha \simeq \map K X$.

title: Structure under Left Operation is Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \gets}$ be an algebraic structure in which the operation $\gets$ is the left operation. Then $\struct {S, \gets}$ is a semigroup.

title: Structure under Right Operation is Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \to}$ be an algebraic structure in which the operation $\to$ is the right operation. Then $\struct {S, \to}$ is a semigroup.

title: Structure with Commutative Idempotent Associative Operations satisfying Absorption Laws is Lattice
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\vee$ and $\wedge$ be binary operations which, when applied to $S$, are both: closed operations commutative operations idempotent operations associative operations. Furthermore, let $\vee$ and $\wedge$ satisfy the absorption laws: $\forall a, b \in S: a \vee \paren {a \wedge b} = a = a \wedge {a \vee b}$ Then there exists a unique lattice ordering $\preccurlyeq$ on $S$ such that: $\forall a, b \in S$: $x \vee y = \sup \set {a, b}$ $x \wedge y = \inf \set {a, b}$ That is: $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preccurlyeq}$ is a lattice.

title: Structure with Element both Identity and Zero has One Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $z \in S$ such that $z$ is both an identity element and a zero element. Then: $S = \set z$

title: Student's t-Distribution with One Degree of Freedom is Standard Cauchy Distribution
snippet: The Student's $t$-distribution with one degree of freedom is a special case of a standard Cauchy distribution.

title: Sturm-Liouville Problem
snippet: Let: $P \in C^\infty \map P x > 0$ $Q \in C^0$ $-\paren {P y'}' + Q y = \lambda y$ $\map y a = \map y b = 0$ Then the Sturm-Liouville problem has an infinite sequence of eigenvalues $\set {\lambda^{\paren n} }$, and to each $\lambda^{\paren n}$ corresponds an eigenfunction $y^{\paren n}$, unique up to a constant factor.

title: Sub-Basis for Initial Topology in terms of Sub-Bases of Target Spaces
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. For each $i \in I$, let $S_i$ be a synthetic basis for $\struct {Y_i, \tau_i}$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $\SS = \set {f_i^{-1} \sqbrk U : i \in I, \, U \in S_i}$ is a synthetic sub-basis for $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Sub-Basis for Real Number Line
snippet: Let the real number line $\R$ be considered as a topology under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then: $\BB := \set {\openint \gets a, \openint b \to: a, b \in \R}$ is a sub-basis for $\R$.

title: Sub-Basis for Topological Subspace
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $K$ be a sub-basis for $\tau$. Let $\struct {S, \tau'}$ be a subspace of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $K' = \set {U \cap S: U \in K}$. That is, $K'$ consists of the $\tau'$-open sets in $S$ corresponding to elements of $K$. Then $K'$ is a sub-basis for $\tau'$.

title: Sub-basis for Uniformity on Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau_d}$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $a, b \in \R$ such that $a a}$ Then $S_{ab}$ is a sub-basis for a uniformity $U$ which generates the usual topology on $\R$. Note that $U$ is clearly not the usual metric uniformity.

title: Subadditivity of Invariant Metric on Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Then: $\map d {n x, {\mathbf 0}_X} \le n \map d {x, {\mathbf 0}_X}$ for each $n \in \N$ and $x \in X$.

title: Subalgebra Generated by Commuting Elements is Commutative
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a non-empty set such that: for all $x, y \in S$ we have $x y = y x$. Let $K \sqbrk S$ be the subalgebra generated by $S$. Then $K \sqbrk S$ is a commutative algebra.

title: Subalgebra Generated by Inclusion and Conjugate is Everywhere Dense in Space of Continuous Functions on Compact Subset of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $K \subseteq \C$ be compact. Let $\map \CC K$ be the space of continuous functions on $K$. Let $\iota : K \to \C$ be the inclusion mapping. Let $\overline \iota : K \to \C$ be the complex conjugate. Let $\AA$ be the subalgebra generated by $1$, $\iota$ and $\overline \iota$. That is, by Explicit Form for Generated Subalgebra: $\ds \AA = \set {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_j z^{n_j} \overline z^{m_j} : n \in \N, \, \alpha_j \in \C, \, n_j, m_j \ge 0}$ Then $\AA$ is everywhere dense in $\map \CC K$.

title: Subalgebra Generated by Self-Adjoint Set is Self-Adjoint
snippet: Let $\tuple {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $S \subseteq A$ be self-adjoint. Let $K \sqbrk S$ be the subalgebra generated by $S$. Then $\C \sqbrk S$ is a $\ast$-subalgebra of $A$.

title: Subband iff Idempotent under Induced Operation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a band. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of the power set of $S$ and the operation induced on $\powerset S$ by $\circ$. Let $X \in \powerset S$. Then $X$ is idempotent $\struct {X, \circ}$ is a subband of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Subband of Induced Operation is Set of Subbands
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a band. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the algebraic structure consisting of: the power set $\powerset S$ of $S$ and the operation $\circ_\PP$ induced on $\powerset S$ by $\circ$. Let $T \subseteq \powerset S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ_\PP}$ be a subband of $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$. Then every element of $T$ is a subband of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Subclass of Set is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\map \phi x$ be a condition in which $x$ is taken to be a set. Then there exists a set that consists of all of the elements of $A$ that satisfies this condition. In ZF, this result is known as the Axiom of Specification.

title: Subclass of Subclass is Subclass
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be classes. Let $A$ be a subclass of $B$. Let $B$ be a subclass of $C$. Then $A$ is a subclass of $C$.

title: Subclass of Well-Ordered Class is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $\RR \subseteq V \times V$ be a relation. Let $A$ be a subclass of $V$ which is well-ordered under $\RR$. Let $B$ be a subclass of $A$. Then $B$ is also well-ordered under $\RR$.

title: Subcontrary Statements/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subcontrary Statements ==

title: Subcover is Refinement of Cover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover for $S$. Let $\VV$ be a subcover of $\CC$. Then $\VV$ is a refinement of $\CC$.

title: Subcover of Open Cover is Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\CC$ be an open cover of $T$. Let $\CC'$ be a subcover of $S$. Then $\CC'$ is also an open cover of $T$.

title: Subdivision (Graph Theory)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subdivisions in the context of Graph Theory ==

title: Subdomain Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of an integral domain $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subdomain of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these conditions hold: $(1): \quad \struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ $(2): \quad$ The unity of $R$ is also in $S$, that is $1_R = 1_S$.

title: Subextensions of Separable Field Extension are Separable
snippet: Let $E / K / F$ be a tower of fields. Let $E / F$ be separable. Then $E / K$ and $K / F$ are separable.

title: Subfactorial/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subfactorials ==

title: Subfield Test
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $K$ be a subset of $F$.

title: Subfield of Subfield is Subfield
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $K_1, K_2$ be fields, such that: $K_1$ is a subfield of $R$ $K_2$ is a subfield of $K_1$ Then $K_2$ is a subfield of $R$.

title: Subframe is a Frame
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $M = \struct{T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ be a subframe of $L$ where $\preceq \restriction_T$ is the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then $M$ is a frame.

title: Subgroup/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subgroups ==

title: Subgroup Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\struct {H, \circ}$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $*: H \times G \to G$ be the subgroup action defined for all $h \in H, g \in G$ as: $\forall h \in H, g \in G: h * g := h \circ g$ Then $*$ is a group action.

title: Subgroup Containing all Squares of Group Elements is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with the property that: $\forall x \in G: x^2 \in H$ Then $H$ is normal in $G$.

title: Subgroup Generated by Commuting Elements is Abelian
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S \subseteq G$ such that: $\forall x, y \in S: x \circ y = y \circ x$ Then the subgroup generated by $S$ is abelian.

title: Subgroup Generated by Infinite Order Element is Infinite
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$ be of infinite order. Let $\gen a$ be the subgroup generated by $a$. Then $\gen a$ is of infinite order.

title: Subgroup Generated by One Element is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$. Then $\gen a$, the subgroup generated by $a$, is cyclic:

title: Subgroup Generated by One Element is Set of Powers
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $a \in G$. Then the subgroup generated by $a$ is the set of powers: $\gen a = \set {a^n : n \in \Z}$

title: Subgroup Generated by Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $H = \gen H$ where $\gen H$ denotes the subgroup generated by $H$.

title: Subgroup Generated by Subgroup and Element
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group. Let $H$ be a proper subgroup of $G$. Let $a \in G \setminus H$. Let $n$ be the indicator of $a$ in $H$. Then: $K = \left\{{x a^k: x \in H, \ 0 \le k < n}\right\}$ is a subgroup of $G$ such that $H \subseteq K$, and each element of $K$ has a unique representation in this form. Moreover: $K = \left\langle{H, a}\right\rangle$ where $\left\langle{H, a}\right\rangle$ denotes the subgroup generated by $\left\{{H, a}\right\}$, and: $\left\vert{K}\right\vert = n \left\vert{H}\right\vert$ where $\left\vert{K}\right\vert$ denotes the order of $K$.

title: Subgroup Product is Internal Group Direct Product iff Surjective
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $\sequence {H_n}$ be a sequence of subgroups of $G$. Let $\ds \phi: \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k \to G$ be a mapping defined by: $\ds \map \phi {h_1, h_2, \ldots, h_n} = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n h_k$ Then $\phi$ is surjective : $\ds G = \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k$ That is, $G$ is the internal group direct product of $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_n$.

title: Subgroup Subset of Subgroup Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ and $K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then: $H \subseteq H \circ K \supseteq K$ where $H \circ K$ denotes the subset product of $H$ and $K$.

title: Subgroup equals Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: g \circ N \circ g^{-1} = N$ $\forall g \in G: g^{-1} \circ N \circ g = N$

title: Subgroup is Closed iff Quotient is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $G / H$ be their quotient.

title: Subgroup is Normal Subgroup of Normalizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. A subgroup $H \le G$ is a normal subgroup of its normalizer: $H \le G \implies H \lhd \map {N_G} H$

title: Subgroup is Normal iff Contains Conjugate Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ : {{eqn | n = 1 | q = \forall g \in G | l = n \in N | o = \iff | r = g \circ n \circ g^{-1} \in N }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall g \in G | l = n \in N | o = \iff | r = g^{-1} \circ n \circ g \in N }}

title: Subgroup is Normal iff Left Cosets are Right Cosets
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : Every right coset of $N$ in $G$ is a left coset or equivalently: The right coset space of $N$ in $G$ equals its left coset space.

title: Subgroup is Normal iff Normal Subset
snippet: Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be a group. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) it is a normal subset of $G$.

title: Subgroup is Normal iff it contains Product of Inverses
snippet: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is normal : $\forall a, b \in G: a b \in H \implies a^{-1} b^{-1} \in H$

title: Subgroup is Subgroup of Normalizer
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. A subgroup $H \le G$ is a subgroup of its normalizer: $H \le G \implies H \le \map {N_G} H$

title: Subgroup is Subset of Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: N \subseteq g \circ N \circ g^{-1}$ $\forall g \in G: N \subseteq g^{-1} \circ N \circ g$

title: Subgroup is Superset of Conjugate iff Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $N$ is normal in $G$ (by definition 1) : $\forall g \in G: g \circ N \circ g^{-1} \subseteq N$ $\forall g \in G: g^{-1} \circ N \circ g \subseteq N$

title: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Abelian
snippet: A subgroup of an abelian group is itself abelian.

title: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Normal
snippet: Every subgroup of an abelian group is normal.

title: Subgroup of Additive Group Modulo m is Ideal of Ring
snippet: Let $m \in \Z: m > 1$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ be the additive group of integers modulo $m$. Then every subgroup of $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ is an ideal of the ring of integers modulo $m$ $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$.

title: Subgroup of Additive Group of Integers Generated by Two Integers
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Let $\gen {m, n}$ be the subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ generated by $m$ and $n$. Then: $\gen {m, n} = \struct {\gcd \set {m, n} \Z, +}$ That is, the additive groups of integer multiples of $\gcd \set {m, n}$, where $\gcd \set {m, n}$ is the greatest common divisor of $m$ and $n$.

title: Subgroup of Circle Group Generated by Distinct Roots of Unity
snippet: Let $K$ be the circle group. Let $m, n \in \Z_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $d = \lcm \set {m, n}$ be the least common multiple of $m$ and $n$. Let $\alpha$ be a primitive $n$th root of unity. Let $\beta$ be a primitive $m$th root of unity. Let $\gamma$ be a primitive $d$th root of unity. Let $H = \gen {\alpha, \beta}$ be the subgroup of $K$ generated by $\alpha, \beta$. Then $H = \gen \gamma$.

title: Subgroup of Cyclic Group is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is cyclic.

title: Subgroup of Direct Product is not necessarily Direct Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $G \times H$ denote the direct product of $G$ and $H$. Let $K$ be a subgroup of $G \times H$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $K$ is of the form: $G' \times H'$ where: $G'$ is a subgroup of $G$ $H'$ is a subgroup of $H$.

title: Subgroup of Elements whose Order Divides Integer
snippet: Let $A$ be an abelian group. Let $k \in \Z$ and $B$ be a set of the form: $\left\{{x \in A : x^k = e}\right\}$ Then $B$ is a subgroup of $A$.

title: Subgroup of Finite Cyclic Group is Determined by Order
snippet: Let $G = \gen g$ be a cyclic group whose order is $n$ and whose identity is $e$. Let $d \divides n$, where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then there exists exactly one subgroup $G_d = \gen {g^{n / d} }$ of $G$ with $d$ elements.

title: Subgroup of Free Group is Free Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a free group. Let $H \le G$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that $H$ is not the trivial group. Then $H$ is also a free group.

title: Subgroup of Index 2 contains all Squares of Group Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ whose index is $2$. Then: $\forall x \in G: x^2 \in H$

title: Subgroup of Index 2 is Normal
snippet: A subgroup of index $2$ is always normal.

title: Subgroup of Index 3 does not necessarily contain all Cubes of Group Elements
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ whose index is $3$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\forall x \in G: x^3 \in H$

title: Subgroup of Index Least Prime Divisor is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n>1$. Let $p$ be the least prime divisor of $n$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ such that: $\index G H = p$ where $\index G H$ denotes the index of $H$ in $G$. Then $H$ is normal.

title: Subgroup of Infinite Cyclic Group is Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G = \gen a$ be an infinite cyclic group generated by $a$, whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G, g \ne e: \exists k \in \Z, k \ne 0: g = a^k$. Let $H = \gen g$. Then $H \le G$ and $H \cong G$. Thus, all non-trivial subgroups of an infinite cyclic group are themselves infinite cyclic groups. A subgroup of $G = \gen a$ is denoted as follows: $n G := \gen {a^n}$ This notation is usually used in the context of $\struct {\Z, +}$, where $n \Z$ is (informally) understood as the set of integer multiples of $n$.

title: Subgroup of Integers is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Every subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ is an ideal of the ring $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$.

title: Subgroup of Order 1 is Trivial
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ has exactly $1$ subgroup of order $1$: the trivial subgroup.

title: Subgroup of Order p in Group of Order 2p is Normal
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a group of order $2 p$. Let $a \in G$ be of order $p$. Let $K = \gen a$ be the subgroup of $G$ generated by $a$. Then $K$ is normal in $G$.

title: Subgroup of Real Numbers is Discrete or Dense
snippet: Let $G$ be a subgroup of the additive group of real numbers. Then one of the following holds: $G$ is dense in $\R$. $G$ is discrete and there exists $a \in \R$ such that $G = a \Z$, that is, $G$ is cyclic.

title: Subgroup of Solvable Group is Solvable
snippet: Let $G$ be a solvable group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is solvable.

title: Subgroup of Subgroup with Prime Index
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $K$ be a subgroup of $H$. Let: $\index G K = p$ where: $p$ denotes a prime number $\index G K$ denotes the index of $K$ in $G$. Then either: $H = K$ or: $H = G$

title: Subgroup of Symmetric Group that Fixes n
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $H$ denote the subgroup of $S_n$ which consists of all $\pi \in S_n$ such that: $\map \pi n = n$ Then: $H = S_{n - 1}$ and the index of $H$ in $S_n$ is given by: $\index {S_n} H = n$

title: Subgroups of Additive Group of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $n \Z$ be the additive group of integer multiples of $n$. Every non-trivial subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ has the form $n \Z$.

title: Subgroups of Additive Group of Integers Modulo m
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. The subgroups of $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ are the additive groups of integers modulo $k$ where: $k \divides m$

title: Subgroups of Cartesian Product of Additive Group of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ denote the additive group of integers. Let $m, n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be (strictly) positive integers. Let $\struct {\Z \times \Z, +}$ denote the Cartesian product of $\struct {\Z, +}$ with itself. The subgroups of $\struct {\Z \times \Z, +}$ are not all of the form: $\struct {m \Z, +} \times \struct {n \Z, +}$ where $\struct {m \Z, +}$ denotes the additive group of integer multiples of $m$.

title: Subgroups of Symmetric Group Isomorphic to Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Let $k \in \closedint 1 n$. Then there are $\dbinom n k$ subgroups of $S_n$ which are isomorphic to $S_k \times S_{n - k}$, where $\dbinom n k$ denotes the binomial coefficient. All of these $\dbinom n k$ subgroups are conjugate.

title: Subgroups of Symmetry Group of Regular Hexagon
snippet: Let $\HH = ABCDEF$ be a regular hexagon. Let $D_6$ denote the symmetry group of $\HH$. 520px Let $e$ denote the identity mapping Let $\alpha$ denote rotation of $\HH$ anticlockwise through $\dfrac \pi 3$ radians ($60 \degrees$) Let $\beta$ denote reflection of $\HH$ in the $AD$ axis. The subsets of $D_6$ which form its subgroups are as follows: Order $1$: $\set e$ Order $2$: $\set {e, \alpha^3}$ $\set {e, \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^2 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^3 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^4 \beta}$ $\set {e, \alpha^5 \beta}$ Order $3$: $\set {e, \alpha^2, \alpha^4}$ Order…

title: Sublinear Functional is Linear Functional iff Dominates Unique Linear Functional
snippet: Let $X$ be a vector space over $\R$. Let $p : X \to \R$ be a sublinear functional. Then $p$ is linear there exists a unique linear functional $f : X \to \R$ such that: $\map f x \le \map p x$ for each $x \in X$.

title: Submartingale Composed with Increasing Convex Function is Submartingale
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}, \Pr}$ be a continuous-time filtered probability space. Let $\sequence {X_t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a $\sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}$-submartingale. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be an increasing convex function such that $\map f {X_t}$ is integrable for each $t \in \hointr 0 \infty$. Then $\sequence {\map f {X_t} }_{t \ge 0}$ is a $\sequence {\FF_t}_{t \ge 0}$-submartingale.

title: Submetacompact Space is Countably Metacompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a submetacompact topological space. Then $T$ is countably metacompact.

title: Submodule Test
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $G$. Then $\struct {H, +, \circ}_R$ is a submodule of $G$ :

title: Submodule is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G}$ be an abelian group. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be an $R$-submodule of $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$. Then $H$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Submodule of Module of Polynomial Functions
snippet: Let $K$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\map P K$ be the set of all polynomial functions on $K$. Consider the set $\map {P_m} K$ of all the polynomial functions: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{m - 1} \alpha_k {I_K}^k$ for some $m \in \N^*$ where: $\sequence {\alpha_k}_{k \in \closedint 0 {m - 1} }$ is any sequence of $m$ terms of $K$. Then $\map {P_m} K$ is a submodule of $\map P K$.

title: Subnet of Convergent Net Converges to Same Limit
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ and $\struct {A, \sqsubseteq}$ be directed sets. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net in $X$ that converges to $x$. Let $\family {x_{\map \phi \alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a subnet of $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$. Then $\family {x_{\map \phi \alpha} }_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ converges to $x$.

title: Subobject Class in Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf {Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf {Set} } } S$ be the category of subobject classes of $S$. Let $\powerset S$ be the order category on the power set of $S$ induced by Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering. Then $\map {\overline {\mathbf {Sub} }_{\mathbf {Set} } } S \cong \powerset S$.

title: Subring Containing Ring Unity has Unity
snippet: Let $\struct{R, +, *}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct{S, +_S, *_S}$ be a subring of $\struct{R, +, *}$. Let $1_R \in S$. Then $1_R$ is the unity of $\struct{S, +_S, *_S}$.

title: Subring Generated by Unity of Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the mapping $g: \Z \to R$ be defined as $\forall n \in \Z: \map g n = n 1_R$, where $n 1_R$ the $n$th power of $1_R$. Let $\ideal x$ be the principal ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ generated by $x$. Then $g$ is an epimorphism from $\Z$ onto the subring $S$ of $R$ generated by $1_R$. If $R$ has no proper zero divisors, then $g$ is the only nonzero homomorphism from $\Z$ into $R$.

title: Subring Module is Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +_S, \times_S}$ be a subring of $R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $\circ_S$ be the restriction of $\circ$ to $S \times G$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_S}_S$ be subring module induced by $S$. Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_S}_S$ is an $S$-module.

title: Subring Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, +, \circ}$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad S \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x + \paren {-y} \in S$ $(3): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x \circ y \in S$

title: Subring is not necessarily Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +_S, \circ_S}$ be a subring of $R$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $S$ is also an ideal of $R$.

title: Subring of Commutative Ring is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct{R, +, *}$ be a commutatve ring. Let $\struct{S, +_S, *_S}$ be a subring of $\struct{R, +, *}$. Then: $\struct{S, +_S, *_S}$ is a commutatve ring

title: Subring of Integers is Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Every subring of $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ is an ideal of the ring $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$.

title: Subring of Non-Archimedean Division Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring with non-archimedean norm $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$. Let $\struct {S, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_S }$ be a normed division subring of $R$. Then: $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_S$ is a non-archimedean norm.

title: Subring of Polynomials over Integral Domain Contains that Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $x \in R$. Let $D \sqbrk x$ denote the ring of polynomials in $x$ over $D$. Then $D \sqbrk x$ contains $D$ as a subring and $x$ as an element.

title: Subring of Polynomials over Integral Domain is Smallest Subring containing Element and Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $x \in R$. Let $D \sqbrk x$ denote the ring of polynomials in $x$ over $D$. Then $D \sqbrk x$ is the smallest subring of $R$ which contains $D$ as a subring and $x$ as an element.

title: Subrings of Integers are Sets of Integer Multiples
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ be the integral domain of integers. The subrings of $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ are the rings of integer multiples: $\struct {n \Z, +, \times}$ where $n \in \Z: n \ge 0$. There are no other subrings of $\struct {\Z, +, \times}$ but these.

title: Subsemigroup/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subsemigroups ==

title: Subsemigroup Closure Test
snippet: To show that an algebraic structure $\struct {T, \circ_T}$ is a subsemigroup of a semigroup $\struct {S, \circ}$, we need to show only that: $(1): \quad T \subseteq S$ $(2): \quad \circ$ is a closed operation in $T$. where $\circ_T$ denotes the restriction of $\circ$ to $T$.

title: Subsemigroup of Cancellable Mappings is Subgroup of Invertible Mappings
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $S^S$ denote the set of mappings from $S$ to itself. Let $\CC \subseteq S^S$ denote the set of cancellable mappings on $S$. Let $\MM \subseteq S^S$ denote the set of invertible mappings on $S$. Then: the subsemigroup $\struct {\CC, \circ}$ of $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ coincides with the subgroup $\struct {\MM, \circ}$ of $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Subsemigroup of Monoid is not necessarily Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$ Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {T, \circ}$ has an identity.

title: Subsemigroup of Ordered Semigroup is Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered semigroup. Let $\struct {T, \circ_T}$ be a subsemigroup of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the ordered structure $\struct {T, \circ_T, \preceq_T}$ is also an ordered semigroup. In the above: $\circ_T$ denotes the operation induced on $T$ by $\circ$ $\preceq_T$ denotes the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T \times T$.

title: Subsequence/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subsequences ==

title: Subsequence Characterization of Cauchy Sequence in Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence : for all strictly increasing sequences $\sequence {n_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {m_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ in $\N$, we have that: $\norm {x_{n_k} - x_{m_k} }_X \to 0$.

title: Subsequence Characterization of Cauchy Sequence in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence : for all strictly increasing sequences $\sequence {n_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {m_k}_{k \mathop \in \N}$ in $\N$, we have that: $x_{n_k} - x_{m_k} \to {\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Subsequence is Equivalent to Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $R$. Let $\sequence {x_{m_n} }$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} {x_n - x_{m_n} } = 0$

title: Subsequence of Basic Sequence in Banach Space is Basic Sequence
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then $\sequence {x_{n_k} }_{k \mathop \in \N}$ is a basic sequence in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$.

title: Subsequence of Cauchy Sequence in Normed Division Ring is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed division ring with zero: $0$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a Cauchy sequence in $R$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then: $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ is a Cauchy sequence in $R$.

title: Subsequence of Real Sequence Diverging to Negative Infinity Diverges to Negative Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a real sequence with $x_n \to -\infty$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_j} }_{j \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $x_{n_j} \to -\infty$

title: Subsequence of Real Sequence Diverging to Positive Infinity Diverges to Positive Infinity
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a real sequence with $x_n \to +\infty$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_j} }_{j \mathop \in \N}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$. Then: $x_{n_j} \to +\infty$

title: Subsequence of Sequence in Metric Space with Limit
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $M$. Let $x$ be a limit point of $S = \set {x_n: n \in \N}$, the set of members of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $\sequence {x_n}$ has a subsequence which converges to $x$.

title: Subsequence of Subsequence
snippet: Let $s$ be a set. Let $\sequence {s_n}$ be a sequence in $S$. Let $\sequence {s_m}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {s_n}$. Let $\sequence {s_k}$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {s_m}$. Then $\sequence {s_k}$ is a subsequence of $\sequence {s_n}$.

title: Subset/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subsets ==

title: Subset Equivalences
snippet: == Definitions == In the following: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$ $S \cap T$ denotes the intersection of $S$ and $T$ $S \setminus T$ denotes the set difference between $S$ and $T$ $\O$ denotes the empty set $\mathbb U$ denotes the universal set $\complement$ denotes set complement.

title: Subset Intersection Set Difference is Empty Iff Subset of Second Set
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$. Then: $A \cap S \setminus T = \O$ $A \subseteq T$

title: Subset Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subset Product == Let $G$ be a group.

title: Subset Product/Singleton/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subset Products with Singletons ==

title: Subset Product Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $\struct {G, \circ}$. For any $S \in \powerset G$ and for any $g \in G$, the subset product action: $\forall g \in G: \forall S \in \powerset G: g * S = g \circ S$ is a group action.

title: Subset Product defining Inverse Completion of Commutative Semigroup is Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $\struct {C, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ be the subsemigroup of cancellable elements of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Let $\struct {T, \circ'}$ be an inverse completion of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then: $S \circ' C^{-1}$ is a commutative semigroup where $S \circ' C^{-1}$ is the subset product of $S$ with $C^{-1}$ under $\circ'$ in $T$.

title: Subset Product is Subset of Generator
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $X, Y \subseteq \struct {G, \circ}$. Then $X \circ Y \subseteq \gen {X, Y}$ where: $X \circ Y$ is the Subset Product of $X$ and $Y$ in $G$. $\gen {X, Y}$ is the subgroup of $G$ generated by $X$ and $Y$.

title: Subset Product of Abelian Subgroups
snippet: Let $\left({G, \circ}\right)$ be an abelian group. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subgroups of $G$. Then $H_1 \circ H_2$ is a subgroup of $G$.

title: Subset Product of Normal Subgroups is Normal
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $N$ and $N'$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Then $N N'$ is also a normal subgroup of $G$.

title: Subset Product of Normal Subgroups with Trivial Intersection
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H, K$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Let $H \cap K = e$. Then $H K$ is isomorphic to $H \times K$ where: $H K$ denotes the subset product of $H$ and $K$ $H \times K$ denotes the direct product of $H$ and $K$.

title: Subset Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ $H$ and $K$ are permutable. That is: $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ : $H \circ K = K \circ H$ where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

title: Subset Product with Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity element $e$. Then $e \circ S = S \circ e = S$, where $\circ$ is understood to be the subset product with singleton.

title: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup as Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let: $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then: $N \lhd \gen {N, H} = N H = H N \le G$ where: $\le$ denotes subgroup $\lhd$ denotes normal subgroup $\gen {N, H}$ denotes a subgroup generator $N H$ denotes subset product.

title: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup is Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let: $(1): \quad H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $(2): \quad N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $H N$ denote subset product. Then $H N$ and $N H$ are both subgroups of $G$.

title: Subset Product within Commutative Structure is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. If $\circ$ is commutative, then the operation $\circ_\PP$ induced on the power set of $S$ is also commutative.

title: Subset Product within Semigroup is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a semigroup. Then the operation $\circ_\PP$ induced on the power set of $S$ is also associative.

title: Subset Products of Normal Subgroup with Normal Subgroup of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let: $(1): \quad H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $(2): \quad K$ be a normal subgroup of $H$ $(3): \quad N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$ Then: $N K \lhd N H$ where: $N K$ and $N H$ denote subset product $\lhd$ denotes the relation of being a normal subgroup.

title: Subset Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: The subset relation is antisymmetric: $\paren {x \subseteq y} \land \paren {y \subseteq x} \iff x = y$ where $x$ and $y$ are sets.

title: Subset Relation is Compatible with Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the subset relation on $S$ is compatible with $\circ_\PP$. That is: {{eqn | q = \forall X, Y, Z \in \powerset S | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {X \circ_\PP Z} \subseteq \paren {Y \circ_\PP Z} | c = }} {{eqn | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {Z \circ_\PP X} \subseteq \paren {Z \circ_\PP Y} | c = }}

title: Subset Relation is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\mathbb S \subseteq \powerset S$ be any subset of $\powerset S$, that is, an arbitrary set of subsets of $S$. Then $\subseteq$ is an ordering on $\mathbb S$. In other words, let $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\mathbb S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set.

title: Subset Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $C$ be a class. The subset relation $\subseteq$ on $C$ is a reflexive relation on $C$.

title: Subset Relation is Transitive
snippet: The subset relation is transitive: $\paren {R \subseteq S} \land \paren {S \subseteq T} \implies R \subseteq T$

title: Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\powerset S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set. The ordering $\subseteq$ is partial $S$ is neither empty nor a singleton; otherwise it is total.

title: Subset and Image Admit Infima and Mapping is Increasing implies Infimum of Image Succeeds Mapping at Infimum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a increasing mapping. Let $D \subseteq S$ such that $D$ admits a infimum in $S$ and $f \sqbrk D$ admits a infimum in $T$. Then $\map f {\inf D} \precsim \map \inf {f \sqbrk D}$

title: Subset and Image Admit Suprema and Mapping is Increasing implies Supremum of Image Precedes Mapping at Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$, $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a increasing mapping. Let $D \subseteq S$ such that $D$ admits a supremum in $S$ and $f \sqbrk D$ admits a supremum in $T$. Then: $\map \sup {f \sqbrk D} \precsim \map f {\sup D}$

title: Subset equals Image of Preimage iff Mapping is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Similarly, let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$. Then: $\forall B \in \powerset T: B = \map {\paren {f^\to \circ f^\gets} } B$ $f$ is a surjection.

title: Subset equals Image of Preimage implies Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let: $\forall B \subseteq T: B = \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B$ where $f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$. Then $f$ is a surjection.

title: Subset equals Preimage of Image iff Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $f$. Then: $\forall A \subseteq S: A = \paren {f^{-1} \circ f} \sqbrk A$ $f$ is an injection where: $f \sqbrk A$ denotes the image of $A$ under $f$ $f^{-1} \circ f$ denotes the composition of $f^{-1}$ and $f$. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as: $\forall A \in \powerset S: A = \map {\paren {f^\gets \circ f^\to} } A$ $f$ is an injection

title: Subset equals Preimage of Image implies Injection
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $f^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping of $f$. Similarly, let $f^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S$ be the inverse image mapping of $f$. Let: $\forall A \in \powerset S: A = \map {\paren {f^\gets \circ f^\to} } A$ Then $f$ is an injection.

title: Subset has 2 Conjugates then Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $S$ be a subset of $G$. Let $S$ have exactly two conjugates in $G$. Then $G$ has a proper non-trivial normal subgroup.

title: Subset implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \subseteq T$. Furthermore, let: $T \sim \card T$ where $\card T$ denotes the cardinality of $T$. Then: $\card S \le \card T$

title: Subset in Neighborhood Space is Neighborhood iff it contains Open Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \NN}$ be a neighborhood space. Let $x \in S$ be a point of $S$. Let $N \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then $N$ is a neighborhood of $x$ there exists an open set $U$ of $\struct {S, \NN}$ such that $x \in U \subseteq N$.

title: Subset in Subsets
