snippet: Let $S, B$ be sets. Let $A$ be subset of $S$. Then: $A \subseteq B \iff \forall x \in S: x \in A \implies x \in B$

title: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $(1): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {z + x} \le \paren {z + y}$ $(2): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {x + z} \le \paren {y + z}$

title: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $(1): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {z \cdot x} \le \paren {z \cdot y}$ $(2): \quad x \le y \implies \paren {x \cdot z} \le \paren {y \cdot z}$

title: Subset is Compatible with Ordinal Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$. Let $x \in y$. Then: $x^+ \in y^+$

title: Subset is Element of Power Set
snippet: Let $x$ be a set. Let $\powerset x$ denote the power set of $x$. Then: $y \in \powerset x \iff y \subseteq x$

title: Subset is Left Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {z + x} \le \paren {z + y}$

title: Subset is Left Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {z \cdot x} \le \paren {z \cdot y}$

title: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Addition
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {x + z} \le \paren {y + z}$

title: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Exponentiation
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies x^z \le y^z$

title: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {x \cdot z} \le \paren {y \cdot z}$

title: Subset not necessarily Submagma
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $T \subseteq S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\struct {T, \circ} \subseteq \struct {S, \circ}$ That is, it does not always follow that $\struct {T, \circ}$ is a submagma of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

title: Subset of Abelian Group Generated by Product of Element with Inverse Element is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be an abelian group. Let $S \subset G$ be a non-empty subset of $G$ such that $\struct {S, \circ}$ is closed. Let $H$ be the set defined as: $H := \set {x \circ y^{-1}: x, y \in S}$ Then $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

title: Subset of Banach Space Bounded Away from Zero including Zero Vector in Weak Closure contains Basic Sequence with Basis Constant Arbitrarily Close to 1
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\cl_w$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $S \subseteq X$ be such that: $\ds \inf_{x \mathop \in S} \norm x_X > 0$ and: ${\mathbf 0}_X \in \map {\cl_w} S$ Let $\epsilon > 0$. Then there exists a basic sequence in $S$ with basis constant $K_b \le 1 + \epsilon$.

title: Subset of Bounded Above Set is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded above. Then $A$ is also bounded above.

title: Subset of Bounded Below Set is Bounded Below
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded below. Then $A$ is also bounded below.

title: Subset of Bounded Subset of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $B$ be a bounded subset of $M$. Let $\map \diam B$ denote the diameter of $B$. Let $C \subseteq B$ be a subset of $B$. Then $C$ is a bounded subset of $M$ such that: $\map \diam C \le \map \diam B$

title: Subset of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of ordered pairs. Then $S$ is the subset of the cartesian product of two sets.

title: Subset of Cartesian Product not necessarily Cartesian Product of Subsets
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Let $A$ and $B$ both have at least two distinct elements. Then there exists $W \subseteq A \times B$ such that $W$ is not the cartesian product of a subset of $A$ and a subset of $B$.

title: Subset of Codomain is Superset of Image of Preimage
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $B \subseteq T \implies \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B \subseteq B$ where: $f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$ $f^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $f$ $f \circ f^{-1}$ denotes composition of $f$ and $f^{-1}$. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as: $\forall B \in \powerset T: \map {\paren {f^\to \circ f^\gets} } B \subseteq B$

title: Subset of Countable Set is Countable
snippet: A subset of a countable set is countable.

title: Subset of Countably Infinite Set is Countable
snippet: Every subset of a countably infinite set is countable.

title: Subset of Cover is Cover of Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover of $S$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let: $\CC_T = \set {C \in \CC : C \cap T \ne \O}$ Then $\CC_T$ is a cover of $T$: $T \subseteq \bigcup \CC_T$

title: Subset of Discrete Set of Subsets is Discrete
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is discrete then $\GG$ is discrete.

title: Subset of Domain is Subset of Preimage of Image
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $A \subseteq S \implies A \subseteq \paren {f^{-1} \circ f} \sqbrk A$ where: $f \sqbrk A$ denotes the image of $A$ under $f$ $f^{-1} \sqbrk A$ denotes the preimage of $A$ under $f$ $f^{-1} \circ f$ denotes composition of $f^{-1}$ and $f$. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as: $\forall A \in \powerset S: A \subseteq \map {\paren {f^\gets \circ f^\to} } A$

title: Subset of Empty Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Then: $A$ is a subset of the empty set $\O$ $A$ is equal to the empty set: $A \subseteq \O \iff A = \O$

title: Subset of Empty Set iff Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\O$ denote the empty set. Then $S \subseteq \O$ $S = \O$.

title: Subset of Euclidean Plane whose Product of Coordinates are Greater Than or Equal to 1 is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^2, \tau_d}$ be the real number plane with the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $A \subseteq R^2$ be the set of all points defined as: $A := \set {\tuple {x, y} \in \R^2: x y \ge 1}$ Then $A$ is a closed set in $\struct {\R^2, d}$.

title: Subset of Excluded Point Space is not Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_{\bar p} }$ be a excluded point space such that $S$ is not a singleton. Let $H \subseteq S$. Then $H$ is not dense-in-itself.

title: Subset of Finite Dimensional Normed Vector Space is Compact iff Closed and Bounded/Sufficient Condition
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\,\cdot\,}}$ be a finite-dimensional normed vector space. Let $K \subset X$ be a compact subset. Then $K$ is closed and bounded.

title: Subset of Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X$ be a finite set. If $Y$ is a subset of $X$, then $Y$ is also finite.

title: Subset of Hilbert Sequence Space with Non-Empty Interior is not Compact
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Let $H$ be a subset of $\ell^2$ whose interior is non-empty. Then $H$ is not compact in $\ell^2$.

title: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Compact
snippet: $H \subseteq S$ is compact in an indiscrete topological space $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$.

title: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Compact and Sequentially Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$.

title: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ containing more than one point. Then $H$ is dense-in-itself.

title: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Everywhere Dense
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$ be an indiscrete topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ such that $H \ne \O$. Then $H$ is everywhere dense.

title: Subset of Indiscrete Space is Sequentially Compact
snippet: $H \subseteq S$ is sequentially compact in an indiscrete topological space $T = \struct {S, \set {\O, S} }$.

title: Subset of Join Semilattice on Total Ordering is Closed
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preccurlyeq}$ be the join semilattice with respect to $\preccurlyeq$. Let $T \subseteq S$ be an arbitrary subset of $S$. Then $\struct {T, \vee, \preccurlyeq}$ is closed under $\vee$.

title: Subset of Linear Code with Even Weight Codewords
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear code. Let $C^+$ be the subset of $C$ consisting of all the codewords of $C$ which have even weight. Then $C^+$ is a subgroup of $C$ such that either $C^+ = C$ or such that $\order {C^+} = \dfrac {\order C} 2$.

title: Subset of Linearly Independent Set is Linearly Independent
snippet: A subset of a linearly independent set is also linearly independent.

title: Subset of Linearly Ordered Space which is Order-Complete and Closed but not Compact
snippet: Let $X = \hointr 0 1 \cup \openint 2 3 \cup \set 4$. Let $\preceq$ be the ordering on $X$ induced by the usual ordering of the real numbers. Let $\tau$ be the $\preceq$ order topology on $X$. Let $Y = \hointr 0 1 \cup \set 4$. Let $\tau'$ be the $\tau$-relative subspace topology on $Y$. Then: $\struct {Y, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice $Y$ is closed in $X$ but: $\struct {Y, \tau'}$ is not compact.

title: Subset of Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Locally Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is locally finite then $\GG$ is locally finite.

title: Subset of Meager Set is Meager Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be meager in $T$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ is meager in $T$.

title: Subset of Metric Space contains Limits of Sequences iff Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then $H$ is closed in $M$ : for each sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of points of $H$ that converges to a point $a \in A$, it follows that $a \in H$.

title: Subset of Metric Space is Closed iff contains all Zero Distance Points
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then $H$ is closed in $M$ : $\forall x \in A: \map d {x, H} = 0 \implies x \in H$ where $\map d {x, H}$ denotes the distance between $x$ and $H$.

title: Subset of Metric Space is Subset of its Closure
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Then: $H \subseteq H^-$ where $H^-$ denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Subset of Module Containing Identity is Linearly Dependent
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be an $R$-module. Let $H \subseteq G$ such that $e \in H$. Then $H$ is a linearly dependent set.

title: Subset of Natural Numbers is Cofinal iff Infinite
snippet: Consider the ordered set $\struct {\N, \le}$, where $\le$ is the usual ordering on the natural numbers. Let $S \subseteq \N$. Then $S$ is cofinal it is infinite.

title: Subset of Natural Numbers is either Finite or Denumerable
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Then $S$ is either finite or denumerable.

title: Subset of Natural Numbers under Max Operation is Monoid
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \N$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Let $\struct {S, \max}$ denote the algebraic structure formed from $S$ and the max operation. Then $\struct {S, \max}$ is a monoid. Its identity element is the smallest element of $S$.

title: Subset of Naturals is Finite iff Bounded
snippet: Let $X$ be a subset of the natural numbers $\N$. Then $X$ is finite it is bounded.

title: Subset of Normed Vector Space is Bounded Away from Zero iff Closure does not contain Zero
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Let $\cl$ be the closure in $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. We have that: $\ds \inf_{x \mathop \in S} 
orm x > 0$ ${\mathbf 0}_X 
ot \in \map \cl S$.

title: Subset of Normed Vector Space is Everywhere Dense iff Closure is Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}}$ be a normed vector space. Let $D \subseteq X$ be a subset of $X$. Let $D^-$ be the closure of $D$. Then $D$ is dense $D^- = X$.

title: Subset of Normed Vector Space is von Neumann-Bounded in Weak Topology iff Norm Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $B \subseteq X$. Then $B$ is bounded in $X$ it is von Neumann-bounded in $\struct {X, w}$.

title: Subset of Normed Vector Space providing Bounded Point Evaluations is Norm Bounded
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Suppose that: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \cmod {\map f x} < \infty$ for each $f \in X^\ast$. Then we have: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} 
orm x_X < \infty$ Hence $S$ is bounded.

title: Subset of Nowhere Dense Subset is Nowhere Dense
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A \subseteq S$ be nowhere dense in $T$. Let $B \subseteq A$. Then $B$ is nowhere dense in $T$.

title: Subset of Open Reciprocal-N Balls forms Neighborhood Basis in Real Number Line
snippet: Let $\R$ denote the real number line with the usual (Euclidean) metric. Let $a \in \R$ be a point in $\R$. Let $k \in \Z$ be some fixed integer. Let $\BB_a$ be defined as: $\BB_a := \set {\map {B_\epsilon} a: \epsilon \in \set {\dfrac 1 n: n \in \N, n > k} }$ that is, the set of all open $\epsilon$-balls of $a$ for $\epsilon$ which are reciprocals of integers greater than $k$. Then the $\BB_a$ is a basis for the neighborhood system of $a$.

title: Subset of Ordinal implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $x$ be an ordinal such that $S \subseteq x$. Then: $\card S \le \card x$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Subset of Ordinals has Minimal Element
snippet: Let $A$ be an ordinal (we shall allow $A$ to be a proper class). Let $B$ be a nonempty subset of $A$. Then $B$ has an $\Epsilon$-minimal element. That is: $\exists x \in B: B \cap x = \O$

title: Subset of Particular Point Space is either Open or Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be any subset of $T$. Then $H$ is either open or closed in $T$. The only sets which are both closed and open in $T$ are $S$ and $\O$.

title: Subset of Partition Space is Open iff Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a partition space : $\forall U \subseteq S: U \in \tau \iff \relcomp S U \in \tau$ That is, a topological space is a partition space : all open sets are closed all closed sets are also open. That is, all open sets and closed sets of a partition space are clopen.

title: Subset of Preimage under Relation is Preimage of Subset
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $X \subseteq S, Y \subseteq T$. Then: $X \subseteq \RR^{-1} \sqbrk Y \iff \RR \sqbrk X \subseteq Y$ In the language of direct image mappings, this can be written: $X \subseteq \map {\RR^\gets} Y \iff \map {\RR^\to} X \subseteq Y$

title: Subset of Real Numbers is Interval iff Connected
snippet: Let the real number line $\R$ be considered as a topological space. Let $S$ be a subspace of $\R$. Then $S$ is connected $S$ is an interval of $\R$. That is, the only subspaces of $\R$ that are connected are intervals.

title: Subset of Real Numbers is Path-Connected iff Interval
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line considered as an Euclidean space. Let $S \subseteq \R$ be a subset of $\R$. Then $S$ is a path-connected metric subspace of $\R$ $S$ is a real interval.

title: Subset of Satisfiable Set is Satisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-satisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\FF'$ be a subset of $\FF$. Then $\FF'$ is also $\mathscr M$-satisfiable.

title: Subset of Set Difference iff Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$ Then: $A \cap T = \O \iff A \subseteq S \setminus T$ where: $A \cap T$ denotes set intersection $\O$ denotes the empty set $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference.

title: Subset of Set is Coarser than Set
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subset of $S$ such that $A \subseteq B$ Then $A$ is coarser than $B$.

title: Subset of Set with Propositional Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $P: S \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on $S$. Then: $\set {x \in S: \map P x} \subseteq S$

title: Subset of Set with Zero Outer Measure has Zero Outer Measure
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\mu^\ast$ be an outer measure on $X$. Let $B \subseteq X$ be such that $\map {\mu^\ast} B = 0$. Let $A \subseteq B$. Then $\map {\mu^\ast} A = 0$.

title: Subset of Sigma-Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Sigma-Locally Finite
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Let $\GG \subseteq \FF$. If $\FF$ is $\sigma$-locally finite then $\GG$ is $\sigma$-locally finite.

title: Subset of Standard Discrete Metric Space is Neighborhood of Each Point
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space where $d$ is the standard discrete metric. Let $S \subseteq A$. Let $a \in S$. Then $S$ is a neighborhood of $a$. That is, every subset of $A$ is a neighborhood of each of its points.

title: Subset of Standard Discrete Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a standard discrete metric space. Let $S \subseteq A$ be a subset of $A$. Then $S$ is an open set of $M$.

title: Subset of Toset is Toset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a totally ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Then $\left({T, \preceq \restriction_T}\right)$ is also a totally ordered set. In the above, $\preceq \restriction_T$ denotes the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$.

title: Subset of Totally Bounded Metric Space is Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a totally bounded metric space. Let $A \subseteq M$. Then $A$ is totally bounded.

title: Subset of Totally Ordered Set can be Uniquely Expressed as Partition of Maximal Order-Convex Sets
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$ Then $H$ can be uniquely expressed as a partition whose components are maximally order-convex sets.

title: Subset of Well-Founded Relation is Well-Founded
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $\QQ$ be a subset of $\RR$. Then $\QQ$ is also a well-founded relation on $S$.

title: Subset of Well-Ordered Set is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then the relational structure $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ is a well-ordered set.

title: Subset of von Neumann-Bounded Set is von Neumann-Bounded
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $E \subseteq X$ be von Neumann-bounded. Let $F \subseteq X$. Then $F$ is von Neumann-bounded.

title: Subsets Greater Than and Less Than Identity of Ordered Abelian Group are Isomorphic Ordered Semigroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered abelian group whose identity element is $e$. Let $G^+$ and $G^-$ denote the subsets of $G$ defined as: $G^+ = \set {x \in G: e \preccurlyeq x}$ $G^- = \set {x \in G: x \preccurlyeq e}$ Then $\struct {G^+, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ and $\struct {G^-, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ are subsemigroups of $G$ such that the inversion mapping $\iota: G \to G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \map \iota g = g^{-1}$ is: an isomorphism from $\struct {G^+, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ to $\struct {G^-, \circ, \succcurlyeq}$ and: an isomorphism from $\struct {G^-, \circ,…

title: Subsets Satisfy Formulation 1 Matroid Base Axiom Iff Complements Satisfy Formulation 5
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr B$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr B^* = \set{S \setminus B : B \in \mathscr B}$. Then: $\mathscr B$ satisfies formulation $1$ base axiom: $\mathscr B^*$ satisfies formulation $5$ base axiom: {{axiom | n = \text B 5 | q = \forall B^*_1, B^*_2 \in \mathscr B^* | mr= x \in B^*_1 \setminus B^*_2 \implies \exists y \in B^*_2 \setminus B^*_1 : \paren {B^*_2 \setminus \set y} \cup \set x \in \mathscr B }}

title: Subsets Satisfy Formulation 5 Matroid Base Axiom Iff Complements Satisfy Formulation 1
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $\mathscr B$ be a non-empty set of subsets of $S$. Let $\mathscr B^* = \set{S \setminus B : B \in \mathscr B}$. Then: $\mathscr B$ satisfies formulation $5$ base axiom: $\mathscr B^*$ satisfies formulation $1$ base axiom: {{axiom | n = \text B 1 | q = \forall B^*_1, B^*_2 \in \mathscr B^* | mr= x \in B^*_1 \setminus B^*_2 \implies \exists y \in B^*_2 \setminus B^*_1 : \paren {B^*_1 \setminus \set x} \cup \set y \in \mathscr B^* }}

title: Subsets in Increasing Union
snippet: Let $S_0, S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_i, \ldots$ be a nested sequence of sets, that is: $S_0 \subseteq S_1 \subseteq S_2 \subseteq \ldots \subseteq S_i \subseteq \ldots$ Let $S$ be the increasing union of $S_0, S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_i, \ldots$: $\ds S = \bigcup_{i \mathop \in \N} S_i$ Then: $\forall s \in S: \exists k \in \N: \forall j \ge k: s \in S_j$

title: Subsets of Disjoint Sets are Disjoint
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be disjoint sets. Let $S' \subseteq S$ and $T' \subseteq T$. Then $S'$ and $T'$ are disjoint.

title: Subsets of Equidecomposable Subsets are Equidecomposable
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \R^n$ be equidecomposable. Let $S \subseteq A$. Then there exists $T \subseteq B$ such that $S$ and $T$ are equidecomposable.

title: Subspace Topology is Initial Topology with respect to Inclusion Mapping
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $Y$ be a non-empty subset of $X$. Let $\iota: Y \to X$ be the inclusion mapping. Let $\tau_Y$ be the initial topology on $Y$ with respect to $\iota$. Then $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ is a topological subspace of $\struct {X, \tau}$. That is: $\tau_Y = \set {U \cap Y: U \in \tau}$

title: Subspace Topology on Initial Topology is Initial Topology on Restrictions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a topological subspace of $X$. Then $\tau_Y$ is the initial topology on $Y$ with respect to $\family {f_i \restriction_Y}_{i \mathop \in I}$.

title: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Closed iff Complete
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\struct {S, d}$ be a subspace of $\struct {M, d}$. Then $S$ is closed $S$ is complete.

title: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Relatively Compact iff Every Sequence has Cauchy Subsequence
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {X, d}$. Then $\struct {H, d_H}$ is relatively compact : every sequence in $H$ has a Cauchy subsequence.

title: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Relatively Compact iff Totally Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a metric space. Let $A \subseteq M$. We have that $A$ is relatively compact in $\struct {M, d}$ $A$ is totally bounded.

title: Subspace of Either-Or Space less Zero is not Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the either-or space. Let $H = S \setminus \set 0$ be the set $S$ without zero. Then the topological subspace $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$ is not a Lindelöf space.

title: Subspace of Euclidean Space is Closed
snippet: Let $\R^n$ be a Euclidean space. Every subspace of $\R^n$ is closed in $\R^n$.

title: Subspace of Finite Complement Topology is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a finite complement topology on an infinite set $S$. Then every topological subspace of $T$, including $T$ itself, is a compact space.

title: Subspace of Metric Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Let $d_H: H \times H \to \R$ be the restriction $d \restriction_{H \times H}$ of $d$ to $H$. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {A, d}$. Then $d_H$ is a metric on $H$.

title: Subspace of Metrizable Space is Metrizable Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a metrizable topological space. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a subspace of $\struct{X, \tau}$. Then: $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ is a metrizable topological space

title: Subspace of Noetherian Topological Space is Noetherian
snippet: Let $X$ be a Noetherian topological space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a subspace. Then $Y$ is Noetherian.

title: Subspace of Normed Vector Space with Induced Norm forms Normed Vector Space
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $Y \subseteq X$ be a vector subspace. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y$ be the induced norm on $Y$. Then $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ is a normed vector space.

title: Subspace of Product Space has Initial Topology with respect to Restricted Projections
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\XX$ be the cartesian product of $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$: $\ds \XX := \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ For each $i \in I$, let $\pr_i: \XX \to X_i$ denote the projection of $\XX$ onto $X_i$. Let $Y \subseteq \XX$ be a non-empty subset of $\XX$. For each $i \in I$, let $\pr_i \restriction_Y$ denote the restriction of $\pr_i$ to $Y$. Let $\tau_\XX$ be the product topology on $\XX$. Let $\tau_Y$ be the subspace topology on $Y$.

title: Subspace of Product Space is Homeomorphic to Factor Space
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds \struct {X, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \struct {X_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$. Suppose that $X$ is non-empty. Then for each $i \in I$ there is a subspace $Y_i \subseteq X$ which is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_i, \tau_i}$.

title: Subspace of Real Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a \le x \le b}$ be a closed interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map C {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map C {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

title: Subspace of Real Differentiable Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map \DD {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all differentiable real functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map \DD {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

title: Subspace of Real Functions of Differentiability Class
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a < x < b}$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map {C^m} {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$ in differentiability class $m$. Then $\struct {\map {C^m} {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

title: Subspace of Riemann Integrable Functions
snippet: Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a \le x \le b}$ be a closed interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map \RR {\mathbb J}$ be the set of all Riemann integrable functions on $\mathbb J$. Then $\struct {\map \RR {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

title: Subspace of Separable Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a separable metric space. Let $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {X, d}$. Then $Y$ is separable.

title: Subspace of Smooth Real Functions
snippet: == Corollary to Subspace of Real Functions of Differentiability Class == Let $\mathbb J = \set {x \in \R: a < x < b}$ be an open interval of the real number line $\R$. Let $\map {C^\infty} {\mathbb J}$ denote the set of all continuous real functions on $\mathbb J$ which are differentiable on $\mathbb J$ at all orders. Then $\struct {\map {C^\infty} {\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$ is a subspace of the $\R$-vector space $\struct {\R^{\mathbb J}, +, \times}_\R$.

title: Subspace of Subspace is Subspace
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $S$ and $\tau_H$ be the subspace topology on $H$. Let $K \subseteq S$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then the subspace topology on $K$ induced by $\tau$ equals the subspace topology on $K$ induced by $\tau_H$.

title: Subspaces of Dimension 2 Real Vector Space
snippet: Take the $\R$-vector space $\left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$. Let $S$ be a subspace of $\left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$. Then $S$ is one of: $(1): \quad \left({\R^2, +, \times}\right)_\R$ $(2): \quad \left\{{0}\right\}$ $(3): \quad$ A line through the origin.

title: Substitution/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Substitution ==

title: Substitution Instance of Term is Term
snippet: Let $\beta, \tau$ be terms of predicate logic. Let $x \in \operatorname {VAR}$ be a variable. Let $\map \beta {x \gets \tau}$ be the substitution instance of $\beta$ substituting $\tau$ for $x$. Then $\map \beta {x \gets \tau}$ is a term.

title: Substitution Instance of WFF is WFF
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of predicate logic. Let $\tau$ be a term of predicate logic. Let $x \in \mathrm{VAR}$ be a variable. Let $\mathbf A \left({x \gets \tau}\right)$ be the substitution instance of $\mathbf A$ substituting $\tau$ for $x$. Then $\mathbf A \left({x \gets \tau}\right)$ is a WFF.

title: Substitution Property of Equality
snippet: Let $\map F z$ be an expression of the variable $z$. Then: $\forall x, y: x = y \implies \map F x = \map F y$.

title: Substitution Rule for Matrices
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Then: $(1): \quad \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \delta_{i j} a_{j k} = a_{i k}$ $(2): \quad \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \delta_{i j} a_{k j} = a_{k i}$ where: $\delta_{i j}$ is the Kronecker delta $a_{j k}$ is element $\tuple {j, k}$ of $\mathbf A$.

title: Substitution Theorem for Terms
snippet: Let $\beta, \tau$ be terms. Let $x \in \mathrm {VAR}$ be a variable. Let $\map \beta {x \gets \tau}$ be the substitution instance of $\beta$ substituting $\tau$ for $x$. Let $\AA$ be a structure for predicate logic. Let $\sigma$ be an assignment for $\beta$ and $\tau$. Suppose that: $\map {\operatorname{val}_\AA} \tau \sqbrk \sigma = a$ where $\map {\operatorname{val}_\AA} \tau \sqbrk \sigma$ is the value of $\tau$ under $\sigma$.

title: Substitution Theorem for Well-Formed Formulas
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of predicate logic. Let $x \in \mathrm{VAR}$ be a variable. Let $\tau$ be a term of predicate logic which is freely substitutable for $x$ in $\mathbf A$. Let $\map {\mathbf A} {x \gets \tau}$ be the substitution instance of $\mathbf A$ substituting $\tau$ for $x$. Let $\AA$ be a structure for predicate logic. Let $\sigma$ be an assignment for $\mathbf A$ and $\tau$. Suppose that: $\map {\operatorname{val}_\AA} \tau \sqbrk \sigma = a$ where $\map {\operatorname{val}_\AA} \tau \sqbrk \sigma$ is the value of $\tau$ under $\sigma$.

title: Substitution for Equivalent Subformula is Equivalent
snippet: Let $\mathbf B$ a WFF of propositional logic. Let $\mathbf A, \mathbf A'$ be equivalent WFFs. Let $\mathbf A$ be a subformula of $\mathbf B$. Let $\mathbf B' = \map {\mathbf B} {\mathbf A \,//\, \mathbf A'}$ be the substitution of $\mathbf A'$ for $\mathbf A$ in $\mathbf B$. Then $\mathbf B$ and $\mathbf B'$ are equivalent.

title: Substitution of Arithmetically Definable Functions is Arithmetically Definable
snippet: Let $f: \N^t \to \N$ and $g_1, g_2, \dotsc, g_t: \N^k \to \N$ be partial functions. Let $h: \N^k \to \N$ be defined by substitution as: $\map h {x_1, \dotsc, x_k} \approx \map f {\map {g_1} {x_1, \dotsc, x_k}, \dotsc, \map {g_t} {x_1, \dotsc, x_k} }$ Suppose that there exists a $\Sigma_1$ WFF of $t + 1$ free variables: $\map {\phi_f} {y, x_1, \dotsc, x_t}$ such that: $y = \map f {x_1, \dotsc, x_t} \iff \N \models \map {\phi_f} {\sqbrk y, \sqbrk {x_1}, \dotsc, \sqbrk {x_t} }$ where $\sqbrk a$ denotes the unary representation of $a \in \N$.

title: Substitution of Constant yields Primitive Recursive Function
snippet: Let $f: \N^{k + 1} \to \N$ be a primitive recursive function‎. Then $g: \N^k \to \N$ given by: $\map g {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} = \map f {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_{i - 1}, a, n_i \ldots, n_k}$ is primitive recursive.

title: Substitution of Elements
snippet: Let $a$, $b$, and $x$ be sets. $a = b \implies \paren {a \in x \iff b \in x}$

title: Substitutivity of Class Equality
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\map P A$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P B$ be the same proposition $\map P A$ with all instances of $A$ replaced with instances of $B$. Let $=$ denote class equality. $A = B \implies \paren {\map P A \iff \map P B}$

title: Substitutivity of Equality
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\map P x$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P y$ be the same proposition $\map P x$ with some (not necessarily all) free instances of $x$ replaced with free instances of $y$. Let $=$ denote set equality. $x = y \implies \paren {\map P x \iff \map P y}$

title: Substructure of Entropic Structure is Entropic
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \odot}$ be an entropic structure: $\forall a, b, c, d \in S: \paren {a \odot b} \odot \paren {c \odot d} = \paren {a \odot c} \odot \paren {b \odot d}$ Let $\struct {T, \odot_T}$ be a substructure of $\struct {S, \odot}$. Then $\struct {T, \odot_T}$ is also an entropic structure.

title: Subtract Half is Replicative Function
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = x - \dfrac 1 2$ Then $f$ is a replicative function.

title: Subtraction/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Subtraction ==

title: Subtraction has no Identity Element
snippet: The operation of subtraction on numbers of any kind has no identity.

title: Subtraction of Complex Numbers
snippet: Let $z_1 := a_1 + i b_1$ and $z_2 := a_2 + i b_2$ be complex numbers. The subtraction operation on $z_1$ and $z_2$ is: $z_1 - z_2 = \paren {a_1 - a_2} + i \paren {b_1 - b_2}$

title: Subtraction of Divisors obeys Distributive Law
snippet: In modern algebraic language: $a = \dfrac 1 n b, c = \dfrac 1 n d \implies a - c = \dfrac 1 n \paren {b - d}$

title: Subtraction of Fractions
snippet: Let $a, b, c, d \in \Z$ such that $b d \ne 0$. Then: $\dfrac a b - \dfrac c d = \dfrac {a D - B c} {\lcm \set {b, d} }$ where: $B = \dfrac b {\gcd \set {b, d} }$ $D = \dfrac d {\gcd \set {b, d} }$ $\lcm$ denotes lowest common multiple $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor.

title: Subtraction of Multiples of Divisors obeys Distributive Law
snippet: In modern algebraic language: $a = \dfrac m n b, c = \dfrac m n d \implies a - c = \dfrac m n \paren {b - d}$

title: Subtraction of Subring is Subtraction of Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be an ring. For each $x, y \in R$ let $x - y$ denote the subtraction of $x$ and $y$ in $R$. Let $\struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S}}$ be a subring of $R$. For each $x, y \in S$ let $x \sim y$ denote the subtraction of $x$ and $y$ in $S$. Then: $\forall x, y \in S: x \sim y = x - y$

title: Subtraction on Integers is Extension of Natural Numbers
snippet: Integer subtraction is an extension of the definition of subtraction on the natural numbers.

title: Subtraction on Numbers is Anticommutative
snippet: The operation of subtraction on the numbers is anticommutative. That is: $a - b = b - a \iff a = b$

title: Subtraction on Numbers is Not Associative
snippet: The operation of subtraction on the numbers is not associative. That is, in general: $a - \paren {b - c} \ne \paren {a - b} - c$

title: Succeed is Dual to Precede
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $a, b \in S$. The following are dual statements: $a$ succeeds $b$ $a$ precedes $b$

title: Successive Solutions of Phi of n equals Phi of n + 2
snippet: Let $\phi$ denote the Euler $\phi$ function. $7$ and $8$ are two successive integers which are solutions to the equation: $\map \phi n = \map \phi {n + 2}$

title: Successor Mapping is Progressing
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $s: V \to V$ denote the successor mapping on $V$: $\forall x \in V: \map s x := x \cup \set x$ Then $s$ is a progressing mapping.

title: Successor Mapping is Slowly Progressing
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $s: V \to V$ denote the successor mapping on $V$: $\forall x \in V: \map s x := x \cup \set x$ Then $s$ is a slowly progressing mapping.

title: Successor Mapping of Peano Structure has no Fixed Point
snippet: Let $\PP = \struct {P, s, 0}$ be a Peano structure. Then: $\forall n \in P: \map s n \ne n$ That is, the successor mapping has no fixed points.

title: Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers has no Fixed Element
snippet: Let $\N$ denote the set of natural numbers. Then: $\forall n \in \N: n + 1 \ne n$

title: Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers is Progressing
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers as defined by the von Neumann construction. Let $s: \omega \to \omega$ denote the successor mapping on $\omega$. Then $s$ is a progressing mapping.

title: Successor Mapping on Natural Numbers is not Surjection
snippet: Let $f: \N \to \N$ be the successor mapping on the natural numbers $\N$: $\forall n \in \N: \map f n = n + 1$ Then $f$ is not a surjection.

title: Successor Mapping on Ordinals is Strictly Progressing
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $s$ denote the successor mapping on $\On$: $\forall \alpha \in \On: \map s \alpha := \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ where $\alpha$ is an ordinal. Then $s$ is a strictly progressing mapping.

title: Successor Set of Ordinal is Ordinal
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $\alpha \in \On$ be an ordinal. Then its successor set $\alpha^+ = \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ is also an ordinal.

title: Successor Set of Ordinary Transitive Set is Ordinary
snippet: Let $x$ be a transitive set which is also ordinary. Let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$: $x^+ = x \cup \set x$ Then $x^+$ is also an ordinary set.

title: Successor Set of Transitive Set is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a transitive set. Then its successor set $S^+ = S \cup \set S$ is also transitive.

title: Successor Sets of Linearly Ordered Set Induced by Convex Component Partition
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a linearly ordered space. Let $A$ and $B$ be separated sets of $T$. Let $A^*$ and $B^*$ be defined as: {{eqn | l = A^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in A, \closedint a b \cap B^- = \O} }} {{eqn | l = B^* | r = \bigcup \set {\closedint a b: a, b \in B, \closedint a b \cap A^- = \O} }} where $A^-$ and $B^-$ denote the closure of $A$ and $B$ in $T$.

title: Successor is Less than Successor
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals and let $x^+$ denote the successor set of $x$. Then, $x \in y \iff x^+ \in y^+$.

title: Successor is Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y \in S$. Then: $x \preceq y$ $y = \map \sup {x, y}$ where $\map \sup {x, y}$ is the supremum of $x$ and $y$

title: Successor of Element of Ordinal is Subset
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Then: $x \in y \iff x^+ \subseteq y$

title: Successor of Omega
snippet: $\omega + 1 = \set {0, 1, 2, \ldots; \omega}$ where $\omega$ is the minimally inductive set and $\omega + 1$ is the successor of $\omega$. Note the use of the semicolon; this is the notation for multipart infinite sets.

title: Successor of Ordinal Smaller than Limit Ordinal is also Smaller
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $\lambda \in \On$ be a limit ordinal. Then: $\forall \alpha \in \On: \alpha < \lambda \implies \alpha^+ < \lambda$

title: Successor to Natural Number
snippet: Let $\N_{> 0}$ be the 1-based natural numbers: $\N_{> 0} = \left\{{1, 2, 3, \ldots}\right\}$ Let $ 0}$: $\forall a, b \in \N_{>0}: a 0}: a + c = b$ Let $a \in \N_{>0}$. Then there exists no natural number $n$ such that $a < n < a + 1$.

snippet: In general, quaternion multiplication does not commute. title: Sufficient Condition for Quotient Group by Intersection to be Abelian
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $N$ and $K$ be normal subgroups of $G$. Let the quotient groups $G / N$ and $G / K$ be abelian. Then the quotient group $G / \paren {N \cap K}$ is also abelian.

title: Sufficient Condition for Square of Product to be Triangular
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $2 n^2 \pm 1 = m^2$ be a square number. Then $\paren {m n}^2$ is a triangular number.

title: Sufficient Condition for Stationary Point to be Local Maximum
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f$ have a stationary point at $\xi \in \openint a b$. Let the second derivative of $f$ at $\xi$ be (strictly) negative. Then $\xi$ is a local maximum.

title: Sufficient Condition for Stationary Point to be Local Minimum
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f$ have a stationary point at $\xi \in \openint a b$. Let the second derivative of $f$ at $\xi$ be (strictly) positive. Then $\xi$ is a local minimum.

title: Sufficient Condition for Twice Differentiable Functional to have Minimum
snippet: Let $J$ be a twice differentiable functional. Let $J$ have an extremum for $y=\hat y$. Let the second variation $\delta^2 J \sqbrk {\hat y; h}$ be strongly positive $h$. Then $J$ acquires the minimum for $y = \hat y$ .

title: Sufficient Condition for Vector Equals Inverse iff Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_\GF$ be a vector space over a field $\GF$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Let $\GF$ be infinite. Then: $\forall \mathbf v, -\mathbf v \in \mathbf V: \mathbf v = - \mathbf v \iff \mathbf v = \mathbf 0$

title: Sufficient Condition for Weak Convergence of Bounded Sequence in Hilbert Space in terms of Everywhere Dense Set
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a bounded sequence in $\HH$. Let $D$ be an everywhere dense set in $\HH$ such that: $\innerprod {x_n} v \to \innerprod x v$ for all $v \in D$, for some $x \in \HH$. Then: $x_n \weakconv x$ where $\weakconv$ denotes weak convergence.

title: Sufficient Conditions for Basis of Finite Dimensional Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $n \ge 0$ be a natural number. Let $E$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $K$. Let $B \subseteq E$ be a subset such that $\card B = n$. $(1): \quad$ $B$ is a basis of $E$. $(2): \quad$ $B$ is linearly independent. $(3): \quad$ $B$ is a generator for $E$.

snippet: Let $J$ be a functional such that: $\ds J \sqbrk y = \int_a^b \map F {x, y, y'} \rd x$ $\map y a = A$ $\map y b = B$ Let $y = \map y x$ be an extremum. Let the strengthened Legendre's Condition hold. Let the strengthened Jacobi's Necessary Condition hold. Then the functional $J$ has a weak minimum for $y = \map y x$.

title: Suffix of String is Substring
snippet: Let $S$ be a string. Let $T$ be a suffix of $S$. Then $T$ is a substring of $S$.

Sum Less Maximum is Minimum
snippet: For all numbers $a, b$ where $a, b$ in $\N, \Z, \Q$ or $\R$: $a + b - \max \set {a, b} = \min \set {a, b}$.

title: Sum Less Minimum is Maximum
snippet: For all numbers $a, b$ where $a, b$ in $\N, \Z, \Q$ or $\R$: $a + b - \min \set {a, b} = \max \set {a, b}$

title: Sum Over Divisors Equals Sum Over Quotients
snippet: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Let $f: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be a mapping on the positive integers. Let $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f d$ be the sum of $\map f d$ over the divisors of $n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f d = \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f {\frac n d}$.

title: Sum Over Divisors of Multiplicative Function
snippet: Let $f: \Z_{>0} \to \Z_{>0}$ be a multiplicative function. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Let $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f d$ be the sum over the divisors of $n$. Then $\ds \map F n = \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map f d$ is also a multiplicative function.

title: Sum Over Divisors of von Mangoldt is Logarithm
snippet: Let $\Lambda$ be von Mangoldt's function. Then for $n \ge 1$: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \map \Lambda d = \ln n$

title: Sum Rule for Convergent Generalized Sums
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +}$ be a commutative topological semigroup. Let $\family {g_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ and $\family {h_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of elements in $G$. Let the generalized sums $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$ and $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} h_i$ be convergent to the following limits: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i = a$ $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} h_i = b$ Then: the generalized sum $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} \paren{g_i + h_i}$ converges to the limit: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} \paren{g_i + h_i} = a + b$

title: Sum Rule for Derivatives
snippet: Let $\map f x, \map j x, \map k x$ be real functions defined on the open interval $I$. Let $\xi \in I$ be a point in $I$ at which both $j$ and $k$ are differentiable. Let $\map f x = \map j x + \map k x$. Then $f$ is differentiable at $\xi$ and: $\map {f'} \xi = \map {j'} \xi + \map {k'} \xi$ It follows from the definition of derivative that if $j$ and $k$ are both differentiable on the interval $I$, then: $\forall x \in I: \map {f'} x = \map {j'} x + \map {k'} x$

title: Sum Rule for Sequence in Normed Vector Space

title: Sum of Absolutely Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ be two real or complex series that are absolutely convergent. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {a_n + b_n}$ is absolutely convergent, and: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {a_n + b_n} = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$

title: Sum of Absorbing Sets is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A, B \subseteq X$ be absorbing sets. Then $A + B$ is absorbing.

title: Sum of Additive Function Values is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\SS$ be an algebra of sets. Let $f: \SS \to \overline \R$ be an additive function on $\SS$. Let $A, B \in \SS$. Then the sum $\map f A + \map f B$ is well-defined in the extended real numbers $\overline \R$.

title: Sum of Adjacent Sequences of Triangular Numbers
snippet: {{eqn | l = T_5 + T_6 + T_7 + T_8 | r = T_9 + T_{10} | c = }} {{eqn | l = T_{11} + T_{12} + T_{13} + T_{14} + T_{15} | r = T_{16} + T_{17} + T_{18} | c = }} and so on. The $n$th line of the pattern can be written as: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = n^2 + n - 1}^{n^2 + 2 n} T_n = \sum_{k \mathop = n^2 + 2 n + 1}^{n^2 + 3 n} T_n$

title: Sum of All Ring Products is Additive Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +}$ and $\struct {T, +}$ be additive subgroups of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $S + T$ be defined as subset product. Let $S T$ be defined as: $\ds S T = \set {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n s_i \circ t_i: s_1 \in S, t_i \in T, i \in \closedint 1 n}$ Then both $S + T$ and $S T$ are additive subgroups of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$.

title: Sum of All Ring Products is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +}, \struct {T, +}, \struct {U, +}$ be additive subgroups of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $S T$ be defined as: $\ds S T = \set {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n s_i \circ t_i: s_1 \in S, t_i \in T, i \in \closedint 1 n}$ Then: $\paren {S T} U = S \paren {T U}$

title: Sum of All Ring Products is Closed under Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {S, +}$ and $\struct {T, +}$ be additive subgroups of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Let $S T$ be defined as: $\ds S T = \set {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n s_i \circ t_i: s_1 \in S, t_i \in T, i \in \closedint 1 n}$ Then $\struct {S T, +}$ is a closed subset of $\struct {R, +}$.

title: Sum of Alternating Sign Reciprocals of Sequence of Pairs of Consecutive Fibonacci Numbers is Reciprocal of Golden Mean Squared
snippet: {{eqn | l = \sum_{k \mathop \ge 2} \left({-1}\right)^k \dfrac 1 {F_k F_{k + 1} } | r = \dfrac 1 {1 \times 2} - \dfrac 1 {2 \times 3} + \dfrac 1 {3 \times 5} - \dfrac 1 {5 \times 8} + \cdots | c = }} {{eqn | r = \phi^{-2} | c = }} where: $F_k$ denotes the $k$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Sum of Angles between Straight Lines at Point form Four Right Angles
snippet: == Corollary to Two Angles on Straight Line make Two Right Angles == If any number of straight lines are drawn from a given point, the sum of the consecutive angles so formed is $4$ right angles.

title: Sum of Angles of Spherical Polygon
snippet: Let $P$ be a spherical polygon with $n$ sides. The sum of the inner angles of $P$ lies strictly between $180 \paren {n - 2}$ and $180 n$ degrees.

title: Sum of Angles of Spherical Triangle
snippet: The sum of the angles of a spherical triangle is between $\pi$ and $3 \pi$ radians.

title: Sum of Angles of Triangle equals Two Right Angles
snippet: In a triangle, the sum of the three interior angles equals two right angles.

title: Sum of Angles of Triangle in Elliptic Geometry
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle embedded in an elliptic geometry. Let $S$ denote the sum of the internal angles of $T$. Then $S$ is greater than $180 \degrees$.

title: Sum of Angles of Triangle in Hyperbolic Geometry
snippet: Let $T$ be a triangle embedded in a hyperbolic geometry. Let $S$ denote the sum of the internal angles of $T$. Then $S$ is less than $180 \degrees$.

title: Sum of Antecedent and Consequent of Proportion
snippet: That is, if $a : b = c : d$ and $a$ is the greatest and $d$ is the least, then: $a + d > b + c$

title: Sum of Arccotangents
snippet: $\arccot a + \arccot b = \arccot \dfrac {a b - 1} {a + b}$ where $\arccot$ denotes the arccotangent.

title: Sum of Arcsecant and Arccosecant
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $\size x \ge 1$. Then: $\arcsec x + \arccsc x = \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\arcsec$ and $\arccsc$ denote arcsecant and arccosecant respectively.

title: Sum of Arcsine and Arccosine
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $-1 \le x \le 1$. Then: $\arcsin x + \arccos x = \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\arcsin$ and $\arccos$ denote arcsine and arccosine respectively.

title: Sum of Arctangent and Arccotangent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\arctan x + \arccot x = \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\arctan$ and $\arccot$ denote arctangent and arccotangent respectively.

title: Sum of Arctangents
snippet: Let $\arctan a + \arctan b \in \openint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ Then: $\arctan a + \arctan b = \map \arctan {\dfrac {a + b} {1 - a b} }$ where $\arctan$ denotes the arctangent.

title: Sum of Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as: $a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$ Then its closed-form expression is: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + \frac {r d \paren {1 - n r^{n - 1} + \paren {n - 1} r^n} } {\paren {1 - r}^2}$

title: Sum of Arithmetic Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be an arithmetic sequence defined as: $a_k = a + k d$ for $k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1$ Then its closed-form expression is: {{eqn | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} | r = n \paren {a + \frac {n - 1} 2 d} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac {n \paren {a + l} } 2 | c = where $l$ is the last term of $\sequence {a_k}$ }}

title: Sum of Banach Space-Valued Simple Functions is Simple Function
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $f, g : I \to X$ be a simple function. Then $f + g$ is simple.

title: Sum of Bernoulli Numbers by Binomial Coefficients Vanishes
snippet: $\forall n \in \Z_{>1}: \ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \binom n k B_k = 0$ where $B_k$ denotes the $k$th Bernoulli number.

title: Sum of Bernoulli Numbers by Power of Two and Binomial Coefficient
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: {{eqn | l = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dbinom {2 n + 1} {2 k} 2^{2 k} B_{2 k} | r = \binom {2 n + 1} 2 2^2 B_2 + \binom {2 n + 1} 4 2^4 B_4 + \binom {2 n + 1} 6 2^6 B_6 + \cdots | c = }} where $B_n$ denotes the $n$th Bernoulli number.

title: Sum of Binomial Coefficients over Lower Index
snippet: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \binom n i = 2^n$ where $\dbinom n i$ is a binomial coefficient.

title: Sum of Binomial Coefficients over Upper Index
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer such that $m \ge 0$. Then: {{eqn | l = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n \binom j m | r = \binom {n + 1} {m + 1} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \dbinom 0 m + \dbinom 1 m + \dbinom 2 m + \cdots + \dbinom n m = \dbinom {n + 1} {m + 1} | c = }} where $\dbinom j m$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Sum of Bochner Measurable Functions is Bochner Measurable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $f, g : I \to X$ be a Bochner measurable function. Then $f + g$ is Bochner measurable.

title: Sum of Bounded Linear Transformations is Bounded Linear Transformation
snippet:
Let $\mathbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces over $\mathbb F$. Let $A, B : \HH 	o \KK$ be bounded linear transformations. Let $
orm \cdot$ be the norm on the space of bounded linear transformations. Then: $A + B$ is a bounded linear transformation with: $
orm {A + B} \le 
orm A + 
orm B$

title: Sum of Cardinals is Associative
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a + \paren {\mathbf b + \mathbf c} = \paren {\mathbf a + \mathbf b} + \mathbf c$ where $\mathbf a + \mathbf b$ denotes the sum of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$.

title: Sum of Cardinals is Commutative
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ be cardinals. Then: $\mathbf a + \mathbf b = \mathbf b + \mathbf a$ where $\mathbf a + \mathbf b$ denotes the sum of $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$.

title: Sum of Cauchy Sequences in Topological Vector Space is Cauchy Sequence
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \in \N}$ be Cauchy sequences in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n + y_n}_{n \in \N}$ is a Cauchy sequence in $X$.

title: Sum of Ceilings not less than Ceiling of Sum
snippet: Let $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling function. Then: $\ceiling x + \ceiling y \ge \ceiling {x + y}$ The equality holds: $\ceiling x + \ceiling y = \ceiling {x + y}$ either: $x \in \Z$ or $y \in \Z$ or: $x \bmod 1 + y \bmod 1 > 1$ where $x \bmod 1$ denotes the modulo operation.

title: Sum of Chi-Squared Random Variables
snippet: Let $n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k$ be strictly positive integers which sum to $N$. Let $X_i \sim {\chi^2}_{n_i}$ for $1 \le i \le k$, where ${\chi^2}_{n_i}$ is the chi-squared distribution with $n_i$ degrees of freedom. Then: $\ds X = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^k X_i \sim {\chi^2}_N$

title: Sum of Closable Densely-Defined Linear Operator and Densely-Defined Bounded Linear Operator is Closable
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a closable densely-defined linear operator with closure $\tuple {\map D {\overline T}, \overline T}$. Let $\tuple {\map D S, S}$ be a densely-defined bounded linear operator with closure $\tuple {\HH, \overline S}$ such that: $\map D T \subseteq \map D S$ Let $\tuple {\map D T, T + S}$ be the sum of $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ and $\tuple {\map D S, S}$.

title: Sum of Closed Linear Subspace and Finite-Dimensional Subspace of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $N$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$. Let $F$ be a finite dimensional linear subspace of $X$. Then $N + F$ is closed in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Sum of Closures is Subset of Closure of Sum in Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A, B \subseteq X$. Then: $A^- + B^- \subseteq \paren {A + B}^-$ where $A^-$, $B^-$ and $\paren {A + B}^-$ denote the closures of $A$, $B$ and $A + B$.

title: Sum of Compact Subsets of Topological Vector Space is Compact
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A$ and $B$ be compact (topological) subspaces of $X$. Then $A + B$ is compact.

title: Sum of Complex Conjugates
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of the complex number $z$. Then: $\overline {z_1 + z_2} = \overline {z_1} + \overline {z_2}$

title: Sum of Complex Exponentials of i times Arithmetic Sequence of Angles

title: Sum of Complex Indices of Real Number
snippet: Let $r \in \R_{> 0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Let $\psi, \tau \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $r^\lambda$ be defined as the the principal branch of a positive real number raised to a complex number. Then: $r^{\psi \mathop + \tau} = r^\psi \times r^\tau$

title: Sum of Complex Integrals on Adjacent Intervals
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \C$ be a continuous complex function. Let $c \in \closedint a b$. Then: $\ds \int_a^c \map f t \rd t + \int_c^b \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t$

title: Sum of Complex Number with Conjugate
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Let $\map \Re z$ be the real part of $z$. Then: $z + \overline z = 2 \, \map \Re z$

title: Sum of Complex Numbers in Exponential Form
snippet: Let $z_1 = r_1 e^{i \theta_1}$ and $z_2 = r_2 e^{i \theta_2}$ be complex numbers expressed in exponential form. Let $z_3 = r_3 e^{i \theta_3} = z_1 + z_2$. Then: $r_3 = \sqrt { {r_1}^2 + {r_2}^2 + 2 r_1 r_2 \map \cos {\theta_1 - \theta_2} }$ $\theta_3 = \map \arctan {\dfrac {r_1 \sin \theta_1 + r_2 \sin \theta_2} {r_1 \cos \theta_1 + r_2 \cos \theta_2} }$

title: Sum of Components of Equal Ratios
snippet: That is: $a_1 : b_1 = a_2 : b_2 = a_3 : b_3 = \cdots \implies \left({a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + \cdots}\right) : \left({b_1 + b_2 + b_3 + \cdots}\right)$

title: Sum of Computable Rational Sequences is Computable
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be computable rational sequences. Then, $\sequence {x_n + y_n}$ is a computable rational sequence.

title: Sum of Computable Real Sequences is Computable
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be computable real sequences. Then $\sequence {x_n + y_n}$ is a computable real sequence.

title: Sum of Conjugate Quadratic Irrationals
snippet: Let $a + \sqrt b$ and $a - \sqrt b$ be conjugate quadratic irrationals. Then their sum is rational: $\paren {a + \sqrt b} + \paren {a - \sqrt b} = 2 a$

title: Sum of Consecutive Odd Index Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: {{eqn | l = F_{2 k - 1} + F_{2 k + 1} | r = \phi^{2 k} + \phi^{-2 k} | c = }} where: $F_k$ denotes the $k$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

title: Sum of Consecutive Triangular Numbers is Square
snippet: The sum of two consecutive triangular numbers is a square number.

title: Sum of Continuous Functions on Topological Ring is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $R$ be a topological ring. Let $f, g : X \to R$ be continuous mappings. Then $f + g : X \to R$ is continuous.

title: Sum of Convergent Nets in Topological Vector Space is Convergent
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $x, y \in X$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ and $\family {y_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ be nets converging to $x$ and $y$ respectively. Then the net $\family {x_\lambda + y_\lambda}_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ converges to $x + y$.

title: Sum of Convergent Sequences in Topological Vector Space is Convergent
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $x, y \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \in \N}$ be convergent sequences with: $x_n \to x$ and: $y_n \to y$ Then $\sequence {x_n + y_n}_{n \in \N}$ converges with: $x_n + y_n \to x + y$

title: Sum of Convex Real Functions is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $f, g : X \to \R$ be a convex real function. Then $f + g$ is a convex real function.

title: Sum of Convex Sets in Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $A$ and $B$ be convex subsets of $X$. Then: $A + B$ is convex.

title: Sum of Cosecant and Cotangent
snippet: $\csc x + \cot x = \cot {\dfrac x 2}$

title: Sum of Cosets of Ideals is Sum in Quotient Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\powerset R$ be the power set of $R$. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be cosets of $J$. Let $X +_\PP Y$ be the sum of $X$ and $Y$, where $+_\PP$ is the operation induced on $\powerset R$ by $+$. The sum $X +_\PP Y$ in $\powerset R$ is also their sum in the quotient ring $R / J$.

title: Sum of Cosines of Angles in Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle. Then: $\cos A + \cos B + \cos C = 1 - 4 \sin \dfrac A 2 \sin \dfrac B 2 \sin \dfrac C 2$

title: Sum of Cosines of Arithmetic Sequence of Angles
