title: Summation of General Logarithms
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let $\ds \prod_{\map R i} a_i$ denote a product over $R$. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \map {\log_b} {\prod_{\map R i} a_i} = \sum_{\map R i} \log_b a_i$

title: Summation of Multiple of Mapping on Finite Set
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\lambda \in \mathbb A$. Let $g = \lambda \cdot f$ be the product of $f$ with $\lambda$. Then we have the equality of summations on finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map g s = \lambda \cdot \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s$

title: Summation of Odd Reciprocals in terms of Harmonic Numbers
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac 1 {2 k - 1} = H_{2 n} - \dfrac {H_n} 2$ where $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number.

title: Summation of Power Series by Harmonic Sequence
snippet: Consider the power series: $\map f x = \ds \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} a_k x^k$ Let $\map f x$ converge for $x = x_0$. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} a_k {x_0}^k H_k = \int_0^1 \dfrac {\map f {x_0} - \map f {x_0 y} } {1 - y} \rd y$ where $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number.

title: Summation of Powers over Product of Differences
snippet: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \begin{pmatrix} {\dfrac { {x_j}^r} {\ds \prod_{\substack {1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n \\ k \mathop \ne j} } \paren {x_j - x_k} } } \end{pmatrix} = \begin{cases} 0 & : 0 \le r < n - 1 \\ 1 & : r = n - 1 \\ \ds \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n x_j & : r = n \end{cases}$

title: Summation of Product of Differences
snippet: $\ds \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {u_j - u_k} \paren {v_j - v_k} = n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n u_j v_j - \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n u_j \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n v_j$

title: Summation of Products of n Numbers taken m at a time with Repetitions
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $b \ge a$. Let $U$ be a set of $n = b - a + 1$ numbers $\set {x_a, x_{a + 1}, \ldots, x_b}$. Let $m \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let: {{eqn | l = h_m | r = \sum_{a \mathop \le j_1 \mathop \le \mathop \cdots \mathop \le j_m \mathop \le b} \paren {\prod_{k \mathop = 1}^m x_{j_k} } | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sum_{a \mathop \le j_1 \mathop \le \mathop \cdots \mathop \le j_m \mathop \le b} x_{j_1} \cdots x_{j_m} | c = }} That is, $h_m$ is the product of all $m$-tuples of elements of $U$ taken $m$ at a time, allowing for repetition.

title: Summation of Reciprocal of Zero of Order 1 Bessel Function by Order 0 Bessel Function of it
snippet: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \dfrac 1 {x_n \map {J_0 } {x_n} } = 0 \cdotp 38479 \ldots$ where: $x_n$ is the $n$th zero of the order $1$ Bessel function of the first kind $\map {J_0 } {x_n}$ is the order $0$ Bessel function of the first kind of $x_n$.

title: Summation of Sum of Mappings on Finite Set
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f, g: S \to \mathbb A$ be mappings. Let $h = f + g$ be their sum. Then we have the equality of summations on finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map h s = \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s + \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map g s$

title: Summation of Summation over Divisors of Function of Two Variables
snippet: Let $c, d, n \in \Z$. Then: $\ds \sum_{d \mathop \divides n} \sum_{c \mathop \divides d} \map f {c, d} = \sum_{c \mathop \divides n} \sum_{d \mathop \divides \paren {n / c} } \map f {c, c d}$ where $c \divides d$ denotes that $c$ is a divisor of $d$.

title: Summation of Unity over Elements
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \Z$ be a set of integers. Let: $n := \ds \sum_{j \mathop \in S} 1$ Then $n$ is equal to the cardinality of $S$.

title: Summation of Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N,\Z,\Q,\R,\C$.

title: Summation of i from 1 to n of Summation of j from 1 to i
snippet: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^i a_{i j} = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \sum_{i \mathop = j}^n a_{i j}$

title: Summation over Cartesian Product as Double Summation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S, T$ be finite sets. Let $S \times T$ be their cartesian product. Let $f: S \times T \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then we have an equality of summations over finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \sum_{t \mathop \in T} \map f {s, t} = \sum_{\tuple {s, t} \mathop \in S \times T} \map f {s, t}$

title: Summation over Finite Index is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct{G, +}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $\family{g }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed subset of $G$ where the indexing set $I$ is finite. Then the summation $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$ is well-defined.

title: Summation over Finite Set Equals Summation over Support
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\map \supp f$ be its support. Then we have an equality of summations over finite sets: $\ds \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s = \sum_{s \mathop \in \map \supp f} \map f s$

title: Summation over Finite Set is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $n$ be the cardinality of $S$. let $\N_{<n}$ be an initial segment of the natural numbers. Let $g, h: \N_{<n} \to S$ be bijections. Then we have an equality of indexed summations of the compositions $f \circ g$ and $f \circ h$: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \map f {\map g i} = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \map f {\map h i}$ That is, the definition of summation over a finite set does not depend on the choice of the bijection $g: S \to \N_{< n}$.

title: Summation over Finite Subset is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct{G, +}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $F \subseteq G$ be a finite subset of $G$. Then the summation $\ds \sum_{g \mathop \in F} g$ is well-defined.

title: Summation over Interval equals Indexed Summation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then the summation over the finite set $\closedint a b$ equals the indexed summation from $a$ to $b$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in \closedint a b} \map f k = \sum_{k \mathop = a}^b \map f k$

title: Summation over Lower Index of Unsigned Stirling Numbers of the First Kind
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\ds \sum_k {n \brack k} = n!$ where: $\ds {n \brack k}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $n!$ denotes the factorial of $n$.

title: Summation over Lower Index of Unsigned Stirling Numbers of the First Kind with Alternating Signs
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: $\ds \sum_k \paren {-1}^k {n \brack k} = \delta_{n 0} - \delta_{n 1}$ where: $\ds {n \brack k}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\delta_{n 0}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Summation over Union of Disjoint Finite Index Sets
snippet: Let $\struct{G, +}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $I$ and $J$ be disjoint finite indexing sets. Let $K = I \cup J$. Let $\family{g_k}_{k \mathop \in K}$ be an indexed family of elements of $G$. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k = \paren{\sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i} + \paren{\sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j}$ where: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k$ is the summation of $g$ over $K$ $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$ is the summation of the restriction of $g$ over $I$ $\ds \sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j$ is the summation of the restriction of $g$ over $J$

title: Summation over k of Ceiling of k over 2
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \ceiling {\dfrac k 2} = \ceiling {\dfrac {n \paren {n + 2} } 4}$

title: Summation over k of Ceiling of mk+x over n
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$. Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\ds \sum_{0 \mathop \le k \mathop < n} \ceiling {\dfrac {m k + x} n} = \dfrac {\paren {m + 1} \paren {n - 1} } 2 - \dfrac {d - 1} 2 + d \ceiling {\dfrac x d}$ where: $\ceiling x$ denotes the ceiling of $x$ $d$ is the greatest common divisor of $m$ and $n$.

title: Summation over k of Floor of k over 2
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \floor {\dfrac k 2} = \floor {\dfrac {n^2} 4}$

title: Summation over k of Floor of mk+x over n
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ such that $n > 0$. Let $x \in \R$. Then: $\ds \sum_{0 \mathop \le k \mathop < n} \floor {\dfrac {m k + x} n} = \dfrac {\paren {m - 1} \paren {n - 1} } 2 + \dfrac {d - 1} 2 + d \floor {\dfrac x d}$ where: $\floor x$ denotes the floor of $x$ $d$ is the greatest common divisor of $m$ and $n$.

title: Summation over k of Floor of x plus k over y
snippet: Let $x, y \in \R$ such that $y > 0$. Then: $\ds \sum_{0 \mathop \le k \mathop < y} \floor {x + \dfrac k y} = \floor {x y + \floor {x + 1} \paren {\ceiling y - y} }$

title: Summation over k to n of Harmonic Number k by Harmonic Number n-k
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n H_k H_{n - k} = \paren {n + 1} \paren { {H_n}^2 - H_n^{\paren 2} } - 2 n \paren {n_n - 1}$ where: $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number $H_n^{\paren 2}$ denotes a general harmonic number.

title: Summation over k to n of Harmonic Numbers over n+1-k
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {H_k} {n + 1 - k} = {H_{n + 1} }^2 - H_{n + 1}^{\paren 2}$ where: $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number $H_n^{\paren 2}$ denotes a general harmonic number.

title: Summation over k to n of Natural Logarithm of k
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \ln k = \map \ln {n!}$ where $n!$ denotes the $n$th factorial.

title: Summation over k to n of Product of kth with n-kth Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n F_k F_{n - k} = \dfrac {\paren {n - 1} F_n + 2n F_{n - 1} } 5$ where $F_n$ denotes the $n$th Fibonacci number.

title: Summation to n of Power of k over k
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {x^k} k = H_n + \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dbinom n k \dfrac {\paren {x - 1}^k} k$ where: $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Summation to n of Reciprocal of k by k-1 of Harmonic Number
snippet: $\ds \sum_{1 \mathop < k \mathop \le n} \dfrac 1 {k \paren {k - 1} } H_k = 2 - \dfrac {H_n} n - \dfrac 1 n$ where $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number.

title: Summation to n of Square of kth Harmonic Number
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n {H_k}^2 = \paren {n + 1} {H_n}^2 - \paren {2 n + 1} H_n + 2 n$ where $H_k$ denotes the $k$th harmonic number.

title: Summation to n of kth Harmonic Number over k
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {H_k} k = \dfrac { {H_n}^2 + \harm 2 n } 2$ where: $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number $\harm 2 n$ denotes the general harmonic number of order $2$ evaluated at $n$.

title: Summation to n of kth Harmonic Number over k+1
snippet: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \dfrac {H_k} {k + 1} = \dfrac { {H_{n + 1} }^2 - \harm 2 {n + 1} } 2$ where: $H_n$ denotes the $n$th harmonic number $\harm 2 n$ denotes the general harmonic number of order $2$ evaluated at $n$.

title: Summations of Products of Binomial Coefficients
snippet: This page gathers together some identities concerning summations of products of binomial coefficients. In the following, unless otherwise specified: $k, m, n \in \Z$ $r, s, t \in \R$.

title: Sums of Consecutive Sequences of Squares that equal Squares
snippet: Apart from $1$, the $24$th square pyramidal number is the only one which is square: $1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + \cdots + 24^2 = 70^2$ while there are several Sum of Sequence of Squares which are square, for example: $18^2 + 19^2 + \cdots + 28^2 = 77^2$ and: $25^2 + 26^2 + \cdots + 624^2 = 9010^2$

title: Sums of Partial Sequences of Squares
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$. Consider the odd number $2 n + 1$ and its square $\paren {2 n + 1}^2 = 2 m + 1$. Then: $\ds \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n \paren {m - j}^2 = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \paren {m + j}^2$ That is: the sum of the squares of the $n + 1$ integers up to $m$ equals: the sum of the squares of the $n$ integers from $m + 1$ upwards.

title: Sums of Sequences of Consecutive Squares which are Square
snippet: The sums of the following sequences of successive squares are themselves square: {{eqn | l = \sum_{i \mathop = 7}^{29} k^2 | r = 7^2 + 8^2 + \cdots + 29^2 | c = }} {{eqn | l = \sum_{i \mathop = 7}^{39} k^2 | r = 7^2 + 8^2 + \cdots + 39^2 | c = }} {{eqn | l = \sum_{i \mathop = 7}^{56} k^2 | r = 7^2 + 8^2 + \cdots + 56^2 | c = }} {{eqn | l = \sum_{i \mathop = 7}^{190} k^2 | r = 7^2 + 8^2 + \cdots + 190^2 | c = }}

title: Sums of Squares/Mistake/Second Edition

title: Sums of Squares in Lines of Order 3 Magic Square
snippet: Consider the order 3 magic square: The sums of the squares of the top and bottom rows are equal, and differ by $18$ from the sums of the squares of the middle row The sums of the squares of the left and right columns are equal , and differ by $18$ from the sums of the squares of the middle column.

title: Sums of Squares of Diagonals of Order 3 Magic Square
snippet: Consider the order 3 magic square: The sums of the squares of the diagonals, when expressed as $3$-digit decimal numbers, are equal to the sums of the squares of those same diagonals of that same order 3 magic square when reversed.

title: Sums of Squares of Lines of Order 3 Magic Square
snippet: Consider the order 3 magic square: The sums of the squares of the rows, when expressed as $3$-digit decimal numbers, are equal to the sums of the squares of those same rows of that same order 3 magic square when reflected in a vertical axis: $\quad\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline 6 & 7 & 2 \\ \hline 1 & 5 & 9 \\ \hline 8 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline \end{array}$ Similarly: The sums of the squares of the columns, when expressed as $3$-digit decimal numbers, are equal to the sums of the squares of those same columns of that same order 3 magic square when reflected in a horizontal axis:…

title: Sums of both 2 and 3 Consecutive Squares
snippet: The following are the smallest positive integers that are the sum of both $2$ and $3$ consecutive non-zero square numbers: $365, 35 \, 645, 3 \, 492 \, 725, 342 \, 251 \, 285, 33 \, 537 \, 133 \, 085, 3 \, 286 \, 296 \, 790 \, 925, \ldots$

title: Sun Tzu Suan Ching/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Problems from ==

title: Superabundant Number/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Superabundant Numbers ==

title: Superabundant Numbers are Infinite in Number
snippet: There are infinitely many superabundant numbers.

title: Superfactorial/Examples/1
snippet: == Example of Superfactorial == The superfactorial of $1$ is given by: $1 \$ = 1! = 1$

title: Superfactorial/Examples/2
snippet: == Example of Superfactorial == The superfactorial of $2$ is given by: $2 \$ = 2!^{2!} = 2^2 = 4$

title: Superfactorial/Examples/3
snippet: == Example of Superfactorial == The superfactorial of $3$ is given by: $3 \$ = 3!^{3!^{3!} } = 6^{6^6} = 6^{46 \, 656}$

title: Supergolden Ratio is Unique Real Root of x^3 - x^2 - 1
snippet: The supergolden ratio $\psi$ is the one real root of the cubic: $x^3 - x^2 - 1 = 0$ Its decimal expansion starts: $\eta = 1 \cdotp 46557 \, 12318 \, 76768 \ldots$

title: Superinductive Class under Strictly Progressing Mapping is Proper Class
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $g: A \to A$ be a strictly progressing mapping on $A$. Let $A$ be superinductive under $g$. Then $A$ cannot be a set, and thus is a proper class.

title: Superset Relation is Compatible with Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\circ_\PP$ be the subset product on $\powerset S$, the power set of $S$. Then the superset relation $\supseteq$ is compatible with $\circ_\PP$.

title: Superset of Absorbing Set is Absorbing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $A$ be an absorbing set. Let $B \supseteq A$. Then $B$ is absorbing.

title: Superset of Co-Countable Set
snippet: Every superset of a co-countable set is co-countable.

title: Superset of Dependent Set is Dependent
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A \subseteq B$ If $A$ is a dependent subset then $B$ is a dependent subset.

title: Superset of Infinite Set is Infinite
snippet: Let $S$ be an infinite set. Let $T \supseteq S$ be a superset of $S$. Then $T$ is also infinite.

title: Superset of Linearly Dependent Set is Linearly Dependent
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of elements of a unitary module. Let $S$ contain a subset $T$ which is linearly dependent. Then $S$ is also linearly dependent.

title: Superset of Neighborhood in Metric Space is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $a \in A$ be a point in $M$. Let $N$ be a neighborhood of $a$ in $M$. Let $N \subseteq N' \subseteq A$. Then $N'$ is a neighborhood of $a$ in $M$.

title: Superset of Neighborhood in Topological Space is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $N$ be a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. Let $N \subseteq N' \subseteq S$. Then $N'$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. That is: $\forall x \in S: \forall N \in \NN_x: N' \supseteq N \implies N' \in \NN_x$ where $\NN_x$ is the neighborhood filter of $x$.

title: Superset of Order Generating is Order Generating
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$ such that $X$ is order generating and $X \subseteq Y$ Then $Y$ is order generating.

title: Superset of Unsatisfiable Set is Unsatisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\FF'$ be a superset of $\FF$. Then $\FF'$ is also $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable.

title: Superspace of Homeomorphic Subspaces may not have Homeomorphism to Itself containing Subspace Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct {S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $H_1 \subseteq S_1$ and $H_2 \subseteq S_2$. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be a homeomorphic. Then it may be the case that there does not exist a homeomorphism $g: T_1 \to T_2$ such that: $g \restriction_{H_1} = f$ where: $g \restriction_{H_1}$ is the restriction of $g$ to $H_1$ $f: H_1 \to H_2$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Supplemental Chords are Perpendicular
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be a pair of supplemental chords of $\CC$. Then $K_1$ and $K_2$ are perpendicular.

title: Supplementary Interior Angles implies Parallel Lines
snippet: Given two infinite straight lines which are cut by a transversal, if the interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.

title: Support a Bucket over Edge of Table using Staff
snippet: == Problem == You have a strong staff, and a bucket almost full of water. Required to support the bucket over the edge of a table.

title: Suprema Preserving Mapping on Ideals Preserves Directed Suprema
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let every filter $F$ in $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$, $f$ preserve the infimum on $F$. Then $f$ preserves directed suprema.

title: Suprema Preserving Mapping on Ideals is Increasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. For every ideal $I$ in $\struct {S, \preceq}$, let $f$ preserve the supremum on $I$. Then $f$ is increasing.

title: Suprema and Infima of Combined Bounded Functions
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions. Let $c$ be a constant.

title: Suprema in Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered group. Let $x, y, z \in G$ be arbitrary. Let any one of the sets $\set {x, y}$, $\set {x \circ z, y \circ z}$ or $\set {z \circ x, z \circ y}$ admit a supremum. Then all three sets admit a supremum, and: {{eqn | l = \sup \set {x \circ z, y \circ z} | r = \sup \set {x, y} \circ z }} {{eqn | l = \sup \set {z \circ x, z \circ y} | r = z \circ \sup \set {x, y} }}

title: Suprema of two Real Sets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be real sets. Let $S$ and $T$ admit suprema. Then: $\sup S \le \sup T \iff \forall \epsilon \in \R_{>0}: \forall s \in S: \exists t \in T: s < t + \epsilon$

title: Supremum Inequality for Ordinals
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \On$ and $B \subseteq \On$ be ordinals. Then: $\ds \forall x \in A: \exists y \in B: x \le y \implies \bigcup A \le \bigcup B$

title: Supremum Metric and L1 Metric on Closed Real Intervals are not Topologically Equivalent
snippet: Let $S$ be the set of all real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $d_1$ be the $L^1$ metric on $S$: $\ds \forall f, g \in S: \map {d_1} {f, g} := \int_a^b \size {\map f t - \map g t} \rd t$ Let $d_\infty$ be the supremum metric on $S$: $\ds \forall f, g \in S: \map {d_\infty} {f, g} := \sup_{x \mathop \in \closedint a b} \size {\map f x - \map g x}$ Then $d_1$ and $d_\infty$ are not topologically equivalent.

title: Supremum Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $M = \struct {A', d'}$ be a metric space. Let $A$ be the set of all bounded mappings $f: S \to M$. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Continuous Mappings is Metric
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $A$ be the set of all continuous mappings $f: M_1 \to M_2$ which are also bounded. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real-Valued Functions is Metric
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real-valued functions $f: X \to \R$. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real Functions on Closed Interval is Metric
snippet: Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Bounded Real Sequences is Metric
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all bounded real sequences. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions ==

title: Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions is Metric
snippet: Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $\mathscr C \closedint a b$ be the set of all continuous functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$. Let $d$ be the supremum metric on $\mathscr C \closedint a b$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Metric on Continuous Real Functions is Subspace of Bounded
snippet: Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $\mathscr C \closedint a b$ be the set of all continuous functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$. Let $\map {\mathscr B} {\closedint a b, \R}$ be the set of all bounded real functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$. Let $d$ be the supremum metric on $\map {\mathscr B} {\closedint a b, \R}$. Then $\struct {\mathscr C \closedint a b, d_{\mathscr C} }$ is a subspace of $\struct {\map {\mathscr B} {\closedint a b, \R}, d}$.

title: Supremum Metric on Differentiability Class/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Supremum Metric on Differentiability Class ==

title: Supremum Metric on Differentiability Class is Metric
snippet: Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $r \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $A := \mathscr D^r \closedint a b$ be the set of all continuous functions $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ which are of differentiability class $r$. Let $d: A \times A \to \R$ be the supremum metric on $A$. Then $d$ is a metric.

title: Supremum Norm is Norm
snippet:
Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $K \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\BB$ be the set of bounded mappings $S 	o X$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\BB$. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ is a norm on $\BB$.

title: Supremum Norm on Vector Space of Real Matrices is Norm
snippet: Supremum Norm forms a norm on the vector space of real matrices.

title: Supremum Operator Norm Need not be Attained
snippet: Let $\Bbb K \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a bounded sequence in $\Bbb K$ such that: $\ds \forall n \in \N_{> 0} : \lambda_n = 1 - \frac 1 n$. Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the normed $2$-sequence space. Let $\mathbf x = \tuple {a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots} \in \ell^2$.

title: Supremum Operator Norm as Universal Upper Bound
snippet:
Let $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $T \in \map {CL} {X, Y}$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm on $\map {CL} {X, Y}$. Then: $ orall x \in X : 
orm {Tx}_Y \le 
orm T 
orm x_X$

title: Supremum Operator Norm is Norm
snippet:
Let $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,} : \map {CL} {X, Y} 	o \R$ be the supremum operator norm such that: $ orall T \in \map {CL} {X, Y} : 
orm T := \sup \set {
orm {Tx}_Y : x \in X : 
orm x_X \le 1}$ Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ is a norm.

title: Supremum Operator Norm is Well-Defined
snippet:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $X, Y$ be normed vector spaces over $K$. Let $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be an operator norm on $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ defined as: $
orm T := \map \sup {
orm {Tx} : x \in X : 
orm x \le 1}$ Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ is well-defined.

title: Supremum Operator Norm of Cesàro Summation Operator
snippet: Let $A : \ell^\infty \to \ell^\infty$ be the Cesàro summation operator. Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. Then $\norm A = 1$.

title: Supremum Operator Norm of Diagonal Operator over 2-Sequence Space
snippet: Let $\Bbb K = \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N_{> 0} }$ be a bounded sequence in $\Bbb K$. Let $\struct {\ell^2, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_2}$ be the normed $2$-sequence space. Let $\mathbf x = \tuple {a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots} \in \ell^2$. Suppose $\Lambda : \ell^2 \to \ell^2$ be a diagonal operator such that: $\Lambda \tuple {a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots} = \tuple {\lambda_1 a_1, \lambda_2 a_2, \lambda_3 a_3, \ldots}$ Let $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm.

title: Supremum Operator Norm of Linear Transformation is Bounded Above by Hilbert-Schmidt Norm
snippet:
Let $T_A : \R^n 	o \R^m$ be the linear transformation such that: $ orall \mathbf x \in \R^n : T_A \mathbf x := A \mathbf x$ Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{HS}$ be the Hilbert Schmidt norm. Then: $
orm {T_A} \le 
orm A_{HS}$

title: Supremum Operator Norm on Continuous Linear Transformation Space is Submultiplicative
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$, $\struct {Z, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Z}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $A : Y 	o Z$ and $B : X 	o Y$ be continuous linear transformations. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be the supremum operator norm. Let $\circ$ denote the composition. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ is submultiplicative: $
orm {A \circ B} \le 
orm A \cdot 
orm B$

title: Supremum Plus Constant
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of the set of real numbers $\R$. Let $S$ be bounded above. Let $\xi \in \R$. Then: $\ds \map {\sup_{x \mathop \in S} } {x + \xi} = \xi + \map {\sup_{x \mathop \in S} } x$ where $\sup$ denotes supremum.

title: Supremum by Suprema of Directed Set in Simple Order Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete meet semilattice. Let $\struct {S \times S, \precsim}$ be the simple order product of $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {S, \preceq}$. Let $D$ be a directed subset of $S \times S$. Then: $\sup D = \tuple {\map \sup {\map {\pr_1^\to} D}, \map \sup {\map {\pr_2^\to} D} }$ where $\pr_1$ denotes the first projection on $S \times S$ $\pr_2$ denotes the second projection on $S \times S$ $\map {\pr_1^\to} D$ denotes the image of $D$ under $\pr_1$

title: Supremum does not Precede Infimum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ admit both a supremum $M$ and an infimum $m$. Then $m \preceq M$.

title: Supremum in Ordered Subset
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $R = \struct {T, \preceq'}$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Let $X \subseteq T$ such that $X$ admits an supremum in $L$. Then $\sup_L X \in T$ $X$ admits an supremum in $R$ and $\sup_R X = \sup_L X$

title: Supremum in Subframe Equals Supremum in Frame
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \preceq}$ be a frame. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $M = \struct{T, \preceq \restriction_T}$ be a subframe of $L$ where $\preceq \restriction_T$ is the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Let $A \subseteq T$. The supremum ${\bigvee}_M A$ of $A$ exists in $M$ and equals the supremum $\bigvee A$ in $L$.

title: Supremum is Coproduct in Order Category
snippet: Let $\mathbf P$ be an order category with ordering $\preceq$. Let $p, q \in P_0$, and suppose they have some supremum $r = \sup \left\{{p, q}\right\}$. Then $r$ is the coproduct of $p$ and $q$ in $\mathbf P$.

title: Supremum is Dual to Infimum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $a \in S$ and $T \subseteq S$. The following are dual statements: $a$ is a supremum for $T$ $a$ is an infimum for $T$

title: Supremum is Increasing relative to Product Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $I$ be a set. Let $f, g: I \to S$. Let $f \sqbrk I$ denote the image of $I$ under $f$. Let: $\forall i \in I: \map f i \preceq \map g i$ That is, let $f \preceq g$ in the product ordering. Let $f \sqbrk I$ and $g \sqbrk I$ admit suprema. Then: $\sup f \sqbrk I \preceq \sup g \sqbrk I$

title: Supremum is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $T$ has at most one supremum in $S$.

title: Supremum is not necessarily Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ admit a supremum in $S$. Then the supremum of $T$ in $S$ is not necessarily the greatest element of $T$.

title: Supremum of Absolute Value of Difference equals Difference between Supremum and Infimum
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function. Let $S$ be a subset of the domain of $f$. Let $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \set {\map f x}$ and $\ds \inf_{x \mathop \in S} \set {\map f x}$ exist. Then $\ds \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \set {\size {\map f x - \map f y} }$ exists and: $\ds \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \set {\size {\map f x - \map f y} } = \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \set {\map f x} - \inf_{x \mathop \in S} \set {\map f x}$

title: Supremum of Absolute Value of Difference equals Supremum of Difference
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty real set. Let $\ds \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \paren {x - y}$ exist. Then $\ds \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \size {x - y}$ exists and: $\ds \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \size {x - y} = \sup_{x, y \mathop \in S} \paren {x - y}$

title: Supremum of Bounded Above Set of Reals is in Closure
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line under the Euclidean metric. Let $H \subseteq \R$ be a bounded above subset of $\R$ such that $H \ne \O$. Let $u = \sup H$ be the supremum of $H$. Then: $u \in \map \cl H$ where $\map \cl H$ denotes the closure of $H$ in $\R$.

title: Supremum of Continuous Bounded Real-Valued Function on Everywhere Dense Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\DD$ be an everywhere dense subset of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $f : X \to \R$ be a continuous bounded real-valued function. Then: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in \DD} \map f x = \sup_{x \mathop \in X} \map f x$

title: Supremum of Doubleton in Totally Ordered Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $D = \set {a, b} \subseteq S$ be an arbitrary doubleton subset of $S$. Then: $\map \sup D \in D$ where $\sup D$ denotes the supremum of $D$.

title: Supremum of Elements of Sublattice not necessarily Same as for Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ be a sublattice of $S$. Let $a, b \in T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\sup_S \set {a, b}$ is the same as: $\sup_T \set {a, b}$

title: Supremum of Empty Set is Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then: the supremum in $S$ of the empty set exists the smallest element of $S$ exists in which case: $\map \sup \O$ is the smallest element of $S$

title: Supremum of Function is less than Supremum of Greater Function
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions. Let $S$ be a subset of $\Dom f \cap \Dom g$. Let $\map f x \le \map g x$ for every $x \in S$. Let $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \map g x$ exist. Then $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \map f x$ exists and: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \map f x \le \sup_{x \mathop \in S} \map g x$.

title: Supremum of Ideals is Increasing
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L$ be the set of all ideals in $L$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\mathord \precsim = \subseteq\restriction_{\map {\operatorname{Ids} } L \times \map {\operatorname{Ids} } L}$ Let $f: \map {\operatorname{Ids} } L \to S$ be a mapping such that: $\forall I \in \map {\operatorname{Ids} } L: \map f I = \sup I$ Then $f$ is an increasing mapping.

title: Supremum of Ideals is Upper Adjoint
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous join semilattice. Let $\map {\mathit {Ids} } L$ be the set of all ideals in $L$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\mathit {Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\mathord \precsim = \subseteq \restriction_{\map {\mathit {Ids} } L \times \map {\mathit {Ids} } L}$ Let $f: \map {\mathit {Ids} } L \to S$ be a mapping such that $\forall I \in \map {\mathit {Ids} } L: \map f I = \sup I$ Then $f$ is an upper adjoint of Galois connection.

title: Supremum of Ideals is Upper Adjoint implies Lattice is Continuous
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below up-complete lattice. Let $\map {\mathit {Ids} } L$ be the set of all ideals in $L$. Let $P = \struct {\map {\mathit {Ids} } L, \precsim}$ be an ordered set where $\mathord \precsim = \subseteq \restriction_{\map {\mathit {Ids} } L \times \map {\mathit {Ids} } L}$ Let $f: \map {\mathit {Ids} } L \to S$ be a mapping such that $\forall I \in \map {\mathit {Ids} } L: f \sqbrk I = \sup I$ Let $f$ be an upper adjoint of a Galois connection. Then $L$ is continuous.

title: Supremum of Lower Closure of Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $s$ be an element of $S$. Then: $\map \sup {s^\preceq} = s$ where $s^\preceq$ denotes the lower closure of $s$.

title: Supremum of Lower Closure of Set
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $L = T^\preceq$ be the lower closure of $T$ in $S$. Let $s \in S$ Then $s$ is the supremum of $T$ it is the supremum of $L$.

title: Supremum of Lower Sums Never Greater than Upper Sum
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval . Let $f$ be a bounded real function defined on $\closedint a b$. Let $S$ be a finite subdivision of $\closedint a b$. Let $\map U S$ be the upper Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to $S$. Let $\map L P$ be the lower Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to a finite subdivision $P$. Then: $\sup_P \map L P \le \map U S$

title: Supremum of Meet Image of Directed Set
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete meet semilattice. Let $f: S \times S \to S$ be a mapping such that: $\forall \tuple {x, y} \in S \times S: \map f {x, y} = x \wedge y$ Let $D$ be directed subset of $S \times S$ in the simple order product $\struct {S \times S, \precsim}$ of $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {S, \preceq}$.

title: Supremum of Power Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\powerset S$ by the relation $\subseteq$. (From Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering, this is an ordered set.) Then the supremum of $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is the set $S$.

title: Supremum of Set Equals Maximum of Suprema of Subsets
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty real set. Let $\set {S_i: i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n} }$, $n \in \N_{>0}$, be a set of non-empty subsets of $S$. Let $S = \bigcup S_i$. Then: $S_i$ has a supremum for every $i$ in $\set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ $S$ has a supremum and, in either case: $\sup S = \max \set {\sup S_1, \sup S_2, \ldots, \sup S_n}$

title: Supremum of Set of Integers equals Greatest Element
snippet: Let $S \subset \Z$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers. Let $S$ be bounded above in the set of real numbers $\R$. Then $S$ has a greatest element, and it is equal to the supremum $\sup S$.

title: Supremum of Set of Integers is Integer
snippet: Let $S \subset \Z$ be a non-empty subset of the set of integers. Let $S$ be bounded above in the set of real numbers. Then its supremum $\sup S$ is an integer.

title: Supremum of Set of Real Numbers is at least Supremum of Subset
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of real numbers. Let $S$ have a supremum. Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $\sup T$ exists and: $\sup T \le \sup S$

title: Supremum of Simple Order Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be ordered sets. Let $\struct {S_1 \times S_2, \precsim}$ be the simple order product of $\struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$. Let $X_1$ be a non-empty subset of $S_1$, $X_2$ be a non-empty subset of $S_2$ such that $X_1$ and $X_2$ admit suprema. Then: $X_1 \times X_2$ admits a supremum and: $\map \sup {X_1 \times X_2} = \tuple {\sup X_1, \sup X_2}$

title: Supremum of Singleton
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then for all $a \in S$: $\sup \set a = a$ where $\sup$ denotes supremum.

title: Supremum of Subgroups in Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $\mathbb G$ be the set of all subgroups of $G$. Let $\struct {\mathbb G, \subseteq}$ be the complete lattice formed by $\mathbb G$ and $\subseteq$. Let $H, K \in \mathbb G$. Let either $H$ or $K$ be normal in $G$. Then: $\sup \set {H, K} = H \circ K$ where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

title: Supremum of Subset
snippet: Let $\left({U, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $S \subseteq U$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $S$ admit a supremum (in $U$). If $T$ also admits a supremum (in $U$), then $\sup \left({T}\right) \preceq\sup \left({S}\right)$.

title: Supremum of Subset Product in Ordered Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ, \preceq}$ be an ordered group. Suppose that subsets $A$ and $B$ of $G$ admit suprema in $G$. Then: $\sup \paren {A \circ_\PP B} = \sup A \circ \sup B$ where $\circ_\PP$ denotes subset product.

title: Supremum of Subset of Bounded Above Set of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers such that $A \subseteq B$. Let $B$ be bounded above. Then: $\sup A \le \sup B$ where $\sup$ denotes the supremum.

title: Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Suprema of Subsets of Real Numbers ==

title: Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers May or May Not be in Subset
snippet: Let $S \subset \R$ be a proper subset of the set $\R$ of real numbers. Let $S$ admit a supremum $M$. Then $M$ may or may not be an element of $S$.

title: Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers. Let $b$ be a supremum of $A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists x \in A: b − x < \epsilon$

title: Supremum of Subset of Union Equals Supremum of Union
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty real set. Let $S$ have a supremum. Let $\set {S_i: i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n} }$, $n \in \N_{>0}$, be a set of non-empty subsets of $S$. Let $\bigcup S_i = S$. Then there exists a $j$ in $\set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ such that: $\sup S_j = \sup S$

title: Supremum of Sum equals Sum of Suprema
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty sets of real numbers. Let $A + B$ be $\set {x + y: x \in A, y \in B}$. Let either $A$ and $B$ have suprema or $A + B$ have a supremum. Then all $\sup A$, $\sup B$, and $\sup \paren {A + B}$ exist and: $\sup \paren {A + B} = \sup A + \sup B$

title: Supremum of Suprema
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\mathbb T \subseteq \powerset S$, where $\powerset S$ is the power set of $S$. Suppose all $T \in \mathbb T$ admit a supremum $\sup T$ in $S$. Then: $\sup \bigcup \mathbb T = \sup {\set {\sup T: T \in \mathbb T} }$ if one of these two quantities exists (in $S$).

title: Supremum of Suprema over Overlapping Domains
snippet: Let $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of the non-negative real numbers $\R_{\ge 0}$ indexed by $I$. Let $\map R i$ and $\map S i$ be propositional functions of $i \in I$. Let $\ds \sup_{\map R i} a_i$ and $\ds \sup_{\map S i} a_i$ be the indexed suprema on $\family {a_i}$ over $\map R i$ and $\map S i$ respectively. Then: $\ds \map \sup {\sup_{\map R i} a_i, \sup_{\map S i} a_i} = \sup_{\map R i \mathop \lor \map S i} a_i$

title: Supremum of Union of Bounded Above Sets of Real Numbers
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ both be bounded above. Then: $\map \sup {A \cup B} = \max \set {\sup A, \sup B}$ where $\sup$ denotes the supremum.

title: Surd/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Surds == $\sqrt 7$ is a pure surd. $6 + \sqrt 5$ is a mixed surd. $\sqrt 3 + 2 \sqrt {11}$ is a pure surd.

title: Surface/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Surfaces ==

title: Surface Area of Cuboid
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a cuboid whose edges are of length $a$, $b$ and $c$. The surface area $S$ of $\CC$ is given as: $S = 2 \paren {a b + b c + a c}$

title: Surface Area of Sphere
snippet: The surface area $A$ of a sphere whose radius $a$ is given by: $A = 4 \pi a^2$

title: Surface Integral/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Surface Integrals ==

title: Surface of Revolution as Warped Product Manifold
snippet: Let $H$ be the open upper half-plane. Let $S_C \subseteq \R^3$ be the surface of revolution, where $C$ is its generating curve. Endow $C$ with the Riemannian metric induced from the Euclidean metric on $H$. Let $\Bbb S^1$ be the $1$-dimensional sphere, that is, a circle endowed with its standard metric. Let $f : C \to \R$ be the distance to the axis of rotation, say the $x$-axis: $\map f {x, y} = y$ Then $S_C$ is isometric to the warped product manifold $C \times_f \Bbb S^1$.

title: Surgery for Rings
snippet: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with unity, and $\phi: R \to S$ a ring monomorphism. Then there is a ring $T$ isomorphic to $S$ that contains $R$ as a subring.

title: Surjection/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Surjections ==

title: Surjection Induced by Powerset is Induced by Surjection
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $\RR^\to: \powerset S \to \powerset T$ be the direct image mapping $\RR$. Let $\RR^\to$ be a surjection. Let $X = \Preimg \RR$, that is, the preimage of $\RR$. Then $\RR {\restriction_X} \subseteq X \times T$, that is, the restriction of $\RR$ to $X$, is a surjection.

title: Surjection by Free Module
snippet: Let $A$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a left $A$-module. Then there exists a free $A$-module $F$ and a surjective $A$-module homomorphism $f : F \to M$.

title: Surjection from Aleph to Ordinal
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Suppose that: $0 < y < \aleph_{x+1}$ Then there is a surjection: $f : \aleph_x \to y$

title: Surjection from Class to Proper Class
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\mathrm P$ be a proper class. Let $f: A \to \mathrm P$ be a surjection. Then $A$ is proper.

title: Surjection from Finite Set to Itself is Permutation
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an surjection. Then $f$ is a permutation.

title: Surjection from Natural Numbers iff Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Then $S$ is countable there exists a surjection $f: \N \to S$.

title: Surjection from Natural Numbers iff Right Inverse
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: \N \to S$ be a mapping, where $\N$ denotes the set of natural numbers. Then $f$ is a surjection $f$ admits a right inverse.

title: Surjection if Composite is Surjection
snippet: Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ and $g: S_2 \to S_3$ be mappings such that $g \circ f$ is a surjection. Then $g$ is a surjection.

title: Surjection iff Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $S$ be non-empty. Then: $0 < \card T \le \card S$ there exists a surjection $f: S \to T$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Surjection iff Epimorphism in Category of Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathbf{Set}$, i.e. a mapping. Then: $f$ is a surjection it is an epimorphism.

title: Surjection iff Right Cancellable
snippet: Let $f$ be a mapping. Then $f$ is a surjection $f$ is right cancellable.

title: Surjection iff Right Inverse
snippet: A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is a surjection : $\exists g: T \to S: f \circ g = I_T$ where: $g$ is a mapping $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$. That is, $f$ has a right inverse.

title: Surjection on Total Ordering reflects Preordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping to an arbitrary set $T$. Let $\RR$ be a relation on $T$ defined such that: $\RR: = \set {\tuple {\map f x, \map f y}: x \preccurlyeq y}$ That is, $a$ is related to $b$ in $T$ they have preimages $x$ and $y$ under $f$ such that $x$ precedes $y$. Then: $f$ is a surjection onto set $T$ $\RR$ is a preordering on $T$

title: Surjection that Preserves Inner Product is Linear
snippet: Let $H, K$ be Hilbert spaces, and denote by ${\innerprod \cdot \cdot}_H$ and ${\innerprod \cdot \cdot}_K$ their respective inner products. Let $U: H \to K$ be a surjection such that: $\forall g, h \in H: {\innerprod g h}_H = {\innerprod {Ug} {Uh} }_K$ Then $U$ is a linear map, and hence an isomorphism.

title: Surjective Embedding is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct{S_1, \tau_1}$ and $T_2 = \struct{S_2, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a surjective embedding. Then $f$ is a homeomorphism.

title: Surjective Field Homomorphism is Field Isomorphism
snippet: Let $E$ and $F$ be fields. Let $\phi: E \to F$ be a (field) homomorphism. Let $\phi$ be a surjection. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism.

title: Surjective Monotone Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be an open set of $\R$. Let $Y$ be a real interval. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a surjective monotone real function. Then $f$ is continuous on $X$.

title: Surjective Restriction of Real Exponential Function
snippet: Let $\exp: \R \to \R$ be the exponential function: $\map \exp x = e^x$ Then the restriction of the codomain of $\exp$ to the strictly positive real numbers: $\exp: \R \to \R_{>0}$ is a surjective restriction. Hence: $\exp: \R \to \R_{>0}$ is a bijection.

title: Survival Analysis/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Survival Analysis ==

title: Survival Function is Decreasing
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $F_f$ be the survival function of $f$. Then $F_f$ is a decreasing function.

title: Survival Function is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Then the survival function $F_f$ is well-defined.

title: Survival Function of Pointwise Scalar Multiple
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $F_{c f}$ be the survival function of the pointwise scalar multiple $c f$. Let $F_f$ be the survival function of $f$. Let $c \in \R \setminus \set 0$. Then: $\ds \map {F_{c f} } \alpha = \map {F_f} {\frac \alpha {\size c} }$ for all $\alpha \in \hointr 0 \infty$.

title: Survival Function preserves Inequality
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g : X \to \overline \R$ be $\Sigma$-measurable functions such that: $\size f \le \size g$ $\mu$-almost everywhere. Let $F_f$ and $F_g$ be the survival functions of $f$ and $g$ respectively. Then: $F_f \le F_g$

title: Swelled Class contains Empty Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a swelled class. Then the empty set is an element of $A$.

title: Swelled Set which is Closed under Chain Unions with Choice Function is Type M
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets which: is closed under chain unions has a choice function $C$ for its union $\ds \bigcup S$. Then: $S$ is swelled $S$ is of type $M$.

title: Syllogism/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Syllogisms ==

title: Sylow Subgroup is Hall Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is a Hall subgroup of $G$.

title: Sylow p-Subgroup is Unique iff Normal
snippet: A group $G$ has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ $P$ is normal.

title: Sylow p-Subgroups of Group of Order 2p
snippet: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a group of order $2 p$. Then $G$ has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup. This Sylow $p$-subgroup is normal.

title: Sylvester's Law of Inertia
snippet: Let $\struct {V, q}$ be the scalar product space. Let $V^*$ be the algebraic dual of $V$. Suppose there exists a basis $\tuple {\beta^i}$ for $V^*$ such that $q$ is expressible as: $q = \paren {\beta^1}^2 + \ldots + \paren {\beta^r}^2 - \paren {\beta^{r + 1} }^2 - \ldots - \paren {\beta^{r + s} }^2$ where: $r, s \in \N : r + s = n$ Then $r$ is the maximum dimension among all subspaces on which the restriction of $q$ is positive definite. Furthermore, $r$ and $s$ are independent of the choice of basis.

title: Symbol Count by Finite State Machine
snippet: Let $\Sigma$ be a finite set. Let $\Pi \subseteq \Sigma$. For a finite sequence $w = \sequence {a_1, a_2, \dotsc, a_n}$ of elements of $\Sigma$: Let $\map c w = \size {\set {i : a_i \in \Pi} }$ Let $k \in \N$. Then, for each of the following, there exists a finite state machine whose accepted languages is all $w \in \Sigma^*$ such that the condition holds: $\map c w k$ $\map c w \ge k$ $\map c w = k$ $\map c w \ne k$

title: Symbol Reduction of Turing Machine
snippet: Let $T$ be a Turing machine with input symbols $\Sigma$ and blank symbol $B$. Then there exists a Turing machine $T'$ such that: The input symbols of $T'$ are $\Sigma$ The tape symbols of $T'$ are $\Sigma \cup \set B$ The language accepted by $T'$ is exactly the language accepted by $T$ The inputs on which $T'$ halts are exactly the inputs on which $T$ halts

title: Symbolization/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Symbolization ==

title: Symmetric Bilinear Form can be Diagonalized
snippet: Let $\mathbb K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K$ of finite dimension $n>0$. Let $f$ be a symmetric bilinear form on $V$. Then there exists an ordered basis for which the relative matrix of $f$ is diagonal.

title: Symmetric Bilinear Form is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\mathbb K$ be a field. Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb K$. Let $b$ be a bilinear form on $V$. Let $b$ be symmetric. Then $b$ is reflexive.

title: Symmetric Closure/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Symmetric Closures ==

title: Symmetric Closure is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $R$ be the set of all endorelations on $S$. Then the symmetric closure operator is a closure operator on $R$.

title: Symmetric Closure of Inverse Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR^{-1}$ be the inverse of $\RR$. Let $\RR^\leftrightarrow$ be the symmetric closure of $\RR$. Then: $\RR^\leftrightarrow = \paren {\RR^{-1} }^\leftrightarrow$

title: Symmetric Closure of Ordering may not be Transitive
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\preceq^\leftrightarrow$ be the symmetric closure of $\preceq$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\preceq^\leftrightarrow$ is transitive.

title: Symmetric Closure of Relation Compatible with Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\RR$ be a relation compatible with $\circ$. Let $\RR^\leftrightarrow$ denote the symmetric closure of $\RR$. Then $\RR^\leftrightarrow$ is compatible with $\circ$.

title: Symmetric Densely-Defined Linear Operator is Closable
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ be a symmetric densely-defined linear operator. Then $\tuple {\map D T, T}$ is closable.

title: Symmetric Difference/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Symmetric Difference ==

title: Symmetric Difference Distributes over Intersection
snippet: Symmetric difference is distributive over intersection: {{eqn | l = R \symdif \paren {S \cap T} | r = \paren {R \symdif S} \cap \paren {R \symdif T} }}

title: Symmetric Difference is Associative
snippet: Symmetric difference is associative: $R \symdif \paren {S \symdif T} = \paren {R \symdif S} \symdif T$

title: Symmetric Difference is Commutative
snippet: Symmetric difference is commutative: $S \symdif T = T \symdif S$

title: Symmetric Difference is Subset of Union
snippet: The symmetric difference of two sets is a subset of their union: $S \symdif T \subseteq S \cup T$

title: Symmetric Difference is Subset of Union of Symmetric Differences
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $R \symdif S \subseteq \paren {R \symdif T} \cup \paren {S \symdif T}$ where $R \symdif S$ denotes the symmetric difference between $R$ and $S$.

title: Symmetric Difference of Complements
snippet: The symmetric difference of two sets equals the symmetric difference of their complements: $\map \complement S \symdif \map \complement T = S \symdif T$

title: Symmetric Difference of Equal Sets
snippet: The symmetric difference of two equal sets is the empty set: $S = T \iff S \symdif T = \O$

title: Symmetric Difference of Events is Event
snippet: Let $\EE$ be an experiment with a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The event space $\Sigma$ of $\EE$ has the property that: $A, B \in \Sigma \implies A \ast B \in \Sigma$ That is, the symmetric difference of two events is also an event in the event space.

title: Symmetric Difference of Unions
snippet: Let $R$, $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \cup T} \symdif \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \symdif S} \setminus T$ where: $\symdif$ denotes the symmetric difference $\setminus$ denotes set difference $\cup$ denotes set union

title: Symmetric Difference of Unions is Subset of Union of Symmetric Differences
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $S_\alpha, T_\alpha$ be sets, for all $\alpha \in I$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} S_\alpha \symdif \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} T_\alpha \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} \paren {S_\alpha \symdif T_\alpha}$ where $S \symdif T$ is the symmetric difference between $S$ and $T$.

title: Symmetric Difference on Power Set forms Abelian Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a set such that $\O \subset S$ (that is, $S$ is non-empty). Let $A \symdif B$ be defined as the symmetric difference between $A$ and $B$. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset S, \symdif}$ is an abelian group.

title: Symmetric Difference with Complement
snippet: The symmetric difference of a set with its complement is the universal set: $S \symdif \relcomp {} S = \mathbb U$

title: Symmetric Difference with Empty Set
snippet: $S \symdif \O = S$ where $\symdif$ denotes the symmetric difference.

title: Symmetric Difference with Intersection forms Boolean Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let: $\symdif$ denote the symmetric difference operation $\cap$ denote the set intersection operation $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \symdif, \cap}$ is a Boolean ring.

title: Symmetric Difference with Intersection forms Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let: $\symdif$ denote the symmetric difference operation $\cap$ denote the set intersection operation $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \symdif, \cap}$ is a commutative ring with unity, in which the unity is $S$. This ring is not an integral domain.

title: Symmetric Difference with Self is Empty Set
snippet: The symmetric difference of a set with itself is the empty set: $S \symdif S = \O$

title: Symmetric Difference with Union does not form Ring
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let: $\symdif$ denote the symmetric difference operation $\cup$ denote the set union operation $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \symdif, \cup}$ does not form a ring.

title: Symmetric Difference with Universal Set
snippet: $\mathbb U \symdif S = \map \complement S$ where: $\mathbb U$ denotes the universal set $\symdif$ denotes symmetric difference.

title: Symmetric Distribution has Zero Skewness
snippet: Let $D$ be a probability distribution. Let $D$ be symmetric about its expectation. Then $D$ has a skewness of zero.

title: Symmetric Function Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables. Let $f$ be of degree $r$ in each of its $n$ variables. Then $f$ is equal to a polynomial of total degree $r$ with integer coefficients in the elementary symmetric functions: $\ds \sum x_i, \sum x_i x_j, \dotsb, \prod x_j$ and the coefficients of $f$.

title: Symmetric Group has Non-Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $S_n$ be the (full) symmetric group on $n$ elements, where $n \ge 3$. Then $S_n$ contains at least one subgroup which is not normal.

title: Symmetric Group is Generated by Transposition and n-Cycle
snippet: Let $n \in \Z: n > 1$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Then the set of cyclic permutations: $\set {\begin {pmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \begin {pmatrix} 1 & 2 & \cdots & n \end{pmatrix} }$ is a generator for $S_n$.

title: Symmetric Group is Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma S$ denote the set of all permutations on $S$. Then $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$, the symmetric group on $S$, forms a group.

title: Symmetric Group is Subgroup of Monoid of Self-Maps
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $S^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to itself Let $\struct {\Gamma \paren S, \circ}$ denote the symmetric group on $S$. Let $\struct {S^S, \circ}$ be the monoid of self-maps under composition of mappings. Then $\struct {\Gamma \paren S, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {S^S, \circ}$.

title: Symmetric Group is not Abelian
snippet: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group of order $n$ where $n \ge 3$. Then $S_n$ is not abelian.

title: Symmetric Group on 3 Letters
snippet: == Group Example == Let $S_3$ denote the set of permutations on $3$ letters. The symmetric group on $3$ letters is the algebraic structure: $\struct {S_3, \circ}$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. It is usually denoted, when the context is clear, without the operator: $S_3$.

title: Symmetric Group on 3 Letters is Isomorphic to Dihedral Group D3
snippet: Let $S_3$ denote the Symmetric Group on 3 Letters. Let $D_3$ denote the dihedral group $D_3$. Then $S_3$ is isomorphic to $D_3$.

title: Symmetric Group on 4 Letters
snippet: == Group Example == Let $S_4$ denote the set of permutations on $4$ letters. The symmetric group on $4$ letters is the algebraic structure: $\struct {S_4, \circ}$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. It is usually denoted, when the context is clear, without the operator: $S_4$.

title: Symmetric Group on 5 Letters or More is not Solvable
snippet: Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Then $S_n$ is not solvable if $n > 5$.

title: Symmetric Group on Greater than 4 Letters is Not Solvable
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ such that $n > 4$. Let $S_n$ denote the symmetric group on $n$ letters. Then $S_n$ is not a solvable group.

title: Symmetric Group on n Letters is Isomorphic to Symmetric Group
snippet: The symmetric group on $n$ letters $\struct {S_n, \circ}$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group on the $n$ elements of any set $T$ whose cardinality is $n$. That is: $\forall T \subseteq \mathbb U, \card T = n: \struct {S_n, \circ} \cong \struct {\Gamma \paren T, \circ}$ where: $\map \Gamma T$ denotes the set of permutations on $T$ {{improve|Link to the actual page defining what $\struct {\map \Gamma T, \circ}$ is without going all the way back to first principles}} $\struct {\map \Gamma T, \circ}$ denotes an algebraic structure with $1$ operation $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings.

title: Symmetric Groups of Same Order are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be sets whose cardinality $\card {T_1}$ and $\card {T_2}$ are both $n$. Let $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_1}, \circ}$ and $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_2}, \circ}$ be the symmetric group on $S$ and $T$ respectively. Then $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_1}, \circ}$ and $\struct {\map \Gamma {T_2}, \circ}$ are isomorphic.

title: Symmetric Integral of Even Function over One Plus Even Function to Power of Odd Function
snippet: $\ds \int_{-a}^a \frac {\map e x} {1 + \map t x^{\map o x} } \rd x = \int_0^a \map e x \rd x$ where: $a$ is a positive real number $\map e x$ and $\map t x$ are arbitrary even functions $\map o x$ is an arbitrary odd function.

title: Symmetric Preordering is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a preordering on a set $S$. Let $\RR$ also be symmetric. Then $\RR$ is an equivalence relation on $S$.

title: Symmetric Regular Right Bipyramid is Isohedral Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a symmetric regular right bipyramid. Then $\PP$ is an isohedral polyhedron.

title: Symmetric Regular Right Bipyramid is not Isogonal Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a symmetric regular right bipyramid. Then $\PP$ is not in general an isogonal polyhedron. The only counterexample is the regular octahdron.

title: Symmetric Regular Right Bipyramid is not Isotoxal Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a symmetric regular right bipyramid. Then $\PP$ is not an isotoxal polyhedron. The only counterexample is the regular octahdron.

title: Symmetric Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Symmetric Relations ==

title: Symmetric Relation equals its Symmetric Closure
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a symmetric relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR^\leftrightarrow$ be the symmetric closure of $\RR$. Then: $\RR = \RR^\leftrightarrow$

title: Symmetric Transitive and Serial Relation is Reflexive
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation which is: symmetric transitive serial. Then $\RR$ is reflexive. Thus such a relation is an equivalence.

title: Symmetric and Antisymmetric Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation in $S$ which is both symmetric and antisymmetric. Then $\RR$ is transitive.

title: Symmetric and Transitive Relation is not necessarily Reflexive
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\alpha \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation on $S$. Let $\alpha$ be both symmetric and transitive. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\alpha$ is also reflexive.

title: Symmetric and Transitive therefore Reflexive
snippet: == Fallacy == Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be a relation which is symmetric and transitive. Then $\RR$ is also always reflexive. Consider $x, y \in S$. Suppose $x \mathrel \RR y$. Then as $\RR$ is symmetric, it follows that $y \mathrel \RR x$. As $\RR$ is transitive, it follows that $x \mathrel \RR x$. Therefore $x \mathrel \RR x$ and so $\RR$ is reflexive.

title: Symmetry (Geometry)/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Symmetries in context of Geometry ==

title: Symmetry Group is Group
snippet: Let $P$ be a geometric figure. Let $S_P$ be the set of all symmetries of $P$. Let $\circ$ denote composition of mappings. The symmetry group $\struct {S_P, \circ}$ is indeed a group.

title: Symmetry Group of Equilateral Triangle/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table of Symmetry Group of Equilateral Triangle == The Cayley table of the symmetry group of the equilateral triangle can be written: $\begin{array}{c|ccc|ccc} \circ & e & p & q & r & s & t \\ \hline e & e & p & q & r & s & t \\ p & p & q & e & s & t & r \\ q & q & e & p & t & r & s \\ \hline r & r & t & s & e & q & p \\ s & s & r & t & p & e & q \\ t & t & s & r & q & p & e \\ \end{array}$ where: 400px

title: Symmetry Group of Equilateral Triangle is Group
snippet: The symmetry group of the equilateral triangle is a group.

title: Symmetry Group of Equilateral Triangle is Solvable
snippet: The symmetry group $D_3$ of the equilateral triangle is a solvable group.

title: Symmetry Group of Equilateral Triangle is Symmetric Group
snippet: Let $D_3$ denote the symmetry group of the equilateral triangle. Let $S_3$ denote the symmetric group on $3$ letters. Then $D_3$ is isomorphic to $S_3$.

title: Symmetry Group of Isosceles Triangle/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table of Symmetry Group of Isosceles Triangle == The Cayley table of the symmetry group of the isosceles triangle can be written: $\begin{array}{c|cccccc} & e & d \\ \hline e & e & d \\ d & d & e \\ \end{array}$ where: $e$ is the identity mapping $d$ is the reflection $d$ in the line through $A$ and the midpoint of $BC$. 240px Category:Examples of Cayley Tables Category:Symmetry Group of Isosceles Triangle

title: Symmetry Group of Line Segment/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table of Symmetry Group of Line Segment == The Cayley table of the symmetry group of the line segment can be written: $\begin{array}{c|cccccc} & e & r \\ \hline e & e & r \\ r & r & e \\ \end{array}$ where: $e$ is the identity mapping $r$ is the plane rotation of $180^\circ$ about the midpoint of $AB$. 340px Category:Examples of Cayley Tables Category:Symmetry Group of Line Segment

title: Symmetry Group of Line Segment is Group
snippet: The symmetry group of the line segment is a group.

title: Symmetry Group of Rectangle is Klein Four-Group
snippet: The symmetry group of the rectangle is the Klein $4$-group.

Let $D_6$ denote the symmetry group of $\HH$. 520px Let $e$ denote the identity mapping Let $\alpha$ denote rotation of $\HH$ anticlockwise through $\dfrac \pi 3$ radians ($60 \degrees$) Let $\beta$ denote reflection of $\HH$ in the $AD$ axis.

title: Symmetry Group of Square is Group
snippet: The symmetry group of the square is a non-abelian group.

title: Symmetry Rule for Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}, k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k = \dbinom n {n - k}$ where $\dbinom n k$ is a binomial coefficient.

title: Symmetry Rule for Gaussian Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $q \in \R_{\ne 1}, n \in \Z_{>0}, k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k_q = \dbinom n {n - k}_q$ where $\dbinom n k_q$ is a Gaussian binomial coefficient.

title: Symmetry in Space Implies Conservation of Momentum
snippet: The total derivative of the action $S_{12}$ from states $1$ to $2$ with regard to position is equal to the difference in momentum from states $1$ to $2$: $\dfrac {\d S_{1 2} } {\d x} = p_2 - p_1$

title: Symmetry of Bernoulli Polynomial
snippet: Let $\map {B_n} x$ denote the nth Bernoulli polynomial. Then: $\map {B_n} {1 - x} = \paren {-1}^n \map {B_n} x$

title: Symmetry of Invariant Metric on Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be a vector space over $K$. Let $d$ be an invariant metric on $X$. Then we have: $\map d {x, y} = \map d {-x, -y}$ for each $x, y \in X$.

title: Symmetry of Relations is Symmetric
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on $S$ which is symmetric. Then: $\tuple {x, y} \in \RR \iff \tuple {y, x} \in \RR$.

title: Syndrome/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Syndromes ==

title: Syndrome Decoding
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear $\tuple {n, k}$-code whose master code is $\map V {n, p}$ To decode a given vector $v$ of $\map V {n, p}$, the syndrome of $v$ can be used as follows. Create an array $T$ of $2$ column consisting of the following: The top row contains: in column $1$: the zero of $C$ in column $2$: its syndrome. The $r$th row subsequent contains: in column $1$: any element of $\map V {n, p}$ of minimum weight which is not already included in the first $r - 1$ rows in column $2$: its syndrome.

title: Syndrome is Zero iff Vector is Codeword
snippet: Let $C$ be a linear $\tuple {n, k}$-code whose master code is $\map V {n, p}$ Let $G$ be a (standard) generator matrix for $C$. Let $P$ be a standard parity check matrix for $C$. Let $w \in \map V {n, p}$. Then the syndrome of $w$ is zero $w$ is a codeword of $C$.

title: Synthetic Basis and Analytic Basis are Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $\BB$ is an analytic basis for $\tau$ $\tau$ is the topology on $S$ generated by the synthetic basis $\BB$.

title: Synthetic Basis formed from Synthetic Sub-Basis
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\SS$ be a synthetic sub-basis on $X$. Define: $\ds \BB = \set {\bigcap \FF: \FF \subseteq \SS, \text{$\FF$ is finite} }$ Then $\BB$ is a synthetic basis on $X$. Thus, by this construction, an arbitrary collection of subsets of $X$ can form a synthetic basis and thus generate a topology on $X$.

title: Synthetic Division/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Synthetic Division ==

title: Synthetic Sub-Basis and Analytic Sub-Basis are Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\SS \subseteq \powerset X$, where $\powerset X$ denotes the power set of $X$. Then $\SS$ is an analytic sub-basis for $\tau$ $\tau$ is the topology on $X$ generated by the synthetic sub-basis $\SS$.

title: System of Forces is Equivalent to Wrench
snippet: Let $S$ be a system of forces. Then $S$ is equivalent to a wrench.
