title: System of Open Neighborhoods are Equal Iff Singleton Closures are Equal
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ne y$. Let $\map \UU x$ and $\map \UU y$ denote the system of open neighborhoods of $x$ and $y$ respectively. Let $\set x^-$ and $\set y^-$ denote the topological closures of $\set x$ and $\set y$ respectively. Then: $\map \UU x = \map \UU y$ $\set x^- = \set y^-$

title: System of Open Neighborhoods is a Completely Prime Filter
snippet: Let $\struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map \UU x$ denote the system of open neighborhoods of $x$ in $\struct{S, \tau}$. Then: $\map \UU x$ is a completely prime filter in the complete lattice $\struct{\tau, \subseteq}$

title: System of Simultaneous Equations may have Multiple Solutions
snippet: Let $S$ be a system of simultaneous equations. Then it is possible that $S$ may have a solution set which is a singleton.

title: System of Simultaneous Equations may have No Solution
snippet: Let $S$ be a system of simultaneous equations. Then it is possible that $S$ may have a solution set which is empty.

title: System of Simultaneous Equations may have Unique Solution
snippet: Let $S$ be a system of simultaneous equations. Then it is possible that $S$ may have a solution set which is a singleton.

title: Szpilrajn Extension Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \prec}$ be a strictly ordered set. Then there is a strict total ordering on $S$ of which $\prec$ is a subset.

title: T0 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a a $T_0$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a a $T_0$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_0$ space is hereditary.

title: T0 Property is Preserved under Closed Bijection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a closed bijection. If $T_A$ is a $T_0$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T0 Property is Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_0$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T0 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_0$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T0 Space is not necessarily T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a be a $T_0$ space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a $T_1$ space.

title: T0 Space is not necessarily T1, T2, T3, T4 or T5
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied except for the $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) axiom.

title: T1/2 Space is T0 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_{\frac 1 2}$ topological space. Then $T$ is $T_0$ space.

title: T1 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_1$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_1$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_1$ space is hereditary.

title: T1 Property is Preserved under Closed Bijection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a closed bijection. If $T_A$ is a $T_1$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T1 Property is Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_1$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T1 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_1$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T1 Space is T0
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_1$ space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_0$ space.

title: T1 Space is T1/2 Space
snippet: Let $T$ be a $T_1$ topological space. Then $T$ is $T_{\frac 1 2}$ space.

title: T1 Space is Weakly Countably Compact iff Countably Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_1$ space. Then $T$ is weakly countably compact $T$ is countably compact.

title: T1 Space is not necessarily T2
snippet: A topological space which is a $T_1$ space is not necessarily also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: T1 Space is not necessarily T2, T3, T4 or T5
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied except for the $T_0$ axiom and $T_1$ axiom.

title: T2.5 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space is hereditary.

title: T2.5 Property is Preserved under Closed Bijection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a closed bijection. If $T_A$ is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2.5 Property is Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2.5 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2.5 Space is T2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: T2.5 Space is not necessarily Regular
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space which is a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space, but is not also a regular space.

title: T2.5 Space is not necessarily Urysohn
snippet: A $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ topological space is not necessarily an Urysohn space.

title: T2 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. That is: The property of being a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space is hereditary.

title: T2 Property is Preserved under Closed Bijection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a closed bijection. If $T_A$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2 Property is Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T2 Space is Fully T4 iff Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) topological space. Then: $T$ is a fully $T_4$ space $T$ is a paracompact space.

title: T2 Space is Noetherian iff Finite
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is Noetherian $S$ is finite.

title: T2 Space is R1
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $R_1$ space.

title: T2 Space is Sober Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then: $\struct {S, \tau}$ is a sober space.

title: T2 Space is T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $T$ is also a $T_1$ space.

title: T2 Space is not necessarily Regular
snippet: A topological space which is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space is not necessarily also a regular space.

title: T2 Space is not necessarily T2.5
snippet: A topological space which is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space is not necessarily also a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: T2 Space is not necessarily T3, T4 or T5
snippet: A topological space which is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space (and hence also a $T_0$ space and $T_1$ space) is not necessarily a $T_3$ space, a $T_4$ space or a $T_5$ space.

title: T3.5 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space is hereditary.

title: T3.5 Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: T3.5 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T3.5 Space is T3
snippet: Let $T$ be a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space. Then $T$ is also a $T_3$ space.

title: T3.5 Space is not necessarily T2
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a be a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $T$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: T3 Lindelöf Space is Fully T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ Lindelöf topological space. Then $T$ is a fully $T_4$ space.

title: T3 Lindelöf Space is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space which is also Lindelöf. Then $T$ is paracompact.

title: T3 Lindelöf Space is Strongly Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space which is also Lindelöf. Then $T$ is strongly paracompact.

title: T3 Lindelöf Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ Lindelöf topological space. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: T3 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_3$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_3$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_3$ space is hereditary.

title: T3 Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_3$ space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: T3 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_3$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T3 Space is Fully T4 iff Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ space. Then $T$ is fully $T_4$ $T$ is paracompact.

title: T3 Space is not necessarily T0, T1, T2, T4 or T5
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied except for the $T_3$ axiom.

title: T3 Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Paracompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis of $T$. Then $T$ is a paracompact.

title: T3 Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Perfectly T4 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis. Then: $T$ is a perfectly $T_4$ space

title: T3 Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Pseudometrizable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis of $T$. Then $T$ is pseudometrizable.

title: T3 Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is T4 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_3$ topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis. Then: $T$ is a $T_4$ space

title: T4 Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_4$ space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: T4 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_4$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T4 Property is Weakly Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $T_K$ be a subspace of $T$ such that $K$ is closed in $T$. If $T$ is a $T_4$ space then $T_K$ is also a $T_4$ space. That is, the property of being a $T_4$ space is weakly hereditary.

title: T4 Property is not Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_4$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then it does not necessarily follow that $T_H$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: T4 Space is not necessarily T0, T1, T2, T3 or T5
snippet: There exists at least one example of a topological space for which none of the Tychonoff separation axioms are satisfied except for the $T_4$ axiom.

title: T4 Space is not necessarily T3.5
snippet: A topological space which is a $T_4$ space is not necessarily also a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: T4 and R0 Space is T3.5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_4$ space which is also an $R_0$ space. Then $T$ is also a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: T4 and T0 Space is not necessarily T3
snippet: A topological space which is both a $T_4$ space and a $T_0$ space is not necessarily also a $T_3$ space.

title: T4 and T3 Space is T3.5
snippet: Let a topological space $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be: a $T_4$ space and also: a $T_3$ space. Then $T$ is also a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: T5 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_5$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_5$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_5$ space is hereditary.

title: T5 Property is Not Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_5$ space, then it is not necessarily the case that so is $T_B$.

title: T5 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_5$ space, then so is $T_B$.

title: T5 Space is T4
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_5$ space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_4$ space.

title: T5 and T0 Space is not necessarily T3
snippet: A topological space which is both a $T_5$ space and a $T_0$ space is not necessarily also a $T_3$ space.

title: Tableau Confutation contains Finite Tableau Confutation
snippet: Let $\mathbf H$ be a countable set of WFFs of propositional logic. Let $T$ be a tableau confutation of $\mathbf H$. Then there exists a finite rooted subtree of $T'$ that is also a tableau confutation of $\mathbf H'$.

title: Tableau Confutation implies Unsatisfiable
snippet: Let $\mathbf H$ be a collection of WFFs of propositional logic. Suppose there exists a tableau confutation of $\mathbf H$. Then $\mathbf H$ is unsatisfiable for boolean interpretations.

title: Tableau Confutation is Finished
snippet: Let $T$ be a tableau confutation. Then $T$ is a finished tableau.

title: Tableau Extension Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T$ be a finite propositional tableau. Let its hypothesis set $\mathbf H$ be finite. Then $T$ can be extended to a finished finite propositional tableau $T'$ which also has hypothesis set $\mathbf H$.

title: Tail of Convergent Net Converges
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $x \in X$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be a net in $X$ converging to $x$. Let $\lambda_0 \in \Lambda$. Then $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \succeq \lambda_0}$ converges to $x$.

title: Tail of Convergent Sequence
snippet: Let $\left\langle{a_n}\right\rangle$ be a real sequence. Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $a \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $a_n \to a$ $a_{n + m} \to a$

title: Tail of Convergent Series tends to Zero
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be a sequence of real numbers. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a convergent series. Let $N \in \N_{\ge 1}$ be a natural number. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n$ be the tail of the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n$ is convergent $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$. That is, the tail of a convergent series tends to zero.

title: Tail of Decreasing Sequence of Sets is Decreasing
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a decreasing sequence of subsets of $X$. Then for each $m \in \N$ we have: $\sequence {E_{n + m} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a decreasing sequence of sets.

title: Tail of Directed Set is Directed
snippet: Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\lambda_0 \in \Lambda$. Let $\Lambda_0 = \set {\lambda \in \Lambda : \lambda \succeq \lambda_0}$. Let $\preceq_0$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $\Lambda_0$. Then $\struct {\Lambda_0, \preceq_0}$ is directed.

title: Tail of Uniformly Convergent Product Converges Uniformly to One
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly on $X$. Then for all $N \in \N$, $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = N}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly and the sequence $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = N}^\infty f_n$ converges uniformly to $1$.

title: Tamref's Last Theorem
snippet: The Diophantine equation: $n^x + n^y = n^z$ has exactly one form of solutions in integers: $2^x + 2^x = 2^{x + 1}$ for all $x \in \Z$.

title: Tamura-Kanada Circuit Method
snippet: == Algorithm == The following algorithm can be used to calculate $\pi$ (pi): $(1): \quad$ Set $A = X = 1$, set $B = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt 2}$, and set $C = \dfrac 1 4$ $(2): \quad$ Set $Y = A$. $(3): \quad$ Set $A = \dfrac {A + B} 2$ $(4): \quad$ Set $B = \sqrt {B Y}$. $(5): \quad$ Set $C = C - X \paren {A - Y}^2$ $(6): \quad$ Set $X = 2 X$ $(7): \quad$ Output $\dfrac {\paren {A + B}^2} {4 C}$ as an approximation to $\pi$. $(8): \quad$ For a better approximation to $\pi$, set $Y$ equal to the output, return to step $(2)$ and continue.

title: Tangent-Chord Theorem
snippet: Let $EF$ be a tangent to a circle $ABCD$, touching it at $B$. Let $BD$ be a chord of $ABCD$. Then: the angle in segment $BCD$ equals $\angle DBE$ and: the angle in segment $BAD$ equals $\angle DBF$.

title: Tangent Formulas
snippet: The tangent formulas are as follows:

title: Tangent Function is Odd
snippet: For all $x \in \C$ where $\tan x$ is defined: $\map \tan {-x} = -\tan x$ That is, the tangent function is odd.

title: Tangent Function is Periodic on Reals
snippet: The real tangent function is periodic with period $\pi$. This can be written: $\tan x = \map \tan {x \bmod \pi}$ where $x \bmod \pi$ denotes the modulo operation.

title: Tangent Half-Angle Substitution for Cosine
snippet: == Corollary to Double Angle Formula for Cosine == $\cos 2 \theta = \dfrac {1 - \tan^2 \theta} {1 + \tan^2 \theta}$ where $\cos$ and $\tan$ denote cosine and tangent respectively.

title: Tangent Half-Angle Substitution for Sine
snippet: == Corollary to Double Angle Formula for Sine == $\sin 2 \theta = \dfrac {2 \tan \theta} {1 + \tan^2 \theta}$ where $\sin$ and $\tan$ denote sine and tangent respectively.

title: Tangent Inequality
snippet: $x < \tan x$ for all $x$ in the interval $\openint 0 {\dfrac \pi 2}$.

title: Tangent Line to Concave Graph
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function that is: continuous on some closed interval $\closedint a b$ differentiable and concave on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then all the tangent lines to $f$ are above the graph of $f$.

title: Tangent Line to Convex Graph
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function that is: continuous on some closed interval $\closedint a b$ differentiable and convex on the open interval $\openint a b$. Then all the tangent lines to $f$ are below the graph of $f$.

title: Tangent Plane to Conical Surface touches along Straight Line
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a conical surface. Let $\TT$ be a tangent plane to $\CC$. Then the element of contact between $\CC$ and $\TT$ is a straight line.

title: Tangent Plane to Cylindrical Surface touches along Straight Line
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a cylindrical surface. Let $\TT$ be a tangent plane to $\CC$. Then the element of contact between $\CC$ and $\TT$ is a straight line.

title: Tangent Points of Incircle in Terms of Semiperimeter
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides are $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Let $s$ denote the semiperimeter of $\triangle ABC$. Then the distance from $A$ to a point tangent to the incircle is equal to $s - a$.

title: Tangent Secant Theorem
snippet: Let $D$ be a point outside a circle $ABC$. Let $DB$ be tangent to the circle $ABC$. Let $DA$ be a straight line which cuts the circle $ABC$ at $A$ and $C$. Then $DB^2 = AD \cdot DC$.

title: Tangent Space as Orthogonal Direct Sum of Horizontal and Vertical Tangent Spaces
snippet: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $x \in M$ be a point. Let $H_x$ and $V_x$ be a horizontal and vertical tangent space of $M$ at $x$ respectively. Let $T_x M$ be the tangent space of $M$ at $x$. Then $T_x M$ decomposes as the orthogonal direct sum of $H_x$ and $V_x$: $T_x M = H_x \oplus V_x$

title: Tangent Space is Vector Space
snippet: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n \in \N$. Let $m \in M$ be a point. Let $\struct {U, \kappa}$ be a chart with $m \in U$. Let $T_m M$ be the tangent space at $m$. Then $T_m M$ is a real vector space of dimension $n$, spanned by the basis: $\set {\valueat {\dfrac \partial {\partial \kappa^i} } m : i \in \set {1, \dotsc, n} }$ that is, the set of partial derivatives with respect to the $i$th coordinate function $\kappa^i$ evaluated at $m$.

title: Tangent Space of Surface is Tangent Plane
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a surface. The tangent space to $\SS$ at a point $P \in \SS$ is the tangent plane to $\SS$ at $P$.

title: Tangent and Cotangent are Cofunctions
snippet: The tangent and cotangent are cofunctions: {{eqn | n = 1 | q = \forall x \in \R, \cos x \ne 0 | l = \tan x | r = \map \cot {90 \degrees - x} }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall x \in \R, \sin x \ne 0 | l = \cot x | r = \map \tan {90 \degrees - x} }}

title: Tangent in terms of Hyperbolic Tangent
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \tan z = \map \tanh {i z}$ where: $\tan$ denotes the tangent function $\tanh$ denotes the hyperbolic tangent $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

title: Tangent in terms of Secant
snippet: Let $x$ be a real number such that $\cos x \ne 0$. Then: {{eqn | l = \tan x | r = +\sqrt {\sec^2 x - 1} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $n \pi < x < \paren {n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi$ }} {{eqn | l = \tan x | r = -\sqrt {\sec^2 x - 1} | c = if there exists an integer $n$ such that $\paren {n + \dfrac 1 2} \pi < x < \paren {n + 1} \pi$ }} where $\tan$ denotes the real tangent function and $\sec$ denotes the real secant function.

title: Tangent is Reciprocal of Cotangent
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\sin \theta \ne 0$ and $\cos \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\tan \theta = \dfrac 1 {\cot \theta}$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent function and $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function.

title: Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\cos \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\tan \theta = \dfrac {\sin \theta} {\cos \theta}$ where $\tan$, $\sin$ and $\cos$ mean tangent, sine and cosine respectively.

title: Tangent of 105 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 105^\circ = \tan \dfrac {7 \pi} {12} = - \left({2 + \sqrt 3}\right)$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 120 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 120 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {2 \pi} 3 = -\sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 135 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 135^\circ = \tan \dfrac {3 \pi} 4 = - 1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 150 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 150 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {5 \pi} 6 = -\dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 15 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 15^\circ = \tan \dfrac {\pi} {12} = 2 - \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 165 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 165 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {11 \pi} {12} = -\paren {2 - \sqrt 3}$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 195 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 195 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {13 \pi} {12} = 2 - \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 210 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 210 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {7 \pi} 6 = \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 22.5 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 22.5 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 8 = \sqrt 2 - 1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 225 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 225 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {5 \pi} 4 = 1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 240 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 240 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {4 \pi} 3 = \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 255 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 255 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {17 \pi} {12} = 2 + \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 285 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 285 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {19 \pi} {12} = -\paren {2 + \sqrt 3}$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 300 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 300 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {5 \pi} 3 = -\sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 30 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 30 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 6 = \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 315 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 315 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {7 \pi} 4 = -1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 330 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 330^\circ = \tan \dfrac {11 \pi} 6 = -\dfrac {\sqrt 3} 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 345 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 345^\circ = \tan \dfrac {23 \pi} {12} = -\left({2 - \sqrt 3}\right)$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 36 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 36 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 5 = 5^{\frac 1 4} \phi^{-\frac 3 2}$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent function.

title: Tangent of 45 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 45 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 4 = 1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 60 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 60 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 3 = \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 67.5 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 67.5 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {3 \pi} 8 = \sqrt 2 + 1$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of 72 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 72 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {2 \pi} 5 = 5^{\frac 1 4} \phi^{\frac 3 2}$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent function.

title: Tangent of 75 Degrees
snippet: $\tan 75 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {5 \pi} {12} = 2 + \sqrt 3$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of Angle in Cartesian Plane
snippet: Let $P = \tuple {x, y}$ be a point in the cartesian plane whose origin is at $O$. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the $x$-axis and the line $OP$. Let $r$ be the length of $OP$. Then: $\tan \theta = \dfrac y x$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent of $\theta$.

title: Tangent of Angle minus Three Right Angles
snippet: $\map \tan {x - \dfrac {3 \pi} 2} = \cot x$

title: Tangent of Angle plus Full Angle
snippet: $\map \tan {x + 2 \pi} = \tan x$

title: Tangent of Angle plus Right Angle
snippet: $\map \tan {x + \dfrac \pi 2} = -\cot x$

title: Tangent of Angle plus Straight Angle
snippet: $\tan \left({x + \pi}\right) = \tan x$

title: Tangent of Angle plus Three Right Angles
snippet: $\map \tan {x + \dfrac {3 \pi} 2} = -\cot x$

title: Tangent of Complement equals Cotangent
snippet: $\map \tan {\dfrac \pi 2 - \theta} = \cot \theta$ for $\theta \ne n \pi$ where $\tan$ and $\cot$ are tangent and cotangent respectively. That is, the cotangent of an angle is the tangent of its complement. This relation is defined wherever $\sin \theta \ne 0$.

title: Tangent of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then:

title: Tangent of Conjugate Angle
snippet: $\map \tan {2 \pi - \theta} = -\tan \theta$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent. That is, the tangent of an angle is the negative of its conjugate.

title: Tangent of Difference
snippet: == Corollary to Tangent of Sum == $\map \tan {a - b} = \dfrac {\tan a - \tan b} {1 + \tan a \tan b}$ where $\tan$ is tangent.

title: Tangent of Full Angle
snippet: $\tan 360^\circ = \tan 2 \pi = 0$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of Half Angle for Spherical Triangles
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\tan \dfrac A 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {\map \sin {s - b} \, \map \sin {s - c} } {\sin s \, \map \sin {s - a} } }$ where $s = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$.

title: Tangent of Half Angle in Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Let $s$ denote the semiperimeter of $\triangle ABC$: $s = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$ Then: $\tan \dfrac C 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {\paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} } {s \paren {s - c} } }$

title: Tangent of Half Angle plus Quarter Pi
snippet: $\map \tan {\dfrac x 2 + \dfrac \pi 4} = \tan x + \sec x$

title: Tangent of Half Side for Spherical Triangles
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\tan \dfrac a 2 = \sqrt {\dfrac {-\cos S \, \map \cos {S - A} } {\map \cos {S - B} \, \map \cos {S - C} } }$ where $S = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$.

title: Tangent of Obtuse Angle is Negative
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an obtuse angle. Then: $\tan \theta < 0$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent function.

title: Tangent of Right Angle
snippet: $\tan 90 \degrees = \tan \dfrac \pi 2$ is undefined where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of Straight Angle
snippet: $\tan 180 \degrees = \tan \pi = 0$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of Sum
snippet: $\map \tan {a + b} = \dfrac {\tan a + \tan b} {1 - \tan a \tan b}$ where $\tan$ is tangent.

title: Tangent of Sum of Series of Angles
snippet: Let $\theta_1, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_n$ be angles. For all $k \in \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots, n}$, let $s_k$ be defined as the sum of the product of $\map \tan {\theta_1}, \map \tan {\theta_2}, \ldots, \map \tan {\theta_n}$ taken $k$ at a time: {{eqn | l = s_1 | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map \tan {\theta_i} | c = }} {{eqn | l = s_2 | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{n - 1} \sum_{j \mathop = i + 1}^n \map \tan {\theta_i} \map \tan {\theta_j} | c = }} {{eqn | l = s_3 | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{n - 2} \sum_{j \mathop = i + 1}^{n - 1} \sum_{k \mathop = j + 1}^n \map \tan {\theta_i} \map \tan {\theta_j}…

title: Tangent of Sum of Three Angles
snippet: $\map \tan {A + B + C} = \dfrac {\tan A + \tan B + \tan C - \tan A \tan B \tan C} {1 - \tan B \tan C - \tan C \tan A - \tan A \tan B}$

title: Tangent of Supplementary Angle
snippet: $\map \tan {\pi - \theta} = -\tan \theta$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent. That is, the tangent of an angle is the negative of its supplement.

title: Tangent of Three Right Angles
snippet: $\tan 270 \degrees = \tan \dfrac {3 \pi} 2$ is undefined where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of Three Right Angles less Angle
snippet: $\tan \left({\dfrac {3 \pi} 2 - \theta}\right) = \cot \theta$ where $\tan$ and $\cot$ are tangent and cotangent respectively.

title: Tangent of Three Right Angles minus Angle
snippet: $\map \tan {x - \dfrac {3 \pi} 2} = \cot x$

title: Tangent of Uniform Distribution has Standard Cauchy Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with a uniform distribution on the closed real interval $\closedint {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$: $X \sim \ContinuousUniform {-\dfrac \pi 2} {\dfrac \pi 2}$ Let $Y$ be a continuous random variable such that: $Y = \tan X$ where $\tan$ denotes the tangent function. Then $Y$ has the standard Cauchy distribution: $Y \sim \Cauchy 0 1$

title: Tangent of Zero
snippet: $\tan 0 = 0$ where $\tan$ denotes tangent.

title: Tangent of i
snippet: $\tan i = \paren {\dfrac {e^2 - 1} {e^2 + 1} } i$ where $\tan$ denotes the complex tangent function and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

title: Tangent over Secant Plus One
snippet: $\dfrac {\tan x} {\sec x + 1} = \dfrac {\sec x - 1} {\tan x}$

title: Tangent times Tangent plus Cotangent
snippet: $\tan x \paren {\tan x + \cot x} = \sec^2 x$ where $\tan$, $\cot$ and $\sec$ denote tangent, cotangent and secant respectively.

title: Tangent to Archimedean Spiral at Point
Tangent to Cycloid
snippet: Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations: $x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$ $y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$ Then the tangent to $C$ at a point $\tuple {x, y}$ on $C$ is given by the equation: $y - a \paren {1 - \cos \theta} = \dfrac {\sin \theta} {1 - \cos \theta} \paren {x - a \theta + a \sin \theta}$

title: Tangent to Cycloid is Vertical at Cusps
snippet: The tangent to the cycloid whose locus is given by: $x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$ $y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$ is vertical at the cusps.

title: Tangent to Cycloid passes through Top of Generating Circle
snippet: Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations: $x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$ $y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$ Then the tangent to $C$ at a point $P$ on $C$ passes through the top of the generating circle of $C$.

title: Tangential Component of Acceleration of Uniform Circular Motion is Zero
snippet: Let $P$ be a particle moving in space in uniform circular motion. Let $\mathbf a$ denote the acceleration of $P$. Then the tangential component of $\mathbf a$ is zero.

title: Tangents to Circle from Point are of Equal Length
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $P$ be a point in the exterior of $\CC$. Let $PA$ and $PB$ be tangents to $\CC$ from $P$ touching $\CC$ at $A$ and $B$ respectively. 400px Then: $PA = PB$

title: Tangents to Circle from Point subtend Equal Angles at Center
snippet: Let $\CC$ be a circle. Let $P$ be a point in the exterior of $\CC$. Let $PA$ and $PB$ be tangents to $\CC$ from $P$ touching $\CC$ at $A$ and $B$ respectively. 400px Then: $\angle OPA = \angle OPB$

title: Tannery's Theorem
snippet: Let $\sequence {p_n}$ be an increasing, unbounded above sequence of natural numbers. For every $r, n \in \N$, let $v_r$ be a mapping: $\map {v_r} n \in \C$ Let $\sequence {w_r}$ be a sequence of complex numbers such that, for every $r \in \N$: $\ds w_r = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {v_r} n$ Let $\sequence {M_r}$ be a sequence of non-negative real numbers such that: $\forall n \in \N, r \le p_n: \size {\map {v_r} n} \le M_r$ and: $\ds \sum_{r \mathop = 0}^\infty M_r$ is convergent Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \sum_{r \mathop = 0}^{p_n} \map {v_r} n = \sum_{r \mathop = 0}^\infty…

title: Tarski's Geometry is Complete
snippet: Tarski's geometry is both consistent and complete.

title: Tarski's Undefinability Theorem
snippet: Let $\ZZ$ be the standard structure $\struct {\Z, +, \cdot, s, <, 0}$ for the language of arithmetic. Let $\operatorname {Th}_\ZZ$ be the sentences which are true in $\ZZ$. Let $\Theta$ be the set of Gödel numbers of those sentences in $\operatorname {Th}_\ZZ$. $\Theta$ is not definable in $\operatorname {Th}_\ZZ$.

title: Tarski-Vaught Test
snippet: Let $\MM, \NN$ be $\LL$-structures such that $\MM$ is a substructure of $\NN$. Then $\MM$ is an elementary substructure of $\NN$ : for every $\LL$-formula $\map \phi {x, \bar v}$ and for every $\bar a$ in $\MM$: if there exists an $n$ in $\nN$ such that $\NN \models \map \phi {n, \bar a}$ then there exists an $m$ in $\MM$ such that $\NN \models \map \phi {m, \bar a}$. The condition on the right side of the statement above can be rephrased as: Every existential statement with parameters from $\MM$ which is satisfied in $\NN$ can be witnessed by an element from the substructure $\MM$.

title: Tartaglia's Formula
snippet: Let $T$ be a tetrahedron with vertices $\mathbf d_1, \mathbf d_2, \mathbf d_3$ and $\mathbf d_4$. For all $i$ and $j$, let the distance between $\mathbf d_i$ and $\mathbf d_j$ be denoted $d_{ij}$. Then the volume $V_T$ of $T$ satisfies: $\quad V_T^2 = \dfrac 1 {288} \det \ \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & d_{12}^2 & d_{13}^2 & d_{14}^2 \\ 1 & d_{12}^2 & 0 & d_{23}^2 & d_{24}^2 \\ 1 & d_{13}^2 & d_{23}^2 & 0 & d_{34}^2 \\ 1 & d_{14}^2 & d_{24}^2 & d_{34}^2 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$

title: Tartaglia's Poem
snippet: == Mnemonic == Tartaglia's poem is a mnemonic for the solution of the cubic equation: When the cube and its things near Add to a new number, discrete Determine two new numbers different By that one; this feat Will be kept as a rule Their product always equal, the same To the cube of a third Of the number of things named. Then, generally speaking The remaining amount Of the cube roots subtracted Will be our desired count. Category:Cardano's Formula Category:Cubic Equations Category:Mnemonics

title: Tautochrone Problem
snippet: == Problem == Let a point $A$ be joined by a wire to a lower point $B$. Let the wire be allowed to be bent into whatever shape is required. Let a bead be released at $A$ to slide down without friction to $B$. What is the shape of the wire so that it takes same time to descend to $B$ from wherever you release the bead between $A$ and $B$?

title: Tautology iff Negation is Unsatisfiable
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of propositional logic. Then $\mathbf A$ is a tautology its negation $\neg \mathbf A$ is unsatisfiable.

title: Tautology is Negation of Contradiction
snippet: A tautology implies and is implied by the negation of a contradiction: $\top \dashv \vdash \neg \bot$ That is, a truth can not be false, and a non-falsehood must be a truth.

title: Taxicab Metric is Metric
snippet: The taxicab metric is a metric.

title: Taxicab Metric is Topologically Equivalent to Chebyshev Distance on Real Vector Space
snippet: For $n \in \N$, let $\R^n$ be a real vector space. Let $d_1$ be the taxicab metric on $\R^n$. Let $d_\infty$ be the Chebyshev distance on $\R^n$. Then $\forall x, y \in \R^n: \map {d_\infty} {x, y} \le \map {d_1} {x, y} \le n \cdot \map {d_\infty} {x, y}$ It follows that $d_1$ and $d_\infty$ are Lipschitz equivalent.

title: Taxicab Metric on Metric Space Product is Continuous
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\AA$ be the Cartesian product $A \times A$. Let $d_1$ be the taxicab metric on $\AA$: $\ds \map {d_1} {x, y} = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map {d_{i'} } {x_{i'}, y_{i'} }$ for $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n} \in \AA$. Then $d_1: \AA \to \AA$ is a continuous function.

title: Taxicab Metric on Real Number Plane is Translation Invariant
snippet: Let $\tau_{\mathbf t}: \R^2 \to \R^2$ denote the translation of the Euclidean plane by the vector $\mathbf t = \begin {pmatrix} a \\ b \end {pmatrix}$. Let $d_1$ denote the taxicab metric on $\R^2$. Then $d_1$ is unchanged by application of $\tau$: $\forall x, y \in \R^2: \map {d_1} {\map \tau x, \map \tau y} = \map {d_1} {x, y}$

title: Taxicab Metric on Real Number Plane is not Rotation Invariant
snippet: Let $r_\alpha: \R^2 \to \R^2$ denote the rotation of the Euclidean plane about the origin through an angle of $\alpha$. Let $d_1$ denote the taxicab metric on $\R^2$. Then it is not necessarily the case that: $\forall x, y \in \R^2: \map {d_1} {\map {r_\alpha} x, \map {r_\alpha} y} = \map {d_1} {x, y}$

title: Taxicab Metric on Real Vector Space is Metric
snippet: The taxicab metric on the real vector space $\R^n$ is a metric.

title: Taxicab Norm is Norm
snippet: The taxicab norm is a norm on the real and complex numbers.

title: Taylor's Theorem
snippet: Every infinitely differentiable function can be approximated by a series of polynomials.

title: Taylor Series of Analytic Function has infinite Radius of Convergence
snippet: Let $F$ be a complex function. Let $F$ be analytic everywhere. Let the restriction of $F$ to $\R \to \C$ be a real function $f$. This means: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \map \Re {\map F {x, 0} }, 0 = \map \Im {\map F {x, 0} }$ where $\tuple {x, 0}$ denotes the complex number with real part $x$ and imaginary part $0$. Let $x_0$ be a point in $\R$. Then: the Taylor series of $f$ about $x_0$ converges to $f$ at every point in $\R$.

title: Taylor Series of Holomorphic Function
snippet: Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $r > 0$ be a real number. Let $f$ be a function holomorphic on some open ball, $D = B \paren {a, r}$. Then: $\ds \map f z = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\map {f^{\paren n} } a} {n!} \paren {z - a}^n$ for all $z \in D$.

title: Taylor Series of Logarithm of Gamma Function
snippet: Let $\gamma$ denote the Euler-Mascheroni constant. Let $\map \zeta s$ denote the Riemann zeta function. Let $\map \Gamma z$ denote the gamma function. Let $\Log$ denote the natural logarithm. Then $\map \Log {\map \Gamma z}$ has the power series expansion: {{eqn | l = \map \Log {\map \Gamma z} | r = -\map \gamma {z - 1} + \sum_{k \mathop = 2}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^k \map \zeta k} k \paren {z - 1}^k }} which is valid for all $z \in \C$ such that $\cmod {z - 1} < 1$.

title: Taylor Series of Lorentz Factor at Low Speeds
snippet: The Lorentz factor has the following Taylor polynomial around $v = 0$: {{eqn | l = \map \gamma v | r = \frac 1 {\sqrt {1 - \frac {v^2} {c^2} } } }} {{eqn | r = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac 1 {n!} \paren {\frac {\paren {2 n - 1} !!} {2 n} } \paren {\frac v c }^{2 n} }} {{eqn | o = \approx | r = 1 + \frac 1 2 \paren {\frac v c }^2 + \frac 3 8 \paren {\frac v c }^4 + \frac 5 {16} \paren {\frac v c}^6 + \cdots }} where $v$ is speed $c$ is the speed of light $!!$ is a double factorial

title: Taylor Series reaches closest Singularity
snippet: Let $F$ be a complex function. Let $F$ be analytic everywhere except at a finite number of singularities. Let a singularity of $F$ be one of the following: a pole an essential singularity a branch point In the latter case $F$ is a restriction of a multifunction to one of its branches. Let $x_0$ be a real number. Let $F$ be analytic at the complex number $\tuple {x_0, 0}$. Let $R \in \R_{>0}$ be the distance from the complex number $\tuple {x_0, 0}$ to the closest singularity of $F$. Let the restriction of $F$ to $\R \to \C$ be a real function $f$.

title: Telescoping Series/Example 1
snippet: Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence whose terms are defined as: $a_k = b_k - b_{k + 1}$ Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_k = b_1 - b_{n + 1}$ If $\sequence {b_n}$ converges to zero, then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty a_k = b_1$

title: Telescoping Series/Example 2
snippet: Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence whose terms are defined as: $a_k = b_k - b_{k - 1}$ Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = m}^n a_k = b_n - b_{m - 1}$

title: Temperature of Body under Newton's Law of Cooling
snippet: Let $B$ be a body in an environment whose ambient temperature is $H_a$. Let $H$ be the temperature of $B$ at time $t$. Let $H_0$ be the temperature of $B$ at time $t = 0$. Then: $H = H_a - \paren {H_0 - H_a} e^{-k t}$ where $k$ is some positive constant.

title: Tempered Distribution Space is Proper Subset of Distribution Space
snippet: Let $\map {\DD'} \R$ be the distribution space. Let $\map {\SS'} \R$ be the tempered distribution space. Then $\map {\SS'} \R$ is a proper subset of $\map {\DD'} \R$: $\map {\SS'} \R \subsetneqq \map {\DD'} \R$

title: Tensor Product is Module
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a $R$-right module. Let $N$ be a $R$-left module. Then: $\ds T = \bigoplus_{s \mathop \in M \times N} R s$ is a left module.

title: Tensor Product of Free Modules is Free
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $F$ and $F'$ be free $A$-modules. Then the tensor product $F \otimes_A F'$ is a free $A$-module.

title: Tensor Product of Projective Modules is Projective
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $P$ and $Q$ be projective $A$-modules. Then the tensor product $P \otimes_A Q$ is a projective $A$-module.

title: Tensor with Zero Element is Zero in Tensor
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a right $R$-module. Let $N$ be a left $R$-module. Let $M \otimes_R N$ denote their tensor product. Then: $0\otimes_R n = m \otimes_R 0 = 0 \otimes_R 0$ is the zero in $M \otimes_R N$.

title: Term of Computable Real Sequence is Computable

title: Termial on Real Numbers is Extension of Integers

title: Terminal Object as Limit
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $\mathbf C$ have a terminal object $1$. Then $1$ is the limit of the unique diagram $D: \mathbf 0 \to \mathbf C$, where $\mathbf 0$ is the zero category.

title: Terminal Object is Unique
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a metacategory. Let $1$ and $1'$ be two terminal objects of $\mathbf C$. Then there is a unique isomorphism $u: 1 \to 1'$. Hence, terminal objects are unique up to unique isomorphism.

title: Terminal Speed of Body under Fall Retarded Proportional to Speed
snippet: Let $B$ be a body falling in a gravitational field. Let $B$ be falling through a medium which exerts a resisting force $k \mathbf v$ upon $B$ which is proportional to the speed of $B$ relative to the medium. Then the terminal speed of $B$ is given by: $v = \dfrac {g m} k$

title: Terminal Speed of Body under Fall Retarded Proportional to Square of Speed
snippet: Let $B$ be a body falling in a gravitational field. Let $B$ be falling through a medium which exerts a resisting force of magnitude $k v^2$ upon $B$ which is proportional to the square of the speed of $B$ relative to the medium. Then the terminal speed of $B$ is given by: $v = \sqrt {\dfrac {g m} k}$

title: Terms in Convergent Series Converge to Zero

title: Terms of Bounded Sequence Within Bounds

Let the limit inferior of $\sequence {x_n}$ be $\underline l$. Then: $\forall \epsilon > 0: \exists N: \forall n > N: x_n 0: \exists N: \forall n > N: x_n > \underline l - \epsilon$

title: Test Function Space with Pointwise Addition and Pointwise Scalar Multiplication forms Vector Space
snippet: Let $\map \DD {\R^d}$ be the test function space. Let $\struct {\C, +_\C, \times_\C}$ be the field of complex numbers. Let $\paren +$ be the pointwise addition of test functions. Let $\paren {\, \cdot \,}$ be the pointwise scalar multiplication of test functions over $\C$. Then $\struct {\map \DD {\R^d}, +, \, \cdot \,}_\C$ is a vector space.

title: Test Function with Vanishing Partial Derivative
snippet: Let $\phi \in \map \DD {\R^2}$ be a test function such that: $\tuple {x, y} \stackrel \phi {\longrightarrow} \map \phi {x, y}$ Suppose $\phi$ is a solution to the following partial differential equation: $\dfrac {\partial \phi} {\partial x} = 0$ Then $\phi$ is identically $0$.

title: Test for Ideal
snippet: Let $J$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $J$ is an ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad J \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in J: x + \paren {-y} \in J$ $(3): \quad \forall j \in J, r \in R: r \circ j \in J, j \circ r \in J$

title: Test for Left Ideal
snippet: Let $J$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $J$ is an left ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad J \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in J: x + \paren {-y} \in J$ $(3): \quad \forall j \in J, r \in R: r \circ j \in J$

title: Test for Right Ideal
snippet: Let $J$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $J$ is a right ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad J \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in J: x + \paren {-y} \in J$ $(3): \quad \forall j \in J, r \in R: j \circ r \in J$

title: Test for Submonoid
snippet: To show that $\struct {T, \circ}$ is a submonoid of a monoid $\struct {S, \circ}$, we need to show that: $(1): \quad T \subseteq S$ $(2): \quad \struct {T, \circ}$ is a magma (that is, that it is closed) $(3): \quad \struct {T, \circ}$ has an identity.

title: Tests for Finite Set Equality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Let $S \subseteq T$. $(a): \quad \card S = \card T$ $(b): \quad \card {T \setminus S} = 0$ $(c): \quad T \setminus S = \O$ $(d): \quad T = S$

The Bulldozers and the Bee
snippet: == Problem == Two (presumably driven by a pair of insane enemies) are $20$ miles apart, heading towards each other at $10$ miles per hour, on a collision course. At the same time, a takes off from the of one bulldozer at $20$ miles per hour, towards the other bulldozer. As soon as the bee reaches the other bulldozer, it reverses direction instantaneously and heads off at $20$ miles per hour back towards the first bulldozer. It continues to do this until the bulldozers collide, squashing the bee between them and killing her. The question is: how far does the bee fly before the collision?

title: Theorem of Even Perfect Numbers
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be an even perfect number. Then $a$ is in the form: $2^{n - 1} \paren {2^n - 1}$ where $2^n - 1$ is prime. Similarly, if $2^n - 1$ is prime, then $2^{n - 1} \paren {2^n - 1}$ is perfect.

title: Theorema Egregium
snippet: The Gaussian curvature of a surface does not change if one bends the surface without stretching it. That is, Gaussian curvature can be determined entirely by measuring angles, distances and their rates on the surface itself, without further reference to the particular way in which the surface is embedded in the ambient $3$-dimensional Euclidean space. Thus the Gaussian curvature is an intrinsic invariant of a surface.

title: Theoretical Justification for Cycle Notation
snippet: Let $\N_k$ be used to denote the initial segment of natural numbers: $\N_k = \closedint 1 k = \set {1, 2, 3, \ldots, k}$ Let $\rho: \N_n \to \N_n$ be a permutation of $n$ letters. Let $i \in \N_n$. Let $k$ be the smallest (strictly) positive integer for which $\map {\rho^k} i$ is in the set: $\set {i, \map \rho i, \map {\rho^2} i, \ldots, \map {\rho^{k - 1} } i}$ Then: $\map {\rho^k} i = i$

title: Theories with Infinite Models have Models with Order Indiscernibles
snippet: Let $T$ be an $\LL$-theory with infinite models. Let $\struct {I, <$ be an infinite strict linearly ordered set. There is a model $\MM \models T$ containing an order indiscernible set $\set {x_i : i \in I}$.

title: Theory of Algebraically Closed Fields of Characteristic p is Complete
snippet: Let $p$ be either $0$ or a prime number. Let $ACF_p$ be the theory of algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$ in the language $\LL_r = \set {0, 1, +, -, \cdot}$ for rings, where: $0, 1$ are constants and: $+, -, \cdot$ are binary functions. Then $ACF_p$ is complete.

title: Theory of Set of Formulas is Theory
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be a set of $\LL$-formulas. Let $\map T \FF$ be the $\LL$-theory of $\FF$. Then $\map T \FF$ is a theory.

title: Theory of Structure is Complete
snippet: Let $\AA$ be a structure for a signature for predicate logic $\LL$. Let $\map {\operatorname{Th}} \AA$ be the theory of $\AA$. Then $\map {\operatorname{Th}} \AA$ is complete.

title: There Exist a Countable Number of Computable Numbers
snippet: The computable numbers form a countably infinite set.

title: There Exists No Universal Set
snippet: There exists no set which is an absolutely universal set. That is: $\map \neg {\exists \, \UU: \forall T: T \in \UU}$ where $T$ is any arbitrary object at all. That is, a set that contains everything cannot exist.

title: There are no 120 consecutive numbers which all have exactly 120 divisors
snippet: Prove that the term $n=120$ in is $0$: $24k$ with $k$ coprime to $6$ has exactly $120$ divisors than $k$ has exactly $15$ divisors than $k$ is a square number than $k$ cannot be $== 5, 7, 11 mod 12$ (since $5, 7, 11$ are not quadratic residues $mod 12$) And we have a theorem: A number $== 120, 168, 264 mod 288$ cannot have exactly $120$ divisors (since such numbers can be written as $24*k$ with $k$ coprime to $6$ and $k == 5, 7, 11 mod 12$) So we have: There are $120$ consecutive integers with exactly $120$ divisors than the start number must be $== 0, 265, 266, 267, 268, 269, 270, 271, 272,…

title: There exist no 4 Consecutive Triangular Numbers which are all Sphenic Numbers
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $T_n$, $T_{n + 1}$, $T_{n + 2}$, and $T_{n + 3}$ be the $n$th, $n + 1$th, $n + 2$th and $n + 3$th triangular numbers respectively. Then it is not the case that all of $T_n$, $T_{n + 1}$, $T_{n + 2}$, and $T_{n + 3}$ are sphenic numbers.

title: Third Apotome/Example
snippet: == Example of Third Apotome== Let $a, b \in \set {x \in \R_{>0} : x^2 \in \Q}$ be two rationally expressible numbers such that $a - b$ is an apotome. By definition, $a - b$ is a third apotome : $(1): \quad a \notin \Q$ $(2): \quad b \notin \Q$ $(3): \quad \dfrac {\sqrt {a^2 - b^2}} a \in \Q$ where $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers. Let $a = \sqrt {11}$ and $b = \sqrt {\frac {143} {49} }$.

title: Third Derivative of Inverse Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is of differentiability class $3$. Let $f$ have an inverse $f^{-1}$, likewise of differentiability class $3$. Then: $\dfrac {\d^3 x} {\d y^3} = -\paren {\dfrac {\d^3 y} {\d x^3} \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} - 3 \paren {\dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} }^2} \paren {\dfrac {\d y} {\d x} }^{-5}$

title: Third Derivative of Natural Logarithm Function
snippet: Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm function. Then: $\map {D^3_x} {\ln x} = \dfrac 2 {x^3}$

title: Third Hyperoperation is Integer Power Operation
snippet: The $3$rd hyperoperation is the integer power operation restricted to the positive integers: $\forall x, y \in \Z_{\ge 0}: H_3 \left({x, y}\right) = x^y$

title: Third Partial Derivative/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Third Partial Derivatives ==

title: Third Partial Derivatives of x^y
snippet: Let: $u = x^y$ Then: $\dfrac {\partial^3 u} {\partial x^2 \partial y} = \dfrac {\partial^3 u} {\partial x \partial y \partial x}$

title: Third Principle of Mathematical Induction
snippet: Let $\map P n$ be a propositional function depending on $n \in \N$. If: $(1): \quad \map P n$ is true for all $n \le d$ for some $d \in \N$ $(2): \quad \forall m \in \N: \paren {\forall k \in \N, m \le k < m + d: \map P k} \implies \map P {m + d}$ then $\map P n$ is true for all $n \in \N$.

title: Third Ring Isomorphism Theorem/Also known as
snippet: == Third Ring Isomorphism Theorem: Also known as == The Third Ring Isomorphism Theorem is also referred to by some sources as the First Ring Isomorphism Theorem, and by others as the Second Ring Isomorphism Theorem. There is little consistency in the literature. It can also be called the Third Isomorphism Theorem for Rings. Category:Third Ring Isomorphism Theorem

title: Third Sylow Theorem
snippet: All the Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group are conjugate.

title: Third of 12 by 7 over 5 is 11
snippet: == Puzzle == One third of twelve if you divide By just one fifth of seven, The true result (it has been tried) Exactly is eleven.

title: Thiruko's Cube Root Approximation Theorem
snippet: This Cube Root Approximation Theorem is a structured method that facilitates the rapid estimation of cube roots of perfect cubes by utilizing digit pattern recognition and interval approximation. Step 1: Identifying the Unit Digit of the Cube Root: Each integer has a distinct relationship between its cube and the unit digit of its cube root. By observing the cube number’s last digit, we can directly determine the unit digit of the cube root. This property allows an immediate determination of the cube root’s last digit. A cube ending in 0 → Cube root ends in 0.

title: Thomae Function is Continuous at Irrational Numbers
snippet: Let $D_M: \R \to \R$ denote the Thomae function: $\forall x \in \R: \map {D_M} x = \begin {cases} 0 & : x = 0 \text { or } x \notin \Q \\ \dfrac 1 q & : x = \dfrac p q : p, q \in \Z, p \perp q, q > 0 \end {cases}$ where: $\Q$ denotes the set of rational numbers $\Z$ denotes the integers $p \perp q$ denotes that $p$ and $q$ are coprime (that is, $x$ is a rational number expressed in canonical form) Then $\map {D_M} x$ is: continuous at all irrational $x$ and at $x = 0$ discontinuous at all rational $x$ such that $x \ne 0$.

title: Thomsen Graph is Toroidal
snippet: The Thomsen graph, that is, the complete bipartite graph $K_{3, 3}$, is a toroidal graph.

title: Thomsen Graph is not Planar
snippet: The Thomsen graph is not planar.

title: Three-Point Form of Equation of Plane/Determinant Form
snippet: Let $P_1 := \tuple {x_1, y_1, z_1}$, $P_2 := \tuple {x_2, y_2, z_2}$ and $P_3 := \tuple {x_3, y_3, z_3}$ be non-collinear points in a cartesian $3$-space. Let $P$ be the plane passing through $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$. $P$ can be expressed in the form: $\begin {vmatrix} x & y & z & 1 \\ x_1 & y_1 & z_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & z_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & z_3 & 1 \end {vmatrix} = 0$

title: Three-Point Form of Equation of Plane/Vector Form
snippet: Let $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ be non-collinear points in a cartesian $3$-space whose position vectors are $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$. Let $P$ be the plane passing through $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$. $P$ can be expressed in the form: $\mathbf r = \mathbf a + \lambda \paren {\mathbf b - \mathbf a} + \mu \paren {\mathbf c - \mathbf a}$ where: $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of an arbitrary point on $P$ $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are real parameters.

title: Three-Way Exclusive Or and Equivalence
snippet: Let $p \iff q$ be the biconditional operator, and $p \oplus q$ be the exclusive or operator. Then: $p \iff q \iff r \dashv \vdash p \oplus q \oplus r$

title: Three Consecutive Sabbath Days on Same Day
snippet: == Problem == Christians the week's first day for Sabbath hold. The Jews the seventh, as they did of old, The Turks the sixth, as we have oft been told. How can these three, in the same place, and day, Have each his own true Sabbath, tell, I pray. It perhaps needs to be elaborated that: The word Sabbath is taken to mean religious holy day, whatever that day might be, rather than the more contemporary meaning of just Saturday The first day of the week is taken to be Sunday, rather than the more contemporary understanding of this being Monday Hence the sixth and seventh days are Friday and…

title: Three Daughters
snippet: == Classic Riddles == One of my neighbours has $3$ daughters. "How old are they?" I asked. "The product of their ages is $36$," he replied. I said, "That's not a great deal of help. Throw me a bone, here." "Okay," he said, "the sum of their ages equals our house number." I went outside to look at the front door to remind myself what that was, and said, "Nope, still can't work it out." "My oldest daughter is the only one in the family who has green eyes." "Aha," I replied, "got it. Their ages are ..." and I told him.

title: Three Eighths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 3 8$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Three Fifths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 3 5$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Three Intersecting Lines Perpendicular to Another Line are in One Plane
Three Non-Collinear Planes have One Point in Common
snippet: Three planes which are not collinear have exactly one point in all three planes.

title: Three Pheasants
snippet: == Classic Problem == A man has $3$ pheasants that he wants to give to $2$ fathers and $2$ sons, giving each of them $1$ pheasant. How can this be done?

title: Three Points are Coplanar
snippet: Let $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ be points in Euclidean $3$-space. Then there exists a plane $\PP$ such that $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ all lie in $\PP$. That is, $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ are coplanar.

title: Three Points in Ultrametric Space have Two Equal Distances
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be an ultrametric space. Let $x, y, z \in X$ with $\map d {x, z} \ne \map d {y, z}$. Then: $\map d {x, y} = \max \set {\map d {x, z}, \map d {y, z} }$

title: Three Points on Sphere in Same Hemisphere
snippet: Let $S$ be a sphere. Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be points on $S$ which do not all lie on the same great circle. Then it is possible to divide $S$ into two hemispheres such that $A$, $B$ and $C$ all lie on the same hemisphere.

title: Three Quarters as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 3 4$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Three Regular Tessellations
snippet: There exist exactly $3$ regular tessellations of the plane.

title: Three Regular n-Dimensional Polytopes over 4 Dimensions
snippet: Let $n \in \N$ be a natural number such that $n > 4$. There exist exactly $3$ $n$-dimensional regular polytopes: the $n$-simplex the $n$-dimensional regular polytope corresponding to the cube the $n$-dimensional regular polytope corresponding to the octohedron.

title: Three Sevenths as Pandigital Fraction
snippet: $\dfrac 3 7$ cannot be expressed as a pandigital fraction.

title: Three Times Sum of Cubes of Three Indeterminates Plus 6 Times their Product
snippet: $3 \paren {a^3 + b^3 + c^3 + 6 a b c} = \paren {a + b + c}^3 + \paren {a + b \omega + c \omega^2}^3 + \paren {a + b \omega^2 + c \omega}^3$ where: $\omega = -\dfrac 1 2 + \dfrac {\sqrt 3} 2$

title: Three Tri-Automorphic Numbers for each Number of Digits
snippet: Let $d \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then there exist exactly $3$ tri-automorphic numbers with exactly $d$ digits. These tri-automorphic numbers all end in $2$, $5$ or $7$.

title: Three times Number whose Divisor Sum is Square
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a positive integer. Let the divisor sum $\map {\sigma_1} n$ of $n$ be square. Let $3$ not be a divisor of $n$. Then the divisor sum of $3 n$ is square.

title: Tietze Extension Theorem
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is normal. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a closed set in $T$. Let $f: A \to \R$ be a continuous mapping from $A \subseteq S$ to the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then there exists a continuous extension $g: S \to \R$, that is, such that: $\forall s \in A: \map f s = \map g s$

title: Time Hierarchy Theorem
snippet: Deterministic Time Hierarchy Theorem Non-deterministic Time Hierarchy Theorem Category:Computer Science Category:Complexity Theory

title: Time Taken for Body to Fall at Earth's Surface
snippet: Let an object $m$ be released above ground from a point near the Earth's surface and allowed to fall freely. Let $m$ fall a distance $s$ in time $t$. Then: $s = \dfrac 1 2 g t^2$ or: $t = \sqrt {\dfrac {2 s} g}$ where $g$ is the Acceleration Due to Gravity at the height through which $m$ falls. It is supposed that the distance $s$ is small enough that $g$ can be considered constant throughout.

title: Time of Travel down Brachistochrone
snippet: Let a wire $AB$ be curved into the shape of a brachistochrone. Let $AB$ be embedded in a constant and uniform gravitational field where Acceleration Due to Gravity is $g$. Let a bead $P$ be released at $A$ to slide down without friction to $B$. Then the time taken for $P$ to slide from $A$ to $B$ is: $T = \pi \sqrt {\dfrac a g}$ where $a$ is the radius of the generating circle of the cycloid which forms $AB$.

title: Time when Hour Hand and Minute Hand at Right Angle
snippet: Let the time of day be such that the hour hand and minute hand are at a right angle to each other. Then the time happens $22$ times in every $12$ hour period: when the minute hand is $15$ minutes ahead of the hour hand when the minute hand is $15$ minutes behind the hour hand. In the first case, this happens at $09:00$ and every $1$ hour, $5$ minutes and $27 . \dot 2 \dot 7$ seconds after In the second case, this happens at $03:00$ and every $1$ hour, $5$ minutes and $27 . \dot 2 \dot 7$ seconds after.

title: Titanic Prime consisting of 111 Blocks of each Digit plus Zeroes
snippet: The integer defined as: $\paren {123456789}_{111} \paren 0_{2284} 1$ where $\paren a_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string, is a titanic prime.

title: Titanic Prime whose Digits are all 0 or 1
snippet: The integer defined as: $10^{641} \times \dfrac {10^{640} - 1} 9 + 1$ is a titanic prime all of whose digits are either $0$ or $1$. That is: $\paren 1_{640} \paren 0_{640} 1$ where $\paren a_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string.

title: Titanic Prime whose Digits are all 9 except for one 1
snippet: The integer defined as: $2 \times 10^{3020} - 1$ is a titanic prime all of whose digits are $9$ except one, which is $1$. That is: $1 \left({9}\right)_{3020}$ where $\left({a}\right)_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string.

title: Titanic Prime whose Digits are all Odd
snippet: The integer defined as: $1358 \times 10^{3821} - 1$ is a titanic prime all of whose digits are odd. That is: $1357 \paren 9_{3821}$ where $\paren a_b$ means $b$ instances of $a$ in a string.

title: Titanic Prime whose Digits are all Prime
snippet: The integer defined as: $7352 \times \dfrac {10^{1104} - 1} {10^4 - 1} + 1$ is a titanic prime all of whose digits are themselves prime. That is: $\underbrace{7352}_{275} 7353$

title: Titius-Bode Law
snippet: == Physical Law == The Titius-Bode law is the observation that the semimajor axes of successive planets of the solar system are governed by the equation: $a = 4 + \floor {2^{n - 1} } \times 3$ where: $a$ is the measure of distance such that the Earth's semimajor axes is defined as $10$ $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$ for successive planets $\floor {2^{n - 1} }$ denotes the floor of $2^{n - 1}$. That is, $a$ is defined by the sequence: $4, 7, 10, 16, 28, 52, 100, 196, \ldots$ While accurate for the planets out as far as Uranus, the law breaks down for Neptune and beyond.

title: Top equals to Relative Pseudocomplement in Brouwerian Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a Brouwerian lattice with greatest element $\top$. Let $a, b \in S$. Then $\top = a \to b$ $a \preceq b$

title: Top in Filter
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a bounded above ordered set. Let $F$ be a filter on $S$. Then $\top \in F$ where $\top$ denotes the greatest element of $S$.

title: Top in Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $P = \left({\tau, \subseteq}\right)$ be an inclusion ordered set of $\tau$. Then $P$ is bounded above and $\top_P = S$ where $\top_P$ denotes the greatest element in $P$.

title: Top is Complete
snippet: The category of topological spaces is complete.

title: Top is Meet Irreducible
snippet: Let $\left({S, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded above meet semilattice. Then $\top$ is meet irreducible where $\top$ denotes the greatest element in $S$.

title: Top is Prime Element
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded above meet semilattice. Then: $\top$ is a prime element where $\top$ denotes the greatest element of $L$.

title: Top of Lattice is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Then $S$ has at most one top.

title: Topological Classification of Uppercase Sans Serif English Letters
snippet: Recall the letters of the English language, written in a sans serif style: They can be divided into homeomorphism classes as follows: $\mathsf A, \mathsf R$ $\mathsf B$ $\mathsf C, \mathsf G, \mathsf I, \mathsf J, \mathsf L, \mathsf M, \mathsf N, \mathsf S, \mathsf U, \mathsf V, \mathsf W, \mathsf Z$ $\mathsf D, \mathsf O$ $\mathsf E, \mathsf F, \mathsf T, \mathsf Y$ $\mathsf H, \mathsf K$ $\mathsf P$ $\mathsf Q$ $\mathsf X$

title: Topological Closure in Coarser Topology is Larger
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on $X$ such that: $\tau_1 \subseteq \tau_2$ That is, such that $\tau_1$ is coarser than $\tau_2$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Then we have: $\map {\cl_2} S \subseteq \map {\cl_1} S$ where $\cl_1$ and $\cl_2$ denote topological closure in $\struct {X, \tau_1}$ and $\struct {X, \tau_2}$ respectively.

title: Topological Closure is Closed
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then the closure $\map \cl H$ of $H$ is closed in $T$.

title: Topological Closure is Closure Operator
snippet: The topological closure operator is a closure operator.

title: Topological Closure of Singleton is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x$ be a point of $T$. Then: $\set x^-$ is irreducible where $\set x^-$ denotes the topological closure of $\set x$.

title: Topological Closure of Subset is Subset of Topological Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq K$ and $K \subseteq S$. Then: $\map \cl H \subseteq \map \cl K$ where $\map \cl H$ denotes the closure of $H$.

title: Topological Closure of Translation in Topological Vector Space is Translation of Topological Closure
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $x \in X$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be non-empty. Let $\cl$ be closure taken in $\struct {X, \tau}$. Then $\map \cl {A + x} = \map \cl A + x$.

title: Topological Dual Space of Hausdorff Locally Convex Space Separates Points
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \PP}$ be a Hausdorff locally convex space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual of $X$. Let $x \in X$. Then $X^\ast$ separates points. That is, if $x, y \in X$ are such that: $\map f x = \map f y$ for all $f \in X^\ast$ we have that $x = y$.

title: Topological Dual Space of Product of Topological Vector Spaces
snippet: Let $\struct {K, \tau_K}$ be a topological field. Let $\struct {X, \tau_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be topological vector spaces over $K$. Let $\struct {X \times Y, \tau}$ be the direct product of $X$ and $Y$ equipped with the product topology. Let $\paren {X \times Y}^\ast$, $X^\ast$ and $Y^\ast$ denote the topological dual spaces. Then $\phi \in \paren {X \times Y}^\ast$ there exists $\phi_X \in X^\ast$ and $\phi_Y \in Y^\ast$ such that: $\map \phi {x, y} = \map {\phi_X} x + \map {\phi_Y} y$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in X \times Y$.

title: Topological Dual Space of Realification of Complex Topological Vector Space is Weak-* Real-Linearly Homeomorphic to Realification of Topological Dual
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a toplogical vector space over $\C$. Let $\struct {X_\R, \tau}$ be the realification of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $\struct {X_\R, \tau}^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $\struct {X_\R, \tau}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $\struct {X^\ast, \tau}^\ast$. Let $w^\ast_\R$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $\struct {X_\R, \tau}^\ast$. Then $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_\R^\ast, w^\ast_\R}$ via a $\R$-linear transformation.

title: Topological Equivalence is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\DD$ be the set of all metrics on $A$. Let $\sim$ be the relation on $\DD$ defined as: $\forall d_1, d_2 \in \DD: d_1 \sim d_2 \iff d_1$ is topologically equivalent to $d_2$ Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation.

title: Topological Equivalence of Definitions of Spectrum of Locale
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale.

title: Topological Evaluation Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces for some indexing set $I$. Let $\family {f_i : X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of continuous mappings. Let $\ds Y = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} Y_i$ be the product space of $\family {Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $f : X \to Y$ be the evaluation mapping induced by $\family{f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Then: $f$ is continuous

title: Topological Group is Hausdorff iff Identity is Closed
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Let $e$ be its identity element. Then $G$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space $\set e$ is closed in $G$.

title: Topological Group is T1 iff T2
snippet: Let $G$ be a topological group. Then $G$ is a $T_1$ space $G$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

title: Topological Manifold is Locally Compact
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological manifold. Then $M$ is a locally compact space.

title: Topological Manifold is Locally Connected
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological manifold. Then $M$ is a locally connected space.

title: Topological Manifold is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological manifold. Then $M$ is a locally path-connected space.

title: Topological Manifold with Boundary is Topological Manifold iff Boundary is Empty
snippet: Let $M$ be a topological manifold with boundary. Then, $M$ is a topological manifold its boundary $\partial M$ is empty.

title: Topological Product of Compact Spaces
snippet: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $T_1 \times T_2$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$. Then $T_1 \times T_2$ is compact both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are compact.
