title: Uniform Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d_M}$ and $\struct {N, d_N}$ be metric spaces. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings from $M$ to $N$ such that: $(1): \quad \forall n \in \N: f_n$ is continuous at every point of $M$ $(2): \quad \sequence {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ Then: $f$ is continuous at every point of $M$.

title: Uniform Limit of Analytic Functions is Analytic
snippet: Let $U$ be an open subset of $\C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n : U \to \C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ converge locally uniformly to $f$ on $U$. Then $f$ is analytic.

title: Uniform Limit of Sequence of Continuous Complex-Valued Functions Vanishing at Infinity Vanishes at Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of functions $f_n : X \to \C$ that vanishes at infinity. Let $f : X \to \C$ be a function such that: $f_n - f$ is bounded for each $n \in \N$ and: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in X} \cmod {\map {f_n} x - \map f x} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$. Then $f$ vanishes at infinity.

title: Uniform Matroid is Matroid
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set of cardinality $n$. Let $0 \le k \le n$. Let $U_{k, n} = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ be the uniform matroid of rank $k$. Then $U_{k, n}$ is a matroid.

title: Uniform Mean Ergodic Theorem
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\mathbb F$. Let $U : \HH \to \HH$ be a bounded linear operator such that: $\forall f \in \HH : \norm {\map U f} \le \norm f$ Then for each $f \in \HH$: $\ds \lim_{N - M \mathop \to \infty} \dfrac 1 {N - M} \sum_{n \mathop = M}^{N - 1} \map {U^n} f = \map P f$ i.e.

title: Uniform Prism is Isogonal
snippet: Let $P$ be a uniform prism. Then $P$ is isogonal.

title: Uniform Prism is Semiregular Polyhedron
snippet: Let $\PP$ be a uniform prism whose bases are specifically not square. Then $\PP$ is a semiregular polyhedron.

title: Uniform Prism is Uniform Polyhedron
snippet: Let $P$ be a uniform prism. Then $P$ is a uniform polyhedron.

title: Uniform Prisms are Countably Infinite
snippet: There are countably infinite different varieties of uniform prisms.

title: Uniform Product of Continuous Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a metric space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly to $f$. Then $f$ is continuous.

title: Uniform Space whose Topology is Metrizable is not necessarily Metrizable
snippet: Let $\UU$ be a uniformity on a set $S$. Let $\struct {\struct {S, \UU}, \tau}$ be the uniform space generated from $\UU$. Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the uniformizable space yielded by $\struct {\struct {S, \UU}, \tau}$. Let $T$ be a metrizable space. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\UU$ is itself a metrizable uniformity.

title: Uniform Tubular Neighborhood Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $S$ be a submanifold of $M$. Suppose $S$ is compact. Then $S$ has a uniform tubular neighborhood in $M$.

title: Uniformity iff Quasiuniformity has Symmetric Basis
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\UU$ be a quasiuniformity on $S$. Then $\UU$ is a uniformity $\UU$ has a symmetric filter basis.

title: Uniformly Absolutely Convergent Product is Uniformly Convergent
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\mathbb K$ be complete. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of bounded mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly absolutely on $X$. Then it converges uniformly.

title: Uniformly Bounded Sequence of Bounded Linear Transformations is Uniformly Equicontinuous
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ and $\struct {Y, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be normed vector spaces. Let $\map \BB {X, Y}$ be the space of bounded linear transformations $X 	o Y$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB {X, Y} }$ be the norm on $\map \BB {X, Y}$. Let $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\map \BB {X, Y}$ such that: $\ds \sup_{n \mathop \in \N} 
orm {T_n}_{\map \BB {X, Y} } < \infty$ Then $\sequence {T_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is uniformly equicontinuous.

title: Uniformly Continuous Function Preserves Uniform Convergence
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $M = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $N = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $\sequence {g_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $g_n: X \to A_1$. Let $g_n$ converge to $g$ uniformly on $X$ as $n \to \infty$. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be uniformly continuous on $A_1$. Then the sequence $\sequence {f \circ g_n}$ converges to $g \circ f$ uniformly on $X$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Uniformly Continuous Function to Complete Metric Space has Unique Continuous Extension to Closure of Domain
snippet: Let $\tuple {X, d}$ be a metric space. Let $\tuple {Y, d'}$ be a complete metric space. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let $f : A \to Y$ be a uniformly continuous function. Then there exists a unique continuous function $g : A^- \to Y$ such that: $\map g a = \map f a$ for all $a \in A$, where $A^-$ denotes the topological closure of $A$. Furthermore, $g$ is uniformly continuous.

title: Uniformly Continuous Semigroup Bounded on Compact Intervals
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\family {\map T t}_{t \ge 0}$ be a uniformly continuous semigroup. Let $\struct {\map B X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map B X} }$ be the space of bounded linear transformations equipped with the canonical norm. Let $T > 0$ be a real number. Then there exists $M > 0$ such that: $\norm {\map T t}_{\map B X} \le M$ for $t \in \closedint 0 T$.

title: Uniformly Convergent Product Satisfies Uniform Cauchy Criterion
snippet: Let $X$ be a compact topological space. Let $\struct {\mathbb K, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a valued field. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to \mathbb K$. Let the infinite product $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge uniformly on $X$. Then $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ satisfies the uniform Cauchy condition for products.

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence Evaluated on Convergent Sequence
snippet: Let $X = \struct {A, d_X}$ and $Y = \struct {B, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $K$ be a subspace of $X$. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $\FF = \sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n: X \to Y$ that converges to $f$ uniformly on $K$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a convergent sequence in $K$ with limit $a \in K$. Then the sequence $\sequence {\map {f_n} {a_n} }$ is convergent such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} {a_n} = \map f a$

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence Multiplied with Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $V$ be a normed vector space over $\mathbb K$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings $f_n: X \to V$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be uniformly convergent. Let $g: X \to \mathbb K$ be bounded. Then $\sequence {f_n g}$ is uniformly convergent.

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Bounded Functions is Uniformly Bounded
snippet: Let $X = \left({A, d}\right)$ and $Y = \left({B, \rho}\right)$ be metric spaces. Let $\left \langle{f_i}\right \rangle_{i \in I}$ be a uniformly convergent sequence of mappings $f_i: X \to Y$. $\forall i \in I$, let $f_i$ be bounded. Then $\left \langle{f_i}\right \rangle$ is uniformly bounded.

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Continuous Functions Converges to Continuous Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions $S \to \R$ converging uniformly to $f: S \to \R$. Let $f_n$ be continuous at $x$ for all $n \in \N$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$.

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence of Continuous Functions is Pointwise Equicontinuous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d_X}$ and $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be metric spaces. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a continuous function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of continuous functions converging uniformly to $f$. Then $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is pointwise equicontinuous.

title: Uniformly Convergent Sequence on Dense Subset
snippet: Let $X$ be a metric space. Let $Y \subset X$ be dense. Let $V$ be a Banach space. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of continuous mappings $f_n : X\to V$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be uniformly convergent on $Y$. Then $\sequence {f_n}$ is uniformly convergent on $X$.

title: Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions Converges to Continuous Function
snippet: Let $S \subseteq \R$. Let $x \in S$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let $f_n$ be continuous at $x$ for all $n \in \N$. Let the infinite series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ be uniformly convergent to a real function $f : S \to \R$. Then $f$ is continuous at $x$.

title: Uniformly Convergent Series of Continuous Functions is Continuous
snippet: Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of real functions. Let each of $\sequence {f_n}$ be continuous on the interval $\hointr a b$. Let the series: $\ds \map f x := \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {f_n} x$ be uniformly convergent for all $x \in \closedint a b$. {{explain|Is $f$ really defined at $xb$? What are the domains of $\sequence {f_n}$?}} Then $f$ is continuous on $\hointr a b$.

title: Uniformly Convergent iff Difference Under Supremum Metric Vanishes
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {Y, d}$ be a metric space. Let $S$ be the set of all bounded mappings from $X$ to $Y$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $S$. Let $f \in S$. Let $d_S: S \times S \to Y$ denote the supremum metric on $S$. Then: $\sequence {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ on $S$ $\map {d_S} {f_n, f} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

title: Uniformly Normal Neighborhood Lemma
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $U \subseteq M$ be a neighborhood of $p \in M$. Then there is a uniformly normal subset which is a neighborhood of $p \in M$ and is contained in $U$.

title: Unilateral Surface/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unilateral Surfaces ==

title: Unimodal Distribution/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unimodal Distributions ==

title: Union Distributes over Intersection
snippet: Set union is distributive over set intersection: $R \cup \paren {S \cap T} = \paren {R \cup S} \cap \paren {R \cup T}$

title: Union Mapping/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Union Mappings ==

title: Union Operation on Supersets of Subset is Closed
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a given subset of $S$. Let $\powerset S$ denote the power set of $S$ Let $\mathscr S$ be the subset of $\powerset S$ defined as: $\mathscr S = \set {Y \in \powerset S: T \subseteq Y}$ Then the algebraic structure $\struct {\mathscr S, \cup}$ is closed.

title: Union as Symmetric Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets. Then: $A \cup B = \paren {A \symdif B} \symdif \paren {A \cap B}$ where: $A \cup B$ denotes set union $A \cap B$ denotes set intersection $A \symdif B$ denotes set symmetric difference

title: Union equals Intersection iff Sets are Equal
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {S \cup T = S} \land \paren {S \cap T = S} \iff S = T$ where: $S \cup T$ denotes set union $S \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

title: Union from Synthetic Basis is Topology
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis on a set $X$. Let $\ds \tau = \set {\bigcup \AA: \AA \subseteq \BB}$. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $X$.

title: Union is Associative
snippet: Set union is associative: $A \cup \paren {B \cup C} = \paren {A \cup B} \cup C$

title: Union is Commutative
snippet: Set union is commutative: $S \cup T = T \cup S$

title: Union is Dominated by Disjoint Union
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. For all $i \in I$, let $S_i$ be a set. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i \preccurlyeq \bigsqcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$ where $\preccurlyeq$ denotes domination, $\bigcup$ denotes union, and $\bigsqcup$ denotes disjoint union.

title: Union is Empty iff Sets are Empty
snippet: If the union of two sets is the empty set, then both are themselves empty: $S \cup T = \O \iff S = \O \land T = \O$

title: Union is Increasing
snippet: Let $U$ be a set. Let $\FF$ and $\GG$ be sets of subsets of $U$. Then $\FF \subseteq \GG \implies \bigcup \FF \subseteq \bigcup \GG$. That is, $\bigcup$ is an increasing mapping from $\struct {\powerset {\powerset U}, \subseteq}$ to $\struct {\powerset U, \subseteq}$, where $\powerset U$ is the power set of $U$.

title: Union is Increasing Sequence of Sets
snippet: Let $\sequence {D_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets. Then: the sequence $\ds \sequence {\bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^n D_k}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing.

title: Union is Smallest Superset
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Then $S_1 \cup S_2$ is the smallest set containing both $S_1$ and $S_2$. That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \iff \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

title: Union minus Symmetric Difference equals Intersection
snippet: $\paren {A \cup B} \setminus \paren {A \symdif B} = A \cap B$

title: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is Locally Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is locally injectively path-connected.

title: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is Locally Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is locally path-connected.

title: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is not Injectively Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is not injectively path-connected.

title: Union of Adjacent Open Intervals is not Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_S}$ be the union of adjacent open intervals: $S = \openint a b \cup \openint b c$ where: $a, b, c \in \R: a < b < c$. $\tau_S$ is the subspace topology induced on $S$ by the usual topology $\tau_d$ on the real numbers $\R$. Then $T$ is not path-connected.

title: Union of Antisymmetric Relation with Inverse is Antisymmetric iff Diagonal
snippet: Let $\RR$ be an antisymmetric relation on a set $S$. Then: $\RR \cup \RR^{-1}$ is antisymmetric $\RR = \Delta_S$ where: $\RR^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $\RR$ $\Delta_S$ denotes the diagonal relation $\cup$ denotes set union.

title: Union of Balanced Sets in Vector Space is Balanced
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\sequence {E_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of balanced subsets of $X$. Then: $\ds E = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} E_\alpha$ is balanced.

title: Union of Bijections with Disjoint Domains and Codomains is Bijection
snippet: Let $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ be sets or classes. Let $A \cap B = C \cap D = \O$. Let $f: A \to C$ and $g: B \to D$ be bijections. Then $f \cup g: A \cup B \to C \cup D$ is also a bijection.

title: Union of Blocks is Set of Points
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \BB}$ be a pairwise balanced design. That is, let $\struct {X, \BB}$ be a design, with $\size X \ge 2$, and the number of occurrences of each pair of distinct points in $\BB$ be $\lambda$ for some $\lambda > 0$ constant. Then the set union of all the subset elements in $\BB$ is precisely $X$.

title: Union of Boundaries
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\partial A \cup \partial B = \map \partial {A \cup B} \cup \map \partial {A \cap B} \cup \paren {\partial A \cap \partial B}$ where $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

title: Union of Boundary Lines in Nested Rectangle Space is Quasicomponent
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be the nested rectangle space in the Euclidean plane. Let $L_1$ and $L_2$ denote the boundary lines of $T$. Then $L_1 \cup L_2$ is a quasicomponent of $T$.

title: Union of Bounded Above Real Subsets is Bounded Above
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ be bounded above. Then $A \cup B$ is also bounded above.

title: Union of Bounded Below Real Subsets is Bounded Below
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets of real numbers. Let $A$ and $B$ be bounded below. Then $A \cup B$ is also bounded below.

title: Union of Chain in Set of Finite Character with Countable Union is Maximal Element
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of sets of finite character. Let its union $\ds \bigcup S$ be countable. Then $\ds \bigcup S$ is a maximal element of $S$ under the subset relation.

title: Union of Chain of Convex Sets in Vector Space is Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $\Gamma$ be a chain of convex sets. Let: $\ds C = \bigcup \Gamma$ Then $C$ is convex.

title: Union of Chain of Orderings is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $C$ be a non-empty chain of orderings on $S$. Then $\bigcup C$ is an ordering on $S$.

title: Union of Chain of Ordinal Sequences is Ordinal Sequence
snippet: Let $C$ be a chain of ordinal sequences. Then $\bigcup C$ is an ordinal sequence.

title: Union of Chain of Proper Ideals is Proper Ideal
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $\struct {P, \subseteq}$ be the ordered set consisting of all ideals of $R$, ordered by inclusion. Let $\sequence {I_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a non-empty chain of proper ideals in $P$. Let $\ds I = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} I_\alpha$ be their union. Then $I$ is a proper ideal of $R$.

title: Union of Chain of Subalgebras is Subalgebra
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $\BB$ be a $\subseteq$-chain of subalgebras of $A$. Then $\bigcup \BB$ is a subalgebra of $A$. Further, if each $A \in \BB$ is commutative, then so is $\bigcup \BB$.

title: Union of Chain of Submodules is Submodule
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $\NN$ be a chain of submodules with respect to inclusion. Let: $N = \bigcup \NN$ Then $N$ is a submodule of $M$.

title: Union of Class is Subclass implies Class is Transitive
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\bigcup A$ denote the union of $A$. Let: $\bigcup A \subseteq A$ Then $A$ is transitive.

title: Union of Class is Transitive if Every Element is Transitive
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\bigcup A$ denote the union of $A$. Let $A$ be such that every element of $A$ is transitive. Then $\bigcup A$ is also transitive.

title: Union of Closed Intervals of Positive Reals is Set of Positive Reals
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers. For all $x \in \R_{> 0}$, let $B_x$ be the closed real interval $\closedint 0 x$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{x \mathop \in \R_{>0} } B_x = \R_{\ge 0}$

title: Union of Closed Locally Finite Set of Subsets is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\FF$ be a closed locally finite set of subsets of $T$. Let $E = \ds \bigcup \FF$. Then: $E$ is closed in $T$.

title: Union of Closure with Closure of Complement is Whole Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$ in $T$. Let $S \setminus H$ denote the complement of $H$ relative to $S$. Then: $H^- \cup \paren {S \setminus H}^- = S$

title: Union of Closures of Elements of Locally Finite Set is Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\AA$ be a locally finite set of subsets of $T$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup \AA}^- = \bigcup \set{A^- : A \in \AA}$ where $A^-$ denotes the closure of $A$ in $T$.

title: Union of Closures of Singleton Rationals is Rational Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\Q, \tau_d}$ be the rational number space under the usual (Euclidean) topology $\tau_d$. Let $B_\alpha$ denote the singleton containing the rational number $\alpha$. Then the union of the closures in the set of real numbers $\R$ of all $B_\alpha$ is $\Q$: $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in \Q} \map \cl {B_\alpha} = \Q$

title: Union of Conjugacy Classes is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H \le G$. Then $H$ is normal in $G$ $H$ is a union of conjugacy classes of $G$.

title: Union of Connected Sets with Common Point is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of connected sets of $T$. Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a connected set of $T$.

title: Union of Connected Sets with Non-Empty Intersections is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\AA = \family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of $S$, all connected in $T$. Let $\AA$ be such that no two of its elements are disjoint: $\forall B, C \in \AA: B \cap C \ne \O$ Then $\ds \bigcup \AA$ is itself connected.

title: Union of Countable Sets of Sets
snippet: Let $\AA$ and $\BB$ be countable sets of sets. Then: $\set {A \cup B: A \in \AA, B \in \BB}$ is also countable.

title: Union of Covers is Cover of Union
snippet: Let $\sequence {S_i}_{i \in I}$ be an indexed family of sets. For each $i \in I$, let $\CC_i$ be a cover of $S_i$. Then, $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} \CC_i$ is a cover of $\ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} S_i$.

title: Union of Derivatives is Subset of Derivative of Union
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let: $\FF \subseteq \powerset S$ be a set of subsets of $S$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{A \mathop \in \FF} A' \subseteq \paren {\bigcup_{A \mathop \in \FF} A}'$ where $A'$ denotes the derivative of $A$.

title: Union of Disjoint Singletons is Doubleton
snippet: Let $\set a$ and $\set b$ be singletons such that $a \ne b$. Then: $\set a \cup \set b = \set {a, b}$

title: Union of Doubleton
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\set {x, y}$ be a doubleton. Then $\bigcup \set {x, y}$ is a set such that: $\bigcup \set {x, y} = x \cup y$

title: Union of Elements of Power Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then: $\ds S = \bigcup_{X \mathop \in \powerset S} X$ where $\powerset S$ denotes the power set of $S$.

title: Union of Empty Set
snippet: Consider the set of sets $\mathbb S$ such that $\mathbb S$ is the empty set $\O$. Then the union of $\mathbb S$ is $\O$: $\mathbb S = \O \implies \bigcup \mathbb S = \O$

title: Union of Equivalence Classes is Whole Set
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence on a set $S$. Then the set of $\RR$-classes constitutes the whole of $S$.

title: Union of Equivalences
snippet: The union of two equivalence relations is not necessarily an equivalence relation itself.

title: Union of Event with Complement is Certainty
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $A \in \Sigma$ be an events of $\EE$, so that $A \subseteq \Omega$. Then the union of $A$ with its complementary event can be evaluated as: $A \cup \overline A = \Omega$ where $\overline A$ denotes the complementary event to $A$. That is: $A \cup \overline A$ is a certainty or: $\map \Pr {A \cup \overline A} = 1$

title: Union of Events/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unions of Events ==

title: Union of Exteriors contains Exterior of Intersection/Mistake
snippet: == Source Work == Part $\text I$: Basic Definitions Section $1$. General Introduction Closures and Interiors

title: Union of Family/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unions of Families ==

title: Union of Filtered Sets is Filtered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$ such that $\forall X \in A: X$ is filtered and $\forall X, Y \in A: \exists Z \in A: X \cup Y \subseteq Z$ Then: $\bigcup A$ is also filtered.

title: Union of Finite Sets is Finite
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Then $S \cup T$ is a finite set.

title: Union of Functions Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\sequence {X_i: i \in \N}$ be an exhausting sequence of sets on $X$. For each $i \in \N$, let $g_i: X_i \to Y$ be a mapping such that: $g_{i + 1} \restriction X_i = g_i$ where $g_{i + 1} \restriction X_i$ denotes the restriction of $g_{i + 1}$ to $g_i$. Then: $\ds \bigcup \set {g_i: i \in \N}$ is a mapping from $X$ to $Y$.

title: Union of Horizontal Sections is Horizontal Section of Union
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $A$ be sets. Let $\set {E_\alpha : \alpha \in A}$ be a set of subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha}^y = \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} \paren {E_\alpha}^y$ where: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in A} E_\alpha$ $\paren {E_\alpha}^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E_\alpha$.

title: Union of Image of Convergent Sequence and Limit in Topological Space is Compact
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a convergent sequence such that: $x_n \to x$ Then: $\ds \set {x_n : n \in \N} \cup \set x$ is compact.

title: Union of Indexed Family of Sets Equal to Union of Disjoint Sets
snippet: Let $\family {E_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a countable indexed family of sets where at least two $E_n$ are distinct. Then there exists a countable indexed family of disjoint sets $\family {F_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ defined by: $\ds F_k = E_k \setminus \paren {\bigcup_{j \mathop = 0}^{k \mathop - 1} E_j}$ satisfying: $\ds \bigsqcup_{n \mathop \in \N} F_n = \bigcup_{n \mathop \in \N} E_n$ where $\bigsqcup$ denotes disjoint union.

title: Union of Initial Segments is Initial Segment or All of Woset
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered non-empty set. Let $A \subseteq X$. Let: $\ds J = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in A} S_x$ be a union of initial segments defined by the elements of $A$. Then either: $J = X$ or: $J$ is an initial segment of $X$.

title: Union of Interiors and Boundary Equals Whole Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ be a subset of $T$. Then: $S = \Int A \cup \partial A \cup \Int {A'}$ where: $A' = S \setminus A$ denotes the complement of $A$ relative to $S$ $\Int A$ denotes the interior of $A$ $\partial A$ denotes the boundary of $A$.

title: Union of Interiors is Subset of Interior of Union
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\H$ be a set of subsets of $T$. That is, let $\H \subseteq \powerset T$ where $\powerset T$ is the power set of $T$. Then the union of the interiors of the elements of $\H$ is a subset of the interior of the union of $\H$: $\ds \bigcup_{H \mathop \in \H} H^\circ \subseteq \paren {\bigcup_{H \mathop \in \H} H}^\circ $

title: Union of Intersections
snippet: $\paren {S_1 \cap S_2} \cup \paren {T_1 \cap T_2} \subseteq S_1 \cup T_1$

title: Union of Intersections of 2 from 3 equals Intersection of Unions of 2 from 3
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \cup \paren {B \cap C} \cup \paren {C \cap A} = \paren {A \cup B} \cap \paren {B \cup C} \cap \paren {C \cup A}$

title: Union of Inverse of Relations is Inverse of their Union
snippet: For $i \in \set {1, 2}$, let $\RR_i \subseteq S_i \times T_i$ be relations on $S_i \times T_i$. Let ${\RR_i}^{-1} \subseteq T_i \times S_i$ be the inverse of $\RR_i$. Then: ${\RR_1}^{-1} \cup {\RR_2}^{-1} = \paren {\RR_1 \cup \RR_2}^{-1}$

title: Union of Inverses of Mappings is Inverse of Union of Mappings
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {f_i: i \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings. For each $i \in I$, let $f^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $f$. Then the inverse of the union of $\family {f_i: i \in I}$ is the union of the inverses of $f_i, i \in I$. That is: $\ds \paren {\bigcup \family {f_i: i \in I} }^{-1} = \bigcup \family {f_i^{-1}: i \in I}$

title: Union of Left-Total Relations is Left-Total
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times T_1$ and $\RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times T_2$ be left-total relations. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is left-total.

title: Union of Local Bases is Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. For each $x \in X$, let $\BB_x$ be a local basis at $x$ which consists entirely of open sets. Then $\ds \BB = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \BB_x$ is a basis for the topology $\tau$.

title: Union of Many-to-One Relations with Disjoint Domains is Many-to-One
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1$ be a many-to-one relation on $S_1 \times T_1$. Let $\RR_2$ be a many-to-one relation on $S_2 \times T_2$. Suppose that the domains of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ are disjoint. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is a many-to-one relation on $\paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cup T_2}$.

title: Union of Mappings which Agree is Mapping
snippet: Let $A, B, Y$ be sets. Let $f: A \to Y$ and $g: B \to Y$ be mappings. Let $X = A \cup B$. Let $f$ and $g$ agree on $A \cap B$. Then $f \cup g: X \to Y$ is a mapping.

title: Union of Mappings with Disjoint Domains is Mapping
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets. Let $f: S_1 \to T_1$ and $g: S_2 \to T_2$ be mappings. Let $h = f \cup g$ be their union. If $S_1 \cap S_2 = \O$, then $h: S_1 \cup S_2 \to T_1 \cup T_2$ is a mapping whose domain is $S_1 \cup S_2$.

title: Union of Matroid Base with Element of Complement is Dependent
snippet: Let $M = \struct {S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $B \subseteq S$ be a base of $M$. Let $x \in S \setminus B$. Then: $B \cup \set x$ is a dependent superset of $B$

title: Union of Meager Sets is Meager Set
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $A$ and $B$ be meager in $T$. Then $A \cup B$ is meager in $T$.

title: Union of Nest of Injections is Injection
snippet: Let $N$ be a nest of mappings which are all injections. Then: $\bigcup N$ is an injection where $\bigcup N$ denotes the union of $N$.

title: Union of Nest of Mappings is Mapping
snippet: Let $N$ be a nest of mappings. Then: $\bigcup N$ is a mapping where $\bigcup N$ denotes the union of $N$.

title: Union of Nest of Ordinal Sequences which is Proper Class
snippet: Let $N$ be a nest of ordinal sequences such that $N$ is a proper class. Let $\bigcup N$ denote the union of $N$. Then $\bigcup N$ is a mapping whose domain is the class of all ordinals $\On$.

title: Union of Non-Disjoint Bounded Subsets of Metric Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $B$ and $C$ be bounded subsets of $M$ such that $B \cap C \ne \O$. Let $\map \diam B$ and $\map \diam C$ denote the diameters of $B$ and $C$. Then $B \cup C$ is a bounded subset of $M$ such that: $\map \diam {B \cup C} \le \map \diam B + \map \diam C$

title: Union of Non-Disjoint Order-Convex Sets is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\CC$ be a set of order-convex sets of $S$ such that their intersection is non-empty: $\bigcap \CC \ne \O$ Then the union $\bigcup \CC$ is also order-convex.

title: Union of One-to-Many Relations with Disjoint Images is One-to-Many
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1$ be a one-to-many relation on $S_1 \times T_1$. Let $\RR_2$ be a one-to-many relation on $S_2 \times T_2$. Suppose that the images of $\RR_1$ and $\RR_2$ are disjoint. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is a one-to-many relation on $\paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \times \paren {T_1 \cup T_2}$.

title: Union of Open Intervals of Positive Reals is Set of Strictly Positive Reals
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers. For all $x \in \R_{>0}$, let $A_x$ be the open real interval $\openint 0 x$. Then: $\ds \bigcup_{x \mathop \in \R_{>0} } A_x = \R_{>0}$

title: Union of Open Irreducible Non-Disjoint Subspaces is Irreducible
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an irreducible topological space. Let $U$ and $V$ be open irreducible subspaces of $T$. Let their intersection $U \cap V$ be non-empty. Then their union $U \cup V$ is an irreducible subspace of $T$.

title: Union of Open Sets Not in System of Open Neighborhoods is Complement of Singleton Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct{S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $\map \UU x$ denote the system of open neighborhoods of $x$. Let $\set x^-$ denote the topological closure of $\set x$. Then: $\bigcup \set{U \in \tau : U \notin \map \UU x} = S \setminus \set x^-$

title: Union of Open Sets is Open
Union of Open Sets of Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

title: Union of Open Sets of Neighborhood Space is Open
snippet: Let $S$ be a neighborhood space. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {U_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be a family of open sets of $\struct {S, \NN}$ indexed by $I$. Then their union $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} U_i$ is an open set of $\struct {S, \NN}$.

title: Union of Open Sets of Normed Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

title: Union of Orderings is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\RR$ and $\SS$ be orderings on $A$. Then $\RR \cup \SS$ is not necessarily an ordering on $A$.

title: Union of Ordinal is Subset of Itself
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be an ordinal. Then: $\bigcup \alpha \subseteq \alpha$ where $\bigcup \alpha$ denotes the union of $\alpha$.

title: Union of Ordinals is Least Upper Bound
snippet: Let $A \subset \On$. That is, let $A$ be a class of ordinals (every member of $A$ is an ordinal). Then $\bigcup A$, the union of $A$, is the least upper bound of $A$: $\ds \forall x \in A: x \le A$ $\ds \forall y \in A: y \le x \implies \bigcup A \le x$

title: Union of Overlapping Order-Convex Sets in Toset is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $U$ and $V$ be order-convex sets in $S$. Let $U \cap V \ne \O$. Then $U \cup V$ is also order-convex.

title: Union of Path-Connected Sets with Common Point is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of path-connected sets of $T$. Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a path-connected set of $T$.

title: Union of Power Sets
snippet: The union of the power sets of two sets $S$ and $T$ is a subset of the power set of their union: $\powerset S \cup \powerset T \subseteq \powerset {S \cup T}$

title: Union of Power Sets not always Equal to Powerset of Union
snippet: The union of the power sets of two sets $S$ and $T$ is not necessarily equal to the power set of their union.

title: Union of Primitive Recursive Sets
snippet: Let $A, B \subseteq \N$ be subsets of the set of natural numbers $\N$. Let $A$ and $B$ both be primitive recursive. Then $A \cup B$, the union of $A$ and $B$, is primitive recursive.

title: Union of Real Intervals is not necessarily Real Interval
snippet: Let $I_1$ and $I_2$ be real intervals. Then $I_1 \cup I_2$ is not necessarily a real interval.

title: Union of Recursively Enumerable Sets
snippet: Let $S, T \subseteq \N$ be recursively enumerable sets. Then $S \cup T$ is recursively enumerable.

title: Union of Reflexive Relations is Reflexive
snippet: The union of two reflexive relations is also a reflexive relation.

title: Union of Regular Open Sets is not necessarily Regular Open
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $U$ and $V$ be regular open sets of $T$. Then $U \cup V$ is not also necessarily a regular open set of $T$.

title: Union of Relation with Inverse is Symmetric Relation
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation on a set $S$. Let $\RR^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $\RR$. Then $\RR \cup \RR^{-1}$, the union of $\RR$ with $\RR^{-1}$, is symmetric.

title: Union of Relations Compatible with Operation is Compatible
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a closed algebraic structure. Let $\FF$ be a family of relations on $S$. Let each element of $\FF$ be compatible with $\circ$. Let $\QQ = \bigcup \FF$. Then $Q$ is a relation compatible with $\circ$.

title: Union of Relations is Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\FF$ be a family of relations from $S$ to $T$. Let $\ds \RR = \bigcup \FF$, the union of all the elements of $\FF$. Then $\RR$ is a relation from $S$ to $T$.

title: Union of Relative Complements of Nested Subsets
snippet: Let $R \subseteq S \subseteq T$ be sets with the indicated inclusions. Then: $\relcomp T S \cup \relcomp S R = \relcomp T R$ where $\complement$ denotes relative complement. Phrased via Set Difference as Intersection with Relative Complement: $\paren {T \setminus S} \cup \paren {S \setminus R} = T \setminus R$ where $\setminus$ denotes set difference.

title: Union of Right-Total Relations is Right-Total
snippet: Let $S_1, S_2, T_1, T_2$ be sets or classes. Let $\RR_1 \subseteq S_1 \times T_1$ and $\RR_2 \subseteq S_2 \times T_2$ be right-total relations. Then $\RR_1 \cup \RR_2$ is right-total.

title: Union of Set of Dense-in-itself Sets is Dense-in-itself
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $\FF \subseteq \powerset T$ such that: every element of $\FF$ is dense-in-itself. Then the union $\bigcup \FF$ is also dense-in-itself.

title: Union of Set of Ordinals is Ordinal
snippet: Let $A$ be a set of ordinals. Then $\bigcup A$ is an ordinal.

title: Union of Set of Sets is Non-empty iff some Set is Non-empty
snippet: Let $\SS$ be a set of sets. Then: $\ds \bigcup \SS \ne \O \iff \exists S \in \SS: S \ne \O$

title: Union of Set of Sets when a Set Intersects All
snippet: Let $F$ be a set of sets. Let $S$ be a set or class. Suppose that: $\forall A \in F: A \cap S \ne \O$ Then: $\ds F = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in S} \set {A \in F: x \in A}$

title: Union of Set of Singletons
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T = \set {\set x: x \in S}$ be the set of all singletons of elements of $S$. Then: $\ds \bigcup T = S$ where $\ds \bigcup T$ denotes the union of $T$.

title: Union of Sigma-Algebras may not be Sigma-Algebra
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_1}$ and $\struct {X, \Sigma_2}$ be $\sigma$-algebras. Then $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2$ may not be a $\sigma$-algebra on $X$.

title: Union of Simply Connected Sets with Path-Connected Intersection is Simply Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \tau}$ be a topological space. Consider all subsets of $T$ as subspaces, equipped with the subspace topology induced by $\tau$. Let $U$ and $V$ be open subsets of $T$ that are simply connected. Let $U \cap V$ be non-empty and path-connected. Let $U \cup V = T$. Then $\struct {T, \tau}$ is simply connected.

title: Union of Singleton
snippet: Consider the set of sets $A$ such that $A$ consists of just one set $x$: $A = \set x$ Then the union of $A$ is $x$: $\bigcup A = x$

title: Union of Slow g-Tower is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a slowly progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a slow $g$-tower. Then $\ds \bigcup M$ is well-orderable.

title: Union of Slowly Well-Ordered Class under Subset Relation is Well-Orderable
snippet: Let $N$ be a class. Let $N$ be slowly well-ordered under the subset relation. Then $\bigcup N$ is well-orderable.

title: Union of Small Classes is Small
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be small classes. Then $x \cup y$ is also small.

title: Union of Subclass is Subclass of Union of Class
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\bigcup A$ and $\bigcup B$ denote the union of $A$ and union of $B$ respectively. Let $A$ be a subclass of $B$: $A \subseteq B$ Then $\bigcup A$ is a subclass of $\bigcup B$: $\bigcup A \subseteq \bigcup B$

title: Union of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H, K \le G$ be subgroups of $G$. Let neither $H \subseteq K$ nor $K \subseteq H$. Then $H \cup K$ is not a subgroup of $G$.

title: Union of Subset of Family is Subset of Union of Family
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of subsets of a set $S$. Let $J \subseteq I$ Then: $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in J} A_\alpha \subseteq \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} A_\alpha$ where $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \mathop \in I} A_\alpha$ denotes the union of $\family {A_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in I}$.

title: Union of Subsets is Subset
snippet: Let $S_1$, $S_2$, and $T$ be sets. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ both be subsets of $T$. Then: $S_1 \cup S_2 \subseteq T$ That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \implies \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

title: Union of Successor Ordinal
snippet: Let $x$ be an ordinal. Let $x^+$ denote the successor of $x$. Then: $\map \bigcup {x^+} = x$

title: Union of Symmetric Differences
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\paren {R \symdif S} \cup \paren {S \symdif T} = \paren {R \cup S \cup T} \setminus \paren {R \cap S \cap T}$ where $R \symdif S$ denotes the symmetric difference between $R$ and $S$.

title: Union of Symmetric Relations is Symmetric
snippet: The union of two symmetric relations is also a symmetric relation.

title: Union of Topologies is not necessarily Topology
snippet: Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be topologies on a set $S$. Then $\tau_1 \cup \tau_2$ is not necessarily also a topology on $S$.

title: Union of Topologies on Singleton or Doubleton is Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set which is either a singleton or a doubleton. Let $\family {\tau_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an arbitrary non-empty indexed set of topologies on $S$. Then $\tau := \ds \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} {\tau_i}$ is also a topology on $S$.

title: Union of Total Ordering with Lower Sections is Total Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {Y, \preceq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $X$ be the disjoint union of $Y$ with the set of lower sections of $Y$. Define a relation $\preceq'$ on $X$ extending $\preceq$ by letting: $y_1 \preceq' y_2 \iff y_1 \preceq y_2$ $y \preceq' L \iff y \in L$ $L_1 \preceq' L_2 \iff L_1 \subseteq L_2$ $L \preceq' y \iff y \in Y \setminus L$ Then $\preceq'$ is a total ordering.

title: Union of Transitive Class is Subclass
snippet: Let $A$ be a transitive class. Let $\bigcup A$ denote the union of $A$. Then: $\bigcup A \subseteq A$

title: Union of Transitive Class is Transitive
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\bigcup A$ denote the union of $A$. Let $A$ be transitive. Then $\bigcup A$ is also transitive.

title: Union of Transitive Relations Not Always Transitive
snippet: The union of transitive relations is not necessarily itself transitive.

title: Union of Turing Machines
snippet: Let $T_1, T_2$ be Turing machines. Let $\Sigma_1, \Sigma_2$ be the input symbols of $T_1, T_2$, respectively. Let $L_1, L_2$ be the languages accepted by $T_1, T_2$, respectively. There exists a Turing machine $T$ such that: The input symbols of $T$ are $\Sigma_1 \cup \Sigma_2$. The language accepted by $T$ is $L_1 \cup L_2$. $T$ halts on some input it is in the accepted language, or both $T_1$ and $T_2$ halt on it.

title: Union of Two Compact Sets is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological spaces. Let $H$ and $K$ be compact subsets of $T$. Then $H \cup K$ is compact in $T$.

title: Union of Union of Cartesian Product
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets such that $A \ne \O$ and $B \ne \O$. Let the ordered pair $\tuple {a, b}$ be defined using the Kuratowski formalization: $\tuple {a, b} := \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ Then: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B$ where: $\cup$ denotes union $\times$ denotes Cartesian product.

title: Union of Union of Cartesian Product with Empty Factor
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be sets such that either $A = \O$ or $B = \O$. Let the ordered pair $\tuple {a, b}$ be defined using the Kuratowski formalization: $\tuple {a, b} := \set {\set a, \set {a, b} }$ Then: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B \iff A = B = \O$ where: $\cup$ denotes union $\times$ denotes Cartesian product. That is, if either $A$ or $B$ is empty: $\ds \bigcup \bigcup \paren {A \times B} = A \cup B$ holds they are both empty

title: Union of Union of Relation is Union of Domain with Image
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $\RR \subseteq V \times V$ be a relation. Let $\Dom \RR$ denote the domain of $\RR$. Then: $\map \bigcup {\bigcup \RR} = \Dom \RR \cup \Img \RR$ where: $\bigcup \RR$ denotes the union of $\RR$ $\Dom \RR$ denotes the domain of $\RR$ $\Img \RR$ denotes the image of $\RR$.

title: Union of Unordered Tuples
snippet: Let $x_1, \dots, x_n, x_{n+1}, \dots, x_m$ be arbitrary. Then $\set {x_1, \dots, x_n} \cup \set {x_{n + 1}, \dots, x_m} = \set {x_1, \dots, x_n, x_{n + 1}, \dots, x_m}$

title: Union of Upper Sections is Upper
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a preordered set. Let $A$ be a set of subsets of $S$ such that: $\forall X \in A: X$ is an upper section. Then: $\bigcup A$ is also an upper section.

title: Union of Vertical Sections is Vertical Section of Union
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\set {E_\alpha : \alpha \in A}$ be a set of subsets of $X \times Y$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha}_x = \bigcup_{\alpha \in A} \paren {E_\alpha}_x$ where: $\ds \paren {\bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $\ds \bigcup_{\alpha \in A} E_\alpha$ $\paren {E_\alpha}_x$ is the $x$-vertical section of $E_\alpha$.

title: Union of g-Tower is Greatest Element and Unique Fixed Point
snippet: Let $M$ be a set. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Then: $\ds \bigcup M \in M$ $\ds \bigcup M$ is the greatest element (under the subset relation) of $M$ $\ds \bigcup M$ is the unique fixed point of $M$.

title: Union of two Zero Loci is Zero Locus
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $A = k \sqbrk {X_1, \ldots, X_n}$ be the ring of polynomials in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $S,T \subseteq A$. Then: $\ds {\map V S} \cup \map V T = \map V {S \cdot T}$ where: $\map V \cdot$ denotes the zero locus $S \cdot T := \set { fg : f \in S, g \in T }$

title: Union with Complement
snippet: The union of a set and its complement is the universal set: $S \cup \map \complement S = \mathbb U$

title: Union with Disjoint Singleton is Dependent if Element Depends on Subset
snippet: Let $M = \struct{S, \mathscr I}$ be a matroid. Let $A \subseteq S$. Let $x \in S : x \notin A$. Let $x$ depend on $A$. Then $A \cup \set x$ is a dependent subset of $M$.

title: Union with Empty Set
snippet: The union of any set with the empty set is the set itself: $S \cup \O = S$

title: Union with Intersection equals Intersection with Union iff Subset
snippet: Let $A$, $B$ and $C$ be sets. Then: $\paren {A \cap B} \cup C = A \cap \paren {B \cup C} \iff C \subseteq A$

title: Union with Relative Complement
snippet: The union of a set $T$ and its relative complement in $S$ is the set $S$: $\relcomp S T \cup T = S$

title: Union with Superclass is Superclass
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Then: $A \subseteq B \iff A \cup B = B$ where: $A \subseteq B$ denotes that $A$ is a subclass of $B$ $A \cup B$ denotes the union of $A$ and $B$.

title: Union with Superset is Superset
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \cup T = T$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$.

title: Union with Universal Set
snippet: The union of a set with the universal set is the universal set: $\mathbb U \cup S = \mathbb U$

title: Unique Accumulation Point of Sequence in Weakly Countably Compact Subset of Banach Space is Limit of Sequence
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $A \subseteq X$ be countably compact in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $x \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $A$ such that: $x$ is the unique accumulation point of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to $x$.

title: Unique Code for State of URM Program
snippet: Every state of a URM program can be assigned a unique code number. This code number is called the state code (or situation code).

title: Unique Code for URM Instruction
snippet: Each basic instruction $I$ in a URM Program can be identified with a unique code number $\beta \left({I}\right)$. We also define the following sets: $\operatorname{Zinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Zero instructions $\operatorname{Sinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Successor instructions $\operatorname{Cinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Copy instructions $\operatorname{Jinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Jump instructions. Then we define $\operatorname{Instr}$ to be the set of codes of all basic URM instructions.

title: Unique Code for URM Program
snippet: Any URM program can be assigned a unique code number.

title: Unique Composition of Group Element whose Order is Product of Coprime Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $g \in G$ be an element of $g$. Let: $\order g = m n$ where: $\order g$ denotes the order of $g$ in $G$ $m$ and $n$ are coprime integers. Then $g$ can be expressed uniquely as the product of two commuting elements $a$ and $b$ of order $m$ and $n$ respectively.

title: Unique Constant in Category of Monoids
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Mon}$ be the category of monoids. Then every object $M$ of $\mathbf{Mon}$ has precisely one constant.

title: Unique Epimorphism from Quotient Group to Quotient Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circledcirc}$ and $\struct {G_2, \circledast}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circledcirc} \to \struct {G_2, \circledast}$ be a group epimorphism. Let $K$ be the kernel of $\phi$. Let $H_1$ be a normal subgroup of $\struct {G_1, \circledcirc}$. Let $H_2 := \phi \sqbrk {H_1}$ be the image of $H_1$ under $\phi$.

title: Unique Factorization Domain is Integrally Closed
snippet: Let $A$ be a unique factorization domain (UFD). Then $A$ is integrally closed.

title: Unique Factorization Theorem for Gaussian Integers
snippet: The ring of Gaussian integers: $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ forms a unique factorization domain. That is, every Gaussian integer can be expressed as the product of one or more Gaussian primes, uniquely up to the order in which they appear.

title: Unique Integer Close to Rational in Valuation Ring of P-adic Norm
snippet:
Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime number $p$. Let $x \in \Q$ such that $
orm{x}_p \le 1$. Then for all $i \in \N$ there exists a unique $\alpha \in \Z$ such that: $(1): \quad 
orm {x - \alpha}_p \le p^{-i}$ $(2): \quad 0 \le \alpha \le p^i - 1$

title: Unique Isomorphism between Equivalent Finite Totally Ordered Sets
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets of the same cardinality. That is: $\card S = \card T$ Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ and $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$ be totally ordered sets. Then there is exactly one order isomorphism from $\struct {S, \preceq}$ to $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq}$.

title: Unique Isomorphism between Ordinal Subset and Unique Ordinal
snippet: Let $\On$ be the class of all ordinals. Let $S \subset \On$ where $S$ is a set. Then there exists a unique mapping $\phi$ and a unique ordinal $x$ such that $\phi : x \to S$ is an order isomorphism.

title: Unique Isomorphism from Quotient Mapping to Epimorphism Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \oplus}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \oplus} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an epimorphism. Let $\RR_\phi$ be the equivalence induced by $\phi$. Let $S / \RR_\phi$ be the quotient of $S$ by $\RR_\phi$. Let $q_{\RR_\phi}: S \to S / \RR_\phi$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_\phi$. Let $\struct {S / \RR_\phi, \oplus_{\RR_\phi} }$ be the quotient structure defined by $\RR_\phi$.

title: Unique Linear Transformation Between Modules
snippet: Let $\struct {G, +_G, \times_G}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \times_H}_R$ be unitary $R$-modules. Let $\sequence {a_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be an ordered basis of $G$. Let $\sequence {b_k}_{1 \mathop \le k \mathop \le n}$ be a sequence of $n$ elements of $H$. Then there exists a unique linear transformation $\phi: G \to H$ satisfying: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: \map \phi {a_k} = b_k$

title: Unique Linear Transformation Between Vector Spaces
snippet: == Corollary to Unique Linear Transformation Between Modules == Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space. Let $H$ be a $K$-vector space (not necessarily finite-dimensional). Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a linearly independent sequence of vectors of $G$. Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence of vectors of $H$. Then there is a unique linear transformation $\phi: G \to H$ satisfying: $\forall k \in \closedint 1 n: \map \phi {a_k} = b_k$

title: Unique Minimal Element may not be Smallest
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ have a unique minimal element. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ has a smallest element.

title: Unique Ordinal Exponentiation Inequality
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Let $x > 1$ and $y > 0$. Then there exists a unique ordinal $z$ such that: $x^z \le y$ and $y < x^{z^+}$

title: Unique Period Prime/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unique Period Primes == In base $10$, the prime numbers $3$, $11$, $37$, and $101$ are the only ones with periods $1$, $2$, $3$ and $4$ respectively. Hence they are unique period primes. But: $41$ and $271$ both have period $5$ $7$ and $13$ both have period $6$ $239$ and $4649$ both have period $7$ $73$ and $137$ both have period $8$. Thus these primes are not unique period primes.

title: Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Convex Subset of Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let $h \in H$. Let $K \subseteq H$ be a closed, convex, non-empty subset of $H$. Then there is a unique point $k_0 \in K$ such that: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K}$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set.

title: Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Linear Subspace of Hilbert Space iff Orthogonal
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let $h \in H$. Let $K \subseteq H$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Then the unique point $k_0 \in K$ from Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Convex Subset of Hilbert Space such that: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K}$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set, is characterised by: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K} \iff \paren {h - k_0} \perp K$ where $\perp$ signifies orthogonality.

title: Unique Quotient in Natural Numbers
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Let $n \in \N$ and $m \in \N_{>0}$ such that: $m \divides n$ where $m \divides n$ denotes that $m$ is a divisor of $n$. Then there exists exactly one element $p \in \N$ such that $m \times p = n$.

title: Unique Readability for Prefix Notation
snippet: Let $\AA$ be an alphabet. Then prefix notation for $\AA$ has the unique readability property.

title: Unique Representation by Ordered Basis
snippet: Let $G$ be a unitary $R$-module. Then $\sequence {a_n}$ is an ordered basis of $G$ : For every $x \in G$ there exists one and only one sequence $\sequence {\lambda_n}$ of scalars such that $\ds x = \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k a_k$.

title: Unique Representation in Polynomial Forms
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral subdomain of $R$. Let $X \in R$ be transcendental over $D$. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials in $X$ over $D$. Then each non-zero member of $D \left[{X}\right]$ can be expressed in just one way in the form: $\ds f \in D \sqbrk X: f = \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^n {a_k \circ X^k}$

title: Unique Representation of Complex Number in Spherical Form
snippet: Let $\PP$ be the complex plane. Let $\mathbb S$ be the unit sphere which is tangent to $\PP$ at $\tuple {0, 0}$ (that is, where $z = 0$). Let the diameter of $\mathbb S$ perpendicular to $\PP$ through $\tuple {0, 0}$ be $NS$ where $S$ is the point $\tuple {0, 0}$. Let the point $N$ be referred to as the north pole of $\mathbb S$ and $S$ be referred to as the south pole of $\mathbb S$. 900px Let $A$ be a point on $P$. Let the line $NA$ be constructed. Then $NA$ passes through exactly one point $A'$ on the surface of $\mathbb S$ apart from $N$.

title: Unique Sequence of Consecutive Odd Numbers which are Prime
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer such that $n > 3$. Then $n$, $n + 2$, $n + 4$ cannot all be prime. That is, the only set of $3$ consecutive odd numbers all of which are prime is $\set {3, 5, 7}$.

title: Unique Subgroup of a Given Order is Normal
snippet: Let a group $G$ have only one subgroup of a given order. Then that subgroup is normal.

title: Unique Tree of Order 2
snippet: There exists exactly one tree of order $2$: 200px

title: Uniqueness Condition for Relation Value
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a relation. Let $\tuple {x, y} \in \RR$. Let: $\exists ! y: \tuple {x, y} \in \RR$ Then: $\map \RR x = y$ where $\map \RR x$ denotes the image of $\RR$ at $x$. If $y$ is not unique, then: $\map \RR x = \O$

title: Uniqueness Theorem/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Uniqueness Theorems ==

title: Uniqueness of Analytic Continuation
snippet: Let $U \subset V \subset \C$ be open subsets of the complex plane. Let $V$ be connected. Suppose: $(1): \quad F_1, F_2$ are functions defined on $V$ $(2): \quad f$ is a function defined on $U$. Let $F_1$ and $F_2$ be analytic continuations of $f$ to $V$. Then $F_1 = F_2$.

title: Uniqueness of Continuously Differentiable Solution to Initial Value Problem
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \R^2$ be a region containing $\tuple {a, b}$. Let $f: D \to \R$ be real-valued mapping such that $f$ and $\dfrac {\partial f} {\partial x}$ are continuous on $D$. Consider the initial value problem: $\dfrac {\d x} {\d t} = \map f {t, x}$ $\map x a = b$ Suppose the initial value problem above has a solution $\phi$ for all $x$ in some interval $J$ containing $a$. Then the solution $\phi$ is unique on $J$.

title: Uniqueness of Jordan Decomposition
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a signed measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$. Let $\tuple {P_1, N_1}$ and $\tuple {P_2, N_2}$ be Hahn decompositions of $\mu$. Let $\tuple {\mu^+_1, \mu^-_1}$ be the Jordan decomposition of $\mu$ corresponding to $\tuple {P_1, N_1}$. Let $\tuple {\mu^+_2, \mu^-_2}$ be the Jordan decomposition of $\mu$ corresponding to $\tuple {P_2, N_2}$. Then: $\mu^+_1 = \mu^+_2$ and: $\mu^-_1 = \mu^-_2$ So: the Jordan decomposition of a signed measure is unique.
