title: Uniqueness of Normal Coordinates
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be an $n$-dimensional Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold. Let $U_p$ be the normal neighborhood for $p \in M$. Then for every normal coordinate chart on $U_p$ centered at $p \in M$ the coordinate basis is orthonormal at $p$. Furthermore, for every orthonormal basis $\tuple {b_i}$ for $T_p M$, there is a unique normal coordinate chart $\tuple {x^i}$ on $U_p$ such that: $\ds \forall i \in \N_{> 0} : i \le n : \valueat{\partial_i} p = b_i$

title: Uniqueness of Polynomial Ring in One Variable
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\struct {R \sqbrk X, \iota, X}$ and $\struct {R \sqbrk Y, \kappa, Y}$ be polynomial rings in one variable over $R$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism $f: R \sqbrk X \to R \sqbrk Y$ such that: $f \circ \iota = \kappa$ $\map f X = Y$ and it is an isomorphism.

title: Uniqueness of Positive Root of Positive Real Number
Uniqueness of Product Measures
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_1, \mu}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_2, \nu}$ be measure spaces. Let $\GG_1$ and $\GG_2$ be generators for $\Sigma_1$ and $\Sigma_2$, respectively. Suppose that $\GG_1$ and $\GG_2$ are closed under intersection. Suppose further that there are exhausting sequences $\sequence {G_{1, n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {G_{2, n} }_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $\GG_1$ and $\GG_2$, respectively, such that: $\forall n \in \N: \map \mu {G_{1, n} } < \infty$ $\forall n \in \N: \map \nu {G_{2, n} } < \infty$ Then there is at most one measure $\rho$ on the product space $\struct {X…

title: Uniqueness of Real z such that x Choose n+1 Equals y Choose n+1 Plus z Choose n
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers which satisfy: $n \le y \le x \le y + 1$ Then there exists a unique real number $z$ such that: $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$ where $n - 1 \le z \le y$.

title: Uniqueness of Representing Objects
snippet: Let $C$ be a locally small category. Let $\mathbf{Set}$ be the category of sets. Let $F : \mathbf C \to \mathbf{Set}$ be a covariant functor. Let $(A, \eta)$ and $(B, \xi)$ be representations of $F$. Then there exists a unique isomorphism $f : A \to B$ such that $\eta \circ h^f = \xi$, where: $h^f$ is the precomposition natural transformation $\circ$ denotes vertical composition of natural transformations

title: Unit-Speed Admissible Curve is Critical Point of Riemannian Length iff Geodesic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $\gamma$ be a unit-speed admissible curve. Let $L_g$ the Riemannian length of some admissible curve. Then $\gamma$ is the critical point of $L_g$ $\gamma$ is geodesic.

title: Unit-Speed Minimizing Curve is Geodesic
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold. Let $I = \closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $\gamma : I \to M$ be an admissible curve. Suppose $\gamma$ is parametrized so that $\gamma$ is a unit-speed curve. Suppose $\gamma$ is minimizing. Then $\gamma$ is a geodesic.

title: Unit Cylinder as Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^3, d}$ be the Euclidean space. Let $S_C \subseteq \R^3$ be the surface of revolution. Let $C$ be a straight line in the open upper half-plane. Let the smooth local parametrization of $C$ be: $\map \gamma t = \tuple {t, 1}$ Then the induced metric on $S_C$ is: $g = d t^2 + d \theta^2$

title: Unit Ideal iff Radical is Unit Ideal
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\mathfrak a$ be an ideal of $A$. Then: $ \mathfrak a = A \iff \map \Rad {\mathfrak a} = A$ where: $A$ is called the unit ideal of $A$ $\map \Rad {\mathfrak a}$ denotes the radical of $\mathfrak a$

title: Unit Ideal is Principal Ideal Generated by Unity
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Then: $A = \ideal 1$ where: $A$ is called the unit ideal of $A$ $\ideal 1$ denotes the principal ideal generated by the unity of $A$

title: Unit Interval is Path-Connected in Real Numbers
snippet: Let $\R$ be the real number line with the usual (Euclidean} metric. The closed unit interval $\I = \closedint 0 1$ is a path-connected metric subspace of $\R$.

title: Unit Matrix is Identity for Matrix Multiplication
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map {\MM_R} n$ denote the metric space of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Let $\mathbf I_n$ denote the unit matrix of order $n$: Then: $\forall \mathbf A \in \map {\MM_R} n: \mathbf A \mathbf I_n = \mathbf A = \mathbf I_n \mathbf A$ That is, the unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ is the identity element for (conventional) matrix multiplication over $\map {\MM_R} n$.

title: Unit Matrix is Orthogonal
snippet: The unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ of order $n$ is orthogonal.

title: Unit Matrix is Proper Orthogonal
snippet: The unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ of order $n$ is proper orthogonal.

title: Unit Matrix is Unity of Ring of Square Matrices
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. The unit matrix over $R$: $\mathbf I_n = \begin {pmatrix} 1_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 1_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 0_R & 1_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 1_R \end {pmatrix}$ is the identity element of $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$.

title: Unit Matrix is its own Inverse
snippet: The inverse of the unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ of order $n$ is $\mathbf I_n$. That is, a unit matrix it its own inverse.

title: Unit Sphere as Surface of Revolution
snippet: Let $\struct {\R^3, d}$ be the Euclidean space. Let $S_C \subseteq \R^3$ be the surface of revolution. Let $C$ be a semi-circle defined by $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ in the open upper half-plane. Let the smooth local parametrization of $C$ be: $\map \gamma \phi = \tuple {\cos \phi, \sin \phi}$ where $\phi \in \openint 0 \pi$. Then the induced metric on $S_C$ is: $g = \d \phi^2 + \sin^2 \phi \rd \theta^2$

title: Unit Sphere is Closed/Normed Vector Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\Bbb S := \set {x \in X : \norm x = 1}$ be a unit sphere in $M$. Then $\Bbb S$ is closed in $M$.

title: Unit Tangent Bundle is Connected iff Manifold is Connected
snippet: Let $\struct {M, g}$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $n > 1$. Let $UTM$ be the unit tangent bundle of $M$. Then $UTM$ is connected $M$ is connected.

title: Unit Vector in Direction of Vector
snippet: Let $\mathbf v$ be a vector quantity. The unit vector $\mathbf {\hat v}$ in the direction of $\mathbf v$ is: $\mathbf {\hat v} = \dfrac {\mathbf v} {\norm {\mathbf v} }$ where $\norm {\mathbf v}$ is the magnitude of $\mathbf v$.

title: Unit Vector in terms of Direction Cosines
snippet: Let $\mathbf r$ be a vector quantity embedded in a Cartesian $3$-space. Let $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf k$ be the unit vectors in the positive directions of the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Let $\cos \alpha$, $\cos \beta$ and $\cos \gamma$ be the direction cosines of $\mathbf r$ with respect to the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Let $\mathbf {\hat r}$ denote the unit vector in the direction of $\mathbf r$. Then: $\mathbf {\hat r} = \paren {\cos \alpha} \mathbf i + \paren {\cos \beta} \mathbf j + \paren {\cos \gamma} \mathbf k$

title: Unit Vectors in Complex Plane which are Vertices of Equilateral Triangle
snippet: Let $\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3$ be complex numbers embedded in the complex plane such that: $\epsilon_1, \epsilon_2, \epsilon_3$ all have modulus $1$ $\epsilon_1 + \epsilon_2 + \epsilon_3 = 0$ Then: $\paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_2} {\epsilon_1} }^3 = \paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_3} {\epsilon_2} }^2 = \paren {\dfrac {\epsilon_1} {\epsilon_3} }^2 = 1$

title: Unit Vectors of Cartesian 3-Space form Basis
snippet: Consider the Cartesian $3$-space $C$. Let $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf k$ denote the unit vectors in the positive directions of the $x$-axis, $y$-axis and $z$-axis respectively. Then $\set {\mathbf i, \mathbf j, \mathbf k}$ forms a basis for $C$.

title: Unit n-Cube under Chebyshev Distance is Subspace of Real Vector Space
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $I^n$ denote the unit $n$-cube: $I^n = \closedint 0 1^n$ that is, the Cartesian product of $n$ instances of the closed real interval $\set {x \in \R: 0 \le x \le 1}$. Let $d_c: I^n \times I^n \to \R$ be defined as: $\ds \map {d_c} {x, y} = \max_{i \mathop = 1}^n \set {\size {x_i - y_i} }$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}, y = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \in I^n$. Then $\struct {I_n, d_c}$ is a metric subspace of $\struct {\R^n, d_\infty}$, where $d_\infty$ is the Chebyshev distance on the real vector space $\R_n$.

title: Unit n-Sphere under Euclidean Metric is Metric Subspace of Euclidean Real Vector Space
snippet: Let $\Bbb S^n$ be the unit $n$-sphere. Let $d_S: \Bbb S^n \times \Bbb S^n \to \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: $\ds \forall x, y \in \Bbb S^n: \map {d_S} {x, y} = \sqrt {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{n + 1} \paren {x_i - y_i}^2}$ where $x = \tuple {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n + 1} }, y = \tuple {y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_{n + 1} }$. Then $\struct {\Bbb S^n, d_S}$ is a metric subspace of $\struct {\R^{n + 1}, d}$, where $d$ is the Euclidean metric on the real vector space $\R^{n + 1}$.

title: Unit of Adjunction Induces Adjunction
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ be locally small categories. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ and $G:\mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: \operatorname {id}_{\mathbf D} \to GF$ be a natural transformation such that: for each object $D$ in $\mathbf D$ the morphism $\eta_D$ is a universal morphism from object $FD$ to functor $G$ For each $D$ in $\mathbf D$ and $C$ in $\mathbf C$ let: $\alpha_{\tuple{D, C}}: \map {\mathrm {Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {FD, C} \to \map {\mathrm {Hom}_{\mathbf D} } {D, GC}$ be the mapping defined by: $\forall g \in \map {\mathrm {Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {FD,…

title: Unit of Integral Domain divides all Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose unity is $1_D$. Let $\struct {U_D, \circ}$ be the group of units of $\struct {D, +, \circ}$. Then: $\forall x \in D: \forall u \in U_D: u \divides x$ That is, every unit of $D$ is a divisor of every element of $D$.

title: Unit of Measurement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Units of Measurement ==

title: Unit of Ring is not Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x$ be a unit of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $x$ is neither a left zero divisor nor a right zero divisor of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$.

title: Unit of Ring of Mappings iff Image is Subset of Ring Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $U_R$ be the set of units in $R$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the ring of mappings on the set of mappings $R^S$. Then: $f \in R^S$ is a unit of $R^S$ $\Img f \subseteq U_R$ where $\Img f$ is the image of $f$. In this case, the inverse of $f$ is the mapping $f^{-1} : S \to U_R$ defined by: $\forall x \in S : \map {f^{-1} } x = \map f x^{-1}$

title: Unit of System of Sets is Unique
snippet: The unit of a system of sets, if it exists, is unique. If $U$ is the unit of a system of sets $\SS$, then $\forall A \in \SS: A \subseteq U$.

title: Unital C*-Algebra is Unital Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra that is unital as an algebra, with identity element ${\mathbf 1}_A \ne {\mathbf 0}_A$. Then $A$ is unital as a Banach algebra.

title: Unital Ring Homomorphism by Idempotent
snippet: Let $A$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $e \in A$ be an idempotent element. Let $\ideal e$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by $e$. Then the mapping: $f: A \to \ideal e: a \mapsto e a$ is a surjective unital ring homomorphism from $\struct {A, +, \circ}$ to $\struct {\ideal e, +, \circ}$ with kernel the ideal $\ideal {1 - e}$ generated by $1 - e$.

title: Unital Subalgebra of Algebraic Field Extension is Field
snippet: Let $E / F$ be an algebraic field extension. Let $A \subseteq E$ be a unital subalgebra over $F$. Then $A$ is a field.

title: Unital Subalgebra of Finite Field Extension is Field
snippet: Let $E / F$ be a finite field extension. Let $A \subseteq E$ be a unital subalgebra over $F$. Then $A$ is a field.

title: Unitary Group is Group
snippet: The set of unitary $n \times n$ matrices forms a group under (conventional) matrix multiplication.

title: Unitary Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unitary Matrices ==

title: Unitary Matrix is Normal
snippet: All unitary matrices are normal.

title: Unitary Method/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unitary Method ==

title: Unitary Module of All Mappings is Unitary Module
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_R$ be the module of all mappings from $S$ to $G$. Then $\struct {G^S, +_G', \circ}_R$ is a unitary module.

title: Unitary R-Modules with n-Element Bases are Isomorphic
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be unitary $R$-modules for some ring with unity $R$. Let $G$ and $G$ both have bases with $n$ elements. Then $G$ and $H$ are isomorphic.

title: Unitary Ratio/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Unitary Ratios == The ratios: $1 : 8$ and: $2 : 1$ are both examples of unitary ratios.

title: Unitization of *-Algebra is *-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra over $\C$. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Define: $\tuple {a, \lambda}^\dagger = \tuple {a^\ast, \overline \lambda}$ for each $\tuple {a, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then $\struct {A_+, \dagger}$ is a $\ast$-algebra.

title: Unitization of Algebra over Field is Unital Algebra over Field
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be an algebra over $K$. Let $\struct {A_+, +_{A_+}, \cdot_{A_+}, \circ_{A_+} }_K$ be the unitization of $A$. Then $\struct {A_+, +_{A_+}, \cdot_{A_+}, \circ_{A_+} }_K$ is a unital algebra over $K$.

title: Unitization of Algebra over Field preserves Subalgebra Relation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be a non-unital commutative algebra over $K$. Let $B$ be a subalgebra of $A$. Let $A_+$ and $B_+$ be the unitizations of $A$ and $B$ respectively. Then $B_+$ is a unital subalgebra of $A_+$.

title: Unitization of Commutative Algebra over Field is Commutative
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $A$ be a commutative algebra over $K$. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Then $A_+$ is commutative.

title: Unitization of Non-Unital Subalgebra of Unital Algebra is Isomorphic to Unital Subalgebra
snippet: Let $A$ be a unital algebra over $\C$. Let $B$ be a subalgebra of $A$ that is not unital. Let $B_+$ be the unitization of $B$. Let $B \oplus \C {\mathbf 1}_A$ be the (internal) direct sum of $B$ and $\C {\mathbf 1}_A$. Define $f : B_+ \to B \oplus \C {\mathbf 1}_A$ by: $\map f {b, \lambda} = b + \lambda {\mathbf 1}_A$ for each $\tuple {b, \lambda} \in B_+$. Then $f$ is a unital algebra isomorphism.

title: Unitization of Normed Algebra is Banach Algebra iff Original Algebra is Banach Algebra
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra over $\GF$ that is not unital as an algebra. Let $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} }$ be the normed unitization of $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} }$ is a Banach algebra $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ is a Banach algebra.

title: Unitization of Normed Algebra is Unital Normed Algebra
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {A, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed algebra that is not unital as an algebra. Let $A_+$ be the unitization of $A$. Define $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} : A_+ 	o \hointr 0 \infty$ by: $
orm {	uple {x, \lambda} }_{A_+} = 
orm x + \cmod \lambda$ for each $	uple {x, \lambda} \in A_+$. Then $\struct {A_+, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{A_+} }$ is a unital normed algebra.

title: Units of 5th Cyclotomic Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ denote the $5$th cyclotomic ring. The units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {i \sqrt 5}, +, \times}$ are $1$ and $-1$.

title: Units of Field of Complex Numbers form Group
snippet: $\C^\times = \C \setminus \set 0$ where $\C^\times$ denotes the group of units of $\C$.

title: Units of Gaussian Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ be the ring of Gaussian integers. The set of units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ is $\set {1, i, -1, -i}$.

title: Units of Gaussian Integers form Group
snippet: Let $U_\C$ be the set of units of the Gaussian integers: $U_\C = \set {1, i, -1, -i}$ where $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i = \sqrt {-1}$. Let $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ be the algebraic structure formed by $U_\C$ under the operation of complex multiplication. Then $\struct {U_\C, \times}$ forms a cyclic group under complex multiplication.

title: Units of Quadratic Integers over 2
snippet: Let $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}$ denote the set of quadratic integers over $2$: $\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2} := \set {a + b \sqrt 2: a, b \in \Z}$ that is, all numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers. Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$ be the integral domain where $+$ and $\times$ are conventional addition and multiplication on real numbers. Then numbers of the form $a + b \sqrt 2$ such that $a^2 - 2 b^2 = \pm 1$ are all units of $\struct {\Z \sqbrk {\sqrt 2}, +, \times}$.

title: Units of Ring Direct Product are Ring Direct Product of Units
snippet: Let $R_1, R_2, \ldots, R_m$ be rings with identity. Then the following group isomorphism holds: $\map U {R_1 \oplus R_2 \oplus \cdots \oplus R_n} \simeq \map U {R_1} \oplus \map U {R_2} \oplus \cdots \oplus \map U {R_n}$.

title: Units of Ring of Arithmetic Functions
snippet: Let $f$ be an arithmetic function. Then $f$ is a unit in the ring of arithmetic functions : $\map f 1 \ne 0$

title: Units of Ring of Polynomial Forms over Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a non-null commutative ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $R \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in an indeterminate $X$ over $R$. Let $\map P X = a_0 + a_1 X + \cdots + a_n X^n \in R \sqbrk X$. Then: $\map P X$ is a unit of $R \sqbrk X$ $a_0$ is a unit of $R$ Also, for $i = 1, \ldots, n$, $a_i$ is nilpotent in $R$.

title: Units of Ring of Polynomial Forms over Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \circ}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $F \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in an indeterminate $X$ over $F$. Then the units of $F \sqbrk X$ are all the elements of $F \sqbrk X$ whose degree is $0$.

title: Units of Ring of Polynomial Forms over Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain. Let $D \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomial forms in an indeterminate $X$ over $D$. Then the group of units of $D \sqbrk X$ is precisely the group of elements of $D \sqbrk X$ of degree zero that are units of $D$.

title: Unity Divides All Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose unity is $1_D$. Then unity is a divisor of every element of $D$: $\forall x \in D: 1_D \divides x$ Also: $\forall x \in D: -1_D \divides x$

title: Unity Function is Completely Multiplicative
snippet: Let $f_1: \Z_{> 0} \to \Z_{> 0}$ be the constant function: $\forall n \in \Z_{> 0}: f_1 \left({n}\right) = 1$ Then $f_1$ is completely multiplicative.

title: Unity and Negative form Subgroup of Units
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Then: $\struct {\set {1_R, -1_R}, \circ} \le U_R$ That is, the set consisting of the unity and its negative forms a subgroup of the group of units.

title: Unity is Unit
snippet: The unity in a ring is a unit.

title: Unity is Unity in Ring of Idempotents
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a commutative and unitary ring whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\left({A, \oplus, \circ}\right)$ be the ring of idempotents of $R$. Then $1_R$ is also a unity for $\left({A, \oplus, \circ}\right)$.

title: Unity of Integral Domain is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Then the unity of $\struct {D, +, \times}$ is unique.

title: Unity of Ordered Integral Domain is Strictly Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times \le}$ be an ordered integral domain whose unity is $1_D$. Then: $\map P {1_D}$ where $P$ is the (strict) positivity property.

title: Unity of Ring is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Then $1_R$ is an idempotent element of $R$ under the ring product $\circ$: $1_R \circ 1_R = 1_R$

title: Unity of Ring is Unique
snippet: A ring can have no more than one unity.

title: Unity of Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

title: Unity of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{R^S} : S \to R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{R^S}} s = 1_R$.

title: Unity of Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

title: Unity of Subfield is Unity of Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose unity is $1$. Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a subfield of $F$. The unity of $\struct {K, +, \times}$ is also $1$.

title: Unity of Subring is not necessarily Unity of Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {S, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_S$. Let $\struct {T, + \circ}$ be a subring of $\struct {S, + \circ}$ whose unity is $1_T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $1_T = 1_S$.

title: Unity plus Negative of Nilpotent Ring Element is Unit
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $x \in R$ be nilpotent. Then $1_R - x$ is a unit of $R$.

title: Universal Affirmative and Negative are both False iff Particular Affirmative and Negative are both True
snippet: Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | q = \map {\mathbf A} {S, P} | lc= The universal affirmative: | ml= \forall x: \map S x | mo= \implies | mr= \map P x }} {{axiom | q = \map {\mathbf E} {S, P} | lc= The universal negative: | ml= \forall x: \map S x | mo= \implies | mr= \neg \map P x }} {{axiom | q = \map {\mathbf I} {S, P} | lc= The particular affirmative: | ml= \exists x: \map S x | mo= \land | mr= \map P x }} {{axiom | q = \map {\mathbf O} {S, P} | lc= The particular negative: | ml= \exists x: \map S x | mo= \land | mr= \neg \map P x }} Then: $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P}$ and $\map…

title: Universal Affirmative and Particular Negative are Contradictory
snippet: Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf A} {S, P}: | lc= The universal affirmative: | t = All $S$ are $P$ }} {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf O} {S, P}: | lc= The particular negative: | t = Some $S$ are not $P$ }} Then $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P}$ and $\map {\mathbf O} {S, P}$ are contradictory.

title: Universal Affirmative and Universal Negative are Contrary
snippet: Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf A} {S, P}: | lc= The universal affirmative: | t = All $S$ are $P$ }} {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf E} {S, P}: | lc= The universal negative: | t = No $S$ is $P$ }} Then in the context of Aristotelian Logic, $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P}$ and $\map {\mathbf E} {S, P}$ are contrary statements.

title: Universal Affirmative and Universal Negative are Contrary iff First Predicate is not Vacuous
snippet:
Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf A} {S, P}: | lc= The universal affirmative: | q =  orall x | m = \map S x \implies \map P x }} {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf E} {S, P}: | lc= The universal negative: | q =  orall x | m = \map S x \implies 
eg \map P x }} Then: $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P}$ and $\map {\mathbf E} {S, P}$ are contrary $\exists x: \map S x$ Using the symbology of predicate logic: $\exists x: \map S x \iff 
eg \paren {\paren { orall x: \map S x \implies \map P x} \land \paren { orall x: \map S x \implies 
eg \map P x} }$

title: Universal Affirmative implies Particular Affirmative iff First Predicate is not Vacuous
snippet: Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | ll = \map {\mathbf A} {S, P}: | lc= The universal affirmative: | q = \forall x | m = \map S x \implies \map P x }} {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf I} {S, P}: | lc= The particular affirmative: | q = \exists x | m = \map S x \land \map P x }} Then: $\map {\mathbf A} {S, P} \implies \map {\mathbf I} {S, P}$ $\exists x: \map S x$ Using the symbology of predicate logic: $\exists x: \map S x \iff \paren {\paren {\forall x: \map S x \implies \map P x} \implies \paren {\exists x: \map S x \land \map P x} }$

title: Universal Approximation Theorem
snippet: Let $I_n$ be the $n$-dimensional unit hypercube $\closedint 0 1^n$. Let $\map C {I_n}$ be the space of continuous functions on $I_n$, equipped with the supremum norm: $\ds \norm f = \sup_{x \mathop \in I_n} \size {\map f x}$ Let $\sigma: \R \to \R$ be a continuous sigmoidal function. That is, $\sigma$ satisfies: $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to -\infty} \map \sigma t = 0$ and: $\ds \lim_{t \mathop \to \infty} \map \sigma t = 1$ Let $S$ be the set of functions $G: I_n \to \R$ of the form: $\ds \map G x = \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^N \alpha_j \map \sigma {y_j^\intercal x + \theta_j}$ where: $N \in \N$ is the…

title: Universal Class is Proper
snippet: Let $V$ denote the universal class. Then $V$ is a proper class.

title: Universal Class less Set is not Transitive
snippet: Let $V$ be a basic universe. Let $a \in V$ be a set. Then: $V \setminus \set a$ is not a transitive class where $\setminus$ denotes class difference.

title: Universal Closures are Semantically Equivalent
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a WFF of predicate logic. Let $\mathbf B, \mathbf B'$ be universal closures of $\mathbf A$. Then $\mathbf B$ and $\mathbf B'$ are semantically equivalent.

title: Universal Cover/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Universal Covers ==

title: Universal Cover is Covering Space for Every Connected Covering Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $C = \struct {X, \phi}$ be a universal cover for $T$. Let $C' = \struct {X', \phi'}$ be an arbitrary connected covering space for $T$. Then $C$ is also a covering space for $C'$.

title: Universal Cover is Unique when it Exists
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let there exist a universal cover $C = \struct {X, \phi}$ for $T$. Then $C$ is unique up to homeomorphism.

title: Universal Morphism from Functor to Object is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\tuple{R_1, u_1}$ and $\tuple{R_2, u_2}$ be a universal morphisms from $F$ to $C$. Then: there exists an isomorphism $i: R_2 \to R_1$ such that $u_2 = u_1 \circ Fi$

title: Universal Morphism from Object to Functor is Unique up to Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ and $\mathbf D$ be metacategories. Let $C$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $F: \mathbf D \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\tuple{R_1, u_1}$ and $\tuple{R_2, u_2}$ be a universal morphisms from $C$ to $F$. Then: there exists an isomorphism $i: R_1 \to R_2$ such that $u_2 = Fi \circ u_1$

title: Universal Negative implies Particular Negative iff First Predicate is not Vacuous
snippet:
Consider the categorical statements: {{axiom | ll = \map {\mathbf E} {S, P}: | lc= The universal negative: | q =  orall x | m = \map S x \implies 
eg \map P x }} {{axiom | ll= \map {\mathbf O} {S, P}: | lc= The particular negative: | q = \exists x | m = \map S x \land 
eg \map P x }} Then: $\map {\mathbf E} {S, P} \implies \map {\mathbf O} {S, P}$ $\exists x: \map S x$ Using the symbology of predicate logic: $\exists x: \map S x \iff \paren {\paren { orall x: \map S x \implies 
eg \map P x} \implies \paren {\exists x: \map S x \land 
eg \map P x} }$

title: Universal Property for Field of Quotients
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain. Let $\struct {F, \oplus, \cdot}$ be a field of quotients of $D$. Then $F$ satisfies the following universal property: There exists a (ring) homomorphism $\iota : D \to F$ such that: for every field $\tilde F$ and and: for every (ring) homomorphism $\phi: D \to \tilde F$ there exists a unique field homomorphism $\psi: F \to \tilde F$ satisfying: $\psi \iota = \phi$ That is, the following diagram commutes: $\xymatrix{ D \ar[r]^{\iota} \ar[dr]_{\phi} & F \ar[d]^{\exists!\psi} \\ {} & {\tilde F} }$ Namely we may take: $\psi: a / b \mapsto \map…

title: Universal Property for Simple Field Extensions
snippet: Let $F / K$ be a field extension. Let $\alpha \in F$ be an algebraic over $K$. Let $\mu_\alpha$ be the minimal polynomial over $\alpha$ over $K$. Let $\psi : K \left({\alpha}\right) \to L$ be a homomorphism. Let $\phi = \psi \restriction_K$. Let $\overline \phi: K \left[{X}\right] \to L \left[{X}\right]$ be the Induced Homomorphism of Polynomial Forms. Then $\psi\left({\alpha}\right)$ is a root of $\overline \phi \left({\mu_\alpha}\right)$ in $L$. Conversely let $L$ be a field. Let $\phi: K \to L$ be a homomorphism. Let $\beta$ be a root of $\overline \phi \left({\mu_\alpha}\right)$ in $L$.

title: Universal Property of Abelianization of Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $G^{\operatorname {ab} }$ be its abelianization. Let $\pi : G \to G^{\operatorname {ab} }$ be the quotient group epimorphism. Let $H$ be an abelian group. Let $f: G \to H$ be a group homomorphism. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $g : G^{\operatorname {ab}} \to H$ such that $g \circ \pi = f$: $\xymatrix { G \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & H\\ G^{\operatorname {ab} } \ar[ru]_{\exists ! g} }$

title: Universal Property of Direct Product of Modules
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Let $\family{M_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of $R$-modules. Let $M = \ds \prod_{i \mathop \in I} M_i$ be their direct product. Let $\family{\psi_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of $R$-module morphisms $N \to M_i$. Then there exists a unique morphism: $\Psi: N \to M$ such that: $\forall i: \psi_i = \pi_i \circ \Psi$ where $\pi_i: M \to M_i$ is the $i$th canonical projection.

title: Universal Property of Direct Sum of Modules
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Let $\family {M_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of $R$-modules. Let $M = \ds \bigoplus_{i \mathop \in I} M_i$ be their direct sum. Let $\family {\psi_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of $R$-module morphisms $M_i \to N$. Then there exists a unique morphism: $\Psi: M \to N$ such that: $\forall i: \psi_i = \Psi \circ \iota_i$ where $\iota_i: M_i \to M$ is the $i$th canonical injection.

title: Universal Property of Field of Rational Fractions
snippet: Let $R$ be an integral domain. Let $\struct {\map R x, \iota, x}$ be the field of rational fractions over $R$. Let $\struct {K, f, a}$ be an ordered triple, where: $K$ is a field $f : R \to K$ is a unital ring homomorphism $a$ is a transcendental element of $K$. Then there exists a unique unital ring homomorphism $\bar f : \map R x \to K$ such that $\bar f \circ \iota = f$ and $\map {\bar f} x = a$: $\xymatrix{ R \ar[d]^\iota \ar[r]^{\forall f} & K\\ \map R x \ar[ru]_{\exists ! \bar f} }$

title: Universal Property of Free Abelian Group on Set
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {\Z^{\paren S}, \iota}$ be the free abelian group on $S$. Let $\struct {G, +}$ be an abelian group. Let $f: S \to G$ be a mapping. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $g : \Z^{\paren S} \to G$ with $g \circ \iota = f$: $\xymatrix{S \ar[d]_\iota \ar[r]^{\forall f} & G\\ \Z^{\paren S} \ar@{-->}[ru]_{\exists ! g} & }$

title: Universal Property of Free Module on Set
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $R^{\paren I}$ be the free $R$-module on $I$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $\family {m_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of $M$. Then there exists a unique $R$-module morphism: $\Psi: R^{\paren I} \to M$ that sends the $i$th canonical basis element to $m_i$, for all $i \in I$. Moreover: $\ds \map \Psi {\family {r_i}_{i \mathop \in I} } = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} r_i m_i$

title: Universal Property of Free Modules
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring. Let $M$ be a free $R$-module with basis $\set {e_i: i\in I}$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Let $\set {n_i: i \in I}$ be a family of elements of $N$. Then there exists a unique $R$-module homomorphism that maps $e_i$ to $n_i$ for all $i\in I$.

title: Universal Property of Group Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $G$ be a group. Let $R \sqbrk G$ be the corresponding group ring. Let $S$ be a commutative ring with unity. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $\beta : G \to S^\times$ be a group homomorphism, where $S^\times$ is the multiplicative group of $S$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism from $R \sqbrk G$ to $S$ which extends $\phi$ and $\beta$.

title: Universal Property of Polynomial Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. The different definitions of a polynomial ring $\struct {\map R x, \iota, x}$ on $R$ satisfy the universal property of a polynomial ring:

title: Universal Property of Quotient Group
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be groups. Let $N \trianglelefteq G$ be an normal subgroup. Let $\pi: G \to G / N$ be the quotient epimorphism. Let $f: G \to H$ be a group homomorphism with $N \subseteq \ker f$. Then there exists a unique group homomorphism $\overline f: G / N \to H$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix{ G \ar[d]^\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & H \\ G/N \ar[ru]_{\exists ! \bar f} }$

title: Universal Property of Quotient Ring
snippet: Let $R, S$ be commutative rings. Let $I \trianglelefteq R$ be an ideal of $R$. Let $\pi : R \to R / I$ be the quotient epimorphism. Let $f: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism with $\map f I = \set 0$. Then there exists a unique ring homomorphism $\overline f: R / I \to S$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix { R \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^{\forall f} & S \\ R/I \ar[ru]_{\exists ! \bar f} }$

title: Universal Property of Quotient Set
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. Let $\pi: X \to X / {\sim}$ be the quotient mapping to the quotient set. Let $f: X \to Y$ be $\sim$-invariant. Then there exists a unique mapping $\overline f : X / {\sim} \to Y$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$. $\xymatrix{ X \ar[d]_\pi \ar[r]^f & Y\\ X/\sim \ar@{.>}[ru]_{\overline f} }$

title: Universal Property of Quotient Space
snippet: Let $X$ and $Y$ be topological spaces. Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on $X$. Let $\pi : X \to X / {\sim}$ be the quotient mapping. Let $f : X \to Y$ be continuous and $\sim$-invariant. Then there exists a unique continuous map $\overline f : X / {\sim} \to Y$ such that $f = \overline f \circ \pi$.

title: Universal Property of Quotient of Topological Group
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ be topological groups. Let $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Let $\pi : G \to G/N$ be the quotient mapping. Let $f : G \to H$ be a continuous group homomorphism whose kernel contains $N$. Then there exists a unique continuous group homomorphism $\overline f: G / N \to H$ such that: $f = \overline f \circ \pi$

title: Universal Quantifier Distributes over Conjunction
snippet: Let $\map \phi x, \map \psi x$ be WFFs of the free variable $x$. Then: $\forall x: \paren {\map \phi x \land \map \psi x} \dashv \vdash \paren {\forall x: \map \phi x} \land \paren {\forall x: \map \psi x}$

title: Universal Quantifier Distributes over Disjunction
snippet: Let $\map \phi x, \map \psi x$ be WFFs of the free variable $x$. Then: $\paren {\forall x: \map \phi x} \lor \paren {\forall x: \map \psi x} \vdash \forall x: \paren {\map \phi x \lor \map \psi x}$

title: Universal Statement/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Universal Statements ==

title: Universal Statement has no Existential Import
snippet: A universal statement of the form: All $A$ are $B$ has no existential import.

title: Universal URM Computable Functions
snippet: For each integer $k \ge 1$, there exists a URM computable function: $\Phi_k: \N^{k+1} \to \N$ such that for each URM computable function $f: \N^k \to \N$ there exists a natural number $e$ such that: $\forall \left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \in \N^k: f \left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \approx \Phi_k \left({e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$. This function $\Phi_k$ is universal for URM computable functions of $k$ variables.

title: Universal URM Programs
snippet: For each integer $k \ge 1$, there exists a URM program $P_k$ such that: For each URM program $P$ there exists a natural number $e$ such that: For all $\left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right) \in \N^k$, the computation using the program $P_k$ with input $\left({e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$ has the same output as the computation using the program $P$ with input $\left({n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k}\right)$. This function $P_k$ is a universal program for URM computations with $k$ inputs.

title: Universal Upper Bound greater than Supremum Operator Norm
snippet:
Let $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ be the continuous linear transformation space. Let $T \in \map {CL} {X, Y}$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}$ be an operator norm on $\map {CL} {X, Y}$ defined as: $
orm T := \sup \set {
orm {Tx}_Y : x \in X : 
orm x_X \le 1}$ Suppose: $\exists M \in \R_{> 0} :  orall x \in X : 
orm {T x}_Y \le M 
orm x_X$ Then: $
orm {T} \le M$

title: Unlike Electric Charges Attract
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be stationary particles, each carrying an electric charge of $q_a$ and $q_b$ respectively. Let $q_a$ and $q_b$ be of the opposite polarity. That is, let $q_a$ and $q_b$ be unlike charges. Then the forces exerted by $a$ on $b$, and by $b$ on $a$, are such as to cause $a$ and $b$ to attract each other.

title: Unordered Pair is Finite
snippet: Let $x, y$ be arbitrary. Then $\set {x, y}$ is finite.

title: Unordered Pairs Exist
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Then: $\forall A, B: \set {A, B} \in U$ where $U$ is the universal class.

title: Unsatisfiable Set Union Formula is Unsatisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi$ be a logical formula. Then $\FF \cup \set \phi$ is also $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable.

title: Unsatisfiable Set minus Tautology is Unsatisfiable
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a logical language. Let $\mathscr M$ be a formal semantics for $\LL$. Let $\FF$ be an $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable set of formulas from $\LL$. Let $\phi \in \FF$ be a tautology. Then $\FF \setminus \set {\phi}$ is also $\mathscr M$-unsatisfiable.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of 0
snippet: $\ds {0 \brack n} = \delta_{0 n}$ where: $\ds {0 \brack n}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\delta_{0 n}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of 1
snippet: $\ds {1 \brack n} = \delta_{1 n}$ where: $\ds {1 \brack n}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\delta_{1 n}$ is the Kronecker delta.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of Number with Greater
snippet: Let $n, k \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Let $k > n$. Let $\ds {n \brack k}$ denote an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind. Then: $\ds {n \brack k} = 0$

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of Number with Self
snippet: $\ds {n \brack n} = 1$ where $\ds {n \brack n}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n+1 with 0
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brack 0} = 0$ where $\ds {n + 1 \brack 0}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n+1 with 1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\ds {n + 1 \brack 1} = n!$ where: $\ds {n + 1 \brack 1}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $n!$ denotes $n$ factorial.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 1}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-2
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 2}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $2$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 2} = \binom n 4 + 2 \binom {n + 1} 4$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 2}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 4$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-3
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 3}$ be an integer greater than or equal to $3$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 3} = \binom n 6 + 8 \binom {n + 1} 6 + 6 \binom {n + 2} 6$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 3}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 6$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Unsymmetric Functional Equation for Riemann Zeta Function
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $\Gamma$ be the gamma function. Then for all $s \in \C$: $\map \zeta {1 - s} = 2^{1 - s} \pi^{-s} \map \cos {\dfrac {\pi s} 2} \map \Gamma s \map \zeta s$

title: Unwarranted Assumptions
snippet: == Fallacy == Let $p$ be a proposition whose truth value is to be proved (either true or false). During the course of a logical argument it is permitted to make an assumption by use of the Rule of Assumption. However, each of the assumptions being made has to be discharged before the proof of $p$ can be considered complete. To fail to discharge all the assumptions is to commit the fallacy of unwarranted assumptions.

title: Up-Complete Lower Bounded Join Semilattice is Complete
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete lower bounded join semillattice. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is complete.

title: Up-Complete Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$, $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ be non-empty ordered sets. Let $\struct {S \times T, \preceq}$ be the simple order product of $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$. Then: $\struct {S \times T, \preceq}$ is up-complete both $\struct {S, \preceq_1}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_2}$ are also up-complete.

title: Upper Adjoint Preserves All Infima
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$, $\left({T, \precsim}\right)$ be ordered sets. Let $g: S \to T$ be an upper adjoint of Galois connection. Then $g$ preserves all infima.

title: Upper Adjoint of Galois Connection is Surjection implies Lower Adjoint at Element is Minimum of Preimage of Singleton of Element
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}, R = \paren {T, \precsim}$ be ordered sets. Let $g: S \to T, d:T \to S$ be mappings such that: $\tuple {g, d}$ is a Galois connection and $g$ is a surjection. Then $\forall t \in T: \map d t = \min \set {g^{-1} \sqbrk {\set t} }$

title: Upper Bound for Abscissa of Absolute Convergence of Product of Dirichlet Series
snippet: Let $f, g: \N \to \C$ be arithmetic functions with Dirichlet convolution $h = f * g$. Let $F, G, H$ be their Dirichlet series. Let $\sigma_f, \sigma_g, \sigma_h$ be their abscissae of absolute convergence. Then: $\sigma_h \le \max \set {\sigma_f, \sigma_g}$

title: Upper Bound for Abundancy Index
snippet: Let $n \in \N_{>0}$ be a non-zero natural number. Let $\map h n$ be the abundancy index of $n$. Then: $\ds \map h n \le \prod_{p \mathop \divides n} \dfrac p {p - 1}$ such that equality holds $n = 1$.

title: Upper Bound for Binomial Coefficient
snippet: Let $n, k \in \Z$ such that $n \ge k \ge 0$. Then: $\dbinom n k \le \left({\dfrac {n e} k}\right)^k$ where $\dbinom n k$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Upper Bound for Harmonic Number
snippet: $H_{2^m} \le 1 + m$ where $H_{2^m}$ denotes the $2^m$th harmonic number.

title: Upper Bound for Lowest Common Multiple
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers such that $a b \ne 0$. Then: $\lcm \set {a, b} \le \size {a b}$ where: $\lcm \set {a, b}$ denotes the lowest common multiple of $a$ and $b$

title: Upper Bound for Lucas Number
snippet: Let $L_n$ denote the $n$th Lucas number. Then: $L_n < \paren {\dfrac 7 4}^n$

title: Upper Bound for Number of Grains of Sand to fill Universe
snippet: The number of grains of sand that would fill the Universe, to the extent it was believed to exist in the days of , is bounded above by $10^{63}$.

title: Upper Bound for Subset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $U$ be an upper bound for $S$. Let $\left({T, \preceq}\right)$ be a subset of $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$. Then $U$ is an upper bound for $T$.

title: Upper Bound is Dual to Lower Bound
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $a \in S$ and $T \subseteq S$. The following are dual statements: $a$ is an upper bound for $T$ $a$ is a lower bound for $T$

title: Upper Bound is Lower Bound for Inverse Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $M$ be an upper bound for $\left({T, \preceq}\right)$. Let $\succeq$ be the dual ordering of $\preceq$. Then $M$ is a lower bound for $\left({T, \succeq}\right)$.

title: Upper Bound is Upper Bound for Subset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $B \subseteq A$ Let $U$ be an upper bound for $A$. Then $U$ is an upper bound for $B$.

title: Upper Bound of Bloch's Constant
snippet: Bloch's constant has an upper bound as follows: $B \le \sqrt {\dfrac {\sqrt 3 -1} 2} \times \dfrac {\map \Gamma {\frac 1 3} \map \Gamma {\frac {11} {12} } } {\map \Gamma {\frac 1 4} }$

title: Upper Bound of Hamming Distance for Length of K-Error-Correcting Code
snippet: Let $C$ be an error-correcting code whose Hamming distance is no less than $2 k + 1$ for some $k \in \N$. Then $C$ is $k$-error-correcting.

title: Upper Bound of Hermite Constant
snippet: Let $\gamma_n$ be the Hermite constant of dimension $n$. Then: $\gamma_n \le \dfrac {\paren {1 + \epsilon_n} n} {\pi e}$ where $e_n \to 0$

title: Upper Bound of Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$ where $x \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\ln x \le x - 1$

title: Upper Bound of Order of Non-Abelian Finite Simple Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a non-abelian finite simple group. Let $t \in G$ be a self-inverse element of $G$. Let $\map {C_G} t$ denote the centralizer of $t$ in $G$. Let $m = \order {\map {C_G} t}$ be the order of $\map {C_G} t$. Then: $\order G \le \paren {\dfrac {m \paren {m + 1} } 2}!$

title: Upper Bound of Ordinal Sum
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be ordinals. Suppose $x > 1$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a finite sequence of ordinals such that: $a_n < x$ for all $n$ Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a strictly decreasing finite sequence of ordinals such that: $b_n < y$ for all $n$ Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n x^{b_i} a_i < x^y$

title: Upper Bound of Pell Number
snippet: For all $n \in \N$: $P_n \le \paren {1 + \sqrt 2}^{n - 1}$ where: $P_n$ is the $n$th Pell number

title: Upper Bounds are Equivalent implies Suprema are equal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$. Assume that $X$ admits a supremum and $\forall x \in S: x$ is upper bound for $X \iff x$ is upper bound for $Y$ Then $\sup X = \sup Y$

title: Upper Bounds for Prime Numbers
snippet: Let $p: \N \to \N$ be the prime enumeration function. Then $\forall n \in \N$, the value of $\map p n$ is bounded above. In particular:

title: Upper Closure in Ordered Subset is Intersection of Subset and Upper Closure
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $\left({T, \precsim}\right)$ be an ordered subset of $L$. Let $t \in T$. Then $t^\succsim = T \cap t^\succeq$

title: Upper Closure is Closure Operator
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T^\succeq$ be the upper closure of $T$ for each $T \subseteq S$. Then $\cdot^\succeq$ is a closure operator.

title: Upper Closure is Compact in Topological Lattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a topological lattice. Suppose that: for every subset $X$ of $S$ if $X$ is open, then $X$ is upper. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\succeq$ is compact where $x^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $x$.

title: Upper Closure is Decreasing
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y$ be elements of $S$ such that $x \preceq y$ then $y^\succeq \subseteq x^\succeq$ where $y^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $y$.

title: Upper Closure is Smallest Containing Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $U = T^\succeq$ be the upper closure of $T$. Then $U$ is the smallest upper section containing $T$ as a subset.

title: Upper Closure is Strict Upper Closure of Immediate Predecessor
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a totally ordered set. Let $b$ be the immediate successor element of $a$: Then: $a^\succ = b^\succcurlyeq$ where: $a^\succ$ is the strict upper closure of $a$ $b^\succcurlyeq$ is the upper closure of $b$.

title: Upper Closure is Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a subset of $S$. Let $U$ be the upper closure of $T$. Then $U$ is an upper section.

title: Upper Closure of Coarser Subset is Subset of Upper Closure
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be a preordered set. Let $A, B$ be subsets of $S$ such that $A$ is coarser than $B$. Then $A^\succeq \subseteq B^\succeq$

title: Upper Closure of Element is Filter
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $s$ be an element of $S$. Then: $s^\succeq$ is a filter in $\struct {S, \preceq}$ where $s^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $s$.

title: Upper Closure of Element is Way Below Open Filter iff Element is Compact
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x \in S$. Then: $x^\succeq$ is a way below open filter on $L$ $x$ is compact

title: Upper Closure of Element without Element is Filter implies Element is Meet Irreducible
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a lattice. Let $x \in S$. Let $x^\succeq \setminus \set x$ be a filter in $L$. Then $x$ is meet irreducible.

title: Upper Closure of Singleton
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $s$ be an element of $S$. Then: $\set s^\succeq = s^\succeq$ where: $\set s^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $\set s$ $s^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $s$

title: Upper Closure of Subset is Subset of Upper Closure
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $X, Y$ be subsets of $S$. Then $X \subseteq Y \implies X^\succeq \subseteq Y^\succeq$ where $X^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $X$.

title: Upper Darboux Integral Never Smaller than Lower Darboux Integral
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a bounded real function. The lower Darboux integral of $f$ over $\closedint a b$ is less than or equal to the upper Darboux integral of $f$ over the same bounds. That is: $\ds \underline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x \le \overline {\int_a^b} \map f x \rd x$

title: Upper Darboux Sum Never Smaller than Lower Darboux Sum
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval of the set $\R$ of real numbers. Let $P = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n - 1}, x_n}$ be a finite subdivision of $\closedint a b$. Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function. Let $f$ be bounded on $\closedint a b$. Let $\map L P$ be the lower Darboux sum of $\map f x$ on $\closedint a b$ belonging to the subdivision $P$. Let $\map U P$ be the upper Darboux sum of $\map f x$ on $\closedint a b$ belonging to the subdivision $P$. Then $\map L P \le \map U P$.

title: Upper Limit of Function is Bounded Below by Value at Limit Point
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a function. Let $\limsup$ be the upper limit. Let $x_0 \in X$. Then we have: $\ds \map f {x_0} \le \limsup_{x \mathop \to x_0} \map f x$

title: Upper Limit of Number of Unit Fractions to express Proper Fraction from Greedy Algorithm
snippet: Let $\dfrac p q$ denote a proper fraction expressed in canonical form. Let $\dfrac p q$ be expressed as the sum of a finite number of distinct unit fractions using Fibonacci's Greedy Algorithm. Then $\dfrac p q$ is expressed using no more than $p$ unit fractions.

title: Upper Section is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be an upper section. Then $T$ is order-convex in $S$.

title: Upper Section with no Minimal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $U \subseteq S$. Then: $U$ is an upper section in $S$ with no minimal element $\ds U = \bigcup \set {u^\succ: u \in U}$ where $u^\succ$ is the strict upper closure of $u$.

title: Upper Section with no Smallest Element is Open in GO-Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a generalized ordered space. Let $U$ be an upper section in $S$ with no smallest element. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$.

title: Upper Sum Never Smaller than Lower Sum for any Pair of Subdivisions
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f$ be a bounded real function defined on $\closedint a b$. Let $P$ and $Q$ be finite subdivisions of $\closedint a b$. Let $\map L P$ be the lower Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to $P$. Let $\map U Q$ be the upper Darboux sum of $f$ on $\closedint a b$ with respect to $Q$. Then $\map L P \le \map U Q$.

title: Upper Sum of Refinement
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed interval. Let $P$ be a finite subdivision of $\closedint a b$. Let $Q$ be a refinement of $P$. Then: $\map U {f, P} \le \map U {f, Q}$ where $\map U {f, P}$ and $\map U {f, Q}$ denote the upper Darboux sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ and $Q$ respectively.

title: Upper Triangular Matrix/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Upper Triangular Matrices ==

title: Upper Triangular Normal Matrix is Diagonal
snippet: A square matrix that is both upper triangular and normal is diagonal.

title: Upper Way Below Open Subset Complement is Non Empty implies There Exists Maximal Element of Complement
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $X$ be upper way below open subset of $S$. Let $x \in S$ such that $x \in \relcomp S X$ Then $\exists m \in S: x \preceq m \land m = \max \relcomp S X$

title: Upper and Lower Bound of Fibonacci Number
snippet: For all $n \in \N_{> 0}$: $\phi^{n - 2} \le F_n \le \phi^{n - 1}$ where: $F_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number $\phi$ is the golden section: $\phi = \dfrac {1 + \sqrt 5} 2$

title: Upper and Lower Closures are Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $a \in S$. Then $a^\succeq$, $a^\succ$, $a^\preceq$, and $a^\prec$ are order-convex in $S$.

title: Upper and Lower Closures of Open Set in GO-Space are Open
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \preceq, \tau}$ be a Generalized Ordered Space/Definition 1. Let $A$ be open in $X$. Then the upper and lower closures of $A$ are open.

title: Upward Löwenheim-Skolem Theorem
snippet: Let $T$ be an $\LL$-theory with an infinite model. Then for each infinite cardinal $\kappa \ge \card \LL$, there exists a model of $T$ with cardinality $\kappa$.

title: Urysohn's Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_4$ topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ be closed sets of $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then there exists an Urysohn function for $A$ and $B$.

title: Urysohn's Lemma Converse
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let there exist an Urysohn function for any two $A, B \subseteq S$ which are closed sets in $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Urysohn's Metrization Theorem
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is regular and second-countable. Then $T$ is metrizable.

title: Urysohn Space is T2.5
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be an Urysohn space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: V Operator on Hilbert Space is Unitary
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space over $\C$. Let $\struct {\HH \times \HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH \times \HH} }$ be the Hilbert space direct sum of $\HH$ with itself. Define $V : \HH \times \HH \to \HH \times \HH$ by: $\map V {x, y} = \tuple {-y, x}$ for each $\tuple {x, y} \in \HH \times \HH$. Then $V : \struct {\HH \times \HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH \times \HH} } \to \struct {\HH \times \HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_{\HH \times \HH} }$ is unitary.

title: Vague Convergence of Uniformly Bounded Sequence of Finite Borel Measures implies Convergence of Integrals of Bounded Continuous Functions Vanishing at Infinity
snippet: Let $M > 0$. Let $\mu$ be a finite Borel measure on $\R$ with $\map \mu \R \le M$. Let $\sequence {\mu_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of finite Borel measures converging vaguely to $\mu$ such that: $\map {\mu_n} \R \le M$ for each $n \in \N$. Let $f : \R \to \R$ be continuous such that: $\ds \lim_{\size x \mathop \to \infty} \map f x = 0$ Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu_n \to \int f \rd \mu$

title: Vajda's Identity
snippet: Let $F_n$ be the $n$th Fibonacci number.

title: Valid Patterns of Categorical Syllogism
snippet: The following categorical syllogisms are valid: $\begin{array}{rl} \text{I} & AAA \\ \text{I} & AII \\ \text{I} & EAE \\ \text{I} & EIO \\ \text{I} & AAI \\ \text{I} & EAO \\ \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{rl} \text{II} & EAE \\ \text{II} & AEE \\ \text{II} & AOO \\ \text{II} & EIO \\ \text{II} & EAO \\ \text{II} & AEO \\ \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{rl} \dagger \text{III} & AAI \\ \text{III} & AII \\ \text{III} & IAI \\ \dagger \text{III} & EAO \\ \text{III} & EIO \\ \text{III} & OAO \\ \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{rl} \S \text{IV} & AAI \\ \text{IV} & AEE \\ \dagger \text{IV} &…

title: Valid Syllogism in Figure III needs Particular Conclusion
snippet: Let $Q$ be a valid categorical syllogism in Figure $\text {III}$. Then the conclusion of $Q$ is a particular categorical statement.

title: Valid Syllogism in Figure II needs Negative Conclusion and Universal Major Premise
snippet: Let $Q$ be a valid categorical syllogism in Figure $\text{II}$. Then it is a necessary condition that: The major premise of $Q$ be a universal categorical statement and The conclusion of $Q$ be a negative categorical statement.

title: Valid Syllogism in Figure I needs Affirmative Minor Premise and Universal Major Premise
snippet: Let $Q$ be a valid categorical syllogism in Figure $\text I$. Then it is a necessary condition that: The major premise of $Q$ be a universal categorical statement and The minor premise of $Q$ be an affirmative categorical statement.

title: Valid Syllogisms in Figure IV
snippet: Let $Q$ be a valid categorical syllogism in Figure $\text {IV}$. Then it is a necessary condition that: $(1): \quad$ Either: the major premise of $Q$ be a negative categorical statement or: the minor premise of $Q$ be a universal categorical statement or both. $(2): \quad$ If the conclusion of $Q$ be a negative categorical statement, then the major premise of $Q$ be a universal categorical statement. $(3): \quad$ If the conclusion of $Q$ be a universal categorical statement, then the minor premise of $Q$ be a negative categorical statement.

title: Valuation Ideal is Maximal Ideal of Induced Valuation Ring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a non-Archimedean normed division ring with zero $0_R$ and unity $1_R$. Let $\OO$ be the valuation ring induced by the non-Archimedean norm $
orm {\,\cdot\,}$, that is: $\OO = \set{x \in R : 
orm x \le 1}$ Let $\PP$ be the valuation ideal induced by the non-Archimedean norm $
orm {\,\cdot\,}$, that is: $\PP = \set{x \in R : 
orm x < 1}$ Then $\PP$ is an ideal of $\OO$: $(a):\quad \PP$ is a maximal left ideal $(b):\quad \PP$ is a maximal right ideal $(c):\quad$ the quotient ring $\OO / \PP$ is a division ring.

orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ is the set: $\PP = p \Z_{\ideal p} = \set {\dfrac a b \in \Q : p 
mid b, p \divides a}$ where $\Z_{\ideal p}$ is the induced valuation ring on $\struct {\Q,
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$

title: Valuation Ideal of P-adic Numbers
snippet:
Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, 
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Then the valuation ideal induced by norm $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ is the principal ideal: $p \Z_p = \set {x \in \Q_p: 
orm x_p < 1}$ where $\Z_p$ denotes the $p$-adic integers.

title: Valuation Ring is Local
snippet: Let $R$ be a valuation ring. Then $R$ is a local ring.

title: Valuation Ring of Non-Archimedean Division Ring is Clopen
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm {\,\cdot\,} }$ be a non-Archimedean normed division ring with zero $0_R$. Let $\OO$ be valuation ring induced by $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$. Then $\OO$ is a both open and closed in the metric induced by $
orm{\,\cdot\,}$.

title: Valuation Ring of Non-Archimedean Division Ring is Subring
snippet:

orm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a non-Archimedean normed division ring with zero $0_R$ and unity $1_R$. Let $\OO$ be the valuation ring induced by the non-Archimedean norm $

orm{x} \le 1}$ Then $\OO$ is a subring of $R$: with a unity: $1_R$ in which there are no (proper) zero divisors, that is: $ orall x, y \in \OO: x \circ y = 0_R \implies x = 0_R 	ext{ or } y = 0_R$

title: Valuation Ring of P-adic Norm is Subring of P-adic Integers
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number. Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the $p$-adic numbers. Let $\Z_p$ be the $p$-adic integers. Let $\Z_{\ideal p}$ be the induced valuation ring on $\struct {\Q,\norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$. Then: $(1): \quad \Z_{\ideal p} = \Q \cap \Z_p$. $(2): \quad \Z_{\ideal p}$ is a subring of $\Z_p$.
