title: Wave Equation is Linear
snippet: Let $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ be particular solutions to the wave equation. Then: $a_1 \phi_1 + a_2 \phi_2$ is also a particular solution to the wave equation.

title: Wave Number of Harmonic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = a \map \cos {\omega \paren {x - c t} }$ The wave number $k$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $k = \dfrac 1 \lambda$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

title: Wave Number of Periodic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a periodic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = \map f {x - c t}$ The wave number $k$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $k = \dfrac 1 \lambda$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of $\phi$.

title: Wave Profile of Harmonic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave which is propagated along the $x$-axis in the positive direction with constant velocity $c$. Then the wave profile of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\paren {\map \phi x}_{t \mathop = 0} = a \cos \omega x$

title: Wavelength of Harmonic Wave
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a harmonic wave expressed as: $\forall x, t \in \R: \map \phi {x, t} = a \map \cos {\omega \paren {x - c t} }$ The wavelength $\lambda$ of $\phi$ can be expressed as: $\lambda = \dfrac {2 \pi} \omega$

title: Way Above Closure is Open
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete continuous topological lattice with Scott topology. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\gg$ is open where $x^\gg$ denotes the way above closure of $x$.

title: Way Above Closure is Subset of Upper Closure of Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then: $x^\gg \subseteq x^\succeq$ where $x^\gg$ denotes the way above closure of $x$ $x^\succeq$ denotes the upper closure of $x$.

title: Way Above Closure is Upper
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\gg$ is upper where $x^\gg$ denotes the way above closure of $x$.

title: Way Above Closures Form Basis
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete continuous topological lattice with Scott topology. Then $\set {x^\gg: x \in S}$ is an (analytic) basis of $L$.

title: Way Above Closures that Way Below Form Local Basis
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \preceq, \tau}$ be a complete continuous topological lattice with Scott topology. Let $p \in S$. Then $\set {q^\gg: q \in S \land q \ll p}$ is a local basis at $p$.

title: Way Below Closure is Directed in Bounded Below Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\ll$ is directed.

title: Way Below Closure is Ideal in Bounded Below Join Semilattice
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\ll$ is ideal in $L$.

title: Way Below Closure is Lower Section
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x \in S$. Then $x^\ll$ is a lower section.

title: Way Below Compact is Topological Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $L = \struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an ordered set where $\preceq \mathop = \subseteq\restriction_{\tau \times \tau}$ Let $x \in \tau$. Then $x$ is compact in $L$ (it means: $x \ll x$) $T_x$ is compact (topologically) where $T_x = \struct {x, \tau_x}$ denotes the topological subspace of $x$.

title: Way Below Relation is Antisymmetric
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ll y$ and $y \ll x$ Then $x = y$

title: Way Below Relation is Auxiliary Relation
snippet: Lrt $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below join semilattice. Then $\ll$ is auxiliary relation where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

title: Way Below Relation is Multiplicative implies Pseudoprime Element is Prime
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous lattice such that $\ll$ is multiplicative relation where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation of $L$. Let $p \in S$. Then $p$ is a pseudoprime element is a prime element.

title: Way Below Relation is Transitive
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y, z \in S$ such that $x \ll y \ll z$ Then $x \ll z$

title: Way Below has Interpolation Property
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Let $x, z \in S$ such that $x \ll z$ Then $\exists y \in S: x \ll y \land y \ll z$

title: Way Below has Strong Interpolation Property
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Let $x, z \in S$ such that $x \ll z \land x \ne z$ Then $\exists y \in S: x \ll y \land y \ll z \land x \ne y$

title: Way Below if Between is Compact Set in Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $L = \struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an ordered set where $\preceq \mathop = \subseteq\restriction_{\tau \times \tau}$ Let $x, y \in \tau$ such that: $\exists H \subseteq S: x \subseteq H \subseteq y \land H$ is compact Then: $x \ll y$

title: Way Below iff Preceding Finite Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall X \subseteq S: y \preceq \sup X \implies \exists A \in \map {\it Fin} X: x \preceq \sup A$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\it Fin} X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

title: Way Below iff Second Operand Preceding Supremum of Directed Set There Exists Element of Directed Set First Operand Way Below Element
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}\right)$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Let $x, y$ be elements of $S$. Then $x \ll y$ for every directed subset $D$ of $S$ such that $y \preceq \sup D$ there exists an element $d$ of $D$: $x \ll d$

title: Way Below iff Second Operand Preceding Supremum of Ideal implies First Operand is Element of Ideal
snippet: Let $\mathscr S = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an up-complete ordered set. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall I \in \map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}: y \preceq \sup I \implies x \in I$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}$ denotes the set of all ideals in $\mathscr S$.

title: Way Below iff Second Operand Preceding Supremum of Prime Ideal implies First Operand is Element of Ideal
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ : for every prime ideal $P$ in $L$: $y \preceq \sup P \implies x \in P$

title: Way Below implies Preceding
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ll y$ where $\ll$ denotes element is way below second element. Then $x \preceq y$

title: Way Below implies There Exists Way Below Open Filter Subset of Way Above Closure
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x \ll y$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation. Then there exists a way below open filter in $L$: $y \in F \land F \subseteq x^\gg$ where $x^\gg$ denotes the way above closure of $x$.

title: Way Below in Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall X \subseteq S: y \preceq \sup X \implies \exists A \in \map {\operatorname {Fin} } X: x \preceq \sup A$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\operatorname {Fin} } X$ denotes the set of all finite subsets of $X$.

title: Way Below in Lattice of Power Set
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $L = \struct {\powerset X, \cup, \cap, \preceq}$ be a lattice of power set of $X$ where $\mathord\preceq = \mathord\subseteq \cap \paren {\powerset X \times \powerset X}$ Let $x, y \in \powerset X$. Then $x \ll y$ for every a set $Y$ of subsets of $X$ such that $y \subseteq \bigcup Y$ then there exists a finite subset $Z$ of $Y$: $x \subseteq \bigcup Z$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

title: Way Below in Meet-Continuous Lattice
snippet: Let $\mathscr S = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a meet-continuous bounded below lattice. Let $x, y \in S$. Then $x \ll y$ $\forall I \in \map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}: y = \sup I \implies x \in I$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation, $\map {\operatorname {Ids} } {\mathscr S}$ denotes the set of all ideals in $\mathscr S$.

title: Way Below in Ordered Set of Topology
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {\tau, \preceq}$ be an ordered set where $\preceq \mathop = \subseteq \restriction_{\tau \times \tau}$ Let $x, y \in \tau$. Then: $x \ll y$ in $\struct {\tau, \preceq}$ for every set $F$ of open subsets of $S$: if $y \subseteq \bigcup F$, then: there exists a finite subset $G$ of $F$: $x \subseteq \bigcup G$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

title: Way Below is Approximating Relation
snippet: Let $L = \struct {S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a bounded below continuous lattice. Then $\ll$ is an approximating relation on $S$.

title: Way Below is Congruent for Join
snippet: Let $L = \left({S, \vee, \preceq}\right)$ be a join semilattice. Then $\ll$ is congruence relation for $\vee$: $\forall a, b, x, y \in S: a \ll x \land b \ll y \implies a \vee b \ll x \vee y$ where $\ll$ denotes the way below relation.

title: Weak-* Closed Linear Subspace of Normed Dual Space is Isometrically Isomorphic to a Normed Dual Space
snippet: Let $X$ be a Banach space. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Let $Y$ be a linear subspace of $X^\ast$ closed in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$. Then there exists a normed vector space $Z$ such that: $Y$ is isometrically isomorphic to $Z^\ast$.

title: Weak-* Closure of Isometric Copy of Set in Second Dual contains Isometric Copy of Weak Closure of Set in Original Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $S \subseteq X$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\cl_w$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X, w}$. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the second normed dual of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^{\ast \ast}$. Let $\cl_{w^\ast}$ be the closure taken in $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, w^\ast}$. Let $\iota : X 	o X^{\ast \ast}$ be the evaluation linear transformation.

title: Weak-* Compact Set in Normed Dual Space of Separable Normed Vector Space is Weak-* Metrizable
snippet: Let $X$ be a separable normed vector space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \in \N}$ be a countable everywhere dense subset of $X$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X$. Let $\struct {K, w^\ast}$ be a compact subspace of $X^\ast$. Define $d : X^\ast \times X^\ast \to \R$ by: $\ds \map d {f, g} = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {2^n} \min \set {\norm {\map f {x_n} - \map g {x_n} }_X, 1}$ for each $f, g \in X^\ast$. From Initial Topology Generated by Countable Family of Functions Separating Points is Metrizable, this is a metric.

title: Weak-* Dense Subset of Normed Dual Space Separates Points
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the normed dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Let $D$ be everywhere dense in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$. Then $D$ separates points.

title: Weak-* Limit in Normed Dual Space is Unique
snippet:
Let $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm \cdot_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space for $\struct {X, 
orm \cdot}$. Let $f, g \in X^\ast$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X^\ast$ such that: $f_n \weakstarconv f$ and: $f_n \weakstarconv g$ where $\weakstarconv$ denotes weak-$\ast$ convergence. Then: $f = g$

title: Weak-* Metrizability of Closed Unit Ball in Normed Dual of Normed Vector Space implies Original Space is Separable
snippet: Let $X$ be a normed vector space such that: $\struct {B_{X^\ast}^-, w^\ast}$ is metrizable where $X^\ast$ is the normed dual of $X$ and $B_{X^\ast}^-$ is the closed unit ball of $X^\ast$. Then $X$ is separable.

title: Weak-* Open Set in Normed Dual Space is Open
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be a weak-$\ast$ topology on $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$. Let $U$ be an open set in $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$.

title: Weak-* Topology and Norm Topology Coincide on Norm Compact Subsets of Normed Dual Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$. Let $\struct {K, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ with $K \subseteq X^\ast$ be compact. Then the open sets of $\struct {K, w^\ast}$ and $\struct {K, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ coincide.

title: Weak-* Topology is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Then $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ is Hausdorff space.

title: Weak-* Unconditionally Convergent Series in Second Dual of Banach Space is Weakly Unconditional Cauchy in Original Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$. Let $\struct {X^{\ast \ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast \ast} } }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X^{\ast \ast}, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^{\ast \ast} } }$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology.

title: Weak Closure of Unit Sphere is Closed Unit Ball
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be an infinite-dimensional normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\cl_w$ be the topological closure in $\struct {X, w}$. Let: $S_X^- = \set {x \in X : 
orm x_X = 1}$ Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$. Then $\map {\cl_w} {S_X} = B_X^-$.

title: Weak Cluster Point of Basic Sequence in Banach Space is Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a basic sequence. Let $x$ be a cluster point of $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $x = {\mathbf 0}_X$.

title: Weak Compactness is Equivalent to Norm Compactness in Schur Space
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space that is a Schur space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $K \subseteq X$. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is compact $\struct {K, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ is compact.

title: Weak Convergence in Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\HH$. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to $x$ $\innerprod {x_n} y \to \innerprod x y$ for each $y \in \HH$.

title: Weak Convergence in Normed Dual Space of Reflexive Normed Vector Space is Equivalent to Weak-* Convergence
snippet:
Let $\mathbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a reflexive normed vector space over $\mathbb F$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $f \in X^\ast$. Then: $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to $f$ $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly-$\ast$ to $f$.

title: Weak Countable Compactness is not Preserved under Continuous Maps
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ be a topological space which is weakly countably compact. Let $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be another topological space. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous mapping. Then $T_B$ is not necessarily weakly countably compact.

title: Weak Existence of Matrix Logarithm
snippet: Let $T$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $\norm {T - I} < 1$ in the norm on bounded linear operators, where $I$ the identity matrix. Then there is a square matrix $S$ such that: $e^S = T$ where $e^S$ is the matrix exponential.

title: Weak Inequality of Integers iff Strict Inequality with Integer plus One
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers. $(1): \quad a \le b$ $(2): \quad a < b + 1$ where: $\le$ is the ordering on the integers $<$ is the strict ordering on the integers.

title: Weak Limit in Normed Vector Space is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm \cdot}$ be a normed vector space. Let $x, y \in X$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X$ such that: $x_n \weakconv x$ and: $x_n \weakconv y$ where $\weakconv$ denotes weak convergence. Then: $x = y$

title: Weak Local Compactness is Preserved under Open Continuous Surjection
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a continuous mapping which is also an open mapping and a surjection. If $T_A$ is weakly locally compact, then $T_B$ is also weakly locally compact.

title: Weak Lower Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preccurlyeq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preccurlyeq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\preccurlyeq T} = T \cap t^{\preccurlyeq S}$ where: $t^{\preccurlyeq T}$ is the weak lower closure of $t$ in $\left({T, \preccurlyeq \restriction_T}\right)$ $t^{\preccurlyeq S}$ is the weak lower closure of $t$ in $\left({S, \preccurlyeq}\right)$.

title: Weak Nullstellensatz
snippet: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $n \ge 0$ be an natural number. Let $K \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $I \subseteq K \sqbrk {x_1,\ldots, x_n}$ be an ideal. $I$ is the unit ideal: $I = (1)$. Its zero-locus is empty set: $\map V I = \O$.

title: Weak Solution/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Weak Solutions ==

title: Weak Solution to Dx u + 3yu = 0 with Heaviside Step Function Boundary Condition
snippet: Consider the boundary value problem: $\begin{cases} \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} + 3 y u = 0 & : x \in \R_{>0},~ y \in \R \\ & \\ \map u {0, y} = \map H y & : y \in \R \\ \end{cases}$ Then it has a weak solution of the form: $u = e^{-3 y x} \map H y$

title: Weak Solution to Dx u = Heaviside Step Function
snippet: Let $H: \R \to \closedint 0 1$ be the Heaviside step function. Let $u : \R \to \R$ be such that: $\map u x = \begin{cases} c & : x 0 \end{cases}$ where $c \in \R$. Let $T_u$ be the Schwartz distribution associated with $u$. Then $u$ is a weak solution of: $u' = H$ That is, in the distributional sense it holds that: $\dfrac \d {\d x} T_u = T_H$

title: Weak Solution to Dx u = u
snippet: $\map u {x, t} = \map H t e^x$ Let $H$ be the Heaviside step function. Let $\map u {x, t} = \map H t e^x$ Then $u$ is a weak solution of the partial differential equation $\ds \dfrac {\partial u} {\partial x} = u$. That is, for the Schwartz distribution $T_u \in \map {\DD'} {\R^2}$ associated with $u$ in the distributional sense it holds that: $\ds \dfrac {\partial T_u} {\partial x} = T_u$

title: Weak Topology and Norm Topology on Normed Vector Space Coincide iff Finite Dimensional
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $d$ be the metric induced on $X$ by $\norm {\, \cdot \,}$. Let $\tau$ be the topology on $X$ induced by $d$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Then $\tau = w$ $X$ is finite-dimensional.

title: Weak Topology and Original Topology Coincide on Originally Compact Subsets of Hausdorff Topological Vector Space
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff topological vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Let $\struct {K, \tau}$ be compact. Let $U \subseteq X$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {K, \tau}$ $U$ is open in $\struct {K, w}$.

title: Weak Topology on Infinite Dimensional Normed Vector Space is not Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be an infinite dimensional normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Then $w$ is not metrizable.

title: Weak Topology on Topological Vector Space over Hausdorff Topological Field is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $K$ be a Hausdorff topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$ with weak topology $w$. Then $\struct {X, w}$ is Hausdorff.

title: Weak Topology on Transpose Dual System is Weak-* Topology on Original System
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$ be a dual system over $\GF$. Let $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$ be the transpose of $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$. Let $\tau_1$ be the weak topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod F E_{F \times E}$. Let $\tau_2$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $F$ induced by $\innerprod E F_{E \times F}$. Then $\tau_1 = \tau_2$. Hence, we can use the notation $\map \sigma {F, E}$ for both topologies without confusion.

title: Weak Upper Closure in Restricted Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preccurlyeq \restriction_T$ be the restricted ordering on $T$. Then for all $t \in T$: $t^{\succcurlyeq T} = T \cap t^{\succcurlyeq S}$ where: $t^{\succcurlyeq T}$ is the weak upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {T, \preccurlyeq \restriction_T}$ $t^{\succcurlyeq S}$ is the weak upper closure of $t$ in $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$.

title: Weak Whitney Immersion Theorem
snippet: Every $k$-dimensional manifold $X$ admits a one-to-one immersion in $\R^{2 k + 1}$.

title: Weakly Cauchy Sequence in Normed Vector Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a weak Cauchy sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is bounded.

title: Weakly Compact Set in Banach Space is Angelic
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is angelic.

title: Weakly Compact Set in Banach Space whose Normed Dual is Weak-* Separable is Weakly Metrizable
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact with $K \subseteq X$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Suppose that $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ is separable. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

title: Weakly Compact Set in P-Sequence Space is Weakly Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$. Let $K \subseteq \map {\ell_p} \GF$ be weakly compact. Then $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

title: Weakly Compact Set in Separable Banach Space is Weakly Metrizable
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a separable Banach space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ be compact with $K \subseteq X$. Let $\struct {K, w}$ is metrizable.

title: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Hilbert Space with Convergent Norm is Convergent
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a Hilbert space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\HH$. Let $x \in X$ be such that: $x_n \weakconv x$ and: $\norm {x_n} \to \norm x$ where $\weakconv$ denotes weak convergence. Then: $x_n \to x$

title: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Normed Dual Space is Weakly-* Convergent
snippet:
Let $\mathbb F$ be a subfield of $\C$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\mathbb F$. Let $\struct {X^\ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_{X^\ast} }$ be the normed dual space of $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $f \in X^\ast$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $X^\ast$ converging weakly to $f$. Then $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly-$\ast$ to $f$.

title: Weakly Convergent Sequence in Normed Vector Space is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a weakly convergent sequence in $X$. Then $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is bounded.

title: Weakly Countably Compact Set in Normed Vector Space is Norm Bounded
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$. Let $C \subseteq X$ be $w$-countably compact. Then: $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in S} 
orm x_X < \infty$ Hence $C$ is bounded.

title: Weakly Countably Compact Space is not necessarily Countably Compact
snippet: A weakly countably compact topological space is not also necessarily a countably compact space.

title: Weakly Lindelöf Space with Sigma-Locally Finite Basis is Second-Countable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly Lindelöf topological space. Let $\BB$ be a $\sigma$-locally finite basis of $T$. Then $T$ is second-countable.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Hausdorff Space is Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $T$ be weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is strongly locally compact.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Metrizable Space is Completely Metrizable
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly locally compact topological space. Let $T$ also be a metrizable space. Then $T$ is completely metrizable.

title: Weakly Locally Compact R1 Space is T3.5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an $R_1$ space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Space is K1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a $k_1$-space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Lindelöf
snippet: A weakly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a Lindelöf space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Sigma-Compact
snippet: A weakly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a $\sigma$-compact space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: A weakly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a strongly locally compact space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact
snippet: A weakly locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact T2 Space is Completely Regular
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a completely regular space.

title: Weakly Locally Compact T2 Space is T3.5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly locally compact. Then $T$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Weakly Null Sequence in Normed Vector Space Multiplied by Bounded Sequence is Weakly Null
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ that converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Let $\sequence {\lambda_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a bounded sequence in $\GF$. Then $\sequence {\lambda_n x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_X$.

title: Weakly Null Sequence in P-Sequence Space is Pointwise Vanishing
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $p \in \closedint 1 \infty$. Let $\struct {\map {\ell_p} \GF, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_p}$ be the $p$-sequence space. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence in $\map {\ell_p} \GF$ that converges weakly to ${\mathbf 0}_{\ell_p}$. Then: $\map {x_n} j \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, for each $j \in \N$.

title: Weakly Open Neighborhood of Zero Vector in Infinite-Dimensional Topological Vector Space contains Infinite-Dimensional Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be an infinite-dimensional topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $w$ be the weak topology of $\struct {X, \tau}$. Let $U$ be an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$ in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $U$ contains an infinite-dimensional vector subspace. In particular, $U$ contains a vector subspace of finite codimension.

title: Weakly Open Set in Hausdorff Topological Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$ with weak topology $w$. Let $U$ be an open set in $\struct {X, w}$. Then $U$ is open in $\struct {X, \tau}$.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact Space is Hemicompact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact space. Then $T$ is a hemicompact space.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact Space is Weakly Locally Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a weakly $\sigma$-locally compact space. Then $T$ is weakly locally compact.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Compact
snippet: A weakly $\sigma$-locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a compact space.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact Space is not necessarily Strongly Locally Compact
snippet: A weakly $\sigma$-locally compact topological space is not necessarily also a strongly locally compact space.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact T2 Space is Normal
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact. Then $T$ is a normal space.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact T2 Space is T4
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space which is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact. Then $T$ is a $T_4$ space.

title: Weakly Sigma-Locally Compact iff Weakly Locally Compact and Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $(1): \quad T$ is weakly $\sigma$-locally compact $(2): \quad T$ is weakly locally compact and Lindelöf

title: Wedderburn's Theorem
snippet: Every finite division ring $D$ is a field.

title: Weierstrass's Elliptic Function is Doubly Periodic
snippet: Weierstrass's elliptic function $\map \wp {z; \omega_1, \omega_2}$ is doubly periodic in $2 \omega_1$ and $2 \omega_2$.

title: Weierstrass's Elliptic Function is Even in z
snippet: Let $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ be non-zero complex constants with $\dfrac {\omega_1} {\omega_2}$ having a positive imaginary part. For $z \in \C \setminus \set {2 m \omega_1 + 2 n \omega_2: \tuple {n, m} \in \Z^2}$: $\ds \map \wp {-z; \omega_1, \omega_2} = \map \wp {z; \omega_1, \omega_2}$ That is, Weierstrass's elliptic function is even in $z$.

title: Weierstrass's Necessary Condition
snippet: Let $\mathbf y: \R \to \R^n$ be an $n$-dimensional vector-valued function such that $\map {\mathbf y} a = A$ and $\map {\mathbf y} b = B$. Let $J$ be a functional such that: $\ds J \sqbrk {\mathbf y} = \int_a^b \map F {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf y'} \rd x$ Let $\mathbf w$ be an $n$-dimensional vector such that $\mathbf w \in \R^n$. Let $\gamma$ be a strong minimum of $J$. Then along $\gamma$ and for every $\mathbf w$: $\map E {x, \mathbf y, \mathbf y', \mathbf w} \ge 0$ where $E$ stands for the Weierstrass E-Function.

title: Weierstrass's Theorem
snippet: There exists a real function $f: \closedint 0 1 \to \closedint 0 1$ such that: $(1): \quad f$ is continuous $(2): \quad f$ is nowhere differentiable.

title: Weierstrass-Casorati Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a holomorphic function defined on the open ball $\map B {a, r} \setminus \set a$. Let $f$ have an essential singularity at $a$. Then: $\forall s < r: f \sqbrk {\map B {a, s} \setminus \set a}$ is a dense subset of $\C$.

title: Weierstrass Approximation Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\Bbb I = \closedint a b$. Then $f$ can be uniformly approximated on $\Bbb I$ by a polynomial function to any given degree of accuracy.

title: Weierstrass Extreme Value Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous in a closed real interval $\closedint a b$. Then: $\exists x_M: \forall x \in \closedint a b: \map f {x_M} \ge \map f x$ $\exists x_m: \forall x \in \closedint a b: \map f {x_m} \le \map f x$

title: Weierstrass Factorization Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be an entire function. Let $0$ be a zero of $f$ of multiplicity $m \ge 0$. Let the sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ consist of the nonzero zeroes of $f$, repeated according to multiplicity.

title: Weierstrass Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $a \in \openint 0 1$. Let $b$ be a strictly positive odd integer such that: $\ds a b > 1 + \frac 3 2 \pi$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be a real function defined by: $\ds \map f x = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty a^n \map \cos {b^n \pi x}$ for each $x \in \R$. Then $f$ is well-defined and continuous.

title: Weierstrass M-Test
snippet: Let $f_n$ be a sequence of real functions defined on a domain $D \subseteq \R$. Let $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in D} \size {\map {f_n} x} \le M_n$ for each integer $n$ and some constants $M_n$ Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty M_i < \infty$. Then $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty f_i$ converges uniformly on $D$.

title: Weierstrass Product Inequality
snippet: For $n \ge 1$: $\ds \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \paren {1 - a_i} \ge 1 - \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n a_i$ where all of $a_i$ are in the closed interval $\closedint 0 1$.

title: Weierstrass Product Theorem
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_k}$ be a sequence of non-zero complex numbers such that: $\cmod {a_n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ Let $\sequence {p_n}$ be a sequence of non-negative integers for which the series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \size {\dfrac r {a_n} }^{1 + p_n}$ converges for every $r \in \R_{> 0}$. Let: $\ds \map f z = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {E_{p_n} } {\frac z {a_n} }$ where $E_{p_n}$ are Weierstrass elementary factors. Then $f$ is entire and its zeroes are the points $a_n$, counted with multiplicity.

title: Weight of Body at Earth's Surface
snippet: Let $B$ be a body of mass $m$ situated at (or near) the surface of Earth. Then the weight of $B$ is given by: $W = m g$ where $g$ is the value of the acceleration due to gravity at the surface of Earth.

title: Weight of Discrete Topology equals Cardinality of Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a discrete topological space. Then: $\map w T = \size S$ where: $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$ $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

title: Weight of Sorgenfrey Line is Continuum
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\R, \tau}$ be the Sorgenfrey line. Then $\map w T = \mathfrak c$ where $\map w T$ denotes the weight of $T$ $\mathfrak c$ denotes continuum, the cardinality of real numbers.

title: Well-Defined Jordan Content Equals Content
snippet: Let $M$ be a bounded subspace of Euclidean space. Let the Jordan content of $M$ be $\map m M$. Then the content $\map V M = \map m M$.

title: Well-Defined Mapping/Motivation
snippet: == Motivation for Well-Defined Mapping == Suppose we are given a mapping $f: S \to T$. Suppose we have an equivalence $\RR$ on $S$, and we want to define a mapping on the quotient set: $\phi: S / \RR \to T$ such that: $\map \phi {\eqclass \cdots \RR} = \map f \cdots$ That is, we want every element of a given equivalence class to map to the same element of the codomain of $f$. The only way this can be done is to set $\map \phi {\eqclass x \RR} = \map f x$.

title: Well-Defined Relation/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Well-Defined Relations ==

title: Well-Founded Induction
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \RR}$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Let $\RR^{-1} \sqbrk x$ denote the preimage of $x$ for each $x \in A$. Let $B$ be a class such that $B \subseteq A$. Suppose that: $(1): \quad \forall x \in A: \paren {\RR^{-1} \sqbrk x \subseteq B \implies x \in B}$ Then: $A = B$ That is, if a property passes from the preimage of $x$ to $x$, then this property is true for all $x \in A$.

title: Well-Founded Proper Relational Structure Determines Minimal Elements
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\struct {A, \prec}$ be a proper relational structure. Let $\prec$ be a strictly well-founded relation. Suppose $B \subset A$ and $B \ne \O$. Then $B$ has a strictly minimal element under $\prec$.

title: Well-Founded Recursion
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\RR$ be a relation that is strictly well-founded on $A$. Let every $\RR$-initial segment of any element $x$ of $A$ be a small class. Let $G$ be a (class) mapping from $A^A$ to $A$. Let $K$ be a class of mappings $f$ that satisfy: $(1): \quad$ The domain of $f$ is some subset $y \subseteq A$ such that $y$ is transitive with respect to $\RR$. $(2): \quad \forall x \in y: \map f x = \map G {f \restriction \RR^{-1} x}$ where $f \restriction R^{-1} x$ denotes the restriction of $f$ to the $\RR$-initial segment of $x$. Let $F = \bigcup K$, the union of $K$.

title: Well-Founded Relation has no Relational Loops
snippet: Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in S$. Then: $\neg \paren {\paren {x_1 \mathrel \RR x_2} \land \paren {x_3 \mathrel \RR x_4} \land \cdots \land \paren {x_n \mathrel \RR x_1} }$ That is, there are no relational loops within $S$.

title: Well-Founded Relation is not necessarily Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Let $\RR$ be a well-founded relation on $S$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\RR$ is also either an ordering or a strict ordering.

title: Well-Orderable Set has Choice Function
snippet: Let $S$ be a well-orderable set. Then $S$ has a choice function.

title: Well-Ordered Class is not Isomorphic to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered class. There exists no order isomorphism from $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ to an initial segment of $A$.

title: Well-Ordered Classes are Isomorphic at Most Uniquely
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq_A}$ and $\struct {B, \preccurlyeq_B}$ be well-ordered classes. Then there exists at most one order isomorphism from $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq_A}$ to $\struct {B, \preccurlyeq_B}$

title: Well-Ordered Induction
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \prec}$ be a strict well-ordering. For all $x \in A$, let the $\prec$-initial segment of $x$ be a small class. Let $B$ be a class such that $B \subseteq A$. Let: $(1): \quad \forall x \in A: \paren {\paren {A \mathop \cap \map {\prec^{-1} } x} \subseteq B \implies x \in B}$ Then: $A = B$ That is, if a property passes from the initial segment of $x$ to $x$, then this property is true for all $x \in A$.

title: Well-Ordered Transitive Subset is Equal or Equal to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\struct {\prec, A}$ be a well-ordered set. For every $x \in A$, let every $\prec$-initial segment $A_x$ be a set. Let $B$ be a subclass of $A$ such that $\forall x \in A: \forall y \in B: \paren {x \prec y \implies x \in B}$. That is, $B$ must be $\prec$-transitive. Then: $A = B$ or: $\exists x \in A: B = A_x$

title: Well-Ordering Minimal Elements are Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S,\preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Then every non-empty subset of $S$ has a unique minimal element.

title: Well-Ordering Principle
snippet: Every non-empty subset of $\N$ has a smallest (or first) element. That is, the relational structure $\struct {\N, \le}$ on the set of natural numbers $\N$ under the usual ordering $\le$ forms a well-ordered set. This is called the well-ordering principle.

title: Well-Ordering is not necessarily Usual Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set of numbers. According to Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem, $S$ can be well-ordered. However, the usual ordering on $S$ may not necessarily be a well-ordering.

title: Well-Ordering on Class is not necessarily Proper
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Let $\preccurlyeq$ be a well-ordering on $A$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $\preccurlyeq$ is a proper well-ordering.

title: Well-Ordering on Set is Proper Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered set. Then $\preccurlyeq$ is a proper well-ordering.

title: Well Inside Elements Form Filter
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive lattice with greatest element $\top$ and smallest element $\bot$. Let $\eqslantless$ denote the well inside relation on $L$. Then: $\forall a \in S : \set{b \in S: a \eqslantless b}$ is a lattice filter

title: Well Inside Implies Predecessor
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive lattice with greatest element $\top$ and smallest element $\bot$. Let $\eqslantless$ denote the well inside relation on $L$. Then: $\forall a,b \in S : a \eqslantless b \implies a \preceq b$

title: Well Inside Relation Extends to Predecessor and Successor
snippet: Let $L = \struct{S, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a distributive lattice with greatest element $\top$ and smallest element $\bot$. Let $\eqslantless$ denote the well inside relation on $L$. Then: $\forall a,b,c,d \in S : a \preceq b \eqslantless c \preceq d \implies a \eqslantless d$

title: Westwood's Puzzle
snippet: 500px Take any rectangle $ABCD$ and draw the diagonal $AC$. Inscribe a circle $GFJ$ in one of the resulting triangles $\triangle ABC$. Drop perpendiculars $IEF$ and $HEJ$ from the center of this incircle $E$ to the sides of the rectangle. Then the area of the rectangle $DHEI$ equals half the area of the rectangle $ABCD$.

title: Weyl Group Permutes Root System
snippet: Let $\struct {E, \Phi}$ be a root system with Weyl group $\mathscr W$. Then $\mathscr W$ permutes $\Phi$.

title: Wheat and Chessboard Problem
snippet: == Classic Problem == The squares of a chessboard are numbered in some way, from $1$st to $64$th. A grain of wheat is placed on the $1$st squares of the chessboard. $2$ grains of wheat are placed on the $2$nd square. $4$ grains of wheat are placed on the $3$rd square. The sequence continues: on the $n$th square, twice as many grains of wheat are placed as there are on the $n - 1$th square. How much wheat is there on the chessboard when the $64$th square has been filled?

title: Whitney Embedding Theorem
snippet: Every smooth $m$-dimensional manifold admits a smooth embedding into Euclidean space $\R^{2 m}$.

title: Whitney Immersion Theorem
snippet: Let $m > 1$ be a natural number. Every smooth $m$-dimensional manifold can be immersed in Euclidean $\paren {2 m - 1}$-space.

title: Who Drinks Hotter Coffee?
snippet: == Problem == Pinky and Perky both order coffee, and receive cups of it at the same temperature at the same time. Pinky adds a small quantity of cool milk immediately, but does not drink his coffee immediately. Perky waits some time before adding exactly the same quantity of milk of the same temperature as that which Pinky added. Both Pinky and Perky then drink their coffee at the same time. Who drinks the hotter coffee?

title: Whole Sample Space represents Certain Event
snippet: Let the probability space of an experiment $\EE$ be $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. The sample space $\Sigma$ represents an event which is certain.

title: Whole Space is Open in Neighborhood Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \NN}$ be a neighborhood space. Then $S$ itself is an open set of $\struct {S, \NN}$.

title: Wholly Real Number and Wholly Imaginary Number are Linearly Independent over the Rationals
snippet: Let $z_1$ be a non-zero wholly real number. Let $z_2$ be a non-zero wholly imaginary number. Then, $z_1$ and $z_2$ are linearly independent over the rational numbers $\Q$, where the group is the complex numbers $\C$.

title: Wieferich's Criterion
snippet: Suppose Fermat's equation: $x^p + y^p = z^p$ has a solution in which $p$ is an odd prime that does not divide any of $x$, $y$ or $z$. Then $2^{p - 1} - 1$ is divisible by $p^2$.

title: Wilson's Theorem
snippet: A (strictly) positive integer $p$ is a prime : $\paren {p - 1}! \equiv -1 \pmod p$

title: Wolstenholme's Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Suppose that: $\dbinom {2 n - 1} {n - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod {n^3}$ where $\dbinom {2 n - 1} {n - 1}$ denotes a binomial coefficient. Then $n$ is a prime number

title: Wolstenholme's Theorem
snippet: Let $p$ be a prime number such that $p \ge 5$. Then: $\dbinom {2 p - 1} {p - 1} \equiv 1 \pmod {p^3}$ where $\dbinom {2 p - 1} {p - 1}$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Word Metric is Metric
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $S$ be a generating set for $G$ which is closed under inverses (that is, $x^{-1} \in S \iff x \in S$). Let $d_S$ be the associated word metric. Then $d_S$ is a metric on $G$.

title: Woset is Isomorphic to Set of its Initial Segments
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Let: $A = \set {a^\prec: a \in S}$ where $a^\prec$ is the strict lower closure of $S$ determined by $a$. Then: $\struct {S, \preceq} \cong \struct {A, \subseteq}$ where $\cong$ denotes order isomorphism.

title: Wosets are Isomorphic to Each Other or Initial Segments
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ and $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ be well-ordered sets. Then precisely one of the following hold: $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ is order isomorphic to $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ or: $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$ is order isomorphic to an initial segment in $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ or: $\struct {T, \preceq_T}$ is order isomorphic to an initial segment in $\struct {S, \preceq_S}$

title: Wronskian of Linearly Dependent Mappings is Zero
snippet: Let $\map {f_1} x, \map {f_2} x, \dotsc, \map {f_n} x$ be real functions defined on a closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n$ be $n - 1$ times differentiable on $\closedint a b$. Then: $\map W x = 0$ there exists a subinterval of $\closedint a b$ on which $f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n$ are linearly dependent.

title: Wythoff Pairs are Winning Positions in Wythoff's Game
snippet: The Wythoff pairs are the winning positions in Wythoff's game.

title: X + y + z equals 1 implies xy + yz + zx less than Half
snippet: Let $x$, $y$ and $z$ be real numbers such that: $x + y + z = 1$ Then: $x y + y z + z x < \dfrac 1 2$

title: X Choose n leq y Choose n + z Choose n-1 where n leq y leq x leq y+1 and n-1 leq z leq y
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $x, y \in \R$ be real numbers which satisfy: $n \le y \le x \le y + 1$ Let $z$ be the unique real number $z$ such that: $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$ where $n - 1 \le z \le y$. Its uniqueness is proved at Uniqueness of Real $z$ such that $\dbinom x {n + 1} = \dbinom y {n + 1} + \dbinom z n$. Then: $\dbinom x n \le \dbinom y n + \dbinom z {n - 1}$

title: X to the x is not of Exponential Order
snippet: Let $f: \R_{>0} \to \R$ be definedas: $\forall x \in \R_{>0}: \map f x = x^x$. Then: $f$ is not of exponential order. That is, it grows faster than any exponential.

title: Y'-independent Euler's Equation

orm {\, \cdot \,}_p$, $

title: Young's Inequality for Increasing Functions
snippet: Let $a_0$ and $b_0$ be strictly positive real numbers. Let $f: \closedint 0 {a_0} \to \closedint 0 {b_0}$ be a strictly increasing bijection. Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers such that $0 \le a \le a_0$ and $0 \le b \le b_0$. Then: $\ds ab \le \int_0^a \map f u \rd u + \int_0^b \map {f^{-1} } v \rd v$ where $\ds \int$ denotes the definite integral.

title: Young's Inequality for Products
snippet: Let $p, q \in \R_{> 0}$ be strictly positive real numbers such that: $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$ Then: $\forall a, b \in \R_{\ge 0}: a b \le \dfrac {a^p} p + \dfrac {b^q} q$ Equality occurs : $b = a^{p - 1}$

title: Yule-Simpson Effect
snippet: The Yule-Simpson Effect is a veridical paradox in the theory of contingency tables. An association that is significant in each of two contingency tables may disappear or be reversed if the two tables are combined.

title: Z-Module Associated with Abelian Group is Unitary Z-Module
snippet: Let $\struct {G, *}$ be an abelian group with identity $e$. Let $\struct {G, *, \circ}_\Z$ be the $Z$-module associated with $G$. Then $\struct {G, *, \circ}_\Z$ is a unitary $Z$-module.

title: Z/(m)-Module Associated with Ring of Characteristic m
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, *}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let the characteristic of $R$ be $m$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m, \times_m}$ be the ring of integers modulo $m$. Let $\circ$ be the mapping from $\Z_m \times R$ to $R$ defined as: $\forall \eqclass a m \in \Z_m: \forall x \in R: \eqclass a m \circ x = a \cdot x$ where $\eqclass a m$ is the residue class of $a$ modulo $m$ and $a \cdot x$ is the $a$th power of $x$. Then $\struct {R, +, \circ}_{\Z_m}$ is a unitary $\Z_m$-module.

title: ZFC requires Axiom Schema
snippet: The system of axiomatic set theory known as Zermelo-Fraenkel Set Theory with the Axiom of Choice requires an axiom schema.

title: Zariski's Lemma
snippet: Let $L / k$ be a field extension. Let $L$ be finitely generated as an algebra over $k$. Then $L / k$ is a finite field extension.

title: Zariski Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \in \N_{>0}$. Let $\tau$ be the Zariski topology on $k^n$. Then $\tau$ is indeed a topology on $k^n$.

title: Zassenhaus Lemma
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be subgroups of $G$ such that: where $\lhd$ denotes the relation of being a normal subgroup. Then: {{eqn | l = \frac {N_1 \paren {H_1 \cap H_2} } {N_1 \paren {H_1 \cap N_2} } | o = \cong | m = \frac {H_1 \cap H_2} {\paren {H_1 \cap N_2} \paren {N_1 \cap H_2} } | mo= \cong | r = \frac {N_2 \paren {H_1 \cap H_2} } {N_2 \paren {N_1 \cap H_2} } }} where: $N_1 \paren {H_1 \cap H_2}$, and so on, denotes subset product $\cong$ denotes group isomorphism.

title: Zeckendorf's Theorem
snippet: Every positive integer has a unique Zeckendorf representation. That is: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Then there exists a unique increasing sequence of integers $\sequence {c_i}$ such that: {{eqn | q = \forall i \in \N | l = c_{i + 1} | o = > | r = c_i + 1 | c = }} {{eqn | l = n | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^k F_{c_i} | c = }} where $F_m$ is the $m$th Fibonacci number. For any given $n$, such a $\sequence {c_i}$ is unique. Note that $c_i = 1$ is excluded from the representation in order to ensure that uniqueness.

title: Zeckendorf Representation of Integer shifted Left
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \floor {x + \phi^{-1} }$ where: $\floor {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function $\phi$ denotes the golden mean. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $n$ be expressed in Zeckendorf representation: $n = F_{k_1} + F_{k_2} + \cdots + F_{k_r}$ with the appropriate restrictions on $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r$. Then: $F_{k_1 + 1} + F_{k_2 + 1} + \cdots + F_{k_r + 1} = \map f {\phi n}$

title: Zeckendorf Representation of Integer shifted Right
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\forall x \in \R: \map f x = \floor {x + \phi^{-1} }$ where: $\floor {\, \cdot \,}$ denotes the floor function $\phi$ denotes the golden mean. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Let $n$ be expressed in Zeckendorf representation: $n = F_{k_1} + F_{k_2} + \cdots + F_{k_r}$ with the appropriate restrictions on $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r$. Then: $F_{k_1 - 1} + F_{k_2 - 1} + \cdots + F_{k_r - 1} = \map f {\phi^{-1} n}$

title: Zenith Distance is Complement of Celestial Altitude
snippet: Let $X$ be the position of a star (or other celestial body) on the celestial sphere. The zenith distance $z$ of $X$ is the complement of the altitude $a$ of $X$: $z = 90 \degrees - a$

title: Zenith Distance of North Celestial Pole equals Colatitude of Observer
snippet: Let $O$ be an observer of the celestial sphere. Let $P$ be the position of the north celestial pole with respect to $O$. Let $z$ denote the zenith distance of $P$. Let $\psi$ denote the (terrestrial) colatitude of $O$. Then: $z = \psi$

title: Zeno's Paradoxes
snippet: == Paradoxes == Zeno's paradoxes are a set of antinomies devised by to demonstrate that the mathematical understanding of motion and space had conceptual gaps. These paradoxes were preserved in the writings of . originals have not survived to the present day.

title: Zermelo's Theorem (Set Theory)
snippet: Every set of cardinals is well-ordered with respect to $\le$.

title: Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then every set is well-orderable.

title: Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem implies Hausdorff's Maximal Principle
snippet: Let Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem hold. Then Hausdorff's Maximal Principle holds.

title: Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem is Equivalent to Axiom of Choice
snippet: Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem holds the Axiom of Choice holds. That is, every set is well-orderable every collection of sets has a choice function.

title: Zero-Sum Game/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Zero-Sum Games ==

title: Zero (Category) is Initial Object
snippet: Let $\mathbf{Cat}$ be the category of categories. Let $\mathbf 0$ be the zero category. Then $\mathbf 0$ is an initial object of $\mathbf{Cat}$.

title: Zero Choose Zero
snippet: $\dbinom 0 0 = 1$ where $\dbinom 0 0$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

title: Zero Choose n
snippet: $\dbinom 0 n = \delta_{0 n}$ where: $\dbinom 0 n$ denotes a binomial coefficient $\delta_{0 n}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

title: Zero Complement is Not Empty
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $S^*$ be the zero complement of $S$. Then $S^*$ is not empty.

title: Zero Definite Integral of Nowhere Negative Function implies Zero Function
snippet: Let $\closedint a b \subseteq \R$ be a closed real interval. Let $h: \closedint a b \to \R$ be a continuous real function such that: $\forall x \in \closedint a b: \map h x \ge 0$ Let: $\ds \int_a^b \map h x \rd x = 0$ Then: $\forall x \in \closedint a b: \map h x = 0$

title: Zero Derivative implies Constant Complex Function
snippet: Let $D \subseteq \C$ be a connected domain of $\C$. Let $f: D \to \C$ be a complex-differentiable function. For all $z \in D$, let $\map {f'} z = 0$. Then $f$ is constant on $D$.

title: Zero Derivative implies Constant Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Suppose that: $\forall x \in \openint a b: \map {f'} x = 0$ Then $f$ is constant on $\closedint a b$.

title: Zero Dimensional Space is T3
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a zero dimensional topological space. Then $T$ is a $T_3$ space.

title: Zero Dimensional Space is T3.5
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a zero dimensional topological space. Then $T$ is a $T_{3 \frac 1 2}$ space.

title: Zero Dimensional Space is not necessarily T0
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a zero dimensional topological space. Then $T$ is not necessarily a $T_0$ (Kolmogorov) space.

title: Zero Dimensional T0 Space is Totally Separated
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a zero dimensional topological space which is also a $T_0$ space. Then $T$ is totally separated.

title: Zero Divides Zero
snippet: Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $0 \divides n \implies n = 0$ That is, zero is the only integer divisible by zero.

title: Zero Divisor Product is Zero Divisor
snippet: The ring product of a zero divisor with any ring element is a zero divisor.

title: Zero Divisor of Ring/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Zero Divisors of Rings ==

title: Zero Element Generates Null Ideal
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring whose zero is $0_R$. For $r \in R$, let $\ideal r$ denote the ideal generated by $r$. Then $\ideal {0_R}$ is the null ideal.

title: Zero Element is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure that has a zero element $z \in S$. Then $z$ is unique.

title: Zero Element of Multiplication on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the zero element of multiplication is zero ($0$).

title: Zero Element of Union and Intersection
snippet: == Source Work == Introduction to Set Theory $1$. Elementary Operations on Sets This mistake can be seen in the 2009 Dover edition: ISBN 0-486-47222-1

title: Zero Equals One
snippet: == Paradox == {{eqn | ll= \leadsto | l = 4^2 - 9 \times 4 + \dfrac {81} 4 | r = 5^2 - 9 \times 5 + \dfrac {81} 4 | c = }} {{eqn | ll= \leadsto | l = \paren {4 - \frac 9 2}^2 | r = \paren {5 - \frac 9 2}^2 | c = }}

title: Zero Function Vanishes in Neighborhood of Infinity
snippet: Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space. Define a function $f : X \to \C$ by: $\map f x = 0$ for each $x \in X$. Then $f$ vanishes in a neighborhood of infinity.

title: Zero Locus of Larger Set is Smaller
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Let $A = k \sqbrk {X_1, \ldots, X_n}$ be the ring of polynomials in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $I, J \subseteq A$ be subsets, and $\map V I$ and $\map V J$ their zero loci. Let $I \subseteq J$. Then $\map V I \supseteq \map V J$.

title: Zero Locus of Set is Zero Locus of Generated Ideal
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Let $A = k \sqbrk {X_1, \ldots, X_n}$ be the ring of polynomial functions in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $T \subseteq A$ be a subset, and $\map V T$ the zero locus of $T$. Let $J = \ideal T$ be the ideal generated by $T$. Then: $\map V T = \map V J$

title: Zero Locus of Vanishing Ideal is Closure
snippet: Let $k$ be a field. Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number. Let $k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Let $\mathbb A^n_k$ be the standard affine space over $k$. Let $\mathbb A^n_k$ be equipped with the Zariski topology. Let $S \subseteq \mathbb A^n_k$. Then: $\map V {\map I S} = S^-$ where: $\map I \cdot$ denotes the vanishing ideal $\map V \cdot$ denotes the zero locus $S^-$ is the closure of $S$.

title: Zero Matrix is Identity for Hadamard Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \cdot}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix space over $S$. Let $\mathbf e = \sqbrk e_{m n}$ be the zero matrix of $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf e$ is the identity element for Hadamard product.

title: Zero Matrix is Identity for Matrix Entrywise Addition
snippet: Let $\map \MM {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over one of the standard number systems. Let $\mathbf 0 = \sqbrk 0_{m n}$ be the zero matrix of $\map \MM {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf 0$ is the identity element for matrix entrywise addition.

title: Zero Matrix is Identity for Matrix Entrywise Addition over Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$ be a $m \times n$ matrix space over $R$. Let $\mathbf 0_R = \sqbrk {0_R}_{m n}$ be the zero matrix of $\map {\MM_R} {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf 0_R$ is the identity element for matrix entrywise addition.

title: Zero Matrix is Zero for Matrix Multiplication
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring. Let $\mathbf A$ be a matrix over $R$ of order $m \times n$ Let $\mathbf 0$ be a zero matrix whose order is such that either: $\mathbf {0 A}$ is defined or: $\mathbf {A 0}$ is defined or both. Then: $\mathbf {0 A} = \mathbf 0$ or: $\mathbf {A 0} = \mathbf 0$ whenever they are defined. The order of $\mathbf 0$ will be according to the orders of the factor matrices.

title: Zero Measure is Absolutely Continuous with respect to Every Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {M, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {M, \Sigma}$. Let $\nu$ be the null measure on $\struct {M, \Sigma}$. Then $\nu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu$.

title: Zero Morphism does not Depend on Zero Object
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $A$ and $B$ be objects of $\mathbf C$. Let $0_1$ and $0_2$ be zero objects of $\mathbf C$. Then the morphism defined as the composition $\beta \circ \alpha : A \to 0_1 \to B$ of the unique morphism $\alpha : A \to 0_1$ and the unique morphism $\beta : 0_1 \to B$ is equal to the morphism defined as the composition $\delta \circ \gamma : A \to 0_2 \to B$ of the unique morphism $\gamma : A \to 0_2$ and the unique morphism $\delta : 0_2 \to B$.

title: Zero Padded Basis Representation
snippet: Let $b \in \Z: b > 1$. Let $m \in \Z_{> 0}$. For every $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ such that $n < b^m$, there exists one and only one sequence $\sequence {r_j}_{0 \mathop \le j \mathop \le m - 1}$ such that: {{eqn | n = 1 | l = n | r = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{m - 1} r_j b^j }} {{eqn | n = 2 | q = \forall j \in \closedint 0 {m - 1} | l = r_j | o = \in | r = \N_b }}

title: Zero Product of Numbers implies Factors are Zero
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the following holds. Let $a \times b = 0$. Then either $a = 0$ or $b = 0$.

title: Zero Product with Proper Zero Divisor is with Zero Divisor
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $x \in R$ be a proper zero divisor of $R$. Then: $\paren {x \divides 0_R} \land \paren {x \circ y = 0_R} \land \paren {y \ne 0_R} \implies y \divides 0_R$ That is, if $x$ is a proper zero divisor, then whatever non-zero element you form the product with it by to get zero must itself be a zero divisor.

title: Zero Set of Semi-Inner Product is Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a semi-inner product space over $\GF$. Let: $N = \set {x \in V : \innerprod x x = 0}$ Then $N$ is a vector subspace of $V$.

title: Zero Sets are Exactly the Closed G-Delta Sets in T4 Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_4$ topological space. Then the zero sets in $T$ are precisely the closed $G_\delta$ subsets of $S$.

title: Zero Simple Staircase Integral Condition for Primitive
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a continuous complex function, where $D$ is a connected domain. Let $\ds \oint_C \map f z \rd z = 0$ for all simple closed staircase contours $C$ in $D$. Then $f$ has a primitive $F: D \to \C$.

title: Zero Staircase Integral Condition for Primitive
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a continuous complex function, where $D$ is an open and connected domain. Let $z_0 \in D$. Suppose that $\ds \oint_C \map f z \rd z = 0$ for all closed staircase contours $C$ in $D$. Then $f$ has a primitive $F: D \to \C$ defined by: $\ds \map F w = \int_{C_w} \map f z \rd z$ where $C_w$ is any staircase contour in $D$ with start point $z_0$ and end point $w$.

title: Zero Strictly Precedes One
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $0$ be the zero of $S$. Let $1$ be the one of $S$. Then: $0 \prec 1$

title: Zero Subspace is Subspace
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$ with zero vector $\mathbf 0$. The zero subspace $\set {\mathbf 0}$ is a subspace of $V$.

title: Zero Vector Scaled is Zero Vector
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_K$ be a vector space over a division ring $K$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \lambda \in K: \lambda \ast \bszero = \bszero$ where $\bszero \in \mathbf V$ is the zero vector.

title: Zero Vector Space Product iff Factor is Zero
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +_F, \times_F}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +_V, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Let $\mathbf v \in \mathbf V, \lambda \in F$. Then: $\lambda \ast \mathbf v = \bszero \iff \paren {\lambda = 0_F \lor x = \bszero}$

title: Zero Vector has no Direction
snippet: A zero vector has no direction.

title: Zero Vector in *-Algebra is Hermitian
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast}$ be a $\ast$-algebra. Let ${\mathbf 0}_A$ be the zero vector of $A$. Then we have: ${\mathbf 0}_A^\ast = {\mathbf 0}_A$

title: Zero Vector is Linearly Dependent
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Then the singleton set $\set e$ consisting of the zero vector is linearly dependent.

title: Zero Vector is Orthogonal to All Vectors
snippet: Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space of $n$ dimensions. Let $\bszero \in \mathbf V$ be the zero vector. Let $\mathbf a \in \mathbf V$ be an arbitrary vector in $\mathbf V$ Then $\bszero$ is orthogonal to $\mathbf a$.

title: Zero Vector is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \circ}_{\mathbb F}$ be a vector space over $\mathbb F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then the zero vector in $\mathbf V$ is unique: $\exists! \mathbf 0 \in \mathbf V: \forall \mathbf x \in \mathbf V: \mathbf x + \mathbf 0 = \mathbf x$

title: Zero Wronskian of Solutions of Homogeneous Linear Second Order ODE
snippet: Let $\map {y_1} x$ and $\map {y_2} x$ be particular solutions to the homogeneous linear second order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + \map P x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map Q x y = 0$ on a closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $y_1$ and $y_2$ be linearly independent. Then their Wronskian is either never zero, or zero everywhere on $\closedint a b$.

title: Zero Wronskian of Solutions of Homogeneous Linear Second Order ODE iff Linearly Dependent
snippet: Let $\map {y_1} x$ and $\map {y_2} x$ be particular solutions to the homogeneous linear second order ODE: $(1): \quad \dfrac {\d^2 y} {\d x^2} + \map P x \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} + \map Q x y = 0$ on a closed interval $\closedint a b$. Then: $y_1$ and $y_2$ are linearly dependent the Wronskian $\map W {y_1, y_2}$ of $y_1$ and $y_2$ is zero everywhere on $\closedint a b$.

title: Zero and One are the only Consecutive Perfect Squares
snippet: If $n$ is a perfect square other than $0$, then $n+1$ is not a perfect square.

title: Zero and Unity of Subfield
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$ and whose unity is $1$. Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a subfield of $F$.

title: Zero is Accumulation Point of Sequence in Sierpiński Space
snippet: Let $T = \struct {\set {0, 1}, \tau_0}$ be a Sierpiński space. The sequence in $T$: $\sigma = \sequence {0, 1, 0, 1, \ldots}$ has $0$ as an accumulation point.

title: Zero is Identity in Naturally Ordered Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$ be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let $0$ be the zero of $\struct {S, \circ, \preceq}$. Then $0$ is the identity for $\circ$. That is: $\forall n \in S: n \circ 0 = n = 0 \circ n$

title: Zero is Integer Multiple of Zero
snippet: Zero is an integer multiple of zero.

title: Zero is Limit Point of Integer Reciprocal Space
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $0$ is the only limit point of $A$ in $\R$.

title: Zero is Limit Point of Integer Reciprocal Space Union with Closed Interval
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $T = \struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $B$ be the uncountable set: $B := A \cup \closedint 2 3$ where $\closedint 2 3$ is a closed interval of $\R$. $2$ and $3$ are to all intents arbitrary, but convenient. Then $0$ is a limit point of $B$ in $\R$.

title: Zero is Omega-Accumulation Point of Integer Reciprocal Space Union with Closed Interval
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $B$ be the uncountable set: $B := A \cup \closedint 2 3$ where $\closedint 2 3$ is a closed interval of $\R$. $2$ and $3$ are to all intents arbitrary, but convenient. Then $0$ is an $\omega$-accumulation point of $B$ in $\R$.

title: Zero is Smallest Ordinal
snippet: The natural number $0$ is the smallest ordinal.

title: Zero is Zero Element for Natural Number Multiplication
snippet: Let $\N$ be the natural numbers. Then $0$ is a zero element for multiplication: $\forall n \in \N: 0 \times n = 0 = n \times 0$

title: Zero is both Positive and Negative
snippet: The number $0$ (zero) is the only (real) number which is both: a positive (real) number and a negative (real) number.

title: Zero is not Condensation Point of Integer Reciprocal Space Union with Closed Interval
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $B$ be the uncountable set: $B := A \cup \closedint 2 3$ where $\closedint 2 3$ is a closed interval of $\R$. $2$ and $3$ are to all intents arbitrary, but convenient. Then $0$ is not a condensation point of $B$ in $\R$.

title: Zero is not a Limit Point of Sequence of Reciprocals and Reciprocals + 1
snippet: Let $\struct {\R, \tau}$ denote the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ denote the sequence in $\struct {\R, \tau}$ defined as: {{eqn | l = a_n | r = \begin {cases} \dfrac 2 {n + 1} & : \text {$n$ odd} \\ \\ 1 + \dfrac 2 n & : \text {$n$ even} \end {cases} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \sequence {\dfrac 1 1, 1 + \dfrac 1 1, \dfrac 1 2, 1 + \dfrac 1 2, \dfrac 1 3, 1 + \dfrac 1 3, \dotsb} | c = }} Then $0$ is not a limit of $\sequence {a_n}$.

title: Zero of Cardinal Product is Zero
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$ be a cardinal. Then: $\mathbf 0 \mathbf a = \mathbf 0$ where $\mathbf 0 \mathbf a$ denotes the product of the (cardinal) zero and $\mathbf a$. That is, $\mathbf 0$ is the zero element of the product operation on cardinals.

title: Zero of Field is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field. The zero of $F$ is unique.

title: Zero of Integral Domain is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \times}$ be an integral domain. Then the zero of $\struct {D, +, \times}$ is unique.

title: Zero of Inverse Completion of Integral Domain
snippet: Let $\struct {D, +, \circ}$ be an integral domain whose zero is $0_D$. Let $\struct {K, \circ}$ be the inverse completion of $\struct {D, \circ}$ as defined in Inverse Completion of Integral Domain Exists. Let $x \in K: x = \dfrac p q$ such that $p = 0_D$. Then $x$ is equal to the zero of $K$. That is, any element of $K$ of the form $\dfrac {0_D} q$ acts as the zero of $K$.

title: Zero of Power Set with Intersection
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be its power set. Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset S, \cap}$, where $\cap$ denotes set intersection. Then the empty set $\O$ serves as the zero element for $\struct {\powerset S, \cap}$.

title: Zero of Power Set with Union
snippet: Let $S$ be a set and let $\powerset S$ be its power set. Consider the algebraic structure $\struct {\powerset S, \cup}$, where $\cup$ denotes set union. Then $S$ serves as the zero element for $\struct {\powerset S, \cup}$.

title: Zero of Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{\R^S}} s = 0$

title: Zero of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with zero $0_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{R^S} : S \to R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{R^S}} s = 0_R$

title: Zero of Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{\R^S}} s = 0$

title: Zero of Subfield is Zero of Field
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0$. Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a subfield of $\struct {F, +, \times}$. The zero of $\struct {K, +, \times}$ is also $0$.

title: Zero of Subring is Zero of Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring whose zero is $0$. Let $\struct {S, +, \times}$ be a subring of $\struct {R, +, \times}$. The zero of $\struct {S, +, \times}$ is also $0$.

title: Zero to the Power of Zero
snippet: == Examples == In light of some mathematicians' (or, indeed, muggles') reticence to define the zeroth power of zero as $1$, the following are examples of reasons why defining $0^0 = 1$ is a good idea.

title: Zeroes of Functions of Finite Order
snippet: Let $\map f z$ be an entire function which satisfies: $\map f 0 \ne 0$ $\cmod {\map f z} \ll \map \exp {\map \alpha {\cmod z} }$ for all $z \in \C$ and some function $\alpha$, where $\ll$ is the order notation. For $T \ge 1$, let: $\map N T = \# \set {\rho \in \C: \map f r = 0, \ \cmod \rho < T}$ where $\#$ denotes the cardinality of a set. Then: $\map N T \ll \map \alpha {2 T}$

title: Zeroes of Gamma Function
snippet: The Gamma function is never equal to $0$.

title: Zeroes of Infinite Product of Analytic Functions
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open connected set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n: D \to \C$. Let $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge locally uniformly to $f$. Let $z_0\in D$. Then: $(1): \quad$ $f$ is identically zero some $f_n$ is identically zero $(2): \quad$ $\map {f_n} {z_0} = 0$ for finitely many $n \in \N$ $(3): \quad$ If $f$ is not identically zero, $\map {\operatorname {mult}_{z_0} } f = \ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \map {\operatorname {mult}_{z_0} } {f_n}$ where $\operatorname {mult}$ denotes multiplicity.

title: Zeroes of Meromorphic Function are of Finite Order
snippet: Let $f: D \to \C$ be a meromorphic function on the open subset $D$ of $\C$. The zeroes of $f$ are of finite order.

title: Zeroes of Non-Constant Analytic Function are Isolated
snippet: Let $U \subset \C$ be some open set. Let $f$ be an analytic function defined on $U$. Then either $f$ is a constant function, or the set $\set {z \in U: \map f z = 0}$ is totally disconnected.

title: Zeroes of Sine and Cosine
snippet: == Theorem == Let $x \in \R$.

title: Zerofree Entire Function of Finite Order is Exponential of Polynomial
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of finite order. Let $f$ have no zeroes. Then $f = \exp P$ for some polynomial $P$.

title: Zeroth Hyperoperation is Successor Function
snippet: The zeroth hyperoperation is the successor function: $H_0 \left({x, y}\right) = y + 1$

title: Zeroth Power of Real Number equals One
snippet: Let $a \in \R_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive real number. Let $a^x$ be defined as $a$ to the power of $x$. Then: $a^0 = 1$

title: Zeta Equivalence to Prime Number Theorem
snippet: Let $\map \zeta z$ be the Riemann $\zeta$ function. The Prime Number Theorem is logically equivalent to the statement that the average of the first $N$ coefficients of $\dfrac {\zeta'} {\zeta}$ tend to $-1$ as $N$ goes to infinity. {{explain|What does $z$ range over, and what does it mean by "first $N$ coefficients" of $\dfrac {\zeta'} {\zeta}$?}}

title: Zorn's Lemma Implies Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem
snippet: Zorn's Lemma implies Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem.

title: Zorn's Lemma implies Axiom of Choice
snippet: Let Zorn's Lemma be accepted. Then the Axiom of Choice holds.

title: Zorn's Lemma implies Hausdorff's Maximal Principle
snippet: Let Zorn's Lemma be accepted as true. Then Hausdorff's Maximal Principle holds.

title: Zorn's Lemma implies Kuratowski's Lemma
snippet: Let Zorn's Lemma be accepted as true. Then Kuratowski's Lemma holds.

title: Zsigmondy's Theorem
snippet: Let $a > b > 0$ be coprime positive integers. Let $n \ge 1$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then there is a prime number $p$ such that $p$ divides $a^n - b^n$ $p$ does not divide $a^k - b^k$ for all $k < n$ with the following exceptions: $n = 1$ and $a - b = 1$ $n = 2$ and $a + b$ is a power of $2$ $n = 6$, $a = 2$, $b = 1$

title: Zsigmondy's Theorem for Sums
snippet: Let $a > b > 0$ be coprime positive integers. Let $n \ge 1$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Then there is a prime number $p$ such that $p$ divides $a^n + b^n$ $p$ does not divide $a^k + b^k$ for all $k < n$ with the following exception: $n = 3$, $a = 2$, $b = 1$

title: Łoś's Theorem
snippet: Let $\LL$ be a language. Let $I$ be an infinite set. Let $\UU$ be an ultrafilter on $I$. Let $\map \phi {v_1, \ldots, v_n}$ be an $\LL$-formula. Let $\MM$ be the ultraproduct: $\ds \paren {\prod_{i \mathop \in I} \MM_i} / \UU$ where each $\MM_i$ is an $\LL$-structure. Then, for all $m_1 = \paren {m_{1, i} }_\UU, \dots, m_n = \paren {m_{n, i} }_\UU$ in $\MM$: $\MM \models \map \phi {m_1, \ldots, m_n}$ the set $\set {i \in I: \MM_i \models \map \phi {m_{1, i}, \ldots, m_{n, i} } }$ is in $\UU$.

title: Łoś-Vaught Test
snippet: Let $T$ be a satisfiable $\LL$-theory with no finite models. Let $T$ be $\kappa$-categorical for some infinite cardinal $\kappa \ge \card \LL$. Then $T$ is complete.
